item.title: Senior Director of Public Relations
item.description: Senior Director of Public Relations Organization: Howard University Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## The Talent Acquisition department The Talent Acquisition department hires qualified candidates to fill positions which contribute to the overall strategic success of Howard University. Hiring staff “for fit” makes significant contributions to Howard University’s overall mission. At Howard University, we prioritize well-being and professional growth. ### Here is what we offer: **Health & Wellness:** Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus mental health support **Work-Life Balance:** PTO, paid holidays, flexible work arrangements **Financial Wellness:** Competitive salary, 403(b) with company match **Professional Development:** Ongoing training, tuition reimbursement, and career advancement paths **Additional Perks:** Wellness programs, commuter benefits, and a vibrant company culture Join Howard University and thrive with us! [https://hr.howard.edu/benefits-wellness] — ## BASIC FUNCTIONS The Senior Director of Public Relations is a senior communications strategist responsible for leading the University’s enterprise-wide media relations, public relations, and external communications initiatives that advance Howard University’s reputation, visibility, and strategic priorities. The Senior Director serves as one of the University’s primary media relations leaders, providing strategic counsel to senior leadership while overseeing proactive and responsive communications that strengthen Howard University’s reputation among key stakeholders. Under the direction of the Vice President and Chief Communications Officer, and as a member of the Office of University Communications leadership team, the Senior Director develops and implements integrated public relations strategies that elevate the University’s local, national, and global profile by promoting academic excellence, research innovation, institutional leadership, faculty expertise, student achievement, alumni success, community engagement, and other strategic initiatives. — ## NATURE AND SCOPE The Senior Director of Public Relations serves as a senior communications leader responsible for advancing Howard University’s reputation through strategic media relations, issues management, executive communications, and risk/crisis communications. The position partners with senior leadership and University stakeholders to support institutional priorities and enhance the University’s visibility and brand. — ## SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY Provides strategic leadership and supervision for the Media Relations staff, student workers and student interns, including assigning work, establishing performance expectations, coaching and mentoring staff, conducting performance evaluations, and supporting professional development. Oversees the Media Relations operating budget, external vendors, and departmental resources to ensure the effective and efficient execution of strategic communications initiatives. — ## PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES ### Strategic Public Relations – Collaborate with the Office of University Communications leadership and management teams to develop and execute comprehensive public relations strategies that support the University’s strategic priorities and institutional goals. – Lead proactive media relations initiatives that increase visibility for Howard University’s academic, research, philanthropic, and institutional accomplishments. – Identify and develop opportunities to position University leaders, faculty, and subject matter experts as trusted voices on issues of national and global importance. – Build and maintain strong relationships with local, regional, national, and international media outlets. – Develop integrated communications plans for major institutional announcements, initiatives, and special projects. ### Media Relations – Serve as a background spokesperson for the University and respond to media inquiries on behalf of the institution. – Develop media pitches, press releases, background materials, talking points, and press kits. – Coordinate interviews, media briefings, editorial board meetings, and press conferences. – Cultivate long-term relationships with journalists, editors, producers, and influencers across print, broadcast, digital, and trade media. – Monitor emerging news opportunities and recommend proactive media engagement strategies. – Serves as the primary OUC liaison to the Office of Student Affairs leadership and leadership of the Divisions/Departments under the Office of Student Affairs, including the Athletics Department. ### Reputation Management & Executive Communications – Advise the Vice President & Chief Communications Officer and senior University leadership on media strategy, messaging, and reputational considerations. – Develop strategic messaging that reinforces Howard University’s mission, values, and institutional priorities. – Support executive visibility initiatives through earned media opportunities and thought leadership strategies. – Provide communications counsel and lead rapid response efforts on sensitive institutional issues and emerging opportunities. ### Issues & Crisis Communications – Assist in developing and implementing crisis communications strategies and issues management plans. – Prepare executive statements, key messages, FAQs, and communications materials during time-sensitive situations. – Monitor emerging issues that may affect the University’s reputation and recommend appropriate communications strategies. – Participate in the University’s emergency communications planning and response efforts. ### Integrated Communications – Collaborate with colleagues across the Office of University Communications to develop integrated communications campaigns that leverage earned media, owned media, digital communications, publications, web, photography, video, and social media. – Partner with academic schools, colleges, research centers, administrative units, and institutional leaders to identify and promote newsworthy stories. – Ensure consistency of messaging, institutional voice, and brand across external communications. ### Media Monitoring & Analytics – Oversee media monitoring and measurement programs and reports to evaluate earned media performance, and analyze media coverage, audience engagement, and communications metrics to inform strategy. – Identify trends in higher education, news media, and public discourse that may influence University communications, and prepare executive reports demonstrating communications outcomes and institutional impact. ### Leadership & Administration – Supervise media relations staff, student workers and student interns, as assigned. – Establish departmental goals, performance expectations, and professional development plans. – Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and agency partnerships related to media relations and public relations initiatives. – Foster a collaborative, innovative, and service-oriented communications culture. – Perform other duties as assigned. — ## CORE COMPETENCIES ### Strategic Leadership and Collaboration – Experience developing enterprise-wide communications strategies aligned with institutional priorities. – Proven ability to exercise sound judgment in high-profile and sensitive situations. – Demonstrates executive presence and strategic thinking. – Builds trusted relationships across diverse internal and external stakeholders. – Works effectively across organizational boundaries to advance institutional goals. – Demonstrates diplomacy, discretion, professionalism, and support of leadership priorities. ### Media Relations – Extensive experience cultivating relationships with journalists and media organizations. – Strong news judgment and storytelling ability. – Skilled spokesperson and media strategist. ### Communications Excellence – Outstanding writing, editing, and message development skills. – Ability to translate complex academic and institutional topics into compelling, accessible narratives. – Demonstrated crisis communications and rapid response writing experience. – Strong presentation, executive presence, and public speaking skills. ### Project & Performance Management – Successfully manages multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. – Uses analytics and performance metrics to measure communications effectiveness. – Leads teams and projects with accountability and results orientation. — ## MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS – Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, Public Relations, Strategic Communications, Marketing, English, or a related discipline. – Master’s degree and experience leading college or university communications preferred but not required. – Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in media relations, public relations, strategic communications, journalism, or corporate communications. – Minimum of seven years of supervisory and leadership experience. – Experience leading higher education, nonprofit, government, or other mission-driven organizations, and strong understanding of higher education communications or similarly complex organizations. – Experience managing crisis communications and issues management. – Demonstrated success managing high-profile communications initiatives and complex media environments. – Experience serving as an institutional spokesperson, and successfully securing national, regional, and international media coverage. – Experience advising senior executives on communications strategy and reputation management. – Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills. – Experience using media monitoring and analytics platforms (e.g., Cision, Meltwater, Muck Rack, or similar), and digital media strategy, content management systems, and AI-assisted communications tools. – Ability to work outside of normal business hours. — ## Compliance Salary Range Disclosure **Expected Salary Range:** $145,000 – $150,000 Apply here Earn a certificate wit

item.title: Public Relations Manager
item.description: Public Relations Manager Organization: Gensler Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 **Description** The Southeast Region is looking for a senior PR leader in Washington, DC to run media relations, thought leadership, and executive communications for one of the firm’s most diverse US Regions. **Your Role** The Public Relations Manager leads PR strategy for the Southeast Region, working with the regional managing principals, regional marketing director, PR specialists, studio directors, and practice area leaders to identify stories, then turn them into proactive content and campaigns, and secure media coverage. The role calls for someone who understands the design and real estate market and can shape Gensler’s brand into compelling stories, while managing multiple deliverables at once with strategic judgment. **What You Will Do** – Develop and lead PR strategy and campaigns for the Southeast Region, in partnership with office and regional leadership – Secure media coverage proactively and manage inbound press inquiries, building and maintaining relationships with local and national outlets covering design, real estate, business, and innovation – Create thought leadership content such as speaking engagement materials, brand publications, website content, and award submissions, and guide its distribution across channels – Develop executive communications and positioning for office and practice area leaders – Serve as a strategic communications partner to clients, ensuring content supports both their goals and Gensler’s – Advise on PR risk and monitor the news cycle as it relates to our work, including outside business hours when needed – Mentor PR and communications team members, and represent the Southeast in the firmwide public relations community – Liaise with a firmwide network of public relations staff to develop messaging, regional digital and social media strategy, and initiatives – Track PR and engagement metrics to inform future strategy **Your Qualifications** – 10–20 years of experience in PR, including experience managing a team; background in architecture, design, or commercial real estate preferred, agency or journalism experience a plus – Established editorial relationships in design, business, and innovation media, in DC and beyond – Excellent communication, writing, and editing skills – Experience managing PR and communications projects independently and in close collaboration with senior leadership – Ability to manage multiple deadlines and thrive under pressure in a fast‑paced environment *This role is not remote or hybrid; we look forward to working with our new PR Leader in our dynamic Washington, D.C. office.* The base salary range will be estimated between $100,000–$140,000. Gensler’s total compensation package is multi‑layered and includes a base salary, plus two annual bonuses paid in December and June. To learn more about our compensation philosophy and full benefits offerings, please visit Great People, Great Rewards | Gensler. **Life at Gensler** At Gensler, we are as committed to enjoying life as we are to delivering best‑in‑class design. From curated art exhibits to internal design competitions to “Well‑being Awareness Week,” our offices reflect our people’s diverse interests. We encourage every person at Gensler to lead a healthy and balanced life. Our comprehensive benefits include medical, dental, vision, disability, wellness programs, flex spending, paid holidays, and paid time off. We also offer a 401k, profit sharing, employee stock ownership, and twice‑annual bonus opportunities. Our annual base salary range has been established based on local markets. As part of the firm’s commitment to licensure and professional development, Gensler offers reimbursement for certain professional licenses and associated renewals and exam fees. In addition, we reimburse tuition for certain eligible programs or classes. We view our professional development programs as strategic investments in our future. **NOTICE TO APPLICANTS** We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer of choice. All aspects of employment decisions will be based on merit, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of any status protected under federal, state, and local law. Individuals with disabilities and protected veterans are encouraged to apply. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with federal, state, and local law. See also Know your rights: Workplace discrimination is illegal, right to work and E‑verify program, as required by law. Gensler endeavors to make gensler.com/careers accessible to all applicants. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us. Regarding Gensler’s approach to recruiting new talent, we will never ask an applicant for sensitive or personal financial information during the recruitment process. We advise all applicants seeking employment with Gensler to review available information on recruitment fraud. Anyone who suspects that they have been contacted by someone falsely representing Gensler should email [email protected] . #LI‑NM1 Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Director, Global Health Security, Health Programs
item.description: Senior Director, Global Health Security, Health Programs Organization: FHI 360 Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/26/2026 **JOB SUMMARY** The Senior Director, Global Health Security (GHS), Health Programs serves as a strategic leader within FHI 360’s Health Programs department, responsible for overseeing the implementation of multiple program portfolios and initiatives spanning epidemic and pandemic prevention, preparedness, detection, and response. Reporting to the Senior (Sr.) Director, Health Programs Global Technical Team, this role provides operational oversight to the GHS division comprised of multiple project teams, fosters innovation, and ensures the delivery of high-quality outcomes aligned with organizational objectives and donor requirements. The Sr. Director, GHS collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to gather and share evidence, lessons learned, and best practices to drive continuous improvement and organizational impact. The Sr. Director, GHS provides leadership, guidance, and direction to the GHS technical team that span award implementation, technical quality, innovation, and knowledge management. Their decisions are guided by organizational strategy and have significant short- and long-term impacts on public health and development outcomes. — **RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES** **Complexity & Problem Solving:** Navigates complex challenges inherent in project implementation including implementation in outbreak-affected, fragile, and rapidly evolving operating environments. Offers strategic direction and innovative solutions for technical challenges. Analyzes project performance and identifies areas for improvement. Recommends actionable solutions to enhance effectiveness and efficiency. Fosters innovation and shares best practices to drive organizational impact. Contributes to achieving sustainable development goals. Makes time-critical technical and operational decisions during outbreaks and public health emergencies, frequently on incomplete information and under compressed timelines. Resolves cross-award technical questions spanning surveillance and early warning, laboratory systems, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement, workforce development, antimicrobial resistance, zoonotic disease and One Health, and emergency preparedness and response, and sets the standard to be applied across the portfolio. Anticipates and mitigates programmatic, security, staff safety, and reputational risks associated with work in outbreak-affected and fragile settings. **Discretion & Impact:** Exercises discretion over project-related GHS technical matters with direct impact on project outcomes and organizational success. Works closely with project leadership to decisions on resource allocation, risk management, and stakeholder engagement. Influences portfolio performance and reputation. Decisions contribute to achieving organizational objectives and driving positive change. Impacts both short- and long-term public health outcomes. **Collaboration & Interaction:** Engages with internal and external stakeholders to gather and share evidence, lessons learned, and best practices. Fosters partnerships with project teams, donors, and implementing partners. Facilitates communication and knowledge exchange to enhance project outcomes. Communication style is characterized by transparency, collaboration, and teamwork. Works cross-functionally to achieve common goals and drive organizational impact. Establishes and maintains relationships across FHI 360, including with all Groups and Enterprise Support colleagues. Represents FHI 360 with ministries of health, national public health institutes, donors, multilateral agencies, and technical working groups and coordination mechanisms on health security. Coordinates across awards and country programs to align technical messaging, avoid duplication, and present a single coherent organizational position to donors and host-country counterparts. Contributes to publications, conferences, and technical convenings, positioning FHI 360 as a thought leader in epidemic and pandemic preparedness and response. Contributes to business development initiatives by providing technical input to proposals, writing relevant sections, and shaping the organization’s health security positioning with current and prospective donors. **Management & Supervision:** Oversees the implementation of all global health security programs within their division, ensuring technical quality, donor compliance, and timely delivery across projects. Provides technical leadership and guidance to GHS project teams. Sets strategic direction, manages budgets, and ensures programmatic quality. Focuses on fostering a culture of excellence and accountability. Manages project staff and shapes the portfolio structure for optimal efficiency and effectiveness. Leads a team of seasoned technical experts, handling supervision, performance management, and professional development. Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team’s multifaceted and evolving responsibilities. Ensures that health security programs are appropriately staffed and technically supported: advises on staffing structures and levels of effort, participates in the recruitment and selection of senior technical positions, and mobilizes surge or specialist support when project needs exceed available capacity. Stays aware of portfolio-level budgets, pipeline, and resource allocation across awards, in coordination with project leadership and enterprise support functions. Maintains organizational readiness for emergency response, including deployment rosters, standard operating procedures, and occupational health and safety provisions for deployed personnel. — **QUALIFICATIONS** **Knowledge & Skills:** Comprehensive knowledge of project management principles. Expertise in program implementation methodologies. Proficient in organizational leadership practices. Demonstrates expertise in strategic planning, risk management, and stakeholder engagement. Proven track record of driving innovation and achieving impactful outcomes within their division. Aims to meet or exceed revenue targets across all segments (USG, foundations/corporations, and other donors). Comprehensive knowledge of global health security concepts and frameworks. Technical breadth across the core health security domains: surveillance and early warning, laboratory systems, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement, health workforce development, antimicrobial resistance, zoonotic disease and One Health, and emergency preparedness and response. Demonstrated experience leading or supporting outbreak and public health emergency response in low- and middle-income settings. Working knowledge of United States Government and other major donor requirements applicable to health security programming. Excellent oral and written communication and analytical skills in English. **Minimum Qualifications:** Bachelor’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Business Administration, International Development, Communication, Social Marketing, Economic Development, Education, Health, Nutrition, Research, Technology, Youth, or a related field. Minimum of 15 years of relevant experience in project management, overseeing complex projects and initiatives; or 12 years and a master’s degree; or 9 years and a PhD; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience to perform job responsibilities effectively. Minimum 8 years of experience in leadership and line management. Proven experience leading and managing complex, strategic portfolios of programs/projects on a national or international scale. Experience leading teams in complex settings, managing financial and human resources. Significant experience working in non-governmental organizations (NGOs). **Preferred Qualifications:** Master’s Degree in a related field. Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification or other recognized project management certification. Certifications relevant to research management or organizational leadership. We welcome candidates with other relevant certifications or their international equivalents. Advanced degree in public health, epidemiology, medicine, or a related field. Formal training in field epidemiology (e.g., FETP) or in emergency or incident management systems. Professional working proficiency in French, Spanish, or Portuguese an added advantage. — **TRAVEL** Approximately 25% travel may be required for this role, primarily to engage with stakeholders, oversee project implementation, and attend meetings and events related to portfolio activities. — **TYPICAL PHYSICAL DEMANDS** Typical office environment. Constantly uses a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time. — **TECHNOLOGY** Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment. — This job posting summarizes the main duties of the job. It neither prescribes nor restricts the exact tasks that may be assigned to carry out these duties. This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time. FHI 360 is an equal opportunity employer whereby we do not engage in practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. **Our values and commitments to safeguarding:** FHI 360 is committed to preventing any type of abuse, exploitation and harassment in our work environments and programs, includ

item.title: Media Relations and Communications Strategist for Lands, Wildlife and Oceans
item.description: Media Relations and Communications Strategist for Lands, Wildlife and Oceans Organization: Earthjustice Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## Earthjustice Earthjustice is the nation’s leading environmental law organization. We wield the power of law and the strength of partnership to protect people’s health, preserve magnificent places and wildlife, advance clean energy, and combat climate change. We are here because the Earth needs a good lawyer. Driven by a passion for justice, inclusion, partnership, and excellence, our core values lead us to seek a broad range of perspectives and backgrounds to achieve our mission and maintain an inclusive environment where all staff are valued and respected. The Media Relations and Communications Strategist for Lands, Wildlife and Oceans will join the Public Affairs and Communications team to develop and carry out earned media and communications strategies for Earthjustice litigation and policy work. This position will report to the Associate Director of Public Affairs and Communications for Lands, Wildlife and Oceans and work under their guidance and strategic leadership to develop communications strategies and deepen and expand press coverage in support of priority issue areas. This is a non-supervisory position. The Media Relations and Communications Strategist is expected to work a full-time (37.5 hours/week) schedule. This role will preferably be based hybrid from our Washington, D.C. office. However, we are open to remote candidates within the U.S. Some domestic travel is required. — ## What You’ll Do ### Media Outreach (55%) • Work with Associate Director of Public Affairs and Communications and communications team, litigators, policy staff, clients, and coalition partners to build, shape, and implement media outreach strategies on Lands, Wildlife and Oceans issues. • Pitch stories to national and regional media outlets including papers, magazines and long-form media outlets, TV and radio stations, online outlets, and other influential news sources. • Track media narratives, identify and pursue earned media opportunities, and build relationships with journalists. • Write and distribute press releases, talking points, and background materials on cases of interest to national, regional, and online media. • Occasionally respond quickly to breaking news moments and seize opportunities for coverage when there are unexpected and fast-moving developments. • Manage media lists and contacts and monitor media coverage. • May coordinate with vendors for communications content (digital ads, photos, etc.). • May lead on arranging virtual or in-person press conferences. • May provide media strategy guidance to team members across Public Affairs and Communications team. • May conduct media outreach on behalf of clients and partners and contribute to joint media efforts with external partners. ### Message Development and Media Training (15%) • Work with program staff to assess media narratives and develop appropriate messages. • Develop talking points, quotes, and statements for program teams and assist program staff members in preparing for media interviews. • Provide media training to program staff. • In collaboration with Associate Director, work with national and grassroots coalitions to support advocacy efforts and develop messaging and media strategy. ### Strategy (20%) • Implement communications strategies for program priorities under the strategic leadership of Associate Director, working directly with clients, partners, coalitions, communications team members, and relevant program staff. ### Administrative and Professional Development (10%) • Attend and contribute to team meetings, support project management, and collaborate across the department on knowledge sharing and content planning. • Attend events, webinars, trainings, and other professional development programs. • Attend internal DEI learning opportunities to increase awareness and actively contribute to creating a diverse, inclusive, and equitable work environment. *Please note that the percentage breakdowns provided above serve as a guideline and that other duties may be assigned as part of the job’s requirement.* — ## What You’ll Bring • Bachelor’s Degree in Journalism, Communications, Political Science, or Marketing preferred. • At least three years’ experience in media relations. • Experience working with nonprofits, advocacy organizations, government, or political campaigns preferred. • Experience working on environmental issues preferred. • Outstanding written and oral communication skills. • Proven ability to develop relationships with journalists and pitch high-impact media stories to advance advocacy campaigns. • Proven ability to succeed in a fast-moving environment with tight deadlines. • Experience using social media, Muck Rack, and/or other media relations software to monitor media narratives, connect with journalists, and amplify earned media placements. • Demonstrated commitment to the creation of a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work culture that encourages and celebrates differences. • Demonstrated commitment to Earthjustice’s values of justice, excellence, inclusion, and partnership. — ## Please Note The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for personnel so classified. — ## Salary and Benefits We offer a competitive salary and excellent, comprehensive benefits. We also offer a casual and congenial work environment. Salaries at Earthjustice are determined by working location and are commensurate with the experience required. **Salary range in Washington, D.C.:** $113,000 – $125,600 **Salaries in other locations will vary:** • **San Francisco, CA and New York, NY:** $119,000 – $132,200 • **Chicago, IL, Seattle, WA, and Los Angeles, CA:** $113,000 – $125,600 • **Denver, CO and Philadelphia, PA:** $107,100 – $119,000 • **Miami, FL, Bozeman, MT, and New Orleans, LA:** $101,200 – $112,400 • **Other remote locations:** $101,200 – $125,600 — ## To Apply Interested candidates should submit the following materials via Jobvite . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled. Incomplete applications will not be considered. • Resume • Cover letter • Two brief writing samples (press statement or pitch preferred, 1–2 pages max) Information about our hiring process and tips for success can be found at: [https://earthjustice.org/about/jobs/hiring-process] Please reach out to [email protected] if you are having technical difficulties submitting your application. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity Statement As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to employment practices that ensure that employees and applicants for employment are provided with equal opportunities without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, or any other factor that is not related to the position. For positions located within the City and County of San Francisco: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. For positions located within the City of Los Angeles: We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring. #LI-Hybrid Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Policy and Legislation Operations Senior Manager
item.description: Policy and Legislation Operations Senior Manager Organization: Earthjustice Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 Founded in 1971, Earthjustice is the premier nonprofit environmental law organization, taking on the biggest, most precedent-setting cases across the country. Partnering with thousands of groups, supporters, individuals, and communities, Earthjustice uses the power of the law to protect people’s health, preserve places and wildlife, advance clean energy, and combat climate change. Headquartered in San Francisco, Earthjustice is a 501(c)(3) charitable organization that maintains offices nationwide and has a distinguished record of achieving significant, lasting environmental protections through litigation and advocacy. Earthjustice Action is a separate 501(c)(4) social welfare organization founded to defend and strengthen bedrock environmental laws and ensure they remain intact and enforceable. Earthjustice Action helps build power to advance environmental, health, climate, and justice goals through federal and state policy advocacy, expanded policy communications, and civic engagement. The Policy and Legislation Operations Senior Manager provides hands-on administrative, operational, finance, and compliance support for the Policy and Legislation (PAL) team and its work on behalf of Earthjustice and Earthjustice Action. This role helps keep day-to-day systems, processes, records, and reporting on track so program staff can advance program and state policy priorities clearly, accurately, and in alignment with organizational guidance. This is a detail-oriented, service-focused role for someone who enjoys managing moving pieces, building practical tools, and helping colleagues navigate complex requirements. For both Earthjustice and Earthjustice Action, the Senior Manager supports Lobby Disclosure Act reporting, lobbying and advocacy operations, timekeeping oversight, contracts, invoices, document retention, and staff training. The role also supports PAL leadership in developing team metrics, tracking systems, and reporting tools that help elevate program successes, identify where additional support is needed, and strengthen overall program effectiveness. This is a supervisory role and is best suited for someone who is eager to own details, follow through consistently, and make complex operations easier for others to manage in an ever-changing political landscape. This role is expected to work a full-time (37.5 hours/week) schedule and will work hybrid from the DC office with a minimum of two days a week in the office. ### Essential Duties and Responsibilities ### Administrative Operations and Program Support (35%) Lead and oversee day-to-day administrative and operational support for fast-paced Policy and Legislation (PAL) team (25–30 staff), ensuring strong coordination, consistency, and service delivery across functions. Serve as PAL’s primary operations liaison with Finance, owning alignment on budgets, expense tracking, invoices, coding, vendor processes, and internal approvals across affiliated entities; identify and resolve discrepancies and improve processes over time. Design and manage systems to support rapid-response work, including tracking deadlines, assignments, approvals, and follow-up items with a high degree of accuracy and accountability. Develop, standardize, and continuously improve tools, trackers, templates, and shared resources to strengthen staff compliance with internal processes and enable efficient, high-quality work. Oversee timekeeping and related review processes, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and consistency through clear guidance, quality control, and coordination with supervisors. ### Lobbying, Advocacy, and Compliance Operations (30%) Manage federal lobbying reporting under the Lobbying Disclosure Act for Earthjustice and Earthjustice Action, including timely collection of staff inputs, accurate reporting of lobbying activities, and maintenance of records documenting lobbying hours and expenses. Support growing state-level lobbying reporting and advocacy operations needs by collaborating with staff, Finance, and the Office of General Counsel (OGC) to ensure accurate and timely jurisdiction-specific filings, documentation, and compliance workflows. Work with General Counsel’s office to support staff following federal congressional lobbying rules, IRS lobbying and advocacy guidance, and approved internal procedures for lobbying, advocacy, timekeeping, documentation, and financial coding. Work with General Counsel’s office to maintain clear guidance, calendars, and records that help staff understand and follow applicable lobbying and advocacy requirements. Track compliance deadlines and process steps, elevating complex questions to PAL leadership, Finance, and OGC as appropriate. ### Departmental Planning, Metrics, and Program Improvement (20%) Serve the PAL leadership team as the team’s operational lead, helping set agendas, prepare materials, capture notes, and track action items to support follow-through and departmental communications. Support the VP of Policy and Legislation and departmental leadership in developing practical planning tools, team metrics, and tracking systems that improve visibility into PAL’s work and impact across affiliated organizations. Support planning processes that help different internal stakeholders share relevant information, identify opportunities for alignment, and, where possible, work toward a cohesive vision. Maintain trackers, reports, or other tools that help leadership elevate program successes, monitor progress against priorities, and identify where additional resources may be needed. Identify recurring operational challenges or information gaps and help develop practical improvements that make the team more effective. ### Supervision, Training, and Information Management (15%) Supervise and develop the Executive Assistant/PAL Associate, setting clear priorities, ensuring high-quality output, and supporting ongoing training, performance management, and professional growth. Train and support staff and supervisors on approved administrative processes, tools, financial coding, timekeeping expectations, documentation practices, and multi-entity-related guidance, ensuring consistent understanding and application. Maintain shared PAL-related operational resources, including document management systems, retention practices, and information governance, translating organizational guidance into clear, accessible, and actionable tools and materials for staff. ### Qualifications Exceptional organizational rigor, precision, and attention to detail, with the ability to design and manage complex workflows, approvals, records, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong operational judgment and ownership, with the ability to anticipate needs, identify systemic gaps, resolve issues, and escalate strategically when appropriate. Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a complex, multi-entity environment, ensuring consistent application of entity-specific guidance across administrative, financial, timekeeping, documentation, and compliance workflows. Clear, practical, and influential communications skills, including the ability to translate complex requirements into scalable, user-friendly tools, guidance, and processes. Advanced project and program coordination skills, including driving action tracking, shaping agendas and documentation, maintaining planning systems, and aligning diverse stakeholders toward shared outcomes. High degree of professionalism, discretion, and service orientation, with experience supporting and advising senior leaders and building trust across functions and levels. Proven commitment to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment and leading collaboration across identities, roles, and perspectives. ### Leadership Competencies Strategic Orientation: Connects day-to-day operations to broader organizational priorities; identifies opportunities to improve systems, scalability, and effectiveness. Operational Excellence: Builds, standardizes, and continuously improves processes that enhance efficiency, clarity, and compliance across teams and entities. Decision-Making & Accountability: Exercises sound judgment in complex situations, takes ownership of outcomes, and drives decisions forward with appropriate stakeholder input. Influence & Stakeholder Management: Builds strong, trust-based relationships across functions; effectively aligns diverse stakeholders and navigates competing priorities. People & Team Enablement: Supports colleagues and partners through clear expectations, accessible tools, and a collaborative, solutions-oriented approach (with or without formal management responsibility). Change Leadership: Leads through ambiguity and change by communicating clearly, maintaining momentum, and helping others adapt to new processes or priorities. Equity-Centered Leadership: Models inclusive practices, advances equitable outcomes in operations and decision-making, and fosters a respectful, collaborative work environment. ### PLEASE NOTE The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for personnel so classified. ### Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience required. At least 7 years of relevant experience in operations, administration, finance support, compliance support, and project coordination. Experience supporting complex finance operations, including budget tracking, invoices, reimbursements, expense coding, accounts payable coordination, and cross-organizational financial processes. item.title: Social Media Associate
item.description: Social Media Associate Organization: CoStar Group Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## Who is CoStar Group? CoStar Group (NASDAQ: CSGP) is a leading global provider of commercial and residential real estate information, analytics, and online marketplaces. Included in the S&P 500 Index, CoStar Group is on a mission to digitize the world’s real estate, empowering all people to discover properties, insights, and connections that improve their businesses and lives. We have been living and breathing the world of real estate information and online marketplaces for over 35 years, giving us the perspective to create truly unique and valuable offerings to our customers. We’ve continually refined, transformed, and perfected our approach to our business, creating a language that has become standard in our industry, for our customers, and even our competitors. We continue that effort today and are always working to improve and drive innovation. This is how we deliver for our customers, our employees, and investors. By equipping the brightest minds with the best resources available, we provide an invaluable edge in real estate. ## Role Overview: Social Media Associate Arlington, VA | In office, Monday–Friday The Social Media Associate owns social media community management, listening, and performance reporting for CoStar Group and CoStar. This role protects and enhances brand reputation, strengthens customer relationships, and generates the insights that power organic content, boosting (paid social), and employee advocacy strategy across the parent company and flagship product. ## Responsibilities ### Community Management Monitor and engage with CoStar Group and CoStar’s social media communities across platforms daily, including comments, DMs, mentions, and tags. Implement strategies to grow and nurture online audience engagement that reinforce our brand voice. Respond to community inquiries and feedback promptly and professionally, proactively identifying opportunities for deeper engagement. Escalate product‑ or service‑related questions to the appropriate internal stakeholders and track resolution. Monitor daily media coverage and translate relevant coverage into timely social media engagement or content opportunities. Support and help refine the team’s social media moderation and crisis management protocols. Strategically follow employee advocates, clients, prospects, and community partners. Monitor compliance with social media guidelines and escalate brand risk as needed. ### Social Listening Monitor social media conversations to surface decision‑ready insights for marketing, sales, product, HR, and analytics teams. Build and maintain listening queries, refining them regularly to ensure accurate, high‑signal data capture. Partner with social media and analytics teams to connect listening insights to strategic content feedback loops. ### Reporting and Insights Track and analyze community engagement and listening metrics, delivering insights to improve strategy. Monitor organic social media content performance and surface recommendations for optimization. Reconcile and analyze boosting (paid social) campaign performance and audience data to inform optimizations. Organize Employee Advocacy users into teams and groups to streamline reporting. Measure employee advocacy program effectiveness and recommend improvements to reach and participation. Develop and drive consistent reporting cadence: weekly team chat standups, monthly management reports, and quarterly business reviews. ### Cross‑Functional Collaboration Proactively monitor and share platform updates and emerging social media trends to ensure social media community management, social listening, and reporting strategies remain aligned with current best practices. Support social media team with organic social, boosting (paid social), and employee advocacy surges and coverage as needed. ## Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Sociology, Psychology, English, or a related field, from an accredited, not‑for‑profit, in‑person University or College. 2+ years of experience in social media, public relations, customer service, communications, or related fields. 1+ years of experience with Sprout Social or a similar monitoring/reporting tool. Strong organizational and time‑management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workflows. Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, with a customer‑centric approach to engagement. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy. ## Preferred Qualifications and Skills Ability to think strategically and act proactively in ambiguous situations. Flexibility and adaptability in a fast‑changing social media environment. Composure and resilience when engaging with challenging or critical public feedback. Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to continued learning and professional development. Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. Experience with Asana or similar project management tools a plus. Ability to read and write in Spanish and/or French a plus. ## What’s In It For You? If you are a driven professional looking for a high‑growth, high‑reward career, CoStar Group offers the ideal opportunity. Be part of a best‑in‑class company with strong year‑over‑year growth that invests in your success. Enjoy a rewarding atmosphere where you can learn, excel, and grow. When you join CoStar Group, you’ll experience a collaborative and innovative culture working alongside the best and brightest to empower our people and customers to succeed. We offer you generous compensation and performance‑based incentives. CoStar Group also invests in your professional and academic growth with internal training and tuition reimbursement. ### Our benefits package includes (but is not limited to): Comprehensive healthcare coverage: Medical / Vision / Dental / Prescription Drug Life, legal, and supplementary insurance Virtual and in‑person mental health counseling services for individuals and family Commuter and parking benefits 401(K) retirement plan with matching contributions Employee stock purchase plan Paid time off Tuition reimbursement On‑site fitness center and/or reimbursed fitness center membership costs (location dependent) Access to CoStar Group’s Employee Resource Groups Complimentary gourmet coffee, tea, hot chocolate, fresh fruit, and other healthy snacks ## Sponsorship We welcome all qualified candidates who are currently eligible to work full‑time in the United States to apply. However, please note that CoStar Group is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position. The final salary or hourly rate offered for this role will fall within the range set forth below based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to geographic location, skills, and competencies. **Base Compensation: $63,000.00 – $85,000.00 Annually** CoStar Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer; we maintain a drug‑free workplace and perform pre‑employment substance abuse testing. #CoStar #LI‑MN2 CoStar Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer; we maintain a drug‑free workplace and perform pre‑employment substance abuse testing. item.title: Senior Communications Specialist
item.description: Senior Communications Specialist Organization: Constellation Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## Pay $90,000.00 – $120,000.00 per year ## Job Description: Senior Communications Specialist Constellation is seeking a Senior Communications Specialist who will assist in developing, updating, and publishing program and organizational materials, designing and distributing them for internal and external audiences. The Specialist will assist in maintaining the program and organizational websites so they remain compelling and current, developing communication plans and managing internal program/organizational communications, and supporting media relations efforts including development and distribution of story ideas, press releases, and media interviews. ## Key Responsibilities – Develop and implement the annual Strategic Communications plan, including tracking activities. – Provide expertise and guidance on leading strategic communications efforts for the client, identifying stakeholders, avenues, and methods for communications, and analyzing communications gaps, along with benchmarking of other federal agency portfolios. – Create, in partnership with subject matter experts and senior leadership, regular and recurring messaging and materials for employees and external partners, including public‑facing materials. – Develop reference materials, guidance, and a repository of information regarding strategic communications. – Facilitate discussions with clients to accomplish strategic communications plans and goals. – Maintain content and materials on the intranet site, promoting organizational successes, opportunities, and new or updated guidance for the appropriate audience, including routine review of content. – Create and publish the quarterly newsletter for posting on the SharePoint page. – Support strategic communications initiatives as required. – Draft talking points, leadership remarks, and comments for various engagements, meetings, and events. – Review and maintain content on the public‑facing cbp.gov site. ## Candidate Requirements – Ability to obtain and maintain a DHS CBP Tier 5 Background Investigation (BI). – Bachelor’s degree in mass communication, business, or related field. – Minimum of 8 years of experience supporting the messaging of complex business functions or programs and providing challenging and professional deliverables, products, and services across multiple social media and communications platforms. – Strong writing and editing skills. – Exceptional communication and collaboration skills. – High proficiency in MS SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite, and relevant software. ## Job Type Full‑time ## Work Location Hybrid ## Benefits – 401(k) – 401(k) contribution – Dental insurance – Medical insurance – Life & Disability insurance – Flexible spending account – Flexible schedule – Professional development – Work‑life balance Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Corporate Communications Manager
item.description: Corporate Communications Manager Organization: CohnReznick Location: Tysons Corner, VA Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## Job Description As CohnReznick grows, so do our career opportunities. As one of the nation’s top professional services firms, CohnReznick creates rewarding careers in advisory, assurance, and tax with team members who value innovation and collaboration in everything they do. CohnReznick helps organizations optimize performance, manage risk, and maximize value through CohnReznick LLP (assurance services) and CohnReznick Advisory LLC (advisory and tax services). Together, the firm provides leaders with deep industry knowledge and relationships, solutions to address clients’ unique business goals and risks, and insight on how emerging market forces can drive opportunity. With offices nationwide, the firm serves organizations around the world as an independent member of Nexia. We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a **Corporate Communications Manager** to join the Corporate Marketing team. CohnReznick is a hybrid firm and most of our professionals are located within a commutable distance to one of our offices. This position is considered hybrid, which means team members are expected to be thoughtful and intentional in how they create opportunities for in‑person collaboration. While the cadence of in‑office presence is determined at the team level, our professionals are encouraged to be in the office/together in person on average three days a week. ## YOUR TEAM Creating opportunities for our people is a core component of CohnReznick’s mission and purpose. As Corporate Communications Manager reporting to the Senior Manager, Corporate Marketing, you will develop integrated communications strategies and content that advance business priorities, elevate the brand, and foster connection, engagement, and alignment across the organization. With a commitment to strategic and collaborative leadership, you will bring deep experience in messaging strategy, stakeholder engagement, and people mentorship, with a proven ability to manage sensitive, high‑visibility projects. ## WHY COHNREZNICK? At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. Whether it’s working alongside your peers to solve a client challenge or volunteering together at the local food bank, there are many ways to find your “why” at the firm. We believe it’s important to balance work with everyday life – and make time for enjoyment and fun. We invest in a robust Total Rewards package that includes generous PTO, a flexible work environment, expanded parental leave, extensive learning and development, and even paid time off for employees to volunteer. ## YOUR ROLE Responsibilities include but are not limited to: – **Write, edit, and coordinate approvals** for internal and external communications content, including presentations, publications, talking points, video scripts, press releases, and social media posts. – **Manage communications requests** and provide editorial guidance to ensure consistency, accuracy, and alignment with brand standards and business objectives. – **Manage corporate campaigns**, including developing assets, leading projects, and collaborating with multiple stakeholders. – **Partner with Senior Manager** to develop strategies and content supporting the firm’s People & Culture goals. – **Manage awards, surveys, and rankings submissions.** – **Own the firm communications calendar**, leading scheduling and channel strategy for timely and effective delivery. – **Manage relationships with brand and PR agencies**, including messaging reviews, approvals, and project coordination. – **Collaborate with creative and digital marketing teams** to develop communications assets and content. – **Manage multiple priorities** and shifting deadlines in a fast‑paced environment. – **Share recommendations** to improve communications effectiveness, processes, and stakeholder engagement. – **Foster a culture** of collaboration, accountability, flexibility, and continuous improvement. ## YOUR EXPERIENCE The successful candidate will have: – Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field. – 8–10 years of experience in corporate communications, executive communications, public relations, or marketing communications within professional services or similar organizations. – Experience supporting communications for senior executives and handling highly confidential information. – Exceptional writing, editing, proofreading, and storytelling skills across audiences and formats. – Strong experience developing executive communications, presentations, speeches, and videos. – Demonstrated ability to balance strategic thinking with hands‑on execution. – Proven success managing multiple projects and competing priorities in a fast‑paced environment. – Strong stakeholder management skills and ability to build trusted relationships across all levels. – Ability to translate leadership priorities into clear, engaging communications. – Advanced PowerPoint and visual communications skills. – Strong project management and organizational skills, including editorial calendar management. – Excellent judgment, diplomacy, discretion, and attention to detail. – Experience collaborating with creative teams, agencies, and cross‑functional stakeholders. – Familiarity with media relations and PR processes. – Experience supporting crisis communications, change management, and/or M&A communications preferred. – Prior experience in accounting, consulting, legal, financial services, or other professional services strongly preferred. – Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, especially PowerPoint and Excel. – Experience with Microsoft Copilot (or similar enterprise AI platforms) and commitment to leveraging AI tools for productivity and communication effectiveness. – Demonstrated critical thinking in AI use cases to maintain accuracy, authenticity, and trust. Please also review our Universal Job Standards. Studies show that candidates often hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. At CohnReznick, we are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every qualification, we still encourage you to apply. ## Compensation In Virginia, the salary range for a Corporate Communications Manager is **$116,000 to $160,000**. Actual compensation will depend on skills, experience, qualifications, location, and applicable employment laws. Salary is one component of the CohnReznick Total Rewards package, which includes a discretionary performance bonus, generous paid time off, expanded parental benefits, and access to best‑in‑class learning and development platforms. To learn more, visit **Life at CohnReznick**. “CohnReznick” is the brand name under which CohnReznick LLP and CohnReznick Advisory LLC and their subsidiaries provide professional services. CohnReznick LLP is a licensed CPA firm providing attest services. CohnReznick Advisory LLC provides tax and business consulting services and is not a licensed CPA firm. CohnReznick is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive team. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability. For more information, please see Equal Employment Opportunity Posters. If you are an individual with a disability needing assistance during the recruitment process, contact ** [email protected] **. This email is reserved for accommodation requests only. CohnReznick does not accept unsolicited resumes from third‑party recruiters unless engaged by written agreement. Any unsolicited resume submission grants CohnReznick the right to hire the applicant without fee. #GD #LI‑ED #IND123 (PMT) Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: External Stakeholder Lead – Senior
item.description: External Stakeholder Lead – Senior Organization: Barbaricum Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/26/2026 ## Barbaricum Barbaricum is a rapidly growing government contractor providing leading‑edge support to federal customers, with a particular focus on Defense and National Security mission sets. We leverage more than 17 years of support to stakeholders across the federal government, with established and growing capabilities across Intelligence, Analytics, Engineering, Mission Support, and Communications disciplines. Founded in 2008, our mission is to transform the way our customers approach constantly changing and complex problem sets by bringing to bear the latest in technology and the highest caliber of talent. Headquartered in Washington, DC’s historic Dupont Circle neighborhood, Barbaricum also has a corporate presence in Tampa, FL, Bedford, IN, and Dayton, OH, with team members across the United States and around the world. As a leader in our space, we partner with firms in the private sector, academic institutions, and industry associations with a goal of continually building our expertise and capabilities for the benefit of our employees and the customers we support. Through all of this, we have built a vibrant corporate culture diverse in expertise and perspectives with a focus on collaboration and innovation. Our teams are at the frontier of the Nation’s most complex and rewarding challenges. Join our team. — ## Senior External Stakeholder Lead Barbaricum is seeking an experienced Senior External Stakeholder Lead to lead external stakeholder engagement and partner coordination under the Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP) Outreach and Digital Enterprise Services (MODES) contract. You will support community and public engagement objectives, strengthen stakeholder understanding and trust, and help align external engagement, messaging, feedback, and reputational risk management with MC&FP priorities. — ## Responsibilities – **External stakeholder engagement** — Lead engagement and coordination with external stakeholders, partners, policy‑focused organizations, advocacy groups, and community‑facing organizations to support MC&FP objectives. – **Primary coordination role** — Serve as the primary coordination point for external stakeholder engagement, ensuring continuity, alignment, and timely communication across functional teams. – **Engagement planning** — Develop and implement stakeholder engagement plans aligned with MC&FP priorities, external affairs strategy, public engagement objectives, and brand reputation needs. – **Relationship management** — Build and manage relationships with national, regional, state, local, and targeted organizations that influence policy dialogue, public perception, and community trust. – **Representation in forums** — Represent MC&FP in stakeholder meetings, coalition forums, working groups, and public‑facing engagements to build goodwill, promote collaboration, and shape policy dialogue. – **Feedback analysis** — Capture, assess, and analyze external feedback to inform planning, messaging, engagement approaches, reputational risk awareness, and senior leadership updates. – **Material development** — Draft, review, and coordinate stakeholder materials, briefings, talking points, engagement summaries, and public‑facing support products. – **Stakeholder mapping** — Lead stakeholder mapping, influence analysis, and engagement strategies for legislative, regulatory, reputational, and community priorities. – **Policy trend monitoring** — Monitor public policy trends, stakeholder concerns, and reputational risks, recommending engagement and crisis response strategies as needed. – **Internal coordination** — Coordinate internal working groups and recurring updates with government affairs, legal, communications, program operations, and senior leadership to ensure consistent messaging and enterprise‑wide visibility. — ## Required Skills – **Stakeholder engagement expertise** — Strong knowledge of stakeholder engagement, external affairs, public affairs, government affairs, advocacy, public policy, community engagement, and strategic communications. – **Relationship building** — Ability to build trust‑based relationships with external stakeholders, partner organizations, government entities, advocacy groups, and cross‑functional internal teams. – **Policy and risk assessment** — Ability to assess stakeholder perspectives, public policy trends, reputational risks, and engagement opportunities in a dynamic and politically sensitive environment. – **Strategic planning** — Strong strategic planning skills with the ability to develop engagement plans, stakeholder maps, influence strategies, and coordinated outreach approaches. – **Communication skills** — Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to present complex concepts clearly and concisely to executives, clients, partners, and public‑facing audiences. – **Briefing development** — Ability to draft and review briefings, talking points, engagement materials, leadership updates, and public‑facing communication products. – **Professional judgment** — Strong judgment, discretion, and professionalism when handling sensitive stakeholder issues, policy concerns, reputational matters, and crisis response support. – **Coordination skills** — Ability to coordinate functional teams, manage competing priorities, track dependencies, elevate risks, and maintain alignment with MC&FP objectives. – **Analytical skills** — Strong analytical and organizational skills, including the ability to synthesize external feedback, identify implications, and recommend practical engagement actions. — ## Required Qualifications – **Advanced degree** — Master’s degree, MBA, or advanced degree in Public Administration, Public Policy, Communications, Public Relations, Government Affairs, Political Science, Organizational Leadership, Business, or a related field is preferred. – **Experience requirements** — 10+ years of experience in stakeholder engagement, public affairs, government affairs, external affairs, advocacy, communications, policy engagement, or related fields. – **Leadership experience** — 5+ years of leadership experience working with or in state or local government, policy organizations, public affairs organizations, advocacy campaigns, or third‑party stakeholder organizations. – **Sector experience** — Experience working within a large corporation, policy organization, public interest group, government environment, or mission‑focused public‑sector program is preferred. – **Policy influence** — Proven ability to manage external relationships and influence policy, engagement, or reputational outcomes through strategic stakeholder coordination. – **Federal policy familiarity** — Familiarity with federal policy, regulatory, legislative, advocacy, or public affairs environments. – **Engagement materials** — Experience developing stakeholder engagement plans, influence strategies, external briefings, leadership materials, and coordinated engagement updates. – **Security clearance** — DoD Secret Security Clearance. — ## EEO Commitment All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. item.title: Senior Legal Counsel, International Trade Compliance
item.description: Senior Legal Counsel, International Trade Compliance Organization: Baker Hughes Location: Houston, TX Date Posted: 08/26/2026 # Would you like to be a part of a leading Trade Compliance Program? Do you enjoy leading projects that promote continuous improvement? # Join our leading Trade Compliance Team Our Legal Team takes responsibility for developing and safeguarding our company’s global legal strategy. We partner with the business to develop, maintain, and follow compliance policies, providing legal advice and guidance to support the business as necessary. Our team provides valuable oversight for Export Controls Rules and Regulations, Sanctions regulations and Customs governance. # Partner with the best In this role, you will lead the development of certain aspects of the Baker Hughes Trade Compliance Program. You will provide legal advice to our business on Export Controls, Sanction regulations and Customs rules. You will lead trade compliance investigations and manage submissions and disclosures to the U.S. government. As a Senior Legal Counsel for International Trade, you will be responsible for: – Providing legal advice to our business on US Customs and Export Controls Rules and Regulations, Sanction regulations – Leading trade compliance investigations and managing submissions and disclosures to the U.S. government as required – Working with a team dedicated to the management of our compliance program through a focus on continual enhancement – Managing ITC Compliance policies and procedures and key elements of the Trade Program within our Compliance program – Monitoring and communicating new international trade laws, rules and regulations that impact our business through internal communications – Managing ITC Compliance training content and annual roll‑out to support our program initiatives # Fuel your passion To be successful in this role you will: – Have a Juris Doctor Degree from an accredited law school or international equivalent – Have a minimum of 5 additional years of experience in Compliance & Regulatory Counsels – Have admission to practice law and be in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar (or equivalent in other jurisdictions) – Demonstrate solid experience with US & EU licensing and registration regimes, including dual use, military, and nuclear – Have experience in international trade law, including export compliance and sanctions – Show strong negotiation and presentation skills and excellent analytical ability – Have excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to explain complex legal and regulatory concerns to non‑legal stakeholders – Demonstrate ability to lead programs and projects # Work in a way that works for you We recognize that everyone is different and that the way in which people want to work and deliver at their best is different for everyone too. In this role, we can offer the following flexible working patterns: – Working flexible hours — flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive # Working with us Our people are at the heart of what we do at Baker Hughes. We know we are better when all of our people are developed, engaged and able to bring their whole authentic selves to work. We invest in the health and well‑being of our workforce, train and reward talent and develop leaders at all levels to bring out the best in each other. # Working for you Our inventions have revolutionized energy for over a century. But to keep going forward tomorrow, we know we have to push the boundaries today. We prioritize rewarding those who embrace change with a package that reflects how much we value their input. Join us, and you can expect: – Contemporary work‑life balance policies and wellbeing activities – Comprehensive private medical care options – Safety net of life insurance and disability programs – Tailored financial programs – Additional elected or voluntary benefits You will be eligible to participate in Company‑sponsored benefit programs, including health & welfare programs and the Thrift Plan (401k). You will have a choice of coverage options that best suit your needs. Coverage options and contribution amounts are related to your benefit elections, base salary level, and specific requirements of each of these plans. This position is eligible for our comprehensive and competitive benefits package, which can be found here, and is further eligible for additional forms of compensation such as bonuses subject to the terms of the applicable benefit plans or policies. The Baker Hughes internal title for this role is: **Legal Senior Manager – Compliance & Regulatory** # About Us We are an energy technology company that provides solutions to energy and industrial customers worldwide. Built on a century of experience and conducting business in over 120 countries, our innovative technologies and services are taking energy forward – making it safer, cleaner and more efficient for people and the planet. # Join Us Are you seeking an opportunity to make a real difference in a company that values innovation and progress? Join us and become part of a team of people who will challenge and inspire you. Let’s come together and take energy forward. Baker Hughes Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.
