item.title: Content & Editorial Strategist
item.description: Content & Editorial Strategist Organization: OSEA Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Description ### About the role Join our fast‑growing beauty brand and become a fundamental member of our expanding team. We are looking for a savvy, passionate **Content & Editorial Strategist** who is excited about brand storytelling, copywriting, sustainability, and beauty. The ideal candidate has a passion for language, brand voice, and clean beauty, thrives in a fast‑paced environment, and shares our commitment to wellness in both our products and work‑life balance. Our mission is to create effective, results‑driven skincare that is safe for the planet and humankind. This role is hybrid, with the expectation to work in‑office 1–2 days per week at our Venice, California headquarters. — ## Responsibilities – **Editorial strategy** — Develop and lead editorial and content strategies that support product launches, integrated campaigns, and key business objectives. – **Brand voice** — Own and evolve OSEA’s content strategy and brand voice across all owned channels, ensuring messaging is consistent, differentiated, and aligned with the brand. – **Messaging frameworks** — Establish messaging frameworks, storytelling pillars, and content strategies that guide execution across every customer touchpoint. – **Copy development** — Develop compelling copy for product launches, integrated campaigns, email, social, retail collateral, events, and seasonal initiatives while creating scalable content systems that support cross‑functional teams. – **Website editorial** — Lead the editorial strategy for OSEAMalibu.com, creating engaging content that strengthens the customer experience, supports SEO, and brings the brand to life through product pages, editorial features, and long‑form storytelling. – **Editorial calendar** — Develop and manage the editorial calendar, aligning content priorities with campaign timelines, product launches, seasonal moments, and business goals. – **Content guidelines** — Create content briefs, messaging hierarchies, editorial guidelines, and channel‑specific frameworks that enable consistent execution across Creative, E‑Commerce, Social, Paid, and Lifecycle Marketing. – **Cross‑functional collaboration** — Partner closely with Creative, Brand Marketing, E‑Commerce, Product Marketing, Education, and Digital teams to shape integrated campaigns from a content‑first perspective. – **Ingredient storytelling** — Translate ingredient science, clinical results, sustainability initiatives, and product innovation into clear, compelling consumer‑facing messaging that educates and inspires. – **Performance insights** — Use performance insights, SEO data, consumer behavior, and competitive analysis to identify content opportunities, optimize existing content, and inform future strategy. – **Trend monitoring** — Monitor beauty, wellness, digital, and cultural trends to evolve OSEA’s storytelling, ensuring content remains relevant, distinctive, and connected to the brand’s point of view. – **Editorial excellence** — Champion editorial excellence by maintaining brand voice standards, ensuring consistency across channels, and continually evolving content best practices. This job description is a summary of duties. It is not an all‑inclusive list but a broad guide of expected responsibilities and is subject to change. — ## Requirements – Excellent communication and interpersonal skills (oral, written, non‑verbal, intuitive, psychic et al) – Must be willing to use AI to optimize workflows and speed – Experience in Figma – 5+ years of copywriting experience, ideally with beauty, wellness, or lifestyle brands – Exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading skills with an impressive portfolio – Proven ability to adapt voice and tone across platforms (digital, print, social, email, video scripts) – Familiarity with SEO best practices and performance copywriting – Strong project management skills; ability to prioritize in a deadline‑driven environment – Must reside in Los Angeles to be considered for this position, with the expectation to work on Pacific Standard Time (PST) – Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this position — ## Compensation The anticipated salary range for this position is **$80,000–$95,000 per year**. The actual salary offer will consider factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. item.title: Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy (Market Access)
item.description: Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy (Market Access) Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Overview** The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Deputy Vice President for the International Advocacy team to support its global market access advocacy efforts. This position will lead the development and implementation of policy positions, advocacy strategies, and stakeholder engagement activities focused on improving patient access to innovative medicines in major global markets. Reporting to the Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy, the Deputy Vice President will serve as a senior leader on international market access issues, including government pricing and reimbursement, health technology assessment (HTA), healthcare financing, value assessment frameworks, and other policies affecting patient access to innovative medicines. The individual will work collaboratively across the organization and with member companies, other trade associations, consultants, and government stakeholders to advance PhRMA’s strategic priorities in key markets around the world. This Washington, DC-based role requires strategic leadership, strong policy expertise, and the ability to operate independently while managing complex projects and stakeholder relationships across multiple geographies and issue areas. **The Deputy Vice President will:** Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance PhRMA’s international market access priorities in major global markets. Lead policy analysis and position development related to pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement, health technology assessment, healthcare financing, value assessment methodologies, and other market access issues. Perform and oversee quantitative analysis related to healthcare policies, market access, and/or international trade. Represent PhRMA in meetings with government agencies, embassies, organizations, member companies, and external stakeholders. Monitor and assess legislative, regulatory, trade, and policy developments affecting patient access to innovative medicines globally. Build and maintain relationships with U.S. and foreign government officials, trade associations, industry partners, think tanks, academic experts, consultants, and other key stakeholders. Lead and facilitate member company workgroups and task forces focused on international market access priorities. Develop policy papers, briefing materials, presentations, talking points, comment letters, and other advocacy materials for internal and external audiences. Coordinate closely with PhRMA’s policy, federal advocacy, communications, alliance development, legal, and economic teams. Manage consultants, research projects, and external vendors to ensure high-quality and timely work products. Oversee project budgets, contracts, and vendor relationships in accordance with organizational policies. Provide strategic counsel and subject matter expertise to senior leadership on international market access developments and advocacy opportunities. Support the development of cross-functional advocacy campaigns that advance patient access to innovative medicines globally. Perform other duties as assigned. **Key Success Factors** PhRMA seeks a visionary, relationship-driven, and impact-focused individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Deputy Vice President leverages deep expertise to guide strategic priorities, anticipates challenges, and aligns departmental efforts with broader organizational goals. A successful DVP is a trusted advisor, skilled in stakeholder influence and resource management, and leads cross-functional initiatives with clarity, confidence, and purpose. **Professional Experience** Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in Public Policy, Health Policy, Economics, International Affairs, Public Health, Law, Political Science, or a related field preferred. 10+ years of professional experience in international health policy, market access, healthcare economics, public policy, government affairs, trade policy, or related field. Expertise in pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies, health technology assessment, and market access policy issues in foreign countries. Strong understanding of healthcare systems and healthcare financing around the world and the policies that impact patient access to innovative medicines. Experience in performing and overseeing quantitative analysis related to healthcare policies, market access, and/or international trade. Proven ability to analyze complex policy issues and develop strategic recommendations. Exceptional writing, presentation, and communication skills, including the ability to synthesize technical information for diverse audiences. Demonstrated experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies involving U.S. and foreign government stakeholders. Demonstrated success managing consultants, vendors, and complex projects with multiple deliverables. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to establish credibility with senior executives, member company representatives, and external stakeholders. Must be willing to travel internationally (Asia, Europe) as needed to support advocacy objectives and stakeholder engagement. Demonstrated commitment to teamwork, integrity, and professional excellence. **Preferred Experience** Advanced degree (Master’s, J.D., Ph.D., or equivalent) in a relevant discipline. Experience working directly with foreign government agencies, multilateral organizations, or trade associations in other countries. Knowledge of how market access policies affect international trade, pharmaceutical innovation, and patient access. Experience engaging with health technology assessment agencies and reimbursement authorities in major international markets. Experience leading high-performing, cross-functional teams. **Potential Salary** $187,100–266,700 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. **Who we are** The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. **Connect with PhRMA** For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.AmericasMedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] **What we offer** In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a well-being program, an on-site fitness facility, back-up care, health advocate service, an employee assistance program, and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated onboarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast-paced career with their personal goals. **Equal Opportunity Employer** PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. The job description contains an overview of the activities and duties for this role. Responsibilities may change and new ones may be assigned at any time. item.title: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances
item.description: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 # Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Director for the Advocacy and Strategic Alliances team to support its stakeholder engagement and advocacy efforts related to prescription medicine access and affordability. The Director will have a particular focus on Medicare Part B and issues affecting physician-administered medicines, including the implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act’s (IRA) Medicare drug price negotiation program, and Most Favored Nation (MFN) and related government pricing policies. The Director will develop and execute stakeholder engagement strategies that advance PhRMA priorities, with a primary focus on health care providers and provider organizations, as well as patient advocacy organizations representing the oncology and mental health communities, and other health care constituencies. The role will assess how emerging federal policy proposals affect providers and patients and translate those implications into effective external engagement strategies. The Director will work closely with colleagues across PhRMA, member companies, and external partners to coordinate advocacy strategies and ensure stakeholder perspectives inform and strengthen PhRMA’s broader policy and advocacy efforts. The Director will report to the Deputy Vice President, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances. ## The Director will: – Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and advocacy strategies related to government price controls and access to medicines, with particular emphasis on Medicare Part B, the Medicare drug price negotiation program, MFN and related federal policy developments. – Serve as a primary Alliance resource on issues affecting Medicare Part B and physician-administered medicines, translating complex policy developments into actionable stakeholder engagement strategies. – Assess the implications of federal pricing and reimbursement policies for providers, patients, and other health care stakeholders and identify opportunities to engage constituencies in support of shared priorities. – Build, strengthen, and maintain relationships with health care providers and provider organizations, with particular attention to constituencies affected by Part B policy and reimbursement changes. – Develop and maintain strategic relationships with patient advocacy organizations – including those focused on oncology and mental health – and other health care stakeholders whose priorities intersect with PhRMA’s policy agenda. – Identify areas of alignment among diverse constituencies and develop opportunities for collaboration, coalition-building, and coordinated advocacy. – Monitor the federal legislative, regulatory, and political environment to identify emerging developments related to government price controls, Medicare Part B, the IRA, MFN, and other policies affecting access to medicines. – Coordinate closely with PhRMA’s Policy, Federal Advocacy, Public Affairs, International and other teams to ensure Alliance strategies are informed by PhRMA policy positions and integrated with broader organizational priorities. – Work with internal subject matter experts to translate complex policy issues into clear, compelling materials and messages appropriate for stakeholder audiences. – Develop briefing materials, presentations, talking points, stakeholder analyses, engagement plans, and other written products that accurately reflect PhRMA’s established positions. – Represent PhRMA with external organizations and stakeholders on established policy positions relevant to the role’s portfolio. – Plan and execute stakeholder meetings, roundtables, briefings, coalition activities, and other engagement opportunities designed to advance shared policy objectives. – Gather stakeholder perspectives and intelligence and communicate relevant developments, opportunities, and risks to PhRMA leadership and cross-functional colleagues. – Support select international advocacy initiatives involving pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies, including issues where international price controls intersect with U.S. policy proposals and stakeholder interests. – Coordinate with member companies to obtain input, identify stakeholder opportunities, and support alignment around advocacy strategies and priorities. – Manage projects and, as appropriate, consultants and external partners, including timelines, deliverables, and coordination across multiple workstreams. – Continuously evaluate engagement strategies and recommend adjustments based on changes in the policy environment, stakeholder landscape, and organizational priorities. – Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a mission-driven, agile, and solutions-oriented individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Director brings strong subject matter expertise, manages multiple complex projects simultaneously, and guides others toward shared objectives. This role requires clear communication, effective relationship management, and the ability to translate strategic goals into actionable plans. A successful Director demonstrates foresight, critical thinking, and the ability to build consensus across diverse stakeholders. ## Professional Requirements – Bachelor’s degree required (Master’s degree in Health Policy, Public Policy, Communications or related field preferred). – 6+ years of relevant professional experience, including experience in leadership roles. – Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder projects or initiatives. – Experience with Medicare Part B policy, prescription drug pricing and reimbursement, government price controls, or related health policy issues. – Exceptional writing, editing, and presentation skills, with experience developing content for executive audiences. – Experience engaging health care providers, patient advocacy organizations, disease-specific organizations, or other health care constituencies. – Demonstrated sound judgment and ability to work independently while recognizing issues that require broader organizational coordination or leadership guidance. – Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities. – Demonstrated experience managing staff and/or overseeing consultants and vendors. – Excellent verbal communication, presentation, active listening, and interpersonal skills. – Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools; experience with project management and budget tracking systems preferred. – Must be willing to travel and be responsive/available after hours and on weekends. ## Preferred Experience – Advanced degree in public policy, health policy, public health, law, political science, or a related discipline. – Experience working on Medicare Part B, physician-administered medicines, Medicare drug price negotiation, IRA implementation, MFN, or other pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement issues. – Established relationships with health care provider organizations, oncology organizations, patient advocacy organizations, mental health organizations, or related constituencies. – Experience developing or executing coalition-based advocacy campaigns at the federal level. – Experience working with Congress, federal agencies, trade associations, advocacy organizations, or other organizations involved in federal health policy. – Familiarity with international pharmaceutical pricing, reimbursement, market access, or government price-control policies. ## Potential Salary $110,500–151,900 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. ## Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. item.title: Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research
item.description: Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Deputy Vice President for the Policy and Research team to support its policy development and research strategy efforts. Reporting to the Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research, this position leads the development, management, and communication of research supporting PhRMA’s advocacy priorities related to prescription drug spending, pharmaceutical reimbursement and distribution, and the 340B Drug Pricing Program. The Deputy Vice President serves as a key internal resource by managing research projects, synthesizing complex evidence, advising cross-functional teams, and translating research into actionable policy and advocacy materials. The Deputy Vice President will focus on: ### Prescription Drug Spending and Market Access Research Lead development and review of research content and advocacy materials related to prescription drug costs, reimbursement, coverage and market access issues. Monitor and analyze trends in drug spending, utilization, pricing, pharmaceutical supply chain dynamics, PBM and insurer business practices, and coverage and access to medicines across public and private health care programs. Identify and analyze emerging policy and market developments that may affect prescription drug costs and coverage. Translate or synthesize complex pricing concepts, analyses, and research findings for senior management, member companies, and external stakeholders. Interface with other departments, internal to PhRMA, to review and advise on talking points, press releases, media requests, legislative and regulatory proposals. Manage internal and external research, oversee project execution and deliverables. Conduct rapid response analyses and data syntheses to inform advocacy, communications, and policy efforts. ### 340B and Hospital Research Partner with the 340B policy team on research development and execution, including advising on methodology, reviewing scopes of work and identifying and engaging research partners. Actively manage research projects, including communicating with outside researchers/analysts, getting internal feedback, communicating with other departments, updating research trackers, and developing summaries as needed. Monitor and evaluate 340B research, including identifying and summarizing new studies to disseminate internally and externally as needed. Draft research updates, summaries, emails, slides, and other materials to keep the department and members informed of relevant 340B research. Track all ongoing PhRMA-funded 340B projects and keep internal systems up to date with current status, deliverables and target release date. Provide analytic and strategic support for other hospital related research. Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a proactive, analytical, and collaborative individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The successful candidate demonstrates exceptional critical thinking and project management skills and can translate complex research into practical policy insights that support organizational priorities. This individual builds strong working relationships across departments and with external research partners, manages multiple priorities under compressed timelines, and exercises sound judgment in a dynamic policy environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills, intellectual curiosity, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently while collaborating across teams are essential for success in this role. ## Professional Experience / Requirements 10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical pricing or market access, policy, health economics, or a related field. Master’s degree in public health, economics, public policy, health services research, or related discipline. Deep expertise in U.S. drug pricing, coverage, reimbursement systems, and public programs and public policy analysis. Proven leadership in cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement. Strong quantitative skills; ability to interpret complex data and synthesize insights. Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills. Experience managing consultants, research vendors, and direct reports. Demonstrated ability to lead teams and mentor staff. ### Preferred Experience MBA, Master’s in Public Policy, PharmD, JD, or Ph.D. in economics, health policy, or related field. Experience in pharmaceutical reimbursement and distribution, PBM and insurer business practices, 340B or market access analytics. ## Potential Salary $224,500–320,000 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. ## Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. Over the last decade, PhRMA member companies have invested more than $850 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. ## Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.Americasmedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] ## What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a wellbeing program, back-up care, health advocate service, employee assistance program and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, seven paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated on-boarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in organization-wide community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast-paced career with their own personal goals. ## Equal Opportunity Employer PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment. item.title: Senior Director, Federal Advocacy
item.description: Senior Director, Federal Advocacy Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Senior Director of the Federal Advocacy team to support its advocacy efforts. The Senior Director is responsible for developing and maintaining relationships while building support for PhRMA’s priorities, policies, and positions. The individual will lobby members of Congress and their staff, with a focus on the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee Democrats. The Sr. Director will: – Lobby Senate Democratic members and their staff on potential/proposed legislation and the impact of such legislation on patients and the pharmaceutical industry. – Coordinate with PhRMA colleagues and member company staff on policy positions and the development of legislative strategy related to PhRMA priorities. – Build and maintain relationships with member company staff and other stakeholders. – Represent the Federal Advocacy team at internal PhRMA meetings and collaborate across departments on policy, engagement strategy, and messaging materials. – Anticipate, track, and analyze legislation relevant to industry priorities, and make recommendations for executing on key initiatives involving PhRMA staff and member company representatives as needed. – Develop relationships with priority Democratic members by conducting situational analyses and anticipating Senate policy positions to lobby. – Manage consultants who provide services to the Federal Advocacy team. – Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a proactive, confident, and action‑oriented individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. Key success factors for this role include a strong sense of team and collaborative focus. The preferred candidate will bring substantive health care communications expertise and be an organized, detail‑oriented, self‑starter with excellent writing skills and the ability to convey content in an audience‑appropriate and compelling manner. Demonstrated consensus building, decision‑making, and interpersonal skills are essential. This is a highly visible, fast‑paced position that is both internally and externally facing. Accordingly, the successful candidate should be adaptable, able to reprioritize and shift gears quickly, comfortable in a high‑pressure environment, and be politically savvy, diplomatic, responsive, and mature. ## Professional Experience / Requirements – Bachelor’s degree in political science, public administration, or in a related field. – 8+ years of combined legislative, White House, government affairs consulting, and/or pharmaceutical industry experience. – Understanding of procedures and protocols of standing committees regarding witnesses, testimony, and Congressional activities; working knowledge of the Congressional process and ethics rules and regulations. – Strong relationship‑building skills, integrity, and reputation. – Strong verbal and written communication skills. – Demonstrated collaboration and ability to be a team player. ## Potential Salary Sr. Director: $169,300–$237,100. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. ## Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser‑focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat, and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. ## Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.Americasmedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] ## What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition, and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a well‑being program, an on‑site fitness facility, back‑up care, health advocate service, an employee assistance program, and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half‑day Fridays preceding holidays, half‑day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated onboarding program, best‑in‑class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on‑site and off‑site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in community service activities, fundraising drives, and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast‑paced career with their personal goals. ## Equal Opportunity Employer PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation, or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. The job description contains an overview of the activities and duties for this role. Responsibilities may change and new ones may be assigned at any time. item.title: Regional Affairs, SME
item.description: Regional Affairs, SME Organization: USfalcon Location: Omaha, NE Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Description USfalcon has an exciting opportunity for a Regional Affairs SME to support USSTRATCOM at Offutt AFB, NE. ## ESSENTIAL DUTIES Provide senior‑level subject matter expertise on regional political, economic, and security affairs with a focus on European regions in support of USSTRATCOM campaign and risk assessments. Support campaign and risk assessments by finding, reading, and comprehending diplomatic, informational, military, and economic information from multiple sources and maintaining working knowledge of applicable policy and strategy guidance. Contribute to development and refinement of measurement criteria (measures of effectiveness, measures of performance, scoring standards) used to assess progression or regression toward strategic deterrence objectives in assigned regions. Analyze regional developments and global factors (diplomatic, information, military, economic) to determine their impact on the Strategic Environment and strategic deterrence, and document assessment logic for use in campaign and risk assessments. Develop, update, and maintain regional components of campaign and risk assessments, synthesizing individual assessment results into key findings and recommendations for senior leaders. Produce graduate‑level quality briefings and written reports with supporting in‑depth analysis and research, following best practices for analytic writing, and brief assessment findings to senior leaders. Collaborate with the Office of the Secretary of War, Joint Staff, interagency, international partners, and other Government agencies on regional issues, ensuring USSTRATCOM perspectives are integrated into interagency and CCMD‑level assessments and planning. Actively and continuously support Joint Force and operations assessments by providing regional context, trend analysis, and recommendations to improve force integration, resource allocation, and strategic alignment. ## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS At least 15 years of interagency and/or Combatant Command desk officer international affairs experience. At least 3 years of overseas experience. At least 6 years of experience working on European affairs. Demonstrated ability to produce graduate‑level quality analytic briefs and written reports, and to brief findings to senior leaders. Demonstrated relevant experience supporting: – Campaign and Risk Assessments: maintaining policy and strategy knowledge (National Security Strategy, Unified Command Plan, National Defense Strategy, Nuclear Posture Review, National Military Strategy, Joint Strategic Campaign Plan, Global Campaign Plans, Operations Plans, Contingency Plans); developing measurement criteria; analyzing information to determine progression toward Strategic Deterrence; documenting assessment logic; and developing campaign and risk assessments. – Applying critical thought to identify trends, developing key findings and recommendations, and producing graduate‑level briefs and written reports. – Collaborating with OSW, Joint Staff, interagency, international, and other Government partners; and supporting Joint Force and operations assessments. ## PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Direct experience supporting USSTRATCOM or other Combatant Command campaign planning, regional strategy development, contingency planning, or strategic engagement activities. Experience advising General/Flag Officers or Senior Executive Service leaders on regional developments, strategic implications, and assessment findings. Experience integrating regional analysis into Joint Force and operations assessments, including identification of cost/benefit of operations, activities, and investments toward shaping the strategic environment. ## EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION Master’s degree in International Affairs, Economics, or equivalent field. ## REQUIRED CLEARANCE Top Secret/SCI ## TRAVEL TBD ## Benefits Offered Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short‑term disability, long‑term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, EAP, parental leave, pet insurance, paid time off, and holidays. USfalcon has grown from our roots in 1984 to become a mid‑tier professional services company supporting a diverse and global customer base of DoD and Federal Agencies. We have been excelling in diverse platforms for almost 30 years and continue to be an industry leader. If you thrive in an organization that values integrity, commitment, stewardship, and service, we want to meet you. We deliver core capabilities in Aviation, Space, Information Technology, and Business Operations and continue to grow and expand our competencies, contracts, and customer base, adding to our long history of supporting customer and community needs. Learn more at [www.usfalcon.com/history]. ## Equal Opportunity Employer / Protected Veterans / Individuals with Disabilities This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the *Know Your Rights* notice from the Department of Labor. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: External Affairs Program Manager
item.description: External Affairs Program Manager Organization: Lee County Electric Cooperative (LCEC) Location: N. Fort Myers, FL Date Posted: 08/27/2026 # JOB TITLE: External Affairs Program Manager Location: North Fort Myers, FL Work Hours: M–F 8–5pm (varied hours) ## Our benefits include – Company-wide annual incentive plan – Medical, vision and dental insurance – 401(k) plan with a generous 6% company match – Company funded Pension Plan – On-site wellness/medical facility – Company paid Short & Long-Term Disability insurance – Health Savings Account with an employer contribution – Flexible Spending Accounts – Paid time off and paid holidays – Wellness program with financial rewards – Tuition reimbursement – Group life insurance – Critical Illness and Accident Insurance LCEC provides reliable, cost-competitive electricity to more than 260,000 members throughout a five-county service territory located in Southwest Florida. We employ approximately 485 skilled employees and are one of more than 900 electric distribution cooperatives located throughout the United States. LCEC has been recognized locally and statewide as an industry leader and continually receives acknowledgment for the work that our employees do in the community along with other civic, environmental and professional honors. ## Position Summary The External Affairs Lead is responsible for developing and executing LCEC’s External Affairs strategy in alignment with organizational priorities and executive leadership direction. This position serves as the cooperative’s primary point of contact for government and community stakeholders, proactively identifying risks, opportunities, and external factors that may impact operations, growth, and organizational positioning. This position manages higher-impact stakeholder relationships and represents LCEC in strategic external engagements, leads resolution of complex community and governmental challenges and provides coordinated solutions related to stakeholder risk, community sentiment, and engagement strategy. The position works collaboratively across departments and supports organizational objectives through proactive issue identification, coordination, and external representation. Working closely with Key Accounts, Operations, and Business Continuity, this role ensures alignment between day-to-day operational execution and long-term external strategy. The External Affairs Lead supports LCEC’s ability to proactively navigate an evolving political and regulatory environment while maintaining strong community relationships and advancing organizational resilience. ## Position Responsibilities – Lead LCEC’s government relations, legislative affairs, and external stakeholder engagement efforts, cultivating relationships with policymakers, governmental leadership, and influential community stakeholders to support organizational priorities and long-term strategic objectives. – Manage relationships with governmental entities in their capacity as policymakers, regulators, and community decision-makers rather than as utility customers or account holders. – Assess emerging legislative, regulatory, political, and community issues; develop engagement strategies and provide recommendations to executive leadership regarding organizational risks, opportunities, and stakeholder impacts. – Monitor local, state, and federal legislative actions, ordinances, and policy discussions that may impact LCEC and assess potential impacts to the organization. – Facilitate cross functional alignment to support timely resolution of government-related challenges, inquiries, or concerns. Support development of response strategies and recommendations for leadership as needed. – Prepare and deliver information to government stakeholders related to LCEC initiatives, infrastructure projects, service issues, rate-related matters, and outage or restoration activity. – Provide input into messaging approaches and support leadership briefings related to governmental matters. Ensure consistency of messaging with internal guidance and organizational priorities. – Represent LCEC in high-visibility or contentious settings requiring independent judgment and discretion. – Support coordination with government partners during emergency events or organizational activations. – Participate in targeted community or civic activities directly related to government relationships. – Operate independently with external stakeholders, manage multiple complex issues simultaneously, and provide frequent updates (verbally & written) and strategic recommendations to leadership. – Maintain effective working relationships with employees and customers at all levels within LCEC. Ensure smooth operations, productive communications, and effective understanding during all interpersonal contacts. Provide current and accurate information to all requesters, courteously and in a timely manner. – Support Storm Restoration efforts when needed. Work in emergency storm situations (i.e. hurricanes) and work long hours (>12 hours per day) for many continuous days/weeks as needed. – Perform other related duties as assigned. ## Education – Bachelor’s degree in communications, public affairs, political science, public relations, business administration, or a related field or experience commensurate to degree. (Required) – Master’s Degree in business, marketing, energy management, or related field. (Preferred) ## Experience – 7+ Years progressively responsible experience in lobbying, government relations, public affairs, community engagement, or stakeholder relations, including engagement with local governments, community organizations, and public-sector stakeholders, and experience with public speaking and presentations. (Required) – 5+ Years Utility, infrastructure, or regulated-industry experience. (Preferred) ## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities – Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. (Required) – Proven ability to build and maintain effective stakeholder relationships in complex environments. (Required) – Ability to exercise judgment, manage sensitive issues, and coordinate across departments. (Required) – Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). (Required) – Knowledge of the local service area and community environment. (Preferred) ## Licenses – Valid driver’s license upon hire (Required) ## Physical Demands and Working Environment The physical demands and working environment characteristics described here must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. **Physical Demands:** Standing Occasionally, Walking Occasionally, Sitting Constantly, Lifting Rarely, Carrying Rarely, Pushing Rarely, Pulling Rarely, Climbing Rarely, Balancing Rarely, Stooping Rarely, Kneeling Rarely, Crouching Rarely, Crawling Rarely, Reaching Rarely, Handling Occasionally, Grasping Occasionally, Feeling Rarely, Talking Constantly, Hearing Constantly, Repetitive Motions Frequently, Eye/Hand/Foot Coordination Frequently. **Working Environment:** Frequently Air-conditioned office environment, Rarely Extreme cold, Rarely Extreme heat, Rarely Humidity, Rarely Wet, Occasionally Noise, Rarely Hazards, Rarely Temperature Change, Rarely Atmospheric Conditions, Rarely Vibration. ## STORM DUTY REQUIREMENTS Responding to storms may be considered a condition of employment: LCEC provides critical services to our community during an emergency. Employees may be required to participate in the response/recovery activities related to emergencies/disasters to maintain service to our LCEC members. Employees are required to work in their normal job duties or other assigned activities. Proper compensation will be made in accordance with the company’s guidelines and procedures. ## Additional Information Please note that at the time a candidate is made a job offer, the candidate will be subject to a background check and a drug screening. item.title: Director, Digital Standards Strategy and Regulatory Science (REMOTE)
item.description: Director, Digital Standards Strategy and Regulatory Science (REMOTE) Organization: U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Description** The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. **Brief Job Overview** USP is seeking a scientific and regulatory leader for its Digital Standards Business Unit who is accountable for defining the scientific framework for USP’s digital pharmacopeial standards and building the coalition of regulators, government stakeholders, and industry partners required to champion and adopt it. Success in Year 1 will include establishing the scientific principles, policy foundations and workflows that govern how USP develops and delivers Digital Standards, securing internal alignment and building engagement with regulators, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to align the field behind that framework. This individual will represent USP in high-stakes external scientific and regulatory forums and serve as a visible thought leader on the future of digital pharmacopeial quality standards. Internally, the Director will work highly cross-functionally with USP’s Science, Quality, Lab Operations, IT, Commercial, and other teams to ensure Digital Standards are embedded in USP’s compendial and commercial processes. The Director will also have functional oversight of the portfolio of Digital Standards products, including USP-ID and MethodConnect, ensuring product direction aligns to the scientific framework. Scale-up and market adoption are priorities in subsequent years that will follow framework and stakeholder alignment. This role requires skills in both internal change management and external stakeholder alignment within the scientific realm. Remote employees must reside in one of the following states: MD, VA, DC, PA, WV, CA, MI, IL, KS, FL, NC, or MN. **How will YOU create impact here at USP?** As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. **Key Responsibilities** 1) Scientific Framework, Enterprise Strategy & Governance Define the scientific framework governing USP’s Digital Standards including scientific principles, structure, rigor requirements, and lifecycle approach, in close collaboration with USP’s Science and Quality teams, and translate that framework into the enterprise strategy and operating model required to scale Digital Standards across USP divisions. Oversee Digital Standards lifecycle governance, ensuring scientific rigor on par with traditional USP Standards and consistent application of the scientific framework across product lines. Ensure Digital Standards integrate with and support USP documentary standards and scientific development processes as the enterprise evolves. Establish and continuously improve cross-functional governance (decision rights, portfolio prioritization, metrics, escalation) to balance speed, rigor, and compliance. Provide executive-level updates, options, and recommendations to the Digital Standards steering committee and senior stakeholders. 2) Regulatory, Scientific & Industry Engagement Own development and execution of the regulator, government, and industry engagement strategy required to build alignment and cultivate champions for the scientific framework across the pharmaceutical ecosystem. Develop and oversee scientific and policy partnerships; collaborate with Legal department and other enterprise stakeholders to structure pilots and collaboration agreements with regulators, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers. Lead high-stakes external engagement with regulators, government agencies, standards bodies, scientific societies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to align the field behind USP’s Digital Standards scientific framework and cultivate external champions. Represent USP as a thought leader through conferences, publications, and industry forums; maintain relationships with key scientific, regulatory, and industry influencers. 3) Policy Frameworks & Implementation Enablement Oversee internal and external policy frameworks for Digital Standards (structure, lifecycle, metadata, interoperability, implementation guidance) and ensure consistency across product lines. Ensure policy is translated into practical implementation assets (schemas/specifications, guidance, training, playbooks) for industry and internal stakeholders. Coordinate cross-division alignment so Digital Standards policies fit within enterprise controls (quality systems, security, legal, and commercial governance). 4) Portfolio Oversight Oversee portfolio-level strategic alignment, implementation plans, annual budgets, forecasts, and KPIs for Digital Standards Business Unit. Translate market insights and performance analytics into portfolio choices. Prioritize development of the portfolio of compendial Digital Standards and Digital Emerging Standards. 5) People Leadership, Talent Strategy & Culture Build, lead, and develop a multi-disciplinary team spanning advocacy, strategic collaborations, scientific development, policy, and program management. Provide functional oversight for the portfolio of digital products relating to Digital Standards to ensure alignment of product development with scientific, regulatory, and policy approaches. Coach and develop leaders; set clear expectations and equitable performance management practices; foster an inclusive culture that supports growth and accountability. Establish scalable operating rhythms (quarterly planning, portfolio reviews, KPI dashboards, stakeholder communications) that enable predictable delivery and learning. Be a visible influencer for Digital Standards both internally and externally; facilitate information sharing and thought leadership through publications, presentations, discussions, and other fora. **Who is USP Looking For?** The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, and the following competencies and experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical sciences, analytical chemistry, regulatory science, or a closely related scientific discipline, with demonstrated scientific credibility recognized by peers in industry, regulators, or standards bodies. 7+ years of people management experience, including building multi-disciplinary teams across advocacy, scientific, policy, and program functions. Proven ability to implement changes across a matrixed organization, including influencing senior stakeholders, and shaping governance, operating models, workflows, and policy frameworks. Demonstrated ability to convene and align regulators, government stakeholders, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers around a shared scientific or policy framework. Advanced degree (PhD, PharmD, MS, or equivalent) in a scientific, pharmaceutical, or analytical discipline, OR a comparable track record of peer-reviewed publications, contributions to public standards development, or recognized leadership in scientific or regulatory working groups. **Additional Desired Preferences** Experience within a regulatory or standard setting body, like FDA, EMA, ICH. Understanding of pharmacopeial standard setting process and its relevance in pharmaceutical product development and quality control. Experience with scientific content workflows and analytical methods and/or digital method lifecycle frameworks. Experience with analytical chemistry technologies, including NMR, FTIR, MassSpec, HPLC, and others. Experience with establishing strategic collaborations, including drafting agreements with pharmaceutical or other life science organizations. item.title: Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance
item.description: Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance Organization: U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Description** The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. **Brief Job Overview** The Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance is a hands-on managerial role responsible for the program management of USP’s global trade compliance program, with primary focus on applicable U.S. trade regulations, tariffs and sanctions requirements, and USP global trade compliance standards. The Senior Manager will work across all geographies, including serving as a functional manager to the India Trade Compliance team, to build and ensure adherence to a consistent global trade compliance framework for USP as the organization continues to evolve. The incumbent will proactively address immediate trade-related compliance needs, monitor sanctions-related developments and exposure, tariffs, and build longer-term plans to address emerging regulatory changes. This individual will take a strategic view to resolve complex import, export, tariff and sanctions compliance issues, including partnering with the Legal team and other business stakeholders to identify practical mitigation strategies for associated trade compliance risk, in a manner that fully complies with all governmental and organization policies, while aligning with business priorities where practical. **How Will YOU Create Impact Here at USP?** As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. **The Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance Has the Following Responsibilities** **Lead Global Trade Compliance Strategy & Execution** Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of USP’s Global Trade Compliance program in alignment with organizational goals, regulatory requirements, and business needs. Translate program priorities into actionable workplans and measurable team activities. **Support Global Alignment, Operational Consistency & Performance Accountability** Coordinate priorities, processes, and execution across geographically dispersed team members (U.S. & India) to promote consistent trade compliance practices. Support governance routines, performance tracking, and issue escalation; assess team capacity, workload, and processes to align resources to priority risks and business needs, improve efficiency, reduce duplication, and support sustainable team effectiveness. **Manage Global Trade Compliance Team Execution** Provide direct and functional leadership to Global Trade Compliance team members in the U.S. and India to align workplans and execution with USP’s global trade compliance standards. Assess team capacity, workload, and operating processes to ensure resources are aligned to the highest-priority compliance risks and business needs. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce duplication, and strengthen execution while supporting sustainable workloads and team effectiveness. **Support Team Development & Performance** Set clear goals and performance expectations for direct reports, provide coaching and constructive documented feedback, and support professional development to strengthen team capability, consistency, and execution. **Promote an Inclusive & Engaged Team Culture** Model inclusive leadership behaviors aligned with USP’s Equity = Excellence philosophy. Create a psychologically safe environment where diverse perspectives are valued, engagement is high, and team members are empowered to contribute and grow. **Partner Across the Organization** Work collaboratively with cross-functional stakeholders to provide practical trade compliance guidance, support risk identification, and integrate compliance requirements into day-to-day business processes. **Align Trade Compliance Risk Tolerance with Organizational Risk Profile** Maintain practical trade compliance risk tolerance levels aligned with USP’s overall organizational risk profile, escalating higher-risk matters and recommending mitigation strategies that balance regulatory requirements, business needs, and mission impact. **Ensure Regulatory Compliance & Risk Mitigation** Monitor and ensure compliance with applicable U.S. import/export laws, tariffs, sanctions requirements, and USP global trade compliance standards. Identify, assess, and help mitigate trade-related risks, in coordination with Legal, business stakeholders, and India-based resources as appropriate. Proactively recommend solutions to emerging issues. **Maintain Policies, Procedures & Program Improvements** Develop, maintain, and update trade compliance procedures, guidance, and best practices. Implement updates based on stakeholder feedback, monitoring results, and regulatory changes. **Oversee Classification, Licensing & Screening Programs** Maintain oversight of classification processes (HTS, Schedule B, ECCN), jurisdiction and license determinations, and global classification databases. Manage restricted party screening programs, resolve escalations, and ensure appropriate training and access controls. **Manage External Partners & Operational Execution** Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and internal stakeholders to support compliant and efficient import/export execution. Monitor service quality, address operational issues, and manage key processes such as AES filings, country-of-origin determinations, valuation, free trade agreements, and recordkeeping. **Support Business Growth & Expansion** Partner with business stakeholders to identify and address trade compliance requirements related to new product launches, global expansion, and evolving business activities. Support practical processes, guidance, and controls to enable compliant and efficient execution. **Develop & Deliver Training Programs** Design and implement role-based training programs to build organizational awareness and capability in import/export compliance, ensuring stakeholders understand responsibilities and requirements. **Who Is USP Looking For?** The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, along with the following competencies and experience: Bachelor’s degree in business administration, economics, or relevant field; or equivalent experience. Minimum of 8 years relevant experience with U.S. import and export regulations and global trade. Minimum of 2 years people managerial experience. Experience collaborating with a global team. Experience in a functional management structure is preferred. Must have extensive knowledge of U.S. export laws and regulations, tariffs, U.S. denied parties and sanctioned country laws and regulations, including OFAC and other country trade regulations. Must have the ability to successfully lead and implement compliance initiatives with a positive and collaborative style. Must have the ability to plan and manage multiple tasks while working with individuals across the organization at all levels. Licensed Customs Broker and/or trade-related certifications required. Must possess strong attention to detail, critical thinking, and excellent problem-solving skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with time-sensitive submissions and strict reporting deadlines. Strong and effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. **Additional Desired Preferences** Experience in the pharmaceutical, chemical, and biologics industry area. Ability to understand potential obstacles to projects, appreciate stakeholder concerns, and positively influence successful completion through alignment. item.title: Regional Manager & Sr. Director, Latin America (LATAM)
item.description: Regional Manager & Sr. Director, Latin America (LATAM) Organization: U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Description The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. ## Brief Job Overview This role is critical to advancing USP’s mission of protecting patient safety and improving global health by ensuring strong regional execution, trusted partnerships, and sustainable growth throughout Latin America. The Regional Manager & Sr. Director, Latin America (LATAM) is responsible for strategic leadership, operational execution, and sustainable growth of USP’s mission, programs, and commercial activities across Latin America. This role serves as USP’s senior regional executive, accountable for strengthening USP’s public health impact, regulatory engagement, stakeholder relationships, and financial performance in a diverse and highly regulated environment. The RM & Sr. Director LATAM will lead multidisciplinary teams across Scientific Programs, Strategic Customers Development, External Affairs, Marketing and Operations, while ensuring full alignment with USP’s global strategy, values, and quality standards. **Location:** This is a Remote role available in the following U.S. States: MD, VA, DC, PA, WV, CA, MI, IL, KS, FL, NC, MN, or NH. ## How will YOU create impact here at USP? As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. ## The RM & Sr. Director LATAM has the following responsibilities: ### Strategic Leadership Define and execute USP’s regional strategy for Latin America, aligned with global priorities and public health objectives. Identify growth opportunities for standards adoption, reference materials, training programs, and partnerships. Act as a trusted strategic advisor to global leadership on regional risks, opportunities, and policy developments. ### Public Health & Regulatory Engagement Lead high-level engagement with health authorities, regulators, ministries of health, trade associations, academy, and public institutions across LATAM. Strengthen USP’s role as a trusted scientific and regulatory partner, supporting medicine quality, supply chain integrity, and patient safety. Represent USP in regional and international forums, technical committees, and policy discussions. ### Business & Financial Management Own revenue growth, cost control, and financial sustainability responsibilities for the LATAM region. Drive development and execution of commercial strategies, business models, and channel access approaches consistent with USP’s non-profit mission. Ensure strong forecasting, budgeting, and performance tracking and measures. ### Operational Excellence Oversee regional operations, ensuring regulatory compliance, quality systems, risk management, and internal controls. Ensure effective coordination across scientific, commercial, and operational teams. Lead crisis management and issue resolution in complex regulatory or geopolitical environments. ### People Leadership & Culture Build, lead, and develop high-performing, diverse, and inclusive teams across multiple countries. Foster a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, and scientific excellence. Ensure talent development, succession planning, and organizational scalability. ### Partnerships & External Relations Develop strategic partnerships and collaboration with Regulatory Agencies, Pharma Industry, Academia, Trade Associations, Key Stakeholders and Convention Members. Support fundraising, grants, and donor-funded initiatives aligned with USP’s mission when applicable. Serve as USP’s senior spokesperson in the region, enhancing brand reputation and trust. ## Who is USP Looking For? The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, along with the following competencies and experience: ### Required Advanced degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Chemistry, Public Health, Business, or related field (MBA or PhD preferred). Minimum 15+ years of progressive leadership experience, including senior management responsibility in Latin America. Demonstrated experience in regulated environments (pharmaceuticals, healthcare, life sciences, or public health). Proven P&L management and experience leading complex, multi-country operations. Deep understanding of LATAM regulatory frameworks, health systems, and market dynamics. Fluency in Portuguese, English and Advanced Spanish required. ### Preferred Experience in non-profit, standards-setting, regulatory, pharmaceutical market, or mission-driven organizations. Established network with regional health authorities and international organizations. Track record of public-private partnerships and donor-funded programs. ## Leadership Competencies Mission-driven and values-based leadership Strategic and systems thinking Executive presence and stakeholder influence Financial and operational acumen Cross-cultural leadership and collaboration High integrity and ethical judgment ## Additional Desired Preferences Desired preferences include highlighting any additional preferred levels of expertise for the role—reminder: items listed here are not requirements and do not disqualify a candidate from consideration. Strategic thinking, strong written and verbal communication skills. Self-motivated and proactive with a sense of urgency, with proven ability to prioritize and focus on key objectives. Proven aptitude for building relationships, credibility, and trust with stakeholders, and creating a collaborative work environment. Ability to influence without direct authority. Solution-oriented and innovative; can identify creative options for resolving issues that respond to multiple stakeholder interests and needs. Availability to travel across the territory (30–40%). ## Supervisory Responsibilities Manager, Finance and Accounts Scientific Affairs Manager Director, Latin America Marketing & Customer Experience Senior Government & Regulatory Affairs Manager External Affairs Director & Mexico Head ## Benefits USP provides the benefits to protect yourself and your family today and tomorrow. From company-paid time off and comprehensive healthcare options to retirement savings, you can have peace of mind that your personal and financial well-being is protected. ## Compensation Base Salary Range: USD $212,500 – $270,175 annually. Target Annual Bonus: % Varies based on level of role. Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate’s skill set, experience, qualifications, equity, and other job-related reasons. Note: USP does not accept unsolicited resumes from 3rd party recruitment agencies and is not responsible for fees from recruiters or other agencies except under specific written agreement with USP. ## Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights [https://www.eeoc.gov/poster] notice from the Department of Labor. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council!
