item.title: Head of Public Affairs
item.description: Head of Public Affairs Organization: TRM Labs Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 # Build a Safer World TRM Labs provides AI‑powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM’s platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. TRM Labs is hiring a **Head of Public Affairs** to lead external communications and public affairs for our government programs. You’ll own publicity, announcements, and message coordination with federal and executive‑branch communications stakeholders — translating complex, sensitive program work into accurate, approved public narratives. ## The Impact You Will Have Lead public affairs for TRM’s government programs — own the external narrative and drive publicity that creates clarity, credibility, and engagement around the missions we are supporting. Own government and agency media relations — build relationships, navigate review and approval cycles, and maintain message discipline across stakeholders. Position TRM and program leaders as credible voices in public moments where appropriate, with sound judgment about what is said, when, and by whom. Lead rapid response during reputational, regulatory, or program‑related events — drafting statements and coordinating with agency comms leads and TRM Policy/Legal before anything goes public. Operate with discretion inside approval‑gated, confidentiality‑heavy environments. ## What We’re Looking For 8–12+ years in strategic communications / public affairs, with meaningful experience in or alongside government (federal agency, Capitol Hill, or a public‑affairs firm serving government clients). Proven ownership of high‑stakes external communications and senior/principal‑level positioning — not just supporting a senior leader. Comfort inside government review, message‑clearance, and approval cycles, with strict confidentiality on sensitive work. Exceptional writing and message framing, and sound judgment in fast‑moving, high‑sensitivity public moments. AI‑fluent in how modern communications work gets done, with a proactive experimentation mindset. Based in (or able to be highly present in) Washington, DC. ## About the Team Our core mission is to drive revenue growth by shaping market perception and activating demand through strategic storytelling and visibility across earned and owned channels. You will partner closely with Insights, Brand & Content, Demand Generation, Product Marketing, Regional Marketing, and the Executive Team. Core collaboration overlap with ET; flexible hours with expectation of responsiveness to media inquiries. ## Compensation Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only. Estimated base salary range: **$150,000 – $210,000**. This role may also be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan. Geographic cost differences outside the United States are factored into compensation. ## Application Instructions If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team. Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role. If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered. ## What to Expect From Our Interview Process Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview. **Recruiter Intro:** Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role. **Hiring Manager:** Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact. **First Round:** Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role. **Final Round:** Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem‑solving, and alignment with TRM. **References:** We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact. **Offer:** If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions. **Welcome to TRM:** Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding. Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way. ## Life at TRM We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day. TRM moves quickly. We are a high‑velocity, high‑ownership team that expects clarity, follow‑through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days. Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem‑solving. At TRM, you should expect: – Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate – Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity – A high level of personal ownership and accountability – Close collaboration across teams and functions – Frequent, high‑touch communication – Creative problem solving and out‑of‑the‑box thinking – A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast‑moving and intense environment. We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure‑test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here. At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission‑driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. ## AI Fluency at TRM AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM. We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks. AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to: – Accelerate repeatable workflows – Structure and solve problems – Improve output quality – Increase speed and leverage You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process. ## Leadership Principles We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions. **Impact‑Oriented Trailblazer:** We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment — test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly. **Master Craftsperson:** We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better every day. **Inspiring Colleague:** We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger. ## Join Our Mission At TRM we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast. TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed‑first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. ## Privacy Policy and Additional Information By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy. We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM. Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law. If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at [email protected] . To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non‑compliant, please submit a report through the provided form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. The u

item.title: VP, Government Affairs
item.description: VP, Government Affairs Organization: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 ## Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count? Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long‑term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world. With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas, and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed, and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career. Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded. The selected colleague will work at an MUFG office or client sites four days per week and work remotely one day. A member of our recruitment team will provide more details. The Vice President of Government Affairs will support MUFG’s engagement with Congress, the Administration, federal regulatory agencies, and industry stakeholders on public policy issues affecting the financial services sector and the broader business environment. The role, which will report to the Director of U.S. Government Affairs and work with colleagues across MUFG’s U.S. and global businesses, combines government affairs strategy and execution, substantive policy expertise, and external advocacy — with particular emphasis on financial services, financial policy and regulation, and policy matters impacting a large global financial institution. The Vice President will help develop and advance policy positions, translate complex policy developments into institutional, business, and client implications and actionable engagement priorities, and work with internal partners to understand MUFG’s priorities and support effective external engagement and advocacy. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Government Affairs & External Engagement – Help lead and execute engagement with Congress, the Administration, federal financial regulators, and other policymakers. – Build and maintain relationships with government officials, industry stakeholders, trade associations, and peer institutions. – Represent MUFG in external meetings, industry coalitions, and policy forums, helping advance institutional priorities and shape collective advocacy efforts. ### Financial Services Policy & Advocacy – Monitor and assess legislative and regulatory developments affecting banking, financial services, and the broader policy environment in which MUFG and its clients operate. – Support the development of policy positions and advocacy strategies in partnership with internal subject‑matter experts, translating complex issues into clear engagement priorities. – Support MUFG’s advocacy on financial services and broader economic policy issues, identifying where direct, collective, or differentiated engagement may be appropriate. ### Strategic Partnership & Policy Translation – Partner with Legal, Regulatory Affairs, Risk, and business teams to connect policy developments with institutional priorities and inform external engagement. – Translate U.S. policy and regulatory developments into clear implications for senior leaders, business partners, and, where appropriate, clients, while connecting Washington priorities across MUFG’s U.S. and global businesses. – Develop executive briefings, policy insights, and materials supporting senior‑level government, industry, business, and selected client engagements. — ## Qualifications – Approximately 7–12 years of relevant experience in government affairs, public policy, financial services, regulatory affairs, government, law, or a related field. – Meaningful experience with financial services policy, banking regulation, or other complex legislative and regulatory matters. – Experience engaging with Congress, federal agencies, regulators, industry associations, or other policymakers and stakeholders. – Demonstrated ability to develop and advance policy positions and translate complex policy issues into practical advocacy, business, or engagement priorities. – Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process, the Washington policy environment, and the implications of public policy for financial institutions and their businesses. – Strong written and oral communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to work effectively with senior internal and external stakeholders. — ## Education J.D. or other advanced degree valued but not required; equivalent relevant experience will be considered. — ## Compensation & Benefits The typical base pay range for this role is between $190K–$225K depending on job‑related knowledge, skills, experience, and location. This role may also be eligible for certain discretionary performance‑based bonuses and/or incentive compensation. Additionally, our Total Rewards program provides colleagues with a competitive benefits package (in accordance with the eligibility requirements and respective terms of each) that includes comprehensive health and wellness benefits, retirement plans, educational assistance and training programs, income replacement for qualified employees with disabilities, paid maternity and parental bonding leave, and paid vacation, sick days, and holidays. — ## Fair Chance & Compliance Statement We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws (including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act) to the extent that: (a) an applicant is not subject to a statutory disqualification pursuant to Section 3(a)(39) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 or Section 8a(2) or 8a(3) of the Commodity Exchange Act, and (b) they do not conflict with the background screening requirements of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) and the National Futures Association (NFA). The major responsibilities listed above are the material job duties of this role for which the Company reasonably believes that criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment, if any. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and committed to leveraging the diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experience of our workforce to create opportunities for our colleagues and our business. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, gender expression, gender identity, sex, age, ancestry, marital status, protected veteran and military status, disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, genetic information, or any other status of an individual or that individual’s associates or relatives that is protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. item.title: VP Public Policy & Government Affairs
item.description: VP Public Policy & Government Affairs Organization: Equinix Location: Redwood City, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 # Who Are We? Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet. A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work. # Job Summary The Leader, Public Policy and Government Affairs (PPGA) is responsible for shaping and advancing a global public policy, regulatory, and geopolitical strategy that enables the Company’s long‑term growth, resilience, and license to operate. This role ensures a supportive legislative, regulatory, and community environment by engaging at the highest levels of government and influencing policy outcomes that directly affect the Company’s global business strategy. Operating as a senior enterprise leader and trusted advisor to the Board, CEO, Executive Team, and senior leadership, the PPGA Leader integrates geopolitical intelligence, regulatory foresight, and systems‑level thinking to anticipate threats and opportunities, and to develop coordinated offensive and defensive strategies that protect and advance the Company’s interests worldwide. # Responsibilities ## Key Stakeholder Engagement Serve as a regular strategic advisor to the Board of Directors, Executive Chair, CEO, Executive Team, and Senior Vice Presidents on public policy, regulatory, geopolitical, and government‑related risks and opportunities. Proactively engage Board members and executive leadership to shape enterprise‑level responses to government, regulatory, community, and geopolitical challenges impacting company strategy, investment decisions, and growth. Partner closely with Regional Presidents, Managing Directors, Legal, Corporate Communications, Strategy, Sustainability, and other senior leaders to align public policy and government engagement with business objectives. Represent the Company externally as the senior voice on public policy and government affairs, strengthening credibility with governments, regulators, industry peers, and other key stakeholders. ## Strategy Development & Systems Thinking Lead the development of a coherent, multi‑year global PPGA strategy, in close partnership with a cross‑functional leadership team, ensuring alignment with the Company’s overall corporate and regional strategies. Apply systems thinking to understand complex interdependencies across geopolitics, regulation, infrastructure, energy, technology, capital investment, and community sentiment—and translate these insights into actionable processes and strategies. Establish enterprise‑wide frameworks that connect geopolitical trends, regulatory developments, and policy risk to business planning, site selection, capital allocation, and market entry decisions. Continuously assess the external environment to identify emerging threats and opportunities, adapting strategy to a rapidly shifting political, regulatory, and geopolitical landscape and an environment of uncertainty and change. ## Geopolitical & Regulatory Leadership Anticipate and interpret geopolitical, regulatory, and legislative developments globally and assess their impact on the Company’s strategy, operations, supply chains, and growth plans. Design and execute offensive and defensive public policy and regulatory strategies to mitigate risk, counter adverse policy developments, and proactively shape favourable outcomes. Lead coordinated engagement with governments at the international, national, state, and local levels, including executive branches, legislatures, regulators, and utilities. Guide the Company’s approach to community engagement and government relations to secure support for development, operations, and long‑term presence in key markets. ## PPGA Team Leadership & Execution Build, develop, and lead a high‑performing global PPGA organization capable of executing against strategic priorities at scale. Translate strategy into clear priorities, operating models, and execution plans, ensuring consistent implementation across regions while allowing for local nuance. Act as a leader of leaders, empowering senior PPGA leaders to execute effectively while maintaining alignment with enterprise strategy. Continuously evolve the PPGA organizational design, capabilities, and resource allocation to address the most material risks and opportunities facing the Company. ## Cross‑Functional & Legal Partnership Lead the PPGA function within the Legal Department, working in close partnership with Legal leadership and cross‑functional teams to ensure cohesive execution and accountability. Establish governance, processes, and metrics to track progress against strategic goals and ensure transparency with executive leadership. Oversee PPGA‑related budgets and external spend, ensuring disciplined investment aligned with strategic priorities and risk mitigation objectives. ## Thought Leadership Build deep connections with legal and regulatory capabilities, driving a commercially grounded, pragmatic, and interconnected approach to cross‑functional PPGA, compliance, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement. Serve as an internal and external thought leader on public policy, regulation, and geopolitics as they intersect with digital infrastructure, energy, sustainability, and technology. Shape and articulate compelling policy positions that reflect the Company’s values, long‑term vision, and business needs. Provide clear, concise, and forward‑looking insights to senior leadership, enabling informed decision‑making in moments of uncertainty and change. # Qualifications Considerable years of overall Public Policy & Government Affairs experience, with at least 10 years in a senior leadership role. Preferably cross‑functional experience such as leading regulatory and compliance strategies and teams. Experience leading a globally diverse team and delivering outcomes across jurisdictions. Experience leading an organization through transformation. Experience as a strategic partner to the business, preferably in the technology/data center sector. Strong leadership skills in motivating a team and delivering on team objectives as a unified team with one voice. Possesses a highly evolved commercial sensibility. Possesses executive presence and ability to influence at the SVP level and above. Ability to standardize global policies while translating for local complexities. Adept at balancing intense short‑term pressures with overall long‑term goals. Adept at inspiring behavior change through motivating teams, planning initiatives, designating priorities, and being decisive when faced with ambiguity. Focus on execution and results—establishing high standards for performance, setting goals and developing plans, following through, and holding people accountable for results. # Compensation United States – Washington DC Office DCS: 272,000 – 408,000 USD / Annual United States – Redwood City Office GHQ: 272,000 – 408,000 USD / Annual Our pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum target for new hire pay for the full‑time position determined by role, level, and location. The pay range shown is based on our compensation structure in place at the time of posting and may be updated periodically based on business needs. Individual pay is based on additional factors including job‑related skills, experience, and relevant education and/or training. The targeted pay range listed reflects base pay only and does not include bonus, equity, or benefits. Employees are eligible for bonus, and equity may be offered depending on the position. # Equinix Benefits As an employee, you become important to Equinix’s success. We ensure all your benefits are in line with our core values: competitive, inclusive, sustainable, connected, and efficient. We keep them competitive within the current marketplace to ensure we’re providing you with the best package possible. Wherever you are in your career and life, you’ll be able to enhance your experience and bring your whole self to work. **Employee Assistance Program:** Available to all employees. **US Benefits:** – **Insurance:** Health, life, disability, and voluntary plans for you and eligible family members. – **Retirement:** You and Equinix may contribute to a retirement plan. – **Paid Time Off (PTO) & Paid Holidays:** Accrued PTO each pay period plus paid holidays. Eligibility requirements apply. Equinix is committed to ensuring that our employment process is open to all individuals, including those with a disability. If you are a qualified candidate and need assistance or an accommodation, please let us know by completing the provided form. Equinix is an Equal Employment Opportunity and, in the U.S., an Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to protected characteristics under applicable law. We use artificial intelligence in our hiring process. This posting is a new position within our organization. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: VP – Government Affairs
item.description: VP – Government Affairs Organization: Government Employees Health Association, Inc. (G.E.H.A) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 ## Government Employees Health Association, Inc. (G.E.H.A) Government Employees Health Association, Inc. (G.E.H.A) is a nonprofit member association that provides health and dental benefits that millions of federal employees and retirees, military retirees and their families have counted on since 1937. Offering one of the largest health and dental benefit provider networks available to federal employees in the United States, G.E.H.A empowers health and wellness by meeting its members where they are, when they need care. G.E.H.A has one mission: To empower federal workers to be healthy and well. The Vice President, Government Affairs is responsible for leading and executing G.E.H.A’s federal government relations strategy, advancing the organization’s legislative, regulatory, and policy priorities and strengthening relationships with key stakeholders across the Executive Branch, Congress, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and other federal agencies, and industry associations. The role serves as the senior leader for the government affairs function and oversees internal and external resources supporting advocacy, public policy, government affairs-related communications, and stakeholder engagement efforts. The position will coordinate the activities of G.E.H.A’s external government affairs consultants and advisors to ensure a unified and effective government affairs function that meets the strategic objectives of the organization. — ## SKILLS ### Essential Duties and Responsibilities ### Government Affairs Strategy & Advocacy Develop and execute a comprehensive government affairs strategy aligned with G.E.H.A’s mission, business objectives and corporate strategy. Monitor and assess legislative, regulatory, and political developments affecting G.E.H.A, the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB), the Postal Service Health Benefits (PSHB) and Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance (FEDVIP) programs and similar federal healthcare programs, and related business interests. Advise executive leadership on emerging policy risks, opportunities, and stakeholder developments. Represent G.E.H.A in interactions with federal policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. Lead advocacy initiatives designed to favorably influence legislation, regulations and public policy outcomes likely to impact the organization. ### Leadership & Team Management Provide strategic leadership and oversight of G.E.H.A’s government affairs function. Direct and support government affairs team members (internal and external), including those responsible for congressional and agency relations, federal healthcare policy analysis, stakeholder engagement, and industry outreach. Foster a collaborative, high-performing team focused on delivering measurable advocacy and policy outcomes. Establish priorities and performance goals for team members. ### External Partner Management Oversee and coordinate the activities of external government affairs consultants and advisors. Collaborate with G.E.H.A’s communications area to oversee and coordinate the government affairs-related work of external public relations and communications partners. Develop and manage coordinated work plans, priorities, and deliverables for external government affairs consultants and advisors. Ensure alignment between G.E.H.A’s business objectives and external government affairs consultants and advisors, and consistent messaging across all functions supporting government affairs. Evaluate the effectiveness of external government affairs engagements and recommend adjustments to maximize return on investment. Establish regular reporting, accountability, and performance metrics for external partners. Coordinate with legal and compliance functions to ensure all advocacy, lobbying, and public affairs activities comply with applicable laws, ethics rules, and disclosure requirements. ### Stakeholder Engagement Develop and maintain relationships with relevant OPM stakeholders, support engagement with OPM by other G.E.H.A functional areas (e.g. product, actuarial and clinical), and ensure alignment across all OPM connection points. Establish and maintain relationships with members of Congress, congressional staff, administration officials, federal agencies, and other key federal healthcare stakeholders. Coordinate executive engagement opportunities with policymakers and influencers. Represent G.E.H.A in relevant industry associations, coalitions, and policy forums, including ongoing engagement with organizations such as Association of Federal Health Organizations (AFHO). Develop strategies to enhance G.E.H.A’s visibility and credibility among policymakers and thought leaders. ### Executive Support & Strategic Counsel Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Legal Officer, Executive Leadership Team, and other senior G.E.H.A executives on policy and government relations matters. Prepare executive briefings, position papers, policy analyses, and stakeholder engagement plans. Support organizational efforts involving federal contracting, healthcare policy, and regulatory compliance as they intersect with government affairs priorities. Coordinate cross-functional government affairs initiatives involving areas such as Legal, Communications, Business Development, and Operations. — ## Qualifications ### Required Education Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government, Law, Healthcare Administration, or a related field. Advanced degree (JD, MBA, MPA, MPH, or similar) preferred. ### Required Experience 10+ years of progressive experience in government affairs, federal advocacy, public policy, congressional relations, or a related field. Demonstrated experience developing and executing successful federal government relations strategies. Experience managing external lobbying, consulting, and public affairs firms. Strong understanding of federal healthcare policy, Congress, federal agencies, and the regulatory process. Experience leading teams and influencing senior executives. ### Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Exceptional strategic thinking and political judgment. Superior written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management capabilities. Ability to analyze complex legislative and regulatory issues and translate them into actionable business recommendations. Demonstrated leadership presence and executive-level influence. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic and fast-changing environment. — ## Reporting Relationship Reports to: Executive Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Legal Officer. — ## Location Washington, D.C. area preferred, with regular travel to congressional offices, federal agencies, industry events, and company offices in Lee’s Summit, MO as required. — ## Success Measures Advancement of G.E.H.A’s legislative, regulatory, and business priorities. Strength and effectiveness of relationships with policymakers and key stakeholders, including but not limited to OPM. Successful coordination of internal and external government affairs resources. Timely identification and mitigation of policy and government affairs-related regulatory risks. — ## Work-at-home requirements Must have the ability to provide a non-cellular High Speed Internet Service such as Fiber, DSL, or cable Modems for a home office. A minimum standard speed for optimal performance of 30×5 (30mpbs download x 5mpbs upload) is required. Latency (ping) response time lower than 80 ms. Hotspots, satellite and wireless internet service is NOT allowed for this role. item.description: Managing Director of Healthcare Regulatory Research Institute Organization: Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy and Healthcare Regulatory Research Institute Location: Alexandria, VA | Remote Date Posted: 08/31/2026 ## Job Description ### Managing Director, HRRI The Managing Director of the Healthcare Regulatory Research Institute (HRRI) oversees and contributes to strategic initiatives relative to HRRI’s and FSBPT’s missions and goals. The Managing Director contributes to projects by helping to define the research agenda, overseeing researchers’ work, and communicating key research through writing, formal presentations, and informal outreach. The Managing Director contributes to overseeing a budget of approximately $2 million, supervises 1–3 staff, and oversees contractor work. ## Key Responsibilities Represents FSBPT and HRRI to key stakeholder groups, including making conference presentations, collaborating with client and peer organizations, and engaging customers at exhibit halls. Broadly contributes to external communications: written reports, research summaries, live presentations, and webinars. Serves as an expert resource to members and other stakeholders in public policy relevant to regulation in healthcare. Develops strategies around engaging stakeholders in utilizing research and regulatory products. Works to position research and products in a favorable light with stakeholders representing diverse perspectives. Helps gather user feedback on research and products and integrate feedback into future work. May help design surveys and facilitate task forces, expert panels, and other stakeholder groups. Oversees contractor work, reviews deliverables, and provides feedback when necessary. Collaboratively works with other senior leaders to develop and oversee the HRRI budget of approximately $2 million. Contributes to shaping and executing organizational strategy through collaboration with leadership, advisors, and other stakeholders. Engages in long‑term planning. Evaluates current and future research partners. Tracks key public policy and legislative issues and develops outreach and response strategies. Coordinates human and physical resources (booth and marketing materials) across events, presentations, and marketing opportunities. Supervises 1–3 administrative staff. ## Key Skills – Expertise in key policy areas (workforce, public policy) – Strategic planning and downstream thinking – Excellent communications – written and verbal – Excellent public speaking skills – informational and persuasive – Project management ## Education Bachelor’s degree required in public policy, law, public health, or related discipline. ## Experience More than eight years of work‑related experience. item.description: Vice President, State Government Affairs Organization: Information Technology Industry Council (ITI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 ## Vice President, State Government Affairs The Information Technology Industry Council (ITI) is the premier advocacy and policy organization for the world’s leading innovation companies. ITI is seeking a **Vice President, State Government Affairs** to join its Government Affairs team. This opportunity is located at ITI’s headquarters in Washington, DC. ITI is committed to attracting creative, talented, and energetic team members. ## Position Summary As the Vice President of State Government Affairs, you will report to the Executive Vice President of Government Affairs and will have a unique opportunity to expand and lead a robust advocacy program representing ITI’s priorities to state governments across the United States. This pivotal role offers the chance to lead a state government affairs function, working closely with ITI member companies and across the organization with other teams to influence the future of tech policy at the state level. ## Key Responsibilities ### Strategic Leadership – **Strategic plan** — Develop and execute a comprehensive strategic plan to expand ITI’s state government affairs function. – **Team recruitment** — Identify, recruit, onboard, and manage a team of government affairs professionals and consultants as needed to support the growing function. – **Policy coordination** — Develop and coordinate state policy objectives with ITI Government Affairs, Public Sector, and Policy teams to ensure cohesive positioning on state and federal policy matters. – **Member guidance** — Provide strategic guidance and intelligence to member companies on priority state legislation nationwide and develop and execute engagement strategies that deliver results. ### Advocacy and Relationship Building – **State advocacy** — Represent ITI member company priorities before state policymakers nationwide by providing in‑person testimony, drafting position letters, submitting regulatory comments, and meeting directly with government stakeholders. – **Senior relationships** — Personally initiate and cultivate relationships at the most senior levels of state governments. – **Policy presence** — Expand ITI’s presence in state‑level policy discussions and advance member priorities through strategic legislation and regulatory measures. – **Political engagement** — Maintain a framework to support ITI and its member companies in the sector’s political engagement. – **Partnership building** — Forge strategic partnerships with key organizations that represent or directly engage with state officials, related third parties, and trade associations. ### Member Engagement and Compliance – **Committee management** — Manage ITI’s State Government Relations Committee by convening regular meetings, building consensus among member companies on state government affairs priorities, and providing timely, detailed updates on key legislative developments. – **Policy translation** — Develop a deep understanding of ITI policy positions and past legislative efforts and translate them into state‑level initiatives. – **Lobbying compliance** — Manage systems to ensure legal compliance with state lobbying registration requirements. ### Operational Management – **Function execution** — Execute all aspects of the state government affairs function. – **Organizational scaling** — Maintain a scalable organizational structure to support future team growth. – **Budget management** — Manage budgets, resources, and performance metrics for the state government affairs function. ## Your Qualifications – 10+ years of experience in state government affairs. – Broad knowledge of technology industry policy. – Previous experience in state government and/or trade association experience, a plus. – Experience in solo project management and execution. – Strong network of contacts in state government affairs. – Excellent verbal and written communication skills. – Strong leadership, strategic planning, and execution capabilities. – Proficiency in identifying, monitoring, and analyzing state legislative activities. – Track record of success in managing advocacy campaigns. – BA/BS degree in political science, policy, business administration, or related field required; advanced degree preferred. – Flexibility for up to 50% travel. ## Your Intangibles – Track record of working well as a member of a team, including cross‑team collaboration. – High emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills. – Strong organizational and project management skills. – Ability to relate effectively with member company executives. – Sound political judgment. – High level of comfort with ambiguity and self‑direction. ## Pay Range $260,000 – $285,000 ## Benefits – Health, dental, vision insurance – Retirement plan – Life and disability insurance – Commuter benefit subsidy – Tuition and Professional Development Reimbursement – Paid time off and holidays ITI is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. item.title: Director, State Advocacy
item.description: Director, State Advocacy Organization: Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy (PPMD) Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/31/2026 # Company Background / Culture Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy (PPMD) is the country’s largest patient organization focused exclusively on Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy. Through comprehensive Advocacy, Care, Education, Research programs and the largest global Duchenne patient registry, PPMD accelerates research, impacts local and federal policy, demands optimal care for all families, and strives to ensure access to approved therapies. In December 2025, Duchenne muscular dystrophy (Duchenne) was added to the Recommended Universal Screening Panel (RUSP), an achievement driven by the community’s commitment to building the research, advocacy and care ecosystem over decades. A current priority is the implementation of newborn screening for Duchenne in all 50 states. # Position Summary The Director, State Advocacy (The Director) provides critical, multi‑faceted support to PPMD’s advocacy and public policy efforts, with direct responsibility for key programs, projects, and initiatives, as well as cross‑functional collaborations across the organization. The Director will champion initiatives that advance PPMD’s federal and state advocacy priorities, with a particular focus on newborn screening (NBS) implementation and the development and execution of state‑based advocacy strategies. The Director will serve as PPMD’s lead for the Duchenne NBS Implementation Collaborative, providing strategic coordination and project management across its working groups, stakeholders, and state implementation efforts. Under the leadership of the Senior Director of Advocacy and in collaboration with other members of the Advocacy team, the Director will monitor state and federal legislation, regulations, policies, and public health initiatives to identify opportunities and challenges that may impact individuals and families living with Duchenne and Becker. The Director will work closely with the Senior Director of Advocacy and PPMD leadership to identify, prioritize, and execute state government affairs opportunities consistent with PPMD’s mission and the priorities of the Duchenne and Becker community. This includes building and strengthening relationships with state policymakers, public health officials, advocacy partners, and other key stakeholders; supporting grassroots advocacy efforts; and developing strategies to advance policies that improve diagnosis, care, access, treatment, and quality of life for individuals and families living with Duchenne and Becker. The Director will also collaborate extensively across PPMD’s programs and departments to support community engagement, educational initiatives, research and data efforts, and organizational priorities. This role requires strong project management, communication, relationship‑building, and strategic thinking skills, as well as the ability to translate complex policy and public health issues into clear and actionable information for diverse audiences. This individual regularly accesses highly confidential and sensitive information, including PHI, and interacts with a diverse group of individuals within PPMD and outside of the organization. It is imperative that the Director maintain discretion, confidentiality, and professionalism, including adherence to HIPAA guidelines. # Essential Duties ## Advocacy Focus Working with the Senior Director of Advocacy, he/she will: – **PPMD Advocacy Team** — Serve as a member of PPMD’s Advocacy team, supporting strategies that advance state and federal policy priorities. – **State-Based Strategies** — Develop and implement state‑based advocacy strategies tailored to individual state environments. – **Policy Monitoring** — Monitor state legislation, regulations, and public health policies relevant to Duchenne and Becker. – **Stakeholder Relationships** — Build and maintain relationships with legislators, health departments, NBS programs, clinicians, advocates, and other stakeholders. – **Representation** — Represent PPMD at legislative meetings, advisory groups, conferences, and public health forums. – **Grassroots Support** — Support grassroots advocacy by engaging families, developing materials, and preparing community members. – **Cross-Team Collaboration** — Work collaboratively with Care, Engagement, Communications, and other internal teams. – **Coalition Building** — Build bipartisan relationships and coalitions across rare disease, disability, public health, and access policy areas. – **Access & Coverage** — Partner with Community Engagement to advance policies related to access, coverage, and reimbursement. – **Workplans & Tracking** — Develop and maintain workplans, timelines, stakeholder lists, and legislative tracking tools. – **Emerging Issues** — Identify emerging policy issues and recommend appropriate engagement. – **Organizational Priorities** — Contribute to broader advocacy initiatives and organizational priorities. ## Newborn Screening Implementation Primary responsibilities include: – **NBS Collaborative Leadership** — Serve as PPMD Lead on the Duchenne NBS Implementation Collaborative. – **Strategic Leadership** — Provide strategic leadership and project management for the collaborative. – **Stakeholder Education** — Support efforts to educate NBS programs, labs, policymakers, clinicians, and other stakeholders. ## Community Research, Data & Cross‑Functional Collaboration – **Data Collaboration** — Work with Registry/Genetics, Care, Research, and other teams to leverage data and insights. – **Registry Projects** — Collaborate on projects using The Duchenne Registry, EHR Study, Decode Duchenne, and other data. – **Gap Analysis** — Identify gaps and opportunities related to NBS, diagnosis, care, and access. – **Cross-Functional Work** — Contribute to cross‑functional initiatives informed by community needs. – **Translation of Data** — Translate research and technical information into actionable insights. # Required Education, Experience, Skills & Attributes ## Education – BA in public administration, public policy, or related government studies; Master’s degree preferred (MPA, MPP, or equivalent). ## Skills, Experience & Competencies – **Self-Starter** — Proactive, able to work independently. – **State Advocacy Experience** — Minimum 2 years state-level advocacy/public policy experience. – **Grassroots Leadership** — Experience mobilizing stakeholders and families. – **Coalition Building** — Ability to bring stakeholders together. – **Public Health Knowledge** — Familiarity with state public health systems. – **Project Management** — Strong organizational and detail-oriented skills. – **Communication Skills** — Ability to tailor complex information for diverse audiences. – **Interpersonal Skills** — Professional, collaborative demeanor. – **Technical Skills** — Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Docs. – **Confidentiality** — Adherence to confidentiality and ethical conduct. – **Community Empathy** — Understanding and empathy for Duchenne/Becker families. ## Preferred Qualifications – Duchenne or neuromuscular clinical experience. – Experience with newborn screening programs. – Multi‑state project management experience. # Physical Requirements – Ability to travel locally and nationally. – Ability to navigate legislative buildings. – Ability to keyboard for 2+ hours/day. – Ability to communicate orally in a clear manner. – Physical stamina for meetings lasting 2+ hours. # Travel Moderate travel required (approx. 15% annually). # Work Authorization Valid authorization to work in the United States. # Compensation National Remote Salary Range: **$100,000 – $120,000 per year**. High end reserved for premier cost‑of‑living metropolitan markets. # Affirmative Action / EEO Statement PPMD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment. # Other Duties This job description is not designed to cover all duties or responsibilities. Duties may change at any time. Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President of Government Affairs
item.description: Vice President of Government Affairs Organization: AI Policy Network (AIPN) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/31/2026 The AI Policy Network (AIPN) is a bipartisan, independent 501(c)(4) advocacy organization dedicated to advancing secure AI development that serves America’s economic prosperity, technological leadership, and national security. We provide policymakers with technically grounded perspectives on emerging AI capabilities and risks, with particular focus on ensuring advanced AI systems remain reliable, controllable, and aligned with their intended purposes. ## I. Position Summary The AI Policy Network is dedicated to preparing America for the era of artificial superintelligence by advancing technically grounded, security‑oriented policy solutions. We work to ensure that as AI systems grow more capable, the United States has the governance frameworks, institutional capacity, and political will to keep these systems safe, secure, and aligned with democratic values. The Vice President of Government Affairs will be central to that effort, serving as a senior role focused on Senate engagement to translate AIPN’s policy vision into durable legislation. Working with the President of Government Affairs, this position co‑leads AIPN’s legislative strategy with primary responsibility for Senate‑focused execution, driving AIPN’s policy priorities into concrete legislative outcomes in the upper chamber. The ideal candidate brings deep, trusted relationships within the Senate, substantive policy expertise, and the political acumen to build bipartisan coalitions around AI safety and national security imperatives. ## II. Responsibilities ### A. Congressional Engagement (Senate Focus) – Build and maintain relationships with Senate leadership, committee chairs, ranking members, and key staff on relevant committees (Commerce/Science/Transportation, Armed Services, Intelligence, Judiciary, Homeland Security & Governmental Affairs, Foreign Relations, Appropriations). – Serve as AIPN’s primary point of contact for half of Senate offices on AI governance questions. – Organize briefings, roundtables, and meetings with Senate members on AI policy issues. – Provide real‑time intelligence on floor schedules, committee markups, and amendment opportunities. ### B. Strategic Advocacy – Develop and execute Senate‑specific legislative strategies around AGI preparedness, frontier AI safety, and national security. – Coordinate with the President of Government Affairs to ensure coherent bicameral strategy. – Identify and capitalize on legislative windows, including appropriations, NDAA, and authorization bills. – Build bipartisan coalitions across national security, civil liberties, and responsible industry stakeholders. ### C. Policy Development – Draft bill language, amendments, hearing questions, testimony, and talking points in collaboration with AIPN’s policy team. – Produce policy memos and briefing materials tailored to Senate audiences. – Craft messaging that frames AI safety through national security, economic resilience, and democratic governance lenses as appropriate. ## III. Qualifications ### A. Required – 8+ years in federal government affairs, lobbying, or senior Senate staff roles. – Deep, established relationships with Senate leadership offices and relevant committee staff. – Proven track record advancing complex technology, national security, or regulatory legislation through the Senate. – Strong understanding of Senate rules, procedures, and strategic opportunities. – Experience with technology, AI, national security, or related policy areas. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. – Bachelor’s degree. ### B. Preferred – Senior staff experience (LD, CoS, Staff Director) on Senate Commerce, Armed Services, Intelligence, Judiciary, or Homeland Security Committees. – Direct experience with appropriations process, NDAA, and other major legislative vehicles. – Track record building bipartisan coalitions on technology or national security issues. – Advanced degree in law, public policy, international relations, or related field. – Familiarity with AI safety concepts and the technical dimensions of AI governance. ## AI Policy Network (AIPN) Role Details **Location:** Washington, D.C. (Hybrid) **Compensation:** $260,000 – $340,000 **Reports to:** President **Benefits:** Technology budget, stipend for health insurance, and unlimited PTO. item.title: Senior Counsel, AI & Product Compliance
item.description: Senior Counsel, AI & Product Compliance Organization: OpenAI Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 09/01/2026 **About the Team** OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI’s mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. If you’re passionate about doing significant and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you. The team comprises professionals from diverse fields, including technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax law, regulatory, and litigation. **About the Role** As a member of our AI Product Counsel team, you will lead legal compliance initiatives for global online safety, platform, and AI regulations, including the UK Online Safety Act, EU Digital Services Act, EU AI Act, and similar emerging frameworks. You will partner closely with Product, Policy, Safety, Engineering, Security, Operations, and other teams to translate complex regulatory requirements into scalable, practical compliance solutions. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. **In this role, you will:** – **Serve as the primary legal expert** on the Online Safety Act, Digital Services Act, EU AI Act, and related global AI, platform, and online safety regulations. – **Lead the design and implementation** of scalable compliance programs, governance frameworks, controls, and operating processes. – **Partner with cross‑functional teams** to translate regulatory obligations into practical product and operational requirements. – **Monitor emerging regulations** and enforcement trends, anticipate their impact, and help shape OpenAI’s compliance strategy. – **Develop repeatable processes**, playbooks, escalation paths, and decision frameworks that enable teams to move quickly while managing risk responsibly. – **Support engagement with regulators**, external counsel, industry groups, and other stakeholders as needed. **You’ll thrive in this role if you:** – **Have 10+ years of experience** with a mix of in‑house or technology‑focused law firm roles. – **Have deep expertise** in the UK Online Safety Act, EU Digital Services Act, EU AI Act, and similar global regulatory frameworks. – **Have experience building scalable compliance programs** in a fast‑moving technology environment. – **Can translate complex legal requirements** into practical product, technical, and operational guidance. – **Build cross‑functional relationships** and communication styles that resonate with teams to balance risk‑taking with responsible development. – **Demonstrate strong ownership**, sound judgment, and comfort operating in ambiguous and rapidly evolving regulatory environments. – **Have a JD and license** or qualification to practice in CA. **About OpenAI** OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general‑purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US‑based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non‑public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non‑compliant, please submit a report. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. item.title: Digital Media Buyer
item.description: Digital Media Buyer Organization: Forbes Tate Partners (FTP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Position Description The Digital Media Buyer is a hands-on execution role on the Digital team, a department within the Public Affairs division at FTP. You will plan, build, traffic, and optimize paid media campaigns across programmatic, paid social, and paid search for the firm’s advocacy and public affairs clients. The work moves fast. Requests often land with same-day turnarounds, and you will own campaigns from setup through pacing, optimization, and reporting. You will operate across both managed-service and self-serve buying platforms, partner closely with Public Affairs account teams to turn client goals into media plans, and work alongside junior analysts on reporting and data pulls during active campaigns. This is a build moment for FTP. As the firm grows its digital practice, you will help shape how paid media is run, measured, and delivered, with real room to show what you can do. **Location:** 777 6th Street, NW, 10th Floor, Washington, D.C. **Reports to:** Executive Vice President, Head of Digital Intelligence & Strategy **Status:** Permanent Full-time, Exempt **Work Arrangement:** Hybrid (three days in person, two days remote) **Salary Grade/Range P19:** $110,503.00 to $130,000.00 — ## As the Digital Media Buyer, you will – Plan, build, and traffic paid media campaigns across a wide variety of paid media platforms and services on time and on budget. – Manage day-to-day campaign execution including pacing, bid and budget management, audience targeting, creative trafficking, and mid-flight optimization. – Operate fluently across managed-service and self-serve buying platforms, and bring a point of view on which channels and tactics fit each client’s goals. – Turn Public Affairs account team objectives into concrete media plans, flighting, and budget recommendations. – Build and manage campaign reporting, turning performance data into clear PowerPoint deliverables that account teams and clients can act on. – Hold fast turnaround times without sacrificing accuracy. Accelerated timelines, including same-day projects, are common in the public affairs and advocacy space. – Partner with and help develop junior analysts on reporting, data pulls, and campaign support, so coverage never depends on a single person. – Collaborate with Public Affairs account teams across sectors to align paid media with broader client strategy. – Manage media and data vendor relationships, and flag where the current stack helps or limits what FTP can deliver. – Track platform changes, ad policy shifts, and emerging formats including creator and influencer, connected TV, and retail media, and bring recommendations back to the team. – Help define how FTP runs paid media as the practice grows, including process, documentation, and operating standards. – Perform other duties as necessary to achieve departmental goals. — ## To be successful, you will need – Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or equivalent experience – 3–5 years of hands-on paid media buying experience, ideally including advocacy, public affairs, political, or issue campaigns – Hands-on experience with programmatic DSPs, paid social ad managers (Meta, LinkedIn, X, TikTok), and paid search platforms – Strong command of audience targeting, pixel and conversion tracking, UTM discipline, and campaign measurement – Comfort building campaign reports and translating performance data into clear PowerPoint deliverables – Fluency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel for budget pacing and reconciliation – Demonstrated ability to effectively and independently manage multiple projects – Effective interpersonal skills – Genuine interest in how paid media drives public policy and advocacy outcomes, not just clicks and impressions – Independent, strategic thinking, and creative problem-solving skills – Demonstrated capacity for teamwork, including the ability to effectively engage supervisors and subordinates under quick, tight deadlines within and across teams – Proven ability to operate with integrity and ethics, and maintain the highest standards of confidentiality – High level of detail and demonstrated work output with few/no errors – Sense of urgency; willingness and ability to meet and exceed established deadlines – Organizational agility — ## We prefer that you have – Experience working with managed-service media partners alongside self-serve programmatic platforms – Experience with connected TV, online video, or creator and influencer campaigns — ## How To Apply Interested parties should send their resume, cover letter, and one writing sample (three pages or less) to ** [email protected] ** with the subject line of the position and departments (i.e., Analyst, Public Affairs). Please save each attachment with your full name (first and last name) and document title. For example: *John Smith Resume*, *John Smith Cover Letter*, *John Smith Writing Sample*. No calls, emails, or faxes please. Qualified candidates will be contacted for an interview. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President, State Government Affairs – Remote in Maryland
item.description: Vice President, State Government Affairs – Remote in Maryland Organization: UnitedHealth Group Location: Annapolis, MD Date Posted: 09/01/2026 UnitedHealth Group UnitedHealth Group is a health care and well-being company dedicated to improving health outcomes for millions around the world. We are comprised of two distinct and complementary businesses, UnitedHealthcare and Optum, working to build a better health system for all. Here, your contributions matter as they will help transform health care for years to come. Make an impact with a team that shares your passion for helping others. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together. Vice President, State Government Affairs The Vice President, State Government Affairs will be part of the UHG Government Affairs organization, responsible for working with colleagues across Government Affairs and the Company to develop and implement strategies on the company’s declared state government advocacy, growth, relationship and reputational priorities, and overall business advancement initiatives with key state policymakers. This individual will be the primary liaison for Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C., between the Company and state and local leaders, including Administration, legislators and their staffs, as well as agency officials and external stakeholders. The candidate will report to the Regional Vice President, State Government Affairs. If you are located in the state of Maryland, you will have the flexibility to work remotely* as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week. Primary Responsibilities Driving and contributing to effective advocacy efforts to advance the company’s state advocacy and growth opportunities Facilitating business segment leaders’ relationships with key state and local elected officials Actively engaging in lobbying activities and advocacy efforts with the State Legislature and the Executive Branch Developing, fostering, and strengthening relationships with key legislative members, legislative staff, and key personnel in the Administration and relevant Executive Branch agencies to impact priority legislative and regulatory outcomes Establishing and maintaining engagement with influential third parties including Health Plan Associations, industry partners and business groups, external coalitions, advocacy groups, thought leaders, and other stakeholders in a position to influence state outcomes Anticipating, influencing, and monitoring legislative and regulatory initiatives that may impact the Company, as well as emerging state issues that impact the Company’s reputation and business, and developing and executing strategies to manage them Directing the company’s state advocacy consultants on key advocacy, growth, and relationship development priorities Proactively contributing to comprehensive strategic plans that leverage direct advocacy, policy and research, coalitions, third‑party engagement, and public opinion to advance the company’s objectives through compelling advocacy at the state level Developing and contributing to a wide range of timely written deliverables with the highest standards of professionalism Working closely with colleagues and in‑market business segments to drive visibility on key Company initiatives in the states Building and managing relationships with internal business leaders and partnering with them on state advocacy and growth initiatives Working closely with Company leaders to develop and execute the Company’s political engagement strategy Responding to inquiries on state issues from senior leaders and keeping senior leaders informed about priority ongoing developments and priority issues Leveraging new and existing relationships to identify and expand Company opportunities Required Qualifications 7+ years of experience working with the State Legislature, the Executive Branch, municipal government officials, government relations, public policy, advocacy, government affairs, or campaigns Local to Maryland with the option to work remotely Preferred Qualifications Political campaign experience Healthcare industry experience \*All employees working remotely will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group’s Telecommuter Policy. Compensation & Benefits Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase, and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). The salary for this role will range from $159,300 – $273,200 annually based on full‑time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable. Commitment to Equity & Inclusion At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone — of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location, and income — deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups, and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes — an enterprise priority reflected in our mission. UnitedHealth Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer under applicable law, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations. UnitedHealth Group is a drug‑free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate General Counsel, Regulatory
item.description: Associate General Counsel, Regulatory Organization: Compassus Location: Brentwood, TN Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## About Compassus Compassus provides a continuum of integrated home-based services, including home health, hospice, home infusion, palliative, and personal care. Over 10,500 teammates and more than 300 access points nationwide provide high-quality care and manage patients’ advanced illnesses in partnership with health systems and long-term care partners. The Compassus *Care for Who I Am* culture reflects its unique care delivery model, which focuses on each person as an individual as well as a patient, to improve their quality of life in a meaningful way. Learn more at compassus.com. ## About the Opportunity Under the direction of the Senior Vice President, Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, the Associate General Counsel, Regulatory provides strategic legal counsel and regulatory guidance across the organization. This role serves as the Company’s subject matter expert on healthcare regulatory compliance, licensing, accreditation, and reimbursement requirements, partnering closely with executive, operational, clinical, and compliance leaders to mitigate risk while supporting high-quality patient care and business operations. ## Key Responsibilities ### Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement – Responsible for, and engages all Company stakeholders in, the Company’s 6 Pillars of Success (Regulatory Compliance, Colleagues, Quality, Service, Growth, and Financial Responsibility). – Advises corporate, operational, and clinical leaders on regulatory compliance issues affecting patient care, reimbursement, and business operations. – Partners with Compliance, Clinical Operations, Revenue Cycle, and Government Affairs to proactively identify and mitigate regulatory risks. ### Legal Expertise and Healthcare Regulation – Serves as the primary legal advisor on federal and state healthcare laws and regulations impacting the organization. – Interprets and advises leadership on healthcare regulatory requirements, including: – Medicare Conditions of Participation – Anti-Kickback Statute – Stark Law – HIPAA/HITECH – Fraud, Waste and Abuse laws – State licensing regulations – Leads the Company’s licensing and Certificate of Need (CON) strategy and processes. – Assists Compliance with investigations and audits. – Assists with Government and Regulatory Affairs. ### Regulatory Risk Management and Monitoring – Supports regulatory due diligence for strategic initiatives and organizational changes. – Monitors changes in federal and state regulations and develops legal guidance for implementation. – Provides legal support during governmental audits, investigations, surveys, and regulatory inquiries. ### Policy Development and Educational Outreach – Develops policies, guidance documents, and educational materials related to healthcare regulations. – Reviews agreements and operational initiatives for regulatory compliance. ### Miscellaneous Duties – Performs other duties as assigned. ## About the Best Candidates – Demonstrates high integrity. – Strong project management and process improvement skills. – Strong leadership and people management skills. – Ability to solve problems multi-dimensionally. – Leads by example. – Deep understanding of key stakeholders of the Company, including patients, families, colleagues, governmental and regulatory agencies, payors, and shareholders. – Ability to mitigate risk pragmatically and exercise reasonable judgment. – Knowledge of statutes, rules, and regulations pertaining to businesses. – Proficient understanding of business sensitivities and confidentiality. ## Key Job Requirements and Preferences ### Education **Required:** Possess a Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school. ### Experience **Required:** At least 6–8 years of legal and professional healthcare experience. Relevant experience, and demonstrated success, in a law firm and/or corporate setting; additional public sector experience preferred. ### Licenses/Certifications **Required:** Requires admittance to a state bar. ## Work Environment and Physical Requirements ### Physical Demands – Prolonged periods of sitting, standing, and walking while working at a computer, conducting meetings, or performing administrative duties. – Occasional lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling of up to 20 pounds, including luggage, presentation materials, and office equipment. – Ability to navigate healthcare environments, including patient care settings, offices, and community locations, which may involve stair climbing, bending, reaching, and extended periods of walking. – Visual acuity sufficient for reviewing reports, analyzing data, and operating standard office technology. ### Communication – Effective communication skills in person, by telephone, and through virtual meeting platforms. ## What We Offer We offer a highly competitive compensation package with an attractive base salary, short- and long-term incentive programs, and competitive benefits. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where every team member feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences, believing that our differences make us stronger. Together, we’re shaping the future of healthcare with compassion, integrity, and opportunity for all. ## Want to Learn More About this Opportunity? Jordan Egan [email protected] #LI-JE1 ## Build a Rewarding Career with Compassus At Compassus, we care for our team members as much as we care for our patients and their families. Through our *Care for Who I Am* culture, we show compassion, respect, and appreciation for every individual. Embark on a career that cares for you while you care for others. ## Your Career Journey Matters We’re dedicated to helping you grow and succeed. Whether you’re pursuing leadership roles, specialized training, or exploring new career paths, we provide the tools and support you need to thrive. ## The Compassus Advantage • **Meaningful Work:** Make an impact every day by honoring the quality of life of our patients, supporting them and their families with compassion, and creating moments that truly matter. • **Career Development:** Access leadership pathways, mentorship, and personalized professional development. • **Innovation Meets Compassion:** Collaborate with a supportive team using the latest tools and technologies to deliver exceptional care. • **Enhanced Benefits:** Enjoy competitive pay, flexible time off, tuition reimbursement, and wellness programs designed for your well-being. • **Recognition and Support:** Be celebrated for your contributions through recognition programs that honor your dedication. • **A Culture of Belonging:** Thrive in a culture where you can be your authentic self, valued for your unique contributions and supported in a community that embraces diversity and inclusion. ## Ready to Join? At Compassus, your career is more than a job—it’s an opportunity to make a lasting impact. Take the next step and join a team that empowers you to grow, innovate, and thrive. We’ve learned about an employment or job scam where individuals are targeting recruitment processes to deceive job seekers into giving personal or financial information. To learn more, visit compassus.com/potential-employment-scam. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
