item.title: Influencer Marketing Manager
item.description: Influencer Marketing Manager Organization: M+C Saatchi Group Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## What are we looking for? We are looking for a highly motivated Influencer Marketing Manager to drive partnerships and content initiatives for our key clients. In this role, you will be the primary point of contact for new influencer inquiries, playing a key role in identifying opportunities, negotiating, and managing campaigns. The ideal candidate is naturally tuned into social media trends and pop culture, with a strong intuition for what resonates with different audiences. They will have a sharp eye for discovering emerging creators across platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, and understand how to leverage content for performance-driven strategies. This role requires creative thinking, relationship management, and hands-on execution. ## Responsibilities – Collaborate closely with internal teams to develop and execute tailored campaign strategies that align with our clients’ objectives – Manage and grow relationships with external partners, including but not limited to influencers, UGC agencies, talent networks, and independent creators – Lead the full influencer campaign process, from talent discovery and outreach to negotiation, scheduling, and performance tracking – Develop clear and compelling briefs to guide partners in creating content and executing campaigns effectively – Ensure timely content delivery, providing feedback to creators and partners as needed to adhere to the brand briefs – Stay informed on industry trends and platform updates to help inform future campaigns – Support marketing efforts by contributing to sales materials, case studies, industry reports, and content for owned channels – Identify opportunities to refine workflows and improve efficiency across influencer, UGC, and affiliate programs – Educate internal teams on best practices and equip them with the knowledge to confidently communicate the value of influencers to clients, helping drive adoption and business growth ## Qualifications – 3+ years of experience managing end-to-end influencer campaigns, preferably with a focus on performance KPIs. Experience with eCommerce, alcohol, or DTC brands is a plus – Hands-on experience with influencer discovery & management platforms (e.g., CreatorIQ, Klear, or similar) – Experience in crafting briefs that align with brand goals and provide clear direction for content execution – Excellent written and verbal communication skills – Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously while coordinating with influencers, talent agencies, and other partners at various stages – High attention to detail and problem-solving skills – Self-starter and ability to work independently ## Additional Information Salary Band: $80,000–$95,000 Competitive benefits package, including 20 vacation days and 401k match Summer Fridays: we aim to stop working at 3:00pm on Fridays from Memorial Day to Labor Day Holiday Break: 11 annual bank holidays, plus Christmas to New Year’s Eve Flexible working and WFH opportunities: Two days per week in the NY office required All candidates must have the ability to work in the US; we are unable to sponsor any work visas for this role ## About M+C Saatchi Performance M+C Saatchi Performance, as part of the M+C Saatchi Group, has pledged its commitment to create a company that values difference, with an inclusive culture. As part of this, M+C Saatchi Group continues to be an Equal Opportunity Employer which does not and shall not discriminate, celebrates diversity, and bases all hiring and promotion decisions solely on merit, without regard for any personal characteristics. If you require any reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment and selection process, please make us aware as part of your application. All employee information is kept confidential according to General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). #LI-CC1 #PERF Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Digital Advocacy Manager
item.description: Digital Advocacy Manager Organization: National Automobile Dealers Association (NADA) Location: Tysons Corner, VA Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Salary Range $90,000.00 to $120,000.00 Annually Are you a strategic, creative digital storyteller who knows how to turn complex public policy into content that grabs attention and moves the conversation? Do you know how to spot the story before everyone else does and recognize when, where, and how an organization should show up to make an impact? Are you constantly tracking what’s happening, finding the unexpected angle, and turning timely moments into digital content people actually stop for? If so, the National Automobile Dealers Association (NADA) is looking for a dynamic Digital Advocacy Manager to shape, sharpen, and elevate NADA’s digital advocacy presence. This is a full‑time position offering a positive work culture, competitive salary, and comprehensive benefits. The role requires occasional travel (up to 10%), including weekday and weekend travel, industry trade shows, and onsite event presence. ## Key Responsibilities – Lead NADA’s digital advocacy strategy across social media and emerging platforms to strengthen visibility, relevance, and authority. – Monitor policy and political developments and identify timely opportunities for NADA to shape conversations and advance advocacy priorities. – Advise Public Affairs strategically on what to communicate, where, when, and how to tell compelling policy stories. – Translate complex policy issues into clear, credible, accessible, and engaging digital content. – Create and manage multimedia content including social posts, videos, graphics, infographics, stories, reels, and other formats. – Develop and expand advocacy campaigns using creative storytelling, new platforms, partnerships, trends, and fresh ideas to drive awareness and engagement. – Maintain an active digital presence year‑round, including real‑time coverage of major advocacy moments and content during slower news cycles. – Manage digital operations and performance, including content calendars, approvals, brand consistency, SOPs, workflows, metrics, testing, and continuous optimization. – Integrate digital advocacy across NADA, coordinating with internal teams and broader communications initiatives to maximize reach, engagement, and policy impact. ## Required Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, political science, public policy, marketing, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience required. – Minimum 5 years of experience in public policy, advocacy, public affairs, social media strategy, and/or digital content creation required. Association, Capitol Hill, government affairs, or related experience strongly preferred. – Demonstrated ability to translate complex public policy, legislative, regulatory, or political issues into compelling and accessible content for digital audiences. – Strong understanding of social media platforms, digital trends, audience engagement, and content strategy, with demonstrated experience creating and executing social media campaigns. – Strong writing, editing, and communication skills, with the ability to adapt messages for different audiences and platforms while maintaining a consistent brand voice. – Experience creating and editing multimedia content, including short‑form video, graphics, photography, and infographics. – Strategic, proactive, and forward‑thinking approach, with the confidence to bring new ideas, identify opportunities, and recommend where and how NADA should engage digitally. – Ability to build strong cross‑functional relationships and collaborate across departments to achieve shared goals. To be considered for this position, please submit your resume and a cover letter detailing the unique strengths and expertise you would bring to the NADA team here . NADA is fundamentally committed to the diversity of our staff. We believe diversity is excellence expressing itself through every person’s perspective and lived experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, disability, gender identity or expression, marital status, national or ethnic origin, political affiliation, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy and lactation), sexual orientation, military status, veteran status, and family medical or genetic information or any other protected class under federal, state, or local law. item.title: Director of Government Relations- Midwest Region
item.description: Director of Government Relations- Midwest Region Organization: IAPMO Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Description The IAPMO Group is hiring a Director of Government Relations to join our Government Relations team! This position focuses on state and local government affairs throughout the Midwest region and other assigned jurisdictions. We’re looking for an experienced government relations professional who can build strong relationships with policymakers and industry stakeholders, navigate complex legislative and regulatory environments, and help advance policies that support IAPMO’s mission and organizational priorities. ## What You’ll Do – Develop and execute state and local government relations and public policy strategies across assigned jurisdictions. – Represent IAPMO and build relationships with policymakers, regulators, government officials, industry organizations, and key stakeholders. – Monitor legislative, regulatory, and political developments and identify emerging issues and opportunities impacting IAPMO. – Lead advocacy efforts, including testimony, public comments, position statements, and legislative and regulatory initiatives. – Partner across IAPMO to support code adoption, public policy, and key organizational priorities. – Promote IAPMO’s expertise in codes and standards, testing and certification, water efficiency, sustainability, public health, and workforce development. – Advance the adoption and implementation of IAPMO codes and standards and support related state and local public policy priorities. – Coordinate strategic engagement with policymakers and support Government Relations leadership on key initiatives. ## What We’re Looking For – Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government Affairs, Communications, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. – 5+ years of experience in government relations, public policy, legislative affairs, political affairs, or related field. – Strong knowledge of state and local legislative and regulatory processes. – Proven ability to build influential relationships and effectively advocate with government, industry, and other key stakeholders. – Excellent communication, public speaking, relationship‑building, and strategic thinking skills. – Ability to manage multiple priorities, exercise sound judgment, and work effectively across teams. – Ability to travel up to 20% as needed. ## Why IAPMO? At IAPMO, you’ll have the opportunity to work at the intersection of public policy, public health, sustainability, codes and standards, and the built environment. You’ll help shape policies, strengthen relationships with government and industry leaders, and advance initiatives that have a meaningful impact on communities. ## Our Benefits Include – 14 paid holidays – 10 vacation days annually from Day 1, with rollover – 15 sick days annually, with rollover – 100% employer‑paid health, dental, life, and AD&D coverage for you and your dependents – 5% 401(k) match + 8% profit sharing – Childcare subsidies up to 60% through KinderCare – Wellness and mental health support through IAPMO Cares – Affordable gym memberships through Fitness Your Way – Annual employee appreciation events – Smart casual dress code – And so much more! If you’re an experienced government affairs professional who enjoys building relationships, navigating complex policy environments, and turning strategy into action, we’d love to hear from you. Join The IAPMO Group and help advance our mission through effective advocacy, collaboration, and public policy leadership. ## Salary $135,000–$160,000 Compensation within the posted range will vary based on geographic location, education, experience, and relevant qualifications. item.title: Director of Communications
item.description: Director of Communications Organization: National Association of Corporate Directors (NACD) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## This is a “hybrid” role The selected candidate will work in NACD’s Arlington, VA office (Tuesdays–Thursdays) on a weekly basis. ## SUMMARY NACD is the leading membership organization for corporate directors in the United States. The Director, Communications owns NACD’s enterprise brand strategy and communications platform, strengthening NACD’s market position, protecting organizational reputation, and increasing member and stakeholder trust. This role leads external communications (earned media, thought leadership, executive visibility, and social storytelling) and internal communications (employee and chapter communications, leadership messaging, and channel governance). As a senior leader within Marketing, the Director operates as an enterprise partner, aligning brand, growth marketing, membership, certification, events, and advisory priorities into one coherent narrative and ensuring disciplined execution with strong fiscal stewardship. ## ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES – Enterprise brand strategy and positioning: define and evolve NACD’s brand narrative, positioning, messaging architecture, and brand guardrails across key audiences and segments. – Enterprise initiative campaigns: lead integrated campaigns for signature programs and priorities (e.g., Blue Ribbon Commission, Directorship 100), ensuring clear narrative, cross‑channel execution, and consistent messaging. – Strategic communications and PR: set annual communications strategy tied to enterprise priorities; lead proactive and reactive media strategy; manage press releases, statements, and communications planning. – Reputation and risk management: serve as a trusted counselor to executive leadership on sensitive issues; build decision frameworks and rapid response protocols; coordinate cross‑functional crisis communications as needed. – Executive visibility and leadership communications: drive a disciplined, year‑round executive visibility program across LinkedIn, speaking opportunities, bylines, interviews, and internal messaging; ensure leadership voice is aligned to strategy. – Thought leadership and content platform: oversee the newsroom/editorial approach, governance content campaigns, and strategic storytelling; ensure content supports both human audiences and AI‑driven discovery. – Internal communications: own internal communications strategy and operating cadence; improve channel discipline and message ROI; support change management for enterprise initiatives; partner with HR/Ops on employee engagement and leadership messaging. – Creative and agency leadership: lead internal and external creative/PR resources; set clear briefs, service levels, and performance expectations; ensure creative output is on‑brand, high‑quality, and efficient. – Measurement and insights: define success metrics for brand, communications, and internal comms; establish reporting cadence that ties visibility and engagement to enterprise outcomes. – Fiscal and operational stewardship: own budgets, forecasting, vendor contracts, and spend accountability; make tradeoffs and resourcing recommendations consistent with a lean organization. – People leadership: lead and develop a high‑performing team; set clear expectations and feedback; build capability across writing, strategy, stakeholder management, and execution discipline. – Other duties as assigned. ## EDUCATION/QUALIFICATIONS – Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field. – 10+ years of progressive experience in communications, including team management and cross‑functional influence. – Demonstrated success building and executing brand and communications strategies that drive measurable visibility, engagement, and trust. – Deep expertise in media relations, executive communications, thought leadership, and digital‑first storytelling (including social platforms). – Experience leading internal communications strategy, including channel governance and change communications. – Strong business acumen, including budget ownership, vendor management, and resource prioritization. – Exceptional writing and editorial judgment; ability to translate complex strategy into clear, compelling messaging for diverse audiences. – Proven ability to lead in a matrixed environment with professionalism, calm judgment, and strong stakeholder management. ## PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS – Experience in membership associations, education, or professional services organizations. – Familiarity with corporate governance, boardroom audiences, or executive education markets. This position description summarizes the main duties of the job. It neither prescribes nor restricts the exact tasks that may be required to carry out these duties. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time. The salary/hourly range for this position is $170,000–$185,000 plus bonus potential. Compensation is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, certifications, etc. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Ex. Director, Texas Energy Buyers Alliance
item.description: Ex. Director, Texas Energy Buyers Alliance Organization: Corporate Energy Buyers Association (CEBA) Location: Remote (TX) Date Posted: 09/01/2026 **Position Title:** Executive Director, Texas Energy Buyers Alliance (TEBA) **Supervisor:** Senior Director of Policy, Organized Markets **Department:** Policy **FLSA:** Exempt **Location:** Remote, Texas **Compensation Range:** $200,000–$225,000 (Excluding Bonus and Benefits) — The Corporate Energy Buyers Association is a business association with a mission to activate a community of energy customers and partners to advance low‑cost, reliable, carbon‑emissions‑free global energy systems. ### Our Guiding Values and Tenets We are grounded in respect for people and the planet, integrity in how we conduct ourselves, service to our mission, stakeholders, and colleagues, and excellence in all of our programs and work. At CEBA, we strive to foster a culture that is mission‑driven and strategy‑grounded, built on a spirit of partnership both within and beyond our organization, and energized by innovation and entrepreneurship through healthy, respectful dialogue. ### About TEBA and CEBA The Texas Energy Buyers Alliance (TEBA) is a state‑based chapter of the Corporate Energy Buyers Association (CEBA), the leading national organization representing large energy customers seeking affordable, reliable, and clean electricity. CEBA’s members include the largest energy buyers in the world. CEBA works with corporations and institutions committed to deploying clean energy at scale and strengthening the electricity system to support economic growth, reliability, and decarbonization. TEBA serves as the unified voice of large electricity customers in Texas, advancing practical, customer‑focused solutions on transmission, market design, resource adequacy, and grid modernization on behalf of both corporate members as well as affiliate local businesses. TEBA works closely with CEBA’s national policy, communications, and membership teams to ensure state advocacy is aligned with broader regional and federal priorities. ### Position Overview The Executive Director of TEBA provides strategic leadership and day‑to‑day management of CEBA’s Texas advocacy and engagement. This role is responsible for setting and executing TEBA’s state‑level policy agenda, representing large energy buyers before policymakers and stakeholders, and building durable coalitions to advance solutions that improve affordability, reliability, and grid resilience in Texas. The Executive Director is a highly external‑facing role, serving as TEBA’s chief spokesperson and lead strategist. The position works in partnership with senior CEBA leadership, policy, communications, and membership teams, and manages day‑to‑day execution as well as TEBA’s consultants and partners supporting TEBA’s work. ### Core Responsibilities #### Strategic Leadership & Management – Provide overall leadership for TEBA, including setting strategic priorities, managing consultants, overseeing timelines and deliverables, and driving progress against annual goals. – Work closely with CEBA senior leadership on strategy, governance, and alignment with CEBA’s national and regional objectives. – Oversee day‑to‑day operations, workflows, and performance across all TEBA activities. – Drive consensus among TEBA members on policy priorities and advocacy positions. #### Policy & Advocacy – Develop and execute TEBA’s Texas energy policy agenda, spanning legislative, regulatory, and administrative venues (e.g., Texas Legislature, Public Utility Commission of Texas, ERCOT, Governor’s and Lieutenant Governor’s offices, and state agencies). – Monitor and analyze state legislation, rulemakings, ERCOT processes, and market developments; translate technical issues into clear advocacy strategies and materials. – Serve as TEBA’s chief representative before lawmakers, regulators, agencies, and stakeholder forums. – Coordinate, draft, and provide testimony, regulatory comments, briefings, and educational materials for policymakers and staff. – Ensure state‑level advocacy is coordinated with CEBA’s broader policy agenda and regional transmission efforts. #### Communications & Organizational Representation – Oversee TEBA’s strategic communications, including messaging, media engagement, digital content, and coordination with CEBA’s communications team. – Ensure policy positions are communicated clearly and effectively to members, funders, policymakers, and the public. – Represent TEBA and CEBA at conferences, public events, and stakeholder convenings. #### Coalition Building & Stakeholder Engagement – Build and maintain strong relationships with policymakers, regulators, utilities, system operators, consumer advocates, business groups, NGOs, and national partners. – Participate in and help lead state and regional coalitions advancing shared energy policy goals. – Convene and support TEBA member engagement through meetings, briefings, working groups, and advocacy initiatives. #### Fundraising & Membership – Lead fundraising and revenue development efforts, including foundation grants, sponsorships, and membership support. – Develop and manage TEBA’s annual budget in partnership with senior CEBA staff. – Support grant reporting and funder communications related to Texas policy and advocacy work. Performs other related duties as assigned. — ### Required Qualifications – 17+ years of experience in relevant industry or; – 12+ years of experience with a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant industry or; – 8+ years of experience with a Master’s degree in a relevant industry – Deep experience in energy policy, electricity markets, transmission, and/or utility regulation, with Texas experience required. ERCOT and PUCT regulatory experience a plus. – Demonstrated success leading policy advocacy efforts and engaging with legislatures, public utility commissions, grid operators, and executive offices. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; comfortable serving as a public spokesperson. – Familiarity with wholesale electricity markets (ERCOT experience strongly preferred; SPP, MISO, or other RTO experience a bonus). – Estimated 10% travel within Texas and occasional regional or national travel is required. ### Preferred Qualifications – Strong coalition‑building and stakeholder management skills, including experience working with corporate energy customers. – Experience managing consultants, budgets, and complex multi‑stakeholder initiatives. – Experience managing a membership‑based organization. – Experience developing and delivering public testimony. – Experience fundraising and managing grant applications. ### Supervisory Responsibilities This role will supervise a team of part‑time consultants supporting lobbying, regulatory, and communications. ### To Apply To be considered for this opportunity, please submit a cover letter and resume. — ### Compensation and Benefits The expected base salary for this role ranges from $200,000 to $225,000, depending on experience and qualifications. All CEBA employees are eligible to participate in the annual bonus incentive plan, which is based on both organizational and individual performance, up to 20% for this role. CEBA provides a competitive benefits package that includes highly subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance plans. In addition, CEBA offers employer‑paid life and disability coverage (both short‑ and long‑term), monthly cell phone stipends, optional flexible spending and savings accounts, a comprehensive Employee Assistance Program, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and an attractive 401(k) match of up to 5%, subject to IRS limitations. Along with 11 federal holidays, paid time off during the period between Christmas and New Year’s, and Sick & Safe leave, employees also enjoy unlimited PTO. — ### At CEBA You Belong CEBA knows that inclusiveness not only makes our organization stronger but also is foundational to our mission success because innovative solutions come from great minds who do not think alike. Our commitment to inclusiveness is embodied in company policy and the way we do business at CEBA and is an important principle of sound business management. All CEBA staff shall be committed to accepting and encouraging different perspectives. Creative solutions to tough problems are fostered by respectful challenges of one another’s thoughts and assumptions. CEBA provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, gender expression, results of genetic testing, caregiver status, and past, present, or prospective service in the military, in addition to any other protected categories required by state, federal, or local regulations. Equal employment opportunities apply to all terms and conditions of employment, including hiring, placement, discipline, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, and training. All of your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Manager, Policy – Utility Partnerships & Innovation Organization: Corporate Energy Buyers Association (CEBA) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ________________________________________________________________________________ **Position Title:** Manager, Policy – Utility Partnerships & Innovation **Supervisor:** Vice President, Policy – Utility Partnerships & Innovation **Department:** Policy **FLSA:** Exempt **Location:** Remote **Salary range:** $105,000–$120,000 (Not Including Bonus and Benefits) _____________________________________________________________________________________ **Our Guiding Values and Tenets** The Corporate Energy Buyers Association is a business association with a mission to activate a community of energy customers and partners to advance low-cost, reliable, carbon emissions free global energy systems. We are grounded in respect for people and the planet, integrity in how we conduct ourselves, service to our mission, stakeholders, and colleagues, and excellence in all of our programs and work. At CEBA, we strive to foster a culture that is mission-driven and strategy-grounded, built on a spirit of partnership both within and beyond our organization, and energized by innovation and entrepreneurship through healthy, respectful dialogue. **Position Overview** The Manager, Policy – Utility Partnerships & Innovation will play a critical role in executing CEBA’s strategic policy initiatives, with a focus on CEBA’s “activate utilities” initiative, which is a national initiative to accelerate utilities’ clean customer programs by putting growing customer electricity demand at the center of utility procurement and customer programs. This role will help shape the future of CEBA’s partnerships with utilities to unlock new areas of collaboration and partnership to serve growing large loads. It includes overseeing high-impact projects and leading engagement with stakeholders. The role requires strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, as well as the ability to collaborate across teams and engage with external partners. The Manager will work closely with the Vice President, Regional Directors, Communications, and other members of the Policy Team to drive policy, market, or programmatic efforts that align with CEBA’s mission. They will manage projects from inception to execution, coordinate cross-functional initiatives, and support CEBA’s advocacy and stakeholder engagement strategies. **Core Responsibilities:** **Strategic Execution & Thought Leadership** Develop and implement key initiatives that align with CEBA’s mission, vision, and core tenets. Contribute to strategic planning by identifying opportunities for program development and market impact. Oversee the execution of assigned programmatic priorities, ensuring high-quality deliverables and measurable outcomes. **Policy & Market Engagement** Advocate for CEBA’s positions with regulatory agencies, policymakers, and industry stakeholders. Conduct research and analysis to inform CEBA’s positions and strategies on expanding access to clean energy, regional transmission policy, and utility decarbonization pathways. Develop thought leadership materials, including white papers, reports, and policy briefs. Manage CEBA’s engagement in public comment processes, coalition-building efforts, and stakeholder convenings. **Project & Team Management** Lead and manage projects, ensuring effective planning, budgeting, and execution. Guide cross-functional collaboration with other CEBA teams to support organizational objectives. Supervise consultants, technical experts, and other external partners to achieve program goals. Provide mentorship and support to junior staff and peers, fostering a collaborative team environment. **Stakeholder Engagement & Communication** Develop and grow relationships with key external partners, including government agencies, policymakers, public utility commissions, businesses, NGOs, and utilities. Lead and facilitate working groups, meetings, and stakeholder convenings to drive CEBA’s policy initiatives. Engage and/or manage CEBA’s engagement in regulatory dockets for utility planning and new and expanding clean energy customer tariffs. Communicate CEBA’s strategic objectives effectively to diverse audiences through presentations, reports, and direct engagement. Represent CEBA at industry conferences and events, advocating for clean energy customer-driven solutions. Performs other related duties as assigned. **Required Qualifications:** 7+ years of experience in a relevant industry: e.g., clean energy, policy, corporate sustainability, or utilities, or Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of experience in a relevant field, or Master’s degree and 3+ years of experience in a relevant field. Minimum 2 years’ experience employed by, or engaged directly with, a vertically integrated utility in a regulatory, advocacy, or partnership capacity. Minimum 1 year experience in policy analysis, market development, regulatory process engagement, or program implementation. Minimum 1 year experience working with multi-stakeholder groups, coalitions, or industry initiatives. Strong ability to analyze complex issues, generate innovative solutions, and communicate recommendations effectively. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical audiences. **Preferred Qualifications:** Experience with design of clean energy customer programs and ratemaking. Familiarity with regulatory processes, transmission policy, and/or utility business and planning processes. Knowledge of corporate, industrial, and institutional clean energy procurement strategies. **Supervisory Responsibilities:** None **To Apply:** To be considered for this opportunity, please provide a resume and cover letter. **Compensation and Benefits:** The expected base salary for this role ranges from $105,000 to $120,000, depending on experience and qualifications. All CEBA employees are eligible to participate in the annual bonus incentive plan, which is based on both organizational and individual performance, up to 10% for this role. Along with 11 federal holidays, paid time off during the period between Christmas and New Year’s, and Sick & Safe leave, employees also enjoy unlimited PTO. **At CEBA You Belong:** CEBA knows that inclusiveness not only makes our organization stronger but also is foundational to our mission success because innovative solutions come from great minds who do not think alike. item.title: Specialist, Public Policy
item.description: Specialist, Public Policy Organization: Greater Houston Partnership Location: Houston, TX Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Description The **Greater Houston Partnership** works to make Houston one of the best places to live, work, and build a business. As the economic development organization for the region, the Partnership champions growth across 12 counties by bringing together business and civic‑minded leaders dedicated to the area’s long‑term success. Representing more than 900 member organizations and approximately one‑fifth of the region’s workforce, the Partnership is the place companies come together to make an impact. When you join the Partnership, you gain the opportunity to work with an organization helping guide the future of the Houston region. Our team of professionals work across multiple disciplines, including Economic Development (Regional and International), Executive, Finance & Accounting, Marketing & Communications, Member Engagement, Public Policy, Regional Workforce Development, Research, Resources, and the Center for Houston’s Future. We look forward to telling you more about the organization and helping determine if a career with the Partnership is right for you. — ## Today, We Are Looking For The **Specialist, Public Policy** will coordinate the Partnership’s local, state, and federal advocacy efforts. The role will manage legislative bill and issue tracking, analyze policy trends and polling data, and provide timely insights to inform advocacy strategies. Working closely with subject matter advocates and the Senior Director of Policy Engagement, the Specialist will align policy priorities with programs, committees, events, communications, and member engagement opportunities. The role will also support policy advisory committees and build relationships with members, policymakers, coalitions, and community partners to advance issues that strengthen the Houston region’s growth and competitiveness. The ideal candidate is analytical, politically astute, relationship‑oriented, and highly organized, with a strong understanding of legislative processes and the ability to move effectively between policy analysis, advocacy, and member engagement. — ## Primary Duties and Responsibilities The following responsibilities are essential to job performance: – **Relationship Building** — Build and maintain strong relationships with members, policymakers, elected officials, government staff, business organizations, nonprofit partners, and other stakeholders to advance the Partnership’s policy priorities. – **Policy Coordination** — Work closely with Public Policy subject matter advocates to support their portfolios, identify cross‑cutting issues, and align advocacy activities across the division. – **Advocacy Support** — Support advocacy efforts at the local, state, and federal levels. – **Legislative Tracking** — Lead legislative session bill tracking by monitoring, analyzing, and reporting on proposed legislation, amendments, hearings, votes, and other developments relevant to the Partnership’s priorities. – **Issue Tracking** — Manage a comprehensive issue‑tracking process across policy portfolios, ensuring leadership and advocates have timely information on emerging issues, risks, opportunities, and required actions. – **Data Analysis** — Conduct frequent data analysis using legislative activity, economic indicators, member feedback, polling data, and other sources to identify trends, inform advocacy strategies, and measure progress. – **Reporting & Dashboards** — Develop dashboards, reports, briefing materials, and tools that clearly communicate advocacy activity, developments, and policy outcomes to the Chief Policy Officer. – **Program Alignment** — Manage alignment between policy priorities and programs, events, committees, and member engagement activities. – **Stakeholder Leverage** — Leverage the Partnership’s Board, members, relationships, and brand to advance policy priorities and deliver tangible outcomes. – **Strategic Guidance** — Provide guidance across divisions on policy development, advocacy strategies, committee priorities, programs, and related initiatives. – **Coalition Work** — Design and execute advocacy strategies and participate in coalitions that advance policy objectives. – **Advocacy Strategy** — Develop and implement strategies focused on issues that expand economic growth and opportunity throughout the Houston region. – **Monitoring Dynamics** — Monitor political, legislative, regulatory, and stakeholder dynamics and adapt strategies as circumstances evolve. – **Committee Alignment** — Align advocacy objectives with Public Policy Advisory Committees and the strategic goals of Houston Next. – **Executive Advising** — Advise the Chief Policy Officer on developments and advocacy matters important to leadership, members, and the region. – **Major Initiatives** — Assist with federal fly‑ins, state advocacy days, legislative visits, fact‑finding missions, coalition activities, communications campaigns, and special projects. – **Representation** — Attend and participate in major events, coalition engagements, hearings, panel discussions, and other opportunities to represent the Partnership. – Other duties as assigned. — ## Requirements ### Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities – Strong written and interpersonal communication skills (comfortable developing presentations and interacting with external entities). – Ability to work well in fast‑paced, deadline‑oriented environments with limited supervision. – Understanding of the unique economic and social challenges facing the Houston region. – Ability to translate major goals into functional objectives. – Comprehensive knowledge of departmental functions. ### Education Requirements Bachelor’s degree preferred. ### Required Experience 2–3 years’ experience in government, public policy, political campaigns, legislative advocacy, and/or government affairs is required. — ## Physical Requirements – Good vision and hearing acuity (with adaptive aids if necessary). – Manual dexterity and skillful use of a computer keyboard. – Physical exertion may include bending, pushing, standing, and walking. Must be able to move or lift approximately 25 pounds on occasion. — ## Mental and Aptitude Requirements Job requires the ability to hear, see, and talk; analytical, conceptual, problem‑solving, planning, and decision‑making skills. — ## Safety Requirements Adhere to office safety policies and procedures. — The Greater Houston Partnership is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants and employees are treated without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other reason prohibited by law. item.description: Manager, Public Policy Organization: Greater Houston Partnership Location: Houston, TX Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Description ## Why the Partnership When you join the Greater Houston Partnership, you get the opportunity to work with an organization helping guide the future of the Houston region. Our team of professionals work across multiple disciplines, including Economic Development (Regional and International), Executive, Finance & Accounting, Marketing & Communications, Member Engagement, Public Policy, Regional Workforce Development, Research, Resources, and the Center for Houston’s Future. The Greater Houston Partnership works to make Houston one of the best places to live, work, and build a business. As the economic development organization for the region, the Partnership champions growth across 12 counties by bringing together business and civic‑minded leaders dedicated to the area’s long‑term success. Representing more than 900 member organizations and approximately one‑fifth of the region’s workforce, the Partnership is the place companies come together to make an impact. We look forward to telling you more about the organization and helping determine if a career with the Partnership is right for you. ## Today, We Are Looking For The Manager, Public Policy supports the development, coordination, and execution of the Greater Houston Partnership’s public policy communications and advocacy materials. This role translates complex policy issues into clear, accurate, and audience‑appropriate content that advances the Partnership’s advocacy priorities and keeps members, elected officials, government staff, coalition partners, and other stakeholders informed and engaged. The Manager will oversee recurring policy communications, develop advocacy materials and other deliverables, and coordinate closely with the Partnership’s Marketing and Communications team to ensure consistency in messaging, brand, and timing. This position will also help manage communications across coalitions and external partnerships, creating dependable processes that support timely and consistent engagement. The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and thoughtful collaborator who is intellectually curious, interested in a broad range of public policy issues, and familiar with federal, state, and local legislative and governmental processes. This individual should be comfortable using emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to strengthen content development, improve efficiency, and support the division’s communications workflow. ## Primary Duties and Responsibilities The following responsibilities are essential to job performance. ### Policy Communications • Develop, edit, and distribute recurring Public Policy Division communications, including: – Weekly legislative session updates – Quarterly Women in Government Relations newsletter – Quarterly Chamber of Commerce & Coalition newsletter – Policy committee newsletters and updates – Communications to elected officials and government staff • Translate complex policy issues, legislative developments, and advocacy priorities into clear and compelling content for a range of internal and external audiences. • Maintain an editorial calendar for policy communications and coordinate deadlines, reviews, approvals, and distribution. • Ensure policy communications are timely, accurate, consistent, and aligned with the Partnership’s positions and organizational voice. • Monitor legislative and policy activity to identify relevant developments, content opportunities, and stakeholder communication needs. ### Advocacy Content and Deliverables • Draft and edit one‑pagers, policy summaries, advocacy letters, position statements, talking points, presentations, briefing materials, meeting summaries, and other deliverables as needed. • Work with policy subject‑matter experts to develop content that accurately communicates the Partnership’s positions and desired policy outcomes. • Tailor content and messaging for members, policymakers, government staff, coalition partners, business leaders, and the broader community. • Maintain organized files and an accessible library of approved policy messaging, communications, and advocacy materials. ### Collaboration and Coordination • Serve as the Public Policy Division’s primary liaison to the Marketing and Communications team for policy‑related content, publications, and campaigns. • Coordinate content development, review, production, and distribution across the Public Policy and Marketing & Communications teams. • Collaborate with policy colleagues to understand their issue portfolios, communication needs, and upcoming priorities. • Provide communications and content‑development assistance to designated team members, including the Policy Engagement Senior Director and Coordinator. • Help ensure alignment between policy communications, member engagement activities, advocacy campaigns, and broader organizational messaging. ### Coalition Communications • Coordinate communications for coalitions and partner organizations supported by the Public Policy Division. • Develop consistent processes and schedules for coalition updates, meeting communications, advocacy materials, and stakeholder outreach. • Draft and distribute coalition communications in coordination with internal policy leads and external partners. • Maintain appropriate contact lists, distribution groups, templates, and records of coalition communications. • Help ensure coalition members receive timely, consistent, and actionable information. ### Artificial Intelligence and Content Innovation • Use approved artificial intelligence tools to support first drafts, content outlines, research synthesis, message adaptation, and other appropriate communications tasks. • Help develop repeatable AI‑assisted workflows or agents that improve the speed and consistency of recurring policy communications. • Apply professional judgment and human oversight to all AI‑assisted work, verifying facts, legislative information, organizational positions, tone, and audience appropriateness before content is distributed. • Protect confidential, sensitive, and proprietary information when using AI or other technology platforms. • Identify opportunities to improve the division’s communications processes through new tools, templates, automation, and workflow enhancements. • Stay informed about emerging communications technologies and recommend responsible applications that support the division’s work. ### Other Duties as Assigned ## Requirements ### Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities • Strong interest in public policy, government affairs, advocacy, or legislative communications. • Strong written communications skills; ability to handle content development, write and edit for various audiences, both internally and externally. • Ability to tailor content, tone, and level of detail for different audiences and communication channels. • Strong interpersonal communication skills; ability to work collaboratively and build relationships. Must be comfortable presenting to and/or interacting with colleagues and external partners. • Demonstrated ability to work well in a fast‑paced, deadline‑oriented environment with limited supervision. • Strong planning and organizational skills; detail‑oriented; ability to handle multiple projects at one time. ### Education Requirements Bachelor’s degree preferred. ### Required Experience 2–3 years’ experience in government, public policy, political campaigns, legislative advocacy, and/or government affairs is required. ### Physical Requirements • Good vision and hearing acuity (with adaptive aids if necessary). • Manual dexterity and skillful use of computer keyboard. • Physical exertion includes bending, pushing, standing, and walking. Must be able to move or lift approximately 25 pounds on occasion. ### Mental and Aptitude Requirements Job requires the ability to hear, see, and talk; analytical, conceptual, problem‑solving, planning, and decision‑making skills. ### Safety Requirements Adhere to office safety policies and procedures. The Greater Houston Partnership is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants and employees are treated without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other reason prohibited by law. ## Apply Earn a certificate with the Council! item.description: Vice President for Policy and Chief Content Officer Organization: U.S. - U.A.E. Business Council Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Position Overview The U.S.-U.A.E. Business Council is seeking a senior policy expert to strengthen the Council’s analysis and written content. This individual will provide thought leadership and oversee reports, policy analysis, event briefs, and other substantive materials. They will report directly to the Council’s President, collaborate closely with the Executive Vice President, and provide editorial guidance to the Council’s directors. This position requires working in the Council’s office in Washington, D.C. ## Responsibilities – Shape the Council’s policy research and publications agenda – Provide substantive leadership for the Council’s policy working groups in key areas such as AI and digital policy, defense, and energy – Lead timely “Council Updates” on developments affecting the U.S.-U.A.E. relationship and their implications for members – Oversee research and reporting on key areas of cooperation in the bilateral trade, commercial, and investment relationship – Enhance event briefs and develop substantive questions and background materials for Council events – Provide editorial oversight of Council publications and other written materials – Support directors in strengthening the analysis, accuracy, and clarity of their written work – Develop relationships and partnerships with Council members, think tanks, and policy institutions in Washington, D.C. and the U.A.E. – Advise Council leadership on policy developments and institutional positioning ## Required Experience and Education – At least 15 years of relevant experience in government, public policy, think tanks, international affairs, business, academia, and/or a related field – Established expertise in Middle East and Gulf affairs, with strong knowledge of international economic policy and related commercial and geopolitical issues – Exceptional policy analysis, research, writing, and editing skills – Demonstrated experience producing or overseeing high-quality policy publications – Sound judgment and the ability to work effectively with senior executives, government officials, and subject‑matter experts – Strong attention to detail – Ability to manage multiple priorities, plan ahead, and meet strict deadlines while being proactive and responsive in a fluid and fast‑paced work environment – Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred ## Salary and Benefits – Salary negotiable based on experience and qualifications – Annual bonus opportunity based on performance – Generous benefits, including eligibility for health, dental, life, and disability insurance; a transportation allowance; and a 401(k) matching contribution ## Application Instructions To apply for this position, please send a cover letter, resume, two writing samples, and a list of relevant publications to Danny Sebright at ** [email protected] **. item.title: Senior Manager, Public Policy
item.description: Senior Manager, Public Policy Organization: Colorado Hospital Association (CHA) Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Colorado Hospital Association (CHA) Colorado Hospital Association (CHA) is the leading voice of Colorado’s hospital and health system community. Representing more than 100 hospitals and health systems throughout the state, CHA serves as a trusted, credible and reliable resource on health issues, hospital data and trends for its members, media, policymakers and the general public. Through CHA, Colorado’s hospitals and health systems work together in their shared commitment to improve health and health care in Colorado. For more information on CHA, visit [www.cha.com]. ## Position Summary The Public Policy Manager supports the development and execution of the Colorado Hospital Association’s public policy and advocacy priorities across legislative, regulatory, and federal policy. The Manager serves as a policy expert, project lead, member convener, and advocate on a dynamic portfolio of health care issues. This position is responsible for quickly developing expertise on complex and emerging policy issues; engaging members to identify priorities and develop solutions; translating complex policy into actionable advocacy strategies; and representing CHA and Colorado hospitals with policymakers, regulators, stakeholders, and coalition partners. The successful candidate will be a versatile public policy professional who can independently manage complex projects from issue identification and policy development through advocacy, negotiation, communication, and implementation. ## Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities ### Policy Analysis, Strategy & Development – Develop expertise across an evolving portfolio of state and federal health care policy issues; monitor emerging developments and identify opportunities, risks, and implications for hospitals. – Analyze complex policy proposals and translate legislative, regulatory, operational, financial, and political considerations into clear recommendations and advocacy strategies. – Develop proactive and defensive policy solutions with CHA leadership, members, and subject‑matter experts, identifying practical paths forward in complex or rapidly changing environments. ### Member Engagement & Policy Development – Convene and facilitate members and subject‑matter experts to gather input, navigate differing perspectives, build consensus, and develop member‑driven policy positions. – Serve as a trusted policy resource to member hospitals, providing strategic guidance on policy developments, implementation considerations, and advocacy opportunities. – Develop member education and engagement opportunities that translate complex issues into actionable information and strengthen participation in the policymaking process. ### Advocacy & External Engagement – Represent CHA and Colorado hospitals with legislators, regulators, federal policymakers, coalitions, stakeholder organizations, and other external audiences. – Advocate for CHA priorities through testimony, public comments, policymaker meetings, negotiations, coalition engagement, and other legislative and regulatory forums. – Build productive relationships and negotiate practical solutions that advance hospital priorities while navigating political realities and diverse stakeholder interests. ### Strategic Communications – Translate complex policy issues into clear, accessible, and actionable information for members, policymakers, stakeholders, and other audiences. – Draft high‑quality policy analyses, memos, talking points, testimony, comment letters, fact sheets, advocacy alerts, presentations, and other strategic materials. – Develop and continually adapt compelling communications that effectively articulate CHA positions and tell the story of Colorado hospitals. ### Project & Portfolio Management – Independently manage a significant and evolving portfolio of public policy initiatives from issue identification and strategy development through advocacy, implementation, and evaluation. – Coordinate complex projects involving members, CHA staff, consultants, policymakers, and external stakeholders while maintaining clear timelines, documentation, decision points, and deliverables. – Take ownership of emerging priorities and special projects, proactively identifying risks, resolving challenges, and improving advocacy and member‑engagement processes. ### Organizational Collaboration – Collaborate across CHA teams to develop and execute coordinated policy and advocacy strategies. – Serve as a strategic thought partner and resource to colleagues, contributing policy expertise, political judgment, and problem‑solving across organizational priorities. – Bring curiosity, flexibility, creativity, and a willingness to jump into emerging issues where additional policy capacity or expertise is needed. ## Knowledge, Skills and Experience Required – Five or more years of relevant experience in public policy, government affairs, health care policy, advocacy, regulatory or legislative affairs, or a related field; Colorado and health care experience preferred. – Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Health Policy, Political Science, or Law; Master’s preferred. – Demonstrated ability to quickly understand complex issues, synthesize significant amounts of information, and translate analysis into practical policy and advocacy strategies. – Experience independently managing complex projects, engaging diverse stakeholders, developing high‑quality written materials, and representing an organization with external audiences. ## Qualifications and Competencies – Exceptional analytical, strategic, written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills. – Strong relationship‑building and facilitation skills, including the ability to navigate disagreement, incorporate diverse perspectives, and build consensus around practical solutions. – Highly organized, adaptable, and self‑directed, with the judgment and initiative to manage multiple complex priorities and take ownership of issues with limited supervision. ## Physical Demands / Work Environment The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. – Working conditions are normal for a fast‑paced office work environment. – Presentation of technical material in group settings required occasionally. – Individuals may need to sit or stand as needed. – Weekend or evening work may be needed. – May include lifting up to 25 pounds for files on a regular basis. Proper lifting techniques required. ## Material and Equipment Directly Used – Company‑issued laptop with Microsoft Office 365 software applications – Cell phone – Printer/copier – AV platforms such as Zoom and Teams ## Hiring Salary Range Hiring salary range: **$90,000–$100,000 annually**, benefits eligible. The hiring salary range represents a targeted hiring range based on candidate’s experience, education, and/or skill level. The actual starting salary may be more or less depending on individual qualifications and does not represent the position’s full salary range. ## Additional Information **NOTE:** This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. The employee will be required to follow any other instructions and to perform any other duties requested by their supervisor. Nothing in this job description shall create or be construed to constitute a contract of employment, express or implied. Employees are held accountable for all duties of this job. ## CHA Workplace Culture CHA strives for a healthy workplace culture where employees are valued for their unique perspectives and backgrounds. CHA does this by offering and prioritizing: – Flexibility and work/life balance – Personal and professional development opportunities – Open and honest discussions about the company and its culture – An environment where each and every person can make an impact – Competitive and comprehensive total rewards packages designed to support employees and their families As an Equal Opportunity Employer, CHA makes employment decisions based on the merit and qualifications of those who apply. CHA is committed to providing equal opportunities for all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. CHA will make every effort to find a reasonable accommodation for any qualified applicant that chooses to disclose a physical or mental limitation/disability. If you believe you require accommodation for any stage of the hiring process, please contact CHA at 720‑489‑1630. ## CHA Culture Statement CHA is committed to achieving equitable health outcomes by eliminating bias and barriers. CHA values different backgrounds, experiences, and viewpoints. By promoting a variety of perspectives among employees and member hospitals, the Association furthers its mission of advancing the health of Colorado communities. item.title: State Affairs Counsel
item.description: State Affairs Counsel Organization: American Association for Justice (AAJ) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/01/2026 ## Overview ### Salary Range $70,000.00 – $85,000.00 Salary/year ### Position Type Full Time ### Job Shift Day ### Education Level JD — ## Description The American Association for Justice (AAJ) works to preserve the constitutional right to trial by jury and to make sure people have a fair chance to seek justice when they are injured by the negligence or misconduct of others — even when it means taking on the most powerful corporations. AAJ is seeking a State Affairs Counsel for its State Affairs department. The State Affairs Counsel provides legal, legislative, and policy research and analysis of state legislation, assists with complex multistate State legislative projects, and supports AAJ’s state and federal advocacy efforts. ### Responsibilities • Analyze and assess state legislation for state trial lawyers’ associations (TLAs) and AAJ’s members. • Monitor the daily progress of state legislative proposals for the department, including providing a regular summation of state legislative proposals that would impact the civil justice system and tracking relevant bills in all fifty states, the District of Columbia, and all U.S. territories. • Draft advocacy material such as one-pagers, fact sheets, and talking points in response to state legislative activities and to promote AAJ’s and the state TLAs’ policy goals. • Draft model legislation and sample amendments. • Work with allied groups on joint legislative goals, including representing AAJ’s interests, working with coalitions, and building a broader group of allies. • Communicate with members, staff, and leadership on policy positions, progress of proposals, and AAJ/TLA advocacy activity. • Assist Director in advising Communications staff on state messaging and state press regarding state legislative proposals. • Assist Director in developing strategy for specific initiatives or policy campaigns as needed. • Perform other duties as assigned. — ## Qualifications • J.D. degree required and member in good standing with at least one state bar or U.S. territory. • Minimum of 1 year experience in legal research and analysis; legislative drafting; and bill tracking. • Familiarity with state and Congressional legislative and regulatory processes and a commitment to civil justice issues. • Excellent writing, communication, and analysis skills, plus the ability to work independently and in teams. • Ability to work with AAJ members, AAJ leadership, and state associations. • A clear understanding of AAJ issues and the ability to advocate for them to others. • Must successfully pass a criminal background check. — ## Compensation The salary range for this position is $70,000–$85,000. Salary will be determined by the candidate’s level of experience and qualifications. — ## Benefits and Perks for Working with AAJ • Hybrid work schedule, onsite Tuesday through Thursday and 100% remote work for the month of August (for most employees) • Comprehensive health insurance, including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, flexible spending account (FSA), and 401K with employer match • Generous paid leave (vacation, sick, personal, parental), 11 federal holidays, and paid time off between Christmas and New Year’s • Subsidized metro transit and/or parking benefits • Professional development opportunities • Company social events • Office conveniently located ½ block from Gallery Place/Chinatown metro station in downtown Washington, DC AAJ is an Equal Opportunity Employer. No phone calls please! Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Communications Director
item.description: Communications Director Organization: Vertical Aviation International (VAI) Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 09/01/2026 **Vertical Aviation International (VAI)** is seeking a strategic Communications Director to lead public relations, executive communications, earned media, and external messaging. This role will work closely with senior leadership to support advocacy, legislative, regulatory, and industry priorities while strengthening VAI’s visibility and influence across the aviation industry. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Public Relations & Media Strategy Develop and execute public relations, earned media, and annual communications plans aligned with VAI’s advocacy and industry priorities. Monitor media coverage, industry trends, and emerging issues to identify communication opportunities. Build and maintain relationships with industry media and key external stakeholders. ### Executive Communications Serve as the primary communications strategist and writer for the President & CEO. Draft speeches, testimony, op-eds, articles, talking points, and executive correspondence. Maintain a consistent executive voice and message across communications. ### Content Development & Editorial Leadership Write and edit press releases, Q&As, backgrounders, website content, articles, newsletters, and related materials. Ensure content is accurate, clear, brand-aligned, and mission-focused. Translate complex policy and technical topics into engaging, accessible content. ### Communications Project Management Manage communications projects from concept through publication and distribution. Develop timelines, project plans, and resource needs to support successful execution. Collaborate with marketing, government affairs, membership, and creative teams on integrated initiatives. ### Digital Communications & Creative Collaboration Partner with design and digital teams to develop visual, multimedia, and multi-platform communications. Support ongoing improvements to VAI’s communications channels and member engagement efforts. ### Other Perform other related duties and special projects as assigned. — ## Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, English, Political Science, or related field. Five (5) or more years of experience in communications, public relations, media relations, public affairs, or related fields. Strong executive writing experience, including speeches, talking points, articles, testimony, or similar materials. Experience with legislative, regulatory, public policy, advocacy, association, nonprofit, or aviation communications preferred. Exceptional writing, editing, proofreading, verbal communication, and attention-to-detail skills. Strong project management, organizational, and cross-functional collaboration abilities. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, WordPress, Adobe Creative Cloud, Teams, and collaboration platforms. Knowledge of AP Style and Chicago Manual of Style. — ## Work Environment and Travel Hybrid role based in Alexandria, Virginia, with at least two in-office days per week and additional days as needed. Approximately 20% travel for conferences, events, and industry meetings. — ## Why Join VAI? ### Impact Shape the voice of the leading association representing the vertical aviation industry. ### Executive Visibility Work directly with senior leadership on communications tied to critical industry issues. ### Meaningful Work Support advocacy, policy, and member engagement initiatives that advance aviation. — ## Compensation & Benefits Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage with 100% employer-paid employee premiums, a generous retirement plan match, tuition reimbursement, and a flexible hybrid work environment. item.title: Associate State Director – Advocacy
item.description: Associate State Director – Advocacy Organization: AARP Location: Columbia, SC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Job ID 2026‑7773 ## Department Social Impact & Engagement ## Salary $94,500.00 – $105,000.00 Yearly — ## Overview AARP is the nation’s largest nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering people 50 and older to choose how they live as they age. With a nationwide presence, AARP strengthens communities and advocates for what matters most to the more than 100 million Americans 50‑plus and their families: health and financial security, and personal fulfillment. AARP also works for individuals in the marketplace by sparking new solutions and allowing carefully chosen, high‑quality products and services to carry the AARP name. As a trusted source for news and information, AARP produces the nation’s largest‑circulation publications, *AARP The Magazine* and the *AARP Bulletin*. The Associate State Director‑Advocacy develops and implements federal, state, and local‑level advocacy goals and objectives within business unit plans and the overall enterprise strategy. Executes state, federal, and local advocacy activities and represents the organization and its interests to elected officials and public policy leaders. Partners with internal and external partners to develop and execute advocacy campaigns and to build constituent support for the organization’s legislative priorities. Develops and executes advocacy volunteer recruitment strategies and tactics. Collaborates with management to identify opportunities to streamline processes and to develop new procedures that support the business unit/department. — ## Responsibilities – Develops and implements advocacy strategies and campaigns at the local, state, and federal levels while collaborating with cross‑functional teams as well as internal and external partners to achieve the organization’s legislative goals. – Represents the organization and its interests to federal, state, or local government agencies. Builds and maintains relationships with governmental representatives, with the goal of advancing and promoting the organization’s goals. Develops and manages relationships with elected officials at all levels. – Collaborates with internal/external partners on advocacy campaign communication strategy development. Utilizes direct action organizing tactics and implements grassroots advocacy tools to build constituent support for the organization’s legislative priorities. – Identifies issues of public policy and organizational importance and implements strategies, such as drafting and distributing memos or releases, to generate government and public support. Advocates for organizational interests in front of legislative bodies. Analyzes legislation for alignment with organizational priorities. Monitors and comments on pending legislation that may impact organizational priorities. – Serves as a deep subject‑matter expert on the state office’s advocacy issues. Uses data and input from diverse stakeholders. Produces written reports or convenes public meetings to disseminate findings, share best practices, and advance solutions through relevant communication channels. – Recruits, trains, develops, and deploys volunteers in accordance with organizational goals. Aligns volunteers’ interests with organizational priorities. Supports volunteer needs and designs opportunities to maximize volunteer engagement. Ensures inclusion of volunteer perspectives in strategic planning. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Public Relations, Community Organizing, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. – 3+ years of experience as a registered state or federal lobbyist with demonstrated success influencing public policy and legislative outcomes. – 5+ years of experience in advocacy, government relations, grassroots organizing, community engagement, campaign management, coalition building, or related public affairs functions. – Proven experience developing and executing advocacy strategies, public policy initiatives, and tactical campaigns that drive stakeholder engagement and measurable impact. – Strong ability to recruit, train, mobilize, and lead volunteers, community advocates, and grassroots networks in support of policy and advocacy objectives. – Exceptional written, verbal, facilitation, public speaking, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively to diverse audiences. – Demonstrated ability to build and sustain strategic, nonpartisan relationships with elected officials, community leaders, coalition partners, and cross‑functional internal stakeholders. – Preferred qualifications include expert knowledge of South Carolina’s legislative process, leadership experience in voter engagement, utilities, caregiver and healthcare policy, financial security and consumer protection, and proficiency with Qualtrics, Springboard, Constant Contact, SharePoint, Salesforce, and related technology platforms. – AARP will not sponsor an employment visa for this position at this time. — ## Additional Requirements – Regular and reliable job attendance – Effective verbal and written communication skills – Exhibit respect and understanding of others to maintain professional relationships – Independent judgment in evaluating options to make sound decisions – In‑office/open office environment with the ability to work effectively surrounded by moderate noise – Ability to occasionally lift up to 25 pounds – Home office environment with the ability to work effectively surrounded by moderate home‑environment noise — ## Hybrid Work Environment AARP observes Mondays and Fridays as remote workdays, except for essential functions. Remote work can only be done within the United States and its territories. — ## Compensation and Benefits AARP offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including a 401(k); 100% company‑funded pension plan; health, dental, and vision plans; life insurance; paid time off to include company and individual holidays, vacation, sick, caregiving, and parental leave; performance‑based and peer‑based recognition; and tuition reimbursement. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity AARP is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. AARP does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law.
