item.title: Communications and Government Relations Specialist
item.description: Communications and Government Relations Specialist Organization: K2 Space Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## **K2 Overview** K2 is building the largest and highest‑power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we’re mass‑producing the highest‑power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space. The rise of heavy‑lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today’s and tomorrow’s massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits. With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we’re Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast‑paced environment and you’re excited about contributing to the success of a high‑growth Series D‑funded company, we’d love for you to apply. — ## **The Role** K2 Space is seeking a Communications & Government Relations Specialist to support our strategic communications and government relations efforts in Washington, DC. This role will provide logistical, operational, and public affairs support across both functions — helping plan and execute communications and government relations campaigns that advance K2’s mission and policy priorities. You’ll work closely with the Strategic Communications Director on major announcements and day‑to‑day media efforts and support the Director of Congressional Affairs on targeted government relations initiatives. This is a great opportunity for someone with a background in congressional, government agency, or think tank work who wants to help build the communications and government relations function of a fast‑growing space company. — ## **Responsibilities** – Provide day‑to‑day support to the Strategic Communications Director on media efforts, communication materials, and major company announcements – Support the Director of Congressional Affairs on targeted government relations efforts, including meeting prep, briefing materials, and follow‑up – Assist with planning and executing communications and government relations campaigns, including content creation and timeline planning – Help create and manage visual assets, including promotional and announcement videos, official photographs, and website content – Monitor K2‑related news and relevant stories to drive communications feedback and shape company communications campaigns – Identify speaking opportunities and coordinate conference attendance, and maintain a strategic calendar of these engagements for K2 leadership – Manage association memberships and track sponsorship opportunities – Draft and edit talking points, briefing documents, press materials, and other written products – Monitor relevant news, legislative activity, and policy developments to keep leadership informed – Coordinate with congressional offices, government agencies, and other external stakeholders as needed – Support event planning and execution for briefings, Hill visits, media engagements, speaking opportunities, VIP visits to K2’s headquarters, and other public affairs activities – Manage the DC office customer relations management tool and mailing list – Provide general operational and administrative support to the Strategic Communications and Congressional Affairs teams — ## **Qualifications** – 3–5 years of experience supporting strategic communications and/or government relations – Experience with using customer relations management (CRM) tools – Background providing logistical, operational, or public affairs support for a congressional office, government agency, or think tank – Strong written and verbal communication skills, with excellent attention to detail – Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment – A start‑up, can‑do mentality – Based in the Washington, DC area (Rosslyn, VA), with occasional travel to K2 Space headquarters in Torrance, California and other locations as needed — ## **Nice to Have** – Existing relationships with congressional staff, agency contacts, or press – Experience with media monitoring and press outreach – Experience supporting a startup or fast‑scaling organization – Familiarity with the space, defense, or aerospace policy landscape — ## **Compensation and Benefits** – Base salary range for this role is $100,000 – $150,000 + equity in the company – Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level – Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other, and non‑traditional career twists and turns are encouraged. If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know. — ## **Export Compliance** As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.” The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license. — ## **Equal Opportunity** K2 Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with K2 Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence, and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. item.title: Director of Congressional Affairs
item.description: Director of Congressional Affairs Organization: K2 Space Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## K2 Space Overview K2 is building the largest and highest‑power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, K2 is mass‑producing the highest‑power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space. The rise of heavy‑lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today’s and tomorrow’s massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits. With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, K2 is Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast‑paced environment and are excited about contributing to the success of a high‑growth Series D‑funded company, K2 encourages you to apply. — ## The Role K2 Space is seeking a Director of Congressional Affairs to build and sustain the company’s presence and relationships on Capitol Hill. This role will be the day‑to‑day lead on Capitol Hill with a focus on the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, the Defense Appropriations subcommittees, and the House and Senate Intelligence Committees, with the goal of advancing K2’s policy priorities and visibility among key defense and space stakeholders in Congress. You will bring deep Hill experience and established relationships on both sides of the aisle to represent K2, staff senior company executives in their interactions with Congress, and manage the company’s Political Action Committee. This is a high‑visibility role for someone who knows how to navigate Capitol Hill, understands the federal budget process, and wants to help shape the policy landscape for a fast‑growing company disrupting national security space. — ## Responsibilities – Build and sustain K2 Space’s presence and relationships on Capitol Hill, focusing on the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, Defense Appropriations subcommittees, and House and Senate Intelligence Committees. – Develop and execute strategies to advance K2’s legislative and policy priorities. – Staff senior K2 executives ahead of and during interactions with Congress, both on Capitol Hill and during site visits to K2 headquarters. – Monitor legislative and appropriations activity relevant to K2’s business and keep leadership informed of developments and opportunities. – Represent K2 at official hearings and meetings, political fundraisers, and other unofficial events to engage directly with relevant congressional stakeholders. – Register as a federal lobbyist and represent K2 Space in direct engagement with congressional offices. – Perform day‑to‑day management of the K2 Space PAC, including leading solicitation campaigns, updating the PAC’s contribution strategy, and overseeing monthly FEC filings. – Build relationships with committee staff, member offices, and other relevant stakeholders on both sides of the aisle. – Partner with the broader K2 Strategy team, including the Strategic Communications Director and the Director of State and Local Government Affairs, to align efforts across all levels of government and broader company messaging. — ## Qualifications – 7–12+ years of congressional affairs experience, predominantly from working on the Hill. – Strong existing relationships with congressional offices and staff on both sides of the aisle. – Meaningful background in defense and/or space issues. – Willingness to register as a lobbyist. – Holds a current TS/SCI security clearance, or has held one previously and is eligible to obtain one again. – Strong written and verbal communication skills. – Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment. – Based in the Washington, DC area (Rosslyn, VA), with regular travel to K2 Space headquarters in Torrance, California, and other locations as needed. — ## Nice to Have – Military, Pentagon, or IC experience. – Experience with lobbying, industry association advocacy, or congressional affairs from a government agency. — ## Compensation and Benefits – Base salary range: $190,000 – $270,000 + equity in the company. – Salary will be based on several factors including knowledge, skills, education, and experience level. – Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks. If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, you are encouraged to still apply. Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other, and non‑traditional career paths are welcomed. If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application or interviews, please let K2 know. — ## Export Compliance As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Consult a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you qualify as a “U.S. Person.” The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including those outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). Therefore, the person hired must either be a “U.S. Person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license. — ## Equal Opportunity K2 Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment is governed on the basis of merit, competence, and qualifications and will not be influenced by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. item.title: Associate
item.description: Associate Organization: Crosscut Strategies Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Crosscut Strategies — Associate Position Crosscut Strategies — a Washington DC-based strategic communications firm working primarily with high-growth start-ups in tech, health care, and other complex sectors — is looking for a talented communicator with experience in politics, policy, communications, and/or technology to join our team. This is a great entry-level opportunity to build your skills as you work closely with our senior leadership to develop and implement communications programs and promote our clients’ initiatives to the media and other stakeholders. The ideal associate candidate will have demonstrated interest or initial experience in journalism, media, communications, or campaigns. You need to be inquisitive, motivated, smart, and able to write quickly and well. Our associates are key members of the team and work closely with managers and directors. They must be problem solvers, able to multitask, and have excellent judgment. ## Responsibilities Include Drafting and editing press releases, fact sheets, talking points, presentations, strategy memos, and other communications documents. Building press lists and pitching reporters to generate media coverage of events, reports, or other client initiatives. Researching issues, policy developments, and media coverage of targeted topics, and distilling this research into clear, concise memos and reports for clients. Proposing creative ideas for helping clients achieve their goals. Monitoring media coverage to identify opportunities and potential risks for clients. Participating in new business development, including research and proposal preparation. Coordinating meetings, calls, and project timelines for clients. ## Required Skills and Qualifications Excellent writing and editing skills. Strong organizational abilities, critical thinking, and attention to detail. Highly self-motivated. Ability to multitask, work quickly to meet deadlines, and manage multiple assignments at once. Advanced proficiency with creating, editing, and formatting professional-quality documents in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Experience with social media, preferably experience using social media to reach target audiences. Prior work, internship, or volunteer experience in communications, political campaigns, marketing, or issue advocacy. We also consider outstanding recent college graduates who have work experience in an unrelated field and a demonstrated interest in communications. ## Preferred Skills 1–2 years of experience working with traditional media, writing materials for public distribution, conducting policy and media research, and coordinating media events. Familiarity with and/or interest in health care, energy, technology, financial services, and related issues. Experience with Agentic AI. Interest in public policy and familiarity with federal and/or state policymaking processes. ## Education Bachelor’s degree in a related field (or a creative case as to how your major relates to this role). Crosscut operates as a hybrid workplace with an office in the heart of the Dupont/Farragut North area that has easy access to Metro, buses, and bikeshare. While employees are not required to come into the office every day, we are expected to come on set days and must live within the DC-metro area to be available for meetings and collaborations that occur in-person. ## Compensation and Benefits The annual salary range for the associate position is $50,000 to $55,000 with a comprehensive benefits package, great team, and a working environment committed to fostering staff growth and leadership. Employee benefits include an employer-matched 401(k) plan with immediate vesting, medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and eligible dependents, paid time off and sick leave, and paid parental leave. Interested candidates should send a cover email and resume to [email protected] . Crosscut Strategies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Specialist Organization: Crosscut Strategies Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Crosscut Strategies — Account Specialist Crosscut Strategies — a Washington DC‑based strategic communications firm working primarily with high‑growth start‑ups in tech, health care, and other complex sectors — is seeking an Account Specialist to join our team. This role is an opportunity to level up in your career, learn more about strategic communications, and develop your managerial skills in client accounts and staff mentorship. The ideal specialist will have at least 3 years of relevant experience in strategic communications at a firm or in‑house. You need to be inquisitive, motivated, and able to write quickly and well. Specialists must be problem solvers, able to multitask, have excellent judgment, and be able to communicate openly and effectively up and down the team as well as to clients. ## Specialist Responsibilities – **Media strategy** — Develop media and social media content strategies, and pitch media strategically and proficiently. – **Interview staffing** — Staff media interviews for clients as needed. – **Drafting materials** — Write and review drafts of bylines/blogs, releases, pitches, and other media materials, grassroots and internal communications. – **Client recommendations** — Help develop strategies and draft recommendations for clients. – **Briefing memos** — Review background briefing memos for clients and provide constructive feedback to junior staff. – **Project management** — Manage and execute multi‑part account projects or strategic initiatives. – **Client coordination** — Coordinate interviews and other client interactions, and provide client updates on calls. – **Mentorship development** — Develop management and mentorship skills. ## Required Skills and Qualifications – **Multitasking** — Effectively multi‑task, work quickly to meet deadlines, and manage multiple assignments at once while updating team members accordingly. – **Proactivity** — Be proactive, take initiative, solve problems, and bring ideas to the table. – **High‑quality work** — Produce high‑quality, client‑ready work and excellent results. – **Client service** — Bring service mentality to clients: anticipate client needs and help solve their problems. – **Team support** — Be willing to help other team members with their work. – **Open communication** — Communicate openly across staff (up and down). – **Professional judgment** — Demonstrate sound professional judgment and interpersonal skills. – **Organization** — Possess strong organizational abilities and attention to detail. – **Writing skills** — Write quickly and well, with near client‑ready first drafts. – **Media experience** — 3+ years of experience working with traditional media, social media, and/or writing materials for public distribution. – **Document proficiency** — Advanced proficiency with creating, editing, and formatting professional‑quality documents in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. ## Preferred Skills – **Digital media** — 1–2 years of digital media experience. – **Agentic AI** — Experience with Agentic AI. – **Sector familiarity** — Familiarity with and/or interest in health care, energy, technology, financial services, and related issues. – **Public policy** — Interest in public policy and familiarity with federal and/or state policymaking processes. ## Education Bachelor’s degree. ## Workplace Model Crosscut operates as a hybrid workplace with an office in the heart of the Dupont/Farragut North area that has easy access to Metro, buses, and bikeshare. While employees are not required to come into the office every day, we are expected to come on set days and must live within the DC‑metro area to be available for meetings and collaborations that occur in person. ## Compensation and Benefits The annual salary range for the specialist position is **$60,000 to $70,000**, with a comprehensive benefits package, great team, and a working environment committed to fostering staff growth and leadership. Employee benefits include: – Employer‑matched 401(k) plan with immediate vesting – Medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and eligible dependents – Paid time off and sick leave – Paid parental leave ## Application Instructions Interested candidates should send a cover email and resume to ** [email protected] **. item.title: Lead Advocacy Officer
item.description: Lead Advocacy Officer Organization: ZERO TO THREE Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 # ABOUT ZERO TO THREE Founded in 1977, ZERO TO THREE works to ensure that babies and toddlers benefit from the early connections that are critical to their well‑being and development. Our mission is to ensure that all babies and toddlers have a strong start in life. At ZERO TO THREE, we envision a society with the knowledge and will to support all infants and toddlers in reaching their full potential. Our Core Values Statement: We believe that how we do our work is as important as what we do. To learn more about ZERO TO THREE, please visit our website at zerotothree.org. # SUMMARY The Policy Center at ZERO TO THREE, a nonpartisan, research‑based resource on infant and toddler development, is seeking a changemaker and coalition‑builder to serve as the Lead Advocacy Officer. The Lead Advocacy Officer will manage the federal policy, government relations, family and community mobilization teams to execute a power‑building, integrated advocacy agenda that advances ZERO TO THREE’s mission of ensuring all babies and toddlers have a strong start in life. The Lead Advocacy Officer will report to the Chief Policy Officer and serve on the Policy Center’s Leadership Team. The LAO will work closely with ZERO TO THREE’s communication and marketing division to develop and implement national and state advocacy campaigns, state and federal government relations strategies, and relationship‑ and coalition‑building efforts with a variety of stakeholders, grassroots organizations, and partners, including Congress and the Administration. The Lead Advocacy Officer will supervise a team of Directors and specialists and work collaboratively with internal colleagues and external partners to ensure ZTT’s advocacy agenda drives meaningful policy and system change for infants, toddlers, and their families. # ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES ## Strategic Leadership and Collaboration The Lead Advocacy Officer will lead the design and advancement of ZERO TO THREE’s advocacy plan in alignment with ZERO TO THREE’s strategic plan and in partnership with ZTT’s external partners and stakeholders. The LAO will collaborate effectively with their team, colleagues, and government relations consultants to design coordinated federal and state advocacy campaigns and government relations strategies. This work will be carried out in an integrated manner, including through mobilization efforts and close partnership with the communications team to develop and implement media and other communications strategies and materials. The LAO will plan and ensure the successful implementation of annual high‑profile advocacy events at a reasonable cadence to build momentum and strengthen stakeholder engagement on ZERO TO THREE’s policy priorities and goals. They will ensure all advocacy efforts comply with relevant laws and ethical standards and reflect transparency and accountability. They will lead their team in developing and fostering strategic partnerships and coalitions at the state and federal levels to drive and maximize impact and to seek input from families, early childhood professionals, stakeholders, and community partners. The Lead Advocacy Officer will be closely attuned to shifts in the political and policy landscape, emerging opportunities and challenges, and their implications for ZERO TO THREE’s advocacy priorities. This requires the ability to operate effectively in dynamic and uncertain environments, to identify and communicate strategic tradeoffs, and to guide timely adjustments in approach and prioritization. The Lead Advocacy Officer will work in close partnership with colleagues across the organization, including policy, advocacy, communications, and research teams, to ensure alignment and integration of strategies and activities. They will also develop, strengthen, and cultivate external partnerships and coalitions that advance shared policy goals and maximize collective impact. ## Strategic Engagement and Communication The Lead Advocacy Officer will serve as an engaged, dynamic, and thoughtful external voice and representative for ZERO TO THREE, actively and capably leveraging their expertise, knowledge, and experience to amplify the reach and impact of ZERO TO THREE’s work. The Lead Advocacy Officer will lead team members in representing ZERO TO THREE with various coalitions and will direct team members to provide technical assistance to federal policymakers and staff, including responding to inquiries for input on legislative language, report language, and comments on legislation and regulations. The Lead Advocacy Officer will maintain robust internal communications to stay abreast of the work of colleagues across the organization and to keep colleagues informed of the department’s work with policy leaders and networks at the federal and local levels. They will work closely with the communications team to draft materials including talking points, messaging, policy briefs, Congressional testimony, regulatory comments, legislative summaries, and other materials of various lengths and formats, and can succinctly and effectively express complex issues to federal policymakers, other key stakeholders, the media, and the public. The Lead Advocacy Officer will lead team members to coordinate with ZERO TO THREE colleagues to organize congressional briefings and other events designed to advance ZERO TO THREE’s federal priorities and will contribute to grant proposals and reports to funders. The Lead Advocacy Officer will keep the Chief Policy Officer and other senior leadership informed about pertinent legislative issues, external factors, and policy proposals and actions that impact infants and toddlers and their families. ## Team Leadership and Supervision The Lead Advocacy Officer will possess the experience and knowledge needed to supervise a team of experienced policy advocates and government relations professionals with strong experience and deep subject matter expertise in their respective issue areas. The Lead Advocacy Officer will provide the level of mentorship, engagement, and support needed to build and retain a proactive team and will leverage the subject matter expertise of team members to develop and build strategies, campaigns, and issue advancement. The Lead Advocacy Officer will ensure that work is planned in collaboration with the various departments within the Policy Center, including the Policy System Integration and Innovation team, the Policy Research and Learning team, the Safe Babies Program, and the Prenatal‑to‑Five Network. The Lead Advocacy Officer will evaluate team member performance and partner with members to establish annual goals and objectives and identify and provide appropriate professional growth and development opportunities. ## Policy Advocacy and Organizational Alignment The Lead Advocacy Officer will possess a deep understanding of the policy arena and how policy relevant to ZERO TO THREE’s policy agenda is informed, shaped, and crafted through the ongoing, dynamic interplay of key national, state, and local stakeholders, including legislators, government agencies, community and grassroots leaders, and partner organizations. The Lead Advocacy Officer will use this knowledge to provide needed nuance and details when advising colleagues on crafting campaigns, implementing strategy, and on the optimal ways of presenting and communicating issues to specific audiences. The Lead Advocacy Officer must possess a strong understanding of Congressional and regulatory processes, particularly regarding the federal budget and annual appropriations process. They must possess the ability to understand and analyze complex legal, factual, and legislative concepts related to ZERO TO THREE’s federal policy agenda. The Lead Advocacy Officer will establish processes to develop goals and priorities and will work with team members to continuously monitor, analyze, and assess proposed and existing relevant federal and state legislation and activities of federal and local agencies. They will maintain a clear‑eyed focus on crafting and directing appropriate campaigns and actions to ensure the needs of infants and toddlers are reflected. The Lead Advocacy Officer also will perform other duties as assigned for the purpose of ensuring the efficient and effective functioning of the advocacy and government relations strategy and advancement of ZERO TO THREE’s comprehensive policy agenda. # ESSENTIAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE Minimum of 12 years of relevant advocacy and policy experience, including experience on Capitol Hill, government relations, lobbying, or related role. Minimum of 8 years of relevant supervisory experience, including experience in leading a cross‑functional team through various priorities, strategies, and goals. Demonstrated advanced knowledge and facility with influencing and advocating at federal and local levels. Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of federal legislative and regulatory processes and procedures, including federal budget and appropriations processes. Strong critical thinker and strategic planner with exceptional judgment and significant experience anticipating challenges and creatively problem‑solving. Strong understanding of early childhood policy issues such as health, mental health, family support, or early learning (preferred). Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills with a track record of cultivating and maintaining respectful relationships at all levels and across identities, including with key members of Congress and Executive Branch agencies. Strong management and supervisory skills, including experience providing reflective supervision. Experience with strategy development and execution, including developing actionable plans with timelines and measurable indicators. Ability to connect research, policy, and practice into a unified strategy. Ability to develop proposals and partner with Development

item.title: Head of Public Relations & Corporate Communications
item.description: Head of Public Relations & Corporate Communications Organization: Remitly Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Job Description At Remitly, we believe everyone deserves the freedom to access, move, and manage their money wherever life takes them. Since 2011, we’ve tirelessly delivered on our promise to customers sending money globally, providing secure, simple, and reliable ways to manage their money, ensuring true peace of mind. Whether it’s supporting loved ones back home, growing a business across continents, or pursuing new opportunities abroad, we’re not just here to move money — we’re here to move our global customers forward. We’re looking for builders, reimaginers, and global thinkers who want to work at the intersection of technology, trust, and transformation. If that’s you and you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career — we invite you to join over 2,800 passionate Remitlians worldwide who are united by our vision to transform lives with trusted financial services that transcend borders. ## About the Role Remitly is looking for a Head of Public Relations & Corporate Communications to run our global PR and communications function, spanning corporate, product, executive, and financial communications for a publicly traded fintech company operating in 175+ countries. You’ll own the systems, relationships, and day‑to‑day execution that keep our external narrative aligned with Remitly’s pace of product innovations and network growth. ## You Will ### Communications Operations – Own the operational infrastructure for PR and communications — media strategy, content calendar, approval workflows, messaging framework, and performance measurement. – Work collaboratively with product leaders to optimize the cadence and impact of external messaging. – Own the press release calendar, translating the product roadmap into a structured release cadence — and reinvent Remitly’s press release voice from boilerplate to a distinctive, creative style that earns attention on its own. – Respond to media inquiries and shape the company’s public‑facing messaging. – Secure media profiles, speaking engagements, and award recognition that build executive credibility. – Partner with Investor Relations and Finance to align earnings communications and investor narratives with broader company messaging. ### Owned Media & Programs – Serve as editor of the company’s newsroom, owning the publishing calendar and content decisions. – Plan and execute major campaign moments — product launches, events — coordinating with internal teams and agencies against budget. – Source and create data‑driven stories that will land coverage and position Remitly as a category and thought leader. – Work with Legal, Finance, Policy, and Brand to manage and execute a crisis communications plan of action when needed. – Define and track key metrics to measure the performance and reach of corporate and financial storytelling efforts. ### AI & Innovation – Implement AI tools and workflows that increase the team’s output and efficiency. ## You Have – 12+ years in public relations or corporate communications, with direct ownership of a communications function at a public company or in a highly regulated industry. – Experience building or overhauling communications operations — editorial calendars, approval workflows, and messaging frameworks that drive consistent output. – Track record of securing executive visibility through top‑tier media placements, speaking engagements, and industry recognition. – Working knowledge of earnings cycles, investor expectations, and disclosure requirements, with experience aligning messaging with Finance and Investor Relations. – Experience owning a corporate newsroom, blog, or similar owned‑media channel as a primary storytelling platform, not just a press‑release archive. – Experience leading complex, multi‑stakeholder programs — product launches, flagship events, integrated campaigns — on budget and with outside agencies. – Crisis communications experience, including developing and executing response plans under pressure. – Strong news judgment and storytelling skills, translating data and business developments into compelling narratives. – Demonstrated use of AI tools to improve communications workflows and team efficiency. – Willingness to execute hands‑on, not just direct, with strong cross‑functional collaboration skills. ## Compensation Details The starting base salary range for this position is typically $208,000–$310,000. In the U.S., Remitly employees are shareholders in our Company and equity is part of our total compensation plan. Your recruiter can share more information about medical benefits offered, as well as other financial benefits and total compensation components offered with this role. ## Our Benefits – Flexible paid time off – Health, dental, and vision + 401k plan with company matching – Paid parental, medical, military, and family care leave – Mental Health & Family Forming Benefits – Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) – Continuing education ## Our Connected Work Culture: Driving Innovation, Together At Remitly, we believe that true innovation sparks when we come together. Our Connected Work Culture fosters dynamic in‑person collaboration, where ideas ignite and challenging problems find solutions faster. Under the Company’s current hybrid‑work expectations, employees in this position work onsite Tuesday through Thursday each week. Additional onsite attendance may be required based on business needs, and the Company may modify its hybrid‑work expectations from time to time. These intentional in‑office moments are vital for deepening relationships, fueling creativity, and ensuring your impact is felt where it matters most. ## Remitly is an E‑Verify Employer At Remitly, we are dedicated to ensuring that our workplace offers equal employment opportunities to all employees and candidates, in full compliance with applicable laws and regulations. item.title: Executive Director, Government Relations Communications & Campaigns
item.description: Executive Director, Government Relations Communications & Campaigns Organization: Kaiser Permanente Location: Oakland, CA Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Job Summary The Advocacy, Campaigns & Government Relations Communications leader serves as the enterprise lead responsible for advocacy campaigns, government relations communications, coalition activation, stakeholder engagement strategies, and public affairs initiatives that advance Kaiser Permanente’s legislative, regulatory, business, and reputation priorities. Reporting to the SVP, Government Relations, this leader works in close partnership with State Affairs, Federal Government Relations, Policy & Regulatory Affairs, Community Affairs, External Communications, Market Public Affairs Leaders, and business leaders to influence key stakeholders, mobilize support, shape external environments, and advance enterprise objectives. The role serves as Kaiser Permanente’s center of excellence for advocacy and campaign strategy, bringing together communications, coalition activation, stakeholder engagement, grassroots and grasstops outreach, digital engagement, thought leadership, events, and third‑party partnerships into coordinated campaigns that drive measurable outcomes. This leader is responsible for helping identify where advocacy, coalition‑building, and stakeholder engagement can accelerate enterprise priorities, developing the strategies and campaigns required to influence outcomes, and providing the tools, frameworks, and support necessary for successful execution across markets and functions. Success in this role requires strong political acumen, campaign experience, stakeholder management expertise, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate complex legislative, regulatory, policy, and business priorities into compelling campaigns that mobilize action and drive impact. — ## Essential Responsibilities ### Advocacy & Campaign Strategy – **Integrated advocacy campaigns** — Develop and lead campaigns that advance Kaiser Permanente’s legislative, regulatory, business, reputation, and stakeholder engagement priorities. – **Campaign strategy design** — Combine coalition activation, communications, digital engagement, events, grassroots and grasstops outreach, thought leadership, and earned media strategies. – **Strategic opportunity identification** — Partner with Government Relations leadership to identify opportunities where advocacy and public affairs campaigns can shape outcomes. – **Campaign frameworks** — Develop activation plans, messaging architectures, stakeholder strategies, and implementation roadmaps. – **Enterprise alignment** — Ensure campaigns align with enterprise priorities and are coordinated across national and market teams. ### Government Relations Communications – **Communications strategy leadership** — Lead communications strategies supporting government relations priorities at federal, state, and local levels. – **Cross‑functional partnership** — Partner with Federal Government Relations, State Affairs, Policy & Regulatory Affairs, Community Affairs, and Market Public Affairs leaders. – **Communications materials development** — Create plans and materials for legislative priorities, regulatory initiatives, policy campaigns, coalition activities, and stakeholder engagement. – **Messaging frameworks** — Produce briefing materials, talking points, presentations, fact sheets, toolkits, campaign assets, and executive materials. – **Stakeholder engagement support** — Support engagement with elected officials, policymakers, trade associations, coalition partners, advocacy organizations, and other external stakeholders. ### Coalition Building & Stakeholder Engagement – **Stakeholder relationship development** — Build relationships with key organizations, trade associations, advocacy groups, employers, community‑based organizations, and industry partners. – **Coalition activation** — Build and activate coalitions that advance strategic, legislative, regulatory, and business priorities. – **Third‑party validator strategy** — Identify opportunities to leverage trusted voices to strengthen advocacy efforts. – **Coordinated outreach** — Partner with State Affairs, Federal Government Relations, Community Affairs, and Market Public Affairs leaders. – **Visibility and influence** — Strengthen Kaiser Permanente’s credibility among key stakeholder audiences. ### Stakeholder & Political Intelligence – **Trend monitoring** — Assess legislative, regulatory, advocacy, and industry trends impacting enterprise priorities. – **Stakeholder mapping** — Create influence strategies and engagement plans. – **Strategic insights** — Provide recommendations regarding opportunities, risks, coalition dynamics, and stakeholder sentiment. – **Proactive engagement** — Identify opportunities to engage stakeholders before issues escalate. ### Digital Advocacy & Stakeholder Activation – **Digital engagement strategies** — Partner with communications, advocacy, and digital teams to develop modern engagement strategies. – **Scalable outreach** — Build scalable approaches to outreach, education, and activation. – **Digital tools** — Create digital tools, resources, and campaign assets. – **Innovative engagement** — Identify approaches that increase participation and influence. ### Market Integration & Execution – **Market coordination** — Partner with market leaders to coordinate campaign execution and stakeholder engagement. – **Enterprise frameworks** — Develop enterprise frameworks adaptable to local markets. – **Resource leverage** — Ensure campaigns use both enterprise resources and local relationships. – **Best practice sharing** — Share lessons learned across markets and functions. ### Campaign Measurement & Effectiveness – **Measurement frameworks** — Assess campaign performance, stakeholder engagement, coalition activation, narrative penetration, and digital engagement. – **Reporting dashboards** — Establish dashboards that provide visibility into effectiveness and engagement trends. – **Evaluation and improvement** — Recommend improvements based on results and insights. – **Continuous improvement** — Use data and feedback to strengthen influence. ### Strategic Counsel & Enterprise Partnership – **Strategic advising** — Advise Government Relations leadership on advocacy, coalition strategy, and stakeholder engagement. – **Enterprise coordination** — Partner across functions to ensure coordinated engagement. – **Stakeholder landscape guidance** — Support leaders in understanding stakeholder ecosystems. – **Policy and organizational alignment** — Ensure efforts advance policy and organizational priorities. ### Team Leadership & Capability Building – **Team leadership** — Lead and develop a high‑performing advocacy and campaign team. – **Capability building** — Build enterprise capabilities, playbooks, tools, governance models, and best practices. – **Culture development** — Foster collaboration, innovation, accountability, and results. – **Scalable execution** — Develop scalable approaches for effective execution across markets. — ## Basic Qualifications ### Experience Minimum ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in advocacy, public affairs, government relations, political campaigns, issue campaigns, coalition management, stakeholder engagement, communications, or related disciplines. ### Education Bachelor’s degree required in communications, public affairs, political science, public policy, journalism, government, business, or a related field. ### License, Certification, Registration N/A ### Additional Requirements – **Advocacy campaign execution** – **Influencing outcomes** – **Coalition building** – **Policy translation** – **Team leadership** — ## Preferred Qualifications Experience working in a trade association, corporate public affairs organization, political campaign, government office, advocacy organization, healthcare organization, or other regulated industry preferred. Healthcare experience preferred but not required. Advanced degree preferred. Pay Range: $247500 – $309375 / year Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Executive Director, Public Relations
item.description: Executive Director, Public Relations Organization: Kaiser Permanente Location: Oakland, CA Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Job Summary Reporting to the head of External Communications, the Executive Director, Public Relations serves as the enterprise leader for Enterprise Newsroom, Intelligence & Analytics and is responsible for newsroom operations, editorial planning, communications intelligence, social listening, stakeholder monitoring, reporting, analytics, and rapid‑response coordination across all regions and national functions. This leader builds and operates Kaiser Permanente’s modern communications operating system — providing leaders with the visibility, insights, and enterprise coordination needed to shape proactive narrative strategy, monitor stakeholder dynamics, measure communications performance, identify emerging risks, and respond effectively in a rapidly changing environment. **Enterprise accountability:** Serves as the central intelligence and coordination hub for External Communications & Reputation by leading enterprise newsroom operations, editorial governance, stakeholder intelligence, rapid‑response coordination, and analytics capabilities that strengthen decision‑making, reputation management, and enterprise alignment across markets and national functions. **Operating model considerations:** This role leads integrated communications transformation across earned, owned, and social channels by modernizing enterprise capabilities, strengthening editorial strategy and channel orchestration, improving how stories and priorities move across the system, and helping the Public Affairs leadership team align communications, reputation, policy, and business priorities during periods of rapid change. Transformation in practice includes capability modernization, stronger cross‑functional alignment, clearer leadership expectations, and a more proactive enterprise storytelling model — not crisis ownership, which sits with Issues Management. This role owns the enterprise’s proactive external voice — shaping the narratives, media agenda, executive visibility, and storytelling platforms that define Kaiser Permanente’s presence in the market. The Executive Director partners closely with Issues Management during high‑stakes moments, but the center of gravity for this role is proactive reputation‑building, earned influence, enterprise storytelling, and brand visibility. The Executive Director serves as a trusted advisor to enterprise and regional leadership, helping shape organizational priorities, influence enterprise decision‑making, and guide executive positioning in moments of opportunity, ambiguity, and change. This role requires judgment, external orientation, and the ability to balance stakeholder expectations while advancing Kaiser Permanente’s mission, reputation, and business objectives. — ## Essential Responsibilities ### Enterprise Newsroom – Builds and leads a modern enterprise newsroom that serves as Kaiser Permanente’s engine for editorial planning, content prioritization, story mining, and enterprise storytelling. – Develops enterprise editorial calendars, content governance processes, and decision rights that align storytelling priorities to enterprise and business objectives. – Surfaces, curates, and elevates stories from markets and national functions to strengthen enterprise narrative development and audience relevance. ### Intelligence & Monitoring – Leads enterprise media monitoring, social listening, stakeholder intelligence, and narrative tracking to identify emerging risks, opportunities, and trends. – Develops intelligence products, insights, and briefing materials that support executive decision‑making and strengthen enterprise readiness. ### Rapid Response Coordination – Operates enterprise rapid‑response capabilities and supports issue escalation, breaking news response, and cross‑market coordination in partnership with Issues Management and market teams. – Maintains operating rhythms and escalation pathways that connect markets and national teams during fast‑moving external developments. ### Analytics & Reporting – Develops enterprise communications measurement frameworks, dashboards, and reporting tools that track reputation, media impact, thought leadership, social engagement, stakeholder sentiment, and campaign effectiveness. – Delivers executive reporting and actionable insights that inform strategy, resource allocation, and continuous performance improvement. ### Enterprise Coordination – Provides visibility into media strategies, campaigns, issues, and stakeholder dynamics across markets and national functions. – Establishes common reporting standards, performance measures, and planning rhythms that support enterprise alignment. — ## Basic Qualifications ### Experience – Minimum twelve (12) years of relevant professional experience. ### Education – Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university **or** four (4) years of experience in a directly related field required. – High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED) required. ### License, Certification, Registration – N/A — ## Additional Requirements – Experience in large, complex, regulated organizations – Exceptional judgment – Ability to influence without authority – Experience operating in matrixed environments – Proven capability building and team leadership – Executive presence and strategic thinking — ## Preferred Qualifications – Healthcare preferred but not required Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Government Relations Director
item.description: Government Relations Director Organization: Heritage Foundation Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 **Title:** Government Relations Director **Reports to:** Vice President, Government Relations **Job Summary:** The Government Relations Director oversees a strategic outreach portfolio, providing policy guidance, educational events, fellowships, and trainings for current members of Congress and their staff, Administration officials, and allies in the conservative movement. The Director serves as a spokesperson for The Heritage Foundation and ensures Heritage policy positions are communicated to Hill and Administration audiences. The Director also informs Heritage analysts of emerging issues in Congress and the Administration and spearheads opportunities for analysts to educate policymakers and their staff. The ideal candidate brings policy expertise in a critical issue set such as culture, life, education, and health care to effectively drive impact with policymakers. — ### Job Duties: – **Strategic policy communication** — Ensure Heritage policy positions are communicated effectively to the Hill through strategic policy briefings, technical assistance, retreats, fellowships, and working groups. – **Department priority execution** — Drive successful achievement of department priorities, including coordinating and leading coalition working groups on strategic priorities, using innovative approaches. – **Administration engagement** — Engage with Administration officials and other key stakeholders to educate on policy issues. – **Cross‑department collaboration** — Lead cross-departmental collaboration by representing government relations in one or more internal policy campaign teams. – **External representation** — Represent Heritage policy positions to external audiences. – **Relationship development** — Develop and foster strategic policymaker relationships for the President of Heritage. – **Fellowship coordination** — Coordinate Heritage Fellowships and staff training programs. — ### Qualifications: **Education:** BA/BS required **Experience:** 5+ years of relevant experience; previous Hill experience strongly preferred **Communication:** Excellent writing, interpersonal, presentation, and public speaking skills **Technology:** Microsoft Suite — ### Other Requirements: – **Mission alignment** — Understand and support the Heritage mission and vision for America, and the department’s goals and objectives. – **Policy consistency** — Promote policies consistent with Heritage’s priorities; speak with one voice. – **Policy expertise** — Proven experience in shaping policy related to the economy, technology, energy, or foreign policy, aligning with Heritage’s mission. – **Strategic thinking** — Strategic thinker, understanding the importance of collaboration. – **Fast‑paced adaptability** — Work well in a fast-paced environment. – **Federal policy knowledge** — Extensive Administration and Congressional relationships and advanced knowledge of federal policy issues. – **Clear communication** — Clear articulation of Heritage policy positions to external stakeholders. — ### Benefits and Salary: The Heritage Foundation offers a highly competitive benefits package that includes, but is not limited to, best-in-class health care, vision, and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement funding, “take what you need” PTO and sick leave, 14 weeks of paid leave for new moms and 6 weeks of paid leave for new dads, among other programs. The salary range for this role is **$120,000 – $145,000 annually**. This range is a good faith estimate, and the final salary offered to a selected candidate depends on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s experience, education, and other qualifications; internal and external market pay for comparable jobs; and level of hire based on aforementioned qualifications. item.title: Communications Senior Associate
item.description: Communications Senior Associate Organization: Greenlight America Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/02/2026 Communications • Full Time • Remote / Occasional Travel • Salary $60,000 – $85,000 ## ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW Greenlight America is the leading grassroots campaign force powering the nation’s clean energy transition at the local level. Our team supports local residents and organizations working to get clean energy built in their communities. Since our founding in 2023, we have enabled volunteers to advance thousands of megawatts’ worth of utility‑scale projects across the country, helping hundreds of communities say yes to the benefits of a clean energy future. ## POSITION OVERVIEW The Communications Senior Associate plays a key role in supporting Greenlight America’s communications and campaign work, providing online research and creating content both on assigned campaigns and across the organization’s communications and messaging priorities. A successful candidate for this position will be a skilled writer and researcher with the demonstrated capacity to produce quality work on deadline. They will also have the ability to get up to speed quickly on complex topics and digital tools, be highly creative and willing to take risks, and exhibit strong skills in project management. The position is remote and reports to the Senior Communications and Digital Manager. ## PRIMARY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES – Produce social listening reports at the start of all Greenlight clean energy campaigns, reviewing local news coverage and social media activity to assess public sentiment and shape campaign messaging priorities and communications tactics around a proposed project, ordinance, or technology in a given community or area. – Support the creation of communications materials for other Greenlight clean energy campaigns as assigned, working closely with other members of the communications and campaigns teams to execute a messaging and content strategy for each campaign. Materials produced may include talking points, fact sheets, letters to the editors, op‑eds, digital content, social media posts, one‑pagers, and presentations. – Support the creation of general volunteer guides and resources and other organization‑wide “evergreen” messaging materials, including research and drafting. ## EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS We are especially interested in candidates with the following qualifications: – 1+ years of experience developing content and/or messaging on deadline. Strong candidates for this role may also have backgrounds in journalism, community organizing, campaigning, clean energy development, or similar. – Strong research and written communications skills. – Passion for accelerating the clean energy transition. – Experience in social media analysis and news monitoring is a plus. – Experience with digital advocacy and Mobilize.us is a plus. ## COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS The base annual salary for this position is $60,000–$85,000. We offer an excellent benefits package which includes 100% employer‑paid premiums for medical, dental, and vision insurance, unlimited paid time off, monthly technology stipend, and retirement contributions through 401k and Roth plans. ## TO APPLY Use this link to submit a resume and responses to the provided questions in lieu of a cover letter. If you require accommodations so that you may participate in the selection process, please email [email protected] . Due to the volume of applicants, we will only contact applicants whose skill sets and experience meet our needs. ## DIVERSITY AND EQUITY OPPORTUNITY Greenlight America is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and an anti‑racist organization that prohibits discrimination in its governance, programs, and activities on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, reprisal, marital status, amnesty, status as a covered veteran, because all or part of an individual’s income is derived from public assistance, or for any other non‑merit‑based factor. Women, people of color, LGBTQ+ people, and members of other historically and presently disenfranchised populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Our goal is for a work experience that has meaning and impact on the world and on our professional lives, and a workplace where you can feel supported and proud. You can learn more about us at greenlightamerica.org. This position also supports Greenlight Action, an affiliated 501(c)(4) organization. While motivated by the same core values, Greenlight America and Greenlight Action operate independently of one another and each organization has its own board of directors. item.title: Senior Media Supervisor, Technology PR
item.description: Senior Media Supervisor, Technology PR Organization: DJE Holdings Location: New York, NY | Washington, DC | Austin, TX | Dallas, TX | Seattle, WA | Atlanta, GA | Chicago, IL | San Francisco, CA | Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 09/02/2026 We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions. Edelman is growing in Tech and growing fast. In the last 12 months, we’ve secured inspiring new partnerships across AI, enterprise software, cloud, data and analytics, cybersecurity, telecommunications, fintech and next‑generation hardware. We’re helping Fortune 500 companies transform how they operate and compete while supporting innovators that are redefining entire industries. Technology is our fastest‑growing sector, and we’re looking for communicators who understand both the technologies shaping the future and the conversations influencing business today. We are looking for a Senior Media Supervisor with deep expertise across enterprise and consumer technology. The ideal candidate combines strong media instincts, exceptional news judgment and a deep understanding of what makes a story timely, relevant and compelling. Thriving in fast‑moving environments, you will build relationships across business, technology and trade media, provide media counsel to clients and executives, and identify opportunities that elevate brand narratives. ### What You’ll Do Develop and execute earned media strategies for leading technology clients. Provide day‑to‑day media counsel and strategic recommendations to clients and internal teams. Drive executive visibility and thought leadership initiatives for brands and executives. Build and strengthen relationships with business, technology, trade and broadcast media. Identify timely media opportunities and develop proactive story ideas that break through the news cycle. Monitor the technology landscape to identify emerging trends and relevant industry conversations. Develop compelling narratives, media strategies and communications materials that translate complex technologies and business trends into stories that resonate with media and key audiences. Serve as a day‑to‑day client contact and help manage account operations, timelines and budgets. Mentor and support junior team members through coaching, feedback and day‑to‑day leadership. Contribute to integrated communications programs and support new business opportunities. ### Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience. 6+ years of experience in communications, public relations, marketing or a related field. ### Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting enterprise technology and/or consumer technology brands. Strong understanding of technology sectors including AI, enterprise software, cloud, cybersecurity and data and analytics. Think like a journalist; you know what makes a story newsworthy, timely and relevant. Established relationships across business, technology, trade and broadcast media, with a demonstrated ability to build new relationships as beats and coverage priorities evolve. Experience supporting executive visibility and thought leadership initiatives. Ability to provide sound media counsel to client stakeholders and executives. Strong writing, storytelling and presentation skills. Experience developing media plans and communications materials with limited oversight. Strong organizational skills, with experience managing timelines, budgets and competing priorities. Demonstrated ability to mentor junior team members and contribute to a collaborative team environment. $80,000 – $120,000 a year #LI‑JLF An employee’s pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, travel requirements, revenue‑based metrics, any contractual agreements, and business or organizational needs. The range listed is just one component of DJEH’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, a Paid Time Off policy, and region‑specific benefits. DJEH offers a wide range of benefits: medical and dental insurance, vision, 401K, life insurance, disability insurance, paid time off, travel assistance and wellness programming. DJEH is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and believes in diversity, equity, and inclusion. We seek applications from all qualified candidates without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, military and veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation in any part of the employment process, please let us know. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Digital Content Specialist
item.description: Digital Content Specialist Organization: Council of Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## Reporting to the Executive Director of Communications and Public Relations The Digital Content Specialist supports the planning, publication, and maintenance of content for the Council of Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) for use on its social‑media channels and multimedia platforms, and supports updates to CHEA’s online directories and related data‑driven content. The specialist combines editorial judgment with hands‑on digital production skills to ensure that published content is clear, accurate, timely, audience‑centered, accessible, and consistent with CHEA’s voice and standards. ## About Council for Higher Education Accreditation A national advocate and institutional voice for academic quality through accreditation, the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) is a U.S. association of degree‑granting colleges and universities and recognizes institutional and programmatic accrediting organizations. CHEA is the only national organization focused exclusively on higher education accreditation and quality assurance. ## Description ### Key Responsibilities – In collaboration with the communications staff, coordinate the organization and publishing of content across various communication channels, including email, websites, social media platforms, and printed materials. – Update webpages, including page headings, links, metadata, images, downloadable files, and related content. – Apply search‑engine‑optimization, accessibility, usability, and plain‑language practices to improve content clarity, findability, performance, and access for diverse audiences. – Assist in monitoring assigned website sections for outdated, duplicate, inconsistent, or broken content; correct routine issues and coordinate larger updates with the Web and Technology Manager and content owners. – Assist in copyediting and proofreading published content for grammar, spelling, punctuation, syntax, clarity, organization, tone, consistency, accuracy, readability, and adherence to CHEA’s editorial and brand standards. – Support in‑person and virtual events, including CHEA Webinars and the Annual Conference. – Support ongoing updates to CHEA’s online directories and related data‑driven content. – Use website, email, webinar, registration, and social‑media analytics to prepare routine reports, identify content‑performance trends, and recommend practical improvements. – Create, edit, and prepare multimedia assets—including graphics, photographs, audio, video, captions, and transcripts—and maintain organized digital files, image and media libraries, permissions and copyright records, and templates. – Carry out other duties as assigned. ### Minimum Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in digital media, marketing, web content, publishing, communications, journalism, English, or a related field. – One to three years of professional experience; relevant internships or substantial applied experience may be considered as part of the experience requirement. – Copyediting and proofreading skills, with strong command of grammar, spelling, punctuation, usage, and organization. – Demonstrated attention to detail and ability to identify factual inconsistencies, broken links, formatting issues, unclear language, and other publication‑quality concerns. – Ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines, maintain organized workflows, and collaborate professionally with colleagues at different levels of the organization. ### Preferred Qualifications – Experience using a content‑management system to build, edit, format, and publish webpages; experience with CRM platforms, Drupal; familiarity with HTML, metadata, SEO, accessibility, and web‑quality assurance is preferred. – Experience supporting email marketing, social media, webinars, virtual events, registration platforms, photography, graphic design, and video is preferred. – Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications; familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, webinar platforms, analytics tools, project‑management systems, or similar digital‑production tools is a plus. – Familiarity with Associated Press style or another professional editorial style guide. ### Employment Status All applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. New hires must complete an I‑9 Form on the first day of employment verifying their identity and employment authorization. CHEA does not sponsor applicants for work visas. ### Location This position requires an in‑office presence three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday). CHEA’s office is located at 1 Dupont Circle NW, Suite 510, Washington, DC. ### Salary $60,000 – $65,000 per year Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Analyst, Domestic Climate Policy
item.description: Policy Analyst, Domestic Climate Policy Organization: Center for American Progress Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/02/2026 ## **Position Details** **Reports to:** Associate Director, Federal Climate Policy **Staff reporting to this position:** None **Department:** Energy and Environment **Position classification:** Exempt, full time; Union – Level 4 **Compensation range:** $65,000–$78,000 per annum **Work site:** On-site (Washington, D.C., office) — ## **Summary** American Progress is seeking a Policy Analyst to join its Energy and Environment department and conduct research and analysis related to energy and climate. The ideal analyst is a team player with strong writing and project management skills; attention to detail; a commitment to addressing climate change and improving diversity, equity, and inclusion in climate and energy policy; and a willingness to work on a wide range of policy issues. The position reports to the Associate Director of Federal Climate Policy on the Climate and Energy team. — ## **Responsibilities** – **Research and analysis** — Conduct quantitative and qualitative research; analyze pending state and federal legislative proposals, administrative policies, and regulatory changes; and provide research support for members of the Energy and Environment department. – **Collaboration** — Partner with organizations, researchers, advocates, and internal policy teams to advance research and policy priorities. – **Writing** — Develop, implement, and manage the production, drafting, and distribution of projects including, but not limited to, reports, issue briefs, columns, social media posts, fact sheets, and other articles across different timelines. – **Communication** — Represent American Progress in external meetings, such as with Capitol Hill staff, diverse coalition partners, and media contacts, to advance the organization’s work. – **Subject matter expertise** — Develop and maintain expertise in assigned areas of responsibility, particularly in the power sector. – **Administration** — Assist in the coordination and planning of meetings and events, as well as issue-based coalition work, as needed. – **Other duties** — Perform other duties as assigned. — ## **Requirements and Qualifications** – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. – At least three years of professional experience in energy and/or climate policy or a related field, or a master’s degree, is preferred. A combination of education, internships, activist roles, and volunteer work will be considered. – Knowledge of energy and/or climate issues and the legislative and administrative policymaking process, as well as the ability to innovate and work across issue domains. – Quantitative skills, such as the ability to work with large datasets and understand graphs and charts, and attention to detail. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate policy matters to a nonpolicy audience. – Ability to independently manage projects from conception to completion, including planning, execution, and coordination with internal and external partners. – Ability to work under and meet deadlines on multiple simultaneous projects in a team setting. – Commitment to treating all partners with courtesy and respecting those of different cultural backgrounds. – Commitment to American Progress’ mission and goals, particularly progressive values such as environmental and social justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion. — ## **Application Requirements** Applicants must submit a cover letter with their application and include, in a single PDF document, responses to the following prompts: **1.** What are the most important considerations for the growing uptake of clean energy in our economy? (Maximum word count: 250) **2.** In a few short sentences, please provide examples of software applications or programs you have used for analyzing or presenting data. American Progress offers a full and competitive benefits package. Candidates from diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. ** Apply Now ** This announcement will remain posted until the position is filled. No phone calls, please. Please note that only those individuals whose qualifications match the current needs of this position will be considered applicants and will receive responses from American Progress. **This is not a remote position.** Thank you for your interest in American Progress. — ## **Additional Information** American Progress operates two separate nonprofit organizations to maximize the progressive agenda: the Center for American Progress and the Center for American Progress Action Fund. This job posting refers collectively to the two organizations under the name “American Progress.” The Center for American Progress is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) tax-exempt research and educational institute. It undertakes research, public education, and a limited amount of lobbying. The Center for American Progress Action Fund is a nonpartisan 501(c)(4) tax-exempt organization dedicated to achieving progress through action. It works to transform progressive ideas into policy through rapid-response communications, legislative action, grassroots organizing, political advocacy, and partnerships with other progressive leaders. The organizations share office space and employees. American Progress is dedicated to promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion. Diversity is more than a commitment at American Progress—it is the foundation of what we do. American Progress recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, sex, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, color, marital status, veteran status, medical condition, and all the other characteristics that make us unique. For more information on the Center for American Progress, please go to [www.americanprogress.org]. For more information on the Center for American Progress Action Fund, please go to [www.americanprogressaction.org]. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
