item.title: Manager, State Growth and Government Outreach
item.description: Manager, State Growth and Government Outreach Organization: Hitachi Location: Santa Clara, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/04/2026 ## About Hitachi America, Ltd. Hitachi America, Ltd. is the regional headquarters for Hitachi Group companies in the Americas, overseeing the U.S., Canada, and Latin America markets. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Hitachi Americas has been deeply committed to its Social Innovation Business since its establishment in 1959, addressing society’s most pressing challenges through innovative solutions. Leveraging its expertise and resources, Hitachi Americas and its subsidiary companies operate across diverse sectors, including transportation, energy, mobility, industrial manufacturing, healthcare, digital engineering, data analytics and others. Driven by Digital, Green, and Innovation, Hitachi Americas remains at the forefront of pioneering solutions that shape the future. For further details, please visit [https://www.hitachi.us/] ## About Hitachi, Ltd. Through its Social Innovation Business (SIB) that brings together IT, OT (Operational Technology) and products, Hitachi aims to be a global leader in continuously transforming social infrastructure through digital, contributing to a harmonized society where the environment, wellbeing, and economic growth are in balance. Hitachi operates worldwide across four sectors – Digital Systems & Services, Energy, Mobility, and Connective Industries – as well as a Strategic SIB Business Unit focused on new growth areas. With Lumada at its core, Hitachi creates value by combining data, technology and domain knowledge to solve customer and social challenges. Revenues for FY2025 (ended March 31, 2026) totaled 10,586.7 billion yen, with 606 consolidated subsidiaries and approximately 290,000 employees worldwide. Visit us at [www.hitachi.com] ## Summary The Manager, State Growth & Government Outreach drives Hitachi’s growth across priority U.S. states by integrating government engagement, policy insight, market intelligence, and business development into a unified state growth strategy. This role serves as a strategic liaison between government stakeholders and Hitachi business units, helping identify, develop, and advance opportunities that support long-term growth objectives. The position also provides executive reporting, pipeline management, and stakeholder engagement support to ensure alignment across Hitachi Group companies. ## Responsibilities ### Government Relations & Strategy • Build relationships with governors’ offices, state agencies, economic development organizations, and local government leaders. • Monitor policy, regulatory, funding, and economic development trends impacting Hitachi businesses. • Align government engagement strategies and messaging across Hitachi Group companies. • Identify emerging public-sector opportunities that support growth initiatives. ### State Growth & Business Development • Partner with Hitachi business units to identify, shape, and advance growth opportunities across priority states. • Support infrastructure, energy, mobility, digital, manufacturing, and government-funded initiatives. • Develop state engagement plans and recommend priority markets based on growth potential, funding availability, and strategic alignment. • Facilitate connections with key government, industry, and economic development stakeholders. ### Pipeline Management & Business Intelligence • Manage and track a portfolio of state-level opportunities through Salesforce and other approved systems. • Monitor pipeline performance, stakeholder engagement, and strategic growth initiatives. • Provide data-driven insights, KPI reporting, and recommendations to leadership. ### Executive Reporting & Communications • Prepare executive briefings, strategic updates, leadership reports, and stakeholder communications. • Develop concise summaries of business opportunities, policy developments, and growth initiatives. • Coordinate reporting and information sharing across Hitachi Group companies. ### Stakeholder Engagement • Lead strategic events, including Hitachi Day and executive engagement activities in priority states. • Represent Hitachi at government, economic development, and industry forums. • Support executive visits and relationship-building activities with public-sector leaders. ## Qualifications / Requirements • 8–10+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, economic development, business development, or state/local government relations. • Proven success building relationships with government leaders, economic development organizations, and public-sector stakeholders. • Strong understanding of how government engagement drives business growth, market access, investment, and strategic partnerships. • Experience supporting infrastructure, energy, transportation, digital, manufacturing, or technology-related initiatives preferred. • Demonstrated ability to work across diverse business units and functions while managing strategic opportunities, CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), and executive reporting. • Strong analytical, communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate policy and market developments into actionable business insights. • Highly organized, able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment, and willing to travel as needed to support growth initiatives. ## Compensation **For California only (SB 1162):** A good faith estimate of the expected salary for this position in our California office is **$126,648 – $158,310**. Pay is determined based on factors including depth of experience. Employees are eligible for Hitachi America’s variable pay program. **For New York City and the DC area:** Expected salary: **$126,648 – $158,310**. This range represents the Company’s good-faith estimate at the time of posting. Pay is determined based on factors including depth of experience. Employees are eligible for Hitachi America’s variable pay program. **For all other remote locations:** Salary range: **$101,318 – $126,648**. This range represents the Company’s good-faith estimate at the time of posting. Pay is determined based on factors including depth of experience. Employees are eligible for Hitachi America’s variable pay program. ## Benefits Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k), vacation, paid sick days, and other company-sponsored benefits. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE) – Females/Minorities/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job at Hitachi, please send the nature of the request and contact information to [email protected] . Queries other than accommodation requests will not be responded to. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Government Relations
item.description: Director of Government Relations Organization: Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/04/2026 ## About the Job ## About the BCSE The Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE) is a coalition of companies and trade associations that deploy clean energy and decarbonization solutions, with a sector focus on energy efficiency, natural gas, renewable energy, energy storage, sustainable transportation, and other technologies. BCSE advocates for policies that support a diverse portfolio of energy options in the United States and expand access to affordable, reliable, and clean and efficient energy solutions. Established in 1992, BCSE members include investor-owned utilities, public power, independent power producers, project developers, technology providers, equipment manufacturers, environmental and energy market service companies, and trade associations. BCSE is a member-driven organization that develops policy positions and advocacy strategies through active member committees and direct engagement with policymakers and stakeholders. For more information, visit bcse.org. ## About the Director of Government Relations Position BCSE is seeking a Director of Government Relations to lead the coalition’s education and advocacy on federal and state policy. This position will serve as a senior member of a small, highly collaborative team and will work directly with BCSE leadership, member companies and associations, policymakers, regulators, and allied organizations to advance the coalition’s policy priorities. The position is based in Washington, DC. ### Responsibilities include: – Support BCSE’s federal and state government relations portfolio, including education, advocacy, legislative engagement, regulatory strategy, and stakeholder outreach. – Manage BCSE member policy committees, including developing work plans, setting agendas, preparing materials, facilitating meetings, inviting and coordinating guest speakers and outreach activities. – Work with BCSE leadership and members to identify policy objectives that reflect the coalition’s diverse membership and advance durable market opportunities for sustainable energy solutions. – Develop and implement education and advocacy strategies, including policymaker outreach, briefings, coalition letters, comments, testimony, talking points, policy memos, and stakeholder events. – Monitor, analyze, and communicate federal and state legislative and regulatory developments affecting BCSE members, identifying emerging risks, opportunities, and recommended courses of action. – Represent BCSE in external coalitions, trade association working groups, regulatory stakeholder processes, conferences, briefings, and public forums. – Coordinate BCSE engagement with Congress and federal agencies and executive branch officials on energy, tax, environmental, infrastructure, appropriations, permitting, market, and related policy matters. – Develop and maintain relationships with state policymakers, regional organizations, and other relevant state and regional stakeholders, as necessary. – Represent BCSE in external coalitions, conferences, briefings, and public forums, as needed. – Prepare clear, concise issue summaries, presentations, and advocacy materials that translate legislative, regulatory, and market issues for members and policymakers. – Support compliance with applicable lobbying, ethics, and reporting requirements in coordination with BCSE leadership and advisors. ## Qualifications Qualified candidates should have three to five years of experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, energy policy, or a closely related field, with meaningful experience at both the federal and state levels. Experience with federal and state legislative and regulatory processes and the ability to assess how state and regional developments interact with federal policy and energy markets. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare persuasive policy materials and communicate complex issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Strong judgment, political awareness, discretion, and the ability to identify when issues require rapid escalation or senior-level engagement. Ability to manage multiple complex policy matters simultaneously, prioritize effectively, meet deadlines, and operate with a high degree of independence in a small-team environment. Collaborative working style, attention to detail, and willingness to contribute across functions when needed. ## Compensation and Benefits This is a full-time, in-person position. Compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. BCSE offers paid annual leave, participation in its 401(k) retirement program, and other benefits. ## Application Process Please submit your application at the following link, where you will be asked to upload a resume and cover letter: [ https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfaQDt-69x2XiTKq-PHrQ5UnX6Tyf4RRlnooPmCuUTpz-PCYQ/viewform?usp=header ] Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. item.title: Director, Congressional Affairs
item.description: Director, Congressional Affairs Organization: American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/04/2026 Director, Congressional Affairs The American Academy of Dermatology is seeking a Director, Congressional Affairs located in our Washington, DC office responsible for leading the Academy’s federal legislative team in the development and implementation of federal legislative policy goals, objectives, and related strategies to promote the Academy’s advocacy priorities. Partner and collaborate with staff to pursue strategies to engage Academy leadership and members to advance the interests of dermatology, dermatologists, practices, and patients. Contribute to planning and implementing Academy strategic initiatives including working collaboratively across the organization to further the Academy’s mission by integrating congressional activities with those of the Advocacy & Policy division and the Academy. Participate in the overall management, direction, and success of the Advocacy & Policy Division. About Us: The American Academy of Dermatology (Academy), founded in 1938, is the largest, most influential, and most representative of all dermatologic associations. A sister organization to the Academy, the American Academy of Dermatology Association is the resource for government affairs, health policy and practice information for dermatologists, and plays a major role in formulating policies that can enhance the quality of dermatologic care. With a membership of more than 21,000 members worldwide, the Academy is committed to: advancing the diagnosis and medical, surgical, and cosmetic treatment of the skin, hair, and nails; advocating high standards in clinical practice, education, and research in dermatology; and supporting and enhancing patient care for a lifetime of healthier skin. To learn more about the Academy please visit our website at [www.aad.org], or follow us on these social media outlets: – **Facebook** [www.facebook.com/aadskin] – **TikTok** [www.tiktok.com/@AADskin] – **Pinterest** [www.pinterest.com/AADskin] – **Instagram** [www.instagram.com/aadskin1] Responsibilities: – **Federal legislative leadership** — Lead the Academy’s federal legislative activities and team, including lobbying consultants. Generate, identify, and prioritize policy-related issues that impact the Academy and its members. Monitor and direct lobbying efforts for all federal legislation that has the potential to affect dermatologic care, patients, and practices. Accountable for accurate and timely filing of required lobbying disclosure reports. – **Federal advocacy development** — Develop federal advocacy positions, working with physician leaders and staff, and based on available research of issues related to dermatology and the broader health care environment. Direct and manage the drafting of policy statements and legislative language as needed. – **SkinPAC collaboration** — Collaborate with Associate Director, Advocacy Engagement to develop and execute strategies and initiatives related to the Academy’s political action committee (SkinPAC) disbursements to federal candidates. – **Congressional education** — Educate Members of Congress and key staff regarding the Academy’s position on relevant issues. Establish and maintain liaison with key congressional staff, medical specialty and state societies, dermatology subspecialty groups, patient groups, and other organizations responsible for and interested in policies and programs that affect the practice of dermatology. Cultivate, facilitate, and coordinate member contacts with Members of Congress and key staff. Represent the AADA at political events and other relevant outside activities. – **Grassroots outreach** — Partner with Associate Director, Advocacy Engagement on AADA’s grassroots outreach and development program. Collaborate with AADA staff to execute the annual Legislative Conference. – **Policy drafting** — Draft and/or contribute to Academy policy statements, legislative testimony, and regulatory comments when appropriate. Respond to inquiries from Congress, government agencies or other organizations or individuals as appropriate. Respond to requests and inquiries from members of the Academy. Work with Communications Department to report on legislative and political activities to membership and respond to related media inquiries. – **Leadership reporting** — Present and report to Academy leadership through regular written updates and through other venues, including conference calls, in-person meetings, state society meetings as needed and appropriate, on pertinent issues and developments. – **Strategic collaboration** — Collaborate with Senior Vice President, Advocacy & Policy in the assessment and development of strategic and financial goals that relate to Advocacy & Policy and the overall Academy mission. Develop and execute approved plans targeted to business strategies and initiatives. Requirements: – **Education requirements** — Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree preferred, preferably in political science, public administration, health policy, or related field. – **Advocacy experience** — Minimum twelve years relevant experience with government and/or private sector advocacy is required. – **Health policy knowledge** — Demonstrated knowledge of health policy and government affairs. – **Congressional experience** — Experience in a federal congressional office preferred. – **Managerial experience** — Demonstrated progressive managerial experience required. – **Congressional relationships** — Extensive experience and established relationships working with members of Congress and their staff, in particular with key health care committees. – **Health care policy expertise** — Experience working on complex health care policy issues, with a working knowledge of Medicare, health system reform and appropriations preferred. – **Lobbying compliance** — Knowledge of relevant LDA rules and filing requirements for lobbying essential. – **People management** — Minimum of 8 years of people management including leading, mentoring, and coaching direct and indirect reports. – **Collaboration** — Establishes and maintains effective work relationships, works cooperatively in group situations. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. – **Communication** — Apply effective verbal, nonverbal, and written communication methods to achieve desired results. Respond intelligently to standard business correspondence. Demonstrate sufficient business vocabulary to communicate effectively. – **Decision making** — Able to exercise discretion and independent judgment to understand issues, identify problems and opportunities to determine the appropriate course of action. Demonstrate sound decision-making skills with an increasing number of alternatives to be reviewed by management. – **Evaluation of results** — Assess how well workplace performance, learning strategies, and results match organizational goals and strategic intent. – **Finance and accounting** — Assist with preparing, managing, and monitoring budget and expenses. – **Integrity** — Demonstrate personal integrity in all interactions. Ability to maintain confidentiality. – **Leadership** — Lead, influence, and coach others to help them achieve desired results. Consider and respond appropriately to the needs and feelings of others; treat others equitably. – **Strategic development** — Create strategies and contingency plans that allow the organization to have a competitive advantage. We offer a competitive compensation plan and benefits package including medical/dental/vision/life insurance as well as a matching retirement contribution, tuition reimbursement, bonus program, pension plan, paid vacation/medical/personal days, work-life balance, recognition program and casual work environment. More information about our compensation and benefits can be reviewed on the detailed job ad on our website. The Academy offers a hybrid work environment; providing time in the office for in-person collaboration and the opportunity to work remotely for focus time. We are building a workplace where our employees are excited to come to work every day because of the culture that we are creating together — one of respect, transparency, and collaboration. A workplace in which we demonstrate care and commitment, celebration, community, and focused learning that contributes to the mission of advancing excellence in dermatologic care. For immediate consideration please apply online at [ www.aad.org ], scroll to the bottom of the page and follow the Employment link. EOE M/F/D/V Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Model Policy Manager
item.description: Model Policy Manager Organization: OpenAI Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 09/05/2026 ## About the Team The Safety Systems team is at the forefront of OpenAI’s mission to build and deploy safe AGI, driving our commitment to AI safety and fostering a culture of trust and transparency. The Model Policy team aligns model behavior with desired human values and norms. We co‑design policy with models and for models by driving rapid policy taxonomy iteration based on data and defining evaluation criteria for foundational models’ ability to reason about safety. Key focus areas include: catastrophic risk, mental health, teen safety, and multimodal safety. ## About the Role Providing access to frontier AI systems raises complex questions around dual‑use science and catastrophic risk. How should models respond to requests involving chemical synthesis, biological experimentation, or pathogen research? Where is the boundary between legitimate scientific inquiry and information that could enable misuse? How do we design policies that meaningfully reduce risk without unnecessarily restricting beneficial research? This is a senior role in which you’ll help shape policy creation and development at OpenAI for addressing biological and chemical risks. You will develop structured policy frameworks and taxonomies to guide safe model behavior. This role sits at the intersection of biosecurity expertise, AI safety research, and policy design. You will help ensure that frontier AI systems can support beneficial life sciences research, such as drug discovery, public health, and biosafety, while reducing the risk that these capabilities could be misused. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. ## In this role, you’ll: – Design and maintain model policies governing chemical and biological risk, defining how models should safely handle dual‑use scenarios. – Develop structured taxonomies of chemical and biological risk that inform model training data, evaluation benchmarks, and safety monitoring systems. – Translate biosecurity and chemical security expertise into actionable model behavior, working closely with research and engineering teams to operationalize policy in training and evaluation pipelines. – Develop a broad range of subject matter expertise while maintaining agility across topics. – Identify emerging risk vectors where frontier AI capabilities could meaningfully lower barriers to harmful activity and develop mitigation strategies. – Engage with internal and external subject‑matter experts in biosecurity, biodefense, and chemical safety to ensure policies reflect real‑world risk landscapes. ## You might thrive in this role if you: – Have strong domain expertise in chemistry, biology, biosecurity, or related fields and are motivated to translate that expertise into principled, operational policies that scale to Frontier AI systems. – Have experience researching LLMs, ML, AI, tech policy, moral reasoning, and/or enjoy classification problems. – Have extensive experience defining, refining, and enforcing policies for ML models across training, evaluation, and deployment. – Are comfortable navigating ambiguous, high‑stakes problem spaces, balancing risk reduction with the benefits of scientific openness and innovation. – Can reason about the benefits and risks of open‑ended problem spaces, generate novel approaches under ambiguity, and take full ownership of end‑to‑end solutions from concept through execution. – Have experience working at the intersection of science, policy, or emerging technology, such as in life sciences research, national security, risk analysis, technology policy, or AI safety. ## Most relevant publications: – Introducing HealthBench – Preparing for future AI capabilities in biology – Safety evaluations hub – OpenAI GPT5 System Card – Evaluating Fairness in ChatGPT – Improving Model Safety Behavior with Rule‑Based Rewards – OpenAI Model Spec ## About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general‑purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US‑based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non‑public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non‑compliant, please submit a report. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. item.title: Government Partnerships Communications Lead
item.description: Government Partnerships Communications Lead Organization: OpenAI Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/05/2026 ## About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general‑purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. Our Communications team includes External Communications, Internal Communications, and other strategic communications functions. The team’s role is to clearly and authentically explain our technology, values, and approach to safely building powerful AI. ## About the Role We are seeking an exceptional communications professional to lead communications support for OpenAI’s partnerships with federal, state, and local governments and our broader public‑sector enterprise work. This person will help tell the story of how governments are using AI, support major customer and partner moments, and communicate about government work happening across priority areas including cybersecurity, biodefense, national security, and science. This role will partner closely with public‑sector go‑to‑market and partnerships, Global Affairs, legal, product, research, safety, and security teams to develop clear external communications for the public, media, policymakers, and customers. The ideal candidate will bring strong strategic and tactical communications judgment, move quickly and collaboratively on complex issues, and have a passion for technology and storytelling. ## In This Role, You Will – **Develop communications plans** that educate press, policymakers, customers, and the public about OpenAI’s government partnerships and public‑sector work. – **Build proactive campaigns** and customer stories that demonstrate how AI can improve public services, strengthen government workforces, and support critical missions. – **Support communications** across priority areas including cybersecurity, biodefense, national security, and science. – **Build media relationships** with national, state, local, technology, policy, and enterprise outlets and manage inbound requests. – **Partner cross‑functionally** with Global Affairs, public‑sector go‑to‑market, legal, product, research, safety, security, and other teams. – **Provide counsel** and communications support to senior leaders and partners across interviews, speeches, events, and other public moments. – **Anticipate communications risks** and develop thoughtful mitigation and response strategies. ## You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have – 7+ years of professional communications and media relations experience, including work on government, enterprise technology, national security, cybersecurity, biodefense, or other highly scrutinized issues. – A strong track record of driving media campaigns in support of policy, partnership, or business priorities. – Experience translating complex technical and policy work into clear, credible external narratives. – Proven success building relationships and collaborating with press, executives, government partners, and cross‑functional teams. – Strong political and policy judgment, high ownership, and comfort operating quickly in an environment with limited structure. ## Workplace & Location This role is based in Washington, DC, and will require occasional travel. ## About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general‑purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US‑based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss, or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non‑public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non‑compliant, please submit a report. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. ## OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. item.title: Associate Director, Global Intranet Communications and Change
item.description: Associate Director, Global Intranet Communications and Change Organization: Eli Lilly & Co. Location: Indianapolis, IN Date Posted: 09/05/2026 At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life‑changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work — but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life‑changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world. This is a rare seat at the table — shape a global employee intranet from the ground up. The Associate Director, Global Intranet Communications and Change leads the communications and change communications strategy for the transformation of Lilly’s global employee intranet, which serves more than 50,000 employees across 70 countries. This is a fixed‑duration, two‑year assignment that begins as the platform vendor is selected and guides the program through platform design and build to a metrics‑driven global launch. This role owns the end‑to‑end communications approach for the program. It shapes the employee experience from the communications side of platform design, leads the change communications that build organizational readiness across leaders and stakeholders, drives adoption among the employees who will use the platform every day, and ensures a seamless launch measured against clear success metrics. Reporting to the Executive Director of Internal Communications, the Associate Director serves as the dedicated communications and change communications lead on the core program team, working at the intersection of communications, human resources, technology, and user experience, and collaborating closely across Lilly’s global communications teams to translate a complex technology transformation into a clear, motivating story for the enterprise. A faster, better‑connected global workforce means faster, clearer decisions in service of the patients Lilly’s work ultimately reaches. — ### Key Objectives / Deliverables #### Communications Strategy and Platform Design Partnership Own the overall communications strategy for the new global intranet, defining the narrative, audience approach, and channel plan from platform design through launch and into early operations. Serve as the communications and employee‑experience voice in platform design and configuration, translating the program’s design principles into practical requirements and advocating for a global workforce before adoption barriers emerge. Partner with the program manager, business owner, technology, user experience, and the selected vendor and implementation partner to align communications and change milestones with the technical delivery plan. #### Change Management Communications Own the enterprise change communications strategy, developing the messages, campaigns, and content that prepare leaders, the 200‑plus editor community, and employees for new ways of working, new governance, and a new platform, and keeping the program sponsors aligned through key decision points. Lead the change management program for the global communications team, guiding communicators through the new platform, editorial tools, workflows, and ways of working so the team is ready to operate confidently at launch and beyond. Partner with the program’s organizational change management resource to turn the change plan and readiness milestones into clear, well‑timed communications for each audience, owning the communications discipline that supports the broader change management approach. #### User Adoption and Engagement Design and lead the adoption strategy for everyone who will use the intranet, from knowledge workers to frontline and deskless colleagues, with campaigns that drive sustained use of its news, search, personalization, and artificial intelligence capabilities. Establish refreshed editorial and publishing guidelines and a refined playbook, alongside plain‑language onboarding and training, that set content editors and employees up to succeed in a new era of technology and ways of working, in partnership with the training lead. Build feedback loops that capture employee and editor signals before, during, and after launch to continuously improve adoption, accounting for accessibility, language, and local needs across Lilly’s global affiliates and multilingual translation model. #### Launch Readiness and Measurement Own the communications and change dimensions of launch readiness, coordinating a seamless go‑live so every audience knows what is changing and how to be successful day one. Define and own the measurement framework, establishing baselines, metrics, and reporting cadences for awareness, adoption, engagement, and satisfaction, in partnership with technology, human resources analytics, and platform owners, and translate the data into clear insights for the program team and governance. Support a clean transition to the ongoing support model at the close of the assignment, handing off the measurement framework, adoption playbook, and editor engagement approach to Enterprise Communications and the business owner. — ### Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing, Organizational Change, or a related field. 7 years of experience in internal or employee communications, change management, or a combination of the two, including demonstrated experience leading communications or change for a large‑scale technology, platform, or digital transformation. Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full‑time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F‑1 CPT, F‑1 OPT, F‑1 STEM OPT, J‑1, H‑1B, TN, O‑1, E‑3, H‑1B1, or L‑1. — ### Other Qualifications Demonstrated experience leading change communications for enterprise programs, including familiarity with established change management frameworks and the ability to partner effectively with a dedicated change management function. Experience leading technology or platform adoption communications, including change management and employee‑facing rollout programs at scale. Demonstrated ability to build and manage communications and adoption measurement frameworks, including familiarity with digital analytics platforms and employee listening tools. Experience partnering across communications, human resources, and information technology functions in a large, matrixed, global organization. Familiarity with intranet, employee experience, or enterprise content platforms, and with the realities of global rollouts across multiple languages and geographies. Familiarity with life sciences or pharmaceutical environments strongly preferred. This is a fixed‑duration, two‑year employee assignment, scoped through go‑live and an initial post‑launch stabilization period. Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (for example, H‑1B or TN status) for this employment position. — ### Additional Skills / Preferences Change Communications Expertise: Deep experience with the communications discipline of change management, with the judgment to sequence, pace, and land change messages across many audiences at once. Digital Platform Partnership: Ability to act as the communications and employee‑experience voice in platform design and vendor conversations, simplifying complex technology into clear value for non‑technical audiences. User Adoption and Engagement: Proven track record designing adoption strategies that move employees from awareness to sustained use, including hard‑to‑reach frontline and deskless populations. Measurement and Analytics: Comfortable building measurement frameworks from the ground up, working across multiple data sources, and translating metrics into clear stories for leadership. Editorial and Communications Craft: Strong writer with the range to move between employee‑facing content, change and readiness materials, and executive and governance reporting without losing quality or clarity. Cross‑Functional Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build alignment across communications, human resources, Tech@Lilly, and user experience, functions that do not always share the same priorities or timelines. Global and Matrixed Agility: Comfortable operating across a distributed, multi‑country organization, with the discipline to prioritize and execute in a fast‑moving program environment. Platform Fluency: Proficiency with modern intranet and internal communications platforms, including Viva Engage, Microsoft Teams, and enterprise email; familiarity with content management, translation, and analytics tools a plus. — Lilly is dedicated to helping individuals with disabilities to actively engage in the workforce, ensuring equal opportunities when vying for positions. If you require accommodation to submit a resume for a position at Lilly, please complete the accommodation request form [https://careers.lilly.com/us/en/workplace-accommodation] for further assistance.

item.title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion
item.description: Senior Manager, Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion Organization: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Location: Sleepy Hollow, NY | Warren, NJ Date Posted: 09/05/2026 **Build Our Future Together** At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life‑changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking a Senior Manager to join our Regulatory Affairs Advertising and Promotion team. This position requires the ability to apply clinical development knowledge in concert with experienced understanding of advertising and promotion regulations/guidance to the development of key product messages presented in Biologic License Applications (BLAs) and Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs). They will provide regulatory advertising and promotion expertise to relevant stakeholders, typically carrying out the responsibilities with minimal guidance from the Regulatory Affairs, Advertising and Promotion Director. The Senior Manager Regulatory Affairs, Advertising and Promotion will oversee therapeutic area(s) and ensure that messages are translated into advertising and promotion initiatives that meet the commercial team’s objectives, while maintaining the necessary state of compliance and corporate integrity. — ### When & where Work Location: Sleepy Hollow, NY or Warren, NJ 4 days per week on site — ### Discover your role – **Regulatory activities** — Management of US and Global (if applicable) regulatory activities associated with advertising and promotion of the company’s marketed products, as well as commercial development of pipeline products. Manages commercial activities from a regulatory advertising and promotion perspective with minimal guidance from the Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion Director. – **Product messaging** — Creatively advise on the development of product messages and materials across multiple functional areas. – **Regulatory guidance** — Provide timely regulatory advice and guidance, with minimal guidance from Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion Director, to Commercial teams and Medical Affairs with respect to conference exhibit activities, disease awareness and speaker programs. – **Material review** — Provide review of US and Global (if applicable) product and disease state materials/communications, with minimal guidance from Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion Director, to support corporate goals and comply with applicable laws, regulations, and guidance. – **Cross‑functional collaboration** — Collaborate cross‑functionally with key stakeholders in areas such as Marketing, Medical Affairs, and Legal. – **Partner communication** — Responsible for establishing working relationships and managing communication with regulatory advertising and promotion professionals at co‑promote partner companies. – **FDA OPDP interactions** — Help lead and assist in all interactions with the FDA Office of Prescription Drug Promotion (OPDP) for assigned company products, responsible for helping to maintain working relationship and effective communication with FDA OPDP reviewers with respect to advertising and promotion matters, including requests for advisory submissions. – **Form 2253 compliance** — Responsible for compliance with promotional material submissions to FDA on Form 2253. – **Regulatory monitoring** — Monitor the external environment to advise product teams on evolving regulatory requirements related to product and disease state communications. – **Enforcement vigilance** — Maintain vigilance with respect to FDA promotional enforcement activities; provide stakeholders with updates on a regular basis; provide guidance to stakeholders with respect to impact of enforcement activities on the company policies. – **Process improvement** — Provide input to direct management with respect to process improvement for promotional review activities and establishment of portfolio‑wide standardization of policies. – **Cross‑training** — Ability to cross‑train across products/indications to ensure continuous Regulatory A&P support is provided to stakeholders. – **Therapeutic area collaboration** — Collaboration with Regulatory Therapeutic Area Leads to review key marketing application summary documents and study reports. – **Submission input** — With minimal guidance from management, help provide input during review cycles to reflect commercialization objectives and messages in the submission documents/reports that are submitted to health authorities. – **Labeling development** — Provide input to management during labeling development and negotiation to reflect commercialization objectives and messages that impact promotion and advertising. — ### This role requires – **A minimum of 3 to 4 years** within regulatory affairs, preferably within advertising and promotion. – **Bachelor’s degree (BS)** in Life Sciences; advanced degree preferred (Masters, PharmD, PhD, MD, DO). Regulatory experience can offset education requirements. – **Advanced knowledge** of regulations, guidelines and precedents related to pharmaceutical product development and marketing, with focus in advertising and promotion. – **Experience with pharmaceutical products** required; biologics experience is a plus. – **Experience with FDA OPDP/APLB** preferred. – **Ability to review promotional materials**, interact with FDA OPDP/APLB, and manage launch products/campaigns while maintaining excellent written/verbal communication skills. – **Ability to support global promotional review**, understanding of clinical trial recruitment materials, and familiarity with labeling regulations. – **Ability to influence cross‑functional teams** and interact with senior management. #GDRAJobs — Does this sound like you? item.description: Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs Organization: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/05/2026 **Build Our Future Together** The Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs at Regeneron is responsible for advancing the company’s public policy priorities through strategic engagement with U.S. federal policymakers. In close partnership with internal stakeholders, this role cultivates relationships and engages with federal legislators, congressional staff, administration officials, and regulators to advance Regeneron’s patient‑centered, science‑driven mission. **When & where:** Work Location: Washington, D.C. Hybrid: 4 days per week on site **Discover your role:** Develop and execute strategic federal advocacy plans to advance Regeneron’s public policy priorities and initiatives, with a focus on patient access and innovation issues. Lead engagement with federal legislators, administration officials, and regulators to proactively shape policy outcomes, serving as a key advocate to House Democratic members and staff, including the Energy & Commerce Committee. Monitor and analyze relevant policy developments to provide strategic guidance and updates to internal stakeholders, leveraging strong knowledge of issues affecting the biopharmaceutical industry and policymaking processes. Partner with Regeneron Policy and Alliance leads to help internal stakeholders incorporate federal policy implications into business and corporate objectives. Engage with trade associations, various organizations, and policy influencers to shape the external environment and elevate Regeneron’s policy perspectives in collective advocacy efforts. Support development of advocacy materials, including policy content and talking points, in partnership with cross‑functional teams, as well as memoranda for senior leaders and internal stakeholders. **This role requires:** Must have a bachelor’s degree or higher in public policy, law, political science, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Minimum of 10 years relevant experience in Congress, a regulatory or policy advocacy organization, or government relations. A strong understanding of government affairs, public policy, and the patient, provider, and health care organization landscape is essential, as is knowledge of the health care system and key policies affecting the biopharmaceutical sector. Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex and changing policy and business issues to internal and external stakeholders. item.title: Director, Corporate Counsel- Corporate and Securities
item.description: Director, Corporate Counsel- Corporate and Securities Organization: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Location: Palo Alto, CA | Philadelphia, PA Date Posted: 09/05/2026 Jazz Pharmaceuticals is a global biopharma company whose purpose is to innovate to transform the lives of patients and their families. We are dedicated to developing life‑changing medicines for people with serious diseases — often with limited or no therapeutic options. We have a diverse portfolio of marketed medicines, including leading therapies for sleep disorders and epilepsy, and a growing portfolio of cancer treatments. Our patient‑focused and science‑driven approach powers pioneering research and development advancements across our robust pipeline of innovative therapeutics in oncology and neuroscience. Jazz is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland with research and development laboratories, manufacturing facilities and employees in multiple countries committed to serving patients worldwide. Please visit [www.jazzpharmaceuticals.com] for more information. ## Brief Description The Director, Corporate and Securities reports to the Executive Director, Corporate and Securities, and is a key member of the team for the Legal department. The Director, Corporate and Securities will provide leadership on a wide range of corporate, securities, and governance matters. The responsibilities will include all securities matters for a publicly traded company, including ensuring compliance with SEC and Nasdaq rules and regulations; preparing and reviewing SEC filings; assisting with matters related to the board of directors; and advising on corporate governance, investor relations, and executive compensation. ## Essential Functions / Responsibilities ### Securities and Corporate Governance Ensure compliance with federal and state securities laws, with focus on ’34 Act and ’33 Act reporting, Nasdaq compliance, Regulation FD and insider trading. Prepare and/or review all SEC filings, including Form 10‑Ks, Form 10‑Qs, Form 8‑Ks, proxy statements and Section 16 filings, as well as registration statements. Maintain governance policies and practices, including corporate governance guidelines, committee charters and other governing documents. ### Investor Relations and Executive Compensation Review, advise and assist with quarterly earnings releases, investor presentations, quarterly and annual reports, sustainability reports and other external communications. Advise on all executive compensation activities, and maintain and update form equity award agreements as well as other related activities. Support the Total Rewards team in their administration of employee compensation benefits programs. ### Other Collaborate with, advise and support a broad range of departments and functions, including finance, accounting, tax, internal audit and others as necessary. Assist with secondary support for capital markets transactions activities, including debt offerings, credit agreements, other treasury‑related matters, strategic transaction initiatives, including mergers and acquisitions support, dispositions, joint ventures and investments. Corporate governance support, including Corporate Sustainability and Social Impact / ESG. Perform additional functions and projects as assigned. ## Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Juris Doctorate (J.D.) from accredited law school; licensed to practice law in the U.S. Membership in good standing in a state bar with no prior suspensions or disciplinary history. ## Required / Preferred Education and Licenses Minimum 7 years of combined experience in‑house and/or with a law firm. Experience with a biotech or pharmaceutical company preferred. Must be self‑motivated, proactive, strategic, and exhibit excellent judgment. Ability to multi‑task, be flexible and quickly pivot in a fast‑moving/changing environment. Possess the ability and willingness to advance new ideas and recognize when decisions may have a broad impact on the global organization. Consistently take action and drive issues to closure and hold self and others accountable for achieving results. Legal analysis and advice are well thought out and accurate; potential legal and compliance issues are consistently identified. Ability to create and deliver effective oral presentations, train, and educate stakeholders and members of the department on legal topics and issues. Strong organizational and project management skills. Strategic, innovative and independent thinker who is action‑oriented and a driver of change, with strong leadership and communication skills and strong interpersonal skills. Ability to look ahead to future possibilities and translate them into breakthrough strategies. Cultivate innovation by creating new and better ways for the organization to be successful. Strong and effective communication skills, developing and delivering multi‑mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Strong ability to communicate effectively and get along well with different personality types across all levels of the Company. Drive engagement by creating a climate where people are motivated to do their best to help the organization achieve its objectives. Drive results by consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances. Instill trust by gaining the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity. #LI‑Remote Jazz Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any characteristic protected by law. ## For U.S. Based Candidates Only Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices and we strive to provide employees with total compensation packages that are market competitive. For this role, the full and complete base pay range is: $224,000.00 – $336,000.00. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, and other pertinent factors. The goal is to ensure fair and competitive compensation aligned with the candidate’s expertise and contributions, within the established pay framework and our Total Compensation philosophy. Internal equity considerations will also influence individual base pay decisions. This range will be reviewed on a regular basis. At Jazz, your base pay is only one part of your total compensation package. The successful candidate may also be eligible for a discretionary annual cash bonus or incentive compensation (depending on the role), in accordance with the terms of the Company’s Global Cash Bonus Plan or Incentive Compensation Plan, as well as discretionary equity grants in accordance with Jazz’s Long Term Equity Incentive Plan. The successful candidate will also be eligible to participate in various benefits offerings, including, but not limited to, medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k retirement savings plan, and flexible paid vacation. For more information on our Benefits offerings please click here: [https://careers.jazzpharma.com/benefits.html] Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director, Sr. Corporate Counsel, IP
item.description: Senior Director, Sr. Corporate Counsel, IP Organization: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Location: Palo Alto, CA | Philadelphia, PA Date Posted: 09/05/2026 Jazz Pharmaceuticals is a global biopharma company whose purpose is to innovate to transform the lives of patients and their families. We are dedicated to developing life‑changing medicines for people with serious diseases — often with limited or no therapeutic options. We have a diverse portfolio of marketed medicines, including leading therapies for sleep disorders and epilepsy, and a growing portfolio of cancer treatments. Our patient‑focused and science‑driven approach powers pioneering research and development advancements across our robust pipeline of innovative therapeutics in oncology and neuroscience. Jazz is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland with research and development laboratories, manufacturing facilities and employees in multiple countries committed to serving patients worldwide. Please visit [www.jazzpharmaceuticals.com] for more information. The Senior Director, Corporate Counsel, Intellectual Property (IP), will develop and execute robust global patent and IP strategies for Jazz’s products, product candidates, platform technologies, and newly acquired or licensed assets, ensuring alignment with corporate growth objectives and maximizing the value of the company’s innovation portfolio. In addition, the Sr. Corporate Counsel, IP will play a critical role in supporting Jazz’s corporate development objectives by leading intellectual property due diligence, integration planning, and strategic portfolio development across acquisitions, licensing transactions, collaborations, and other strategic business opportunities. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor to Corporate Development, R&D, Business Development, and senior leadership, providing sophisticated IP analyses that inform transaction structures, valuation, risk assessment, and post‑transaction integration strategies. Initially, this position reports directly to the VP of Legal & IP. ## Key Job Responsibilities Serve as a critical IP advisor to Corporate Development teams, providing strategic support for acquisitions, licensing transactions, collaborations, joint ventures, divestitures, and other strategic transactions. Conduct comprehensive IP due diligence for potential acquisitions, in‑licensing opportunities, collaborations, and strategic partnerships, including freedom‑to‑operate evaluations, portfolio strength analyses, exclusivity assessments, and identification of material IP risks and value drivers. Prepare and communicate clear, actionable diligence findings and recommendations to executive leadership, transaction teams, and legal leadership to support decision‑making, valuation, negotiation strategy, and transaction structuring. Partner closely with Transformation Office and cross‑functional stakeholders to develop and execute post‑transaction integration strategies, including patent portfolio optimization, ownership alignment, prosecution strategy harmonization, and identification of opportunities to enhance long‑term asset value. Develop and execute sophisticated global patent strategies that support business objectives, strengthen competitive positioning and exclusivity, and maximize the value of both internally developed and externally acquired or licensed assets. Build and manage high‑value global patent portfolios from invention capture through patent issuance and lifecycle management, ensuring alignment with product development and commercialization strategies. Provide strategic input into transaction documents, including licensing agreements, collaboration agreements, acquisition agreements, due diligence reports, representations and warranties, IP covenants, and integration‑related provisions. Build effective partnerships with stakeholders across research, development, commercial, regulatory, business development, and corporate development functions to deliver practical, business‑focused IP advice. Conduct freedom‑to‑operate, infringement, validity, patentability, and competitive landscape analyses and develop risk mitigation strategies in support of business objectives. Effectively manage outside counsel supporting patent prosecution, IP due diligence, litigation, opinions, and other strategic matters to ensure high‑quality, efficient, and commercially focused outcomes. Counsel senior management and cross‑functional teams on intellectual property risks, opportunities, exclusivity strategies, competitive positioning, and portfolio optimization initiatives. Review publications, presentations, press releases, and other public disclosures to protect patent rights and support external communication strategies. Advise on and/or lead contentious and adversarial matters involving company assets, including patent litigation, IPRs, PGRs, European oppositions, and related proceedings. Lead and contribute to departmental initiatives aimed at enhancing IP operations, diligence capabilities, portfolio management processes, and overall organizational effectiveness. ## Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Fully qualified U.S. Patent Attorney or Agent with 10+ years of relevant intellectual property experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, including substantial in‑house experience supporting corporate development, licensing, collaborations, mergers and acquisitions, or other strategic transactions. Undergraduate degree in biological sciences, biochemistry, chemistry, or another discipline relevant to pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, or life sciences; advanced degree preferred. Significant experience leading IP due diligence for acquisitions, licensing transactions, collaborations, venture investments, and other strategic corporate transactions. Demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and maximizing the value of acquired or licensed patent portfolios and intellectual property assets. Deep expertise in patent portfolio development, lifecycle management, exclusivity strategies, freedom‑to‑operate analyses, and competitive intelligence. Ability to work in dynamic, fast‑paced team environment; flexible and responsive self‑starter who can operate independently as well as collaboratively across the business. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to distill complex legal and scientific concepts into clear business recommendations for senior executives. Strategic thinker who anticipates business challenges, identifies opportunities to create and protect enterprise value, and develops creative, practical solutions. Proven ability to influence decision‑making across cross‑functional teams and build trusted partnerships with executives, researchers, commercial leaders, and corporate development professionals. Strong project management, prioritization, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple high‑impact initiatives simultaneously. Experience in patent litigation, post‑grant proceedings, oppositions, and other adversarial matters is a plus. #LI-Remote Jazz Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any characteristic protected by law. ## FOR US BASED CANDIDATES ONLY Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices and we strive to provide employees with total compensation packages that are market competitive. For this role, the full and complete base pay range is: $259,200.00 – $388,800.00 Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, and other pertinent factors. The goal is to ensure fair and competitive compensation aligned with the candidate’s expertise and contributions, within the established pay framework and our Total Compensation philosophy. Internal equity considerations will also influence individual base pay decisions. This range will be reviewed on a regular basis. At Jazz, your base pay is only one part of your total compensation package. The successful candidate may also be eligible for a discretionary annual cash bonus or incentive compensation (depending on the role), in accordance with the terms of the Company’s Global Cash Bonus Plan or Incentive Compensation Plan, as well as discretionary equity grants in accordance with Jazz’s Long Term Equity Incentive Plan. The successful candidate will also be eligible to participate in various benefits offerings, including, but not limited to, medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k retirement savings plan, and flexible paid vacation. For more information on our Benefits offerings please click here: [https://careers.jazzpharma.com/benefits.html] Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Digital Marketing Strategist
item.description: Senior Digital Marketing Strategist Organization: Stanley Consultants Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 09/05/2026 # Stanley Consultants Stanley Consultants is an award-winning and industry-leading global consulting engineering firm, with an unmatched commitment to culture, values, and ethics. We are dedicated to client experience and solve the most complex challenges to create a sustainable, connected, and enriched world for all. As the world changes, Stanley strategically evolves with it, integrating the latest technology, innovation, and resiliency practices. With over a century of experience serving the energy, federal government, transportation, and water sectors, we have helped improve lives and shape the infrastructure systems that connect us. As an employee-owned organization with a People First approach, we stand apart from other engineering consulting and services firms. At Stanley, your voice counts, your growth matters, and your success is our success. Stanley Consultants offers flexible work options, competitive pay and great benefits, a strong sense of community, and the chance to build a meaningful, long-term career! — ## Job Title: Senior Digital Marketing Strategist Location: Denver, CO (Centennial) Job Type: Hybrid Requisition ID: 11323 — ## Job Summary The Senior Digital Marketing Strategist is responsible for creating and managing integrated organic and paid media campaigns across multiple digital marketing channels including search engines, social media platforms and web. This role combines strategic campaign planning with hands-on content creation and cross-channel execution. The ideal candidate will develop compelling campaign content that aligns with market and business priorities; collaborate closely with Graphic Design, Digital Marketing and internal stakeholders to develop campaign visuals and measure campaign success; manage campaign refreshes to maintain relevance; and drive consistent brand voice across all marketing touchpoints. This position requires staying current with campaign best practices, AI search trends and integrating digital strategies with the overall marketing plan to drive measurable results. — ## What You Will Be Doing – Develop integrated organic and paid campaign strategies across Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising (Bing), LinkedIn and other relevant digital platforms. – Lead campaign creation and management, including the development of ad copy, messaging frameworks and campaign themes that align with business development objectives and market sector priorities. – Collaborate with the Graphic Design team to develop campaign visuals, ensuring creative assets align with campaign messaging and brand guidelines. – Manage campaign refreshes and optimization cycles to keep content current, maintain engagement and improve performance across all channels. – Coordinate cross-channel campaign launches, ensuring consistent brand voice and messaging across search, social media, email, display and other digital touchpoints. – Align campaign content and strategy with market trends, competitive landscape and business priorities through regular consultation with internal stakeholders. – Collaborate with the Digital Marketing team to monitor and optimize campaign performance using Google Analytics, platform-specific analytics and other marketing tools to meet ROI objectives. – Stay current with digital marketing best practices, platform updates, algorithm changes and emerging trends in paid and organic campaign management. – Conduct A/B testing on campaign content, ad creative, landing pages and targeting strategies to continuously improve performance. — ## Required Qualifications ### Education Bachelor’s degree in marketing, digital communications, advertising or related field. ### Experience 7+ years of progressive digital marketing experience with demonstrated expertise in multi-channel campaign creation and management. AEC or professional services industry experience is a plus. Proven track record of developing and executing successful organic and paid campaigns across search engines and social media platforms. Experience collaborating with creative teams (graphic designers, video producers, etc.) to develop compelling campaign visuals. Experience with Adobe Creative Suite and Canva are preferred. Experience with marketing automation, CRM systems (HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce, etc.) and campaign management tools is a plus. ### Skills – Expert knowledge of paid advertising platforms including Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising, LinkedIn Campaign Manager and other social media advertising platforms. – Advanced campaign content creation skills including copywriting, messaging development and storytelling for digital marketing. – Strong creative collaboration abilities to work effectively with Graphic Design teams, providing clear creative direction and feedback. – Deep understanding of multi-channel campaign strategy and how to create cohesive campaigns across search, social, display and other digital channels. – Experience managing campaign refreshes and optimization cycles to maintain relevance and performance. – Strong brand management skills with ability to drive consistent brand voice across all campaign touchpoints. – Knowledge of SEO principles and how organic and paid campaigns work together. – Knowledge of campaign best practices including audience targeting, ad formats, bidding strategies and content optimization. – Excellent project management capabilities to coordinate multiple concurrent campaigns across various platforms and stakeholders. – Strong collaboration skills to integrate campaigns with overall marketing plan and other marketing initiatives. – Experience with marketing analytics tools (Google Analytics 4, platform analytics dashboards) to measure campaign effectiveness. – Strategic thinking to develop campaign concepts that support business development objectives. — ## Compensation $94,100 – $120,875 a year (Salary range for CO location) Stanley Consultants is committed to maintaining transparency in our hiring process, including providing information about compensation. The starting salary for the successful candidate in this position is competitive and will be determined by the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience, geographic location, internal equity, company policy and practices. In compliance with pay transparency laws, pay ranges are disclosed for positions and locations where required. — ## Work Environment Primarily office-based with occasional travel. Hybrid schedule available. — ## Work-Life Balance We realize there’s more to life than just work. We help you meet the demands of work, family and personal life through several flexible options. — ## What We Offer **Member-Owned.** Member-ownership is at the heart of our culture, aligning client satisfaction, company performance, and personal reward. **Paid Time Away.** Numerous paid holidays, generous PTO, parental leave, and professional development leave. **Health Insurance.** Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, FSA, HSA, Doctor On Demand, wellness reimbursement, and mental health resources. **Financial Health.** Life insurance, disability insurance, identity theft protection, and more. **Professional Growth.** Tuition assistance, professional society membership, and additional development opportunities. **Financial Rewards.** Company stock ownership, generous 401K match, incentive compensation, and profit-sharing contributions. — ## Additional Information Stanley Consultants does not welcome unsolicited resumes from staffing and recruiting agencies. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to Stanley Consultants, including but not limited to resumes submitted directly to Stanley Consultants members or representatives, will be deemed the property of Stanley Consultants. — ## Equal Opportunity Employer / Protected Veterans / Individuals with Disabilities The contractor will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is: (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information. 41 CFR 60-1.35(c) — ## Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
