item.title: Director, Public Policy
item.description: Director, Public Policy Organization: Investment Company Institute (ICI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/05/2026 Salary Range: $174,450.00 To $189,300.00 Annually ## Job Duties Identifies and analyzes key regulatory and policy initiatives in the Asia‑Pacific region affecting the global fund industry and the impacts of such developments on ICI member firms in Chinese (Cantonese and/or Mandarin) and English. Develops recommendations and policy positions on key proposals and initiatives in the Asia‑Pacific region and leads the drafting of relevant position papers and other materials, working in collaboration with ICI members and other ICI departments as appropriate. Designs and implements engagement and advocacy strategies with regulators and policymakers in support of ICI advocacy activities in the Asia‑Pacific region. Briefs ICI staff and ICI members on regulatory and policy developments through written and oral communications, including member memos, webinars, and other products. Prepares briefings for the CEO, Chief Global Affairs Officer, and the MD for Asia and Global Analytics on key topics and in support of meetings with senior officials and other key stakeholders in Asia‑Pacific. Designs and executes webinars, roundtables, and other member events in Asia‑Pacific, including identifying relevant discussion topics, securing public official and expert speakers, managing logistics, and ensuring seamless execution. Develops content and talking points on APAC and EMEA issues for ICI senior leaders’ participation in external seminars, luncheons, and other public speaking engagements. Builds relationships with regulators, policymakers, and key stakeholders (e.g., local industry associations) in the Asia‑Pacific region in Chinese (Cantonese and/or Mandarin) and English. Supports structuring of effective and efficient meetings of ICI steering and policy committees for Asia‑based members, and topic‑specific working groups, including developing agendas and leading relevant discussion items. Helps to ensure the accuracy and reliability of information and analysis collected and used in ICI materials. Drafts final reports of research results for internal use and use in ICI publications. Works effectively with external consultants and vendors to support ICI projects and ICI goals. Performs other duties as assigned. ## Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or related field and 96 months of experience in the job offered or as an analyst or researcher in the asset management or financial regulatory space. Alternatively, will accept a Master’s degree and 60 months of experience in the positions listed above. All candidates must possess written and spoken fluency in English and Chinese (Cantonese or Mandarin). Reference check required. Must have 5 years of: 1) knowledge of APAC financial institutions and financial markets; 2) experience independently managing multiple workflows against tight deadlines; 3) experience collaborating with and presenting to colleagues and consultants across regions, jurisdictions, and time zones. Must also have 3 years of: 1) experience synthesizing information, analysis, and data to respond to queries from members and policymakers; 2) experience analyzing the impacts of regulatory initiatives and policy issues on the asset management industry in Asia, translating industry concerns into policy positions and advocacy strategy, and executing the strategy. Position is based out of 1401 H St. NW, Suite 1200, Washington, DC 20005. Must travel to the Asia‑Pacific region, Europe, and domestically throughout the year. Typically travels to Asia a minimum of 6 times per year to meet with Asia members. Partial remote schedule: 3 days in office and 2 days WFH, with Tuesday and Wednesday as core in‑office days. Must be able to work outside US business hours (Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm) as needed for meetings with Asia members. Rate of Pay: $174,450.00–$189,300.00 per year. As a member of the Strategic Communications department reporting to the Director, Digital Strategy, the Specialist, Content and Events Marketing is responsible for managing day-to-day execution of full-scale marketing plans to promote ICI’s business, brand, conferences, events, and webinars. **MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES** Works with the Director, Digital Strategy and Strategic Communications leadership to operationalize the broader communications vision for ICI into effective storytelling across audiences. Builds and executes full-scale marketing plans for conferences, workshops, webinars, and other ICI events, leveraging tactics including social media, email, SMS, paid promotion, and more. Works closely with subject matter experts to market events to appropriate groups, ensure customer list accuracy, and curate customer databases for future promotions. Builds long-term relationships with digital stakeholders and partners with colleagues at member firms and allied organizations. Creates daily newsletters published each morning of a conference sharing panel highlights, speaker insights, and more. Drafts pre- and post-conference blogs, previewing and recapping conference highlights. Partners with the creative team to develop video promotions, on-the-ground testimonials, and sizzle reels. Supports the broader digital team on the promotion of ICI Viewpoints blogs, research reports, and other ICI priorities. Collects rigorous metrics and KPIs to inform a proactive, forward-looking approach that can improve ICI’s marketing. **If you have the following credentials, we encourage you to apply:** Bachelor’s degree preferred and minimum of 2 – 4 years related experience in event promotions and meetings. Previous management of social channels and digital platforms. Experience supporting the development and execution of tailored communications and/or marketing campaigns. Experience in finance or other heavily regulated industries is a plus. Outstanding written communication abilities. Outstanding understanding of social and digital strategy. Commitment to the creation of creative, impactful, and compelling content contributing to ICI’s strategic goals. Excellent professional judgement. Ability to delegate tasks while maintaining high standards of quality. Deep understanding of digital and social platforms and relevant strategies. Ability to collect and use data, analytics, and other KPIs for campaign development and execution. ICI offers a competitive compensation and benefits package to include a comprehensive medical plan, generous 401(k) retirement savings plan, paid leave, commuting subsidies, and tuition reimbursement as well as training and development opportunities. Based in Washington, DC, ICI is conveniently located next to McPherson Square Metro station. This is a hybrid position with three days in the office and two working from home. To be considered for the position, please provide your cover letter and resume here . ICI is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity and inclusion in the workplace. item.title: Senior Marketing Manager
item.description: Senior Marketing Manager Organization: Mainely Grass Holdings Location: Newington, NH Date Posted: 09/05/2026 ## Job Type Full-time ## Description Mainely Grass is a fast-growing, multi-location lawn care company serving homeowners across New England—and a nationally recognized Lawn & Landscape Best Place to Work. We’re looking for a Senior Marketing Manager to lead the day-to-day execution of our marketing function while helping shape the strategy behind how we grow. You’ll work closely with the CEO, internal department leaders, and a network of specialized agencies and contractors—but you’ll be the quarterback of the marketing function. You’ll help set the direction, translate strategy into action, lead our external partners, and ensure great plans turn into great execution. This is a high-ownership role for someone who moves quickly, cares deeply about the details, and is equally comfortable thinking strategically and rolling up their sleeves to get things done. You’ll have the opportunity to make a significant impact on the growth of the business and how Mainely Grass shows up in the market. **Compensation:** $90,000 base salary, plus a meaningful annual bonus tied to performance — ## Responsibilities – Develop and execute the annual marketing plan in partnership with the CEO, aligning campaigns, channels, budgets, and priorities with the company’s strategic objectives, seasonal needs, and growth goals. – Own the day-to-day execution of the marketing function, coordinating internal stakeholders and managing external agencies, contractors, and vendors to ensure work is delivered on time, on brand, and on budget. – Monitor and improve marketing performance across key marketing metrics, including lead volume, conversion rates, and customer acquisition cost. – Lead keeping the website current, keeping content refreshed, and maintaining and creating landing pages, overseeing all contractor/agency SEO changes and additions, as well as regularly seeking improvements to its conversion. – Work with head of customer experience to develop current customer communication campaigns, maintain communication calendars, and own execution of email + SMS, including seasonal upsell, annual renewal, and educational campaigns, with full accountability for performance on those channels and continuous improvement. – Work with head of sales to develop and execute communication campaigns to prior cancelled customers and rejected estimates via email + SMS, with full accountability for performance on those channels and continuous improvement. – Monitor and respond to customer reviews across platforms and maintain accurate digital listings to protect and strengthen our online reputation. – Manage organic social presence across platforms, with a focus on educational, seasonal content alongside internal team events. – Act as brand steward, maintaining and evolving brand guidelines and ensuring consistency in voice, messaging, and visual identity across all customer-facing communications. — ## Requirements – Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience – 5 years of marketing experience, preferably within the home services industry or a similar local business – HubSpot proficiency preferred – Demonstrated strength in project management, including the ability to manage multiple campaigns, deadlines, and external partners simultaneously – Experience managing agencies, contractors, and media vendors with a track record of holding partners accountable to deliverables and brand standards – Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret performance data and translate insights into action – Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a high standard for quality and attention to detail – Creative thinker with the ability to develop effective campaigns across multiple channels – Self-directed, high ownership, low ego, and comfortable taking the lead across a broad range of marketing responsibilities — ## Salary Description $90,000 base salary, plus annual bonus Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director / VP of Marketing
item.description: Director / VP of Marketing Organization: Barletta Boats Location: Bristol, IN Date Posted: 09/05/2026 # Director / Vice President of Marketing Barletta Boats is seeking a strategic and commercially minded marketing leader to help shape the next chapter of our premium brand. This opportunity may be structured as either Director of Marketing or Vice President of Marketing, depending on the selected candidate’s skills, experience, leadership scope, and demonstrated ability to influence both business‑unit and enterprise‑level outcomes. This leader will be responsible for advancing Barletta’s brand, market position, digital retail strategy, social presence, marketing technology, analytics, and AI‑enabled marketing capability. We are looking for someone who can move marketing beyond traditional execution into a more strategic, insight‑led, digitally enabled, and commercially connected function that supports long‑range growth and strengthens Barletta’s position as a premium pontoon brand. Founded on a commitment to creating exceptional boating experiences, Barletta Boats is proud to be part of Winnebago Industries (NYSE: WGO), a family of premium outdoor recreation brands that includes Winnebago, Grand Design RV, Newmar, and Chris‑Craft. Together, these brands share a passion for innovation, quality, and craftsmanship while retaining their own unique identities and legacies. Through the strength of the Winnebago Industries portfolio, Barletta combines entrepreneurial agility with the resources, expertise, and vision of a global leader in outdoor recreation. ## About the Opportunity The Director / VP of Marketing will define how Barletta shows up in the market, how customers and dealers experience the brand, and how marketing strategy translates into measurable business impact. This role requires progressive thinking around brand strategy, the future of boat buying and digital retail, dealer and customer engagement, marketing analytics, AI‑enabled workflows, VOC‑driven insights, and cross‑functional commercialization. The ideal candidate will bring strong emotional intelligence, practical resourcefulness, and the ability to build momentum by leveraging expertise across the enterprise, dealer partners, agencies, vendors, and external thought leaders. This is a highly critical leadership role for someone who can connect brand, customer, dealer, product, digital, social, analytics, and commercial priorities into one integrated marketing agenda. Role level will be determined by experience: Candidates with strong functional leadership, team development, digital marketing, and brand execution experience may be considered at the Director level. Candidates with broader enterprise leadership experience, executive influence, measurable commercial impact, strategic transformation, and proven ability to lead a modern marketing function at scale may be considered at the Vice President level. ## What You’ll Lead – **Brand strategy** and market position: Elevate and protect Barletta’s premium brand position across customer, dealer, media, product, social, digital, and internal touchpoints. – **Digital and social** and marketing technology: Establish a clear roadmap for the website, dealer portal, digital retail capabilities, social media platforms, asset management, lead‑management workflows, web analytics, and related marketing technologies. – **Customer and dealer experience**: Shape Barletta’s point of view on how premium boats are researched, configured, purchased, supported, and experienced over time. – **Marketing analytics** and performance: Build dashboards, scorecards, and operating rhythms that connect marketing activity to outcomes such as brand health, website traffic, lead generation, lead quality, conversion visibility, campaign ROI, dealer engagement, and growth priorities. – **AI‑enabled innovation**: Identify practical ways to develop AI competency and automation to improve speed, quality, personalization, insight generation, lead scoring, campaign optimization, content development, asset organization, customer segmentation, and workflow efficiency. – **VOC and market intelligence**: Partner with Sales, Product Development, CX, and dealer partners to organize customer and dealer signals into actionable recommendations. – **Commercial storytelling** and growth support: Translate Barletta’s long‑range growth strategy into marketing actions that support market share expansion, lead generation, dealer confidence, lot‑share improvement, new dealer support, and targeted distribution priorities. – **Product launches** and commercialization: Lead integrated marketing planning for model year rollover, new product introductions, product updates, dealer communications, website updates, social content, asset readiness, and go‑to‑market execution. – **Dealer enablement** and industry presence: Ensure dealers have the tools, content, communications, events, training support, and brand confidence needed to represent Barletta effectively. – **Content and PR**: Lead the strategy for boat tests, editorial opportunities, boating publications, influencer relationships, customer stories, testimonials, premium visual assets, and public relations. ## What We’re Looking For – **Progressive marketing leadership experience** with responsibility for brand strategy, digital marketing, marketing operations, analytics, customer experience, and team leadership. – **Experience leading marketing transformation**, technology adoption, agency/vendor partnerships, content strategy, events, and integrated campaign execution. – **Strong understanding of dealer, channel, retail, or durable goods environments**; marine, powersports, RV, automotive, or premium lifestyle product experience is preferred. – **Ability to use data, dashboards, insights, and measurable rhythms** to guide decisions and improve outcomes. – **Growing fluency with AI‑enabled tools**, marketing automation, CRM/lead management, digital asset management, web analytics, and customer journey optimization. – **Executive presence, strategic communication skill, emotional intelligence**, and the ability to influence cross‑functional leaders, dealer partners, external agencies, and industry stakeholders. – **Demonstrated resourcefulness** in building capability, solving problems, and delivering outcomes by leveraging internal teams, enterprise expertise, dealer partners, agencies, vendors, and external thought leaders in a budget‑conscious environment. ## Leadership Characteristics That Will Matter – **Strategic and enterprise‑minded**: Understands how marketing influences brand equity, customer demand, dealer confidence, product commercialization, market share, and long‑term growth. – **Progressive and future‑oriented**: Curious about digital retail, social media, customer journey design, AI, data‑driven marketing, customer segmentation, content personalization, and the future of premium boat buying. – **Emotionally intelligent and relationship‑driven**: Builds trust quickly, listens well, adapts communication style, and influences effectively across internal teams, dealers, agencies, vendors, and external partners. – **Commercially grounded**: Connects marketing to lead generation, website traffic, dealer engagement, conversion, market share, product launch success, brand strength, and ROI. – **Creative but disciplined**: Values storytelling, content quality, events, PR, social engagement, structure, prioritization, timelines, accountability, and follow‑through. – **Resourceful and collaborative**: Leverages internal talent, enterprise expertise, dealer partners, agencies, vendors, industry relationships, and external thought leaders. ## Success in the First 12–24 Months – A clear marketing strategy aligning brand, dealer support, product launches, digital retail, social presence, VOC insights, analytics, and commercial priorities. – Improved consistency and strength of Barletta’s premium brand presence across customer, dealer, media, social, product, and internal touchpoints. – A modernized digital, social, and marketing technology roadmap with clearer ownership, improved usability, stronger data flow, and measurable performance expectations. – More visible customer journey and lead performance insights, including lead generation, website traffic, lead quality, conversion visibility, dealer engagement, and follow‑up effectiveness. – Improved execution discipline around model year rollover, product launch readiness, boat shows, dealer communications, content planning, social activation, and event support. – Practical adoption of AI and automation with clear use cases, governance, and measurable productivity, quality, or insight improvements. – A stronger, more scalable marketing team operating model with defined priorities, accountability, cross‑functional alignment, resourceful use of internal/external expertise, disciplined budget management, and a consistent cadence of reporting and decision‑making. ## Why Barletta? At Barletta, marketing is more than a support function. It is a critical connector between our brand, our dealers, our customers, our products, and our long‑range growth strategy. This is an opportunity to help shape how a highly regarded premium pontoon brand continues to grow, differentiate, innovate, and deliver a customer and dealer experience that reflects who we are. If you are a marketing leader who combines strategic thinking, modern digital fluency, commercial discipline, creativity, collaboration, and a genuine interest in building future‑ready capability, we would like to connect with you. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Assistant General Counsel
item.description: Assistant General Counsel Organization: Winnebago Industries Location: Eden Prairie, MN Date Posted: 09/05/2026 **Salary Range:** $210,000.00 To $250,000.00 Annually Are you looking to join an organization with strong values and brand reputation? Winnebago Industries is seeking a highly organized, motivated, and energetic attorney to join our team as Assistant General Counsel based in Eden Prairie, MN. This role will manage legal support of commercial matters, innovation and dispute resolution. This position will report to the Vice President, Chief Compliance Officer and will play a critical role in partnering with the Winnebago Legal department as well as internal and external business stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a growth mindset and the desire to learn to take on new challenges. **Day to Day of the Role:** Manage legal support for commercial matters, including contracts, marketing, and the company’s dealer channel. Manage legal support of intellectual property, including patents and trademarks. Manage general litigation, pre-litigation claims, and all related matters, including litigation risk mitigation. Manage legal support for real estate matters. Perform special projects and support continuous improvement of legal department standard work, knowledge management and process. Identify, supervise and partner with outside counsel to ensure that all aspects of the company’s legal representation are of the highest quality. Offer counsel on a variety of legal issues. Serve as an accountable, strategic business partner to business and function leaders, providing actionable advice and guidance to address legal risks. Contribute to strategic planning, direction, and goal setting for the Legal function. Support development of policies, practices, and procedures that have a significant impact on the organization. Support the development of the department budget. Provide training to the company on legal topics. Other duties assigned are based on business need. **Qualifications and Skills:** JD degree from an ABA accredited law school. Admitted to practice in the State of Minnesota. Minimum of 8+ years of litigation experience in a law firm or in-house legal department. Experience working with product warranty and/or product liability is highly preferred. Strong leadership skills, proven ability to build trust, lead, energize, influence and drive action at all levels within the organization including senior leadership. Experience with drafting and negotiating contracts is strongly preferred. This posting includes a range of the salary across a geographical market. The base pay for this position ranges from $210,000 in our lowest geographic market up to $250,000 in our highest geographic market. Pay is based on a number of factors including market location, internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Dependent on the position other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits. For more information, please visit [https://www.winnebagoind.com/careers/total-rewards.] Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Quality & Compliance Systems Specialist
item.description: Quality & Compliance Systems Specialist Organization: Winnebago Industries Location: Middlebury, IN Date Posted: 09/05/2026 ## Winnebago Industries Winnebago Industries is a prominent manufacturer of outdoor lifestyle products under the iconic Winnebago, Grand Design, Chris‑Craft, and Newmar brands. Our 6,500+ team members across Iowa, Indiana, Minnesota, and Florida deliver on our vision to be the trusted pacesetter in outdoor lifestyle solutions by providing unmatched innovation, quality, and service in the industries we engage. We believe our employees are our most valuable asset, and we are committed to providing a safe and engaging environment where you can be passionate about the work you do and have opportunities to learn and grow. Winnebago is excited to provide equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. Winnebago Towables has an immediate need for an experienced candidate to fill a **Quality & Compliance Systems Specialist** position. This position will be based in Middlebury, Indiana. ## Primary Objective of Position Winnebago Towables has an immediate opening for a Quality and Compliance Systems Specialist to support and enhance quality assurance activities throughout the manufacturing process. This role is involved across the full manufacturing lifecycle—from incoming materials to finished goods—ensuring products meet internal requirements as well as external regulatory and industry standards. The Quality and Compliance Systems Specialist conducts inspections, audits, testing, and data analysis; creates quality documentation; and drives continuous improvement using structured problem‑solving methodologies. This position plays a key role in maintaining compliance with Recreational Vehicle Industry Association (RVIA) and Canadian Standards Association (CSA) requirements while partnering cross‑functionally to improve product quality, reduce warranty issues, and support operational excellence. ## Key Areas of Responsibility – Perform Quality Focus Group audits related to process adherence, defect prevention, standard work, and employee training. – Audit and verify proper installation and assembly per component manufacturer specifications; identify gaps and recommend process or design improvements. – Ensure manufacturing processes and finished products meet applicable industry and regulatory standards (RVIA, CSA). – Support and lead efforts to ensure appropriate inspection and testing procedures are defined, implemented, and sustained. – Develop and maintain visual work instructions, inspection aids, and quality documentation to support production and audit readiness. – Create, distribute, and follow up on Quality Alerts to drive prompt containment and corrective action. – Review customer and warranty claim data to identify trends, perform root cause analysis, and support cross‑functional warranty reduction initiatives. – Facilitate structured problem solving and corrective actions (e.g., containment, root cause, corrective/preventive actions) to prevent recurrence. – Partner with Operations, Service, Supply Chain, and Product Development to drive continuous improvement initiatives. – Identify, contain, and document nonconforming materials or components; coordinate communication and disposition with appropriate departments. – Collect, analyze, and report quality data to support decision‑making and continuous improvement efforts. ## Education & Experience High School Diploma / GED 3–5 years of experience in quality, engineering, or manufacturing Experience in print reading and part measurement Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple cross‑functional groups at multiple levels of the company RVIA/RVDA Certification a plus ## Physical Demands Office sitting and standing environment Position may require sitting for long periods of time At Winnebago, we believe ALL people are leaders and hold each other accountable to high expectations. ## Leadership Expectations ### Connect with Purpose – Be inclusive; seek out different perspectives. – Focus on the Customer; put yourself in the customer’s shoes. – Communicate Clearly; say what needs to be said and listen. ### Execute with Excellence – Explore Possibilities; ask, “What if?” and embrace new ideas. – Set Direction; prioritize, plan, and align; balance thinking and action. – Drive Results; get the right things done; work with a sense of urgency. ### Build the Future – Transform the Road Ahead; anticipate opportunities; seek new opportunities for continuous improvement. – Navigate Change; be agile and flexible; take on new challenges. – Inspire Growth; help each other improve; commit to personal development. ## Benefits If you are the right candidate for this position, as a Winnebago Team Member you will be eligible for the following benefits: – Medical, Dental, Vision, Group Life Insurance, Accidental Injury, Critical Illness, Short & Long‑Term Disability – Health Savings Account (HSA) – Flexible Spending Account (FSA) – 401(k) with match – Employee Stock Purchase Program – Tuition Reimbursement – Holiday and Vacation Pay Winnebago Towables is an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: Communications Manager, Nature
item.description: Communications Manager, Nature Organization: Bezos Earth Fund Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## Major Function The Bezos Earth Fund is accelerating progress toward a more equitable, sustainable, and climate-resilient world. We are seeking a Communications Manager to support its nature portfolio, which spans conservation, species recovery, landscape restoration, and food systems transformation. This person should be a seasoned communications professional with experience developing integrated communications plans that can reach several different audiences, shaping narratives, and producing high-quality communications materials. They should be able to dive deeply into complex subject matters, think creatively, and identify compelling stories across a broad grant portfolio to deliver results across various channels – including press, events, social, and emerging channels. They should feel comfortable and have proven experience working with media, influencers, and other advocates to reach audiences where they are. The Communications Manager will work closely with program colleagues and grantee partners, helping tell a coherent story about the Bezos Earth Fund’s nature work across individual grants and initiatives, as well as broader stories about the areas in which Bezos Earth Fund is working. They should be able to provide counsel to senior leaders, be comfortable staffing leadership at events, during interviews, or other activities. This person should be able to work autonomously while collaborating closely with colleagues and external partners. The role requires strong judgment, attention to detail, and comfort working in a fast-paced environment. The Communications Manager will report to the Head of Communications for the Nature Portfolio. ## Key Responsibilities Develop and execute communications plans for the Nature Portfolio, identifying key milestones, storytelling opportunities, and communications needs around major convenings. Actively work with media to land interviews, develop stories and drive positive press around our work. Develop messaging that translates complex scientific and programmatic work to the Bezos Earth Fund’s broader mission. Draft and edit briefing documents, talking points, web and social copy, and other communications materials. Develop creative briefs and collaborate with agency partners through ideation, production, review, and approval for videos and assets to be used on social or other channels, ensuring that deliverables accurately reflect the work and align with communications objectives. Participate in program and grantee meetings to anticipate communications needs and surface content opportunities across the grant portfolio. Develop mechanisms and processes to work with grantees that help gather stories to shape communications plans. Help sustain a regular cadence of owned content (i.e. social media, website) that highlights Bezos Earth Fund work and impact in this area. Provide counsel and meet regularly with program leads to help shape plans and activity. Performs other duties as assigned. ## Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree or higher. 7+ years of experience working in communications. Proven ability to think big and deliver results that build awareness and understanding among priority audiences. Proven experience developing and executing integrated communications plans. Proven experience working with press across national, broadcast, and/or trade. Professional working proficiency in at least one of the following languages is required: Spanish, Portuguese, or French. ## Skills and Abilities Excellent writing and editing skills. Strong strategic judgment and storytelling instincts. Eagerness, think big, positive attitude. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work respectfully and effectively with colleagues, grantees, and external partners. Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Detail-oriented, adaptable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. “No job is too small” mindset, with the ability to support and collaborate across the organization as needed. ## Physical Requirements and Working Conditions Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer. May require extended and/or weekend hours for urgent issues or to meet established deadlines. This position is hybrid and based in Washington, D.C. Domestic and international travel may be required. **Salary Range:** $140,000 to $165,000 This is a paid position. Bezos Earth Fund is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all federal, state, and local laws concerning employment discrimination. The Earth Fund recognizes diversity as an asset essential to accomplishing its work. We actively welcome all qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds and will not discriminate on the basis of race, color, age, sex, gender identity or expression, genetic information, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, national origin, ethnicity, disability, military/veteran status, compensation history or any other basis prohibited by law. item.title: Social Media Specialist
item.description: Social Media Specialist Organization: Bezos Earth Fund Location: Washington, D.C. | Boston, MA | New York, NY Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## The Bezos Earth Fund is looking for a Social Media Specialist The Bezos Earth Fund is looking for a Social Media Specialist who lives and breathes all things digital: someone who can spot a trend before it peaks, turn a complex story into a scroll‑stopping Reel, and build an engaged community around work that matters. This hands‑on role owns day‑to‑day social media strategy and execution, creates original content, and grows and engages audiences across Instagram, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and emerging platforms. Working closely with external and internal partners across the organization, the Social Media Specialist translates the Bezos Earth Fund’s work into clear, accurate, and engaging stories. The ideal candidate is a strong operator who can move work forward independently while navigating a collaborative, multi‑stakeholder environment. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Social Media Strategy and Channel Management – Own the Bezos Earth Fund’s day‑to‑day presence across social platforms, with an initial focus on Instagram, growing support for LinkedIn, X, and YouTube. – Develop channel‑specific strategies, editorial calendars, and content plans that advance organizational priorities and grow audience engagement. – Stay ahead of platform trends, emerging formats, and creator culture; bring new ideas to the team and pressure test them quickly. ### Content Creation and Publishing – Create original, platform‑native content (including writing copy and building graphics) that makes complex climate, nature, and science topics accessible and compelling. – Own the full content workflow from concept through publication, including drafting, coordinating creative assets, and managing approvals. – Maintain a consistent voice and visual identity across channels while ensuring content is accurate, timely, and on‑brand. – Coordinate with creative agencies and other external partners as needed. ### Measurement and Continuous Improvement – Define and track channel and campaign performance metrics; turn data into clear insights that sharpen content and audience strategy. – Monitor peer organizations and platform shifts to identify opportunities for growth, experimentation, and innovation. — ## Required Skills/Abilities – Demonstrated experience managing social media channels and producing platform‑native content for an organization, brand, agency, or mission‑driven institution. – Hands‑on content creation skills: comfortable writing scripts, editing short‑form video, and creating static content. – Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to make complex subjects visually engaging and appropriate for different audiences and platforms. – Fluency with social media management and analytics tools, as well as native platform analytics. – Working knowledge of content creation tools (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, CapCut). – Sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to manage sensitive or high‑visibility communications. — ## Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in communications, marketing, journalism, digital media, or a related field. Four to six years of relevant experience in social media, digital communications, content strategy, or a related area, including hands‑on responsibility for managing multiple social platforms. — ## Physical Requirements – Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. – May require extended hours for urgent issues, major announcements, events, or established deadlines. – This role may require travel. While this position is based in Washington, DC, highly qualified candidates located outside the area in NYC or Boston will be considered. **Salary Range:** $111,000 to $140,000 This is a paid position. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement Bezos Earth Fund is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all federal, state, and local laws concerning employment discrimination. The Earth Fund recognizes diversity as an asset essential to accomplishing its work. We actively welcome all qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds and will not discriminate on the basis of race, color, age, sex, gender identity or expression, genetic information, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, national origin, ethnicity, disability, military/veteran status, compensation history, or any other basis prohibited by law. item.title: Regional Campaign Manager
item.description: Regional Campaign Manager Organization: Riders Alliance Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/08/2026 # REGIONAL CAMPAIGN MANAGER Riders Alliance is a grassroots advocacy organization that builds the power of transit riders to win better public transportation. Since our founding in 2012, we’ve grown a small, collaborative staff and a membership base of more than 50,000 riders, winning major campaigns including Fair Fares and congestion pricing. The Regional Campaign Manager will lead the development of Riders Alliance’s first campaign focused on improving commuter rail and public transit in strategic communities beyond New York City’s five boroughs. Working as part of the fundraising and organizational development team and collaborating closely with colleagues across the organization, the Regional Campaign Manager will build relationships with regional riders and supporters, create meaningful opportunities for them to participate in advocacy, and develop a growing constituency for fast, frequent, affordable, and reliable regional transit. — ## Key Responsibilities – **Campaign Strategy** — Build Riders Alliance’s first regional campaign, including driving campaign strategy and goals. Work with organizational leadership and colleagues across teams to develop and advance the campaign’s goals, strategy, priorities, and tactics. – **Campaign Implementation** — Manage campaign implementation. Maintain work plans, timelines, budgets, expenses, events, and logistics for campaign activities. – **Regional Constituency Building** — Identify and engage riders, civic leaders, and other prospective members and supporters motivated to improve commuter rail and regional transit service, affordability, reliability, and connections. – **Strategic Partnerships** — Build strategic relationships with community organizations, civic institutions, labor unions, journalists, elected officials, and other potential allies that can expand the campaign’s reach and influence. – **Participation Pathways** — Design accessible opportunities for new members and allies to contribute through 1:1 meetings, community and social events, canvassing, digital outreach, and campaign activities. Maintain data and track engagement against strategic goals. – **Donor & Champion Cultivation** — Partner with colleagues on the fundraising team to identify and engage prospective donors, including individuals who may support Riders Alliance at the Conductors Council level and/or serve as grass‑tops voices to influence key elected officials. – **Regional–City Alignment** — Help regional members and leaders understand New York’s transit network as an interconnected system. As relationships deepen, create opportunities for them to support shared priorities impacting riders across the region, including NYC’s bus and subway service. – **Cross‑Team Collaboration** — Coordinate closely with the organizing, policy, and communications teams to exchange knowledge, align strategies, and devise tactics, ensuring the regional campaign aligns with Riders Alliance’s broader mission and priorities. — ## Salary **$75,000 – $80,000** — ## Employment Type Full‑time, 40 hours per week (with some schedule flexibility). We are currently a hybrid office. — ## Benefits Riders Alliance offers: – Employer premium support for medical and dental insurance – Vision insurance – 403(b) retirement account with generous employer match – Life insurance – Access to commuter benefits – Additional benefits and supports — ## Expectations Riders Alliance is entering an exciting new chapter. Alongside our continued work organizing bus and subway riders across New York City, we are expanding our organizing beyond the five boroughs to build a stronger regional constituency for public transit. We’re looking for a new team member excited to help shape this work from the ground up: building relationships in communities served by commuter rail, developing new rider leaders, and creating a shared sense of identity and power among riders whose trips and communities are connected by the same regional transit system. We aspire to a workplace culture characterized by effective communication, collaboration, creativity, and a shared commitment to ambitious, strategic goals. — ## Qualifications – Values making public transit more reliable, accessible, affordable, and world‑class – Meaningful experience as a volunteer or professional in a political campaign, community organizing, and/or fundraising effort – Entrepreneurial, self‑motivated, and creative approach to projects and community building – Ability to prioritize and juggle multiple assignments – Highly organized and attentive to detail, especially names and numbers – Clear, concise, compelling communication skills – Demonstrated innovative thinking and problem‑solving abilities – Proficiency using a CRM for relationship and communication management – Experience with online project management tools such as Asana, Trello, or Monday is a plus — ## How to Apply – Please send a thoughtful cover letter and resume to ** [email protected] ** with the subject line: **“Regional Campaign Manager.”** – Applications are considered on a rolling basis; early applications are encouraged. — ## Commitment to Diversity Riders Alliance values variety in backgrounds and experiences reflective of the city it serves. Applicants of all backgrounds are strongly encouraged and welcomed to apply. item.title: AI Innovation Attorney – Litigation
item.description: AI Innovation Attorney – Litigation Organization: Cozen O’Connor Public Strategies (CPS) Location: Philadelphia, PA | Washington, DC | New York, NY Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## Job Description Cozen O’Connor is building a multidisciplinary Legal AI & Practice Transformation team to rethink how legal services are delivered. Our mission is to use AI and other emerging technologies to help our lawyers deliver the best possible advice and outcomes for clients. We are not just adding AI tools to existing ways of working; we are building the expertise and capabilities needed to redesign how legal work gets done. The **AI Innovation Attorney – Litigation** will partner with the firm’s litigation practices to identify and implement high‑value opportunities to use AI, redesign workflows, and improve how legal work is delivered. The role combines practice innovation, AI enablement, product implementation, and change management—helping lawyers use AI effectively on real matters and turning successful experiments into repeatable, scalable firm capabilities. This is an opportunity for an experienced litigator who is actively using generative AI and wants to help shape how litigation is practiced in an AI‑enabled future. The ideal candidate will bring strong AI fluency, an informed point of view about how generative AI can improve litigation, sound judgment about its limitations, and the credibility to serve as a trusted peer. — ## Responsibilities ### Partner with litigation practices and redesign workflows Build trusted relationships with practice leaders, lawyers, and other professionals and develop a detailed understanding of how work is handled across practices and matters. Analyze litigation workflows, identify pain points, and prioritize opportunities for AI and process improvement. Advise lawyers on where AI can meaningfully improve legal work and where it cannot or should not be used. Help litigators use AI in live matters by selecting the right tools, structuring effective prompts and context, and bringing in cross‑functional expertise—while preserving legal judgment, confidentiality, quality, and appropriate lawyer oversight. ### Develop and scale AI‑enabled capabilities Lead pilots and initiatives from problem definition through design, testing, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement. Serve as a power user and practice‑facing expert for the firm’s AI platforms, building and testing prompts, workflow agents, and matter‑specific solutions. Establish clear success criteria and evaluate solutions using representative matters, exemplar work product, lawyer‑defined quality standards, and structured feedback. Convert successful approaches into reusable playbooks, prompts, templates, and knowledge assets that can be adapted across practices, matters, and clients. Bring together practicing lawyers and experts in legal engineering, applied AI, knowledge management, data, technology, training, project management, and vendor solutions to develop high‑impact AI‑enabled solutions. ### Enable lawyers and drive adoption Provide practical guidance through consultations, demonstrations, working sessions, office hours, and individual support. Design and deliver training and practical resources that translate AI capabilities, limitations, and governance requirements into concrete use cases and help lawyers determine when to use available tools, structure effective workflows, and evaluate outputs. ### Advance client value and firm strategy Partner with lawyers and client teams to develop differentiated approaches to litigation delivery and support client‑facing proposals, demonstrations, and engagements. Stay current on AI, agentic workflows, litigation technology, legal service delivery, and the vendor market, translating developments into practical recommendations. — ## Qualifications J.D. from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing. At least five years of substantive litigation experience. A deep understanding of litigation workflows, lawyer decision‑making, quality standards, and the demands of client service. Active, hands‑on experience using generative AI in legal work, with an informed point of view about where it can impact quality, efficiency, and outcomes in litigation. Ability to translate among legal, technical, and business audiences and turn ambiguous needs into practical solutions. Strong project ownership, organization, and follow‑through, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and stakeholders. A practical, curious, and low‑ego mindset, including a willingness to experiment, learn from failure, challenge assumptions constructively, and remain accountable for results. — ## About Us Known for its commitment to action and tangible results, Cozen O’Connor has rapidly grown to become one of North America’s fastest‑growing law firms. Offering full‑service expertise in litigation, business law, and government relations, the firm serves a diverse clientele, including global Fortune 500 companies, growing middle‑market firms, startups, and high‑profile individuals. Established in 1970, Cozen O’Connor has more than 1,000 attorneys who help clients manage risk and make better business decisions. The firm counsels clients on their most sophisticated legal matters in all areas of the law, including litigation, corporate, and regulatory law. Representing a broad array of leading global corporations and middle‑market companies, Cozen O’Connor services its clients’ needs through 35 offices across two continents. The firm is consistently ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and has received recognition from prestigious legal and business organizations such as Chambers & Partners, The American Lawyer, The Legal 500, and Best Lawyers. Cozen O’Connor is dedicated to excellence and strives to achieve the right results for its clients, no matter how complex or critical the legal challenges may be. Cozen O’Connor is committed to fostering greater inclusion in the legal profession. We understand the organizational effectiveness that comes from welcoming and valuing differences within the firm, and we know that assembling a team with a breadth of perspectives and experience is necessary to provide the highest quality legal service. We encourage candidates to apply and join us in this effort. Cozen O’Connor actively welcomes applicants who have previously left the workforce and are looking to return to their careers. Gaps in experience are not penalized. Cozen O’Connor is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disabled and veterans. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Director of External Communications (Litigation)
item.description: Associate Director of External Communications (Litigation) Organization: Cooley Law Firm Location: New York, NY | Santa Monica, CA | Los Angeles, CA | Palo Alto, CA | Chicago, IL | Washington, DC | Boston, MA | Remote (CO) | Seattle, WA | San Francisco, CA | San Diego, CA | Reston, VA Date Posted: 09/08/2026 # Associate Director of External Communications (Litigation) Cooley is seeking an Associate Director of External Communications for Litigation to join the Communications team. ## Position Summary Working closely with the Director of Communications, firm leadership, the broader communications team and other business functions, the Associate Director of External Communications – Litigation will help shape and execute strategic external communications programs that enhance, differentiate and protect the department’s and Cooley’s reputation. The role will lead proactive media relations and reputation‑building efforts across the department, helping to bring Cooley’s perspective and client work to the forefront of the business, technology and legal developments shaping the innovation economy. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: ## Position Responsibilities – Lead and manage a team of in‑house and agency communications professionals responsible for building and maintaining relationships with influential media – Work closely with the Department Chair and litigation practice leadership to develop communications strategies that support business priorities, strengthen Cooley’s position in key markets and highlight the distinctive capabilities of the firm, its practices and lawyers – Oversee the strategic direction of the awards and recognitions program for the department, including prioritization, processes and the development of key submissions – Write and edit press releases, media pitches, talking points, statements and other firm communications – Develop and maintain reporting, policies, protocols and resources that support a coordinated and effective external communications function – Identify and shape compelling stories around the department, its clients and its lawyers, particularly across the industries and issues driving the innovation economy – Lead proactive external communications campaigns that position Cooley litigation lawyers as authoritative voices through earned media, social media, thought leadership and content promotion – Serve as a spokesperson and primary point of contact for media inquiries – Advise firm leaders and lawyers on media strategy, reputation management and sensitive or high‑profile matters – Provide crisis communications counsel, media training and interview preparation – Develop messaging, media strategies, anticipated questions and responses, and other communications materials ## Team Leadership and Management – Serve as mentor to direct reports – Provide day‑to‑day supervision of direct reports, ensure compliance with assigned work hours and monitor for compliance with all firm and department policies – Support business professional development and continued educational opportunities – In collaboration with immediate supervisor and HR, participate in hiring, performance appraisals, counseling, termination and other employee lifecycle events – Perform other duties as assigned or required ## Skills and Experience ### Required – After orientation at Cooley LLP, exhibit proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite, iManage and other firm applications – Ability to work extended and/or weekend hours, as required – Ability to travel, as required – Minimum 8 years’ direct experience (e.g., communications, public relations experience with B2B clients and at a management level) with 4+ years’ management experience (some at the senior level preferred) – Bachelor’s degree preferably in English, Journalism, Communications, Marketing, Business or related field – Experience operating at a level beyond current role expectations, providing strategic leadership, influencing key decisions, and guiding team direction – Experience leading people and teams, including hiring, employee development, work assignment, performance management, coaching and corrective counseling – Strong working knowledge of and contacts within national print, broadcast and online media; strong handle on financial markets and business concepts and related subject matter – Experience with crisis and issues management communications – Understanding of digital marketing, social media strategies, and content creation best practices ### Preferred – Experience working in a law firm, professional services, PR agency environment, and/or in government service/political realms – 10+ years applicable experience strongly preferred ## Competencies – Strong executive presence and ability to build credibility and trust with partners on strategy and execution of communications objectives – Excellent written and verbal communication skills – Exceptional writing skills and strong attention to detail – Ability to lead others in developing and executing initiatives and large‑scale projects – Ability to motivate others and build effective and cooperative work teams – Strong interpersonal skills with ability to negotiate challenging situations and grasp internal politics – Judicious, fast‑thinking and able to excel in a fast‑paced environment – Ability to consistently meet deadlines, including self‑set and multi‑tasked – Ability to develop professional relationships internally (with department members, lawyers and firm business professionals) and externally (with industry/regional associations, etc.) – Ability to simplify complex legal and business information into clear, accessible communication Cooley offers a competitive compensation and excellent benefits package and is committed to fair and equitable employment practices. EOE. ## Compensation The expected annual pay range for this position with a full‑time schedule is $200,000 – $240,000. Final offer amount will depend on geographic location, applicable experience and skillset of the candidate. ## Benefits We offer a full range of elective benefits including medical, health savings account (with applicable medical plan), dental, vision, health and/or dependent care flexible spending accounts, pre‑tax commuter benefits, life insurance, AD&D, long‑term care coverage, backup care for children and/or adults and other parental support benefits. In addition to elective benefit options, benefited employees receive firm‑paid life insurance, AD&D, LTD, short‑term medical benefits, 25 days of Paid Time Off (“PTO”) and 10 paid holidays each year. We provide generous parental leave and fertility benefits. New employees will attend a detailed benefit orientation to learn more about our many benefits and resources. People Leader – Serve as direct supervisor and mentor to direct reports – Provide day-to-day supervision of direct reports, ensure compliance with assigned work hours and monitor for compliance with all firm and department policies – Manage staffing coverage, review and process time logs/time off requests – Support business professional development and continued educational opportunities – In collaboration with immediate supervisor and central HR, participate in hiring, performance appraisals, counseling, termination and other employee lifecycle events – All other duties as assigned or required — ## item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Executive Director Organization: National Organization of Veterans’ Advocates (NOVA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## The Opportunity Under the direction of the President and Board of Directors, the **EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR** will lead the nation’s premier organization dedicated exclusively to advocacy for veterans, shaping the legal and legislative strategy that determines how disabled veterans, survivors, family members, and caregivers are treated under federal law. This is a rare opportunity to bring deep command of veterans benefits law to NOVA’s highest levels of practice, serving as its primary voice before Congress, the VA, and the courts, while guiding the staff, research, and training that advance the field nationally. The Executive Director must move confidently between the courts, stakeholder meetings, Capitol Hill, and boardroom as a credible, apolitical leader trusted across a broad and diverse membership, carrying out the Board’s policies and guiding NOVA’s next chapter. **Responsibilities include:** ### Legislative and Outreach – **Original research** — Conducts original research and prepares reports and analysis that inform NOVA’s strategy and strengthen its advocacy positions. – **Primary liaison role** — Represents NOVA across the veterans benefits community, engaging and testifying with Congress, the VA, the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC), Veterans Service Organizations, and Bar Associations. – **Registered lobbyist duties** — Serves as NOVA’s primary registered lobbyist, driving its presence on Capitol Hill while ensuring full compliance with federal reporting requirements. – **Legislative strategy execution** — Leads development and Board‑approved execution of NOVA’s legislative strategy, supervising and coordinating with any outside lobbyists. – **Training delivery** — Delivers training on veterans law and serves as a sought‑after speaker for organizations seeking expertise in the field. — ## The Opportunity (Continued) ### Legal – **Interpretation of laws** — Interprets laws, rulings, and regulations on behalf of NOVA, reviewing proposed laws and regulations and shaping the challenges or changes needed to meet mission objectives, in collaboration with Congressional Testimony and Regulation Comment Committees, and drafting legislative and regulatory comments for committee and Board review and filing. – **Drafting legal documents** — Drafts pleadings, legal correspondence, and other documents essential to the development of a NOVA matter or cause, coordinating closely with NOVA retained legal counsel. – **Amicus and litigation support** — Staffs NOVA’s Amicus and Litigation Committee, developing strategy and arguments, serving as liaison to pro bono counsel, and reviewing legal briefs drafted by retained amici in furtherance of NOVA’s mission. – **Court filings** — Files pleadings and other documents with courts, administrative bodies, and government agencies relative to NOVA’s business and interests. — ## Administrative / Managerial – **Team leadership** — Builds and leads NOVA’s administrative team, overseeing hiring, performance management, and salary decisions, and developing higher levels of expertise in staff members through professional development. – **Advisor to Board** — Serves as a trusted advisor to the President and Board, participating in Board meetings and providing timely updates on operations, events, NOVA’s operational and program reports, strategic direction, and any other information the Board needs to govern effectively. – **Policy enforcement** — Upholds and enforces the policies and procedures established by NOVA’s President and Board. – **Operational improvements** — Continuously reviews NOVA’s practices and methods, introducing new approaches as necessary to reduce costs, encourage growth, and improve efficiency. – **Meeting participation** — Organizes and participates in meetings, conferences, and cross‑functional project team activities. – **Oversight of assets** — Selects, reviews, and monitors insurance policies, inventory, intellectual property, and contracts relative to NOVA’s interests. – **Financial support** — Provides direct support and cooperation to NOVA’s accountants for the filing of tax forms and end‑of‑year financial reports. – **Financial viability** — Consults with NOVA’s Treasurer, President, and appropriate committees to ensure proper accounting of NOVA resources and long‑term financial viability. — ## The Candidate ### Required Qualifications – **Veterans issues expertise** — Extensive and substantive knowledge of issues affecting veterans, survivors, family members, caregivers, and accredited representatives – **Legal writing skills** — Strong legal research, writing, and drafting skills, including pleadings, legislative/regulatory comments, and litigation briefs – **Adaptability** — Adaptability and sound judgment in a fast‑changing regulatory and legislative environment – **Apolitical orientation** — Ability to demonstrate an apolitical/nonpartisan orientation – **Communication skills** — Strong, clear, and diplomatic written and verbal communication skills – **Management experience** — Minimum 3 years of management/supervisory experience – **Education** — Minimum Master’s degree required; J.D. strongly preferred ### Preferred Qualifications – **Veterans benefits law experience** — Minimum 7 years practicing veterans’ benefits law, with working knowledge of legacy and AMA claims systems – **Accreditation** — VA accreditation and/or admission to practice before the CAVC and/or U.S. Court of Appeals – **Relationship building** — Experience building and managing relationships with Congress, VA, CAVC, veteran service organizations, and bar associations – **Lobbying experience** — Experience as a registered lobbyist or navigating federal lobbying and reporting compliance – **Technology guidance** — Aptitude and knowledge to guide NOVA’s membership through emerging technologies, including AI – **Legal education** — J.D. degree preferred in law, government relations, legislative affairs, policy, or business – **Nonprofit management** — Prior experience managing a nonprofit or member‑based organization of comparable size – **Military background** — Military service/military spouse background – **Financial/contract management** — Experience managing financial or contractual business relationships, including vendor and membership management systems — ## Submit Your Application [ https://driwaterstonehc.com/position/ed-nova/ ] ### Salary Range $150,000 – $180,000 (salary commensurate with experience) ### Location Washington, DC (Hybrid role) ### Travel Conferences twice yearly, plus additional conventions/presentations upon request DRiWaterstone has been exclusively retained for this engagement. All first‑round interviews for this position will take place via video conference with DRiWaterstone. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Counsel or Senior Policy Counsel
item.description: Policy Counsel or Senior Policy Counsel Organization: Americans United for Separation of Church and State (AU) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## About Americans United Americans United for Separation of Church and State is a nonpartisan educational and advocacy organization dedicated to advancing the constitutional principle of church-state separation as the only way to ensure freedom of religion, including the right to believe or not believe, for all of us. Founded in 1947, Americans United is a diverse and dynamic organization composed of people from all walks of life: lawyers and lobbyists, students and activists, religious leaders and impassioned Americans. AU includes people of faith and people who don’t profess any particular faith. It is a community that welcomes people of all genders, races, ethnicities, religions or beliefs, sexual orientations, ages, socioeconomic backgrounds, and abilities. Because we work on a wide variety of issues with many different communities, we value what diversity and diverse perspectives bring to our work. ## Position Summary The Policy Counsel (or Senior Policy Counsel) works in collaboration with other members of the Public Policy department to help drive the state and federal public policy agenda that furthers the organization’s goals. This position’s primary focus will be supporting Americans United’s state policy efforts, rather than its federal policy work, but tasks will be assigned as needed. The position reports to the Public Policy department’s Managing Policy Counsel. ## Essential Duties & Responsibilities Duties and responsibilities will be adjusted to match the candidate’s level of experience. Draft policy and advocacy materials, including legislation, AU and coalition letters, backgrounders, talking points, and reports. Perform necessary research and analysis, including on legal and policy issues and current events; and develop, implement, and assess strategies to achieve policy goals at the state and federal level. Coordinate and lead cross-departmental advocacy initiatives with policy, organizing, communications, and legal strategies to advance church-state separation. Represent AU with partner organizations, coalitions, state and federal policymakers and staff to build support for AU’s policy goals. Track and analyze pending state and federal legislation and proposed regulations and policies related to church-state separation. Provide expert analysis and advice, including through collaboration with other departments, to develop strategies to educate people about relevant issues and work, mobilize people in support of our policy efforts, further our litigation goals, and continuously build a knowledge base, including tracking and monitoring relevant legal and policy trends. ## Skills and Experience *Research shows candidates from marginalized groups are less likely to apply for positions when they don’t meet 100% of listed requirements; please consider applying even if you don’t match 100% of these criteria.* Americans United seeks a candidate with a minimum of 1–2 years of work experience for the Policy Counsel role. Candidates with 7 or more years of experience may qualify for the Senior Policy Counsel role. Additionally, the candidate has: Experience with: Conducting advocacy, legal research, analysis, writing in support of legislative and policy efforts, ideally involving church-state separation or other civil rights issues, and working with coalitions and policymakers. A J.D., and is licensed to practice in the District of Columbia or eligible and willing to become a member of the bar of the District of Columbia. Strong organizational, analytical, writing, research, and speaking skills. Ability to work collaboratively as a member of a team in an often fast-paced environment with tight deadlines. Ability to collaborate productively with stakeholders of differing viewpoints, work across diverse communities (e.g., race, age, class, LGBTQ+, religious/nonreligious), and integrate diversity, equity and inclusion into our work. Ability to produce high-quality legal analysis and advocacy materials on deadline and with accuracy. Understanding of the legislative or regulatory process or policy advocacy strategies. Demonstrated interest in progressive advocacy, civil rights, civil liberties, and/or church-state separation. The following skills and experience are preferred, but not required: Experience working as a legislative or executive staff member in state or federal government. Knowledge, experience, and/or existing networks related to church-state separation and/or inclusive religious freedom, LGBTQ+ rights, public education, and/or reproductive rights. Knowledge or experience working on state or federal budget or appropriations process. Americans United welcomes applicants of all genders, races, ethnicities, religions and beliefs, sexual orientations, gender identities, ages, socio-economic backgrounds, and abilities. Because we work on a wide variety of issues and with many different communities, we value what diversity and diverse perspectives bring to our work. ## Working Conditions & Physical Requirements This is a hybrid position that primarily involves working from a home office and/or professional office environment. The role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and video conferencing tools. It requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, communicate effectively, and occasionally move about within the workspace. ## Compensation and Benefits The salary range for Policy Counsel is $87,822–$109,777. The salary range for Senior Policy Counsel is $109,777–$131,733. This stated range includes a 5% locality pay adjustment for the Washington, DC metropolitan area. The successful candidate’s placement within that range will be consistent with AU’s compensation framework, which is based on role placement and years of related experience. Americans United offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes employer-paid premiums for health care, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) with match, and commuter subsidy. ## Equal Opportunity Employer AU is an equal opportunity employer. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital or veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. If you need an accommodation for a disability to apply to this position, please let us know by emailing [email protected] . ## Application Information We will only be accepting applications from candidates who currently live in or would be willing to relocate to the Washington, DC metro area. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled. We will begin reviewing applications on September 25. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Engagement and Coalitions
item.description: Director, Engagement and Coalitions Organization: Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## Director, Engagement and Coalitions The **Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget** (Committee) is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization devoted to educating policymakers, the media, and citizens about the fiscal challenges facing the country, as well as the possible solutions. The Committee is made up of some of the nation’s leading budget experts, including many of the past Chairmen and Directors of the Budget Committees, the Congressional Budget Office, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Government Accountability Office. The Committee is seeking a driven and proactive **Director, Engagement and Coalitions**. This role will be responsible for building, managing, and engaging the Committee’s diverse stakeholder communities in Washington and across the country. The position will also support the Committee’s public engagement campaigns and work to build strategic partnerships with external organizations and groups. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional project management, organizational, and communication skills—both written and verbal—and have a proven track record in issue advocacy, particularly in engaging and collaborating with multiple stakeholders. The Director, Engagement and Coalitions will work with the Committee’s policy and legislative teams and report to the Senior Vice President and Chief of Staff. — ## Primary Responsibilities – **Develop and execute strategy** for recruiting, communicating with, and activating outside stakeholders to support the organization’s objectives – **Engage and build coalitions** of civic, business, thought, and political leaders, former elected officials, and activists inside and outside Washington to support the Committee in its bipartisan work on budget policy, tax policy, healthcare policy, long‑term investments, economic growth, and addressing polarization – **Develop and cultivate relationships** with key outside stakeholders – **Convene and facilitate meetings** for coalitions and other stakeholder/partner groups – **Identify and address coalition needs** related to advocacy and program implementation and align engagement approaches accordingly – **Exercise judgment** to prioritize opportunities; prepare talking points, speeches, presentations, and other supporting material as needed – **Support senior leadership** in all engagement‑related matters — ## Qualifications – **Self‑starter mindset** with ability to develop and enact multiple creative coalition initiatives – **Team‑oriented approach** and ability to thrive in a fast‑paced environment – **Excellent organizational and project management skills** — able to establish and implement systems and identify resources to ensure successful completion of projects – **Strong communication skills** (written & oral), extremely polished and professional demeanor, and excellent interpersonal skills capable of acting as one of the faces of the organization – **Organizing experience**; Capitol Hill or statewide advocacy, electoral, and/or ballot initiative experience is a plus – **Innovative thinker** with a track record for translating strategic thinking into action plans and output – **10+ years of relevant professional experience** – **Passion for the Committee and its mission** – **Bachelor’s degree required** — ## How to Apply Please submit a cover letter, resume, and contact information for three references to ** [email protected] **. When applying, please write **“Director, Engagement and Coalitions”** in the subject line. No phone calls, please. — ## Salary **$125,000 to $160,000**, with generous benefits including health, dental, life and long‑term disability insurance; 403(b) contribution; and paid time off. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget is committed to fostering an equitable, diverse, and inclusive working environment. The Committee is an Equal Opportunity Employer and provides equal opportunity to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, mental or physical disability, pregnancy, military or veteran status, and other such factors in accordance with U.S. state and federal laws.
