item.title: Assistant Director for Economic and Business Diplomacy, Center for New Middle East (CNME)
item.description: Assistant Director for Economic and Business Diplomacy, Center for New Middle East (CNME) Organization: American Jewish Committee (AJC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## **About AJC** American Jewish Committee (AJC) is the global advocacy organization for the Jewish people. We create trusted partnerships with leaders around the world to ensure Jews and Israel are safe and thriving. With an unparalleled reach spanning six continents, AJC engages leaders in more than 110 countries through 40 offices and dozens of partnerships with Jewish communities worldwide. Wherever the Jewish people and Israel need us, AJC is there—empowering leaders in government, education, partner communities, and the private sector to counter antisemitism and act as allies. The challenges we face are global. AJC is leading the global response. Join us. — ## **Your Department** AJC’s Center for a New Middle East (CNME) utilizes AJC’s unparalleled global advocacy network to foster deeper diplomatic, economic, and civic ties between Israel and its Arab neighbors. It builds upon AJC’s historic success in cultivating trust and opening doors to all levels of government across the Arab world. Drawing upon the relationships AJC has nurtured since its initial visits to Morocco in the 1950s, and expanded since the Madrid Peace Conference of 1991, AJC pursues programs across three principal sectors: diplomacy, business, and civil society. AJC actively promotes U.S. commitment to Israel’s security and its full integration in the Middle East and North Africa, regional business collaboration, and interfaith dialogue to advance Israeli‑Arab understanding. This holistic approach, combined with AJC’s global architecture—with 15 international posts, including offices in Jerusalem and Abu Dhabi, and a range of government contacts and communal partners around the world—uniquely positions the Center to advance AJC’s policy and institutional agendas. By bringing together decades of trust, international architecture, and multifaceted programs, the Center for a New Middle East can do things that no other organization can accomplish. The Center will have the power to convene the best and brightest from across the world to build bridges, shape policies, and instill the hope needed to truly create a new Middle East. — ## **Your Impact** The Assistant Director for Economic and Business Diplomacy supports the AJC Center for a New Middle East’s (CNME) economic and business diplomacy vertical by helping to develop, manage, and execute high‑level programs and strategic initiatives that advance relationships among the United States, Israel, and the Arab world. Working closely with CNME colleagues in Jerusalem and Abu Dhabi, as well as partners across AJC, the Assistant Director plays a leading role in coordinating major events, cultivating relationships with key stakeholders, and supporting cross‑departmental initiatives that promote commercial diplomacy, regional integration, and cross‑border cooperation. In this role, the Assistant Director helps ensure that AJC’s programming remains innovative, strategic, and responsive to a rapidly evolving regional landscape. Responsibilities include preparing briefing materials, managing relationships with government, business, and civil society leaders, supporting the development and execution of engagement strategies, and contributing to the planning and implementation of high‑profile conferences, delegations, special initiatives, and alumni engagement efforts. The ideal candidate brings experience from the private sector and is a dynamic, self‑motivated, and collaborative professional with strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills. They should be capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously, building relationships across diverse constituencies and cultures, and working effectively with teams, departments, and international regions. Familiarity with the Middle East and international business, investment, entrepreneurship, or commercial diplomacy is strongly preferred. — ## **Your Role** – Contribute to the development and execution of the department’s strategy, goals, objectives, and action plans – Manage and facilitate advocacy and outreach programs, projects, initiatives, events, meetings, trainings, and/or missions – Implement new opportunities to expand departmental initiatives beyond existing programs – May participate and support the work of Boards, committees, task forces, or working groups – Leverage resources to help build awareness of and support for the AJC and department initiatives – May assist with development efforts, including participation in fundraising initiatives and plans, donor outreach, providing materials for grant applications and reports, and related activities – Maintain and manage programmatic spending for initiatives they work on – Research, monitor, and report on developments, issues, and trends impacting the department and AJC priorities – Coordinate, attend, and/or lead meetings – Develop relationships with and engage strategic contacts, groups, and organizations – Support the building of coalitions, partnerships, and initiatives with organizations and other external partners to further AJC’s mission – Assist in representing AJC and the department in the community, at functions, and in other public forums – Draft, edit, and disseminate communications resources and materials — ## **Supervisory Role** Individual contributor — ## **Education, Training, and Experience** – Bachelor’s degree (Master’s degree preferred) – Minimum of 5 years of related work experience and intermediate job skills and knowledge – Experience in international business, investment, entrepreneurship, or commercial diplomacy – Fluency in the language of international business and commerce — ## **Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities** – Passion for the mission, goals, and objectives of AJC – Committed to AJC’s core values: respect, accountability, integrity, innovation, and collaboration – Demonstrates professionalism and high standards of conduct – Ability to work collaboratively with individuals from diverse backgrounds – Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, and listening) – Strong organization and project management skills, including the ability to set priorities and meet deadlines – Capacity to multitask and work in a fast‑paced and changing environment – Willing and able to work outside of standard working hours, including early mornings, evenings, and/or weekends – Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Outlook), Google Suite applications, and Zoom – Familiarity with international business, investment, entrepreneurship, or commercial diplomacy — ## **Physical Demands** Office employees: – Remaining in a stationary position, often sitting or standing for prolonged periods – Repeating motions that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers – Communicating with others to exchange information – Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another — ## **Disclaimers** The duties listed above are intended only as illustrations of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position. The job description does not constitute a contract between the employer and employee and is subject to change by the employer as the needs of the employer and the requirements of the job change. — ## **Compensation** The salary for this position is $67,000 – $80,000 depending on relevant experience and location. — ## **Benefits** Regular Full‑time employee benefits: – Medical, vision, and dental plans – Flexible Spending Account options – Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) – 15 vacation days per year, increasing with continued employment – Paid Holidays (many Federal and major Jewish Holidays) – Hybrid work schedule – 403(b) participation after one year of employment – Transit plan – Competitive Paid Parental Leave *After applicable waiting or probationary periods have been met* Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Legislative and Political Advocate
item.description: Legislative and Political Advocate Organization: AFSCME Maryland Council 3 Location: Baltimore, MD Date Posted: 09/08/2026 AFSCME Maryland Council 3 represents over 55,000 workers who work in public service. Council 3 members keep our public universities and community colleges running, maintain our libraries and museums, care for the elderly, provide social services to those in need, represent defendants in court, provide support in our schools, provide public safety for our communities, and maintain our parks and roads. We organize in the workplace and fight for dignity, respect, and a fair standard of living for all public service workers in Maryland. We are accepting applications for two Legislative and Political Advocate positions. This person will work on the Legislative and Political Team that is responsible for advocating for legislation that improves public services, recruiting members who will elect politicians who support workers, increasing participation in the union’s political action committee (AFSCME PEOPLE), and working to hold politicians accountable. This position is based in our AFSCME Maryland Baltimore office at 1410 Bush Street, Baltimore MD 21230 and in Annapolis during legislative session. Additionally, travel throughout Maryland will be required. The position reports directly to the Council’s Legislative and Political Director. ### Responsibilities ● Advocate before the Maryland General Assembly, state regulatory bodies, and local governments including, but not limited to, county councils, school boards, and library boards. ● Develop and foster union member engagement for legislative and political advocacy campaigns at the state and local level. ● Track budgetary and legislative priorities at the state and local government level and assist members with testimony preparation and public hearing preparation. ● Work with local unions and staff to build political organizing and advocacy campaigns. ● Recruit union members who help elect and hold politicians accountable. ● Organize and implement political programming to help elect AFSCME endorsed political candidates. ● Increase participation in AFSCME’s political action committee by working with local unions and staff on coordinated PAC drives. ● Assist local unions and staff with the candidate endorsement recommendation process. ● Conduct site visits and attend union meetings to identify issues and increase engagement in the union’s legislative and political program. ● Work extended hours, including evenings and weekends, when necessary, in order to perform assigned responsibilities. ● Work with the Council 3 team to advance all union priorities and goals. ### What We Are Looking For ● Two or more years of experience in labor, community, or political advocacy. ● Familiarity with Maryland state and local government structure and elected officials. ● Dedication to workers’ rights and the labor movement. ● Familiarity and knowledge of unions and/or the labor movement. ● Ability to organize and mobilize union members to advocate for AFSCME’s legislative and political goals at the state and local level. ● Ability to work independently and collaboratively to accomplish the mission and goals of Council 3. ● Excellent oral and written communication skills. ● Experience collaborating with diverse communities and in a multi-cultural environment. Sensitivity to and appreciation of ethnic, cultural, and societal differences is required. ● Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with co-workers, union members, and community members. ● Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite programs, Zoom, VAN, other campaign platforms, and social media platforms. ● A valid driver’s license is a requirement. ### Compensation The salary range is $60,978 – $92,235. Benefits include fully paid comprehensive single or family health insurance (medical, dental, prescription, and optical), car allowance, 3 weeks paid vacation, 16 paid holidays, 12 sick days, pension, 401k, and life insurance. This is a bargaining unit position and is represented by a staff union. AFSCME Maryland Council 3 is an inclusive and diverse organization, committed to advocating for social, racial, and economic justice. We promote diversity and strongly encourage applications from people who believe in our mission. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ people to apply. ### To Apply Send cover letter and résumé to [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Staff Attorney/Senior Staff Attorney – National Litigation
item.description: Staff Attorney/Senior Staff Attorney – National Litigation Organization: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (Reporters Committee) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## Company Description Established in 1970, the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (Reporters Committee) provides pro bono legal representation, amicus curiae support, and other legal resources to protect First Amendment freedoms and the newsgathering rights of journalists. Reporters Committee serves news organizations, reporters, documentary filmmakers, media lawyers, and many more who use its online resources. — ## Job Description The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press is hiring a staff attorney or senior staff attorney to join its National Litigation program. This attorney will be responsible for designing and executing strategic litigation, providing rapid legal responses to threats against press freedom, and bolstering the newsgathering rights of journalists across the United States. The attorney’s primary focus will be providing direct representation to journalists and newsrooms, but they will also have the opportunity to participate in other Reporters Committee programs and advocacy efforts. This full‑time position reports to the Director of National Litigation. Starting salary, based on experience, will range from USD 128,800 – USD 153,100. The priority deadline to apply is September 25. — ## Key Responsibilities Include: – Representing journalists and news organizations in litigation involving access to judicial records/proceedings, freedom of information requests, Administrative Procedure Act claims, Section 1983 cases, and other newsgathering and First Amendment matters. This includes, among other things: intake/case selection; drafting correspondence, administrative appeals, pleadings, briefs, and other filings in trial and appellate courts; negotiating with opposing counsel; conducting discovery; and appearing on behalf of clients in state and federal courts. – Developing and pursuing impact litigation in federal and state court to address emerging and systemic issues affecting reporters and newsrooms. – Supervising legal fellows and interns at the Reporters Committee on pre‑litigation and litigation matters, working with co‑counsel and law school clinics, and, depending on experience level, supervising the work of more junior Reporters Committee attorneys. – Working with the policy and amicus teams at the Reporters Committee on a wide variety of issues affecting the news media, including drafting amicus briefs, administrative comments, and advocacy letters. – Educating journalists about First Amendment and newsgathering rights, including by conducting trainings for journalists and news organizations on media law topics. — ## Qualifications – Admitted to practice law in Washington, D.C. or eligible for admission to practice law in Washington, D.C. – A minimum of eight years of experience litigating cases in state and federal court. Substantial experience with media law matters is preferred. Judicial clerkships may qualify for up to two years of experience. – A passion for protecting press freedom and a strong desire to support the work of journalists across the country. – Outstanding legal research skills, and excellent written and oral communication skills. – Strong leadership skills with the ability to supervise—or demonstrated experience successfully managing—the work of less‑experienced attorneys. – Excellent public speaking and oral communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and effectively with a broad range of clients and stakeholders. – Sound judgment and the highest level of professional integrity. — ## Additional Information **Physical Demands:** The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and operate computer equipment. The employee is occasionally required to stand and walk. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. **Compensation:** RCFP is committed to offering competitive pay and generous benefits, including group medical insurance, short‑ and long‑term disability insurance, retirement benefits, health‑reimbursement accounts, and paid family leave. The salary range for this position is USD 128,800 – USD 153,100. **How to apply:** Please submit a resume and cover letter explaining your interest in the position here by the priority deadline of September 25, 2026. Please submit materials in one PDF or Word file. Applications received after the priority deadline will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RCFP is an Equal Opportunity Employer. At the Reporters Committee, we celebrate the diversity of our employees and our leadership. RCFP is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Michigan LLI Attorney
item.description: Michigan LLI Attorney Organization: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (Reporters Committee) Location: Detroit, MI Date Posted: 09/08/2026 Company Description Established in 1970, the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (**Reporters Committee**) provides pro bono legal representation, amicus curiae support, and other legal resources to protect First Amendment freedoms and the newsgathering rights of journalists. The organization serves news organizations, reporters, documentary filmmakers, media lawyers, and many others who rely on its online resources. Job Description The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press is hiring a **Michigan Local Legal Initiative (LLI) Attorney**. The Local Legal Initiative, launched in 2020, provides pro bono legal support to journalists and news outlets engaged in local enterprise and investigative journalism. The Michigan LLI Attorney will advise and represent news organizations and individual journalists in Michigan in matters involving access to judicial records and proceedings, freedom of information, and other newsgathering and First Amendment issues. The attorney will also contribute to the Reporters Committee’s amicus and pre‑publication/vetting practices for matters within Michigan; conduct trainings for journalists and news organizations; and collaborate with stakeholders across the state to increase the visibility of the LLI. This full‑time position reports to the Director of the Local Legal Initiative. The Michigan LLI Attorney must be based in Michigan; the Detroit, Lansing, and Grand Rapids metropolitan areas are preferred. Some travel throughout Michigan and to the Reporters Committee’s office in Washington, D.C. is required. Key Responsibilities Include: – Representing Michigan journalists and news organizations in litigation and other matters involving access to judicial records/proceedings, freedom of information, and other newsgathering and First Amendment matters. This includes intake/case selection, strategy decisions, drafting correspondence, administrative appeals, pleadings, briefs, and other filings in trial and appellate courts, and appearing on behalf of clients in state and federal court. – Providing counsel to Michigan journalists on legal issues related to newsgathering, access to information, libel, and privacy. – Drafting amicus briefs and—depending on seniority and experience—supervising junior RCFP attorneys on amicus briefs in cases involving newsgathering and First Amendment issues in Michigan. – Educating Michigan journalists about First Amendment and newsgathering rights, including conducting trainings for journalists and news organizations on media law topics. – Responding to hotline inquiries from journalists in Michigan and working with RCFP communications staff to provide comment to local journalists and news organizations for publication. – Working collaboratively with stakeholders in Michigan and internally at RCFP to promote the LLI and its strategic goals. – Depending on seniority and experience, working with the Vice President of Legal Programs and the Director of the Local Legal Initiative to provide guidance, supervision, and performance feedback to legal fellows and staff attorneys. Qualifications – Admitted to practice law in Michigan or eligible for admission. – 3+ to 10+ years of litigation and advising experience, with significant experience representing journalists and media clients in matters involving newsgathering, access to public records, and other media law and First Amendment issues. – Self‑directed, with the ability to independently handle all aspects of litigation, including drafting papers, formulating strategy, and negotiating with opposing parties. – Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage litigation matters and the work of less‑experienced attorneys. – Outstanding legal research skills and excellent written communication skills. – Excellent public speaking and oral communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with a broad range of clients and stakeholders. – Good judgment and the highest level of professional integrity. Additional Information Physical Demands: The employee is frequently required to sit and operate computer equipment. Occasional standing and walking are required. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities. Compensation: RCFP offers competitive pay and generous benefits, including group medical insurance, disability insurance, retirement benefits, health‑reimbursement accounts, and paid family leave. The salary range for this position is **$117,300 to $130,500**. How to apply: Submit a resume and cover letter in **one PDF file** here . Only complete applications will advance in the hiring process. The role will remain open until filled. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RCFP Is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The organization celebrates the diversity of its employees and leadership. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: State Government Affairs Director (Southeast)
item.description: State Government Affairs Director (Southeast) Organization: Foundation for Government Accountability (FGA) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## **OVERVIEW** The Foundation for Government Accountability (FGA) is hiring a State Government Affairs Director (Southeast) to own our government affairs work across Alabama, Arkansas, North Carolina, and South Carolina. In this role, you’ll build the legislative strategy for each state, cultivate the relationships that move bills, and shepherd FGA’s reform priorities through the 2027 sessions. You’ll drive FGA’s agenda in your states and become the go-to strategist for the lawmakers who decide which bills move. When a legislative fight heats up, you run the war room: set the strategy, rally the partners, and get the reform passed. The ideal candidate brings at least five years in state government affairs, policy advocacy, or related political work, with a track record of winning tough policy fights. This role is remote, and we strongly prefer candidates who live in Alabama, Arkansas, North Carolina, or South Carolina. Expect regular travel across these four states, with the heaviest stretches during session. — ## **CULTURE AND FIT** The people who consistently succeed at FGA are those whose actions and behavior reflect our five Core Values. If you adhere to these values and answer “yes” to each of the following questions, you may be a fit. ### 1) Candid to Solve Being willing to have tough conversations in order to solve issues and build trust. · Do you seek out constructive feedback—and provide it to others—to solve issues and build trust with coworkers? ### 2) Grow or Die We don’t have a neutral gear; we must consistently challenge ourselves and each other to grow in our talents and skills. · Are you aware of your strengths and weaknesses, and do you seek out complementary skills and growth in order to mitigate your weaknesses? ### 3) Politically Savvy Policy doesn’t change in a vacuum, but in a political reality that we must understand and account for. · Do you agree that embracing the realities of politics is necessary to change public policy? ### 4) Partnership-Oriented Internal and external relationships are not transactional. That starts with our team members and the perspective that we need the rest of the team to succeed in order to win personally. · Are you comfortable creating your own structure for work, such as setting work hours, your own priorities, and creating clarity and a work plan from a broad goal? ### 5) Bought in to Win We’re at FGA because we want to change policy. No one is counting hours or widgets. We are here to get results, and sometimes, that will require going the extra mile or doing a job that isn’t technically ours. · Do you fully support FGA’s mission and believe that lives are improved through work, not welfare, and that free markets create more freedom and opportunity than government control? The vast majority of those who don’t get hired (or don’t last) at FGA are due to a lack of fit with these values. Be prepared to have very candid conversations about them in our interview process. — ## **ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** As State Government Affairs Director (Southeast), you will have four primary areas of responsibility: ### 1) Build and Execute State Strategy · Create and own the strategy for each state in your portfolio, evaluating the political environment, identifying the policy openings, aligning stakeholders, and mapping the path for every reform priority. · Shepherd FGA’s priorities through the 2027 legislative sessions by securing sponsors, managing collateral needs, and tracking initiatives from introduction through final passage. ### 2) Cultivate Relationships with Policymakers and Allies · Become the trusted resource for governors’ offices, legislators, legislative and executive staff, agency leaders, and allied third-party groups across all four states. · Conduct in-person stakeholder meetings throughout the portfolio and represent FGA in briefings and small-group settings. ### 3) Manage FGA’s In-State Contractors · Set goals with each in-state contractor, keep a clear communication cadence, and hold them accountable for the state agenda. · Put your contractors’ relationships to work opening doors with key decision-makers. ### 4) Serve as FGA’s Internal Point Person for the Southeast · Own the flow of information between your states and FGA’s Federal Affairs, Development, Policy and Research, and Communications teams. · Use Basecamp to file clear requests, answer internal questions quickly, and bring colleagues into state trips and lawmaker meetings with enough lead time to be useful. — ## **REQUIREMENTS** 🔹 Five or more years of experience in state legislative, government affairs, campaign, or public policy roles. 🔹 Strong preference for candidates who reside in Alabama, Arkansas, North Carolina, or South Carolina, plus regular travel throughout the portfolio that lightens in the off-season. 🔹 Deep understanding of state legislative and executive policymaking, with the political judgment to identify the decision-makers and influencers who move legislation. 🔹 Exceptional communicator with the organization to quarterback legislative calendars, hearings, policymaker communications, and collateral needs across four states at once. 🔹 Fluent with technology and AI tools, including platforms like Basecamp and Quorum, to track data, manage projects, and speed up research and drafting. 🔹 Match FGA’s Core Values (described above). — ## **TIMING, LOCATION, AND COMPENSATION** FGA is seeking to fill this position as soon as possible. Beyond travel across your portfolio, expect legislative fly-ins and quarterly team meetings. FGA’s headquarters are in Naples, FL, but nearly all of our staff work remotely from across the country. We build our systems and culture around clarity, flexibility, and strong communication. Key elements include: · Quarterly in-person team meetings at which you’ll build deeper relationships, set clear goals aligned with FGA’s big vision, and brainstorm how to seize new opportunities · An intensive 90-day orientation to familiarize you with the FGA team, our policies, and how we operate · Home office setup, including equipment and communication tools you need to hit the ground running FGA offers a competitive salary between $100,000–$130,000, depending on experience and qualifications, along with a benefits package that includes a six percent retirement match, health benefits, and generous paid leave. — Teams Government Affairs Locations Remote, USA Yearly salary $100,000 – $130,000 Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Executive Director, REL Government Relations (P1-6377418-1)
item.description: Executive Director, REL Government Relations (P1-6377418-1) Organization: Panda Restaurant Group Inc. Location: Rosemead, CA Date Posted: 09/08/2026 ## Summary of Job Description The Executive Director, Real Estate Legal Government Relations and Public Policy is responsible for creating, leading, and executing Real Estate Legal’s government relations, public policy, and public affairs strategies in support of Panda Restaurant Group’s national growth and development objectives. This position serves as the Company’s primary liaison with federal, state, and local government agencies, elected officials, regulatory agencies, municipalities, utility providers, and other stakeholders impacting restaurant development, real estate operations, and business initiatives. The Executive Director plays a critical role in managing third‑party consents, fostering positive governmental and community relationships, and representing the Company on legislative, regulatory, and public policy matters affecting Panda nationally. This position monitors emerging legislation, regulatory developments, and public policy trends, evaluates business impacts, and develops strategic advocacy plans to support favorable outcomes. — ## Job Responsibilities Leads Panda Restaurant Group’s Real Estate Government Relations, Public Policy, and Legislative Affairs function, monitoring, analyzing, and influencing federal, state, and local legislative, regulatory, and administrative matters affecting restaurant development, operations, permitting, zoning, land use, utilities, transportation, taxation, and other business interests. Represents the Company before governmental agencies, elected officials, industry associations, community stakeholders, utility providers, and transportation authorities to advance business objectives, protect strategic interests, enhance brand reputation, and reduce development timelines nationwide. Develops and executes government relations and stakeholder engagement strategies that support restaurant growth and development initiatives. Monitors political, regulatory, construction, and community sentiment trends, proactively identifying risks, opportunities, and mitigation strategies affecting development and operational objectives. Partners with Restaurant Development, Real Estate, Construction, Design, Legal, and other internal stakeholders to secure required third‑party consents, approvals, and stakeholder support for development projects. Interprets and applies relevant laws, contracts, restrictions, and regulatory requirements while resolving objections, negotiating solutions, and accelerating project execution. Builds and maintains strategic relationships with governmental entities, municipalities, community organizations, major retailers, restrictive‑use operators, consultants, and other external stakeholders to facilitate approvals, foster goodwill, and support the successful completion of development initiatives. Provides leadership and oversight of the REL Government Relations team, including organizational design, talent selection, coaching, training, performance management, and professional development to support the Company’s long‑term growth strategy. Collaborates with enterprise government relations partners to align advocacy efforts, share best practices, leverage resources, and eliminate duplication across initiatives while strengthening organizational capabilities. Directs project communications, documentation, compliance tracking, and executive reporting related to government relations activities, stakeholder engagement, consent approvals, and strategic initiatives, providing leadership with timely updates on project status, risks, outcomes, and business impact. — ## How We Reward You – Hybrid work schedule – 401K with company match – Yearly bonus opportunity* – Full medical, dental, and vision insurance* – On‑site fitness center, biometric screen, and flu shot clinic – Discounts at Panda restaurants, theme parks, and gym memberships – Paid time off starting at 15 days with 7 federal holidays* – Continuous education assistance and scholarships* – Income protection including Disability, Life, and AD&D insurance* – Bereavement leave* *Benefits available for eligible permanent full‑time associates. — ## Your Background and Experience Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, marketing, or a related field and a law license required; construction, regulatory, and negotiation experience required. 12–15 years of experience in real estate, public relations, and community engagement or a similar role with increasing management responsibility. Successful completion of initial and periodically required trainings. Obtaining a valid Food Handler’s Card within 30 days of employment is a requirement of this position. — ## Pay Range **M5: $205,000 – $288,000 / Annual** *Within the range, individual pay is determined using various factors, including work location and experience.* #LI‑Hybrid #LI‑ZP1 — ## Panda Strong Since 1983 Founded in Glendale, California, we are now the largest family‑owned American Chinese Restaurant concept in America. With close to 2,800 locations globally, we continue our mission of delivering exceptional Asian dining experiences by building an organization where people are inspired to better their lives. Whether it’s impacting our team or the communities we work in, we’re proud to be an organization that embraces family values. — ## You’re Wanted Here Panda Restaurant Group, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to providing equal opportunity, and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by law, including but not limited to sex/gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related conditions), gender expression, race, color, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, ancestry, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, and veteran status. Additionally, Panda Restaurant Group, Inc. complies with all federal, state, and local laws regarding requests for workplace accommodation. The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) prohibits discrimination against qualified individuals on the basis of disability. Applicants are entitled to reasonable accommodations, absent undue hardship, to effectively participate in the application and hiring process, for example, sign language interpreters. If you believe you require an accommodation for the application or interview process or for the position for which you are applying, please reach out to ** [email protected] **. item.title: Specialist – Corporate Affairs
item.description: Specialist – Corporate Affairs Organization: Lidl Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/09/2026 **Corporate Affairs Associate – Lidl US** The corporate affairs team at Lidl oversees internal communications, external communications/PR, government relations, and CSR/corporate giving. We’re looking for a detail‑oriented, self‑starter who is ready to support all parts of the corporate affairs function. This jack‑of‑all‑trades role supports the Head of Corporate Affairs and helps execute Lidl US’ corporate affairs strategy. The ideal candidate has a keen eye for detail, proactively manages workstreams, and thrives under tight deadlines. — ### Responsibilities #### Internal Communications – Support execution of internal communications strategy – Help develop content for internal channels (intranet, internal app, etc.) – Help maintain content calendars – Support town hall meetings as needed (deck creation, in‑person execution) #### PR Support – Work with internal teams to gather information and facilitate approvals – Draft PR reactive statements as needed – Periodically travel to store openings #### CSR Support – Manage corporate donations – Support development of CSR report – Support employee engagement CSR initiatives #### Corporate Web & Social Media – Partner with Head of Corporate Affairs to plan and create corporate social channel content (videos, images, text, etc.) – Support executive team LinkedIn needs as necessary – Support corporate website content and design — ### About You – You are task‑ and detail‑oriented – You are a self‑starter; you proactively communicate project status, identify challenges, and welcome feedback – You are interested in and familiar with corporate communications, brand PR, executive communications, internal communications, government relations, CSR/corporate giving – You are eager to learn more about all aspects of corporate affairs – You excel at designing materials (social content, slide decks, fact sheets, emails) – You can write engaging material on quick deadlines – You work collaboratively and comfortably with various stakeholders – You organize workstreams, create content calendars, and manage multiple projects – You enjoy finding creative ways to communicate with employees — ### Required Knowledge, Skills, Abilities – Strong writing and design skills – Ability to learn, adapt, and strive for continuous improvement – Ability to prioritize tasks and manage a diverse workload with strong organizational skills — ### Required Education, Certifications, Related Experience – Bachelor’s Degree – 1–3 years of experience in corporate communications, marketing, or related field — ### Physical Requirements – Ability to work in a fast‑paced environment – Ability to sit, stand, walk, squat, and/or bend more than half the time – Ability to operate equipment requiring constant use of hands/fingers/wrists more than half the time – Ability to spend more than half the time viewing computer monitors – Ability to identify and distinguish between colors more than half the time – Position commutes between regional stores/offices/distribution centers less than 25% of the time – Position requires overnight domestic travel up to 20% of the time – Travel may be by car, air, and/or train — ### Our Values **Performance** We thrive together to pursue ambitious goals, develop ourselves, and turn complex challenges into opportunities. **Respect** We put people at the center, treat each other fairly, ensure equal opportunities, and value diversity as a cultural strength. **Trust** We believe in each other, communicate openly, remain reliable, and treat mistakes as learning opportunities. **Grounded** We dream big while staying down to earth, choosing simplicity and focusing on meaningful results. **Belonging** We stand up for one another, leverage collective strengths, and focus on sustainable, long‑term relationships. — ### What You’ll Receive At Lidl, we know that for our people to do their best, they must feel their best. That’s why we offer one of the most generous benefits packages in the industry. All Lidl employees are eligible for: – Starting pay of **$33.66** (with potential to earn **$38.47**) – Medical & Prescription | Dental | Vision coverage – Paid Holiday & Paid Time Off (PTO) – Dedicated training plans – 401K Plan (+ 5% company match) – Voluntary Term Life & AD&D Insurance – Total Well‑Being Program – DailyPay (voluntary benefit for early access to earned pay) Lidl US views Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) through actions that are **Good for the Environment, Good for People, and Good for You.** #teamlidl #LI‑AL1 Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Associate Vice President of Marketing & Communications
item.description: Associate Vice President of Marketing & Communications Organization: Levine Music Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 ## Department: Marketing & Communications ## Reports to: Chief Operating Officer ## Supervises: Director of Marketing & Communications and Digital Media Producer ## Salary Range: $105,000 – $115,000 ## Job Type: Full-Time, In Person ## Start Date: January 2027 — ## Position Summary Levine Music seeks a strategic, collaborative, and hands-on Associate Vice President of Marketing & Communications to lead the Marketing and Communications department and help advance Levine’s mission, visibility, enrollment, and institutional brand. Following a successful rebranding and website development initiative, Levine’s marketing function is ready to step into an exciting new chapter under the AVP’s leadership. Reporting to the COO, the AVP will develop and implement integrated marketing and communications strategies that support student enrollment, program visibility, institutional storytelling, events, community engagement, and long-term brand growth. This leader will supervise a small yet high-performing team, manage external partners, and work closely with colleagues across the organization to ensure consistent, compelling, and mission-aligned communications. — ## Essential Duties and Responsibilities ### Strategic Leadership – Lead the development and execution of Levine’s annual marketing and communications strategy in alignment with organizational priorities. – Translate institutional goals into integrated marketing plans that support enrollment, retention, earned revenue, performances, community engagement, and institutional visibility. – Partner with the COO, CEO, and senior leaders to position Levine consistently and effectively across audiences and channels. – Establish clear priorities, workflows, and measures of success for the department. – Manage the daily functions of the Marketing budget, making recommendations to the COO regarding the necessary advertising investment and allocation. – Work with campus and programmatic leadership to develop location- and program-specific visibility and student recruitment initiatives. ### Brand and Communications – Serve as the lead steward of Levine’s brand, voice, and messaging across the organization. – Ensure that all communications reflect Levine’s mission, values, and commitment to community and accessibility. – Oversee development of compelling content for website, email, digital campaigns, print materials, video, advertising, and institutional communications, ensuring the effective production and consistent quality of all materials representing Levine’s brand and programs. – Hire and guide graphic designers, as budgets allow, to realize and grow Levine’s visual brand identity. – Serve as a keen editor and thought partner for internal and external communications across departments. ### Enrollment and Program Marketing – Develop and execute data-driven strategies that acquire audiences for tuition programs and events on Levine’s extensive performance calendar. – Implement an omnichannel strategy that ensures an annual pipeline of new student applications and registrations. – Partner with Education, Student Services, and other departments to effectively position programs for successful enrollment. – Oversee campaign calendars and promotional plans tied to key enrollment periods and program cycles. – Provide regular reports and analysis to the COO and VP of Music Education on the efficacy and optimization of campaigns. ### Fundraising and Institutional Advancement – Partner with colleagues on the Development team on fundraising initiatives, particularly initiatives that require print, web, or video support. – Oversee integration solutions between communication platforms and fundraising CRM systems. – Serve as a thought partner on strategic communication messaging to achieve contributed revenue goals, bridging the donor and program audience perspectives. – Contribute to the messaging, branding, digital media needs, and overall success of major fundraising events, such as the annual gala. ### Digital Strategy and Content – Oversee Levine’s digital presence, including website content strategy, email marketing, social media direction, and digital advertising. – Manage website developers when necessary and ensure the health and optimization of Levine’s website and other external-facing digital properties. – Collaborate with internal staff and contractors on content planning, production, and publishing. – Manage the Digital Media Producer and serve as the lead director of Levine’s major video projects. ### Public Relations and Institutional Visibility – Help shape external communications and earned media opportunities that elevate Levine’s profile regionally and nationally. – Serve as the organization’s primary press liaison and spokesperson. – Draft or oversee press releases, institutional statements, and media materials as needed. – Seek and acquire opportunities for positive press exposure for Levine’s programs, stories, and mission. – Support executive communications and high-visibility institutional messaging. ### Team and Project Management – Supervise and develop the Director of Marketing and Digital Media Producer. – Foster and lead a supportive and creative team environment and, by example, contribute to a positive and collaborative interdepartmental culture. – Oversee external contractors, freelancers, agencies, and vendors as assigned. – Create efficient department workflows, timelines, approvals, and production processes. – Lead a service-oriented team culture with strong accountability and communication. ### Analytics, Budget, and Operations – Monitor and report on campaign performance, audience engagement, and other key metrics. – Provide regular updates and recommendations to the COO and senior leadership. – Manage the marketing and communications budget responsibly and recommend investments aligned with priorities. – Maintain organized systems for content planning, asset management, and departmental operations. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, public relations, arts administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. – 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in marketing, communications, or related fields. – Demonstrated experience managing multiple communications channels, tracking performance, and growing institutional visibility. – Proven experience managing large-scale, omnichannel paid advertising campaigns that drive earned revenue, analyzing performance, and reporting on ROI. – Experience liaising with media outlets on behalf of an organization is required. – Prior supervisory or team leadership experience preferred. – Excellent writing, editing, and message development skills. – Strong project management and organizational skills. – Experience working in a mission-driven, nonprofit, arts, education, or cultural organization preferred. – Experience with digital marketing, email platforms, website content management, analytics, and vendor management preferred. – Appreciation for music, arts education, and community-centered programming strongly preferred. — ## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities – Strategic thinker with strong execution skills – Strong judgment and decision-making ability – Ability to manage up, across, and down in a collaborative organization – Ability to balance creativity, deadlines, and competing priorities – Strong visual and editorial instincts – Commitment to inclusive, audience-aware communications – Ability to work occasionally during evenings or weekends for performances and special events — ## To Apply Please submit a cover letter, resume, portfolio, and a brief statement of your marketing approach via email to: **Maria Williams** Senior Director of Human Resources Levine Music 2801 Upton Street, NW Washington, DC 20008 [email protected] [www.levinemusic.org] — ## Equal Opportunity Statement Levine Music is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Levine Music’s employment policy is committed to anti-discrimination of employees or applicants based on sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law concerning any employment practices. item.title: Director, Political Operations
item.description: Director, Political Operations Organization: Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 # Director, Political Operations The Director, Political Operations plays a key role in advancing ICBA’s federal political program by supporting the development and execution of ICBA PAC’s fundraising strategy, donor engagement initiatives, political disbursement strategy, compliance program, and grassroots political activities. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Political Operations, this position helps drive the growth of one of the nation’s leading federal trade association PACs through strategic fundraising campaigns, donor cultivation and stewardship, political event management, financial oversight, and strict adherence to Federal Election Commission (FEC) regulations. The Director works closely with ICBA’s Congressional Relations team, leadership bankers, state association partners, and volunteer leaders to strengthen political engagement, expand donor participation, and support ICBA’s advocacy priorities. This position is open to applicants in the Washington, DC area. — # What You’ll Do ## Political Fundraising & Donor Engagement Support the development and execution of ICBA PAC’s annual fundraising strategy, including donor acquisition, retention, stewardship, and campaign planning to achieve fundraising goals. Develop and implement multi-channel fundraising campaigns, including digital, direct mail, peer-to-peer, payroll deduction, event-based, and leadership giving initiatives. Identify, cultivate, and engage new donor audiences while strengthening relationships with existing contributors, leadership bankers, and volunteer advocates. Analyze fundraising performance and donor trends to identify opportunities for increased participation and revenue growth. Assist Congressional Relations staff in planning and hosting political fundraising events and donor engagement activities nationwide. Work in partnership with the ICBA Meetings & Events Department to plan and execute ICBA PAC fundraising events, including the ICBA PAC Silent Auction, regional fundraising events, VIP donor recognition programs, and targeted fundraising campaigns. Oversee the ICBA PAC Directors Club Program, including participant recruitment, recognition, annual renewals, and stewardship initiatives. Manage the ICBA PAC Payroll Deduction Program, coordinating participating banks, maintaining compliance documentation, facilitating recurring contributions, and expanding participation. ## Political Operations & Compliance Support the development and implementation of ICBA PAC’s political strategy in conjunction with the Senior Vice President, Congressional Relations staff, leadership bankers, state association partners, and key stakeholders. Participate in ICBA PAC compliance and financial operations, including contribution processing, candidate disbursements, financial reconciliations, maintenance of solicitation and authorization records, and preparation of Federal Election Commission (FEC) reports. Manage the PAC compliance database and maintain accurate financial records, including receipt processing, ACH transactions, bank reconciliations, and coordination with affiliated PACs and ICBA Accounting. Prepare candidate disbursement materials, maintain disbursement budgets, coordinate approvals, process checks and ACH payments, and ensure timely execution of political contributions. Compile and analyze contribution, fundraising, and disbursement reports for senior leadership and committee presentations. Manage annual prior approval campaigns and solicitation authorization records in accordance with FEC regulations. ## Advocacy & Stakeholder Relations Collaborate with ICBA’s grassroots advocacy team to recruit, retain, and engage grassroots advocates while strengthening participation in ICBA PAC. Prepare meeting materials, reports, presentations, and fundraising updates for ICBA PAC Committee meetings and leadership discussions. Support strategic initiatives that strengthen ICBA’s political advocacy efforts and advance the community banking industry’s federal legislative priorities. Perform other related duties as assigned. — # What You Bring Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Affairs, Public Administration, Communications, Business, or related field required. Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in political fundraising, PAC management, campaign finance, government relations, association management, nonprofit fundraising, or public policy. Experience managing a federal PAC and fundraising for a trade association, membership organization, campaign committee, or advocacy organization, including planning political fundraising events and donor recognition programs preferred. Demonstrated success developing and executing fundraising campaigns, donor cultivation strategies, or political fundraising initiatives. Working knowledge of Federal Election Commission (FEC) regulations and campaign finance compliance. Knowledge of congressional campaigns, federal political committees, and Capitol Hill operations preferred. Experience managing fundraising databases, CRM systems, or PAC compliance software (Quorum or similar preferred). Experience working with volunteer boards or fundraising committees preferred. Strong financial management and reporting skills with exceptional attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build relationships with senior executives, volunteer leaders, elected officials, and donors. Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and work independently in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret fundraising metrics and prepare executive-level reports. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Adobe Acrobat, and database applications. Ability to travel approximately 5–6 times annually. We recognize that candidates may not meet every qualification listed. If your background and experience are close to what we’re seeking, we encourage you to apply. — # Benefits of Working at ICBA Generous and competitive benefits package 401(k) savings plan offering 100% employer match of up to 6% of annual earnings. Hybrid work environment, monthly work from home stipends, and flexible work hours Fitness discounts, telemedicine, on-demand therapy, and work-life balance tools Tuition reimbursement and allowances for professional development Frequent company social events Friendly and inclusive workplace culture The target annual salary range for this role is currently $105,000 to $125,000 based on a regular, full-time schedule. The amount of compensation offered will be determined by several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications, location, market data and internal equity. ICBA is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. ICBA does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. — # About ICBA The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA)’s guiding mission is to create and promote environments where community banks flourish. We are: • Dedicated advocates providing community bankers, policymakers and the public with authoritative insights and resources to support and strengthen community banking. • Knowledgeable, applying their expertise to offer personalized service that addresses the distinct challenges and opportunities facing community banks. • Community-centered, driving meaningful change that strengthens community banks and the communities they serve. We turn commitment into action and deliver real results. ICBA’s workplace culture is built on our core values: • Caring – We support and prioritize your well-being and professional growth. • Connected – We foster strong relationships that create meaningful impact. • Collaboration – We are team-oriented and results driven where diverse perspectives are valued, and innovative ideas are encouraged to achieve our common goals. — # Join ICBA Join ICBA and further your career while making a lasting impact! Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Digital Marketing & Communications Manager
item.description: Digital Marketing & Communications Manager Organization: Greater DC Diaper Bank Location: Silver Spring, MD Date Posted: 09/09/2026 **Description** **About Greater DC Diaper Bank** Greater DC Diaper Bank (GDCDB) works to ensure that families across the Washington, DC region have access to the diapers and other essentials they need to thrive. Founded in 2010, GDCDB has grown into one of the largest diaper banks in the country, working alongside more than 80 community partners across DC, Maryland, and Virginia to get millions of free diapers into the hands of families each year. As GDCDB enters its next chapter, we are strengthening and expanding the partnerships that make this work possible while deepening our understanding of diaper insecurity and the solutions that can support families across our region. — **Position Summary** Greater DC Diaper Bank is seeking an experienced Digital Marketing & Communications Manager to lead our digital marketing and social media strategy, serving as the primary storyteller and content creator across our online channels, with additional responsibility for broader communications support. This role combines strategy and hands-on execution, working closely across the organization to create clear, compelling, accessible content that increases awareness around diaper insecurity and inspires engagement with the organization. This position is ideal for someone who is a strong storyteller and implementer with strategic instincts. If you are excited to build systems, enjoy collaborating with a fun and passionate team, and love creating content, please apply! — **Key Responsibilities** ### Digital Marketing & Social Media Strategy – Own GDCDB’s social media strategy and day-to-day execution across Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn, driving audience growth, engagement, and community connection. – Manage GDCDB’s social media presence with a focus on community engagement and brand integrity. – Test and iterate on content formats, timing, and messaging based on platform performance data. – Plan and execute social media campaigns in partnership with volunteer programs to support product drives and other community engagement initiatives. – Oversee and update an annual marketing and communications plan that elevates GDCDB’s issue, brand, and impact and strengthens engagement across key audiences. – Track, test, and analyze campaign performance and recommend data-informed improvements to inform ongoing strategy and content decisions. ### Content Creation & Storytelling – Manage and maintain a content calendar across channels, including social, website, and email. – Develop community-centered stories that highlight families, partners, volunteers, and supporters and illustrate GDCDB’s impact. – Capture photography and short-form video at events, volunteer sessions, and partner visits. – Produce high-quality, on-brand graphics and everyday creative assets using Canva. ### Channel & Digital Platform Management – Ensure website updates, coordinating non-technical edits and content refreshes. – Ensure accessibility best practices are followed across all digital communications. – Manage GDCDB’s email communications program, including newsletters, partner communications, and other audience-specific email streams, working with appropriate internal teams on content and priorities and leading content planning, audience segmentation, scheduling, and performance analysis. ### Fundraising Communications and Digital Engagement – Partner with the development team to support digital fundraising campaigns, bringing expertise in digital strategy, audience engagement, and communications best practices. – Build and optimize fundraising emails, landing pages, donation pages, and other digital campaign assets, with a focus on engagement and conversion. – Review and strengthen digital and direct mail fundraising communications for clarity, effectiveness, and alignment with organizational messaging and brand. – Develop strategies to deepen engagement across GDCDB’s community, including converting volunteers to donors, donors to volunteers, and other supporters to deeper forms of involvement. ### Systems Building & Infrastructure – Create and document marketing & communications processes, templates, style guides, and workflows. – Strengthen communications systems and digital engagement practices to support scalable, measurable growth. ### Additional Collateral & Cross-Department Partnership – Lead development of key GDCDB assets, including the annual report and marketing collateral such as one-pagers and presentations, in partnership with organizational leadership, coordinating content, design, and production. – In partnership with GDCDB’s volunteer programs, develop and implement strategies to engage volunteers, strengthen their connection to GDCDB’s mission and impact, and encourage new and continued involvement. – Coordinate with external creative or strategic partners as needed, including GDCDB’s public relations consultant, to support media relations and earned media opportunities. – Build strong working relationships across teams to ensure communications accurately reflect GDCDB’s work, priorities, and impact. – Collaborate with the development, programs, and operations teams to ensure consistent messaging and streamlined collaboration. – Support all staff in understanding and using brand guidelines and organizational messaging. – Attend events, including some evenings and occasional weekends, to support content capture and live storytelling. — **Qualifications** ### Required – Demonstrated experience planning and executing social media campaigns, including experience creating compelling content for Instagram, Facebook, or LinkedIn, with results in audience growth or engagement. – Four+ years of progressively responsible experience in digital marketing, social media, communications, or related roles. – Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to translate complex information into snackable, compelling, audience-appropriate content across channels. – Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, relationships, and priorities simultaneously. – Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments, build trust, gather input, and provide communications guidance. – Familiarity with accessibility standards and best practices for digital content. – Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work. – Ability to work both independently and collaboratively, exercise sound judgment, and take ownership of projects from strategy through execution. – Located in the Washington, DC region with the ability to attend events, site visits, and community activities, including occasional evenings and weekends. – Commitment to GDCDB’s mission and to ensuring families across our region have access to the essentials they need. ### Preferred – Experience working in nonprofit, community-based, or other mission-driven communications. – Experience capturing quality photography and short-form video for digital communications. – Proficient in Canva or similar tools, with the ability to produce polished, on-brand graphics, layouts, and communications materials. – Experience supporting fundraising, donor communications, volunteer engagement, or other constituent engagement strategies. – Experience using email marketing, CRM, and audience engagement platforms, including audience segmentation and performance tracking. – Experience using analytics, testing, and performance data to strengthen digital communications and campaigns. – Familiarity with website content management systems and basic SEO principles. — **Benefits** – Medical, dental & vision insurance – Retirement plan with employer contribution to 401(k) – Paid time off, including 11 Federal holidays and a week off in the summer and a week off during winter holidays – Flexible spending account – Monthly technology stipend – Life, short-term & long-term disability insurance – Employee assistance program – Work from home hybrid option available — **To Apply** Applications are only being accepted via email. Please apply no later than September 18, 2026 by directing your cover letter and resume to Kris Minor at [email protected] . Put “Digital Marketing & Communications Manager” in the subject of the e-mail. — **Anticipated Timeline of Search** – Sept. 18: posting closes – Oct 5–8: first-round interviews (virtual) – Oct 13–16: finalist interviews (in-person) – Early to mid Nov: start date Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Manager, Social Media Strategy & Marketing
item.description: Senior Manager, Social Media Strategy & Marketing Organization: Choice Hotels International Location: North Bethesda, MD Date Posted: 09/09/2026 **Job Summary** Choice Hotels International is seeking a **Senior Manager, Social Media Strategy & Marketing** to lead enterprise social strategy across platforms, creators, and content ecosystems. This role defines how social media, influencer marketing, and organic content work together to tell meaningful brand stories that drive relevance, engagement, and business impact. The position evolves social from a channel‑execution function into a fully integrated content and demand driver, ensuring alignment across brand, media, search, and emerging ecosystems. The Senior Manager establishes the strategic foundation for how social content contributes to discoverability, including integration with SEO and generative‑AI search environments. This role partners closely with internal stakeholders, external agencies, and cross‑functional teams to strengthen key messages, RTBs, and brand positioning. The ideal candidate understands cultural trends and identifies opportunities to amplify them through authentic brand‑led storytelling. **Note:** This role is **4 days onsite in North Bethesda, MD** and is **not eligible for visa sponsorship** now or in the future. — ### **Responsibilities** — ### **Enterprise Social Strategy Leadership** – Develop the enterprise social media strategy, defining the role of each platform and how organic, creator, and paid social efforts work together. – Translate business and marketing goals into integrated social and content strategies that drive measurable impact. – Establish enterprise frameworks for messaging and success measurement. – Assist in developing long‑term social strategy roadmaps, platform POVs, and capability evolution. – Translate paid social objectives, audience strategies, and performance insights into social and creator content approaches. – Maintain a steadfast commitment to KPIs that grow engagement, build brands, and drive demand. — ### **Creator & Influencer Strategy** – Lead enterprise creator and influencer strategy, including use cases, content frameworks, and governance models. – Oversee creator sourcing, briefing, and content direction with agencies and internal partners. – Serve as a strategic advisor to brand, loyalty, and segment teams on creator marketing. – Evaluate and guide onboarding of influencer and creator platforms, vendors, and partnerships. — ### **Organic Content Strategy & Social Leadership** – Set strategic direction for organic social content across enterprise and brand channels. – Define content testing and optimization frameworks to improve engagement and performance. – Ensure integration between organic content, paid amplification, and broader campaign execution. – Partner with Brand, PR, and Loyalty teams to elevate social as a strategic marketing channel. — ### **Social Content Discoverability & GEO/AEO** – Partner with SEO and content strategy teams to ensure social and creator content supports discoverability across search, generative AI, and emerging ecosystems. – Collaborate with Paid Media on GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) content strategies. – Work with email marketing to ensure cohesive messaging and lifecycle engagement across channels. – Establish best practices for structuring, tagging, and distributing content to improve indexing and visibility. – Determine signals that improve content performance beyond engagement, partnering with Analytics and SEO teams. – Support enterprise initiatives such as LLM visibility and content discoverability. — ### **Cross‑Functional Leadership & Enterprise Impact** – Own social media plans with Paid Media, SEO, Analytics, and PR to ensure integrated strategy and execution. – Serve as a subject matter expert, providing POVs and recommendations on social and creator strategy. – Support relationships with key social platform partners (Meta, TikTok, Snap, Reddit, Pinterest), including JBPs and strategic opportunities. – Align social strategy with broader marketing priorities and business objectives. – Drive visibility and understanding of social strategy across stakeholders. — ### **Agency & Partner Leadership** – Act as the lead for social and creator agency partners, setting expectations and performance standards. – Ensure agency partners operate as extensions of the internal team. – Manage external partnerships across influencer platforms and content vendors. — ### **Innovation & Capability Evolution** – Stay ahead of platform capabilities, cultural trends, and technology shifts and translate them into actionable strategies. – Lead test‑and‑learn initiatives across social platforms, creator models, and content formats. – Identify opportunities to scale new capabilities that enhance engagement and discoverability. — ### **Team Leadership & Development** – Build and lead a high‑performing social strategy team. – Coach and develop team members to increase autonomy and enterprise thinking. – Foster a culture of innovation, curiosity, and continuous learning. — ### **Qualifications** — ### **Employment Experience** – 7–10 years of experience in social media, digital marketing, content strategy, or related fields. – 3+ years of management experience with direct reports and cross‑functional initiatives. — ### **Technical & Functional Expertise** – Deep expertise across major social platforms (Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Reddit, Snap, YouTube, etc.) and awareness of emerging platforms and trends. – Strong understanding of creator and influencer marketing models. – Experience integrating social strategy with paid/organic social, brand marketing, and SEO. – Familiarity with content discoverability and AI‑driven ecosystems preferred. – Understanding of performance metrics and testing frameworks. — ### **Leadership & Business Competencies** – Proven ability to lead cross‑functional initiatives with enterprise impact. – Strong strategic thinking and problem‑solving skills. – Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. – Strong collaboration and ability to influence. — ### **Education** Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred. — ### **Salary Range** **$123,663.00 – $145,486.00** This role is also eligible for an annual bonus under Choice’s Management Incentive Plan (MIP). — ### **Benefits** Choice prioritizes associate wellbeing through a comprehensive, competitive, and flexible benefits program, including: – Competitive compensation and medical, dental, and vision coverage – Leave and paid time‑off for holidays, vacation, personal, family, volunteer, sick, jury duty, bereavement, military, and religious observance – Retirement and health savings financial benefits – Employee recognition programs – Discounts at Choice hotels worldwide — ### **About Choice** Choice Hotels International, Inc. (NYSE: CHH) is one of the world’s largest lodging franchisors, with **7,500 hotels in 45+ countries and territories**. The company supports strivers, dreamers, and entrepreneurs — reflecting its own culture of innovation and ambition. Choice operates from: – **North Bethesda, MD** — Worldwide headquarters at Pike & Rose – **Scottsdale, AZ** — Technology, eCommerce, and customer service hub – **Minneapolis, MN** — Select roles based near Highway 394 – **Field/Remote** — Select roles requiring home‑office work and virtual collaboration — ### **Choice’s Cultural Values** Welcome and Respect Everyone | Be Bold | Be Quick | Listen | Be Curious | Show Integrity ### **Choice’s Leadership Principles** Act with Intention | Lead with Authenticity | Grow & Deliver Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
