item.title: Analyst Program
item.description: Analyst Program Organization: Edelman Smithfield Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. | Chicago, IL | San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 09/09/2026 # We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions. # Edelman Smithfield Analyst Program – Role & Opportunity Overview Eligible for 2027 college graduates with a start date in July 2027 To be considered, please submit your application by October 31, 2026 ## Launch Your Career in Financial Communications | A Boutique with the Full Reach and Resources of Edelman Edelman Smithfield is a global financial communications firm with the power and scope of Edelman, the world’s largest integrated communications agency. We advise senior leaders and management teams navigating complex matters that impact reputation and valuation and have deep expertise in serving and communicating to the financial markets. Serving clients in the United States, Canada, EMEA, APAC, and beyond, Edelman Smithfield offers a deep and talented bench of approximately 250 financial market specialists across more than 25 cities and 15 countries. Edelman Smithfield’s Analyst Program provides college graduates the opportunity to launch their careers in financial communications at the largest communications agency in the world. Our full-time, 15‑month‑long program is designed to develop the next generation of financial communications leaders. Analysts will work alongside global companies and financial services brands – including some of the world’s pre‑eminent financial services firms and Fortune 500 companies – and develop media relations, research and writing skills while learning the intricacies of financial services, deal work, special situations, investor relations, and digital financial communications. Following the successful completion of the program, Analysts will have the opportunity to be promoted into the Account Executive role to continue their career at Edelman Smithfield. The Analyst Program has opportunities in our New York, Washington DC, Chicago, and San Francisco offices. We offer a flexible, hybrid work schedule with at least three days per week in the office. ## Hands-On Experience and Opportunity Analysts will gain exposure to all aspects of the financial communications verticals within Edelman Smithfield, participating in both tactical and strategic elements of account management and client counsel, including: – Drafting and editing materials including press releases, investor presentations, Q&As and other materials – Conducting in‑depth research/peer benchmarking of financial metrics, company disclosure, sell‑side analyst commentary and estimates – Working with various media outlets to manage reporter contacts, inquiries, and interviews – Monitoring client‑related news and filings daily, and alerting teams to breaking news events – Demonstrating a comprehensive understanding of clients’ businesses and key stakeholders, imparting critical knowledge to account team members – Honing exceptional writing and narrative development, messaging and creative skills – Acting as a collaborative team member and serving as daily client support, partnering with the client lead when appropriate – Participating in new business processes including research, proposal and pitch preparation ### Additional skills and experiences include: – Create financial communications plans for strategic situations as well as investor relations, including both tactical and strategic elements – Aid in providing counsel to clients on messaging and positioning across all external investor and financial communications, including quarterly earnings news releases and conference call scripts, material corporate news, investor presentations, and general communications with the investment community – Support traditional “retainer” based clients as well as transaction‑oriented project work (including M&A, IPOs, shareholder activism, and investor days) – Interact with client shareholders and sell‑side analysts, discussing client business attributes, collecting feedback, supporting bank‑sponsored non‑deal road shows, and reacting to investment community informational needs ## A Selective Program for the Leaders of Tomorrow This position is ideal for an individual looking to take part in a fast‑paced, intellectually challenging environment and to acquire the experience necessary to become a successful financial communications practitioner and advisor to companies of all sizes and industry sectors. The following skills and experience will be prioritized when seeking candidates: – Excellent organization, keen attention to detail and the ability to adapt to new conditions, assignments and deadlines – Excellent written and verbal communications skills and ability to delegate tactical assignments and accurately judge and edit work of others – Strong analytical skillset, including comfort synthesizing company disclosures and financial data – Ability to take ownership of assigned projects and accountability of deliverables and tasks from start to finish – A solid knowledge of MS Office Suite – A strong work ethic and consistent dedication to providing quality work – Demonstrate personal initiative and leadership skills through internships, student organizations, prior work experiences and/or volunteerism or other similar activities – Candidates should be interested in experience in financial communications and/or related experience in research, investment management, consulting, marketing and finance – Previous internship experience with financial communications, investor relations, investment banking, management consulting or other communications agencies a bonus $60,000 – $72,500 per year #LI-NM1 An employee’s pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, travel requirements, revenue‑based metrics, any contractual agreements, and business or organizational needs. The range listed is just one component of DJEH’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, a Paid Time Off policy, and region‑specific benefits. DJEH offers a wide range of benefits: medical and dental insurance, vision, 401K, life insurance, disability insurance, paid time off, travel assistance and wellness programming. DJEH is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and believes in diversity, equity, and inclusion. We seek applications from all qualified candidates without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, military and veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation in any part of the employment process, please let us know. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Communications Associate
item.description: Communications Associate Organization: MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 ## Inspired by Jewish Values and Ideals Inspired by Jewish values and ideals, MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger is a national advocacy organization working to end hunger among people of all faiths and backgrounds in the United States and Israel. For more than 40 years, MAZON has worked to ensure that laws, policies, and regulations governing access to food are available, accessible, and meaningful to all those in need. Our focus areas include college students, immigrants, Indigenous communities, members of the LGBTQ+ community, military families, the people of Puerto Rico, single mothers, and veterans. Our efforts are designed to provide people with the resources they need in a manner that is dignified and without judgment. All people — regardless of circumstance — must have access to adequate, nutritious food, while retaining their choice, agency, and dignity. MAZON is a leading national voice on anti-hunger issues. We work independently and in coalition with partners to protect and strengthen government nutrition programs that help people put food on the table, explore innovative solutions to persistent challenges to food security, and undertake unique strategies to bring such solutions to fruition. We educate communities across the country about the reality of hunger and how they can join us to help end it. We also provide funding to expand advocacy, training, and resources to nonprofit organizations across the United States and Israel, which includes a range of partnerships with local advocacy groups, food banks, legal-service organizations, and statewide coalitions. — ## Position Overview The Communications Associate helps implement a strategic, multi-faceted communications program designed to promote MAZON’s advocacy priorities, raise funds, and grow brand visibility. The position is based in the organization’s Washington, DC office in a remote/in-office hybrid environment. This position is covered by a collective bargaining agreement. — ## Duties and Responsibilities – Under the direction of the Director of Communications, assists with day-to-day department projects, events, meetings, and general operations. – Works closely with the Senior Communications Manager to implement cross-channel communications strategy and various public relations tactics to advance MAZON’s advocacy, development, and programmatic goals. – Executes systems to maintain and improve MAZON’s online presence, including website and social media platforms. Compiles regular data and statistics about MAZON’s digital footprint. – Monitors MAZON in the news and anti-hunger issues in mainstream and niche media outlets, identifying opportunities for MAZON to engage, advance policy priorities, and raise visibility. – Curates MAZON’s story bank, media library (photos, videos, audio files, etc.), press lists, editorial calendars, and tracking documents. – Helps draft newsletter articles, talking points, speeches, opinion pieces, infographics, blog posts, and other materials as needed. – Other duties and responsibilities as assigned. – Some nights and weekends required. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. – At least 1–2 years of experience working in a nonprofit and/or public affairs organization, preferably in a communications role. Social justice, anti-hunger, public policy, or Jewish community experience is highly preferred. – Experience with WordPress, Canva, Google Analytics, and social media management. Experience with Salesforce, Quorum, Tableau, Feathr, or similar systems is a plus. – Excellent judgment, critical thinking, analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills. – Keen eye for design and attention to detail. – Excellent oral and written communication skills. – Ability to take direction well, manage deadlines efficiently, work independently, and collaborate effectively with various teams and partners. – Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities effectively. – High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism in all interactions. – Deep commitment to MAZON’s mission to end hunger. — ## Compensation and Benefits MAZON offers a compensation package with a competitive salary range of $60,000 to $64,000 annually. Employer-paid benefits include comprehensive medical insurance and Life/Disability/AD&D insurance. Other benefits include a 401K plan with an employer match, FSA participation, dental, vision, and AFLAC insurance at a discounted group rate. MAZON offers a very generous vacation, sick time plan, and holiday schedule, including all major Jewish holidays. We close early on Fridays in observance of Shabbat. We have a fun office environment (even virtually!) and a fantastic team who are dedicated to the meaningful work we do. — ## How to Apply Please send a cover letter, writing sample, and resume to [email protected] . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and applicants will be contacted within 4–6 weeks of submission (potentially earlier) if they have been selected for an interview. Please note: Applicants who meet our minimum application qualifications as outlined in the Job Description may be contacted to submit additional materials required by our hiring committee. Incomplete applications will not be considered. — ## Equal Opportunity Employer MAZON is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer committed to diversity and inclusion, and encourages applications from all qualified individuals, including people of color, people with disabilities, people of all gender identities, people of all races and national origins, veterans, and LBGTQIA individuals. We strive for a diverse workforce, and we acknowledge that our diversity also comes from our experiences and perspectives. We want all staff and team members to be treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to ensuring that you can carry out your assigned mission in an environment that is free from discrimination and harassment. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Director of State Policy Organization: MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger Location: Los Angeles, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 ## Inspired by Jewish values and ideals Inspired by Jewish values and ideals, MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger is a national advocacy organization working to end hunger among people of all faiths and backgrounds in the United States and Israel. For more than 40 years, MAZON has worked to ensure that laws, policies, and regulations governing access to food are available, accessible, and meaningful to all those in need. Our focus areas include college students, immigrants, Indigenous communities, members of the LGBTQ+ community, military families, the people of Puerto Rico, single mothers, and veterans. Our efforts are designed to provide people with the resources they need in a manner that is dignified and without judgment. All people — regardless of circumstance — must have access to adequate, nutritious food, while retaining their choice, agency, and dignity. MAZON is a leading national voice on anti-hunger issues. We work independently and in coalition with partners to protect and strengthen government nutrition programs that help people put food on the table, explore innovative solutions to persistent challenges to food security, and undertake unique strategies to bring such solutions to fruition. We educate communities across the country about the reality of hunger and how they can join us to help end it. We also provide funding to expand advocacy, training, and resources to nonprofit organizations across the United States and Israel, which includes a range of partnerships with local advocacy groups, food banks, legal-service organizations, and statewide coalitions. — ## Position Overview The Director of State Policy directs the organization’s state advocacy program, working closely with the Vice President of Public Affairs to develop policy priorities, create materials, and devise strategies to advance policy priorities. This is a hybrid position based in MAZON’s Los Angeles office or D.C. office, but we will consider candidates in other locations. — ## Duties and Responsibilities Under the direction of the Vice President of Public Affairs: – Develop and advance the organization’s state policy agenda, including collaborating with key staff to identify, implement, evaluate, and update the organization’s policy priorities, advocacy positions, and strategies, and the relationship between its grantmaking, community engagement, legal advocacy, and state legislative work. – Serve as an effective and visible spokesperson for the organization, increasing awareness of the organization’s state policy goals, and broadening the organization’s reputation and visibility among elected and appointed officials, partner organizations, the media, and others. – Monitor and lead the organization’s response to state anti-hunger legislation, communicating the organization’s perspective or input to key government offices, and providing technical assistance to state lawmakers, grantee partners, Jewish community partners, and others. – Collaborate with the Director of Federal Policy to produce policy-related materials such as action alerts, memos, fact sheets, background information, and presentations for meetings and briefings to engage key stakeholders in MAZON’s state advocacy work. – Work closely with the Director of Communications to provide content for digital and print materials. – Lead the organization’s representation in various coalition and committee settings. – Work closely with the Outreach and Programs teams to strengthen and cultivate relationships with a wide array of partners from the Jewish community, interfaith community, and anti-hunger community to advance policy goals. – Build and foster collaborative relationships with other departments within the organization to stay informed and abreast of new and ongoing initiatives. – Provide strong leadership and strategic direction, including developing and monitoring individual and departmental team performance goals. – Identify staffing needs and department infrastructure requirements, advising the Vice President of Public Affairs on trends and capacity needs for MAZON’s state policy work as a whole. – Direct assigned personnel, establish work assignments, advise on priorities, schedules, and staffing based on operational needs. – Monitor productivity, provide feedback, conduct performance evaluations, and recommend hiring, discipline, promotion, termination, and other personnel actions. – Enforce company policies, safety and quality standards, and regulations; communicate management expectations; participate in management meetings; and maintain confidentiality of sensitive personnel and business information. The Director of State Policy is a management-level position responsible for directing daily operations, allocating work, maintaining operational standards, and ensuring that department objectives are achieved. The position exercises independent judgment in managing workflow, directing personnel, addressing performance issues, and making recommendations concerning staffing and employee performance. The position is expected to exercise independent judgment in carrying out its management responsibilities and is accountable for the results of decisions made within its assigned area of responsibility. Other duties and responsibilities as assigned. — ## Qualifications **Required** – Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree preferred. – Eight or more years of prior/related work experience with government agencies, state-based advocacy organizations, or relevant public policy organizations strongly preferred. – Knowledge of or experience with food insecurity policy issues strongly preferred, in addition to familiarity with the organization’s policy priorities. – Outstanding relationship builder with the integrity, maturity, confidence, wisdom, and collaborative skills necessary to work effectively with a wide array of stakeholders. – Record of success as a positive and persuasive leader and team player. – Familiarity with the use of digital/social media technology in advocacy campaigns desired. – Ability to work independently, take initiative, and be self-directed. – Demonstrated proficiency with MS Office required; experience with Salesforce and Asana preferred. – Ability to travel, including to represent the organization at outside meetings, events, and conferences. – Excellent oral and written communication skills and strong analytical ability, particularly around policy analysis. – Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with state policymakers and their staff, partners, board members, and colleagues. – Ability to develop and implement effective advocacy strategies to achieve goals. – Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities effectively. – High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism in all interactions. – Deep commitment to MAZON’s mission to end hunger. – Highly motivated and able to work independently with a strong sense of ownership. — ## Compensation and Benefits MAZON offers a compensation package with a competitive salary range of $110,000 to $119,000 annually. item.title: Digital Director, Central Communications
item.description: Digital Director, Central Communications Organization: New America Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 # About New America’s mission is to generate big ideas and bold solutions for a new America. We envision an America that represents and serves the public, where institutions work for all Americans, where workers, families, and communities can thrive, and where people are secure from existential threats. # Primary Function New America is seeking a visionary, creative, and highly organized digital leader to serve as Digital Director within its Central Communications team. The Digital Director will shape and lead New America’s digital communications strategy, including its website and digital publishing platforms, visual brand, data visualization, analytics, and responsible adoption of emerging technologies. The Digital Director will oversee four direct reports on the Central Communications digital team: the Front-End Developer, Digital Marketing Manager, Senior Data Visualization Developer, and Senior Visual Designer and Brand Lead. The Digital Director will establish priorities, support professional development, and foster an effective, collaborative team responsible for digital product development, marketing, visual storytelling, brand implementation, and performance measurement. Building on the successful launch of New America’s redesigned website and refreshed brand in 2026, the Digital Director will lead the critical next phase of the organization’s digital evolution: turning these foundational investments into sustained audience growth, deeper engagement, and greater influence for New America’s ideas. The opportunity is to move from launch to measurable impact—continually improving how audiences discover, understand, and act on New America’s work; developing more ambitious digital products and storytelling formats; strengthening the organization’s brand and reputation across channels; and building the systems, insights, and practices needed to reach new and evolving audiences. The Digital Director will define what comes next and establish a clear roadmap for delivering it. Reporting to the Vice President of Content and Communications, and working closely with other Central Communications colleagues, New America’s experts, emerging leaders, program teams, and operations colleagues, the Digital Director will translate organizational goals into a cohesive digital strategy and product roadmap. The ideal candidate combines strategic vision with technical fluency, sound management, creative problem-solving, and the ability to lead complex work involving multiple stakeholders and competing needs. # Responsibilities ## Digital strategy and product leadership Set the vision and strategy for New America’s website, digital publishing tools, audience-development channels, and data visualizations/interactive storytelling capabilities. Develop and oversee a digital product roadmap that aligns organizational goals, audience needs, and available resources, while ensuring digital products adhere to best practices for accessibility, user experience, privacy, performance, and search visibility. Lead product-development processes involving internal stakeholders and external vendors. Identify opportunities to expand New America’s interactive storytelling and data-visualization capabilities in ways that increase the reach and impact of its research and policy ideas. Evaluate New America’s digital systems on an ongoing basis and make informed budget, staffing, technology, and vendor recommendations to the VP of Content and Communications. ## Website management and digital publishing Lead the next phase of New America’s website strategy, ensuring that the site continues to evolve as an effective digital publishing, storytelling, and audience-engagement platform. Develop and manage a website roadmap centered on audience growth, content discovery, usability, accessibility, and performance. Partner with editorial, research, policy, development, events, and communications colleagues to understand their evolving needs and translate them into scalable digital solutions. Manage relationships with web-development agencies and technical vendors, including project scope, budgets, timelines, deliverables, and performance. Champion user-centered product development, incorporating audience research, usability testing, analytics, and staff feedback loops to inform continuous improvement. Establish clear governance for website content workflows, feature requests, quality assurance, maintenance, and publishing responsibilities. ## Audience development and analytics Guide New America’s digital analytics and measurement strategy, ensuring performance data connects clearly to communications and impact goals. Translate analytics into actionable recommendations for content strategy, audience development, and resource allocation across teams. Establish ethical, privacy-conscious standards for how the organization collects, targets, and experiments with audience data. Champion organization-wide fluency with digital insights, presenting findings in ways that resonate with both technical and non-technical colleagues. ## Brand stewardship Serve as New America’s primary organizational brand steward. Lead the continued evolution of New America’s visual identity to ensure that it remains distinctive, credible, accessible, and aligned with the organization’s mission and reputation. Partner closely with the Senior Visual Designer and Brand Lead and other Central Communications colleagues to maintain a consistent and high-quality look, feel, and voice across New America’s website, publications, events, campaigns, social channels, and other public-facing products. Establish and maintain brand standards, templates, tools, training, and review processes that enable colleagues across the organization to apply the brand effectively. Advise senior leaders and program teams on high-visibility brand decisions and identify opportunities to strengthen New America’s reputation over time. Monitor how New America’s brand is expressed and perceived across channels, using audience feedback, research, and performance data to recommend thoughtful improvements. ## Team leadership and organizational collaboration Lead, manage, and mentor a multidisciplinary team spanning web development, digital marketing, data visualization, visual design, and brand. Establish clear responsibilities, goals, workflows, and performance expectations while supporting staff growth and professional development. Foster an inclusive, creative, accountable, and collaborative team culture. Develop internal processes, guidelines, and service models that support effective collaboration on digital communications. Present digital strategies, product concepts, recommendations, and tradeoffs clearly and persuasively to senior stakeholders with varying levels of technical and design knowledge. Build productive relationships with external agencies, consultants, technology providers, and other partners. ## Emerging technologies and responsible AI Develop a forward-looking vision for how emerging technologies—including AI—can responsibly strengthen New America’s research communications, digital publishing, audience engagement, internal capabilities, and reputation as a public policy think tank. Evaluate and pilot tools that could improve content discovery, accessibility, workflow efficiency, audience understanding, data visualization, or digital storytelling. Serve as a vital member of the AI governance committee to develop responsible practices for selecting and using AI-enabled tools and ensure experimentation reflects New America’s standards for accuracy, transparency, editorial and research integrity, accessibility, and human oversight. Monitor digital trends and best practices and recommend investments that advance New America’s mission without compromising trust or quality. ## Digital governance, security, and operational resilience Partner with New America’s IT and operations teams to assess cybersecurity, privacy, data-governance, and technology needs related to the organization’s public-facing digital platforms. Maintain appropriate governance and documentation for critical digital systems, domains, integrations, administrative access, vendors, and account ownership. Support incident-response planning for website outages, account compromises, publishing errors, misinformation, and other digital or reputational risks. # Qualifications Candidates should have: At least eight years of relevant professional experience, including at least three years managing staff. Demonstrated experience developing and implementing an organization-wide digital strategy. Significant experience leading digital product development, website management, web design, or a related function. Experience managing and mentoring multidisciplinary staff and building effective, collaborative teams. Demonstrated ability to develop product roadmaps, prioritize competing needs, and lead complex projects from planning through implementation and evaluation. Working knowledge of HTML and CSS. Familiarity with modern web-development technologies and frameworks, including JavaScript and React, and content management systems such as WordPress or Drupal. Experience with Google Analytics or comparable analytics platforms and the ability to translate performance data into strategic recommendations. Experience with project-management tools such as Asana, Trello, Jira, Monday.com, or similar platforms. Knowledge of current user experience, user interface, web accessibility, privacy, and digital publishing practices. Experience incorporating user or audience research throughout the product design and development lifecycle. Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated success collaborating with senior leaders and colleagues across diverse disciplines, roles, and levels of tech

item.title: Senior Director, International Development Executive Advisor
item.description: Senior Director, International Development Executive Advisor Organization: Goodwill Industries International (GII) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Summary Provide enterprise leadership for the organization’s global growth strategy by identifying, evaluating, and advancing international development opportunities that expand mission impact and strengthen long-term sustainability. The International Development Executive Advisor builds and manages a robust pipeline of markets, partners, and funding sources; leads due diligence and negotiation; oversees launch and performance of international partnerships and programs; and serves as a senior advisor to leadership on global opportunities, risks, and operating models. Basic Function Set and execute a multi-year international development strategy aligned with organizational priorities, values, and growth goals. Develop and steward strategic relationships with international stakeholders (e.g., NGOs, foundations, corporate partners, governments, and peer networks). Evaluate new markets and partnership opportunities through structured discovery, feasibility assessments, and risk-based due diligence. Design scalable partnership and program models (e.g., replication, licensing, joint initiatives) that balance mission outcomes, financial sustainability, and local context. Oversee financial planning for international initiatives, including budget development, forecasting, and performance management. Specific Duties Create and maintain a prioritized international opportunity pipeline, including clear go/no-go criteria, business cases, and resourcing plans. Lead license/partner identification, engagement, and negotiation; draft and finalize MOUs, partnership agreements, license agreements, and related documentation in collaboration with Legal. Direct market entry and expansion planning, including stakeholder mapping, operating model selection, implementation timelines, and transition plans. Guide the development of playbooks, toolkits, and operating standards that enable consistent, high-quality execution across international partnerships and licenses. Oversee program and partner performance against agreed-upon objectives, budgets, and impact indicators; ensure timely reporting and course correction. Identify, pursue, and steward international funding opportunities (e.g., grants, philanthropy, corporate partnerships, fee-for-service arrangements) to diversify and grow revenue. Establish measurement frameworks to track outcomes, operational performance, and return on investment; communicate results to executive leadership and key stakeholders. Proactively monitor external factors (economic, regulatory, geopolitical, and sector trends) that affect international strategy and recommend adjustments as needed. Represent the organization in international forums and cultivate thought leadership that strengthens credibility, partnerships, and mission visibility. Relationships Internal: Partner with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to design, launch, and support international initiatives. External: Build trusted relationships with international licensees, partners, funders, government agencies, multilateral organizations, and subject-matter experts to advance strategy and strengthen program effectiveness. Skills Needed Strategic leadership with demonstrated ability to translate vision into executable plans and measurable outcomes. Strong business acumen, including financial modeling, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management. Strong Artificial Intelligence (AI) knowledge with the ability to integrate into operations. Experience building and managing complex licenses and partnerships; strong negotiation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills. Knowledge of international development practices, cross-cultural leadership, and operating effectively across diverse geographies. Comfort with ambiguity and ability to assess risk, prioritize, and make sound decisions with incomplete information. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level presentations and partner-facing communications. Bi-lingual with fluency in English and Korean language. Strong project/program management and process improvement skills; ability to develop scalable playbooks and standards. Education Bachelor’s degree in business, international relations/development, public administration, finance, or a related discipline required. Master’s degree (e.g., MBA, MPA, MA in International Development) preferred or equivalent experience. Experience 15+ years of progressive experience in international development, global partnerships, market expansion, strategy, or related leadership roles; including 5+ years leading teams and managing budgets. Demonstrated success developing and executing growth strategies, forming partnerships, and delivering measurable results in complex environments. Strong analytical skills with the ability to bridge performance metrics to operational and mission impact. Experience working across functions and time zones; ability to build alignment among diverse stakeholders. Nonprofit, social enterprise, or network/affiliate-model experience preferred. Decision Making Exercises independent judgment in assessing international opportunities, recommending investment and operating approaches, and negotiating partnership terms. Make timely, risk-informed decisions that align with organizational strategy, capacity, and mission impact. Physical Effort Sedentary work with periodic travel (30-40%), including international travel, as business needs require. Occasional lifting to 25 pounds and rarely up to 50 pounds. Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and using a computer are required; walking and standing occasionally. Emotional Effort Work environment can be fast-paced and complex with periods of high stress, including time-sensitive decisions and work across multiple time zones. Must demonstrate a positive, solutions-oriented attitude in meeting daily challenges. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Defensive Attorney
item.description: Defensive Attorney Organization: Murray Osorio PLLC Location: Fairfax, VA | Silver Spring, MD | Haddonfield, NJ Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Salary Range: $85,000.00 To $105,000.00 Annually Location: Fairfax, VA, Silver Spring, MD, or Haddonfield, NJ Reports to: Partner Department: Defensive FLSA Status: Exempt About Us Murray Osorio PLLC is a fast-growing immigration law firm with offices in Virginia, Maryland, and New Jersey. We are dedicated to making a positive impact on people’s lives. Our firm represents individuals and companies before courts, government offices, and consular posts worldwide. We specialize in removal defense, humanitarian applications, family-based immigration, criminal immigration, employment-based immigration, naturalization, and appellate and federal litigation. At Murray Osorio PLLC, we pride ourselves on collaboration, professionalism, and a deep commitment to our mission of providing exceptional legal services while fostering a supportive, inclusive, and energetic workplace. Position Overview We are seeking a passionate and motivated Defensive Attorney to join our thriving legal team in either our Fairfax, Virginia, or Silver Spring, Maryland office. This is a fantastic opportunity for attorneys eager to build their careers, develop leadership skills, and pursue a clear, performance-based path to partnership. This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Fairfax, VA, Silver Spring, MD, or Haddonfield, NJ, with the expectation of on-site presence three days a week. As a Valued Member of Our Firm, You Will Manage your own caseload while meeting case progression benchmarks. Collaborate closely with paralegals and fellow attorneys to ensure seamless case handling. Participate in firm committees under the guidance of firm partners, contributing to the firm’s operations and success. Enjoy a hybrid work model that blends flexibility with opportunities to meet clients and attend in-office events. Key Responsibilities Conduct comprehensive legal research and analysis of immigration law cases. Provide legal advice and guidance to clients on immigration matters, including asylum, cancellation of removal, and general removal defense. Prepare and draft legal documents and correspondence with precision and attention to detail. Provide effective guidance and support to clients throughout the immigration process. Lead and manage multiple case files with strong organizational skills. Collaborate with team members to enhance legal strategies and case outcomes. Stay updated on evolving immigration laws and policies to ensure compliance. Qualifications Active bar membership. 0-3 years of experience in immigration law. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Proven ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple tasks efficiently. High level of attention to detail and problem-solving ability. Strong teamwork and leadership skills. Proficiency in conducting thorough legal research using legal platforms. Preferred Qualifications Fluency in Spanish and/or other languages. Additional experience in specific immigration law specialties or areas of practice. item.title: Director of Strategic Communications
item.description: Director of Strategic Communications Organization: Vision360 Partners Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Vision360 Partners is seeking a Director of Strategic Communications to join our team. We are a privately held, non-partisan, medium-sized strategic communications firm, seeking a mid-level professional to support our public affairs, crisis and litigation communication clients. Vision360 Partners boasts a track record and client roster that spans close to 30 years and covers state and federal policy and regulatory battles across many sectors, including financial services, healthcare, technology, transportation, energy and more. The agency also ranks among the few with deep experience in litigation support and crisis management. Our litigation communications work supports top law firms and corporations across the country in high profile matters. This new team member can expect to work across all our lines of business. What We’re Looking For Ideal candidates are self-starters with the ability to grasp complex subject matters and communicate quickly and strategically. Candidates should have strong writing and research skills, media relations experience, management experience, and the ability to formulate effective communication strategies and messages for public affairs and/or crisis and litigation clients. At least seven (7) years of professional (full-time employment) experience including an agency is required. Key qualifications in candidates for this mid-level role: Prior experience in developing and advising clients on communications strategy and execution: developing messaging and content across channels, including social media; monitoring emerging issues; and helping clients communicate effectively with key audiences. Also work with agency leadership in helping clients stay ahead of their issues, make recommendations, and manage the execution of client work. Leadership within integrated communications campaigns: developing and executing issue advocacy (legislative/regulator), crisis (legal/reputation), and digital campaigns shaping narratives and engaging target audiences. Earned media expertise: pitching reporters, cultivating media relationships, rapid response, booking interviews, and placing op-eds. Alliance development/coalition building: identifying, recruiting and activating allied third party experts (individuals and organizations) or prior experience working on a multi-stakeholder issue advocacy coalitions. Managing team work flows: assist in the day-to-day management of client work and account teams, ensuring work is assigned, written products are professional quality and error free and all work is executed with care and precision. What We Offer We provide exciting opportunities to work with large, fast-paced clients on front page issues. We have a proud record of supporting professional development, internal promotion, collaboration and teamwork. Vision360 Partners is a results-oriented, hybrid work environment. We are among the few agencies in DC that still offer the option of working mostly from home. All applicants should be in the DMV area and work from the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We provide home office equipment. We offer competitive compensation, generous paid time off that can grow with tenure, extended time off around the holidays, a 100% 401(k) match, and fully paid family leave. The salary range for this position is based on prior experience and ranges between $85,000 and $120,000+. Vision360 Partners compensation also includes a discretionary year-end bonus. Interested candidates should apply by sending resume and cover letter to [email protected] . Please put “Director” in the subject line. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Legislative Associate
item.description: Senior Legislative Associate Organization: Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Senior Legislative Associate The Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC) is seeking a Senior Legislative Associate in our Washington, DC office. This individual will join our Federal Affairs team and report to our Federal Legislative Director. The Senior Legislative Associate will develop an active network on Capitol Hill, contacts in the environmental and conservation community, and will be able to develop strong collaborative relationships with colleagues at SELC. This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly successful, nationally recognized organization that is effectively addressing some of the most pressing and challenging environmental issues throughout the South and the nation. The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of 3 years of progressively challenging work experience in federal or state legislative and administrative advocacy or political campaigns. They have the skills and experience to support SELC’s federal efforts on multiple issues with direct supervision. SELC has a hybrid work model that offers employees flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week. This is a full-time, exempt position. The anticipated start date for this position is flexible, with the ideal candidate able to begin anytime between now and early January. Primary Responsibilities Collaborate with the Federal Legislative Director, attorneys, communications professionals, advocacy, and policy staff to develop and advance legislative and advocacy goals for assigned issue areas. Serve as a primary federal affairs representative and subject matter resource on wildlife, public lands, forests, and other assigned environmental policy issues. Cultivate, maintain, and strengthen relationships with members of Congress, congressional staff, administrative agencies, coalition partners, and other key stakeholders. Develop and execute federal advocacy strategies through legislative targeting, stakeholder engagement, power mapping, and issue-based campaign planning. Schedule, prepare for, participate in, and follow up on lobbying meetings, providing additional information and resources to policymakers and staff as needed. Research legislative, regulatory, and policy developments and assess regional, state, and district-specific impacts to inform advocacy efforts and organizational decision-making. Draft and review advocacy materials, including talking points, fact sheets, letters, testimony, press releases, coalition communications, and other externally facing documents. Monitor congressional hearings, briefings, and legislative activity; prepare summaries, analyses, and memoranda for attorneys and internal stakeholders. Facilitate the exchange of information between the federal affairs team and staff across the organization, ensuring alignment on priorities, strategy, and emerging issues. Represent the organization in coalitions, working groups, and external partnerships, collaborating with peer organizations to advance shared advocacy objectives. Help guide coalition strategies and activities to support organizational goals while fostering productive relationships within the environmental and conservation community. Participate in team meetings, retreats, and cross-functional initiatives, contributing to a collaborative and supportive organizational culture. Maintain awareness of political, legislative, energy, environmental, and conservation trends, ensure compliance with lobbying reporting requirements, and support fundraising and communications initiatives as needed. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. 3 years minimum of progressively challenging work experience in federal or state legislative and administrative advocacy or political campaigns. Demonstrated knowledge of the federal legislative and regulatory process. Proven ability to build and maintain productive relationships with policymakers, coalition partners, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams. Strong written and verbal communication skills and experience drafting advocacy, policy, or public-facing materials. Desired Qualifications Connection to the people and places of the South. A genuine interest in and commitment to helping SELC create and foster an equitable and inclusive workplace that welcomes people from across the rich racial and cultural diversity of our region. About SELC The Southern Environmental Law Center is one of the nation’s most powerful defenders of the environment, rooted in the South. With a long track record, SELC takes on the toughest environmental challenges in court, in government, and in our communities to protect our region’s air, water, climate, wildlife, lands, and people. Nonprofit and nonpartisan, the organization has a staff of 250, including more than 160 legal and policy experts and advocates. Headquartered in Charlottesville, VA, SELC has offices in Asheville, Atlanta, Birmingham, Chapel Hill, Charleston, Nashville, Richmond, and Washington, DC. At our core, we are place-based, rooted in our region, and connected with the communities and clients we serve. We believe in an equitable and inclusive workplace that welcomes people from across the rich racial and cultural diversity of our region and values diverse perspectives. We approach our work with the highest level of integrity, holding ourselves to high standards with an emphasis on honesty, accountability, and thoughtfulness. We value collaboration and camaraderie, realizing we are strongest when we work together and knowing that everyone has a critical role to play. We strive for impact through a strategic, bold, pragmatic, and ambitious outlook that is dedicated to achieving powerful results. We believe in these values and in the power of SELC. We hope you consider joining us. Learn more at https://www.selc.org/ . Compensation & Benefits SELC offers salaries competitive with other leading environmental nonprofits nationally and provides an excellent benefits package. The starting salary range for this position is $88,000 – $97,350 which includes a 10% location premium for the Washington, DC metro area. Actual placement within the range will depend on factors such as relevant experience, education, skills, and internal equity considerations. For more details about our benefits package, please visit our Careers page. SELC is a PSLF (Public Service Loan Forgiveness) eligible employer. All employees are required to reside in our region. SELC will provide relocation reimbursement up to a specific dollar amount for those relocating at least 50 miles from their current primary residence. To Apply To apply, click on ‘ Apply Now ‘ to be directed to an online application where you may upload your application materials. Applicants must submit a cover letter, resume, and professional references. Please note that all attachments must be submitted in PDF format. The initial deadline for receipt of complete applications is Sunday, October 4th at 11:59 pm ET. SELC is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace environment. We are eager to welcome new team members who share this commitment. Qualified individuals of all backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Communications Specialist
item.description: Senior Communications Specialist Organization: Southland Industries Location: Dulles, VA Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Position Summary Executes and helps shape Southland’s internal communications strategy by leading enterprise communication initiatives that keep employees informed, engaged, and connected. Serves as a strategic communications partner to business leaders by developing communication strategies, leading internal campaigns, supporting employee engagement initiatives, and ensuring consistent, high-quality messaging across the organization. Position Details Develops communication plans for company initiatives, organizational changes, and employee programs. Develops communications for key Southland leadership, applying specific voice and style to match individual personas. Serves as a trusted communications advisor to cross-functional stakeholders, providing recommendations on messaging, timing, channels, and employee engagement. Identifies opportunities to improve communication effectiveness and employee experience through new approaches, tools, and best practices. Helps establish governance, editorial standards, and communication guidelines across internal channels. Partners with leaders across HR, Operations, Safety, IT, Learning & Development, and regional teams to translate complex information into clear, engaging communications. Facilitates content reviews and approvals while balancing business objectives, timelines, and communication quality. Maintains and organizes communication assets, templates, and shared content libraries. Leads communication campaigns supporting culture, safety, organizational initiatives, technology implementations, benefits enrollment, employee recognition programs, including the annual Awards Show, and business transformation efforts. Develops communication strategies, messaging frameworks, FAQs, toolkits, and leadership resources for major initiatives. Ensures communication efforts are coordinated across departments to deliver a consistent employee experience. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in corporate communications, internal communications, employee engagement, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience leading enterprise communication and change management campaigns and managing multiple stakeholders. Exceptional writing, editing, storytelling, and executive communication skills. Advanced knowledge of SharePoint, Viva Engage, Microsoft Teams, and enterprise communication platforms. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization. Experience using communication analytics and employee engagement metrics to drive continuous improvement. Benefits As a 100% employee-owned company, we offer a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family: 401(k) plan with 50% company match (no cap) and immediate 100% vesting Medical, dental, and vision insurance (100% paid for employee) Annual bonus program based upon performance, achievement, and company profitability Term life, AD&D insurance, and voluntary life insurance Disability income protection insurance Pre-tax flexible spending plans (health and dependent care) Paid parental leave Paid holidays, vacation, and personal time Training/professional development opportunities and company-paid memberships for professional associations and licenses Wellness benefits About Southland Industries As one of the nation’s largest MEP companies, Southland Industries is built on the foundation of great people. Since 1949, we have put our people first, enabling growth, professional achievement, and innovation. If you want to join a fast-paced environment where you’re engaged, challenged, and valued, apply now to join our dynamic team. Southland Industries and all its subsidiaries are an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We are committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all employees and to providing our employees with a safe work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions at Southland Industries are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, gender, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical condition, marital status, family care or medical leave status, veteran status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. Southland Industries will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. Pay: Final pay is determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, internal equity, and alignment with market data. For Virginia this ranges from $85,000.00 – $106,000.00 plus annual incentive, benefits, and retirement program as outlined above. Contingent Employment: All employment offers are contingent upon successful drug tests, background checks, and professional reference checks. Roles that include driving as an essential job duty will be required to have a successful Motor Vehicle Record check (MVR). We are not able to offer sponsorship of employment at this time. External Agency Announcement: It is Southland Industries’ policy not to accept candidate submissions from recruiting agencies without an active and authorized work order. Candidate ownership can only be established after a bona fide work order is issued by a member of the Southland Industries Talent Acquisition team and the candidate is appropriately submitted through our Applicant Tracking System (ATS). item.title: Media Relations Specialist – Senior
item.description: Media Relations Specialist – Senior Organization: W2 Communications Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/09/2026 About the job We are seeking a skilled and driven Media Relations Specialist to support communications operations for a government agency. In this role, you will work alongside a team of dedicated communications professionals to manage and advance the agency’s media presence across traditional and digital platforms. This position is based in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. Candidates must be available for onsite work at agency facilities as required by the program. Flexibility for a hybrid schedule may be available depending on contract requirements. Key Responsibilities: Develop media engagement strategies for campaigns, announcements, and events, including identifying target media outlets and reporters and crafting media pitches and supporting products. Produce media clips and ad hoc analysis of print and online coverage to assess the effectiveness of agency outreach efforts. Conduct weekly social media analysis and ad hoc topic analysis to support the development of strategies, infographics, and content that enhances public awareness of the agency’s programs. Prepare monthly media analysis reports covering national media highlights, evolution of media coverage by audience size, social media engagement, outreach campaign rollups, regional highlights, top feature outlets, and national topic breakdowns. Assist in the preparation of media kits, press releases, fact sheets, and query responses for media inquiries or proactive outreach related to agency initiatives, programs, and services. Support the development and maintenance of local and regional media lists for targeted outreach activities. Provide transcription support as directed. Maintain media database records and leverage industry-leading monitoring tools such as Critical Mention and Muck Rack. Support executive leadership with media training, briefing preparation, and strategic communications counsel. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 5–7 years of experience in public and/or media relations, with minimum 1 year of experience in B2G (business-to-government) or government agency communications, and minimum 3 years of experience supporting cybersecurity-related communications. Knowledge of the cybersecurity press corps. Demonstrated experience crafting, pitching, and placing stories in external media outlets. Proficiency with media monitoring and analytics platforms (e.g., Critical Mention, Muck Rack). Strong writing skills, including press releases, media pitches, background memos, talking points, and fact sheets. Ability to work efficiently and accurately in a fast-paced environment, both independently and collaboratively. Proactive work ethic with strong attention to detail. Preferred Qualifications: Prior experience supporting federal agency communications. Experience with executive media training and strategic communications counsel. SharePoint proficiency. Background in managing or contributing to regional media outreach programs. Experience with podcast outreach and emerging media formats. Contract Contingency Notice: Employment in this position is contingent upon award of the applicable government contract. Candidates who receive a conditional offer of employment will be notified of final hiring decisions following contract award. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Strategy Communications Lead
item.description: Strategy Communications Lead Organization: Lockheed Martin Location: Bethesda, MD | Arlington, VA | Denver, CO | Fort Worth, TX | Grand Prairie, TX | Orlando, FL | King of Prussia, PA Date Posted: 09/09/2026 Job Description We’re looking for a motivated communications professional to join the Global Media and Strategy Communications team to help drive key initiatives related to business strategy, financial communications and overall brand reputation. Under the direction of the senior manager of Global Media and Strategy, the ideal candidate will become a subject matter expert and develop compelling narratives that support the business area’s strategy and key financial communications. This role will develop strategic content, coordinate integrated communications initiatives, and deliver tactics through a variety of both internal and external communications channels including Tier-1 media engagements. This position serves as a trusted communications partner across the Corporate Communications organization, collaborating closely with CEO/COO Communications, Investor Relations, Finance, Government Affairs, Legal, Global Business Development & Strategy, and business area communications teams. The ideal candidate combines exceptional writing ability with strong business acumen, project management discipline, and intellectual curiosity. This individual is comfortable synthesizing complex business, financial, geopolitical, and national security issues into compelling communications that resonate with diverse audiences. Key Responsibilities Support Enterprise Strategy Narratives Develop messaging, presentations, briefing materials, talking points, and written content that clearly communicate the larger enterprise strategy and corporate priorities. Translate complex business, financial, technology, and policy topics into compelling talking points tailored for external and internal stakeholders. Drive consistency of messaging across executive communications, enterprise campaigns and media relations. Provide recommendations for proactive media pitching related to long-term strategic priorities. Support Financial Communications Assist in the development and coordination of communications supporting quarterly earnings, investor messaging, the annual report, and other financial milestones. Develop content that drives key financial narratives for both internal and external audiences to drive business success. Draft supporting communications materials, including executive talking points, Q&A documents, messaging frameworks, fact sheets, and internal communications. Executive Communications & Thought Leadership Support preparation for media interviews, conferences, customer engagements, and policy forums. Partner to drive significant growth pillar focus areas while partnering with counterparts across the business. Research emerging industry, defense, geopolitical, technology, and policy developments to strengthen executive positioning. Communications Planning and Operations Manage timelines, deliverables, approvals, editorial planning documents, and cross-functional coordination across multiple concurrent initiatives ensuring that communications activities remain aligned with business priorities. Monitor industry trends, competitor communications, investor sentiment, public policy developments and media narratives. Produce executive-ready summaries, strategic insights, and communications recommendations. Support measurement of communications effectiveness through media analysis, message penetration, and executive engagement metrics. Serve as a liaison for enterprise messaging resources and as a partner to representatives across the business. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college, or equivalent experience/combined education, with 3+ years of professional experience. Experience in corporate communications, public affairs, executive communications, investor relations support, journalism, public policy communications, or related field. Demonstrated experience writing for executive audiences. Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Experience managing multiple concurrent projects with competing priorities. Ability to work independently under general direction while collaborating effectively across teams. Ability to travel as required. Desired Skills & Experience Experience supporting communications within a publicly traded company, government organization, aerospace and defense company, or strategic communications consulting firm. Familiarity with financial communications, including earnings announcements, annual reporting, investor messaging, or corporate disclosures. Strong research and analytical capabilities with the ability to synthesize complex information quickly. Experience and/or desire to learn general web development for resource management. Excellent executive writing skills, including speeches, talking points, presentations, briefing documents, and messaging frameworks. Understanding of media relations, reputation management, and executive positioning. Knowledge of national security, defense, aerospace, technology, or geopolitical issues. Strong organizational and project management skills with exceptional attention to detail. Proficiency using Microsoft Office, collaboration tools, and communications planning platforms. Who You Are An intellectually curious communications professional who enjoys understanding complex business issues. A strong writer capable of translating technical, financial, and strategic topics into compelling stories. Compelled to do research and compare multiple sources to develop a robust communications product. A self-starter who works independently while knowing when to seek guidance. Eager to learn from senior leaders while taking ownership of increasingly strategic work. Success in This Role Looks Like Enterprise messaging is consistently executed across communications products with clarity, accuracy, and alignment. Senior leaders and cross-functional partners view this communicator as a trusted, responsive communications resource. Strategic research and analysis inform communications planning and improve message effectiveness. Multiple high-priority initiatives are managed simultaneously with strong attention to detail and disciplined execution. This communicator demonstrates increasing ownership of enterprise communications initiatives and is prepared to assume broader strategic responsibilities over time. Pay Information GeoZone Definition: GeoZones are geographic groupings created by Lockheed Martin to align compensation ranges with regional labor markets and cost-of-labor differences across the United States. Locations are assigned a Geo Zone based on the primary work location of the role. Full-time salary range (GEOZONE 1): $90,600.00 – $168,200.00 Includes metropolitan areas such as Sunnyvale, CA; Palo Alto, CA; New York City metropolitan area; Newark, New Jersey; etc. Full-time salary range (GEOZONE 2): $81,500.00 – $151,300.00 Includes metropolitan areas such as Denver, CO; King of Prussia, PA; Stratford, CT; Moorestown, NJ; etc. Full-time salary range (GEOZONE 3): $72,500.00 – $134,600.00 Includes metropolitan areas such as Dallas–Fort Worth, TX; Orlando, FL; Grand Prairie, TX; Marietta, GA; etc. Full-time salary range (GEOZONE 4): $65,200.00 – $121,200.00 Includes metropolitan areas such as Camden, AR; Lexington, KY; Ocala, FL; Lufkin, TX; etc. At Lockheed Martin, we know mission success starts with taking care of our people. Our Total Rewards program is designed to attract top talent, support your well-being, and help you grow—both professionally and personally. The salary range for this position is as listed on the requisition. Please note that the salary information listed is a general guideline only. Lockheed Martin considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills as well as market (work location) and business considerations when extending an offer. Benefits offered: Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible work arrangements and schedules (e.g., 4×10), 401(k) match, Paid time off, Holidays, Parental Leave, EAP, Flexible Spending Accounts, Education Assistance, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability. Annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs may be offered depending on the position. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and can vary from year to year and are tied to a range of performance metrics. Represented full-time employees accrue 6.67 hours of Vacation per month; accrue up to 52 hours of sick leave annually; receive at least 96 hours for holidays. item.title: Director of Federal Government Relations
item.description: Director of Federal Government Relations Organization: CropLife America (CLA) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/09/2026 CropLife America (CLA), located in Arlington, VA, is the national trade association representing the pesticide industry. Its members drive innovation by discovering, producing, selling, and distributing the essential pesticide products that empower America’s farmers to produce food, fuel, and fiber for our nation and the world. They are seeking a Director of Federal Government Relations to join their team. CLA offers competitive compensation, a generous benefits package, and a flexible hybrid arrangement. POSITION SUMMARY Reporting to the Vice President of Government Relations, the Director of Federal Government Relations is responsible for representing the association on federal policy matters. This role will manage and engage critical external allies and member company relationships through association committees, direct outreach to policymakers, and stakeholder coalitions. RESPONSIBILITIES Serve as a lobbyist responsible for industry policy and advocacy related to the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act (PRIA), the Endangered Species Act (ESA), federal appropriations, and other relevant pesticide issues. Support the association’s Federal Affairs Committee (FAC) and facilitate its input into legislative strategies and initiatives. Cultivate and maintain relationships with stakeholders and allies at the national level, including the Pesticide Policy Coalition (PPC) and the broader industry. Support association engagement with the PRIA Coalition. Cooperatively manage federal lobbyists and ally relationships. Direct various association resources and strategic relationships to help ensure the pesticide industry’s right to operate. Lead within the CLA government relations team and broader staff to proactively develop and deliver effective legislative strategies at the federal level. SKILLS & ABILITIES Ability to develop and successfully maintain effective relationships with association members, policymakers, allies, lobbyists, coalitions, stakeholders, and teammates Strong verbal and written communication skills with an ability to produce effective communication materials, including the ability to distill complex and/or technical information into concise, influential communications Ability to communicate science-related issues, including data development required to support pesticide registrations Ability to demonstrate flexibility, sound judgment, discretion, and political acumen Proven ability in consensus building and trust/credibility maintenance Strong analytical, interpretive, evaluative, and constructive thinking skills Ability to travel up to 15% REQUIRED EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, history, or a similar field Minimum of 10 years of experience in a related position Working understanding of the federal legislative process, including relevant committees and current Members of Congress Working knowledge of the primary statutes and regulations governing the pesticide industry Basic understanding of science-related issues, including data development required to support pesticide registrations Prior work experience in federal government relations and/or Congress is strongly preferred HOW TO APPLY If you believe you meet the requirements, please submit a resume, cover letter, and two writing samples highlighting legislative engagement to the following job link (or copy/paste link to a new window): Apply to CropLife America Director, Federal Government Relations Salary: $160,000 – $190,000 Additional inquiries and questions can be emailed to Beth Cessna at [email protected] or contact 202-232-1765. ABOUT CROPLIFE AMERICA (CLA) CropLife America partners with agricultural stakeholders across the U.S. and around the world to advance a science-and risk-based regulatory framework that accelerates innovation in pesticide technology and modern agriculture, strengthens trade, and supports conservation. Its work helps growers protect their crops, preserve their livelihoods, and produce safe, affordable, and abundant food. CLA engages in policy, legislative, regulatory, and legal forums to help ensure pesticide products can reach the marketplace. ABOUT CESSNA & ASSOCIATES, LLC Cessna & Associates, LLC is a boutique HR consultancy partnering with mission-driven organizations. Our goal is to identify the best potential candidates that the market has to offer. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
