item.title: Climate & Energy Attorney (Connecticut)
item.description: Climate & Energy Attorney (Connecticut) Organization: Conservation Law Foundation (CLF) Location: New Haven, CT Date Posted: 09/14/2026 Description Conservation Law Foundation (CLF) is seeking a full-time Senior Attorney or Staff Attorney II to join our Climate & Energy team. Based in CLF’s New Haven office, the attorney will play a leading role in advancing innovative strategies to drive the transition to a clean, affordable, and equitable energy future. The position offers a unique opportunity to shape state and regional climate and energy policy through a combination of regulatory advocacy, legislative engagement, litigation, and coalition-building. The attorney will focus primarily on climate and energy issues in Connecticut, with opportunities to collaborate on regional initiatives. Flexible and hybrid work arrangements are available. What you’ll do This role combines legal advocacy, policy development, coalition building, and public engagement to advance CLF’s climate and clean energy goals. Working both independently and collaboratively with state-based and regional teams, the attorney will lead and support high-impact advocacy efforts in the energy, transportation, building, and industrial sectors while centering environmental justice in all aspects of their work. The attorney will: Develop and implement legal, regulatory, and legislative strategies to advance CLF’s climate and energy priorities. Represent CLF in litigation, administrative proceedings, and regulatory matters, including proceedings before Connecticut’s Public Utilities Regulatory Authority, and participate in regional energy market discussions at ISO New England. Advocate before the Connecticut General Assembly and other governmental bodies through written and oral testimony. Draft legal filings, public comments, testimony, policy analyses, and other advocacy materials. Build and maintain strong relationships with community organizations, environmental justice advocates, policymakers, clean energy stakeholders, and other partners. Lead and support coalitions that advance CLF’s environmental and climate justice goals. Engage in public education and communications activities that support CLF’s advocacy and public policy goals. Support fundraising and development activities, including donor engagement, grant proposals and reporting, and board relations. Advance CLF’s commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice, and contribute to a collaborative workplace culture. What you’ll need We are looking for a collaborative and strategic attorney who can work independently while contributing to a supportive and mission-driven team of talented and diverse advocates located throughout New England. To succeed in this role, you’ll need: A J.D. from an accredited law school and admission to practice law in Connecticut, or admission in another U.S. jurisdiction and the ability and willingness to obtain admission in Connecticut within a reasonable period following hire. Relevant legal experience, preferably in climate, energy, environmental, administrative, or regulatory law or significant litigation experience, with the following minimum requirements: Senior Attorney: At least 7 years of relevant legal experience Staff Attorney II: At least 5 years of relevant legal experience Experience in litigation, administrative proceedings, public utility regulation, legislative advocacy, or comparable advocacy work. Strong analytical, research, writing, oral advocacy, and project-management skills. Ability to understand and communicate complex legal, technical, and policy issues effectively to a variety of audiences. Demonstrated commitment to environmental justice and experience building respectful, productive relationships with community partners and other stakeholders. Our highest priority is finding the best candidate for the job. Research has shown that people of color and women are less likely to apply for jobs if they don’t believe they meet every one of the qualifications described in a job description. Our hiring process is centered on assessing candidates with various lived experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t believe you meet every one of our described qualifications or have a less traditional background. About CLF Conservation Law Foundation (CLF) protects New England’s environment for the benefit of all people. A non-profit, member-supported organization, CLF uses the law, science, and the market to solve the region’s most challenging environmental problems, from climate change to ocean conservation to transportation. Every day, CLF advocates stand up for New Englanders—in statehouses, courthouses, boardrooms, regulatory hearings, and community gatherings—to forge innovative paths to environmental progress and economic prosperity for all in our region. To that end, CLF frequently works with communities of color, and those that are economically or otherwise disadvantaged, which often suffer disproportionately from the impacts of environmental degradation. CLF is committed to diversity among our staff, volunteers, boards, and membership and creating a positive, inclusive workplace culture where all can thrive. Salary and Benefits CLF offers a competitive salary, and extensive benefits plan, and an open, inclusive, and accepting work environment where differences are highly respected. Salary ranges are based on position level: Senior Attorney (minimum 7 years of relevant legal experience): $106,000–$127,000. Staff Attorney II (minimum 5 years of relevant legal experience): $94,000–$111,000. Placement within the salary range will be determined by relevant experience, skills, and qualifications, with significant consideration given to internal pay equity. CLF is committed to ensuring compensation decisions are fair, consistent, and aligned with the experience and contributions of current employees in similar roles. We recognize the value of work-life balance and also strive to create opportunities for growth for all employees through professional development. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: PAC Manager/Senior Political Associate
item.description: PAC Manager/Senior Political Associate Organization: J Street Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/14/2026 Position Title: PAC Manager/Senior Political Associate Reports to: National Political Director Start Date: Immediately Location: Washington, DC (in person) Hours: Full Time, Exempt About J Street J Street organizes pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy Americans to promote US policies that align with Jewish and democratic values, that help secure the State of Israel as a just, democratic homeland for the Jewish people, and that advance freedom, safety and self-determination for the Palestinian people. J Street focuses its work in three main areas: (1) Advocating and demonstrating support for pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy policies in Congress, the media and the Jewish community; (2) Endorsing and raising money for federal candidates who share J Street’s agenda; and (3) Educating the public and raising awareness of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the two-state solution. Our Core Values At J Street, everything we do is grounded in three core values that guide how we work, collaborate, and show up for our mission. Impactful — We act with intention. We measure success not just by what we do, but by the progress we make and the change we help bring about. Adaptable — We treat every challenge as an invitation to think creatively, reframe the problem, and find a better path forward. Aligned — We are united by shared principles and an unwavering commitment to our mission. Our strength comes from believing in what we’re building together. The Opportunity J Street’s political program supports a rapidly growing national network of pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy advocates and donors who work to elect federal candidates that share our values and vision. JStreetPAC is the nation’s largest pro-Israel political action committee, distributing millions of dollars each cycle to endorsed candidates. This individual will play a key role in the Political team’s fundraising operations and donor engagement, as well as cultivating relationships with campaigns, candidates, and members of Congress. The ideal candidate is a self-starting, entrepreneurial thinker with keen political instincts, strong relationship management skills, and a track record of setting and hitting ambitious fundraising goals. 2-3 cycles of experience working on political campaigns, on the Hill, and/or for advocacy or political fundraising organizations is preferred for this role. Specific Responsibilities Political Fundraising & Donor Engagement Steward our high- and medium-dollar political fundraising programs Manage JStreetPAC’s national events calendar and own the national conduit fundraising portfolio Maintain trackers of political fundraising and giving progress in spreadsheets and Salesforce, keeping goal-to-actual data current for leadership Political Program Support Foster and grow relationships with fundraisers, staffers, and partners across the political ecosystem to advance J Street’s political work and reputation Grow J Street’s political communication program Serve as a go-to resource for internal and external stakeholders on J Street’s political and PAC work Contribute to the organization’s strategic political planning as a member of the public affairs team Support the National Political Director and VP of Political and Digital Strategy on other key political priorities possibly to include J Street presence at the Democratic National Convention, other presidential engagement, and independent expenditure work Candidate Engagement Support day-to-day management of the endorsement process Create opportunities for J Street leadership to engage with endorsed candidates, including meetings and fundraising events during candidate travel Required and Desired Skills and Characteristics 2-3 cycles of political, campaign, advocacy, or fundraising experience Strong familiarity with the motivations and dynamics that drive federal campaigns and political fundraising Proven ability to manage multiple projects and donor relationships with precision and attention to detail Strong relationship-building and communication skills, including with major donors and political stakeholders Comfortable working collaboratively across teams in a fast-paced political environment Experience managing spreadsheets (Google Sheets/Excel) and Salesforce or a comparable CRM required Formal education requirements are less important than relevant hands-on experience Physical Requirements There are no extraordinary physical requirements for the essential functions of this role. J Street will make reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job tasks. Minimal travel may be requested and can be discussed if it presents a barrier to applying. Compensation and Benefits The annual salary range for this full-time exempt position is $66,000 to $71,000 depending on qualifications and experience. J Street recognizes a staff bargaining unit affiliated with IFPTE Local 70, a union for non-profit workers. Our comprehensive benefits package includes: Unlimited personal time off, accrued sick leave, sabbatical leave Generous parental and family leave, up to 12 weeks Paid time off on many federal and Jewish holidays Employer-contributed health, dental, and vision insurance Company-paid life insurance 401k program including an employer-matched contribution Pre-tax benefits such as commuter benefits and a flexible spending account J Street recognizes a staff bargaining unit affiliated with IFPTE Local 70. This position is included in J Street’s bargaining unit and covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. To Apply Please submit: Resume Answer the following questions: Why do you want to work for JStreetPAC? What race(s) are you watching most closely in the 2026 midterm cycle? Why? OR If you had $10,000 to distribute to federal candidates, how would you divide the funds and why? How would you describe J Street’s place in the ecosystem of political pro-Israel organizations? Contact information for three references Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the position will be filled as quickly as possible. At J Street we value an inclusive, welcoming, and diverse workplace. We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to understanding and valuing each other’s perspectives at all levels of the organization thereby creating a culture that allows us to better serve our employees, and the communities we work with. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law. This policy applies with regard to all aspects of one’s employment and fellowship, including hiring, transfer, promotion, compensation, eligibility for benefits, and termination. item.title: Associate Director of Policy – Eastern Nebraska
item.description: Associate Director of Policy – Eastern Nebraska Organization: Center for Rural Affairs (CRA) Location: Lyons, NE Date Posted: 09/14/2026 Associate Director of Policy Do you have the appetite for advocacy, leadership, and creating lasting impact? The Center for Rural Affairs is seeking an Associate Director of Policy to be a key member of the Policy team. Read on. We might be looking for you! In this role, you’ll help drive Nebraska policy initiatives, support and develop a talented team, manage key grant funded projects, cultivate relationships with stakeholders and advocates, and advance a mission driven strategy that creates lasting impact across the state. Who We Are The Center for Rural Affairs is a dynamic, energetic non-profit organization working to build a better rural future for all. We’ve done this work for more than 50 years and we do it from rural places with a flexible work environment. The Center focuses on capital access, community capacity, and policy advocacy strategies with work in areas of food systems, community resources, small business support, and environment and resilience. The Center’s work is rooted in our mission-aligned values. We believe that a diversity of people and ideas strengthens our work, our workplace, and our communities. We take equal opportunity seriously and we welcome applicants from a variety of backgrounds. Additional information can be found at www.cfra.org . What You’ll Do The Associate Director of Policy reports to the Director of Policy and will work closely with the Policy team. The Associate Director of Policy is responsible for the following: Leading and supporting Nebraska policy initiatives that advance the Center’s mission and strategic goals. Supervise, mentor, and develop policy team members while helping manage the day-to-day program operations. Build and maintain strong relationships with advocates, coalition partners, funders, and other key stakeholders. Research policy issues and contribute to reports, grant proposals, media communications, and advocacy materials. Manage grant-funded projects and ensure successful execution of initiative, deliverables, and reporting requirements. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves) To be successful in this job, you will excel in five areas: Relationship building: You know how to talk with people to learn what needs they have through conversation and inquiry. People trust you because you’re efficient with their time and have their best interests in mind. You’re able to build networks, as well as alliances, and find points of collaboration even when there are competing interests on your time. You develop and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with a diverse group of stakeholders and can bring in allies and partners. Drive to achieve results: You know how to work to your strengths to achieve your own ambitious goals, and you anticipate hurdles as merely a momentary inconvenience. You possess a competitive drive and have the ability to set a high bar and meet it because you think three (or 30) steps ahead to come up with pragmatic, yet innovative, solutions. You take a strategic approach in your work and have an affinity for the details. Inclusive leadership and management: You approach leadership in your work with a mindset of “power with” rather than “power over” and regularly include others with lived experience and/or expertise in decision-making. You use resources wisely and can provide clear direction to staff, partners, and contractors to leverage time and resources for impact. Setting and managing priorities: You have experience managing multiple projects and keeping tasks from slipping through the cracks. You use resources wisely and can provide clear direction to leverage time and talent for impact. You understand the importance of effective delegation and empower others by assigning responsibilities that align with their strengths to maximize efficiency and results. Commitment to social justice: You recognize the role of race, income, age, immigration status, and other identities in addressing barriers. You recognize how your own identities show up in the work, and welcome, reflect on, and act on feedback with an eye toward continuous learning about difference to overcome barriers. You recognize that investment in communities, people, and entrepreneurship are pathways to better outcomes. You’re a leader (or willing to become a leader) in incorporating the Center’s Core Values effectively into internal processes, external programming and communications, and work relationships, as well as identifying opportunities to build your own capacity to center these values into your work. If You Were Here Right Now, You Would Be: Preparing for meetings at the State Capital to advocate for key policy priorities. Coaching and supporting members of the policy team through regular collaboration, feedback, and development. Helping translate policy topics into clear, compelling communications for stakeholders and the public. Representing the Center with funders, advocates, policymakers, and community leaders. Balancing big-picture strategy with hands-on work that moves initiatives forward every day. You Have Experience With the Following: Developing and implementing policy, advocacy, or public affairs strategies that advance organizational goals and drive measurable impact. Building and maintaining relationships with diverse stakeholders, including community partners, advocates, funders, policymakers, and coalition members. Leading, coaching, and developing teams while fostering collaboration, accountability, and a strong sense of belonging. Researching, analyzing, and communicating complex policy or legislative issues through reports, presentations, grant proposals, and public-facing communications. Managing multiple priorities, projects, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment while adapting to changing circumstances and emerging opportunities. Securing and managing grant-funded initiatives, including proposal development, reporting, stakeholder engagement, and project oversight. Navigating complex organizational, political, and community dynamics while using sound judgment, strategic thinking, and effective communication to build support and achieve results. What Else You Should Know This is a full-time exempt position. This position will require regular travel to the Nebraska state capital and other locations and include both overnight and out-of-state travel on occasion. Compensation and benefits: This position has a salary range of $70,000 – $80,000 with top-notch benefits that have a cash value of $10,000 to $29,500, depending on family status and tenure with the Center. Benefits include a 97% employer-paid family health insurance that includes a contribution to a Health Savings Account, retirement options, a fantastic Employee Assistance Program, 12 paid holidays plus paid time off between Christmas Eve and New Year’s Day, Friday Summer Hours, and vacation and sick pay. The Center for Rural Affairs is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-Verify, is committed to the full inclusion of all individuals, and takes steps to ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. How to Apply If you would like to work for an organization that has a national reputation as one of the top organizations in the country working to make rural communities more vibrant, apply by sending your resume, cover letter, and three professional references by clicking below. In the cover letter, please include: How your personal and/or professional experiences have positioned you for success in this role and any Equity-related work, skills, or expertise you want us to know about. Let us know how you heard about this position and why you want to work for the Center. Ready to apply? Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Public Relations Manager I (DHS Suitability)
item.description: Public Relations Manager I (DHS Suitability) Organization: CTEC Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/15/2026 CTEC is a leading technology firm that provides modernization, digital transformation, and application development services to the U.S. Federal Government. Headquartered in McLean, VA, CTEC has over 300 team members working on mission-critical systems and projects for agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security, Internal Revenue Service, and the Office of Personnel Management. The work we do affects millions of U.S. citizens daily as they interact with the systems we build. Our best-in-class commercial solutions, modified for our customers’ bespoke mission requirements, are enabling this future every day. The Company has experienced rapid growth over the past 3 years and recently received a strategic investment from Main Street Capital Corporation (NYSE: MAIN). In addition to our recent growth in Federal Civilian agencies, we are seeking to expand our capabilities in cloud development and footprint in national-security focused agencies within the Department of Defense and U.S. Intelligence Community. Cybermedia Technologies (CTEC) is seeking an experienced Public Relations Manager I (DHS Suitability) to join our team. PROGRAM OVERVIEW CISA’s Stakeholder Engagement Division requires an integrated team to support council and sector governance, approximately 500 annual engagements, stakeholder coordination, policy and risk analysis, executive communications, records, and contract management. The work spans unclassified and classified environments and requires products that are accurate, accessible, compliant, and ready for government use. POSITION SUMMARY Develop strategic communications and stakeholder-outreach products supporting CISA councils and advisory operations. Despite the title, this is primarily a federal strategic-communications role focused on executive messaging, engagement materials, and polished public-facing content. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Develop emails, memoranda, public messaging, executive summaries, outreach materials, graphics, social-media content, and other communication products. Translate complex cyber, critical-infrastructure, policy, and council information into audience-appropriate language. Support communication and outreach plans for councils, working groups, meetings, and stakeholder initiatives. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to gather input, solicit participation, and prepare materials. Manage designated mailboxes, acknowledge inquiries promptly, route requests, and maintain inquiry logs. Prepare leadership talking points, briefings, announcements, invitations, and post-engagement communications. Apply DHS/CISA branding, tone, templates, accessibility, and quality standards. Track communication activities and analyze engagement results to improve future outreach. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 2+ years experience in strategic communications, public relations, stakeholder engagement, journalism, marketing communications, or graphic design. Strong writing, editing, message-development, and client-service skills. Ability to manage multiple communications products, audiences, and deadlines. Experience coordinating with senior leaders, SMEs, and external stakeholders. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience supporting federal advisory committees, councils, executive leadership, CISA, or DHS. Graphic-design or digital-content experience. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, Microsoft 365, Drupal, or social-media publishing tools. CLEARANCE: Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable DHS Fitness Determination (Public Trust/DHS Suitability); U.S. citizenship required. WHAT CANDIDATES SHOULD UNDERSTAND Work is expected to be onsite in Arlington, Virginia; approved telework may be available only as authorized by the Government. Positions are contingent upon contract award and successful completion of applicable security or suitability processing. For cleared positions, the recruiting requirement is an active Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain SCI—not necessarily current SCI access on day one. For suitability positions, candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a favorable DHS Fitness Determination. Prior DHS service may help, but a previous Public Trust is not automatically transferable or guaranteed to reactivate. PAY RANGE: $75,000–$95,000 Annually + Benefits (Compensation and employment offer are negotiable and will be finalized based on the candidate’s relevant experience and interview assessment). The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. Cybermedia Technologies management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, where applicable and available, reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions of this position. Please note: Candidate(s) will be required to go through pre-employment screening. Cybermedia Technologies, Inc. is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer! (EOE; M/F/D/V) If you are looking for a fun and challenging environment with talented, motivated people to work with, CTEC is the right place for you. In addition to employee salary, we offer an array of employee benefits including: Paid vacation & Sick leave Health insurance coverage Career training Performance bonus programs 401K contribution & Employer Match 11 Federal Holidays Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Public Relations Manager II (DHS Suitability)
item.description: Public Relations Manager II (DHS Suitability) Organization: CTEC Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/15/2026 CTEC is a leading technology firm that provides modernization, digital transformation, and application development services to the U.S. Federal Government. Headquartered in McLean, VA, CTEC has over 300 team members working on mission-critical systems and projects for agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security, Internal Revenue Service, and the Office of Personnel Management. The work we do affects millions of U.S. citizens daily as they interact with the systems we build. Our best-in-class commercial solutions, modified for our customers’ bespoke mission requirements, are enabling this future every day. The Company has experienced rapid growth over the past 3 years and recently received a strategic investment from Main Street Capital Corporation (NYSE: MAIN). In addition to our recent growth in Federal Civilian agencies, we are seeking to expand our capabilities in cloud development and footprint in national-security focused agencies within the Department of Defense and U.S. Intelligence Community. Cybermedia Technologies (CTEC) is seeking an experienced Public Relations Manager II (DHS Suitability) to join our team. PROGRAM OVERVIEW CISA’s Stakeholder Engagement Division requires an integrated team to support council and sector governance, approximately 500 annual engagements, stakeholder coordination, policy and risk analysis, executive communications, records, and contract management. The work spans unclassified and classified environments and requires products that are accurate, accessible, compliant, and ready for government use. POSITION SUMMARY Lead strategic communications, executive messaging, and stakeholder outreach supporting CISA sector-risk-management operations. This mid-senior role owns high-visibility products and coordinates inputs and approvals across complex federal and industry stakeholder groups. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Develop communication strategies and a broad range of executive and external-facing products, including emails, memos, talking points, summaries, briefings, graphics, and social content. Translate sector risk, cybersecurity, resilience, and policy information into clear, audience-specific messages. Coordinate communication support for sector and cross-sector engagements, working groups, and emergent events. Gather and reconcile input from federal leads, SMEs, industry partners, and other stakeholders. Manage designated mailboxes, inquiries, routing, response tracking, and communication logs. Review products for accuracy, clarity, tone, branding, accessibility, and DHS/CISA style compliance. Support rapid-response communications and after-action products during urgent operational events. Use engagement data and stakeholder feedback to refine outreach and messaging. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 5+ years experience in strategic communications, public relations, public affairs, or stakeholder engagement. Strong executive writing, editing, message development, and project-management skills. Experience coordinating high-visibility products through complex review and approval processes. Ability to advise clients and work effectively with senior government and industry stakeholders. Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable DHS Fitness Determination (Public Trust/DHS Suitability); U.S. citizenship required. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Prior CISA, DHS, critical-infrastructure, or federal advisory experience. Experience with executive communications, graphic design, or digital content. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, Microsoft 365, Drupal, and collaboration platforms. CLEARANCE Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable DHS Fitness Determination (Public Trust/DHS Suitability); U.S. citizenship required. WHAT CANDIDATES SHOULD UNDERSTAND Work is expected to be onsite in Arlington, Virginia; approved telework may be available only as authorized by the Government. Positions are contingent upon contract award and successful completion of applicable security or suitability processing. For cleared positions, the recruiting requirement is an active Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain SCI—not necessarily current SCI access on day one. For suitability positions, candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a favorable DHS Fitness Determination. Prior DHS service may help, but a previous Public Trust is not automatically transferable or guaranteed to reactivate. PAY RANGE: $90,000–$115,000 Annually + Benefits (Compensation and employment offer are negotiable and will be finalized based on the candidate’s relevant experience and interview assessment.) The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. Cybermedia Technologies management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, where applicable and available, reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions of this position. Please note: Candidate(s) will be required to go through pre-employment screening. Cybermedia Technologies, Inc. is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer! (EOE; M/F/D/V) If you are looking for a fun and challenging environment with talented, motivated people to work with, CTEC is the right place for you. item.title: Director, Internal Communications & Employer Brand
item.description: Director, Internal Communications & Employer Brand Organization: Circle Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com. What you’ll be part of Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we’re expanding into some of the world’s strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder. What you’ll be responsible for As Director, Internal Communications & Employer Brand, you’ll drive two of our most visible functions shaping how Circle is understood — by employees, by candidates, and by the world. This is a highly cross-functional role for a strategic builder, operator, and storyteller who can shape programs, elevate standards, and partner across the business to deliver clear, credible, and compelling communications. You’ll play a central role in advancing Circle’s internal communications approach across a distributed, global, remote-first workforce — helping employees stay informed, aligned, and connected to the company’s strategy, priorities, and culture. You’ll also advance Circle’s employer brand, translating the employee experience into a strong, differentiated presence in the talent market. What you’ll work on Internal Communications Partner with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, including HR and Corporate Communications, to develop internal communications plans for major initiatives, organizational moments, and company priorities – not reactive support, but proactive counsel on what to say, when, and how. Help shape how Circle communicates company strategy and OKRs internally, translating priorities into messaging that feels relevant and actionable for employees across functions and regions. Build and scale internal communications programs in partnership with the Employee Experience Director and other cross-functional partners to support engagement, connection, and understanding across a distributed workforce. Evolve and maintain the operational infrastructure that makes communications effective and scalable, including: editorial planning, channel governance, distribution practices, and measurement frameworks. Support Circle’s intranet strategy and evolution, serving as the business owner steering this work in partnership with IT. Support sensitive, high-stakes, and change-related communications with sound judgment, strong stakeholder partnership, and attention to timing, tone, and employee impact. Employer Brand Drive the ongoing evolution of Circle’s employee value proposition (EVP) in partnership with Talent Acquisition, People leadership, and Marketing, ensuring it reflects real employee experience and talent priorities. Lead employer brand storytelling and content strategy across priority channels — careers content, employee stories, social content, recruiting campaigns, and talent-facing moments. Partner with Talent Acquisition to strengthen candidate experience as a brand touchpoint, using survey insights, feedback, and market signals to identify opportunities for improvement. Build and maintain employer brand intelligence infrastructure — including LLM/AI sentiment monitoring across major platforms and competitive benchmarking against talent peers. Drive Circle’s presence in employer awards, recognition programs, and talent-focused external opportunities that reinforce the company’s reputation as a destination employer. Build and own Circle’s alumni network — selecting and launching the right platform, developing community strategy, and creating engagement touchpoints that keep former Circlers connected to the brand as advocates, referral sources, and potential boomerangs. Ensure alignment between employer brand, people narrative, and broader corporate story so candidates and employees experience a consistent, authentic picture of Circle. Content & Cross-Functional Partnership Oversee the development of high-quality content across internal and talent-facing audiences — executive messaging, employee features, onboarding communications, event content, and campaign materials. Partner closely with Corporate Communications, Talent Acquisition, Employee Experience, and the broader People & Workplace team to ensure messaging is coordinated, timely, and mutually reinforcing. Drive key communications moments in the employee lifecycle, especially new hire and onboarding communications, in partnership with program owners. Serve as a trusted thought partner and communications advisor to People & Workplace leadership, Corporate Communications and cross-functional stakeholders. Bring a change-management lens to communications planning, helping teams communicate in ways that build understanding, reduce ambiguity, and support adoption. AI-First Operations Build repeatable, AI-enabled workflows across internal communications and employer brand that improve speed, consistency, and scale while preserving quality and editorial judgment. Use AI tools across the communications lifecycle — research, synthesis, drafting, localization, content adaptation, measurement, and workflow design. Contribute reusable prompts, templates, and automations to Circle’s shared AI ecosystem so the function benefits from scalable ways of working. Identify where automation can improve the operating model — recurring content workflows, campaign support, insights generation, and process coordination. Model strong judgment around where AI should accelerate work and where human voice, sensitivity, or relationship context should remain central. What you’ll bring to Circle Core Requirements 12+ years of progressive experience in internal communications, marketing, HR communications, content strategy, or a related field, including meaningful experience operating in complex, cross-functional environments. Exceptional writing and editorial judgment across formats, with the ability to adapt voice and messaging for executives, employees, candidates, and cross-functional audiences. Strong strategic instincts paired with operational discipline — able to move between big-picture program design and the details required to make systems run well. Strong track record driving internal communications programs at a fast-moving, global company — including communications planning, leadership messaging, editorial strategy, and stakeholder advisory work. Experience shaping or scaling employer brand efforts, including EVP development, talent storytelling, campaign planning, or employer brand measurement. Comfort using data and insights to assess effectiveness, identify opportunities, and improve communications outcomes. Proven ability to influence across functions and levels, build trust quickly, and drive progress through partnership rather than formal authority. People management experience, with a track record of developing talent, giving clear feedback, and building strong, resilient teams. Demonstrated AI fluency in a communications, content, or brand context — you actively use AI to improve quality, speed, and scale, and can translate that into practical team workflows. Preferred Background in financial services, fintech, digital assets, or another fast-evolving, highly regulated industry. Experience supporting communications through rapid growth, organizational change, or major business inflection points (IPO, M&A, rapid scaling). Circle is on a mission to create an inclusive financial future, with transparency at our core. We consider a wide variety of elements when crafting our compensation ranges and total compensation packages. Starting pay is determined by various factors, including but not limited to: relevant experience, skill set, qualifications, and other business and organizational needs. Please note that compensation ranges may differ for candidates in other locations. Base Pay Range: $200,000 – $257,500 We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status, or any other protected status required by the laws in the locations where we hire. Additionally, Circle participates in the E-Verify Program in certain locations, as required by law. Should you require accommodations or assistance in our interview process because of a disability, please reach out to [email protected] for support. We respect your privacy and will connect with you separately from our interview process to accommodate your needs. #LI-Remote Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Product & Technology Communications
item.description: Director, Product & Technology Communications Organization: Circle Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com. What you’ll be part of: Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we’re expanding into some of the world’s strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder. What you’ll be responsible for: Circle is looking for a Director of Product & Technology Communications to own the company’s media narrative and public profile of Circle’s platforms and products, including the Arc Platform, Circle Agent Stack, Circle Payments Network, and Circle Digital Assets and Services. This role is the primary communications partner to the product organization, embedded early in roadmap planning for all critical products and leading product launch communications, media relationships, and stage presence. It shapes how Circle is positioned with customers, builders, journalists, and the broader industry as the company expands its role in the future of money and commerce, including the emerging agentic economy. This is a San Francisco- or Palo Alto-based role. What you’ll work on: Building Arc’s public narrative as a platform — not a series of announcements. Developing a long-horizon story that makes Arc the most-referenced platform for coordinating economic activity and positions Circle as a technology company, not just a payments company. Owning Circle’s narrative in the agentic economy with press — building and placing the story of how AI agents transact using USDC, Circle Agent Stack, and Arc infrastructure with reporters and conference audiences, shaping the next generation of autonomous systems. Embedding with the product organization early in the development cycle — in planning and scoping, not just pre-launch — to shape narratives before they reach announcement day. Setting media and stages strategy and execution for all Arc and critical product launches and major platform milestones, including earned media campaigns, executive positioning, and collaboration with commercial and product organizations regarding partner and developer community communications. Developing and owning the stage and speaking strategy for Circle’s product and technology leaders: identifying the right conferences, panels, and keynote opportunities — including the AI and agentic economy circuit in the Bay Area (GTC, AI Summit, developer AI events) alongside crypto and fintech stages — building the messaging that goes with them, and managing executive prep end-to-end. Owning Circle’s tier-1 technology media relationships — TechCrunch, The Information, Wired, Fortune, Bloomberg Technology, Ars Technica, and developer-focused outlets — and building the AI and agentic economy press relationships that matter as autonomous systems move from research to infrastructure. Building and managing the executive thought leadership pipeline for product and technology leaders, including briefing materials, op-ed and byline development when appropriate, and narrative frameworks for media, investor, and developer audiences. Collaborating with the community team on the developer and builder communications strategy for Arc’s ecosystem — positioning Arc as the infrastructure layer that builders choose, with messaging tailored to the developer community alongside mainstream press. Serving as an essential partner to Public Affairs and Reputation Management in crisis and issues management situations involving Arc, agentic products, or other cornerstone Circle products — providing the product expertise, narrative context, and press relationship intelligence that effective crisis response requires. Architecting AI-powered communications workflows to scale media monitoring and briefing prep. Modeling the team standard for strategic independence, product fluency, and narrative ownership. What you’ll bring to Circle: Core Requirements 10+ years of experience in product or technology communications, with substantial in-house experience at a technology company. A demonstrable track record of building product brands over time — not just managing launches — including developing narrative strategy well ahead of announcement moments. Deep relationships with Tier 1 technology and business media, specifically with reporters who cover infrastructure, developer platforms, fintech, or the future of payments. Experience with developer-facing products or platforms, with an understanding of how to communicate to builder and technical communities alongside mainstream press. Familiarity with the AI agent landscape and the media and stages covering it — understanding how programmable money infrastructure connects to the agentic economy, and comfort operating in a space where the narrative is still being defined. Strong technical fluency — ability to read product documentation and engineering briefs, understand what matters commercially and narratively, and translate technical detail into media-ready positioning without losing accuracy. Experience developing executive thought leadership programs, including speaker strategy, stage management, and long-form narrative development for product and technology leaders. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to move between technical depth and accessible storytelling depending on the audience. Strong news judgment and experience managing a high-velocity, multi-stakeholder product communications calendar across launch cycles. A track record of operating with high autonomy — identifying the work, building the strategy, and executing without waiting for direction. Familiarity with generative AI models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) and their application to communications workflows. Must be based in San Francisco or Palo Alto. Preferred Requirements In-house experience at a FAANG company or major fintech, or high-growth technology platform. Background in or deep familiarity with blockchain, digital assets, programmable money infrastructure, or developer platforms. Existing relationships with AI, ML, or agentic economy media alongside mainstream technology and crypto outlets. Experience with developer community communications, ecosystem evangelism, or platform go-to-market. Existing relationships with crypto, Web3, or fintech trade media alongside mainstream technology outlets. Experience building or managing AI-driven communications workflows or operational tooling. Familiarity with Slack, Apple MacOS, and Google Suite. Circle is on a mission to create an inclusive financial future, with transparency at our core. We consider a wide variety of elements when crafting our compensation ranges and total compensation packages. Starting pay is determined by various factors, including but not limited to: relevant experience, skill set, qualifications, and other business and organizational needs. Our purview includes corporate and brand media relations, issues and reputation management, financial communications, and associate communications, as well as a full-service content and creative storytelling team that brings the story of Capital One to life on internal and external channels. We are communicators, writers, creative directors and multimedia experts, and we are all storytellers. As a team supporting external communications for our Premium Products and Experiences line of business, we are strategic counselors to our partners throughout the enterprise, sitting at the intersection of value creation and risk mitigation. We help drive business initiatives forward while enhancing the reputation of Capital One. We are seeking talented individuals to join our growing Communications team. This position requires exceptional judgment, an ability to build relationships in a highly matrixed environment, and a sustained focus on delivering results. Creative problem-solving, an ability to read the data and the room, and a passion for storytelling are all critical to success in this role. Empathy, teamwork and a sense of humor are essential. About the Role As a Senior Manager, you will lead strategic communications initiatives that enhance Capital One’s reputation and support key business objectives. You’ll manage high-impact programs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and work with internal and external partners to deliver creative and effective communication strategies. Primary Responsibilities Serve as a strategic advisor to internal leaders and partners to plan and execute data-backed, integrated communications campaigns on behalf of the Premium Products and Experiences line of business. By joining our team, you’ll be expected to push the envelope in driving premium narrative around Premium Products & Travel and Loyalty, Marketing & Spend Experiences to external audiences. Develop compelling, consistent, tailored messages for various audiences and channels, including in response to media opportunities Maintain a deep understanding of current and emerging internal and external risks and sensitivities and how to manage related stakeholder needs Collaborate effectively across highly matrixed, cross-functional teams, offering real-time counsel on communications strategies to optimize results, mitigate risk and ensure stakeholder engagement Leverage data to evaluate results, extract insights and optimize future programs Identify new opportunities to institute best practices and improve enterprise governance Oversee team operations and exhibit excellent judgment Act as a highly collaborative self-starter in a fast-paced environment Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or military experience At least 6 years of communications experience Preferred Qualifications At least 1 year of public relations or communications experience in financial services, technology, or consumer brands At least 1 year of experience in developing and implementing change management strategies at a publicly traded company At least 3 years of developing and executing thought leadership and consumer campaigns At least 3 years of experience supporting, partnering and interacting with internal business clients or serving as a consultant for external business clients At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position. Working across teams, you’ll help deliver impactful campaigns and foster strong relationships with key stakeholders. This position requires exceptional judgment, strong project management skills, an ability to build relationships in a highly matrixed environment, and a sustained focus on delivering results. Creative problem-solving, an ability to read the data and the room, and a passion for storytelling are all critical to success in this role. Empathy, teamwork and a sense of humor are essential. Primary Responsibilities: Assist in the development and execution of proactive communication, talent and tastemaker campaigns and team operations under the guidance of senior team members Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to execute program elements Liaise with media on in-bound media inquiries Create materials such as media messaging, pitches, media lists, briefing books, social posts for executives Provide project management support horizontally across team, including developing workback plans, keeping project trackers, distilling meetings into actionable next steps Assist with the development of measurement and media coverage reports Coordinate contract deliverables and logistics for talent and tastemaker partners Manage and optimize communications reporting and analytics Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or military experience At least 3 years of external communications experience Preferred Qualifications: Public relations or communications experience in financial services, technology, or consumer brands At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position. The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations, and refers to the amount Capital One is willing to pay at the time of this posting. item.description: Communications Associate, Content Writer Organization: Capital One Location: McLean, VA | Richmond, VA | New York, NY Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Overview Communications Associate, Content Writer Within the Premium Products & Travel (PP&T) organization, the Concierge team harnesses the power of artificial intelligence, the warmth of human experts and the convenience of the latest interfaces to help high-performance people actualize the full potential of their lives. From access to the hottest restaurants to guaranteed upgrades at the world’s finest resorts, our concierge team is available 24/7/365 via our proprietary app to support our customers and fulfill their requests. It’s concierge, reimagined for the digital age. We’re looking to add an Associate Content Writer to our team to write editorial stories about the world’s most inspiring experiences, from dining to travel, to help our members live richer lives. You will create content including recommendations and reviews, profiles, trend stories, and features, across our app, emails, and social media channels. Capital One provides a fast paced, dynamic environment where you can excel in your career. At Capital One, mission and values are at our core, sparking and enabling us to do good for our associates, customers and communities. Guided by our shared values, we thrive in an environment where collaboration and openness are valued. We nurture an environment that attracts and develops talent from all backgrounds and experiences, and empower our associates to do great work by creating a culture of belonging that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas – and are routinely recognized as one of the best companies to work for. What we’re looking for: A storyteller, who sees words as an incredibly powerful tool for connecting with people A creative problem solver with the ability to produce original, brand-elevating copy A strong writer who is able to adapt tone and personality as they shift between writing long form content, to snackable social copy, to informational web communications Someone who approaches assignments from a customer-centric perspective A research obsessive who sweats accuracy, and can always find the most engaging elements of every story You’ll love your job the most if you: Have a clear understanding of tone and the ability to quickly adapt your writing style Work quickly without compromising quality, knowing that iteration and testing are just part of creating exceptional experiences Take initiative, aren’t afraid to fail, ask thoughtful questions, and constantly seek better ways of working and communicating Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or military experience At least 2 years of editorial writing or marketing copywriting experience Preferred Qualifications: 3+ years of editorial writing or marketing copywriting experience 2+ years of brand experience in multichannel marketing 2+ years experience as a freelancer or staff writer for a media organization, newspaper, magazine, or editorial website At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position. item.title: Marketing & Communications Associate
item.description: Marketing & Communications Associate Organization: Aspen Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 ABOUT US The Aspen Institute is a global nonprofit organization whose purpose is to ignite human potential to build understanding and create new possibilities for a better world. Founded in 1949, the Institute drives change through dialogue, leadership, and action to help solve society’s greatest challenges. It is headquartered in Washington, DC, and has a campus in Aspen, Colorado, as well as an international network of partners. PUBLIC PROGRAMS DEPARTMENT The Public Programs team at the Aspen Institute produces a number of events each year that are open to members of the general public. This position will support the major events and activities of the department, with special emphasis on Aspen Ideas Festival, held every summer over seven days on the Aspen Institute’s campus in Aspen, CO. The Aspen Ideas Festival is the nation’s premier public gathering for leaders from around the globe and across many disciplines to engage in deep and inquisitive discussions about ideas and issues that shape our lives and challenge our times. The Aspen Ideas Festival fosters attendees and speakers from a wide range of international sectors and industries to engage in meaningful dialogue. Each year, the Festival covers a wide range of timely and critical topic areas through panels, workshops, book clubs, debates, deep dives, and interviews. ABOUT THIS ROLE The Associate is a strategic and creative storyteller who will elevate the digital presence of Aspen Ideas across platforms and audiences. This role leads social content strategy and execution for the Aspen Ideas Festival, Ideas extension events, and other public programs throughout the year. The ideal candidate is an agile creator, a sharp strategist, and a collaborative communicator who loves translating big ideas into compelling, shareable social content. This position will report directly to the Associate Director. The salary range for this position is $60,000 – $75,000. In accordance with our Reimagining Work policy, the Marketing and Communications Associate should be willing to be in-person with colleagues a minimum of 40% of the time while having the flexibility to work remotely for the balance. WHAT YOU WILL DO Content Strategy & Calendar Management Develop and own the year-round social media content strategy for @AspenIdeas and associated events. Collaborate with an appointed member of the Aspen Ideas: Health team on related cadence and content, as well as other programs, as assigned. Build and maintain the social media editorial calendar, including event promotion, real-time event coverage, and evergreen storytelling throughout the year. Ensure content aligns with brand voice, strategic priorities, and audience growth goals. Content Creation (Owned Channels) Lead creation of all social media assets, including short-form video editing, graphic design, photographs, and copywriting to amplify Aspen Ideas sessions, podcasts, articles, collections, website, and more. Produce high-quality, platform-optimized content for Instagram, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, and emerging platforms as approved. Manage asset workflow before, during, and after events. Website Management Draft and post copy to the aspenideas.org website, including blog posts, session collections, and promotional offers. Support the event speaker coordinator team with public facing data entry both before and after the Festival (and other events, as assigned); to include speaker biographies, image assets, and session information. Cross-Channel & Partner Coordination (Earned Channels) Coordinate earned social content with underwriters, speakers, media partners, and other collaborators. Develop social media toolkits and associated branded assets for partners to utilize to maximize sharing. Work closely with the Aspen Institute digital team to amplify Aspen Ideas and other Public Programs content on main Institute channels. Ensure brand consistency and messaging alignment across all touchpoints. Paid Social & Campaign Support Support development and execution of paid social media campaigns to promote pass sales, event registrations, and broadcast content. Collaborate with internal teams and external agencies on creative assets, targeting, and optimization. Community Management & Social Listening Lead day-to-day community management, including responding to audience questions, moderating conversations, and fostering a lively and inclusive online community. Conduct regular social listening to identify trends, conversations, and opportunities for engagement. Analytics & Performance Reporting Track, analyze, and report on social media metrics, content performance, and audience insights. Use data to refine strategy, inform content decisions, and communicate impact to leadership. Trend Monitoring & Platform Innovation Stay current with platform updates, emerging social tools, and cultural trends. Proactively recommend new formats, experiments, and platform opportunities to keep Aspen Ideas at the forefront of digital storytelling. Team & Contractor Management Manage digital contractors and agency partners supporting social content—particularly during Aspen Ideas Festival and assigned Aspen Ideas extensions. Other work may include support of Aspen Community Programs or other Public Programs and Institute events in Aspen and elsewhere. Provide clear creative briefs, oversee workflows, and ensure execution aligns with strategy and brand standards. WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO THRIVE 1-3+ years of professional communications or marketing experience, including social media management; ideally in a fast-paced, mission-driven, media, cultural, or event-based environment. Demonstrated expertise in content strategy, community building, and multi-platform growth. Strong portfolio of social content, including video editing and graphic design work. Excellent writing and storytelling skills, with an ability to translate complex ideas into clear, engaging content. Proficiency with video editing tools (e.g., Adobe Premiere, CapCut), design platforms (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Canva), and social media management tools (e.g., Sprout Social, Later, Hootsuite). Experience managing paid social campaigns or collaborating with performance marketing teams. Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects on tight deadlines, especially during live events. Comfortable working cross-functionally with senior leaders, partners, and external talent. A deep curiosity about big ideas across policy, culture, science, health, technology, and society. Preferred Qualifications Experience capturing content and covering live events, conferences, or festivals. Background in journalism, digital media, communications, or related fields. Familiarity with intellectual, cultural, or policy-oriented content. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The Aspen Institute offers a generous benefits package including health, dental, vision, and prescription benefits, retirement benefits, and paid leave. The Aspen Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all District and federal laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or protected veteran or disabled status and will not be discriminated against. The Aspen Institute welcomes individuals with disabilities to participate in its programs, including the interview process. If you would like to request accommodations or have questions about accessibility, please email [email protected] or call 202-736-2127 in advance of your visit. Requests for ASL or CART services should be made at least two weeks in advance when possible. We will make every effort to fulfill requests, subject to availability. item.title: Analyst/Sr Analyst, Federal Affairs
item.description: Analyst/Sr Analyst, Federal Affairs Organization: American Airlines Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Intro Are you ready to explore a world of possibilities, both at work and during your time off? Join our American Airlines family, and you’ll travel the world, grow your expertise and become the best version of you. As you embark on a new journey, you’ll tackle challenges with flexibility and grace, learning new skills and advancing your career while having the time of your life. Feel free to enrich both your personal and work life and hop on board! Why you’ll love this job The Analyst, Federal Affairs supports American Airlines’ engagement with federal regulatory and legislative stakeholders by conducting research and analysis, evaluating emerging regulatory issues, and providing strategic insights on matters impacting the aviation industry and the company. Based in Washington, D.C., this role assists in tracking legislative and regulatory activity, preparing briefing materials, and gathering insights to support Government Affairs initiatives. Working closely with internal stakeholders and team members, the Analyst helps ensure the company remains informed about federal policy developments and emerging regulatory matters. Pay Range: $72,000-$131,000 What you’ll do As noted above, this list is intended to reflect the current job but there may be additional essential functions (and certainly non-essential job functions) that are not referenced. Management will modify the job or require other tasks be performed whenever it is deemed appropriate to do so, observing, of course, any legal obligations including any collective bargaining obligations. Monitor, analyze, and assess federal regulatory, legislative, and policy developments affecting the airline industry Conduct research and analysis on federal issues and summarize findings for Government Affairs leadership and business partners Assist in preparing briefings, reports, presentations, and background materials for internal and external meetings Evaluate and summarize regulatory actions, legislative proposals, and industry developments and communicate potential impacts to stakeholders Support responses to information requests and assist with regulatory and compliance-related activities Maintain tracking tools, databases, and reporting materials related to policy and regulatory matters Collaborate with internal business partners to collect information and support ongoing regulatory initiatives Assist with meeting preparation, stakeholder communications, and administrative activities related to Government Affairs priorities Support special projects and analyses as assigned All you’ll need for success Minimum Qualifications – Education & Prior Job Experience Bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, economics, business, law, or a related field 2 years of experience in government affairs, public policy, regulatory affairs, legislative affairs, research, congressional, or federal agency environments Preferred Qualifications – Education & Prior Job Experience Recent experience working in or with federal agencies, and/or congressional offices Exposure to federal legislative or regulatory processes Experience conducting research and preparing reports or presentations Familiarity with aviation, transportation, or other highly regulated industries Experience supporting projects involving multiple stakeholders Skills, Licenses & Certifications Demonstrated ability to analyze complex regulatory and policy issues, synthesize information from multiple sources, and communicate business implications to senior leadership Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills Ability to gather, organize, and summarize information from multiple sources Effective written and verbal communication skills Ability to prepare clear reports, presentations, and briefing materials Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment Ability to learn and apply knowledge of regulatory and legislative processes What you’ll get Feel free to take advantage of all that American Airlines has to offer: Travel Perks: Ready to explore the world? You, your family and your friends can reach 365 destinations on more than 6,800 daily flights across our global network. Health Benefits: On day one, you’ll have access to your health, dental, prescription and vision benefits to help you stay well. And that’s just the start, we also offer virtual doctor visits, flexible spending accounts and more. Wellness Programs: We want you to be the best version of yourself – that’s why our wellness programs provide you with all the right tools, resources and support you need. 401(k) Program: Available upon hire and, depending on the workgroup, employer contributions to your 401(k) program are available after one year. Additional Benefits: Other great benefits include our Employee Assistance Program, pet insurance and discounts on hotels, cars, cruises and more. Feel free to be yourself at American From the team members we hire to the customers we serve, inclusion and diversity are the foundation of the dynamic workforce at American Airlines. Our 20+ Team Member Business Resource Groups are focused on connecting our team members to our customers, suppliers, communities and shareholders, helping team members reach their full potential and creating an inclusive work environment to meet and exceed the needs of our diverse world. Are you ready to feel a tremendous sense of pride and satisfaction as you do your part to keep the largest airline in the world running smoothly as we care for people on life’s journey? Feel free to be yourself at American. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
