item.title: PAC & Government Relations Manager
item.description: PAC & Government Relations Manager Organization: Blue Origin Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! This role is part of Blue Origin corporate functions, providing centralized support across Blue Origin business unit teams, functions, and locations. This is a high-visibility role responsible for managing the Blue Origin Political Action Committee (Blue PAC) and supporting the Government Relations team. The PAC & Government Relations Manager will be tasked with achieving a top-100 company goal: aggressively expanding PAC membership and employee engagement to meet ambitious participation targets. This position is critical to evolving our PAC strategy, managing the PAC budget and fundraising cycles, and strengthening advocacy efforts. The ideal candidate is a passionate and energetic self-starter with a bias for action and a natural talent for recruitment and relationship-building. This role requires frequent travel and direct engagement with employees at all Blue Origin sites, as well as regular interfacing with C-suite and SVP-level executives. Special Mentions Significant travel (approximately 25-50%) is expected to all Blue Origin sites to meet with eligible employees. Responsibilities Drive significant growth in Blue PAC membership through aggressive and innovative recruitment strategies to meet ambitious, CEO-level company goals. Develop and execute a comprehensive strategy for PAC member engagement, including creative communications and high-quality events. Manage the PAC budget, including forecasting and reporting, in alignment with federal regulations and fundraising cycles. Plan and execute engaging PAC events and fundraisers for employees, executives, and external stakeholders. Regularly interface with, brief, and staff senior executives (SVPs and C-Suite) for PAC-related activities and events. Represent Blue Origin and the Blue PAC at external political fundraisers and events. Manage the use of supplier data and relationships to support federal advocacy efforts. Conduct political and legislative research, tracking key issues and providing analysis to the Government Relations team. Interface with and support efforts involving external consultants and internal business units. Qualifications Required: BA or BS is required. Proven experience with federal campaigns, fundraising, political donations, and/or running a corporate PAC. A full understanding of federal campaign finance law and compliance. A passionate, proactive, and outgoing personality with a natural ability to build relationships, recruit, and influence others. Exceptional interpersonal skills and outstanding verbal and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to multitask with strong attention to detail and a bias for action. Deep understanding of the U.S. federal policymaking process and government relations. Ability to creatively communicate the political and legislative process to current and prospective PAC members. Desired: Demonstrated success in a recruitment, sales, or fundraising role with aggressive growth targets. Experience working directly with federal elected officials, political parties, companies, consultancies, trade associations, or governmental agencies. Experience working with suppliers, trade associations, and/or industry coalitions. Experience working with or on cross-functional business teams. Base Pay Range For VA applicants: $121,023.00 – $169,432.20 Other site ranges may differ Culture Statement Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. Export Control Regulations Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Background Check Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training. Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical Benefits Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program. Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week) Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays. Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company’s intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company’s results, or other factors at the company’s sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. Equal Employment Opportunity Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here. Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at [email protected] . item.title: Media Relations Manager
item.description: Media Relations Manager Organization: Hudson Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Description Hudson Institute seeks a media relations manager to develop and operationalize Hudson’s media strategy, proactively promote Hudson’s research and analysis, and interface with press. This is a full-time position based out of Hudson’s Washington, DC, office, reporting to the director of external affairs. About Hudson Institute Hudson Institute is a research-focused public policy think tank headquartered in Washington, DC, dedicated to promoting American leadership for a secure, free, and prosperous future. For more than half a century, Hudson Institute has been challenging conventional thinking by developing new ideas and practical solutions to shape critical foreign and domestic policy decisions. Responsibilities Develops and executes Hudson’s media strategy to broaden awareness among key audiences: journalists, policymakers, experts, and supporters. Proactively secures media opportunities for Hudson by pitching experts, research, policy memos, reports, and commentary to journalists covering breaking news and long-term policy issues. Builds and maintains relationships with reporters, editors, producers, and bookers across print, digital, television, radio, and podcast outlets. Fields and responds to press inquiries and schedules and facilitates interviews for experts with media outlets. Pitches op-eds for experts, facilitating communication between editors and Hudson experts throughout the publication process. Maintains comprehensive media lists and facilitates media coverage of Hudson events. Collaborates with digital media manager to identify Hudson experts, research, and content to promote across social media channels, including coordinating newsworthy social media content and event highlights. Engages Hudson’s research staff to identify, develop, and communicate compelling stories, and regularly implements new communications approaches. Tracks breaking news and trending topics to leverage Hudson’s policy work and expertise in real-time media opportunities. Tracks Hudson media coverage, requesting corrections when necessary. Requirements Commitment to Hudson Institute’s mission and supporting the work of the Institute’s experts and staff. Three years’ relevant experience in communications, politics, policy, journalism, or other relevant fields. Strong news judgment and public policy savvy. Demonstrated ability to build relationships with reporters and successfully pitch stories to national and policy media. Excellent time and project management skills. Excellent communication and comprehension skills, both written and oral, including professional and tactful demeanor in dealing with press. Ability to work closely and effectively with others. Creative and entrepreneurial mindset. Commitment to acting with integrity and the utmost professionalism. Compensation and Benefits Salary: $60,000 – $80,000 per year Health insurance (medical, dental, and vision coverage) Retirement savings plan with employer matching contributions after one year with Hudson Paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, and holidays Life and disability insurance Paid parental and family leave Commuter benefits Application Instructions Please submit a personal resume and cover letter here . Cover letters should be written by the applicant—not by generative AI. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President of Communications
item.description: Vice President of Communications Organization: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (Reporters Committee) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Company Description The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (Reporters Committee) provides pro bono legal representation, amicus curiae support, and other legal resources to protect First Amendment freedoms and the newsgathering rights of journalists. The Reporters Committee serves news organizations, reporters, editors, documentary filmmakers, media lawyers, and many more who use its online resources. Job Description The Vice President of Communications leads strategy for external communications to advance the Reporters Committee mission to provide free legal services for journalists. The VP of Communications elevates the visibility and impact of work across the organization by creating opportunities through owned content and digital channels, executive positioning, media engagement, strategic events, and stakeholder relationships that increase awareness of the importance of legal support for journalism and amplify the organization’s policy and advocacy priorities. The Vice President of Communications reports to the President and is a member of the Executive Team. They lead and mentor a high-performing team that supports organizational communications priorities. The Vice President for Communications is a(n): Architect of the organization’s communication strategy that advances the mission to provide free legal services to journalists and newsrooms Strategic counselor with input on overall organizational strategy and decision making as a member of the Executive Team Skilled leader who leverages budget and talent to manage the external messaging and brand positioning with key audiences across channels Responsibilities Communications Strategic Planning and Execution Refine and implement a strategic communications plan, including a robust digital strategy, that is aligned with and integrated into Reporters Committee’s organization-wide strategic and programmatic goals Educate and collaborate with colleagues across the organization to ensure that all members of the organization are communicating consistently and effectively Recognize trends, stay on top of developments and strategy, and advise on communication opportunities (both planned and impromptu) Brand and Message Development Ensure consistent and effective messaging across Reporters Committee’s social media, web presence, external communications, and public speaking Develop messaging around emerging and new areas of engagement for the organization to ensure that Reporters Committee is an influential thought leader shaping the conversation Develop and oversee internal processes to enable Reporters Committee’s external communications, particularly in response to fast breaking news related to the organization’s mission and work Oversee the development and delivery of internal and external communications for senior executive levels, including briefing materials, scripting/messaging for briefing materials, scripting/messaging for internal keynotes, presentations, media engagements, social media, and events External Stakeholder Engagement Collaborate with internal staff and external partners and manage vendors to develop and implement communications products across a variety of media channels Collaborate with development team to ensure that messaging and distribution advances development strategy Develop partnership with outside organizations, media companies, board and major donors to further Reporters Committee’s reach and mission Oversee marketing budgets and conference speaking proposals to leverage Reporters Committee’s expertise with key journalism audiences and maximize opportunities to educate people about our resources and services Management and Leadership Oversee Content, Digital, and Media teams responsible for the core pillars of Communications deliverables Recruit, manage, and mentor team members, ensuring contributions support exceptional quality communications, aligned with the strategic goals Promote a culture of high performance, collaboration, effective, respectful and inclusive teamwork Contribute to Executive Team thinking and decision making related to overall management and leadership of the organization Develop policies and trainings for staff on media relations, social media use, public speaking and other core communications functions Identify challenges facing Reporters Committee and work with Executive Team colleagues and staff to identify communications opportunities and solutions, and execute strategies in response Qualifications 20+ years of experience in strategic communications, Legal Communications, Public Relations, Marketing or other related area At least 10 years experience managing people and teams, preferably in a nonprofit environment, although corporate, association, and government communications experience is also applicable Ability to understand the needs of each audience and channel the organization’s voice in creating highly effective communications to reach those audiences Demonstrated expertise in message development, audience segmentation and engagement, editorial and content planning, operational delivery, developing and executing campaigns that shape policy or opinion; measurement of results; and managing the work of communications’ colleagues Demonstrated skill in building relationships with top-tier reporters and editors, in successfully positioning content with the media and online to achieve high-impact results Direct knowledge of, or experience in advocacy around democracy, journalism, human rights, and/or related issues preferred Skills and Attributes Ability to think strategically while simultaneously overseeing tactical implementation Creativity about utilization of social, email, and online communications Creativity to effectively leverage a variety of media technologies Exceptional written and editing skills with a relentless commitment to accuracy and attention to detail Strong analytic capacity, ability to master new subject matter quickly and articulate complex concepts clearly and effectively Proven track record for new, innovative approaches and smart risk taking Brings judgment, creative problem-solving, and responsiveness Excellent organizational and management skills with a focus on achieving measurable and ambitious goals, including willingness to assume accountability for all areas of responsibility Demonstrated ability to meet tight deadlines, developing and moving projects forward with a high degree of independence and autonomy Ability to collaborate effectively within a team and across organizational boundaries. Strong and diplomatic interpersonal skills, demonstrating both a collaborative spirit and the ability to make decisions Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and highly professional environment that emphasizes excellence, collegiality and teamwork Ability to work effectively with multiple business partners, including cross-group teams, virtual and global teams, vendors and agency partners Additional Information Compensation: Reporters Committee is committed to offering competitive pay and generous benefits, including group medical insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, retirement benefits, health-reimbursement accounts, and paid family leave. The salary range for this position is $167,900 to $185,300. How to apply: Submit a resume and cover letter here . NOTE: Please submit materials in one PDF file. Only complete applications will advance in the hiring process. The role will remain open until filled. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and operate computer equipment. The employee is occasionally required to stand and walk. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. RCFP Is an Equal Opportunity Employer. At the Reporters Committee, we celebrate the diversity of our employees and our leadership. RCFP is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Public Relations & Media Specialist
item.description: Public Relations & Media Specialist Organization: Links Global Location: Gaithersburg, MD Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Salary Ceiling: $68,000-$82,000 Job Description: Performs public relations and media activities for communication programs for a variety of government and private sector clients. Primary functions including but not limited to are planning, coordination, implementation and evaluation of: public relations programs; media relations plans; production and distribution of multimedia materials; and market research. Orchestrates, coordinates and executes special events, book tours, concerts and art shows, special presentations, public meetings, discussion groups, film showings, trade shows and exhibits, and conferences. Directs media activities including but not limited to media and spokesperson training, materials development and dissemination (press releases, speeches, briefings, media advisories, scripts, fact sheets and other resources), media pitching and story placement, and outreach activities (partnerships, press events, and interviews). Creates materials and coordinates production and distribution of multimedia products including but not limited to: web streaming, satellite media tours, PSAs, VNRs, ANRs, on-demand packages, documentaries, audio tours, commercials, and new media targeted to multiple audiences. Oversees market research activities including but not limited to public opinion polls, focus groups, intercepts, media placement analysis, trade shows interactions, environmental scans and needs assessments. Performs other promotional and outreach duties required. Participates in company-wide business development, and marketing activities. Position may require occasional domestic and international travel. Minimum Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree, in communications, political science or related field 8 years experience working in journalism, public relations, or media development 3 years experience working with national and international media Project management, budget monitoring and staff supervision Demonstrated ability to work tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple assignments, and work well with other interdisciplinary teams Proven record of customer satisfaction, detailed oriented and extremely organized Exceptional communication and writing ability Desired Qualifications: Experience targeting multicultural and age-specific audiences Content knowledge in any of the following areas: health, environment, science and technology, humanities, socio anthropology, arts, and entertainment preferred Skills Prerequisite: Knowledge of word processing, database, spreadsheets and project management software and general office communication equipment Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. item.title: Senior Manager, U.S. Federal Affairs
item.description: Senior Manager, U.S. Federal Affairs Organization: Netflix Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode – pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next. The Team When your mission is to entertain the world, you must not only contend with content and technological challenges, but also a variety of public policy and regulatory issues. To meet the latter needs, Netflix’s Global Affairs team conducts government relations, policy development, advocacy and lobbying across the globe. Through the Global Affairs team’s efforts, Netflix is able to develop strategies to enter new markets and continue to innovate by successfully navigating sensitive regulatory landscapes and complex situations. Through their work, the Global Affairs team creates the environment Netflix needs to continue producing exciting content and world-class innovations that thrill audiences worldwide. The Opportunity Netflix is seeking a Senior Manager to support its work on U.S. federal policy within the U.S. & Canada (“UCAN”) Global Affairs team. The role reports to the Senior Director of U.S. Public Policy, and is based in Washington, D.C., with domestic and international travel as needed. The UCAN Global Affairs team advocates for a legislative and regulatory environment conducive to Netflix’s growth in the U.S. and Canada and serves as a strategic partner to internal business groups as they navigate the policy world. As part of this team, the successful candidate will be immersed in the unique content for which Netflix is known and support U.S. policy advocacy on all matters related to content creation, production, and delivery. The Senior Manager will help advance business and policy objectives in Washington, build and maintain strong relationships with policymakers, provide thought leadership on critical issues, collaborate with industry and civil society partners, and serve as a resource to internal stakeholders on U.S. federal legislative developments. Responsibilities Partner with the Senior Director of U.S. Public Policy to develop and execute advocacy strategy to support Netflix’s U.S. federal policy priorities. Develop high-impact advocacy materials, including policy strategy, legislative analysis, talking points, and presentations. Build and maintain strong relationships with U.S. federal policymakers, including members of Congress, executive branch officials, and their staff. Monitor congressional hearings, markups, and other legislative developments on a wide range of issues impacting the business. Conduct legislative research and analysis. Collaborate with internal teams as well as external consultants, trade associations, and other stakeholders to develop strategy and proactively advocate for Netflix’s interests on a variety of policy issues. Advise internal teams on key policy developments and their impact on the business. Attend company events, trade association meetings, congressional briefings, and industry receptions. Requirements Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience in U.S. federal policy and/or advocacy, including roles in the U.S. Congress, federal agencies, major corporations, law firms, trade associations, and/or civil society. Experience working on technology, media, and/or telecom policy is preferred. Exceptional written and verbal communication. Strong interpersonal skills and experience collaborating successfully with multiple teams. Excellent judgment, research skills, and attention to detail. Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $325,000.00 – $515,000.00. Netflix provides comprehensive benefits including Health Plans, Mental Health support, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with employer match, Stock Option Program, Disability Programs, Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts, Family-forming benefits, and Life and Serious Injury Benefits. We also offer paid leave of absence programs. Full-time hourly employees accrue 35 days annually for paid time off to be used for vacation, holidays, and sick paid time off. Full-time salaried employees are immediately entitled to flexible time off. See more details about our Benefits here. Netflix is a unique culture and environment. Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner. We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, caste, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic makeup, marital status, or military service. item.title: Director, Influencer Marketing
item.description: Director, Influencer Marketing Organization: Orchestra Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 09/15/2026 ABOUT ORCHESTRA Orchestra is a strategic communications and marketing company built for today’s complex and fragmented world. From decoding audiences to designing bold strategies, Orchestra integrates people, platforms, and stories that stick to help clients build lasting influence. The company offers programs that span from the highest level strategic business counsel through to tactical execution. Orchestra brings together 700+ people with experience across consumer and lifestyle, technology, nonprofit and philanthropy, real estate, sports, travel, hospitality, and more. Made up of leading firms BerlinRosen, Civitas Public Affairs Group, Derris, Glen Echo Group, Inkhouse, M18, Message Lab, Onward and Small Girls PR. It also launched Brightmode, a talent acquisition firm for communications professionals, and Versus Media Group, a strategy-first political media team. Learn more at www.orchestraco.com. People of all backgrounds and abilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Orchestra is committed to building and maintaining a diverse staff, and recognizes that its continued success depends on hiring and retaining high-quality creative professionals with a variety of backgrounds and experiences. Opportunities for advancement exist, and we are committed to helping all staff develop and grow. ABOUT THIS ROLE We’re seeking a Director, Influencer Marketing to lead innovative campaigns that connect brands with culture across politics, sports, fashion, wellness, tech, and more. You’ll oversee everything from influencer casting and negotiation to campaign strategy and reporting, ensuring authentic partnerships that drive measurable impact. In this role, you’ll collaborate with PR and integrated teams to shape storytelling that bridges online engagement with real-world action. You’ll bring deep knowledge of platforms, advocacy strategies, and trends to keep Orchestra ahead of the curve. If you’re a strategic, creative leader who thrives on building relationships and delivering results, this role is for you. Role location: This role is based in our New York, N.Y. or Washington, D.C. office on a hybrid basis. The Impact team is in-office at least 3 days per week. ACCOUNTABILITIES AND QUALIFICATIONS As the Director, Influencer Marketing you will… Ideate, build, and execute multi-faceted influencer campaigns (from one-off activations to long-term relationship-based programs) across industries from politics, sports, tech, real estate, health to fashion, beauty, wellness, lifestyle and more Develop client-facing strategies and social media reports on campaign and influencer performance. Present results and optimize future campaigns based on insights Collaborate with PR and integrated teams to create influencer strategies aligned with brand messaging and campaign storytelling across channels Connect online and offline efforts, leveraging digital campaigns to drive real-world action. Strong understanding of the interplay between brand, media, and audience Oversee influencer casting, negotiation, contracting, and content management. Deliver top-tier client service through clear communication, data-driven recommendations, and proactive relationship management Stay ahead of emerging platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Discord, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Snapchat, etc.), technologies, influencers, and trends Foster positive relationships between clients, influencers, and consumers Build and maintain strong influencer partnerships to create authentic, engaging branded content. Manage outreach, budgets, and negotiations Support new business development by fielding calls, drafting scopes of work, and contributing to proposals Act as agency liaison with major social platforms, digital influencers, and partner agencies Essential skills: 5-7 years of relevant experience in influencer marketing, social media and/or PR with a demonstrated track record of success Demonstrated ability to think through communication strategies and deliver tangible results Understanding of the current social / digital as well as activation landscape and the unique advocacy strategies across platforms Deep knowledge of emerging trends and talent, with a finger on the pulse of what is relevant in our culture and societies today Expertise in both organic and paid advocacy strategies Ability to be detail-oriented, manage multiple clients and meet deadlines while also keeping the bigger picture in mind Experience with daily management of junior level staff members as well as management up to senior executive Capable of working both independently and in a dynamic, high energy, team-oriented atmosphere, being a proactive problem-solver yet elevating concerns when you have them Comfortable working across industries with an ability to connect the dots between their similarities Desire to constantly innovate and test new things, not just follow a pre-established playbook Preferred skills: Experience working in a political or advocacy environment WORKING AT ORCHESTRA Salary range (commensurate with experience and skills): $110,000-$130,000 #LI-Hybrid #LI-BM1 Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Manager, Policy, Research and Analysis
item.description: Manager, Policy, Research and Analysis Organization: Pew Charitable Trusts Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Please note: The application deadline is 5:00pm Eastern time on Wednesday, September 30th. Manager, Policy, Research & Analysis, Substance Use Prevention and Treatment Initiative The Government Performance Portfolio within Program Pew’s Government Performance team provides the nonpartisan research, solutions, and momentum decisionmakers need to ensure our institutions improve the health of people in the United States and enable them to successfully climb the economic ladder. Those goals are pursued through a wide range of the portfolio’s policy-focused projects (with explorations into new areas underway)—from ensuring states’ finances are prepared for future volatility, to unlocking gateways to mental health care, to addressing the nation’s lack of attainable housing. Pew’s Government Performance team is successful when we: Foresee systemic challenges that could be avoided, mitigated, or resolved before they become insurmountable or politically toxic. Fill information gaps with data, research, and proven models. Hold leaders of institutions accountable to ensure they anticipate future challenges and operate efficiently. Minimize missed opportunities when people intersect with our nation’s institutions. We hope policymakers, funding partners, and other stakeholders celebrate when Pew’s Government Performance team enters a new policy space, launches a new effort, or expands an existing project because they recognize we help: Elevate the public profile of a problem Demonstrate that success is possible Bring cohesion to siloed fields Create momentum for broader and lasting change Substance Use Prevention and Treatment Initiative (SUPTI) The substance use prevention and treatment initiative works to develop and support policies that increase initiation of medications for opioid use disorder. The project provides direct, in-depth technical assistance by invitation of states interested in improving access to evidence-based, high-quality treatment for people with opioid use disorder. The project also conducts advocacy in Washington, D.C., to achieve its programmatic objectives. To inform this work, the project conducts and publishes research and other information on evidence-based and emerging practices and maintains relationships with external experts and other stakeholders. The team comes from a wide variety of professional backgrounds with policy, advocacy, and research experience. Position Overview The Manager, Policy, Research & Analysis, Substance Use Prevention and Treatment Initiative, will inform and influence public policy and health quality by conducting research and analysis and providing technical expertise to achieve the goals of the substance use prevention and treatment initiative. The responsibilities for this position include managing direct reports, executing project objectives and deliverables, developing and executing detailed research projects, leading the development of Pew-branded and peer-reviewed publications, and generating analyses and resources to support state and federal policy efforts. The Manager works closely with other SUPTI team members, as well as Pew colleagues in Communications, Research Quality and Support, Government Relations, Human Resources, and other operations areas. The position, based in Pew’s Washington, D.C. office, reports to the Project Director, Substance Use Prevention and Treatment Initiative. The position has a set time frame that could be extended based on the success of the program, funding sources, and board decisions on continued support. This position participates in Pew’s hybrid work program with core days in the office and the flexibility to telework the remaining days. Staff also enjoy four telework “flex weeks” per year. Responsibilities Foster a work environment that inspires excellence, values impact, encourages transparency, builds mutual trust and respect, embraces and values diversity, and is collaborative, caring and compassionate. Manage the day-to-day execution of SUPTI’s research objectives and milestones. Develop a research strategy to advance state policy objectives for medications for opioid use disorder in collaboration with the state team’s senior manager and managers. Manage and oversee the daily operations of a team responsible for policy research and analysis (PRA), and project coordination, including PRA meetings and budget. Collaborate with the project director and senior manager to develop and track project metrics. Collaborate with external partners on research and policy initiatives, including developing and overseeing contracts, while building and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders across the substance use research and policy community. Advise the project director and behavioral health director in achieving the project’s strategic direction and campaign strategy and future behavioral health initiatives at Pew. Manage the development of background research and analysis and other written products, including supervising staff, reviewing and editing documents, and ensuring alignment with project strategy. Serve as the primary reviewer on the project’s research publications, collaborating with Pew’s communication department to increase dissemination of completed publications, including to state and federal policymakers. Liaise with internal partners, including communications and research quality and support to ensure publications follow established procedures and adhere to rigorous quality standards, and to identify efficiencies. Serve as the team subject matter expert on research process and ensure compliance with the organization’s research standards. Maintain a broad knowledge of substance use policy and keep abreast of evolving research on methadone, opioid treatment, and harm reduction interventions; develop deep expertise and serve as a resource to project staff on priority topics, including the project’s measurement-related goals. Present on project research topics to internal and external audiences. Attend and represent the initiative at conferences, convenings and serve as spokesperson to media. Lead special assignments, including convening meetings and stakeholder communications, as needed, and contribute to and participate in tasks of the project and department as assigned, as well as broader Pew-wide projects and committees as needed. Requirements Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required. Advanced degree in public health, public policy, social work, economics, law or similar fields are preferred. Generally, a minimum of eight years of applicable research and policy work in public health or behavioral health fields. Prior experience directly supervising staff, including managing performance, conducting evaluations, and providing coaching, guidance and career development advice support. Prior to commencing employment with Pew, candidates for this position who were registered to lobby in any jurisdiction must certify termination of previous registration(s) and provide copies of termination notices with said jurisdiction(s) to Pew. Effectively focuses on the key aspect of an issue, as well as to identify, understand, and synthesize different policy perspectives. Demonstrated time-management skills, including the experience thinking strategically, juggling multiple priorities, adjusting to changing circumstances, resolving problems creatively and logically, organizing time efficiently, and remaining attentive to details. Develops and manages productive relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders and partners. Works professionally and collegially within a creative, fast-paced corporate culture that emphasizes excellence and teamwork. Key attributes and preferred experience Demonstrated experience in analyzing and presenting complex information, including experience writing clearly and cogently for internal audiences, policymakers, the media, and the public is required. Demonstrated experience conducting health policy research and analysis, including using qualitative and quantitative methods and software such as NVivo, R, SAS is required. Demonstrated experience developing and writing research and policy products that synthesize large amounts of information with identified themes is required. Expertise in behavioral health research and policy. Communicates effectively with diverse audiences, including stakeholders, policymakers, legislators, and people with lived experience. Travel Occasional overnight travel as required for state engagements, meetings, and conferences. Work Authorization Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country for which they are seeking employment without visa sponsorship. Salary Range United States Pay Range: $137,800 – $154,000 The salary range represents a reasonable estimate of the annual salary based on Pew’s commitment to provide equitable and market-competitive pay. The actual salary offered will take into consideration many factors including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills and experience, internal pay equity, and business need. Total Rewards We offer a competitive salary and benefit program, including: comprehensive, affordable health care through medical, dental, and vision coverage; financial security with life and disability insurance; opportunities to save using health savings and flexible spending accounts; retirement benefits to help prepare for the future; and work/life benefits to maintain a good balance. Pew is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, or any other protected characteristics. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Program Influence (Communications & Advocacy), USPP
item.description: Director, Program Influence (Communications & Advocacy), USPP Organization: The Rockefeller Foundation Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Salary Range: $175,000.00 To $210,000.00 Annually Position Overview The Program Influence team helps advance The Rockefeller Foundation’s programmatic “Big Bets” and strategic priorities by using communications, policy, and advocacy as tools for influence — translating program strategy and evidence into public narrative, policy engagement, and stakeholder mobilization that strengthen the Foundation’s institutional narrative. The Director, Program Influence (Communications & Advocacy), US Program and Policy (USPP) spends roughly 85% of their time on US Program priorities and 15% on cross-program and institutional work. The U.S. Program and Policy team advances the mission of The Rockefeller Foundation (RF) by partnering with communities, policymakers, employers, and other stakeholders to expand economic opportunity and improve outcomes for people across the United States. Reporting to the SVP, Program Integration, with secondary reporting lines to the SVP, US Program and Policy and SVP, Strategic Communications, the Director, Program Influence (Communications & Advocacy) operates as a hands-on individual contributor, delivering results through close partnership with program leadership, fellow Program Influencers, and institutional colleagues in Communications. Work Schedule: This role follows a hybrid schedule and is required to be in the New York City office Monday through Thursday. Pay Range: $175,000 – $210,000. This represents the present low and high end of the Foundation’s pay range for this position. Actual pay will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to experience. Principal Duties and Responsibilities Develop and execute an evidence-based program influence strategy — identifying priority audiences and building outreach and engagement plans that advance program objectives, expand media engagement, and deepen public, private, and philanthropic investor interest. Partner with program leads to surface proof points and impact stories, and pipeline them to Communications and Policy on a standing cadence so the institutional narrative stays credible, current, and grounded in programmatic impact. Craft a unifying external narrative for the program that amplifies its impact and builds on the Foundation’s institutional message architecture, which the Communications team manages, translating complex program work into persuasive messaging for policymakers, partners, and philanthropic audiences. Lead the identification and execution of strategic convenings and tent-pole moments, and represent the Foundation and its leadership at regional, global, and multilateral events. Advance the program’s ideas, solutions, and partnerships by working through institutional channels — Communications, Policy & Advocacy, Connected Leaders, and the media accelerator — rather than building parallel capacity, coordinating closely with fellow Program Influence colleagues so strategies are built together rather than in isolation. Partner with the Communications team to develop the program’s annual channel and content plan — priorities, formats, and platforms — and execute against it. Use audience insight and analytics to track reach, recognition, and influence, and refine the plan with Communications accordingly. Work within institutional editorial standards, message architecture, prioritization, voice, and visual identity across all program content and channels. Help shape where USPP’s evidence base can be most persuasive with policymakers, and work with regional teams to monitor policy risk and validate impact claims before they are used externally. Serve as a thought partner to program leadership on narrative positioning, and contribute to cross-Foundation learning on storytelling, audience engagement, and influence. Oversee a project management system tracking milestones and deliverables, contribute to Board-level materials as needed, and select and manage grantees, consultants, and vendors. Support colleagues on other programs and institutional projects as assigned, deliver against annual goals covering both the program’s Big Bet objectives and the coherence of its narrative with the institutional story, set jointly with Program Strategy and Communications, and participate in the weekly institutional communications meeting, applying the Foundation’s communications playbook to decisions about what the Foundation says publicly. Education, Experience, and Skills Generally expected to have 10+ years of strategic communications, policy, and advocacy experience Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field. Strong understanding of U.S. economic opportunity and workforce development and preferable experience working with domestic policymakers. Ability to manage multiple workstreams and stakeholders in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Exceptional stakeholder engagement and coalition-building skills; comfortable working with senior leaders and external partners. Experience managing complex initiatives, with multiple vendors and stakeholders. Ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling stories and narratives, with strong command of the new media environment (social, podcasts, creator and influencer channels, and emerging digital platforms). Proven exceptional writing, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, and professional presence. Skilled in media relations, digital strategy, and content creation. Experience in handling sensitive information, including crisis management. At ease navigating among nonprofit, government, and corporate sectors both domestically and globally. Self-motivated, creative, and entrepreneurial, with a strong work ethic. Experience designing and leading high-profile convenings and events, and representing an organization at external forums Competencies Action Oriented: Takes on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm. Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives. Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high-quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. Nimble Learning: Learns through experimentation when tackling new problems, using both successes and failures as learning fodder. Strategic Mindset: Sees ahead to future possibilities and translates them into breakthrough strategies. Develops Talent: Develops people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals. About The Rockefeller Foundation The Rockefeller Foundation is a pioneering philanthropy built on collaborative partnerships at the frontiers of science, technology, and innovation that enable individuals, families, and communities to flourish. We make big bets to promote the well-being of humanity in food, health, energy, and finance, including through our public charity, RF Catalytic Capital (RFCC). For more information, sign up for our newsletter at www.rockefellerfoundation.org/subscribe and follow us on X @RockefellerFdn and LinkedIn @the-rockefeller-foundation . The Rockefeller Foundation offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes health insurance programs, tuition reimbursement and student loan repayment, a generous 401K, parental leave, and various forms of paid time off, all to help our employees feel energized, cared for, and engaged. As an organization, we focus on six values to advance our culture and continue our success. We are dedicated to being Transparent, Optimistic, Accountable, Collaborative, Trusted, and Equitable. item.title: Associate Director, Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Associate Director, Federal Government Affairs Organization: Takeda Pharmaceuticals Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Job Description About the role: The Associate Director, Federal Government Affairs (FGA) will contribute to Takeda’s advocacy efforts and help execute strategies aligned with legislative and executive branch priorities. As a key internal expert on the external environment, this role will provide strategic insights identifying threats and opportunities related to commercial, clinical, and operational practices. You will collaborate with internal teams and external stakeholders to advance good policy and mitigate against harmful ones, ensuring alignment with Takeda’s business objectives. This individual will be responsible for building a variety of strong, meaningful networks and staying current on critical policy issues will facilitate readiness to deliver on Takeda’s mission and values. This is a hybrid role located in Washington, D.C. How you will contribute: Support the development and implementation of strategies and tactical plans to influence Congress, the White House, and related agencies concerning Takeda priorities. Assist in building professional networks with elected leaders and key stakeholders to promote access to innovative bio-pharmaceuticals and Takeda’s presence as a leading pharmaceutical company. Collaborate on external meetings and advocacy efforts that strengthen Takeda’s federal relationships. Provide input into lobbying efforts with Members of Congress, executive branch officials, and federal agencies including executive engagement. Contribute to cross-functional teams to help identify risks and opportunities for Takeda commercial, clinical, and operational practices. Provide insights and recommendations on federal legislative, executive, and regulatory activities impacting Takeda to support leadership decisions. Monitor and report on legislative opportunities that align with business goals and recommend advocacy strategies to influence legislation and agency actions. Represent Takeda in relevant PhRMA work groups and trade associations to advance shared advocacy objectives. Collaborate with Takeda teams, including State Government Affairs, Public Policy & Reimbursement, and Operations, to ensure alignment of strategic activities. Manage external consultants on specific initiatives under senior leader direction. Enhance Takeda’s visibility in Washington, D.C., by supporting branding initiatives and policy advocacy efforts. Minimum Requirements/Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required. 7+ years’ experience working directly in an advocacy and policy-related field required. Talented networking skills and competent understanding of stakeholder dynamics affecting government policy. Strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize and adapt actions based on a fluid macroenvironment. Proven track record in developing and influencing practical and implementable policy solutions. Strong writing skills; a writing sample will be required. Experience in project management and directing the work of external consultants and stakeholders. Ability to collaborate effectively across cultures and functions. Demonstrated leadership skills, both with and without formal authority. Travel Requirements: Willing to travel in the US up to 15%; minimal overseas travel if applicable More about us At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best in class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that will inspire and empower you to grow through life-changing work. Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace, in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to deliver Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world. This position is currently classified as “hybrid” in accordance with Takeda’s Hybrid and Remote Work policy. Takeda Compensation and Benefits Summary We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. We are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. For Location: Washington DC, USA U.S. Base Salary Range: $154,400.00 – $242,550.00 The estimated salary range reflects an anticipated range for this position. The actual base salary offered may depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. The actual base salary offered will be in accordance with state or local minimum wage requirements for the job location. EEO Statement Takeda is proud in its commitment to creating a diverse workforce and providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, parental status, national origin, age, disability, citizenship status, genetic information or characteristics, marital status, status as a Vietnam era veteran, special disabled veteran, or other protected veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws, and any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Associate Director, Global Financial Crimes Sanctions Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation
item.description: Associate Director, Global Financial Crimes Sanctions Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation Organization: S&P Global Location: New York, NY | Englewood, CO | Washington, DC | Miami, FL | Chicago, IL | Dallas, TX | Houston, TX Date Posted: 09/15/2026 Job Description About the Role: Grade Level (for internal use): 11 The Role: Associate Director, Global Financial Crimes Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation The Team: The Associate Director, Global Financial Crimes Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation will directly report to and work with the Director, Global Financial Crimes Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation. The Impact: The Associate Director, Global Financial Crimes Compliance Enterprise Threat Mitigation plays a critical role in safeguarding S&P Global by supporting the centralized review, investigation, escalation, and disposition of transaction screening and third-party screening alerts. The role is responsible for helping ensure that potential sanctions, AML, anti-bribery and corruption, and due diligence risks involving clients, vendors, event attendees, and other third parties are identified, assessed, and mitigated through timely, well-documented, and risk-based decision-making. This role requires a combination of sanctions and financial crimes compliance expertise, technical knowledge of screening systems and workflows, strong analytical judgment, and a practical understanding of S&P Global’s businesses. The Associate Director will work closely with Compliance, Legal, Technology, Operations, and business stakeholders across regions to enhance screening effectiveness, improve alert management processes, and support a globally consistent approach to financial crimes risk mitigation. Responsibilities: Serve as a senior point of escalation for transaction screening alerts involving clients, vendors, event attendees, third parties, and other relevant counterparties, applying sanctions, AML, anti-bribery and corruption, and due diligence expertise to resolve complex or high-risk cases. Oversee the review and disposition of screening alerts generated through automated and manual screening processes, ensuring decisions are well-documented, risk-based, and aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and internal standards. Evaluate potential sanctions, AML, PEP, adverse media, and other financial crimes risks identified through transaction and third-party screening activity, including the review of name matches, ownership/control considerations, geographic exposure, and risk indicators. Support the optimization of transaction screening controls, rules, and escalation criteria to improve the effectiveness of alert generation, reduce false positives, and ensure screening logic remains responsive to evolving regulatory expectations and financial crime typologies. Conduct Second Line of Defense reviews of transaction screening frameworks and operating models to identify potential control gaps, process inefficiencies, or areas of compliance vulnerability, and escalate findings as appropriate. Review and enhance policies, procedures, and guidance related to transaction screening and financial crimes compliance to help protect S&P Global and ensure adherence with relevant sanctions, AML, anti-bribery and corruption, and third-party risk requirements. Partner with technology, data, operations, legal, and business stakeholders to support enhancements to screening systems, data quality, workflow design, alert documentation, and case management processes. Monitor emerging sanctions, AML, and financial crimes risks that may impact S&P Global’s products, services, clients, vendors, event attendees, and other third-party relationships, and assess implications for screening practices. Track and analyze transaction screening trends and performance metrics, including alert volumes, escalation patterns, resolution timelines, match quality, and recurring risk themes, to support program oversight and continuous improvement. Deliver targeted training to analysts and relevant stakeholders on transaction screening requirements, escalation standards, sanctions and AML risk indicators, documentation expectations, and complex screening scenarios. Participate in Global Financial Crimes Compliance governance bodies and working groups, providing subject matter expertise on transaction screening risks, control effectiveness, operational challenges, and remediation efforts. Support Second Line of Defense management of audits and regulatory examinations related to transaction screening, including preparation of materials, review of evidence, explanation of screening processes, and support for remediation activities. Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates) S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,909 to $150,000 USD. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here . What We’re Looking For: Basic Required Qualifications: 7+ years of Compliance experience in Financial Services or a Brokerage Firm, with demonstrated experience operating within a financial crimes compliance, sanctions, AML, or enterprise risk management function. 5+ years of demonstrated Sanctions and Transaction Screening experience, including experience reviewing, investigating, and resolving screening alerts involving clients, vendors, counterparties, transactions, third parties, or other relevant entities. Strong understanding of sanctions laws, regulations, and screening expectations, including experience assessing potential matches, false positives, ownership and control considerations, geographic risk, and escalation requirements. Familiarity with broader Financial Crimes Compliance areas, including AML, anti-bribery and corruption, customer and third-party due diligence, adverse media, monitoring, tracking, and advising on compliance issues. Experience with Financial Crimes Compliance systems and tools, including screening platforms, case management systems, workflow tools, and reporting or analytics used to monitor alert volumes, trends, and escalation activity. Experience working in a team-oriented, collaborative environment, with the ability to partner effectively with Compliance, Legal, Technology, Operations, and business stakeholders. Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to clearly document alert decisions, explain complex regulatory issues, provide practical guidance, and present to stakeholders or governance forums. Self-motivated, organized, and able to work well under pressure, with the ability to prioritize competing tasks, manage high-volume alert activity, and support time-sensitive escalations. Forward-thinking approach to technology and automation, with proven experience using AI, automation, data analytics, or modern workflow tools to reduce manual effort, improve screening accuracy, enhance audit trails, and streamline compliance operations. Additional Preferred Qualifications: ICA, ACAMS, ACSCA or other industry related sanctions certification preferred Right to Work Requirements: This role is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States. Return to Work: Have you taken time out for caring responsibilities and are now looking to return to work? As part of our Return to Work initiative, Restart, we are encouraging enthusiastic and talented returners to apply, and will actively support your return to the workplace. About S&P Global Market Intelligence At S&P Global Market Intelligence, a division of S&P Global we understand the importance of accurate, deep and insightful information. Our team of experts delivers unrivaled insights and leading data and technology solutions, partnering with customers to expand their perspective, operate with confidence, and make decisions with conviction. For more information, visit www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence . What’s In It For You? Our Mission: Advancing Essential Intelligence. Our People: We’re more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we’re able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all. From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference. Our Values: Integrity, Discovery, Partnership Throughout our history, the world’s leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. We start with a foundation of integrity in all we do, bring a spirit of discovery to our work, and collaborate in close partnership with each other and our customers to achieve shared goals. Benefits: We take care of you, so you can take care of business. We care about our people. That’s why we provide everything you—and your career—need to thrive at S&P Global. Our benefits include: Health & Wellness: Health care coverage designed for the mind and body. Flexible Downtime: Generous time off helps keep you energized for your time on. Continuous Learning: Access a wealth of resources to grow your career and learn valuable new skills. Invest in Your Future: Secure your financial future through competitive

item.title: Senior Counsel -US Rare Tumors
item.description: Senior Counsel -US Rare Tumors Organization: Merck & Co., Inc. Location: Boston, MA Date Posted: 09/16/2026 Work Your Magic with Us! Start Your Next Chapter and Join EMD Serono Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans, and so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives through our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our diverse mix of people, customers, patients, and the planet. That’s why we are always looking for curious minds who see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us. United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve, and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices, and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology, and Fertility. Our teams work together across six continents with passion and relentless curiosity to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team means becoming part of a diverse, inclusive, and flexible working culture that offers excellent opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe. This role does not offer sponsorship for work authorization. External applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. Your Role The Senior Counsel, Rare Tumors will provide comprehensive legal support to a Therapeutic Area, including both Commercial and Medical functions. Specifically, this role will be part of the legal team supporting Rare Tumors, one of EMD Serono’s key Therapeutic Areas, and will report to an Associate General Counsel. The role requires a deep understanding of healthcare laws and regulations applicable to pharmaceutical commercialization, including: Anti-Kickback Statute False Claims Act FDA promotional regulations OIG guidance Laws governing patient support and affordability programs The ideal candidate will be a proactive, collaborative legal partner who enables business goals while ensuring compliance with ethical standards. Key Responsibilities Primary Legal Counsel: Serve as lead attorney for a key brand within the Rare Tumors Therapeutic Area, including: Review of marketing and promotional materials Advice regarding Marketing and Sales Operations Review of scientific (non-promotional) materials Advice regarding Medical Affairs and Medical Operations Management of outside counsel when specialized advice is required for Therapeutic Area projects Collaboration with paralegals Compliance & Regulatory Oversight: Ensure all activities comply with FDA, OIG, CMS, and state requirements, as well as company policies and industry codes, including the PhRMA Code. Contracting & Negotiations: Draft, review, and negotiate agreements with advertising agencies, consultants, call centers, and Therapeutic Area-specific distributors. Support contracting with healthcare professionals, including advisory boards and consulting arrangements. Training & Education: Deliver legal training on applicable healthcare laws and company compliance requirements. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Commercial, Compliance, Medical Affairs, and Regulatory teams to align business practices with legal standards. Collaborate with U.S. and global colleagues to ensure business strategies and objectives comply with applicable laws, regulations, and policies. Risk Management: Proactively identify, assess, and communicate potential legal risks. Manage risks through counseling, training, and the practical application of legal and regulatory requirements, company policies, and procedures across Therapeutic Area operations. Who You Are Minimum Qualifications Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited U.S. law school Active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction 7 to 10 years of legal experience in a law firm and/or in-house legal department Strong ability to interpret and apply laws, regulations, and guidance in a practical, business-oriented manner Excellent communication, drafting, and negotiation skills Proven ability to work collaboratively across multiple functions in a dynamic, fast-paced environment Preferred Qualifications Prior in-house experience at a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company Demonstrated expertise in healthcare fraud and abuse laws, FDA regulatory matters, and patient support program compliance Experience supporting commercial business units, including contracting and the development of commercial strategies Experience participating in or advising MLR/Promotional Review Committees Background in compliance counseling or interaction with government agencies, including OIG, DOJ, and FDA Competencies Strategic thinker with strong business acumen Excellent judgment and risk-based decision-making skills Collaborative, practical, and solutions-oriented approach Ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders effectively Commitment to ethics, compliance, and patient-centered values Compensation Pay Range: $188,600 – $283,000 The offer range represents the anticipated low and high end of the base pay compensation for this position. Actual compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, experience, education, skills, and other job-related considerations. This position may also be eligible for sales-based or performance-based bonus opportunities. Benefits offered by the Company include: Health insurance Paid time off (PTO) Retirement contributions Additional employee benefits and perquisites For more information about benefits, visit: https://careers.emdgroup.com/us/en/benefits What We Offer We are curious minds from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe this diversity drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for everyone to develop and grow at their own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress.
