item.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
item.description: President and Chief Executive Officer Organization: MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger Location: Los Angeles, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/17/2026 President and Chief Executive Officer MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger Los Angeles, California, or Washington, D.C. MAZON: A Jewish Response to Hunger (MAZON) seeks a President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization into its next chapter. For more than forty years, MAZON has advanced systemic solutions to hunger through public policy, strategic investment, and community engagement. In the United States, MAZON advances systemic change through policy advocacy, strategic grantmaking, legal advocacy, public education, research, and community engagement. In Israel, MAZON supports partner organizations working to advance food security through advocacy, coalition building, public education, research, grantmaking, and policy reform. Today, the organization enters this transition with a strong reputation, financial stability, an accomplished staff, a dedicated board, and deep credibility within the anti-hunger, policy, philanthropic, and Jewish communal sectors. The next CEO will assume leadership at a pivotal moment for both MAZON and the broader anti-hunger movement. Programs that protect people from hunger are under extraordinary pressure. The federal policy landscape has become more challenging, states are playing an increasingly important role, and long-standing assumptions about bipartisan support for nutrition assistance can no longer be taken for granted. At the same time, many in the Jewish community are seeking meaningful ways to translate Jewish values into action. Under the leadership of outgoing CEO Abby J. Leibman, MAZON has evolved into a sophisticated national advocacy organization with a strong presence in Washington, D.C., growing engagement in selected states, and deep relationships across the anti-hunger and Jewish communal sectors. The organization also supports a network of advocates across 19 states and Puerto Rico. The next CEO will inherit a highly capable organization with significant expertise and momentum and will help determine where MAZON can have its greatest influence and impact in the years ahead. The successful leader will bring strategic judgment, strong relationship-building skills, and the ability to lead through complexity and change. They will understand how organizations drive change through advocacy, coalition building, and public policy and will be excited to lead one of the nation’s most respected anti-hunger advocacy organizations. Direct experience in hunger policy is welcome but not required, given the substantial expertise already within the organization. More important is the ability to harness MAZON’s strengths, deepen relationships across the Jewish community and beyond, expand philanthropic support, and build on MAZON’s legacy as one of the nation’s leading advocates for ending hunger. The CEO must live and work in, or be willing to relocate to, either the Los Angeles or Washington, D.C., metropolitan area. Los Angeles is MAZON’s headquarters and home to much of its senior leadership, while Washington, D.C., is central to the organization’s policy and advocacy work. Regardless of home base, the CEO will maintain a meaningful presence in both locations and will travel regularly for Board meetings, policy engagement, fundraising, conferences, and meetings with partners and donors. MAZON anticipates a salary range of $275,000 to $315,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications, along with a competitive benefits package. Isaacson, Miller is assisting in this search. Screening applications is ongoing. Submit inquiries, nominations, and applications (resume/CV and letter of interest) via the Isaacson, Miller website . For reasonable accommodations, contact Harley Bartles at [email protected] . MAZON is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer committed to diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all qualified individuals, including people of color, people with disabilities, people of all gender identities, people of all races and national origins, veterans, and LGBTQIA+ individuals. We strive for a diverse workforce, and we acknowledge that our diversity also comes from our experiences and perspectives. We want all staff and team members to be treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to ensuring that you can carry out your assigned mission in an environment that is free from discrimination and harassment. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Strategic Communications Manager
item.description: Strategic Communications Manager Organization: Crosscut Strategies Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Strategic Communications Manager Crosscut Strategies, a Washington, DC-based strategic communications firm working primarily with high-growth startups in technology, health care, and other sectors, is seeking a Strategic Communications Manager to join our team. The Strategic Communications Manager will be responsible for overseeing client projects and initiatives, playing a critical role in managing our accounts, working directly with clients, and helping to execute our communications strategies, including writing, media relations, and social media. About the Role A Strategic Communications Manager is the deputy on Crosscut account teams. You will work closely with a senior team member as a thought partner and implementer. You need to be inquisitive, motivated, creative, and nimble, and be able to write well under tight deadlines. You must be equally comfortable offering strategic counsel to senior client decision-makers as you are rolling up your sleeves to get a job done. A key part of this role is managing the entire team’s workflow, from making assignments to ensuring deadlines are met, as well as editing junior team members’ work. Being organized and having strong attention to detail is essential. The ideal candidate will have at least five years of relevant experience in strategic communications, either at a firm or in-house. Skills and Qualifications At least 5 years of relevant communications experience. Experience in management role(s) in communications or a directly related field. Excellent writing and editing skills. The ability to write quickly and effectively is critical. Ability to identify media opportunities for clients. Proven experience pitching to reporters and developing media relationships, including on-the-record experience. Ability to efficiently research issues, policy developments, and media coverage of targeted topics, and distill findings into clear, concise memos and reports for clients. Experience managing complex assignments and working with clients or other senior-level stakeholders. Experience managing junior staff and leading colleagues toward achieving goals. Knowledge of and experience with federal and/or state policymaking processes. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Bachelor’s degree. Advanced proficiency with standard business software. Experience with digital media, including graphic design, video creation, social media content and strategy, digital marketing, online campaigning, or a related field preferred. Experience with Agentic AI preferred. Strong familiarity with and/or interest in health care and technology preferred. Crosscut operates as a hybrid workplace with an office in the heart of the Dupont Circle/Farragut North area, offering easy access to Metro, bus lines, and bikeshare options. While employees are not required to be in the office every day, the team works together on designated in-office days. Employees must live within the DC metropolitan area to be available for in-person meetings and collaboration. Compensation and Benefits The annual base salary range for the Manager position is $80,000 to $100,000, along with a comprehensive benefits package, a great team, and a working environment committed to fostering staff growth and leadership. Employee benefits include: Employer-matched 401(k) plan with immediate vesting Medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and eligible dependents Paid time off Sick leave Paid parental leave How to Apply Interested candidates should send a cover email and resume to: [email protected] Equal Opportunity Employer Crosscut Strategies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: Manager, Political Affairs
item.description: Manager, Political Affairs Organization: Finseca Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Manager, Political Affairs Classification: Exempt Reports to: Senior Vice President, Federal and Political Affairs Job Summary Finseca is looking for a political engagement professional to be part of the team that runs our political programs. This role works directly with members on PAC and candidate fundraising, member education, and grassroots and grasstops activation. You’ll own a large advocate portfolio, carrying individual and event fundraising goals, coordinating legislative meetings, and recruiting members and developing them into high-quality political advocates. You’ll plan and execute our political trainings and annual fly-in. Duties & Responsibilities Execute Finseca’s Ambassador Program and political advocacy strategy for Finseca’s growing membership. The Ambassador Program is Finseca’s political engagement program designed to build grasstops relationships between our members and policymakers. Core program responsibilities are: Plan and execute fundraising events, owning event-level goals and conducting individual fundraising outreach. Work with external partners to organize meetings between Ambassadors and policymakers. Recruit and develop new Finseca Ambassadors and donors. Develop strategies to expand member engagement and advocacy activity. Manage day-to-day operations of Finseca’s PAC, including: Process and track disbursements, coordinating with the SVP on candidate contribution decisions and maintaining the disbursement calendar against budget. Manage receipts and contributor records, ensuring activity complies with FEC regulations and Finseca’s PAC policies. Coordinate with outside counsel on FEC filings and reconciliation. Maintain criteria and documentation for contribution decisions, and report on PAC performance against fundraising and disbursement goals. Design and deliver political trainings for members, and manage planning and on-site execution of Finseca’s annual fly-in. Work across the Association to raise member awareness of Finseca’s political programs through membership communications, website materials, and Finseca meetings and events. Track legislative developments affecting the financial security profession and the broader political environment. Support the federal and state teams on legislative and policy strategy and engagement. Communicate political and legislative updates to members. Maintain the database as the system of record for all political activity, ensuring records are accurate, timely, and complete. Draft and deploy grassroots activations, donor drives, and other membership-wide initiatives. Represent Finseca at political fundraising events and candidate meetings. Perform other duties as required. Skills & Experience 4–6 years of experience in political operations, political or PAC fundraising, or a campaign setting. Strong political fundraising background, including event management, individual solicitation of both major and small-dollar contributions, and donor stewardship. Demonstrated ability to build relationships with members, policymakers, and other key stakeholders. Experience planning advocacy events in Washington, DC, and in districts and states throughout the year, while managing an ongoing engagement strategy. Working knowledge of FEC rules and PAC compliance. Excellent verbal and written communication skills; comfortable with public speaking. Sound independent judgment, strong attention to detail, and a high degree of organization. Experience with Quorum, BGOV, or comparable CRM and advocacy platforms is a plus. Education College degree required. Work Environment This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Physical Demands The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, or sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; talk or hear; taste or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move objects up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Position Type / Expected Hours of Work This is a full-time, exempt position. Travel Some travel is expected for this position. Compensation and Benefits Pay Range: $80,000-$90,000 (depending on skills and relevant experience) This is a full-time, exempt position. Salary is commensurate with experience. We offer a generous benefits package including: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Health Savings Account (HSA) 401(k) plan with an organizational match of up to 5% of annual salary Generous paid time off Eleven paid holidays per year Additional benefits and employee programs We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome new and diverse people who can strengthen our team. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion In principle and in practice, Finseca values and seeks diversity and inclusion practices within our organization. We celebrate multiple approaches and points of view. We believe diversity drives innovation. We are building a culture where we maximize engagement and create access to leadership opportunities across different groups that include, but are not limited to, age, disability, ethnicity, gender, nationality, race, religion, and sexual orientation. More importantly, we are establishing an environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work by driving creativity and success. To Apply: Please email your resume and a brief cover note to [email protected] with the subject line “Manager, Political Affairs – [Your Last Name].” In your note, please include: Your years of experience in political fundraising, PAC operations, or a campaign setting Any experience with FEC compliance or PAC administration Any experience planning fundraising events or advocacy fly-ins Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. item.title: Senior Legislative Representative/Counsel, Toxics
item.description: Senior Legislative Representative/Counsel, Toxics Organization: Earthjustice Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Earthjustice is the premier nonprofit environmental law organization. We take on the biggest, most precedent-setting cases across the country. We wield the power of law and the strength of partnership to protect people’s health, preserve magnificent places and wildlife, advance clean energy, and combat climate change. We partner with thousands of groups, supporters, individuals, and communities to engage in the critical environmental issues of our time and bring about positive change. We are here because the earth needs a good lawyer. Founded in 1971, Earthjustice has a distinguished track record of achieving significant, lasting environmental protections. We achieve this by hiring people who share a passion for justice and a healthy environment. Our headquarters are in San Francisco, with offices in Anchorage, Bozeman, Chicago, Denver, Honolulu, Houston, Juneau, Los Angeles, Miami, New Orleans, New York, Philadelphia, Seattle, Tallahassee, and Washington, D.C. Earthjustice Policy & Legislation Team The Earthjustice Policy & Legislation (PAL) team is hiring a Senior Legislative Representative to provide legislative and administrative strategy development and implementation on issues related to industrial chemical pollution and regulatory toxics issues. This position will report to the Legislative Director of Healthy Communities. The position directly interfaces with relevant congressional offices, committees, and staff, executive branch offices, and other related offices and entities. This position will be hybrid from the Washington, D.C., office twice weekly. Please note: Candidates with a JD will receive the title of Senior Legislative Counsel. Responsibilities Lobby Strategy Development and Implementation (60%) Develop and implement legislative and administrative advocacy strategies relating to assigned issues. Directly lobby Congress and the Administration. Educate the Administration and Congress on key legal challenges and rulings. Serve as spokesperson for Earthjustice on assigned issues. Track legislation and policy initiatives relating to assigned issues. Work with the Legislative Director and, as warranted, internal issue-area experts to develop positions and strategies on relevant legislation and administrative actions. Work with relevant litigation staff when developing and implementing legislative and administrative advocacy strategies and positions related to practice areas. Develop lobbying and educational materials, including fact sheets, letters, action alerts, and blogs. Work with the Communications Department to develop media strategies and conduct media outreach, including creating social media content, blogs, op-eds, and other strategic communications tools on assigned issues. Perform policy, legislative, and legal analysis. Plan and implement initiatives to educate the public and foster broader public advocacy for assigned issues. Develop, maintain, and expand trusted relationships with staff of key decision-makers. Coalition and Partnerships (20-30%) Create and maintain a leadership position within the D.C. environmental community on assigned issues, as well as with regional and local environmental and social justice communities as appropriate. Represent Earthjustice in coalitions and with allies on assigned issues. Create opportunities for partners and allies to engage in education and advocacy on assigned issues and participate in strategy development where appropriate. Cultivate and expand the range of allies, thoughtful partnerships, and coalitions supporting assigned issues. Facilitate and encourage relationships between litigators and advocacy partners as appropriate. Coordinate briefings, seminars, and informational sessions with partners, as well as support partners’ traditional and social media outreach where appropriate. Plan and execute events such as fly-ins, lobby days, and similar activities. Perform other duties as assigned. Internal Coordination and Administration (15%) Represent PAL on Earthjustice working groups related to assigned issues. Liaise with the Earthjustice Legislative Director, relevant litigators, and communications staff working on assigned issues. Act as a team player, including assisting other PAL lobbyists when needed to complete actions pertaining to their assigned issues. Coordinate with other PAL lobbyists on shared legislation or cross-cutting issues. Ensure the PAL Vice President, Legislative Director, and other PAL lobbyists are aware of work that may impact them to facilitate coordination. Contribute to Earthjustice’s Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) mission through involvement in training and internal working groups. Ensure timely submission of attendance records, time accounting, and reimbursement requests. Participate in and contribute to strategy meetings regarding possible or pending litigation that may impact advocacy efforts on covered issues. Assist in efforts to cultivate diversity, equity, and inclusion within the organization and the broader environmental community. Additional Responsibilities for a Senior Legislative Representative/Counsel Manage and coordinate relationships between litigators and advocacy partners as appropriate. Assist in fundraising efforts related to assigned issue areas as requested by the Earthjustice Development Department. Supervision (5% Potential Future Supervision, Up to 10%) Supervise projects and other efforts performed on assigned issues by Earthjustice Legislative Counsels, Representatives, Associates, Assistants, Interns, or contractors. A Senior Legislative Representative/Counsel may be assigned direct supervisory responsibility for one employee. Qualifications 6+ years of experience in the legislative or federal agency advocacy process. Master’s degree or equivalent experience. Candidates with a JD will receive the title of Senior Legislative Counsel. Substantial knowledge of and experience with the administrative rulemaking process. Substantial knowledge of the legislative process at the federal level. Strong professional working relationships with relevant congressional committees, key staff of relevant federal agencies and departments, and other regulatory bodies. Familiarity with and experience in the administrative rulemaking process. Substantial knowledge of and experience with the legislative process, primarily at the federal level. Experience with U.S. environmental and/or energy laws is a plus. Proven ability to develop and implement successful legislative and administrative strategies and public education initiatives. Demonstrated leadership within the D.C. environmental community on assigned issues. Ability to manage multiple tasks, projects, and deadlines. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Proven ability to work effectively in coalitions and with allies and to grow those relationships. Significant experience working with traditional and social media. Proven ability to work independently and proactively. Demonstrated awareness and sensitivity to the needs and concerns of individuals from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and orientations. Contribute to recruiting, hiring, developing, and retaining a diverse and inclusive workforce. Compensation and Benefits We offer a mission-focused and employee-centered work environment and a competitive compensation package, including excellent benefits. Earthjustice is an equal opportunity employer and highly values diversity. As a 501(c)(3) organization, Earthjustice is a qualifying employer for purposes of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. Salary is dependent on experience and location. Senior Legislative Representative/Counsel Salary Range (Washington, D.C.) $140,000 – $155,500 To Apply Interested candidates should submit: Resume Cover Letter As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to employment practices that ensure employees and applicants for employment are provided equal opportunities without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, or any other factor not related to the position. item.title: PR and Communications Manager
item.description: PR and Communications Manager Organization: Babylist Location: Remote (NY) Date Posted: 09/17/2026 What the Role Is Babylist is looking for a hands-on PR & Communications Manager to shape how consumers, media, partners, investors, and prospective leaders understand who we are and where we’re going. You’ll create a proactive communications roadmap that positions Babylist as a category-defining family platform and modern technology company. Connecting product innovation, business growth, partnerships, leadership perspectives, and cultural moments, you’ll tell cohesive stories about how we build and why it matters to modern families. You’ll own consumer and corporate PR, develop distinctive executive points of view, and match the right leaders with high-impact opportunities across press, podcasts, and industry events. You’ll also lead an awards strategy that strengthens credibility and demonstrates Babylist’s momentum. Who You Are You’ve spent 8-10 years in PR or communications, ideally a mix of in-house and agency (or editorial) time, with enough in-house experience to know what it’s like to have real skin in the game. You’re an excellent, independent writer. You can ghostwrite a leadership LinkedIn post or a founder’s Substack essay in someone else’s voice. You think in cohesive narratives, not one-off announcements. You can connect a product launch, company milestone, executive perspective, or partnership to a larger story about where Babylist is headed. You can tell a human story as well as you can tell a tech or product story, and vice versa. You are able to get into real debates about the right angle for us and are able to see around the corner when it comes to press, PR, and communications. You’re plugged into media, ecommerce, and employer branding trends, and you know how to balance the numbers (reach, coverage quality) with what’s actually on-brand. You’re comfortable prepping senior leaders for press and standing next to them when it happens, including showroom activations, live press moments, and executive visibility work. You have real relationships across digital, print, and broadcast media, and know how to land the right placement, Forbes or New York Times caliber, not just any hit. You work East Coast hours and can travel to NYC on short notice. You don’t need to live in New York, but you need to live in the NY tri-state area, be online and available on East Coast time, and be able to travel at a moment’s notice. You’re comfortable with a lot of trust and not a lot of hand-holding. This role reports to a manager who wants to delegate real ownership. You naturally reach for AI in your work. At Babylist, every team uses AI daily. You’re already using it to move faster and improve your output, and you stay curious about what’s coming next. How You Will Make an Impact Build an integrated PR and communications roadmap across leadership, business growth, product and technology innovation, partnerships, social impact, and workplace culture. Grow consumer press coverage beyond what our agency partners currently drive. Amplify our work with celebrity, influencer, and social-impact partners, and turn moments like our past high-profile partnerships into real, sustained coverage. Build a distinctive thought leadership platform for Babylist executives through ghostwriting, media opportunities, podcasts, and relevant industry stages. Land targeted executive placements at the outlets and podcasts that actually matter to our category, not a scattershot pitch list. Manage our external PR and influencer agency partners day to day, and know when their ideas are worth running with. Own our corporate communications collateral, including team and press pages, press releases, and leadership presentations. Show up in person for press moments and showroom activations. Partner across Product, Data, Insights, Partnerships, Social Impact, and People teams to proactively identify stories and build a consistent communications pipeline. Build the internal playbooks that let the rest of the company tell our story consistently. Own Babylist’s awards strategy, using recognition and external validation as proof points for the company’s broader story. Establish clear measures of impact across awareness, credibility, quality of coverage, executive visibility, and engagement. Why This Role Babylist is on an incredible growth trajectory, and this role is critical to ensuring our story keeps pace with the business we’re becoming. You’ll shape how Babylist is understood and make sure our story reaches the right audiences in the places that matter, from consumers and media to partners, investors, and prospective leaders. This is a high-visibility role with direct access to senior executives. You’ll help develop their points of view, advise where and how they show up, and translate company priorities into compelling external narratives. We haven’t built a proactive PR function yet. You’d be the one to build it, not maintain someone else’s plan. Babylist has unmatched reach into what’s actually happening with new parents, paired with real tech-company scale. Few places let you tell both stories at once. You’ll report to a manager who wants to hand off real ownership: weekly 1:1s, not day-to-day oversight. You’ll have a direct hand in our highest-visibility moments, like celebrity and creator partnerships and executive press, not just supporting them from the sidelines. About Compensation We use a market-based approach to compensation. The starting salary range for this role is: $121,400 to $161,900 Your starting salary will be based on your location, experience, and qualifications, with increases over time tied to performance, role growth, and internal pay equity. Who We Are Babylist is the leading platform for expecting and new families. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year, making it the go-to destination for seamless purchasing, guidance, and expert recommendations. As a modern, AI-forward tech company, Babylist has expanded from a universal registry into a full ecosystem, including the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health, Babylist Money, NYC and LA showrooms, branded content, and more, generating $750M in revenue in 2025. Building the generational brand in baby, Babylist is reshaping the $235B kids and baby market and helping parents feel confident, connected, and cared for at every step. Our Ways of Working Babylist is remote-first with team members across the U.S. and Canada who move fast, think smart, and use AI as part of how they work every day, not as an experiment, but as an expectation. We come together twice a year to build the relationships behind the work, and we hire people who are genuinely excited about what’s possible and prove it through how they show up. Why You Will Love Working at Babylist Our Culture We work with focus and intention, then step away to recharge. We believe in exceptional management, and we invest in the tools and the time to connect with colleagues. We build products that positively impact millions of people’s lives. AI is part of how we work, not a side experiment. You’ll have leading tools like Claude and ChatGPT from day one, with no waiting on access, so the busywork gets handled and your judgment goes where it counts. Growth & Development Competitive pay and meaningful opportunities for career advancement. We believe technology and data can solve hard problems. We’re committed to career progression and performance-based advancement. Benefits Company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance. Retirement savings plan with company matching and flexible spending accounts. Generous paid parental leave and PTO. Winter Wonder Week: the whole company takes a paid week off at the end of the year, whether or not you celebrate anything, so everyone’s out at once and comes back refreshed. Remote work stipend to set up your office. Perks for physical, mental, and emotional health, parenting, childcare, and financial planning. Important Notices Recorded Interviews Babylist uses an interview recording tool to record and transcribe interviews for evaluation purposes in accordance with applicable privacy laws. By participating in an interview, you consent to this recording and transcription. Interview Integrity AI is part of how we work at Babylist. We expect you to use it too. Your application and interviews should still reflect you and your own thinking. We’ll tell you when AI is encouraged. Misrepresentation at any stage may result in removal from consideration for this and future roles. How We Review Applications We use AI throughout our hiring process to help review, screen, and assess applications. These tools support our team’s review; they do not replace it, and every hiring decision is made by a person. Connections at Babylist If you have a family member or close personal relationship with a current Babylist employee, please let your recruiter know. This helps us keep our process fair and transparent for everyone. Protect Yourself from Scams All official outreach comes from the Babylist Talent Team via @babylist.com email addresses only. We will never ask for payment or personal financial information. If you receive outreach via WhatsApp, Telegram, or a non-Babylist email address, it’s not us. Verify open roles at babylist.com/careers. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Analyst, Compliance Technology
item.description: Senior Analyst, Compliance Technology Organization: Coinbase Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you’re ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase: https://www.coinbase.com/careers We’re hiring an Analytics Engineer to join the Compliance Technology team within the Platform organization. This team builds and operates data and detection capabilities that enable Coinbase to meet global BSA/AML and related regulatory obligations at scale, partnering with Compliance, Product, and Engineering to ensure monitoring and investigative controls are effective, measurable, and auditable. You’ll build and own end-to-end data pipelines that power compliance detection and decision-making, improving signal quality, defining control performance measurement, and creating scalable tooling that makes compliance data easier to trust and use. What You’ll Do Build and maintain curated datasets and data models (e.g., case, alert, entity, transaction, and risk features) that power compliance controls across Transaction Monitoring, EDD/KYC, and Screening systems. Own data quality for compliance datasets by implementing validation checks, monitoring, lineage tracking, and documentation to ensure outputs are accurate, complete, and audit-ready. Partner with cross-functional engineering teams and Compliance stakeholders to close upstream data gaps, standardize instrumentation, and translate control requirements into scalable data structures and feature sets. Drive detection signal quality improvements by analyzing detection outputs, identifying opportunities to reduce non-actionable noise while protecting sensitivity, and defining success metrics for controlled rollouts. Execute measurement frameworks for compliance control effectiveness, including coverage, timeliness, stability, and outcome-based metrics, and build repeatable reporting pipelines consumable by Compliance leaders, operations teams, and auditors. Required Skills and Experience Minimum 5 years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or data-heavy technical roles. Advanced SQL proficiency, including complex transformations, performance tuning, and data quality checks. Experience building and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines and data models using tools such as dbt, Airflow, or equivalent orchestration and transformation frameworks. Demonstrated ability to execute on ambiguous, cross-functional projects in regulated environments with clear written and verbal communication. Python skills applied to automation, pipeline development, and data analysis. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. Pay Transparency Notice Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, as well as benefits including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k). Annual Base Salary Range (Excluding Equity and Bonus): $167,280–$196,800 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of three applications within a six-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. US Applicants: View the following resources: Employee Rights: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/eppac.pdf Know Your Rights: https://www.eeoc.gov/sites/default/files/2023-06/22-088_EEOC_KnowYourRights6.12.pdf E-Verify Notice of Participation: https://static-assets.coinbase.com/e-verify.pdf Accommodations: If you are an individual with a disability who needs a reasonable accommodation, email your request and contact information to accommodations[at]coinbase.com. Need screen reading technology? Free compatible screen reader: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/screen-reader/kgejglhpjiefppelpmljglcjbhoiplfn Tutorial: http://www.chromevox.com/tutorial/ Data Privacy & Arbitration: By submitting your application, you agree to the Candidate Privacy Notice: https://www.coinbase.com/legal/applicant_privacy_notice US applicants: By submitting your application, you agree to Arbitration of Disputes: https://www.coinbase.com/legal/application-arbitration-agreement Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Internal Communications Manager – Go To Market (GTM)
item.description: Senior Internal Communications Manager – Go To Market (GTM) Organization: PagerDuty, Inc. Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Senior Internal Communication Manager PagerDuty, Inc. (NYSE: PD) is the global leader in AI-first digital operations. By automatically detecting, diagnosing, and remediating issues, the PagerDuty Platform orchestrates AI agents and automated workflows with context from over 750 integrations. Trusted by approximately two-thirds of the Fortune 100 and nearly half of the Fortune 500, PagerDuty is the industry standard for organizations scaling resilient, autonomous operations. Notable customers include Chipotle, Cloudflare, Docusign, Fox, Nvidia, Salesforce, Spotify, Zoom, and more. We are growing rapidly and hiring top talent with leading AI skills across engineering, sales, product, marketing, and beyond as we build the leading digital operations platform. The Senior Internal Communication Manager will develop and execute communication strategies for PagerDuty’s Go-to-Market and Commercial organizations, including senior leadership. This role shapes and delivers key messages across pre-sales, post-sales, partner, and customer success audiences, building consistent, compelling communications that keep teams engaged and informed. We’re looking for a creative storyteller who can distill complex messages into clear, concise content across multiple channels, work closely with GTM leadership and cross-functional partners, and thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. This role will be required to come into our San Francisco offices 2 times per week. Role Responsibilities Develop and implement strategic communication plans aligned with the Chief Revenue Officer and his organization’s goals. Build and expand communication platforms for the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO). Craft key messages and narratives for a global audience, tailored by region and audience. Create, execute, and measure content across email, Slack, video, and other channels. Own Town Hall agendas, content, and slides, spotlighting customer stories to inspire GTM teams. Manage customer communications on critical matters by teaming with the CRO and Chief Customer Officer. Produce content for announcements, presentations, newsletters, blog posts, and FAQs. Build stakeholder relationships and incorporate feedback into communication strategy. Find creative ways to engage hundreds of GTM personnel, from customer wins to organizational news. Moderate large-scale meetings, including content, Slack monitoring, FAQs, and KPI reporting to leadership. Partner with other Communications leaders to align GTM messaging with the broader executive team. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or equivalent experience. 7+ years of experience in communications, spanning internal, external, executive, or enablement communications. Proven track record launching and managing communication plans and campaigns, with metrics-driven iteration. Experience partnering with GTM or executive leaders on positioning and change management. Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to think strategically and creatively across matrixed content involving multiple personas, industries, and products. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience with generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini) to accelerate content creation. Experience managing a communications calendar and distribution lists across groups. Comfort operating in a fast-paced, agile, results-oriented environment. Strong program and project management skills. Familiarity with Zoom Webinars, Google Workspace or Microsoft Office Suite, Slack, and email communication tools. Compensation The base salary range for this position is $114,000 to $191,400 USD. This role may also be eligible for bonus, commission, equity, and/or benefits. Our base salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range, which is subject to change based on primary work location, reflects the minimum and maximum base salary we expect to pay newly hired employees for the position. Within the range, we determine compensation based on factors including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience. Your recruiter can share more details about the specific offerings for this role, as well as the salary range applicable to your primary work location during the hiring process. Hesitant to Apply? We encourage you to submit your resume even if you don’t meet every requirement. We value potential and consider each candidate’s full professional story. Whether you’re exploring a career change or taking your next step, we look forward to reviewing your application. If this isn’t the right role or the right time, sign up for job alerts. Where We Work PagerDuty operates a hybrid work model with offices in eight major cities: Atlanta Lisbon London San Francisco Santiago Sydney Tokyo Toronto While we offer flexibility within our established locations, we cannot employ candidates residing in certain regions. Location Restrictions Australia Northern Territory Queensland South Australia Tasmania Western Australia Canada Alberta Manitoba Newfoundland and Labrador Northwest Territories Nunavut Prince Edward Island (PEI) Quebec Saskatchewan Yukon United States Alaska Hawaii Iowa Louisiana Mississippi Nebraska New Mexico Oklahoma Rhode Island South Dakota West Virginia Wyoming Candidates must reside in an eligible location, which may vary by role. How We Work Our values guide how we support customers, collaborate with colleagues, develop products, and foster a culture of belonging. They define not just our actions, but what it means to be a Dutonian. People Leaders at PagerDuty are responsible for creating high-performance environments that drive accountability. PagerDuty has four key dimensions that define Leadership Impact: Lead Self Lead the Team Lead the Business Lead the Future Each dimension includes three associated competencies that provide leaders with a shared framework for development, career progression, promotion, and succession planning discussions. Our Manager Expectations serve as a practical guide to help managers understand their responsibilities, prioritize effectively, and drive engagement and performance. What We Offer As a global organization, our total rewards approach is competitive with industry standards and aligned with local laws and regulations. Country-specific details are available on our benefits site. Your Package May Include Competitive salary Comprehensive benefits package Flexible work arrangements Company equity* Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)* Retirement or pension plan* Generous paid vacation time Paid holidays and sick leave Dutonian Wellness Days and HibernationDuty, company-wide paid days off in addition to PTO Paid parental leave: 22 weeks for the pregnant parent 12 weeks for the non-pregnant parent Some countries may offer longer leave periods in accordance with local laws Paid volunteer time off: 20 hours per year Company-wide hack weeks Mental wellness programs Eligibility may vary by role, region, and tenure. About PagerDuty PagerDuty, Inc. (NYSE: PD) is a global leader in digital operations management. The PagerDuty Operations Cloud is an AI-powered platform that empowers business resilience and drives operational efficiency for enterprises. With a generative AI assistant at its core, PagerDuty enables teams to: Detect and resolve issues in real time Orchestrate complex workflows Drive continuous improvement across digital operations Trusted by nearly half of both the Fortune 500 and the Forbes AI 50, as well as approximately two-thirds of the Fortune 100, PagerDuty is essential for delivering always-on digital experiences to modern businesses. PagerDuty is: Great Place to Work Certified™ A Fortune Best Workplace for Millennials A Fortune Best Medium Workplace A Fortune Best Workplace in Technology A top-rated product on TrustRadius and G2 Go behind the scenes on our careers site and follow @pagerduty on Instagram. Additional Information PagerDuty is an equal opportunity employer. PagerDuty does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, parental status, veteran status, or disability status. Your privacy is important to us. By submitting an application, you confirm that you have read and understand PagerDuty’s Privacy Policy. PagerDuty is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities during the job application process. If you require accommodation, please email [email protected] and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs. PagerDuty uses the E-Verify employment verification program. item.title: Senior IT Governance & Compliance Manager
item.description: Senior IT Governance & Compliance Manager Organization: LogicGate® Location: Bellevue, WA | Chicago, IL Date Posted: 09/17/2026 LogicGate LogicGate® is the leading AI GRC platform for the Enterprise, helping governance, risk, and compliance teams limit surprises, strengthen resilience, augment program performance, and confidently quantify impact and business value. Built to provide a centralized view of risk and compliance, with AI intelligence woven into the platform’s core, LogicGate delivers real-time insights and actionable data to help drive current business decisions, with the flexibility to scale alongside evolving business needs. Recognized as a Leader in the GRC Market, LogicGate continues to further solidify its position as a best-in-class platform. Excited About LogicGate but Not Familiar with GRC? GRC stands for Governance, Risk, and Compliance. GRC professionals help their companies manage uncertainty, act with integrity, and stay on the right side of the law. The GRC market is rapidly expanding with continuous growth opportunities. The current market size was valued at $50.5 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $104.5 billion by 2031. Senior IT Governance & Compliance Manager Location: Bellevue, WA or Chicago, IL (Hybrid) At LogicGate, we recognize that exceptional talent comes in all shapes and forms, and that there is no such thing as a “perfect” candidate. The qualifications below represent the core competencies, skills, and experiences that align most closely with the day-to-day responsibilities of this role. If you don’t check every single box and are excited about this work, we still highly encourage you to apply. About the Role LogicGate is seeking a Senior IT Governance & Compliance Manager to serve as a principal subject matter expert and trusted advisor driving our enterprise security and compliance posture. In this high-impact individual contributor role, you will partner cross-functionally with Sales, Legal, Product, and Engineering to embed risk-aware thinking across the business while streamlining audit readiness and vendor risk operations. You will balance regulatory rigor with business agility, using automation and modern GRC strategies to safeguard customer trust and accelerate enterprise growth. What You’ll Do Program Strategy: Drive the continuous maturity, scaling, and operational excellence of LogicGate’s IT governance, risk, and compliance frameworks in alignment with evolving business goals and regulatory standards. Third-Party Risk Management: Own and scale our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program end-to-end, conducting thorough risk assessments of vendors and subprocessors to deliver actionable risk mitigation strategies. Sales & Revenue Enablement: Partner with Sales and Revenue Operations to handle complex enterprise customer security inquiries, leveraging automation to accelerate response times and remove deal friction. Cross-Functional Advisory: Provide expert risk and compliance guidance on cybersecurity contract terms, vendor agreements, and strategic business initiatives in close collaboration with Legal and Operations. Audit & Compliance Execution: Lead internal preparation and external audit execution for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and recurring compliance attestations to demonstrate ongoing control effectiveness. Policy & Risk Governance: Author, maintain, and enforce enterprise security policies, standards, and risk management frameworks that support a high-performance, security-first culture. AI & Automation Integration: Evaluate and deploy modern AI-driven tools, automated evidence-gathering workflows, and platform intelligence to eliminate manual compliance overhead and optimize program performance. Thought Leadership: Act as an internal authority and external representative on IT governance, providing actionable insights on emerging industry trends, regulatory changes, and GRC best practices. What You Bring Required Domain Expertise: 7+ years of progressive experience in IT governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), IT auditing, or cybersecurity, with a track record of driving enterprise compliance programs. Framework Mastery: Deep hands-on experience managing and auditing frameworks such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, and relevant data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA). AI Literacy & Technological Curiosity: Demonstrated experience leveraging AI tools, LLMs, or automated GRC platforms to streamline evidence collection, vendor risk evaluations, or security questionnaire workflows. Strategic Communication: Strong consultative and advisory skills with a proven ability to translate complex risk concepts into clear, business-focused recommendations for executive leadership and cross-functional partners. Flexibility for On-Site Engagement: Willingness and ability to travel as needed for team planning workshops, customer meetings, and company gatherings. Nice to Have Industry Certifications: Hold active professional certifications such as CISA, CRISC, CISM, or CISSP. Platform Experience: Direct experience administering or building workflows in modern GRC platforms (ideally LogicGate Risk Cloud). AI Governance Exposure: Familiarity with emerging AI governance frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001) or evaluating risk within cloud-native environments (AWS). The anticipated base salary range for the role is $115,000 – $140,000 per year, plus variable compensation, equity, and benefits. Actual salaries may vary and will be based on factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Internal candidates who have current pay within or above the hiring range are still encouraged to apply if interested. Office Location This role is classified as Hybrid, based out of our Chicago headquarters or Bellevue office. You are expected to be available to work from the office as needed to support in-person collaboration with your team, which may include recurring in-office days. At LogicGate, our people are the foundation of everything we do. We are committed to delivering an exceptional experience for our employees and our customers by empowering and enabling our people to take ownership, make an impact, and deliver their best work. Total Rewards We are proud to offer a variety of competitive, inclusive, and comprehensive total rewards that are designed to support the unique needs of our employees both inside and outside of the workplace. In addition to offering competitive salary and variable compensation plans, equity options, and flexible health and wellness benefits, we are proud to offer generous PTO, annual company holidays, Health Days, and Summer Fridays. Employees’ growth and development are supported throughout their career journey through informal and formal programs and activities, including access to LinkedIn Learning, regular People Leader training, and our internal Mentorship Program. Our Culture At LogicGate, our culture and employee experience are grounded in our core values of Be as One, Do the Right Thing, Embrace Curiosity, Own It, Empower Customers, and Raise the Bar, which guide how we show up for each other, our customers, and everyone we interact with. We believe that the strongest teams are made up of individuals who bring their different identities, experiences, and perspectives to the table. We are committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where employees’ differences are celebrated and everyone is encouraged to bring their authentic selves to work. We encourage everyone to join one of our Employee Resource Groups (AAPI @ LogicGate, Pride at LogicGate, and Women in LogicGate) to participate in and contribute to conversations that foster an inclusive culture. LogicGate also believes strongly in giving back to the communities in which we live and work. To enable our teams to give back, we offer paid volunteer hours and company-wide charitable activities supporting a variety of organizations and causes. We are proud to have been recognized as a top workplace by Built In, Crain’s Chicago Business, the Chicago Tribune, and more. Visit our website to learn about our latest recognition. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Sr. Director, Media Planning and Buying
item.description: Sr. Director, Media Planning and Buying Organization: KAYAK Location: Cambridge, MA Date Posted: 09/17/2026 KAYAK, part of Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), is a leading travel search engine. With billions of queries across our platforms, we help people find their perfect flight, stay, rental car, and vacation package. We’re also transforming business travel with a new corporate travel solution, KAYAK for Business. As an employee of KAYAK, you will be part of a travel company that operates a portfolio of global metasearch brands including momondo, Cheapflights, and HotelsCombined, among others. From start-up to industry leader, innovation is in our DNA and every employee has an opportunity to make their mark. Our focus is on building the best travel search engine to make it easier for everyone to experience the world. Senior Director, Media Planning & Buying KAYAK is looking for a strategic Senior Director, Media Planning & Buying to shape how we invest in media across markets and channels. You will partner with Brand, Growth, Creative, Analytics, Finance, Product, and Commercial teams to build effective, measurable campaigns that support audience growth and business outcomes. This role will be required to work from our Cambridge, MA office 3 days per week. In This Role, You Will: Define and lead KAYAK’s multi-market media planning and buying strategy across offline and digital channels. Own annual and quarterly media planning cycles, including budget allocation, forecasting, pacing, optimization, and performance reviews. Develop integrated media plans spanning TV and video, out-of-home (OOH), radio, paid social, display, programmatic, search, and other relevant channels. Balance brand impact, audience growth, efficiency, and measurable business results across media investments. Establish measurement frameworks and feedback loops to evaluate reach, effectiveness, incrementality, efficiency, and return on investment. Partner with Analytics and external measurement providers on attribution, incrementality testing, and media mix modeling. Use campaign performance, consumer insights, competitive intelligence, and market trends to develop clear investment recommendations. Manage strategic relationships with media agencies, publishers, broadcasters, technology partners, and other vendors. Collaborate with Creative and Brand teams to translate audience and media insights into compelling, channel-appropriate campaigns. Partner with Finance, Product, Growth, and Commercial leaders to align media investment with business priorities and communicate trade-offs clearly. Lead, coach, and develop media professionals while building strong working practices across distributed, cross-functional teams. Please Apply If You Have: 10+ years of progressive experience in media planning and buying, including responsibility for multi-market campaigns and substantial budgets. Proven track record of using media investment to drive measurable brand awareness growth while delivering strong ROI and business results. Demonstrated expertise across offline and digital media, including TV/video, out-of-home, radio, paid social, display, programmatic, and search. A track record of developing and executing integrated media strategies that deliver measurable business results. Experience leading annual and quarterly media planning cycles, including budget allocation, forecasting, pacing, optimization, vendor negotiation, and performance evaluation. Strong knowledge of marketing measurement, including KPI development, incrementality testing, attribution, media mix modeling (MMM), and ROI or ROAS analysis. Advanced Excel skills and the ability to use data to develop clear, actionable recommendations. Experience hiring, managing, coaching, and developing high-performing media or marketing teams. Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior agencies, publishers, broadcasters, technology partners, and internal stakeholders. Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to explain complex media decisions to senior audiences. A bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Advertising, Communications, Business, Economics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Benefits and Perks Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year. Focus on mental health and well-being: Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth. Company-paid subscription to HeadSpace. Company-wide week off each year so the whole team can fully recharge and return without a pile-up of work. No Meeting Fridays. Paid parental leave. Generous paid vacation plus time off for your birthday. Paid volunteer time. Focus on your career growth: Development Dollars. Leadership development. Access to thousands of on-demand e-learning courses. Travel discounts. Employee Resource Groups. Competitive retirement and health plans. Free lunch 2 days per week. There are a variety of factors that go into determining a salary range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought or required. The range for this Massachusetts-based role is $185,000 – $215,000, not inclusive of annual bonus and recurring RSU grants. We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including health benefits, flexible spending accounts, retirement benefits, life insurance, paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays, and paid holidays), and parental leave benefits. Apply here Inclusion At KAYAK, we want everyone to have the space to grow, share ideas, and do great work. That’s why we’re focused on hiring the best talent from all walks of life and experiences, supporting them well, and making sure no one feels like they have to fit a mold to belong here. Need any adjustments for the interview, application, or on the job? No problem, we’ve got you. #LI-AS1 Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Legal Content Analyst
item.description: Legal Content Analyst Organization: Clio Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Clio Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely. We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice. Summary We are currently seeking a new Legal Content Analyst to join our CalendarRules team. This role is available to candidates in the US Remote. What Your Team Does CalendarRules helps legal professionals stay on top of critical deadlines while navigating increasingly complex court rules and systems. Acquired by Clio in 2021, CalendarRules offers a legal calendaring database that thousands of active subscribers use to run millions of date calculations each month. Our automated deadlines help users save time and reduce errors, providing legal technology that law firms rely on to run efficient and seamless practices in the best interests of their clients. CalendarRules currently provides rule sets for state and federal courts in the United States and Canada. We regularly build new rule sets, and our team is growing. Who You Are You are excited about technology and the impact it can have on transforming the legal experience for all. You appreciate the critical nature of deadlines for a busy law practice and have an interest in helping legal professionals navigate those deadlines. You are able to understand and communicate the nuances of different legal workflows. You interact easily, kindly, and professionally with individuals from various backgrounds and cultures. You are genuinely empathetic and seek ways to help customers while developing meaningful connections. You are comfortable addressing groups of professionals and can break down problems and processes into understandable components. You have a problem-solving mentality and enjoy digging into complex issues. You are looking for a position with growth potential at a company that will treat you with dignity and respect. What You’ll Work On Build and maintain rule sets by researching and analyzing applicable state, federal, and agency statutes, rules, local rules, and standing orders, and translating legal requirements into structured triggers, deadlines, and calculation logic for use in calendaring software. Manage rule updates by monitoring amendments and other legal developments, determining their impact on existing content, implementing necessary rule set changes, and drafting clear update notes. Provide customer support through email, Zoom, and other communication channels by investigating rules-related questions and calculation results, explaining applicable calendaring logic, and escalating complex issues as needed. Deliver customer and partner training on litigation calendaring protocols and legal content, including “train the trainer” programs for integration partners. Conduct rule set audits and peer reviews to ensure legal accuracy, consistency, completeness, and compliance with established content standards. Develop and deliver presentations and written content, such as newsletter articles, on legal content and litigation calendaring topics, including participation in customer trainings, conferences, and webinars. Exercise sound legal judgment when faced with ambiguous, conflicting, or interrelated procedural authorities, including determining when a requirement can appropriately be translated into automated calendaring logic. Make day-to-day decisions regarding rule set structure, triggers, deadlines, and calculation logic within established standards, protocols, and precedent. Independently research and resolve routine customer questions involving rules and calculation results, escalating novel, high-risk, or complex issues as appropriate. Identify potential content gaps, conflicts, and calculation risks and recommend appropriate resolutions. Operate with moderate autonomy while seeking guidance on high-impact, complicated, or novel analyses. What You Bring Licensed to practice law in the United States. 3+ years of litigation experience. Knowledge of how to find and calculate legal deadlines. Familiarity with the U.S. legal system. Strong legal research and analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate state and federal statutes, procedural rules, local rules, agency rules, and standing orders. Adept at translating complex legal requirements into clear, standardized, structured content suitable for automated litigation calendaring. Able to apply procedural knowledge to draft precise triggers, deadlines, and calculation logic, including service methods, time computation rules, court holidays, and related procedural requirements. Proficient in monitoring rule changes across jurisdictions, assessing their impact on existing content, and implementing accurate and timely revisions. Strong writing and editing skills, including the ability to explain complex procedures clearly to both legal and non-legal audiences. Exceptional attention to detail when building, auditing, and peer-reviewing rule sets for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and compliance with content standards. Comfortable and proficient with AI and emerging technologies, using them to support legal research, analysis, customer support, and workflow efficiency while independently evaluating outputs and applying legal judgment to ensure accuracy and quality. What You Will Find Here Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture. Some Highlights of Our Total Rewards Program Include Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance. Hybrid work environment, with an expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin, and Sydney) to be in the office a minimum of twice per week. Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year. EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources. 401(k) matching and Child Education Savings. Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgment at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years. The expected salary range for this role is $93,800 to $127,000 USD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skill set, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile. Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility Our team shows up as their authentic selves and is united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We pride ourselves on building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. Learn more about our culture at: https://www.clio.com/about/careers/ We’re a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we’ve built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions. Disclaimer We only communicate with candidates through official @clio.com email addresses. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Advisor Science and Innovation Policy Advocacy
item.description: Senior Advisor Science and Innovation Policy Advocacy Organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/17/2026 Senior Advisor Science and Innovation Policy Advocacy Department: MIT Washington Office Date: September 2026 Position Overview This position serves as a key advocate representing MIT’s research policy interests at the federal level across all science domains before Congress, federal agencies, the White House, and the Washington higher education advocacy community, including leading associations. Drawing on prior experience in science, research, and/or higher education policy, this position advises MIT’s policy and government affairs leadership, including the Vice President of Government Affairs and the Director of the Washington Office, as well as the campus community, including academic departments and administrative offices, on federal policies that impact the Institute’s research and training mission. The position will create and maintain strong working relationships with senior federal science agency staff, Congressional staff including leadership and professional staff members of committees, and national higher education-focused associations. A key element of the position is to identify and analyze complex policy proposals to determine the impact on MIT and the likelihood of adoption, communicate the impacts and timeframes to relevant campus stakeholders, and help develop MIT’s advocacy approach and messaging. The individual in this position also influences institutional views and designs advocacy strategies and messages for MIT’s proactive policy initiatives through strong professional networks, direct advocacy, and participation in coalitions and associations in Washington. This role also assists faculty and students with injecting their ideas into federal policy circles when aligned with MIT institutional objectives. Specific policy issues and duties will depend on the makeup and needs of the office but will include a strong focus on science and research issues, including the availability of funding and regulations governing research. The successful candidate may also participate in areas impacting MIT’s contributions to a broader set of innovation policy activities, including intellectual property licensing, climate and sustainability, and higher education governance. Principal Duties and Responsibilities Recommend proactive and defensive federal policy strategies in Washington to MIT’s government affairs leadership and campus departments targeting Congress and the Executive Branch, with a particular focus on topics including, but not limited to, biotechnology, basic science, emerging technologies, research regulations, research funding, general research policy, higher education, student visas and skilled immigration, intellectual property, and related issues. Serve as an external-facing and community-recognized advocate and lobbyist for MIT, representing the Institute’s interests to Congress, federal agencies, and the White House. Advise and inform MIT’s government affairs leadership and campus community of pending policy proposals and final decisions, emerging opportunities, and strategic risks in science, research, and higher education policy, as well as other areas as assigned. Help develop advocacy strategies and key messages to support MIT positions and policy initiatives on relevant topics. Arrange and prepare MIT faculty and leadership, including the President, for meetings with federal policymakers and influencers. Staff senior MIT officials in key meetings with federal policymakers. Serve as the Washington representative for MIT within science policy and advocacy coalitions, including staffing associations and working groups deemed most impactful to MIT’s science and higher education policy interests. Write and present regular memos, briefings, and policy updates to campus constituencies; inform faculty, students, and leadership of the evolving federal policy landscape. Mentor and support the professional development of junior members of the MIT Washington Office, including the regular rotation of interns in the office. Supervision Received Self-initiates work and completes projects independently while working with the Office Director and the Vice President of Government Affairs. Reports to the Director of the Washington Office. May provide mentorship and guidance to junior office staff and may supervise office trainees. Qualifications & Skills Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of five years of relevant experience, or a graduate degree in an applicable field and at least three years of relevant experience, is required. A PhD with experience in research programs is highly desirable. Relevant experience includes work in government relations or within a government agency or Congress. An applicable academic field for a PhD generally means a field in which MIT offers a degree. Demonstrated expertise in science and research policy, higher education policy, and/or technology policy issues, along with the ability to advise senior leadership, is required. Strong written and oral communication skills and analytical capabilities are required, including experience preparing and presenting memos and policy briefings. Leadership experience within advocacy coalitions and mentoring junior staff is preferred. Candidates must be willing and able to take initiative, manage a diverse portfolio, and work both independently and as part of a team. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council!
