item.title: Director Federal Policy
item.description: Director Federal Policy Organization: Pfizer Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 09/18/2026 ROLE SUMMARY The U.S. Federal Policy Team is responsible for developing, shaping, and advancing public policies to support patients’ access to innovative medicines in the U.S. and other Pfizer business objectives. This Director role focuses on U.S. Federal policy, including issues such as affordability and access, drug pricing, coverage and reimbursement, and payment and delivery system reforms as they impact government healthcare programs (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid). Responsibilities include tracking and analyzing legislative and regulatory developments, translating these issues to key internal audiences, shaping Pfizer policy positions and strategies, and developing presentations and effective advocacy materials. The individual in this role provides leadership, subject matter expertise, and strategic insights and advice on US healthcare policy with the goal of understanding how to effectively operate in the policy environment and how to advocate for policies favorable to innovative new medicines. The Director is responsible for anticipating, identifying, and communicating US healthcare policy issues/trends/changes occurring in the regulated environment that have the potential to impact patients and access to Pfizer’s current and future medicines. The Director partners with internal stakeholders to respond to developments, both independently and through external stakeholders, and work to shape the legislative and regulatory environment to advance Pfizer’s policy goals. The role will work closely with key internal partners including the broader US Policy & Government Relations (USPGR) teams, the US Commercial therapeutic business units and Global Hospital and Biosimilars, Federal Government Relations, Public Affairs, Payer and Channel Access, US Market Access and Patient Services, Finance, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, and others as needed. In addition to building and maintaining strong internal relationships, the Director of Federal Policy will maintain a deep external network across stakeholders, including the relevant industry trade associations and other industry organizations, think-tanks, and policy organizations to support Pfizer key policy priorities. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES Develop and execute specific policy and advocacy strategies to advance Pfizer’s U.S. healthcare policy objectives, including policies with broad impact and targeted policies and strategies to advance specific US Commercial and Global Hospital and Biosimilars business priorities. Lead drafting and submission of public comments in response to Federal regulatory issuances (e.g., HHS, CMS, or other relevant agency regulatory or sub-regulatory actions). Align with key business partners to ensure business priorities are reflected. Provide technical expertise and strategic direction to USPGR on emerging issues, including the review of proposed legislation/regulations for impact and relevancy, development of amendments and alternative approaches, and preparation of advocacy materials (issue assessments, key messages, leave-behinds, infographics) to advance Pfizer’s federal policy priorities. Work closely within USPGR, and across key business teams to influence strategic direction of stakeholder groups on federal policies. Initiates and independently leads internal, cross-functional workgroups to quantitatively assess highly complex changes in healthcare policy to guide decisions and inform Pfizer of financial implications on US Oncology, US Primary Care, US Specialty Care, and Global Hospital and Biosimilars. Actively monitor and analyze the healthcare policy landscape to anticipate, identify, and communicate trends and developments that could impact patients and Pfizer’s medicines, including our pipeline of transformative medicines. Develop and implement Policy Advocacy initiatives by engaging with external stakeholders, including government bodies, regulatory agencies, and industry organizations, to support policy outcomes that advance business goals; represent Pfizer at trade organizations and associations by serving on committees and working groups to advance Pfizer policy positions. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact. Bachelor’s degree required; minimum of 8+ years working on federal healthcare policy and advocacy in government or relevant private sector experience; or master’s degree with 7+ years’ experience. Advanced degree in public health, public policy, law, or related field strongly preferred. Experience in U.S. government healthcare programs. Experience in policy analysis, research, and development. Experience in implementing strategic and tactical plans. Proven track record for sharp strategic analysis and understanding, including incorporating policy into decision making for senior leadership. Demonstrated project management expertise, with the ability to manage multiple high-profile, complex workstreams simultaneously while maintaining strong attention to accuracy and technical detail. Must be confident, decisive and adept at navigating a fast-paced and evolving environment with competing priorities and stakeholders. Must demonstrate excellent networking and relationship-building skills and the ability to interact with confidence with various levels and functions. Excellent verbal, analytical, written and interpersonal communication skills, particularly in interpreting and distilling complex information. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience with CMS-specific drug coverage and payment systems (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid). Experience in health-related federal administrative agency or on Congressional legislative committee staff. Experience working in or with academic experts, think-tanks, or healthcare policy or advocacy organizations. Ability to understand and guide financial or quantitative analyses. Proficiency in PowerPoint and strong overall business communication skills. Other Job Details: Last Date to Apply for Job: September 30th, 2026. Ability to travel based on business needs NOT eligible for Relocation Package Locations: NYHQ and Washington DC This position is hybrid and requires working onsite 2 to 3 days per week #LI-PFE The annual base salary for this position ranges from $176,600.00 to $294,300.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. item.title: Director, Government Relations
item.description: Director, Government Relations Organization: REGENT Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/18/2026 About REGENT At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We’re not just building vehicles, we’re creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today’s battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo – connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production – and building the team to make it happen. Role Overview REGENT is building a new category of vehicle – and bringing Seagliders to market will require more than great technology. It will require strong partnerships across government, a policy environment that understands what we’re building, and a clear strategy for how REGENT engages at the federal and state level. We’re looking for a Director of Government Relations to own REGENT’s federal and state government relations strategy, deepen relationships across Congress, the executive branch, defense stakeholders, and Rhode Island, and help position REGENT as a trusted voice in defense, transportation, and emerging policy. A major focus will be supporting the growth of our defense business by connecting policy, appropriations, and government relationships to meaningful opportunities for REGENT. You’ll work closely with leaders across the company to set our government relations agenda, advise leadership on where and how REGENT should engage, and build understanding and support for a technology that doesn’t fit neatly into existing frameworks. You’ll have the opportunity to shape REGENT’s approach while personally driving the relationships and advocacy that matter most. If you’ve built credibility in government, know how to turn relationships into meaningful business and policy outcomes, and are energized by the opportunity to help shape the landscape around a technology and industry that didn’t exist before, we’d love to meet you. What You’ll Do Lead Federal Government Relations: Own REGENT’s relationships across Congress, the executive branch, and relevant federal agencies — strengthening existing relationships, building new ones, and focusing our engagement on the stakeholders and policy priorities that can meaningfully advance the business. Drive Defense Advocacy: Lead government relations efforts supporting the growth of REGENT’s defense business. Navigate authorization, appropriations, acquisition, and policy priorities; engage DoD stakeholders, defense committees, congressional offices, and other decision-makers; and help position REGENT as funding and program opportunities develop. Lead Rhode Island Government Relations: Own REGENT’s state government relations strategy, building relationships across the Governor’s Office, legislature, state agencies, economic development organizations, and transportation stakeholders and connecting those relationships to REGENT’s broader priorities. Shape the Policy Environment for Seagliders: Build understanding and support for a category that doesn’t fit neatly into existing frameworks. Translate complex technology into clear, compelling policy narratives and bring together customers, industry partners, trade associations, and other stakeholders who can strengthen REGENT’s advocacy. Advise Leadership: Serve as a trusted government relations advisor to the CEO and senior leadership — helping determine where REGENT should engage, how we use our time and political capital, and how leaders should approach high-stakes government meetings and external engagements. Partner Across the Company: Work closely with Defense, Business Development, Marketing, Engineering, Manufacturing, Legal, and leadership to connect government relations to company strategy, defense growth, regulatory priorities, and external communications — bringing the right internal expertise into government engagement at the right time. What You’ll Bring Active Federal Network: You have real, current relationships on the Hill and across relevant executive branch agencies — people who know you, take your calls, and trust your credibility. You can bring an established network to REGENT while continuing to expand it around the company’s priorities. Defense Acquisition & Appropriations Fluency: You understand how defense authorization, appropriations, and acquisition actually work — including NDAA cycles, DoD budgets, defense committee dynamics, and where and how companies can influence the process. You can connect that landscape to concrete opportunities to grow REGENT’s defense business. State-Level GR Experience: You’ve independently led state government relations work — building relationships with governors’ offices and legislators, advancing priorities through state processes, and working with economic development, transportation, and other relevant agencies. You understand that state GR requires a different set of relationships, levers, and instincts than federal work. End-to-End GR Leadership: You’ve owned government relations strategy from development through execution — setting priorities, mapping stakeholders, developing messaging, building relationships, and directly driving advocacy. You’re comfortable being the senior GR voice in the room and building the playbook rather than waiting for one. Emerging Technology Advocacy: You’ve built credibility for a company, technology, or industry that didn’t fit neatly into an existing policy framework. You know how to translate something complex and unfamiliar into a compelling case for policymakers and help shape the conversation as government catches up with innovation. Political & Executive Judgment: You know that access alone isn’t strategy. You can read the political landscape, understand competing interests and reputational considerations, and advise senior leaders on where to engage, how to show up, and when the smartest move may be not to engage at all. Who We’re Looking For Collaborative Team Player: You see government relations as a lever for advancing company priorities, not an end in itself. You understand how GR connects to defense growth, business development, regulatory strategy, and company reputation, and you build strong relationships across the company to focus our efforts where they can have the greatest impact. Creative Problem Solver: You’re comfortable navigating problems without an obvious playbook. You can look at a complicated political or policy landscape, understand the stakeholders and competing interests, and find creative paths to advance REGENT’s priorities — especially when the technology or policy question doesn’t fit neatly into an existing framework. Adaptable & Agile: You’re comfortable operating in an environment where political dynamics, funding opportunities, and company priorities can change quickly. You know when to move quickly, when to play the long game, and when new information means the strategy needs to change — without losing sight of the broader objective. Innovative Mindset: You’re energized by the opportunity to help government understand and engage with something genuinely new. You challenge conventional approaches, look for new ways to build support and credibility, and think creatively about how policy, partnerships, and government engagement can help create the conditions for REGENT and the Seaglider category to succeed. What We Offer Competitive compensation including a robust equity incentive plan. Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance – we cover 100% of your premiums. 401(k) with company matching, so you can plan for the future. Generous flexible time off, paid parental leave, and company-wide holiday breaks. Relocation packages available for those moving to join our team. Daily, free catered lunches Learning & professional development opportunities If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Global Public Policy and Strategy Manager
item.description: Global Public Policy and Strategy Manager Organization: Infoblox Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/18/2026 Job Description At Infoblox, every breakthrough begins with a bold “what if.” What if your ideas could ignite global innovation? What if your curiosity could redefine the future? We invite you to step into the next exciting chapter of your career journey. Bring your creativity, drive, your daring spirit, and feel what it’s like to thrive on a team big enough to make an impact, yet small enough to make a difference. Our cloud-first networking and security solutions already protect 70% of the Fortune 500, and we’re looking for creative thinkers ready to push that influence even further. Join us and discover how far your bold “what if” can take the world, your community, and your career. How we empower our people is extraordinary: we’re recognized as a Glassdoor Best Place to Work 2025, Great Place to Work-Certified in five countries, and honored by Cigna as a Healthy Workforce honors for three consecutive years; and what we build is world class: named CybersecAsia’s Best in Critical Infrastructure 2024 — clear evidence that when first-class technology meets empowered talent, remarkable careers take shape. So, what if the next big idea, and the next great career story, comes from you? Become the force that turns every “what if” into “what’s next.” In a world where you can be anything, Be Infoblox. Global Public Policy and Strategy Manager (12-month contract to start) We have an opportunity for a Global Public Policy and Strategy Manager (12-month contract, with possibility for extension or conversion to FTE), to join our Legal and Public Policy team in Washington, DC, reporting to the VP, Global Public Policy and Strategy. In this pivotal role, you will lead Infoblox’s day-to-day legislative and regulatory advocacy efforts, helping shape policy outcomes that impact cybersecurity, networking, and critical digital infrastructure. You will serve as a trusted representative of Infoblox before Congress, executive branch agencies, regulators, trade associations, and key public-sector stakeholders. Leveraging your deep understanding of the Washington, DC policy environment, you will develop and execute advocacy campaigns, build bipartisan relationships, and advance policy priorities that support the company’s strategic objectives. Be a Contributor — What You’ll Do Lead Infoblox’s U.S. federal government affairs and advocacy strategy across Congress, Executive Branch agencies, global partners, and key regulatory stakeholders Develop and execute advocacy campaigns that advance Infoblox’s public policy objectives and business priorities Build and maintain trusted bipartisan relationships with policymakers, congressional staff, agency officials, and industry stakeholders in Washington, DC Represent Infoblox in meetings, briefings, and discussions with government officials, trade associations, and policy influencers Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative and regulatory developments affecting cybersecurity, networking, cloud technologies, and related policy areas Draft policy positions, comment letters, consultation responses, briefing materials, and advocacy strategies Lead Infoblox’s policy engagement for operational collaboration with cyber centers and law-enforcement partners, translating threat research into trusted information sharing, government advisories, and policy or business outcomes Partner with Legal, Product, Security, Communications, and executive leadership teams to develop and advance policy priorities Engage with industry associations, standards organizations, and policy coalitions to influence outcomes and strengthen Infoblox’s industry presence Leverage AI-enabled tools to support policy research, legislative tracking, advocacy planning, and content development Support global public policy initiatives and international stakeholder engagement where business priorities intersect with global policy developments Be Prepared — What You Bring 12+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, or a related field Deep experience in networking and/or cybersecurity with demonstrated success developing and executing advocacy campaigns and influencing legislative or regulatory outcomes Significant experience engaging with Congress, Executive Branch agencies, regulators, or related government stakeholders Established bipartisan relationships across government, policy, and industry communities Strong understanding of the Washington, DC policy environment and political landscape Experience driving policy outcomes via operational partnerships with government cyber centers, law enforcement, or critical-infrastructure stakeholders Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with experience producing policy, regulatory, or advocacy-related materials Proven ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders across complex organizations and external environments Experience using AI-enabled research, analytics, or content-generation tools to improve decision-making and productivity Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, International Relations, Law, Cybersecurity, Business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred Be Successful — Your Path First 90 Days: Immerse in our culture, connect with mentors (Blox Buddies), and map the systems and meet with key stakeholders that rely on your work. Discuss and create short/long term goals Six Months: Establish and execute a U.S. government affairs engagement plan for priority issues, including a mapped network of key Congressional and agency stakeholders Deliver a recurring, AI-enabled policy watch report highlighting top legislative and regulatory developments for Infoblox leadership and cross-functional partners Lead or co-lead at least one major regulatory or legislative response (e.g., comment letter, RFI/RFC response, consultation submission) on a core cybersecurity or networking policy issue Establish a process for driving policy outcomes via operational collaboration with priority cyber centers and law-enforcement partners Build active participation for Infoblox in at least one high-impact industry association or coalition working group aligned to our policy and business objectives One Year: Demonstrate measurable impact on at least two priority policy outcomes (e.g., influencing legislative language, shaping regulatory approaches, or securing participation in key government programs) Mature a data- and AI-driven advocacy pipeline that integrates policy intelligence with business development, enabling earlier identification of risks, opportunities, and government-funded initiatives Complete at least one policy outcome via operational collaboration with priority cyber centers and law-enforcement partners, such as a joint advisory Be viewed as a trusted advisor to senior executives on U.S. policy risks and opportunities, with a clear, repeatable cadence for briefings and cross-functional alignment Support expansion of Infoblox’s global public policy footprint, including contributions to international advocacy efforts (e.g., EU cybersecurity and AI policy) informed by U.S. experience Belong — Your Community Our culture thrives on inclusion, rewarding the bold ideas, curiosity, and creativity that move us forward. In a community where every voice counts, continuous learning is the norm. So, whether you code, create, sell, or care for customers, you’ll grow and belong here. Be Rewarded Global employee resource groups, and a “No Jerks” policy that keeps collaboration healthy Modern offices with EV charging, healthy snacks (and the occasional cupcake), plus hackathons, game nights, and culture celebrations We practice pay transparency and reward performance. Offers reflect role location, internal equity, experience, skills, education, and certifications. The rate for this position: $100 – $115 per hour Ready to Be the Difference? Infoblox is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis. #LI-MA1 #LI-Remote Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Manager, External Relations
item.description: Senior Manager, External Relations Organization: Sony Corporation of America Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/18/2026 Sony Corporation of America, located in New York, NY, is the U.S. headquarters of Sony Group Corporation, based in Tokyo, Japan. Sony’s principal U.S. businesses include Sony Electronics Inc., Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC, Sony Music Entertainment, Sony Music Publishing and Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. With some 900 million Sony devices in hands and homes worldwide today, a vast array of Sony movies, television shows and music, and the PlayStation Network, Sony creates and delivers more entertainment experiences to more people than anyone else on earth. To learn more: https://www.sony.com/en POSITION SUMMARY Sony Corporation of America (SCA) is seeking a Senior Manager, External Relations with a proven track record to join our dynamic Global External Relations & Geopolitical Strategy team. SCA’s External Relations Department works closely with the external relations teams of our global affiliates and parent company. In this role, you will participate in developing, implementing and executing strategies to represent the company’s interests in government related affairs. This position will be on a hybrid schedule with 3 days per week in our Washington, DC office. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES Engage with key discussions across the Semiconductor and Electronics industries, including trade policy, delivering strategic insights that influence regulatory outcomes and advance the company’s interests. Cultivate and leverage a robust external network of experts, politicians, industry groups, and other relevant third parties to enhance the company’s presence and gather critical insights, aligning with Sony’s strategic direction and business priorities. Actively engage in legislative and regulatory advocacy to promote favorable laws and regulations for Sony’s businesses while mitigating unfavorable ones, collaborating with internal stakeholders to align on company priorities. Monitor and analyze U.S. political, legal, and regulatory developments to identify trends affecting Sony, transforming information into actionable insights for internal stakeholders and management. Honesty, trustworthiness and ethical conduct are material requirements for the responsibilities outlined above. QUALIFICATIONS FOR POSITION Your qualifications and experience should include: Minimum 7 years of experience in tech-related industry associations government affairs, public policy, trade affairs, or a related field, with a demonstrated understanding of legislative and regulatory processes. Bachelor’s degree required; degree in Political Science, Public Administration, or related field preferred. Experience working on Capitol Hill and/or Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security strongly preferred. Strong interest in technology, particularly in semiconductors and related policy and regulatory developments. Global mindset with the ability to assess issues from a cross-border perspective and align U.S. developments with global business and policy priorities. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other workplace productivity tools, including AI. Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills. Strong attention to detail with outstanding organizational skills. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Demonstrated ability to take initiative, adapt to feedback, and manage multiple tasks effectively, sometimes under time pressure. Experience with project management preferred. Japanese speaker is preferred. Must be authorized to work in the United States. The anticipated annual base salary for this position is $170,000 to $185,000. In addition to the annual base salary, this role has an annual bonus target of 17%. This range does not include any other compensation components or other benefits that an individual may be eligible for. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include as applicable, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any basis protected by applicable federal, state, or local law, ordinance, or regulation. Disability Accommodation for Applicants to Sony Corporation of America Sony Corporation of America provides reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in job application procedures. For reasonable accommodation requests, please contact us by email at [email protected] or by mail to: Sony Corporation of America, People Experience Department, 25 Madison Avenue, New York, NY 10010. Please indicate the position you are applying for. We are aware that unauthorized individuals or organizations may attempt to solicit personal information or payments from job applicants by impersonating our company through fraudulent job postings. We take these matters seriously but cannot control third-party websites. To protect your personal information, please verify that any job posting you respond to also appears on our official Careers page: https://www.sonyjobs.com . Please also be advised that we never request personal identifying information (such as Social Security numbers, bank details, or copies of identification documents) during the initial stages of our application process. If you have any doubts about the authenticity of a job posting or communication, please contact [email protected] before submitting any information. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Executive and Corporate Communications
item.description: Director, Executive and Corporate Communications Organization: PrizePicks Location: Atlanta, GA Date Posted: 09/18/2026 At PrizePicks, we are the fastest-growing sports company in North America, as recognized by Inc. 5000. As the leading platform for Daily Fantasy Sports, we cover a diverse range of sports leagues, including the NFL, NBA, and Esports titles like League of Legends and Counter-Strike. Our team of over 550 employees thrives in an inclusive culture that values individuals from diverse backgrounds, regardless of their level of sports fandom. Ready to reimagine the DFS industry together? PrizePicks is seeking a Director of Executive & Corporate Communications to shape how our leadership team shows up in the world. You’ll be the strategic partner for our senior executives — turning business strategy into compelling narratives, preparing leaders for high-stakes moments, and making sure the PrizePicks’ team is part of the conversation happening across sports gaming, daily fantasy, and prediction markets. What you’ll do: Build our executives’ thought-leadership platform from the ground up – identifying the moments where our leaders should have a point of view – including industry events. Turn business strategy and product milestones into narratives – defining the two or three ideas each leader should be known for, and build a high-impact content plan around them. Create compelling executive-authored owned content — LinkedIn posts, bylines, newsletters, digital assets and blog posts — writing in each leader’s voice to reinforce the company’s strategy, culture and reputation. Own PrizePicks’ corporate social channels, including LinkedIn and PrizePicks News on X, to develop a cadence of stories that drive engagement and enhance the company’s reputation. Collaborate with other departments across PrizePicks, as well as members of the communications team, including policy & product, brand & growth and internal communications – to develop compelling corporate stories to increase our share of voice. Work closely with the CCO and the communications team to prepare executives for conferences, investor and partner organizations and industry events. Keep a close eye on the competitive and regulatory landscape, and use those developments to sharpen what our leaders say. Track what’s actually landing — which posts, ideas, and formats build our thought leadership — and use it to sharpen the plan, not just produce more content. Ensure consistency of messaging across earned, owned, executive and corporate channels. Establish communications processes, editorial planning, and governance that improve consistency, collaboration and execution. This is a highly specialized, individual contributor role with no direct reports. What you have: 10+ years in communications, with meaningful experience in executive and corporate communications, especially counseling an executive leadership team. Experience operating inside a regulated, high-growth industry — where the news cycle moves fast and the stakes are real. A track record of turning business objectives into compelling narratives. Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills across multiple executive formats. Sound judgment under pressure. You’ve drafted a statement on a tight deadline before and know the difference between fast and reckless. Strong news judgment and a real interest in the categories PrizePicks competes in — you should already have opinions on how this industry is evolving. The ability to operate as a senior individual contributor, setting strategy, influencing without authority and delivering personally where required. Nice to Have: Direct experience in sports gaming, daily fantasy sports, or prediction markets. Experience supporting an executive through a major public moment. Where you’ll live: This is a hybrid position based at our PrizePicks headquarters in Atlanta, GA. #LI-Hybrid Working at PrizePicks: The typical salary range for this position is $135,000 to $165,000. At PrizePicks, we consider your role, level, and where you’ll be working when determining our salary ranges. The compensation info you see on our job postings gives you an idea of the starting pay range for the position. Your actual pay within that range will depend on your specific work location, as well as your skills, experience, and education. Your recruiter will be happy to chat more about the specific pay range for your location and how we arrived at it during the hiring process. Benefits you’ll receive: In addition to your great compensation package, full-time employees will be eligible for the following perks: Company-subsidized medical, dental, & vision plans 401(k) plan with company match Annual bonus Flexible PTO to encourage a healthy work/life balance (2 weeks STRONGLY encouraged!) Generous paid leave programs, including 16-week paid parental leave and disability benefits Workplace flexibility and modern work schedules focused on getting the job done, not hours clocked Company-wide in-person events and team outings Lifestyle enhancement program Company equipment provided (Windows & Mac options) Annual performance reviews with opportunities for growth and career development You must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. PrizePicks is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status. item.title: Government Relations Manager
item.description: Government Relations Manager Organization: Vatn Systems Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/18/2026 Position Summary Vatn Systems is building out its Government Relations function and seeks a Government Relations Manager to serve as the company’s day-to-day architect and operator of Government strategy with particular focus on Congress. This person will report to the VP of Government Relations to manage congressional engagement across various House and Senate Committees, with a particular focus on the defense appropriations process (markup cycles, committee hearings, program plus-ups, report language) and authorization priorities affecting naval, undersea, and unmanned systems. Key Responsibilities Monitor, analyze, and report on the annual National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and Defense Appropriations bills, tracking provisions, report language, and funding lines relevant to Vatn Systems’ programs and the broader unmanned maritime systems portfolio. Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress, committee staff, and relevant caucuses on the House and Senate Armed Services Committees (HASC/SASC) and Defense Appropriations Subcommittees (HAC-D/SAC-D). Develop and execute legislative strategies to secure, protect, and grow program funding lines and advance policy provisions that support the company’s technology and contracting priorities. Translate technical program information (e.g., undersea vehicle capabilities, launch platform integration, production timelines) into congressionally digestible narratives tied to member priorities, state/district economic impact, and military requirements. Coordinate closely with the VP of Government Relations on overall legislative strategy, and with company leadership on the timing and framing of legislative landscape, political dynamics, and impacts on defense policy affecting the company. Monitor and report on legislative developments affecting Vatn’s product lines and the broader undersea/unmanned systems portfolio, including NDAA and appropriations conference dynamics. Support preparation for CEO and other company executives for engagements, briefings, and site visits (including coordination of CODEL and STAFFDEL facility tours to Bristol, RI, military exercises and demonstrations, and other events). Represent Vatn at relevant congressional and industry events, hearings, and markups. Partner with outside lobbying support and trade associations as needed, ensuring consistent messaging. Assist Growth team in additional outreach activities including trade shows, demonstrations, and other events as required. Required Qualifications Minimum 3 years of experience as a professional staff member, member staff, or equivalent experience with the House or Senate Armed Services Committees and Appropriations Committees. Direct, hands-on experience with the defense authorization and/or appropriations markup process, including drafting bill and report language. Established current relationships with committee staff, clerks, and/or member offices relevant to defense programs. Demonstrated fluency in the legislative and budget calendar, including continuing resolution dynamics, conference processes, and omnibus negotiations. Ability to obtain and maintain SECRET clearance. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical defense program detail into clear legislative asks. Willingness to travel regularly between Washington, DC and Bristol, RI. Preferred Qualifications Prior exposure to Navy undersea warfare programs, unmanned maritime systems, or shipbuilding/submarine industrial base issues. Experience supporting or coordinating with program executive offices (e.g., PEO SSN, PEO UWS, PAE USW) or NAVSEA. Familiarity with rapid acquisition pathways (e.g., APFIT) and non-traditional defense contracting. Prior private-sector or defense-industry government relations experience. Vatn Systems is an equal opportunity employer. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Manager, Federal Government Relations Organization: Kaiser Permanente Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/18/2026 Job Summary Partners with internal stakeholders on government relations by advising key stakeholders on developments, researching solutions and leading responses to key issues, and communicating positioning. Establishes and maintains relationships with key external stakeholders to promote and advocate for KP with minimal guidance. Essential Responsibilities Promotes learning in others by proactively providing and/or developing information, resources, advice, and expertise with coworkers and members; builds relationships with cross-functional/external stakeholders and customers. Listens to, seeks, and addresses performance feedback; proactively provides actionable feedback to others and to managers. Pursues self-development; creates and executes plans to capitalize on strengths and develop weaknesses; leads by influencing others through technical explanations and examples and provides options and recommendations. Adopts new responsibilities; adapts to and learns from change, challenges, and feedback; demonstrates flexibility in approaches to work; champions change and helps others adapt to new tasks and processes. Facilitates team collaboration to support a business outcome. Completes work assignments autonomously and supports business-specific projects by applying expertise in subject area and business knowledge to generate creative solutions; encourages team members to adapt to and follow all procedures and policies. Collaborates cross-functionally and/or externally to achieve effective business decisions; provides recommendations and solves complex problems; escalates high-priority issues or risks, as appropriate; monitors progress and results. Supports the development of work plans to meet business priorities and deadlines; identifies resources to accomplish priorities and deadlines. Identifies, speaks up, and capitalizes on improvement opportunities across teams; uses influence to guide others and engages stakeholders to achieve appropriate solutions. Promotes KPs interests by: establishing and maintaining effective relationships with elected and appointed officials, policymakers, trade associations, and other groups with minimal supervision; communicating with and influencing key external stakeholders on KP as directed; leveraging relations with strategic partners to persuade them to take positions consistent with KP with minimal supervision; and representing KP following minimal guidance. Partners with internal stakeholders on government relations by: advising key internal stakeholders and senior leadership on developments in legislation, regulations, legal proposals, public policy, key personnel changes, national/state/local issues with general guidance; independently researching approaches and solutions to key issues; leading planning efforts and response to proposed legislation, regulations, legal proposals, public policy, national/state/local issues with general guidance; and providing recommendations and communicating positioning to internal audiences as directed. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: (Core) Ambiguity/Uncertainty Management Attention to Detail Business Knowledge Communication Critical Thinking Cross-Group Collaboration Decision Making Dependability Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Support Drives Results Facilitation Skills Health Care Industry Influencing Others Integrity Learning Agility Organizational Savvy Problem Solving Short- and Long-term Learning & Recall Teamwork Topic-Specific Communication Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: (Functional) Business Documentation Business Value Communication Government Operations Information Gathering Market Risk Knowledge Persuasion Reputational Management Risk Management Written Communication Minimum Qualifications Minimum three (3) years of experience in legislative, regulatory, or government relations at the local, state, or federal level, health policy, communications, public affairs, or a directly related field. Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university AND Minimum five (5) years of professional experience (includes internship and unpaid work experience) OR Minimum eight (8) years of experience in legislative, regulatory, or government relations at the local, state, or federal level, health policy, communications, public affairs, or a directly related field. Preferred Qualifications Master’s from an accredited college or university. Experience with healthcare lobbying or policy. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Head of Government and Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Head of Government and Regulatory Affairs Organization: Resolution Life Location: Washington, DC | West Chester, PA | New York, NY Date Posted: 09/18/2026 As part of the application process, a candidate account is required to log in and view application(s). Please be sure to check email regularly for information regarding our employment process. Position Summary Resolution Life is seeking a Head of Government and Regulatory Affairs to shape, promote, and execute the company’s governmental and regulatory strategy in support of the company’s business objectives and growth priorities. The role will report to the Head of Legal & Compliance and will also work closely with the Chief Executive Officer, North America, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Legal, People & Partnerships Officer, and other senior leaders across the global business. The Head of Government and Regulatory Affairs will be accountable for establishing and operating a coordinated government and regulatory affairs function, including identifying and assessing legislative, regulatory, supervisory, and public policy developments that may affect Resolution Life, developing and implementing results-drive advocacy strategies to advance key business priorities, coordinating regulatory and government engagement, and representing the company with regulators, government officials, industry forums, and trade associations. The successful candidate will bring strong judgment, credibility with regulators and industry stakeholders, and the ability to translate complex regulatory developments into practical, business-focused advice, action plans, and executive-level recommendations. Key Responsibilities Lead and be accountable for Resolution Life’s government and regulatory affairs function, including developing and executing a proactive regulatory affairs strategy that supports Resolution Life’s business objectives and growth priorities. Develop and maintain senior relationships with regulators, policymakers, and governmental officials in the U.S. and Bermuda to promote Resolution Life’s interests. Partner with Growth & Value, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Finance, Actuarial, Investments, and Operations teams to identify, monitor, and assess legislative, regulatory, supervisory, and policy developments that could affect the company. Set enterprise standards and expectations for regulatory communications, government engagement, industry participation, issue escalation, and stakeholder briefings, working across Resolution Life’s global business to ensure a coordinated approach. Serve as a senior point of coordination for regulatory relationship management, helping ensure that interactions with regulators are consistent, well-prepared, appropriately documented, and aligned across the company. Translate complex regulatory and legislative developments into timely, practical communications and recommendations for senior leadership, business partners, boards, and relevant committees. Work with leadership and impacted business areas to determine the company’s priorities and positions on regulatory and legislative matters and develop advocacy strategies to advance those positions. Represent Resolution Life in industry trade organizations and working groups on matters affecting the life insurance and reinsurance sectors and manage the company’s relationships with such organizations. Support internal governance processes for regulatory affairs, including horizon scanning, stakeholder briefings, issue tracking, and escalation of material regulatory developments. Ensure that senior leaders and internal stakeholders are appropriately briefed before regulatory or industry engagements, including with respect to key messages, background materials, and follow-up actions. Perform other duties as required. Position Requirements Bachelor’s degree required; law degree, public policy degree or other relevant advanced degree preferred. 10+ years of relevant experience in regulatory affairs, government affairs or public policy role, including experience working with or in governmental bodies, regulatory agencies, trade associations, or highly regulated financial services organizations. Strong understanding of regulatory processes, legislative and policy development, and supervisory engagement, preferably with experience in the life insurance / reinsurance sector. Demonstrated ability to develop and implement results-driven advocacy strategies and to build credibility with regulators, policymakers, industry organizations, and senior internal stakeholders. Excellent judgment and ability to provide clear, practical advice on complex regulatory, legislative, and policy matters to individuals at every level of the company. Superior interpersonal, organizational, written, and oral communication skills, including the ability to prepare executive-level briefings, regulatory communications, and concise summaries of complex developments. Ability to work under pressure with a high degree of attention to detail, effectively prioritize and manage competing demands, and meet deadlines in a changing, fast-paced environment. Willingness and ability to travel as required. Preferred Attributes Experience engaging with Bermuda, and U.S. federal and state regulators. Experience with NAIC, ACLI, BILTIR, or other insurance industry trade associations, committees, or working groups. Knowledge of regulatory issues affecting life insurers and reinsurers, including capital, solvency, investments, risk management, and reinsurance matters. Ability to operate as a strategic advisor, external representative, and a hands-on executive who drives priorities while ensuring disciplined execution, follow-through, and stakeholder alignment. Location: West Chester, PA, New York, NY (#Hybrid – 3 days per week in the office), Washington, D.C. (#Remote) Resolution Life US is committed to disclosing a reasonable estimate of the base salary for our job roles. These estimates consider a wide range of factors in making base salary decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. In addition to salary, Resolution Life US offers a comprehensive benefits package, including our health & wellness program, incentive and recognition programs, and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). The salary range reflects figures based on the primary location, which is listed first. The range for the role may differ based on the location. West Chester, PA: $285,000 – $440,000 Washington, DC & New York, NY: $310,000 – $480,000 Critical Skills At Resolution Life, we have identified the following critical skills which are key to success in our culture: Customer Focused: Passionate drive to delight our customers and offer unique solutions that deliver on their expectations. Critical Thinking: Thoughtful process of analyzing data and problem solving data to reach a well-reasoned solution. Team Mentality: Partnering effectively to drive our culture and execute on our common goals. Business Acumen: Appreciation and understanding of the financial services industry in order to make sound business decisions. Learning Agility: Openness to new ways of thinking and acquiring new skills to retain a competitive advantage. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Regional Communications Manager
item.description: Regional Communications Manager Organization: Stand Together Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Stand Together is a philanthropic community that helps America’s boldest changemakers tackle the root causes of our country’s biggest problems, from education to the economy, broken communities, and toxic division, among dozens of other pressing issues. We provide our partners with access to resources including funding, thought leadership, a network of peers, and a playbook for applying proven principles to transform lives and society. As a Regional Communications Manager on our Stand Together Communications team, you will serve as a strategic partner to Americans for AFP (AFP), the nation’s premier grassroots advocacy organization. In this role you will serve as the communications lead supporting and promoting the wide-ranging work of Stand Together’s partners in business, government, and throughout grassroots communities across the country. You will be responsible for the implementation of all communications-related activities in your assigned states to generate positive brand awareness and position earned media opportunities. We welcome remote candidates, or this role may be based at our Arlington, VA headquarters. How You Will Contribute Partner with stakeholders across the Stand Together community to develop and implement long-term communications strategies with tactics to achieve those goals. Collaborate with respective stakeholders and capability teams to proactively identify earned media opportunities to advance policies, principles, and create a movement of millions with our shared goals. Work alongside capability teams to craft compelling, media-facing materials such as media advisories, press releases, ICYMIs, etc. Establish messaging frameworks to guide grassroots, content, digital, and creative capabilities in various efforts. Collaborate with digital and creative teams to develop collateral to maximize earned media and grassroots impact. Proactively build relationships with press, editorial boards, producers, bookers, and hosts to ensure media coverage as needed. Pitch media and place stories on events and campaign rollouts throughout the country. Identify media opportunities in traditional and non-traditional venues. Work to build relationships with in-state coalitions and influencers and establish brand identity and partnership opportunities. Advise and collaborate with stakeholders to inform messaging strategy and earned media opportunities surrounding paid media efforts, such as direct mail, TV, and radio advertisements. Prepare stakeholders for media interviews to ensure consistent messaging. Monitor and track day to day media coverage to identify outreach opportunities and inform stakeholders of emerging trends. Create rapid-response materials and backgrounders; circulate key media hits and narratives that should be addressed in each state for long-term reputation management positioning. Draft messaging and manage copy for public and grassroots-facing materials, including but not limited to landing pages, press releases, opinion pieces, website, and website blog posts. What You Will Bring 5+ years in congressional, executive branch (state or federal), political campaign or political committee, trade association, or agency experience. Experience working in multi-tiered, fast paced environments. Experience working in a state or regional capacity with media or public affairs across multiple media markets. Stakeholder, spokesperson, public relations manager or other supervisory experience. Grassroots engagement and coalitions building experience is a plus. Enthusiasm to contribute to Stand Together’s vision and principled approach to solving problems, and a commitment to stewarding our culture, which champions values including transformation and innovation, entrepreneurialism, humility, and respect. What We Offer Competitive Benefits: Enjoy a 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting, flexible time off, comprehensive health and dental plans, plus wellness and mental health support through Peloton and Talkspace. A meaningful career: Join a passionate community of over 1,300 employees dedicated to improving lives and driving innovative solutions to complex social challenges. Commitment to growth: Thrive in a non-hierarchical environment that empowers employees to discover, develop and apply their unique talents. Competitive compensation: Our approach rewards the value you create through competitive salaries and bonus opportunities, allowing you to share in the success you help drive. $90,000 – $105,000 a year For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $90,000–$105,000 per year. This role may also be eligible for additional bonus compensation designed to align total compensation with an employee’s overall contribution to the organization. Our Principles-Based Management™ (PBM) compensation philosophy is grounded in an individualized approach that rewards the long-term value each person creates for the organization. Compensation decisions are informed by a variety of factors, including relevant experience, capabilities, demonstrated skills, role responsibilities, and expected contribution. Consistent with this approach, base salary may vary within or outside of the anticipated range based on these considerations. Our Values: Working for an organization within the Stand Together philanthropic community is different from many other places. The culture is deeply rooted in Principle Based Management® (PBM®), a framework guided by the principles that drive human progress, such as dignity, openness, and bottom-up empowerment. PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. That is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, and respect. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director of Communications
item.description: Senior Director of Communications Organization: American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Reports to: Chief Executive Officer FLSA Status: Full Time – Exempt Location: Remote Salary Range: $185,000 – $215,000 Anticipated Start Date: October 2026 POSITION DESCRIPTION The Senior Communications Director is a battle-tested campaign strategist and war-room leader who operates at the speed of political campaign news cycles. Reporting to the CEO and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, the Senior Communications Director leads an aggressive, high-velocity communications engine designed to win votes, persuade targeted policymakers, and shape national narratives across federal and state battlegrounds. The Senior Director pivots instantly as news breaks, executing intra-day rapid response, deploying high-impact spokespeople, driving rapid-turnaround paid/earned/digital campaigns, and fiercely countering opponent narratives to advance ABIC’s mission and priorities. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES Proactive Narrative Framing & Campaign Execution Proactively define and drive ABIC’s national and battleground narrative; develop offensive messaging playbooks designed to persuade targeted policymakers, sway fence-sitters, and win key legislative votes on immigration solutions. Transform communications operations into a high-velocity daily campaign apparatus, constantly injecting ABIC’s narrative positioning into fast-moving news cycles to dictate media coverage across targeted state and federal markets. Rapid Response & “War-Room” Management Build and lead a nimble, “war-room” rapid-response capability to monitor breaking federal/state legislative and political developments, instantly draft counter-messaging, issue reactive press statements, and position ABIC spokespeople during high-velocity news cycles. Direct real-time media monitoring to deploy messaging, statements, and op-eds continuously throughout the day to drive headlines and control the narrative as news develops. Spokespeople Deployment & Management Build, train, and manage a rapid-deployment spokespeople group featuring business CEOs, influencers, and bipartisan coalition voices. Ensure ABIC spokespeople are prepped, cleared, and deployed onto broadcast, print, radio, and digital outlets within minutes of news breaking across key battlegrounds. Opposition Counter-Strategy & Narrative Defense Direct aggressive counter-messaging operations designed to neutralize opponent talking points, dismantle hostile narratives, and support ABIC’s priorities. Implement real-time digital and media intelligence to track opponent campaigns, identify narrative threats early, and launch immediate strategic counter-offensives. QUALIFICATIONS Campaign & War Room Record: Proven track record of executive leadership in senior level political or issue campaigns, high-stakes advocacy war rooms, or fast-paced legislative fights. Rapid Response Track Record: Demonstrated experience operating in high-pressure, rapid-response political or media environments, with a track record of driving headlines and controlling narratives during fast-moving news cycles. Intra-Day Deployment Experience: Proven ability to manage daily media cycles, pre-clear high-level surrogates, and execute rapid response across TV, radio, digital, and print throughout the day. Legislative Persuasion Focus: Deep understanding of how to align communications strategy directly with vote-counting, policymaker persuasion, and constituency mobilization under tight deadlines. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Submit a resume and cover letter to [email protected] with the subject line: Senior Director of Communications_First Name, Last Name. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT ABIC is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. We strongly encourage candidates of all backgrounds, including those from communities directly affected by immigration policy to apply. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS ABIC offers a competitive salary of $185,000 – $215,000 commensurate with experience, along with: 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance, plus 70% coverage for family Unlimited PTO and 11 paid company holidays 401(k) match up to 4% $1,000 annual Lifestyle Spending Account Additional benefits including life and disability insurance, an Employee Assistance Program, telemedicine, and a monthly cell phone stipend are outlined in full for candidates during the offer process. ABOUT ABIC The American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) promotes common sense immigration reform that advances economic competitiveness, provides companies with the talent they need, and allows the integration of immigrants into our economy as consumers, workers, entrepreneurs, and citizens. ABIC members include CEOs, retired CEOs, business associations, small business owners as well as hospitals and universities. ABIC works in partnership with diverse immigrant advocates to support pro-immigrant legislation at the state and federal levels. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director of Policy and Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Director of Policy and Government Affairs Organization: American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Reports to: Chief Executive Officer FLSA Status: Full Time – Exempt Location: Remote and in person (Must be based in Washington, DC) Anticipated Start Date: January 2027 Salary Range: $185,000 – $215,000 POSITION SUMMARY The American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) is seeking a seasoned, politically astute, and deeply passionate individual to serve as our Senior Director of Policy and Government Affairs to report to the Chief Executive Officer. This individual will develop the ABIC’s strategy for building support among federal and some key state elected officials for its common sense immigration policy campaigns. This includes driving ABIC’s analysis of policy proposals, managing relationships with elected officials’ offices, and ensuring ABIC’s Field team and business leader supporters are effectively advocating with electeds. Capitol Hill experience prioritized. ABIC is interested in candidates who are looking to apply their policy and relationship-building expertise on the Hill to a mission-driven advocacy organization. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES Build a Policy and Government Affairs Strategy: Lead organizational efforts to build and activate support among elected officials for ABIC-supported common sense immigration solutions, including but not limited to: Providing a high-level analysis of federal and some key state policy proposals that impact immigration, immigrant workforces, and sectors of the economy reliant on immigrant workers. Working with the Campaign Director, National Field Director and Field staff to identify, develop, assess and adjust policy opportunities and strategies related to ABIC campaigns. Conducting research that identifies the specific immigration-related political, economic or business interests of concern to elected officials or their districts, in conjunction with other field team members. Identifying priority elected officials to build relationships with and sharpening arguments to win their support. Policy and Advocacy Skills Training and Development: Design, build and implement a training and mentoring process that prepares the staff and business leader supporters to advocate for ABIC’s common sense immigration solutions, working in conjunction with the National Field Director and field team. Prepare state of play updates and educational programs for ABIC staff and business leader supporters. Legislative Strategy Execution: Ensure ABIC is building (across its staff and business leader supporters) meaningful relationships with priority Senators and Members of Congress, Congressional offices, committees and caucuses, the White House and Administration officials. Develop systems to track elected officials’ degree of support and leadership on ABIC’s issues and ABIC’s engagement with electeds. Ensure ABIC communications and outreach to electeds are well coordinated and strategic. In key states work with Field team members to identify and assess key pieces of state legislation; help map key state electeds; and propose possible state advocacy campaign strategies. Identify missing segments of the business community and other constituencies that might be important for ABIC to be engaging in order to reach key elected officials. Identify and drive the creation of policy-related materials and tactics. Build and maintain a cadre of key relationships with employer members, bipartisan lawmakers, and/or organizational allies around legislative strategy. Regularly communicate and identify when and how ABIC can best partner and drive the organization toward effective partnerships. Organizational Leadership: Lead subsections of our organizational planning processes. Represent ABIC in external meetings, conferences, discussions, etc. Provide input and information in support of campaign, communications, and fundraising strategy related to policy/GA issues. Work with colleagues in other departments to help coordinate work. Take on other tasks as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS A deep commitment to advocating for a path to citizenship and comfort and ease advocating for undocumented immigrants. At least 7-10 years experience working directly for a Member of Congress, the White House, Department or a Congressional Committee, or advocating with Members of Congress. Can leverage in-depth knowledge of the legislative and administrative process and procedures, rulemaking, executive actions, to develop proactive strategies to advance ABIC priorities. Substantive knowledge of policy related to immigration and economic development. Experience analyzing policy proposals and communicating their impact to a broad range of stakeholders. Skills in training, mentoring, and developing staff and community or business leaders’ skills in understanding and advocating for policy. Committed to and capable of engaging with and messaging to partners, lawmakers, constituencies from a vast range of political leanings from the right to the left. Experience with organizing unlikely allies, businesses, rural and faith leaders, and a willingness to work with electeds from both parties. Strong understanding of national and state political and electoral landscape and how best to make strategic impact at scale. Experience developing, writing, and executing successful policy advocacy plans that demonstrate strategic focus and creativity. Proficient with data, polling, the latest campaign technologies, and best practices in the field, including the ability to learn various systems for data tracking, email, mobile, volunteer recruitment, and fundraising. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Submit a resume and cover letter to [email protected] with the subject line: Senior Director of Policy and Government Affairs_ First Name, Last Name. Cover letters should speak to relevant policy or Hill experience and interest in immigration policy. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT ABIC is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. We strongly encourage candidates of all backgrounds, including those from communities directly affected by immigration policy to apply. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS ABIC offers a competitive salary of $185,000 – $215,000, commensurate with experience, along with: 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance, plus 70% coverage for family Unlimited PTO and 11 paid company holidays 401(k) match up to 4% $1,000 annual Lifestyle Spending Account Additional benefits including life and disability insurance, an Employee Assistance Program, telemedicine, and a monthly cell phone stipend are outlined in full for candidates during the offer process. Ecke is a Muskogee word for “mother” and reflects the role of the holding company. PCI Federal provides the common connection and integration that enables our collective success. Our portfolio of companies share the Tribe’s values of fairness, trustworthiness, commitment to something bigger than self, perseverance, respect for contribution, open, and honest communication, collaboration, open to new ideas and accomplishment. Through these values, PCI Federal focuses on delivering exceptional services that exceed our customers’ expectations. At PCI Federal, we are passionate about helping our employees meet their professional goals and achieve success, while maintaining work/life balance. We offer an excellent benefits package that includes vacation and personal time off, as well as a generous 401(k) match. Position: Communication Strategist II Location: Edwards, CA Remote Status: On-Site Communication Strategist II – Strategic Aircraft Operations Liaison Hiring Company: PCI Productions (PCI‑P) Location: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center, Edwards, CA Contract: NASA Communication Services (NCS) Contract Position Type: Full-Time, On-Site Clearance: U.S. Citizenship Required Position Overview PCI‑P is seeking a Strategic Communications Specialist II to serve as a communications liaison supporting NASA Armstrong’s role as the agency’s Flight Test & Aircraft Operations Center of Excellence. This position delivers operationally aligned communications expertise for aircraft capabilities, research flight operations, developmental programs, airborne science missions, and specialized aviation facilities. The role also provides surge capacity for high‑visibility missions, media engagement, and emergency or contingency communications. Key Responsibilities 1. Enterprise & Mission Coordination Serve as a liaison between Armstrong’s communications and aircraft operations teams and NASA HQ’s Office of Communications, mission directorates, projects, and partner centers. Ensure aircraft operations and flight test communication products align with enterprise messaging, clearance processes, and agency priorities. Support multi‑center coordination for cross‑center flight projects. 2. Flight Test & Aircraft Operations Communications Maintain awareness of aircraft schedules, capabilities, mission readiness, test milestones, demonstrations, and facility activities. Provide story development, media support, and on-site communications during flight test operations, airborne research campaigns, developmental aircraft activities, and specialized demonstrations. 3. Media & Public Affairs Support Respond to media queries and develop accurate, timely messaging informed by operational realities and subject‑matter experts. Support news releases, media coordination, features, public information responses, and other aviation‑related communications products. 4. Surge & Contingency Support Provide scalable communications support during peak mission periods, major events, VIP visits, or high‑visibility milestones. Strengthen Armstrong’s readiness for emergency, mishap, or contingency communications. 5. Cross‑Mission Integration & Emerging Projects Support early-stage or emerging aviation-related projects, including new aircraft modifications, research campaigns, and specialized flight demonstrations. Collaborate with pilots, flight operations personnel, engineers, and project managers to develop accurate communication plans and products. Required Skills & Competencies Strong understanding of aviation, flight operations, aircraft systems, or demonstrated ability to rapidly learn complex operational environments. Excellent writing skills (writing samples required). Ability to translate complex technical and operational content into clear, accessible messaging for the public. Experience in public affairs, media engagement, and strategic or enterprise-level communications. Ability to work effectively in fast-paced operational environments with shifting priorities. Familiarity with NASA communications standards, clearance processes, enterprise tools, and crisis communications protocols. Preferred Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, aviation communication, or a related field. Experience supporting aviation, aerospace, or government programs. Experience providing on-site support for operational activities or field campaigns. About PCI Productions (PCI‑P) PCI‑P is part of the PCI Federal Services group of companies and delivers high‑quality communications support to NASA and other federal customers. We are committed to supporting our team members through competitive benefits, professional development, and meaningful mission-focused work. PCI Federal (PCIF) and its subsidiaries are an equal-opportunity employer. PCIF does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, national origin, religion, marital status, sexual orientation or identity, Veterans or Disability status. Preference may be extended to qualified Native American Indian candidates in accordance with applicable federal law.
