item.title: Chief Operating Officer
item.description: Chief Operating Officer Organization: National Disability Rights Network (NDRN) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 The National Disability Rights Network seeks a strategic, collaborative, and results-oriented Chief Operating Officer to help lead a national civil rights organization advancing the rights of people with disabilities. As NDRN’s chief internal leader and strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the COO will strengthen organizational effectiveness, align resources with strategic priorities, and enhance NDRN’s capacity to advance disability rights nationwide. Who We Are The National Disability Rights Network (NDRN) is the nonprofit membership organization for the federally mandated Protection and Advocacy (P&A) Systems and Client Assistance Programs (CAP) serving people with disabilities nationwide. Collectively, the P&A System is the nation’s largest provider of legal advocacy for people with disabilities, advancing civil and human rights through systemic advocacy, litigation, and policy reform. Through advocacy, training, technical assistance, legal support, public policy leadership, and network capacity building, NDRN works to advance the rights, inclusion, and self-determination of people with disabilities nationwide. About the Role Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO will translate organizational priorities into coordinated action, strengthen accountability for results, and align NDRN’s policy, legal, programmatic, and network-support functions. The COO will oversee major grants and contracts, lead and develop four directors, advance organizational performance, and ensure NDRN’s people, systems, and resources are aligned to achieve strategic objectives and mission impact. The CEO serves as NDRN’s primary external leader, focused on advocacy, fundraising, coalition building, government relations, public engagement, and governance. The COO complements that leadership by providing executive oversight of internal operations, strengthening organizational alignment, and ensuring strategic priorities are translated into measurable results. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to disability rights, accessibility, equal opportunity, and fostering an organizational culture where employees are respected, empowered, and able to succeed. Core Competencies Strategic Leadership & Execution Organizational Effectiveness & Accountability People Leadership & Talent Development Collaboration & Cross-Functional Leadership Grants, Contracts & Resource Stewardship Policy & Advocacy Acumen Relationship Management & Influence Mission-Driven Leadership & Commitment to Disability Rights Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness Partner with the CEO to implement organizational priorities and strategic goals. Lead the execution of enterprise-wide initiatives and organizational work plans. Ensure alignment and collaboration across departments and functions. Establish systems that promote accountability, performance measurement, and continuous improvement. Monitor progress toward organizational goals and recommend operational improvements. Leadership & Talent Development Directly supervise four directors and provide coaching, mentorship, and leadership development. Establish clear expectations and accountability measures for direct reports. Lead the recruitment, selection, performance management, and professional development of direct-report staff, in partnership with Human Resources as appropriate. Partner with the Human Resources Director to ensure timely performance evaluations, professional development planning, and succession planning throughout the organization. Foster a culture of inclusion, collaboration, accountability, and excellence. Grants, Contracts & Organizational Accountability Provide executive oversight of federal grants, cooperative agreements, contracts, and foundation-funded initiatives. Ensure compliance with funding requirements and successful completion of deliverables. Monitor project implementation, outcomes, and reporting obligations. Support the development and implementation of strategic funding opportunities. Policy, Program & Network Coordination Ensure effective coordination among NDRN’s policy, legal, programmatic, technical assistance, and network-support activities. Promote cross-functional collaboration to maximize organizational impact. Support initiatives that strengthen the Protection and Advocacy (P&A) Network. Ensure organizational activities align with strategic priorities and funding requirements. Executive & Board Support Support the CEO in preparing materials and reports for the Board of Directors. Participate in Board and committee meetings as requested. Provide updates regarding organizational performance, strategic initiatives, and operational priorities. This is an exceptional opportunity to serve as the chief internal leader of the nation’s leading legal advocacy membership organization for the P&A System and the Client Assistance Programs, helping drive organizational excellence, mission impact, and long-term sustainability. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience. Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience, including significant experience leading senior staff, managing complex organizational initiatives, and overseeing cross-functional operations. Demonstrated success leading senior leaders and high-performing teams in complex organizational environments. Proven ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable outcomes and drive execution across multiple functions or programs. Significant experience overseeing complex grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, or other externally funded initiatives, including accountability for performance, compliance, and results. Experience managing organizational change, improving operational effectiveness, and implementing systems that strengthen accountability and performance. Demonstrated success building collaborative relationships and influencing decision-making across diverse stakeholders, including executive leadership, boards, funders, coalition partners, and external organizations. Experience engaging with congressional offices, federal agencies, national coalitions, or other high-level stakeholder groups. Exceptional leadership, communication, relationship management, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated commitment to disability rights and advancing the mission and values of NDRN. Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree in public policy, public administration, business administration, law, nonprofit management, organizational leadership, or a related field. Fifteen or more years of executive or senior leadership experience. Leadership experience in disability rights, civil rights, health, human services, or social justice sectors. Experience working for a national nonprofit, membership association, advocacy organization, or federally funded entity. Familiarity with the Protection and Advocacy (P&A) Network, disability rights law and policy, or related civil rights systems. Experience working with Congress, federal appropriations, federal grant-making agencies, or national public policy initiatives. Experience supporting boards of directors and governance processes. Experience leading organizational growth, strategic transformation, or agency-wide change initiatives. Compensation & Benefits Salary range: $190,000 – $200,000 Location: This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC. Candidates from outside the Washington, DC, Maryland, and Virginia (DMV) region are encouraged to apply. Exceptional candidates will be considered based on qualifications and experience. Benefits: A comprehensive benefits package including health, dental and vision insurance, paid time off and holidays, retirement plan options, and a flexible work environment. item.title: Account Director
item.description: Account Director Organization: Beekeeper Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Beekeeper Group seeks an Account Director with direct experience in strategic communications, social media, and advertising in the policy/advocacy space for our growing Hive! We are looking for people who love a challenge and are not afraid of tackling multiple projects and building strong client relationships for a variety of clients simultaneously. Experience working for an advocacy organization, public affairs agency, political consulting firm, or campaign is a major plus – but not a deal-breaker. Our ideal candidate will build their own practice within the Beekeeper Group framework, can write anything from reports to social media posts, possesses great digital savvy, and can quickly learn about complex policy issues and technology. If you aren’t afraid of diving in and getting it done, we want to hear from you! What will you be doing? Managing direct client relationships Overseeing day-to-day activities on client accounts Interfacing with both internal and external teams Growing, managing, and mentoring a team of account support staff Actively manage, develop, inspire, and motivate staff to excel Anticipate potential challenges and evaluate strategies with senior leadership Provide expert communications and/or advocacy counsel to clients in line with their respective business priorities Overseeing operational performance of accounts, ensuring quality work, deadline, and budget adherence Effectively lead account teams on complex communications challenges and in the creation of communications plans and goals; manage against them Recognize and apply impactful communications trends, and translate those insights into actionable ideas Working closely with account team to ensure high-quality and timely delivery of internal and external work to the overall satisfaction of assigned clients and supervisors Coordinating multiple aspects of client campaigns, as well as digital projects, including website designs and development Building networks and supporting new business opportunity efforts Identify emerging opportunities to add greater value for clients Formulating reporting formats that showcase firm’s efforts and meet client needs Writing memos, analyses, and case studies Writing in a succinct and skilled manner; also proofing junior team members’ work product Identifying and building relationships with client community stakeholders Developing actionable strategies for blogs and social media Skills 5-7 years full-time experience Ability to multitask with shifting priorities based on client needs Comfortable working on tight deadlines and in a team environment Basic familiarity with paid social advertising Superior strategic thinking, writing, and presentation skills required Experience managing budgets and teams Experience managing multiple social media accounts simultaneously A strong desire to stay aware of the trends in communications and public affairs Knowledge of social media scheduling software Familiarity with monitoring metrics Compensation The annual compensation for this role is between $90k-$110k, with the expectation that a successful candidate will be able to leverage our competitive business incentive structure (details available upon request). Applicants can apply here at Beekeeper Group.com Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Executive Director, Federal Government Relations
item.description: Executive Director, Federal Government Relations Organization: Kaiser Permanente Location: Washington, DC | Oakland, CA Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Job Summary The Executive Director, Federal Government Relations – D.C. Office serves as a senior federal advocate responsible for advancing Kaiser Permanente’s federal legislative agenda. Reporting to the Vice President, Federal Government Relations, this role leads advocacy strategies across an assigned portfolio of enterprise priorities and represents Kaiser Permanente before Congress, congressional committees, and other key federal stakeholders. The Executive Director is a senior lobbyist responsible for developing and executing comprehensive advocacy strategies that build congressional support for Kaiser Permanente’s policy objectives. Working in close partnership with policy leaders, public affairs, and internal stakeholders, this position translates organizational priorities into coordinated federal engagement strategies that advance Kaiser Permanente’s integrated, value-based care model. The ideal candidate is a strategic, mission-driven government relations leader with deep knowledge of the federal legislative process and established credibility on Capitol Hill. This individual must understand and champion Kaiser Permanente’s commitment to high-quality, affordable, equitable, and prevention-focused health care, and effectively communicate the organization’s policy positions to lawmakers, congressional staff, trade associations, coalition partners, and external stakeholders. Based in Washington, D.C., the Executive Director develops and maintains senior relationships with Members of Congress, committee staff, and key external organizations aligned with assigned issue priorities. This role leads lobbying efforts on the organization’s highest-priority federal issues, coordinates advocacy strategies across relevant trade associations and coalitions, and partners closely with colleagues across Kaiser Permanente to ensure consistent, enterprise-wide alignment on legislative priorities. The Executive Director also provides leadership and mentorship to assigned staff, manages approximately one to two direct reports, and contributes to the continued growth and effectiveness of Kaiser Permanente’s federal affairs function through collaboration, strategic insight, and operational excellence. Essential Responsibilities * Lead the development and execution of comprehensive federal advocacy strategies for an assigned portfolio of Kaiser Permanente’s highest-priority legislative issues. * Serve as a senior advocate before Congress, congressional committees, and other federal policymakers on assigned issue priorities. * Develop and maintain strategic relationships with Members of Congress, senior congressional staff, committee staff, and key Administration officials. * Support Kaiser Permanente’s engagement with national trade associations, coalitions, and external stakeholders aligned with assigned legislative priorities. * Identify legislative opportunities and risks, develop advocacy strategies, and recommend courses of action to advance enterprise objectives. * Partner with Policy, Public Affairs, Permanente Medical Groups, Risant Health, and other enterprise leaders to ensure alignment on federal legislative priorities and advocacy strategies. * Provide strategic counsel and policy updates to senior leaders regarding congressional activity, political developments, and legislative strategy. * Develop congressional champions and expand Kaiser Permanente’s influence with key policymakers and stakeholders. * Supervise, coach, and develop assigned Directors while fostering a collaborative, high-performing advocacy team. * Represent Kaiser Permanente at congressional hearings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and other external events. * Support the Vice President in advancing departmental priorities, strategic initiatives, and organizational objectives. * Ensure advocacy activities are conducted in compliance with all applicable lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements. Basic Qualifications Experience * Minimum twelve (12) years of relevant professional experience. * Minimum ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in federal, state, or local government relations, legislative affairs, health policy, public affairs, communications, or a closely related field. * Minimum five (5) years of experience leading complex advocacy initiatives, government relations functions, teams, or high-profile legislative campaigns. Education * Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university or four (4) years of experience in a directly related field required. * High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED) required. License, Certification, Registration * N/A Additional Requirements * Demonstrated success developing and executing legislative advocacy strategies, influencing public policy outcomes, and building trusted relationships with Members of Congress, congressional committees, federal agencies, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications * Significant experience advocating on federal health care policy issues. * Experience working with Congress, the Executive Branch, a national health care organization, trade association, congressional office, or federal agency. * Demonstrated experience advising senior executives on legislative strategy, political developments, and advocacy priorities. * Experience leading cross-functional teams and building consensus across complex organizations. Primary Location District of Columbia, Washington, Government Relations Offices Additional Locations Oakland, CA Job Details * Job number: 1438322 * Scheduled Weekly Hours: 40 * Shift: Day * Workdays: Mon – Fri * Working Hours Start: 08:00 AM * Working Hours End: 05:00 PM * Job Schedule: Full-time * Job Type: Standard * Employee Status: Regular * Worker Location: Flexible * Employee Group/Union Affiliation: NUE Executives | NUE | Non Union Employee * Job Level: Director/Senior Director * Department: Po/Ho Corp – Gov Relations-Oakland – 0308 * Pay Range: $247,500 – $309,375 / year Kaiser Permanente strives to offer a market competitive total rewards package and is committed to pay equity and transparency. The posted pay range is based on possible base salaries for the role and does not reflect the full value of our total rewards package. Actual base pay determined at offer will be based on labor market data, internal alignment, and a candidate’s years of relevant work experience, education, certifications, skills, and geographic location. * Travel: Yes, 25% of the Time Kaiser Permanente is an equal opportunity employer committed to fair, respectful, and inclusive workplaces. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic or status. item.title: Senior Director, Federal Policy
item.description: Senior Director, Federal Policy Organization: Corporate Energy Buyers Association (CEBA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Chaloner has partnered with the Corporate Energy Buyers Association on the search for a Senior Director, Federal Policy to join their team. Our Guiding Values and Tenets The Corporate Energy Buyers Association is a business association with a mission to activate buyers and partners to advance low-cost, reliable, carbon-emissions free global energy systems. We are grounded in respect for people and the planet, integrity in how we conduct ourselves, service to our mission, stakeholders, and colleagues, and excellence in all of our programs and work. At CEBA, we strive to foster a culture that is mission-driven and strategy-grounded, built on a spirit of partnership both within and beyond our organization, and energized by innovation and entrepreneurship through healthy, respectful dialogue. Position Overview Reporting to the SVP, Policy, the Senior Director, Federal Policy will set and lead CEBA’s federal policy agenda — owning the positions that inform how CEBA advocates at the federal level and shaping the strategic priorities the organization pursues. This position is responsible for shaping and driving CEBA’s federal policy and strategy, informed by member priorities, and engagement with federal policymakers. The Senior Director, Federal serves as a visible representative of CEBA, exercising independent judgment in complex policy environments and translating member priorities into effective federal policy outcomes. The position offers a hybrid work arrangement, with team collaboration days on Mondays and Wednesdays and one additional in-office day each week, determined by team priorities. Core Responsibilities Federal Policy Strategy & Leadership Set and lead CEBA’s federal policy agenda, establishing policy priorities on access to carbon-emissions-free energy, transmission and interconnection, permitting, financing, and critical issues affecting members. Direct the monitoring and assessment of actions from federal agencies and commissions, the White House, and Congress, ensuring CEBA anticipates and responds to developments affecting members. Identify opportunities for CEBA input and public comment, and guide the development of comments, testimony materials, and policy submissions. Serve as a senior strategic partner to CEBA’s Government Affairs team, setting the sequencing and prioritization of federal policy asks and ensuring advocacy is grounded in rigorous, member-informed analysis. Manage the development of CEBA’s thought leadership platform on federal policy, including presentations, white papers, reports, and policy briefs. Serve as a voice in trade association meetings, industry coalitions, and policy forums, coordinating closely with Government Affairs to ensure consistent messaging. Partner cross-functionally with Government Affairs, Communications, and other senior leaders to align policy development with advocacy execution and organizational strategy. Represent CEBA’s federal policy positions to member executives, the Board, and industry leadership as needed. Member Engagement & Communication Lead CEBA’s federal policy working groups and convenings, setting agendas and ensuring outcomes are documented and acted upon. Develop member communications and briefing materials on major federal policy developments. Represent CEBA at industry conferences and events as a senior subject-matter expert on federal clean energy policy. Performs other related duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Minimum 10 years of experience in electricity, clean energy, corporate sustainability, utilities, or related fields. Deep working knowledge of energy and electricity policy, with a track record of shaping policy positions at the federal level. Demonstrated experience leading policy analysis, market development, regulatory engagement, or program strategy in a senior or leadership capacity. Proven ability to partner effectively across departments — particularly with Government Affairs leadership — to translate policy analysis into advocacy strategy. Ability to work in-person three days per week at CEBA’s Washington, D.C. office. In-office days are Monday and Wednesday, with a floating third day. Willingness to travel up to 10% as needed. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing or mentoring staff, and leading cross-functional or multi-stakeholder initiatives. Knowledge of corporate, industrial, and institutional clean energy policy priorities and strategies. Senior-level experience working with federal agencies and commissions, Capitol Hill, or utilities. Excellent judgment and communication skills, with experience presenting to senior executives, Boards, or similarly senior audiences. Familiarity with federal agency and/or regulatory processes or Congress. Extraordinary interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence. Supervisory Responsibilities No direct reports. Compensation and Benefits The expected base salary for this role ranges from $180,000 to $200,000, depending on experience and qualifications. All CEBA employees are eligible to participate in the annual bonus incentive plan, which is based on both organizational and individual performance, up to 20% for this role. CEBA provides a competitive benefits package that includes highly-subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance plans. In addition, CEBA offers employer-paid life and disability coverage (both short- and long-term), monthly cell phone stipends, optional flexible spending and savings accounts, a comprehensive Employee Assistance Program, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and an attractive 401(k) match of up to 5%, subject to IRS limitations. Along with 11 federal holidays, paid time off during the period between Christmas and New Year’s, and Sick & Safe leave, employees also enjoy unlimited PTO. At CEBA You Belong CEBA knows that inclusiveness not only makes our organization stronger but also is foundational to our mission success because innovative solutions come from great minds who do not think alike. Our commitment to inclusiveness is embodied in company policy and the way we do business at CEBA and is an important principle of sound business management. All CEBA staff shall be committed to accepting and encouraging different perspectives. Creative solutions to tough problems are fostered by respectful challenges of one another’s thoughts and assumptions. CEBA provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, gender expression, results of genetic testing, caregiver status, and past, present or prospective service in the military in addition to any other protected categories required by state, federal or local regulations. Equal employment opportunities apply to all terms and conditions of employment, including hiring, placement, discipline, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leave of absence, compensation, benefits and training. All of your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. To Apply To be considered for this opportunity, please provide a resume and cover letter. Interested candidates should apply by using the application form here . Chaloner will review all applicants and, upon qualification, contact you to determine next steps. item.title: Public Affairs Associate
item.description: Public Affairs Associate Organization: Ralph Lauren Corporation Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Pay Range: The pay range for this job is $62000 – $95935 annually; actual pay is dependent on experience and geographic location. Benefits: Base pay is only one part of our employee value proposition, which includes a robust benefits package, above-market time off, hybrid working arrangements, incentive compensation, where applicable, and varied learning opportunities. COMPANY DESCRIPTION Ralph Lauren Corporation (NYSE:RL) is a global leader in the design, marketing and distribution of premium lifestyle products in five categories: apparel, accessories, home, fragrances, and hospitality. For more than 50 years, Ralph Lauren’s reputation and distinctive image have been consistently developed across an expanding number of products, brands and international markets. The Company’s brand names, which include Ralph Lauren, Ralph Lauren Collection, Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Double RL, Lauren Ralph Lauren, Polo Ralph Lauren Children, Chaps, among others, constitute one of the world’s most widely recognized families of consumer brands. At Ralph Lauren, we unite and inspire the communities within our company as well as those in which we serve by amplifying voices and perspectives to create a culture of belonging, ensuring inclusion, and fairness for all. We foster a culture of inclusion through: Talent, Education & Communication, Employee Groups and Celebration. POSITION OVERVIEW The Ralph Lauren Public Affairs team is looking for a highly organized, detail-oriented and entrepreneurial candidate who can help us maintain and strengthen Ralph Lauren’s reputation as well as advance our public policy and advocacy priorities. The role requires an understanding of the political, social and economic landscape in key markets where Ralph Lauren operates as well as the ability to quickly identify and react to emerging issues in these regions. Job responsibilities include a wide range of projects, such as tracking legislation, initiating policy research and analysis, drafting communications and issues briefs, creating presentations and maintaining team calendars and project trackers. You will report to the Director of Public Affairs and interface with a range of teams across the business, including Sustainability, Citizenship, Sourcing, Legal, Corporate Communications and the Local Commercial teams. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES ​​​Monitor, analyze and report on global and regional policy trends, legislation and developments that impact Ralph Lauren’s business operations or reputation. Support cross-functional issues management and the development of risk mitigation strategies to maintain and strengthen the company’s reputation. Draft communications and engage with a range of stakeholders to advance Ralph Lauren’s public policy and advocacy priorities. Build and strengthen Ralph Lauren’s engagement with its associations and memberships. Develop briefings for executive engagements with government officials. ​Coordinate with key business partners including but not limited to global corporate communications, sourcing, sustainability, citizenship, legal and the local commercial teams to develop policy positions and align on advocacy needs across the organization. Develop public affairs strategies to support major Company or Foundation announcements. ​Review company communications from a policy, geopolitical and reputational lens. Update KPIs as part of quarterly reporting to measure effectiveness of engagement. ​Keep workstreams on track and share updates on a weekly basis.​​ EXPERIENCE, SKILLS & KNOWLEDGE ​​​2-3 years of public affairs or communications experience ideally in an agency, in-house or in a political environment. Bachelor’s Degree in areas of communications, political science, international relations or a comparable field is preferred. ​Excellent verbal and written communications skills. Creative and entrepreneurial mindset. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and ability to multitask. Ability to comprehend and effectively synthesize complex information, especially related to public policy and issues in the news. ​Ability to work closely and effectively with others—including senior management, business partners and external partners. Excellent time and project management skills.​​ Ralph Lauren will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in a manner consistent with the requirements of the law, including any applicable fair chance laws. Please note background checks will be evaluated individually. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Head of Government Affairs
item.description: Head of Government Affairs Organization: Einride Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Want to be part of transforming road freight? Einride is showing the world a new way to move, based on the latest digital, autonomous and electric technologies. We build the technology that hauls freight efficiently, and we put it to work for the world’s leading manufacturers, retailers, logistics providers and defense organizations, all working toward a future where moving goods cost less for our customers, and less for the planet. Founded in 2016, Einride became the first company in the world to deploy a cab-less autonomous electric vehicle on a public road (Sweden, 2019). In 2022, we were the first to successfully operate such a vehicle on a U.S. public road. In June 2026, Einride became a publicly listed company on Nasdaq, a milestone that reflects a decade of turning what once looked like science fiction into everyday reality. Today, our technology moves freight across North America, Europe, and the Middle East for some of the world’s biggest shippers. You will: Formulate and execute proactive legislative and regulatory strategies to enable driverless autonomous freight operations across target markets. Build and maintain high impact relationships with key decision makers across the U.S. Congress, USDOT, NHTSA, FMCSA, and relevant state regulators. Represent Einride in industry associations, policy coalitions, and regulatory workshops to shape industry wide transport and autonomous vehicle standards. Partner with internal Autonomous Technology, Safety, and Legal teams to translate technical systems and safety cases into compelling policy positions. Coordinate policy strategy across target U.S. states and identify relevant federal and state grant opportunities. Provide strategic policy alignment across global initiatives, serving as an advisor on European regulatory developments and international market expansion as needed. We expect you to have: Extensive senior level public policy background, with a strong preference for expertise at the intersection of autonomous technology and freight mobility. Prior experience working within the U.S. government, particularly USDOT, key regulatory agencies, or relevant Congressional committees. An established, trusted network across Capitol Hill, executive branch agencies, and the broader D.C. transport policy ecosystem. Exceptional communication skills, with a proven track record of translating complex regulatory and technical concepts for policymakers. Exposure to European transport policy, international regulatory bodies (e.g., EU frameworks, UNECE), or global government affairs strategy is a plus. What we offer: Competitive salary and incentive program Health, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) with company match Paid time off and holidays The salary range is between 260-310k This is a full-time position based in Washington DC. We recommend that you submit your application as soon as possible since selection and interviews are held continually. Please note that as part of our standard recruitment process, we conduct a background control on the final candidate for this role. This may include verification of education, employment history, any relevant professional certifications or other information that may be of our interest. Born autonomous. Born electric. Since 2016, our technology has connected global communities with the things they need – and all without the emissions. We’re made up of experts in multiple fields and that’s how we’ve developed a new way to move goods. This is technology purpose-built for the industry. This is safer, cleaner, and more reliable movement. We are Einride and this is how we build a better future. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: VP of Government Affairs & Strategic Projects
item.description: VP of Government Affairs & Strategic Projects Organization: Subcritical Systems Inc. Location: Austin, TX Date Posted: 09/21/2026 ABOUT SUBCRITICAL SYSTEMS Subcritical Systems, Inc. is a venture-backed startup in Austin, Texas building the accelerator driven systems and the only US commercial manufacturer of accelerator cavities. What Space X did for rockets, we plan to do for accelerator cavities and commercialize across applications of power production, medical isotopes, semiconductors and waste transmutation. We are in the process of building the Energy Amplifier — a novel nuclear fission system in which a particle accelerator drives a subcritical core, making meltdown physically impossible for clean power production. Due to its inherent safety, our system has a more streamlined licensing process. Our founding team includes successful entrepreneurs with a track record of building several multibillion dollar companies in deep-tech, and scientists who were leading U.S. national labs with deep experience in accelerator & nuclear technologies. We are actively hiring to expand our team as we work toward licensing, regulatory submissions, and construction of our first energy amplifier. More information is available at subcritical.com. ROLE SUMMARY Subcritical is seeking a senior Government Affairs leader to build and lead the company’s government relations function from the ground up, with responsibility for developing and executing a coordinated federal, state, and local strategy. You will manage relationships with Congress, DOE, and NRC to advance siting, licensing, and funding pathways, while leading state and local engagement in target siting markets, beginning with Texas. As the company’s primary advocate with policymakers and regulators, you will translate government engagement into tangible outcomes and ensure policy, regulatory, and funding realities inform site selection and deployment strategy. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead with corresponding Technical Team Key Projects from strategy to successful completion Develop a strategy and work with nuclear leadership on successfully setting up nuclear waste transmutation program Engage in DOE/DOW/Commerce funding and partnership opportunities Work on Government projects currently in discussion: Defense application, Fusion Prototypic Material Testing (FPNS), Energy Dominance Financing Federal CHIPS award as Subcritical has already received state CHIPS funding Federal Engagement Build the nuclear waste transmutation project of accelerator-driven technology Build and manage relationships with Congress, DOE, DOW, and other relevant federal agencies to advance siting, licensing, and funding priorities Track and pursue federal funding opportunities (DOE programs, loan guarantees, grants) aligned with deployment milestones Develop and execute federal tax and appropriations strategy, including engagement with tax-writing committees (Senate Finance, House Ways & Means) on nuclear tax credit and incentive policy Monitor federal legislative and regulatory developments affecting advanced nuclear siting and permitting Draft policy positions, comment letters, and advocacy materials for federal proceedings, press and community engagement State & Local Engagement Develop and execute a state and local government relations strategy for target siting markets, starting with Matagorda County and the state of Texas Build relationships with state legislators, the Governor’s office, relevant state agencies, and local officials in host communities Engage state utility/siting regulators and monitor legislation relevant to advanced nuclear deployment Build a legislative-monitoring system to track policy trends across priority states Compliance & Coordination Manage outside lobbyists and consultants; ensure compliance with federal and state Lobbying Disclosure Act requirements Coordinate cross-functionally with legal, regulatory, and site development teams to align GR strategy with deployment timelines Brief executive leadership on policy developments, funding opportunities, and stakeholder dynamics Represent the company in industry coalitions and trade associations QUALIFICATIONS Required Working knowledge of the federal legislative process, appropriations, and/or state legislative and regulatory processes Demonstrated relationships with congressional offices, federal agencies, and/or state policymakers Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfort drafting testimony and policy materials Willingness to travel U.S. citizenship (required for compliance with nuclear-related export control regulations) Preferred Experience in energy, nuclear, or infrastructure policy specifically Experience managing outside lobbyists/consultants BENEFITS Benefits: We offer health, dental, and vision insurance. LOCATION & WORK POLICY This role is fully remote, with some limited travel to our HQ in Austin as required. HOW TO APPLY Submit your resume and a brief cover letter to [email protected] with the subject line “VP of Government Affairs – Application”. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. item.title: Federal Government Relations – Executive Director
item.description: Federal Government Relations – Executive Director Organization: JPMorgan Chase Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Base Pay/Salary Washington, DC $190,000.00-$300,000.00 Job Description Global Government Relations (GGR) is housed within Corporate Responsibility and is responsible for developing and implementing a comprehensive policy, regulatory and advocacy strategy on behalf of JPMorgan Chase. This includes engaging in balanced advocacy with regulators and policymakers, understanding and providing thought leadership on how policies affect the firm’s clients and economic growth overall, and governing internal coordination among regions and lines of business on global regulatory reform issues. As an Executive Director within the Federal Government Relations (FGR) team, you will be working in collaboration with the Global Government Relations Team to oversee legislative activities, scrutinize policy and political trends, and enlighten Congressional and Executive Branch public officials on matters of mutual interest. Your responsibilities will also include closely liaising with the firm’s business lines and clients to comprehend emerging issues, and to devise, support, and advocate for the progression of public policy priorities that influence the firm and our clients. Job Responsibilities Own a portfolio of priority federal legislative issues, setting advocacy strategy and driving end-to-end execution of legislative and public policy initiatives to advance firm objectives. Serve as a trusted advisor to JPMorganChase senior leadership, aligning stakeholders on policy priorities, tradeoffs, and engagement plans to ensure a unified firm position. Build and sustain high-impact relationships with federal policymakers across Congress and the Executive Branch, enhancing access, credibility, and influence on priority issues. Develop and lead multi-stakeholder advocacy efforts with industry and external partners; provide strategic direction to trade associations to maximize effectiveness and outcomes. Design and execute targeted advocacy campaigns to advance the firm’s priorities with federal policymakers, integrating messaging, outreach cadence, and stakeholder mapping. Produce executive-ready briefing materials (memos, talking points, and presentations) that translate complex policy developments into clear business implications and recommended actions. Lead cross-functional working teams, driving governance, accountability, and on-time delivery across policy initiatives. Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills 12+ years of experience in policy and/or legislative development and analysis Deep understanding of capital markets, financial services, and business issues Demonstrated leadership skills, strategic thinking, policy acumen, and strong work ethic Proven and effective lobbying outcomes at the federal level Exceptional relationships and considerable experience with navigating and understanding federal politics and legislative processes Demonstrated excellent written and verbal communications skills, including both public speaking and the ability to engage with senior executives Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills Strong project management and organizational skills Ability to excel and maintain a positive attitude in a high-performance, fast-paced professional environment, while managing multiple projects under tight deadlines Management and leadership experience is a plus JD or MBA is a plus About Us JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world’s most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management. We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process. We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants’ and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation. JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans About the Team Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we’re setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success. The Corporate Responsibility (CR) department mission is to advance a stronger, more durable and safe financial system and an inclusive economy and society for clients, customers and communities around the world. The department includes sub-departments focused on policy advocacy and lobbying, philanthropy, sustainability, impact finance, community engagement and data analysis and research. item.title: Vice President, Federal Relations
item.description: Vice President, Federal Relations Organization: University of South California (USC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Vice President, Federal Relations Position Summary The Vice President, Federal Relations (VPFR) is USC’s senior federal strategist and principal representative in Washington, D.C., responsible for advancing the university’s academic, research, and institutional priorities with Congress, the White House, federal departments and agencies, and other national stakeholders. Reporting to the Senior Vice President for University Relations, the VPFR helps shape USC’s federal strategy and is responsible for translating that strategy into coordinated advocacy, engagement, and action. The VPFR serves as a trusted adviser to university leadership regarding the federal political, legislative, regulatory, and funding environments. The VPFR builds cross-partisan relationships, connects USC’s research and expertise to federal opportunities, and helps position USC as a leading national voice on issues relevant to its mission. The VPFR leads USC’s three-person federal relations team, directly supervising two employees. The role works as a full partner across USC’s government relations and University Relations teams and maintains strong relationships with university leadership, deans, faculty, researchers, and academic and medical partners across USC. This is a full-time position based in Washington, D.C., at the USC Capital Campus. Travel to Los Angeles is required approximately four to six times per year. For full consideration, please submit your application materials by the priority deadline of September 24, 2026. Key Responsibilities will include the following: Work with the Senior Vice President, University Relations, and senior university leadership to develop and execute USC’s federal agenda, including legislative, policy, appropriations, funding, and regulatory priorities. Serve as a trusted adviser to senior leadership on federal political, legislative, regulatory, and funding environment, anticipating developments and assessing institutional risks, opportunities, and recommended actions. Represent USC and build sustained, cross-partisan relationships with members of Congress, congressional committees and staff, White House and Administration officials, federal agency leaders, and other key stakeholders. Advance USC priorities on higher education, scientific research, health, innovation and technology, appropriations, and other federal matters related to the university’s mission. Align federal advocacy with USC’s academic and research priorities in coordination with the Provost, Office of Research and Innovation, and other university partners. Build strong relationships with deans, faculty, researchers, and university leaders and coordinate federal strategy, priorities, and messaging across USC. Connect faculty, students, researchers, and senior leaders with policymakers through meetings, campus visits, briefings, testimony, and other engagements; prepare and staff the president, provost, Senior Vice President, deans, trustees, and other leaders for federal engagements, as needed. Provide timely, actionable federal intelligence to university leadership and other internal audiences through briefings, written updates, and issue-specific alerts. Represent USC on the Association of American Universities (AAU) Council on Federal Relations and with other relevant higher education and research associations. Maintain collaborative relationships with peer institutions in the AAU and Big Ten. Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing federal relations team and manage the federal relations budget, consultants, and vendors. Partner with the Executive Director of the USC Capital Campus to support shared opportunities for engagement and programming. Support the Trojan Congressional Caucus through strategic programming, member engagement, and relationship-building. Serve as a collaborative partner across USC’s government relations and University Relations teams, promoting coordinated advocacy, information sharing, and a high-performing team culture. Register as a federal lobbyist and ensure compliance with the Lobbying Disclosure Act and related university reporting requirements. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required. At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in federal relations, government affairs, public policy, or a closely related field, including at least five years of leadership and management experience. Senior-level knowledge and experience with federal legislative, appropriations, regulatory, budget, and agency processes. Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted, bipartisan relationships with elected officials, senior congressional staff, Administration officials, federal agency leaders, and other key Washington stakeholders. Strong leadership and project management skills, with demonstrated success leading high-performing teams and complex initiatives. Demonstrated ability to build productive internal partnerships and influence across a complex organization, including with senior leaders, faculty, deans, researchers, and others who do not report to the position. Excellent judgment, political acumen, and discretion in complex, sensitive, and fast-moving situations, with the credibility and executive presence required to advise senior leadership and represent USC externally. An established network of relationships in Washington and demonstrated ability to convene policymakers, institutional leaders, and other stakeholders around shared priorities. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex policy and political matters for senior leaders and non-specialist audiences. Preferred Qualifications Master’s, law, or other professional degree. Previous experience working on Capitol Hill, in an Administration or federal agency, or in a comparable government affairs or public policy role. Experience representing a research university, academic medical center, health system, or other complex research-intensive organization. Experience leading or managing a Washington office or federal government affairs function, including budget, consultant, and vendor management. Experience with coalition leadership and national higher education, research, science, health, or other relevant policy associations. Confidence as a public speaker and experience representing an organization in public forums and with national media. Familiarity with California and the Los Angeles region, including relationships with or knowledge of the California congressional delegation. Required Documents and Additional Information Resume and cover letter required (may be submitted as one attachment). The annual base salary range for this position is $300,000-$325,000 plus at-risk compensation to be determined based on annual FY performance objectives. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer alignment, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations. To support faculty and staff well-being, USC provides benefits-eligible employees with a broad range of benefits and perks to help protect their and their dependents’ health, wealth, and future. These benefits are available as part of the overall compensation and total rewards package. The University of Southern California is an Equal Opportunity Employer. #LI-Hybrid Minimum Education Bachelor’s degree Minimum Experience 10 years of experience in federal/governmental relations or related fields. 5 years of experience in management/supervisory roles. Minimum Skills Senior-level experience with federal legislative and agency processes. Ability to establish strong relationships with government officials and agencies. Ability to lead with influence, expertise, and advocacy with key internal/external stakeholders. Demonstrated interpersonal skills for collaborating across multiple departments, building consensus strategies and implementing plans. Exemplary oral and written communication skills, exercising diplomacy, tact, discretion and confidentiality while interacting with various communities and groups of colleagues. Ability to compile and summarize information in succinct, understandable reports and formats. Demonstrated project management, organizational and critical thinking skills, able to adjust to changing demands and pressing issues. Preferred Education Master’s degree Preferred Skills Extensive leadership experience on Capitol Hill and/or in the executive branch. Demonstrated public speaking and/or media experience. Working knowledge of California and multi-state employment law. Knowledge and/or understanding of cultural issues (e.g., immigration, socioeconomic, LGBTQIA+). Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Communications Strategist, L D Wilder School of Government & Public Affairs
item.description: Communications Strategist, L D Wilder School of Government & Public Affairs Organization: Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) Location: Richmond, VA Date Posted: 09/21/2026 Advertising Summary The VCU L. Douglas Wilder School of Government and Public Affairs invites applications for a Communications Strategist. Reporting to the Director Communications and External Relations, the position is responsible for managing and executing a broad portfolio of communications initiatives that support the school’s mission, strategic priorities and national reputation. Applicants must have the ability to identify and develop stories that highlight the school’s contributions to public policy, public administration, criminal justice, social equity and community engagement for a variety of audiences and communications platforms. Unit: L D Wilder Sch of Govt & Pub Affrs Department: L D Wilder Sch of Govt & Pub Affrs About the Wilder School The L. Douglas Wilder School of Government and Public Affairs at Virginia Commonwealth University is a nationally recognized leader in public affairs education, research and community engagement. Named for L. Douglas Wilder, the nation’s first elected African American governor, the school reflects his enduring commitment to public service, independent thought, principled leadership, civic engagement and excellence in government. The Wilder School’s mission is to: Engage, teach and inspire students and leaders to understand and solve challenges in our world. Advance research that informs public policy and decision-making to improve our communities. Collaborate with communities through innovative partnerships to enhance the quality of life. Ranked among the top 20 percent of schools of public affairs nationwide and home to the No. 8 graduate program in homeland security and emergency preparedness, the Wilder School prepares the next generation of public service leaders while advancing evidence-based solutions to society’s most pressing challenges. Through nationally recognized academic programs, research centers and community partnerships, the school addresses critical issues in public policy, public administration, criminal justice, homeland security and emergency preparedness, and urban and regional planning. Across these areas, the school advances social equity, strengthens communities and develops solutions that improve quality of life. The Wilder School’s faculty are nationally recognized scholars whose research informs public policy, advances knowledge and shapes conversations on issues of local, state and national significance. Through its integration of research, teaching and public service, the school works to strengthen institutions, improve communities and expand opportunity across Virginia and the nation. For additional information about the Wilder School, please visit our website at https://wilder.vcu.edu Position Summary The Communications Strategist serves as a key member of the Wilder School communications team and plays an important role in advancing the visibility and reputation of one of the nation’s leading schools of public affairs. Reporting to the Director of Communications & External Relations, the position is responsible for managing and executing a broad portfolio of communications initiatives that support the school’s mission, strategic priorities and national reputation. Working closely with faculty, researchers, administrators, students and external stakeholders, the Communications Strategist identifies and develops stories that highlight the school’s contributions to public policy, public administration, criminal justice, social equity and community engagement. The position translates complex research and scholarly work into accessible and engaging content for a variety of audiences and communications platforms. The successful candidate will thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and possess exceptional writing skills, strong attention to detail and a demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. The ideal candidate will be intellectually curious, highly organized and proactive, with the initiative and professional judgment to move projects forward independently while collaborating effectively with diverse stakeholders. This position offers the opportunity to work directly with nationally recognized faculty, senior university leaders, policymakers, community leaders and alumni whose work is helping shape the future of public service and public affairs. The successful candidate will bring a commitment to mission-driven work, an interest in communications assessment and metrics, and a passion for helping tell stories that demonstrate the Wilder School’s impact. Primary Responsibilities Communications Project Management (35%) Manage a high volume of communications projects with competing deadlines while maintaining accuracy, responsiveness and attention to detail. Coordinate communications activities involving faculty, staff, students, alumni, university partners and external stakeholders. Develop and maintain editorial calendars, project timelines and content schedules. Monitor project progress and proactively identify opportunities to improve workflows, systems and communications processes. Serve as a project lead for communications initiatives, ensuring projects move efficiently from concept through execution. Anticipate needs, identify potential challenges and develop solutions that support successful project outcomes. Content Development and Storytelling (35%) Research, write and edit news stories, feature articles, profiles, newsletters, website content, executive communications and other communications materials. Translate complex research findings, policy issues and scholarly work into clear, compelling and accessible content. Conduct interviews with faculty, researchers, students, alumni, donors and community partners. Exercise strong editorial judgment in identifying stories that advance institutional priorities and demonstrate impact. Develop content that supports reputation-building, audience engagement and strategic communications goals. Strategic Communications and Assessment (20%) Support implementation of communications strategies aligned with school priorities. Track communications metrics and engagement data to assess performance and identify opportunities for improvement. Assist in preparing communications reports and evaluating the effectiveness of content and outreach efforts. Recommend strategies to increase audience engagement and strengthen communications outcomes. Stay informed about emerging trends and best practices in higher education communications, public affairs communications and digital storytelling. Digital and Multimedia Communications (10%) Support website, email and social media communications efforts. Assist with multimedia storytelling initiatives, including video, photography and visual communications projects. Ensure communications materials align with university and school branding, editorial and accessibility standards. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, English or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum of five years of progressively responsible communications experience. Exceptional writing, editing, interviewing and storytelling skills. Demonstrated experience managing multiple high-priority projects and competing deadlines in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Strong interpersonal, relationship-building and collaboration skills, with the ability to establish credibility and work effectively with faculty, researchers, administrators, students, alumni and community partners. Demonstrated ability to translate complex research, policy or technical subject matter into engaging content for broad audiences. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and professional judgment. Demonstrated initiative and ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and managing projects from conception through execution. Demonstrated ability to work in and foster an environment of respect, professionalism and civility with a population of faculty, staff, and students from all backgrounds and experiences, or a commitment to do so as a staff member at VCU. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, higher education administration, public administration or a related field. Seven or more years of professional communications experience. Experience in higher education communications. Experience writing about academic research, public policy, public administration, government, criminal justice, social equity or related fields. Experience working in public affairs, public relations, government communications or mission-driven organizations. Experience supporting executive communications or working with senior leaders. Experience using communications metrics and analytics to evaluate content performance and audience engagement. Experience managing editorial calendars, communications workflows and complex multi-stakeholder projects. Experience with website content management systems, email marketing platforms and digital communications tools. Experience with graphic design, multimedia storytelling and video production. University Benefits All full-time university staff are eligible for our generous benefits package that includes choices for health, vision, and dental coverage, life-insurance, short and long-term disability coverage, retirement planning, tax-deferred annuity and cash match programs, flexible spending accounts, tuition benefits, significant paid-time off, 12 paid holidays, and more. Application Submission/Other Information All applications must include a cover letter, three (3) writing samples, and a detailed resume with the names and contact information of three professional references. Review of applications will begin immed

item.title: Director of Marketing Events & Digital Communications
item.description: Director of Marketing Events & Digital Communications Organization: American Farmland Trust (AFT) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Overview Salary Range $120,000.00 – $130,000.00 Salary/year Level Senior Position Type Full Time Description Who We Are American Farmland Trust is the only national organization that takes a holistic approach to agriculture, focusing on the land itself, the agricultural practices used on that land, and the farmers and ranchers who do the work. Since our founding in 1980, AFT has helped permanently protect over 6.5 million acres of agricultural lands, advanced environmentally sound farming practices on millions of additional acres, and helped thousands of farm families make a go of it, primarily through programs that increase farm viability and/or enhance farmland access. Long a pioneering leader, AFT is now riding a new wave of growth, driven by agriculture’s most pressing needs and opportunities. Job Purpose The Director of Marketing, Events & Digital Communications leads AFT’s branding, marketing strategy, and national paid media campaigns. This position manages the Marketing Division and oversees national websites, email, social media, and outreach channels with the help of a team of communication specialists. Position Summary The Director of Marketing, Events & Digital Communications serves as AFT’s brand leader, driving integrated marketing and digital strategies that expand reach, deepen stakeholder engagement, and increase supporter growth. In partnership with the Vice President for Communications, the Director leads multi-channel campaigns, signature engagement initiatives, and creative content development to advance the organization’s mission and visibility while overseeing team performance, metrics, and marketing best practices. Duties & Responsibilities Project/Program Leadership and Execution Design, create, and improve content for national dissemination. Maintain the AFT brand, refine and enforce brand standards, and keep AFT on the cutting edge. Test the health of the brand with key audiences and against competitors. Lead supporter acquisition strategy and coordinate cross-department tactics to grow the database. Monitor the competitive environment, market changes, and political developments, and leverage trends and patterns to maximize communication impact. Collaboration and Organizational Alignment Foster internal and cross-divisional collaboration through informed guidance, coaching, and expertise in relevant areas. Collaborate with other Directors and Deputy Directors on cross-divisional efforts and work to break down organizational silos to ensure effective execution of strategic initiatives. Innovation and Continuous Improvement Identify, develop, and promote new programmatic and operational initiatives that drive organizational growth, improve effectiveness, enhance efficiency, quality, and engagement, while encouraging and supporting a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and adaptability. Communication Leadership Lead the execution of national communications strategy as tailored to divisional priorities and capabilities. Ensure the production of written and other materials that communicate the division’s work to target audiences. Support strong collaboration with the National Communications team to maintain consistency and alignment across all internal and external messaging. Develop compelling messaging and storytelling opportunities across mediums, formats, and geographies. Establish new communications channels and expand effective channels to reach new audiences. This is not necessarily an all-inclusive list of job-related responsibilities, duties, skills, efforts, requirements, or working conditions. While intended to reflect the current job accurately, management reserves the right to revise the position or require that other or different tasks be performed as assigned. Qualifications Advanced degree (Master’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, or a related field) preferred, along with 10+ years of progressively responsible national PR, communications, or marketing experience, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. Demonstrated expertise in marketing, communications, advertising, and media relations as proven through portfolio examples and published samples. Outstanding communication and organizational skills. Demonstrated experience leading and managing teams, including providing direction, supporting staff development, and fostering a collaborative work environment. Advanced knowledge and understanding of social media platforms including Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, and Facebook, as well as related trends, analytics, and planning tools. Experience managing email marketing, online fundraising, event registration, and digital advocacy platforms in a nonprofit or cause marketing role. Experience directing websites, including building new websites, updating webpages, creating workflows, and planning staff resources. Excellent organizational and project management skills with the ability to establish and implement systems and identify resources to ensure successful, on-time completion of projects. Knowledge of and demonstrated experience using a diverse range of tools such as Canva, Adobe InDesign, Photoshop, and Illustrator. Collaborative and strategic leader who builds alignment and engagement through influence. Working Conditions Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to meet deadlines. This position requires domestic travel, estimated at approximately four to five trips per year, primarily for conferences, meetings, and other organizational events. Supervisory Responsibility This position has supervisory responsibility for: Social Media & Marketing Manager & Marketing Coordinator Compensation American Farmland Trust offers excellent vacation, medical, retirement, and other benefits. The salary range for this position is $120,000 to $130,000, based on experience. American Farmland Trust Offers a Full Benefits Package for Full-Time Employees Insurance coverage begins on the first day of the month following the date of hire. Medical & Prescription Coverage Dental Coverage Vision Coverage Company-Paid Life Insurance & Long-Term Disability (LTD) Voluntary Life Insurance Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for Healthcare & Dependent Care Health Savings Account (HSA) 401(k) Plan Sick Leave: Regular full-time employees accrue 13 sick days per year. Vacation Leave: Accrue 15 days during the first year, increasing by one day per year up to a maximum of 20 days annually. Holidays: AFT observes twelve fixed holidays and provides a week off between Christmas and New Year’s Day when all offices are closed, plus up to three floating holidays depending on the hiring month. Why You Should Apply Be part of a purpose-driven, committed, knowledgeable, high-performing, experienced, and fun team. Work in a diverse and inclusive environment. Support a cause and mission you can be proud of. Receive competitive compensation and benefits. Enjoy a remote work opportunity. Timeline To be considered, applicants must submit a resume, answer all screener questions, and include a cover letter explaining why they are the right fit for both AFT and this role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.
