item.title: Director of Media Relations
item.description: Director of Media Relations Organization: American Farmland Trust (AFT) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Overview Salary Range $120,000.00 – $130,000.00 Salary Level Senior Position Type Full Time Description Who We Are American Farmland Trust is the only national organization that takes a holistic approach to agriculture, focusing on the land itself, the agricultural practices used on that land, and the farmers and ranchers who do the work. Since our founding in 1980, AFT has helped permanently protect over 6.5 million acres of agricultural lands, advanced environmentally sound farming practices on millions of additional acres, and helped thousands of farm families make a go of it, primarily through programs that increase farm viability and/or enhance farmland access. Long a pioneering leader, AFT is now riding a new wave of growth, driven by agriculture’s most pressing needs and opportunities. Job Purpose Reporting directly to the VP of Communications, the Media Relations Director develops and implements AFT’s media relations strategy and contributes to general AFT communications efforts, working across AFT departments, especially with program staff. Position Summary As an integral part of the AFT Communications team, the Media Relations Director develops and implements policies and procedures for the relationship between the media and AFT. The Media Relations Director works to expand understanding of AFT’s business, performance, and strategy. Duties and Responsibilities Project/Program Leadership and Execution Contributes to the development and leads the implementation of AFT’s media relations strategy. Cultivates and maintains relationships with key members of the media, particularly agriculture reporters. Serves as the primary point of contact for members of the media and a liaison between media and AFT’s subject matter experts. Leads project execution by setting priorities, defining deadlines, and coordinating across teams and with external partners to ensure collaborative and timely delivery of outcomes. Applies subject matter expertise to lead high-impact projects and processes, ensuring effective design, implementation, and delivery in support of divisional and organizational goals. Ensures successful project and team outcomes by prioritizing tasks, managing deadlines, and aligning efforts with strategic and budgetary goals. Collaboration and Organizational Alignment Fosters internal and cross-divisional collaboration through informed guidance, coaching, and knowledge and/or expertise in relevant areas. Collaborates with other Directors and Deputy Directors on cross-divisional efforts and works to break down silos within the organization to ensure effective execution of strategic initiatives. Staffs AFT’s President and CEO and other spokespeople during interviews and at media-related events as needed. Innovation and Continuous Improvement Identifies, develops, and promotes new programmatic and operational initiatives that drive organizational growth, improve effectiveness, enhance efficiency, quality, and engagement, while encouraging and supporting a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and adaptability. Communication Leadership Leads the execution of National Communications strategy as tailored to divisional priorities and capabilities. Oversees the development and production of written and multimedia communications that effectively convey the division’s priorities, programs, and impact to target audiences. Partners closely with the National Communications team to ensure consistency, coordination, and alignment across internal and external communications and messaging. Develops and oversees press materials highlighting AFT initiatives, research, events, and other newsworthy developments. Develops and secures placement of op-eds, opinion pieces, and other thought leadership content in national and regional media outlets. Drafts, edits, and provides strategic guidance on op-eds, opinion pieces, and other executive or organizational communications. Writes talking points, FAQs, briefing materials, and other communications resources to support organizational leaders and spokespeople. Pushes for reporter coverage by developing proactive media outreach strategies, cultivating relationships with reporters, and pursuing opportunities to elevate AFT’s research, programs, and projects. This is not necessarily an all-inclusive list of job-related responsibilities, duties, skills, efforts, requirements, or working conditions. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or require that other or different tasks be performed as assigned. Qualifications Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, prioritize competing demands, and make timely, strategic decisions. Proven ability to respond effectively and professionally to media inquiries, including time-sensitive requests and reporter deadlines. Demonstrated ability to translate complex, technical, or academic topics into clear, compelling, concise, and on-message communications for media. Strong knowledge of media relations principles and best practices, with a commitment to staying current on evolving communications strategies and industry trends. Proficiency with Meltwater and other relevant communications and public relations tools. Interest in agriculture, conservation, and related policy issues, with a commitment to American Farmland Trust’s mission. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders, partners, and media contacts across the country. Education & Experience Advanced degree (Master’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, or a related field) and 10+ years of progressively responsible media relations experience, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. Working Conditions This is a remote position. Occasional work in the evenings or on weekends may be required to meet deadlines. Travel Occasional domestic travel is required for this position. Supervisory Responsibility The position has supervisory responsibility for: Media Relations Associate Compensation American Farmland Trust offers excellent vacation, medical, retirement, and other benefits. The salary range for this position is $120,000 to $130,000, based on experience. American Farmland Trust offers a full benefits package for full-time employees: Insurance coverage begins the first day of the month following the date of hire. Medical & Prescription Coverage Dental Coverage Vision Coverage Company-Paid Life Insurance & Long-Term Disability (LTD) Voluntary Life Insurance Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for Healthcare & Dependent Care Health Savings Account (HSA) 401(k) Plan Sick Leave: Regular full-time employees accrue 13 sick days per year. Vacation Leave: Accrue 15 days during the first year, increasing by one day per year up to a maximum of 20 days annually. Holidays: AFT observes twelve fixed holidays and provides a week off between Christmas and New Year’s Day (all offices closed), plus up to three floating holidays depending on the hiring month. Why You Should Apply Be part of a purpose-driven, committed, knowledgeable, high-performing, experienced, and fun team. A diverse and inclusive work environment. A cause and mission you can be proud of. Competitive compensation and benefits. Remote work opportunity. Timeline To be considered, applicants must submit a resume, answer all screener questions, and include a cover letter explaining why they are the right fit for both AFT and this role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applicants Must Directly Apply Here: Director of Media Relations Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Associate, Digital Marketing & Communications
item.description: Associate, Digital Marketing & Communications Organization: American College of Cardiology (ACC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Department Corporate Communications Target Salary Range at Hire $65,000 – $75,000 Apply Now Job Description The Associate, Digital Marketing and Communications will be responsible for placement of the College’s paid social media marketing, as well as day-to-day postings across ACC channels, and monitoring, tracking, and reporting on campaign results. This position will also work with the College’s Social Media team to support organic social media coverage. Responsibilities Paid Social Campaign Execution Implement the College’s paid social media marketing campaigns across platforms, ensuring accurate setup, deployment, and ongoing management. Ensure all campaigns are correctly configured prior to launch, including creative assets, landing pages, campaign naming conventions, and tracking parameters (UTMs). Conduct pre-launch quality assurance checks to ensure campaign integrity, accuracy, and alignment with intended objectives. Maintain accuracy and consistency of live campaigns, including documenting any post-launch edits or optimizations that may impact reporting or performance interpretation. Identify and resolve campaign setup errors or inconsistencies in real time or as they are identified. Campaign Tracking and Operational Oversight Maintain an internal system to track all active, paused, and completed paid media campaigns, including key details such as assets, targeting, dates, and tracking links, to ensure visibility, accuracy, and reporting consistency across the MarCom team. Best Practices and Cross-Team Support Serve as a partner to business line marketing managers, supporting alignment of paid media campaigns with marketing objectives, campaign plans, and execution needs. Collaborate closely with Social Media and broader Marketing and Communications teams to establish and maintain paid media best practices, workflows, and standards. Participate in planning discussions with business line marketing managers to ensure paid media setup and tracking are aligned with campaign goals and measurement requirements. Provide guidance to business lines on paid media execution, campaign setup standards, and performance optimization based on channel expertise and platform knowledge. Stay current on paid media and digital marketing best practices and proactively apply insights to improve campaign execution and reporting consistency. Search Engine Marketing Manage ACC’s search engine marketing placements, working closely with Marketing and Communications colleagues and the Web team (Google and Bing) to ensure effective campaign execution. Reporting and Optimization Track, analyze, and report on campaign performance across paid social and search channels. Recommend and implement improvements based on campaign performance insights to optimize future campaigns. Content Support Support the Social Media team in developing and posting content for ACC channels as needed. Other Duties Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Marketing, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in digital or social media marketing. 2+ years of hands-on experience managing paid social and search engine marketing campaigns. Experience with Google Ads and Bing Ads campaign management. Experience with social media and digital performance reporting and analysis. Working knowledge of Google Analytics (GA4), UTMs, and campaign tracking principles. Proficiency with social media and marketing tools (e.g., Sprout, Canva, Google Analytics). Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong organizational and project management skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite. Desired Qualifications Familiarity with healthcare and/or association environments. Experience working with senior leadership or management within an organization. About Us At the American College of Cardiology, we bring our hearts to work. We are a 500-person organization dedicated and committed to our mission to transform cardiovascular care and improve heart health for all for more than 75 years. When you join our team, you become part of a culture that envisions a world where science, innovation, and knowledge optimize cardiovascular care and outcomes. Every day, we are committed to supporting our more than 60,000 members and their patients around the globe. In doing so, we ensure our staff have a positive environment of teamwork, collaboration, professionalism, and excellence. To learn more about why ACC has been recognized as a great place to work, please visit: https://www.acc.org/jobs What We Offer ACC values all members of our College family, including ACC staff. As the foundation of the organization, ACC staff enjoy world-class benefits and a culture of work-life balance. Our benefit offerings include: Medical, dental, and vision insurance. Basic life insurance. Short-term and long-term disability coverage. Supplemental insurance options. Generous paid time off, including: Pre-loaded vacation and sick leave. 12 holidays. An organization-wide shutdown during the last week of the year. Parental leave. Two community service days. Half-day summer Fridays. Tuition assistance. A highly competitive 10% retirement contribution after one year of service. Additional benefit offerings. For an overview of ACC’s full benefits, visit: https://ibyrjb.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/ACCJobs/jobs Please note that these offerings may change at any time. ACC believes in fair and equitable pay. Multiple factors are taken into consideration when determining compensation for a selected candidate. These factors include, but are not limited to: Scope and responsibilities of the role. Relevant work experience. Education and training. Internal equity considerations. Market conditions. Business considerations. Salary ranges vary based on the cost of labor in the local market where the job will be performed. ACC’s Recruitment Team can provide additional information regarding local salary ranges during initial discussions. EEOC Statement ACC is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all candidates and employees. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. ACC is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and protected veterans. ACC is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans throughout the job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact: Katie Sarreal HR Business Partner Email: [email protected] Phone: (202) 375-6351 Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Communications
item.description: Director, Communications Organization: Affordable Homes & Communities (AHC) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Salary Range: $135,000.00 To $150,000.00 Annually Affordable Homes & Communities (AHC) is a mission-driven, nonprofit organization committed to developing affordable, workforce, and mixed-income rental housing in Maryland, Virginia, and Washington DC. With a resident-centric approach, we manage over 8,000 apartments in 54 communities, providing educational programs and social services through our Resident Services team. About the Team The Community Relations department provides strategic fundraising, public relations, and crisis communications services for AHC and its subsidiaries. About the Job The Director of Communications leads AHC’s internal and external communications strategy and serves as a trusted communications advisor to the CEO, Vice President of Community Relations, and senior leadership. The Director strengthens AHC’s visibility and reputation, supports organizational priorities, and ensures clear, consistent, and effective communications across the organization. The Director leads communications for significant organizational initiatives, including strategic priorities, organizational change, major announcements, and high-profile events. The position also serves as AHC’s communications lead during significant incidents and crises, coordinating with leadership, relevant departments, and third parties to protect AHC’s reputation and ensure communications are accurate, timely, coordinated, and appropriate. The ideal candidate is a strategic communications professional and exceptional writer with strong judgment, organizational skills, and the ability to manage sensitive issues, competing priorities, and complex communications with discretion and professionalism. Responsibilities Include but are not limited to the following: Communications Strategy • Lead AHC’s internal and external communications strategy in alignment with its mission, priorities, and goals. • Serve as a communications advisor to the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and department leaders. • Maintain AHC’s organizational voice, messaging, and brand standards across departments and communications channels. • Develop communications plans for major initiatives, announcements, campaigns, and events. • Identify opportunities to increase awareness of AHC’s work, impact, leadership, and role in affordable housing and community development. Crisis Communications & Media Relations • Lead communications during significant organizational, property, resident, employee, safety, operational, technology, or reputational incidents. • Maintain crisis communications protocols, templates, escalation procedures, and spokesperson guidance. • Coordinate with leadership, Human Resources, Property Management, Asset Management, Real Estate, Resident Services, Legal, Information Technology, and external partners during significant incidents. • Develop and coordinate crisis communications, including employee and resident messages, media statements, talking points, FAQs, and stakeholder updates. • Lead media relations, respond to media inquiries, develop press materials, and prepare executives for interviews and public appearances. • Monitor media and emerging issues and advise leadership on reputational risks and appropriate responses. Internal Communications & Organizational Change • Lead communications for significant organizational changes, including technology implementations, operational changes, restructuring, policy changes, and strategic initiatives. • Partner with leaders to clearly communicate what is changing, why it matters, the impact on employees and stakeholders, and any actions required. • Translate complex organizational, technical, and operational information into clear, accessible communications. • Develop employee announcements, leadership messages, FAQs, presentations, newsletters, and other internal communications. Content & Executive Communications • Develop and edit executive remarks, speeches, talking points, presentations, statements, articles, marketing, and other leadership communications. • Oversee AHC’s website, social media, newsletters, presentations, collateral, and other institutional communications. • Develop compelling content that communicates AHC’s mission, accomplishments, developments, programs, and resident impact. • Lead communications for major organizational events and high-profile external engagements. Team & Communications Operations • Supervise and develop the Manager of Communications (who manages the Communications Coordinator) and provide direction to interns, contractors, and other communications resources. • Manage communications vendors, consultants, projects, budgets, timelines, and deliverables. • Establish effective communications processes, standards, templates, and approval workflows. • Advise departments on communications strategy and review high-profile materials for clarity, accuracy, consistency, and alignment with AHC’s brand. Qualifications The position requires a detail-oriented, creative individual who is an excellent writer, a multi-tasker, a leader, and a team player. • Minimum of 10 years of experience in corporate or nonprofit communications, including oversight of websites, social media channels, and collateral marketing materials. • Demonstrated experience developing and executing communications for organizational change, including technology implementations, operational changes, or other major initiatives. • Experience working with media outlets and reporters. • Excellent written and oral communication skills. • Proficient in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and communications software such as Canva. • Strong interpersonal and organizational skills. • Ability to work independently as well as in a team. Working at AHC • AHC has a Hybrid Work Schedule with staff working onsite on our core days (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). Staff may work remotely on Wednesday and Friday. AHC offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; a health reimbursement account (HRA) for eligible employees; employer-paid life insurance; employer-paid short- and long-term disability coverage; health and dependent care flexible spending accounts (FSA); a 403(b) retirement plan with employer matching and discretionary contributions; voluntary benefits such as pet insurance, life and AD&D, identity theft, and legal coverage; transit and cellphone stipends; free parking; mental health support including an Employee Assistance Program (EAP); paid federal holidays, including time off during Christmas week; paid vacation and sick leave; and professional development opportunities. AHC is a drug-free workplace. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and drug screening. AHC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable federal, state, and local law. item.title: Manager/Sr. Manager, Energy Policy – Reliability & Security
item.description: Manager/Sr. Manager, Energy Policy – Reliability & Security Organization: Data Center Coalition (DCC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Ready to advance a growing industry that provides essential digital infrastructure? The Data Center Coalition (DCC) is the membership association for the data center industry, empowering and championing the data center community through public policy advocacy, thought leadership, stakeholder outreach, and community engagement. Data centers are the backbone of the modern economy, and our members are investing tens of billions of dollars in capital in new data center facilities across the country to meet unprecedented demand for the digital services that have become increasingly central to Americans’ daily routines and how we live. The way we work, learn, shop, bank, and even access medical care now occurs online. Data centers make this possible by enabling the apps, platforms, and services individuals and organizations of all types increasingly rely on every day to keep us connected in our modern digital lives. DCC represents and advances the interests of the data center industry by aggregating industry expertise and thought leadership, partnering with policymakers and other collaborators, and supporting communities where data center teams live and work through active engagement. To learn more, go to: http://www.datacentercoalition.org About the Role and Opportunity The Manager/Sr. Manager, Energy Policy – Reliability & Security will manage DCC’s engagement on grid reliability matters. This position will work directly with DCC members to identify, organize, and build consensus around positions and policy priorities that impact data center development and operations. They will advocate for the organization’s positions and priorities related to grid reliability with a focus on the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), regional electric reliability organizations (EROs), RTOs/ISOs, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), and state utility commissions. This role will report to DCC’s Director of Energy Policy – FERC and RTOs and work collaboratively and regularly with the entire DCC team. This is a fully remote position that will include occasional travel (up to 15%) to engage DCC members and support DCC’s participation in regulatory proceedings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and other events. Responsibilities Lead DCC’s energy policy and regulatory advocacy on grid reliability matters with a primary focus on NERC committees and stakeholder processes, engagement with regional EROs, as well as in related RTO/ISO processes and state regulatory proceedings on grid reliability. Track, analyze, and summarize evolving NERC standards, FERC regulations, and emerging policy and regulatory trends that could impact data center operations. Serve as a data center industry thought leader on technical grid reliability matters, including reliability standards, voltage ride-throughs, curtailment procedures, demand response, and other grid reliability topics. Establish constructive working relationships with NERC, EROs, RTO/ISOs, regulatory commissions, and other key reliability stakeholders. Support DCC’s State Policy and Federal teams with bill analysis and testimony development related to legislation on grid reliability and security matters. Organize and lead virtual meetings, member work groups, and initiatives related to DCC’s energy policy priorities and regulatory proceedings, including meeting agenda development, execution, decision tracking, follow-up, and coordination with outside counsel, experts, and consultants. Provide regular briefings, reports, and summaries to members on important energy policy and regulatory issues and work with DCC members to identify and prioritize engagement opportunities. Manage DCC’s consultants, including scopes of work, budgets, filing assignments, testimony development, hearing preparation, and alignment with DCC positions. Support DCC’s in-person participation at NERC committee and stakeholder meetings, RTO/ISO meetings, regulatory proceedings, technical conferences, workshops, industry conferences, and other events as needed. Other tasks as assigned. This position’s duties may evolve over time as the needs of the organization change. Basic Qualifications 5+ years of experience in successfully advancing key energy policy and/or regulatory initiatives related to grid reliability and security, preferably in NERC committees and stakeholder processes, FERC proceedings, and/or RTO/ISO stakeholder processes. Ability to clearly and effectively communicate DCC’s priorities and positions to member companies and external stakeholders, including NERC, EROs, commissioners, commission staff, policymakers, utilities, generators, grid operators, and trade associations. Strong strategic planning, regulatory analysis, and communication skills (oral and written). A member-services mindset and an aptitude for building and maintaining relationships with energy subject matter experts from DCC member companies. Ability to independently manage multiple workstreams, submission deadlines, member work groups, consultants, and internal priorities while collaborating closely as part of a team. High degree of professionalism and attention to detail. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work with executives, technical experts, outside counsel, consultants, policy staff, and external stakeholders. Tact and diplomacy, with the ability to maintain confidentiality, professionalism, composure, and discretion. Preferred Qualifications Background in electrical engineering, power systems, or NERC regulations and compliance. Experience managing NERC compliance with mandatory reliability standards for a NERC-registered entity. Deep understanding of NERC standards (CIP, PRC, FAC, MOD, TOP, etc.). Familiarity with NERC’s inverter-based resource (IBR) registration initiative and current efforts to register large computational loads. Experience working with membership associations, coalitions, large energy customers, or trade associations. Familiarity with ongoing reliability efforts underway at FERC and the RTOs/ISOs. Additional Details Full-time position with a growing benefits package, which currently includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance, 401(k) matching, and vacation and sick leave that start accruing on Day 1. This is a virtual position with the ability to work from a home office. DCC may provide office space at a co-working or shared office facility if preferred. Travel (up to 15%) may be required. Must be eligible to work in the United States. Compensation is negotiable and will be based on your skills, experience, and geographic location. National Remote Salary Range: $120,000 to $150,000 base per year. Please note: The high end of this range is reserved for candidates residing in premier cost-of-living metropolitan markets. How to Apply We would love to hear from you! Email your resume to: [email protected] Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Equal Opportunity Employer We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, national origin, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform crucial job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Communications
item.description: Director of Communications Organization: Umbra Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Description Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra’s ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed. About the Job Umbra is seeking a seasoned, strategic Director of Communications to lead the company’s internal and external communications and shape how Umbra tells its story to employees, customers, media, policymakers, industry stakeholders, and the broader public. Reporting to the VP of Communications, the Director will lead the day-to-day execution of Umbra’s communications strategy, with responsibility for media relations and press engagement, internal communications, executive communications, corporate messaging, and major company announcements. This individual will serve as a trusted communications advisor to senior leaders across the company and help build and protect Umbra’s reputation as a leading American space technology company. The ideal candidate is an exceptional writer and communicator with strong news judgment, deep media relations experience, and the ability to translate complex technical and business topics into clear, compelling narratives. This role requires someone who can operate strategically while also moving quickly and executing directly in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. This position is based on-site in our Arlington, VA office. Key Responsibilities External Communications & Media Relations Lead Umbra’s day-to-day media relations and press activities, serving as a primary point of contact for journalists and managing both inbound and proactive media engagement. Build and maintain strong relationships with national, trade, defense, space, technology, and business media. Develop and execute proactive media strategies that elevate Umbra’s capabilities, leadership, business priorities, and role in the broader space and national security ecosystem. Lead communications planning and execution for company announcements, product and mission milestones, partnerships, contracts, launches, and other significant developments. Draft and edit press releases, statements, speeches, talking points, op-eds, executive communications, Q&As, briefing materials, and other external content. Prepare and advise senior executives for media interviews, public speaking engagements, panels, and other high-profile opportunities. Manage press inquiries and coordinate responses across leadership, Legal, business units, and other relevant stakeholders. Monitor the media and external environment to identify emerging opportunities, issues, and reputational risks. Lead communications response to sensitive, high-profile, or rapidly evolving issues, ensuring messaging is timely, accurate, and coordinated. Internal & Executive Communications Lead Umbra’s internal communications efforts, helping ensure employees are informed, aligned, and connected to the company’s mission, strategy, and priorities. Develop and execute internal communications plans around company priorities, organizational developments, milestones, and other important employee matters. Establish and manage a consistent cadence of internal communications across channels, including Slack, newsletters, all-hands meetings, and leadership communications. Partner closely with senior leadership to develop executive messaging, talking points, presentations, company-wide announcements, and other leadership communications. Partner with People, Legal, Operations, and business leaders on sensitive or complex employee communications. Ensure internal communications are clear, timely, and consistent with Umbra’s voice, values, and broader corporate narrative. Corporate Narrative & Communications Strategy Partner with the VP of Communications to develop and execute Umbra’s overarching communications strategy and corporate narrative. Help ensure a clear and consistent Umbra story across the company’s three business units: Remote Sensing, Space Systems, and Mission Solutions. Translate complex technology, missions, and business priorities into clear and compelling communications for technical and non-technical audiences. Partner with business leaders to identify stories, milestones, and opportunities that advance Umbra’s strategic objectives and strengthen its external profile. Partner with People, Legal, Operations, and business leaders on sensitive or complex employee communications. Ensure internal communications are clear, timely, and consistent with Umbra’s voice, values, and broader corporate narrative. Develop and maintain core corporate messaging, executive talking points, company background materials, and other foundational communications resources. Ensure consistency of voice, positioning, and messaging across earned media, internal communications, executive engagement, social media, and digital channels. Establish processes and metrics to assess communications effectiveness and continuously improve how Umbra reaches key audiences. Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as a trusted communications partner to executives and leaders across Umbra’s business units and corporate functions. Collaborate closely with Marketing, Government Affairs, Business Development, People, Legal, and other teams to ensure communications are coordinated and aligned with company priorities. Partner with digital and content teams on integrated communications efforts spanning earned media, social media, web, and internal channels. Provide communications counsel on emerging issues, reputational considerations, and significant company decisions. Manage external communications agencies, consultants, and other partners as needed. Help strengthen communications processes, planning, and coordination across the organization as Umbra continues to grow. Requirements Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Political Science, or a related field. 10+ years of communications experience, including significant responsibility for media relations, corporate communications, executive communications, and internal communications. Demonstrated experience developing and executing communications strategies for complex, high-profile, or mission-driven organizations. Deep media relations experience, including a track record of developing reporter relationships, securing meaningful earned media opportunities, and managing press inquiries. Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills across formats, including press releases, statements, speeches, op-eds, executive messaging, internal communications, and digital content. Experience advising and preparing senior executives for media interviews, public appearances, and sensitive communications. Strong news judgment and demonstrated ability to manage both proactive communications opportunities and fast-moving issues. Ability to understand complex technical, business, and policy topics and communicate them clearly to a range of audiences. Excellent judgment and discretion, particularly when handling sensitive, confidential, or high-profile matters. Proven ability to work effectively across functions and influence stakeholders at all levels of an organization. Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Desired Qualifications Experience in aerospace, defense, national security, technology, or another highly technical industry. Established relationships with national, defense, aerospace, technology, or business media. Experience communicating on matters involving the U.S. government, national security, or public policy. Experience leading communications around significant corporate announcements, crises, or other high-profile events. Familiarity with digital communications, social media strategy, communications analytics, and content management platforms. Experience managing communications agencies, consultants, or external partners. Benefits Flexible Time Off, Sick, Family & Medical Leave Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, LTD, STD (employer funded) Voluntary Life, Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, and Pet Insurance (employee funded) 401(k) with 3% non-elective company contribution Stock Options Free Parking Free lunch daily in office Equal Opportunity Employer Umbra is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Employment Eligibility Verification In compliance with federal laws, all hired persons will be required to verify their identity and eligibility to work in the United States by completing the required Employment Eligibility Verification Form (I-9 Form) upon hire. ITAR/EAR Requirements This position may include access to technology and/or data that is subject to U.S. export controls pursuant to ITAR and EAR. To comply with federal export controls, all persons hired must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, U.S. lawful permanent resident, refugee or asylee as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3), or must otherwise be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. item.title: Chief Communications Officer (Salary Range $90k – 120k)
item.description: Chief Communications Officer (Salary Range $90k – 120k) Organization: Scouting America – National Capital Area Council Location: Bethesda, MD Date Posted: 09/23/2026 POSITION TYPE: Full-Time In Office CLASSIFICATION: Exempt LOCATION: Bethesda, MD POSITION SUMMARY As a member of Scouting America National Capital Area Council’s (NCAC) Executive Cabinet, the Chief Communications Officer (C.C.O.) provides leadership to advance the Council’s mission by ensuring positive brand amplification through communications, marketing, and public relations efforts. The C.C.O. builds and sustains the Council’s reputation for quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction while handling all communication sent to the public, current and potential members, and current and potential donors. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Strategic Plan: Assist with the development and execution of a forward-looking, comprehensive marketing and communications strategy for NCAC and contribute to the Council’s vision by building trust around a shared narrative and amplifying the mission with creativity and clarity. Provide perspective and guidance on current and emerging opportunities and challenges that influence NCAC’s ability to fulfill its mission and meet its goals. Develop and execute plans supporting high-priority initiatives, as well as support other Strategic Plan goals as they relate to marketing and communication for long-term impact. Branding and Design: Ensure brand positioning and brand management, including for the NCAC website, social media sites, recruiting materials, marketing and departmental communication collateral, and fundraising materials. Design and produce collateral promotional materials as needed across all channels, including the annual report, board documents, and other projects. Support all departments in handling inquiries and requests related to the Scouting America and NCAC brands. Quality Control: Enforce consistent messaging of the Scouting America and NCAC brand. It is the responsibility of the C.C.O. to ensure all communication produced by the Council is reflective of the high quality of NCAC and its constituents. Media Relations and Issues Management: Establish and maintain relationships with local media to increase media coverage of priority initiatives and respond to inquiries. Draft, edit, and review statements, FAQs, and other media materials, while working with team members and partner agencies to ensure widespread distribution and follow-through. Serve as a public spokesperson as needed. Train other spokespeople, including volunteers, through media training, coaching, and support. Ensure that NCAC’s Cabinet and Board are appropriately advised and supported. Crisis Management: Be prepared to address crisis issues quickly, effectively, and accurately through the rapid assimilation and distribution of complex material. Systems and Digital Footprint: Establish a best-in-class online presence that drives organizational impact, financial donations, and volunteer support. Oversee the design, maintenance, content, and control of the Council website, social media sites, and other internal and external Council communication tools. Create an impactful social media presence that empowers stakeholders to spread the mission organically. Work closely with other leaders to communicate information clearly, consistently, concisely, and in a timely manner while continually identifying opportunities to increase the Council’s visibility and profile in the community. Volunteer Leadership: Serve as staff advisor for the Marketing Committee(s). Provide support to NCAC’s Executive Committee as needed. Train and assist in recruiting Marketing Vice Chairs for all Districts. Staff Leadership: Manage, guide, and coach members of the communications team and ensure the group is structured and resourced to accommodate the needs of NCAC. Council Support: Perform other duties as assigned based on the short-term and long-term needs of the Council. RESPONSIBILITY FOR STAFF SUPERVISION Provide staff leadership, with emphasis on both results and staff member development, to the Marketing Director and additional staff if the department expands. MATERIALS AND EQUIPMENT USED 100% of time Motor vehicle Computer Copier Telephone Smartphone Audio-visual equipment PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES AND REQUIREMENTS 100% of time This position involves both sedentary office work and active duties at events and camps. While in the office, work is primarily sedentary and requires the ability to sit for extended periods, operate a computer keyboard, and perform repetitive and stretching motions. Essential functions include: Reaching Standing Walking Fingering Grasping Lifting Feeling Talking Hearing Computer keyboarding Occasional lifting of boxes, files, and equipment weighing up to 35 pounds is required in the office. The position also requires maintaining a valid driver’s license and current automotive insurance, as well as the ability to drive a personal motor vehicle for Council business, with mileage reimbursement provided. MENTAL DEMANDS 100% of time Reading Detailed work Confidentiality Stress management Problem solving Language skills Training Math Reasoning Verbal communication Written communication Customer contact Multiple concurrent tasks Frequent interruptions in a fast-paced environment Continual change WORKING CONDITIONS 100% of time This position operates in a professional office setting with work hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required, along with limited travel. The employee is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions. When visiting Council camps, the employee may be exposed to some special adverse environmental conditions. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS, SUPERVISION, VOLUNTEER RELATIONS 100% of time Recognize the importance of a positive working relationship with other staff members. Recognize the importance of a close and harmonious working relationship with all volunteers. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Education Bachelor’s Degree Experience Marketing, Advertising & Public Relations: 10 years (Preferred) Strategic Planning: 5 years (Preferred) Management Experience ESSENTIAL SKILLS REQUIRED Polished ability to communicate with clear, consistent messaging. Ability to utilize analytical tools and research to uncover trends and determine new digital strategies. Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to meet deadlines. Ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects from start to completion. Project tracking skills. Advanced proofreading and editing abilities. Ability to represent the organization in public. Customer service orientation. Adaptability and a team-focused mindset. Demonstrated expertise, savvy, and passion for social media optimization that inspires audiences. Strong photography and video skills, including editing capabilities. Proficiency in WordPress, Elementor, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, and Microsoft Office. Knowledge of project and email management systems such as Basecamp and iContact. Submit any Cover Letters/Resumes to [email protected] Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Advocacy Campaigns Manager – West
item.description: Advocacy Campaigns Manager – West Organization: Constellation Location: Sacramento, CA | Austin, TX | Washington, DC | Houston, TX | Chicago, IL | Walnut Creek, CA Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Job Description Who We Are As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation’s largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind, and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we’re creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country’s energy needs today and tomorrow. Total Rewards Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered: Bonus program 401(k) with company match Employee stock purchase program Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits Robust wellbeing programs Disability and life insurance benefits Paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days And much more Expected salary range: $126,900 to $141,000, based on experience, plus a comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus eligibility and 401(k). Primary Purpose of Position This position will be responsible for devising and executing proactive, externally focused communications strategies to build and maintain relationships with key NGOs, trade associations, think tanks, and nuclear energy and consumer influencers. A priority focus will be organizing and coordinating coalitions designed to influence assigned state policies, primarily in California and Texas, as well as federal policies related to low- and zero-emissions energy. This role requires understanding political and policy pressure points and identifying opportunities to advance reliable energy policies. Stakeholder management will be a key aspect of the role, including identifying and working with key community, industry, grassroots, grasstops, and third-party influencers, as well as building and managing networks of supporters and activists. This role also leads the execution of Constellation’s advocacy, education, and engagement campaigns across a variety of channels and tactics, including grassroots mobilization, coalition engagement, stakeholder outreach, events, media, and digital advocacy to build momentum and galvanize support for key policy and business priorities. The position will report to the Senior Manager, Public Affairs Campaigns and work collaboratively with Government Affairs & Public Policy, Communications, the Generation and Commercial businesses, Marketing, Brand and Reputation, Investor Relations, Legal, and other Constellation organizations. Primary Duties and Accountabilities Partner with Government Affairs, Communications, Marketing, Legal, and other teams to develop and execute strategic and comprehensive campaign plans in support of key local, state, and federal policy objectives. Identify, engage, and cultivate relationships with key stakeholders, community leaders, industry partners, and third-party advocates to advance business and policy priorities. Lead advocacy, education, and stakeholder engagement efforts across multiple channels, including grassroots mobilization, coalition activation, stakeholder outreach, events, digital advocacy, and direct engagement with policymakers. Monitor emerging issues from federal and state executive branches and legislatures. Provide strategic recommendations to advance support for business and policy priorities. Create and execute strategic and comprehensive campaign plans in support of key state and federal public policy objectives. Develop and maintain relationships with key thought leaders, influencers, NGOs, and allied advocacy groups. Build and maintain grassroots coalitions. Manage agency contracts and relationships to build modern, state-of-the-art digital campaigns and develop messaging materials for public policy priorities and stakeholder activation initiatives, including fact sheets, FAQs, mailers, digital advertisements, and other collateral. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree 8+ years of experience in political or policy communications, advocacy, journalism, public relations, or a related field Excellent writing skills and strong analytical thinking abilities Familiarity with digital campaigning and social media campaigning Demonstrated talent for strategic problem-solving with a bias for action Demonstrated organizational agility Demonstrated excellence in project management Preferred Qualifications Experience gained from a political campaign, advocacy group, think tank, journalism organization, Congressional office, or similar organization Existing relationships with influential NGOs, academic organizations, and/or think tanks in the environmental or energy sector Experience and knowledge of energy policy and politics Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Grassroots Advocacy Manager
item.description: Grassroots Advocacy Manager Organization: American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Grassroots Advocacy Manager Job Description Title: Grassroots Advocacy Manager Job Code: GAM Reports To: Director, Congressional Affairs Department: Advocacy Division: Programs Supervises: Not applicable Position Summary The Grassroots Advocacy Manager leads the planning and execution of the AAN’s grassroots and grasstops advocacy engagement efforts, driving member involvement and influencing policymakers. This role works closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to ensure program success, enhancing the overall effectiveness of the AAN’s advocacy efforts. Essential Accountabilities Advocate Grassroots and Grasstops Engagement Develop strategies in partnership with the Director, Congressional Affairs, for grassroots and grasstops engagement with policymakers. Plan and execute established strategies for grassroots and grasstops engagement with policymakers. Develop and present advocacy training and development content for members of the AAN’s grasstops network. In coordination with members of the Advocacy team, manage grassroots content on the AAN’s advocacy platform. In coordination with the Director, Congressional Affairs, create all external-facing content for grassroots advocacy. Work with the Advocacy Engagement Subcommittee and provide input to continue the development of neurology advocacy leaders throughout the year and encourage continued involvement in AAN advocacy initiatives. Advocacy Engagement Planning In coordination with the Director, Congressional Affairs, develop external-facing content for policymakers. Develop and implement all processes and programming to ensure the success and growth of the AAN’s fly-in events. Collaborate with internal stakeholders and advise on processes and curriculum for advocacy programs. Identify and manage relationships with external consultants for all advocacy programming. Responsible for budget preparation and tracking for associated projects, committees, and divisional categories. Prepare business plans and actively seek funding to support advocacy activities where applicable. Lead the onsite execution of fly-in events and assist in the onsite execution of advocacy leadership programs. Collaboration and Advocacy Work with the Director, Congressional Affairs, to ensure alignment of legislative strategy and grassroots goals. Attend hearings, briefings, coalition meetings, and other congressional activities for assigned areas. Represent the Academy in business meetings with members of Congress and congressional staff. This job description may not cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee for this position. Duties, activities, and responsibilities may change at any time, with or without notice. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Communications, Public Policy, or a related field. Minimum of 5 years of experience in advocacy program management. Demonstrated ability to uphold the AAN’s values. Demonstrated proficiency using Microsoft Office, specifically Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Strong organizational skills, including planning, delegating, and program development. Demonstrated exceptional attention to detail. Demonstrated advanced oral and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously. Relevant education and/or experience exceeding the required qualifications may be substituted on a year-for-year basis. Preferred Qualifications Association experience. Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information. Exhibits independent analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to consistently provide exceptional customer service in person, by phone, and through written and electronic correspondence. Additional Position Information FLSA Classification: Exempt Travel Requirements: Some travel required, up to 10%. Location: Washington, DC. This position is designated as hybrid and requires working in the office while allowing remote work for part of the week. Schedule: Occasional evening and weekend work required. AI Utilization: The utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) is assumed and expected to be conducted in a responsible, ethical, and transparent manner. Human judgment, critical thinking, and creativity remain essential to AAN’s operations and decision-making. Physical Requirements: Standard office setting, with the ability to sit, stand, or utilize alternative seating arrangements for extended periods as needed. Occasional use of stairs or accessibility devices. Regular use of a computer and office equipment, with consideration for adaptive technologies as necessary. Lifting requirements of up to 10 lbs., with accommodations provided for individuals with varying physical capabilities. The physical demands outlined above are essential to the successful performance of this position. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable all individuals, including those with disabilities, to fulfill these essential functions. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion is a commitment of the AAN. The AAN is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability status, sexual orientation, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Assistant Director, Grassroots & Political Engagement
item.description: Assistant Director, Grassroots & Political Engagement Organization: American Farm Bureau Federation (AFBF) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 POSITION OBJECTIVE Engage state Farm Bureaus and their members in grassroots advocacy tactics, political initiatives, and Farm Bureau’s policy development process. Strengthen and expand the organization’s political and advocacy impact through innovative programming, strategic initiatives, and data-driven analysis. REPORTS TO Managing Director, Advocacy & Political Affairs LOCATION Washington, DC; eligible to earn telework 2 days/week PAY RANGE $95,000 – $115,000 annually, commensurate with experience DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Identify opportunities to optimize AFBF’s grassroots advocacy efforts and political affairs initiatives using original analysis and data-backed strategy. Execute collective strategy to broaden AFBF’s reach and political footprint. Develop, prepare, and deliver training programs, specifically campaign training seminars, that will help state Farm Bureaus increase their overall effectiveness in grassroots advocacy and political affairs activities. This includes delivering presentations during state Farm Bureau visits, national conferences, AFBF leadership committee meetings, and as needed for other groups. Manage political engagement programs, such as iFarmiVote. Track key races and political trends and analyze them in the context of agriculture and rural America. Identify and recruit agriculture advocates and leaders to regularly engage in advocacy and the political process. Serve as a subject matter expert to promote and build strong political affairs programs with state Farm Bureaus. Deliver legislative and political briefings, political analysis, and other information to AFBF and state Farm Bureaus. Increase the effectiveness of advocacy programs for state partners and grassroots advocates. Serve on internal cross-functional teams in support of organizational goals and objectives. Execute online grassroots advocacy campaigns as needed. Assist in the preparation and management of the AFBF Policy Development Process, including the annual Resolutions Committee meeting and Business Session of the Delegate Body. Assist with the annual voting delegate session, including creating and editing materials related to the AFBF policy book and distributing materials to states. Assist with planning, preparation, and marketing of AFBF conferences with an advocacy track. Develop and cultivate strong working relationships with state Farm Bureau leadership and staff. RELATIONSHIPS Communicate with AFBF staff and state Farm Bureau staff regarding grassroots advocacy, congressional relations, and policy implementation. Operate as a team member of the Public Affairs Department. EDUCATION OR TRAINING REQUIRED Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED Minimum of three (3) years of relevant professional experience. Strong operational understanding of the executive and legislative branches of the federal government. Experience serving on internal cross-functional working groups, committees, or task forces. Strong organizational and program management skills. Strong communication and public speaking skills. PREFERRED EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/TRAINING/SKILLS Capitol Hill, Executive Branch, or political campaign experience. Training or facilitation experience. Familiarity with advocacy software. Knowledge of agriculture. OTHER REQUIREMENTS Ability to travel for on-site meetings. Ability to work evenings or weekends as needed. TO APPLY Please submit a cover letter and resume here . item.title: Director, Leadership Programs
item.description: Director, Leadership Programs Organization: Across the Aisle™ Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 About the Organization Since 2016, Across the Aisle™ , a nonpartisan, nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization, has been providing young Americans (ages 14 to 35) with opportunities to learn, lead, and find bipartisan solutions to our country’s biggest challenges. We work with experts from both sides of the aisle to empower voters with reliable facts and a framework to make their own informed decisions. Our leadership programs identify and prepare students and early-career professionals from both parties for decision-making positions on Capitol Hill, in the executive branch, and in other public service roles. Our core policy areas include fiscal issues like the national debt and the federal budget, as well as entitlement programs like Social Security and Medicare. Ready to use your time and talents to make a meaningful difference? Let’s talk. Position Description Across the Aisle™ is hiring a Director of Leadership Programs for its Answer the Call™ program to help us engage, educate, and empower the next generation of public policy leaders. The Director will manage a growing team of HQ-based staff, vendors, and remote consultants and will serve a program cohort of over 200 undergraduates and more than 600 alumni. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of: Producing engaging programs from concept through execution Scaling operations to serve a national cohort Managing a young and diverse group of program participants and alumni Juggling multiple projects at once Solving problems on the fly This job is perfect for someone who cares deeply about our country’s future, enjoys helping emerging leaders reach their potential, and wants to provide pathways to public service for young Americans. Strong preference will be given to candidates who: Are veterans and/or have experience providing educational programming or leadership training to veterans and/or members of the armed forces. Have higher education and program management experience at colleges or universities, nonprofits, or similar institutions. Core Duties Reporting directly to the Chief Operations Officer (COO), the Director of Leadership Programs will: Work with the COO to develop the department’s long-term strategic plan, including budgeting, staffing, objective setting, success metrics, program development, and geographic expansion. Manage a growing team located in Washington, D.C., overseeing and coordinating their work in admissions, on-campus programming, leadership training, and alumni programming. Manage a growing leadership program that serves more than 200 college and graduate students and over 600 alumni across the country. Build out leadership training and continuing engagement opportunities. Work with the Policy Department to refine and expand educational curriculum and leadership training offerings. Work with the Events and Logistics Manager in the planning, production, and execution of in-person events that serve leadership participants and alumni, including: Orientation and Ambassador Weekends Campus events Virtual events Educational programming and leadership initiatives currently in the pilot testing phase Work closely with the Director of Communications and Marketing to identify content programming opportunities and promote existing projects and programs. Produce, host, and manage FtF events across the country. Represent FtF at key meetings with program partners, hosts, and participants. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in student affairs, hospitality, political science, public policy, communications, or a related field. 4+ years of experience in higher education, program management, or a closely related field. Substantial knowledge of curriculum development, student affairs management, event planning logistics, and/or on-site staff management. Ability to balance multiple projects simultaneously, delegate work effectively, meet deadlines, and work within established budgets. Ability to travel 30% or more of the year, both locally and nationally. Flexibility to work evening hours and occasional weekends. Familiarity with the following software platforms is a plus: Slack Google Workspace Asana HubSpot Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge Zoom Navan Ability to meet the demands of an on-site event environment: Ability to remain in a stationary position for an extended period of time Ability to lift and/or move boxes and equipment Ability to position oneself under tables or stages and/or lower oneself to the floor Collaborative with a positive, solutions-oriented mindset and an ability to effectively represent the organization by engaging with others in an approachable, fair-minded, and accessible way that encourages discussion and engagement. Additional Information For more information, visit: Website: www.acrosstheaisle.org Instagram: @freefactsorg Email: [email protected] (Attention: COO Camden Stuebe) Term: Full-time in office, salaried role Salary: $120,000 – $195,000 Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Federal Government Relations
item.description: Manager, Federal Government Relations Organization: Walgreens Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Job Summary The Manager, Federal Government Relations, supports and advances Walgreens’ federal advocacy strategy, with primary responsibility for operating the company’s federal PAC and supporting federal political programs and communications. Reporting to the Senior Director, Federal Government Relations, this role combines policy and political judgment with strong program management. The Manager monitors federal developments, prepares clear advocacy materials, coordinates internal and external engagement, and maintains the tools and operating rhythm that enable an effective federal government relations program. Experience working on Capitol Hill, within a federal agency, in a corporate or trade association PAC, or in a government relations function is strongly preferred. The position is based in and enhances Walgreens’ Washington, D.C., presence. In Addition: Monitors federal legislative, regulatory, and political developments; identifies emerging issues, deadlines, and engagement opportunities; and provides timely updates to the federal government relations team. Maintains accurate trackers, calendars, stakeholder records, and project plans for priority federal initiatives, political programs, and external engagement. Prepares issue briefs, policy summaries, meeting materials, legislative background, talking points, and other materials for internal leaders and external engagement. Coordinates meetings, events, and follow-up with congressional offices, agencies, coalitions, trade associations, external lobbying firms, and internal business partners. Manages day-to-day operations of the PAC, including eligible employee engagement, solicitation and fundraising activities, contribution request intake and tracking, records management, reporting support, and program communications. Partners across the Government Relations team and other internal and external partners in support of PAC and political program operations consistent with applicable campaign finance, lobbying, and corporate policies. Supports the development and execution of federal political program, stakeholder engagement campaigns, and communications activities that advance Walgreens’ advocacy priorities and strengthen policymaker engagement. Contributes to effective management of federal government relations vendors, consultants, budgets, and program metrics. Based in Walgreens’ Washington, D.C., office to maintain the in-person presence, relationships, and responsiveness this role requires with federal stakeholders. Job Responsibilities Lobbying & Government Relations Support Monitor legislative activity and provide timely updates to the team on emerging issues and engagement opportunities. Maintain internal trackers and timelines for key legislative initiatives, ensuring deadlines, deliverables, and stakeholder inputs are organized and up to date. Assist in preparing policy briefs, issue summaries, and background materials for internal stakeholders and external engagement. Coordinate logistics for meetings with policymakers, including scheduling, preparing briefing materials, and compiling relevant background information. Partner with internal stakeholders to gather input and ensure alignment between advocacy priorities and business objectives. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including state government affairs, to support integrated advocacy efforts. Project Coordination & Team Operations Support the development and execution of grassroots advocacy campaigns to engage pharmacists, employees, and key stakeholders. Draft and distribute communications (emails, toolkits, alerts) that clearly translate policy priorities into actionable steps for stakeholders. Help grow and maintain a network of engaged advocates by tracking participation and identifying opportunities to increase involvement. Track and report on grassroots campaign performance, including engagement metrics and outcomes. PAC Support Provide administrative and coordination support for PAC activities, including tracking contributions and maintaining accurate records. Assist with targeted outreach and communications to support PAC engagement and fundraising efforts, as needed. About Walgreens Founded in 1901, Walgreens (www.walgreens.com) proudly serves nearly 9 million customers and patients each day across its approximately 8,500 stores throughout the U.S. and Puerto Rico. Walgreens has approximately 220,000 team members, including nearly 90,000 healthcare service providers, and is committed to being the first choice for pharmacy, retail, and health services, building trusted relationships that create healthier futures for customers, patients, team members, and communities. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree and at least 2 years of experience in government relations, trade association and/or a healthcare public policy environment; OR High School diploma/GED and at least 5 years of experience in government relations, trade association and/or a healthcare public policy environment. Experience supporting policy research, legislative tracking, and/or advocacy initiatives, including experience with the United States Congress (e.g., Capitol Hill offices or committees). Knowledge of the legislative process, including how bills move through Congress, committee structure, and key stakeholder roles. Experience managing multiple priorities, timelines, and deliverables in a fast-paced environment. Experience collaborating with cross-functional internal teams. Experience translating complex policy topics into accessible materials for a range of audiences. Experience managing projects, including maintaining trackers, accurately organizing data/information, and/or communicating with stakeholders. Willing to travel up to 25% of the time for business purposes (within state and out of state). Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Communications, Business, or a related field. Prior experience in government relations, advocacy, or public affairs (corporate, trade association, consulting, or government). Prior experience operating or supporting the management of a federal PAC, campaign finance compliance, or political program operations. Experience on Capitol Hill, in a federal agency, in a corporate government relations function, or at a trade association. Experience in healthcare, pharmacy, retail, reimbursement, or another regulated industry. Experience using legislative tracking tools, policy databases, constituent relations systems, campaign advocacy management platforms, CRM systems, or similar tools. Experience supporting political engagement or campaign-adjacent programs (e.g., fundraising events, candidate briefings, political action committee governance). Experience supporting legislative tracking, policy research, advocacy, political engagement, stakeholder outreach, or related program operations. Working knowledge of Congress and the federal legislative process, including how bills move through Congress, committee structure, and the roles of key stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, data, and deliverables accurately in a fast-paced environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex policy topics into clear materials for varied audiences. Experience collaborating effectively with cross-functional internal teams and external partners. Willing to travel up to 25% of the time for business purposes (within and outside the Washington, D.C., area). We will consider employment of qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. The salary below is being provided to promote pay transparency and equal employment opportunities at Walgreens. The actual salary within this range that you will be offered will depend on a variety of factors, including geography, skills and abilities, education, experience, and other relevant factors. This role will remain open until filled.
