item.title: Partner Manager, Government, Politics, and Advocacy
item.description: Partner Manager, Government, Politics, and Advocacy Organization: Meta Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Partner Manager, Government, Politics, and Advocacy Meta is seeking an experienced Partner Manager who will serve as a critical partner to Government, Politics and Advocacy clients utilizing our commercial products to build community and advance their organizational goals through digital advertising. In this role, you will establish and strengthen key client relationships by providing advertiser education and support. A successful Partner Manager has demonstrated knowledge of and experience in the Government, Politics, Advocacy, and Compliance ecosystem, seeks to understand the nuances of the industry, makes progress on projects when requirements or priorities are evolving, and has effective communication skills, as well as demonstrated experience collaborating across teams. This person will have demonstrated experience working well within a team, experience using Meta, managing cross-functional projects and relationships, and demonstrated experience partnering with Government, Politics, Advocacy, and Compliance organizations in the digital advertising space. Partner Manager, Government, Politics, and Advocacy Responsibilities Establish relationships and manage existing relationships across the Government, Politics, Advocacy, and Compliance marketing and advertising ecosystem, building trust and credibility in Meta and its suite of products. Understand key decision-makers and influencers, as well as clients’ organizational objectives; establish and maintain actionable relationship maps. Demonstrate the value of Meta products as a key driver for impact, inform partners of vertical-specific processes, and provide Meta best practices specific to Government, Politics, Advocacy, and Compliance objectives. Navigate a complex ecosystem of partners, with new challenges and opportunities arising every day, and thoughtfully facilitate escalations internally. Develop and implement creative solutions that align Meta’s approach to Government, Politics, Advocacy, and Compliance with partner needs. Manage sophisticated relationships with a wide-ranging group of internal cross-functional teams, including social impact, policy, sales operations, creative, marketing science, and policy teams, ensuring the group delivers on expectations. Project manage complex workstreams. Attend and present at events to represent Meta Advertising solutions. Serve as an external product consultant and lead agency, client, and industry trainings to educate stakeholders on paid and organic products (market permitting). Supervise internal account operations and partner with the concierge service operations team to drive high-quality solutions at scale for the government, politics, advocacy, and compliance vertical. Identify relevant industry trends and capture product and innovation needs based on client and industry feedback. Inform and respond to RFPs with appropriate target audiences. Synthesize data and insights for internal and external audiences. Partner with cross-functional teams to deliver service solutions across the government, politics, and advocacy vertical, ensuring teams deliver on expectations and escalating as needed. Develop productive and trusting relationships with partners and their stakeholders by demonstrating the value of Meta products as a key driver for civic engagement. Minimum Qualifications 5+ years of experience partnering and managing marketing-focused relationships, or 3+ years with an MBA or Master’s degree. 2+ years of experience working on digital media platforms, advertising metrics, and industry trends. Experience introducing new products, processes, and systems to clients. Experience working with advertising agencies or consultants, policymakers, governments, politicians, nonprofits, or advocacy organizations. Willingness to travel as needed. Understanding of the overall government, politics, and advocacy vertical and geopolitical climate. In-depth knowledge of government, politics, and advocacy trends, partners, sensitivities, Meta’s unique relationship with each partner, and the associated risks. Experience developing thought leadership in the government, politics, and advocacy space. Demonstrated experience managing ongoing partner priorities independently, using sound judgment and problem-solving skills. Experience navigating internal resources and building trusted relationships with cross-functional stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications Experience with digital media platforms, advertising metrics, and industry trends, including direct response marketing, data and technology solutions, ad-tech, and partnerships. Experience partnering with compliance and legal functions. Demonstrated experience communicating and presenting to groups of stakeholders. Experience managing relationships with cross-functional teams, including partnership with executive leadership. Bachelor’s degree in a technical or marketing field, or equivalent work experience. Performance marketing experience and/or brand advertising experience. About Meta Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram, and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences such as augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today, beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics. Compensation and Benefits United States of America: $105,000 to $155,000 per year, plus bonus, equity, and benefits. Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Compensation details listed in this posting reflect the base hourly rate, monthly rate, or annual salary only and do not include bonus, equity, or sales incentives, if applicable. In addition to base compensation, Meta offers a comprehensive benefits package. Learn more about Meta benefits. Equal Employment Opportunity Meta is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. item.title: Communications Manager
item.description: Communications Manager Organization: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 About ARI ARI is a nonprofit organization advocating for artificial intelligence policy in the public interest. We believe in establishing a thoughtful governance framework for rapidly advancing AI technology that protects the public from harm while continuing to foster innovation. ARI takes a bipartisan approach, building coalitions across the political spectrum. Overview ARI is seeking a Communications Manager for Frontier AI Safety to help drive public understanding and policy momentum on some of the most urgent questions in AI governance. This role sits at the intersection of communications, government affairs, and policy, translating complex ideas into compelling narratives and grassroots momentum that shape how lawmakers, journalists, and the public understand AI. Reporting to the VP of Communications, the Communications Manager will play a critical role in advancing ARI’s work on key issues including frontier safety, interpretability, and the federal oversight of advanced AI models. This person will help ensure ARI is not just part of the conversation, but shapes it. The Communications Manager will also help strengthen the communications infrastructure of existing AI safety organizations that regularly engage on policy but lack in-house communications support, media relationships, or rapid-response systems. This person will provide communications support functions for AI safety organizations, covering media engagement, message discipline, op-ed drafting, and crisis response. Key Responsibilities Manage proactive and reactive media communications for a portfolio of issues related to frontier AI risks. Work closely with ARI’s policy, government affairs, and coalitions teams to design strategic media campaigns in support of policy objectives. Draft, edit, and pitch media statements and exclusives with national news outlets. Monitor the media and policy landscape and identify opportunities for ARI to engage quickly and effectively. Develop shared communications templates, rapid-response toolkits, talking points, and narrative frameworks that provide support across the AI safety community. Help partners develop rapid-response plans that identify spokespeople, messaging, and approval flows for key scenarios (preemption threats, export-control rollbacks, safety incidents, etc.). Publish timely online commentary in coordination with the policy team and ensure ARI is there first in key moments of public debate. Sustain a drumbeat of coverage and content that builds momentum and focuses policymaker attention on priority issues. Qualifications Required 4–5+ years of experience in policy communications, public affairs, or policy advocacy. Strong writer with the ability to translate complex policy issues into clear, compelling language. Experience working on technology and AI policy. Proven ability to engage with media and contribute to successful communications campaigns. Sound judgment and comfort operating in fast-moving, high-stakes policy environments. Previous professional engagement on artificial intelligence and its societal impacts. Preferred An established digital presence and a track record of engaging relevant audiences on online platforms. On-the-record media experience. Compensation, Benefits, and Location This is a full-time position based in Washington, DC. Relocation assistance may be available. ARI maintains a flexible hybrid work schedule, working in person Tuesday through Thursday and remotely on Monday and Friday. The salary range for this role is $115,000–$135,000, commensurate with experience. ARI offers a comprehensive benefits package, including: Healthcare insurance: 85% of healthcare, vision, and dental insurance premiums are covered for employees, partners, and dependents. Discretionary PTO and approximately 20 office holidays, including all federal holidays and the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day. 401(k) Retirement Plan with 6% employer match. Wellness Benefit: $150 per month taxable stipend to support physical and mental well-being. Internet & Utilities Reimbursement: $150 per month taxable stipend to cover internet and utility expenses associated with remote work. Home Office Expenses for New Employees: Up to $500 for home office setup expenses. Professional Development Stipend: Up to $2,500 annually to support building new knowledge and skills. Basic Life, Basic AD&D, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability insurance: 100% employer-paid, with optional employee-paid supplemental coverage. Flexible Spending Accounts: Dependent Care FSA, Medical FSA, Transit FSA, and Parking FSA. How to Apply To apply, please submit a resume, cover letter, and two writing samples reflecting relevant communications work here . The priority deadline for this role is September 30. Anticipated Hiring Process We plan to use the following steps for this hiring process. We are aiming for the person in this role to start by the end of June. Application Review: Our team will review submitted applications and decide which candidates will move forward to the next step of the process. Hiring Manager Interview: Virtual one-on-one conversation with the Hiring Manager. Hiring Exercise: A roughly three-hour hiring exercise. Candidates who submit an exercise will be compensated for their time. Panel Interview: In-person panel interview at our office. Finalist Interview: In-person interview with the President. Reference Checks: We will request references from the top candidate(s) to help confirm and support a final hiring decision. Due to the anticipated volume of applications, we may not be able to respond to every applicant in a timely manner. We apologize in advance for any communication delays. Referral Bonus Know a great fit for any roles for which we’re hiring? We value your network and will reward non-employees for successful referrals to help us attract and hire the very best talent to advance our mission. If you refer a candidate who receives and accepts our offer, you will receive a referral bonus of $3,000 for any Director- or Vice President-level role, and $1,500 for all other positions. To qualify: The candidate must list your name as the referral source in the application. The candidate must receive and accept the offer. The candidate must start and remain employed with us for at least 30 days. To participate in this program, you must be a legal resident of the United States. If the referral is successfully hired by ARI, an ARI representative will contact you to obtain the required documents (such as a W-9 form) needed to receive the referral bonus. The bonus will be paid within 60 days after the candidate has completed the required 30-day tenure period and all required documentation has been submitted. Pay Range $115,000-$135,000 USD Americans for Responsible Innovation is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, national origin, marital status, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, personal appearance, family responsibilities, political affiliation, or protected veteran status. item.title: Vice President of State Government Affairs
item.description: Vice President of State Government Affairs Organization: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Overview Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is seeking a Vice President of State Government Affairs to build and lead a new state advocacy operation. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Government Affairs, the VP of State Government Affairs will establish ARI’s presence in state capitals across the country, defend against harmful AI legislation, and advance responsible AI policy at the state level. The VP will hire and lead a team of Regional Directors of Government Affairs and manage a national network of contract lobbyists. About Us ARI is a nonprofit organization advocating for artificial intelligence policy in the public interest. We believe in establishing a thoughtful governance framework for rapidly advancing AI technology that protects the public from harm while continuing to foster innovation. ARI takes a bipartisan approach, building coalitions across the political spectrum. About the Role Major AI companies and allied industry groups have moved aggressively into state capitals, backed by substantial lobbying operations and political spending. State legislators, who typically have limited staff and little independent technology policy expertise, are frequently presented with industry-drafted legislation and few alternatives. ARI is building a state operation to meet that challenge. The VP of State Government Affairs will lead it. The role has two mandates. The first, and primary, is defensive: work with policy staff and lobbyists to monitor legislation across all fifty states, identify industry-friendly and preemption-oriented bills early, and intervene where it matters. The second is proactive: advance sound state legislation in the issue areas where ARI already has expertise. The VP will set the annual fifty-state strategy, hire and manage four Regional Directors of Government Affairs, and represent ARI to national bodies including NCSL, CSG, NGA, and state legislative leadership. We are looking for someone who has built or run a multi-state program before and wants to apply that experience to one of the most consequential technology policy questions of the decade. Key Responsibilities Strategy and Leadership • Set and own ARI’s annual fifty-state advocacy plan, including which states to defend, where to advance legislation, and what not to pursue. • Recruit, hire, and lead a distributed team of four Regional Directors of Government Affairs. • Work closely with the federal government affairs team so that state activity strengthens ARI’s federal advocacy, and vice versa. Legislative Advocacy • Lead rapid-response advocacy when harmful bills are moving, including direct lobbying in state capitals. • Support the advancement of pro-guardrails legislation in ARI’s existing issue areas, including frontier AI governance, children’s safety, creator protections, bias and discrimination, and data centers and energy. • Recruit and support state legislators willing to engage federal policymakers in opposition to sweeping preemption of state AI law. • Hold and manage a contract lobbying budget, including retaining, directing, and evaluating contract lobbyists in key states. External Relationships • Represent ARI to the National Conference of State Legislatures, the Council of State Governments, the National Governors Association, and state legislative leadership. • Build relationships with state attorneys general offices, governors’ policy and legislative staff, and state agency officials. • Serve as ARI’s principal working link to allied organizations operating at the state level, ensuring our work complements rather than duplicates theirs. • Build and strengthen partnerships with state-level consumer, parent, labor, creator, and faith organizations. Qualifications Required • 10+ years of experience in government affairs, advocacy, or government, including at least 5 years leading multi-state advocacy work. • A demonstrated record of building or running a state government affairs program at an advocacy organization, trade association, corporation, or comparable setting. • Direct experience retaining and managing contract lobbyists across multiple states. • Substantive knowledge of state legislative process, including session calendars, procedural deadlines, and the differences between professionalized and citizen legislatures. • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with legislators of both parties. • Management experience, including hiring and retaining a geographically distributed team. • Passion for the responsible governance of AI and emerging technology, and alignment with ARI’s mission and values. • Reputation for trustworthiness and integrity. • Willingness to travel frequently, particularly during legislative sessions from January through May. Preferred • Experience with technology, privacy, consumer protection, or telecommunications policy at the state level. • Service as a state legislator, legislative staff director, governor’s legislative director, or in a comparable state role. • Familiarity with AI policy and the current state and federal legislative landscape. • Experience building bipartisan or cross-ideological coalitions at the state level. • Experience with state ballot measure campaigns. Compensation, Benefits, and Location This is a full-time position based in Washington, DC. ARI maintains a flexible hybrid work schedule, working in person Tuesday through Thursday and remotely on Monday and Friday. Relocation assistance may be available. This role requires substantial travel, concentrated during state legislative sessions. The salary range for this role is $300,000-$350,000, commensurate with experience. ARI offers a comprehensive benefits package, including: • Healthcare insurance: 85% of healthcare, vision, and dental insurance premiums are covered for employees, partners, and dependents. • Discretionary PTO and approximately 20 office holidays, including all federal holidays and the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day. • 401(k) Retirement Plan with 6% employer match. • Wellness Benefit: $150/month taxable stipend to support physical and mental well-being. • Internet & Utilities Reimbursement: $150/month taxable stipend to cover internet and utilities expenses related to remote work. • Home Office Expenses for New Employees: Up to $500 for home office setup expenses. • Professional Development Stipend: Up to $2,500 annually to build new knowledge and skills. • Basic Life, Basic AD&D, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability coverage: 100% employer-paid, with optional employee-paid supplemental coverage. • Flexible Spending Accounts: Dependent Care FSA, Medical FSA, Transit FSA, and Parking FSA. How to Apply To apply, please complete the application form and submit: • Resume. • A cover letter, which can be just a few sentences, introducing who you are, explaining what makes you a fit for the role, and including a brief description of a multi-state advocacy program you have built. Anticipated Hiring Process We plan to use the following steps for this hiring process: Application Review Our team will review submitted applications and decide which candidates will move forward in the process. Hiring Manager Interview Virtual one-on-one conversation with the SVP of Government Affairs. At this stage, candidates will also be asked to provide a work sample demonstrating how they have set strategy for a multi-state program in the past. Government Affairs Panel Interview In-person conversation at our office with members of the Government Affairs team. Cross-Departmental Panel Interview In-person conversation at our office with colleagues from Communications, Policy, and Operations. Final Interview In-person interview with the President. Reference Checks References will be requested from the top candidate(s) to help confirm and inform the final hiring decision. Due to the anticipated volume of applications, we may not be able to respond to every applicant in a timely manner. We apologize in advance for any communication delays. Referral Bonus Know a great fit for any roles for which we’re hiring? We value your network and will reward non-employees for successful referrals to help us attract and hire the very best talent to advance our mission. If you refer a candidate who receives and accepts our offer, you’ll receive a referral bonus of: • $3,000 for any Director- or Vice President-level role. • $1,500 for all other positions. To Qualify • The candidate must list your name as the referral source in the application. • The candidate must receive and accept the offer. • The candidate must start and remain employed with us for at least 30 days. To participate in this program, you must be a legal resident of the United States. If the referral is successfully hired by ARI, an ARI representative will contact you to obtain the required documents (such as a W-9) needed to receive the referral bonus. The bonus will be paid within 60 days after the candidate has completed the required 30-day tenure period and all required documentation has been submitted. Pay Range $300,000-$350,000 USD Americans for Responsible Innovation is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, national origin, marital status, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, personal appearance, family responsibilities, political affiliation, or protected veteran status. item.title: Senior Director, Public Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Public Affairs Organization: Story Partners Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/23/2026 Senior Director, Public Affairs Story Partners, a leading public affairs firm in Washington, D.C., is seeking a Senior Director to manage client campaigns and drive strategy and execution across a broad range of client accounts. The successful candidate will have at least eight years of public affairs experience, including three to four years at a public affairs agency. Experience on Capitol Hill and in the energy sector is strongly preferred. Story Partners is a hybrid work environment offering flexibility and balance between working from home and going into the office. Responsibilities • Develop and execute public affairs strategies that align with client goals. • Lead day-to-day client work including media relations, grassroots advocacy, digital and social media, events, executive positioning, and thought leadership. • Prioritize client accounts by engaging regularly with clients, handling many of the day-to-day deliverables, and consistently pursuing impactful, innovative, and creative strategies. • Lead the creation of communications materials, including opinion pieces, press releases, digital and social media content, newsletter content, fact sheets, website content, and advertising copy. • Develop and implement tailored earned media strategies and generate media placements on behalf of clients. • Participate in business development opportunities such as idea generation, building campaign strategies, drafting proposals and presentations, and pitching new business. • Manage vendors such as media buyers, videographers, and photographers. • Collaborate with all members of the Story Partners team to support client accounts. • Manage and mentor junior account managers. Qualifications • Demonstrated relationship-building, leadership, project management, and problem-solving skills. • Proven ability to develop and execute successful public affairs campaigns. • Strong event management skills, with the ability to plan and execute high-profile events such as press conferences, forums, and salon dinners. • Leverage a deep understanding of the social media landscape and digital advertising strategies to drive client outcomes. • Strong writing skills with a persuasive writing portfolio. • Detail-oriented team player and self-starter who works well in a fast-paced environment. • Based in the Washington, D.C. area. • Bachelor’s degree. This is an excellent growth opportunity for an ambitious team player with a solid record of achievement in public affairs. Story Partners offers an excellent salary and benefits package, including a new business incentive plan, health insurance, 401(k), Paid Time Off (PTO), holidays, and opportunities for professional development. Salary is commensurate with experience. Interested candidates should send a resume and cover letter to [email protected] Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Internal Communications
item.description: Director of Internal Communications Organization: DLA Piper Location: New York, NY | San Diego, CA | San Francisco, CA | Washington, DC | Wilmington, DE | Phoenix, AZ | Los Angeles, CA | Houston, TX | Boston, MA | Austin, TX | Atlanta, GA | Raleigh, NC | Baltimore, MD | Dallas, TX | Palo Alto, CA | Short Hills, NJ | Minneapolis, MN | Seattle, WA | Philadelphia, PA | Miami, FL Date Posted: 09/24/2026 DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together. The Role The Director of Internal Communications is a collaborative leader with a track record of delivering high-quality internal communications in a professional environment. As a key member of the Communications leadership team, this individual will work with senior executives to use communications to advance firm priorities, strengthen engagement, and help bring the firm’s vision to life. The Director leads the Internal Communications team and is responsible for developing and executing a cohesive internal communications strategy, using technology to maximize the team’s quality of work product and speed, and holding the team accountable for delivering consistently excellent written product. Location This position can sit in any of our US offices. What You Will Be Responsible For Strategic & Executive Communications Design, implement, and manage internal communications aligned with business objectives and the firm’s culture of excellence. Establish, lead, and evolve a sophisticated internal communications team that fosters engagement and connection to the firm’s vision. Develop narratives, messaging frameworks, and campaigns that support firm priorities. Act as a trusted advisor to partners and administrative leaders on strategic communications planning, executive messaging, and engagement strategies. Align messaging and voice across internal and external communications, in coordination with Public Relations, Marketing, and related teams. Team Leadership & Development Provide oversight, guidance, and mentorship to the Internal Communications team, advancing professional development, editorial excellence, process improvements, and innovative thinking. Foster a culture of excellence, coaching team members to deliver high-quality work and develop their capabilities as communicators. Content Creation Produce, oversee, and distribute engaging, strategically aligned content across various channels, including the firm’s intranet, town halls, email communications, video messages, newsletters, and other platforms. Develop multi-format content—articles, scripts, videos, briefings, and presentations. Measurement, Analytics & Continuous Improvement Establish metrics and analytics frameworks to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness and impact of communications initiatives, channels, and campaigns. Leverage data-driven insights to make informed improvements, demonstrate measurable results, and continuously refine strategies for maximum impact. Who You Will Work With You will report to the Chief Communications Officer. Qualifications Experience & Expertise 10+ years of progressive experience developing strategy and producing high-quality communications content within a legal, corporate, academic, military, or other professional environment. Experience working with C-suite or equivalent senior leaders in complex, global, or matrixed organizations. Demonstrated success managing communication strategies for large-scale organizational changes and strategic initiatives. Background in journalism, writing, PR, marketing, executive communications, strategic content, or corporate communications. Skills & Competencies Exceptional strategic communications planning capabilities. Commitment to precision and sophistication in communications Excellent writing and editing skills, with the ability to craft clear narratives for a range of audiences—from executive leadership to broad employee populations across levels and geographies. Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills. Experience managing internal channel platforms (intranets, digital workplace tools) across global audiences. People leadership experience, including coaching, collaboration across teams, and the ability to lead effectively in a matrixed organization. Strong project management and organizational capabilities, with the ability to manage time effectively, prioritize competing demands, and handle multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency with Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and modern collaboration tools. Education Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Business, Marketing, or a related field required. Essential Job Expectations All DLA Piper employees are expected to demonstrate excellence in how we serve our clients and develop our people, upholding our firm values as part of our culture. Specific expectations include: Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with clients, lawyers, business professionals, and external audiences. Produce high-quality work and respond to correspondence in an efficient, timely, and professional manner. Meet deadlines, manage competing priorities, and commit to meeting high standards. Comply with firm policies and procedures. Maintain confidences as required in a law firm environment. Physical Demands This is primarily sedentary work, requiring occasional exertion of up to 10 pounds of force to lift, carry, push, pull, or move objects. The role involves sitting for extended periods, with occasional walking and standing, and occasional travel, both domestic and international. Work Environment The selected candidate will have the opportunity for a hybrid work arrangement combining remote and in-office work. The specific arrangement will be determined at the time of hiring and may be modified at the firm’s discretion. Compensation & Benefits The firm’s expected hiring range for this position is $193,750 – $313,893, depending on the candidate’s geographic location, experience, skills, educational background, and overall qualifications. DLA Piper offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, and additional benefits. Application Process Interested candidates must apply directly online . Application materials sent via email will not be accepted. Reasonable accommodations may be made upon request to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position or participate in the selection process. For accommodation requests, please contact [email protected] . Agency applications will not be considered. No immigration sponsorship is available for this position. Disclaimer This job description provides a concise overview of the role and is not intended to describe all work elements that may be performed. It should not serve as the sole criteria for personnel decisions. Job duties, requirements, and expectations may be modified at the firm’s discretion at any time. This job description does not alter the at-will nature of employment. We are committed to excellence in how we serve our clients and develop our people. #LI-GB1 #LI-Hybrid DLA Piper is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. item.title: Vice President, Strategic Engagement & Communications
item.description: Vice President, Strategic Engagement & Communications Organization: Manufacturing Institute (MI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Who We Are: The Manufacturing Institute (MI) aims to build and strengthen the manufacturing workforce for individual opportunity, community prosperity, and a competitive manufacturing industry for the future. Through our vision to ensure a manufacturing workforce resilient to the challenges and prepared for the opportunities of the 21st century, the MI’s initiatives support all American workers through skilled training programs, community building and career growth. As the 501(c)3 nonprofit workforce development and education affiliate of the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM), the MI is a trusted adviser to manufacturers, equipping them with resources necessary to solve the industry’s toughest challenges. Position Overview: The Manufacturing Institute is seeking a strategic, entrepreneurial and highly collaborative Vice President, Strategic Engagement & Communications in a new role created to lead and integrate the MI’s communications function across marketing, brand positioning, enterprise-wide messaging, stakeholder communications, media relations and executive communications functions. Reporting to the President of the Manufacturing Institute, this senior role will develop, shape and strengthen the MI’s brand awareness, narrative and communications strategy, ensuring the Institute’s mission, programs, research, partnerships and impact are clearly positioned for priority audiences, including manufacturers, philanthropic entities, workforce organizations, economic development and educational entities, policymakers, partners, media and internal stakeholders. The Vice President will serve as the senior communications strategist within the MI’s leadership team, translating the MI’s strategic priorities into compelling narratives, identifying opportunities to elevate the Institute’s national leadership and ensuring communications efforts reinforce the organization’s mission, reputation, and long-term goals. This position will work closely with the MI’s affiliate, the NAM’s strategic communications leads as well as the MI program leaders to align priorities, elevate the MI’s national workforce leadership, support fundraising and partner engagement. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute an integrated communications strategy that advances the MI’s mission, strategic priorities, and organizational objectives. Build and lead an integrated communications function across content, executive communications, marketing, media relations, and digital communications. Develop and drive the MI’s marketing strategy to strengthen organizational positioning and increase awareness of the MI’s impact and capabilities. Identify opportunities to strengthen the MI’s reputation as the national leader in manufacturing workforce development and education. Develop and lead a comprehensive partner and funder communications strategy in close collaboration with the VP of Partnerships & Philanthropy and MI leadership, ensuring all stewardship, recognition, and impact communications reinforce the value and outcomes of partner engagement. Collaborate with the NAM’s Strategic Communications team to set the MI’s media strategy and coordinate with them on proactive media engagement, message development, publication rollouts, rapid response and opportunities to amplify MI priorities. Manage the MI’s editorial strategy across all channels to maximize reach, amplify priorities, and ensure brand alignment. Oversee the MI’s Content Team to translate program outcomes, research findings, convenings, employer engagement and workforce solutions into high-impact content. Serve as the primary point of contact for the MI with the NAM’s strategic communications team to support integrated planning and ensure the MI’s work is appropriately reflected in broader NAM reports, speeches, campaigns, events and external communications. Plan and execute communications, including but not limited to, message architecture, rollout planning, stakeholder alignment and audience-specific materials. Maintain awareness of workforce, manufacturing, education, labor market, media and policy trends to identify opportunities for relevant insights and thought leadership. Establish communications planning, governance and decision-making processes that improve coordination, prioritization and organizational impact. The above list of responsibilities represents the position and is not intended to limit or preclude other duties and tasks that may be associated with or added to the position. Supervisory Responsibilities: Directly supervise the Director of the MI’s Workforce Content Team, providing strategic direction, performance management, coaching and professional development. Oversee external communications contractors, consultants and agency partners as needed. Qualifications: 12+ years of progressively responsible communications, marketing, public affairs or external relations experience; Experience working in an association, nonprofit, workforce development, education or manufacturing environment preferred. Demonstrated ability to develop and execute integrated communications strategies that advance organizational priorities, shape narratives and reach multiple audiences. Strong track record of managing multiple portfolios simultaneously, balancing long-term strategic objectives with immediate, high-priority opportunities. Exceptional writer and editor, with experience producing high-impact content, remarks, op-eds, donor communications, briefing materials and public-facing content. Experience advising senior executives and translating complex issues into digestible communications. Strong media relations judgment and ability to coordinate proactive and responsive communications in partnership with internal and external stakeholders. Ability to manage complex projects independently, balance competing priorities and deliver high-quality work under deadlines. And finally, it’s essential that you have… Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Relationships are important; this role will build, support and strengthen relationships with staff, partners, donors, media and other stakeholders. A team-oriented attitude with a developed customer service focus. The MI’s work is collaborative and often shaped through relationships across the organization and with external partners. Sound judgment, discretion and a commitment to producing accurate, high-impact communications that reflect the MI’s mission and values. Salary Range: $152,000 – $210,000 annually. This salary range represents a good faith estimate of the lowest to the highest salary for this position. The final salary offered will be based on qualifications and experience. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Equal Opportunity Employer The Manufacturing Institute is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer that is committed to inclusion and diversity. We welcome and celebrate everyone’s uniqueness here at the MI. We provide equal opportunities to individuals regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with conviction histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. At the MI, we believe in Second Chances! The MI is committed to offering equal employment opportunities to ALL. We only require that you have the qualifications, talent and passion to be successful in your role. The MI is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at [email protected] . By joining the MI, you become part of a spirited and dynamic team that is driven to succeed. We recognize and reward our staff with competitive pay and annual performance-based bonus programs. We offer an outstanding benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, life, short-term and long-term disability, flexible spending accounts, SmarTrip, and a 401(k) Salary Deferral plan with employer match and contributions, vacation, and sick leave, and more. Become part of a fast-paced team passionate about keeping the United States the world leader in manufacturing. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Vice President, Public Affairs (Healthcare) Organization: Omnicom Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Description: Overview This position will work with senior leaders at the firm to build, support and manage communications and advocacy campaigns for clients across the healthcare ecosystem. A successful candidate will have experience supporting clients and/or multifaceted campaigns, excellent interpersonal skills and will possess strong project and team management skills. Experience creating and overseeing high-quality deliverables, ensuring the accuracy of details. Willingness to be an agile, flexible team player is a must. The ideal candidate will have a public affairs, public relations, nonprofit or political background and experience managing multichannel communications and advocacy campaigns. The position will be based in Washington, DC, where our culture includes being in the office 3 days a week. VOX Global believes a diverse team brings a wider range of personal and professional experiences and perspectives. We recognize that diversity and inclusion benefit our agency, clients, and the communities in which we work and live. To that end, we strongly encourage applications from people of color, members of the LGBTQ+ community, veterans, and individuals with disabilities. Qualifications 8-10 years of experience in strategic communications, public relations, public affairs, social media, campaign or political communications. Experience managing a team of mid-level managers and junior staff under tight deadlines while displaying strong people skills and ensuring quality deliverables. Experience interfacing directly with clients in a fast-paced environment and preparing and staffing senior executives. Strong project management skills and ability to ensure teams are meeting established goals, timelines, and budgets Experience with multichannel communications strategies and tactics, including earned media, social and paid media, and event execution. Proven ability to develop and edit high-quality written materials, including press releases, executive thought leadership (including bylines), social media copy, talking points, executive briefing materials, analytical pieces, website/creative copy, and more. Account and budget management experience – familiarity with agency billing practices, scoping projects and managing budgets. About VOX Based in Washington, D.C., VOX Global uses a wide variety of communications skills to deliver messaging that resonates with our clients’ target audiences. VOX Global is a bi-partisan public affairs firm and is part of the Omnicom strategic communications network. We are committed to personal growth through unique opportunities and professional development. For more information, visit www.voxglobal.com. VOX Global is committed to equal employment opportunity and affirmative action. VOX Global does not discriminate in any aspect of employment on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, age, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where VOX Global does business. Our policy is to employ, advance, and reasonably accommodate all qualified employees and applicants. The anticipated salary range for the Vice President level is $115,000-$150,000. Salary is based on a range of factors that include relevant experience, knowledge, skills, other job-related qualifications and geography. A range of medical, dental, vision, 401(k) matching, paid time off and/or other benefits also are available. Omnicom’s policy requires employees to work in the office for a minimum of three days a week, unless additional in-office days are directed by their agency or manager. Our objective is to increase this requirement over time, and many of our agencies as well as Omnicom’s corporate group already require five days of in-office attendance. Omnicom is committed to hiring and developing exceptional talent. We agree that talent is uniquely distributed, and we’re focused on developing inclusive teams that can bring the best solutions to everything we do. item.title: Account Supervisor – Corporate Reputation + Media Relations
item.description: Account Supervisor – Corporate Reputation + Media Relations Organization: Omnicom Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Description: Overview FleishmanHillard’s Washington D.C. office is seeking an experienced and versatile communications professional to join the firm’s Corporate Reputation practice as an Account Supervisor focused on media relations. This is a hybrid role. This position provides a fantastic opportunity for a mid-level communications professional with a background in and passion corporate communications to work with collaborative teams on communications strategy and campaigns, media relations, corporate positioning, business development and content creation on behalf of our industry-leading clients. In this role, you will work directly with clients across industries to help devise and execute large-scale communications campaigns that directly impact their bottom line, with a focus on media engagement and storytelling. Our clients will depend on you to be responsive, thoughtful and proactive with ideas, own and drive communications programs from concept through execution, delivering measurable results. You will own and advance media relations efforts on behalf of these clients across top-tier business, trade, and policy outlets. The ideal candidate is extremely organized, a self-starter who both initiates and executes, and demonstrates an ability to find synergies between multiple workstreams. They bring creative instincts to open-ended challenges and precision execution to tightly scoped ones, switching between both modes fluidly. FleishmanHillard values the importance of impact and inclusion to strengthen the bonds between us, grow our people and create spaces for everyone to thrive. We stay true to our commitment to our people and the communities in which we live and work. As part of our ongoing effort to be the world’s most inclusive agency, we are committed to seeking candidates who possess and demonstrate a profound interest in furthering our impact and inclusion goals. Responsibilities Build traditional and nontraditional media relations strategies, manage and execute campaigns and projects with a team, for our clients across sectors. Identify and pursue proactive opportunities (story angles, rapid response opps, newsjacking moments, etc.) without waiting to be asked, bringing a clear point of view on how to capitalize. Develop and maintain strong media relationships with business and policy reporters and pitch ideas. Help shape client stories and messages with partners across media and platforms, with the goal of integrating clients into the broader news cycle. Lead, support, and motivate teams to successfully build and maintain relationships with and correspondence to external: top-tier reporters, client partners, SMEs, etc. Write and edit communications materials that capture relevant audiences and reflect an understanding of our clients’ businesses – ranging from internal to external documents, including pitches, plans, memos, research, written content, media materials, website and social media content, client correspondence, and collateral. Play a pivotal role in overseeing and finding synergies between several client workstreams and account teams, including managing budgets and forecasts, overseeing projects and clients, and pursuing new business by leading and contributing to proposals and opportunities. Manage multiple client contact relationships and deliver according to individual contact needs. Qualifications A minimum of 5+ years of public relations agency experience, with an emphasis on media relations, corporate reputation, crisis work, issues management, executive positioning and message development. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in public relations, communications, journalism, or related field. Knowledge of media trends and issues and strong understanding of media environment. Extremely detail oriented and organized, with experience driving large initiatives and major projects from inception to completion Excellent writing and editing abilities. Demonstrated self-starter with a track record of driving projects forward and course-correcting when things shift. Brings energy and ownership to every account, without waiting to be directed. Creative thinker who can develop original concepts and storylines independently, not just execute against briefs handed down by senior staff. Equally comfortable operating in white space and ambiguity as in executing precisely against tight parameters, mandated messaging, or strict brand standards. Strong strategic planning and demonstrated client counsel capabilities. Analytical thinking and an ability to understand complex industries and business concepts quickly. Firm understanding of multichannel editorial content creation, development and distribution in order to manage editorial content and campaigns for client teams. An ability to work well within a team environment, complementing senior leads and managing junior staff. Agency experience is a plus. 61,000 – 94,000 Omnicom’s policy requires employees to work in the office for a minimum of three days a week, unless additional in-office days are directed by their agency or manager. Our objective is to increase this requirement over time, and many of our agencies as well as Omnicom’s corporate group already require five days of in-office attendance. Omnicom is committed to hiring and developing exceptional talent. We agree that talent is uniquely distributed, and we’re focused on developing inclusive teams that can bring the best solutions to everything we do. We strongly believe that celebrating what makes us different makes us better together. Join us—we look forward to getting to know you. We will process your personal data in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice. The Senior Account Executive supports campaign strategy and execution, managing client relationships and leading tactical implementation across multiple projects. A successful candidate will have strong writing, research and project management skills, excellent interpersonal abilities, attention to detail, the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously, and a team-oriented attitude focused on excellence. item.description: Coordinator/Manager. Government Relations Organization: Security Industry Association Location: Silver Spring, MD Date Posted: 09/24/2026 General Duties Assist in the implementation of the Security Industry Association’s (SIA) public policy initiatives and related programs. Work closely to support the Senior Director and Associate Director of Government Relations on legislative and regulatory issues. Serve as an additional liaison to the SIA government relations committee, working groups, outside consultants, and external associations/organizations. Represent SIA before external audiences as directed by the GR team. Key Responsibilities Government Relations Track and analyze state and local legislation relevant to the security industry for SIA Government Relations and provide timely information on developments to the SIA Policy Council and various member groups as needed. Assist in similar tracking and analysis of federal legislation. Assist in coordinating member committees and working groups as assigned. Represent SIA in relevant industry coalitions on policy matters as determined by SIA GR. Represent SIA before policymakers and staff on select state and local legislative matters, as determined and guided by SIA GR, including travel to support these initiatives. Assist in Congressional outreach and relationship-building on Capitol Hill. Assist SIA member-led advocacy projects as assigned. Communications Draft letters, issue papers, memos, issue updates, presentations and talking points within assigned areas of responsibility. Provide support in the development and delivery of state and local bill testimony. Work closely with SIA communications team to generate relevant GR digital and social media content, including online public policy updates (blogs, webinars, videos, etc.) and in-depth reports as needed. Event Planning/Management Support the development and execution of SIA Security Hill Day, Government Summit, and SIA policy briefing and relevant networking events. Coordination with partner organizations and with the SIA membership, marketing, and operations teams. Cross-departmental support for other SIA events as needed. Requisite Skills and Attributes Strong research, writing and presentation skills. Ability to analyze complex public policy issues and recommend potential actions. Strong member service orientation and commitment to the success of the association and the security industry. Willingness to learn new issues particularly around the use of security technology. Ability to complete projects simultaneously and help to ensure completion by stated deadlines. Professional attitude and presence. At ease with supporting internal colleagues on cross-department initiatives. Proficient in computer applications, including Microsoft Office, database management, and social media. Availabity and comfort level to travel (~20%) in support of SIA programs and initiatives. Education and Experience Baccalaureate degree in Political Science, Government, Public Policy or related field. Relevant experience with government agencies, legislative offices, law enforcement agencies or trade associations. 1-5 years of relevant work experience (Manager level position). item.title: Lead Associate, Global Development Policy (P2)
item.description: Lead Associate, Global Development Policy (P2) Organization: Save the Children Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Details Description Save the Children For over 100 years, Save the Children has been fighting for the rights of children. The right to a healthy start in life. To have access to education. To be in a safe environment, protected from harm. We work in some of the world’s hardest-to-reach places – over 100 countries, including the U.S. No matter what your role is, when you join Save the Children, you’re creating positive, irreversible change for children, and the future we all share. The Role As a Lead Associate, Global Development Policy, you’ll be integral to our work in helping vulnerable children achieve a brighter future. You will provide policy and technical support for Save the Children’s public policy & advocacy and government relations work related to U.S. foreign assistance budget and appropriations. You will analyze policy and track legislative developments on Capitol Hill, develop and maintain relationships with congressional offices, and contribute to strategy development. You will also support Save the Children’s policy and advocacy work on other priority global development issues, as assigned. This position reports to the Managing Director, Global Development Policy. Location Hybrid – Washington DC office What You’ll Be Doing (Essential Duties) *not inclusive of all role responsibilities. May be subject to change Coordinate and implement advocacy to Congress and administration on foreign assistance budget and appropriations (60%) In coordination with the Managing Director of Global Development Policy, advocate to Congress and administration on funding for priority humanitarian and development assistance funding lines. Provide timely analysis of policy and legislative developments related to budget and appropriations process. Represent Save the Children’s policy priorities in relevant advocacy coalitions. Represent Save the Children’s policy priorities at meetings with Congressional offices and/or Administration officials. Develop and manage strategic relations with relevant congressional offices. Develop materials for advocacy and/or external engagement including fact sheets, policy statements, outside witness testimony, talking points for senior level staff and grassroots advocates, etc. Coordinate with Domestic Policy Team on appropriations advocacy across priority accounts. Plan and execute advocacy events as needed. Actively contribute to P&A’s broader congressional relations strategy (30%) Contribute to P&A’s general knowledge of political developments and dynamics. Contribute to implementation of the broader congressional relations strategy. Contribute to biweekly policy updates. Track and communicate relevant hearings, briefings, mark-ups, and other legislative developments for department colleagues. Internal coordination and communication (5%) Serve as resource on budget and appropriations for other Save the Children departments and divisions, including SCAN, Impact & Evidence and Marketing & Growth. Perform other duties as necessary (5%) Required qualifications for the role Minimum of a High School Diploma or equivalent, plus at least 3 years of relevant experience Successful work experience in a Congressional office, or in an NGO, or Executive Branch position focused on congressional relations and/or advocacy Strong understanding of the appropriations process on Capitol Hill Demonstrated ability to successfully deliver multiple projects and assignments, often with competing priorities and deadlines Ability to work independently on assigned tasks with direction, using informed time management and problem-solving Professional proficiency in MS Office suite Professional proficiency in spoken and written English including policy-oriented writing, research and analytical skills This position may require the incumbent to operate a motor vehicle to fulfill certain essential functions of the job. The incumbent should maintain a valid driver’s license and remain in compliance with any Save the Children policies pertaining to the safe operation of motor vehicles. Preferred qualifications for the role Experience working in large, complex matrixed organization Professional experience specifically focused on federal budget and appropriations Professional experience focused on international development issues Experience working in coalitions and networks. Compensation Save the Children is offering the following salary ranges for this position, dependent on candidate location: Geo 1 – NY Metro, DC, and other locations with labor costs significantly above national average: Target Salary for this position is $72,250 – $80,750 base salary Geo 2 – Locations around the US National Labor Cost Average: Target Salary for this position is $65,450 – $73,150 base salary Geo 3 – Locations significantly below the US National Labor Cost Average: Target Salary for this position is $59,500 – $66,500 base salary The salary ranges listed above are for US based candidates. For candidates located outside of the US, salary ranges will be based on the salary scales of the local employer of record. Actual base salary may vary based on, but not limited to, relevant experience, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location (more information on job structure is available here). About Us We are looking to build an inclusive team at Save the Children. We offer a range of outstanding benefits to support this goal: Flexible schedules and time off: Flexible schedules, generous PTO, 11 paid holidays plus 2 floating holidays and hybrid working opportunities Health: Competitive health care, dental and vision coverage for you and your family Family: A variety of paid leaves: caregiver, parental/adoption, critical child illness and fertility benefits Employee Rewards Program: Annual merit increases and/or additional incentives for eligible employees Retirement: A retirement savings plan with employer contributions (after one year) Wellness: 15 safety and wellness days annually (if hired on or after July 1, safety and wellness days prorated to 8 days), mental health benefits and support through Calm and company-hosted events Employee Assistance Program: free and confidential assessments, short-term counseling, referrals, and follow-up services Learning & Growth: Access to internal and external learning & development opportunities and mentorships Click here to learn more about how Save the Children US will invest in you. item.description: Lead Associate, Media Relations (P2) Organization: Save the Children Location: Fairfield, CT | Washington, DC | Lexington, KY Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Details Description Save the Children For over 100 years, Save the Children has been fighting for the rights of children. The right to a healthy start in life. To have access to education. To be in a safe environment, protected from harm. We work in some of the world’s hardest-to-reach places – over 100 countries, including the U.S. No matter what your role is, when you join Save the Children, you’re creating positive, irreversible change for children, and the future we all share. The Role The Lead Associate for Media Relations will execute key media relations and strategic communications functions that advance the priorities of Save the Children, including a special, but not exclusive, focus on policy and advocacy of the agency and its advocacy arm, Save the Children Action Network (SCAN). Working collaboratively to implement communications strategies, the Lead Associate helps identify and engage key audiences—including media, coalition partners, policymakers, advocates, and the public—through clear, compelling communications. The position maintains regular contact with traditional and emerging media, including journalists across local, state, and national markets; drafts and edits communications materials; and plays a key role in monitoring, analyzing, and evaluating media advocacy efforts and their impact. Location Hybrid – Washington DC, Fairfield, CT or Lexington, KY office locations What You’ll Be Doing (Essential Duties) Strategic Communications and Content Development 35% Support implementation of communications and media outreach plans that advance SCAN’s priorities in alignment with broader federal policy goals. Draft and edit communications materials including press releases, talking points, media advisories, statements and spokesperson briefing materials. Collaborate with policy, advocacy, and technical experts to translate complex information into clear communications products. Monitor policy developments and news trends and share opportunities with communications team members. Assist with coordinating communications activities across internal stakeholders and external partners. Media Relations 50% Support day-to-day media activities, including developing pitches, coordinating and scheduling interviews, and maintaining press lists. Help establish and maintain relationships with journalists, producers and media contacts across local, state and national outlets, as well as other influential content creators. Assist in preparing spokespeople for media opportunities by gathering background materials and coordinating logistics. Partner with Media team members to support Save’s international portfolio, with a primary focus on the Middle East. Develop and maintain a diverse roster of subject matter experts and backup spokespeople. Media Monitoring and Reporting 15% Monitor media coverage related to organizational priorities and policy issues. Produce regular media coverage summaries and reports. Maintain media tracking systems and communications calendars. Compile basic metrics and reporting to support evaluation of media outreach efforts. Track communications deliverables and help coordinate workflows across the Media team. Required qualifications for the role Minimum of a High School Diploma or equivalent, plus at least 3 years of relevant experience Proven writing and editing skills Demonstrated attention to detail Proven ability to organize and execute tasks for several campaigns simultaneously Ability and eagerness to engage across the political spectrum and to champion the organization’s bipartisan approach to effective policymaking Professional proficiency in MS Office suite and knowledge of media monitoring tools Professional proficiency in spoken and written English Preferred qualifications for the role Experience pitching stories and cultivating relationships with journalists and media professionals, with a focus on political reporters in Washington, DC, and across the United States. Experience in advocacy and/or grassroots campaigns. Experience preparing spokespeople for media interviews. item.title: Assistant Director of Immigration
item.description: Assistant Director of Immigration Organization: Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Details Description SEIU (Service Employees International Union) JOB TITLE: Assistant Director for Immigration GRADE: MGT F ANNUAL SALARY: $135,609.02 LOCATION: Washington, DC HQ ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW: We are the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), a union of about 2 million diverse members in healthcare, the public sector, and property services. We believe in and fight for our Vision for a Just Society: where all workers are valued and all people respected, no matter where we come from or what color we are; where all families and communities can thrive; and where we leave a better and more equitable world for generations to come. We are an anti-racist union determined to check corporate power and uproot structural racism through unions, worker power, collective action, and government, legislative, and political action. We fight for Unions for All and a Government that Works for All so that all of us, across race and place, can have power together in unions and participate fully in our democracy. PURPOSE: The Assistant Director of Immigration is responsible for core aspects of the Union’s Immigration campaign that includes legislative & executive branch strategy, elected & key staff relationships, immigration coalition relationships and political strategy input designed to achieve SEIU goals on immigration and build power for SEIU members and working people. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Any one position may not include all of the specific duties and responsibilities listed. Examples provide a general summary of the work required and should not be treated as a total and complete list of expected duties to be performed by employees in the classification. Lobbying & relationships with members of Congress and Executive Branch officials on policy and legislation, including developing strategy and related activities. Works with the Deputy Director of Immigration & the Legislative Director in developing strategies for moving our affirmative pro-immigration legislation, including our North Star, a path to citizenship, and defeating anti-immigrant legislative and executive branch efforts, which includes developing materials for lobbying activities. Assists with building the International Union’s relations with Congressional committees, staff and Members of Congress to advance SEIU’s federal Immigration legislative priorities. At the direction of the Deputy Director for Immigration & the Legislative Director, assists in leading staff in the development of various legislative documents- including but not limited to legislative explainers, target lists, correspondence and reports. Acts as a liaison and advocates on behalf of union members on Immigration legislative issues. At the direction of the Deputy Director of Immigration & the Legislative Director, takes a lead role in the research, analysis of proposed pro and anti-immigrant legislation, preparation of testimonies, explainers, and other relevant materials. In collaboration with the Deputy Director of Immigration coordinates SEIU Immigration federal legislative strategies with the AFL-CIO and other unions, immigration coalition allies, congressional allies, national state and local coalitions, allied organizations, and other SEIU departments as appropriate. Assists in the development and coordination of SEIU Immigration projects as they relate to federal immigration legislative priorities and grassroots campaigns including legislative policy development, advice on polling, and media. Participates in SEIU’s grassroots infrastructure for immigration legislative and political campaigns, including immigration political and legislative action efforts with SEIU regional, state council and local political & legislative staff and leaders. Advises the Deputy Director of Immigration & Directors for Legislation and Government Relations on strategies for representation by the International at national immigration events, immigration demonstrations, immigration issue conventions, conferences and other forums on immigration legislative priority issues. At the direction of the Deputy Director for Immigration represents SEIU, at conferences, commissions where appropriate. Collaborates with team members & Deputy Director of Immigration on plans and develops immigration legislative education, training and related materials. Reports to the Deputy Director of Immigration and as needed works with the Director of Government Relations to advance SEIU priorities. DIRECTION & DECISION MAKING: This position reports to the Deputy Director for Immigration and works independently. QUALIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE: Graduation from an accredited four-year college or university with a bachelor’s degree in Public Policy or related field (Politics, History, Economics). Five to seven (5-7) years of experience in direct immigration lobbying of elected officials or government agencies and drafting immigration legislation; OR, eight (8) years of experience as an immigration legislative assistant for a Member of Congress, Congressional committee or regulatory agency. Four (4) years prior experience working in immigration issues campaigns, immigration political action and election campaigns at a senior level, immigration policy analysis, community advocacy on immigration or drafting of immigration legislation or regulations in relevant immigration issue areas. Thorough knowledge of the immigration congressional legislative process or immigration government agencies and drafting immigration legislation. Thorough knowledge of working in immigration campaigns, immigration political action and election campaigns at a senior level, immigration policy analysis, community advocacy or drafting of immigration legislation or regulations in immigration issue area. Thorough knowledge of the office workings of a legislative office for elected officials and immigration regulatory agencies. Thorough knowledge of immigration information systems for lobbying activity. Knowledge of unions and their issues. Knowledge of training and educational methods. Ability to conduct training sessions. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing; ability to make formal presentations and write advocacy papers. Ability to use a personal computer, including carrying out on-line research services. Ability to work with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures. Ability to conduct formal research, analyze data and make sound, logical conclusions. Ability to handle multiple “priority” projects and meet established timelines. Ability to work effectively with union leaders, elected leaders and staff in complex and sometimes political situations. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Work is generally performed in an office setting, but may be required to work in other settings conducive to performing the work required to complete the assignment, such as field assignments. Long and extended hours and travel required. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS: SEIU offers a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package that reflects our values as a labor organization and our commitment to the well-being and long-term security of our staff. Benefits include: A comprehensive, employer-sponsored health benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage A defined benefit pension plan Paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, and holidays Additional benefits consistent with a mission-driven workplace SEIU believes that workers deserve dignity, stability, and the ability to plan for their futures, and our benefits are designed to support that belief. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
