item.description: Senior Campaign Communications Specialist-Worker Power Organization: Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job Details Description SEIU (Service Employees International Union) JOB TITLE: Senior Campaign Communications Specialist – Worker Power GRADE: PS-3 ANNUAL SALARY: $92,989.90 LOCATION: All USA or Washington, DC HQ ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW: We are the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), a union of about 2 million diverse members in healthcare, the public sector, and property services. We believe in and fight for our Vision for a Just Society: where all workers are valued and all people respected, no matter where we come from or what color we are; where all families and communities can thrive; and where we leave a better and more equitable world for generations to come. We are an anti-racist union determined to check corporate power and uproot structural racism through unions, worker power, collective action, and government, legislative, and political action. We fight for Unions for All and a Government that Works for All so that all of us, across race and place, can have power together in unions and participate fully in our democracy. PURPOSE: The Senior Campaign Communications Specialist for Worker Power is responsible for the development and implementation of communications plans and materials for various union outreach efforts spanning the union’s work in organizing, mobilization, bargaining, and campaigns. May help lead local union communications staff and specialists in developing and coordinating public relations, media relations, and general communications support for campaigns and other union projects. Working on the Narrative & Engagement Worker Power team, they are part of a team that translates the union’s strategic organizing goals into actionable, amplified, and cohesive communications plans and campaigns. They ensure a consistent, compelling, and coordinated message that drives membership growth and strengthens the union’s presence across key sectors and geographies. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Any one position may not include all of the specific duties and responsibilities listed. Examples provide a general summary of the work required and should not be treated as a total and complete list of expected duties to be performed by employees in the classification. Provides strategy recommendations and assists in the development of strategies to improve the public image and visibility of SEIU and various locals. Develops, plans and directs communications strategies and calendars for various campaigns within the International and various locals. Writes op-eds, background pieces, fact sheets, press kit materials, leaflets and other collateral materials as needed for various campaigns. Assists various locals and IU teams in the development and coordination of communications strategies for campaign projects. Writes talking points, statements, letters to the editor, podcast outreach, worker speeches, influencer collaborations, and other written materials as needed. Develops and coordinates a network of local union communications representatives as needed for various campaigns. This coordination may include media training and other support. Provides support for International officers or local officers attending campaigns or other events. Monitors media coverage of various campaigns, maintains clipping files, makes recommendations on ways to improve media coverage and outreach. Provides background briefings for International and Local Union Officers, field staff, and workers; coordinates event logistics and interviews (i.e. videography, still photography, advisories, news releases, stage-setting collateral, etc.) Develops and implements pro-active earned media outreach, as well as the targeting and placement of paid advertisements to support various campaigns and political action. Performs other duties as required to support the department and its mission. CONTACTS: Include SEIU staff and other experts on campaign communications issues. DIRECTION & DECISION MAKING: This position reports to a Communications Program Manager, and the incumbent works independently. QUALIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE: Four (4) years of work experience in media relations, digital communications, public affairs, or campaign communications including all aspects of the media or communications production process or thorough knowledge of labor movement or other advocacy organizations. Thorough knowledge of digital and print media systems; knowledge of advertising techniques preferred. Knowledge of organizing and political campaign strategies preferred. Ability to perform pro-active media outreach, maintaining good working relationships with journalists, podcasters, influencers, and generating positive media coverage. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. Ability to take initiative and work independently. Ability to work with elected leaders and staff in complex and sometimes political situations. Ability to act and organize time with extreme independence. Ability to handle multiple “priority” projects simultaneously and meet established deadlines. Skilled in the use of personal computers including the Internet and Google Docs. Skilled in performing proactive media outreach. Skilled in developing “Media Pitch” to various outside journalistic outlets. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Work is generally performed in an office setting, but may be required to work in other settings conducive to performing the work required to complete the assignment, such as field assignments. Long and extended hours and travel required. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS: SEIU offers a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package that reflects our values as a labor organization and our commitment to the well-being and long-term security of our staff. Benefits include: A comprehensive, employer-sponsored health benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage A defined benefit pension plan Paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, and holidays Additional benefits consistent with a mission-driven workplace SEIU believes that workers deserve dignity, stability, and the ability to plan for their futures, and our benefits are designed to support that belief. item.title: Senior Associate, Energy & Air Quality
item.description: Senior Associate, Energy & Air Quality Organization: U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Salary Range: $70,000.00 To $85,000.00 Annually HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT As a Senior Associate, Energy and Air Quality, you’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact by helping advance the goals of the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) and its Technical Development team. The Technical Development team is seeking a skilled professional to expand our technical capabilities and contribute to two critical topic areas: energy and carbon and indoor environmental quality. In this role, you will assume ownership of pertinent committee operations and help guide the ongoing evolution, refinement, and optimization of USGBC products—including LEED—to ensure they remain rigorous, relevant, and aligned with USGBC’s mission and strategic objectives. You’ll report to the Director of Energy and Carbon and be part of a highly collaborative matrixed team environment where your contributions will help shape impactful outcomes through USGBC products and thought leadership. You’ll work closely with Technical Development colleagues and other teams like Education, Innovation and Research, and Product Management and may regularly partner with Technical Customer Service or Certification to resolve questions regarding the interpretation of rating system language in relevant topic areas. Key Responsibilities Support the implementation of strategic goals for energy and carbon and indoor environmental quality for LEED and other USGBC/GBCI products in key technical areas in such as: Energy benchmarking, building performance standards, and decarbonization. Indoor air quality (ventilation, filtration, monitoring, etc.). High-performance design analysis and practices. Identify and help understand the implications of new and developing industry issues, trends, scientific research, publications, technologies, regulatory requirements, and standards with a focus on the nexus between energy and air quality. Facilitate technical conversations, conduct research, and build consensus on technical solutions that enhance the usability, implementation, and impact of USGBC/GBCI products worldwide. Aid in the development and optimization of technical tools and resources, such as rating system guidance, addenda, sample forms, and adaptions to existing rating systems that support specific project types, regions, and innovative approaches. Cultivate engagement with global external subject matter experts focused on the built environment. Support the vision for volunteerism at USGBC by leading committee operations for at least two LEED Technical Advisory Groups (Energy and Atmosphere and Indoor Environmental Quality), including document development, agenda drafting, meeting coordination and facilitation, note taking, and acting as staff point of contact for volunteer industry professionals. Support in public speaking engagements and create technical content presentations, effectively communicating technical information on energy and environmental quality to diverse audiences. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience At least 2–5 years of relevant technical experience in engineering or energy management General knowledge of ASHRAE standards, especially 90.1 and 62.1 Robust exposure to and familiarity with building energy management and high-performance building systems, including HVAC, and their interactions General knowledge of LEED rating systems Experience with LEED-certified projects preferred Combination of US and relevant international experience a plus Education Bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, or a related field required Key Skills Understanding of and ability to contribute to high-performance building design processes, with a focus on energy and air quality aspects and the interaction among building systems Familiarity with building decarbonization approaches, such as building electrification measures, carbon assessments/projections, and strategic decarbonization planning Familiarity with prevalent model energy and IAQ codes Awareness of resilience considerations in the built environment Analytical thinking and problem-solving skills Collaborative and constructive mindset with demonstrated success in team-oriented environments Ability to establish and maintain interpersonal relationships with a diverse array of colleagues and external stakeholders Ability to research and present complex solutions to varied audiences Strong written and oral communication Consistent self-management, including balancing competing priorities and attention to detail Commitment to USGBC mission Technology/System(s) Microsoft Office Suite proficiency required, including advanced Excel capabilities Experience with data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau, or similar) preferred Experience with energy modeling (EnergyPlus/OpenStudio, eQUEST, IES, or similar) strongly preferred Proficiency with Smartsheet and Salesforce preferred but not required Certifications LEED Accredited Professional (or ability to obtain within 12 months of hire) Language English ABOUT OUR TOTAL REWARDS PACKAGE Salary Final compensation and benefits will be confirmed at the time of offer and may vary based on factors such as internal equity, relevant experience, qualifications, and employment status. Please note that salary negotiations will not extend beyond the top of the internal salary range. Benefits We offer you: Competitive compensation 401(k) with employer matching Professional development reimbursement We offer a healthcare plan through Cigna that includes medical, dental, vision, and prescription drugs. USGBC covers 100% of the premiums and an HRA that will assist you and your dependents in reaching the in-network medical deductible. You will only be responsible for the $300 individual / $600 family up front deductible for medical services before the employer funded HRA will process payments for your in-network claims Generous paid time off (12 paid holidays, 9 paid personal sick days and based on career level either 2 to 3 weeks PTO), including operations closed for a full week between Christmas and New Year’s 6 weeks paid renewal leave after 7 years of continuous service LOGISTICS Location: This position is in the Washington DC office or remote in the U.S. Work Schedule: Monday to Friday, 9:00 am–5:30 pm, in the team member’s local time zone, with occasional meetings scheduled in Eastern Time Travel %: approximately 5% for occasional conferences, speaking events, and team retreats EEO STATEMENT The U.S. Green Building Council is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. ABOUT US U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) is a mission-driven nonprofit dedicated to accelerating and scaling the transformation of the built environment. Through LEED—the world’s most widely used green building rating system— and initiatives likes Greenbuild, the Center for Green Schools and advocacy, USGBC empowers professionals to drive market transformation that advances human and environmental health, climate resilience, and equity. Green Business Certification Inc. (GBCI) is the world’s leading sustainability and health certification and credentialing body, independently recognizing excellence in performance. GBCI administers project certifications and professional credentials and certificates including LEED, PERFORM, SITES, and TRUE Zero Waste. We are proud to be globally recognized for our leadership in green building, environmental performance, and sustainable development. Our Global Impact Over 120,000 LEED-certified commercial projects worldwide Millions of square feet of certified healthy, efficient, low-carbon space Recognition in 180+ countries for innovation in green building and business practices Why Join Us At USGBC and GBCI, you’ll work alongside passionate, mission-aligned professionals who care deeply about people, the planet, and progress. We offer: A purpose-driven, inclusive culture Opportunities to grow your career and take ownership of meaningful work A chance to make a measurable impact on global sustainability efforts We’re seeking team members who thrive in collaborative environments, are committed to excellence, and want to build lasting partnerships that drive change in the built environment. Meet Our Leaders and Learn More about our Mission: U.S. Green Building Council Leaders Green Business Certification Inc Leaders Culture and Values Statement Working together, each of us advances our mission by respecting all voices, trusting and supporting one another, excelling through collaboration and accountability, and continuously improving ourselves and our organization. item.title: Managing Director, Communications & Marketing
item.description: Managing Director, Communications & Marketing Organization: Washington Area Community Investment Fund (WACIF) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Who We Are Established in 1987, the Washington Area Community Investment Fund’s (WACIF) mission is to increase economic opportunity in communities in the Washington, DC area by investing knowledge, social, and financial capital in low- and moderate-income entrepreneurs. Our mission is driven by three strategic pillars: entrepreneurship, community wealth building, and economic development, and is fulfilled by providing access to capital products and services, and capacity building technical assistance to low- and moderate-income entrepreneurs. WACIF has been continuously certified as a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) since 1996, making the organization one of the nation’s first CDFIs. Position Summary The Managing Director, Marketing & Communications is responsible for leading WACIF’s organization-wide marketing, communications, brand, and storytelling strategy. This role ensures that WACIF communicates with a clear, consistent, and compelling voice across audiences and that the organization’s communications and marketing efforts strengthen its reputation, expand its reach, support fundraising and partnerships, and connect entrepreneurs and communities to WACIF’s programs, capital, and resources. The Managing Director will lead and develop communications staff, including supervising the Director of Communications, and will work closely with leaders across Programs, Lending, the Anacostia Arts Center, Development, and Operations to ensure WACIF presents a unified organizational story. This is both a strategic and management role. The successful candidate will be comfortable setting direction, developing people, managing multiple priorities, making decisions, and stepping into execution when necessary. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Brand Strategy Organizational Storytelling & Content Marketing & Audience Engagement Media Relations & External Communications Executive & Internal Communications Team Leadership & Management Cross-Functional Leadership Budget, Vendors & Performance Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Journalism, Business Administration, or a related field; advanced degree preferred. 10+ years of progressive experience in corporate communications, marketing, public relations, brand management, or a related field, including experience leading organization-wide communications strategy. Proven experience serving as a strategic advisor to CEOs and senior executives on internal and external communications, executive messaging, media relations, reputation management, and sensitive or crisis communications. In addition to having the ability to anticipate communications opportunities. Proven strategic leadership experience developing and executing integrated communications, marketing, brand, and storytelling strategies that support organizational goals and produce measurable results. Strong people and operational leadership experience, including the ability to translate organizational strategy, complex issues, and business priorities into compelling communications that engage employees, clients, funders, partners, media, and other external audiences. Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex organizational, financial, programmatic, or technical information into clear, compelling messages for diverse internal and external audiences. Location: Washington D.C. – Hybrid Salary Range $101,249.00 – $170,000 .00 Benefits Healthcare HSA & FSA Dental Vision Life & AD&D Short- & Long-Term Disability Matching 401(k) Paid Holidays PTO Education Assistance To Apply: Please submit your resume and cover letter for consideration here . Equal Employment Opportunity WACIF is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. item.title: Senior Policy Manager, Federal Advocacy
item.description: Senior Policy Manager, Federal Advocacy Organization: Campaign Legal Center (CLC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 The Senior Policy Manager is a key member of Campaign Legal Center’s federal advocacy team, which works to develop and advance the organization’s policy priorities in Congress and the executive branch of the federal government. Reporting to CLC’s Director of Federal Advocacy, this position directly lobbies policymakers, builds and maintains relationships across the ideological spectrum, and helps to design strategies and solutions to advance CLC’s federal policy goals. The Senior Policy Manager supports federal advocacy across all of CLC’s program areas and teams, including voting rights, redistricting, campaign finance, government ethics, electoral structural reform, and the rule of law. Under the supervision of the Director, this position will manage CLC’s ongoing lobbying efforts on a subset of these issues, to be determined based on interests and experience. This includes conducting outreach to congressional offices and executive branch agencies, reviewing and providing input on proposed legislation, tracking administrative rules and submitting comments in rulemakings, coordinating with internal experts and external partners, monitoring political developments, and writing advocacy materials. The Senior Policy Manager may also lead other discrete projects and workstreams based on the needs of the organization. The Senior Policy Manager supports CLC’s engagement with federal coalitions, representing the organization in partner meetings, identifying opportunities for collaboration, and helping to strengthen CLC’s relationships across civil society. The Senior Policy Manager must register as a federal lobbyist and comply with all applicable legal requirements. The position is eligible to take part in CLC’s telework and flexible work programs but should be prepared to report in-person in Washington, D.C., when lobbying efforts require. Key Responsibilities: Support CLC’s federal policy work by maintaining relationships with congressional offices, monitoring legislation, hearings, floor votes, and other formal proceedings in Congress, identifying opportunities for CLC engagement, and helping the Director of Federal Advocacy to devise and implement CLC’s overall lobbying strategies. Manage ongoing federal advocacy efforts for a subset of CLC’s issue areas, to be determined after hiring based on the candidate’s interests and experience, while remaining engaged across CLC’s full federal advocacy portfolio and available to support other issues as needed. In coordination with any relevant CLC program teams, support and drive advocacy to advance the organization’s policy priorities in the executive branch. Draft and help develop written materials, including reports, memos, bill explainers, fact sheets, advocacy letters, blogs, talking points, and other resources to advance CLC’s federal policy priorities. Contribute to the analysis and drafting of federal legislation and administrative policy proposals, as well as related advocacy strategies, in coordination with relevant CLC program teams. Support CLC’s engagement with congressional hearings, including drafting testimony and statements for the record, developing resource materials for lawmakers, and helping to prepare any CLC witnesses for invited testimony. Track administrative rulemakings relevant to CLC’s work, and participate in the full range of rulemaking advocacy, including meetings and drafting comments. Build and maintain productive relationships with reform community allies and coalition partners at the federal level and represent CLC in coalition meetings. When needed, lead discrete federal advocacy projects or workstreams across CLC program areas, including developing project plans, coordinating internal input, and tracking progress toward clear deliverables. Track federal bill endorsements, legislative developments, and coalition activity, and help maintain internal systems for cross-team coordination and decision-making. Help to manage the electronic system CLC uses for congressional communications. With the Director, regularly update CLC staff and leadership on major events related to the organization’s work in Congress and in federal coalitions. Support compliance with federal lobbying disclosure requirements by maintaining accurate internal records and coordinating with the Director of Federal Advocacy, Senior Director of Policy, and General Counsel as needed. Qualifications: Five to ten years of experience in one or more of the following areas: Legislative work in the office of a member of Congress or congressional committee; Federal lobbying or government relations; Federal policy advocacy and research; or Managing or supporting federal legislative campaigns. Substantive expertise in one or more of CLC’s program areas (voting rights, redistricting, campaign finance, government ethics, structural reform, and the rule of law) is preferred but not required. Commitment to the nonpartisan nature and overall mission of CLC, including the organization’s Culture Principles. Ability to blend substantive policy knowledge with astute political insights. Demonstrated ability to support and implement federal advocacy strategies and/or navigate the legislative process. Experience in one or more of the functional tasks of legislative research, policy analysis, legislative drafting, and lobbying. Experience building relationships with legislative offices, agency staff, coalition partners, and other external stakeholders. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with an ability to work collaboratively and earn trust with policymakers and advocates across the political and ideological spectrum. Strong writing skills and ability to translate complex policy issues into clear, concise, and persuasive advocacy materials. Strong organizational judgment, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving policy environment. Comfort with public speaking and external representation, including at coalition meetings, briefings, and media appearances or other events. Experience leading projects, tracking deliverables, and coordinating input from multiple contributors is preferred but not required. Ability to comply with all applicable federal lobbyist registration and reporting requirements. Compensation and Benefits Salary Range: $107,100 – 150,550 Campaign Legal Center is committed to fostering a workplace that supports every team member’s personal and professional well-being. Our compensation is competitive and placement within the posted salary range is commensurate with experience. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive and inclusive benefits package tailored to meet the diverse needs of our staff. Some of our benefits include: Generous health, dental, and vision insurance with low employee premiums A 401(k) retirement plan with a dollar-for-dollar match up to 6%, with immediate vesting 20 vacation days, 12 sick days, and 3 floating holidays annually 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave,10 days of bereavement leave, and 8 weeks of sabbatical leave for those who qualify Office closures for all federal holidays, plus typically a week in late summer, and a week in the winter. Flexible Spending and Dependent Care Accounts A $1,000 annual professional development stipend and bar membership reimbursement A $500 annual technology allowance Pre-tax metro smart benefits New family and family planning support, including reimbursement for travel to access legal reproductive healthcare An Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with free, confidential support for personal, financial, and family matters. At CLC, we believe that caring for our team is essential to sustaining our mission. We strive to create a culture where everyone can thrive inside and outside work. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Campaign Legal Center (CLC) is an equal opportunity employer committed to maintaining a nondiscriminatory work environment. CLC is proud to be an inclusive organization. It does not make hiring or advancement, or other employment decisions, based on race, national origin, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, familial status or responsibilities, personal appearance, pregnancy, political affiliation, ancestry, military or veteran status, genetic information, disability, record of arrest or conviction, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, District of Columbia, or local law. This policy applies to all aspects of employment including, but not limited to, recruitment, selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, termination, benefits, and training. Disclaimer: This description of the position summary, key responsibilities, benefits, and compensation is intended to provide an overview of this position and is not all inclusive. The incumbent in this position will be expected to perform other duties as required. Responsibilities may change over time. This description of the position summary, key responsibilities, benefits, and compensation is provided for informational purposes only and does not form the basis of a contract. item.title: Policy Advisor
item.description: Policy Advisor Organization: Arnold & Porter Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Arnold & Porter is an international law firm with offices throughout the United States, Europe, and Asia. The firm advises clients on complex regulatory, litigation, and transactional matters across a broad range of industries, including many of the world’s leading companies and organizations. Arnold & Porter is seeking an experienced Policy Advisor to join its Legislative and Public Policy Practice Group in Washington, DC. The ideal candidate brings deep experience navigating the federal legislative and regulatory process and a demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic advocacy plans. The Legislative and Public Policy Practice Group is Chambers-rated among the leading legislative practices at national law firms. Our approximately 40-person team works in a high-energy, collaborative environment focused on exceptional client service. We provide congressional and regulatory advocacy for globally recognized brands, Fortune 500 companies, innovative start-ups, leading associations, utilities, manufacturers, healthcare systems, educational institutions, local governments, foreign governments, and coalitions. This position is based in the Washington, DC office and follows a hybrid work schedule. Key Responsibilities Advise clients on federal legislative, regulatory, and public-policy matters. Develop and execute strategic advocacy plans tailored to client objectives. Lead client-service teams on discrete policy issues and advocacy initiatives. Monitor, analyze, and communicate developments in relevant policy areas. Work collaboratively with attorneys, policy professionals, and clients in a fast-paced environment. Manage and mentor junior-level staff, as appropriate. Produce clear, accurate, and high-quality written work products. Register on behalf of firm clients, as required, under the Lobbying Disclosure Act and the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required. Minimum of eight years of experience in Congress, an Executive Branch department or agency, or government relations for a nonprofit or for-profit organization, trade association, or interest group. Strong knowledge of the federal legislative and regulatory process. Demonstrated expertise in two or more of the following areas: appropriations, education, energy/environmental, national defense, tax, technology, or trade policy. Proven ability to develop and execute strategic advocacy plans. Experience managing junior-level staff and leading client-service teams. Strong strategic judgment, initiative, self-motivation, and drive to action. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality deliverables. Strong interpersonal, organizational, decision-making, and multitasking skills. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively while managing competing priorities. Willingness to register for firm clients under the Lobbying Disclosure Act and the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Please submit a cover letter, resume, and a 3-5 page writing sample on an advocacy-based topic of their choosing here . Submitting a writing sample of more than 5 pages will eliminate a candidate from consideration. The anticipated base salary for this position is $200,000 to $225,000. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. For benefits information, please click here https://www.arnoldporter.com/en/careers/professional-staff/benefits. The firm may provide a discretionary bonus annually. #LI-HYBRID Arnold & Porter is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy and childbirth (including breastfeeding and related medical conditions), age, marital or partnership status, familial status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family leave status, citizenship status, immigration status, ancestry, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal laws, rules or regulations. Our Firm’s equal opportunity policy applies to all employment practices and terms and conditions, including, without limitation, recruitment, employment, assignment, training, compensation, benefits, promotions, disciplinary action and terminations. For purposes of the firm’s Anti-discrimination and Anti-harassment Policies, the term “race” includes, without limitation, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, such as braids, locks, and twists. Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP endeavors to make www.arnoldporter.com accessible to any and all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process, please contact Director of Support Staff Stephanie Denmark at +1 202.942.6068. This contact information is for accommodation requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications. Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP uses E-Verify, which is a web-based system, to confirm the eligibility of our employees to work in the United States. As an E-Verify employer, we verify the identity and employment eligibility of newly hired employees by electronically matching information provided by employees on the Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, against records available to the Social Security Administration (SSA) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). We use E-Verify because we are a federal contractor containing the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) E-Verify clause. Please see the posters for details regarding E-Verify or contact Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP’s Human Resources Department for more information. item.title: Senior Manager, Communications & Advocacy
item.description: Senior Manager, Communications & Advocacy Organization: American College of Preventive Medicine (ACPM) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/24/2026 The American College of Preventive Medicine is seeking a full-time Senior Manager, Communications & Advocacy. The Senior Manager executes ACPM’s communications and advocacy strategies in the media, on Capitol Hill and within the Administration to advance the issues of interest to the preventive medicine community. The Senior Manager works cross-functionally with other departments in the organization to build strong relationships with ACPM members as advocates, spokespeople, and issue-area experts. This role also represents the College through coalitions, partner engagement, and high-profile meetings with policymakers while ensuring a bipartisan position. Responsibilities include: Advocacy • Develop and execute ACPM’s advocacy/legislative agenda as aligned with the strategic plan and identify opportunities to advance agenda with ACPM Advocacy Committee. • Serve as staff liaison to the ACPM Advocacy Committee, supporting related activity and initiatives (e.g., advocacy training, workshops at PM Conference) and engaging committee members. • Establish and maintain bipartisan liaison with administration officials, members of Congress, key congressional staff, physician groups, and other relevant organizations. • Manage and execute grassroots advocacy campaigns among ACPM members and constituents, maximizing the use of the online ACPM Action Center and other resources. • Monitor, evaluate, and advocate for legislation that has the potential to positively or negatively impact the preventive medicine profession. • Analyzes policy, legislative proposals and coalition opportunities and recommend and track ACPM “sign-on” to letters, reports, and positions. • Lead ACPM’s activities in the AMA House of Delegates in collaboration with leadership team. • Coordinates activities surrounding the AMA House of Delegates Section Council on Preventive Medicine and Public Health. • Educate government officials/staff and media about preventive medicine and build support for ACPM’s policy agenda, ensuring ACPM policies and positions, as well as its advocacy activities, are being appropriately promoted to policymakers, media, members and other stakeholders. Communications • Draft and disseminate media releases, statements, talking points, letters of support, fact sheets, reports and testimony. • Manage ACPM’s editorial-related activities for the American Journal of Preventive Medicine and lead content development for designated pages. • Maintain oversight and action plan for the ACPM ambassador/spokesperson program, ensuring exchange of member information, profile development, media access/training, etc. • Provide communications support by writing content (editorial, digital and multi-media) for ACPM newsletters, website and social media; even more so to communicate legislative developments and ACPM positions and actions to ACPM’s members and stakeholders. • Serves as project manager for the development and launch of the ACPM annual report. • Leads social media strategy and execution for the College, working closely with staff to identify priorities and engagement opportunities. • Work closely with staff and vendors to enhance and maintain ACPM.org. • Contribute to the overall success of ACPM by performing all other essential duties and responsibilities as assigned. Ideal candidates will have 5+ years of applicable experience. A bachelor’s degree is required. The position requires up to 10% travel. The College is a professional medical society representing more than 2,000 physicians dedicated to the practice of preventive medicine and public health for more than 70 years. The College focuses on improving the health and quality of life of individuals, families, communities, and populations through disease prevention, health promotion and health policy initiatives. For more information about the College please visit, www.acpm.org. The American College of Preventive Medicine is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. The College believes in the fundamental principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion and is committed to actively fostering varying experiences and perspectives. Starting salary is $78,000 – $82,000. The College offers a health and welfare benefits package plus retirement. The College is a 100% remote organization with request for monthly meet up in Washington, DC. Interested candidates should send their resume and salary expectations to Elizabeth Richards at [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Digital Marketing Manager
item.description: Digital Marketing Manager Organization: AARP Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Job ID 2026-7805 Salary $112,500.00 – $125,000.00 Yearly Overview: AARP is the nation’s largest nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering people 50 and older to choose how they live as they age. With a nationwide presence, AARP strengthens communities and advocates for what matters most to the more than 100 million Americans 50-plus and their families: health and financial security, and personal fulfillment. AARP also works for individuals in the marketplace by sparking new solutions and allowing carefully chosen, high-quality products and services to carry the AARP name. As a trusted source for news and information, AARP produces the nation’s largest-circulation publications, AARP The Magazine and the AARP Bulletin. The Digital Marketing Manager leads enterprise marketing technology adoption and marketing operations for email, app notification and SMS initiatives that enhance customer engagement and organizational effectiveness. This role drives key elements of change management, stakeholder engagement, training, and communications strategies for these key marketing platforms, including AEM, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketing Hub, and Amazon SES. Partnering across business, marketing, and technology teams, the manager ensures successful adoption, operational readiness, and governance while overseeing enterprise email marketing operations, agency partnerships, and execution standards to deliver business results. Responsibilities: Designs and implements communications and outreach strategies tailored for target audiences, digital channels, and strategic objectives that inform, educate, and influence both internal and external audiences. Manages the organization’s digital properties. Supports and manages the overall strategic direction of organizational digital platforms. Optimizes online channels against key performance indicators and makes data-informed decisions. Oversees content creation for various digital platforms. Leads efforts to identify and document strategies for campaigns, working with multiple business units. Provides analyses and recommendations on digital strategies that align with organizational initiatives and goals. Identify appropriate channels. Designs campaigns to meet specific and varied business unit objectives. Tracks performance and implements necessary changes. Works with internal and external teams to develop and execute digital marketing strategies that increase organizational brand equity and build affinity and engagement among programs. Builds and manages strategic partnerships across the enterprise to enhance business unit effectiveness on digital and social channels. Tracks and measure results and KPIs and adjusts tactics, accordingly. Keeps abreast of the latest digital trends and best practices to inform digital marketing strategies, as well as to aid internal knowledge sharing. Provides exceptional client service by developing timelines to meet project commitments and ensuring deliverables from across the organization and external partners are on time. Develops and maintains relationships with internal clients, ensuring a solid understanding of their objectives, developing plans to achieve them across channels (e.g., Email, SMS, Paid Search, etc.), proactively surfacing new opportunities, and productively resolving any challenges. Identifies vendors best suited to advance organizational goals and proactively manage vendor relationships to ensure successful completion of projects, obligations, and expectations. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Digital Marketing, Marketing, Information Systems or other related field. 2+ years experience in digital marketing, marketing operations, marketing technology, or related disciplines including experience in email, and/or SMS marketing operations or digital agency supporting email or SMS. Experience leading enterprise-scale marketing technology implementations, transformations, or adoption initiatives. Hands-on experience with enterprise marketing platforms such as Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketing Hub, Amazon SES, or similar solutions. Proven ability to develop and execute communication, training, and enablement strategies that drive user adoption and operational readiness across cross-functional teams. Preferred: Experience managing enterprise email marketing operations, including governance, campaign execution standards, vendor/agency management, and performance oversight. Formal training or certification in change management methodologies (e.g., Prosci, ADKAR) and/or project management frameworks. Experience working in a complex, matrixed organization and influencing senior leaders, business stakeholders, and technology teams. AARP will not sponsor an employment visa for this position. Additional Requirements Regular and reliable job attendance. Effective verbal and written communication skills. Exhibit respect and understanding of others to maintain professional relationships. Independent judgement in evaluation options to make sound decisions. In office/open office environment with the ability to work effectively surrounded by moderate noise. AARP will not sponsor an employment visa for this position. Hybrid Work Environment AARP observes Mondays and Fridays as remote workdays, except for essential functions. Remote work can only be done within the United States and its territories. Compensation and Benefits AARP offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including a 401(k); 100% company-funded pension plan; health, dental, and vision plans; life insurance; paid time off to include company and individual holidays, vacation, sick, caregiving, and parental leave; performance-based and peer-based recognition and tuition reimbursement. Equal Employment Opportunity AARP is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. AARP does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. item.title: Senior Director, Public Policy
item.description: Senior Director, Public Policy Organization: Enterprise Community Partners Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Enterprise is a national nonprofit that exists to make a good home possible for the millions of families without one. We support community development organizations on the ground, aggregate and invest capital for impact, advance housing policy at every level of government, and build and manage communities ourselves. Since 1982, we have invested $92.0 billion and created 1.1 million homes across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands – all to make home and community places of pride, power and belonging. Working at Enterprise At Enterprise, you’ll be part of a diverse, committed team making a difference every day. You will collaborate with some of the smartest minds and biggest hearts in our field. You’ll be empowered to drive systems change and take bold steps to advance racial equity. And you will find a career home where you’re valued and supported in your growth journey. Enterprise offers career opportunities in our offices across the country with an exceptional benefits package. Job Description Summary The Senior Director of Public Policy is a leader on Enterprise’s best-in-class federal policy team. The Senior Director will be responsible for setting the advocacy strategy around tax policy specific to affordable housing and community development and then managing execution and driving outcomes. Job Description Responsibilities: Develop and execute Enterprise’s federal tax policy and advocacy agenda, spearheading a portfolio that includes but is not limited to: LIHTC New Markets Tax Credits Opportunity Zones Neighborhood Homes Tax Credit Additional Treasury Department programs such as the CDFI Fund and Capital Magnet Fund Housing Finance Reform and advocacy around the Community Reinvestment Act, GSEs, and FHFA Lobby on statutory and regulatory policy priorities with Congress and the Executive Branch. Build and maintain strong, ongoing relationships with key Congressional staff, the Administration, and relevant federal agencies. Serve in leadership and management positions and otherwise represent Enterprise within key coalitions to advance our federal tax policy priorities. Co-chair the ACTION Campaign on behalf of Enterprise. Monitor and analyze federal legislation, regulations, and new proposals that impact Enterprise’s public policy, programmatic, and financial products. Serve as a subject matter expert on the federal policy landscape; inform federal, state, and local policy efforts and partner and serve as a resource to other Enterprise divisions and external partners. Work with Enterprise’s External Affairs team on internal and external communications and research content, utilizing social media, press releases, op-eds, and other earned media to advance advocacy efforts. Qualifications: Eight (8) years of relevant experience; graduate degree may be substituted for up to two (2) years of experience. Federal government relations and policy development experience required; experience working in Congress or the executive branch preferred. Deep understanding and expertise on a range of housing and community development policies, in particular LIHTC, NMTC, and OZs. Leadership, strategy, and management skills; previous experience managing staff required. Relationships with policymakers in the legislative and executive branch required, preferably with tax writing committees and Treasury Department. Experience working with tax policy stakeholders required. Excellent communication skills, including the ability to effectively communicate complex policy issues to a broad audience. Public speaking, media relations, and public relations experience preferred. Demonstrated professionalism, diplomacy, composure, flexibility, and ability to adapt to change and overcome obstacles. Strong initiative and autonomy. Strong organizational skills and ability to coordinate complex activities, prioritize conflicting demands and meet deadlines. Ability to work independently, solve problems, and take responsibility for moving tasks forward with minimal supervision. Occasional travel and evening/nontraditional hours required. Positive contribution to work culture and effective, collaborative team member. Salary Transparency You will be joining a team of talented professionals motivated by serving the community and addressing the need for affordable housing. Enterprise offers a comprehensive total rewards package for you and your family. The pay range for this position is $130,000-$155,000. The salary range represents the low and high end of what may be paid for this position. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range, and compensation decisions may be influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Total Rewards at Enterprise This range is just one component of our total rewards package, which also includes annual performance bonuses and generous paid leave programs. Our benefits form a major part of the total rewards package. These include dental, health, and vision care plans, as well as family-building benefits such as adoption and surrogacy support. Enterprise supports flexible work arrangements to promote work-life balance and offers health advocacy, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and mental health benefits. We round out our package with financial education, wellness programs, and auto-enrollment in the company’s 401(k) plan with employer matching contributions. Finally, you will have access to learning and development opportunities, including tuition reimbursement for job-related courses and certifications. item.title: AVP, Policy
item.description: AVP, Policy Organization: Enterprise Community Partners Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Enterprise is a national nonprofit that exists to make a good home possible for the millions of families without one. We support community development organizations on the ground, aggregate and invest capital for impact, advance housing policy at every level of government, and build and manage communities ourselves. Since 1982, we have invested $92.0 billion and created 1.1 million homes across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands – all to make home and community places of pride, power and belonging. Join us at enterprisecommunity.org Working at Enterprise At Enterprise, you’ll be part of a diverse, committed team making a difference every day. You will collaborate with some of the smartest minds and biggest hearts in our field. You’ll be empowered to drive systems change and take bold steps to advance racial equity. And you will find a career home where you’re valued and supported in your growth journey. Enterprise offers career opportunities in our offices across the country with an exceptional benefits package. Job Description Summary The AVP is a senior leader on Enterprise’s best in class policy team. This role sits on our government relations and advocacy team and focuses on supply-side housing policy. The AVP will be responsible for setting GR strategy around treasury, tax, energy, disaster resilience, housing finance, and additional housing and community development policies, and then driving outcomes and managing execution for multiple direct reports. Job Description Responsibilities: Lead the development and execution of Enterprise’s federal supply-side policy and advocacy agenda, spearheading a portfolio that includes but is not limited to: Tax policy, specifically LIHTC, New Market Tax Credits, and Opportunity Zones Additional Treasury Department programs such as the CDFI Fund and Capital Magnet Fund Housing Finance Reform and advocacy around the Community Reinvestment Act, GSEs, and HFHA The cost of Insurance and Housing Development Energy and Disaster Recovery Implementation of Housing and Community Development Authorizing Legislation Coordinate supply-side policy work across the organization, collaborating closely with capital, development, market and program staff, and the state & local policy team to identify high impact policy engagement. Lobby on statutory and regulatory policy priorities, with Legislative and Executive federal government branches and, as needed, Judicial. Serve as a point person on the intersection between housing supply policy and the other Enterprise divisions, identifying collaborative opportunities around execution and communications and with philanthropy. Serve as a subject matter expert on the federal policy landscape; inform federal, state, and local policy efforts and partner and serve as a resource to other Enterprise divisions such as capital and solutions, and external partners. Build, lead, and participate in coalitions by working closely with other advocates and community-based partners on priority policy efforts. Work with Enterprise’s External Affairs team to develop internal and external communications and research content, utilizing social media, press releases, op-eds and other earned media to advance advocacy efforts. This role requires significant communications expertise. Perform senior-level operations and administrative tasks as needed, for example around procurement and management of consultants, onboarding new systems, and partnering with internal leadership on HR, IT, Finance, and grants. Qualifications: Deep understanding and expertise on a range of housing and community development policies, in particular the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC), the CDFI Fund and Capital Magnet Fund, Housing Finance, CRA, and energy and resilience policy. Exceptional leadership, strategy, and management skills, previous experience managing staff required. Federal government relations and policy development experience required; experience working in Congress or the Executive branch preferred. Longstanding relationships with policy makers in the legislative and executive branch. Experience working with housing and community development stakeholders required, specifically with Treasury, LIHTC and the Action Campaign and in the tax policy space, housing finance, energy and disaster resilience, or other relevant sectors. Ten (10) years relevant experience; graduate degree may be substituted for up to two (2) years of experience. Excellent communications skills, including the ability to effectively communicate complex policy issues to a broad audience. Public speaking, media relations and public relations experience. Demonstrated professionalism, diplomacy, composure, flexibility and ability to adapt to change and overcome obstacles. Strong initiative and autonomy. Strong organizational skills and ability to coordinate complex activities, prioritize conflicting demands and meet deadlines. Ability to work independently, solve problems and take responsibility for moving tasks forward with minimal supervision. Occasional travel and evening/nontraditional hours required. Positive contribution to work culture and effective, collaborative team member. Salary Transparency You will be joining a team of talented professionals motivated by serving the community and addressing the need for affordable housing. Enterprise offers a comprehensive total rewards package for you and your family. The pay range for this position is $170,000-$190,000. The salary range represents the low and high end of what may be paid for this position. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range, and compensation decisions may be influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Total Rewards at Enterprise This range is just one component of our total rewards package, which also includes annual performance bonuses and generous paid leave programs. Our benefits form a major part of the total rewards package. These include dental, health, and vision care plans, as well as family-building benefits such as adoption and surrogacy support. Enterprise supports flexible work arrangements to promote work-life balance and offers health advocacy, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and mental health benefits. We round out our package with financial education, wellness programs, and auto-enrollment in the company’s 401(k) plan with employer matching contributions. Finally, you will have access to learning and development opportunities, including tuition reimbursement for job-related courses and certifications. Thank you for your interest in joining the Enterprise team and contributing to our mission to serve others. #LI-NU1 #ID Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, External Communications
item.description: Manager, External Communications Organization: Airlines Reporting Corp. (ARC) Location: Arlington, VA | Tampa, FL | Louisville, KY Date Posted: 09/24/2026 About The Role: It’s a great time to join us at Airlines Reporting Corporation (ARC)! ARC accelerates the growth of global air travel by delivering forward-looking travel data, flexible distribution services and other innovative industry solutions. We are a leading travel intelligence company with the world’s largest, most comprehensive global airline ticket dataset, including more than 15 billion passenger flights. By working here, you can contribute to solutions and expertise that strengthen economies and enrich lives. We think big, embrace challenges and explore new ideas to lead the way for the travel industry. ARC is looking for a talented Manager, External Communications to join our team! In this role, you will develop, coordinate and execute overarching content and media strategies to strengthen the ARC brand. You will create awareness and demand for ARC’s solutions among target audiences. These strategies must align with ARC’s corporate strategy and create a lasting positive impression among customers, partners and media. The Manager, External Communications will develop and deliver social media, media and marketing plans for both new and established solutions to achieve brand and revenue objectives. You’ll lead the development and execution of ARC’s content strategy, telling ARC’s story through marketing and communications channels. You will also lead a team of skilled communications experts and ensure alignment of activities. You’ll establish goals and expectations and evaluate performance using data, qualitative assessments, and feedback. And, you will work collaboratively with internal business leaders and cross-functional groups, make decisions, maintain confidentiality, multitask, and prioritize in a high-volume environment. What You’ll Get to Do: Develop strategic marketing plans and KPIs for the ARC brand and solutions portfolios. Lead the execution of these plans through content and promotional opportunities in partnership with the broader brand and marketing team, business stakeholders, customer engagement, and other leaders. Plan, develop and deliver content across a range of brand and marketing channels using a shared calendar. Communications include web-based communications, social media, email, paid and/or earned media, and conference topics. Monitor, track and analyze the cost, quality and effectiveness of marketing activities. Present status updates on strategic marketing campaigns and programs to key stakeholders throughout the company. Lead efforts to track brand health and marketing positioning of competitors. Create and/or edit content with an eye for detail and make recommendations for strategic accuracy. Craft executive talking points, communications and other content as needed. Support review of content that includes emails, social media, presentations, webpages and video scripts. Support ARC customer engagement. Build and maintain close relationships with internal stakeholders, members of the media and ARC partners to further business goals. Supervise, mentor and develop direct reports and extended team members; provide direction, leadership and coaching to project teams to execute brand and product marketing plans. You’ll Bring These Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in communications, English, journalism, marketing, business or related field required; equivalent experience considered 6+ years of experience in strategic marketing; ideally some experience in the airline industry Knowledge of branding and marketing principles Experience directly leading individuals and teams Customer-focused with commitment to quality Outstanding communication, leadership and conflict-resolution skills A strategic, analytical and creative thinker and nuanced communicator with excellent organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks in a high-volume environment. ARC123 What We Can Offer You: Joining ARC means joining a team that is motivated, diverse, creative, collaborative and solutions-oriented. We think big, embrace challenges, and explore new ideas to lead the way for the travel industry. Our employees value the hands-on learning and professional development opportunities that allow them to expand their skills and grow their career in new, dynamic ways. ARC offers WorkFlex. WorkFlex is ARC’s hybrid work program which offers eligible employees the flexibility to work from home while also requiring in office workdays throughout the year to foster collaboration and connection throughout the organization. We’ve designed WorkFlex to enable employees to succeed and thrive while maintaining strong connections to one another and ARC – both of which are critical to our shared success. We offer a highly competitive, comprehensive benefits package so you can worry less and focus on what truly matters. Please click here to review our benefits on our company website. By joining ARC, you will partner with top minds in the industry as we use data and technology to innovate how the world travels. item.title: Principal Analyst – Corporate & External Affairs
item.description: Principal Analyst – Corporate & External Affairs Organization: FIS Location: Dublin, IE Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Position Type : Full time Type Of Hire : Experienced (relevant combo of work and education) Are you curious, motivated, and forward-thinking? At FIS you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun. About the role: As FIS’ senior policy voice in Europe, the Head of EMEA Policy is responsible for the company’s EU policy strategy and engagement. The role carries enterprise-wide influence and executive autonomy, setting policy direction, aligning stakeholders, and advising leaders on strategic decisions that shape the company’s European business. This is an exciting opportunity to serve as the primary representative across EU institutions and trade associations to shape the company’s position on key policy areas, including the Digital Euro, PSD3, the EU AI Act, critical third party regimes, and cloud and tech sovereignty. The role builds the coalitions and institutional relationships needed to advance FIS’ interests with various EU government entities. Based in Dublin, with travel to Brussels and other European capitals as needed, the role combines a high-profile external mandate with direct executive partnership. You will oversee external government-affairs consultants and report directly to the Vice President of Global Public Policy in Washington, DC. What you will be doing: Build and maintain strategic relationships with European Union institutional stakeholders—including the European Commission, European Parliament, Council of the EU—as well as select EU member state government authorities Drive proactive legislative and regulatory monitoring and engagement across priority policy areas, with a particular focus on key topics such as Digital Euro, PSD3, the EU AI Act, DORA/operational resilience, digital assets/MiCA, data privacy, cybersecurity, and EU digital sovereignty frameworks Represent FIS in EU-based trade associations coordinating and advancing the company’s policy positions Partner with European sales teams and the Commercial Office leadership to address tech sovereignty concerns in client engagements and RFP contexts, translating policy developments into actionable commercial guidance and building FIS’ trust narrative Serve as the primary EU policy counterpart to the Head of Global Public Policy and the Head of Regulatory Legal, ensuring alignment between EU advocacy efforts and global company strategy Advise senior leaders across FIS on emerging EU regulatory and legislative developments, shaping business strategy and product priorities with respect to key policy areas Develop strategic policy positions, prepare high-quality briefing materials, and lead responses to European regulatory consultations and legislative proposals Lead advocacy strategy to advance FIS’ policy goals, with a particular focus on positioning FIS as a trusted partner within the European ecosystem and countering geopolitical and regulatory movements that could disadvantage U.S.-based fintech providers Manage and direct external government affairs consultants, including selecting, directing, and evaluating third-party advisory firms to extend FIS’s reach and effectiveness across EU policy venues, ensuring cost-effective and consistently excellent service delivery Oversee policy project management, ensuring clear deliverables, timely progress tracking, and strong alignment with business and executive stakeholders What you bring: 8+ years of experience in EU public policy, government affairs, or related government/institutional roles, with a demonstrated track record of effective engagement with EU institutions Deep understanding of EU legislative and regulatory processes, including the roles of the European Commission, European Parliament, Council of the EU, and European Supervisory Authorities Knowledge of the payments, financial services, and / or technology sectors, with familiarity with key EU regulatory frameworks such as DORA, MiCA, PSD3, and the AI Act Strategic, politically savvy thinker with the ability to translate complex EU policy developments into actionable guidance for a U.S.-headquartered financial technology company operating across European markets Proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships across EU institutions, national delegations, and industry coalitions, and to collaborate effectively across geographically distributed teams Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to manage tight deadlines and operate effectively in high-pressure, fast-paced environments Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence and presence to communicate at the executive level and represent the company in public forums Demonstrated ability to work with great authority and limited day-to-day oversight, exercising sound judgment and initiative Preferred: Existing network within the EU policy community, particularly in Brussels Experience working in or advising U.S.-headquartered financial services or technology companies on EU regulatory matters What we offer you: A multifaceted job with a high degree of responsibility and a broad spectrum of opportunities A modern, international work environment and a dedicated and motivated team A broad range of professional education and personal development possibilities – FIS is your final career step! A competitive salary and benefits A variety of career development tools, resources and opportunities The chance to work on some of the most challenging, relevant issues in financial services & technology Privacy Statement FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice. Sourcing Model Recruitment at FIS works primarily on a direct sourcing model; a relatively small portion of our hiring is through recruitment agencies. FIS does not accept resumes from recruitment agencies which are not on the preferred supplier list and is not responsible for any related fees for resumes submitted to job postings, our employees, or any other part of our company. #pridepass Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Political Compliance Manager
item.description: Senior Political Compliance Manager Organization: Aristotle Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Description About Aristotle Aristotle is the leading political technology and data company in the world. Our team of experts comes from all facets of tech, political and corporate backgrounds to offer the most powerful tools to campaigns, elected officials, voters, government organizations, corporations, nonprofits and PACs all over the world, no matter their democratic ideology. The Senior Political Compliance Manager will provide Political Action Committee (PAC) and lobbying compliance and management services to our clients. The incumbent will be responsible for preparing federal and state campaign finance and other regulatory filings corporate and association clients. Regular tasks include entering or managing the entry of data in client PAC databases; screening proposed contributions against relevant prohibitions and limits; performing regular bank reconciliations; and, assisting clients in PAC management and internal reporting. Senior Managers will be expected to carry out certain of these activities without supervisory review. Senior Managers will serve as mentors and assist their junior colleagues with compliance and client relations issues, including reviews of draft reports as assistance is needed by the VP and SVP. This position also requires the employee to contribute actively to both their immediate team and the broader division. This includes helping train new employees, stepping in to provide coverage when needed, and potentially serving as a team lead. For selected clients, the incumbent will act as primary relationship manager and will be responsible for managing client expectations, communicating project status, increasing customer satisfaction, ensuring customer retention, identifying, and pursuing up sell opportunities, and resolving product/business issues experienced by the clients. This position requires extreme attention to detail, ability to manage or switch among multiple tasks rapidly, and ability to meet multiple statutory deadlines. Duties & Responsibilities: Prepare and file Federal and State campaign finance reports with appropriate agencies, while serving as a collaborative team member available to support team operations when needed. May serve as a team lead, which includes training new team members, delegating work to ensure coverage during absences, and contributing ideas to improve department operations. Prepare and file lobbying, pay-to-play and non-profit tax forms for clients as needed. Import or enter receipt and disbursement activity and HR files in PAC software. Serve as primary point of contact and overall relationship manager for assigned customers. Perform banking services (account set-up, deposits, check preparation, ledger, and reconciliation) for client PACs. Track disbursement limits and prohibitions. Develop detailed operating procedures for each client. Train clients on the proper use of the software to meet their PAC program goals and objectives. Prepare financial and PAC management reports. Prepare letters to accompany disbursements as needed. Respond to client requests in a timely manner. Establish and maintain positive relationships with clients. Assist in new client software conversions and custom programming needs. Work with Compliance and Development teams to resolve client data or functionality issues. Attend events and conferences as a representative of the company and the department. Salary Range: $85k-$100k/year. Requirements BA/BS in accounting, political science, business, or related field. 5+ years of relevant work experience. Experience in filing federal (required) and state (desirable) campaign finance reports. Professional and interpersonal skills required to develop and foster positive relationships. Outstanding communication skills (both verbal and written). Proficiency in Microsoft software suite and tools, including Excel. Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision, as well as a part of a team. General knowledge of the legislative process and interest in politics. Excellent time management and organizational skills. Desired: Training, experience, or advanced degree in law or accounting. Experience in filing Federal or state lobbying disclosure reports. Experience in filing non-profit tax returns (990, 1120 POL) Facility with QuickBooks. Basic HTML knowledge. Benefits All positions are Full-Time, with competitive compensation, medical benefits, paid vacation, 401k plan and stock options. Casual dress code and a non-corporate atmosphere make this a fun place to work and learn in a team environment. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
