item.title: Public Policy Associate
item.description: Public Policy Associate Organization: Perplexity Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 ABOUT PERPLEXITY Perplexity is AI for people who expect more: more accuracy, more agency, more signal, and less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress. As our footprint grows, so does the number of policymakers, agencies, and civil society leaders who want to understand what we are building and how we think. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Public Policy Associate in Washington, D.C. to sit at the center of Perplexity’s engagement with Congress, the executive branch, trade associations, think tanks, and the broader D.C. ecosystem. This work happens where Washington happens: in Hill offices, in coalition meetings across town, and at the occasional evening event where the conversations that matter most actually take place. This is a relationship-heavy, execution-heavy seat. You’ve already worked both sides of the table, once inside a congressional office and once representing an organization before Congress, and you know how policy actually moves. Our Comms team and executive leadership set the strategy. You’re our boots on the ground who makes it real. You’ll build the stakeholder map, carry our message into the rooms that matter, and bring back what policymakers are saying so that Perplexity shows up early, credibly, and consistently on the policy questions shaping AI. This role reports to the Senior Director, Product, Privacy & Regulatory Legal. WHAT YOU’LL DO Execute our policy communications strategy set by our Comms and executive leadership teams. Turn company positions into talking points, event backgrounders, and rapid response materials, and feed intelligence back to our legal, policy, and product teams. Build and hold relationships with Hill staff in personal offices and on committees, executive branch staff, trade associations, think tanks, and civil society organizations. Advocate directly. Take meetings, deliver our positions, and follow bills and rulemakings that affect Perplexity, working within the company’s lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements. Run our D.C. event footprint. Manage Hill staff briefings, roundtables, product demos, receptions, dinners, and off-site events. Own guest lists, venues, run-of-show planning, and follow-up activities. Represent Perplexity in coalitions and trade association working groups. Track what’s being said, flag what matters, and bring our point of view into the conversation. Partner with think tanks and civil society groups on convenings, research launches, and joint programming. Prepare our leaders for D.C. engagements. Create briefing books, meeting preparation materials, and post-meeting recaps that actually get read. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR At least 3 years of professional experience, including time on Capitol Hill in a personal office or on a committee. Congressional experience is strongly preferred. External lobbying experience, either at a government relations or law firm representing clients, or in-house at a company. Registered lobbying experience under the Lobbying Disclosure Act is strongly preferred. A real Washington network that you built yourself, along with the instinct to keep growing it. Event execution. You can run a 20-person Hill staff briefing or a 150-person reception end-to-end without anything slipping. Strong writing. You can turn a meeting into a two-paragraph readout and transform a briefing book into something a principal will actually use. Sound judgment. You know what to escalate, what to handle, and how to represent a company in a room without a script. Genuine curiosity about AI policy and the substance of what Perplexity is building. You don’t need to be a technologist, but you do need to want to learn. Comfort with the pace. Mornings, days, and evenings. This is a role for someone energized by the D.C. schedule. Based in Washington, D.C. and able to work in the office four days a week, with occasional travel. BONUS Hill experience on judiciary, commerce, intelligence, or AI-focused portfolios. Experience staffing a principal at a company, agency, or trade association. Existing relationships across the AI and tech policy community in Washington, D.C. COMPENSATION $185K to $200K base salary Equity included as part of the compensation package Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director Government Relations
item.description: Senior Director Government Relations Organization: Home Depot Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/24/2026 Position Purpose The Senior Director, Government Relations serves as a primary executive advocate and strategist representing The Home Depot before elected officials and high-level decision-makers at the federal and state level. This role shapes and executes the company’s legislative agenda, aligning political strategy with enterprise business goals to mitigate risk, drive growth, and enhance shareholder value. In addition to leading policy strategy across the organization, the Senior Director oversees multi-million dollar departmental and PAC operational budgets, manages external advocacy resources, and leads a high-performing team of government relations professionals and retained lobbying firms. Key Responsibilities 30% Strategic Enterprise Policy Management – Formulate and direct proactive, high-impact government relations strategies across enterprise-critical policy portfolios, including e-commerce, data privacy/security, corporate tax, international trade, supply chain/global sourcing, and labor. Assign legislative portfolios and delegate strategic priorities across internal lobbying teams and external consulting firms to ensure company objectives are effectively advanced. Manage external consultants and ensure they represent the company to elected officials. Manage relationships with all trade associations, including directing them to engage on behalf of the company. 20% Department Budgeting & PAC Governance: Financial & Resource Oversight – Develop, manage, and optimize the government relations department operating budget, ensuring efficient capital allocation across internal operations, external counsel, and advocacy campaigns. Political Action Committee (PAC) – Direct the financial governance, strategic disbursement, fundraising initiatives, and compliance of The Home Depot Political Action Committee (PAC) in alignment with corporate goals and legal standards. 25% Legislative Advocacy & Direct Stakeholder Engagement – Serve as a senior representative of The Home Depot to Members of Congress, Administration/White House leadership, federal regulatory agencies, and industry trade associations. Facilitate and moderate high-level engagements between C-suite executives, Board members, and key government leaders. 10% Senior Leadership Reporting & Political Intelligence – Provide real-time strategic counsel and executive briefings to Senior Leadership and relevant business units on regulatory trends, legislative risks, and political shifts impacting the enterprise. 15% Team Leadership & Development – Lead, develop, and coach an experienced team of government relations professionals. Establish clear priorities, build team capabilities, and foster an environment that drives engagement, accountability, and professional growth. Attract and retain top talent consistent with The Home Depot’s values and culture of doing the right thing. Direct Manager/Direct Reports This position typically reports to the Vice President, Government Relations and External Communications. Direct management of 4-6 professional direct reports and oversight of external retained lobbying firms and consultants. Travel Requirements Typically requires overnight travel 5% to 20% of the time. Frequent travel within Washington, D.C. and to key federal, state, and local government meetings, industry conferences, and company locations. Physical Requirements Most of the time is spent sitting in a comfortable position, and there is frequent opportunity to move about. On rare occasions, there may be a need to move or lift light articles. Working Conditions Located in a comfortable indoor area. Any unpleasant conditions would be infrequent and not objectionable. Minimum Qualifications Must be eighteen years of age or older. Must be legally permitted to work in the United States. Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government Affairs, Business Administration, or a related field. 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in federal government relations, congressional staff leadership, administrative agencies, or corporate public policy settings. Preferred Qualifications People Leadership: Proven track record of managing and developing direct reports and leading high-performing government affairs teams within public, consumer-facing companies or major corporate trade associations. Bipartisan Network: Extensive, established bipartisan relationships across both chambers of Congress, key legislative committees, and executive branch agencies. Financial Management: Demonstrated experience building, forecasting, and managing multi-million dollar operational and political budgets. Minimum Education The knowledge, skills, and abilities typically acquired through the completion of a bachelor’s degree program or equivalent degree in a field of study related to the job. Preferred Education The completion of a Juris Doctor or equivalent and required certifications for practicing law. Minimum Years of Work Experience 10 Minimum Leadership Experience 5+ years of previous leadership experience. Competencies Executive Presence: Mastered ability to negotiate and interact effectively with C-suite executives, Cabinet officials, and Members of Congress. Financial Acumen: Strong budget management skills, including contract negotiation with external firms and financial reporting. Strategic Communication: Superior written, verbal, and executive presentation capabilities. Crisis & Pressure Management: Exceptional sound judgment and decision-making under high-pressure, ambiguous, and fast-moving political environments. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Associate, Lobbyist
item.description: Senior Associate, Lobbyist Organization: American College of Physicians (ACP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 The Governmental Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) Division of the American College of Physicians (ACP) is seeking a candidate for the position of Senior Associate, Lobbyist for the Legislative Affairs department. ACP, a national organization of internal medicine physicians with headquarters in Philadelphia, is the largest medical specialty organization and the second-largest physician group in the United States. The Senior Associate, Lobbyist advocates ACP’s positions with members of Congress and their staff and assists in the development of policy options and strategies to achieve ACP’s stated goals and objectives with Congress. They will consult with the ACP Services PAC staff and consultants to recommend contributions to various political candidates based on set criteria approved by the ACP Services PAC Board of Directors. This is a hybrid role in Washington DC with at least two days in the office per week required. Responsibilities: Provides legislative and political advice that should be considered in the development of policy and action options by ACP. Maintains an excellent understanding of all ACP policies and communicates such policies to congressional staff and Members of Congress through frequent Congressional engagement and written communications. Establishes ongoing relationships with congressional staff for key health committees and the staff, particularly the House Energy and Commerce, for individual members who serve on those committees. Assists in the development of testimony and other communications to Congress as necessary to advocate ACP positions and looks for opportunities for ACP’s governance to testify before Congress. Articulates ACP policy and recommendations in coalitions established to encourage joint actions on issues of common concern. Briefs ACP leaders on policy and responds to specific member inquiries. Make presentations on federal policy matters to ACP committees, chapters, Annual Session, and meetings of other organizations. Assists ACP Services in conducting its fly-ins and lobby days. Provides reports to management staff and other colleagues on significant legislative and political developments on ACP issues. Attends fundraisers and other external activities in support of ACP Services PAC activities. May deliver PAC contributions to candidates. Help coordinate activities of College interns in DC office. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in political science or related field. Graduate degree is preferred. A minimum of five years’ experience as congressional staff or in a government affairs role for a health-related association, or other comparable and relevant experience, is required. A comprehensive understanding of complex health issues is required. Demonstrated record of success with Congress. Ability to analyze and interpret data, to understand scientific reports in health policy literature, and to analyze and evaluate legislative materials is essential. Excellent oral and written communication skills essential to interact effectively with a variety of audiences including members of Congress, congressional committees, members, and all levels of College staff. ACP offers a competitive salary, superior benefits, and a supportive work environment. Find out more about ACP at: https://www.acponline.org/working-at-acp. Interested candidates should apply through our ADP link with a cover letter, writing sample, and resume. ACP is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their age, race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected class. item.title: Government Relations Manager
item.description: Government Relations Manager Organization: Obvio Location: College Park, MD Date Posted: 09/26/2026 About Obvio AI Each year, more than 40,000 people in the U.S. leave home and never make it back due to traffic crashes. At Obvio, we believe these deaths are preventable. We deploy solar-powered, AI-assisted cameras to enforce traffic laws where pedestrians are most vulnerable, automating enforcement in ways that traditional systems cannot. Our approach has already led to a 50% reduction in reckless driving in early partner cities. Founded by the team behind Motive’s AI dashcam and backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Khosla Ventures, we are building the intelligence layer for safer streets globally. About the Role We’re looking for a Government Relations Manager to support Obvio’s state and local legislative and regulatory efforts. To date, Obvio’s founders have helped pass bills in the states of Maryland and Virginia, opening the door to operate in select counties. As we expand into new states and cities, you’ll be on the ground executing the campaigns, relationships, and research that make that expansion possible — working closely with our Head of Government Relations to turn strategy into results. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role for someone who wants to build deep expertise in state and local government relations at a fast-growing company with real policy momentum. You’ll be a critical partner in making it happen, with real ownership over specific states, relationships, and projects. What You’ll Do Support and help execute state and county-level legislative campaigns across multiple states, working closely with the Head of Government Relations on strategy and sequencing Track legislative and regulatory developments relevant to Obvio across target states and cities, and flag risks and opportunities to leadership Build and maintain relationships with local officials, staffers, and coalition partners in target jurisdictions Help identify, coordinate, and manage day-to-day work with local lobbyists and consultants engaged in active legislative sessions Draft materials that support GR communications — talking points, one-pagers, testimony, and briefing documents for meetings with officials Represent Obvio at city council meetings, county hearings, and community/stakeholder events in target markets Support coalition-building efforts by identifying and engaging local advocates, safety organizations, and community stakeholders Maintain organized tracking of bill status, relationship contacts, and campaign timelines across all active states What We’re Looking For 5-8 years of experience in state or local government relations, public affairs, campaigns, or a related field Direct experience supporting or helping execute a state or local legislative campaign (bill tracking, coalition support, stakeholder outreach, or similar) Solid understanding of how state legislatures and county/city government processes work Strong written and verbal communication skills — comfortable drafting materials for officials and representing Obvio in external meetings Highly organized, with the ability to track multiple states, relationships, and timelines simultaneously Comfortable operating with autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment, and willing to travel to target states/cities as needed Genuine interest in public safety and road safety policy Nice to have: Prior experience at a public affairs or government relations consulting firm Existing relationships with state legislators, county officials, or advocacy organizations in target markets Experience with polling, message testing, or public communications campaigns Why Obvio Your work will help save lives and improve road safety Series A of $54M Fast-moving startup environment with meaningful ownership Competitive compensation and early-stage equity Obvio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Obvio considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. Obvio is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let your recruiter know. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. This position requires considerable substantive participation in department projects and initiatives. The Manager will assist the team with coordinating meetings, developing advocacy documents such as letters and testimony, attend and summarize legislative hearings, gathering data, and developing presentations, monitoring legislative activity, and providing other assistance as needed. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Include the Following: Assist the SVP Government Affairs and team on all aspects of coordinating, organizing, executing, and reporting of Federal legislative advocacy as legislative issues arise throughout the year. Draft, proofread, fact-check, and distribute printed materials with Government Affairs team. Attend congressional hearings and prepare summaries for distribution to member companies. Assist Government Affairs team on lobbying and congressional outreach with Association members, consultants, and other outside parties. Compile information for distribution to members, consultants, or other interested constituencies on wireless issues. Keep apprised of industry developments and potential impacts on Association objectives. Work with the PAC Director on creation of materials, compiling data, and distributing materials. Proficiency in proofreading skills and strong communications skills are required. item.title: Public Policy and Grassroots Advocacy Manager
item.description: Public Policy and Grassroots Advocacy Manager Organization: Hearing Loss Association of America (HLAA) Location: McLean, VA Date Posted: 09/26/2026 About HLAA The Hearing Loss Association of America (HLAA) is the nation’s leading nonprofit organization representing people with hearing loss. HLAA opens the world of communication through information, education, support, and advocacy. With more than 50 million Americans living with hearing loss, HLAA works nationally and locally to promote hearing health and provide vital resources that help people with hearing loss and their families live better lives. Job Purpose Guide HLAA’s public policy and advocacy program and strengthen HLAA’s impact on federal, state, and local policy affecting people with hearing loss. Leverage HLAA’s reputation as the leading consumer voice to ensure the needs of people with hearing loss are reflected in legislation, regulations, and technology development. Job Summary Advocacy is central to HLAA’s mission. Public policy determines whether people with hearing loss have access to effective communication and affordable hearing health care. HLAA educates lawmakers, regulatory bodies, and industry partners about the needs of people with hearing loss and works with technology companies to ensure accessibility is built into product design. The Public Policy and Grassroots Advocacy Manager represents HLAA to key decision makers while expanding HLAA’s grassroots network and strengthening communication access programs. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Build and maintain a strong network of volunteers with deep personal connections to HLAA’s mission. Represent HLAA to lawmakers, regulatory bodies, coalition partners, corporate partners, and HLAA members. Establish and maintain strategic partnerships to advance policy, legislative, and regulatory improvements. Collaborate with the Executive Director on strategic planning for HLAA’s public policy agenda, including legislation such as Medicare hearing aid coverage and the Communications, Video, and Technology Accessibility Act. Monitor federal proceedings and prepare or contribute to written comments on agency proposals, coordinating with coalition partners as needed. Support state-level advocacy networks (HLAA Chapters, State Organizations, individual members) through training and HLAA-owned technology. Educate members of Congress and staff through virtual and in-person meetings, written communications, and phone calls. Serve on selected federal advisory committees (FACA), industry advisory boards, and consumer coalitions. Partner with HLAA’s communications team to develop clear, empowering advocacy content. Respond to inquiries from public officials and media regarding HLAA’s advocacy efforts. Translate complex policy and technology issues into plain-language communications, including topics such as ADA communication access and hearing aid compatibility requirements. Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Public Health Education, Government Relations, International Relations, Communications, or a related field. 5-7 years of experience in advocacy or public policy at the federal and/or state level. Experience in consumer advocacy, disability rights, public health, or communication access preferred. Experience with grassroots education or advocacy campaigns. Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex legislative and technological concepts in plain language. Qualifications Knowledge of hearing loss and the impact of communication access barriers. Understanding of hearing aids, cochlear implants, assistive listening devices, captioning, speech-to-text apps, and related technologies. Strong written communication skills for consumer audiences, government officials, and federal agencies. Familiarity with social media and modern communication strategies. Ability to use CRM systems and apply data to inform advocacy actions. Ability to serve as a subject matter expert for staff, grassroots advocates, and external stakeholders. Understanding of federal disability law, including the ADA and accessibility provisions of the Communications Act. Experience communicating with Congressional policymakers and staff. Ability to use data to shape policy messages and initiatives. Experience in coalition-building and teamwork. Ability to communicate complex information clearly in writing and presentations. Strong organizational and interpersonal skills. Integrity, credibility, and professionalism. Proactive, strategic thinker able to develop policy plans with the Executive Director. Experience in nonprofit environments. Ability to produce high-quality materials under tight deadlines and manage multiple projects. Comfortable as a self-starter and team collaborator. Ability to facilitate group meetings, presentations, and webinars. Technical Skills Microsoft 365 Digital advocacy and Constituent Relationship Management tools Research skills Working knowledge of social media Experience with hearing assistive technology Work Environment Office environment with required travel to HLAA’s annual convention, local meetings, and other events as needed. Employment Details Type: Full-Time Status: Exempt Terms of Employment: At-will Location: McLean, Virginia (Hybrid) Benefits Comprehensive package including employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance; disability insurance; TIAA 403(b) retirement plan; paid holidays; PTO; and a flexible work schedule. Equal Opportunity Statement HLAA is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to recruiting and maintaining a diverse staff. Individuals from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. HLAA does not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy, parenthood, or any other category protected by law. How to Apply Submit a resume and cover letter with salary range requirements to [email protected] with “Policy and Grassroots Advocacy Manager” in the subject line. We will review only applications sent to the jobs mailbox with all required materials. We will contact viable candidates for interviews. Annual Salary Range: $70,000-$90,000K Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Government Relations Manager
item.description: Government Relations Manager Organization: Syngenta Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Compensation: USD 105,700 – USD 196,300 – yearly About Syngenta At Syngenta Group, we’re a global community of 56,000 innovators across 90 countries, united by a 250-year legacy of agricultural excellence. As the world’s most local agricultural technology partner, we create tailor-made solutions that transform farming while protecting our planet, driven by our commitment to innovation, ethics, and integrity. Through our welcoming environment and varied perspectives, we pioneer breakthrough solutions for farmers, society, and future generations. Join our worldwide teams of agricultural pioneers in creating a more resilient and equitable food system for all. Job Description At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers’ success. To support this mission, Syngenta’s Crop Protection Sustainability and Corporate Affairs Team is seeking a Government Relations Manager in Washington, DC. This role will represent the company in legislative and regulatory matters and provide comprehensive support to the Director, Federal Affairs, and the Head of Public Affairs, NA, in advancing Syngenta’s interests through effective engagement with government officials, agencies, and industry stakeholders. This role will help shape public policy that supports Syngenta’s business goals and values, with a focus on building relationships, conducting research, preparing materials, coordinating the company’s legislative advocacy efforts, and contributing to the overall strategic direction of Syngenta’s government relations efforts in North America. Accountabilities: Drive policy outcomes that align with Syngenta’s strategic objectives. Assist in building and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders, including government officials, industry associations, and advocacy groups. This may involve attending meetings, coordinating communications, working with consultants, and preparing materials for meetings. Develop and own relationships with government officials and others where appropriate. Analyze policy developments and conduct relevant research. Prepare talking points, presentations, and other communication materials for the Director and other Syngenta representatives. Assist in drafting correspondence and other communications. Monitor legislative activity at the federal and state levels, tracking bills and amendments relevant to Syngenta’s interests. Provide timely updates and analysis to the Director and broader public affairs team. Assist with management of Syngenta’s political action committee (PAC). Assist in the planning and execution of events, such as conferences, meetings, and briefings. Network with peer companies and relevant stakeholders. Contribute to the strategic planning and execution of Syngenta’s government relations program in North America. Qualifications A bachelor’s degree in Government, Public Administration, Political Science, or a related field from an accredited institution. 5 years of proven experience working in a public affairs function or a public relations function. Experience developing and working with coalitions of interested stakeholders to achieve desired results. Experience advocating before and working with Congress and the Executive Agencies. Strong judgment skills and political acumen, especially in fields of agriculture, defense, trade, crop protection, and related issues. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Experience with all branches of the federal government. Strong political judgment and political acumen. Ability and desire to work across multiple time zones, countries, and cultures. Values a global audience with varied perspectives. Critical Success Factors & Key Challenges Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to build relationships and network both internally and externally. Ability to navigate a complex political environment. Strong judgment and political acumen. Collaborative, team-player ethos are essential. Proactive and detail-oriented in a fast-paced environment. Strong advocacy skills and the ability to effectively represent Syngenta’s interests in complex policy discussions that impact the agricultural sector. Additional Information What We Offer: A culture that celebrates belonging and collaboration, promotes professional development and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members. item.title: Social Policy Government Affairs Manager
item.description: Social Policy Government Affairs Manager Organization: The Niskanen Center Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 The Niskanen Center seeks a government affairs professional to lead outreach for our growing Social Policy Team. This team is responsible for advancing a fundamental premise of the Niskanen Center: ongoing social progress and widespread prosperity depend on both a robust system of social insurance and a vibrant, innovative private sector. To advance this vision, the team engages in traditional work and family issues (family benefits, unemployment insurance, paid leave) as well as emerging supply-side issues (housing, healthcare). This position will cover the work and family portfolio. Description Department: Social Policy Location: Washington, D.C. Schedule: Flexible hybrid, minimum 3 days in-office per week Job Status: Full-Time Experience: 3+ years working with the federal legislative or executive branch or equivalent experience on a government affairs team. Salary: $100,000-$113,000, plus a generous benefits package Reports to: Director of Social Policy and Director of Government Affairs The Niskanen Center seeks a government affairs professional to lead outreach for our growing Social Policy Team. This team is responsible for advancing a fundamental premise of the Niskanen Center: ongoing social progress and widespread prosperity depend on both a robust system of social insurance and a vibrant, innovative private sector. To advance this vision, the team engages in traditional work and family issues (family benefits, unemployment insurance, paid leave) as well as emerging supply-side issues (housing, healthcare). This position will cover the work and family portfolio. To support this work, the government affairs manager collaborates with our policy and communication staff to advance and promote the team’s research and policy proposals with Congress, the Administration and Executive Branch Agencies, key stakeholders, and coalitional allies. Applicants should have experience working across ideological lines and enthusiasm for strengthening the economic security of American families. The position reports to the Director of Social Policy and to the Director of Government Affairs as a member of the Government Affairs Team. This position does not require prior lobbying registration, but it may involve registering in the future. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and track outreach strategies to advance Niskanen social policy research and proposals with Congress, the Administration and Executive Branch Agencies, key stakeholders, and coalitional allies. This will include activities ranging from direct engagement with policymakers to coalition building and management. Monitor and interpret legislation and policy implementation to ascertain any impact on Niskanen social policy priorities. Draft briefing and educational materials, testimony, statements, questions for the record, speeches, and talking points. Build, coordinate, and maintain partnerships with other nonprofits, public interest groups, coalitions, and related organizations engaged in advancing family economic security. Represent Niskanen in the coalitions, community events, public forums, and the media, including print, radio, television, and social media. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. At least three years of experience working with the federal legislative or executive branch, or equivalent experience on a government affairs team. Excellent written and verbal communications skills. A track record of working independently, creative thinking, and managing multiple projects and priorities. Ability to translate policy ideas to appeal to audiences across the political spectrum. Success working with diverse stakeholders such as policy experts, advocates, thought leaders, as well as Congress, the Administration, and federal administrative and executive agencies. Working knowledge of, or familiarity with, social insurance (UI, PFML, SSDI) social assistance (SSI, TANF), and tax credit (CTC, EITC) policies. How to Apply We only review applications after the deadline: applications must be submitted by 11:59 pm ET on September 30, 2026. Please include a cover letter and resume combined into one PDF here . Be prepared to present additional materials during the interview process. Salary $100,000 – $113,000 per year Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Government Affairs
item.description: Manager, Government Affairs Organization: News Corp Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Job Description : News Corp is a global diversified media and information services company focused on creating and distributing authoritative and engaging content to consumers and businesses throughout the world. The company comprises businesses across a range of media, including: news and information services, book publishing, digital real estate services and cable network programming in Australia. News Corp seeks a government affairs professional to be Manager, Government Affairs. This role will play a key part in shaping the policy environment impacting journalism, digital platforms, and emerging technologies, helping to advance News Corp’s strategic priorities in Washington. Responsibilities include advocacy of the company’s positions with the Administration and Congress; executing advocacy and engagement strategies; and maintaining strong relationships with federal policymakers and key state policymakers on behalf of the company. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including congressional and executive branch staff, third-party groups, and coalitions. Track and provide policy and political analysis on legislation pertaining to issues like generative AI, privacy, intellectual property, etc. Support the development and execution of federal advocacy strategies aligned with News Corp’s public policy priorities. Represent the company at congressional hearings, briefings, and industry forums, synthesizing insights into actionable recommendations for internal stakeholders. Prepare briefings, talking points, and other materials to support News Corp executive leadership engagements with Members of Congress, Executive Branch officials, and other relevant senior stakeholders. Preparing backgrounders, statements, lines of questioning, questions for the record, and other relevant information for congressional hearings. Engage with trade associations and industry coalitions to coordinate on shared policy priorities. Partner cross-functionally with legal, communications, product, and business teams to align policy positions with company strategy. Work as part of a small and nimble team to advance the goals of the company, and perform other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE: A minimum of five (5) years of relevant government affairs or public policy experience, including direct experience working on Capitol Hill, the Executive Branch, a political consulting firm, or within a company’s government affairs department. Established relationships with Congressional offices, committee staff, and relevant federal agencies. Deep knowledge of federal legislative rules, procedures, and processes, including the ability to monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative and regulatory developments in real time. Experience working on technology, media, or intellectual property policy issues preferred. Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and drive outcomes in a complex policy environment. Strong political judgment and ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment. Ability to establish and maintain excellent working relationships. Outstanding research, writing, and communication skills, with the demonstrated ability to distill complex policy issues into clear and concise materials for internal and external audiences. Flexible team player with the ability to effectively prioritize concurrent projects, execute tasks, and meet deadlines while demonstrating professionalism. Ability to work independently while demonstrating exceptional judgment and discretion. TRAVEL HOURS & WORK: The position may require extended work hours as attendance at certain evening events will be required. Equal Opportunity Employer All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other protected characteristic. EEO/Disabled/Vets Reasonable Accommodation We are committed to providing reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application and/or interview process. If you need assistance or accommodation in completing your application or participating in an interview due to a disability, email us at [email protected] . Please put “Reasonable Accommodation” in the subject line and provide a brief description of the type of assistance you need. This inbox will not be monitored for application status updates. Please refer to the privacy notice at the bottom of this page for submitting any data access, deletion, or other data subject rights requests, where permitted under your local laws and regulations. Base Pay Range: $150,000 – $175,000 + Bonus We’re committed to offering competitive and flexible compensation to attract top talent. This pay range reflects our good faith estimate for the role and may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, and other relevant factors. For bonus-eligible roles, targets are determined based on multiple considerations, including market benchmarks and individual contributions. For benefits-eligible roles, we offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package covering health, retirement, wellbeing, and more, along with optional benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. item.description: Manager of Government Relations Organization: Ryder Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Job Description : Summary The Manager Government Relations will support Ryder’s Government Relations efforts with a focus on state and local issues, project management, and internal policy development while also contributing to select federal initiatives. This position will report to the Senior Director of Corporate Affairs and will work closely with cross-functional teams in the development and implementation of sophisticated policy-related strategies and initiatives. This includes educating and advocating on key public policy issues to drive Ryder’s business priorities while maintaining effective relationships with key key civic, government, community, business leaders, and other stakeholders. Essential Functions Manage the internal government relations programs, policies, and initiatives of Ryder by providing full project management support such as developing and maintaining core governing policies, internal controls, procedures, documents, systems, etc. Monitor and analyze federal, state, and local regulations and legislation relevant to Ryder and define and track measurable advocacy integrate government relations strategies into business planning, project execution, community engagement, and external messaging Develop written analyses, talking points, advocacy, and additional materials to support Ryder’s government relations objectives such as creating content (i.e., write copy) for communications (policies, emails, web pages, etc.) and manage contributors, content creators, and contractors/third-party vendors to ensure that all projects assigned are completed accurately and on time Liaison and manage relationships with internal/external stakeholders, including federal, state, and local governments/policymakers, trade associations, customers, consultants, and other stakeholders Additional Responsibilities Maintain working knowledge of Ryder’s advocacy priorities, key regulations and legislation impacting the company, industry, customers, and other stakeholders A high level of discretion and sensitivity is required in performing the work Responsible for enterprise program outcomes, stakeholder alignment, and execution of strategic initiatives Performs other duties as assigned Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree Political Science, Economics, Public item.description: Government Affairs Lead, Public Sector Organization: InterSystems Location: Vienna, VA Date Posted: 09/26/2026 InterSystems technology powers some of the world’s most mission-critical applications, managing over one billion patient records globally. The Government Affairs role is responsible for shaping public policy and legislation, building relationships with government stakeholders, and ensuring our business strategy aligns with evolving healthcare and data interoperability policies. This role serves as a strategic bridge between public sector policy and sales and marketing to support growth while advancing policies that improve patient outcomes and systems efficiency. Responsibilities Monitor and analyze federal healthcare policy, legislation, and regulatory developments affecting health IT, data interoperability and privacy. Develop and execute government affairs strategies that support the InterSystems Public Sector business objectives. Advocate for policies that enable adoption of software solutions through direct engagement with policymakers, regulators, and staff. Draft policy positions, comment letters, testimony, and briefing materials. Assist with influencing public policy and providing input with proposed and existing legislation. Build and maintain relationships with Congressional leadership and key staff. Coordinate executive participation in Congressional meetings, hearings, and industry events. Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable guidance for internal teams. Track emerging policy trends and assess risks and opportunities for the business. Ensure compliance with lobbying, ethics and disclosure requirements. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree and 5–10+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, healthcare policy, or regulatory affairs. Strong understanding of the U.S. healthcare system and health technology policy landscape. Experience engaging with federal and/or state policymakers and regulatory agencies. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience using AI-assisted tools (e.g. copilots, summarisation tools, or chatbots) with an ability to critically evaluate and verify AI-generated outputs Demonstrated ability to learn, evaluate, adapt to, propose and implement AI-augmented workflows in order to continually enhance your own, and the team’s productivity Regional Benefits Comprehensive health/dental insurance plans through BCBS Generous PTO Performance bonus 401K Plan w/company profit sharing Continued Learning/Tuition Assistance We are an equal-opportunity employer and do not discriminate because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, age, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity or expression or any other legally protected category. InterSystems is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. InterSystems is providing a current good faith estimate of the anticipated base salary range for this position depending on a variety of factors including experience, education, skills, and performance. Other compensation may include a discretionary annual variable target incentive. The company also provides generous employee benefits including: Medical, vision, and dental insurance Short-term and long-term disability, and life insurance 401(k) Profit Sharing Contribution Paid Time Off and Holidays Parental Leave Tuition reimbursement This position may be eligible for sales incentives based on certain sales goals, achievements, and results. While sales incentives, if any, vary they generally will result in payment of 15% to 25% of base pay, assuming on-target achievement. The estimated base compensation range for this role is: $133,000 – $163,000 USD About InterSystems InterSystems, a creative data technology provider, delivers a unified foundation for next-generation applications for healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and supply chain customers in more than 80 countries. Our data platforms solve interoperability, speed, and scalability problems for large organizations around the globe to unlock the power of data and allow people to perceive data in imaginative ways. Established in 1978, InterSystems is committed to excellence through its 24×7 support for customers and partners around the world. Privately held and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, InterSystems has 38 offices in 28 countries worldwide. For more information, please visit InterSystems.com. item.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Technology State Policy Advocate
item.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Technology State Policy Advocate Organization: Public Citizen Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Public Citizen seeks a strategic and organized self starter to serve as AI Governance and Tech State Policy Advocate. The Policy Advocate will work closely with the Campaign Director of State AI Governance and Tech Policy to put forth model state AI legislation to establish guardrails to protect the American people from a variety of AI abuses, from deepfake manipulation to chatbot deception. They will be a driving force in the advocacy to move critical legislation forward, including working with the Director to develop strategy and messaging, tracking the landscape of state AI and tech policy, and building and maintaining relationships with state lawmakers and other key partners on both sides of the aisle. The Policy Advocate will also work closely with colleagues and coalition partners on a variety of other efforts to address AI abuses and curb excessive corporate power and wealth concentration and rein in Big Tech. Public Citizen is a national, nonpartisan public interest organization with more than one million members and supporters. We hold governments and corporations accountable through campaigns and advocacy before all branches of government on issues including money in politics, open government, financial regulation, fair trade, consumer protection, access to justice, workplace safety, and drug and medical device safety. Responsibilities State legislative advocacy. Provide expertise on a variety of tech policy issues and legislative solutions. Form and maintain relationships with lawmakers from both sides of the aisle. Identify and engage in advocacy activities to support state legislation. Create written resources to support advocacy efforts. Draft and review legislative language. Work with the Director to develop state legislative strategy. Build a deep understanding of the AI legislative landscape and help identify areas for future legislative work. Manage interns as needed. Research and tracking. Research issues in the area of AI and Big Tech. Draft reports and other written products. Draft and maintain internal and external legislative tracking resources. Other advocacy. Support other advocacy efforts relating to AI and Big Tech including efforts to push back on federal preemption and to hold big tech accountable. Coalition work. Build and maintain relationships with partner organizations and other key stakeholders in the AI and tech regulatory space Media engagement. Respond to press inquiries, and help develop media strategies as needed. Qualifications College degree required. 4+ years of relevant research and advocacy experience, with a preference given to those with specific expertise on AI and/or Big Tech platforms. Exceptional analytic, research, and written and oral communications skills. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in coalitions and networks. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, respond to short-term deadlines and balance multiple responsibilities; maintain strong attention to detail and accuracy. Collaborative, energetic, and mission-driven. Ability to take initiative and drive projects from concept through completion. Strong commitment to and interest in regulating and reining in big tech SALARY AND BENEFITS: Competitive salary and generous benefit package. Below is a list of some of our benefits (please note that some benefits have eligibility requirements). Salary range: $85,383 – 141,633 Benefits include: Great medical and dental coverage, 100% paid by PC, including full coverage for children Three weeks paid vacation for new employees, plus five personal days 401K plan with a 5% contribution from PC after one year of employment 12 weeks of paid parental leave after one year of employment Sabbatical after 8 years of employment Student loan reimbursement program TO APPLY: Please send your resume and cover letter to [email protected] to apply. item.description: Policy Communications Consultant Organization: MetLife Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 About the job Joining Global Marketing & Communications (GMC) means contributing to the company’s customer-centric growth engine by helping customers live more confident futures. Whether driving external or internal marketing and communications, you’ll be fostering engagement and alignment with MetLife’s purpose and values that enable positive customer experiences. Become part of a dynamic team that harnesses an agile and data-driven approach across paid, owned, and earned channels to deliver meaningful and measurable outcomes for MetLife’s key stakeholders: associates, communities, customers, and shareholders. The Opportunity The Policy Communications Consultant will play a key role in shaping and executing strategic communications that advance MetLife’s public policy priorities, regulatory positions and reputation among policymakers, regulators, trade associations and other stakeholders. This individual will partner with various functions and regions within Global Government Affairs, including policy subject matter experts and external affairs teams to craft consistent, credible and effective messaging on legislative, regulatory and political issues affecting the business. Key Responsibilities Develop and manage internal/external communications for government affairs and policy initiatives (briefs, talking points, exec messaging, stakeholder materials). Draft, edit, and align content for policymakers, regulators, and partners; advise enterprise comms on policy, regulatory, and political issues. Support public policy engagement (forums, briefings, trade associations) with remarks, presentations, and policy summaries. Monitor political and policy developments; produce timely updates and maintain consistent tone, branding, and messaging. Contribute to digital/social content and media relations messaging; support PAC communications and engagement efforts. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Political Science, Public Policy, Journalism, or related field; 5+ years of relevant experience. Strong writing/editing skills with ability to simplify complex policy issues for diverse audiences. Deep understanding of policy, regulatory, and political processes, including media and emerging platforms. Experience supporting senior executives and managing cross-functional projects in fast-paced environments. Sound judgment with strong awareness of political context, reputation management, and key influencers. Preferred Qualifications Strong understanding of the financial services industry and client-business dynamics. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (design tools a plus). Location Expectation: This is a hybrid role requiring a minimum of 3 days per week in office. The expected salary range for this position is $89,700 – $119,500. This role may also be eligible for annual short-term incentive compensation and stock-based long-term incentives. All incentives and benefits are subject to the applicable plan terms. Benefits We Offer Our U.S. benefits address holistic well-being with programs for physical and mental health, financial wellness, and support for families. We offer a comprehensive health plan that includes medical/prescription drug and vision, dental insurance, and no-cost short- and long-term disability. We also provide company-paid life insurance and legal services, a retirement pension funded entirely by MetLife and 401(k) with employer matching, group discounts on voluntary insurance products including auto and home, pet, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and accident insurance, as well as Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and digital mental health programs, parental leave, paid time off, paid holidays, volunteer time off, tuition assistance and much more! For more information regarding MetLife’s U.S. benefits, please click here. About MetLife Recognized on Fortune magazine’s list of the “World’s Most Admired Companies”, Fortune World’s 25 Best Workplaces™, as well as the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For®, MetLife, through its subsidiaries and affiliates, is one of the world’s leading financial services companies; providing insurance, annuities, employee benefits and asset management to individual and institutional customers. With operations in more than 40 markets, we hold leading positions in the United States, Latin America, Asia, Europe, and the Middle East. As part of our New Frontier strategy, MetLife is building an AI-enabled, people-centered future. We’re looking for people who bring curiosity, adaptability, and a growth mindset as we use AI to enhance how we serve customers, support communities, and evolve the way work gets done. At MetLife, AI is a responsible partner that supports human judgment, creativity, and continuous improvement while helping us build trust, inclusion, and long-term value. Our purpose is simple – to help our colleagues, customers, communities, and the world at large create a more confident future. United by purpose and guided by our core values – Win Together, Do the Right Thing, Deliver Impact Over Activity, and Think Ahead – we’re inspired to transform the next century in financial services. At MetLife, it’s #AllTogetherPossible. Join us! MetLife is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All employment decisions are made without regards to race, color, national origin, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or domestic/civil partnership status, genetic information, citizenship status (although applicants and employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States), uniformed service member or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law (“protected characteristics”). If you need an accommodation due to a disability, please email us at [email protected] . This information will be held in confidence and used only to determine an appropriate accommodation for the application process. MetLife maintains a drug-free workplace. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liabilities. item.title: Policy Development Manager
item.description: Policy Development Manager Organization: Constellation Location: Baltimore, MD | Washington, DC | Chicago, Illinois Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Job Description Who We Are As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation’s largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we’re creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country’s energy needs today and tomorrow. Total Rewards Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more. Expected salary range of $138,600 to $154,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k). PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION The Manager, Policy Development supports the creation, editing, maintenance, and production of Constellation’s technical policy content. Working under the strategic direction of leadership, this role transforms approved policy positions, analytical findings, and subject matter expertise into high-quality written materials that support advocacy efforts, executive decision making, customer engagement, regulatory proceedings, and industry participation. The role serves as a technical policy content professional for Constellation, ensuring that approved positions are accurately, consistently, and effectively reflected across all policy communications and supporting materials. The position maintains and leverages relationships with internal and external stakeholders across the business units in order to understand policy position impact on advocacy, generation, commercial positions and other actions driving value for the company’s operations and assets. PRIMARY DUTIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Develop policy memos and other work products to explain proposed legislative or regulatory changes and their impact on Constellation. Develop talking points, FAQs, one-pagers, fact sheets, presentations, and supporting materials for internal and external audiences. Translate complex policy, legislative, regulatory, environmental, market, and commercial issues into clear, concise, and compelling content. Adapt approved policy positions for different audiences while maintaining consistency and technical accuracy. Maintain style guides, editorial standards, formatting requirements, and content templates. Conduct quality assurance reviews to ensure content is accurate, consistent, and aligned with approved company positions. Maintain repositories of approved policy materials, talking points, testimony, issue briefs, executive materials, and supporting content. Manage document version control and content refresh processes. Partner with Sustainability, Government Affairs, Regulatory, Commercial, Legal, Finance, Public Advocacy, and Policy Analytics teams to gather inputs and develop content. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS • Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Communications, Journalism, Political Science, English, Environmental Studies, Energy Policy, or a related discipline. • 8+ years of experience in policy communications, legislative communications, regulatory communications, government affairs, corporate strategy, energy or financial markets, public policy, sustainability, or related fields. In lieu of degree, 9 years of experience. • Exceptional technical communication, writing, and editing skills. Strong PowerPoint skills. • Conversant with trends and policy implications of current financial, energy, and legal issues associated with this industry • Demonstrated ability to translate complex policy and regulatory issues into clear and persuasive communications to a variety of audiences, including senior management. • Experience managing multiple high-priority content projects simultaneously. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Advanced degree in Public Policy, Communications, Journalism, Law, or related field Experience in energy policy, clean energy markets, environmental regulation, sustainability, or utility industry policy Knowledge of commodities trading concepts and origination activities Working knowledge of electricity market value chain and wholesale and retail market structures Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build strong relationships with stakeholders Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Manager Legislative Affairs 1 (Outreach and Advocacy Manager)
item.description: Manager Legislative Affairs 1 (Outreach and Advocacy Manager) Organization: Northrop Grumman Location: Falls Church, VA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people’s lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation’s history – from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they’re making history. Northrop Grumman’s Legislative Affairs organization is seeking a Manager, Outreach and Advocacy 1, to lead third-party engagements and implement its advocacy strategies. Reporting to the Director, Policy and Advocacy, the Manager is responsible for developing and executing external engagement strategies in support of Northrop Grumman programs and priorities; coordinating internal company parties in support of advocacy efforts; and collaborating with suppliers, third-party organizations, and other external stakeholders. The individual will be required to engage and develop relationships with a variety of elected officials and their staff, suppliers/partners, state and local leaders, and third parties. This position is located in the Falls Church, VA corporate office with the ability to also work out of the Washington, D.C. Capitol Hill office. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in related discipline, and at least 8 years of experience in government relations, legislative, communications, or advocacy activities OR Master’s degree in related discipline, and at least 6 years of experience in government relations, legislative, communications, or advocacy activities. Excellent written and oral communications skills, and the proven ability to take in large amounts of information and synthesize key messages in fast-paced environment; Experience executing advocacy strategy, collaborating effectively across teams, as well as demonstrated ability to set and meet objectives while reacting to dynamic environments are a must; Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain internal and external relationships related to aerospace and defense and/or political affairs; Experience communicating with federal leaders and key decision-makers is required; Great facility with databases and using their content to execute and assist others in executing email campaigns; and A high level of integrity and a hands-on approach to problem-solving are required, as well as a professional presence for interacting with public policy decision-makers and company executives. Preferred Qualifications: Proven ability to synthesize complex problems/public policy issues while identifying their related business implications and advocacy approaches; Ability to operate in fast-paced environments and demonstrate strong judgment/decision-making skills and political acumen; A strong commitment and ability to work cooperatively in a team environment is paramount; The demonstrated ability to build and foster effective relationships with others; Knowledge of the budget, legislative process, authorization process, and appropriations process; and Experience collaborating across business areas, third parties, and suppliers. Primary Level Salary Range: $121,000.00 – $181,600.00 The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate’s experience, education, skills and current market conditions. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. item.title: U.S. State Government Affairs Manager
item.description: U.S. State Government Affairs Manager Organization: Cisco Location: Washington, DC | Atlanta, GA | Austin, TX | Boston, MA | Research Triangle Park, NC Date Posted: 09/26/2026 Job Description The application window is expected to close on: 10/05/2026 Location: Washington DC, most preferred Meet the Team Cisco is seeking a government affairs and public policy professional to join a global team as a U.S. State Government Affairs Manager. Reporting to the Vice President of State Government Affairs & Community Relations, this individual will help lead Cisco’s government engagements and public policy efforts across multiple states. Cisco’s Government Affairs team represents the company with governments around the world to build relationships with key leaders, advance Cisco’s public policy goals, and educate governments about our industry. Government Affairs is involved in all key legislative, regulatory, and global issues that impact the technology industry. We are comprised of government and public policy experts across two dozen countries who represent Cisco at the highest levels of government. The team has extensive experience in and out of government and are recognized leaders in the industry. Your Impact As a U.S. State Government Affairs Manager, you will develop and implement strategies to strengthen Cisco’s presence and influence with state government stakeholders and technology associations. In collaboration with internal teams—including People, Policy & Purpose (3P), Sales, Communications, Legal, and Product Development—you will drive innovative policy solutions that support Cisco’s business goals and mission to power an inclusive future for all. Key responsibilities include: Advising and preparing senior leaders for engagements with state and local officials, ensuring alignment with Cisco’s business objectives and overall strategy Monitoring, analyzing, and reporting on relevant state legislative, regulatory, and budget developments Building trusted relationships with legislators, legislative staff, governors’ offices, and state agencies to strengthen Cisco’s public sector leadership Educating policymakers on Cisco’s technology and its role in AI, cybersecurity, broadband access, economic development, and public safety Advancing policy priorities aligned with purpose-driven initiatives Representing Cisco in state-level hearings, meetings, and industry coalitions Drafting and presenting testimony, position papers, and advocacy materials Minimum Qualifications: 7+ years of political and public policy experience in government, corporate government affairs, public affairs, trade associations, or public policy institutions Strong understanding of legislative and regulatory processes related to technology policy and familiarity with public policy issues affecting the technology industry Excellent political judgment and relationship-building skills Strong communication, writing, collaboration, and advocacy abilities with a demonstrated ability to build consensus across internal teams in pursuit of shared objectives Ability to travel throughout the U.S. and, on occasion, internationally Preferred Qualifications: Experience in state and local government relations, government affairs, public policy, public affairs, political campaigns, lobbying, outreach, or research Proven success leading policy or public affairs initiatives, such as lobbying or advocacy campaigns Extensive experience driving cross-functional collaboration with senior stakeholders and influencing decisions at all organizational levels Skilled in managing executives with exceptional leadership, communication, and collaboration skills Deep knowledge of technology policy and commitment to Cisco’s vision of a secure and accessible Internet Demonstrated ability to integrate public policy with business strategy and corporate development objectives Why Cisco? At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint. Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. We are Cisco, and our power starts with you. Message to applicants applying to work in the U.S. and/or Canada: The starting salary range posted for this position is $161,300.00 to $204,800.00 and reflects the projected salary range for new hires in this position in U.S. and/or Canada locations, not including incentive compensation*, equity, or benefits. Individual pay is determined by the candidate’s hiring location, market conditions, job-related skillset, experience, qualifications, education, certifications, and/or training. The full salary range for certain locations is listed below. For locations not listed below, the recruiter can share more details about compensation for the role in your location during the hiring process. U.S. employees are offered benefits, subject to Cisco’s plan eligibility rules, which include medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with a Cisco matching contribution, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability coverage, and basic life insurance. Please see the Cisco careers site to discover more benefits and perks. Employees may be eligible to receive grants of Cisco restricted stock units, which vest following continued employment with Cisco for defined periods of time. U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies: 10 paid holidays per full calendar year, plus 1 floating holiday for non-exempt employees 1 paid day off for employee’s birthday, paid year-end holiday shutdown, and 4 paid days off for personal wellness determined by Cisco Non-exempt employees** receive 16 days of paid vacation time per full calendar year, accrued at rate of 4.92 hours per pay period for full-time employees Exempt employees participate in Cisco’s flexible vacation time off program, which has no defined limit on how much vacation time eligible employees may use (subject to availability and some business limitations) 80 hours of sick time off provided on hire date and each January 1st thereafter, and up to 80 hours of unused sick time carried forward from one calendar year to the next Additional paid time away may be requested to deal with critical or emergency issues for family members Optional 10 paid days per full calendar year to volunteer For non-sales roles, employees are also eligible to earn annual bonuses subject to Cisco’s policies. Employees on sales plans earn performance-based incentive pay on top of their base salary, which is split between quota and non-quota components, subject to the applicable Cisco plan. For quota-based incentive pay, Cisco typically pays as follows: .75% of incentive target for each 1% of revenue attainment up to 50% of quota; 1.5% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 50% and 75%; 1% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 75% and 100%; and Once performance exceeds 100% attainment, incentive rates are at or above 1% for each 1% of attainment with no cap on incentive compensation. For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid. The applicable full salary ranges for this position, by specific state, are listed below: New York City Metro Area: $173,400.00 – $265,200.00 Non-Metro New York state & Washington state: $161,300.00 – $235,500.00 * For quota-based sales roles on Cisco’s sales plan, the ranges provided in this posting include base pay and sales target incentive compensation combined. ** Employees in Illinois, whether exempt or non-exempt, will participate in a unique time off program to meet local requirements.
