item.title: Senior Marketing Counsel
item.description: Senior Marketing Counsel Organization: Harvey Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 09/27/2026 Why Harvey At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job’s Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we’re never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we’d love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. Role Overview We are looking for a Senior Counsel- Marketing to join Harvey’s growing legal team. In this role you will be the primary legal point of contact for all marketing and communications activity at Harvey. You will also assist with the contracts and commercial relationships that power our marketing engine, safeguard the integrity of our promotional messaging, and act as a hands-on partner to the teams driving Harvey’s growth. This is a high-impact, cross-functional role for a commercially minded lawyer who wants to sit at the intersection of law, brand, and go-to-market strategy. What You’ll Do Review and advise on marketing language across all promotional material, product announcements, including web copy, advertising, social media, email campaigns, sales enablement content, and event and press materials, to ensure claims are accurate, substantiated, and compliant. Balance commercial, marketing, compliance, and privacy concerns across advertising campaigns (US and internationally). Advise on targeted and digital advertising practices, including the data, privacy, tracking of direct to consumer marketing such as email marketing. Act as the embedded legal partner to Marketing and Comms leadership, providing practical, business-oriented guidance that enables campaigns to launch quickly and responsibly. Partner closely with cross-functional teams to keep pace in a fast-moving environment, knowing when to move independently and when to escalate matters to the right internal stakeholders. Collaborate with the commercial team on global marketing agreements. What You Have J.D. and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar. 8+ years of relevant experience at a law firm and/or in-house, with meaningful exposure to marketing, advertising, and commercial contracting. Strong command of advertising and marketing law, including claims substantiation, and consumer protection. Working knowledge of privacy and data protection issues relevant to targeted advertising and direct-to-consumer marketing. Demonstrated ability to draft and negotiate a high volume of marketing commercial agreements independently. Excellent judgment, a business-first mindset, and the ability to give clear, practical advice under tight timelines. Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and partnering closely with non-legal stakeholders. Compensation $210,300 – $281,500 USD Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. #LI-ML3 Harvey is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made by emailing [email protected] Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Regulatory Compliance Engineer
item.description: Regulatory Compliance Engineer Organization: Re:Build Manufacturing Location: Kalamazoo, MI Date Posted: 09/27/2026 About Re:Build Manufacturing and Re:Build Tekna: Tekna was founded in 1988 in the heart of Southwest Michigan where creative vision and hard work laid the foundation for a business that continues to grow in a rapidly evolving industry. The rigor and attention to detail that comes with designing for the medical industry has awarded us success in supporting both major companies and start-ups from early stage development to commercialization. The same principles apply as we’ve expanded to serve customers in a wide variety of other industries including consumer and industrial goods, electronics, and appliances. Tekna’s project portfolio is incredibly diverse covering medical, life science, consumer and industrial product categories. Tekna is largely client focused offering design consulting, contract manufacturing and original equipment manufacturing services. Tekna’s cross functional teams include Design Engineering, Industrial Design, CAD, Procurement, Production and Quality which offers a friendly and supportive team atmosphere. Re:Build Manufacturing is a growing family of industrial and engineering businesses combining enabling technologies, operational superiority, and strategic M&A to build America’s next generation industrial company. At Re:Build we deploy deep expertise in engineering, operations management, and technology to supercharge the performance of our member companies. We leverage deep professional expertise and a candid, principled operating culture to drive differentiated outcomes. Ours is a fast-paced environment where individuals can stretch and be challenged to pursue their fullest potential. Re:Build was founded to pioneer a profitable model for the revitalization of US manufacturing. We’ve assembled a powerful set of complimentary capabilities and lines of business that enable us to pursue a wide range of end markets. Our acquired businesses are grounded in build-to-print and by-the-hour engineering and design services, and we’re leveraging their combined expertise to migrate to increasingly sophisticated program development and production, as well as the generation of our own products. Our unique set of capabilities lend themselves to highly complex systems and products, and we offer customers a range of services including product and systems design, automation, fabrication, assembly, and large volume contract manufacturing. Our customers span a wide array of industries including aerospace, defense, mobility, healthcare, pharma, biotech, clean tech, chemicals, energy, lifestyle, food production, and industrial equipment. Who we are looking for If you like a fast-paced environment where individuals can stretch and be challenged with a diverse set of projects, we offer a great deal of variety and empower our staff to take on as much responsibility as they can handle, offering a helping hand and experienced-based coaching and the support of a highly competent team. Our goal is to enable our employees to achieve their fullest potential, and through our association with Re:Build, provide avenues for personal and professional growth. The Regulatory Compliance Engineer is responsible to execute tasks as directed by Tekna’s Quality Management System in support of New Product Development and to ensure product safety, efficacy, reliability, and compliance to applicable regulatory requirements. What you’ll get to do Support the Core Leadership role on NPD projects. Delegate and provide mentorship of other compliance engineers assigned to your NPD projects. Support the Project Manager in the creation of a Design History File and ensure conformance/compliance with the Quality Management System. Initiate and maintain project plans that optimize product quality, project schedule, and project/product cost per the Master Project Plan. Conduct necessary research and establish product requirements. Lead risk management and coordinate the Risk Management Board review. Complete the Risk Management report required to achieve product launch. Support the Production Engineer, typically an Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME), with 6M analysis as part of developing the production process. Support the Procurement Specialist with supply chain management and PPAP. Support the Design Engineer and Production Engineer with Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMECA). Overwatch design for basic safety requirements ensuring compliance with applicable safety standards. Conduct Design for Manufacturing Analysis. Support the Production Engineer in completing Process Flow and Layout Diagrams. Design and develop verification processes/procedures for incoming, in-process, and final inspection in support of the established production process. Support the Production Engineer in completing the Process verification and validation matrix. Support the Production Engineer in completing process qualification (installation qualification, operational qualification, and performance qualification) achieving Cpk/Ppk objectives. Support the Design Engineer in setting up and qualifying in-house verification test methods and coordinating 3rd party certification testing in compliance with applicable standards/regulations. Support design transfer from NPD DHF to Operations PDM. What you bring to the team Bachelor of science degree in engineering preferred. 1 to 3 years’ experience in Regulatory Compliance or Advanced Quality and/or 5 or more years’ experience in new product development preferred. Proficiency in statistical analysis and control preferred. Read blueprints Computer literacy Problem solving skills Communication skills Organizational skills We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate Re:Build Manufacturing is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason. Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at [email protected] or you may call us at 617.909.6275. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Manager, Communications
item.description: Senior Manager, Communications Organization: CLEAR Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/27/2026 CLEAR is building THE secure identity company of the future. Our mission is to make experiences safer and easier—physically and digitally. With more than 43 million Members and a growing network of partners across the world, CLEAR’s secure identity platform is transforming the way people live, work, and travel. Whether it’s at the airport, stadium, or throughout your everyday life, CLEAR unlocks the magic of frictionless experiences. CLEAR is looking for a modern, highly strategic communications leader to drive earned media and bring our biggest partnerships, products, and company moments to market. You’ll build a proactive communications engine across CLEAR1, CLEAR+, and other key initiatives, developing the strategy while rolling up your sleeves to write, pitch, launch, and execute the work. What you’ll do: Own communications approach and execution for major CLEAR announcements, partnerships and launches across CLEAR1, CLEAR+, and other priority areas of the business Build and maintain strong relationships with national, business, technology, travel and trade media, as well as new media types, proactively developing stories and opportunities that drive awareness, consideration and understanding of CLEAR Turn business priorities into compelling narratives and integrated communications plans, identifying how earned media, executive visibility, partners, owned channels and other communications levers can work together to maximize impact Lead announcements from idea through execution, developing messaging, writing press materials, pitching media, preparing spokespeople, coordinating internal and external stakeholders and ensuring flawless launch execution Build the processes, rhythms and tools that make CLEAR’s communications function increasingly proactive and scalable, creating visibility into upcoming moments and identifying opportunities to tell a bigger, more connected CLEAR story How you’ll measure success: Quality, relevance and reach of earned media coverage across priority audiences and outlets Share of voice and positive sentiment around CLEAR’s priority products, partnerships and company narratives Awareness and consideration generated by communications campaigns and major announcements Growth in proactive storytelling opportunities and consistent execution against CLEAR’s communications calendar What you’re great at: 8+ years of communications, public relations or media relations experience, with a track record of personally developing and executing high-impact announcements and earned media strategies Exceptional media relations instincts and strong reporter relationships, with the ability to identify what makes a story compelling and earn attention in a rapidly changing media landscape Strategic storytelling—you can understand complex business objectives, find the story within them and build a communications approach that reaches the right audiences through the right channels Operating as both a builder and a doer—you’re energized by creating new processes and strategies, but equally comfortable writing the press release, pitching the story and owning the details required to get an announcement over the finish line Cross-functional leadership and excellent judgment—you can create clarity among senior leaders, business teams and external partners, manage multiple high-priority workstreams and move quickly in an environment where priorities evolve Experience and deep curiosity and excitement, about how AI can be used to accelerate communications, outcomes, and performance. How You’ll be Rewarded: At CLEAR, we help YOU move forward – because when you’re at your best, we’re at our best. You’ll work with talented team members motivated by our mission of making experiences safer and easier. Our offices are bright and energetic with an open concept and plenty of conference rooms and casual co-working spaces. We also offer catered lunches every day and have fully stocked kitchens. Outside of the office, we invest in your well-being and learning & development with stipends and reimbursement programs. We offer holistic total rewards, including comprehensive healthcare plans, family-building benefits (fertility and adoption/surrogacy support), flexible time off, annual wellness stipend, free OneMedical memberships for you and your dependents, a CLEAR Plus membership, and a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match. The base salary range for this role is $150,000.00 – $180,000.00, depending on levels of skills and experience. The base salary range represents the low and high end of CLEAR’s salary range for this position. Salaries will vary depending on various factors which include, but are not limited to location, education, skills, experience and performance. The range listed is just one component of CLEAR’s total compensation package for employees and other rewards may include annual bonuses, commission, Restricted Stock Units. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. CLEAR provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities or protected needs. Please let us know if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job or perform your job. Examples of reasonable accommodation include, but are not limited to, time off, extra breaks, making a change to the application process or work procedures, policy exceptions, providing documents in an alternative format, live captioning or using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment. We are committed to a transparent and secure hiring process. All communications related to this role will come directly from a CLEAR employee through valid CLEAR channels (e.g., a valid @clearme.com email address or verified CLEAR LinkedIn profile). item.title: Compliance Manager
item.description: Compliance Manager Organization: Anyscale Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 09/27/2026 At Anyscale, we’re on a mission to democratize distributed computing and make it accessible to software developers of all skill levels. We’re commercializing Ray, a popular open-source project that’s creating an ecosystem of libraries for scalable machine learning. Companies like OpenAI, Uber, Spotify, Instacart, Cruise, and many more, have Ray in their tech stacks to accelerate the progress of AI applications out into the real world. With Anyscale, we’re building the best place to run Ray, so that any developer or data scientist can scale an ML application from their laptop to the cluster without needing to be a distributed systems expert. Proud to be backed by Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and Addition with $250+ million raised to date. About the Role Anyscale’s security and compliance needs are growing as we work with larger and more demanding customers. Compliance is increasingly a customer-facing, contractual function rather than an internal exercise, and we are looking for someone to own it. This role owns that function end to end: our audits, our evidence base, our risk register, and the security diligence that customers put us through before and during a contract. You will work directly with the Head of Security and across engineering, IT, legal, and sales. This is a program-ownership role with the autonomy and accountability that implies. You will not have a senior compliance function above you to defer to; you are that function. In your first year, success looks like a complete and defensible evidence base with clean audit outcomes, a repeatable way to answer customer security diligence, and a risk register that leadership actually uses. What You’ll Do Own our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 programs, and future frameworks as we take them on, including scope, evidence, control operation, and the relationship with our external auditors. Own and complete the control evidence base in our compliance automation platform, moving controls from partially substantiated to audit-ready and keeping them there. Lead security diligence for enterprise and regulated customers: security questionnaires, audit responses, right-to-audit requests, and the recurring reporting these customers require. Own the risk register and mature risk management from a security-team activity into a recorded, enterprise-aligned program. Coordinate the compliance obligations that come with customer contracts, including data protection, breach-notification timelines, and vendor and subprocessor assessments, in partnership with legal. Assess and stand up new certifications as the customer pipeline requires them. Partner with engineering and IT to make evidence collection a byproduct of how systems already run, rather than a manual scramble before each audit. What You’ll Bring 7+ years in governance, risk, and compliance, ideally including time at a high-growth startup. Demonstrated ownership of SOC 2 and ISO 27001 programs, including running audits end to end with external auditors. Experience fronting security diligence for enterprise or regulated customers. You have sat across from a customer’s auditors or security reviewers and held your own. Working fluency with compliance automation platforms (such as Vanta or equivalent) and with turning tooling into genuinely audit-ready evidence, not just dashboards. A strong grasp of security controls and how they operate in a cloud and SaaS environment, enough to work credibly with engineers rather than only collecting their attestations. The judgment and communication to run a program independently, coordinate across functions, and be trusted as the single owner of compliance. Nice to Have Experience with regulated-customer contractual security obligations: data protection agreements, breach notification, and right-to-audit provisions. Exposure to newer or higher-bar frameworks (for example FedRAMP) and a sense of what standing them up would take. Experience building a compliance function or team, since this role can grow into one as the company scales. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure or AI or ML platforms. Why Anyscale We’re on a mission to make scalable computing effortless. Ray is the AI Compute Engine at the center of some of the world’s most powerful AI platforms Our tech is in production at companies like OpenAI, Uber, Spotify, Instacart, and Cruise We’re backed by Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and Addition, with $250M+ raised to date Recent partnerships with Azure, CoreWeave, and Google Cloud are putting AI-native compute directly into enterprise environments Competitive salary and equity, plus health/dental/vision coverage (many plans up to 99% employer-covered) We offer flexible time off, paid parental leave, and mental health support Anyscale Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Candidates are evaluated without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, disability, national origin, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal or state law. Anyscale Inc. is an E-Verify company and you may review the Notice of E-Verify Participation and the Right to Work posters in English and Spanish Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, B2B & Corporate Communications
item.description: Director, B2B & Corporate Communications Organization: OpenTable Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/27/2026 With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture. Restaurants are undergoing a tech revolution — and OpenTable is at the center of it. We are seeking a strategically minded Director of B2B & Corporate Communications to own the global narrative that drives our presence and credibility within the hospitality industry. Reporting to the Head of Global Communications, you will serve as a high-impact leadership figure responsible for positioning the company as a strategic technology and data partner. In this role, you will ensure that every touchpoint with restaurant customers, technology partners, and the broader business community strengthens our reputation as an industry leader. Your focus will be on building trust as an ultimate differentiator and expanding our corporate narrative globally. Responsibilities Develop and execute comprehensive B2B communication strategies to strengthen relationships with restaurant customers, prospects, partners, and industry influencers — working hand-in-hand with marketing and go-to-market teams to make every campaign land harder. Own communications for global partnerships, integrations, and emerging business units, orchestrating co-announcements and shared storylines with major technology platforms. Lead external storytelling around product innovation, AI developments, and industry milestones to advocate for restaurant success and solidify OpenTable’s global market presence. Get OpenTable’s story in front of the people who matter — pitching, shaping, and landing coverage across mainstream and emerging media, and turning reactive moments into opportunities to lead the conversation. Manage the executive bench in partnership with brand communications by crafting talking points, speeches, bylines, and preparing leadership for high-profile industry appearances. Support crisis navigation, operational resiliency, and data policy defenses to protect and enhance OpenTable’s corporate reputation. Build the backbone that makes it all work — approval workflows, escalation paths, messaging guardrails, and KPI reporting that ties communications directly to business impact. Minimum Qualifications 10+ years of experience in B2B public relations or corporate communications within the technology or hospitality sectors. Experience managing public relations and communications strategy on a global scale. Proven track record managing high-stakes issues, policy responses, and competitive positioning. Experience advising executive leadership on complex communications and reputational matters. Based in New York City or the Tri-State area, willing to work in a hybrid capacity from the NYC or Norwalk, CT office. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing co-marketing or joint-communication strategies with global technology platforms and enterprise partners. Demonstrated ability to utilize data insights and performance metrics to shape corporate messaging and inform strategic business decisions. Prior experience collaborating across brand, product, and legal teams within a global matrixed organization or parent company environment. Strong background in managing communication frameworks for emerging business units or rapidly scaling technology solutions. Benefits and Perks Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year Focus on mental health and well-being: Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth Company-paid subscription to Headspace Annual company-wide week off a year – the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!) Paid parental leave Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday Paid volunteer time Focus on your career growth: Development Dollars Leadership development Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings Travel Discounts Employee Resource Groups Free lunch 5 days per week Beautiful office in the Empire State Building with lots of building amenities, such as a gym, multi-purpose room, in-building Starbucks, and more. The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility. There are a variety of factors that go into determining a salary range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought/required. The range for this United States based role is $185,000 – $200,000. We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus and equity grant. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Creative Director, Brand & Content Organization: Smartly Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 09/27/2026 Smartly is looking for a Creative Director to join our Brand & Content team and help shape how our brand comes to life across campaigns, content, events, digital experiences, and marketing initiatives. Reporting to the SVP of Brand & Content, this role combines creative leadership, people management, and conceptual thinking to create work that is distinctive, effective, and aligned with our business goals. You’ll lead a team of designers, develop strong creative concepts, and partner across the business to bring Smartly’s story to life. This role is ideal for someone who began their career in design, has evolved into a conceptual art director, and enjoys helping creative teams produce their best work. What You Will Do Lead, coach, and develop a team of designers, creating an environment where people can do their best work and grow their careers Develop creative concepts and campaigns that strengthen Smartly’s brand and connect with target audiences Provide clear creative direction and feedback throughout the creative process, from brief through final execution Partner with Brand, Content, Product Marketing, Communications, and other stakeholders to translate business objectives into compelling creative solutions Elevate the quality, consistency, and effectiveness of Smartly’s visual identity across all channels and touchpoints Review and approve creative work, ensuring it meets strategic objectives, brand standards, and quality expectations Help establish and refine creative processes, workflows, and ways of working that enable the team to scale its impact Stay current on design, advertising, and cultural trends, bringing fresh thinking and new approaches to the team’s work What We Are Looking For Experience leading and developing creative teams, including direct people management responsibilities Strong background in graphic design, brand design, visual communication, or a related creative discipline Experience as a conceptual Art Director, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong campaign thinking and creative problem-solving Ability to translate strategy, messaging, and business goals into engaging creative concepts and visual storytelling Strong design craft and a deep understanding of typography, layout, visual systems, and brand identity Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders and navigating feedback from multiple audiences Excellent communication, presentation, and collaboration skills Ability to balance creative excellence with practical business outcomes Experience working with consumer-facing brands or B2C marketing is preferred, but not required Experience working in technology, SaaS, or high-growth environments is a plus What We Offer You Five weeks paid time off (PTO), 11 company paid holidays, unlimited sick days Generous healthcare packages & mental health benefits 401K plus matching & equity grants for all new Smartlies Wellness benefit & learning reimbursement opportunities Volunteer time off days & company donation matching opportunities And so much more… The base pay range for this position is as mentioned below per year, plus an annual performance bonus. We take into consideration an individual’s background, expertise, and experience in determining final salary. In addition to annual salary, Smartly’s total rewards provide employees with stock options, medical/dental/vision insurances, retirement savings benefits, parental leave, 5 weeks vacation, unlimited sick days, life insurance, and disability benefits. This information is provided in accordance with applicable law. Base pay information is based on market location. Salary in USD: 120,000-180,000 Curious what it’s like to work at Smartly? Visit our Careers page to see how we grow, collaborate, and make impact together. About Smartly Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers. Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. Our end-to-end technology, unmatched access to media platforms and exceptional customer service help Fortune 500 brands to reach and engage consumers and learn what performs best.Smartly is a multinational and diverse team of 750+ Smartlies from 60+ nationalities, working in 13 countries. Together, we want to create and maintain an inclusive environment where everyone feels respected and heard. Our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion approach is at the heart of it. item.title: Content Lead
item.description: Content Lead Organization: Sage Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/27/2026 The first baby boomers turn 80 this year. Over the next decade, the population most likely to need daily care will grow faster than the buildings, the staff, or the systems available to serve it. Sage is the care intelligence platform for senior living and skilled nursing. We connect the hardware senior care runs on, including nurse call, fall management, and wander management, with software caregivers actually use. That consistent use is what produces reliable data, and reliable data is what gives operators a true picture of how their communities are running. Sage is a collaborative team of ambitious, multi-disciplinary entrepreneurs on a mission to reinvent senior care with a modern operating system for caregivers. Millions of people depend on this care getting better, and we move with the urgency that deserves. About this Role As a Content Lead, you will define and own Sage’s content strategy, then execute against it through compelling, narrative driven storytelling that drives brand awareness, educates our audiences, and fuels growth. This is a hands-on role that owns content end to end, from strategy and planning through writing, editing, distribution, and measuring content performance. You will also lead our Social Media Manager, ensuring our social channels consistently reflect Sage’s brand, voice, and content strategy while maximizing audience engagement. Success in this role depends on three things above all: being strategic enough to define what content should exist and why before determining how to execute it, being a strong communicator who can translate complex healthcare and technology topics into content that is clear and engaging, and being comfortable operating in ambiguity within a fast paced, mission driven environment where you are building process as you go. Responsibilities Develop and maintain our overarching content strategy across audiences and formats (web, email, blog, social, long-form, and more). Own content calendars and campaign planning in collaboration with marketing, product, and GTM teams. Define and execute Sage’s SEO and generative engine optimization (GEO) strategy to increase discoverability across search engines and AI-powered platforms. Create and manage high-quality editorial content—from thought leadership to case studies, newsletters to landing pages. Collaborate cross-functionally to align content with business goals, voice, and positioning. Measure content performance, uncover audience insights, and continuously optimize content strategy based on data. Lead and mentor the Social Media Manager, setting the strategy for Sage’s social channels and ensuring content is aligned with our brand, voice, and business objectives. Uphold and evolve Sage’s brand voice while managing freelance writers, agencies, and other creative partners as needed. Minimum Qualifications 4-6+ years of experience in content strategy, brand storytelling, or editorial leadership. Demonstrated ability to craft thoughtful, strategic content across digital channels. Strong writing and editing skills, with a portfolio that shows both creativity and clarity. Experience working in fast-growing, cross-functional teams—particularly in mission-driven or healthcare-related companies. Comfort working in ambiguity, rolling up your sleeves, and managing content end-to-end. Preferred Qualifications Preference for B2B experience. Open to D2C, but need to have reported into the Marketing function Background in brand development or content design, or experience in virtual healthcare, wellness, or adjacent sectors. Benefits and Pay Our headquarters are located near New York City’s Union Square. We believe in cross team collaboration. We think good ideas can come from anyone, and we’ve designed our processes to encourage participation from all. While we take our mission seriously, we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We like to host offsites, outings, and team meals where we can connect as people, not just as colleagues. We offer office lunch and a fully stocked snack bar. While we are an in office culture, we allow up to 2 remote days per week. Our benefits package for employees includes competitive base compensation along with stock options. The expected annual salary range for this role is $155,000-195,000 USD, depending upon the job level, which will depend on your level of expertise, your experience, and your qualifications. We also provide fully-paid health and dental insurance coverage for all of our employees, along with other health benefits including vision insurance, membership to premium primary and urgent care, and online medical health providers. We also have a take as you need time off policy, in addition to 7 paid holidays and a company wide winter break during the holidays. EEO Statement Sage is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Sage makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Content Marketing Manager
item.description: Senior Content Marketing Manager Organization: Instrumentl Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/27/2026 Hello, we’re Instrumentl. 👋 Nonprofits do some of the most important work in the world, and most of them are still managing grants in spreadsheets. We’re fixing that. Instrumentl is a profitable, hypergrowth, YC-backed SaaS platform building the operating system for grant-funded organizations. More than 5,500 nonprofits use Instrumentl to discover, track, and win grant funding, from local community organizations to the San Diego Zoo and the University of Alaska. Collectively they’ve moved over $1 billion through our platform. We’re growing quickly, customers love us (check out our G2 reviews!), and we’re hiring people who want to build something that matters. About the role: We’re hiring a Senior Content Marketing Manager, reporting to the Head of Growth Marketing, to build and run the content engine that turns nonprofit awareness into pipeline. You’ll help tell our category story as Instrumentl evolves from a grant discovery tool into the operating system for grant-funded organizations, with writing that is versatile across both short and long form content, strategically designed across the full demand funnel and connects emotionally, moving people to act. This is a performance role, too: you’re passionate about measuring outcomes and using data to keep improving it. What you’ll do: Versatile, conversion-first content Write compelling content across formats — long-form thought leadership, benchmark reports, one-pagers, ads, social posts & website content Have a POV on what types of messaging works best and adjust for each channel including social/digital/SEM/AEO Tell our strategic category story — why Instrumentl is becoming the operating system for grant-funded organizations, and why that matters to the people using it Full-funnel strategy & execution Map content to funnel stage — awareness, consideration, decision — and build sequences that move nonprofits from first touch to customer Build and manage a content calendar coordinating campaigns in partnership with the broader marketing team Help executives and other internal thought leaders build a consistent voice and posting cadence on social — developing themes, calendar, and content that reflects each person’s POV, not just amplifying the company page. Data-driven performance marketing Understand our audience deeply — who they are, what they do and how we can meet their needs Track what’s working and what isn’t, and use those learnings to optimize SEO and AEO: Stay ahead of how generative and agentic search is changing how nonprofits find and evaluate solutions, and create content that moves the needle. What we’re looking for Required 6+ years of experience in content marketing, performance marketing, or content strategy Experience owning content across the full funnel, from top-of-funnel editorial to bottom-of-funnel conversion assets like landing pages and ad copy Strong command of SEM and SEO fundamentals, plus working knowledge of AEO/GEO and agentic search A performance mindset: comfortable with data and quick to turn results into sharper work Strong writer with sharp editorial judgment and an instinct for the emotional and practical reasons an audience acts Ability to quickly build subject matter expertise in a complex domain through research and SME interviews Nice to Have Experience with nonprofit, social impact, or mission-driven organizations Background in grants, fundraising, or nonprofit operations Hands-on experience running or optimizing paid digital advertising Experience managing freelancers and agency relationships Compensation & Benefits For US-based candidates, the target salary range for this role is $125,000 – $150,000 USD, plus equity. Final compensation is determined based on experience, skillset, scope of responsibility, interview performance, and geographic location. We’re committed to paying competitively and equitably. Benefits 100% covered health, dental, and vision insurance for employees (50% for dependents) Generous PTO, including parental leave 401(k) Company laptop and home-office stipend Bi-annual company retreats Instrumentl is evolving rapidly. You’ll always have new challenges and opportunities to grow here. Instrumentl is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, or any other legally protected status. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: AV Compliance Lead, Fleet & Operator Compliance
item.description: AV Compliance Lead, Fleet & Operator Compliance Organization: Waymo Location: Mountain View, CA Date Posted: 09/27/2026 Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world’s most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World’s Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. As part of Waymo’s Legal team, you will work on the exciting legal issues surrounding our transformational autonomous driving technology and help drive our business lines forward from technology ideation through scaled commercial deployment. We partner with our public policy, safety, security and privacy experts to define transportation policy for the autonomous driving world to come, advising on regulatory changes that support and protect our users around the world. We collaborate with our engineering, product, strategy and operations teams to develop and protect our intellectual property portfolio and drive our corporate and commercial transactions. We ensure compliance with an increasingly complex and dynamic range of global regulations. And we anticipate, mitigate, and litigate high-profile and precedent-setting legal matters. This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to the Head of AV Compliance. You will: Own and execute a comprehensive strategy and implementation plan for Waymo vehicle and operator compliance activities to enable the company’s rapid global scaling Build and maintain relationships with regulators, government agencies, and vendors Provide close, active oversight of fleet and operator compliance vendors Manage the team’s execution of vehicle and driver compliance activities such as permitting, registration, compliance materials shipment and management, and renewals Provide timely reporting to executives on critical compliance activities, vehicle status, risks, and blockers Scale Waymo’s fleet and operator compliance program through new processes and automation, including through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Design and implement comprehensive KPI frameworks and reporting structures to monitor, assess, and drive improvements in team and vendor performance. Establish documentation standards for compliance processes and lead communication strategies for vendors and executive stakeholders. Drive cross-functional collaboration with internal software development teams to build consistent, scalable technical solutions for evolving regulatory requirements. You have: At least 10-12 years of experience in regulatory compliance and operational roles, preferably within a safety-focused or transportation organization. Proven track record of people management and active management of complex vendor engagements or projects, including holding partners accountable to rigorous compliance and performance metrics. Top-notch, strategic program management skills, with high responsiveness, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple workstreams in parallel. Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to interact with diverse audiences from regulators to engineers to executives. Advanced “gap-finding” and risk-assessment abilities, with experience proactively mitigating issues before they impact operations. High-level organizational and project management skills, with a demonstrated ability to lead initiatives from concept to completion. Data and technology-driven mindset, with the ability to transform manual, repetitive tasks into sophisticated, automated workflows at scale. We prefer: Strong technical aptitude with the ability to influence the development of proprietary software tools. Demonstrated resilience and leadership in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, with a focus on problem-solving. High EQ and mentorship mindset, with a history of scaling systems efficiently within a team. Deep expertise in transportation industry regulations, specifically involving autonomous vehicle technology and policy. Experience “owning the room” when conceptualizing and operationalizing new processes that close critical gaps in existing operational flows. Experience scaling a compliance program during a period of significant company growth or international expansion. Ability to speak multiple languages. Travel Requirements: This individual will be required to travel to build relationships with vendors and local regulators, potentially both domestically and internationally. Travel is expected to be 10-15% of the year with a maximum of 20%. The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. item.title: Ecosystem Marketing Lead
item.description: Ecosystem Marketing Lead Organization: Lattice Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/27/2026 This role owns how Lattice turns its partner and integration ecosystem into a GTM advantage. It goes beyond traditional HR partnerships: the goal is to build relationships and joint go-to-market motions with the broader AI and work-tech ecosystem, including future-of-work platforms like OpenAI, Anthropic, Slack, and other tools Lattice integrates with, so Lattice reaches managers and functional leaders, not just HR buyers. What You Will Do Own the partner-facing GTM strategy and packaging for Lattice’s ecosystem partnerships and integrations. Partner closely with Product and Integrations teams on what Lattice builds, while owning how partner-enabled capabilities are positioned and brought to market. Develop joint launches, campaigns, events, content, customer stories, and executive programs with strategic partners. Translate partner-enabled capabilities into clear customer value, use cases, messaging, and differentiated positioning. Build repeatable partner marketing motions across co-marketing, field activation, account opportunities, customer advocacy, and sales enablement. Work with Sales and Field Marketing to activate partners through events, regional programs, account-based opportunities, and customer-facing moments. Identify and prioritize partners that can create distribution, credibility, pipeline, and category leadership, in addition to integration value. Expand Lattice’s reach into managers, functional leaders, and broader business stakeholders through strategic ecosystem programs. Own partner-facing launch timing, marketplace distribution opportunities, and Lattice’s presence in relevant third-party marketplaces. Represent Lattice at strategic partner events, virtually and in person, and lead event-based commercial activation alongside partners. Educate partners on Lattice’s integration capabilities, limitations, and dependencies in collaboration with Product Marketing, Product, and Engineering. Establish clear goals and measurement for partner marketing programs, using results to improve future investments and partner plans. What You Will Bring to the Table 8+ years of experience in partner marketing, ecosystem marketing, alliances, field marketing, or a related B2B SaaS go-to-market role. Experience developing and executing joint go-to-market programs with technology partners, including campaigns, events, content, launches, and sales activation. Ability to translate technical products, integrations, and platform capabilities into relevant customer stories and commercial programs. Experience partnering effectively with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, Sales, and Field Marketing teams. A track record of managing multiple cross-functional and external stakeholder relationships, setting priorities, and driving programs from concept through execution. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority. A practical, metrics-oriented approach to evaluating program performance, partner value, and future investment. Comfort representing Lattice with senior partner contacts and in external settings. Experience in HR technology, AI, or adjacent work-tech ecosystems is a plus. What success looks like Success in this role will be measured through the following outcomes: Partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline is measured consistently with Commercial Partnerships and shows meaningful contribution. Strategic partners have clear joint GTM plans and a regular cadence of high-quality launches, campaigns, and field activations. Lattice has a more visible, accurate presence in relevant partner marketplaces and third-party ecosystem channels. Partner commercial teams understand Lattice’s capabilities and can effectively bring joint value to customers. Lattice expands its reach with managers, functional leaders, and broader business stakeholders, measured through audience and engagement indicators. Lattice’s position in the AI-native workplace ecosystem is strengthened through partner reach, visibility, and strategic opportunities. The estimated annual cash salary for this role is $140,000 – $198,000. This position is also eligible for incentive stock options, subject to the terms of Lattice’s applicable plans. Benefits: The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: Medical insurance; Dental insurance; Vision insurance; Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance; Emergency Weather Support; Wellness Apps; Paid Parental Leave, Paid Time off inclusive of holidays and sick time; Commuter & Parking Accounts; 401(k) retirement plan; Financial Planning; Learning & Development Budget *Note on Pay Transparency: Lattice provides an estimate of the compensation for roles that may be hired as required by state regulations. Compensation may vary based on (a) location, as Lattice factors in specific location when benchmarking compensation for most roles; (b) individual candidate skills and qualifications; and (c) individual candidate experience. Additionally, Lattice leverages current market data to determine compensation, so posted compensation figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. Lattice reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law. About Lattice Lattice is on a mission to build cultures where employees and their companies thrive. In an age where employees have more choices than ever before, businesses that put employees first are winning 🏅– and Lattice is building the tools to empower those people-centric companies. Lattice is a people success platform that offers performance reviews, employee engagement surveys, real-time feedback, weekly check-ins, goal setting, and career planning in a way that allows companies to focus on employee development, growth, and engagement – yielding stronger employee retention, performance, and impact to the bottom line 📈. Since launching in 2016, we have grown to over 5,000+ customers globally, including brands like Loom, Robinhood, and Gusto. Lattice is committed to equal treatment and opportunity in all aspects of recruitment, selection, and employment without regard to gender, race, religion, national origin, ethnicity, disability, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other category protected under the law. Lattice is an equal opportunity employer; committed to a community of inclusion, and an environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. By clicking the “ Submit Application ” button, you consent to Lattice processing your personal information for the purpose of assessing your candidacy for this position in accordance with Lattice’s Job Applicant Privacy Policy. item.title: Legal Operations & Compliance Lead
item.description: Legal Operations & Compliance Lead Organization: TwelveLabs Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/27/2026 Who we are Video is 90% of the world’s data. Most of it is invisible to machines. TwelveLabs builds the intelligence layer to change that. Our multimodal AI models understand video the way humans do — across sight, sound, and motion — and power production-scale AI workloads across media, entertainment, sports, security, and government. We have raised more than $210 million from NEA, Radical Ventures, Amazon, NVIDIA, Snowflake, Databricks, Index Ventures, NAVER Ventures, Korea Investment Partners, Quadrille Capital, Red Bull Ventures, and AI pioneers including Fei-Fei Li, Silvio Savarese, and Alexandr Wang. We are a global company, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Seoul, New York, and London, and employees around the world. We believe the differences in our cultural, educational, and life experiences make our products stronger. Building technology that understands the world in all its complexity requires people who see it from every angle. We are looking for individuals who are driven by hard problems and want their work to matter. Come build it with us! About the Role Twelve Labs is hiring a Legal Operations & Compliance Manager to build and run the operational backbone of our Legal function. You’ll own the systems, processes, and records that let a small Legal team support a fast-growing global business, spanning contract operations, corporate governance administration, outside-counsel management, IP portfolio coordination, compliance-program administration, and legal technology. Candidates must be able to travel up to 10% of the time annually to attend conferences, off-site meetings, and other business-related events as required by the role. This role may require participation in on-site interviews and/or completion of in-person onboarding processes. In this role, you will Own Legal intake, triage, matter tracking, workflow administration, and status reporting. Identify opportunities to replace repetitive manual work with standardized workflows, self-service tools, or automation. Serve as the operational owner of the existing CLM and lead requirements gathering for future legal technology. Maintain corporate records, governance calendars, and support board/committee meetings, filings, and entity administration. Maintain a consolidated compliance calendar covering policies, training, audits, certifications, filings, assessments, and recurring reviews. Coordinate compliance projects across Legal, Security, Engineering, Product, Finance, People, and other operational owners. Support the legal and administrative components of SOC 2, CMMC, privacy, accessibility, AI governance, and similar initiatives. Maintain policy inventories, review cycles, approval records, version histories, and employee acknowledgments. Maintain Legal playbooks, standard operating procedures, decision trees, training materials, precedents, and internal guidance. Coordinate cross-functional Legal projects and ensure that decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-up actions are documented. Serve as a responsive point of contact for questions regarding Legal processes, intake, contract status, signatures, records, and documentation. Train employees on Legal systems and workflows. You may be a good fit if you have 5+ years in legal operations, senior paralegal, corporate governance, contract operations, or compliance operations, ideally in-house at a tech/software/AI company. A track record of designing and owning processes, not just administering existing ones. Experience with a CLM or matter-management system, contract repositories/metadata/renewals, and corporate governance recordkeeping. Experience tracking outside-counsel budgets, invoices, or matter data. Strong project management across functions, high attention to detail, and good judgment on when to escalate to an attorney. Comfort with confidential and privileged information, and the ability to work autonomously while keeping Legal leadership informed. Preferred Qualifications Paralegal certificate, project management credential, or legal-ops certification. Experience with SpotDraft, Ironclad, DocuSign, HubSpot, Carta, or similar applications. Experience supporting privacy, security, AI, or accessibility compliance programs (SOC 2, CMMC, GDPR). Experience supporting an international business or a venture-backed Series B/C company. Benefits and Perks 🤝 An open and inclusive culture and work environment 🚀 Work closely with a collaborative, mission-driven team on cutting-edge AI technology 🏥 Full health, dental, and vision benefits 🌴 Extremely flexible PTO and parental leave policy. Office closed the week of Christmas and New Years 💪 Monthly wellness stipend 📚 Annual Learning & Development stipend to invest in your growth 💼 Global offices in San Francisco and Seoul, and coworking office memberships for remote team members 🛂 VISA support where applicable 🚆 Transportation stipend (SF onsite only) 🍲 Daily lunch & dinner provided (SF onsite only) Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Global Public Policy
item.description: Global Public Policy Organization: Thinking Machines Location: San Francisco, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 About Thinking Machines The mission of Thinking Machines is to build AI that extends human will and judgment. We are training frontier models with Inkling, developing Tinker to let people make models their own, and crafting interfaces that broaden human-AI communication. We believe the future worth building is human, and we’re hiring people who want to build it. About the Role We’re looking for a founding policy leader to build and lead Thinking Machines’ global public policy function. You’ll be the company’s principal policy strategist and advocate across a wide range of policy issues that shape how Thinking Machines can build and deploy frontier AI responsibly.These could span U.S. federal and state policy, the EU AI Act, international regulatory regimes, export control and national security frameworks. You’ll work with leadership to set the company’s substantive policy positions, build and lead the team that executes on them, and represent Thinking Machines directly with legislators, regulators, and industry counterparts. This is a build role that will take ownership of it end-to-end: hiring and developing a team while scaling the company’s engagement across every jurisdiction where policy affects its ability to operate. What You’ll Do Set and drive Thinking Machines’ global public policy strategy, from U.S. federal legislation and executive action to EU AI Act implementation and policy developments in other key jurisdictions. Build and lead the public policy team, including hiring, structuring the function, and establishing how it partners with Research, Product, Safety, Legal, Communications, and the executive team. Represent Thinking Machines directly with legislators, regulators, and agency staff, and manage relationships with outside counsel, lobbyists, and advocacy partners. Lead the company’s engagement on the issues most material to its business: frontier model legislation, safety and disclosure frameworks, open-weight model policy, and societal impact, translating fast-moving developments into clear positions and recommendations for leadership. Build and manage coalition relationships with peer labs, industry groups, and trade associations, and represent Thinking Machines in relevant multi-stakeholder forums. Develop the internal infrastructure for policy decision-making, including state-of-play tracking, position papers, and clear escalation paths, so policy considerations are built into product and research decisions early. Skills and Qualifications Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience in technology policy, government relations, or a related field with a demonstrated track record of shaping policy outcomes on complex technology policy issues, including significant experience in U.S. federal policy and direct engagement with legislators or regulators. Experience building and leading a policy or government affairs function, including hiring and managing a team. Working knowledge of the US state, federal, and international regulatory landscape for AI, including the EU AI Act, and experience engaging on policy issues across multiple jurisdictions. Excellent judgment translating complex, fast-moving regulatory developments into clear, actionable recommendations for executive leadership. Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to represent the company credibly with government officials, industry counterparts, and internal stakeholders alike. Preferred qualifications—we encourage you to apply if you meet some but not all of these: Experience in a frontier AI company, national security, or export control policy context, with familiarity with issues like deemed exports, compute governance, or model release policy. Prior government, Hill, or agency experience (e.g., Congress, Commerce/BIS, OSTP, or similar). Experience building coalitions with peer companies and trade associations on emerging technology policy issues. Familiarity with the technical fundamentals of frontier AI development (training, fine-tuning, model release processes) sufficient to engage credibly with research and engineering teams. Logistics Location: This role is based in Washington, D.C. with regular travel to San Francisco, CA and other jurisdictions as needed. Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $300,000-360,000 USD. Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can’t guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you’re the right fit, we’re committed to working through the visa process together. Benefits: Thinking Machines offers generous health, dental, and vision benefits, unlimited PTO, paid parental leave, and relocation support as needed. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll tell the story of American reindustrialization at giga scale to the world. What you’ll do Own Solx’s global narrative and voice — building the story of a next-generation, AI-driven manufacturing company reshoring one of the world’s most strategic supply chains. Lead corporate communications strategy and execution across product, executive, and employee communications. Run media relations end to end — building relationships with journalists and landing earned media in top-tier business, energy, technology, and trade press. Own social media strategy and the company’s owned channels. Lead executive communications and thought leadership for the CEO and leadership team. Manage analyst relations and shape how the industry understands Solx. Build and scale internal and employee communications as the company grows. Own issues and crisis communications, and protect and strengthen the brand. Partner closely with leadership on messaging, positioning, launches, and milestones. Exceptional writer and storyteller who can translate complex industrial and technical work into a clear, compelling narrative. Depth across executive communications, analyst relations, social strategy, and internal comms. Comfortable operating with autonomy in a fast-moving, build-focused environment, reporting directly to the CEO. Spanish a plus. Hybrid remote. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Organization: Hologic Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Hologic helps women around the world live healthier lives. We develop life-changing medical technologies that deliver exceptional results essential to effectively detect, diagnose and treat health conditions that affect women globally. We are propelled by the passion and courage of our employees to make a difference and innovate in all we do. We create opportunities for those who want to make a meaningful difference in improving health, particularly for women. Our commitment extends beyond our products. We are a catalyst for change in the world. We champion women’s health globally, working in partnership with others to raise awareness and inspire policy and action to break down barriers that affect women disproportionately and prevent them from receiving the care they need and deserve. We know women face unique health challenges at every stage of life, and we work tirelessly to improve the health and lives of all women, everywhere, every day. At Hologic, women’s health is more than a business, it is our purpose. Position Overview This is a hybrid role based in our Washington DC office. Hologic is seeking a Director of Government Affairs to serve as a key leader within the company’s Government Affairs Department. Reporting to the Senior Director of Government Affairs, the ideal candidate will be a strategic professional with deep healthcare policy expertise, have a strong mission-driven mindset, and be skilled in navigating and shaping the legislative and regulatory landscape. The successful candidate will be highly visible internally and externally and will make meaningful contributions to Hologic’s partnership development, federal lobbying, and advocacy strategies, with lobbying as a key function of the role in driving and advancing Hologic’s overall policy priorities. Position Duties and Responsibilities Promote Hologic as a worldwide leader in women’s health in relevant policy, patient advocacy, and healthcare circles. Manage strategies and activities related to federal legislation, public programs, and executive branch affairs. Develop and maintain relationships with relevant legislative and executive branch officials, patient and disease groups, industry trade associations, and industry stakeholders in support of Hologic public policy priorities. Coordinate internally with cross-functional teams including market access, commercial, legal, and regulatory to identify opportunities to elevate Hologic and advance company priorities. Contribute to the formation and execution of Hologic policy agenda, stakeholder outreach and development and advocacy strategies. Represent Hologic in trade associations, coalitions, patient advocacy organizations, and industry groups to advance company priorities and help shape coordinated Congressional and state advocacy efforts. Direct contract lobbyists in support of Hologic’s advocacy objectives. Essential Qualifications 8 -10 years of relevant U.S. Congressional and/or executive branch agency experience or as a government affairs professional in a healthcare company, trade association or consultancy. A passion for women’s health and commitment to reducing barriers to access to care. Experience with Congressional Committees and federal agencies with jurisdiction over healthcare. Strong connections across Republican Congressional offices, committees, the Administration, and affiliated organizations. Exhibits a high degree of initiative and self-direction, with proven effectiveness in both independent and team-based settings. Proven track record advancing strategic end-to-end advocacy campaigns, working collaboratively with multiple internal and external stakeholders, and managing political risk. Excels in written and verbal communication, with a crisp, clear style that effectively influences senior executives while building authentic connections with stakeholders at all levels. Education Bachelor’s degree, Masters preferred The annualized base salary range for this role is $163,400- $250,600 and is bonus eligible. Final compensation packages will ultimately depend on factors including relevant experience, skillset, knowledge, geography, education, business needs and market demand. Agency And Third-Party Recruiter Notice Agencies that submit a resume to Hologic must have a current executed Hologic Agency Agreement executed by a member of the Human Resource Department. In addition, Agencies may only submit candidates to positions for which they have been invited to do so by a Hologic Recruiter. All resumes must be sent to the Hologic Recruiter under these terms or they will not be considered. Hologic’s employees are subject to third-party COVID-19 vaccination requirements, including from customers and governmental entities. Hologic is an equal opportunity employer and consistent with federal, state, and local requirements, will consider requests for reasonable accommodation based on disability or sincerely-held religious beliefs where it is able to do so without undue hardship to the company. Hologic, Inc. is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer inclusive of disability and veterans. #LI-MP3 Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
