item.title: Director, Government Relations
item.description: Director, Government Relations Organization: Vantor Location: Herndon, VA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Vantor is forging the new frontier of spatial intelligence, helping decision makers and operators navigate what’s happening now and shape what’s coming next. Vantor is a place for problem solvers, changemakers, and go-getters—where people are working together to help our customers see the world differently, and in doing so, be seen differently. Come be part of a mission, not just a job, where you can: Shape your own future, build the next big thing, and change the world. To be eligible for this position, you must be a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, Asylee, or Refugee. Export Control/ITAR: Certain roles may be subject to U.S. export control laws, requiring U.S. person status as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). Please review the job details below. Vantor is currently seeking a Director of Government Relations who will support our overall U.S. government engagement strategy, reporting to the Vice President of Government Relations. The position is based in Herndon, VA but allows for some telecommuting throughout the week based upon mission requirements. Current TS/SCI clearance is preferred. Ability to obtain clearance is required. The Government Relations Director works as part of the Government Relations team to develop and execute federal advocacy activities in support of Vantor policy, regulatory, legislative, and budget objectives. This position will represent the Company with both the legislative and executive branch representatives, coordinating content and messaging with industry leads. Further, the position will coordinate Vantor engagement with certain industry groups and associations, and support senior-level engagements in a wide variety of settings in support of strategic messaging objectives. The Government Relations Director must have extensive knowledge of the legislative process, the ability to build relationships, and the ability to define and articulate policy positions. In addition, he or she should have experience working with executive branch departments and agencies and a working understanding of their processes. Responsibilities Foster relationships to educate legislative and executive branch decision-makers and influencers on Vantor products, services, and technologies Develop, drive, and manage legislative and executive branch outreach strategy and activities Monitor, analyze, respond to, and influence federal (and from time-to-time state and local) policy and regulatory trends affecting the aerospace and defense industry Understand US Government customer processes, problems, and interests with a specific focus on the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and/or Department of Homeland Security Work closely with other corporate business functions (e.g., business development, sales, communications, and marketing) to ensure a coordinated communications strategy in pursuit of strategic objectives Incorporate an enterprise perspective (Vantor-wide) in strategy and message development Identify/develop industry leadership opportunities and partnerships to advance Vantor’s goals Represent the company among various industry groups and associations, and prepare and implement strategies to maximize the value of such groups Prepare and edit correspondence, white papers, presentations, and other communications Minimum Qualifications Ability to operate with uncompromising integrity, working in a collaborative team environment Knowledge of legislative and executive branch processes, U.S. Government budget cycle, and U.S. Government agency behaviors and cultures; must be able to successfully maneuver corporate issues through the U.S. Government budget and policy decision-making processes and possess a minimum of 10 years’ Capitol Hill and/or related experience A substantial knowledge of issues related to the Department of War and/or related agencies, the Intelligence Community, and/or the Department of Homeland Security Polished writing and interpersonal skills, especially when dealing with corporate executives and senior government officials and leaders; must know proper etiquette and protocol, and be able to confidently and convincingly represent corporate issues before them Self-starter, able to manage time and multi-task effectively in a hectic, fast-paced, and very demanding environment Bachelors degree, preferably in Political Science or a related field U.S. citizenship and ability to get and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance is required Some travel (up to 20%) required Preferred Qualifications The ability to thrive in a small team environment Ability to quickly grasp and communicate complex technical concepts Current TS/SCI clearance preferred Pay Transparency: To support pay transparency, Vantor includes salary ranges in all U.S. job postings. Starting pay for this role will fall within the listed range and will be based on factors such as experience, qualifications, skills, location, and market conditions. Candidates who meet the minimum requirements for the role should not expect to receive compensation at the top of the range. The listed range reflects the expected pay for this position, and final offers will be determined based on each candidate’s experience, expertise, and alignment with the role. ● The base pay for this position within the Washington, DC metropolitan area is: $182,000.00 – $242,000.00 – $266,200.00 annually. For all other states, we use geographic cost of labor as an input to develop market-driven ranges for our roles, and as such, each location where we hire may have a different range. Benefits: Vantor offers a competitive total rewards package that goes beyond the standard, including a robust 401(k) with company match, mental health resources, and unique perks like student loan repayment assistance, adoption reimbursement and pet insurance to support all aspects of your life. You can find more information on our benefits at: https://www.Vantor.com/careers Additionally, this position is incentive eligible with a target based on contribution, company performance, and/or individual results achieved; the specific incentive plan and target amount will be determined based on the role and breadth of contributions. To apply, submit your application via Vantor’s Career page . EEO Policy: Vantor is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace. We believe in fostering an environment where all team members feel respected, valued, and encouraged to share their ideas. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Director of Government Relations (MPL)
item.description: Director of Government Relations (MPL) Organization: Stinson LLP Location: Minneapolis, MN Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Job Details Description Under general supervision and according to established policies and procedures, the Director of Government Relations navigates the communication channels and bureaucracy of state and local government. The Director of Government Relations attends sessions at the State Capitol and state and local governments; monitors, provides coverage, and reports back to department regarding current events; writes briefings, memos, newsletters and client communications; and coordinates meetings with government officials and clients. Please submit your application by no later than 45 days following the posted date. Applications received after this date may not be considered. Required Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree in Government Affairs, Public Policy, Law or related field. 5 years or more of government relations experience required. Essential Functions Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Communication (40%) Develop and implement communication plans. Draft and submit timely client updates, legislative summaries, fact sheets, newsletters and alerts. Complete research and writing assignments on a variety of client-related topics and issues. Lobbying Activities (50%) Monitor and report on legislative committee activities and hearings. Organize lobbying activities during legislative sessions and the interim. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with clients, members of the Minnesota legislature and their staff, state executive and agency personnel, and coalition partners. Represent clients in meetings with legislative staff, executive officials and numerous advocacy organizations. Analyze and interpret legislation that impacts clients. Assist firm clients in the administration of association activities. Coordinate client communications efforts such as news alerts and newsletters. Monitor and provide coverage of activities at the Minnesota Legislature by attending hearings at the State Capitol; tracking, analyzing, and interpreting legislation; reporting current events to the government relations team and writing brief updates. General and Administrative (10%) Performs other duties as assigned. Competencies Strong verbal and written communication skills. Self-motivated with excellent organizational skills and attention to detail. Highly professional with a strong customer service orientation, commitment to meeting deadlines, and ability to multitask in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Strong professional, independent thinking skills with strength in problem solving and the ability to offer constructive opinions and creative solutions. A team player who motivates and educates other team members. Regular and predictable attendance is an essential function of the position. Supervisory Responsibility This position has no supervisory responsibilities. Travel Travel is expected between both offices and other locations as deemed necessary. Work Environment & Physical Demands This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines. While performing the responsibilities of the position, these work environment characteristics are representative of the environment the person in this position will encounter. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will work in a professional, fast paced office environment that may require additional hours to complete work. These physical demands are representative of the physical requirements necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. If an employee is unable to perform the essential functions of the position, Stinson LLP will evaluate whether a reasonable accommodation can be made to enable the employee to perform the described essential functions of the position. Generally, due to the nature of this office position, while performing the responsibilities of the position, the employee is required to talk and hear. The employee is often required to sit and use their hands and fingers, to handle or feel. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, reach with arms and hands, climb or balance, and to stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Vision abilities required by the job include close vision. Benefits & Compensation At Stinson LLP, we are committed to the success of our employees. We are equally committed to providing competitive, affordable health and wellness benefits to help take care of yourself and your family, including: Medical, dental, and vision health plans Medical savings accounts Firm-provided Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Wellness Program, and Caregiving Support Concierge Services Employer-paid life insurance and AD&D Short- and long-term disability benefits Generous paid time off for holidays, vacation, bereavement, jury duty, and paid leave for sick and safe time, parental, and military Excellent work-life programs, including service bonuses, back-up child, elder, and pet care, and an employee discount program The salary range for this role is $149K – $171K. The salary range for this position is based on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, and location. The range is provided as an initial approximation at the time of posting and may vary based on the individual’s unique qualifications and experience. EEO Statement Stinson LLP is an equal employment opportunity (EEO) employer. We encourage qualified minority, female, veteran, disabled, and other diverse candidates to apply to be considered for open positions. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package. We conduct criminal background checks on all individuals offered employment. Information gathered through applicant voluntary self-identification will be used for statistical reporting and to measure the effectiveness of our EEO outreach efforts. All information is requested on a voluntary basis and will be kept confidential. We will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. item.title: Immigration Legal Services Managing Attorney, Pro Bono & Strategic Partnerships
item.description: Immigration Legal Services Managing Attorney, Pro Bono & Strategic Partnerships Organization: Global Refuge Location: Baltimore, MD Date Posted: 09/28/2026 If you are passionate about transforming communities with a mission-driven organization, then we have the opportunity for you! Reporting to the Director for Legal Affairs, the Immigration Legal Services Manager, Pro Bono Project & Strategic Partnerships will lead the development and implementation of a sustainable pro bono strategy that expands Global Refuge’s capacity to provide high-quality immigration legal services to low-income refugees, immigrants, and individuals seeking protection in the United States. The Manager will oversee the systems, partnerships, staffing, volunteer engagement, and performance measures necessary to ensure that pro bono resources are effectively aligned with client and program needs. The Immigration Legal Services Manager, Pro Bono Project & Strategic Partnerships is a management-level position responsible for the strategy, development, and operations of Global Refuge’s pro bono legal services function and its strategic partnerships with law firms, corporations, bar associations, law schools, community organizations, and other stakeholders. The Manager will serve as a key member of the Immigration Legal Services leadership team and will work closely with the Director for Legal Affairs, Managing Attorneys, and other Global Refuge teams to identify opportunities for strategic growth, strengthen external partnerships, and integrate pro bono capacity into the broader legal services strategy. The Manager will supervise pro bono program staff and delegate day-to-day coordination activities while maintaining responsibility for program strategy, quality, performance, partner relationships, and outcomes. The position will also contribute to technical assistance, training, and professional development for pro bono attorneys and partners, with an emphasis on client-centered, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive legal services. This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Baltimore, MD, with regular work at Global Refuge offices, field offices, community partner locations, and external partner sites as needed. Responsibilities/Duties Program Leadership & Strategy Lead the overall strategy, development, and continuous improvement of Global Refuge’s pro bono legal services program in alignment with the organization’s legal services priorities and strategic goals. Develop and implement annual and multi-year goals for pro bono capacity, volunteer engagement, case placement, strategic partnerships, client outcomes, and program growth. Establish systems, policies, workflows, and performance measures that support a high-quality, sustainable, and scalable pro bono function. Identify opportunities to expand pro bono capacity into emerging areas of legal need and strategically align volunteer resources with client and program priorities. Monitor program performance, identify trends and operational challenges, and recommend adjustments to strengthen program effectiveness and sustainability. Collaborate with the Director for Legal Affairs and Managing Attorneys to integrate pro bono services into broader GR ILS program planning, service delivery, and growth strategies. Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement Lead the development and stewardship of strategic partnerships that expand Global Refuge’s legal services capacity and advance the organization’s mission. Develop and maintain senior-level relationships with law firms, corporate legal departments, bar associations, law schools, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, and other strategic partners. Develop partnership strategies that move beyond individual case referrals to create sustained institutional engagement, including firm-wide pro bono commitments, volunteer pipelines, training partnerships, and other capacity-building opportunities. Represent Global Refuge in professional networks, coalitions, conferences, and partner meetings and serve as a key organizational ambassador for the Immigration Legal Services program. Assess prospective partnerships and make recommendations regarding opportunities that align with Global Refuge’s legal services priorities, organizational capacity, and client needs. Steward existing relationships through regular communication, performance monitoring, recognition, and opportunities for deeper engagement. Collaborate with Global Refuge’s development, mobilization, communications, and program teams to maximize the impact of strategic partnerships. Pro Bono Program Management Oversee the recruitment, onboarding, engagement, retention, and deployment of pro bono attorneys and other volunteers through a coordinated and strategic volunteer-management system. Supervise Pro Bono Coordination staff and delegate day-to-day volunteer and case coordination activities while maintaining accountability for program performance and service quality. Establish and monitor systems for identifying, screening, assigning, and tracking cases referred to pro bono attorneys. Ensure that cases are appropriately matched with volunteer capacity, expertise, client needs, and legal deadlines. Oversee systems for monitoring case status, deadlines, outcomes, and volunteer engagement. Ensure that databases and program records accurately capture volunteer activity, case placement, client outcomes, and other program metrics. Develop strategies to strengthen volunteer retention and create meaningful pathways for attorneys to deepen their engagement with Global Refuge. Oversee regular communications and engagement strategies for the pro bono attorney network, including newsletters, targeted outreach, training opportunities, and recognition. Legal Training, Quality & Technical Assistance Work with the Director for Legal Affairs and Managing/Supervising Attorneys to develop and oversee substantive legal training and professional-development opportunities for pro bono attorneys. Ensure that pro bono attorneys have access to appropriate legal resources, practice guidance, templates, and technical assistance. Promote consistent standards for client-centered, trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and ethical legal services across the pro bono program. Identify training needs and develop or coordinate resources to address emerging legal issues and practice needs. Support quality-assurance systems for pro bono services in collaboration with the legal services leadership team. Grant Management, Data & Program Accountability Support the development and implementation of grant-funded pro bono initiatives and ensure that program activities align with grant requirements and organizational priorities. Establish systems for tracking program outputs, outcomes, volunteer engagement, case placement, and other grant-related metrics. Monitor performance against program goals and provide regular analysis and recommendations to the Director for Legal Affairs. Prepare program data, narratives, and other information needed for grant reports, proposals, organizational reporting, and strategic planning. Maintain systems that support accurate and timely documentation of pro bono program activities and outcomes. Use data and partner feedback to assess program effectiveness and inform future program development. Community Engagement & Organizational Representation Support community outreach, education, legal information sessions, and other activities that strengthen awareness of Global Refuge’s legal services and pro bono opportunities. Represent Global Refuge at community, professional, coalition, and partner meetings. Develop relationships with organizations serving immigrant and refugee communities to better understand unmet legal needs and identify opportunities for pro bono engagement. Collaborate across Global Refuge teams to connect community needs with available pro bono resources and strategic partnerships. Management & Leadership Expectations The Manager is expected to function as the organizational owner of the pro bono and strategic partnerships function, rather than as the primary day-to-day coordinator of individual volunteers or cases. The position will establish strategy, build systems, manage relationships, supervise staff, monitor performance, and ensure that the function effectively advances GR ILS’s broader mission. Success in this role will be measured not only by the number of pro bono attorneys recruited or cases placed, but by the Manager’s ability to build a sustainable, high-performing pro bono infrastructure and strategic partner network that materially expands Global Refuge’s capacity to serve clients. Qualifications Juris Doctor (J. D.) and active law license are required At least 5 years of experience representing immigrants before DHS, Immigration Courts and BIA strongly preferred Experience managing pro bono attorneys, volunteers, and relationships with law firm pro bono programs Strong substantive understanding of U.S. immigration law and legal practice Experience working with survivors of trauma and immigrants Excellent legal analysis, written and oral advocacy and presentation skills Responsible, self-initiating, and focused, with proven ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team-based decision-making environment Experience designing trainings and presenting to legal and non-legal audiences Meticulous organizational habits with an ability to manage caseloads, establish priorities, and meet deadlines Strong interpersonal skills and record of cultural competence and cross-cultural communication skills; experience working with clients, staff and interns of diverse backgrounds Demonstrated fluency in any language of the populations we serve such as, Spanish, Dari/Pashto, Arabic, Haitian Creole, is highly preferred Understanding of the law firm and pro bono culture a plus. Excellent MS Office Suite skills, particularly in Word and Excel, required. P

item.title: Program Officer, Southeast Asia
item.description: Program Officer, Southeast Asia Organization: National Endowment for Democracy (NED) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Position Title: Program Officer, Southeast Asia Grade Level: Level 5 – Exempt Reports to: Senior Program Manager About NED The National Endowment for Democracy supports freedom around the world. At NED, we deliver on the belief that freedom is a universal aspiration. Headquartered in Washington, DC, NED is a private, nonprofit foundation, mandated by Congress, dedicated to strengthening democratic institutions worldwide. NED reflects an enduring American commitment to stand with those striving for dignity, justice, and opportunity. In 2025, NED made 1,552 grants totaling $271 million to support the work of nongovernmental organizations advancing democratic goals in more than 90 countries, including some of the world’s most challenging and repressive environments. We seek talented, entrepreneurial professionals motivated by purpose and committed to excellence. At NED, you will join a dynamic team of experts who bring their skills, curiosity, and judgment to a consequential mission at a critical moment for democracy around the world. Our work is guided by our shared values: excellence, respect, empathy, accountability, and adaptability. Position Summary The Program Officer will work with Asia program leadership to manage grants and coordinate NED’s programming in Southeast Asia, with a particular focus on Thailand and the Philippines. This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC, and is part of the bargaining unit. Primary Responsibilities Work closely and flexibly with a diverse range of activists working on media freedom, human rights, rule of law, public policy, civic education, and other areas. Monitor the implementation of NED-approved projects and evaluate the effectiveness and the institutional growth of NED grantees by analyzing grantee reports, providing feedback on implemented activities, maintaining continuous communication over the grant cycle, and conducting regular field visits. Produce written materials and presentations to provide funding recommendations to NED leadership. Monitor political developments in the region relevant to the portfolio to inform NED strategies and programming, including reading various US- and regional-based publications, meeting with political analysts and other contacts, keeping abreast of the changing political environment, and actively coordinating with other Asia team members on their country portfolios. Build and maintain relationships with like-minded organizations, including other donors, NED partners, and regional organizations. Travel to monitor existing grantees, identify new funding opportunities, and gain an on‑the-ground perspective on the political situation. The visits will include meetings with NED grantees, meetings with core institutes, potential civil society partners, other donors, and political analysts and opinion-makers. Think creatively about how to improve team effectiveness, grantee-reporting guidelines, communications with other teams at NED, etc. Liaise with other NED teams; participate in various working groups, and other efforts to improve NED’s overall functioning and effectiveness. Mentor junior staff, where applicable. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in International Affairs, Political Science, International Development, or a related discipline required; Master’s degree preferred. 4–7 years of relevant professional experience in international development, democracy support, human rights, civil society, or a related field, including experience living and/or working in Southeast Asia. Significant experience in nonprofit work. Experience in financial monitoring and reporting. Knowledge of program evaluation techniques. Demonstrated understanding of broader political issues and trends in the Asia region, with a particular focus on Southeast Asia. Thai language proficiency preferred. Ability and willingness to travel to countries within the region, as needed. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Ability to communicate complex ideas effectively, both verbally and in writing. Exceptional analytical and interpersonal skills. Ability to maintain professionalism under pressure. High degree of organization and initiative. Demonstrated ability to work as a team player, including coordination and facilitation skills. Authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or transfer sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. Talent in Action Consistent with NED’s talent statement, and grounded in our values, the successful individual in this role will demonstrate the following competencies in the delivery of their work while supporting NED’s efforts to advance democratic change: Purpose-Driven Reliable Expertise Respectful Collaboration Curiosity Results-Oriented An Optimistic Mindset NED Total Compensation The anticipated compensation range for this position is USD $64,500 – $116,000. The salary for this position is determined based on a wide variety of factors, including but not limited to an individual’s professional experience, qualifications, education, and other business needs along with internal equity considerations. Employees are not typically hired at the top of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are based on the aforementioned circumstances. NED also offers a generous benefits package that demonstrates its commitment to employee health and well-being. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Quality Assurance – Wellness Center
item.description: Manager, Quality Assurance – Wellness Center Organization: The People Concern Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Summary: The People Concern is funded through the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health (LAC DMH) and LA Care to deliver Mental Health and Enhanced Care Management (ECM) services. These programs provide mental health treatment, case management, and care coordination to individuals experiencing homelessness, transitioning into permanent supportive housing, or residing in permanent housing. In collaboration with the Clinical Quality Assurance Leadership team, the Quality Assurance Manager will ensure adherence with The People Concern’s philosophies and current standards for quality of care and other requirements as defined by Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health (DMH) and LA Care. This position will oversee the supervision of the Quality Assurance Specialists and provide project management, leadership and training to all staff around quality assurance standards. The ideal candidate is technically savvy, detail-oriented, able to work independently, collaborative with team members and staff, demonstrates initiative and leadership in designing new protocols and policies, and serves as a data champion and support to staff at all levels throughout the organization. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Ensure the agency’s adherence to Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health (LAC DMH) and LA Care Enhanced Care Management (ECM) policies and procedures. Assist with the preparation of federal, state, county and/or city audits. Coordinate, develop, and assist with delivery of ongoing trainings and resources to Mental Health staff on Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health (LAC DMH) and LA Care Enhanced Care Management (ECM) documentation standards and EHR workflows. Supervise Quality Assurance Specialists through weekly structured supervisions and providing ongoing support, growth and accountability of staff. Responsible for data collection and reporting. Manage, monitor and train DMH program staff on Service Request Tracking System (SRTS). Reconcile internal and external data sources to remain in compliance with DMH policies and procedures. Responsible for the maintenance of Network Adequacy Provider & Practitioner Administration (NAPPA) monthly and as needed. Assist with processing records request received by the Agency. Assist with the administration of Electronic Health Record, EYXM/Credible. Identify and lead implementation of process improvement projects. Complete monthly and as needed file reviews for COS and Mental Health charts. Collaborate and consult effectively with all levels of staff in Clinical Quality Assurance, Billing, Mental Health and any other staff/programs to ensure adherence to policies and procedures. Attend scheduled and as-needed internal and external trainings and meetings. Adhere to The People Concern personnel policies. Other duties not specified in the position description as requested by the Director or Assistant Director of Clinical Quality Assurance. Qualifications: High School Diploma or GED or Equivalent Minimum of three (3) years’ experience ensuring adherence to Los Angeles County and State standards to chart documentation for respective funding sources, specifically Medi-Cal and LA County DMH Excellent written and oral communications skills, ability to develop and conduct training sessions and ability to assist with developing policies and procedures: (i.e., data entry/support services) Knowledge of HIPAA standards and practices Knowledge of Electronic Health Record Possess attention to detail, ability to be thorough and accurate Able to work effectively both individually and as part of a team Strong communication, interpersonal and team building skills Possess the ability to be a skilled trainer, perform virtual (Zoom) and in-person training presentations, and develop effective training materials. Outstanding organizational and project management skills, with thorough knowledge of nonprofit service provision and administration Demonstrated ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously and to work independently and creatively Must possess a valid California Driver’s license and maintain an insurable driving record Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree Two (2) years of leadership/management experience in a supervisory role Knowledge of Exym or Credible Work Environment: Primarily indoor office environment Walk or drive to different local sites at least 25% of the time Regularly required to sit, stand, bend; occasionally lift or carry up to 35 lbs. On occasion walk or drive to different local sites. May necessitate working in busy and loud environments. May be exposed to elements like cold, heat, dust, noise and odor. May need to bend, stoop, twist, and sit throughout the day. EXPECTED BEHAVIORS OF ALL STAFF Act as a role model Demonstrate a sense of responsibility Continuously learn and improve Acknowledge your own areas of improvement Hear and provide honest, specific and direct feedback Create an environment where everyone is welcomed valued and respected Collaborate Equal Opportunity Employer The People Concern is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to non-discrimination in employment. We select the most qualified individual for the job based on job-related qualifications regardless of race, color, age, sex, religion, national origin, disability, ancestry, marital status, credit history, sexual orientation, arrest and court record, genetic information, veteran status or any other status protected by federal, state or other applicable laws. About the People Concern The People Concern empowers the most vulnerable among us to rebuild their lives. One of Los Angeles County’s largest social services agencies, The People Concern was formed in 2016 in a merger of two trusted social service organizations based in Los Angeles County, OPCC and Lamp Community. Informed by more than fifty-eight years of work in the community, The People Concern is a leading provider of, and advocate for, evidence-based solutions to the multi-faceted challenges inherent in homelessness and domestic violence. With compassion and profound respect for those we serve, we provide a fully integrated system of care – including outreach, interim housing, mental and medical health care, substance abuse services, domestic violence services, life skills & wellness programs, and permanent supportive housing – tailored to the unique needs of homeless individuals, survivors of domestic violence, challenged youth, and others who have nowhere else to turn. The People Concern’s model of integrated and comprehensive care empowers our participants to navigate the multi-faceted obstacles in their lives, become their best selves, and ultimately, connect with and contribute to their communities. item.title: Legal & Policy Officer, MENA Region
item.description: Legal & Policy Officer, MENA Region Organization: Human Rights Foundation (HRF) Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Job Description About the Human Rights Foundation: The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization that promotes and protects human rights globally, with a focus on closed societies. HRF unites people in the common cause of defending human rights and promoting liberal democracy. Our mission is to ensure that freedom is preserved and promoted worldwide. We seek, in particular, to sustain the struggle for liberty in those areas where it is most under threat. HRF produces the Oslo Freedom Forum, an annual human rights conference in Norway. For more information on HRF and its work, please visit our website at www.hrf.org. To learn more about the Oslo Freedom Forum, please visit www.oslofreedomforum.com Position Summary: The Legal & Policy Officer, Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, reports to the Director of Policy and Research and provides support for the planning and execution of the organization’s research initiatives, legal cases, campaigns, advocacy, and events as they pertain to the MENA region. This individual works closely with various internal departments and external partners to help ensure adherence to the organization’s mission and goals for the region. Additionally, this role interacts with many HRF programs, projects, and events such as but not limited to: HRF’s Political Regime Research Project, Impact Litigation, Sportwashing, Art in Protest, and the Oslo Freedom Forum in relation to the MENA region. This position requires knowledge and demonstrated interest in human rights, democracy, and a deep familiarity with the MENA region. Responsibilities and Expectations: Specific duties include, but may not be limited to… Proposing and spearheading MENA-region campaigns, programs, research, and writing, including reports, policy notes/academic articles, op-eds, petitions, Universal Periodic Reviews, and legal petitions; Acting as a spokesperson for the organization’s work on the MENA region Assisting with speaker and panel coordination, including award nomination (Maseko and Havel Prizes) and guiding talk development for the Oslo Freedom Forum with special attention to the MENA region; Supporting HRF’s political regime research project team on the MENA region by reviewing summaries and full reports; Collaborating with Freedom Fellows, grant recipients, and other community members toward executing public events, campaigns, and projects as it pertains to ongoing MENA region developments. Building and managing a team to execute HRF’s work on the MENA region in the long term Key Skills and Qualifications: Education: An undergraduate degree and/or master’s degree in Middle Eastern studies, History, Human Rights, International Relations, Political Science or a related field is required. Mid-level experience working on the MENA region is required. An understanding of the non-profit space in the MENA region and the human rights situation and geopolitics of the region is required Exposure to democratization and authoritarianism-related field is strongly preferred Strong research, writing, and analytical skills Professional experience with social science research methods is a plus. Language Skills: Arabic is required and French and/or Farsi is a plus. Strong time management and leadership skills Strong communication skills Detail-oriented Strong social media skills preferred Compensation: $75,000–$90,000 per year, commensurate with experience How to Apply: To apply, please complete the form here and include a resume/CV, cover letter, and 1–2 writing samples demonstrating expertise in the MENA region. item.title: Senior Communications Specialist – Cover Letter Required, No AI
item.description: Senior Communications Specialist – Cover Letter Required, No AI Organization: n-Lorem Foundation Location: San Diego, CA Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Description Position Title: Senior Communications Specialist Reporting to: Vice President, Foundation Development and External Relations Location: On-site (San Diego- Mira Mesa area) Employment: Full-Time Salary Range: $80,000 – $100,000 (Compensation may vary based on related skills, experience, and relevant key attributes) n-Lorem Foundation Though n-Lorem is pioneering a novel non-profit model, to provide personalized experimental ASO treatments for free, for life to patients with the rarest of mutations (nano-rare), we are functionally a biotechnology company. We have a large and growing portfolio of ASO medicine discovery programs, ASO medicines in development and multiple clinical programs. With a seasoned leadership team and strategic partnerships, the n-Lorem Foundation provides the framework, funds and access for nano-rare patients who are amenable to our technology to receive personalized ASO medicines for free, for life. We hope that you will consider joining us as we strive to change the world, one nano-rare patient at a time. If you are a professional with strong communications experience and would like to join a cohesive, experienced team committed to the belief that we can change the world one patient, one family at a time, we may have a position for you. Job Overview Reporting to the Vice President, Foundation Development and External Relations, the Senior Communications Specialist will support and advance n-Lorem’s presence across social media, website, podcast, and partner channels. This role will lead the day-to-day execution of digital communications, including content development, multimedia creation, social media management, website updates, podcast coordination and promotion, and development of sponsor and partner materials. The specialist will implement integrated campaigns, translate complex scientific and organizational information into clear and engaging content, monitor digital performance, and provide insights and recommendations to strengthen audience engagement and reach. Working collaboratively across Communications, Fundraising, Scientific, and Patient Engagement teams, this role will independently manage digital projects and support events, conferences, fundraising initiatives, and other organizational priorities. Key Responsibilities Social Media & Digital Execution • Manage day-to-day digital communications across social media platforms including LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube. • Draft, edit, and distribute press releases in alignment with organizational priorities. • Develop engaging platform-appropriate content (copy, graphics, short-form video) that aligns with leadership-driven messaging and strategy. • Implement multi-channel campaigns designed by the Communications team. • Engage with followers, monitor conversations, and escalate issues when needed. • Identify appropriate measures, track and produce monthly performance insights with recommendations. • Stay current on social media trends and platform changes, and recommend opportunities to improve audience engagement and reach. • Maintain content calendars that support consistent and timely publishing across appropriate channels. Content Development • Serve as a primary writer and editor for digital communications, including social media, website content, campaigns, event materials, and organizational announcements. • Write clear, compelling, accurate content while maintaining a consistent organizational voice and tone. • Edit and proofread content for grammar, clarity, accuracy, style, accessibility, and brand consistency. • Translate complex scientific concepts into accessible and engaging digital content for patients, families, advocates, donors, partners, and the broader public. • Collaborate with internal subject matter experts to gather information, identify compelling stories, and develop content. • Create compelling digital assets, including infographics, reels, animated slides, thumbnails, and promotional graphics. • Develop content packages and storytelling assets for internal teams, events, and sponsorship efforts. Website Management • Manage ongoing updates to website pages, news items, events, and program content. • Coordinate with external developers on technical improvements, layout updates, or functionality issues. • Identify opportunities to improve website content, structure, and user experience. • Ensure content accuracy, SEO optimization, and consistency with brand guidelines. Podcast Management • Manage logistics: scheduling interviews, coordinating guest communications, and aligning with production timelines. • Work with production staff to prepare, edit, and finalize episodes. • Develop promotional materials such as snippets, thumbnails, short clips, and cross-platform campaigns. • Provide input on episode planning and manage episode release schedules to maximize audience impact. Sponsor & Partner Support • Develop and update sponsor decks, one-page materials, and digital assets. • Track deliverables for sponsor visibility and ensure assets are accurate and delivered on schedule. • Prepare promotional tools for partners and conferences. Analytics & Optimization • Monitor social media, website, and podcast metrics to evaluate performance and effectiveness. • Recommend refinements to boost audience growth, engagement, and content quality. • Maintain organized digital libraries and documentation. Cross-Functional Collaboration • Partner with Communications, Fundraising, Scientific, and Patient Engagement teams. • Independently manage assigned digital projects from planning through execution. • Support digital components of events, conferences, and campaigns. • Contribute to special initiatives requiring digital expertise. n-Lorem offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 403(b), four weeks paid vacation, paid sick time, life insurance, employee assistance program. n-Lorem is a small foundation with an extraordinary mission, to provide hope and potentially help to nano-rare patients. Every employee in our organization is a significant contributor to this mission. We know that our work could have a profound impact on the life of a patient today. n-Lorem is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status. n-Lorem is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance or accommodations due to a disability, please let us know. For more information on n-Lorem, please visit our website www.nlorem.org Requirements Key Requirements • U.S. work authorization without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, digital media, journalism, or related field. • 3-5 years of professional experience in communications, content marketing, journalism, public relations or related field (healthcare, science or advocacy sector preferred). • Exceptional writing and editorial skills with demonstrated ability to produce high-quality digital content (portfolio requested). • Graphic design proficiency with an eye for layout, typography, and visual storytelling. • Proficiency with Canva or similar software. • Experience managing social media channels with measurable growth outcomes. • Experience with web CMS platforms (WordPress or equivalent). • Basic understanding of web coding (HTML and JavaScript) or a strong willingness to learn. • Working knowledge of SEO, Google Analytics 4, email marketing tools and social scheduling platforms (e.g. Hootsuite, Buffer) preferred. • Experience developing digital sponsor or event materials preferred. Additional Requirements • Excellent time management; able to juggle multiple concurrent deadlines. • Detail-oriented with a high standard for accuracy and brand consistency. • Analytical mindset; able to translate data into actionable recommendations. • Professional maturity to handle sensitive patient-related content. • Team-oriented with the ability to work independently when needed. item.title: Communications and Content Manager
item.description: Communications and Content Manager Organization: Constructive Dialogue Institute Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/28/2026 About CDI The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation. About the Role CDI is seeking a versatile, fast, and editorially sharp Communications & Content Manager to serve as the production engine behind our communications and thought leadership. Reporting to the VP of Strategic Communications, you will turn CDI’s research and point of view into a steady stream of high-quality, on-message content that grows our audience and strengthens our reputation as a leading national voice on constructive dialogue in higher education. This is a hands-on maker role. You will write and produce our higher education newsletter, blog, and social content; turn our flagship research into a full family of related pieces; and produce the materials that equip our Partnerships team to win new partnerships. You will support on keeping all the pieces of the shared editorial moving on a predictable cadence, coordinating closely with our subject-matter experts and Partnerships colleagues. You will also help build press relationships and contribute to CDI’s media coverage, giving our VP of Strategic Communications added reach. You will partner closely with our Demand Generation lead, who runs the marketing funnel: you create the audience and the content, and they convert that attention into pipeline. Responsibilities Manage the editorial calendar and owned content Write, build, and send CDI’s higher education newsletter, and produce the blog, maintaining a reliable publishing cadence, growing our audience over time, and holding a high bar for quality, accuracy, and on-message voice. Run a single, unified organic social calendar across brand, executive, and thought-leadership content, coordinating contributions from across the team to grow reach and engagement. Collaborate with Partnerships and Marketing to align communications initiatives with other key workstreams such as webinars and conferences, tailor content for target segments, and sequence content for outsized pipeline impact. Produce and repurpose thought leadership Turn CDI’s research (white papers, briefs, studies) into a full family of related content, blog posts, op-ed drafts, social posts, and newsletter features, maximizing the reach of each release. Draft and package thought-leadership content while our subject-matter experts provide the underlying substance. Coordinate production timelines with the Impact team and our subject-matter experts so content ships on time without overloading contributors. Support earned media and track coverage Help build and maintain CDI’s press lists, draft pitches, and support the VP in securing media coverage. Track and log CDI’s media coverage and mentions, contributing to CDI’s earned-media goals. Build more direct media relationships over time, as your familiarity with CDI’s work grows. Produce marketing collateral and maintain brand standards Produce audience-facing marketing collateral, directing external designers to a high standard and on deadline. Maintain and steward CDI’s brand templates and standards (set with the VP), and run the intake and triage process for design requests. Produce marketing case studies and testimonials, partnering with the Demand Generation lead (who selects and secures permissions) and the Impact team (who supports research). Job requirements About You An experienced comms professional. You bring 5+ years in communications, content marketing, editorial, or journalism, ideally in a mission-driven, B2B, higher education, or advocacy context, with a portfolio of published work across formats (newsletters, articles or blogs, social, long-form). A strong editorial operator (our top priority). You think in calendars, cadences, and systems, and you can keep many pieces of content moving at once without dropping quality or missing deadlines. You have thrived in a startup or scrappy environment, driving execution independently while building for scale. An exceptional writer and editor. You produce clear, accurate, on-message content across many formats, and you do it fast, with a sharp editorial eye. A sharp cross-functional collaborator. You work fluidly across subject-matter experts, marketing, and partnerships colleagues, and you keep work on track without constant direction. Media-aware. You understand what makes a story newsworthy and are comfortable drafting pitches and building press relationships. Direct media experience is a plus. Brand- and design-minded. You have a strong eye, can direct external designers, and can maintain templates and standards that keep a brand consistent. Canva experience a plus. Politically astute and mission-aligned. You have the judgment to communicate constructively and credibly across ideological lines, you understand why nonpartisan restraint matters as much as visibility, and you are genuinely motivated by CDI’s mission. Familiarity with the higher education landscape is a plus. Fluent with tools, and with AI. You are comfortable with content and marketing tools (a CMS, an email platform such as HubSpot, social schedulers), and you use modern AI tools to accelerate drafting and production while treating human editing and judgment as non-negotiable, especially on sensitive topics. Benefits Compensation — $85,000-$95,000 A Mission-Driven Culture — our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness Remote-First — CDI was founded as a remote-first organization, and we work hard to maintain a strong team culture across vast distances Unlimited PTO — as well as 13 company holidays Remote Work Support — up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment (like desks, chairs, or webcams) and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expenses Other Benefits — employer-supported health, vision and dental plans, subsidized parental leave, 3% 401k match, short- and long-term disability insurance, life and AD&D insurance, $1,000 annual professional development budget Role Specs Reports to: VP of Strategic Communications Direct Reports: None Schedule: Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones Target start date: ASAP Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Engagement Coordinator
item.description: Policy Engagement Coordinator Organization: Voices for Children in Nebraska Location: Omaha, NE | Lincoln, NE Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Job Title Policy Engagement Coordinator Reports to Policy Director Location: Must be a Nebraska resident, located in or near the Omaha or Lincoln metro area (in-state travel required) Position type Full-Time, Hybrid Starting salary $60,000 Job Summary: Voices for Children in Nebraska is looking for a dynamic, positive, and relationship-driven individual to support our efforts to engage young people and communities across the state in our policy advocacy work. The ideal candidate will be a self-motivated goal-setter who is optimistic about the potential for policy change and the power of youth voice. They will enjoy working alongside youth advocates, empowering young voices in the advocacy process. Strong interpersonal skills, relationship-building, and a commitment to fostering meaningful connections will be key to success in this role. Organization Overview: VFC has been a leader in data-informed and engagement-driven systemic change on key children’s issues in Nebraska for almost 40 years. Our mission is to advocate for equitable opportunity for kids in our state through research, policy, and community engagement. Our vision is a Nebraska with strong communities where every child has all they need to lead a healthy, secure, and fulfilling life. Our primary areas of focus include youth justice, child welfare, economic stability, and health care access. Role Overview: Youth & Community Policy Advocacy Program: Work with policy and engagement staff to identify and create opportunities to elevate youth voices and others with lived experience of our child-serving systems in the policy development, advocacy, and decision-making process. This includes, with training: Leading our Nebraska Youth Justice Policy Fellowship and other identified youth advocacy cohorts, talking walls, listening sessions, and trainings. Planning, coordinating, and executing our annual Spring Break Policy & Advocacy Camp and supporting other youth summits or youth lobby days we may be involved with. Collaborating with our Youth and Family Engagement Coordinator to support the connection between our Omaha-based Youth Advisory Council and our state policy agenda. Providing outreach and direct support for youth, families, and other impacted individuals to participate in state policymaking. During Legislative Session, liaising between Policy Directors and communications staff to provide regular, accessible policy updates for social media, website, and newsletters. Community Partnership Development: Help us to sustain strong, collaborative relationships with organizations and stakeholders across Nebraska, especially outside of the Omaha and Lincoln metro areas, including nonprofits, government agencies, schools, and advocacy groups. This includes: Representing VFC at community meetings and events, coalition meetings, and conferences to enhance organizational visibility and strengthen community trust. Supporting grassroots mobilization efforts such as town halls, listening sessions, community education events, and representing VFC in ballot initiative campaigns and issue-specific policy coalitions. Desired Skills & Abilities Must be a “people person” who is extroverted and able to engage positively with a variety of stakeholders, especially young people, including in times of stress Commitment to centering youth voice and engaging meaningfully in community Outstanding organizational skills, high attention to detail, and experience balancing multiple projects and deadlines Preferred: Some experience with policy advocacy, particularly with the Nebraska Unicameral Legislature Preferred: Bilingual English and Spanish Physical & Other Requirements Driver’s license in good standing and reliable transportation Willingness and ability to pass background check for working with youth and complete child safety training Ability to lift and carry items up to 20 pounds Flexibility to work some evening and weekend hours as needed at meetings, community events, and legislative or other policy opportunities. Benefits Health, dental, and vision insurance offered. VFC pays 100% of individual health insurance premiums for employees on our insurance plan, plus 25% of any dependent child premiums. Alternatively, a monthly employer contribution to HSA or DCFSA, up to $600/month as allowed by IRS contribution limits. 401(k) with employer match up to 2% beginning 6 months following employment Group life insurance and optional additional insurance offerings Access to employee assistance program 12 paid federal holidays, 2 paid floating holidays, as well as generous vacation, sick, and child sick leave starting from date of employment Longevity sabbatical at 5 years Paid parental leave and bring your baby to work policy Flexible workweek and hybrid remote/in-office structure Paid parking for in-office days and mileage reimbursement for work travel outside home city Please forward resume and cover letter to: [email protected] . No phone calls, please. Voices for Children in Nebraska is an equal opportunity employer. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. Up to 32 days of paid time off 14–16 paid holidays annually Potential for annual raises and profit sharing Health, dental, and vision insurance/Medical opt-out payment (up to $1,000/year) 401K with up to 4% employer match Employee Assistance Program: Free mental health counseling Free childcare referrals Access to legal services Grief/eldercare support Financial planning resources Your Impact as the Community Engagement Coordinator The Community Engagement & Events Coordinator is the primary driver of The Summit Center’s event portfolio and community presence. item.title: Team Relations Manager, XPRIZE Accelerate Learning
item.description: Team Relations Manager, XPRIZE Accelerate Learning Organization: XPRIZE Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/28/2026 XPRIZE Overview XPRIZE is an established global leader in designing and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. As a 501(c)3, our unique model democratizes innovation by incentivizing crowd-sourced, scientifically viable solutions to create a more equitable and abundant future for all. Since our founding in 1994, we’ve launched $519 million in prize competitions that are driving more than $31 billion in social and economic impact — a 60x return on philanthropic investment. These competitions not only de-risk early-stage breakthrough ideas but also mobilize capital, talent, and momentum to accelerate solutions from concept to real-world scale. We operate across 5 areas of impact, including: Deep Tech + Exploration Energy + Climate + Nature Food + Water + Waste Health Learning + Society Join XPRIZE to help create meaningful impact as we strive to empower humanity to achieve breakthroughs and architect a more equitable and abundant future for all. Position Description XPRIZE is seeking an experienced Team Relations Manager to play an integral role during the Team Recruitment phase of the Accelerate Learning Prize. This person will lead external communications with potential competing teams during the first year of the competition, become intimately familiar with the prize guidelines to answer inbound questions, and, in coordination with the internal team, answer technical questions about the prize. They will liaise with IT on implementation and customization of the Prize Operations Platform (POP) for team recruitment. They will develop high-quality recruitment status reports for the team and the sponsor. Contribute ideas to the team recruitment strategy, execute team outreach and recruitment webinars, and develop materials for team recruitment. Team Relations Responsibilities: Support the development and execution of the team recruitment strategy in coordination with the rest of the operations team and marketing Lead communication efforts with potential and future competing teams Communicate on complex technical topics related to education in collaboration with the rest of the operations team Develop materials for team recruitment, respond to team questions, and host webinars Assist in tracking and organizing inbound public comments on the competition Guidelines. Participate in relevant online community discussions to drive participation in the prize Identify and participate in industry events virtually and in-person, representing the prize to expand the ecosystem Organize and lead team recruitment calls and webinars Work closely with IT to customize XPRIZE’s online competition portal (Prize Operations Platform, aka “POP”) for team management, prize submissions, and judging Monitor and manage the team Slack channel Ensure alignment of team activities with competition guidelines and other competition documents Support other project management activities as needed Qualifications 4-6 years of relevant professional experience managing external communities, project management, competitions, and related projects Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent relevant experience Experience managing or supporting projects in India or Sub-Saharan Africa Experience with community management Experience managing and customizing technology platforms Direct experience and knowledge in the domain of education Curious, motivated, and interested to learn more about the rapidly expanding world of education innovation Ability to lead or co-lead senior-level meetings, webinars, workshops, etc. Experience building and working with partner organizations and external communities Excellent business and technical writing and professional verbal communication skills. Excellent interpersonal skills and situational awareness Ability to travel 15% of the time, domestically and internationally Ability to thrive and think creatively and calmly in highly fluid situations and under intense schedules and deadlines Competencies required for this role: Action Oriented Manages Ambiguity Collaborates Communicates Effectively Customer Focus Drives Engagement Global Perspective Interpersonal Savvy Builds Networks Organizational Savvy Resourcefulness Situational Adaptability Instills Trust Optimizes Work Processes Manages Conflict Nimble Learning Why Work at XPRIZE: In addition to working for a mission-driven company that catalyzes industries, pushes innovation forward, and is creating an abundant and equitable future, we offer the following benefits: Remote-first environment (must live and work in the United States) Quarterly company-paid All-Hands meetings in Los Angeles for frequent in-person collaboration Employee and dependent medical, dental, and vision options A 401(K) program with employer match Ample paid time off, including vacation, floating holidays, sick days, and company-paid holidays An Employee Assistance Program for confidential, professional support with personal, family, or other challenges Employee stipends/reimbursements for cell phone, internet, health & wellbeing, and learning & development Generous Paid Parental Leave for all employees welcoming a new child to their family One meeting-free block per week and four focus weeks per year to ensure uninterrupted time for strategic projects The anticipated base salary for this position is $80k to $100k and may also qualify for an annual incentive. This role is eligible for our extensive benefits package and generous paid time off including vacation, sick, and holidays. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors including the qualifications of the individual applicant, years of relevant experience for the role, level of education attained, and certifications and/or other licenses held. XPRIZE is a remote-first environment. All employees must be authorized to work in the United States and work from within the United States full-time. The XPRIZE FOUNDATION is an equal opportunity employer and does not unlawfully discriminate in employment. Equal access to employment, services, and programs is available to all persons. Those applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application and/or interview process should notify a representative of the organization. Please note: Though submitting a resume to the XPRIZE FOUNDATION implies that you are interested in a position(s), it does not imply that you are an applicant. You are not considered an applicant until you have been contacted directly by a Talent Acquisition representative requesting that you begin the designated application process, which may involve phone and/or in-person interview(s), job-related testing, and background checks. item.title: Vice President, Government Affairs & Public Policy
item.description: Vice President, Government Affairs & Public Policy Organization: Chapters Health System Location: Remote (FL) Date Posted: 09/28/2026 It’s inspiring to work with a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they’re doing! When you become part of the Chapters Health Team, you’ll realize it’s more than a job. It’s a mission. We’re committed to providing outstanding patient care and a high level of customer service in our communities every day. Our employees make all the difference in our success! The Vice President, Government Affairs & Public Policy role will build and lead Chapters Health’s Government Affairs & Public Policy function, shaping the development and execution of federal and multistate government affairs strategies to advance Chapters Health’s strategic priorities and mission. Reporting to the COO, this executive will serve as a key advisor to senior leadership and partner cross-functionally to proactively identify and address government policy risks and opportunities. The Vice President will play a critical role in elevating Chapters Health’s reputation among policymakers and ensuring the health system has a strong and influential voice in public policy decisions related to healthcare innovation, patient access, Medicare and Medicaid policy, reimbursement, regulatory frameworks, and other emerging healthcare reforms impacting the system. This leader will also provide strategic oversight of Chapters Health’s external lobbying relationships and political action committee (PAC), ensuring advocacy resources and activities are effectively managed, compliant, and aligned with the organization’s strategic priorities. Qualifications This leader must exemplify Chapters Health’s core values, including a strong commitment to patients, impeccable integrity, and outstanding teamwork and collaboration. 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, public policy, advocacy, or a related field within the healthcare sector. Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree (MBA, MPH, JD, PhD, or related field) strongly preferred. Demonstrated success developing and executing federal and multistate government affairs strategies within a complex, highly regulated environment. Strong influence and negotiation skills with demonstrated success influencing federal and state healthcare policy, legislation, and regulatory matters. Deep expertise in U.S. healthcare policy, including Medicare, Medicaid, reimbursement, healthcare regulation, and relevant federal agency requirements. Demonstrated experience overseeing and managing external lobbyists, government affairs consultants, and other advocacy partners across federal and/or state markets. Experience with PAC strategy, governance, compliance, contribution strategy, and fund management strongly preferred. Strong political judgment and demonstrated ability to build effective bipartisan relationships with policymakers, regulators, government officials, and other external stakeholders. Exceptional executive leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills, with demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, complex, and rapidly changing environments. Proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams and collaborate cross-functionally within a complex, matrixed organization where influencing without direct authority is essential. Key Responsibilities Develop and lead a comprehensive federal and multistate government affairs strategy aligned with Chapters Health’s strategic and business objectives. Provide strategic direction and coordination of state government affairs activities, ensuring state-level priorities are aligned with federal strategy and broader system objectives. Proactively lead, shape, and influence federal and state legislation and policy related to reimbursement, Medicare and Medicaid, regulatory frameworks, tax and innovation incentives, patient access, and other emerging healthcare reforms, safeguarding the system’s ability to deliver transformative, high-quality healthcare. Represent Chapters Health in Washington, D.C., and key state markets, including participation in coalitions, trade associations, public hearings, and other policy forums. Build and maintain strong bipartisan relationships with key policymakers, congressional staff, state officials, agency leaders, and key federal agencies, including HHS, CMS, and FDA. Lead strategic engagement with Congress, key committees, federal and state agencies, legislatures, and relevant regulators. Coordinate executive participation in hearings, briefings, and policy forums and prepare senior leaders for high-stakes government and policy interactions. Provide strategic oversight and direction to external lobbyists, government affairs consultants, and advisors across federal and state markets. Establish clear priorities, expectations, and accountability for external partners and ensure lobbying activities are coordinated, effective, and aligned with Chapters Health’s legislative and policy objectives. Provide strategic oversight of Chapters Health’s political action committee (PAC), including governance, compliance, contribution strategy, stakeholder engagement, and responsible stewardship of PAC resources. Ensure PAC activities support the organization’s government affairs strategy and are conducted in accordance with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and organizational policies. Collaborate closely with the COO and senior management team, as well as Legal, Compliance, Clinical, Medical Affairs, and other key stakeholders, to assess legislative and regulatory developments and proactively identify policy risks and opportunities. In partnership with Corporate Affairs, translate organizational priorities, healthcare advancements, and emerging issues into compelling policy narratives that support government engagement, advocacy, and public policy efforts. Establish metrics, reporting mechanisms, and other measures of effectiveness to evaluate government affairs, lobbying, PAC, and advocacy activities and communicate outcomes and emerging priorities to executive leadership. Build, lead, and develop a high-performing federal and state government affairs team capable of supporting Chapters Health’s continued growth and expanding geographic footprint. Serve as a visible and credible external leader, strengthening Chapters Health’s reputation and relationships with policymakers, agency officials, trade associations, lobbyists, healthcare organizations, community partners, and other stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem. Compensation Pay Range: $30,000.00 – $700,000.00 This position requires consent to drug and/or alcohol testing after a conditional offer of employment is made, as well as on-going compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Policy. All Chapters Health System employees performing services for Florida affiliates are submitted through the Florida Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse to verify eligibility after a conditional offer of employment is made as well as ongoing eligibility. For more information, please visit https://info.flclearinghouse.com/. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
