item.title: Senior State Government Relations Manager (Southern Region)
item.description: Senior State Government Relations Manager (Southern Region) Organization: The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research (“the Foundation”) Location: Tallahassee, FL Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Position Summary: The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research (“the Foundation”) is seeking top talent for its Senior State Government Relations Manager in the Southern Region of the United States. Reporting to the Director of State Government Relations, this position assists in developing, communicating, and clarifying the Foundation’s stance on legislation, regulations, and other proposals to state lawmakers, regulators, and government officials. This role monitors legislative and regulatory activities, identifies relevant areas for the Foundation, and maintains strategic relationships with state elected officials and agency staff. This individual’s legislative portfolio will cover the Southern Region of the United States. This position will be based remotely within the following states: AL, AR, FL, GA, KY, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC, TN, TX, VA, and WV. Key Responsibilities: Legislative Affairs: Develop, communicate, and explain the Foundation’s position on legislation, regulations, and other proposals to state lawmakers, regulators, and other government officials, with oversight and supervision from manager Manage a portfolio of states within assigned territory in the country Lead legislative and regulatory priorities and identify areas of importance to the Foundation Build and maintain strategic relationships with state lawmakers, staff, and agencies Draft written testimony, talking points, briefings, and PowerPoint Presentations for various audiences. Provide in-person and remote legislative testimony before legislative committees and external stakeholder organizations including but not limited to, other Parkinson’s organizations and non-Parkinson’s organizations Issue Monitoring and Analysis: Stay informed about legislative and regulatory developments at the state level that may impact the Foundation’s community. Conduct thorough analysis to assess potential implications and inform strategic advocacy efforts Develop subject matter expertise on a range of policy issues that impact the Parkinson’s community Advocacy Efforts: Work in a team environment in conjunction with the Foundation’s Advocacy team toward more “in-state” policy-oriented events such as Lobby Days and coordinated coalition efforts with the patient community Duties may include assistance with planning and logistics regarding policy-related events and webinars Coalition Engagement: Support creating and maintaining strong relationships with other research, healthcare, and patient organizations. As assigned, serve as the Foundation’s representative in various coalitions and work groups Develop and build relationships for coalition engagement opportunities to support overall government relations priorities Team Administration/Operations: Attend staff meetings, internal and external coalition group meetings, support and/or manage other duties as they are assigned Compliance and Reporting: Ensure compliance with relevant lobbying and disclosure requirements, and accurately report on advocacy activities, expenditures, and outcomes Qualifications and Skills: Relevant experience working in state government affairs, public policy, public relations, political campaigns, trade association, nonprofit organization or a related role Relevant experience working directly with state lawmakers is preferred Ability to register as a state lobbyist in multiple states Strong organization and time management skills, acute attention to detail, and knowledge of MS Office (including Excel, PowerPoint and Word) are essential Ability to synthesize large amounts of information into compelling, actionable insights, and an understanding of the political landscape Demonstrated ability to research and grasp complex policy issues. History of effective interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills evidenced in part through successful presentations Resourceful, results oriented, team-player Working knowledge of SharePoint, Quorum, and Salesforce Ability to collaborate with team members to accomplish project goals and also be able to operate independently and take on projects proactively Approximately 20% day or overnight travel during peak legislative season to various states for legislative hearings, lobby days, press conferences, and other related events Occasional overnight or day travel to NYC office, Washington, D.C., local events, and events around the country. Minimal to occasional evening/weekend work Compensation & Benefits Individual compensation for this role is dependent on a variety of factors, including, but not limited to, qualifications, skillsets, and applicable laws. In addition to salary, the Foundation offers a comprehensive benefits package, including: 15+ options for medical insurance (with the Foundation paying 90 percent of the premiums) Competitive dental and vision plans 401(k) plan with 6 percent employer contribution Flexible spending accounts Employer paid life and disability insurance 18 Vacation Days; 12 Well-Being (Sick) Days; 2 Personal Days; summer Fridays (office closure at 2pm) and a summer holiday week over July 4 Flexible work environment. We trust all employees to work closely with their manager and colleagues to determine when, where and how programs and projects get done. Employees are also eligible for a discretionary bonus on an annual basis. The Foundation provides staff and leadership cultivation through regular training courses and events. Salary Range $110,000 – $130,000 USD How to Apply: Interested candidates should submit a resume and thoughtful cover letter describing through examples, their specific qualifications and interest in the position here . If you think that your skills are transferable and can add value to this role, please apply . Applicants who best match the position’s needs will be contacted. About Us: The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research was founded in 2000 with one clear objective: accelerating meaningful therapeutic advances and, ultimately, a cure for Parkinson’s disease (PD). The Foundation applies extraordinary scientific, business and media assets to this singular focus—thus creating a unique and dynamic organization. Since inception, MJFF has quickly grown into the largest nonprofit funder of Parkinson’s disease research, having funded over $2 billion in research projects in both academic and industry labs worldwide. Visit www.michaeljfox.org for more information. Research has shown that people from marginalized communities apply to roles only when they meet 100% of the job requirements. If you think that your skills are transferable and can add value to this role, and you are someone who will contribute to our efforts to build and support a diverse, equitable and inclusive workforce, we strongly encourage you to apply. item.title: Policy Strategist
item.description: Policy Strategist Organization: American Civil Liberties Union of New Jersey (ACLU-NJ) Location: Newark, NJ Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Position Overview The American Civil Liberties Union of New Jersey (ACLU-NJ) seeks a creative, strategic champion of civil rights and liberties to join our team as a policy strategist. The policy strategist will work collaboratively across the organization and alongside allied community partners, using strategic policy advocacy tactics to advance bold and impactful change in areas such as privacy and technology protection, racial justice, criminal legal reform, democracy and voting rights, and immigration. The ideal candidate has strong policy research and analysis skills, a deep understanding of advocacy tactics to influence policymakers and elected officials, and a commitment to advancing civil rights and liberties for all New Jerseyans. Organizational Overview For more than 60 years, the ACLU of New Jersey has defended liberty and justice guided by the vision of a fair and equitable New Jersey for all. Our mission is to preserve, advance, and extend the individual rights and liberties guaranteed to every New Jerseyan by the state and federal constitutions in courts, in the legislature, and in our communities. We are committed to repairing and transforming spaces where constitutional promises have not been delivered. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Legislative Advocacy and Policy Strategy Advance ACLU-NJ’s legislative and public policy agenda at the federal, state, city, and county levels. Research and analyze laws and policies affecting New Jersey communities. Develop and implement lobbying and advocacy strategies with the legislature, governor’s office, and other government bodies. Track legislation and support advocacy during legislative and special sessions, including testimony, briefing materials, policy recommendations, and meetings with policymakers. Build bipartisan relationships and use data to inform policy priorities. Develop advocacy materials, including testimony, policy papers, fact sheets, talking points, letters, guides, and public commentary. Relationship Building and Community Partnerships Build and maintain relationships with government officials, community leaders, allied organizations, legislative staff, agencies, and lobbyists. Represent ACLU-NJ in community groups, coalitions, working groups, and stakeholder meetings. Partner with the community engagement team to involve members and volunteers in legislative advocacy. Communications and External Relations Support communications on priority legislation and campaigns, including social media, website updates, action emails, bill summaries, talking points, and videos. Occasionally serve as an organizational spokesperson through media interviews, op-eds, and articles. Represent ACLU-NJ at public forums, conferences, meetings, and other external events. Reporting and Administrative Duties Maintain organized policy records, resources, legislative calendars, and advocacy timelines. Prepare reports and updates on legislative developments, advocacy activities, and outcomes. Support departmental planning, project management, and administrative needs. Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging Advance ACLU-NJ’s commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging in advocacy strategies, organizational practices, and community partnerships. Contribute to department and organization-wide efforts to ensure programs, policies, and engagement practices are inclusive, equitable, and responsive to impacted communities. Candidate Requirements The successful candidate will possess many of the following qualifications and attributes. If you are excited about the position but unsure whether or not you are qualified, we encourage you to apply. At least two years of experience in public policy advocacy and research at state or local levels. Demonstrated commitment to civil rights and civil liberties consistent with the mission and goals of ACLU-NJ. Excellent policy analysis, research, and written and oral advocacy skills, including the ability to articulate complex issues and communicate them effectively to various audiences. Experience with legislative procedures, bill drafting, policy development, and analysis. Ability to proactively build and cultivate effective relationships across the political spectrum. Familiarity with the New Jersey political landscape, state and local government issues, and the legislative process. Experience working in coalition, including developing shared plans, coordinating communications, and managing dynamics among partner groups. Demonstrated commitment to centering the voices and leadership of directly impacted people and communities. Ability to stay organized in a fast-paced environment, manage several projects simultaneously, and adjust to frequently changing demands while maintaining strong attention to detail. Ability to work independently and in a team environment with support and collaboration from the supervisor. Willingness and ability to work irregular hours, especially during the legislative session, and to attend occasional evening and weekend meetings. Experience using relevant technical tools and knowledge-sharing resources, e.g., legislative tracking tools, databases, etc. Comfortability producing qualitative and quantitative data analytics. Preferred Qualifications: The following are not required, but will strengthen a candidate’s application: Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish (or another language spoken by New Jersey communities). Existing relationships with members of the New Jersey congressional delegation, members of the NJ legislature, or their staff. Experience working on civil rights, criminal justice reform, immigrant rights, LGBTQ+ rights, or voting rights campaigns. Experience with federal agency advocacy or administrative rulemaking processes. Experience using legislative tracking tools. Compensation The salary range for this position is $80,000, commensurate with experience based on the ACLU-NJ salary bands. The ACLU-NJ supports and plans for staff member professional growth and skill development through internal and external opportunities. We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package which currently includes 30 days paid time off, 12 office holidays and 16 health care leave days; medical, vision, and dental insurance; 20 weeks (100 days) paid family leave; life and long-term disability insurance; pre-tax transit benefits; and a 401(k) plan with employer match. This position is exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act. About our Culture We are a diverse workforce and take pride in our ability to attract and retain employees with a huge array of backgrounds and experiences. We work hard but also like to celebrate our successes. We strive to bring humility, empathy, kindness, and generosity to our work, internally within the organization and externally with our partners and those whom we are serving. We seek to build a work culture with a sense of respect and collegiality, and a willingness to be generous with our expertise and resources. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager/Senior Manager Communications
item.description: Manager/Senior Manager Communications Organization: Alliance of Community Health Plans (ACHP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Reports to: Director of Communications Location: Washington, D.C. Compensation: $65,000 – $110,000, plus generous benefits package COMPANY PROFILE The Alliance of Community Health Plans (ACHP) represents the nation’s top-performing nonprofit health organizations to improve affordability and outcomes in health care. ACHP member organizations embrace a unique partnership model in health care, bringing together health plans and providers on behalf of the patients and communities they serve. ACHP advocates on behalf of its members, highlighting tested solutions impacting communities nationwide and a proven approach that delivers better value for patients, employers and taxpayers. ACHP is committed to a diverse workforce that respects all points of view. We encourage different perspectives, identities and backgrounds, regardless of job function, to create a more resilient organization that supports a strong, equitable health industry. We foster this by encouraging openness and transparency that creates opportunities for all. POSITION SUMMARY ACHP seeks an enthusiastic, experienced communications professional to execute a strategy that advances its vision and mission. As a central member of the communications team, this individual will bring creative and strategic thinking to a fast-paced Washington, DC, advocacy organization. The successful candidate will be passionate about shaping messages at the intersection of politics, policy and health care. Working collaboratively across ACHP, this person will help tell the distinctive story of local health plans partnering closely with clinicians. The ideal candidate is a self-starter, skilled writer and editor and trusted multitasker who can support both member and external communications. This results-oriented role requires exceptional attention to detail and offers significant opportunities for professional development and career growth. CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Media Engagement (40%) Partner with the Communications Director to drive consistent coverage of ACHP, its member companies and initiatives. Conduct proactive media pushes, manage incoming requests and facilitate interviews. Nurture press relationships, including expanding ACHP’s network of reporter contacts. Develop press releases, media statements, op-eds and talking points. Manage daily monitoring of news clips. Oversee media contact databases including national, trade and digital media. Content Development (35%) Lead the creation and design of high-quality communications collateral, including advocacy one-pagers, issue briefs, infographics, member communications, e-newsletters and the ACHP annual report. Project manage multiple communications endeavors, including major reports and publications. Work closely with vendors and external consultants. In partnership with other teams, brainstorm and create new collateral and manage updates to existing collateral. Serve as backup for social and website content. Thought Leadership (15%) Manage ACHP’s external speaking engagement calendar and research and secure speaking opportunities for ACHP leadership and subject matter experts. Manage policy influencer contact database and communications. Assist with speeches/presentations, including slide creation and talking points, for ACHP CEO and other leadership. Member Engagement (10%) Develop marketing strategy, in partnership with Communications Director, for ACHP events, including creating email campaigns and designing event branding and collateral. Build and maintain strong working relationships with communications leads at member companies. Gather and develop member plan stories for use in advocacy and media efforts. Demonstrate continued knowledge of industry and member issues. Other duties as assigned. PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND OTHER QUALIFICATIONS Required Bachelor’s degree in communications, Journalism, English or related field. At least 3 years of communications experience – at least 5 years for senior manager – in complex settings; health care, policy and/or nonprofit communications experience a plus. Strong project management abilities, capable of advancing multiple communications priorities and working independently with a strong sense of urgency under tight deadlines. Strong skills using MS Office applications (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Publisher). Expertise using social media and digital tools to reach target audiences. Exceptional writing and editing skills with the ability to boil down complex issues and data into easy-to-understand, compelling messaging. Functional proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Premiere, Photoshop). Preferred Knowledge of federal health policy and/or community health plan business is a plus. Significant experience using AI in the communications realm with tools such as ChatGPT, Claude and Granola. Experience working with the news media, with a record of print media placement a plus. Clear understanding of membership organizations and how to elevate the voice of member companies. WORKING CONDITIONS Work is in an office environment, with three in-office days per week. Must reside in the DMV area. Position is hybrid but not remote. Some travel required. APPLICATION PROCESS Please send your resume and cover letter to ACHP Human Resources at [email protected] . Include ‘Manager/Senior Manager, Communications’ followed by your first initial and last name in the subject line of your email. ACHP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, citizenship status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, related medical conditions, and a woman’s right to breastfeed), disability (physical or mental), age (18 and older), genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, matriculation, family responsibilities, personal appearance, political affiliation, marital status, veteran or military status, tobacco use, credit information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. We do not sponsor applicants for work visas. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: LIBRE Regional Field Manager
item.description: LIBRE Regional Field Manager Organization: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) Location: Harrisburg, PA Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Job Description Rooted in the Hispanic community, The LIBRE Initiative brings people together to advance public policy solutions that create the freedom and opportunity that people need to chase their American Dream. LIBRE empowers our communities by fixing our broken immigration system, encouraging affordable and flexible healthcare options, building an individualized education system, and promoting a robust economy that helps everyone succeed. The LIBRE Initiative is a part of Americans for Prosperity and the Stand Together philanthropic community. As a Regional Field Manager (internally referred to as a Grassroots Engagement Director) you will identify, recruit, and engage grassroots leaders in the Harrisburg Tri-County area and mobilize them to take action, and drive policy reforms that open opportunities for all. How You Will Contribute Identify activists in various parts of the state who are currently – or could become leaders – in their local communities, and motivate them to advocate for change. Equip these local leaders to advocate for changes that are consistent with principles LIBRE believes in. You will do this, in part, by connecting them to the training and other resources of LIBRE. Organize events where you and other activists can engage the public through phone calls, social media, walking through neighborhoods to talk with people face-to-face. You’ll also be free to innovate by creating fun or unique ways to reach people to educate them on public policy issues and initiatives. Ensure that the LIBRE Initiative stays in regular contact with our activists to keep them motivated, educated, and active. Manage part-time canvassing contractors, including but not limited to, time management, compliance with laws and regulations, and best practices. What You Will Bring Passion for people, ability to build relationships quickly with people from all walks of life, and understand how to inspire and motivate them. Knowledge of state and federal public policy landscapes. Self-motivation, always looking for the best way to use your time to accomplish objectives. Organization skills and the ability to keep multiple events and activities on track for yourself and the people you engage to help you. Works well with a team of people, including LIBRE staff and activists. Excitement to canvass neighborhoods and make phone calls for LIBRE and AFP priority initiatives and AFP Action endorsed candidates, as well as motivate and coordinate volunteers to do the same. A valid driver’s license to be able to travel to meet with people in your area and across the state, as needed. Willingness to work a flexible and changing work schedule, including evenings and weekends as needed. Integrity, humility, and an entrepreneurial attitude. Enthusiasm to contribute to Stand Together’s vision and principled approach to solving problems, and a commitment to stewarding our culture, which champions values including transformation and innovation, entrepreneurialism, humility, and respect. Standout Candidates Will Bring Fluency in Spanish and English. Experience in grassroots advocacy, community organization, and/or political campaigns. Volunteer or staff supervisory experience. What We Offer Competitive benefits: Enjoy a 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting, flexible time off, comprehensive health and dental plans, plus wellness and mental health support through Peloton and Talkspace. A meaningful career: Join a passionate community of over 1,400 employees dedicated to improving lives and driving innovative solutions to complex social challenges. Commitment to growth: Thrive in a non-hierarchical environment that empowers employees to discover, develop and apply their unique talents. Competitive compensation: Our approach rewards the value you create through competitive salaries and bonus opportunities, allowing you to share in the success you help drive. Our Values: Working for an organization within the Stand Together philanthropic community is different from many other places. The culture is deeply rooted in Principle Based Management® (PBM®), a framework guided by the principles that drive human progress, such as dignity, openness, and bottom-up empowerment. PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. That is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, and respect. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Government Affairs Sr. Coordinator
item.description: Government Affairs Sr. Coordinator Organization: Smithbucklin Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/28/2026 Smithbucklin, a 650-person, employee-owned professional services company with more than 70 years of success serving the association market, with primary offices in Chicago and Washington, D.C., is looking for a Government Affairs Sr. Coordinator to join our team in our D.C. office. Smithbucklin, a 100 percent employee-owned association management company, is looking for a Government Affairs Sr. Coordinator to serve our clients, the National Association of Local Housing Finance Agencies and the National Association for County Community and Economic Development. The Sr. Coordinator is responsible for the development, management and execution of legislative and regulatory initiatives at the federal and state levels, working with volunteer committees, managing grassroots activities, working with industry coalitions, and communicating legislative and regulatory activities in association publications, webinars, podcasts and at conferences. At Smithbucklin, we embody a culture driven by optimism, ambition, expertise, and thoughtfulness, where every team member is empowered to exceed expectations and deliver exceptional results for our clients. Join us in shaping the future of association management, where our values serve as the cornerstone of our success. What You Will Do: • Research, analyze and summarize legislative and regulatory issues impacting the client associations. • Collect and analyze relevant proposed regulations and legislation at the federal and state level. • Represent the client associations before policymakers and in industry coalitions. • Manage the grassroots activities and databases for both client associations. • Provide primary staff support to client Government Affairs Committees. • Manage client legislative/regulatory tracking and grassroots databases. • Develop issue alerts and press releases on key issues. • Write and produce content for association member e-newsletters, websites, webinars and podcasts. • Regularly communicate with association volunteers on industry and association issues. • Assist in preparation of association conferences and meetings. Basic Qualifications: • Bachelors degree from a four-year accredited college/university. • 3-5 years’ experience in government, agency, non-profit management or related industry. • PC experience with Windows operating system. • Strong interpersonal skills and focus on customer service. • Strong written communication skills. • Strong verbal, public speaking and communication skills. • Proficient in time management and organizational skills. Preferred Qualifications: • Experience with single and multi-family affordable housing programs, such as HOME Investment Partnerships Program, Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC), Private Activity Bonds (PABs). • Experience working with the White House Administration, Federal Agencies, including U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and U.S. Department of Treasury. Where Do You Fit? Whether you are just beginning your career or are a mid- or senior-level professional, working at Smithbucklin will offer you countless opportunities to develop transferable skills, acquire meaningful knowledge and gain rich experiences at an accelerated pace. By working collaboratively with smart, ambitious, multi-talented, genuine and hardworking colleagues, you will build meaningful, deep and enduring relationships that will serve you well throughout your career, regardless of your chosen path. In addition, as a 100 percent employee-owned company, Smithbucklin offers all of our people – regardless of position or compensation – an equal chance to experience the fulfillment and reap the benefits of ownership. As owners, our employees control the destiny of Smithbucklin and are unified in the goal of building a great, enduring company. Smithbucklin is a hybrid work environment with in-office days established as Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Employees will work a standard 40-hour week, with the possibility of additional hours based on project deadlines. Smithbucklin considers several factors when determining compensation, including a candidate’s recent coursework, training, experience, and certifications, among other considerations. The expected pay for this role is $71,000-$75,000. Equal Employment Opportunity At Smithbucklin, Equal Employment Opportunity is our commitment and goal. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status or any other protected status designated by federal, state or local law. Applicants are encouraged to confidentially self-identify when applying. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a reference and background investigation based on position. Smithbucklin will not sponsor applicants for work visas and as a precondition of employment. You must be authorized to work in the United States permanently. item.title: Strategic Communications Specialist
item.description: Strategic Communications Specialist Organization: LV8D Solutions Location: Chantilly, VA Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Description Mission Context LV8D Solutions supports national security space and intelligence customers delivering next-generation sensing and exploitation capabilities. has an opportunity for a Strategic Communications Specialist in Chantilly, VA to provide direct strategic communication support. Position Overview LV8D Solutions is looking for a Strategic Communications Specialist. The selected individual will identify and create connections with fellow communicators across IC, DoD and civilian agencies to communicate the mission, goals, and strategies. Additionally, the individual will provide program advocacy to agencies and intelligence users via multiple media types to increase awareness of satellite capabilities and the data they provide Note: An active Top Secret/SCI clearance with Poly is required to be considered for this role Interested candidates need to thrive in an innovative, fast-paced environment; are highly motivated and not afraid to take on uncharted territory; possess strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills; and be able to prioritize their time to be effective in a dynamic environment. Requirements Key Responsibilities Expand awareness of customer priorities across stakeholder audiences by preparing and delivering a wide-range of internal and external products and documents including high-level intelligence briefings, intelligence summaries, news articles, website content, video scripts, speeches and more. Fulfill the role of liaison between customer and its larger Office of Public Affairs via regular communication to ensure coordination of communications initiatives, receive feedback in the development and approval for communication products, and seek opportunities for customer participation in external engagements. Work closely with customer program offices to produce content based on specific program office needs (e.g. program advocacy, increased user engagement, and increase awareness of new capability) for internal and external publication. Identify, build and maintain connections with communicators across IC, DoD, and civilian agencies where customer publications would have meaningful impact, and regularly submit content to those outlets. Establish standardization and consistency between customer leadership, program offices and outreach teams to relay the customer mission in a cohesive manner. Serve as lead writer responsible for developing content for newsletter, articles, scripts, congressional testimony and more. Develop tailored briefs and talking points for leadership upon request. Assist in the planning, coordination, marketing and content creation for all customer mission-related events/conferences. Learn and brief customer material when necessary, where user outreach support is needed. Required Qualifications: BA in Broadcast Journalism, Communications, or similar discipline with 15 years or more experience; Masters and 13 or PhD and five 10 or more years of experience in strategic communications, public affairs, or media relations. Experience developing communication products (presentations, graphics, videos, articles and fact sheets). Experience interfacing with Senior leaders to develop internal and external communication strategies, messaging approaches, branding campaigns, engagement plans, etc. Exceptional written, public speaking, and interpersonal skills. Desired Qualifications: MA in Broadcast Journalism, Public Affairs, Communications, or similar discipline. Security Requirements: U.S. Citizenship Active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance Active Counterintelligence (CI) or Full Scope (FS) Polygraph Work Environment: On-site work in a government or contractor facility Occasional travel (up to 10%) About LV8D Solutions LV8D Solutions is an elite Systems Engineering and Technical Advisory (SETA) company that delivers advanced systems engineering, integration, acquisition, mission operations, network communications, and cybersecurity support to our defense and intelligence customers. Founded in 2019, we apply our deep technical expertise, understanding, and mission-first mindset to design, acquire, and implement complex, high-impact solutions for our Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of War (DoW) customers. We specialize in every aspect of our customers’ space and ground mission systems while offering exceptional work-life balance and an exemplary compensation and total rewards package designed to recruit, train, and retain top talent and committed to national defense and career growth. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement LV8D Solutions LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity and inclusion. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, religion, gender, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other protected categories. Benefits Performance & Recognition Period of Performance (PoP) Bonus Opportunities Performance-based bonus opportunities tied to contract or organizational performance. Retention Incentive Benefit Bounty Receive a payout for unused annual company contributions designated for health insurance premiums and professional training. Referral Bonus Earn up to $5,000 for each successful employee referral. Customer Recognition Letter of Appreciation (LoA) Bonus Opportunities Bonus opportunities based on customer recognition received through Letters of Appreciation. Milestone Rewards Celebrate your career achievements with anniversary awards on your 1st, 5th, 10th, and 20th years of service. Financial & Retirement Benefits Profit Sharing Receive an annual contribution equal to 4% of your W-2 gross earnings into your 401(k), with immediate vesting. 401(k) Company Match The company matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to 6% of your monthly contribution, with immediate vesting. Career Development The company invests in your professional growth through: Annual financial support for professional training and industry certifications. Enhanced financial support for employees actively pursuing a degree at an accredited institution. Work-Life Balance Support for a healthy work-life balance includes: Flexible work hours Competitive paid time off (PTO) Company holidays Health & Wellness Benefits The company offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family. Medical Coverage Three comprehensive Medical/Rx insurance plan options to meet the unique and individualized benefit needs of our employees Dental & Vision Comprehensive dental insurance for employees and eligible dependents. item.title: Senior Manager, Social Media Campaigns & Content
item.description: Senior Manager, Social Media Campaigns & Content Organization: National Geographic Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Job Summary: National Geographic is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Social Media to lead creative social campaigns across Editorial content and TV programming. In this role, you will be a key contributor in planning, managing and executing the social marketing strategy focused on content strategy for editorial digital stories, magazine features, and TV programming. The Senior Manager will lead best-in-class creative execution from production through launch, with an audience-first approach that ladders up to key business goals: growing magazine and digital subscriptions, driving acquisition to Disney+, and enhancing brand affinity. To be successful, you will need to be a storyteller and marketer with excellent judgement to balance audience interests and business goals. You’ll have a deep passion, appreciation, and understanding of editorial and entertainment broadly, with a deep breadth of knowledge spanning Natural History/Animal, Science, History, Travel and Adventure, Culture, and Kids topics. Responsibilities: Project Management & Leadership Serve as a social lead and strategic partner to Nat Geo Editorial & Content teams, participating in story planning and all phases of content production. Establish best-in-class approaches to campaigns, content & distribution. Partner with subject matter experts, photographers, explorers, and creators to develop content tied to key initiatives. Influence upstream planning to ensure social is embedded early. Lead the development of tentpole social moments. Content Development & Production Oversee the end-to-end creative pipeline – ideation and creative direction through production and final sign-off from leadership and stakeholders. Partner with agency partners, creative teams, platform strategists, PR, and talent representatives to ensure all output ladders up to the overarching social strategy. Direct hands-on production of social-first content, including talent and subject-matter-expert interviews, on-set creative direction, and social video shoots. Creator Content Strategy Guide creative ideation, campaign development, and execution for creator initiatives. Partner with Content, Marketing, PR/Comms, Editorial, and Creative teams to develop innovative creator-first content experiences across owned and earned channels. Champion experimentation with emerging content formats while maintaining brand integrity and audience relevance. Innovation & Growth Drive testing and learning across platforms, formats, and tools. Identify and scale new opportunities to expand reach and influence. Measurement & Performance Review social platform and Adobe Analytics data to identify high-performing stories and the content patterns that drive audience growth and conversion to NatGeo.com. Use data, insights, and social intelligence to continuously optimize strategy. Establish clear success metrics that go beyond engagement to reflect impact. Cross-Functional Leadership Partner closely with Editorial, Strategy, PR/Comms, Paid Media, Synergy, and Partnerships teams to ensure integrated planning and execution. Team Leadership & Operations Lead, develop, and scale a high-performing team. Set a high bar for quality, clarity, and execution across all work. Build systems and processes that enable speed, consistency, and innovation. Basic Qualifications: 7+ years’ experience in social media strategy and marketing, preferably managing large-scale brand or media portfolios. Demonstrated expertise across major social platforms (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Reddit) with a strong understanding of platform ecosystems and trends. Proven track record developing and executing data-driven social strategies that drive audience growth, engagement, and brand impact. Experience launching creator-led franchises, original programming, or large-scale digital content initiatives. Deep understanding of the creator economy, creator monetization models, audience behaviors, and evolving platform ecosystems. Strong campaign leadership experience, translating marketing priorities into integrated, platform-native social activations. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, partnering with editorial, marketing, creative, and external stakeholders. Experience managing external partners or agencies, including oversight of publishing, community management, and performance reporting. Deep understanding of content production workflows, with the ability to optimize and evolve processes for speed, scale, and quality. Strong experience developing creator-led content strategies across platforms including TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat, and emerging digital channels. Proficiency with social media management, analytics, and reporting tools, with the ability to translate insights into actionable strategies. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present strategies and performance insights to stakeholders. Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities, operate in fast-paced environments, and meet deadlines. Proficiency with project management tools- AirTable, Asana, etc. Experience managing large budgets. Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to experiment with new digital formats and platforms. Proven ability to operate with sound judgment in issues-sensitive environments. Creative, proactive, and independent thinking. Strong solutions-oriented mindset. Experience with social media content management and reporting systems. Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Advertising, Digital/Social, TV/Film preferred. The hiring range for this position in Washington, D.C. is $112,700 to $154,800 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered. item.title: Senior Manager, Government Affairs and Policy
item.description: Senior Manager, Government Affairs and Policy Organization: National Public Radio (NPR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 OVERVIEW A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR. Intro to Position Under NPR’s Employee Code of Conduct, the Senior Manager, Policy and Representation will be considered “Outward-Facing Employee”, and as such should (i) avoid public participation in political and partisan activities in order to protect NPR’s reputation and its ability to pursue its mission; and (ii) refrain from public statements or actions that might call into question NPR’s commitment to accuracy and fairness. Application Deadline The application window will be open until Friday, October 9, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Responsibilities Track, analyze, and brief internal leadership on legislative, regulatory, and industry developments impacting NPR, including copyright, artificial intelligence, telecommunications, and privacy policy. Build and maintain a sophisticated political network across Capitol Hill and federal agencies, serving as a registered lobbyist; manage LDA compliance activities pertaining to NPR. Meet with Hill staff, including Committees relevant to NPR, to educate them on NPR and its role and impact in the public radio system. Conduct in-depth research on Members of Congress and executive branch officials to develop effective political and advocacy strategies. Lead NPR’s representation with federal regulatory bodies, including the Federal Communications Commission, including monitoring regulatory developments and collaborating with internal offices to evaluate and respond to the impacts of FCC proceedings on public radio. Proactively build and maintain relationships with associations, media industry organizations, and other national-level stakeholders that engage on matters of importance to NPR; represent NPR policy perspectives at the national level. Research and track upcoming congressional events, industry convenings and administrative policy announcements and keep NPR leadership informed on policy developments relevant to NPR. Partner with the NPR Sr. Manager for Communications & Engagement on communications to a wide variety of policy stakeholders. The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time. Minimum Qualifications Excellent skills in tracking legislative and policy developments and demonstrated policy experience in copyright, artificial intelligence, telecommunications or privacy issues. Existing professional networks on the Hill, particularly in telecommunications or AI policy. Experience navigating the legislative process and working on nonpartisan advocacy initiatives. Strong verbal and written communication skills, particularly in supporting external policy-related communications across a wide range of stakeholders. Proficient in the use of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Google suite products Exceptional organizational and time management skills and ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously. Collaborative working style, experience working in small teams, and the ability to complete high-quality independent work. Preferred Qualifications Experience creating new programs, policies or coalitions to advance company outcomes Experience representing media organizations within their industry and in other industries that affect media Affinity for public radio’s mission and service Experience working with a variety of stakeholders and external partners on complex policy issues Education Requirements Bachelor’s degree in public policy, government affairs, journalism or related field Work Location & Requirements Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role require duties better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the Washington, D.C. office 3 days per week, on Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. The employee must also reside in an NPR-supported location. Job Type This is a full-time, exempt position. Compensation Salary Range: The anticipated U.S.-based salary range for this opportunity is $147,000-$165,000, plus benefits. The displayed range reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to offer new hires for the position across all US locations. NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees. Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you. Apply here #LI-HYBRID The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations. NPR Pay Range $147,000 – $165,000 USD NPR is an Equal Opportunity Employer. NPR is committed to being an inclusive workplace that welcomes diverse and unique perspectives, all working toward the same goal – to create a more informed public. Qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, age, religion, religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, lactation, and reproductive health decisions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, transgender status, gender non-conforming status, intersex status, sexual stereotypes, nationality, citizenship status, personal appearance, marital status, family status, family responsibilities, military status, veteran status, mental and physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, genetic characteristics of yourself or a family member, political views and affiliation, unemployment status, protective order status, status as a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking, or any other basis prohibited under applicable law. item.title: Manager, Communications
item.description: Manager, Communications Organization: National Public Radio (NPR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 OVERVIEW A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR. Application Deadline: Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST on Friday, October 2nd, 2026. Intro to Position This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with DMU. The Manager, Communications supports NPR’s institutional communications, helping manage day-to-day media inquiries, departmental logistics, coverage tracking, and social media execution. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Corporate Communications, this role serves as an operational engine for the Communications team, ensuring efficient handling of incoming press requests, smooth execution of speaking appearances, and dynamic public engagement across social channels. The Manager plays a central role in managing the main media relations queue, facilitating approvals, producing media coverage reports, and contributing to NPR Extra social channels to highlight organizational milestones, champion journalists and talent, and share behind-the-scenes content that reinforces NPR’s value to the public. The ideal candidate is a proactive, highly organized, and media-savvy communicator with strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to balance multiple fast-moving priorities. Responsibilities Media relations and speaker queue management Manage the central media relations and speaker queues for all incoming press and event requests involving NPR talent, journalists, and executives. Oversee the vetting process for incoming media inquiries and speaking invitations, ensuring proper routing, internal reviews, and executive approvals. Escalate sensitive, complex, or high-risk requests to the Senior Manager and Vice President, Communications. Serve as a responsive, professional primary contact point for journalists, event organizers, and external organizations. Departmental coordination and logistical support Manage end-to-end logistics for executive and talent speaking appearances, panel invitations, and press interviews. Coordinate scheduling, gather briefing materials, and prepare logistical details for leadership and talent appearances. Draft backgrounders, event prep notes, briefing documents, and administrative materials to support engagements. Social media and digital PR Drive content development for NPR Extra social channels to highlight organizational milestones, champion journalists and talent, and share behind-the-scenes content that reinforces NPR’s value to the public. Translate corporate milestones, institutional announcements, and PR wins into compelling social content tailored for industry and public audiences. Coordinate with internal design, brand, and social teams to align visuals and messaging across channels. Media monitoring and analytics Track, compile, and distribute regular media coverage reports to internal stakeholders and executive leadership. Monitor industry trends, news developments, and mentions of NPR across digital and print publications. Oversee PR analytics, tracking campaign performance, media reach, and social engagement metrics to evaluate communications impact. The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time. Minimum Qualifications 3–5 years of experience in public relations. Excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Strong project management and organizational abilities. Experience coordinating projects involving multiple stakeholders. Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills. Ability to train more junior staff at basic skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing stakeholder communications. Familiarity with project management software and collaboration tools. Experience developing presentations and briefing materials. Required Skills/Competencies Exceptional writing and editing skills. Strong organization and attention to detail. Excellent project management skills. Strong collaboration and relationship-building abilities. Sound judgment and professionalism. Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic environment. Initiative and follow-through. A commitment to accuracy, quality, and continuous improvement. Education Requirements Equivalent hands-on experience, in lieu of a bachelor’s degree Work Location & Requirements Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. item.title: Senior Digital Media Advisor
item.description: Senior Digital Media Advisor Organization: Third Way Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Third Way is a national think tank and advocacy organization that champions moderate policy and political ideas. Since our founding in 2005, we have served as a critical bulwark against political extremism by advancing values-driven, reform-oriented solutions on the defining issues of our time. Our work is grounded in the mainstream American values of opportunity, freedom, security, and democratic capitalism, and we advocate for the vital center across seven major areas: climate and energy, economy, education, health care, national security, politics, and social policy. Third is looking for a Senior Digital Media Advisor to manage Third Way’s social media strategy and platforms as a means to participate in the political conversation, interact with journalists and influencers, and to promote Third Way’s views, campaigns, and products. This role will have a big impact in national politics including the race for the White House, elevating a generation of center-left leaders, building durable majorities in Congress, and bolstering the broader moderate movement. The Senior Digital Media Advisor is ideal for someone who is highly creative, able to identify openings in national political and policy conversations and can create engaging content using basic design and video editing tools. As the Senior Digital Media Advisor, a typical day might include… Drafting timely, creative digital content on Third Way’s political narrative and policy products; Preparing the strategy for Third Way’s digital communications outreach in collaboration with the Deputy Director of Marketing and manages the development and execution of tactics to implement that strategy and monitor the progress; Developing Third Way’s year-round advertising plan across platforms in partnership with the Deputy Director of Marketing. Oversees the execution, monitors and proposes adjustments where necessary to ensure the success of the plan; Leading topic specific, multi-platform digital campaigns as assigned; Partnering with Third Way communications staff and program staff on digital campaign plans for paid advertisements, drafting copy, preparing audience targets, proposing and collaborating on creative development, and monitoring their progress; Identifying opportunities for the Third Way handle and other organizational accounts and spokespeople to engage in the political conversation online and build relationships with influential people and groups; Monitoring important digital conversations for Third Way’s engagement and flags opportunities for relevant senior leaders; Pitching and executing digital content in a variety of mediums (eg. video, graphics, tweet threads); Tracking and monitoring Third Way’s brand performance and the progress toward our digital objectives; Collaborating with Third Way teams to help plan and execute digital content for events and product roll-outs; Advising and training Third Way staff and programs on best practices for the platforms and digital communications; May supervisor staff; and Performing other duties as assigned. —————————————– Salary Range: $84,000 – $95,000, annually At Third Way, we are committed to non-discrimination and fair pay practices. The final starting salary offer will be determined based on your experience and qualifications. Job requirements Competencies: Written Communication Storytelling Creativity Digital literacy Problem Solving Critical Thinking Interpersonal skills Analytical & Research Skills Political awareness Knowledge Management Accountability for Self Respectfulness This might be the job for you, if you have… An undergraduate degree in a relevant field plus 3-5 years relevant work experience in US government, on a political campaign, as a journalist, or in the private sector. An understanding of US politics and its major Democratic players; Video editing and design skills are highly desired; A solid grasp of online culture and norms and excellent judgment on which norms and language are a good fit for the organization; A demonstrated ability to write accurate, pithy, culturally relevant content for a wide audience; Passion for creative storytelling; Experience interacting with and responding to high impact organizations and leaders on social media; Familiarity with paid advertising on social platforms; and Comfort working in digital platforms and programs potentially including the Adobe suite, Canva, and Snapstream. In the Third Way Culture, we are looking for: Self-starters: People who see and seize opportunities, take risks, learn from failure, and will bring a sustained passion for our mission. Collaborators: People who work in teams—sharing ideas, brainstorming, co-authoring products, and advancing our shared priorities. Creators: People who foster divergent thinking; who aren’t afraid to take on the orthodoxies of the left or the right. Team members come up with original insights, find unique ways to look at data, and challenge their preconceptions. Results-oriented: People who function with an organizational commitment to clear objectives, ambitious timelines, accountability for results, and a focus on impact. Respectful: People who embrace the diverse perspectives of everyone and foster the values of non-discrimination and inclusivity at all times. WITHIN 1 MONTH, YOU’LL… Participate in Third Way’s comprehensive onboarding program. You’ll learn about all aspects of Business Operations, which includes HR, Benefits, IT, Finance, and office operations. Meet your Third Way Buddy, be introduced to the entire staff, and start to learn the TW’s culture. Learn our current processes for payroll, compliance, and labor tracking, and how you will partner with Finance and the rest of the Business Operations team on these processes. Participate in weekly one-on-ones with your manager to ensure you fully understand the expectations of the job. Attend weekly team meetings. You’ll learn about the key goals of each member of your program, their progress toward these goals, what challenges they face, and how you will contribute. Familiarize yourself with Third Way’s social media presence and online voice. Participate in messaging conversations and briefings with your supervisor about Third Way’s priorities, ongoing campaigns, and our work in the political and policy space. Join the communications team in developing creative digital ideas and products to support our top campaigns. WITHIN 2 MONTHS, YOU’LL… Gain an understanding of each employee’s role and their contribution to the organization. Attend program overview sessions to learn more about each team’s contribution to TW’s mission. Incorporate TW’s Style Guide and Production process into your work products. Participate in, at least, one of our internal Professional Development trainings or a Center for Fun activity. Draft all of Third Way’s social media posts and manage the day-to-day posting on all digital platforms. Prepare regular reports on platform analytics and provide key insights. Bring new ideas and suggestions to your weekly one-on-ones with your manager. WITHIN 3 MONTHS, YOU’LL… Feel a sense of comfort and familiarity with the staff, your team, and your work. Continue to attend weekly departmental meetings with a stronger understanding of your team’s strategic goal. Bring new ideas and suggestions to your weekly one-on-ones with your manager. Attend and participate in external functions with other members of your team. Complete your 90-day self-evaluation and performance review with your manager. Partner with your manager to establish your long-term goals for the remainder of the year. Take over primary management of Third Way’s social media channels. Create and manage Third Way’s social media content calendar. Lead content creation for all of Third Way’s digital media accounts. Partner with other members of the communications team and our policy and political analysts to prepare content to elevate important findings and data. —————————————— In addition to competitive salaries, your health and wellness is our priority. We offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance; Health Reimbursement Account (HRA); and Flexible Spending Account (FSA, DCA, Parking, and Transit); Life Insurance; Accidental Death & Dismemberment Insurance; Retirement plan; Accrued Paid Sick and Vacation leave; Long-term Disability, Employee Assistant Program (EAP). Third Way offers a hybrid work environment to support our employees’ healthy work-life balance. This position is based in Washington, DC, and Third Way’s in-office days are Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Third Way is an equal-opportunity employer committed to non-discrimination. We will consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, sexual orientation or gender identity, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable laws. Third Way does not provide employment-based visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship. item.title: Senior Director, Social Media & Content Strategy, Global
item.description: Senior Director, Social Media & Content Strategy, Global Organization: Vantage Data Centers Location: Denver, CO | Sterling, VA Date Posted: 09/29/2026 About Vantage Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands. Marketing Department The marketing team is responsible for Vantage’s brand, identity and positioning in the global marketplace. The department also leads public and analyst relations to ensure constituents are educated on Vantage’s products, services and markets. The team partners with sales, new site development, construction, finance, people and culture, public policy, internal communications, sustainability and other departments to grow market share, acquire and retain customers, expand into new geographies, understand customer sentiment and promote the company as an employer of choice. Position Overview This role can be based in our Sterling, VA or Denver, CO, or other Vantage locations, in alignment with our flexible work policy (3 days onsite, 2 days remote). Reporting to Vantage’s Global Marketing Lead, and working closely with the Chief Marketing & Communications Officer, the Senior Director, Social Media & Content Strategy will lead Vantage’s global social media and digital content function, developing and executing an audience-first strategy that strengthens the company’s reputation, builds stakeholder trust, and increases understanding of the critical role digital infrastructure plays in modern society. This role is responsible for transforming Vantage’s digital presence through strategic storytelling, compelling multimedia content, and platform-specific audience engagement. The Senior Director will establish a clear purpose, audience, content strategy, and success metrics for every social and digital channel, ensuring each platform effectively supports Vantage’s business, reputation, community engagement, and stakeholder relations objectives. A primary focus of the role will be building and leading a scalable content engine capable of producing high-quality, engaging, and accessible content that resonates with a broad range of audiences, including: Local communities Policymakers and government officials Economic development stakeholders Employees and prospective employees Media and influencers Industry stakeholders Customers and partners Investors and analysts The ideal candidate is a strategic and creative leader with deep expertise in content strategy, digital communications, social media, audience engagement, storytelling, editorial planning, and emerging digital platforms. This individual will work closely with Media Relations, Policy and Government Affairs, Sustainability, Human Resources, Sales, Regional Marketing, and executive leadership to elevate Vantage’s voice and strengthen its reputation across global markets. Essential Job Functions Social Media Strategy & Leadership Develop and lead Vantage’s global social media strategy, defining the purpose, audience, content framework, and success metrics for each platform. Identify key target audiences and establish platform-specific strategies for LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, podcasts, and emerging digital channels. Create audience engagement programs designed to build trust and foster dialogue with communities, policymakers, industry stakeholders, employees, recruits, and customers. Drive audience growth, engagement, share of voice, and positive sentiment across digital channels. Establish governance, policies, content standards, and publishing best practices across the organization. Continuously evaluate platform effectiveness and identify opportunities for innovation and growth. Stakeholder & Reputation Storytelling Develop content strategies that increase understanding of Vantage’s role in enabling the digital economy and supporting modern society. Create storytelling programs that highlight economic development impact, job creation and workforce development, community investment, sustainability initiative, energy innovation, customer successes, and employee stories and culture Translate complex topics into engaging, easily understandable content for non-technical audiences. Partner with Policy, Sustainability, Development, and Operations teams to create educational content that addresses common questions and concerns about data centers and digital infrastructure. Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership Develop and oversee a global content strategy aligned with business priorities, reputation objectives, emerging issues, and stakeholder needs. Build and manage a global editorial calendar aligned with community engagement efforts, reputation campaigns, major announcements, industry events, policy priorities, and executive thought leadership. Partner with regional teams to identify meaningful local stories and stakeholder engagement opportunities. Ensure content is audience-centric, visually engaging, accessible, and aligned to brand standards. Maintain consistency in messaging across all digital and social platforms. Content Engine & Multimedia Development Build and lead a centralized content engine capable of supporting global and regional storytelling needs. Prioritize modern content formats including: short-form video, social-first video content, reels and TikTok content, infographics, motion graphics, podcasts, interactive digital content, and executive and colleague video messaging Develop systems that allow content to be efficiently repurposed across multiple channels and audiences. Create scalable processes for turning announcements, community events, sustainability initiatives, customer stories, media coverage, and insights into compelling digital content. Explore emerging platforms and content formats that help reach new audiences and strengthen stakeholder engagement. Leverage emerging AI, automation, and content technologies to increase efficiency while maintaining quality and authenticity. Manage a content budget that supports a network of agencies and external content creators, influencers and paid digital spend with a constant focus on ROI Misinformation & Digital Reputation Management Develop digital content strategies that proactively address misinformation and disinformation impacting Vantage, local projects, and the broader data center industry. Monitor social channels and digital platforms for emerging issues, false narratives, and stakeholder concerns. Work closely with Global Media Relations, Public Policy, Government Affairs, Sustainability, and regional teams to develop fact-based educational content. Create proactive campaigns that improve understanding of data centers, community benefits, energy use, sustainability efforts, and economic impact. Build rapid-response content frameworks that help address misinformation before it gains momentum. Identify, vet, and engage credible third-party digital creators, subject matter experts, community voices, and industry influencers who connect with broader audiences in authentic and accessible ways. Develop and manage strategic influencer and creator partnerships to amplify fact-based content, increase stakeholder reach, and counter misinformation and disinformation through trusted voices across social, video, podcast, and emerging digital platforms. Executive & Thought Leadership Communications Partner with the Executive Leadership Team to develop digital thought leadership programs and manage Linked In presence for select executive leaders. Create social and multimedia content that elevates Vantage leaders as trusted voices in digital infrastructure, AI, sustainability, economic development, and public policy. Measurement & Analytics Establish comprehensive KPIs measuring audience growth, stakeholder engagement, reach and awareness, sentiment, share of voice, content effectiveness, reputation impact Develop executive dashboards and reporting programs demonstrating business and reputation outcomes. Use audience insights and performance data to continuously refine content investments and channel strategies. Partner with web and digital marketing teams to continuously improve content discoverability, engagement, and user experience. Ensure digital channels remain relevant, current, visually engaging, and audience focused. Team and cross-Functional Leadership Partner closely with Global Marketing, Media Relations, Public Policy, Government Affairs, Sustainability, Human Resources, Sales, Operations, and regional marketing teams. Support regional reputation campaigns and community engagement initiatives through integrated social and digital content programs. Serve as a strategic advisor on social media trends, digital engagement, content effectiveness, and stakeholder communications. Lead and mentor content creators, social media specialists, agency partners, and freelance contributors. Additional duties as assigned by Management Job Requirements The ideal candidate has successfully built modern social media and content functions in industries facing public perception challenges and has experience using digital channels to educate stakeholders, shape narratives, build trust, and drive meaningful engagement across diverse audiences. Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Digital Media, Public Relations, Public Affairs, or a related field required. 10+ years of progressive experience in social media, content strategy, digital communications, corporate communications, marketing, or related disciplines. Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing teams, agencies, and cross-functional initiatives. Proven success developing and scaling enterprise social media and content programs
