item.title: Director, State Government Relations
item.description: Director, State Government Relations Organization: Diageo Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Job Description : About us With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations. Bring your talent, curiosity and ambition, and strive for your personal best alongside people who challenge, support and learn from each other. Together, as one outstanding team, we keep learning, improving and raising the bar for our brands, our business and each other. Join us and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more. About the Function Corporate Relations (CR) is where we shape how the world sees Diageo, and how we show up in it. Working at the intersection of business and society, this team builds trusted relationships with the people and organisations that matter most, from media and investors to governments, NGOs and partners. It’s fast-paced, high-impact work that protects our reputation while helping move our business forward. Across communications, policy and ESG, you’ll collaborate globally, navigate complex challenges and play a key role in earning and maintaining our licence to operate. It’s a space for people who are curious, credible, annfident in making their voice heard About the Role Diageo North America is seeking a Director, State Government Relations to lead the development and execution of government relations and public policy strategy across the Central Region. The Director will be a senior representative of Diageo with state and local policymakers, regulators, trade associations and other external stakeholders and will play a critical role in protecting and advancing Diageo’s reputation, license to operate and ability to grow. This role requires a sophisticated understanding of multi-state government affairs, strong political and business judgment, and the ability to translate public policy developments into commercial implications and effective advocacy strategies. The Director will anticipate emerging legislative and regulatory risks and opportunities, develop and execute strategies aligned with Diageo’s business priorities, and provide trusted counsel to senior leaders across the organization. The Director will work closely across Corporate Relations and partner with Legal, Commercial, Finance, Regulatory, Supply and other functions to ensure Diageo brings an integrated perspective to complex policy issues. The role will also manage external government affairs consultants and engage trade associations, business organizations and other third-party stakeholders to advance shared priorities. Key Responsibilities Government Relations Strategy & Advocacy Develop and execute a comprehensive government relations strategy for an assigned portfolio of states, aligned with Diageo’s North America business priorities and broader Corporate Relations strategy. Represent Diageo before governors’ offices, state legislatures, regulatory agencies and other state and local policymakers, building trusted relationships and advocating effectively on behalf of the company. Establish clear advocacy objectives and strategies for priority issues and continuously evaluate progress, external developments and business needs to adapt plans as appropriate. Identify opportunities for Diageo to proactively shape the policy environment rather than solely respond to legislative and regulatory developments. Coordinate with federal government relations, communications and other Corporate Relations colleagues where issues cross jurisdictions or require an integrated external affairs strategy. Policy, Legislative & Regulatory Leadership Anticipate and assess emerging legislative, regulatory and political developments that could create risks or opportunities for Diageo, its brands, customers and consumers. Lead state-level policy strategy on issues affecting the beverage alcohol sector and Diageo’s business, including taxation, market access and route-to-market, digital commerce and delivery, regulatory modernization, product and category treatment, responsible drinking, sustainability and other emerging issues. Translate complex policy developments into clear commercial and reputational implications for senior leaders and business partners. Develop policy positions, advocacy materials, executive briefings, testimony, talking points and other communications that articulate Diageo’s perspective credibly and persuasively. Provide timely, actionable counsel and recommendations to senior management on significant legislative and regulatory developments. Stakeholder & Coalition Leadership Develop and maintain trusted relationships with strategically important, elected officials, regulators, policy leaders and other external stakeholders across the region. Build coalitions and third-party support around priority policy objectives, working where appropriate with customers, suppliers, business organizations, community partners and other stakeholders. Represent Diageo within relevant state and national trade associations and help shape association strategy, priorities and advocacy positions. Determine when Diageo should lead independently, work through a trade association or participate in a broader coalition to achieve the strongest policy outcome. Business Partnership Develop a deep understanding of Diageo’s commercial strategy, route to market, brands and business model and incorporate that understanding into government relations strategy. Build strong partnerships with Commercial, Legal, Finance, Regulatory, Supply and other functions to ensure policy priorities reflect business needs and that stakeholders understand the potential impact of government action. Bring an external perspective into the organization by identifying political, regulatory and societal trends that may affect Diageo’s long-term strategy. Help business leaders understand the role government relations can play in enabling growth, managing risk and protecting Diageo’s reputation and license to operate. External Resource & Budget Management Select, direct and manage state government affairs consultants and other external resources, setting clear objectives and ensuring strong performance and accountability. Manage government relations resources and budgets effectively across the assigned region. Ensure consultants and external partners operate consistently with Diageo’s standards, policies and advocacy priorities. Governance, Compliance & Reputation Conduct all government relations activities with the highest standards of integrity and in accordance with applicable lobbying, ethics, disclosure and political-engagement requirements and Diageo policies. Partner with Legal, Compliance and Corporate Relations colleagues to identify and appropriately manage political, regulatory and reputational risks. Exercise sound judgment in representing Diageo externally and ensure advocacy positions reinforce Diageo’s reputation as a responsible and constructive participant in public policy. What You’ll Bring Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in political science, public policy, government, law, business, communications or a related field; advanced degree is a plus. 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in state government affairs, public policy, lobbying, government service, political advocacy or a related field, with significant experience working across multiple states. Strong existing relationships within state government and demonstrated ability to develop trusted bipartisan relationships with policymakers and other stakeholders. Deep understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes and demonstrated experience developing and executing successful advocacy strategies. Strong political judgment and the ability to assess complex and rapidly evolving issues, identify implications and recommend a clear course of action. Demonstrated commercial acumen and ability to connect public policy issues to business strategy, customers, consumers and financial outcomes. Experience influencing through trade associations, coalitions and third-party organizations. Demonstrated ability to counsel and influence senior executives and collaborate effectively across a complex matrixed organization. Exceptional written, verbal and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex issues clearly and persuasively to internal and external audiences. Experience managing external consultants, budgets and multiple concurrent legislative and regulatory priorities. High degree of initiative, discretion, resilience and accountability, with the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving external environment. Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout the assigned region and to other locations as business needs require. Working with Us Flexibility is key to our success. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you so that you’re supported to manage your wellbeing and balance your priorities from day one. Rewards & Benefit We recognise and value performance, offering our people a highly competitive Rewards and Benefits package. Feel inspired? Then this may be the opportunity for you. If you require a reasonable adjustment, please ensure that you capture this information when you submit your application. Recruitment Scam Warning Protecting candidates is very important to us. All communications regarding your application will come from an email address ending in @diageo.com. In our recruitment process, we’ll never ask for money. Worker Type: Regular Primary Location: Chicago Sales Office Job Posting Start Date: 2026-09-28 CHICAGO, ILLINOIS: SALARY RANGE IS FROM $149.625 TO $249.375 (ANNUAL) At Diageo certain roles are eligible for additional rewards, including annual incentive payment and stock awards. US-based employee

item.title: Director, Social Media
item.description: Director, Social Media Organization: Monumental Sports & Entertainment (MSE) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 In order to be considered for this role, after clicking “ Apply Now ” above and being redirected, you must fully complete the application process on the follow-up screen. Monumental Sports & Entertainment (MSE) is one of the leading integrated sports and entertainment companies globally. MSE’s portfolio spans premier professional sports teams, world-class venues, and next-generation media properties, with marquee assets including the NHL’s Washington Capitals, NBA’s Washington Wizards, WNBA’s Washington Mystics, NBA G League’s Capital City Go-Go, Capital One Arena, and Monumental Sports Network, along with an investment in Team Liquid. Rooted in the nation’s capital, MSE brings Washington, D.C’s distinct influence, ambition, and leadership to the global sports and entertainment landscape. The company harnesses the power of its platform to drive continuous innovation and deliver extraordinary experiences that inspire and unite our community, our fans, and our people. Our success is powered by talented people who bring passion, creativity, and collaboration to everything they do. If you’re looking to build your career in a dynamic, fast-paced organization that’s shaping the future of sports and entertainment, we’d love to hear from you. Position Overview: The Director, social media is responsible for establishing and implementing the overall social media strategy, editorial calendar, and promotional plans across the full ecosystem of Washington Mystics social media channels. This position will work collaboratively with the Marketing and Content teams and across the organization to develop social media content that drives growth and engagement. Ideal candidates will possess a deep understanding of how audiences digest and engage with social content and have hands-on experience leading content strategy. Do you have a passion for sports, entertainment, and pop culture? Apply today! We’d love to hear from you! Responsibilities: Create and maintain the Mystics social media strategy based on business priorities and long-term planning. Maintain awareness of emerging platforms, tools and technology. Develop data-capture strategies to improve engagement and reach, staying on top of trends. Collaborate with other departments to drive goals for the Mystics (ticketing, retail) and sponsors. Manage and track social media budget, expenses and revenue. Communicate social strategy to internal departments, manage expectations and implement content across each social media platform. Develop opportunities for social monetization. Create new opportunities to improve visibility for the Mystics and players. Drive the strategy for using social influencers and content creators to generate engagement and reach new audiences for the Mystics organic social channels. Curate, capture and publish live coverage of all Mystics games (home and away), practices, and events across the regular season schedule, full practice schedule, and season-long event calendar. Handle daily community management for all platforms. Lead monthly and weekly digital reporting across social channels, working with social team to pull results and analyze data to create strategies and tactics for continual audience engagement and growth. Work with basketball operations and players to develop a level of trust to ensure everyone surrounding the team is comfortable with social media presence. Work with internal departments to proactively respond to fan concerns/complaints via social media platforms in a timely manner. Serve as a resource for players/coaches seeking to become more involved with the Mystics via social media. Other duties as assigned. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Communications, or related field. 7+ years of experience in social media role preferred, preferably in the sports or live entertainment industry. Knowledgeable about current and emerging social media platforms and trends. Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. Strong proof-reading skills; outstanding attention to detail. Strong visual design eye, with regard to graphics, photography, and produced video content. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite and Content Management Systems (Sprout Social, Asana). Experience compiling and analyzing social media KPIs and metrics to impact strategy, sponsor opportunities and business decisions. Ability to effectively work in a fast-paced environment and demonstrate the ability to juggle multiple tasks and projects. Able and willing to travel (road games, events, etc.) Knowledgeable about WNBA players, teams and experience in professional sports. Flexibility to work nights, weekends, and holidays as needed. Pay Range: $95k-110k USD. Benefit Eligibility: This role is eligible to participate in health and welfare benefits. We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.description: Social Media and External Communications Manager Organization: Google Location: Mountain View, CA | New York, NY | Seattle, WA | San Francisco, CA | Washington D.C. Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Applicants in San Francisco: Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. In accordance with Washington state law, we are highlighting our comprehensive benefits package, which is available to all eligible US based employees. Benefits for this role include: Health, dental, vision, life, disability insurance Retirement Benefits: 401(k) with company match Paid Time Off: 20 days of vacation per year, accruing at a rate of 6.15 hours per pay period for the first five years of employment Sick Time: 40 hours/year (increased to 69 hours/year for Seattle) including 5 discretionary sick days per instance Maternity Leave (Short-Term Disability + Baby Bonding): 28-30 weeks Baby Bonding Leave: 18 weeks Holidays: 13 paid days per year Note: By applying to this position you will have an opportunity to share your preferred working location from the following: Mountain View, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA; Seattle, WA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Washington D.C., DC, USA. Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 10 years of experience in communications, public relations, or public affairs, with a focus on social media. Preferred qualifications: Experience working on political campaigns and other large company initiatives that require cross-functional collaboration. Effective team player who can meet project deadlines with exceptional attention to detail. Ability to think strategically and develop creative comms strategies that drive results. Ability to quickly learn about various areas of public policy and the energy industry. Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet tight deadlines. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to craft compelling social media messaging and build relationships with key stakeholders. About the job As a member of the Global Communications & Public Affairs team, you will work cross-functionally to help communicate with journalists and other thought leaders; devise specific communications materials and campaigns; engage in face-to-face meetings with commentators and other opinion formers; and develop print and web-based material supporting these campaigns. We’re looking for great communicators who can understand complex issues and explain them in person and also via well written, simple blog posts, FAQs, video scripts and more. As a Social Media Manager managing our local data center campaign efforts, you will define and oversee the overall social media strategy to reach hyperlocal audiences across U.S. markets where Google operates data centers. In this role, you will manage an external social media agency of record to execute comprehensive monitoring, paid social, creative asset production, and community management initiatives across various social media platforms. Working with Google’s Marketing and the Data Center Brand teams, you will serve as the primary advisor, responsible for reviewing social media content to ensure every touchpoint reinforces Google’s core data center narratives of community-focused outcomes, responsible execution, and economic opportunity. Working cross-functionally across Global Communications and Public Affairs and external partners, you will play a central role in demystifying data centers, cultivating local trust, and communicating Google’s long-term support of the communities we call home. Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. US: $171000 – $247000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits Responsibilities Develop and execute a targeted social media strategy tailored to hyperlocal audiences in U.S. markets across various social media platforms, working closely with our agency of record and Google’s community development managers (CDMs). Review and approve copy, visual assets, and engagement strategies to ensure high quality and brand consistency. Ensure all social media activations rigorously align with Google’s narratives around innovation, affordability, environmental protection, and community benefits. Establish KPIs and sentiment metrics with the agency, using real-time data to optimize social strategies and report insights to leadership. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions. Edelman is growing in Tech and growing fast. In the last 12 months, we’ve secured inspiring new partnerships across AI, enterprise software, cloud, data and analytics, cybersecurity, telecommunications, fintech and next-generation hardware. We’re helping Fortune 500 companies transform how they operate and compete while supporting innovators that are redefining entire industries. Technology is our fastest-growing sector, and we’re looking for communicators who understand both the technologies shaping the future and the conversations influencing business today. We are looking for a Senior Media Supervisor with deep expertise across enterprise and consumer technology. The ideal candidate combines strong media instincts, exceptional news judgment and a deep understanding of what makes a story timely, relevant and compelling. Thriving in fast-moving environments, you will build relationships across business, technology and trade media, provide media counsel to clients and executives, and identify opportunities that elevate brand narratives. Drive executive visibility and thought leadership initiatives for brands and executives. Build and strengthen relationships with business, technology, trade and broadcast media. Identify timely media opportunities and develop proactive story ideas that break through the news cycle. Monitor the technology landscape to identify emerging trends and relevant industry conversations. Develop compelling narratives, media strategies and communications materials that translate complex technologies and business trends into stories that resonate with media and key audiences. Serve as a day-to-day client contact and help manage account operations, timelines and budgets. Mentor and support junior team members through coaching, feedback and day-to-day leadership. Contribute to integrated communications programs and support new business opportunities. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting enterprise technology and/or consumer technology brands. Strong understanding of technology sectors including AI, enterprise software, cloud, cybersecurity and data and analytics. Think like a journalist; you know what makes a story newsworthy, timely and relevant. Established relationships across business, technology, trade and broadcast media, with a demonstrated ability to build new relationships as beats and coverage priorities evolve. Experience supporting executive visibility and thought leadership initiatives. Ability to provide sound media counsel to client stakeholders and executives. Strong writing, storytelling and presentation skills. Experience developing media plans and communications materials with limited oversight. Strong organizational skills, with experience managing timelines, budgets and competing priorities. item.title: Account Director, Corporate & Public Affairs (Health Policy)
item.description: Account Director, Corporate & Public Affairs (Health Policy) Organization: Burson Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Who we are: Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation. WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram. More about the role: Burson is seeking an Account Director, Corporate & Public Affairs to be based in Washington, DC. This role will serve as a policy and regulatory affairs counselor within Burson’s Corporate & Public Affairs practice, with a primary focus on healthcare policy and regulatory issues. The Account Director will provide strategic counsel to clients navigating complex legislative, regulatory, and reputational environments, translating policy developments into integrated communications and stakeholder engagement strategies. Healthcare policy expertise is critical for this role. The ideal candidate will bring a strong understanding of how health policy is developed and influenced across Congress, federal agencies, trade associations, think tanks, patient advocacy organizations, media, and other key stakeholders within the broader Washington policy ecosystem. While healthcare will be the primary focus, the role will also support clients and opportunities across a range of policy-driven sectors including energy, infrastructure, sustainability, trade, and other highly regulated industries. This is a highly client-facing position requiring both policy fluency and exceptional communications skills. The ideal candidate can connect policy developments to business outcomes, translate complex issues into compelling narratives, and help clients proactively engage in policy conversations that shape markets, industries, and reputation. This is an opportunity to become immersed in multifaceted public affairs campaigns while playing a leading role in policy communications, stakeholder engagement, account growth, and business development. What you’ll do: Serve as a health policy subject matter expert across a diverse portfolio of clients and new business opportunities. Monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, and policy developments, identifying risks, opportunities, and implications for clients. Develop integrated communications strategies that align policy priorities, stakeholder engagement, reputation objectives, and business goals. Translate complex healthcare and public policy issues into clear, actionable recommendations for clients and stakeholders. Advise clients on policy-driven initiatives, advocacy efforts, stakeholder engagement programs, thought leadership, and executive visibility strategies. Map and engage key policy stakeholders, including policymakers, trade associations, patient organizations, think tanks, third-party experts, and influential media. Provide strategic communications support during policy-related issues, regulatory challenges, and reputation management situations. Help clients move from reactive monitoring to proactive policy engagement by identifying emerging issues and opportunities before they become business challenges. Collaborate with colleagues across Burson’s Corporate & Public Affairs, Health, Crisis, and Corporate Reputation teams to deliver integrated solutions. Support business development efforts by identifying emerging policy issues, stakeholder opportunities, and new client solutions. Lead account teams, mentor junior practitioners, and build strong client relationships. Experience that contributes to success: 7-10+ years of experience in public affairs, policy communications, regulatory affairs, government relations, strategic communications, or a related field. Deep knowledge of healthcare policy, regulatory affairs, and legislative processes in the United States. Experience working on or around congressional committees, federal agencies, trade associations, think tanks, advocacy organizations, or within a communications agency is highly preferred. Strong understanding of the Washington, DC policy ecosystem and the stakeholders that influence policy development and implementation. Ability to connect policy developments to business, reputational, and communications implications for clients. Demonstrated experience developing integrated communications strategies tied to policy, regulatory, legislative, or advocacy objectives. Experience supporting stakeholder engagement, advocacy campaigns, thought leadership initiatives, public education efforts, and executive visibility programs. Strong writing, client counseling, and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to explain complex policy issues to diverse audiences. Familiarity with policy areas beyond healthcare, including energy, infrastructure, sustainability, trade, or other regulated sectors, is a plus. #LI-FB1 Burson is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers. Individual compensation varies based on job-related factors, including location, business needs, level of responsibility, experience, and qualifications. We offer a competitive benefits package; click here for more details: https://mybenefits.wpp.com/public/welcome. The base salary for this position at the time of this posting may range between: $60,000—$140,000 USD You belong at Burson: Our vision is for Burson to be the leading ‘academy company’ for creative communications professionals and emerging leaders. We provide a dynamic environment where ambitious colleagues come to elevate their skills, expand their networks, and ultimately, produce the best solutions for today’s leading brands. Our commitment to your growth is reflected in our robust benefits and people programs, which include professional development opportunities, mentorship programs with industry leaders, a vibrant and inclusive company culture fostering collaboration and innovation and packages designed to reward and retain top talent. We invest in our people because we believe their success is our success. At Burson, we’re an agency of learn-it-alls. We recognize that the things we do best, creativity and communications, require a level of nuanced understanding. That’s why it’s imperative for us to hire extraordinarily talented people of all backgrounds and identities. Without that we can’t do the essential work of inspiring bold ideas, fostering constructive dialogue, cultivating meaningful experiences, and driving innovation and creativity for our partners. Your unique point of view—your talent—is what makes you a #BursonPerson, and it’s how we deliver exceptional results for our clients, together. We believe the best work happens when we’re together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That’s why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process. When you click the “ Submit Application ” button , this will send any information you add below to Burson. Before you do this, we think it’s a good idea to read through our Recruitment Privacy Policy. California residents should read our California Recruitment Privacy Notice. This explains what we do with your personal data when you apply for a role with us, and, how you can update the information you have provided us with or how to remove it. item.description: Program Appropriations & Congressional Analyst (supporting NOAA) Organization: ASRC Federal Location: Silver Spring, MD Date Posted: 09/29/2026 ASRC Federal is a leading government contractor furthering missions in space, public health and defense. As an Alaska Native owned corporation, our work helps secure an enduring future for our shareholders. Join our team and discover why we are a top veteran employer and Certified Great Place to Work™ Data Networks, Inc (DNC), a subsidiary of ASRC Federal, is seeking a Program Appropriations & Congressional Analyst to support our NOAA program located in Silver Spring, MD. This role is highly collaborative and preparatory, focusing on managing congressional relations, annual budgets, and strategic communications. This is an onsite/hybrid position, expected to be in the Silver Spring office several days each week. Meet regularly with customers to discuss performance, propose new initiatives, and establish organizational priorities. Essential Skills: Excellent written communication skills with experience drafting clear and concise reports/briefing materials. Technical skills: Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides), Google Drive, Gmail, Google Meet, Microsoft Excel. You will support a fast-moving team and senior executives, particularly on confidential content and highly strategic executive work. You will have excellent communication skills with the ability to present complex issues in clear and concise documentation, you will be required to demonstrate a strong record of client delivery and thrive in a dynamic work environment, exhibiting the ability to be flexible. The scope of this role spans across the American Nurses Enterprise, supporting executives, strategic and highly confidential content across the American Nurses Association (ANA), the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), and the American Nurses Foundation (ANF). The role holder must be able to write executive-level speeches. As an ideal candidate, you must be a versatile storyteller that is both strategic and creative with a strong understanding of brand voice, and the ability to translate complex topics into clear, engaging, and actionable messaging. You will need to be able to develop, manage and handle highly sensitive information and engage with executive officers on highly confidential topics. Join the American Nurses Enterprise (ANE) and be part of the team building a healthy world through the power of nurses. Our goals are to (1) Elevate the Profession of Nursing Globally (2) Evolve the Practice of Nursing to Improve Health, Health Care, and Health Equity and (3) Ensure the Professional Success of Nurses. Our core values: Trusted, Inclusive, Innovative and Empowered guide everything we do. We are committed to creating a supportive and dynamic workplace where employees can thrive. We understand the importance of work-life balance and offer flexible work arrangements and generous paid time off. Our modern office spaces are designed to foster collaboration and creativity. The collaborative culture and supportive team environment make ANE a great place to grow your career. What You Will Do: Develop and write highly confidential, sensitive, and executive level content. Collaborate with the team to fully understand internal and external communications needs, executive communication needs, confidential communication needs and BOD (board-of-directors) level communication needs. Assist in building communications and stakeholder products, including highly confidential stakeholder products, the consistently facilitate organizational communications goals Ability to understand stakeholder needs and plan messages to impact perceptions. Ability to understand strategic communications across a wide variety of subject matter areas, including policy, brand, marketing, executive communications and public relations, and be able to help shape a consistent messaging approach. Develop communication materials to include briefings, reports, white papers, brochures, talking points and other documentation to support communication and organizational objectives. Compose draft speeches for senior management and assist with finalizing speeches. Evaluate success of campaigns when completed. The role may require occasional after-hours or weekend support based on business needs. Other responsibilities as assigned. What you bring to the American Nurses Enterprise: Education Undergraduate degree from a 4-year institution required (in advertising, marketing or communications preferred), master’s degree preferred. Related Work Experience 3-5 years of experience in strategic communications, PR or related field Exceptional oral and written communication skills to articulate complex messages in a simple, understandable manner to a variety of audiences. Strong analytical skills to assess the effectiveness of communication strategies, identify gaps, and develop effective solutions. Knowledge of digital communication technologies and platforms, including social media, email marketing, and content management systems. Basic understanding of video scripting and editing, graphics design portfolio preferred. Excellent research skills to stay current with communication trends, technologies, and best practices, and apply this knowledge to communication strategies. Interpersonal skills to work effectively with a variety of stakeholders, including management, employees, and external partners. Problem-solving skills to address communication challenges and find innovative, effective solutions. Organizational skills to manage multiple projects simultaneously, meet deadlines, and maintain attention to detail. Experience in data analysis and reporting, using data to measure the effectiveness of communication strategies and make recommendations for improvement. Optimistic and solution-oriented mindset. Experience supporting confidential and highly sensitive projects. What ANE Offers You: Join us and support more than 5 million Registered Nurses in the United States. Every role within ANA contributes to a healthier world through the “Power of Nurses.” An opportunity to help transform a 130-year-old organization to meet the future needs and demands within Health Care. Be a role model for embracing and empowering the uniqueness of every employee. Continuously innovating through creative and strategic initiatives. Exceptional benefits including, but not limited to 401K retirement contributions of up to 7%, generous PTO which includes the week-off between Dec 25 and Jan 1, in addition to Personal Days-off, 11 paid Holidays, excellent health/medical benefits, and much more Commitment to your career development and advancement through ANE learning and development programs (internally and externally). Work Schedule: Hybrid employees must work a minimum of 20% in the office. Location: Our main office is located at: 8403 Colesville Road, Suite 500, Silver Spring, MD 20910 Learn more about the American Nurses Enterprise: https://www.nursingworld.org/ana-enterprise-jobs/ https://www.linkedin.com/company/american-nurses-association The American Nurses Enterprise: Founded in 1896, the American Nurses Enterprise is the family of nonprofit organizations that comprise of the American Nurses Association, including the American Nurses Association (ANA), the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), and the American Nurses Foundation (ANF) Equal Opportunity Employer: The ANE is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. item.title: Clean Power Institute Executive Director
item.description: Clean Power Institute Executive Director Organization: American Clean Power Association (ACP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 About Us The American Clean Power Association (ACP) is the leading voice of today’s multi-tech clean energy industry, representing energy storage, wind, utility-scale solar, clean hydrogen, and transmission companies. ACP is committed to meeting America’s energy and national security goals and building our economy with fast-growing, low-cost, and reliable domestic power. Learn more at cleanpower.org. The Clean Power Institute (CPI) is ACP’s 501(c)3 affiliate organization. CPI’s mission is to build the public support and workforce to fuel the clean energy future. CPI advances its mission through programming that builds a stable, skilled, and diverse workforce and creates strategic partnerships that promote the benefits of clean energy investments across the country. Position Summary The Clean Power Institute (CPI) is seeking an entrepreneurial and highly collaborative Executive Director to lead the organization through its next phase of growth. Reporting to the COO of ACP/President of CPI and working closely with the CPI Board of Directors, the Executive Director will lead CPI’s day-to-day operations and develop the strategies, programs, partnerships and resources needed to expand its national impact. CPI is building a national approach to clean energy workforce development that connects industry, educators, workforce organizations and communities to create stronger pathways into clean energy careers. The Executive Director will identify opportunities for growth, develop new programs and business cases, strengthen and scale existing initiatives, and build the partnerships and financial resources necessary to execute them. This is a hands-on leadership role, with the Executive Director expected to directly develop and execute key initiatives while leading CPI’s broader strategy and growth. CPI’s relationship with ACP provides direct access to the companies investing in, building, operating and supplying America’s clean energy infrastructure. The Executive Director will leverage that connection to ensure CPI’s workforce and education programs respond to real industry needs, while expanding CPI’s partnerships across philanthropy, education, workforce development and communities nationwide. Essential Functions/Major Responsibilities To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet business needs. Strategy & Organizational Growth Lead the development and execution of CPI’s long-term vision, strategy, and operating priorities in partnership with the CPI Board of Directors and ACP leadership. Build the organizational capabilities, team, systems, partnerships, and resources necessary to grow CPI from a portfolio of successful initiatives into an integrated national platform. Identify opportunities for new programs, partnerships, and areas of growth; develop strategies and business cases to evaluate opportunities and bring forward recommendations for investment and execution. Establish CPI as a nationally recognized leader and convener on clean energy workforce development, education, economic opportunity, and community engagement. Establish clear goals and measures of success across CPI’s work and ensure accountability for execution and results. Programs, Workforce & Education Lead a national workforce strategy focused on building sustainable talent pipelines in the communities where clean energy projects are developed and operated, particularly rural communities. Build upon CPI’s existing workforce models and expand its reach across wind, solar, energy storage, transmission, electrical trades, manufacturing, and emerging clean energy careers. Lead the creation of an integrated education-to-career strategy that introduces students to clean energy early and connects them through high school, community colleges, apprenticeships, universities, military pathways, and employment. Build partnerships with K–12 systems, educators, community colleges, and national youth-serving organizations to dramatically expand clean energy career awareness. Lead the development and growth of the Clean Energy Academy as the industry’s premier learning platform and the educational backbone of CPI’s national workforce strategy. Ensure the Academy connects early career awareness, workforce preparation, professional development, and lifelong learning into a cohesive educational ecosystem. Use data, partner feedback, and program outcomes to evaluate impact, identify opportunities, and guide the continued growth of CPI’s programs. Partnerships, Fundraising & External Engagement Serve as CPI’s chief fundraiser and develop a comprehensive, diversified fundraising strategy capable of supporting CPI’s national ambitions. Build and maintain strong relationships with foundations, corporations, individual philanthropists, and other institutional funders interested in clean energy, workforce development, education, economic mobility, rural communities, STEM, and the future of work. Develop a compelling philanthropic case for investment that connects CPI’s workforce and education mission with economic opportunity, community impact, and the long-term strength of American clean energy. Ensure strong stewardship of philanthropic investments through measurable outcomes, effective reporting, compelling storytelling, and sustained relationships with funders. Build a national network of strategic partnerships across philanthropy, education, workforce development, youth-serving organizations, economic development organizations, and state and regional clean energy associations. Serve as a national convener capable of bringing organizations with different perspectives and capabilities together around shared workforce and education challenges. Work with state and regional organizations to translate CPI’s national strategy into locally relevant programs and resources, recognizing that clean energy projects ultimately succeed at the community level. Serve as CPI’s principal external ambassador and a compelling national voice on clean energy workforce development, education, economic opportunity, and community impact. Represent CPI with CEOs and industry leaders, philanthropic organizations, policymakers, educators, workforce leaders, community organizations, conferences, media, and other national forums. Build CPI’s national profile and reputation as a trusted, solutions-oriented organization capable of bringing industry and external partners together to solve complex workforce and education challenges. Organizational Leadership Lead CPI’s day-to-day operations and team, establishing clear priorities, accountability, and expectations across the organization. Develop a strong and highly collaborative partnership with the CPI Board of Directors, engaging the Board as strategic advisors, ambassadors, fundraisers, and champions of CPI’s mission. Engage individual Board members strategically based on their expertise, relationships, and ability to advance CPI’s priorities, including industry engagement, fundraising, partnerships, and external visibility. Provide the Board with clear updates on CPI’s performance, major initiatives, and emerging opportunities, and bring forward significant strategic priorities and recommendations for Board consideration. Make CPI’s relationship with ACP and its member companies a defining strategic advantage for the organization. Engage ACP member companies not simply as employers at the end of the talent pipeline, but as partners in identifying workforce needs, shaping curricula and credentials, providing career exposure, creating internships and apprenticeships, and investing in workforce solutions. Position CPI as the place where the clean energy industry can collectively address workforce and talent challenges that individual companies cannot solve alone. Work collaboratively with ACP leadership and staff, leveraging ACP’s industry expertise, relationships, and organizational resources while establishing a strong identity, strategy, and external presence for CPI. Lead and develop CPI staff, establishing clear expectations and accountability while building an entrepreneurial and collaborative organizational culture. Assess CPI’s organizational and staffing needs as the organization grows and recommend the structure, talent, and resources necessary to support its priorities. Education, Experience & Skills 15+ years of progressively responsible leadership experience, including significant experience in a senior organizational, program, or executive leadership role. Experience in clean energy, workforce development, education, philanthropy, economic development, nonprofit leadership, government, or a related field is strongly preferred. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience required; advanced degree in business, public policy, education, nonprofit management, workforce development, economics, energy, or a related field preferred. Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy, translate broad organizational goals into actionable plans, and lead complex programs or initiatives from concept through execution and evaluation. Hands-on, execution-oriented leadership style with the ability to move between strategy and direct execution as needed to advance CPI’s priorities. Strong business and financial acumen, including experience developing business cases, managing budgets and resources, evaluating investments and opportunities, and making recommendations that support organizational growth and long-term sustainability. item.title: Vice President, Government Relations & Political Affairs
item.description: Vice President, Government Relations & Political Affairs Organization: League of Conservation Voters (LCV) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Title: Vice President, Government Relations & Political Affairs Department: Government Affairs Status: Exempt Reports to: Senior Vice President, Government Affairs Positions Reporting to this Position: Director of Political Affairs; Congressional Champions Campaign Director; Senior Judiciary & Democracy Director Location: Washington, DC Remote Work Eligibility: Regular Hybrid Work Travel Requirements: Up to 25% Union Position: No Job Classification Level: M-IV Salary Range (depending on qualified experience): $147,900 – $200,940 General Description: For over half a century, the League of Conservation Voters, Inc. (“LCV”), has led the charge for clean air, clean water, public lands, healthy communities, and a sustainable planet for all. LCV has built political power and infrastructure at the intersection of climate policy and electoral strategy – advancing environmental protections, electing pro-environmental lawmakers and aligning action across an integral multi-state network. We envision a world in which tackling the climate crisis, confronting environmental injustice and strengthening our democracy leads to cleaner and healthier communities, good, well-paying jobs and a just, equitable and sustainable future for all. LCV is hiring a Vice President, Government Relations & Political Affairs to serve as a senior leader and highly visible member of the Government Affairs Department. Working closely with the Senior Vice President, Government Affairs and other senior staff, this position will be responsible for designing and executing federal government relations and political strategies to achieve our policy goals. Responsibilities include leading engagement with federal policymakers and overseeing coordinated-side political activities, including candidate endorsements and LCV Action Fund. The Vice President will have deep experience in federal legislative strategy and/or political campaigns. They will need to excel at strategy, relationship building, and coordinating with external partners. They will also possess strong communication, people and project management skills, as well as a commitment to advancing racial and environmental justice. This position is classified as “Regular Hybrid Work” and is required to work in-person in the Washington, D.C. office a minimum of two days per week. General working conditions: Operate in a professional office or home office environment, and routinely use standard office equipment including, but not limited to, computers, phones, photocopiers, and audiovisual systems. Largely sedentary, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods. Communicates with internal and external stakeholders using electronic platforms. Applicants must be located in and legally authorized to work in the United States. Applicants must reside in the location listed above. Responsibilities: Regularly working in close partnership with the SVP and program leaders, develop and execute a comprehensive federal government relations strategy to advance progress on top priority climate, clean energy, clean air, clean water, public lands and democracy goals. Serve as one of LCV’s most senior lobbyists and external representatives; develop and maintain high-level relationships with members of Congress, committee and leadership staff; and staff organizational principals on high-impact policymaker engagements. Manage federal candidate endorsement process, including interviewing candidates, making endorsement recommendations, and working directly with campaigns, political committees, and other stakeholders, including members of the board. Help direct LCV’s coordinated-side political activities, including overseeing the LCV Action Fund budget of over $1 million per cycle and strategizing on key opportunities for coordinated field programs. Develop and execute new systems and programs to deepen our communication with candidates, elected officials and their staff. In partnership with the SVP and other senior staff, develop and execute an innovative and effective program influencing 2028 presidential candidates. Advise on political strategy for the GiveGreen federal and state candidate fundraising program, which is the largest progressive issue-based candidate fundraising program. Serve as a senior spokesperson and help shape our communications messaging and strategy, including through informing polling and other message research. Supervise and mentor staff, including a team of three direct reports. Work cross-departmentally with senior organizational leaders on strategy development and program execution and support fundraising and accountability efforts. Build and maintain strong relationships with other environmental and allied partner organizations and coalitions, working closely on key priority issues. Partner with the Conservation Voter Movement, a network of over 30 state affiliates, on various projects spanning federal legislation and coordinated political programs. Travel within DC is expected regularly for in-person work. Travel outside of the DC area is expected up to 20% of the time. Travel in and outside of DC includes meetings with elected officials and their staff, electoral-related travel, staff retreats, conferences, and professional development opportunities, as needed. Help lead the department’s long-term process to advance equity and racial justice in its government relations and political strategies, as well as in its internal culture and operations. Qualifications: Work Experience: Required – At least 10 years of experience, including working in issue advocacy, on Capitol Hill, or with electoral campaigns. Experience with politics, coalitions and lobbying. Experience setting strategy, drafting and implementing campaign advocacy plans that reflect a commitment to racial justice and equity, elevate the voices and leadership of people of color and young people and develop authentic relationships with organizational partners. Demonstrated supervisory experience successfully managing high performing teams. Preferred – Experience managing budgets as well as designing, implementing and evaluating programs. Skills: Required – Ability to set high-level strategy in a collaborative manner, including connecting political strategy to issue advocacy campaign strategy. Federal government relations, coalition-building, strong political judgment, excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to relay complex issues in a clear and compelling manner. Strong interpersonal and management skills with an ability to develop relationships with individuals representing a rich mix of race, gender, talent, experience, and background. Passionate about protecting the environment and communities impacted by climate change and environmental injustice. Collaborative; organized and attentive to details; commitment to teamwork and community; ability to handle multiple tasks, effectively prioritize, and thrive in a fast-paced setting. Preferred – Confirmed success in budget management; proven track record in program design. Racial Justice and Equity Competencies: Demonstrated awareness of how one’s life experiences influence one’s personal attitudes, biases, and assumptions. Demonstrated commitment to continual learning and ability to successfully deliver culturally responsive services. Commitment to equity and inclusion as organizational practice and culture. Understands how environmental issues intersect with racism, economic and social inequality in the U.S. and has a passion for working to dismantle these systems. LCV offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes vacation, sick and parental leave, personal days, paid holidays, health insurance (two plan options for staff to choose from), dental and vision insurance, life and disability insurance (short- and long-term), Flexible Spending Account, 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contribution, commuter benefits program, sabbatical, and student loan assistance. Apply by October 12, 2026. No phone calls please. All applicants must include the month and year for the experience provided on their uploaded resume. Final resumes must be completed and submitted at the time of application, and should include all relevant experience to meet the minimum requirements and for salary considerations. Applications are reviewed by humans; we do not use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the hiring process. Pre-employment Screening All employment is contingent upon the completion of a background check, employment verifications and reference checks. LCV is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a racially just, equitable and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information, or any other protected status. LCV is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the employee selection process, including, completing the application, interviewing, or pre-employment testing, please contact [email protected] . Our organization participates in E-Verify as a part of the onboarding process. We are required to provide the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with information from each new employee’s Form I-9 to confirm work authorization. Please note that we do not use E-Verify to pre-screen job applicants and may only initiate the process after an offer has been accepted. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Vice President, Public Policy
item.description: Vice President, Public Policy Organization: American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Position Overview The VP, Public Policy oversees policy analysis, research, and advocacy strategies to shape government regulations for a vital sector that makes the essential paper and packaging products Americans use every day. The vice president is expected to be a thought leader, anticipate and evaluate policy opportunities and threats, develop policy positions, and effectively lead and implement strategies to support member priorities. The below description provides more detail on American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA), this important role and how you will impact the industry. Working at AF&PA The American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA) values diverse backgrounds and capabilities and invites all talented individuals to apply to be part of our team and support our culture and mission. We encourage the exchange of knowledge, innovative ideas and different perspectives to reach our goals and we support work/life balance. Essential Job Functions To be successful, it is critical for the Vice President, Public Policy to effectively collaborate with members. They must also coordinate extensively with government affairs, industry affairs and communications to develop and execute advocacy strategies that achieve policy priorities, and with the legal department on litigation and other legal matters pertaining to public policy. Oversee analyses of proposed regulations and legislation, assess short- and long-term impacts to the industry and provide strategic counsel to AF&PA members Lead development of regulatory and policy positions and development and implementation of advocacy strategy Direct research and development of legal, scientific, or technical analysis to support AF&PA policy positions and advocacy efforts Draft persuasive comments on regulatory proposals, support government affairs colleagues on legislative initiatives, and collaborate with colleagues from strategic communications department Serve as the Association’s senior policy expert and spokesperson, and advocate on key regulatory issues before federal, state, and other regulatory bodies Persuasively represent and advance member interests with federal agencies, regulatory authorities, and selected international organizations Partner with the Legal Department and outside counsel in anticipation of potential litigation of regulatory policy through comments, legal analysis, and litigation strategies Develop and maintain strategic relationships with members, allied associations, government agencies, think tanks, NGOs and other outside groups Engage in membership outreach and recruitment efforts on a regular basis Serve as a member of key policy and cross-functional teams across AF&PA Develop and oversee budgets for the department, its programs and issues Provide leadership, mentorship and oversight for the public policy staff and function, including: Guide, inspire, and align staff to support the success of the department and AF&PA Develop and support highly trained and deeply knowledgeable policy and technical experts to advance competitiveness of the industry As a member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT), this position will work with other staff leaders to guide the human and financial resources of the Association, set strategic priorities for the organization, identify strategic issues for consideration by the SLT and ensure collaboration on issue identification, prioritization and implementation. This person has a responsibility to ensure that Association policies are followed and applied consistently, and to respond judiciously to confidential/sensitive member and Association issues. Qualifications If your knowledge, skills and abilities are transferrable and you think you’re a great candidate for AF&PA – please consider applying even if you do not meet all the criteria listed below. Advanced degree in public policy, environmental policy, government, or related field required; Juris Doctor strongly preferred Ten (10) or more years of experience with regulatory policy advocacy, technical or economic analyses, and filing public comments on agency rulemakings Seven (7) or more years of experience effectively managing, coaching and developing people to deliver excellent results in policy analysis and/or advocacy roles Experience serving as a policy spokesperson and expert in government policy proceedings Experience with two or more policy issues impacting the industry (e.g., air, water, climate, solid waste, energy, chemicals and product stewardship, workplace health and safety, wood fiber supply and forestry issues, and sustainability and third-party standards) Experience with trade association dynamics preferred Solid understanding of federal regulatory process to effectively influence rulemakings required Understanding of the pulp, paper, packaging and tissue products industry and its policy priorities Ability to identify emerging issues, think strategically, develop policy positions and advocate before regulatory and legislative bodies Excellent public speaking and writing skills to communicate with credibility to staff, member companies, partners, members of the government, and the media Ability to operate in a collaborative, cross-functional and multi-disciplinary organization and achieve consensus-based strategies and solutions Ability to build/maintain strong relationships with staff, members, key stakeholders, and partners Solid leadership skills; including taking ownership and accountability, and prioritizing to drive results Strong interpersonal skills including actively listening and communicating professionally Ability to lead and develop a staff with highly specialized knowledge, skills and abilities Ability to travel within the US approximately 5-10% of the time Compensation and Benefits The base salary for this position is expected to be between $300,000-$350,000. This is a good-faith estimate based on market data for comparable positions and the current budgeted amount for this role. In addition, the vice president is eligible for an annual bonus of up to 20%. Factors to be considered when determining the salary of the selected candidate include relevant skills, experience and knowledge, and the alignment of these qualities with those of existing staff. We offer a generous benefits package that currently includes: Paid Vacation, Personal and Sick leave totaling 27-42 days per year (based on relevant experience), plus holidays and paid Parental Leave 94%-80% paid CareFirst medical plans for employees and their families Generous 401(k) retirement plan with up to 9% employer contribution (after waiting period) Free fitness center and pickleball courts at the DC office location Plus dental, vision, life insurance, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Account… Location We are located on 13th Street, NW between F and G, (directly above Metro Station). Our office is hybrid, which includes up to two days of remote work; however, due to the nature of the work, we expect the selected person to be in DC more frequently for local meetings. About AF&PA AF&PA serves to advance public policies that foster economic growth, job creation and global competitiveness for a vital sector that makes the essential paper and packaging products Americans use every day. The U.S. forest products industry employs more than 925,000 people, largely in rural America, and is among the top 10 manufacturing sector employers in 44 states. Our industry accounts for approximately 4.7% of the total U.S. manufacturing GDP, manufacturing more than $435 billion in products annually. AF&PA member companies are significant producers and users of renewable biomass energy and are committed to making sustainable products for a sustainable future through the industry’s decades-long initiative — Better Practices, Better Planet 2030. Visit AF&PA online at afandpa.org or follow us on X @ForestandPaper. Equal Employment Opportunity AF&PA is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and welcomes all talented individuals regardless of race, color, national origin, religion, age, sex, disability, veteran status or other category protected by law. Your Rights Applicants have rights under federal employment laws. Information may be found on the Department of Labor’s website ( https://www.dol.gov ) as well as through these available notices: Know Your Rights; Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA); and Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA). item.title: Vice President of Media Engagement
item.description: Vice President of Media Engagement Organization: Groundwork Collaborative Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/29/2026 ABOUT GROUNDWORK COLLABORATIVE Launched in 2018, Groundwork Collaborative (Groundwork) is driven by the idea that We Are The Economy: when all of us are doing well, that is when our economy thrives. We fight for progressive economic policy and narrative change that builds accountable public power, breaks up concentrations of private power, and centers people too long left out of prosperity. Taken together, these actions can help build a stronger and more resilient economy. Groundwork’s unique structure – part strategic communications organization, part think tank, and part issue advocacy organization – enables us to drive narrative and policy change with credibility, expertise, and impact. We work across four core audiences – the media, policymakers, economic experts, and grasstops leaders – using targeted policy campaigns, timely research, and compelling messaging to advance a truly inclusive economic worldview. THE OPPORTUNITY Groundwork Collaborative is seeking a Vice President of Media Engagement to lead the organization’s press and earned media operation and expand the reach and influence of its economic narrative work. This is a new senior leadership role within Groundwork’s communication team, created to bring together two powerful assets: a growing in-house press operation and the Economic Speakers Bureau, which is helping diversify the expert voices sharpening coverage and conversation about the economy. The Vice President will build the strategy, relationships, systems, and team necessary to ensure that Groundwork’s research, experts, campaigns, and ideas consistently break through in a dynamic, rapidly evolving media environment. They will translate Groundwork’s broader communications and organizational priorities into high-impact media strategies—from proactive narrative campaigns and major report launches to rapid response and opportunities to shape breaking news. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Communications, the Vice President will directly manage Groundwork’s press team and provide strategic leadership for the Economic Speakers Bureau. They will serve as a senior member of the communications team and a trusted advisor to executive leadership, working closely with Policy, Advocacy, Research, Partnerships, and Digital staff to build integrated campaigns that move both policy and narrative. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead Groundwork’s press and earned media strategy Set the vision, strategy, priorities, and operating approach for Groundwork’s press and earned media work, ensuring a proactive, coordinated, and high-impact presence across national broadcast, print, digital, podcast, newsletter, and emerging media. Translate Groundwork’s organizational and communications strategies into targeted media campaigns, proactive narrative opportunities, rapid response, and sustained press engagement. Identify the moments, messengers, stories, and platforms that can move economic debates and expand Groundwork’s reach. Build systems for prioritizing opportunities, coordinating across teams, and measuring the impact of Groundwork’s media work. Build and lead a high-performing press operation Directly manage and develop a press team of 2-4 staff, providing strategic direction, editorial leadership, coaching, feedback, and professional development opportunities. Establish clear goals, workflows, and decision-making processes that enable the team to operate effectively in a fast-moving news environment. Serve as a senior editor and strategic thought partner on press materials, including releases, media advisories, statements, talking points, briefings, op-eds, and other communications products. Advise the SVP of Communications and senior leadership on emerging media opportunities, risks, trends, and developments in the information ecosystem. Lead and grow the Economic Speakers Bureau Provide strategic leadership for the Economic Speakers Bureau (ESB), ensuring that its growing network of economic experts is effectively integrated into Groundwork’s broader communications and narrative strategy. Partner with the ESB pitching and booking operation to expand and steward a diverse, high-quality roster of expert spokespeople, and maximize opportunities for them to shape economic media coverage. Ensure experts receive the preparation, messaging support, and strategic guidance needed to be effective media voices. Oversee the continued growth of the ESB’s national operation as well as its Spanish-language and New York-based expert cohorts. Develop strategies to expand ESB’s reach across traditional media and emerging platforms, including podcasts, newsletters, and creator-driven media. Establish clear goals and measures for assessing ESB’s reach, effectiveness, and impact. Build and sustain a powerful media network Cultivate trusted relationships with journalists, editors, producers, bookers, hosts, newsletter writers, podcasters, and other influential voices throughout the national media landscape. Develop and maintain relationships with both established media institutions and emerging outlets and platforms, with an eye toward reaching audiences in an increasingly fragmented information environment. Represent Groundwork externally among media partners, coalition allies, and other stakeholders. Drive integrated organizational campaigns Partner closely across organizational verticals and within communications team to develop and execute integrated communications strategies for reports, campaigns, major announcements, events, partnerships, and other organizational priorities. Ensure seamless coordination and cross-amplification between press, digital, and other communications channels. Help Groundwork respond quickly and strategically to breaking economic and political developments. Organizational-Wide Leadership Responsibilities Lead projects that span multiple verticals, coordinating across teams to keep strategy and execution aligned. Serve as a cross-organizational connector between Communications, Partnership and Influence, and Policy, Advocacy, and Research. Represent Communications in senior leadership discussions, stepping in for the SVP as needed. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS While no one candidate will possess all the qualifications listed below, the ideal candidate will be passionate about Groundwork’s mission and bring many of the following skills and experiences: 10-15+ years of progressive experience in advocacy, political, nonprofit, government or other external communications roles, with a strong track record of generating high-impact press coverage at the national level. A demonstrated track record of generating high-impact national press coverage and using earned media strategically to advance organizational goals. Experience building teams, systems, and infrastructure, with a track record of creating effective operations in a fast-paced environment. Deep relationships across the national media landscape, including with broadcast bookers and producers, print and digital reporters, editors, and emerging voices in new and alternative media. Strong people management skills and a demonstrated commitment to coaching, developing, and motivating high-performing teams. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to turn complex economic policy into compelling, accessible media content under deadline pressure. A deep understanding of the news cycle and what makes a story break through, and the ability to anticipate opportunities before they emerge. Fluency in the evolving media ecosystem, including newsletters, podcasts, and media content creators, and have smart ideas for how to reach audiences in a fragmented information environment. Strong strategic instincts and the ability to connect day-to-day media opportunities to broader organizational goals and narrative strategy. Well-versed in wonky economic topics like inflation, tax policy, or labor markets, and are energized by translating them into messaging that resonates with broad audiences. Strong organizational skills, sound judgement, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining focus on the highest-impact opportunities. Familiar with the progressive economic policy, think tank, and advocacy community in Washington, D.C. and on Capitol Hill. A commitment to a just, inclusive, and robust economy that delivers opportunity and dignity to all. Preferred Qualifications Experience leading or overseeing a speakers bureau, surrogacy program, expert network, or similar initiative. Experience serving in a senior press or communications leadership role in an advocacy organization, political campaign, congressional office, government agency, or think tank. Deep expertise in economic policy issues, including areas such as fiscal policy, labor, trade, or financial regulation. Established relationships with influential voices in new and alternative media, including podcast producers, newsletter writers, content creators, and creator networks. Experience building or expanding communications infrastructure or launching a new organizational function. WORK LOCATION, COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Work Location: This role is hybrid position, with Monday and Wednesdays in the office and three days remote, as well as the occasional need to work in-person for events and special projects. The Groundwork Collaborative is based in Washington, D.C. Salary and Benefits: The compensation range for this full-time, exempt position is $180,000 to $200,000 annually commensurate with the candidate’s relevant experiences, capabilities, and skills. A generous benefits package is also provided through Groundwork Collaborative, which includes: Excellent health benefits with 100% employer-paid coverage and a generous HRA. Five weeks of vacation and personal leave, two week-long office closures, and additional time off for floating and federal holida
