item.title: Senior Vice President, Government Relations
item.description: Senior Vice President, Government Relations Organization: Solx Location: Washington, D.C. | San Juan, PR Date Posted: 09/29/2026 Develop and implement Solx’s government affairs strategy across the Government of Puerto Rico and the U.S. federal legislative and executive branches. Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll be the company’s advocate with policymakers — protecting and advancing the policy that underpins American solar manufacturing at giga scale. What you’ll do Own and execute Solx’s government affairs strategy with the executive and legislative branches at the federal level and across the Government of Puerto Rico. Build and maintain relationships with members of Congress and their staff, the Administration, and agencies including DOE, Treasury/IRS, and Commerce. Advance and defend the federal policy that underpins domestic solar manufacturing — the Advanced Manufacturing Production Tax Credit (45X), the ITC/PTC, trade and tariff enforcement, domestic-content and Buy American provisions, and permitting. Partner with the Government of Puerto Rico — the Governor’s office, DDEC/PRIDCO, the Energy Bureau, and the Legislature — on incentives, energy policy, workforce, and the island’s industrial agenda. Represent Solx in coalitions, trade associations, and industry groups, and manage outside lobbying firms, consultants, and counsel. Monitor and analyze legislation, rulemakings, and regulation; brief leadership on risks and opportunities and shape the company’s response. Support economic-development, tax-incentive, grant, and financing engagements with federal and Puerto Rico agencies. Partner with Communications and leadership on positioning, testimony, and the public-policy narrative. What you bring A very senior government relations or public policy leader (15+ years) with a proven record moving policy at the federal level and with state or territorial governments. Deep, bipartisan relationships across Congress and the executive branch and agencies. Experience in energy, defense, or deep tech strongly preferred. Direct experience with federal clean-energy or manufacturing incentives (45X, ITC/PTC), trade and tariffs, or industrial policy. Familiarity with the Puerto Rico government, economic development, and energy policy a strong plus. Skilled at managing lobbyists, coalitions, and complex multi-stakeholder campaigns. Exceptional judgment, discretion, and executive presence; comfortable representing the company to senior officials and in public. Spanish strongly preferred given the Puerto Rico engagement. Hybrid; based in or near Washington, D.C. or San Juan, with regular travel. Ready to build? Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Brand Manager
item.description: Senior Brand Manager Organization: Thumbtack Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes. Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance, and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know projects to do, when to do them, and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together. About the Brand Strategy Team We act as the architects of the Thumbtack brand – claiming a distinct position in the market, defining a brand promise that delivers on that position, and partnering with skilled experts across the company to bring it to life. Our work spans brand insights, brand strategy, content strategy, and integrated marketing. We set the roadmap for the brand and extend our influence beyond Marketing & Communications into all parts of the organization to make sure every touchpoint strengthens the brand. About the role As the Senior Brand Manager focused on our pro audience, you’ll help define how we position the company, what we promise pros, and how that promise comes to life across every touchpoint. Reporting directly to the Director of Brand Strategy, you’ll set vision for major brand workstreams while shaping how the team and the company think about the pro side of our brand. What you’ll do Lead foundational workstreams to help roll out our new brand playbook, including defining pro positioning and content strategy, educating and training partner teams, and more — and refresh these artifacts as the market shifts and new learnings emerge. Identify high-leverage opportunities for the brand to drive growth on the pro side of our business, then translate them into clear creative briefs and strategic direction for internal and external creative partners. Own pro brand insights work that informs strategy — including audience deep dives, creative experimentation, competitive analysis, and brand health tracking — and turn findings into clear, actionable recommendations. Partner with channel owners across Marketing and Communications to translate pro brand strategy into an integrated content strategy and creative calendar that meets business and brand goals. Extend the brand’s influence beyond Marketing and Communications by building relationships with cross-functional partners in the product, service and sales organizations; create proactive moments to communicate brand vision and align company priorities to it. Lead brand support for AI-driven content, building prompts, skills, brand review systems, and other infrastructure that allows the brand to scale as content creation becomes more decentralized. Orchestrate brand strategy and creative work for tentpole moments, including campaign launches, product launches, and major events like our annual Pro Summit. Serve as a senior voice on the Brand Strategy team — setting standards, shaping how we work, and driving alignment with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. In order to be successful, you must bring: 6-8+ years of brand marketing experience, with a strong focus on brand strategy, positioning, and messaging; experience marketing to SMBs is a plus Experience defining and implementing brand strategy – including brand promises, positioning frameworks, playbooks, and messaging architecture Experience setting brand vision and roadmap, not just managing executions – comfortable operating upstream of campaigns and influencing how the broader org thinks about brand Experience designing and managing brand health measurement programs (brand tracking, awareness, perception, brand lift) and translating findings into clear strategic action Strong creative judgment, including experience writing compelling creative briefs, providing strategic guidance to creative agencies and in-house studios, and partnering with creative teams to develop standout work Experience designing and running creative experimentation programs that improve campaign performance and feed back into brand strategy Analytical rigor — comfortable planning and executing research with the help of internal or external research partners. Adept at synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data into insights, recommendations, and business cases Expected salary ranges For candidates living in San Francisco / Bay Area, San Jose, New York City, or Seattle metros, the expected salary range for the role is currently $147,100 – $190,300. For candidates living in Austin, TX or Washington DC metros or in California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, or Washington states, the expected salary range for the role is currently $132,600 – $171,600. For candidates living in all other US locations, the expected salary range for this role is currently $125,000 – $161,700. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Public Relations & Consumer Storytelling
item.description: Manager, Public Relations & Consumer Storytelling Organization: FICO Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/30/2026 FICO (NYSE: FICO) FICO (NYSE: FICO) is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential! The Opportunity As the Manager of Public Relations & Consumer Storytelling at FICO, you will help tell the story of one of the most trusted financial tools in the United States, the FICO® Score. This role is ideal for a consumer-first communicator who can translate complex financial concepts into clear, compelling stories that build understanding and trust with the public. Working closely with senior communications leaders and cross-functional partners, you will help execute consumer-facing communications, support media relations, and develop proactive storytelling across product innovation, consumer education, data insights, and financial well-being. What You’ll Contribute Help develop and execute consumer communications and media outreach strategies that increase awareness, understanding, and trust in FICO Scores. Bring creative ideas and a strong consumer lens to the team’s storytelling and media programs. Build and maintain relationships with consumer, personal finance, and mainstream reporters; proactively pitch stories and help manage inbound media inquiries. Write and develop high-quality communications materials, including press releases, media pitches, Q&As, talking points, consumer explainer blogs, etc. Support consumer-facing narratives around product launches, score and credit education, data insights, and broader financial literacy topics. Partner with product, analytics, legal, marketing, and other stakeholders to ensure communications are accurate, timely, and aligned with business priorities. Prepare and support spokespeople for interviews, briefings, and media engagements, helping ensure clarity, confidence, and message consistency. Monitor media coverage, consumer conversations, and industry trends to identify proactive storytelling opportunities and flag emerging issues or risks. Track and analyze earned media performance, translating results into useful insights and recommendations for the communications team and internal stakeholders. Manage assigned projects from planning through execution, keeping workstreams organized, stakeholders informed, and deliverables on track. What We’re Seeking Bachelor’s degree in Public Relations, Communications, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field. 4-7+ years of experience in communications, media relations, or public relations, with meaningful experience in consumer-facing communications; experience in financial services, fintech, or another highly regulated industry is strongly preferred. Applicants with agency experience is encouraged. Proven ability to simplify complex topics and craft clear, compelling messages for consumer and mainstream media audiences. Well versed in the evolving media landscape and able to craft stories tailored to specific audiences and platforms. Experience developing press materials and building media relationships across consumer, financial, or business outlets. Demonstrated ability to manage communications projects and move work from concept through execution with appropriate guidance and collaboration. Highly collaborative, with the ability to build strong cross-functional relationships. Comfort managing multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Experience using PR tools such as Muck Rack for media monitoring, outreach, and reporting. Proactive, curious, and comfortable taking ownership, asking smart questions, and looking for ways to improve the work. Our Offer to You An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others. The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences. Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so. An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie. The targeted base pay range for this role is: $81,900 to $1,28,700 with this range reflecting differences in candidate knowledge, skills and experience. #LI-BR1 #LI-Remote Why Make a Move to FICO? At FICO, you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. You’ll play a part in our commitment to help businesses use data to improve every choice they make, using advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, and much more. FICO makes a real difference in the way businesses operate worldwide: Credit Scoring — FICO® Scores are used by 90 of the top 100 US lenders. Fraud Detection and Security — 4 billion payment cards globally are protected by FICO fraud systems. Lending — 3/4 of US mortgages are approved using the FICO Score. Global trends toward digital transformation have created tremendous demand for FICO’s solutions, placing us among the world’s top 100 software companies by revenue. We help many of the world’s largest banks, insurers, retailers, telecommunications providers and other firms reach a new level of success. Our success is dependent on really talented people – just like you – who thrive on the collaboration and innovation that’s nurtured by a diverse and inclusive environment. We’ll provide the support you need, while ensuring you have the freedom to develop your skills and grow your career. Join FICO and help change the way business thinks! Learn more about how you can fulfil your potential at www.fico.com/Careers FICO promotes a culture of inclusion and seeks to attract a diverse set of candidates for each job opportunity. We are an equal employment opportunity employer and we’re proud to offer employment and advancement opportunities to all candidates without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. Research has shown that women and candidates from underrepresented communities may not apply for an opportunity if they don’t meet all stated qualifications. While our qualifications are clearly related to role success, each candidate’s profile is unique and strengths in certain skill and/or experience areas can be equally effective. If you believe you have many, but not necessarily all, of the stated qualifications we encourage you to apply. Information submitted with your application is subject to the FICO Privacy policy at https://www.fico.com/en/privacy-policy Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Trade Compliance Manager
item.description: Trade Compliance Manager Organization: SiTime Corporation Location: Santa Clara, CA Date Posted: 09/30/2026 About SiTime SiTime is the Precision Timing company. Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. For decades, quartz devices, non-silicon technology, have kept systems in sync, but they struggle in harsher, more demanding environments. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT. Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power, and better reliability. With more than 4 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit: www.sitime.com. Job Summary The Trade Compliance Manager will be responsible for the day-to-day management of SiTime’s global trade compliance program. This role will serve as the company’s primary operational trade compliance resource, ensuring compliance with U.S. export control, sanctions, and customs regulations while supporting business growth and customer responsiveness. The successful candidate will partner closely with Legal, Customer Support, Engineering, Operations, Finance, Human Resources, and external trade compliance advisors to manage export classifications, restricted party screening, end-user reviews, licensing determinations, audits, training, and compliance process improvements. The position will also play a key role in implementing automation and scalable compliance processes as SiTime continues to grow. It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position. Responsibilities: Export Compliance Program Ownership Manage and continuously improve SiTime’s global export compliance program. Maintain trade compliance policies, procedures, and internal controls. Monitor regulatory developments and assess potential business impacts. Support compliance audits and corrective action initiatives. Maintain records necessary to demonstrate compliance with applicable regulations. Export Controls & Licensing Review export transactions for compliance with U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), OFAC sanctions programs, and other applicable trade regulations. Analyze end-users, end-uses, intermediaries, and destinations for export compliance risks. Conduct military end-user, military end-use, diversion risk, and other escalated reviews. Prepare licensing analyses and support export license applications when required. Provide practical guidance to commercial teams on export control requirements. Product Classification Partner with Engineering to determine and maintain export classifications. Support classification reviews for new products and acquisitions. Screening & Due Diligence Manage restricted party screening activities and investigate screening alerts. Support Know Your Customer (KYC) and diversion-risk assessments. Escalate significant compliance concerns to Legal leadership. Operational Support Work closely with Customer Support to ensure compliant order processing. Serve as the primary point of contact for internal compliance inquiries. Assist with customs and import compliance matters as needed. Systems, Automation & Analytics Support and enhance trade compliance systems and screening tools. Lead trade compliance automation initiatives and systems integration projects. Develop metrics, dashboards, and reporting for management. Drive process improvements that reduce manual effort while maintaining regulatory compliance. Training & Culture Develop and deliver trade compliance training programs. Promote a culture of compliance through practical business engagement and cross-functional collaboration. Qualifications & Requirements: Required Bachelor’s degree in Business, International Trade, Supply Chain, Engineering, Law, or a related discipline. 8+ years of experience in export compliance, global trade compliance, customs compliance, or related regulatory functions. Strong working knowledge of the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), BIS licensing requirements, OFAC sanctions regulations, restricted party screening, export classifications and licensing, and end-user and end-use controls. Experience supporting technology, semiconductor, electronics, aerospace, or defense-related products. Experience managing systems implementations. Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, operations, supply chain, and commercial organizations. Strong analytical, communication, and project management skills. English proficiency is required, including the ability to effectively communicate, collaborate, and perform job responsibilities in a professional business environment. Preferred Semiconductor industry experience is highly preferred. Experience with Descartes or comparable trade compliance platforms. Experience implementing compliance automation initiatives. Why Join SiTime? Help shape and scale a rapidly growing global trade compliance program. Work directly with executive leadership and legal leadership on strategic compliance initiatives. Support cutting-edge semiconductor technologies serving AI, communications, IoT, aerospace and defense, industrial, and automotive customers. Scale a compliance program that balances regulatory excellence with operational efficiency. Opportunity to grow into a leadership role managing future compliance team members as the function expands. Compensation Range: At SiTime, we believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive compensation package designed to attract top talent. The annual base salary range for this role is $138,960 – $191,070. The final offer is determined by factors such as location, experience, education, and training. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a quarterly bonus tied to the achievement of innovation goals—reflecting our commitment to recognizing meaningful impact. We also offer equity grants, providing a meaningful opportunity to share in the company’s future growth and success. Benefits offered: 401k plan, health and wellness that includes medical, dental, vision, life, parental leave, legal services, and time off plans. SiTime is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We treat each person fairly and we do not tolerate discrimination or harassment against anyone on the basis of any protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy, political affiliation, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, or marital status or other characteristics protected by law. SiTime participates in the E-Verify program. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President of Communications
item.description: Vice President of Communications Organization: Acumatica Location: Bellevue, WA Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Company Description Acumatica is a company on a mission. We are a leading innovator in cloud ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) solutions with growing businesses worldwide. Acumatica is different by design and purposely built to help small and midsized companies thrive in today’s digital economy. Our industry-specific business management solution is engineered to address real-world needs, featuring intelligent workflows and market-leading usability that enable companies to manage risk, anticipate disruption, and seize new opportunities. Our principled business practices, growth-friendly licensing, and flexible deployment options put organizations in control of their own future. Acumatica is more than just a product, we are a community of partners, customers, and creators committed to elevating business performance. Our ecosystem is driven by collaboration, merging leading technology and real-world insights to put organizations control of their future. In July of 2025, Acumatica was acquired by Vista Equity Partners, a global investment firm focused on enterprise software, data and technology-enabled businesses. Acumatica’s culture is collaborative and high-energy. We are passionate about our product and our mission, and we are loyal to each other and our company. We value work/life balance, efficiency, simplicity, freakishly friendly customer service, and making a difference in the world. Acumatica offers exceptional professional and financial growth potential. To learn more about Acumatica’s mission, please visit: http://www.acumatica.com. Job Description Acumatica is looking for an energetic VP of Communications to drive and execute public relations, analyst relations, and corporate communications to achieve brand and communications goals. This is a full-time position reporting to the CMO. Essential Responsibilities/Objectives: Media Relations: Develop and execute a comprehensive earned-media strategy encompassing corporate and product news, customer success, executive thought leadership, and proactive storytelling. Build and maintain strong relationships with business and technology journalists, editors, and other influential voices. Serve as a company spokesperson, prepare executives for media engagements, and ensure timely, accurate responses to emerging issues. Establish clear measures for coverage quality, message pull-through, share of voice, and reputation impact. Analyst Relations: Develop and execute a focused analyst relations strategy that builds understanding of Acumatica’s business, product innovation, customer value, and competitive differentiation. Identify priority analysts and influencers; manage briefings, inquiries, evaluations, research submissions, and product demonstrations; and maintain a high-touch engagement cadence. Partner closely with Product Marketing, Product Development, and other teams to deliver clear, evidence-based narratives, translate analyst feedback into actionable insights, and selectively develop analyst-led research and thought leadership content. Brand Perception and Awareness: Develop communications programs that strengthen Acumatica’s visibility, credibility, and market reputation. Advance executive speaking opportunities, corporate storytelling, awards, external communications assets, and other initiatives that demonstrate customer value and market leadership. Collaborate with Brand, Marketing, and cross-functional teams to develop communications that consistently reinforce the company narrative, positioning, and standards. Writing and Message Development: Own and evolve Acumatica’s corporate narrative, messaging framework, and priority storylines. Write and edit press releases, thought leadership articles, presentations, broad-reach employee and partner communications, and content for relevant corporate, press, and event pages. Integrate customer and partner evidence into news and thought leadership campaigns, and keep messaging current and aligned across leadership, Marketing, Sales, Product, and other teams. Use AI-enabled tools thoughtfully to support research, drafting, editing, and workflow efficiency while maintaining human review, accuracy, confidentiality, and a distinctive Acumatica voice. Executive Communications: Develop and execute communications strategies for senior executives, including speeches, presentations, talking points, thought leadership pieces, and executive social content. Provide trusted counsel on messaging, positioning, audience needs, media interactions, and public appearances. Lead content development for priority company moments, including Acumatica Summit, all-company meetings, partner community webinars, roadshows, and other executive engagements. Social Media Management: Oversee corporate and executive social media strategies that strengthen brand visibility, thought leadership, and audience engagement. Collaborate with agency partners and internal teams to maintain a consistent, timely, and audience-relevant presence across priority platforms. Use channel analytics, social listening, and emerging-issue monitoring to improve performance and inform broader communications strategies. Editorial and Content Quality Oversight: Lead the editing and writing function to maintain clear, accurate, consistent, and high-quality communications across channels. Establish editorial standards, review and approval processes, and practical quality controls for both human- and AI-assisted content. Ensure communications reflect the company’s messaging, tone, accessibility standards, and business priorities. Communications Budget Management: Own and manage the public relations, analyst relations, content, social media, and communications program budget. Lead annual planning and forecasting, manage agency and vendor relationships, evaluate program effectiveness, and allocate resources to the initiatives with the greatest strategic and business impact. Qualifications Who you are… Strategic thinker: Build messaging and positioning strategy for the company, including key differentiation and value propositions. Results-oriented. Self-starter with excellent multi-tasking skills. Must be able to work independently in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment. Communicator. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Adaptable. Strong project management capabilities to drive multiple projects/priorities simultaneously. Experienced. Minimum of 15+ years relevant communications experience. Previous experience with a B2B software company preferred. BS degree or equivalent required. Additional Information Acumatica is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please e-mail [email protected] . This email is created exclusively to assist disabled job seekers whose disability prevents them from being able to apply online. Only emails sent for this purpose will be returned. Emails sent for other purposes, such as following up on an application or technical issues not related to a disability, will not receive a response. For this role, the salary range is $240,000-260,000 annually. This range represents the low and high end of the salary range for this job and may vary based on location. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including skills, qualifications, experience and other relevant elements. At Acumatica, certain roles are eligible for additional rewards, including annual bonus and stock. These awards are allocated based on individual performance. In addition, certain roles also have the opportunity to earn sales incentives based on revenue or utilization, depending on the terms of the plan and the employee’s role. Benefits/perks listed here may vary depending on the nature of your employment with Acumatica and the country where you work. US-based employees gain access to healthcare benefits (medical, dental and vision insurance for you and your dependents), employer paid Short-Term/Long-Term Disability and Basic life coverage, 401(k) plan with company match, Flexible time off, sick and safe leave, among others. item.title: Director of Advocacy and Communications
item.description: Director of Advocacy and Communications Organization: National Council For Adoption (NCFA) Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Recruitment Partner National Council For Adoption has partnered with Big Fish on this search. For questions or referrals, please contact Angel Fimbres-Barcelo at [email protected] . Position Title: Director of Advocacy and Communications Reports To: Vice President of Operations and President & CEO Supervises: None Employment Status: Full-time Salary Range: $80,000 – $90,000 Position Overview This position would coordinate NCFA’s government relations, advocacy, and external communications work. The person would manage NCFA’s government relations consultant, coordinate internal policy and advocacy activities, and oversee NCFA’s social media presence and email communications, including newsletters, advocacy alerts, and other campaigns. They would ensure that NCFA communicates clearly, consistently, and effectively with policymakers, members, partners, and the public. The person would not necessarily serve as NCFA’s primary lobbyist but would be responsible for keeping NCFA’s advocacy and communications work coordinated, timely, and moving forward. Key Responsibilities The following are the primary responsibilities of this position, including major areas of work, recurring responsibilities, and important projects or functions that this position owns or supports. Manage the relationship, priorities, and work plan with NCFA’s government relations consultant. Coordinate NCFA’s federal policy and advocacy priorities, timelines, meetings, materials, and follow-up. Monitor relevant legislative and regulatory developments in partnership with staff, consultants, members, and other stakeholders. Draft or coordinate advocacy alerts, policy updates, talking points, letters, testimony, public statements, and other external materials. Support congressional meetings, Advocacy Day, coalition engagement, and other government relations activities. Manage NCFA’s social media presence, including developing the content calendar, gathering content and expertise from staff and partners, adapting materials for different platforms, scheduling posts, and monitoring engagement. Plan and execute NCFA’s email communications and campaigns, including newsletters, advocacy alerts, organizational announcements, and other audience-specific outreach. Develop and manage an integrated editorial calendar across social media, email, website, advocacy, and other external communications. Manage website content and routine updates in coordination with NCFA’s external marketing and website consultants. Ensure that NCFA’s messaging is accurate, consistent, accessible, and respectful of the diverse experiences within adoption. Track communications and advocacy metrics and use them to strengthen future outreach and engagement. Qualifications NCFA recognizes that not every candidate will bring all of the knowledge, skills and experiences listed below, and welcomes candidates with a variety of experiences. Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in advocacy, public policy, communications, government relations, or a related field. Excellent written communication and demonstrated ability to translate complex policy issues for different audiences. Experience coordinating advocacy campaigns, coalitions, consultants, or legislative activity. Familiarity with federal policymaking and congressional processes. Experience managing organizational social media, email campaigns, and editorial calendars. Sound judgment when communicating about sensitive or contested issues. Experience with child welfare, adoption, family policy, or a related field preferred. Collaboration & Relationships Internal: Vice President of Operations, President and CEO, NCFA staff, and other staff involved in policy, programming, research, and external communications. External: Government relations consultant, policymakers and congressional offices, coalition partners, members, external marketing and website consultants, and other advocacy and communications partners. Other Duties: This position may be asked to perform other duties and responsibilities that are reasonably related to the position and support NCFA’s mission and organizational needs. item.title: Vice President, Communications
item.description: Vice President, Communications Organization: Comella & Co. Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Vice President, Communications At Comella & Co., we help organizations tell their most important stories and reach the audiences that matter most. We were founded by Maria Comella, a nationally recognized strategist who has been described as a political unicorn because she is one of the few leaders to have earned trust and delivered results on both sides of the aisle. From the campaign trail to the C-suite, Maria has guided presidential campaigns, led communications for fast-growing companies, and advised governors in both New York and New Jersey. Her experience across politics, government, and the private sector gives our work its distinctive edge: clear strategy, creative thinking, and the ability to navigate complexity with purpose and impact. We are an entrepreneurial and fast-growing firm seeking a Vice President of Communications to lead at the highest level: someone who can set strategy, drive media engagement, and deliver results that shape conversations locally and nationally. This is a senior leadership role for a proven media operator with strong corporate and agency communications experience and deep relationships across the technology and business press, with a track record of breaking through in competitive news environments. This person will not only execute but define strategy, elevate our clients’ profiles, and expand our firm’s reach. What You’ll Do Serve as senior communications strategist across a portfolio of high-profile clients in business, public affairs, and beyond. Develop and lead comprehensive, integrated communications strategies aligned with client growth, reputation, and policy objectives. Leverage extensive relationships with media relationships to secure top-tier coverage across print, digital, broadcast, and emerging platforms, and proactively identify new reporters, editors, producers, and platforms aligned with evolving client narratives. Demonstrate a genuine passion for relationship building by researching, pursuing, and cultivating new connections, even without prior relationships, and thoughtfully matching the right story to the right audience. Proactively identify narrative opportunities and aggressively drive story placement in competitive news cycles. Shape executive visibility strategies, including major interviews, thought leadership placements, keynote speaking engagements, and opinion pieces. Contribute to business development efforts, including participating in pitches and helping expand client relationships. Refuse to accept “no.” Relentlessly pursue creative angles, alternative pathways, and breakthrough ideas to achieve results. What You’ll Bring 12+ years of communications experience in a fast moving environment such as a start-up or political campaign. Extensive, active relationships with top-tier technology and business press, and a proven ability to build new relationships from the ground up. A demonstrable history of successful media relations and extensive on the record experience. Experience advising senior executives, political leaders, or high-profile principals. Exceptional writing, editing, and message development skills. Strategic mindset with the ability to see around corners and anticipate risks and opportunities. Strong leadership presence with experience managing teams and mentoring talent. Entrepreneurial drive and comfort operating in a fast-paced, growing firm. Creativity, fearlessness, and the confidence to push boundaries when needed. Why Join Us You’ll join a collaborative, ambitious team that values creativity, curiosity, and results. As a senior leader, you’ll help shape the future of the firm, drive marquee accounts, and build a best-in-class communications operation grounded in strategy and bold execution. This role offers significant leadership opportunities, influence over firm growth, and the ability to make an impact through meaningful client work. This is a hybrid role. Work from home or in the office on Tuesday and Friday, and in our New York City office Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. At Comella & Co., we offer: Medical Dental Vision 401(k) 20 days of PTO $160,000 – $180,000 a year Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Manager, Government Relations & Grassroots Advocacy
item.description: Manager, Government Relations & Grassroots Advocacy Organization: Lupus Foundation of America (LFA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Salary Range: $65,000.00 To $75,000.00 Annually Position Title: Manager, Government Relations & Grassroots Advocacy Supervisor/Manager: Senior Director Advocacy & Government Relations Employment Classification: Exempt Date: June 2026 Location: Washington, DC Salary: $65,000 – $75,000 POSITION SUMMARY The Lupus Foundation of America (LFA) is dedicated to improving the quality of life for all people affected by lupus through programs of research, education, and advocacy. The Manager, Government Relations and Grassroots Advocacy will be an integral member of the Lupus Foundation of America’s Advocacy and Government Relations team by assisting in implementing the Foundation’s year-round public policy program. This is a hybrid position, based in the national headquarters of the Lupus Foundation of America in Washington, D.C. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Roles and responsibilities of the Manager, Government Relations and Grassroots Advocacy include, but are not limited to: Manage the Lupus Foundation of America’s grassroots program, including developing materials to support grassroots engagement and recruitment of advocates across LFA programs. Conduct grassroots advocacy campaigns, including developing advocacy alerts and updates, talking points and supporting materials for advancing the Foundation’s federal and state policy priorities. Monitor Federal and State legislative issues relating to the Foundation’s public policy priorities, including those impacting access to care and research (e.g. Medicare, Medicaid, National Institutes of Health, Food and Drug Administration, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention among others.) Partner with LFA Network Development staff to ensure Advocacy activities in all regional activities, including educational conferences, support groups, and walks. Work with Advocacy & Government Relations team to coordinate participation in and development of strategic coalitions on federal and state policy issues. Represent the Foundation in meetings with members of Congress and regulatory agencies. Support planning and implementation of the Foundation’s National Lupus Advocacy Summit and other advocacy conferences and events. Create policy communications for distribution on the Foundation’s website, social media, electronic newsletters and other communications channels. Convey a professional and positive image that reflects favorably on the Foundation. Other duties as assigned. POSITION REQUIREMENTS A cover letter is required with this application. Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university. Three+ years related experience preferably on Capitol Hill, the patient advocacy community, in government or the equivalent combination of education and work experience. Excellent interpersonal skills and proficient computer and internet research skills are a must. Understanding of the legislative process. Experience developing and conducting grassroots campaigns and working with advocates. Detail oriented and strong organizational skills required. Capable of handling diversified assignments and highly adaptable. The ability to work well in a fast-paced environment interfacing with all levels of management and volunteers, as well as Congressional staff and other elected officials. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Self-starter Working at Lupus The Lupus Foundation of America prioritizes the health and well-being of its employees. The Foundation offers a highly competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision and life insurance covered at 100% for the employee. We provide sick, vacation, and personal leave, and we follow the federal government for holiday closures. Other benefits include Health Reimbursement Arrangement, Flexible Spending Accounts and an Employee Assistance Program. Other Details Candidates who reside in the Washington, DC area will report in office at least twice a week. Must have a dedicated home office or workspace with reliable internet connectivity, ensuring the ability to perform job duties effectively and participate in virtual meetings without disruptions. Ability to interact with people of all ages and cultural backgrounds. LFA participates in E-Verify. Background checks are required. JOIN US If you’re a dynamic, mission-driven individual passionate about driving positive change and improving lives, we encourage you to apply! At LFA, your contributions will help solve the mystery of lupus and create a world where people with lupus can live healthier, fuller lives while making a lasting difference. Equal Opportunity Employer The Lupus Foundation of America is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. item.title: Director, Regulatory Affairs – Europe
item.description: Director, Regulatory Affairs – Europe Organization: Breakthrough T1D Location: Remote (BE) Date Posted: 09/30/2026 As the leading global type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy organization, Breakthrough T1D helps make everyday life with T1D better while driving toward cures. We invest in the most promising research to turn ideas into life-changing therapies and devices. We work with government, regulatory officials, and insurance companies to address issues that impact the T1D community — breaking through barriers that limit access to care worldwide. We provide resources and guidance that makes it easier to live and thrive with T1D. This is more than a moment — we’re empowering a movement for the T1D community. Share your support and help educate and empower individuals facing type 1 diabetes. Our mission is to improve lives today and tomorrow by accelerating life changing breakthroughs to treat, prevent and ultimately, cure T1D and its complications. Always, we are guided by a single purpose: As we drive towards curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it. This position is based in a Country located within the European Union. BROAD FUNCTION AND SCOPE OF THE POSITION: Working closely with the Senior Director, Regulatory Affairs and cross-functional colleagues in the European Union (EU) and the United States (US), implement Breakthrough T1D’s regulatory strategy in the EU, with the goal of accelerating the development, evaluation, and regulatory approval of therapies for type 1 diabetes (T1D). Provide regulatory leadership across Breakthrough T1D’s EU activities, with particular focus on regulatory affairs and regulatory science, evidence generation and clinical trial design, and engagement with partners across the T1D ecosystem. Strengthen Breakthrough T1D’s role as a leader in regulatory innovation across the EU. SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES: Implement Breakthrough T1D’s regulatory strategy to accelerate the development and regulatory approval of T1D products in the EU, including cell therapies, disease modifying therapies, and therapies to improve glucose control and address T1D-realted complications. Identify and develop solutions to key regulatory and regulatory science challenges in the development and approval of T1D therapies, including advancing T1D biomarkers and surrogate endpoints, clinical outcome assessments, use of digital-health technologies, use of real-world data/real-world evidence, and other approaches to accelerate the development of novel therapies. In close collaboration with Advocacy colleagues, help shape the regulatory priorities, perspectives, and policies of decision makers across the EU T1D development ecosystem Strengthen and expand Breakthrough T1D’s role as a leader and trusted partner in regulatory innovation in the EU Develop and maintain effective relationships with leading T1D experts and regulatory stakeholders in the EU, including leadership and staff at the European Medicines Agency and other national competent authorities. Engage with industry partners to understand and address regulatory challenges and advance regulatory approaches that support T1D product development in the EU. Provide regulatory guidance for Breakthrough T1D funded researchers and initiatives to help align research and evidence generation with regulatory expectations. Track, assess and evaluate relevant EU legislative and regulatory policy development and identify implications and opportunities for to advance Breakthrough T1D priorities. Report on progress and advise Breakthrough T1D leadership on regulatory issues in the EU, as needed. Identify needs for outside regulatory advisors or consultants and oversee work as necessary. Engage and collaborate with Breakthrough T1D Affiliates on overall strategy, common regulatory policy priorities, and approach to key decision makers. Collaborate closely with members of the Breakthrough T1D Research, Advocacy, and Medical Affairs programs Perform other duties as assigned by his/her immediate supervisor. EDUCATION: Advanced scientific, legal, or business degree preferred. YEARS OF EXPERIENCE: 8+ years of related experience in regulatory affairs, regulatory science, or other medical product development disciplines. Type 1 diabetes related experience preferred. KNOWLEDGE: Extensive knowledge of EU regulatory laws, guidelines, processes, and officials. Knowledge of other regulatory agencies or national competent authorities a plus. OTHER REQUIREMENTS: Proven track record of success in regulatory policy, regulatory affairs, or regulatory science for complicated medical therapies Highly collaborative with demonstrated ability to work effectively across functions, disciplines, geographies, and organizations. Experience successfully managing projects and initiatives as part of a coordinated strategy Experience working with a wide variety of external stakeholders, including academic researchers, industry, and regulators preferred A self starter with ability to work independently and in close coordination with other staff Ability to effectively multi-task, establish priorities, and demonstrate flexibility and responsiveness. Excellent written, oral, communication, and interpersonal skills. Travel within Europe and to the U.S. (approximately 10%). Targeted salary range will be provided to candidate prior to initial phone screen. Essential Functions: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands or fingers, handle or feel objects, tools or controls. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, sit, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and infrequently up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Benefits: Breakthrough T1D offers competitive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 403(b) retirement plan, voluntary benefits, flexible spending and commuter benefit accounts, an employee assistance program (EAP), life and disability insurance, performance-based bonuses, and generous paid time off. Benefits may vary by job level and full time or part time status. Additional information: Requests for medical, religious, and other exemptions will be considered on an individual basis. Breakthrough T1D will comply with all federal, state, and local laws. Breakthrough T1D supports a diverse and inclusive workforce. Breakthrough T1D is an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: Director, Health Policy
item.description: Director, Health Policy Organization: Breakthrough T1D Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/30/2026 As the leading global type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy organization, Breakthrough T1D helps make everyday life with T1D better while driving toward cures. We invest in the most promising research to turn ideas into life-changing therapies and devices. We work with government, regulatory officials, and insurance companies to address issues that impact the T1D community — breaking through barriers that limit access to care worldwide. We provide resources and guidance that makes it easier to live and thrive with T1D. This is more than a moment — we’re empowering a movement for the T1D community. Share your support and help educate and empower individuals facing type 1 diabetes. Our mission is to improve lives today and tomorrow by accelerating life changing breakthroughs to treat, prevent and ultimately, cure T1D and its complications. Always, we are guided by a single purpose: As we drive towards curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it. The Director of Health Policy will drive strategic efforts to advance access to care, devices, and drugs for people with T1D. This role will be primarily responsible for advancing broad, affordable access to diabetes devices including continuous glucose monitors, insulin pumps, automated insulin delivery systems, and continuous ketone monitors. Working closely with Breakthrough T1D’s leaders, research colleagues, and volunteers, the Director of Health Policy will lead national commercial health plan and public policy efforts to eliminate coverage barriers and modernize coding in order to accelerate the adoption of life-changing diabetes technology. The person in this role must be a motivated, executive-paced self-starter with a proven track record of leading successful, cross-functional policy and commercial reimbursement projects. Specific Responsibilities Strategy Execution: Enhance and lead the execution of Breakthrough T1D’s diabetes technology and device access strategy to identify and systematically remove coverage barriers in both public and commercial markets. Payer & Stakeholder Engagement: Develop and maintain effective, impactful relationships with commercial health plans, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), employers, coding bodies (AMA/HCPCS), and other relevant external stakeholders. Regulatory Analysis: Lead the technical review and analysis of CMS rulemaking and private payer medical policies impacting access to T1D care. Community Resource Design: Provide technical guidance and subject matter expertise to support the development of external communication resources for the T1D community and other external stakeholders. Executive Communication: Translate complex public policy, reimbursement codes, and health economics data into clear, concise talking points and one-pagers for internal leaders and external stakeholders. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate closely with colleagues across Breakthrough T1D Advocacy, Research, Medical Affairs, and Communications teams to ensure technical alignment. External Representation: Serve as the access subject matter expert at Congressional meetings, agency briefings, workshops, and major healthcare industry conferences. Team Integration: Support other Breakthrough T1D access goals related to insulin, care, and general health policy priorities, as needed. Education Bachelor’s Degree required. Advanced Degree/Masters in related healthcare, business, or policy field strongly preferred. Experience & Requirements Years of Experience: 10+ years of experience in advocacy, market access, health care policy, medical device reimbursement, or digital health technology. Commercial and Government Payer Policy Expertise: Expert knowledge of public and private payer landscapes, reimbursement coding (HCPCS/CPT), and public policies impacting access. Systems Knowledge: Deep understanding of the US healthcare system is required. Detail & Self-Management: Detail-oriented, self-starter, with strong organizational skills who can manage processes autonomously. Communication Skills: Demonstrated ability to concisely present complex technology or financial concepts through exceptional written and verbal communication. Relationship Management: A team player with a proven ability to build and manage relationships with all levels of staff, volunteers, external industry partners and government officials.. Speed & Precision: Proven track record of working in dynamic environment to synthesize complex policies and deliver polished outputs under tight deadlines. Software: Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Travel: Ability to travel (less than 30%). item.title: Outreach Director – Western Region
item.description: Outreach Director – Western Region Organization: U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/30/2026 The U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) is seeking an experienced Outreach Director – Western Region to lead a dynamic Western Outreach Team. The Director will be responsible for USGLC’s engagement with our network of influential business, national security, non-profit, civic and foreign policy local leaders to support America’s role in the world and further efforts with members of Congress to support strategic investments in diplomacy and international assistance, alongside a strong military, that strengthen U.S. national security and our economic interests as well as reflect American values. The Outreach Director – Western Region will be an experienced professional with the knowledge and connections to sustain USGLC’s existing state-based coalitions and expand our network of supporters to advance U.S. economic and national security through USGLC’s mission. This is a full-time exempt position. The ideal candidate will reside preferably in the Western Region and will require frequent travel within the region and to Washington, DC headquarters. At USGLC, we are committed to a culture of inclusiveness and belonging among staff, volunteers, and partners. Responsibilities Develop USGLC’s Western State Outreach Strategy. Develop a multi-faceted educational and outreach strategy in select states (Texas, New Mexico, Colorado, Oklahoma, Utah, Arizona, Nevada, Idaho and Washington) by identifying, recruiting and working with influential business, civic, military, academic and faith-based leaders to support USGLC’s outreach goals and congressional engagement. Implement the Western State Outreach Strategy. Develop and execute local events and meetings, regular communications, Advisory Council engagement at the local level and other mobilization actions. Manage the Regional Outreach Team. Manage the Outreach Director, who has responsibility for a subset of the Western Region states, and the regional associate. Implement USGLC’s Impact Educational Activities. Lead these activities in the western states in coordination with others on the Outreach Team. Represent USGLC. Represent USGLC at local events in the western states and nationally as needed on the importance of a strong diplomatic and international assistance effort. Position Requirements The ideal candidate will have: A minimum of five years of experience in a political campaign and/or issue-advocacy setting. Presidential, senatorial and/or congressional campaign experience is highly desirable, with experience preferred in western states. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, international relations or another related field preferred. Demonstrated ability to proactively engage prominent leaders in the political, business, faith-based, military, academic and civic communities in the western states. Experience planning meetings and large events, writing, organizing and training local influencers. Experience successfully managing and mentoring staff. Demonstrated ability to set priorities, meet deadlines, work under pressure in a team-based environment and proactively anticipate and address department needs. Outstanding public speaking skills, the ability to create and deliver presentations before high-profile audiences and knowledge of international relations. Ability to work and thrive in a fast-paced, fluid and flexible team environment. Ability and desire to travel domestically, primarily in the Western states, on a frequent basis. Compensation A projected salary range of $90,000 to $110,000 will be offered, commensurate with experience and qualifications. USGLC also provides a package of benefits, including health and disability insurance, a retirement plan, paid annual and sick leave and federal holidays. To Apply Please email a cover letter and resume to [email protected] . Please reference “Outreach Director – Western Region” in the email subject line. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted. No calls, please. About USGLC The U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) is a bipartisan, broad-based, influential network of 500 businesses, non-profit organizations, national security and foreign policy experts, and business, veteran, agriculture, faith-based, academic and civic leaders in all 50 states who support strategic, cost-effective investments in diplomacy and international assistance, alongside a strong defense, to advance U.S. interests and values and strengthen American leadership in the world. item.title: Policy & Outreach Manager
item.description: Policy & Outreach Manager Organization: National Taxpayers Union (NTU) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/30/2026 National Taxpayers Union (NTU) and National Taxpayers Union Foundation (NTUF) are seeking a full-time Policy & Outreach Manager to lead the organization’s efforts to reduce regulations and other barriers that hinder the free flow of commerce, such as trade, logistics and transportation. The expected salary range is $75,000 – $90,000. This is a hybrid position based out of our Washington, DC office, with at least three days per week spent in office. The Manager may also need to attend evening and weekend events. The Manager will serve as NTU and NTUF’s primary point of coordination on logistical, trade and related regulatory policies, such as the Jones Act and other maritime commerce matters. The position will involve developing a strategic reform agenda; building and managing relationships with coalition partners, policymakers, congressional offices, and other stakeholders; monitoring legislative and political developments; and ensuring that the organization can respond quickly and effectively to emerging opportunities and challenges. Responsibilities: Develop and execute strategies for reducing or repealing regulatory barriers to commerce. Build and maintain relationships with congressional offices, relevant committees, executive-branch officials, coalition partners, and other key stakeholders. Expand and coordinate a coalition of organizations and advocates working on regulatory, economic, transportation, maritime, energy, and taxpayer issues. Track legislative, regulatory, administrative, and political developments to identify and capitalize on opportunities for reform. Coordinate coalition activities, including joint statements, advocacy campaigns, briefings, and events, and represent the organization in relevant policy discussions. Monitor congressional activity and ensure the organization is positioned to respond quickly and effectively to emerging opportunities and developments. Qualifications: Experience working in public policy, government affairs, congressional relations, advocacy, or a related field. Strong understanding of the federal policymaking and legislative processes. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with policymakers, advocacy organizations, and other stakeholders. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously. Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and respond quickly to rapidly changing political circumstances. Familiarity with regulatory policy, maritime policy, transportation policy, or related issues. NTU is a 501(c)(4) nonprofit, nonpartisan citizen group whose supporters work every day for lower taxes and smaller government at all levels. NTUF is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization, the research and educational arm of NTU. NTU and NTUF are equal opportunity employers and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need. While we thank all applicants in advance for their interest in this position, we are only able to contact those to whom we can offer an interview. No phone calls please. item.title: Associate Director Government Affairs
item.description: Associate Director Government Affairs Organization: American Civil Liberties Union of New Jersey (ACLU-NJ) Location: Trenton, NJ Date Posted: 09/30/2026 Position Overview The American Civil Liberties Union of New Jersey seeks an Associate Director of Government Affairs to join its growing Political Advocacy Department. This position is a senior member of the ACLU-NJ Political Advocacy team, responsible for developing and maintaining the organization’s strategic relationships across local, state, and federal government to advance and protect the ACLU-NJ’s civil liberties priorities. Alongside the Executive Director and the Political Director, the Associate Director of Government Affairs serves as a primary external representative of the organization in government-facing contexts, bringing a combination of relationship management, legislative acumen, and advocacy strategy to a broad portfolio of policy campaigns. Organizational Overview For more than 60 years, the ACLU of New Jersey has defended liberty and justice guided by the vision of a fair and equitable New Jersey for all. Our mission is to preserve, advance, and extend the individual rights and liberties guaranteed to every New Jerseyan by the state and federal constitutions in courts, in the legislature, and in our communities. We are committed to repairing and transforming spaces where constitutional promises have not been delivered. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Government Relations and External Representation: Develop, cultivate, and manage strategic relationships with elected officials, legislative staff, and executive branch officials at the local, state, and federal levels. Serve as an external representative of the ACLU-NJ in meetings with legislators, congressional staff, and government agencies. Advocate directly on behalf of the ACLU-NJ’s positions with legislators, their staff, and executive branch officials, alongside ACLU-NJ subject matter experts. Represent the ACLU-NJ at legislative hearings, briefings, press events, lobby days, and other government-facing engagements and serve as a spokesperson in the media. Maintain compliance with all applicable lobbying registration and disclosure requirements. Legislative Strategy: Provide strategic counsel to the Political Director, Executive Director and other senior leaders, and the Political Advocacy team on government relations matters and political landscape developments. Identify and pursue opportunities to advance ACLU-NJ priorities through legislative, regulatory, and executive action, in partnership with the Political Advocacy team. Coordinate with the National ACLU and peer affiliates on federal advocacy priorities, joint campaigns, and legislative strategy alignment. Internal Collaboration: Partner closely with the Political Advocacy team to ensure government relations work is grounded in policy expertise and aligned with campaign strategies. Collaborate with subject matter experts and with the Communications team to develop government-facing messaging, including testimony, briefing materials, and stakeholder one-pagers. Supervise, mentor, and provide direction to junior staff and Policy Fellows as assigned. Contribute to organizational planning and priority-setting as a senior member of the Political Advocacy team in collaboration with other members of the Political Advocacy team. Administrative: Prepare regular reports on government affairs activities for the Political Director and senior leadership. Other duties as assigned. Support departmental planning, project management, and administrative functions as needed. Equity, Inclusion and Belonging: Advance ACLU-NJ’s commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging in advocacy strategies, organizational practices, and community partnerships. Contribute to department and organization-wide efforts to ensure programs, policies, and engagement practices are inclusive, equitable, and responsive to impacted communities. Candidate Requirements Demonstrated track record of building and maintaining effective, trust-based relationships with elected officials and government staff. Experience working in, or directly with, New Jersey state government or the New Jersey legislature strongly preferred. Experience in civil rights, social justice, nonprofit advocacy, or a mission-driven organization preferred. Experience with federal legislative or administrative advocacy a plus. Prior management or supervisory experience preferred. This position will be primarily based in Trenton, with regular travel around the state, including to the ACLU-NJ headquarters in Newark. Knowledge and Skills: Deep knowledge of the legislative and regulatory process, particularly at the New Jersey state level. Existing relationships with New Jersey legislators, legislative staff, and/or executive branch officials strongly preferred. Strategic thinker with the ability to identify policy opportunities, assess political dynamics, and develop effective advocacy approaches. Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to represent the organization credibly and persuasively in high-stakes external settings. Skilled at building trust and credibility with a broad range of stakeholders — from elected officials and government staff to community organizations and coalition partners. Strong judgment and discretion, with the ability to navigate complex political environments with integrity. Ability to manage a broad portfolio of relationships and concurrent advocacy campaigns simultaneously. Familiarity with lobbying compliance and registration requirements preferred. Values and Commitment: Demonstrated commitment to civil liberties, civil rights, and social justice, and alignment with the ACLU-NJ’s mission and values. Commitment to equity, inclusion, and authentic partnership with the communities the ACLU-NJ serves. Ability to engage respectfully and effectively with individuals across the political spectrum in pursuit of civil liberties goals. Willingness to occasionally work non-traditional hours to attend meetings and events in the evenings or weekends. Preferred Qualifications: The following are not required, but will strengthen a candidate’s application: Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish (or another language spoken by New Jersey communities). Existing relationships with members of the New Jersey congressional delegation or their staff. Experience working on civil rights, criminal justice reform, immigrant rights, LGBTQ+ rights, or voting rights campaigns. Experience with federal agency advocacy or administrative rulemaking processes. Experience using legislative tracking tools. Compensation The salary range for this position starts at $110,000 and will be commensurate with experience based on the ACLU-NJ salary bands. The ACLU-NJ supports and plans for staff member professional growth and skill development through internal and external opportunities. We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package which currently includes 30 days paid time off, 12 office holidays and 16 health care leave days; medical, vision, and dental insurance; 20 weeks (100 days) paid family leave; life and long-term disability insurance; pre-tax transit benefits; and a 401(k) plan with employer match. This position is exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act. About our Culture We are a diverse workforce and take pride in our ability to attract and retain employees with a huge array of backgrounds and experiences. We work hard but also like to celebrate our successes. We strive to bring humility, empathy, kindness, and generosity to our work, internally within the organization and externally with our partners and those whom we are serving. We seek to build a work culture with a sense of respect and collegiality, and a willingness to be generous with our expertise and resources. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Marketing Associate
item.description: Marketing Associate Organization: Management and Planning Associates (MPA) Location: Remote Date Posted: 09/30/2026 ​MPA is seeking a Marketing Associate to support the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). You will work on a national effort to strengthen cybersecurity and physical security resilience among state, local, tribal, and territorial (SLTT) audiences. You will design and conduct research that reveals what SLTT audiences know, believe, and need, then translate those findings into communications messages and materials that move stakeholders from awareness to action. You will work with an integrated team of marketing communications professionals to ensure every product the team delivers is evidence-based, written in plain language, and built for SLTT audiences. ​The responsibilities of this position include: ​Design and execute primary and secondary research (e.g., environmental scans, literature reviews, stakeholder interviews, focus groups, surveys, and social listening) to identify best practices for SLTT-level cybersecurity programs Assess SLTT awareness of CISA and its resources, and establish baselines and recommend where communications can and will have the greatest effect Develop and maintain a content strategy and editorial calendar across web, email, social, video, print, and event channels, ensuring a consistent voice and alignment with CISA brand and messaging guidance Write and edit clear, accurate, audience-focused content, including fact sheets, statistics and data points, talking points, articles, blog posts, newsletters, web copy, social content, and scripts for short-form video Build a toolkit of custom materials that CISA and SLTT stakeholders can adapt to train others on essential cybersecurity actions Provide content support for live and livestreamed events, including research-informed agendas, speaker briefs and talking points, presentation narratives, moderator and discussion guides, invitation copy, and post-event summaries Define and track measurement by establishing key performance indicators and analyzing content performance, conducting pre- and post-communications awareness measurement, and delivering findings and optimization recommendations Conduct content audits and comparative reviews of peer agency and partner communications to identify gaps, redundancies, and opportunities Manage source documentation, fact-checking, and version control of communications products and/or materials, and support review and clearance workflows, incorporating subject matter expert and stakeholder feedback while preserving message integrity Collaborate closely with the Program Manager, designers, video producers, event staff, and CISA stakeholders to keep research, creative, and logistics aligned Stay current on the SLTT policy and cybersecurity landscape, communications research methods, and emerging artificial intelligence-enabled tools Ensure all work products and deliverables meet Section 508 and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 AA accessibility standards, plain-language requirements, and federal editorial and style conventions The ideal candidate will have the following: ​Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, public policy, the social sciences, or a related field 4+ years of experience in communications, with demonstrated expertise in research content strategy and/or closely related disciplines, preferably with federal government agencies that have cybersecurity missions Demonstrated experience supporting qualitative and quantitative research, such as interviews, focus groups, surveys, literature reviews, environmental scans, and/or social listening, particularly with SLTT audiences Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deliverables and deadlines simultaneously Excellent collaboration and interpersonal skills, with experience working across research, creative, digital, and account or program management functions Working knowledge of Section 508/WCAG accessibility requirements and plain-language principles U.S. citizenship required, with the ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Entry on Duty suitability determination Please send your resume and any applicable work samples to [email protected] Earn a certificate with the Council!
