item.title: Manager, Legislative Counsel
item.description: Manager, Legislative Counsel Organization: Lyft Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 09/30/2026 At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Lyft is looking for a Legislative Counsel to join our fast-growing and fast-paced team. Based in Washington D.C this stellar individual will be directly involved in shaping the policy framework for the evolving ridesharing industry as a pivotal part of our Public Policy team. Responsibilities: Provide legal expertise to Lyft’s Public Policy team on legislative issues. Track, analyze, and evaluate proposed legislation across topic areas, identifying risks and opportunities. Draft legislative language, amendments, and recommendations that reflect the interests of Lyft’s users and business. Identify legislative trends and develop responsive strategies across subject matters and jurisdictions. Collaborate cross-functionally to assess legislative impacts and inform decision-making. Partner with Lyft’s regional Public Policy team members on market-specific legislative efforts. Develop leading expertise on a specific issue area, in coordination with their manager. Coordinate with Lyft’s compliance, legal, and operations teams as new regulatory frameworks are implemented. Experience: Law degree required. 5+ years of experience with legislative drafting for a local, state and/or federal legislative body, or at a trade association or company. Exceptional ability to critically analyze policy and legal issues. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, demanding (and sometimes unstructured) environment. Self-starter; intrinsically motivated. Experience with insurance, transportation, technology, AI, privacy, or labor and employment law a plus but not required Benefits: Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled Mental health benefits Family building benefits Child care and pet benefits 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible Subsidized commuter benefits Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. Your recruiter can share more information about the various in-office perks Lyft offers. Additionally, hybrid roles have the flexibility to work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year. #Hybrid The expected base pay range for this position in the Washington D.C. area is $118,000 – $147,500, not inclusive of potential equity offering, bonus or benefits. Salary ranges are dependent on a variety of factors, including qualifications, experience and geographic location. Your recruiter can share more information about the salary range specific to your working location and other factors during the hiring process. item.title: Director of Social Media
item.description: Director of Social Media Organization: Sierra Club Location: Washington, DC | Oakland, CA | Remote Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Context: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees. Scope: The Director of Social Media is a strategic, creative leader who shapes how Sierra Club shows up on social media. They do this by leveraging data and audience segmentation and combining an understanding of the latest social trends and creative content to tell a cohesive public narrative, generate concrete campaign wins, and foster meaningful engagement. This position requires a proven track-record of managing people, projects, and platforms to achieve successful outcomes around list growth and retention, campaigning and organizing, culture change, fundraising, and brand objectives. This person must be comfortable working in a fast-paced, multi-tasking environment and managing a small team within a much larger group of stakeholders. The Director of Social Media will advocate for the strategies and build and manage the systems, processes, and standards that enable effective social media collaboration across the organization. They will serve as a strategic partner and educator to a variety of internal stakeholders, helping our colleagues understand how to work effectively with the Social Media team and support them in translating their expertise and priorities into compelling content for our social media audiences. To be successful, the Director of Social Media will be on the leading edge of understanding social media trends, platforms, technologies, and marketing techniques; with a track record of using metrics to adapt these strategies and improve results. The ideal candidate will have an understanding of climate and environmental issues, tracking movement in narratives and cultural trends that can help the movement do the vital work of protecting people and planet while advancing solutions. Job activities include but are not limited to: Social Media Identity Development: Leads on the creative development and delivery of Sierra Club’s social media identity – including voice, visual style, creative content, and innovative platform strategies – in close partnerships with key cross-departmental stakeholders. They will also coach and advise regarding social strategy for key organizational leaders and stakeholders. Creative and Reflexive Content Strategy: Stays nimble and on top of latest industry trends, breakthrough creative campaigns, pop culture, and current events – taking advantage of moments and trends in real-time. Balances multiple issues and shifting priorities to unify and strategically use our organizational voice(s) to respond to the world in real time. Diversifies content and leverages different social media platforms to develop visual and story-based content and market the organization, including its campaigns. Drives content strategies that foster meaningful engagement and a sense of community for both existing and expansion audiences. Developing and Advancing the Team: Develops a team of strategists, creatives, and content developers, managing individuals to contribute at their highest level. Fosters a team culture of innovation, collaboration and accountability alongside concrete near-term and long-term strategic planning. Works to create professional development and project management opportunities for staff. Programming: Sets and achieves programmatic goals through the integration of marketing functions, fundraising, storytelling, list growth, crisis response, influencer engagement and organizing tactics. Supports the development of data-informed strategies, tracking and reporting insights from audience segments, content and platform engagement, with monthly and quarterly social media reporting. Process and Governance: Develops, adapts, and supports a governance structure for our social program; including social media processes for internal and external Sierra Club audiences and key stakeholders. Establishes and enforces content intake, scheduling and review processes. Trains internal staff, chapters, and volunteers on social media best practices and brand standards. Manages contracts and projects with external vendors. This position directly relates to the 24-hour news cycle which will sometimes require weeknight and weekend hours. A successful candidate must have the following skills and experiences: A Do-er and a Director. You have experience doing top-to-bottom of what is required of a Social Media team; and have a demonstrated track record of both directing a team to successful outcomes, and rolling up your sleeves to do the work alongside of your team as needed. Creative. Your social media and change-making strategies have been driven through innovative and story-based content. You’ve worked with organizations to develop their tone and identity to successfully carve out their niche in the world. And you have the technical skill and creative tool proficiencies to bring these stories to life. Building a Program. You have the ability to build a social media program from top-to-bottom: A proven history of developing the processes and infrastructure needed to establish and grow a program; experience with developing and executing qualitative and quantitative data-informed strategies; success navigating competing priorities with internal and external stakeholders; and managing a team through the creation and execution of effective story-based content. Leadership. You’ve had significant management experience with a demonstrated ability to effectively communicate, coach, and support teams in working effectively together. You’ve navigated complex organizational structures to facilitate collaborative partnerships between stakeholders to keep workflow consistent and shared goals attainable. You are familiar with creating governance structures for social programming and strategies for training and educating content creators on best practices and brand standards. Social Technology. You have deep expertise with social media platforms e.g., Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, and Substack; with a history of adapting technology, tactics, metrics, and innovation in line with social trends. In addition, you have robust knowledge of social media scheduling, monitoring, analytics and reporting software. Equity. You model effective equity analysis and practice and demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of how group dynamics impact supervisory relationships, organizational culture, partnerships, campaigns and coalition work. Your decision-making is consistent, intentional, and committed to creating equitable outcomes at all levels. You have led high-performing and leaderful teams across group identities. You intervene when challenging group dynamics play out, in ways that build understanding, trust, and deeper self-awareness of team members. The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following experience, skills and competencies: Knows Our Work. You have experience in the environmental movement or social justice advocacy space: Campaigning, creating public demand for a policy, training volunteers, holding the decision makers accountable, and/or taking delivery on campaign goals. You are in tune with the communities we work with; able to leverage cultural trends to generate enthusiasm, growth, and real power; and be able to convey this information through various digital media platforms. Influencer Partnerships. Influencer cultivation and partnership have been a core part of your past social media strategy and programmatic development. You come to this work with existing influencer partnerships, are in tune with the communities we work with, and will be able to leverage these collaborations and cultural trends to generate enthusiasm, growth, and real power. Top-Notch Organization Skills. There’s a lot to keep track of in this role, and things cannot fall through the cracks. Managing multiple priorities, timeliness, and attention to detail is key, as is knowing when to ask for support. $140,000 – $150,000 a year Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this position is $140,000 – $150,000 annually. The Sierra Club offers a competitive salary package commensurate with skills and experience plus excellent benefits that include medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a retirement savings 401(k) plan. This is a category 3, exempt, non-represented, supervisory position. Sierra Club values the expertise and talents of foreign nationals. Sierra Club sponsors both nonimmigrant and immigrant visas when certain criteria are met, based on immigration laws and organizational needs. Such sponsorship is at the discretion of the Department Head and Sierra Club People Department in consultation with the employee’s manager. The Sierra Club cannot guarantee the approval of a visa petition. The Sierra Club is an equal opportunity employer committed to workforce belonging. To Apply, click here The Sierra Club provides

Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees. The Associate Press Secretary coordinates and executes communications strategies on key priorities determined in collaboration between themselves, their manager, and the Regional Field Director relating to the Sierra Club’s Energy and Conservation work in a set portfolio of states as designated on the Regional Turf Map. Any changes to the Regional Turf Map will be discussed and agreed upon in writing. Working with local staff, volunteers, and intersectional partners, the Associate Press Secretary is responsible for developing and disseminating strategic narratives that advance Sierra Club’s goals while remaining rooted in our organizational values: balance, collaboration, justice, transformation, and anti-racism To support that work, the Associate Press Secretary coordinates the development of creative assets to inform and influence decision makers; project manages the creation and distribution of advertising, videos, and other produced media; drafts and edits written content; and ensures messaging resonates effectively with various audiences. This position is responsible for an array of media communications, ensuring timely and accurate materials with a consistent tone and message. A key component of the Associate Press Secretary’s role is leading media outreach by organizing press conferences and other media events; coordinating the submissions of op-eds and letters to the editor; pitching stories; tracking and reporting coverage; compiling data; and nurturing relationships to grow a diverse bench of spokespeople. The ideal candidate should have a solid grasp of Sierra Club’s legacy conservation work, a conversational understanding of climate and environment issues, a personal commitment to and knowledge of social justice, and a passion for advancing progressive social change. They will also have the ability to articulate and reinforce the intersections of Sierra Club’s legacy work and communicate the challenges and opportunities we face, centered on justice and equity. Job activities include but are not limited to: Plan and implement communications strategy for the Sierra Club in a portfolio of states. Serve as liaison across internal teams and committees, as well as with external partners and stakeholders, to advise on communications strategies and tactics. Track media coverage of relevant issues. Develop and execute long-term and rapid-response media outreach plans to advance narratives and outcomes in a portfolio of states in adherence to the Jemez Principles for Democratic Organizing. Develop messaging, written, and produced assets to advance Sierra Club goals in collaboration with state teams. Develop media messages, op-eds, press releases, video/audio, talking points, and other materials, and coordinate media events as necessary. Work with federal press secretaries to localize federal agency media opportunities.Create strategic media responses to relevant reports, Environmental Law Program work underway, and other external developments. Contributes to staff strategy meetings, and stays current on substantive and political developments in major conservation campaigns by reading latest literature, attending meetings and maintaining contact with relevant sources. Build relationships with local, regional, and trade reporters and influencers. Serve as a point of contact for those reporters in order to advance media coverage. Pitch relevant stories and connect reporters with spokespeople Train and coach state-based staff and volunteers in strategic communications skills. Identify, train, and place compelling spokespeople. Support staff, volunteers, and partners with media training, messaging guidance, and interview preparation. The successful candidate must have the following skills and experience: Experience with media relations. You have professional experience as a journalist, media liaison, spokesperson, press secretary, or other position involving public relations. You have an understanding of best practices for using media to advance Sierra Club goals. Excellent writing and verbal communications skills. You are a strong writer and communicator who is comfortable interacting with reporters, developing compelling messages, and drafting written materials for various audiences. Ability to interact cooperatively and effectively with internal and external partners. You think collaboratively and can build strong relationships with staff, volunteers, and other stakeholders. You are capable of navigating challenging dynamics to achieve shared goals. Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate. Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go. The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following experience, skills, and competencies: Demonstrated knowledge of energy, lands, and/or climate issues and relevant media landscape Experience executing creative tactics including audio/video, podcasts, projections, murals, performance art, and advertising Ability to build alignment between stakeholders while project managing competing priorities Proficiency with Cision and/or other media outreach and tracking tools Spanish language proficiency preferred $71,000 – $79,000 a year Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this position is $71,000 – $79,000 annually, depending on location. This position is represented by a collective bargaining unit and is subject to the terms and conditions of the contract between Sierra Club and Progressive Workers Union or Sierra Employee Alliance, depending on location. The Sierra Club offers a competitive salary package commensurate with skills and experience plus excellent benefits that include medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a retirement savings 401(k) plan. This is a category 5, exempt, represented position. Sierra Club values the expertise and talents of foreign nationals. Sierra Club sponsors both nonimmigrant and immigrant visas when certain criteria are met, based on immigration laws and organizational needs. Such sponsorship is at the discretion of the Department Head and Sierra Club People Department in consultation with the employee’s manager. The Sierra Club cannot guarantee the approval of a visa petition. The Sierra Club is an equal opportunity employer committed to workforce belonging. To Apply, click here The Sierra Club provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, lived experience and skills. The Sierra Club does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law. The Sierra Club values applicants who are people that identify as Black, Indigenous, and other minoritized groups; women; queer, transgender, gender non-conforming, and gender fluid people. Explore, enjoy and protect the planet. Applications will be accepted through Monday, October 12. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. item.title: Director of Government Affairs
item.description: Director of Government Affairs Organization: Groundwork Collaborative Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Reports to: Vice President of Government Affairs Status: Full-time; Exempt Location: Washington D.C. This is a hybrid workplace, with Mondays and Wednesdays in the office and three days remote, as well as the occasional need to work in person for events and special projects. Overtime Status: Exempt Salary: $145K-$179K About Groundwork Collaborative Launched in 2018, Groundwork Collaborative is driven by the idea that We Are The Economy: when all of us are doing well, that is when our economy thrives. We fight for progressive economic policy and narrative change that builds accountable public power, breaks up concentrations of private power, and affirmatively centers people too long left out of prosperity. We understand that taken together, these actions will lead to a stronger and more resilient economy. Groundwork’s unique structure – part strategic communications, part think tank, and part issue advocacy organization – allows us to drive narrative and policy change with credibility, expertise, and impact. We work across four core audiences – the media, policymakers, economic experts, and grasstops leaders – and use targeted policy campaigns and timely research and messaging to advance a truly inclusive economic worldview. Position Summary This is a pivotal moment for economic policymaking. As Groundwork’s Director of Government Affairs, you will lead direct, substantive engagement with Congress and the executive branch, shape the strategy for how we engage with policymakers, and connect Groundwork’s experts, research, and messaging with the lawmakers and staff who need them. Reporting to the Vice President of Government Affairs, you will serve as a senior member of Groundwork’s Partnerships and Influence team. Groundwork’s impact has grown considerably in recent years, powered by a best-in-class government affairs program that makes our research, policy, and communications work accessible for elected officials and their staff. If you know how to shape a government engagement agenda, build durable relationships across Washington, and represent an organization with credibility and impact, the role was built for you. As Groundwork’s Director of Government Affairs, you will… Partner with the Vice President of Government Affairs and Associate Director of Congressional Affairs to design and drive an outreach strategy that advances both immediate and long-term economic policy priorities. Broaden and deepen relationships with congressional committees and offices to amplify Groundwork’s core messages. Serve as Groundwork’s liaison to the federal government, spotting and seizing opportunities for strategic engagement. Craft sharp, persuasive materials for policymakers and their staff including but not limited to talking points, fact sheets, letters, testimony, and more. Lead meetings, briefings, hearing prep, and other high-stakes engagement with government officials and staff. Keep colleagues informed on legislative and executive branch activity. Proactively communicate across internal and external stakeholders. Support and mentor staff members, especially those on the Partnerships and Influence team. Serve as a trusted thought partner and technical resource to the team and organizational leadership on all things government. Move fast when news breaks, analyzing and responding to Congressional and executive developments in real time. Qualifications You bring relevant experience in government relations, legislative work on the Hill, congressional affairs work in the executive branch, and/or government affairs work at a nonprofit organization. You are experienced in preparing witnesses for congressional committee hearings. You have a commitment to creating a just, inclusive, and robust economy that delivers opportunity and dignity to all. You bring a strong familiarity with federal economic policymaking institutions (including Congress, executive branch agencies, and the White House). You bring existing government staff relationships and policy coalition networks. You write and speak with clarity and persuasion. You are highly organized and thrive driving work forward under tight deadlines in a fast paced environment. You think creatively and bring an entrepreneurial drive to developing new strategies that secure advocacy wins. You have experience interfacing directly and managing relationships with government officials and senior staff. Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. If this role excites you and you meet most — but not all — of these criteria, we encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is $145,000 – $179,000 annually. We offer a generous benefits package, including five weeks of vacation and personal leave, two week-long office closures, additional time off for floating and federal holidays, zero-premium health insurance, a generous HRA, a retirement contribution of up to 6%, up to 16 weeks parental leave, and health club and cell-phone reimbursements, among other benefits. We are a hybrid workplace, with two days a week in the office and three days remote, as well as the occasional need to work in person for events and special projects. Groundwork is a unionized workplace and is represented by the Nonprofit Professional Employees Union (NPEU). This position is not in the bargaining unit. How to apply To begin the application process, please submit an application on our career page , including a resume and cover letter. The cover letter should describe your specific experience related to this position and what excites you about this work Thank you for your interest! Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Issues-Based Digital Campaigns Advisor
item.description: Issues-Based Digital Campaigns Advisor Organization: ExxonMobil Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 About us At ExxonMobil, our vision is to lead in energy innovations that advance modern living while reducing emissions. As one of the world’s largest publicly traded energy and chemical companies, we are powered by a unique and diverse workforce fueled by the pride in what we do and what we stand for. The success of our Upstream, Product Solutions and Low Carbon Solutions businesses is the result of the talent, curiosity and drive of our people. They bring solutions every day to optimize our strategy in energy, chemicals, lubricants and lower-emissions technologies. We invite you to bring your ideas to ExxonMobil to help create sustainable solutions that improve quality of life and meet society’s evolving needs. Learn more about our What and our Why and how we can work together. About Houston ExxonMobil’s state-of-the-art campus north of Houston serves as home to its Upstream, Product Solutions, and Low Carbon Solutions businesses and their associated service groups. By bringing many global functional groups together, the campus provides employees with the tools and capabilities needed today, and in the future, to achieve business objectives and accelerate the discovery of new resources, technologies and products. It was designed to foster improved collaboration, creativity and innovation and enhance the company’s ability to attract, develop and retain the top talent in the industry. The campus is located in Spring, Texas, on 385 wooded acres immediately to the west of Interstate Highway 45 (I-45), at the intersection of I-45 and the Hardy Toll Road, approximately 25 miles from the cultural vibrancy of downtown Houston. The campus was constructed to the highest standards of energy efficiency and environmental stewardship. Its design incorporates extensive research into best practices in building and workplace design through extensive benchmarking of the world’s top academic, research, and corporate facilities. Core Competencies Strategic & Policy-Savvy: Connects policy dynamics to brand outcomes; can scenario-plan and manage risk Operator’s Mindset: Moves from strategy to execution swiftly; sets clear workflows and SLAs Data-Driven: Obsessed with hypotheses, testing, and measurable outcomes Creative Storyteller: Simplifies the complex; advocates for high-quality content and design Stakeholder Leadership: Influences without authority; aligns senior leaders and cross-functional teams Bias for Compliance: Balances speed with governance and platform policy adherence Brand & Reputation Lift: Awareness, favorability, trust, thought leadership perception among target segments Audience Quality & Engagement: Target reach, qualified traffic, time on page, content completion, return visits Advocacy Outcomes: Stakeholder actions (e.g., sign-ups, toolkit downloads, event attendance), legislator/stakeholder engagement proxies where appropriate Governance & Risk: Policy/claims compliance, approval cycle times, and platform policy adherence What you will do 8–10 years leading issues-based, advocacy, or policy-driven digital campaigns from strategy through execution and measurement—in B2B contexts Proven marketing and brand background with demonstrated ability to translate complex, technical, or policy-heavy topics into clear, compelling brand narratives DC political campaign experience or experience within public affairs, issue advocacy, or policy communications Expertise across modern digital platforms (paid social, programmatic/display, search, video, email/marketing automation, web/SEO) and advocacy tools (e.g., grassroots mobilization, petitioning/patch-through calling platforms, legislator lookup) Strong command of audience strategy and segmentation: ABM, stakeholder mapping, and intent-based targeting Advanced analytical skills: campaign attribution, brand lift, audience reach/quality, sentiment, and funnel performance; comfort building dashboards and narratives from data Experience working in regulated or complex sectors (energy, industrials, infrastructure, or similar), collaborating closely with Policy, Legal, and Corporate Affairs Exceptional storytelling and writing skills; can craft concise, on-brand messages under time pressure Demonstrated agency/vendor leadership, budget management, and cross-functional influence B.S. degree is required Preferred Qualifications Energy sector familiarity (upstream/midstream/downstream, power, renewables, low carbon solutions, carbon markets, LNG, hydrogen, etc.). Experience with ABM platforms (e.g., Demandbase/6sense), automation/CRM (e.g., Marketo, Pardot, Eloqua; Salesforce), social listening/monitoring (e.g.,Talkwalker/Kohros, Sprinklr), analytics/BI (e.g., GA4, Looker/Power BI/Tableau), and A/B testing tools Background in crisis/rapid response digital, brand reputation management, or high-scrutiny communications Your benefits An ExxonMobil career is one designed to last. Our commitment to you runs deep: our employees grow personally and professionally, with benefits built on our core categories of health, security, finance, and life. We offer you: Pension Plan: Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. The basic benefit is a monthly annuity to be paid to you in retirement for the rest of your life Savings Plan: You can contribute between 6% and 20% of your pay and are encouraged to enroll right away. If you contribute at least 6% to your savings plan, the Company will contribute a 7% match Workplace Flexibility: We have several programs such as “Flex your Day”, providing ad-hoc flexibility around when and where you work, as well as longer-term programs such as leaves of absence and part-time work Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans Culture of Health: Programs and resources to support your wellbeing Employee Health Advisory Program: Provides confidential professional counseling for you and your family, including tools and resources promoting mental health and resiliency at no additional cost to you Disability Plan: Income replacement for when you cannot work due to illness or injury occurring on or off the job. Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you More information on our Company’s benefits can be found at www.exxonmobilfamily.com. Please note benefits may be changed from time to time without notice, subject to applicable law. Nothing herein is intended to override the corporate separateness of local entities. item.title: Senior Writer, Brief Writer
item.description: Senior Writer, Brief Writer Organization: ExxonMobil Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 About us For well over a century, ExxonMobil has been at the heart of creating and growing a modern world. We embrace the power and promise of technology, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. For billions around the world, lives are better and last longer because of the innovative problem solving and reliable energy we provide. And when it comes to developing industrial solutions to reduce carbon emissions, ExxonMobil is truly the leader. We don’t stop at “good enough.” We are committed to doing what’s right, even if it’s difficult or unpopular. We hold ourselves to high standards, challenge what’s possible and invest in innovation to meet society’s critical needs. Real change begins with bold questions, drive, and ambition. Here, your talent, determination and contributions shape how far you’ll go and the impact you’ll make along the way. Our future success depends on exceptional people. We invest in developing talent through meaningful work, challenging assignments, mentorship, and experiences that help build the next generation of leaders. Our Culture We are uniquely ExxonMobil. Integrity, care, excellence, resilience and courage, these core values determine how we work every day. At ExxonMobil, our values aren’t just words— they’re how we show up, focused on delivering the right answer, the right way, every day. What role you will play on our team We are seeking a highly skilled and politically astute Executive Brief Writer to support the Office of the Chairman and CEO. This role is critical in preparing high-impact, insight-driven briefing materials for the Chairman’s engagements with global leaders, policymakers, regulators, media, and internal stakeholders. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in political communications, public affairs, or government relations, and excels at distilling complex global issues into clear, concise, and actionable briefs. This is a high-visibility role requiring discretion, strategic thinking, and exceptional writing skills. What you will do Research, draft, and edit comprehensive briefing documents for the Chairman’s meetings, speeches, panels, and strategic engagements Collaborate with internal teams (e.g., Government Affairs, Legal, Strategy Planning, Communications) to gather intelligence and ensure accuracy and alignment. Monitor geopolitical, regulatory, and industry developments to inform briefings with timely and relevant context. Tailor content to diverse audiences, including heads of state, Fortune 500 executives, international media, and internal leadership. Maintain a consistent tone and voice aligned with the Chairman’s communication style and the company’s global brand. Manage tight deadlines and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment. About you Qualifications: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Political Science, International Relations, Communications, Journalism, or a related field. 7+ years of experience in executive communications, political writing, government affairs, or public policy. Proven ability to write for C-suite executives or senior government officials. Deep understanding of global political and economic landscapes. Exceptional research, synthesis, and writing skills. High level of discretion and professionalism. Preferred Qualifications: Experience working in or with multinational corporations, international institutions, or government agencies. Familiarity with global regulatory environments and public policy trends. Your benefits An ExxonMobil career is one designed to last. Our commitment to you runs deep: our employees grow personally and professionally, with benefits built on our core categories of health, security, finance and life. We offer you: The expected annual salary range for this position is $130,000 – $255,000. Individual pay will be determined based on various factors, which may include skills, abilities, qualifications, work experience, and education. Pension Plan: Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. The basic benefit is a monthly annuity to be paid to you in retirement for the rest of your life Savings Plan: You can contribute between 6% and 20% of your pay and are encouraged to enroll right away. If you contribute at least 6% to your savings plan, the Company will contribute a 7% match Workplace Flexibility: We have several programs such as “Flex your Day”, providing ad-hoc flexibility around when and where you work, as well as longer term programs such as leaves of absence and part-time work Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans Culture of Health: Programs and resources to support your wellbeing Employee Health Advisory Program: Provides confidential professional counseling for you and your family, including tools and resources promoting mental health and resiliency at no additional cost to you Disability Plan: Income replacement for when you cannot work due to illness or injury occurring on or off the job. Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. More information on our Company’s benefits can be found at www.exxonmobilfamily.com. Please note benefits are subject exclusively to the terms of each plan’s governing documents and may be changed from time to time without notice, subject to applicable law. item.title: Government Affairs Advisor
item.description: Government Affairs Advisor Organization: ExxonMobil Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 About us For well over a century, ExxonMobil has been at the heart of creating and growing a modern world. We embrace the power and promise of technology, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. For billions around the world, lives are better and last longer because of the innovative problem solving and reliable energy we provide. And when it comes to developing industrial solutions to reduce carbon emissions, ExxonMobil is truly the leader. We don’t stop at “good enough.” We are committed to doing what’s right, even if it’s difficult or unpopular. We hold ourselves to high standards, challenge what’s possible and invest in innovation to meet society’s critical needs. Real change begins with bold questions, drive, and ambition. Here, your talent, determination and contributions shape how far you’ll go and the impact you’ll make along the way. Our future success depends on exceptional people. We invest in developing talent through meaningful work, challenging assignments, mentorship, and experiences that help build the next generation of leaders. Our Culture We are uniquely ExxonMobil. Integrity, care, excellence, resilience and courage, these core values determine how we work every day. At ExxonMobil, our values aren’t just words— they’re how we show up, focused on delivering the right answer, the right way, every day. What Role You Will Play on Our Team You will serve as a strategic intelligence and emerging risk advisor, helping the organization anticipate, understand, and respond to global developments that could create risks or opportunities for the business. In this role, you will be responsible for identifying early indicators of change, assessing their potential impact, and ensuring that leadership has timely, actionable insights to support decision-making. You will work across functions to strengthen the company’s strategic risk capabilities, drive continuous improvement in risk identification and assessment processes, and help integrate forward-looking intelligence into enterprise risk management activities. You will also serve as a key liaison with external experts, consultants, and thought leaders to bring fresh perspectives and innovative approaches to emerging risk analysis. What You Will Do Analyze global trends and identify early signals of potential disruptions, strategic risks, and emerging opportunities. Monitor and maintain a portfolio of risk and opportunity signposts to support proactive decision-making. Develop and deliver emerging risk reports, trend analyses, and executive-ready intelligence products. Support the design and enhancement of risk dashboards, signpost tracking tools, and monitoring frameworks. Coordinate special projects focused on strategic and emerging risk initiatives. Lead or facilitate workshops, scenario discussions, and cross-functional engagements on emerging risk topics. Partner with third-party consultants, think tanks, and external experts to gather insights and coordinate risk-focused engagements. Ensure signpost monitoring and emerging risk intelligence are effectively integrated into enterprise risk management processes. Recommend and implement improvements to risk identification, intelligence gathering, and assessment methodologies. Contribute to the ongoing evolution of risk governance practices and enterprise resilience capabilities. Promote innovative intelligence, foresight, and analytical techniques to improve risk monitoring and strategic planning About you Skills and Qualifications Master’s degree preferred (MBA, MPP, MA in International Affairs, Security Studies, Economics, or related discipline). Strong analytical, research, and critical-thinking skills with the ability to convert complex information into actionable business insights. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare executive-level briefings and reports. Preferred Qualifications/ Experience 5+ years of experience in strategic risk, enterprise risk management, intelligence analysis, geopolitical risk, strategy, consulting, public policy, government affairs, or a related field. Experience monitoring global political, economic, technological, regulatory, and societal trends and assessing their business implications. Proven track record of identifying emerging risks and opportunities and communicating findings to senior leaders. Experience developing risk indicators, signposts, early-warning systems, or horizon-scanning programs. Experience producing strategic intelligence products, trend reports, scenario analyses, or risk assessments. Demonstrated success facilitating workshops, tabletop exercises, scenario planning sessions, or cross-functional risk discussions. Experience working with external experts, think tanks, research organizations, consultancies, or industry associations. Familiarity with quantitative and qualitative risk assessment methodologies. Experience managing complex projects involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities. Your benefits The expected annual salary range for this position is $185,000 – $230,000. Individual pay will be determined based on various factors, which may include skills, abilities, qualifications, work experience, and education. Pension Plan: Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. The basic benefit is a monthly annuity to be paid to you in retirement for the rest of your life. Savings Plan: You can contribute between 6% and 20% of your pay and are encouraged to enroll right away. If you contribute at least 6% to your savings plan, the Company will contribute a 7% match. Workplace Flexibility: We have several programs such as “Flex your Day,” providing ad-hoc flexibility around when and where you work, as well as longer-term programs such as leaves of absence and part-time work. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans. Culture of Health: Programs and resources to support your wellbeing. Employee Health Advisory Program: Provides confidential professional counseling for you and your family, including tools and resources promoting mental health and resiliency at no additional cost to you. Disability Plan: Income replacement for when you cannot work due to illness or injury occurring on or off the job. Enrollment is automatic and at no cost to you. More information on our Company’s benefits can be found at www.exxonmobilfamily.com. Please note benefits may be changed from time to time without notice, subject to applicable law. item.title: Manager of Housing Policy
item.description: Manager of Housing Policy Organization: Economic Innovation Group (EIG) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Manager of Housing Policy The Economic Innovation Group (EIG) is a bipartisan public policy organization dedicated to forging a more dynamic American economy. Headquartered in Washington, DC, EIG produces nationally recognized research and partners with policymakers to develop ideas that empower workers, entrepreneurs, and communities. About the Role EIG is seeking a Manager of Housing Policy to lead and expand our work at the intersection of housing, economic dynamism, and place-based policy. Building on EIG’s growing body of research and policy work on housing affordability, supply, and the barriers to building, this role will shape a high-impact federal policy agenda focused on expanding housing supply, reimagining incentives, and supporting local vitality. Reporting directly to the President and CEO and working closely with the Senior Director of Policy and Coalitions, the Manager will drive legislative engagement, develop and design policy ideas, translate EIG’s housing research into actionable insights, and serve as a key resource to Congress, the Administration, and stakeholders at all levels of government. The ideal candidate brings strong policy fluency, political judgment, and a commitment to cross-partisan impact. Key Responsibilities Lead EIG’s housing policy work, with a focus on supply-side incentives and regulatory barriers. Key issue areas include Right to Build Zones, model zoning codes, LIHTC, and more. Shape and advance legislative proposals to expand housing supply, reduce barriers to development, and strengthen incentives for state and local reform. Cultivate strong relationships with congressional staff, agency officials, state and local leaders, and national stakeholders. Organize and lead convenings with policy experts to gather feedback on legislative ideas and develop and shape EIG’s thinking in a new policy area. Produce high-quality policy materials, including legislative text, memos, testimony, comment letters, and regulatory analysis. Lead EIG’s Housing Advisory Council, including shaping its agenda, cultivating and engaging members, and translating insights from the Council into EIG’s broader research and policy work. Monitor and analyze housing-related developments across the legislative and executive branches to inform strategy. Work closely with EIG’s research team to translate new findings into policy recommendations and identify opportunities for further analysis. Identify new opportunities for EIG to add value to the national housing policy conversation. Qualifications At least 5 years of experience in housing policy, with direct exposure to Congress, federal agencies, or national advocacy. Exceptional verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex policies clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences. Strong writing skills and a proven ability to produce polished, publication-ready content with minimal oversight. A track record of building bipartisan coalitions and navigating politically diverse environments. Highly organized and self-directed, with excellent project management instincts. Comfort working in a dynamic, entrepreneurial team environment. Apply Please send a cover letter, resume, and writing sample to [email protected] with the subject line “Manager of Housing Policy.” The salary range for the role is $100,000 to $130,000, commensurate with experience. EIG is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We consider applications for employment without regards to race, color, ancestry, religion, gender, gender identity, parental or pregnancy status, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or Veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law. item.title: Director of Special Initiatives
item.description: Director of Special Initiatives Organization: Cato Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Description The Cato Institute is seeking a Director of Special Initiatives to join its Public Affairs team. Reporting to the Vice President for Public Affairs, the Director will lead the development and execution of high-priority engagement initiatives that advance Cato’s institutional and policy objectives. The Director will oversee several of Cato’s signature policymaker engagement programs, including but not limited to the Congressional Fellowship Program and Congressional Policy Summit, while developing new approaches to connect Cato scholars and research with policymakers, journalists, and other influential audiences. This Director will also assist in translating organizational priorities into coordinated campaigns, events, and outreach initiatives. This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC, reporting to the Vice President for Public Affairs. The projected salary range for this role is $115,000 to $150,000 per year. Compensation is based on the successful candidate’s educational background, experience, and skills. About Cato The Cato Institute is a public policy research organization — a think tank — dedicated to the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace. Its scholars and analysts conduct independent, nonpartisan research on a wide range of policy issues. Founded in 1977, Cato owes its name to Cato’s Letters, a series of essays published in 18th-century England that presented a vision of a society free from excessive government power. Those essays inspired the architects of the American Revolution. And the simple, timeless principles of that revolution — individual liberty, limited government, and free markets — turn out to be even more powerful in today’s world of global markets and unprecedented access to information than Jefferson or Madison could have imagined. Social and economic freedom is not just the best policy for a free people, it is the indispensable framework for the future. The Cato Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Key Duties & Responsibilities Lead the execution and expansion of signature Public Affairs engagement programs, including Cato’s Congressional Fellowship Program, Congressional Policy Summit, and other initiatives aligned with institutional priorities. Develop new engagement concepts, events, and programs that bring policymakers, congressional and state legislative staff, journalists, and other influential audiences into meaningful interaction with Cato scholars and research. Work closely with Government Affairs and Communication staff to ensure Cato-wide coordination of the Institute’s efforts. Lead cross-functional working groups to ensure the promotion of Cato publications and coordination of enterprise-wide campaigns. Develop goals, performance measures, and evaluation frameworks to assess the reach, effectiveness, and impact of major programs and initiatives. Manage the Special Initiatives team, providing strategic direction, oversight, and professional development to ensure effective execution of team priorities. Requirements Experience and Skill Sets 7 to 10 years’ experience working in an external outreach position, such as: public affairs, government affairs, or communications. item.title: Social Media Manager
item.description: Social Media Manager Organization: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Description The Social Media Manager, who sits in the AAAS Office of Communications, oversees the enterprise strategy and content for organizational-level social media accounts with support from the Communications Associate. The Manager collaborates with the communications team on public affairs and digital storytelling campaigns, multimedia development, issues management, and digital analytics. The Manager also coordinates closely with social media managers across the organization, including amplifying content, sharing best practices, managing social media scheduling and listening tools, and providing strategic guidance. Help us ignite the next era of science. What You’ll Do Oversee strategy, content development and community management for organizational-level social media accounts with support from the Communications Associate and public relations agency of record. Partner with the communications team on integrated digital storytelling and public affairs campaigns, organizational and program announcements, executive visibility, and editorial calendar. Coordinate with the external affairs track of the communications team and Science social media team on issues management. Provide strategic guidance on development of multimedia assets and create assets when appropriate. Manage the Marketing Communications (MarComms) Network Social Media Subgroup, including running monthly meetings, providing social media guidance, and coordinating organization-wide campaigns. Collaborate with the Digital Communications Manager on digital analytics to inform data-driven decisions and improve performance; participate in cross-department Digital Analytics Group and initiatives. Provide paid media expertise across the organization and manage team-led paid media campaigns. Manage social media management platforms, including social media scheduling and listening tools. Serve as lead strategist for the establishment of social media accounts and presence on any new platforms. Stay abreast of best practices in social media to evolve strategy and serve as subject matter expert. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism or another relevant field. 5-7 years’ experience with social media strategy, tactics, and analytics. Experience navigating social media crises. Experience managing earned and paid media campaigns. Familiarity with building audience profiles and identifying where those audiences engage online. Familiarity with AP style, content management systems, and video and social media platforms. Experience with project and social media management tools, such as Sprout Social and Meltwater. Application Process Submit a resume, portfolio, and cover letter outlining qualifications and interest in the position by October 29, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. A Recruiter will contact you with next steps if you are selected for an interview. The anticipated initial rate of compensation for this position is $90,000 – $95,000 per year. AAAS currently provides the following benefits for this position: paid vacation leave, paid sick leave, paid holidays, health insurance, flexible spending account, dental insurance, life insurance, vision insurance, retirement benefits, short- and long-term disability, each subject to the terms of the applicable program. Additional benefits may apply. Any actual offer of employment, reflecting the total compensation package and benefits, will be made in the sole discretion of AAAS and will be based on a variety of factors, including years of experience, depth of experience, and other relevant factors. AAAS reserves the right to amend or modify its employment benefits and compensation structure at any time. AAAS is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category. Verbal or written communications from any employee of AAAS shall not be considered binding obligations. item.title: Coalition Director
item.description: Coalition Director Organization: Secure Democracy Foundation Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Role Overview Secure Democracy Foundation is a national, nonpartisan 501(c)(3) organization building stronger elections, state by state. We combine deep election policy expertise with a cross-partisan approach, working with lawmakers, election officials, organizations, and communities across the political spectrum to identify common ground and advance practical solutions that strengthen free, fair, and secure elections. The Coalition Director serves as the primary relationship manager and strategic coordinator for the Advancing Liberty Coalition. This national, multi-organization coalition brings together organizations and leaders with different political perspectives and constituencies around shared goals for strengthening elections and democratic institutions. This role leads coalition operations, member engagement and recruitment, grassroots organizing initiatives, and program development. The Coalition Director will help members identify opportunities for collective action, develop and test organizing approaches, strengthen coalition infrastructure, and expand the coalition’s reach and impact. The ideal candidate is an experienced coalition builder and grassroots organizer who is skilled at finding common ground and building trusted relationships across political and ideological differences. They can work effectively with executives and senior leaders while remaining closely engaged in the hands-on work of organizing, facilitation, recruitment, program development, and follow-through. A Note on the Advancing Liberty Coalition The Advancing Liberty Coalition brings together organizations and communities that don’t typically share a table, including center-right democracy organizations, veterans and military families, Mormon and evangelical women’s organizations, disability advocates, and business leaders. The coalition is grounded in the belief that strong elections benefit all Americans and that durable solutions require participation from people with different political perspectives, experiences, and constituencies. Members do not need to agree on every issue. The work requires identifying areas of common ground, building trust across differences, and creating opportunities for organizations to act together around shared objectives. We welcome candidates whose professional backgrounds and networks come from across the political spectrum. Success in this role requires genuine curiosity about different perspectives and demonstrated experience building productive relationships with people and organizations that may not share the same political worldview. Cross-partisan coalition building is not peripheral to this position; it is a central responsibility of the Coalition Director. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Coalition Management, Member Engagement & Organizing Manage and coordinate a national coalition of partner organizations working together on cross-ideological democracy and election-policy initiatives. Develop organizing models and opportunities that advance coalition campaigns, strengthen member organizations, and increase their collective reach and impact. Serve as the primary point of contact for coalition members, building strong relationships and maintaining meaningful engagement. Plan and facilitate coalition meetings, including developing agendas, identifying decisions and action items, and ensuring follow-through. Identify member needs and translate them into coalition programs, resources, and initiatives. Build trusted relationships with member organizations, executives, and other senior stakeholders that enable organizations with different perspectives to pursue shared objectives. Strategy, Programs & Growth Develop coalition programming based on member needs, opportunities, and strategic priorities. Recruit and onboard new coalition members to broaden participation and strengthen the coalition’s reach and impact. Lead the collaborative development and implementation of coalition strategy with members, advocacy teams, and organizational leadership. Develop, test, evaluate, and refine coalition programs based on member feedback and evidence of effectiveness. Build and strengthen the processes, systems, and infrastructure necessary for the coalition’s long-term sustainability and growth. Understand and monitor coalition programs across VRL’s state portfolio and identify opportunities for members to contribute to state-level campaigns and initiatives. Help members identify opportunities to build organizational capacity, increase influence, and expand collective impact. Communications & External Representation Serve as a spokesperson for the coalition alongside members of the advocacy team. Develop materials and reports that communicate the coalition’s work and impact to external audiences. Collaborate with communications and development teams to align messaging, storytelling, and fundraising opportunities with coalition priorities. Represent the coalition in external meetings, conferences, convenings, and strategic partnerships. Help communicate coalition priorities in ways that resonate with audiences representing different political and ideological perspectives. Operations & Systems Management Manage coalition databases and CRM systems to ensure accurate tracking of members, relationships, engagement, and activities. Develop systems for tracking commitments, action items, participation, and program outcomes. Establish meaningful qualitative and quantitative measures that help determine whether coalition strategies and programs are working. Use member feedback, participation data, and program results to identify opportunities for improvement and inform strategy. Support reporting and evaluation efforts that demonstrate coalition impact and organizational learning. Required Experience 10+ years of professional experience with substantial responsibility for grassroots organizing and coalition building, including experience working with multi-organization initiatives. Demonstrated success building, growing, engaging, and mobilizing coalitions or networks of organizations. Experience designing, leading, and scaling grassroots organizing or advocacy initiatives. Experience working directly with executives, organizational leaders, and other senior stakeholders. Demonstrated experience building trusted professional relationships across political and ideological differences, including experience working with moderate, conservative, center, or center-right organizations and leaders. Ability to identify areas of common ground and move people with different perspectives toward shared goals and collective action. Genuine interest in working with colleagues, partners, and coalition members whose political perspectives, values, or approaches may differ meaningfully from your own. Strong facilitation skills, including experience helping groups navigate disagreement, competing priorities, or different approaches and move toward decisions and action. Proven ability to design, implement, evaluate, and adapt programs based on member needs and results. Experience representing an organization, network, or coalition externally. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with audiences representing different perspectives. Experience collaborating across communications, advocacy, development, policy, or related functions. Experience developing the systems and infrastructure needed to manage a coalition or network effectively, including CRM/database systems, engagement tracking, and accountability processes. Strong project-management, organization, and follow-through skills. Ability to balance strategic thinking, relationship management, organizing, and hands-on execution. We do not expect candidates to come from one particular political, ideological, or organizational background. We are interested in candidates who can demonstrate a sustained record of bringing people and organizations together, building trust across differences, and translating relationships into effective collective action. Salary & Benefits The Coalition Director is in the Director pay band, with a hiring range of $110,00 to $130,000. The base salary offered will take into account internal equity and may vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other relevant factors. Eligible employees currently receive: Medical, dental, and vision insurance that is majority employer-funded 401(k) retirement plan with up to a 6% employer match Unlimited flexible vacation leave, two weeks of sick leave, 13 paid holidays, winter holiday closure, parental leave, volunteer time, and other PTO opportunities Medical and dependent-care flexible spending accounts Short- and long-term disability insurance Basic-term life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance, with an employee buy-up option Work-from-home, cell phone, and fitness benefits Voting Rights Lab and Secure Democracy Foundation are initiatives of SD Foundation, a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. With that you may see branding or contact information associated with both Voting Rights Lab and Secure Democracy Foundation throughout the recruitment process. Equal Employment Opportunity Secure Democracy Foundation is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining exceptional people and creating a workplace where employees can contribute and thrive. Secure Democracy Foundation’s work environment is open to employees and partners across the full spectrum of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and other classifications protected by applicable law. item.title: Associate Director of Media Relations
item.description: Associate Director of Media Relations Organization: Voting Rights Lab Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/01/2026 Role Overview Voting Rights Lab, a national nonpartisan 501(c)(3), and its 501(c)(4) affiliate are fighting the state-level battles that will shape elections in 2026, 2028, and for decades to come. In 2025 alone, we stopped a wave of proof-of-citizenship mandates in red and purple states from Texas to Michigan, and produced the first-ever map of election law vulnerabilities — showing where losing candidates can exploit state laws to challenge legitimate results. Grounded in deep state-level relationships and cross-ideological credibility, we anticipate threats and deliver solutions where democracy is most at risk. As the Associate Director of Media Relations, you will manage our earned media work and other strategic communications efforts to secure, protect, and defend voting rights for all Americans. You will be responsible for directing earned media strategy for the organization’s brands as well as building the CEO’s profile with journalists and media influencers. You will be the go-to resource for national journalists seeking expertise on voting and election issues and translate complex policy details into compelling messages and pitches. Media relations for Voting Rights Lab just doesn’t mean writing and editing press releases – it’s about building long term relationships with key reporters, landing exclusive placements, and being a strategist for our executive, program team, and partners to better tell our story. Voting Rights Lab is a fully remote organization, and this position can be based anywhere in the United States. We offer a collaborative and innovative work environment, competitive compensation, and opportunities for professional advancement. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Earned Media & Communications Support Grow strategic earned media opportunities and strategy for the organization’s family of brands and its executive Identify opportunities and trends to engage reporters Pitch and maintain relationships with journalists Assist in product creation used for earned media purposes Direct interview preparation and spokesperson needs Engage strategic partners and outside spokespeople in earned media opportunities Independently execute and/or supervise the execution of media-facing events, including press briefings, meet-and-greets, and other public events/webinars Assist in the development of policy and advocacy-related communications products, including research memos, reports, and strategic pitches Develop a growth plan to engage with the newest media, including but not limited to online newsletters, blogs, and podcasts. Provide and/or oversee the delivery of excellent communications-related services to the organization, including managing subscriptions, media monitoring, talking point development, etc. CEO Profile Building Develop and execute a plan to build the profile of Voting Rights Lab’s CEO in the media and with democracy movement influencers Coordinate with Chief of Staff and prep CEO for media interviews, including creating interview guides, talking points, and holding practice interviews Identify potential opportunities for the CEO to provide thought leadership on current events or policy trends to the press, media influencers, and partners Management & Operations Manage consultants or projects as assigned Model and encourage communication, collaboration, and a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive Provide internal communications support as assigned Participate in organizational activities, events, and learning Support an environment of cross-team collaboration and communication Manage regular personal administration, including timely submission of receipts, reimbursement requests, travel planning, scheduling/calendaring, etc. Requirements Required Experience: A minimum of five years of relevant communications experience with a proven track record of: Directly owning a substantial portion of earned-media strategy/opportunities Regularly identifying new hooks, pitching reporters, securing coverage, preparing spokespeople, cultivating long-term reporter relationships Demonstrated experience in successfully pitching state and national print and online media, as well as radio, television media, and state/local political or policy reporters Proven communication skills, both verbal and written, including ability to translate complex ideas, particularly relating to policy, legislation, legal developments, research, and data, into understandable messages that inform, engage, and persuade targeted audiences Record of directly advising and strategically preparing senior executives or subject matter experts for high-stakes media engagement, building on our current media profile Skilled in rapid, strategic communications judgment, able to quickly recognize newsworthiness and how/when to engage Strong analytical and interpersonal skills Attention to detail Experience managing a multi-step, time-sensitive content production and review processes across diverse teams and departments Demonstrated ability to function effectively in a high-paced, fully remote, tech-forward work environment and manage competing priorities A learning orientation, with the ability to maintain momentum through uncertainty and to adapt within rapidly changing priorities Desired Experience: Experience working on communications campaigns at the state level for nonprofits, government agencies, or political campaigns Experience working with, pitching, and creating content for new media platforms, including podcasts, Substack, and content creators Experience working on or knowledge of democracy and/or voting/elections issues Experience working in or knowledge of state legislative processes Experience managing public relations or earned media contractors or firms Experience communicating on behalf of multiple brands, as well as communicating on behalf of 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations Note: We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation assistance Benefits Salary and benefits: We value our staff by offering competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package. The Associate Director of Media Relations is in the Director pay band, and the hiring range for this position is $90,000 to $110,000 annually. The base pay offered will take into account internal equity and may also vary depending on the candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, among other factors. The total compensation package may include the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, depending on the level and position offered. At this time, we provide the following benefits for eligible employees: Medical, dental, and vision insurance that is majority employer-funded 401(k) retirement plan, with up to 6% employer match Generous paid time off package, including unlimited flexible vacation leave, 2 weeks sick leave, in addition to 13 paid holidays, winter holiday closure, and other PTO opportunities such as parental leave, volunteer time, and more Flexible spending account for medical and dependent care Short-term and long-term disability insurance Basic-term life and accidental death and dismemberment (ADD) insurance, with an employee buy-up option Additional benefits include work-from-home benefits, cell phone benefits, and fitness benefits, and learning and development benefits. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement: Voting Rights Lab is a non-profit organization that is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining exceptional people, and to creating a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding, and enables each of us to realize our potential. Voting Rights Lab’s work environment is safe and open to all employees and partners, respecting the full spectrum of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and all other classifications protected by law in the locality and/or state in which you are working. Part of Voting Rights Lab’s mission is to ensure that people with records of arrest or conviction can vote. As such, we give full and fair consideration to all applicants, regardless of a past record of arrest or conviction. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. You will also play a core role in Voting Rights Lab’s work to build a firewall around our elections by translating deep audience research into innovative paid and organic content strategies. Finally, you will shape the organization’s social and online editorial strategy and help the organization build the next iteration of digital research products relied on by national and state media and the pro-democracy movement. This position is housed within the Communications Department. You will bring exceptional strategic thinking, writing, and editorial skills, a strong understanding of digital platforms and trends, and the ability to collaborate with various stakeholders to produce engaging digital content in a fast-paced environment. Voting Rights Lab is a fully remote organization, and this position can be based anywhere in the United States.
