item.title: Senior Regulatory Permitting Specialist
item.description: Senior Regulatory Permitting Specialist Organization: WRA, Inc. Location: Remote (CA) Date Posted: 10/03/2026 About the job We’re currently hiring a Senior Regulatory Permitting Specialist in the Sacramento/Central Valley region. On Team 12, you will work closely with WRA’s Principals, Directors, and executive leadership to develop, manage, and deliver multifaceted regulatory projects primarily throughout California’s Central Valley and Foothills. As WRA continues to expand our presence in this region, this is a unique opportunity to join WRA at a pivotal point in our growth, helping build out our presence and practice in the Central Valley and Foothills from the ground up. In this role you will collaborate with clients, regulatory agencies, and interdisciplinary WRA teams to develop innovative solutions, lead complex consultation processes, and support successful project implementation. This is a remote position within the state of California; however, candidates residing in or near the greater Sacramento/Central Valley region will be prioritized throughout the process. We will consider candidates within the state of California who have established relationships in the region and are willing to travel regularly to field sites, client and agency offices, and WRA office locations as needed to support project work. This position reports to Rob Schell, Wildlife and Fisheries Director. In this role, you will: Work with Principals as well as Director and Executive-level staff, including subject matter experts, engineers, attorneys, clients, prime or subconsultants to develop a project from idea, through planning and permit consultations in support of critical infrastructure and development in California’s Central Valley and Foothills Merge technical expertise with regulatory experience to guide and advise clients on project due diligence, design, opportunities and constraints to develop and deliver a permitting strategy, schedule, and budget that reflects client priorities Coordinate, delegate, and oversee multidisciplinary teams, stakeholders, staff, and subconsultants on the preparation of technical studies necessary to support the permitting process Oversee or directly prepare permit applications Proactively manage budgets, prepare scopes of work and change orders. Identify and communicate project risks to Principal-level staff Oversee and mentor early career professionals on regulatory processes, project management, and professional development Participate in internal and external thought leadership at conferences or professional technical groups through publications, presentations, white papers, panel discussions, or similar To be successful in this role, you will need: A bachelor’s degree in biological sciences, engineering, policy, or related field At least 10 years of professional experience working in the consulting field At least 6 years of expertise preparing and consulting on 401, 404, 1600 LSAA, USFWS/NMFS Section 7 or Section 10 consultations, CDFW 2081 ITPs Proven experience building and managing across multidisciplinary teams Proven track record in a supervisory or leadership role Demonstrated experience in Transportation, Water, or Mine/Quarry Markets At least 5 years of project management experience, including preparing scopes of work, budgets and change orders At least 5 years working in California’s Central Valley or Foothills regions A growth mindset Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical information to a lay audience A valid driver’s license, reliable transportation (while WRA has fleet vehicles that can be reserved for field use, during busy field seasons a truck may not always be available) and willingness to travel to field sites and meetings The ability to walk, hike, and work outside for long periods of time Desired but not required skills: Specialized expertise with Mitigation, SMARA, FERC Business Development experience Experience working on competitive proposals Strong leadership skills WRA has an established internal leveling system for our staff that maps to salary bands that have been informed by market data. Our leveling system is dependent on years of relevant industry experience, education, and the level of responsibility and autonomy at which you’re expected to operate. The salary range for this position is $108,000 – $146,000 which represents 2 job levels that WRA is open to considering for this role. In your first conversation with our recruiter, you may discuss leveling and compensation to make sure that expectations are aligned. Additionally, while the position is being advertised as a Senior Regulatory Permitting Specialist, based on leveling conversations, we may determine that Regulatory Permitting Specialist is the appropriate title for you. There will be opportunities to discuss this toward the end of the interview process; however, if you wish to discuss titles earlier in the interview process, please do so with your recruiter. Who are we? WRA’s an employee-owned environmental consultancy. We are a tenacious team of planners, engineers, and scientists, and we aim to leave the lands we love better than we found them. Our clients and partners hire us because we’re skilled at navigating through challenging projects involving wildlands, parks, community spaces, and infrastructure. We bring over four decades of expertise, long-standing relationships, and connections to our local communities to make sure that projects are pursued in responsible ways where both people and the environment thrive. As an organization, we believe that independence and interdependence are not mutually exclusive. We invest in systems, processes, and employee programs to support our staff’s collective engagement and success. At the same time, we encourage our employees to operate with an ownership mindset, taking responsibility for outcomes and being true to our commitments. WRA’s company vision is to cultivate a sustainable future where people and the environment thrive, and that effort starts first with our staff. We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment, and we have developed flexible policies, internal practices, and are investing in programs that prioritize learning and sustainability. We aim to create conditions that allow employees to prioritize their families, lead healthy and balanced lives, and to bring their authentic selves to work every day. We believe that by creating an exceptional workplace, our employees will be able to do their best work and be able to meaningfully contribute to the sustainability of the environment and the communities in which we live. WRA is an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to creating a diverse environment. We recruit, employ, train, compensate and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: International Regulatory & Policy Manager
item.description: International Regulatory & Policy Manager Organization: Yoti Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/03/2026 About the Job Who We Are Born in 2014, Yoti is a digital identity and biometric technology company that makes it safer for people to prove who they are. Our technology helps millions of people securely prove their identity, age and other trusted attributes while giving them greater privacy and control over their personal information. Today, more than twenty million people have downloaded the Yoti app. Our product portfolio has expanded to include digital identity, age assurance, identity verification, reusable digital credentials, eSignatures, AI-powered anti-spoofing technologies and authentication solutions that help organisations build trust online and in person. We work with governments, financial institutions, technology companies, regulators and businesses around the world to help shape trusted digital ecosystems. As digital identity becomes increasingly central to financial services, payments, online safety and AI, we continue to develop products and contribute to policy that enables innovation while protecting privacy and security. Purpose of the Role This role sits at the intersection of law, technology, professional/financial services and business strategy, supporting Yoti’s international growth by helping the business anticipate regulatory change, identify commercial opportunities and engage confidently with customers, policymakers and strategic partners. Working across international markets, with a particular focus on the United States, Europe and Latin America, the successful candidate will analyse legal, regulatory and market developments, contribute to policy engagement and consultation responses, and translate complex legal and technical issues into practical commercial insight. The role spans the rapidly evolving digital trust ecosystem, including digital identity, reusable digital credentials, digital wallets, authentication, trust frameworks, interoperability, trust and safety, payments, Open Finance, Smart Data, AI governance, biometrics and online safety. Working closely with Product, Commercial, Compliance and Marketing teams, the successful candidate will help ensure Yoti is well positioned to respond to market developments, support customers navigating regulatory change, influence policy discussions and strengthen Yoti’s position as a trusted leader in digital identity. Role Dimensions Reporting to the Chief Policy & Regulatory Officer, the International Regulatory & Policy Associate will work across Yoti’s international markets, represent Yoti externally in the US & Latam markets and support colleagues across Product, Commercial, Compliance, Marketing and Executive Leadership. The role combines stakeholder engagement and commercial support, working with colleagues and external partners across multiple jurisdictions, with legal and regulatory analysis, public policy. National and international travel will be required. Principal Responsibilities Support Yoti’s engagement with governments, regulators, elected representatives, trade associations, standards bodies, civil society and industry coalitions. Represent Yoti at conferences, industry events, customer meetings, working groups and policy forums, delivering presentations where appropriate. Support Yoti’s engagement with governments, regulators, elected representatives, trade associations, standards bodies, civil society and industry coalitions. Build and maintain relationships with external stakeholders, including law firms, professional services, financial services, technology trade bodies and digital identity ecosystems. Identify emerging regulatory trends, commercial opportunities and strategic risks affecting Yoti, its customers and partners. Contribute to Yoti’s external profile through articles, webinars, conference presentations and participation in industry discussions. Support customer and partner engagement through the preparation of market analysis, regulatory briefings, presentations and relevant materials. Assist in planning and delivering stakeholder roundtables, workshops, policy events and customer engagement activities. Research and draft consultation responses, policy papers, position statements, customer briefings and thought leadership across multiple jurisdictions. Collaborate with the Global Regulatory Intelligence Researcher to identify emerging policy trends and develop practical regulatory guidance to support client engagement, translate regulatory developments into practical guidance that supports product development, customer engagement and market expansion. Support awareness of domestic and international trust frameworks, certification schemes, accreditation programmes and emerging interoperability initiatives relevant to Yoti’s products and services. Develop an understanding of emerging digital trust ecosystems, including reusable digital credentials, digital wallets, payment ecosystems, Open Finance, Smart Data and orchestration services, assessing their implications for Yoti and its customers. Knowledge, Skills, Qualifications and Experience We’re looking for someone who is intellectually curious, commercially minded and excited by the intersection of law, technology and professional services. The successful candidate will enjoy understanding new technologies, analysing legal and regulatory developments, and translating complex issues into practical advice that supports business growth and customer success. Essential Law degree 5-8 years’ post-graduation experience in legal, regulatory, public policy, strategic advisory or government affairs roles within an international law firm, professional services, financial institution, technology company, consultancy, regulator or trade association. Strong understanding of legal analysis and the ability to interpret legislation, regulatory guidance, consultation documents and technical standards. Excellent written and confident verbal and public speaking skills, with the ability to explain complex legal, technical and commercial issues clearly to different audiences. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with excellent judgement and attention to detail. Commercial awareness and an interest in how regulation enables innovation, customer adoption and international market growth. Experience working with senior stakeholders across legal & data protection, commercial, technical and policy functions. Ability to manage multiple priorities across different jurisdictions and time zones. Excellent spoken and written English. Willingness to travel and attend out of hours events Desirable Master’s degree in Technology Policy, Public Policy, International Relations, Digital Regulation or a related discipline. Understanding of digital identity, identity verification, reusable digital credentials, authentication, trust services or digital wallets. Spanish language proficiency. Familiarity with regulations for online platforms, financial services, payments. Awareness of international digital identity trust frameworks, certification schemes, interoperability standards and digital identity ecosystems. Experience working with government consultations, industry associations, standards organisations or policy forums. Understanding of or strong interest in AI governance, biometrics, cybersecurity, privacy and online safety regulation. Experience using AI-enabled research, knowledge management or workflow tools What You’ll Bring Intellectual curiosity and a desire to understand how technology, regulation and markets evolve together. A collaborative approach and the confidence to work across legal, commercial and technical disciplines. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with customers, policymakers, regulators and industry partners. A practical, solutions-oriented mindset and the ability to balance legal, commercial and operational considerations. An interest in helping shape the future of trusted digital identity and digital trust and safety internationally. What’s in it for you? Benefits will vary depending on where you are based. Flexible working with hybrid arrangements and core working hours. Performance-based discretionary annual bonus. Medical insurance. Life and accident insurance. Gratuity in accordance with local legislation. 10 days’ annual leave plus 6 days’ sick leave. (medical + via Oyster) 10 public holidays. Fully paid Selfie Time (equivalent to 5 days) each year for personal development, volunteering or community activities. Team and company events Annual learning and development budget, including conferences and professional development opportunities. This is an opportunity to join a company at the forefront of trusted digital identity. You’ll work on significant policy, regulatory and commercial developments shaping digital identity, financial services and digital trust, collaborating with governments, regulators, banks, technology companies acting as an Ambassador for Yoti to help build safer, more trusted digital ecosystems. AI Usage During the Recruitment Process Please read our AI Usage in Recruitment policy to know more about how Yoti uses AI in the recruitment process and our stance on how candidates can use AI during the interview process. We Believe in Equal Opportunities It takes a diverse community of passionate, talented and committed people to build a simpler, more secure way of proving identity. We’re an equal opportunity employer, so we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, with different outlooks and experiences. We are proud to be a Disability Confident employer and we’re committed to making our recruitment process as inclusive and accessible as possible. If you have a disability or long-term condition and need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us

item.title: Director of Federal Affairs
item.description: Director of Federal Affairs Organization: Energy Transition Capital (ETC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/03/2026 About the job Title: Director of Federal Affairs Location: Washington, D.C. metropolitan area (including adjacent locations); hybrid flexibility ETC Overview Energy Transition Capital Management (“ETC”) is a U.S.-based private equity firm investing in and developing critical American energy infrastructure. Our mission is to deliver market-leading, net, after-tax returns to investors through investment in highest-value U.S. energy infrastructure assets. With deep expertise across the U.S. power sector, ETC is positioned to deliver innovative energy solutions that create lasting economic, societal, and environmental impact, supporting the next century of America’s energy and economic leadership. Position Overview Energy Transition Capital Management (ETC) is seeking a Director of Federal Affairs to lead its Washington, D.C.–focused government relations and public affairs activities. The Director will develop and maintain relationships with policymakers, congressional offices, federal agencies, and relevant industry stakeholders, with particular attention to federal energy and infrastructure matters affecting ETC and its affiliated development activities in Puerto Rico.Working closely with executive leadership and the Puerto Rico-based team, this individual will translate complex energy, infrastructure, and investment priorities into clear, credible communications; monitor federal policy and funding developments; and coordinate engagement across stakeholders with diverse political perspectives. The position calls for a relationship-oriented professional with demonstrated experience working effectively with both Democratic and Republican offices or administrations. The preferred location is Washington, D.C. or the surrounding metropolitan area, with periodic travel, including to Puerto Rico, as needed. Key Responsibilities· Develop and execute a federal affairs strategy aligned with ETC’s energy infrastructure investment and development priorities, including its affiliated activities in Puerto Rico.· Build and maintain substantive, professional relationships with members of Congress, bipartisan congressional staff, relevant federal agencies, industry associations, and other Washington stakeholders.· Serve as a primary Washington-facing representative for ETC, coordinating meetings, briefings, coalition engagement, and other federal stakeholder outreach.· Monitor and analyze federal legislative, regulatory, appropriations, and administrative developments affecting energy infrastructure, grid reliability, project financing, permitting, and Puerto Rico.· Provide timely, practical briefings and recommendations to executive leadership on federal developments, engagement opportunities, and potential implications for the company’s projects.· Coordinate closely with ETC leadership, external advisers, and Coquí Power’s Puerto Rico-based government and community affairs counterparts to ensure consistent messaging and complementary federal and local engagement.· Prepare executive briefing materials, policy summaries, talking points, correspondence, presentations, and materials for meetings with federal officials and other stakeholders.· Communicate technical, financial, and policy matters accurately and accessibly to audiences with varied backgrounds and perspectives.· Identify and develop constructive relationships with industry organizations and potential partners on shared federal energy and infrastructure priorities.· Oversee and coordinate external federal government relations advisers as applicable, maintaining clear objectives, reporting, and accountability.· Conduct all government relations activities in accordance with applicable laws, disclosure requirements, and company policies. Qualifications & Experience Required· Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Public Administration, Government, International Relations, Law, Communications, or a related field. An advanced degree, such as a Juris Doctor (J.D.), Master of Public Policy (MPP), or Master of Public Administration (MPA), is preferred.· Substantial experience in federal government relations, public affairs, congressional affairs, federal policy, or related Washington-based roles, with a record of independently managing senior stakeholder relationships.· Demonstrated professional experience engaging effectively with both Democratic and Republican policymakers, offices, or administrations, and an ability to work constructively across the political spectrum.· Established understanding of the federal legislative and administrative process and experience navigating Congress, federal agencies, and Washington stakeholder networks.· Strong strategic judgment, discretion, executive presence, and exceptional written and verbal communication skills.· Ability to understand and communicate complex policy, technical, and commercial issues, coordinate multiple workstreams, and operate effectively with senior leadership.· Ability to work from the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area and travel as business needs require. Preferred· Knowledge of Puerto Rico’s federal policy landscape, energy sector, public institutions, or related infrastructure priorities, with relevant stakeholder relationships.· Professional experience with energy, electric utilities, infrastructure development, permitting, federal funding, or project finance.· Professional proficiency in both English and Spanish.· Experience coordinating federal and local government affairs strategies and managing external advisers. Compensation· Compensation is competitive and based on experience.· Salary plus performance-based bonus.· Competitive healthcare, dental, and 401(k) matching package. Contact· Please send cover letter and resume to [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Policy and Compliance, Certification
item.description: Manager, Policy and Compliance, Certification Organization: LegitScript Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/03/2026 Manager, Policy and Compliance, Certification At LegitScript, we are passionate about making the internet and payment ecosystems safer and more transparent. We help companies of all sizes keep their services legal and safe for consumers. To do this, LegitScript combines big data with the world’s leading team of experts skilled in highly regulated and complex sectors, including transaction laundering detection, pharmaceuticals, online gambling, and more. The result? Unmatched accuracy and deep risk analysis that identifies which commercial entities play by the rules, and which do not. Our diverse industry partnerships provide unique insights that keep businesses and governments at the forefront of emerging trends. That’s why LegitScript is trusted by the world’s largest search engines, internet platforms, payment companies, and regulatory agencies. Overview: The Manager, Policy and Compliance – Certification is responsible for overseeing Certification’s compliance frameworks and proactively monitoring industry trends, laws, and regulations to keep the Certification business unit ahead of regulatory change. At its core, this role ensures the certification team stays current on regulatory developments and partners with cross-functional teams to effectively integrate policy expertise into Certification Operations. A core part of this work involves translating complex policy and technical regulatory requirements into clear, plain language that clients and internal stakeholders can easily understand and act on. This role also oversees the Policy and Compliance team’s escalation-based support for analysts’ review work, providing guidance and hands-on support when compliance-related escalations arise during application and monitoring reviews. A key part of this role involves partnering closely with the legal and research team to ensure internal compliance frameworks remain current, certification standards and terms and conditions are updated as needed, and escalations related to denials, suspensions, and certification operations are adequately addressed — including joining external calls as needed. This role also carries responsibility for leading critical calls with clients around complex compliance concerns and considerations, at times requiring close coordination with LegitScript’s legal team given the sensitive nature of these conversations. As the leader of Certification’s subject matter expertise, the Manager, Policy and Compliance, will partner closely with the Director of Certification Program Risk Strategy in guiding certification jurisdictional and scope expansions. What You’ll Do: Lead subject matter experts (SMEs) for Certification program offerings, staying informed about industry trends, regulatory updates, and market changes. Utilizes knowledge to adapt operational strategies and guide the team in responding to shifts in the regulatory landscape. Report on key regulatory shifts and trends tailored to different levels of the organization, offering documentation outlining insights, key takeaways, and forecasting potential business impacts and opportunities. Identify and lead cross-functional initiatives that strengthen certification standards, streamline compliance operations, and scale P&C’s processes to keep pace with jurisdictional, regulatory, and business growth Oversee and update compliance frameworks as needed, including leading the annual Certification Standards Refresh. Join customer calls as needed to support compliance client-facing work. Support Sales with documentation needs/requests, scoping decisions, and client questions. Develop policy team members through coaching, feedback, and growth planning; monitor team capacity and provide recommendations to leadership when adjustments to the Policy and Compliance team’s structure or resourcing are needed. Partner with theCertification Innovation Leader to identify ongoing opportunities to introduce AI and automation into policy and compliance workflows, improving efficiency and accuracy Partner with the legal team on denials, escalations, suspensions, litigation concerns, and other matters as needed — joining calls and creating documentation to support the Certification compliance risk framework Support the Director of Certification Program Risk Strategy on scope expansions by conducting discovery into the relevant regulatory facts, helping guide decisions about regulatory requirements and operational feasibility, creating documentation, and supporting team upskilling. Manage day-to-day operations of the Policy and Compliance team, including hiring, coaching, and holding team members accountable to KPIs and performance standards. Actively engage in behaviors that reflect LegitScript’s core values. What You’ll Bring: In-depth knowledge of policy management, industry regulations, and compliance standards across relevant verticals. Strong experience in managing risk and compliance programs, with a demonstrated ability to oversee policy development, implementation, and monitoring across operations. Extensive subject matter expertise, with the ability to develop and execute strategies that align with industry trends, business needs, and regulatory requirements. A forward-thinking approach to staying informed about industry trends and regulatory developments. Demonstrated experience in building, coaching, and managing high-performing teams, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, and guiding teams through periods of growth and change. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to work across departments, operational strategies, and with broader business goals. Strong ability to work in dynamic and evolving markets with a continuous improvement mindset. Open to feedback and adaptable to change, viewing it as an opportunity for growth and enhancement of operational processes. Excellent time management and problem-solving skills, allowing for the delivery of high-quality work even under pressure. Proficient in MacOS, Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs, etc.), and Microsoft Excel. Skilled in professional writing, with experience developing and reviewing documentation to support team efficiency and compliance initiatives. Well-developed ability to speak, read, comprehend, and write English. Open to candidates with a 4-year college degree or a comparable blend of education and experience. We value practical skills, a strong work ethic, and a passion for learning, regardless of formal education 2-4 years of experience managing people and/or policy & compliance related programs. We succeed together, care deeply, stay curious, and inspire trust — and we look for those qualities in the people we hire. LegitScript offers competitive compensation, flexible work options, and a team that’s genuinely invested in your success. If our mission resonates with you, we’d love to hear from you. This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of all activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Specialist, Regulatory Affairs, Team Telecom
item.description: Senior Specialist, Regulatory Affairs, Team Telecom Organization: SES Satellites Location: McLean, VA Date Posted: 10/03/2026 Senior Specialist, Regulatory Affairs, Team Telecom ROLE DESCRIPTION SUMMARY SES must implement the compliance requirements of the National Security Agreement (“NSA”) between SES and the U.S. Goverment “Team Telecom” national security regulators (Department of Defense, Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security). The incumbent is responsible for supporting the NSA Security Officer by interacting with multiple functional areas within the company to collect information and process requests for national security approvals of equipment, vendors, personnel, and transactionsas well as managing and updating associated databases and records. S/he supports the team’s management and operation of the internal controls implemented to ensure the company’s NSA compliance. S/he works closely with the VP, Legal & Regulatory Affairs, the NSA Security Officer, and the Team Telecom Specialists, and will collaborate with stakeholders in legal, HR, operations, IT, procurement, and other departments to implement NSA compliance. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES / KEY RESULT AREAS Carry out and manage NSA compliance tasks. Process and follow-up on requests for Team Telecom approval of Principal Equipment, Service Providers, Foreign Persons with Access, Changes to Protected Facilities, Data Storage Locations, Business Operations, and transaction related clearances Prepare routine and support the preparation of non-routine filings and work with commercial teams to gather and maintain required data (e.g., Principal Equipment, Service Providers, Personal Verifiable Information, Foreign Access Summary etc.), and preparation of Quarterly and Annual Reports Support LEPOC, and Cyber team handling of Security Incident Reports and Law Enforcement requests Support preparation of responses to information requests from Team Telecom Continually assess compliance posture through exercising control matrix and conducting internal audits, enforcing access controls Operate compliance framework & controls – continually assess risks and work with stakeholders to identify gaps Manage periodic internal & external audits (quarterly, annual) Drive stakeholder training Track and archive all tasks, filings and communications COMPETENCIES Ability to lead a cross functional team in a fast-paced demanding environment. Project management skills, with the ability to navigate complex projects, drive progress, and deliver results that align with the company’s strategic and operational objectives Continuous learner, eager to develop experience in the satellite industry and national security issues Excellent leadership, team-building, and interpersonal skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail Willingness to challenge status quo and drive continuous improvement proactively Ability to work collaboratively, leading cross-functional teams to timely deliver project objectives QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s or higher degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Engineering 5-10 years experience in the following: Experience working with compliance or audit teams Experience in external/internal audit, legal/regulatory compliance, project management or related fields Experience in communications industry or national security Proven track record of successful delivery of results, managing multiple matters simultaneously Effective management and analytical skills, capable of working both independently and collaboratively Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Office 365, SAP Ability to manage databases or data analytics tools OTHER KEY REQUIREMENTS / COMMENTS Fluency in English If non-U.S. Citizen, will require prior approval from U.S. Team Telecom agencies The salary range (US only) for this full-time position is $105,360 – $144,900. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and geographic location. Individual compensation within the range is determined based on work location and a variety of factors, including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, and relevant education or training. Additional compensation and benefits may apply depending on the location and terms of employment. SES and its Affiliated Companies are committed to providing fair and equal employment opportunities to all. We are an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, protected veteran status, disability, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law. item.title: VP, Regulatory & Public Affairs
item.description: VP, Regulatory & Public Affairs Organization: Center for Aquaculture Technologies (CAT) Location: San Diego, CA Date Posted: 10/03/2026 The Opportunity Center for Aquaculture Technologies (CAT) is seeking a Vice President, Regulatory & Public Affairs to build and lead our global regulatory and public affairs capability as CAT’s Genome Editing (GE) and other advanced technology programs progress toward commercialization. This is a strategic and highly visible leadership role at the intersection of science, regulation, market access, commercialization and external affairs. The VP, Regulatory & Public Affairs will shape CAT’s global regulatory strategy, strengthen engagement with regulators, policymakers and other key stakeholders, and help create clear pathways for the responsible adoption and commercialization of advanced technologies in aquaculture. The role will initially report directly to the CEO and work closely with CAT’s scientific, R&D, commercial and executive teams. As the commercialization of Genome Editing develops and CAT’s organization evolves, the reporting structure and scope of the role may evolve accordingly. This role will involve significant domestic and international travel. Key Areas of Responsibility Lead CAT’s global regulatory strategy for Genome Editing and other advanced technology programs across priority markets. Define regulatory pathways, priorities, evidence requirements, milestones and decision points for active and future programs. Develop and execute CAT’s Public Affairs strategy, including stakeholder mapping, engagement priorities and key messages. Build trusted relationships with regulators, policymakers, government agencies, industry organizations, certification bodies, clients and other influential stakeholders. Represent CAT in relevant regulatory, policy, scientific and industry forums. Monitor and interpret emerging regulatory frameworks, policies and precedents, particularly where regulation of Genome Editing and other novel technologies is still evolving. Promote credible, transparent and science-based dialogue around Genome Editing and its responsible application in aquaculture. Integrate regulatory, market-access and stakeholder considerations early into CAT’s R&D, technology and commercial decision-making. Partner with Commercial and Business Development teams to support market access, client adoption and commercialization. Advise the CEO and executive leadership on regulatory developments, policy trends, stakeholder considerations and associated business opportunities and risks. Build CAT’s regulatory intelligence and institutional knowledge, including regulatory precedents, submissions, evidence and stakeholder engagement history. Coordinate external regulatory, legal, scientific and public-affairs expertise where jurisdiction-specific or specialist support is required. Build a scalable Regulatory & Public Affairs capability as CAT’s technology portfolio and commercialization activities expand. Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $210,000-$230,000 USD, with a target annual bonus of 20%. Actual compensation will depend on experience, skills, and qualifications. The Candidate We are looking for a senior leader who combines scientific credibility, regulatory expertise, commercial understanding and strong external leadership skills. Experience in Genome Editing, genetics and genomics, aquaculture, biotechnology, animal breeding, novel technology regulation, market access, government or public affairs, international regulatory strategy, or stakeholder engagement would be particularly valuable. Relevant education and professional experience in life sciences, biotechnology, genetics, aquaculture, regulatory affairs, public policy, or a related field. Significant experience in regulatory affairs within biotechnology, life sciences, animal health, aquaculture, agriculture or another highly regulated science-based industry. Experience developing regulatory strategies for novel or emerging technologies, ideally involving Genome Editing, genetics or genomics. Strong understanding of the pathway from R&D and regulatory strategy through market access to commercial adoption. Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with regulators, policymakers, industry organizations, clients and other external stakeholders. Sufficient scientific and technical depth to engage credibly with scientists, regulators and technical experts. A strong commercial mindset, connecting regulatory strategy with market opportunities, client adoption and business priorities. Excellent communication and influencing skills, including the ability to translate complex science into clear and credible messages for technical and non-technical audiences. Ability to work across scientific, commercial and executive functions and influence without relying solely on formal authority. A pragmatic, entrepreneurial approach – able to operate strategically while remaining hands-on when required. Strong judgment regarding when to lead internally and when to engage specialist external expertise. Willingness and ability to undertake significant domestic and international travel. item.title: Regulatory Affairs Advisor
item.description: Regulatory Affairs Advisor Organization: Natera Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/03/2026 POSITION SUMMARY Title: Regulatory Advisor – FDA Pharma & IVDR Natera is a clinical genetic testing company specializing in non-invasive, cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and liquid biopsy testing. The Regulatory Advisor plays a key role in developing and driving regulatory strategy on behalf of the regulatory affairs (RA) team, specifically focusing on FDA Pharma and IVDR initiatives. At Natera, we remember there is a person behind every sample. This role combines strong technical knowledge and an understanding of regulatory requirements (US FDA, CAP/CLIA/NYS, EU, or Japan) to support the approval and registration of products that proactively inform disease management. You will represent the RA team to internal and external stakeholders through written and verbal communication. This role maintains product registrations, change assessments, post-market surveillance reports, and records of communication with regulatory authorities. You will support the overall effectiveness of the RA team through contributions to staff development, process improvements, and maintaining a deep understanding of current regulatory requirements in the evolving diagnostics landscape. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Represent the regulatory function on designated cross-functional teams. Conduct business interactions with customers and regulatory authorities regarding regulatory pathways, performance claims, supporting data, and labeling in the context of submissions or registrations. Build and execute bold, practical regulatory strategies for complex regulatory affairs programs, with a heavy emphasis on FDA Pharma, IVDR, and In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) systems. Advocate for the least burdensome approaches to product clearance and approval while strictly interpreting and adhering to regulatory requirements. Coordinate and prepare regulatory submissions with minimal supervision, including EU/IVD/IVDR Technical Documentation, classification requests, pre-submissions, 510(k) premarket notifications, investigational device exemptions, NYS DoH submissions, and critical worldwide registrations. Mentor regulatory associates and support their career advancement. Deliver training on regulatory topics across internal teams. Lead cross-functional teams to address major regulatory changes, compliance with new registration requirements, or process improvements. Contribute to setting individual and departmental annual goals aligned with business objectives. Review and ensure regulatory compliance of advertising, promotion, and labeling across a common product line. Take personal accountability for identifying gaps in processes and proactively build data-driven solutions to improve them. Evaluate product changes for global regulatory submission impact. May lead small teams. Other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in a life science field (biology, microbiology, chemistry, engineering, medical technology, regulatory science, etc.) or equivalent. Advanced degree in life sciences (MS, PhD, etc.) and/or MBA preferred. Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC) preferred. Minimum of 8+ years of direct applicable regulatory experience in medical devices, laboratory-developed tests (LDTs), or pharma. Direct experience with FDA Pharma and IVDR submissions is highly preferred. Experience in Organ Health or Women’s Health diagnostics is ideal and strongly preferred. In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx) experience is a plus. PMA experience preferred. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES Working knowledge of U.S. and EU Medical Device/IVD/IVDR, FDA Pharma, and/or laboratory developed test regulatory requirements. Proactive, self-directed, and highly engaged. Emphasis on talent development and team building. Use sound scientific judgment to solve problems and make decisions even when rigid policies do not exist. Manage multiple projects with urgency, staying organized and focused on delivering results. Demonstrated ability to effectively formulate and drive change. Experienced in continuous improvement projects, project management, and product development processes. Thrive in ambiguity by navigating rapid change and actively building structure and standard operating procedures where they are missing. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate across cultures, work effectively with technical and scientific personnel, and negotiate clearly with Regulators. Computer literacy (PC, Microsoft Word/Excel/PowerPoint). The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $146,100 – $182,600 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits – Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com. Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Manager – Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Manager – Regulatory Affairs Organization: Constellation Location: Chicago, IL | Washington, DC | Baltimore, MD | Kennett Square, PA Date Posted: 10/03/2026 Job Description Who We Are As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation’s largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we’re creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country’s energy needs today and tomorrow. Total Rewards Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more. Expected salary range of $124,200 to $138,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k). Primary Purpose of Position Support Constellation’s regulatory affairs strategy in contested cases and similar proceedings before state utility commissions. In consultation and coordination with a cross-functional team across the company’s policy, legal and business organizations, the position coordinates and supports litigation positions, builds external coalitions, engages with external stakeholders, and supports advocacy strategies to realize regulatory outcomes that create value for the company. The position prepares, and coordinates regulatory advocacy materials such as briefs, expert analysis and testimony, comments and position papers. To further Constellation’s advocacy interests, the position maintains and leverages relationships with regulators and regulatory staff, industry participants, and other stakeholders and advises the business units regarding the impact of and opportunities created by regulatory litigation, including making recommendations for advocacy, commercial positions and other actions driving value for the company’s operations and assets. Primary Duties and Accountabilities Manage the company’s regulatory affairs activity in contested cases and similar proceedings before state utility commissions, including support for and development of litigation positions, building external coalitions, and executing regulatory affairs strategies to realize outcomes that create value for the company. Prepare and coordinate the preparation of regulatory advocacy materials, including briefs, expert analysis and testimony, comments, and position papers. Lead efforts with our retail and commercial teams and Retail Energy Supply Association (RESA) to coordinate Constellation participation in retail related proceedings and rate cases (where appropriate) to ensure fair-rate allocation and designs for both our existing and potential customers. Additionally, they will play a role in supporting, defending, and in certain instances expanding state retail energy opportunities in competitive states and new states identified by the Commercial Team. Monitor and attend relevant commission general meetings and share all retail/commercial related pertinent information with the broader Policy, retail and commercial teams. Monitoring legislation or rule implementation at the commission level, including rulemakings, workshops, and technical conferences related to retail matters. Maintain and leverage relationships with regulators and regulatory staff, industry participants, and other stakeholders to further Constellations regulatory advocacy interests, including representing the company at conferences and industry gatherings. Manage and support key docketed proceedings and ensuring the development and evolution of data center tariffs across our key states. The manager will collaborate with relevant internal departments to develop and enhance tools and reports to keep the organization informed on data center tariff developments, among other new large load related matters. Coordination of engagements at NARUC, MACRUC, MARC and other conferences as determined in the Regulatory Advocacy Affairs Strategy. Perform other duties as assigned by the Department VP or Director. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree and 8-years of experience, in lieu of degree 12-years of experience 8-years of professional experience with two or more specializing in government affairs, public advocacy and/or communications or a minimum of 6 years of professional experience with 4 or more specializing in government affairs, public advocacy and/or communications Demonstrated comprehensive knowledge of legal principles, practices, and procedures, with the ability to apply them to complex assignments Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build strong relationships with team members and business stakeholders Excellent legal research, analytical abilities, and knowledge of federal and or state law Preferred Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Political Science, Public Policy or related field advanced degree in political science, public policy or related field or law Demonstrated ability to build strong network of contacts within government and local agencies at multiple levels Understanding of energy industry broadly, and the electric generation sector specifically, is preferable. item.title: Government Affairs South Central Regulatory Lead
item.description: Government Affairs South Central Regulatory Lead Organization: Intersect Location: Austin, TX Date Posted: 10/03/2026 About the job We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation. Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet. Location & Team Gatherings Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016. We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office – we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations – SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON. We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture. GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS SOUTH CENTRAL REGULATORY LEAD About this role The Government Affairs Regulatory Lead for the South Central region is the regional large load expert within the Government Affairs team and will support our active development within ERCOT, and future development within SPP. This position is responsible for the coordination of the politics of regulatory issues with relevant teams including Development, Engineering, and the Head of Texas Government Affairs. This role will collaborate with these other teams to address regulatory activity affecting the company’s business interests—including engagement with relevant state agencies such as utility commissions, grid operators and other state agencies as needed. The role includes external representation with trade associations, digital infrastructure organizations, and NGOs. The individual will strategize and lead campaigns to achieve Intersect’s regulatory goals, ensure alignment of company priorities with political and market realities, and support the company’s growing digital infrastructure strategy. The position reports to the Head of State Government Affairs and works closely with regional Development, Engineering, and Community Engagement teams. The role is based in-region (Austin, Texas preferred) with required in-person engagement across assigned states. Team overview This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the renewable energy transition by shaping policy environments that enable large-scale energy infrastructure development. Government Affairs partners closely with Development, Permitting, Community Engagement, and executive leadership to align public policy strategy with commercial objectives. By building strong relationships with policymakers, regulators, and industry stakeholders, the team ensures Intersect can responsibly scale its impact while navigating complex legislative and regulatory landscapes. What you’ll do Attend and represent the company at public utility commission meetings, with grid operators and other relevant agencies at the state level. Build and maintain strong relationships with important policymakers, executive officials, and staff (Texas agencies, with future expansion to Oklahoma and New Mexico are the priority for this responsibility). Identify and advance strategic policy priorities enabling rapid buildout of energy infrastructure. Advocate the company’s positions and build consensus across regulatory staff, grid operators, and industry partners. Lead campaigns and deploy resources to accomplish Government Affairs objectives at the state level. Serve as an internal expert on government and regulatory dynamics in assigned states and translate emerging risks into recommended actions. Engage actively in assigned regional and national associations related to energy development. Build coalitions of aligned corporate, community, and third‑party interests to advance priority outcomes. Understand critical milestones for development, permitting, and community engagement teams and provide support where a government affairs nexus exists. Plan, budget, and manage outside consultants, lobbyists, technical advisors, and legal counsel. Coordinate reporting on policy issues, regulatory news, and advocacy efforts with other regulatory roles within the company. Potentially manage regional Government Affairs staff as the team expands. Other responsibilities as required to support company objectives. What you’ll bring At least 5+ years of utility or private-sector experience with electric power system planning for large loads, including interconnection, transmission constraints, and new generation or storage strongly preferred. Familiarity with ERCOT market design and interconnection processes strongly preferred. Working knowledge of environmental resource issues associated with large energy‑intensive facilities (e.g., energy and water usage, emissions, renewable energy procurement) and ability to advocate for practical, data‑driven policy solutions. Excellent problem solving and strategic thinking skills. Highly driven, detail-oriented, and self-motivated. Ability to summarize complex issues and drive them into actionable strategies. Demonstrated success in coalition-building and stakeholder alignment. Strong political judgment and commercial sensibility. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a remote-first environment. Ability to maintain discretion and sound judgment. Total Rewards Total Compensation: $200,000 – $225,000 (total compensation includes base salary + bonus) Equity: Beyond your salary, you’ll receive an Equity Grant, giving you a meaningful stake in our parent company. Health & wellness: 100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision Time to recharge: Unlimited PTO, plus two company-wide breaks (Fourth of July & end of year) Family support: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning and family care support through Carrot and Maven Mental health: Free access to Spring Health, including 5 free therapy and psychiatry sessions, plus a Headspace account for mindfulness and meditation through our physical health vendor, Wellhub+ Perks & extras: $150 monthly food stipend, $150 monthly reimbursement for cell phone and internet, pet insurance allowance, full home office setup, free access to UrbanSitter with $625 in quarterly company-paid credits, ActiveHero, and One Medical Intersect maintains a work environment free from discrimination, one where all employees are treated with dignity and respect. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling Intersect’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. Intersect does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by and consistent with applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. We adhere to these principles in all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, promotion, benefits, social and recreational programs, and discipline. We sometimes use AI-powered note taking tools during interviews to support our team. They’re used only for documentation and don’t replace human judgment. item.title: Assistant Vice President, Government, Public & Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Assistant Vice President, Government, Public & Regulatory Affairs Organization: Moody's Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/03/2026 At Moody’s, we unite the brightest minds to turn today’s risks into tomorrow’s opportunities. We do this by striving to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome to be who they are—with the freedom to exchange ideas, think innovatively, and listen to each other and customers in meaningful ways. Moody’s is transforming how the world sees risk. As a global leader in ratings and integrated risk assessment, we’re advancing AI to move from insight to action—enabling intelligence that not only understands complexity but responds to it. We decode risk to unlock opportunity, helping our clients navigate uncertainty with clarity, speed, and confidence. If you are excited about this opportunity but do not meet every single requirement, please apply! You still may be a great fit for this role or other open roles. We are seeking candidates who model our values: invest in every relationship, lead with curiosity, champion diverse perspectives, turn inputs into actions, and uphold trust through integrity. Skills and Competencies 5–9 years of experience analyzing U.S. public policy, regulatory, and legal developments and their business impact within a financial services company, regulator, government body, financial technology provider, or similar organization Strong understanding of U.S. government institutions, regulatory processes, and policymaking dynamics, with a demonstrated track record of regulatory and public policy analysis, strategy development, and stakeholder engagement Prior experience at a U.S. financial regulatory agency or other government body with responsibility for financial services policy or regulation is preferred Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex regulatory and policy issues clearly and effectively to senior leadership and diverse stakeholder groups Strong interpersonal, collaboration, and leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to build relationships and drive execution across functions, business lines, and geographies Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders simultaneously Demonstrated proficiency in artificial intelligence concepts, with hands-on experience using AI tools to streamline workflows and enhance operational efficiency. Proven ability to implement AI-powered solutions to solve business challenges. Demonstrates a growing awareness of AI risk management and a commitment to responsible and ethical AI use. Education Bachelor’s degree in legal studies, finance, economics, political science, public policy, communications, international relations, or a related discipline required Responsibilities The AVP plays a key role in guiding U.S. regulatory analysis, advancing external stakeholder engagement, and supporting Moody’s Government, Public and Regulatory Affairs strategy. Specific responsibilities may include: Guiding analysts in tracking and analyzing regulatory and policy developments, preparing briefings and policy updates relevant to Moody’s business, including those related to credit rating agencies, capital markets, private credit, insurance regulation, risk assessment tools, financial crime compliance, trade policy, and geopolitical issues Preparing and presenting clear, well-structured verbal and written briefings and position papers on regulatory developments for senior leadership and business stakeholders Assessing the business implications of proposed and adopted regulation, translating complex legal and regulatory texts into actionable analysis Helping foster relationships with regulators, policymakers, trade groups, and other external stakeholders; attending external events and sharing insights with internal stakeholders Preparing briefing materials, talking points, and background research ahead of senior-level meetings with government officials and regulators Coordinating the internal adoption of technology for stakeholder engagement tracking, including the collection, monitoring, and reporting of engagement activity and related metrics, with a focus on efficiency and continuous improvement Working closely with Government, Public and Regulatory Affairs colleagues globally to ensure regulatory positions are aligned with global strategy and messaging; supporting internal working groups and team-led events Collaborating with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and business line teams to gather input, leverage subject matter expertise, and ensure alignment on regulatory and public policy matters About the Team Moody’s Government, Public and Regulatory Affairs (GPRA) team is a global, strategic function within Global Corporate Affairs, reporting directly to the Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. The team is responsible for providing expertise in government relations, public policy, regulatory analysis, and geopolitical affairs that inform Moody’s strategy, commercial activities, and risk management across all business lines and markets. GPRA shapes Moody’s positions on regulatory policy worldwide, builds and maintains relationships with governments, regulators, and multilateral institutions, and advances thought leadership that strengthens Moody’s reputation with policymakers. By joining our team, you will be part of high-impact work spanning U.S. and global markets, including emerging policy areas such as artificial intelligence and technological innovation, where the team actively contributes to shaping Moody’s forward-looking engagement strategy. For US-based roles only: the anticipated hiring base salary range for this position is $140,200.00 – $203,350.00, depending on factors such as experience, education, level, skills, and location. This range is based on a full-time position. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for incentive compensation. Moody’s also offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, parental leave, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, a discounted employee stock purchase plan, and tuition reimbursement. Moody’s is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, gender, age, religion or creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital or familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Moody’s also provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities or based on a sincerely held religious belief in accordance with applicable laws. If you need to inquire about a reasonable accommodation, or need assistance with completing the application process, please email [email protected] . This contact information is for accommodation requests only, and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications For San Francisco positions, qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. This position may be considered a promotional opportunity, pursuant to the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. Candidates for Moody’s Corporation may be asked to disclose securities holdings pursuant to Moody’s Policy for Securities Trading and the requirements of the position. Employment is contingent upon compliance with the Policy, including remediation of positions in those holdings as necessary. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Manager – Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Senior Manager – Regulatory Affairs Organization: Covista Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 10/03/2026 About Covista Covista (NYSE: CVSA) is America’s largest healthcare educator, serving 100,000 students and supported by a community of 400,000 alumni across five accredited institutions. Through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, Covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. Covista is the parent company of American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, Chamberlain University, Ross University School of Medicine, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine and Walden University. Our colleagues come from a wide range of backgrounds, business, academia, healthcare, government and nonprofits, and are part of a culture where doing exceptional work and making a meaningful difference for students and society aren’t separate goals—they’re one and the same. This means creating an environment where colleagues can develop new skills, build careers that match their ambitions and see the tangible impact of their work on healthcare education and workforce development. Colleagues who deliver results and embrace new tools to work smarter are valued for their contributions. But what makes working at Covista distinctive is our impact. Our faculty and colleagues don’t just support healthcare education—they shape it. This isn’t abstract purpose work. It’s solving real problems for real people in real communities while advancing careers. We operate on a hybrid schedule with four in-office days per week (Monday–Thursday). This approach enhances creativity, innovation, communication, and relationship-building, fostering a dynamic and collaborative work environment. Job Description Opportunity at a Glance Under the general direction of the Senior Director of Regulatory Affairs, the Senior Manager, Regulatory Affairs serves as a regulatory advisor responsible for translating complex regulatory, legislative, accreditation, and policy developments into practical business guidance, implementation strategies, and operational guardrails across Covista institutions and business units. The position provides regulatory leadership through proactive monitoring, research, impact assessment, stakeholder consultation, and implementation support. The Senior Manager leads the Strategy and Research function, establishes priorities, reviews and advances the team’s analyses and recommendations, and supports development of team members. The position leads or supports significant regulatory initiatives from rulemaking and impact assessment through operational implementation, while maintaining continuity of regulatory interpretations, decisions, and institutional knowledge. The role collaborates with institutional and functional leaders to identify regulatory implications, develop practical and compliant solutions, promote consistent decision-making, and support regulatory readiness across Covista institutions. Responsibilities Provide regulatory interpretation, consultation, and practical guidance regarding complex and evolving regulatory requirements; respond to regulatory inquiries, projects, and business initiatives in a timely manner. Participate in strategic planning, implementation, and operational discussions to advise management regarding growth initiatives, business strategies, institutional changes, regulatory risks, and corrective action strategies. Serve on cross-functional workgroups and implementation teams to support compliance with federal, state, and accreditor requirements and promote effective execution of regulatory initiatives. Develops regulatory guidance, procedures, training, and implementation resources to support organizational compliance, regulatory awareness, and consistent operational practices. Partners with institutional and business stakeholders to identify regulatory risks, compliance gaps, implementation challenges, and opportunities for process improvement; recommend practical solutions and operational standards where appropriate. Reviews student-facing, public-facing, and operational communications, including websites, marketing materials, enrollment communications, disclosures, policies, forms, and guidance documents to promote regulatory accuracy and consistency. Conduct research, analysis, benchmarking, and environmental scans related to federal, state, accreditor, and policy matters; assess institutional impacts, compliance considerations, strategic opportunities, and implementation requirements. Analyze, interpret, and communicate regulatory developments and emerging requirements; develop executive summaries, impact assessments, reports, presentations, and other decision-support materials for leadership and key stakeholders. Review and respond to regulatory inquiries, projects, and business initiatives by conducting research, evaluating regulatory implications, and providing practical guidance, compliance recommendations, and implementation considerations. Maintain regulatory monitoring frameworks, reporting tools, tracking systems, and research resources to support timely and consistent communication of regulatory developments. Provides leadership, coaching, and oversight for Strategy and Research personnel, including prioritizing work, reviewing analyses and recommendations, supporting staff development, and managing departmental workflows. Performs other duties as assigned Complies with all policies and standards Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree required and Master’s Degree preferred. 8+ years of experience in regulatory assurance, compliance or licensing required. 2+ years of supervisory experience required. Experience with U.S. Department of Education regulations, Title IV requirements, federal rulemaking, accreditation, or multi-institutional operations preferred. Excellent interpersonal, organizational, written and verbal communication skills. Excellent working knowledge of with MS Word, SharePoint, PowerPoint and Excel a must. Must be familiar with the standards and requirements of multiple state authorizing agencies and institutional / programmatic accreditors. Demonstrate the ability to establish and develop positive relationships with senior leaders and other key stakeholders. Must possess strong critical thinking skills to decipher regulatory requirements that may not be explicit. Additional Information In support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected salary range for this position is between $85,000 and $120,000. Actual pay will be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. Our Talent Acquisition Team will be happy to answer any questions you may have, and we look forward to learning more about your salary requirements. The position qualifies for the below benefits. Covista offers a robust suite of benefits including: Health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance 401k Retirement Program + 6% employer match Participation in Covista’s Flexible Time Off (FTO) Policy 12 Paid Holidays For more information related to our benefits please visit: https://careers.covista.com/benefits You are also eligible to participate in an annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.
