item.title: Manager, Government Affairs
item.description: Manager, Government Affairs Organization: American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/07/2026 Manager, Government Affairs Apply Here This is a great opportunity to do substantive advocacy work and advance an industry that supports economic growth and job creation and makes essential paper and wood products that Americans use every day! As part of a collaborative team, you’ll use strategic and critical thinking skills to advocate for member interests and move the industry forward. You’ll have an opportunity to build upon existing federal legislative experience, develop new expertise, manage a portfolio, and be in the thick of high-profile issues (i.e., energy, transportation and manufacturing). The below description provides more detail on American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA), this important role and how you will impact the industry. Essential job functions: • Develop, coordinate and implement advocacy strategies to achieve industry policy positions • Analyze, report on, and respond to assigned legislative and regulatory initiatives • Build and maintain relationships with key congressional members and staff • Ensure AF&PA legislative goals are coordinated with other AF&PA departments and related industry groups, including coalition engagement • Represent AF&PA to outside audiences, organizations and strategic alliances through meetings and attending political events • Maintain relationships and coordinate with outside interest groups in coalitions on shared federal legislative goals, leading where appropriate • Develop educational opportunities for federal legislators and their staff that serve to highlight the industry accomplishments • Write letters, testimony and various association member communications • Manage policy committees for the industry, and monitor/engage on issues facing the industry. This includes developing and implementing budgets, running meetings, coordinating member input on key issues, and developing advocacy strategies • Serve on internal issue teams; manage, plan, and run meetings on relevant issue topics affecting the association • As a registered federal lobbyist, ensure all actions demonstrate the highest level of compliance and ethical standards Qualifications: If your knowledge, skills and abilities are transferrable and you think you’re a great candidate for AF&PA – please consider applying even if you do not meet all the criteria listed below. • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in one of the social or agricultural sciences • Five or more years of experience in one or more of the following environments: Capitol Hill legislative staff, government affairs office for a trade association, lobbying firm, policy staff/political campaigns • Working knowledge of the federal legislative process required • Excellent communication skills in writing, editing and public presentation • Strong organizational and project management skills to effectively balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment • Strong critical thinking, analytical and research skills • Ability to produce high quality work within tight deadlines • Ability to analyze, evaluate and present statistical data • Ability to exercise judgment and discretion with integrity, initiative and limited supervision • Ability to maintain confidentiality, and exercise discretion in sensitive AF&PA matters and on policy and market issues • Excellent interpersonal skills; ability to maintain positive rapport with co-workers in a collaborative, diverse environment • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint • Understanding of environment, energy, forest product industry or other manufacturing sector is a plus Compensation and Benefits: The salary for this position is expected to be between $94,000-$110,000. This is a good-faith estimate based on market data for comparable positions and the current budgeted amount for this role. Factors to be considered when determining the salary of the selected candidate include relevant skills, experience and knowledge, and the alignment of these qualities with those of existing staff. We offer a generous benefits package that currently includes: • Paid Vacation, Personal and Sick leave totaling 27-42 days per year (based on relevant experience), plus holidays and paid Parental Leave • 94%-80% paid CareFirst medical plans for employees and their families • Generous 401(k) retirement plan with up to 9% employer contribution (after waiting period) • Free fitness center and pickleball courts at the DC office location • Plus dental, vision, life insurance, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Account… Location: We are located on 13th Street, NW between F and G, (directly above Metro Center Station). Our office is hybrid, which includes up to two days of remote work; however, due to the nature of the work in federal government affairs, we suspect the person hired may frequently spend more than three days a week on the Hill and in the DC office. Working at AF&PA: The American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA) values diverse backgrounds and capabilities and invites all talented individuals to apply to be part of our team and support our culture and mission. We encourage the exchange of knowledge, innovative ideas and different perspectives to reach our goals and we support work/life balance. About AF&PA AF&PA serves to advance public policies that foster economic growth, job creation and global competitiveness for a vital sector that makes the essential paper and packaging products Americans use every day. The U.S. forest products industry employs more than 925,000 people, largely in rural America, and is among the top 10 manufacturing sector employers in 44 states. Our industry accounts for approximately 4.7% of the total U.S. manufacturing GDP, manufacturing more than $435 billion in products annually. AF&PA member companies are significant producers and users of renewable biomass energy and are committed to making sustainable products for a sustainable future through the industry’s decades-long initiative — Better Practices, Better Planet 2030. Visit AF&PA online at afandpa.org or follow us on X @ForestandPaper. Equal Employment Opportunity AF&PA is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and welcomes all talented individuals regardless of race, color, national origin, religion, age, sex, disability, veteran status or other category protected by law. Your Rights Applicants have rights under federal employment laws. Information may be found on the Department of Labor’s website (https://www.dol.gov) as well as through these available notices: Know Your Rights; Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA); and Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA). item.title: Corporate Information Program Manager
item.description: Corporate Information Program Manager Organization: Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/07/2026 Corporate Information Program Manager As the Corporate Information Program Manager, represents and promotes the image and reputation of the Airports Authority as a key internal and external communications contact. Serves as a communications resource within the Corporate Communications Division, providing editorial leadership, executive communications support, media relations support, strategic messaging development and support, corporate publication management, and backup support to the Noise Information Office. Serves in the Corporate Communications Division within the Office of Communications and Government Affairs at Corporate Headquarters. General Responsibilities Provides communications support to the Director of Corporate Communications and other leadership by developing and disseminating accurate, timely, and effective corporate messages to internal and external stakeholders. Develops and coordinates communications and outreach plans by gathering, analyzing, and reporting information from other airports and related organizations; identifies and implements communications best practices applicable to the Airports Authority. Produces communications materials and publications for internal and external audiences, including correspondence, speeches, presentations, talking points, position papers, newsletters, corporate reports, and other materials prepared for internal and external audiences. Serves as publisher and chief editor of the weekly On Good Authority employee newsletter, setting editorial priorities and schedules, coordinating news writing and visual coverage, managing contributions and distribution, and identifying opportunities to improve the publication and its coverage. Also serves as editor of the quarterly business-to-business stakeholder newsletter and similar corporate publications. Provides editorial support for corporate reports and publications produced by the Office of Revenue and other organizational functions, including Regulatory Compliance and Community Engagement, ensuring materials are accurate, effective, and professionally presented. Manages executive communications in consultation with the Director of Corporate Communications and Vice President for Communications and Government Affairs, developing speech texts, talking points, video scripts, background materials, presentations, and related communications including public appearances, Board meetings, employee forums, and other organizational events. Provides logistical support as needed. Provides communications and technical support to the Noise Information Office, serving as backup to the Noise Information Office Manager and supporting public relations, reporting, technical communications, and related initiatives. Supports preparation of the Authority’s Annual Aircraft Noise Report and provides communications and administrative support for the Reagan National Airport Community Noise Working Group. Coordinates with Planning, Engineering, and other organizational functions on communications and information needs related to airport encroachment, flight-path obstruction, and other noise-related or airport operational matters, including development of materials used to communicate these issues to internal and external stakeholders. Assists the Media Relations team with drafting press releases, statements, position papers, presentation materials, and other media communications; assists with planning and management of media events and serves as a member of the Media Relations On-Call Team. Provides communications support during corporate emergencies and other sensitive or high-visibility situations, responding to media inquiries and assisting with the development and coordination of timely corporate communications. Maintains awareness of emerging communications, public affairs, and media practices and applies appropriate methods and technologies to strengthen the Airports Authority’s communications effectiveness, reputation, and relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Performs other duties as assigned. Qualifications Six years of progressively responsible experience in corporate communications or a related field, including community and media outreach; developing communications and outreach strategies; drafting speeches and visual materials for senior management; preparing news releases and related materials; managing corporate publications; and developing communications for internal and external audiences. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. Superior writing and editing skills, including the ability to develop polished communications for executive and public audiences. Superior public speaking and presentation skills, with the ability to coach others in writing, editing, and public presentations. Superior skills in corporate message formulation and dissemination to build and safeguard the Airports Authority’s image and reputation. Demonstrated ability to manage communications involving public criticism, political issues, emergency situations, corporate advocacy, and other sensitive public relations matters. Knowledge of generally accepted public affairs, public information, media relations, and corporate communications principles, objectives, standards, and techniques, with the ability to apply them to ensure accurate, timely, and effective communications. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with senior leadership, internal business units, media representatives, community stakeholders, and other external parties. Ability to quickly move between multiple airport and company locations when required. Education Bachelor’s degree in Communications or a related field. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in Communications or a related field. Experience with videography, photography, and video/audio editing used in media and corporate communications. Certifications and Licenses Required Valid driver’s license in good standing. Necessary Special Factors Operates a motor vehicle airside and landside and requires an AOA permit. May be required to work nights, holidays, or weekends in support of Airports Authority meetings, events, emergency communications, and the Media Relations on-call rotation. Participates in the Media Relations on-call rotation and may be required to provide coverage for reporter inquiries and corporate emergencies. What We Offer A career with the Airports Authority comes with more than just a paycheck; it offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family’s health, financial security, and professional growth. Benefits include: Medical, dental, and vision coverage Well-being resources Health savings and flexible spending accounts Pension and retirement plans Ongoing training and development opportunities Discover more about our benefits package here. A background security investigation will be required for all new hires. Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Follow us on Twitter @MWAAcareers. Apply At: https://mwaa.wd1. myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/MWAA/ details/Corporate-Information- Program-Manager_R0007543 Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: IC Congressional Budget Resource Advisor
item.description: IC Congressional Budget Resource Advisor Organization: MITRE Location: McLean, VA Date Posted: 10/08/2026 At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future. The Influence and Integration Department advances ODNI’s enterprise priorities by translating policy intent into integrated, executable approaches across the Intelligence Community. The department supports ODNI’s policy and mission integration efforts by shaping policy frameworks, strengthening governance and oversight, and guiding capability development that connects strategic direction to mission execution. Through disciplined analysis, enterprise coordination, and sustained partnership, the department aligns policy, mission priorities, and analytic leadership to enable coherent implementation of modernization initiatives and reinforce ODNI’s role as the strategic leader of the IC. Roles & Responsibilities: The Influence and Integration Department seeks a IC Congressional Budget & Resources Advisor to provide strategic and operational support to our Government sponsor in coordinating mission management, budget analysis, budget and execution, and other congressional resource matters. The sponsor requires trusted advisors to perform this strategic work and provide unbiased and independent recommendations on programming resources to achieve planned objectives. Responsibilities Include: Assist sponsor in serving as a liaison for congressional resource matters, coordinating with budget, programming, legislative affairs, acquisition, policy, legal, and senior leadership stakeholders. Analyze authorization and appropriations legislation, committee reports, and congressional marks to determine impacts on funding and resourcing decisions. Develop and coordinate responses to Congressional Directed Actions (CDAs), requests for information, and other congressional taskers. Prepare decision briefs, issue papers, talking points, correspondence, and leadership updates on congressional resource issues and execution impacts. Track congressional actions throughout the budget cycle and monitor implementation of directed funding, reporting requirements, and suspense items to ensure timely compliance. Assess resource, execution, and policy implications of proposed or enacted congressional actions and recommend courses of action to leadership. Support budget justification, reclama, appeals, spend plan, and resource realignment efforts related to congressional direction and funding changes. Maintain effective working relationships across internal and external stakeholders to translate congressional direction into actionable resource plans and organizational decisions. Provide direct and routine coordination with the Office of Legislative Affairs Basic Qualifications: Typically requires a minimum of 10 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 8 years with a Master’s degree; or 5 years with a PhD; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Experience with the Congressional Budget Justification Book (CBJB), the National Intelligence Programs (NIP), or Military Intelligence Programs (MIP). Experience with the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) cycle or the Intelligence Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Evaluation (IPPBE) cycle. Must have an active Top Secret/SCI w/Poly U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance. Due to the lengthy clearance process and our urgent need, candidates without an existing TS/SCI clearance with polygraph cannot be considered for this opening. This position has an on-site requirement of 5 days a week on-site Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, Data Science/Analytics, Public Policy, National Security Studies, Intelligence Studies, or related field. Experience with government budget systems and processes. Experience with analysis conducted using Microsoft Excel. Experience as a Congressional Liaison. Familiarity with concepts covered in the Certified Defense Financial Manager (CDFM) or the Certified Government Financial Manager (CGFM) certifications. Strong professional writing and editing abilities. Ability to lead a financial-related study, conduct research, collaborate with a multi-disciplinary team, and communicate results for decision makers. Ability to interact with senior level government officials in a fast-paced environment. This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s): Top Secret/SCI/Polygraph This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s): Top Secret/SCI/Polygraph Salary compensation range and midpoint: $161,600 – $202,000 – $242,400 Annual Work Location Type: Onsite Commitment to Non-Discrimination All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local or international law. MITRE intends to maintain a website that is fully accessible to all individuals. If you are unable to search or apply for jobs and would like to request a reasonable accommodation for any part of MITRE’s employment process, please email [email protected] for general support and [email protected] for intern positions. This service is for individuals requiring reasonable accommodation requests. Please note that vendor solicitations will not receive a reply. Benefits information may be found here. item.title: Paid Media Planner
item.description: Paid Media Planner Organization: Freddie Mac Location: McLean, VA Date Posted: 10/08/2026 At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is what motivates us, and it’s at the core of everything we do. Since our charter in 1970, we have made home possible for more than 90 million families across the country. Join an organization where your work contributes to a greater purpose. Position Overview: We are seeking a skilled Paid Media Planner with hands-on experience developing, managing, and executing integrated media campaigns across multiple channels. In this role, you will be responsible for overseeing and optimizing media strategies to ensure maximum performance and efficiency across various lines of business and audiences (B2B/B2C). Your expertise will help drive impactful results and elevate our brand presence across all media channels. Our Impact: At Freddie Mac, our mission is to provide liquidity, stability and affordability to the U.S. housing market. You will be part of a team helping to Make Home Possible for more families across the nation. Our team is a group of experienced marketers responsible for Freddie Mac’s enterprise paid media advertising initiatives. We deliver awareness, engagement, education and lead-generation campaigns that raise the profile of Freddie Mac and the products, tools and services we provide. Our team is responsible for the design and implementation of effective media and marketing strategies, the optimization of all campaigns and the creation of new engagement strategies. We collaborate across Freddie Mac to ensure alignment with business objectives and deliver with excellence. Your Impact: Reporting to the Senior Manager, Enterprise Advertising, your work will include the following responsibilities: Campaign Management: Manage end-to-end paid media campaigns across various channels (social, direct to publisher, SEM, emerging, traditional, and programmatic) ensuring alignment with overall marketing and campaign strategies. Develop and implement new media campaigns as needed, including planning, creative development and hands-on execution directly within ad platforms. Develop and manage budgets for paid media campaigns, ensuring efficient allocation of resources to increase return on investment. Coordinate invoices and collaborate with finance and accounting teams to reconcile as needed. Support media planning and buying across various platforms, adapting to evolving business needs. Strategy Development: Develop strategic, omni-channel integrated marketing campaigns that connect business objectives, audience insights, messaging and media execution. Lead comprehensive paid media strategy across lines of business (B2B/B2C) and target audiences that align with overall business goals. Ensure seamless integration of media campaigns with other marketing channels and initiatives, enhancing overall campaign effectiveness. Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and best practices in paid media advertising, continuously adapting strategies to leverage new opportunities and provide best practices to the wider team. Analytics and Reporting: Analyze campaign performance data to identify trends and insights, using this information to refine strategies and optimize effectiveness. Implement and manage tracking mechanisms and measure results using analytics tools. Prepare holistic data storytelling and campaign reporting, including recommendations for business partners and stakeholders. Qualifications: 5-7 years paid media experience required, with at least 2+ years’ experience leading media strategies for large corporate brands. Must have hands-on experience executing paid media campaigns directly within ad platforms (Meta, LinkedIn, Google Ads, programmatic platforms, etc.). Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, business, or related field (or equivalent experience). Comprehensive knowledge of media planning, buying, campaign management, optimization techniques, and budget management. Strong proficiency in analytics tools, conversion tracking, tagging, and attribution. Ability to strategically assess new opportunities and make data-driven decisions resulting in tangible improvements in media performance. Exceptional written and verbal communicator with strong attention to detail. Agency and finance/housing industry paid media experience is a plus. Keys to Success in this Role: Proven ability to synthesize performance measurements and trends into concise narratives and recommendations. Familiarity with data visualization tools, marketing automation, CRM, web analytics, and other associated measurement tools. Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team setting. Strong ability to prioritize; you’ll manage multiple campaigns with competing deadlines and priorities within the organization. Experience in developing processes and working closely with cross-functional teams. Proven track record of launching large projects successfully through project management and process creation. Familiarity and experience with website development and content management systems. Ability to build rapport to influence decisions at all levels. Current Freddie Mac employees please apply through the internal career site. We consider all applicants for all positions without regard to gender, race, color, religion, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, physical and mental disability, pregnancy, ethnicity, genetic information or any other protected categories under applicable federal, state or local laws. We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. A safe and secure environment is critical to Freddie Mac’s business. This includes employee commitment to our acceptable use policy, applying a vigilance-first approach to work, supporting regulatory mandates, and using best practices to protect Freddie Mac from potential threats and risk. Employees exercise this responsibility by executing against policies and procedures and adhering to privacy & security obligations as required via training programs. CA Applicants: Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Notice to External Search Firms: Freddie Mac partners with BountyJobs for contingency search business through outside firms. Resumes received outside the BountyJobs system will be considered unsolicited and Freddie Mac will not be obligated to pay a placement fee. If interested in learning more, please visit www.BountyJobs.com and register with our referral code: MAC. Time-type: Full time FLSA Status: Exempt Freddie Mac offers a comprehensive total rewards package to include competitive compensation and market-leading benefit programs. Information on these benefit programs is available on our Careers site. This position has an annualized market-based salary range of $92,000 – $138,000 and is eligible to participate in the annual incentive program. The final salary offered will generally fall within this range and is dependent on various factors including but not limited to the responsibilities of the position, experience, skill set, internal pay equity and other relevant qualifications of the applicant. item.title: Enterprise Communications Strategist III (Job# 119465BR)
item.description: Enterprise Communications Strategist III (Job# 119465BR) Organization: Edward Jones Location: Tempe, AZ | Washington, DC | Saint Louis, MO | New York, NY Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Position Schedule: Full-Time This job posting is anticipated to remain open for 30 days, from 29-Sep-2026. The posting may close early due to the volume of applicants. As an Enterprise Communications Specialist, Community Communications, you will lead communications strategy and execution to strengthen the firm’s market leadership across all generational spectrums of financial education and community impact. The person in this role must have experience working in highly complex, matrixed environments, providing strategic communications guidance that supports business objectives at the enterprise level while leading and strengthening community and financial education programs at the local and national level. This role will be responsible for working with a team to support the design and execution of communications strategies in support of the firm’s community relations programs, primarily focused on financial education, early savings/wealth building and retirement. This includes the development and leadership of the communications strategy and tactical implementation for initiatives at the local and national level, as well as larger enterprise-wide campaigns where community impact and financial education serve as a component. This individual will operate as a key cross-functional member of the firm’s External Communications and Public Relations department working closely with colleagues inside the department (Media Relations, Executive Visibility, Reputation Management), as well as across various functions across External Affairs and the enterprise including Home Office and Field Communications in support key firm initiatives and programs. In addition, this person will lead and/or support strategy that amplifies the division’s focus on its three strategic pillars: financial education, entrepreneurship, and caregiving. What You’ll Do: Lead and Support Strategic Execution – Lead and support execution of communications strategies in support of key programs and campaigns across the firm’s Financial Education pillar, and in support of Edward Jones’ 2030 strategy. External Stakeholder Engagement – Cultivate working relationships with key strategic partners, local and national media, influencers, non-profit and community leaders, and business stakeholders. Internal Stakeholder Engagement – Work cross-functionally, collaborate with and influence a vast network of internal peers and leaders across firm to ensure that the progress, impact, and value of the firm’s programs are amplified across key internal stakeholder groups. Events and convenings – Oversee the development and logistics of targeted events aimed at raising awareness and firm influence across key strategic pillars. Project Management – Lead communications strategy and its tactical implementation for programs at the local and national level with an ability to deliver under tight deadlines and within specified budgets. KPIs and Benchmarking – Develop clear and concise KPIs that showcase program value and return across various internal stakeholder groups. Establish benchmarks along with identify milestones that amplify progress over extended periods of time. Edward Jones’ compensation and benefits package includes medical and prescription drug, dental, vision, voluntary benefits (such as accident, hospital indemnity, and critical illness), short- and long-term disability, basic life, and basic AD&D coverage. Short- and long-term disability, basic life, and basic AD&D coverage are provided at no cost to associates. Edward Jones offers a 401k retirement plan, and tax-advantaged accounts: health savings account, and flexible spending account. Edward Jones observes ten paid holidays and provides 15 days of vacation for new associates beginning on January 1 of each year, as well as sick time, personal days, and a paid day for volunteerism. Associates may be eligible for bonuses and profit sharing. All associates are eligible for the firm’s Employee Assistance Program. For more information on the Benefits available to Edward Jones associates, please visit our benefits page. Hiring Minimum: $86300 Hiring Maximum: $146700 What Experience You Need: 7+ years of external and internal communications experience, with a background in corporate communications, public relations, community affairs, or related roles. Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant certification preferred. Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to craft clear, compelling, and audience-appropriate content across formats. Strong project management skills, with the ability to delegate effectively and align the right capabilities to deliver in a dynamic, matrixed environment. Proven track record of delivering results and communicating effectively across teams. Ability to establish and optimize project workflows, processes, and budgets. Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate, influence, and drive alignment across teams. Effective at engaging external stakeholders and influencers to build awareness and advance strategic narratives. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Teams), supporting high-quality content development, data analysis, and cross-team collaboration. Excellent interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills. **Candidates that live within a commutable distance from our Tempe, AZ and St. Louis, MO home office locations are expected to work in the office four days per week effective June 1, 2026. Before June 1, 2026, candidates that live within a commutable distance from our Tempe, AZ and St. Louis, MO home office locations are expected to work in the office three days per week, with preference for Tuesday through Thursday.** Join a financial services firm where your contributions are valued. Edward Jones is a Fortune 500¹ company where people come first. With over 9 million clients and 20,000 financial advisors across the U.S. and Canada, we’re proud to be privately-owned, placing the focus on our clients rather than shareholder returns. Behind everything we do is our purpose: We partner for positive impact to improve the lives of our clients and colleagues, and together, better our communities and society. We are an innovative, flexible, and inclusive organization that attracts, develops, and inspires performance excellence and a sense of belonging. People are at the center of our partnership. Edward Jones associates are seen, heard, respected, and supported. This is what we believe makes us the best place to start or build your career. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Copy Generalist – Communications Lead
item.description: Senior Copy Generalist – Communications Lead Organization: Deloitte Location: Rosslyn, VA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Position Summary Our Deloitte Customer team empowers organizations to build deeper relationships with customers through innovative strategies, advanced analytics, Generative AI, transformative technologies, and creative design. We can enhance customer experiences and drive sustained growth and customer value creation and capture, through customer and commercial strategies, digital products and innovation, marketing, commerce, sales, and service. We are a team of strategists, data scientists, operators, creatives, designers, engineers, and architects. Our team balances business strategy, technology, creativity, and ongoing managed services to solve the biggest problems that affect customers, partners, constituents, and the workforce. Work you’ll do As a Senior Copy Generalist on the Government & Public Services team, you will be responsible for: Developing strategic communications plans that align messaging, audience needs, program goals, and mission priorities Creating narrative frameworks, key messages, and executive-ready content for internal and external stakeholder audiences Advising leaders on crisis, issues, and reputational communications in time-sensitive or high-visibility situations Coordinating across government, legal, investigative, executive, and interagency stakeholders to align communications strategy and execution Translating complex operational information into clear recommendations, communication products, and performance-oriented reporting A successful candidate would possess these skills: Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team Effective written and verbal communication skills Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product Ability to build and sustain professional relationships Ability to lead projects or workstreams Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor Ability to meet deadlines Ability to provide clear guidance to others The Team Deloitte’s Government & Public Services (GPS) practice – our people, ideas, technology and outcomes – is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise. Our Advertising, Marketing, & Commerce offering designs and implements solutions that engage and activate customers through the customer journey. Qualifications Required: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Affairs, Public Policy, English, Marketing, Business, or similar 4+ years of experience in strategic communications, executive communications, public affairs, content strategy, or crisis communications 4+ years of experience supporting government, homeland security, law enforcement, justice, or public sector programs 1+ years of experience developing communication plans, message architecture, and audience-specific content for multiple stakeholder groups Active Secret clearance required Ability to travel 0-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future. Preferred: Master’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Affairs, Public Policy, English, Marketing, or Business Experience advising senior executives or program leadership on issues management and stakeholder communications Experience supporting crisis communications or reputational risk communications Experience translating operational, investigative, legal, or policy information into leadership-ready written deliverables Experience using performance measures or reporting to assess communications effectiveness The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,400 to $197,900. You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance. Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at [email protected] . Recruiting tips From developing a stand out resume to putting your best foot forward in the interview, we want you to feel prepared and confident as you explore opportunities at Deloitte. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte recruiters. Benefits At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you. item.title: Senior Public Policy Analyst – Medicaid (Hybrid)
item.description: Senior Public Policy Analyst – Medicaid (Hybrid) Organization: CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Resp & Qualifications PURPOSE: The Senior Public Policy Analyst monitors, evaluates, and provides recommendations on strategy and communications regarding federal and state public policy issues in support of the companys business priorities. The Senior Analyst is responsible for policy development on key issues, ensuring the Public Policy and Government Affairs (PPGA) team effectively communicates federal and state policy proposals and their specific impacts to the rest of the organization, as well as identifying issues for potential advocacy external to CareFirst. The incumbent will have primary responsibility for issues related to Medicaid. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Serving as policy subject matter expert on key legislative and regulatory developments impacting Medicaid and Medicaid managed care organizations. Providing internal education and policy briefings on government action and policy trends to assist in business decisions across the company. Conducting legislative, regulatory, and policy research and analysis. Developing external communications, written materials, and thought leadership to communicate CareFirsts policy perspective and advance meaningful discussion on pressing health policy issues (e.g., talking points, fact sheets, public comments, blog posts, subject matter expert panels). Providing guidance on external messaging on CareFirst initiatives. Conducting internal policy development on key issues to position CareFirst as a thought leader. Monitoring and participating in legislative, regulatory, and stakeholder bodies and workgroups. Building relationships with business leadership by providing clear executive-level presentations, regular check-in meetings, and rapid response policy analysis. Representing CareFirst on work groups at our trade and other external organizations. Conducting research for use in drafting position papers, written and verbal testimony for presentation before legislative and regulatory bodies, correspondence, and other responses for public policy and governmental affairs purposes and research leading to the development of corporate positions. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY: Position does not have direct reports but is expected to assist in guiding and mentoring less experienced staff. May lead a team of matrixed resources. QUALIFICATIONS: Education Level: Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science, Health Policy, Mathematics, Finance or related field OR in lieu of a Bachelor’s degree, an additional 4 years of relevant work experience is required in addition to the required work experience. Experience: 5 years experience in health care policy environment focused on policy and communication. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s Degree in Public Health, Health Policy, Health Administration or Related Field Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSAs) Knowledge of state legislative and regulatory processes, public policy analysis. In-depth understanding of healthcare payor industry and operational processes and impacts of regulatory guidance. Understanding of insurance products and regulatory environment. Proven analytical and problem-solving skills to evaluate business processes and recommend effective solutions. Experience in project management, business process analysis, workflow, and task analysis. Analytical skills and understanding of where to find information germane to mandates. Written and oral communications skills. Ability to work with all levels within the organization and to build highly cooperative and productive relationships. Ability to coordinate multiple public policy activities within a dynamic environment. Ability to communicate to diverse audiences through a variety of methods. Ability to work with senior management and with their full confidence. Ability to present complex ideas to create a clear picture of impacts to the organization. Ability to act on behalf of management in a manner that is consistent with divisional vision. Ability to act in consultative manner to project teams charged with operationalizing mandates. PC skills, including Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Must be able to meet established deadlines and handle multiple customer service demands from internal and external customers, within set expectations for service excellence. item.description: Director, U.S. Public Policy Organization: Boehringer Ingelheim Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Description The Director of US Public Policy will lead the development and execution of enterprise-wide public policy strategies that advance Boehringer Ingelheim’s priorities related to patient access and affordability, drug pricing, and innovation policy. The incumbent will serve as a strategic advisor to Public & Government Affairs leadership and key business partners regarding the impact of legislative, regulatory, and policy developments on company objectives. Additionally, this role Identifies risks and opportunities in the evolving healthcare policy landscape and develop strategies to shape public policy outcomes that support patient access to innovative medicines and long-term business success. The incumbent will represent Boehringer Ingelheim with external stakeholders, industry associations, and coalition partners to advance company priorities and strengthen the organization’s reputation as a trusted healthcare partner. As an employee of Boehringer Ingelheim, you will actively contribute to the discovery, development, and delivery of our products to our patients and customers. Our global presence provides an opportunity for all employees to collaborate internationally, offering visibility and the opportunity to directly contribute to the company’s success. We realize that our strength and competitive advantage lie with our people. We support our employees in several ways to foster a healthy working environment, meaningful work, mobility, networking, and work-life balance. Our competitive compensation and benefit programs reflect Boehringer Ingelheim’s high regard for our employees. Compensation Data The base salary range for this position is $230,400 to $345,600. The position may be eligible for a role-specific discretionary bonus, relocation assistance, and/or other compensation elements. We continuously review market data and may adjust salary ranges as needed in the future. Actual compensation will be based on job-related factors such as skills, experience, qualifications, and other factors permitted by law. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement savings opportunities, paid time off, paid holidays, disability and life insurance benefits, and other company-sponsored benefits. Duties & Responsibilities Lead development and execution of enterprise public policy strategies supporting patient access and affordability, medical innovation, and pharmaceutical policy objectives. Serve as a strategic partner to PGA leadership and cross-functional business partners regarding the impact of legislative, regulatory, and policy developments. Monitor and evaluate emerging federal and state policy developments and identify risks, opportunities, and trends impacting Boehringer’s business and portfolio. Develop and maintain company policy positions related to relevant pharmaceutical and other key healthcare issues. Support the design and implementation of advocacy strategies with policymakers, regulatory agencies, trade associations, and other stakeholders to advance company priorities. Represent Boehringer in industry trade associations, coalitions, policy forums, and stakeholder engagements to influence public policy outcomes. Lead and coordinate cross-functional teams focused on strategic policy initiatives and enterprise objectives. Develop policy briefs, executive presentations, position papers, issue analyses, and other strategic communications for senior leadership and stakeholders. Requirements Bachelor’s Degree required. Advanced Degree preferred (JD, MPH, MPP, MPA, MBA, PhD, or equivalent) Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in public policy, government affairs, healthcare policy, market access, consulting, trade associations, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, or government sectors Demonstrated expertise in U.S. healthcare policy, including Medicare, Medicaid, reimbursement, coverage, drug pricing, healthcare reform, and 340B policy issues Proven experience developing and executing policy strategies that influence legislative, regulatory, or stakeholder outcomes Demonstrated ability to serve as a strategic advisor to senior leadership and influence decision-making in a matrixed organization Strong understanding of the healthcare ecosystem and policy implications for biopharmaceutical innovation and patient access Exceptional analytical, strategic thinking, written, verbal, and presentation skills; Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with policymakers, industry organizations, patient groups, and other external stakeholders Strong leadership, collaboration, and project management skills, including the ability to lead cross-functional teams and manage multiple priorities simultaneously Demonstrated sound judgment, executive presence, integrity, discretion, and accountability Eligibility Requirements: Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without restriction. Must be willing to take a drug test and post-offer physical (if required). Must be 18 years of age or older. Our Company Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry’s top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,300 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com. Why Boehringer Ingelheim? With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths – and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better. Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed. Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after – as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you’ll be helping to transform lives for generations. Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/us/careers Explore our total rewards here: Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/us/careers/benefits-rewards All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to a person’s actual or perceived race, including natural hairstyles, hair texture and protective hairstyles; color; creed; religion; national origin; age; ancestry; citizenship status; marital status; sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical condition); gender identity or gender expression (including transgender status); sexual orientation; disability; protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law; military service and veteran status; genetic information (including the refusal to submit to genetic testing); or any other class or characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws and ordinances. item.title: Director, Employee & Executive Communications
item.description: Director, Employee & Executive Communications Organization: BAE Systems Inc, HQ Location: Falls Church, VA Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Job Description BAE Systems, Inc. is looking for an experienced and dynamic professional to join us as the Director of Employee and Executive Communications. In this role, you’ll shape and drive communication strategies that connect our mission, values, and business objectives. You will serve as a strategic communications partner to our core corporate functions, including Human Resources, IT, Supply Chain, Legal, Finance, and Government Relations. Working closely with senior leadership, you will craft craft clear, authentic messaging that strengthens engagement and drives alignment across the organization. This position reports to the Senior Director of People Communications & Content. If you’re someone who can lead with purpose, think strategically, and thrive on collaboration, we’d love to hear from you! Key Responsibilities Strategic Function Partnership Develop and deliver tailored communication strategies for key corporate functions, with a focus on Human Resources, IT, Supply Chain, Legal, Finance, and Government Relations. Shape each strategy around the distinct goals, audiences, and priorities of the functions you support. Act as a trusted advisor to functional leaders, translating complex initiatives into clear, compelling messages that resonate with employees at every level. Anticipate communication needs early, addressing potential challenges before they surface to keep the organization informed and aligned. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner across BAE Systems, Inc. functions and segments to ensure consistent, streamlined messaging that reflects our shared priorities. Build strong, collaborative relationships with teams across the company, serving as the connective tissue that keeps communication cohesive and coordinated. Strategic Messaging and Planning Create clear, consistent, and impactful communications that support key initiatives, functional goals, and leadership priorities. Plan and execute communications for campaigns, events, and organizational changes. Use data and insights to refine channels, engage stakeholders, and deliver measurable results. Executive Communications Craft and deliver powerful messaging for executive leaders that aligns with company goals and reflects our values. Partner with executives to connect authentically with their audiences, both inside and outside the organization. Required Education, Experience, & Skills At least 12 years of experience and a Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing or similar field or 8 years with an advanced degree in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing or similar field. Proven experience in corporate communications, specifically in employee engagement and executive messaging. Exceptional writing, editing, and public speaking skills with the ability to craft clear, compelling messages for varied audiences. Strong people leadership skills and experience with a demonstrated ability to manage high-impact projects and cross-functional teams. Ability to think strategically, balancing long-term vision with day-to-day execution. Adept at working in a fast-paced environment while maintaining a collaborative, professional approach. Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills Measurement and insights expertise. AP style guru. Experience in HR- or IT-related communications and event support. Previous experience in the aerospace, defense, or technology industries. Advanced degree in Communications, Public Relations, or a related field. Pay Information Full-Time Salary Range: $138267 – $235053 Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience. Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics. About BAE Systems, Inc. BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support. Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn’t a tagline here. It’s what drives us. We’re developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you’re not just building a career. You’re contributing to a mission that truly matters. This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. A bridge builder, capable of fostering relationships with, and authentically advocating for the interests of, an ideologically diverse set of clients. A strong leader with a growth and innovation mindset. By passion or by habit, you are fully engrossed in the federal policy environment. WHAT YOU’LL DO Research, Policy and Client Account Support Work with client leads to develop short-and-long-term strategy around key client priorities. Provide policy support. Identify industries or clients in need of engagement (i.e. – higher education) based on current political or policy environment. Manage and delegate the Research Team’s hearing coverage and completion of internal and client legislative, public policy, and political research deliverables. Supervise & mentor research team and junior staff. Marketing & Business Development Partner with the marketing team to cultivate leadership opportunities and business development opportunities for the GR team. Collaborate across internal functions to prepare memos, decks, coordinate background research, etc. in support of new business opportunities. Develop new deliverables and add-ons for clients on both sides of the business– both for new clients in the “pitch” or business development stage, and for existing clients. Represent Avoq at conferences/events. Liaise with outside counsel to ensure strict adherence to ethical standards, compliance with laws and regulations, and other required filings Maintain familiarity with and knowledge of issues important to GR clients, GR team members, and Avoq overall Requirements YOUR EXPERIENCE As a qualified candidate, you have experience in all areas below: 5-7 years of administrative/executive support/operations management experience, preferably including experience on the Hill, Lobbying or a professional services including in a government relations/public affairs setting Strong communication skills Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment, with limited supervision, while keeping a professional demeanor Strong skills with Microsoft Office (Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) Ability to manage multiple projects and deliverables simultaneously Exceptional attention to detail A positive, professional and “can-do” attitude, as well as being flexible and adaptive to a changing environment Candidates need not possess every attribute listed above to qualify for a role. item.title: Director, Corporate Communication
item.description: Director, Corporate Communication Organization: UVA Health Medical Center Location: Charlottesville, VA Date Posted: 10/08/2026 At UVA Health University Medical Center, communications is a strategic driver of reputation, influence, and organizational impact. We are seeking an accomplished Director of Corporate Communications to lead enterprise-wide communications initiatives that elevate our brand, strengthen executive thought leadership, and increase visibility for one of the nation’s premier academic health systems. This high-profile leadership role serves as a trusted advisor to senior executives and key stakeholders across UVA Health, the UVA School of Medicine, and the Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology. Through strategic storytelling, proactive media engagement, and executive communications, the Director will help shape how UVA Health’s mission, innovation, and clinical excellence are shared with audiences locally, regionally, and nationally. The Role As Director of Corporate Communications, you will lead a broad communications portfolio spanning media relations and executive communications. This role is ideal for a seasoned communications leader who thrives in a dynamic, mission-driven environment and is energized by influencing organizational reputation at both regional and national levels. On a typical day, you may be partnering with executives to develop keynote speaker engagements and remarks, collaborating with media professionals on emerging stories, guiding strategic communications plans for major organizational initiatives, and coaching a growing team of communications experts. Key responsibilities include: Lead the development and execution of enterprise communications strategies that strengthen UVA Health’s brand, reputation, and stakeholder engagement. Serve as a strategic communications advisor to senior executives, helping articulate vision, priorities, and organizational impact through compelling messaging and thought leadership. Direct proactive media relations efforts focused on increasing regional and national visibility for UVA Health, the School of Medicine, and the Manning Institute. Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with journalists, media outlets, and external communications partners. Develop high-impact content across print, digital, video, presentation, and live-event channels. Guide crisis and issues communications while ensuring alignment with institutional priorities. Lead and mentor a growing communications team currently consisting of four direct reports. Partner closely with leaders across marketing, operations, clinical services, legal, finance, academic medicine, and community health initiatives. Measure communications effectiveness and provide strategic insights that inform leadership decision-making. This position follows a hybrid work model, with regular in-person collaboration in Charlottesville, typically on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Why UVA Health UVA Health is one of the nation’s premier academic health systems, bringing together patient care, education, and research to improve health outcomes across Virginia and beyond. This role offers the opportunity to influence communications strategy at an organization known for innovation, clinical excellence, and groundbreaking research. What makes this opportunity exceptional: Direct access to executive leadership, serving as a trusted advisor on high-profile communications initiatives. A unique opportunity to build proactive public relations and executive thought leadership programs that shape organizational reputation at a national level. Leadership of an expanding communications team with significant opportunity to develop talent and scale capabilities. Collaboration across one of the most respected academic medicine environments in the country, where innovation and discovery are transforming the future of healthcare. Access to leading physicians, researchers, operational leaders, and educators whose work presents powerful opportunities for storytelling and brand elevation. A culture that values collaboration, inclusion, innovation, and continuous improvement. For communications professionals seeking a role that combines executive influence, strategic leadership, media engagement, and meaningful organizational impact, this position offers an outstanding career-defining opportunity. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: Education: Bachelor’s degree required. Experience: 8+ years relevant professional experience, to include 3+ years of formal managerial experience required. Licensure: None. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: This is primarily a sedentary job involving extensive use of desktop computers. The job does occasionally require traveling some distance to attend meetings, and programs. The pay range for this role is $109,147.00 – $218,293.00 annually. Individual compensation will be determined by the selected candidate’s qualifications, previous work experience, and/or education. Benefits Comprehensive Benefits Package: Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Generous Paid Time Off Retirement Savings Long-term and Short-term Disability Health Saving Plans, and Flexible Spending Accounts Certification and Education Support UVA Health is a world-class Magnet Recognized academic medical center and health system with a level 1 trauma center. 2023-2024 U.S. News & World Report “Best Hospitals” guide rates UVA Health University Medical Center as “High Performing” in 5 adult specialties and 14 conditions/procedures. We are one of 70 National Cancer Institute designated cancer centers. UVA Health Children’s is named by 2023-2024 U.S. News & World Report as the best children’s hospital in Virginia with 9 specialties ranked among the best in the nation. Our footprint also encompasses 3 community hospitals and an integrated network of primary and specialty care clinics throughout Charlottesville, Culpeper, Northern Virginia, and beyond. The University of Virginia is an equal opportunity employer. All interested persons are encouraged to apply, including veterans and individuals with disabilities. Learn more about UVA’s commitment to non-discrimination and equal opportunity employment. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Associate General Counsel Organization: US Chamber of Commerce Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 About Us: If you are passionate about the ability of American business to improve lives, solve problems, and strengthen society, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce is the place for you. As the world’s largest business organization, we believe in building a future that gives everyone the opportunity to pursue a better tomorrow. We make it our job today–and every day–to build the strongest relationships possible among the American people, business leaders, and elected officials in Washington, D.C., state capitals, and countries around the globe. For them and the businesses we represent, the U.S. Chamber is a trusted advocate and partner. We are driven by the pursuit of innovation and partnership and hold ourselves to the highest standards. Our commitment to our members is matched only by our commitment to our employees. As part of our team, we will support your long-term career development while delivering relevant learning opportunities. We will empower you to lead, develop deep expertise, and find new approaches to solving the toughest challenges. Position Overview: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce is seeking an attorney to serve as the primary in-house counsel for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation, the 501(c)(3) public charitable organization affiliate of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. This position is housed within the U.S. Chamber’s Office of the General Counsel and reports directly to the general counsel of the U.S. Chamber and the U.S. Chamber Foundation. The Foundation is in a high-growth period in which exciting new programs are emerging, and it is looking for an attorney to serve as a partner in this period of growth. Responsibilities: Advise regarding the laws applicable to tax-exempt organizations. Review the Foundation’s contracts, including grant agreements, technology contracts, event contracts, and consulting agreements. Inform the Foundation on new program developments, legal structure for strategic partnerships, grants fundraising, and sponsorships. Help staff strategically plan programs and agreements to ensure compliance with all applicable law. Advise on qualified sponsorships, UBTI, charitable activities, educational activities, grantmaking, Form 990 reporting, structuring and managing relationships with affiliated entities, lobbying activities, and other tax matters. Work on charitable solicitation registration and related issues. Function as an integral part of a friendly, collaborative in-house legal team. Work closely with other operational departments such as Finance, Human Resources, and Information Technology. Work with the Office of General Counsel’s other lawyers to provide assistance on specific projects and take on a portfolio of work that supports the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, not just the Foundation. Qualifications: Experienced attorney with 6+ years’ legal experience working with tax-exempt organizations, preferably with a strong background in analyzing and negotiating contracts and grants. Juris Doctor with strong academic performance during law school. Membership in good standing in, or eligibility to waive into, the District of Columbia Bar. Strong business sense. Demonstrated commitment to client service. Ability to oversee the work of outside counsel. Exceptional legal research and analytical skills. Outstanding verbal and written communication skills. Intellectual curiosity and resourcefulness. Ability to work independently. Ability to manage multiple matters for multiple stakeholders and set and adjust priorities. Sound judgment. Able to collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders. Previous law firm experience is a plus. Previous in-house legal experience is a plus. The salary range for this position is $240,000.00 to $250,000.00. The actual salary paid for this position will vary based on market data, an applicant’s qualifications, relevant degrees, certifications, and other factors. Our full-time employees are eligible for benefits, including health care, vision, dental, retirement, and paid leave. item.title: Senior Director, Retirement Policy
item.description: Senior Director, Retirement Policy Organization: US Chamber of Commerce Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 About Us: If you are passionate about the ability of American business to improve lives, solve problems, and strengthen society, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce is the place for you. As the world’s largest business organization, we believe in building a future that gives everyone the opportunity to pursue a better tomorrow. We make it our job today–and every day–to build the strongest relationships possible among the American people, business leaders, and elected officials in Washington, D.C., state capitals, and countries around the globe. For them and the businesses we represent, the U.S. Chamber is a trusted advocate and partner. We are driven by the pursuit of innovation and partnership and hold ourselves to the highest standards. Our commitment to our members is matched only by our commitment to our employees. As part of our team, we will support your long-term career development while delivering relevant learning opportunities. We will empower you to lead, develop deep expertise, and find new approaches to solving the toughest challenges. Position Overview: Manage all aspects of retirement policy for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, including savings, defined benefit and defined contribution plans, other investment plans, administration of Trump accounts, ERISA litigation, fiduciary duties, investments, and corresponding disclosures. Oversee comments for pending regulations, work with the administration on guidance and other regulatory and subregulatory items, and lobby Congress on legislation and other Chamber priorities. Responsibilities: Represent the Chamber nationally on retirement policy, including before Congress, with the administration, with the media, and on several national coalition steering committees. Meet with members of Congress, the administration, and regulatory agencies (e.g., SEC, DOL, Treasury) to promote the Chamber’s retirement policy agenda. Manage Chamber retirement committees and work with members as well as internal stakeholders to formulate policy positions and advocacy strategies. Work with the Chamber’s lobbying team and internal stakeholders. Work with Chamber members to draft comments to proposed agency rulemakings. Work with the administration on subregulatory guidance. Create, develop, and implement programming for relevant Chamber retirement security summits, events, and conferences. Draft reports, one-pagers, op-eds, and blogs promoting the Chamber’s retirement policy agenda. Monitor state developments in the retirement field, particularly regarding ERISA preemption. Work with the Chamber Litigation Center on legal challenges to particular policies where appropriate. Qualifications: 5+ years of policy work in relevant areas. Association and government (congressional or administrative) experience is ideal; law firm or company experience is also relevant. Detailed knowledge of retirement issues. Experience with ERISA. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Proven program management, strong organization, and time management. Knowledge of the legislative and rulemaking process. Sound judgment and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of personnel. Able to multitask in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment with minimal supervision. Team player with the flexibility to work long hours. The salary range for this position is $134,475.00 to $173,000.00. The actual salary paid for this position will vary based on market data, an applicant’s qualifications, relevant degrees, certifications, and other factors. Our full-time employees are eligible for benefits, including health care, vision, dental, retirement, and paid leave. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. #LI-Hybrid Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council!
