item.title: Senior Director Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Director Government Affairs Organization: Aramark Location: Washington, DC | Philadelphia, PA Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Job Description The Senior Director, Government Affairs will coordinate Aramark’s engagement with federal, state and local governments across all of our operating markets and lines of business. Aramark engages with all levels of government on a variety of issues affecting all 11 US lines of business. We seek and hold significant contracts with the federal government and many state and local governments, and we also operate businesses that are regulated by all levels of government. This role sits at the center of how we protect and grow our business; monitoring policy, influencing legislation, and ensuring the right relationships are in place before decisions get made that affect our people, our contracts, and our operations. This is a high-visibility position that requires a deep understanding of government operations, policy formulation, and legislative processes. The right person has done this before at scale; in a large, complex organization. And brings the network, instincts, and credibility to represent Aramark effectively at the federal, state, and local levels. Supporting internal stakeholders and collaborating across functions and lines of business will be a crucial aspect of this job. Aramark has hundreds of government touchpoints and dozens of employees who directly engage with government in some capacity. The successful candidate will be able to quickly map this network, collaborate across functions and lines of business, and help set and drive a cohesive government affairs strategy that addresses the needs of disparate stakeholders. Key focus areas include stakeholder and policy engagement representing Aramark with government leaders and agencies while monitoring and advocating on legislation that affects our business and overseeing the work of outside government relations professionals, executive advising, ensuring leadership is informed and prepared to navigate the political and regulatory environment with confidence and clarity. Job Responsibilities Develop and support Aramark’s federal, state and local government affairs strategy, including direct lobbying and oversight of external lobbyists and consultants in priority markets. Build strong relationships with stakeholders and colleagues with a role in Aramark’s government relationships across our lines of business and corporate functions. Monitor legislation and regulatory activity across our operating markets; flagging risks early, identifying opportunities, and developing responses that protect the business. Represent Aramark with key government leaders, agencies, third-party groups, and industry associations; maintaining a visible and credible presence in the markets that matter most. Develop and maintain trusted relationships with governors, state legislators, city and county officials, and regulatory agency leaders across party lines and geographies. Partner with HR and Legal on labor and workforce policy issues and represent Aramark’s position in legislative settings. Support growth by assessing the government affairs landscape in target markets, identifying incentive opportunities, and navigating licensing, permitting, and zoning for new and existing locations. Counsel senior leadership on political and regulatory matters, translating complex policy issues into clear, actionable guidance that supports business decision-making. Ensure all lobbying and political activity fully complies with applicable registration, disclosure, ethics, and reporting requirements. Qualifications Required Experience 5-10 years of experience in government affairs, public affairs, or legislative/regulatory affairs with meaningful time at a large, complex organization. Significant federal lobbying experience Hands-on experience managing state and/or local lobbying across multiple jurisdictions. A proven relationship-builder with elected officials, government staff, and regulators. Ability to connect the dots between external policy activity and internal business operations; understanding what legislative changes mean for a company like Aramark. Strong communicator; written, verbal, and in the room. Able and willing to travel 60-70% of the time. Preferred Experience Experience in hospitality, food service, facilities management, or another large-scale service business. A J.D. or background in labor, employment, or regulatory law. Prior experience inside federal, state or local government. Existing network of external government affairs professionals across states and municipalities. Location Washington, DC or Philadelphia, PA Benefits COMPENSATION: The hourly rate or salary range for this position is $150,000 to $200,000. If both numbers are the same, that is the amount that Aramark expects to offer. This is Aramark’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation for this position as of the time of posting. BENEFITS: Aramark offers comprehensive benefit programs and services for eligible employees including medical, dental, vision, and work/life resources. Additional benefits may include retirement savings plans like 401(k) and paid days off such as parental leave and disability coverage. Benefits vary by location and are subject to any legal requirements or limitations, employee eligibility status, and where the employee lives and/or works. For more information about Aramark benefits, click here Aramark Careers – Benefits & Compensation. There is no predetermined application window for this position, the position will close once a qualified candidate is selected. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable law, including, but not limited to, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, the California Fair Chance Act, and the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance to the extent that those laws apply to the opportunity. About Aramark Our Mission Rooted in service and united by our purpose, we strive to do great things for each other, our partners, our communities, and our planet. At Aramark, we believe that every employee should enjoy equal employment opportunity and be free to participate in all aspects of the company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, pregnancy, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, military status, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by applicable law. About Aramark The people of Aramark proudly serve millions of guests every day through food and facilities in 15 countries around the world. Rooted in service and united by our purpose, we strive to do great things for each other, our partners, our communities, and our planet. We believe a career should develop your talents, fuel your passions, and empower your professional growth. So, no matter what you’re pursuing – a new challenge, a sense of belonging, or just a great place to work – our focus is helping you reach your full potential. Learn more about working here at http://www.aramarkcareers.com or connect with us on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Vice President – US Policy Campaigns
item.description: Associate Vice President – US Policy Campaigns Organization: Eli Lilly & Co. Location: Washington, DC | Remote (IN) Date Posted: 10/08/2026 At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. Position Overview: As a Global Public Policy Leader with a focus on US policy, you will report to the VP, Head of US Policy and play a pivotal role in advancing policy priorities at the federal and state levels. You will oversee the development and execution of campaigns that enable Lilly to meet its policy goals and mitigate threats before they materialize. You will be action-oriented and outcomes-focused, with a primary responsibility for executing comprehensive policy campaigns to eliminate barriers in the external environment and improve the ecosystem in support of enterprise-wide policy priorities – working in close partnership with colleagues in Government Affairs, business units, and Lilly USA to advance the goals of the US Policy team. This position requires a keen understanding of US political dynamics, regulatory frameworks, communications, advocacy and a strategic mindset to drive business growth while ensuring compliance with local laws and regulations. At a high level, you will: Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships to support policy campaigns that advance US policy priorities. Identify opportunities to harness stakeholder engagement to create momentum for policymaker action in priority areas, such as price control mitigation, PBM reform, prevention policy and other areas as assigned. Execute plans to amplify key policy arguments and critical resources (e.g., white papers, advocacy briefs) with external stakeholders. Coordinate with business unit (therapeutic area) and Government Affairs teams to ensure alignment on activities that advance preferred policy outcomes in the US. Support the Head of US Policy by partnering with subject matter experts on the team to develop coordinated policy-shaping plans across a defined set of enterprise-wide policy goals. Key Responsibilities: Identifying Policy Shaping Opportunities: Drive outcomes by developing and deploying the full array of tools, resources, analytics, and strategic partnerships. Influence development and oversee execution of comprehensive policy campaigns to drive progress on preferred policy outcomes. Develop cohesive policy narratives that make the case for redressing harms of emerging policy threats. Leverage strategic-thinking to develop tactics to create public support for policy change Other projects and emerging topics, as assigned. Communication and Stakeholder Engagement: Engage with internal and external stakeholders to build consensus around strategic actions and advocacy initiatives to create regulatory, legislative, or political momentum for desired policy changes. Lead and direct external consultants to support an integrated and strategic-minded approach to drive change within the policy ecosystem. Build support for the value of prescription drugs and efforts to rebuild public trust in science. Create action with internal stakeholders (Government Affairs, Communications, Legal, Business Units, Lilly USA) by incorporating feedback into strategic plans to advance policy goals. Coordinate with business unit (therapeutic area) corporate affairs teams to ensure alignment between short term and longer-term policy objectives and policy shaping efforts. Strategic Partnerships: Develop, influence, and direct diverse, multi-stakeholder coalitions that can articulate harms of policy threats and drive support for policy alternatives. Leverage external relationships to gain insights into emerging issues, regulatory / legislative trends, and political risks that may impact the organization’s business operations. Required Skills and Qualifications: 7+ years experience with Master’s degree (or Bachelor’s with 10+ years experience) in biopharmaceutical industry, trade association, government, stakeholder organization, academic think-tank, or payer organization preferred. Demonstrated innovator and self-starter with the ability to create action through relationship-building and by working collaboratively across functional teams to drive consensus. Ability to handle multiple priorities in a dynamic and evolving environment. Excellent oral presentation skills with a demonstrated ability to present complex information accurately and concisely. Strong organization skills and meticulous attention to detail. In-depth knowledge of political and regulatory environments. Proven track record of successful relationship-building efforts with industry associations and other stakeholders. Designed and delivered integrated public affairs strategies for various clients and projects. Strong strategic thinking capabilities, with the ability to anticipate and respond effectively to emerging challenges and opportunities. Additional Information: Location: Washington, DC, but remote will be considered. Travel Percentage: 15%-30% Lilly is dedicated to helping individuals with disabilities to actively engage in the workforce, ensuring equal opportunities when vying for positions. If you require accommodation to submit a resume for a position at Lilly, please complete the accommodation request form (https://careers.lilly.com/us/en/workplace-accommodation) for further assistance. Please note this is for individuals to request an accommodation as part of the application process and any other correspondence will not receive a response. Lilly is proud to be an EEO Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. Our employee resource groups (ERGs) offer strong support networks for their members and are open to all employees. Our current groups include: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia (AMECA), Black Employees at Lilly (BE@Lilly), Chinese Culture Network (CCN), EnAble, Evolve, Lilly Indian Network (LIN), Organization of Latinx at Lilly (OLA), Pride (LGBTQ+ Allies), Veterans Leadership Network (VLN) and Women’s Initiative for Leading at Lilly (WILL). Actual compensation will depend on a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. The anticipated wage for this position is $253,500 – $371,800 Full-time equivalent employees also will be eligible for a company bonus (depending, in part, on company and individual performance). In addition, Lilly offers a comprehensive benefit program to eligible employees, including eligibility to participate in a company-sponsored 401(k); pension; vacation benefits; eligibility for medical, dental, vision and prescription drug benefits; flexible benefits (e.g., healthcare and/or dependent day care flexible spending accounts); life insurance and death benefits; certain time off and leave of absence benefits; and well-being benefits (e.g., employee assistance program, fitness benefits, and employee clubs and activities).Lilly reserves the right to amend, modify, or terminate its compensation and benefit programs in its sole discretion and Lilly’s compensation practices and guidelines will apply regarding the details of any promotion or transfer of Lilly employees. #WeAreLilly Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Vice President for Government Relations
item.description: Vice President for Government Relations Organization: Montgomery College Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Job Description Vice President for Government Relations At Montgomery College, our students pursue their goals, transform their futures, and contribute to the vitality of Montgomery County and beyond. We believe higher education changes lives, strengthens communities, and fuels economic mobility. Our College serves a diverse and talented student population through academic excellence, workforce development, innovation, and community engagement. Our mission is rooted in being a place where students discover their passions and unlock their potential to transform lives, enrich the community, and change the world. We are committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive environment where every student can thrive. Through dedicated faculty and staff, strategic partnerships, public investment, and thoughtful advocacy, Montgomery College is committed to enhancing access, completion, and post-completion success with a focus that is student-centered, data-informed, and equity-minded. To help achieve these aspirations, we seek an experienced and strategic Vice President for Government Relations who will lead the College’s legislative, policy, and advocacy efforts at the local, state, and federal levels. This is a unique opportunity to influence public policy, strengthen strategic partnerships, and advance the priorities of one of the nation’s leading community colleges. Reporting directly to the President, the Vice President for Government Relations serves as a trusted advisor and thought partner, helping to position Montgomery College for continued success through effective government relations, coalition building, and advocacy. Position Overview The Vice President for Government Relations provides executive leadership for the Office of Government Relations and serves as the College’s chief advocate on governmental, legislative, and policy matters. The Vice President develops and executes a comprehensive government relations strategy that advances the College’s mission, Strategic Plan, and Transformational Aspirations. Working closely with the President, senior leaders, elected officials, government agencies, business leaders, community partners, and other entities, the Vice President builds strong relationships that support the College’s legislative priorities, public funding priorities, and long-term institutional success. Key Responsibilities The Vice President for Government Relations will: Serve as the President’s strategic advisor on governmental, legislative, policy, and political matters affecting the College. In consultation with the President, develop and execute a comprehensive federal, state, and local government relations strategy, including annual advocacy goals, aligned with institutional priorities. Translate institutional priorities into a focused legislative, policy, and budget agenda and lead efforts to advance that agenda. Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative, regulatory, fiscal, and political developments impacting higher education and the College and provide timely advice and recommended actions to the President and senior leadership. Build and maintain productive relationships with elected officials, government agencies, policymakers, business leaders, community organizations, and education partners. Represent Montgomery College before local, state, and federal entities and at professional associations and community organizations. Develop coalitions and partnerships that advance shared higher education priorities. Work closely with the President’s Office and senior leadership to ensure coordination of government relations activities, elected official engagement, and matters requiring the President’s attention. Coordinate testimony, advocacy materials, remarks, talking points, and strategic communications on behalf of College leadership. Collaborate with Marketing and Communications to develop annual advocacy and government relations communication strategies. Support and coordinate appropriate advocacy engagement among trustees, alumni, students, faculty, staff, board leadership, and community partners. Ensure coordinated institutional responses to requests, inquiries, visits, meetings, and engagement opportunities involving elected officials and government stakeholders. Provide strategic leadership, direction, and development for Government Relations staff, ensuring alignment with institutional priorities and advocacy objectives. Maintain an effective approach to tracking government relations activities, outcomes, and follow-up to support coordination, accountability, and alignment with College priorities. Perform other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications: Master’s degree or other advanced degree in public administration, public policy, law, political science, government, education policy, or a related field. A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in government relations, government affairs, public policy, higher education, advocacy, external affairs, coalition building, or a related field. Experience supervising staff, developing organizational strategy, managing complex stakeholder relationships, and advancing institutional priorities. Demonstrated experience developing relationships with senior leaders, elected officials, policymakers, and external stakeholders. Proven record of advancing organizational, legislative, policy, or public funding priorities. Leadership Competencies Strategic problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to navigate complex and high-impact challenges. Independent judgment and initiative to advance priorities, drive results, and advance institutional goals with broad executive guidance. Strong communication, relationship-building, and collaboration skills with diverse internal and external stakeholders. Deep understanding of government relations, public policy, higher education, legislative processes, and fiscal matters. A commitment to inclusivity, equity, and servant leadership, with the ability to build consensus, foster engagement, and create an environment where all individuals can contribute and succeed. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with state government. Demonstrated success in coalition building and advocacy within higher education. Experience navigating legislative, policy, and fiscal processes affecting public higher education institutions. Hiring Range: $135,044 – $185,671 annually. Initial salary placement for new hires falls between the minimum and midpoint of the range and is based on relevant candidate experience and internal equity. The maximum salary for this position is $236,298 annually. According to the College’s policy and search committee affirmation, all information from and about candidates will be kept in strict confidence. To apply, please click on Vice-President for Government Relations The position will remain open until filled. Best consideration date for online applications is Friday, October 16, 2026. To be considered, applications must consist of the following: A resume/curriculum vitae (CV). A cover letter is required. For degrees earned outside of the U.S., a copy of your education equivalency, conducted by a nationally recognized evaluation service, must be included in your application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Please ensure that all employment dates are included in your application materials. For degrees earned outside of the U.S., a copy of your education equivalency, conducted by a nationally recognized evaluation service, must be included in your application. As a condition of employment, the following are required at the time of hire: Successful completion of a background check and degree verification (if applicable). Participation in a Maryland State Retirement System plan (Pension or Optional Retirement Plan, depending on the position). If you are already retired from the Maryland State Retirement System, you may not enroll in a Maryland State Retirement System plan at Montgomery College and may have earn​ings restrictions, per state law. Our benefits package includes: generous paid vacation, sick, paid holidays, medical, dental, vision, group legal benefits, professional development, retirement plan, educational assistance, tuition waiver for employee and dependents, wellness programming including onsite gyms, pools and classes. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact Human Resources and Strategic Talent Management at 240-567-5353 or [email protected] . We require at least two weeks advance notice to enable us to provide the requested accommodation. Montgomery College is an equal opportunity employer committed to promoting and fostering diversity among its student body, faculty, and staff. Montgomery College is a tobacco-free and smoke-free workplace. Closing Date Open Until Filled Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President Government Affairs
item.description: Vice President Government Affairs Organization: Charles River Laboratories Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 For 75 years, Charles River employees have worked together to assist in the discovery, development and safe manufacture of new drug therapies. When you join our family, you will have a significant impact on the health and well-being of people across the globe. Whether your background is in life sciences, finance, IT, sales or another area, your skills will play an important role in the work we perform. In return, we’ll help you build a career that you can feel passionate about. Job Overview BASIC SUMMARY: The Vice President of Government Affairs will serve as a key advocate for the Charles River’s interests before federal policymakers, with a primary focus on drug development issues. This individual will develop and execute global education and advocacy strategies, engage with congressional offices and federal agencies, manage third-party lobbyists, and help shape policy outcomes that support the Charles River’s strategic objectives. The role requires strong policy acumen, exceptional relationship‑building abilities, and the capacity to translate complex business issues into clear and compelling public‑policy positions. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in a fast‑paced, highly collaborative environment and brings deep experience working within the federal legislative and regulatory landscape. The ideal candidate will blend visionary leadership with a hands-on approach to advance the organization’s mission and shape critical legislative outcomes. Job Description ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Duty % of Time Spent (no less than 10%) Strategic Policy Development & Vision: Design and execute comprehensive global government strategies that align with the organization’s purpose and goals. Assess the impact of legislative or regulatory proposals, and establish short- and long-term policy priorities. Lead direct advocacy efforts with congressional staff, elected officials, and federal regulators on issues impacting Charles River 25% Stakeholder Engagement & Coalition Building: Cultivate and maintain strategic relationships with key global government officials, lawmakers, industry partners, and advocacy groups. Build and lead high-impact coalitions to amplify the organization’s voice and drive consensus on critical policy issues. Monitors the legislative and regulatory environment and communicates developments to Charles RIver stakeholders 20% Advocacy & Government Relations: Direct third-party lobbying activities and grassroots advocacy and education efforts to advance or oppose specific legislation and regulations. Prepare compelling testimony, policy briefs, and advocacy campaigns designed to influence policymakers and key regulatory bodies. 20% Board Communication & Organizational Leadership: Serve as the primary subject matter expert on all federal issues and support the Chief Legal Officer and Chief Communications Officer in their support of, and education to, the Board of Directors on these matters. Translate complex political, economic, and social issues into actionable updates, ensuring the board is informed of emerging risks and opportunities. 15% Research Analysis & Impact: Oversee the data collection, research, and rigorous evaluation of public policy outcomes. Ensure all policy positions are backed by evidence and measure the effectiveness of advocacy initiatives to demonstrate value to stakeholders 10% Budget & Resource Management: Develop and manage the annual budget for the public policy department. Allocate necessary resources for policy research, lobbying efforts, and public awareness campaigns while ensuring strict compliance with lobbying and financial disclosure regulations 5% Stakeholders include Chief Communications Officer, Chief Scientific Officer, CEO. Compensation Data The hiring range for this position in the US is $250,000/yr – $280,000/yr. Please note that salaries vary within the range based on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, education, certifications, location and any collective agreements, if applicable. Job Requirements MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Master’s degree in public policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Law or related field, or advanced scientific degrees in the field Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in public policy, government relations, or legislative advocacy. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted as a satisfactory substitute for the specific education and experience listed above. Other: 5+years in a senior leadership position or a position that interacts with Board of Directors and/or Executive Leadership roles. Deep understanding of local, state and federal legislative and regulatory processes Proven track record of successfully building coalitions and influencing public policy outcomes. Exceptional written communications skills for drafting briefs, testimonies and board reports Strong media literacy and experience serving as an official organizational spokesperson WORKPLACE REQUIREMENTS: Lives and located in Washington D.C As a remote worker, has sufficient internet and technical infrastructure and a home-based location suitable for creating a professional environment for video conference calls. About Corporate Functions The Corporate Functions provide operational support across Charles River in areas such as Human Resources, Finance, IT, Legal, Sales, Quality Assurance, Marketing, and Corporate Development. They partner with their colleagues across the company to develop and drive strategies and to set global standards. The functions are essential to providing a bridge between strategic vision and operational readiness, to ensure ongoing functional innovation and capability improvement. About Charles River Charles River is an early-stage contract research organization (CRO). We have built upon our foundation of laboratory animal medicine and science to develop a diverse portfolio of discovery and safety assessment services, both Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and non-GLP, to support clients from target identification through preclinical development. Charles River also provides a suite of products and services to support our clients’ clinical laboratory testing needs and manufacturing activities. Utilizing this broad portfolio of products and services enables our clients to create a more flexible drug development model, which reduces their costs, enhances their productivity and effectiveness to increase speed to market. With over 20,000 employees within 110 facilities in over 20 countries around the globe, we are strategically positioned to coordinate worldwide resources and apply multidisciplinary perspectives in resolving our client’s unique challenges. Our client base includes global pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, government agencies and hospitals and academic institutions around the world. At Charles River, we are passionate about our role in improving the quality of people’s lives. Our mission, our excellent science and our strong sense of purpose guide us in all that we do, and we approach each day with the knowledge that our work helps to improve the health and well-being of many across the globe. We have proudly worked on 80% of the drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the past five years. We’re committed to providing benefits that elevate your quality of life. Based on your position these may include: bonus/incentives based on performance, 401K, paid time off, stock purchase program, Health and wellness coverage, employee and family wellbeing support programs, and work life balance flexibility. Equal Employment Opportunity Charles River is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all qualified applicants and employees without regard to race, color, sex, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, mental or physical disability, family status, pregnancy, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. It is unlawful in some states (including Massachusetts) to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. If you are interested in applying to Charles River Laboratories and need special assistance or an accommodation due to a disability to complete any forms or to otherwise participate in the resume submission process, please contact a member of our Human Resources team by sending an e-mail message to [email protected] . This contact is for accommodation requests for individuals with disabilities only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications. For more information, please visit www.criver.com. item.title: Manager, Political Programs & Office Operations
item.description: Manager, Political Programs & Office Operations Organization: Cencora Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/08/2026 Manager, Political Programs & Office Operations Work Hours: Full Time Preferred Location: Washington, DC/MD/VA Work Arrangement: Hybrid Role About Cencora Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today! Job Details Join Cencora’s U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy team and help shape the company’s political engagement strategy. This Washington, D.C.-based role oversees the Cencora PAC, grassroots advocacy initiatives, political engagement programs, and compliance activities while building relationships that advance Cencora’s policy priorities, as well as the operational efficiency of office operations. The ideal candidate is a strategic, detail-oriented professional who thrives at the intersection of public policy, political engagement, communications, and operations. Responsibilities Lead and manage Cencora’s Political Action Committee (Cencora PAC), including fundraising and growth opportunities to expand it as one of the company’s core political and strategic resources that advances Cencora’s mission and objectives in Washington, DC, and relevant states. Lead Cencora’s grassroots program and get-out-the-vote political programs. Create and execute political program events for internal audiences. Oversee the day-to-day operations, budget, compliance, and growth of the Cencora PAC. Manage office administration, office operations, lobbying compliance reports, and political giving compliance reports, with support from another team member. Prepare PAC presentations and communications. Manage and prepare documents and briefings for the Cencora PAC Board and PAC Board meetings. Execute employee fundraising campaigns. Develop and distribute PAC communications, including educational and solicitation materials. Establish and maintain a network of relationships with campaign fundraisers and industry colleagues. Establish a strategic plan for the Cencora PAC and political engagement opportunities. Manage FEC compliance, ensuring adherence to FEC regulations and state and federal campaign finance laws. Manage lobbying compliance for federal and state entities, ensuring timely and accurate registrations and reporting. Administer political engagement governance activities by maintaining operating procedures, required filings, controls, and audit-ready documentation. Evaluate legislative and regulatory developments and develop impact assessments, scenario considerations, and advocacy action recommendations. Develop executive briefings, talking points, and internal updates that align leadership on how PAC and political programs support policy positions, risks, and engagement priorities. Execute government and stakeholder engagement activities by planning outreach, preparing meeting materials, and ensuring follow-through on action items. Develop grassroots and grasstops communication materials by aligning messaging, timing, and channels with advocacy objectives and stakeholder needs. Maintain the PAC database and PAC recognition awards distribution list. Plan and execute annual events for supporters of the Cencora PAC. Prepare the PAC annual report and newsletters. Prepare the annual political engagement statement. Coordinate with fundraisers to plan and execute PAC events in Washington, DC. Enhance existing PAC resources and create new materials, including website updates, communications assets, videos, and related resources. Perform other duties as assigned. Education and Work Experience Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Journalism, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent experience required. 4+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, advocacy (state and/or federal), legislative or regulatory analysis, stakeholder management, or a related field required. Experience managing a federal PAC. Working knowledge of FEC rules. Thorough understanding of the U.S. government, political processes, and legislative procedures. Thorough understanding of U.S. federal and state campaign finance laws. Experience interacting with and presenting to executives and senior leadership. Experience developing and implementing processes that improve efficiency and collaboration. Experience managing a corporate PAC preferred but not required. Skills and Knowledge Strong project, program, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to handle competing priorities and multiple initiatives simultaneously. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present information effectively to diverse audiences. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to assess policy, legislative, and regulatory developments and synthesize key implications. Exceptional organizational skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships, collaborate across internal and external stakeholders, and resolve issues efficiently. Ability to work independently, take initiative, exercise sound judgment, and represent the organization professionally and discreetly. Experience managing budgets and financial resources. Experience leading and managing people, programs, and cross-functional initiatives. Knowledge of common business productivity and presentation tools, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, email, and design/layout software. Ability to implement and maintain processes that support compliance, governance, reporting, and audit-ready documentation. Ability to travel as needed. What Cencora Offers We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings such as medical, dental, and vision care, we provide a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. These benefits may include: Backup dependent care Adoption assistance Infertility coverage Family-building support Behavioral health solutions Paid parental leave Paid caregiver leave To support personal and professional growth, Cencora also offers: Training programs Professional development resources Mentorship opportunities Employee resource groups Volunteer activities Additional career development opportunities For more information, visit: https://www.virtualfairhub.com/cencora Candidates can apply directly to the role on our careers website using this link: https://careers.cencora.com/ us/en/job/R2616282/Manager- Political-Programs-Office- Operations Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Government Affairs Analyst, Consultant
item.description: Government Affairs Analyst, Consultant Organization: Blue Shield of California Location: Sacramento, CA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Your Role The State Policy and Advocacy team serves as the company’s primary liaison to the State Assembly, Senate, Governor’s Office, and Regulatory Agencies and Departments – working closely with various business units to understand operational interworking’s as well as overarching company goals, with the ultimate mission to make healthcare better and more sustainably affordable for Californians. The Government Affairs Analyst, Consultant will report to the Senior Manager, Government Affairs. In this role you will actively engage in the legislative process, advocating for or against polies that affect Blue Shield of California and its members, under the direction of the Senior Manager and Vice President of Government Affairs. Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for leaders that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning. Responsibilities Your Work In this role, you will: Identify, track, and monitor state legislative proposals that impact company Advocate for the company’s position with the Legislature and Governor’s Administration Assist in policy development, drafting legislation and advocacy strategy to defeat and pass legislation Actively participate in meetings with health-plan trade associations Implement strategies to work with other influential constituencies to advance policy positions, including health plans, providers, brokers, labor, business and consumer representatives Monitor and provide input on federal policy matters and state regulatory matters (including coordinating company responses to regulatory data requests) Provide input on strategies to advance the company’s interests in the political arena, including candidate and ballot measure campaigns Qualifications Your Knowledge and Experience ​Requires a Bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree Requires a minimum of 7 years of prior relevant experience in legislative/external affairs or related field ​Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills ​Requires deep knowledge of the Government Affairs function ​Advanced degree (e.g., Juris Doctorate, J.D., or Master Public Policy, M.P.P.) preferred Broad knowledge of project management preferred Prior experience working in the Legislature and/or in a Government Affairs role (lobby firm or in-house) preferred Hybrid This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week. Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need. ABOUT US About Blue Shield of California As of January 2025, Blue Shield of California became a subsidiary of Ascendiun. Ascendiun is a nonprofit corporate entity that is the parent to a family of organizations including Blue Shield of California and its subsidiary, Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan; Altais, a clinical services company; and Stellarus, a company designed to scale healthcare solutions. Together, these organizations are referred to as the Ascendiun Family of Companies. At Blue Shield of California, our mission is to create a healthcare system worthy of our family and friends and sustainably affordable. We are transforming health care in a way that genuinely serves our nonprofit mission by lowering costs, improving quality, and enhancing the member and physician experience. To achieve our mission, we foster an environment where all employees can thrive and contribute fully to address the needs of the various communities we serve. We are committed to creating and maintaining a supportive workplace that upholds our values and advances our goals. Blue Shield is a U.S. News Best Company to work for, a Deloitte U.S. Best Managed Company and a Top 100 Inspiring Workplace. We were recognized by Fair360 as a Top Regional Company, and one of the 50 most community-minded companies in the United States by Points of Light. Here at Blue Shield, we strive to make a positive change across our industry and communities – join us! Our Values: Honest. We hold ourselves to the highest ethical and integrity standards. We build trust by doing what we say we’re going to do and by acknowledging and correcting where we fall short. Human. We strive to listen and communicate effectively, showing empathy by understanding others’ perspectives. Courageous. We stand up for what we believe in and are committed to the hard work necessary to achieve our ambitious goals. Our Workplace Model We believe in fostering a workplace environment that balances purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility – providing clear expectations while respecting the diverse needs of our workforce. Our workplace model is designed around intentional in-person interaction, collaboration, connection, creativity and flexibility: For most teams, this means coming into the office two days per week. Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location, out of state employees, and employees in certain member-facing roles should work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need. For employees with medical conditions that may impact their ability to work in-office, we are committed to engaging in an interactive process and providing reasonable accommodations to ensure their work environment is conducive to their success and well-being. The Company reserves the right to require more presence in the office based on business needs, and requirements are subject to change with periodic reviews. Physical Requirements: Office Environment – roles involving part to full time schedule in Office Environment. Based in our physical offices and work from home office/deskwork – Activity level: Sedentary, frequency most of work day. Equal Employment Opportunity: External hires must pass a background check/drug screen. Qualified applicants with arrest records and/or conviction records will be considered for employment in a manner consistent with Federal, State and local laws, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status or disability status and any other classification protected by Federal, State and local laws. item.title: Director, Government & Regulatory Affairs – Northwest
item.description: Director, Government & Regulatory Affairs – Northwest Organization: Western States Petroleum Association Location: Olympia, WA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 About the Job Salary: DOE Range $140k – $185k and Bonus Eligible Health and Welfare Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision; Flexible Spending Account and Dependent Care Account; Short-term and Long-term Leave; Sick Leave; Vacation; Life Insurance (4x annual salary); 401(k) with 6% company match; Pension Plan; Maternity and Paternity Leave. Position Summary The Director, Government & Regulatory Affairs is responsible for leading WSPA’s legislative and regulatory advocacy in Washington and Oregon across an assigned portfolio of issues. The position evaluates proposed legislation, regulations, and related policy developments; develops and recommends advocacy strategies and positions; and represents WSPA before legislators, regulatory agencies, and other decision-makers. The Director works closely with WSPA members, lobbyists, technical experts, consultants, industry partners, and other stakeholders to develop informed positions and advance industry priorities. The role requires strong independent judgment, strategic thinking, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to understand complex policy and technical issues and translate them into effective advocacy strategies. Support for local issues may be provided as needed. Essential Functions Lead development and execution of legislative and regulatory advocacy strategies in Washington and Oregon across assigned issue areas. Evaluate proposed legislation, regulations, and agency actions; assess potential impacts on members; and develop recommended WSPA positions, priorities, and responses. Anticipate emerging legislative and regulatory issues, identify strategic implications, and recommend when and how WSPA should engage. Integrate relevant technical information, member expertise, political considerations, and outside analysis into advocacy strategy and decision-making, including directing technical consultants and subject-matter experts as needed. Represent WSPA before legislators, legislative staff, regulatory agencies, hearings, technical working groups, task forces, and other government forums. Prepare and deliver testimony, presentations, comment letters, narrative reports, talking points, and other advocacy materials. Build and maintain effective relationships with policymakers, agency staff, members, lobbyists, industry associations, coalitions, and other stakeholders necessary to advance WSPA priorities. Direct and coordinate member, technical, consultant, lobbyist, and coalition resources in support of legislative and regulatory advocacy. Provide strategic leadership for assigned WSPA committees, including setting priorities, facilitating member consensus, guiding issue strategy, and overseeing related budgets and consultants. Support local and other regional policy matters as needed. Qualifications Juris Doctor strongly preferred; bachelor’s degree required. Approximately 15 years of progressive, relevant experience in government affairs, regulatory affairs, public policy, law, industry advocacy, or a related field, with consideration given to candidates with less experience based on the relevance and depth of their experience. Significant experience with Washington and Oregon legislative and regulatory processes, including direct engagement with policymakers and regulatory agencies and a strong working knowledge of legislative procedures, agency rulemaking processes, and the functions of key state regulatory agencies. Experience in the energy, petroleum, environmental, natural resources, or related industries preferred. Experience analyzing statutes, code, and research and providing external communications to broad audiences with varied knowledge levels of the topic. Demonstrated ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment with limited supervision. Key Skills and Competencies Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to prepare and deliver persuasive presentations, narrative reports, testimony, comment letters, and other advocacy materials. Ability to understand and distill complex legislative, regulatory, policy, and technical issues for varied audiences. Strong strategic thinking and judgment, including the ability to identify priorities, evaluate competing considerations, and recommend a course of action. Strong facilitation skills, including the ability to lead member discussions, develop consensus, and translate member input into clear positions. Ability to work effectively across a broad range of environmental, energy, safety, operational, and related policy issues, including matters outside the Director’s immediate subject-matter expertise. Ability to manage multiple complex policy and advocacy matters simultaneously and deliver high-quality work within legislative and regulatory deadlines. Ability to build credibility and work effectively with members, policymakers, agency staff, lobbyists, technical experts, and other stakeholders. Working Conditions Travel within Washington and Oregon is required, generally several days per month, with periods of increased travel depending on legislative sessions, regulatory proceedings, meetings, and other business needs. Limited travel to other Western states may be required. Occasional evening and weekend work is required. Supervisory Responsibility Sr. Manager, CA Policy and Multi-State Consultants Physical Requirements This position requires the employee to be on the road through the use of air and ground travel. Perform essential networking and relationship-building duties, including but not limited to a fluctuating schedule that includes evenings, late nights, early mornings, and weekends that require talking and hearing. The employee is frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel, and reach with hands and arms. Equal Employment Opportunity Policy The Western States Petroleum Association (WSPA) is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing a non-discriminatory employment environment for all of its employees. It is WSPA’s long-standing policy to provide equal employment opportunity without regard to race, religion, creed, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental impairment, military service, citizenship of individuals legally authorized to work in the United States, or any other basis prohibited by law. Call (916) 498-7750 for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Policy Specialist
item.description: Senior Policy Specialist Organization: Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Arnold & Porter is seeking a Senior Policy Specialist to join its Chambers-ranked Legislative and Public Policy Practice Group in Washington, DC. This role will support clients on a broad range of policy matters, including education, technology, artificial intelligence, appropriations, congressional investigations, energy, financial services, defense, tax, transportation, and related regulatory and legislative issues. The position will focus primarily on education and education technology policy work. Key responsibilities include monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory developments; supporting policy and funding advocacy strategies; and, advising clients on cradle to career issues, (including child care, workforce, defense research, privacy, artificial intelligence, etc.) . The practice group includes approximately 40 professionals and represents Fortune 500 companies, startups, trade associations, educational institutions, foundations, local governments, and foreign sovereigns in congressional and regulatory advocacy matters. Qualifications: A minimum of four years of experience in federal legislative or public policy roles, including experience in Congress, the Executive Branch, government relations, trade associations, or related organizations. Bachelor’s degree and strong academic credentials required. Excellent research, writing, and analytical skills. Must be eligible to register as a lobbyist under the Lobbying Disclosure Act. Please submit: Cover letter Resume Transcripts 3–5 page advocacy-focused writing sample Applications missing transcripts or including writing samples longer than 5 pages will not be considered. The anticipated base salary for this position is $95,000 to $185,000. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. For benefits information, please click here https://www.arnoldporter.com/en/careers/professional-staff/benefits. The firm may provide a discretionary bonus annually. #LI-HYBRID Apply Here for Washington, DC Arnold & Porter is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy and childbirth (including breastfeeding and related medical conditions), age, marital or partnership status, familial status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family leave status, citizenship status, immigration status, ancestry, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal laws, rules or regulations. Our Firm’s equal opportunity policy applies to all employment practices and terms and conditions, including, without limitation, recruitment, employment, assignment, training, compensation, benefits, promotions, disciplinary action and terminations. For purposes of the firm’s Anti-discrimination and Anti-harassment Policies, the term “race” includes, without limitation, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, such as braids, locks, and twists. item.title: Director, Global Regulatory and Scientific Policy
item.description: Director, Global Regulatory and Scientific Policy Organization: EMD Serono Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Work Your Magic with us! Start your next chapter and join EMD Serono. Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That’s why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us. United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology and Fertility. Our teams work together across 6 continents with passion and relentless curiosity in order to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team is becoming part of a diverse, inclusive and flexible working culture, presenting great opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe. This role does not offer sponsorship for work authorization. External applicants must be eligible to work in the US. Why Join Us? Shape the Future of Drug Development and Regulatory Policy. This role offers the opportunity to help shape the future regulatory landscape for innovative medicines and medical products. You will work with internal and external leaders to advance policies that support scientific innovation, regulatory modernization, and better outcomes for patients. If you are intellectually curious, energized by complex policy challenges, and passionate about advancing innovation in healthcare, we encourage you to apply. Your Role We are seeking a strategic, scientifically grounded, and highly collaborative Director, US Regulatory and Scientific Policy to help shape the regulatory environment supporting the development and delivery of innovative medical products. This role sits at the intersection of science, policy, and strategy, providing a unique opportunity to influence regulatory frameworks that impact patients, drug development, and healthcare innovation. As a trusted advisor to Research & Development, Regulatory Affairs, and senior leadership, you will monitor emerging regulatory, legislative, and scientific policy trends; provide strategic insights to support development programs; and engage with regulators, industry associations, and other stakeholders to advance science-based regulatory frameworks. Candidates with experience in drug development, regulatory affairs, regulatory policy, and health authority engagement are encouraged to apply. Experience at FDA or another health authority is highly valued. Key Responsibilities Monitor and assess evolving regulatory, legislative, scientific, and healthcare policy developments that may impact the company, its pipeline, and the broader drug development ecosystem. Provide strategic policy analysis and actionable recommendations to product teams, regulatory leaders, R&D stakeholders, and senior management. Advise development teams on regulatory opportunities, emerging pathways, policy risks, and innovative approaches that may accelerate development and patient access. Identify and help shape policy frameworks that support innovation in areas such as regulatory science, clinical development, digital health technologies, New Alternative Methods (NAMS), AI, rare diseases, and other emerging topics. Represent the company in interactions with trade associations, policy organizations, and other external stakeholders. Develop and advance company positions on key regulatory and legislative issues, including coordinating responses to guidance documents, requests for information, and other policy initiatives. Develop and support advocacy strategies that advance science-based, patient-focused regulatory policies. Develop briefing materials, policy analyses, presentations, executive communications, and training content for internal stakeholders. Serve as an internal subject matter expert in strategic policy areas and facilitate cross-functional collaboration across Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, CMC, Legal, Government Affairs, and other functions. Build strong internal and external relationships, lead through influence, and foster a culture of curiosity, innovation, continuous learning, and excellence. Who You Are: Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in biological sciences, healthcare, public health, policy, regulatory affairs, legal studies, or a related discipline with substantial relevant experience required; advanced degree strongly preferred (MS, PharmD, PhD, MD, MPH, JD, or equivalent), 5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, regulatory, policy, government, consulting, or related fields. Strong knowledge of drug development and the regulatory environment governing pharmaceuticals and biologics. Understanding of FDA regulations, guidance development processes, and international regulatory frameworks, including ICH. Preferred Qualifications: Experience at FDA, another health authority, or a policy-making organization. Experience developing regulatory policy positions and advancing regulatory reform initiatives. Excellent analytical, strategic thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and build consensus in a matrixed organization. Familiarity with legislative and healthcare policymaking processes. Experience working with trade associations, public-private partnerships, patient organizations, or multi-stakeholder collaborations. Demonstrated effectiveness engaging with senior executives, regulators, scientific experts, and industry leaders. Expertise in one or more emerging areas of regulatory science and innovation. What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress! item.title: Director, International Government Relations
item.description: Director, International Government Relations Organization: Ocean Conservancy Location: Washington, DC | Remote Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Salary Range: $130,000.00 To $140,000.00 Annually POSITION TITLE: Director, International Government Relations DEPARTMENT/PROGRAM: Conservation Programs REPORTS TO: Vice President, External Affairs STATUS: Regular, Full-Time, Exempt LOCATION: Washington, DC preferred (hybrid); other states considered: AK, CA, FL, MD, OR, TX, VA, WA, WV ABOUT OCEAN CONSERVANCY For more than 50 years, Ocean Conservancy has delivered effective, evidence-based solutions for the ocean and all who depend on it. Today, we continue to unite science, people and policy to protect our ocean from the greatest challenges it faces: climate change, plastic pollution and biodiversity loss. We are a 501(C)3 headquartered in Washington, D.C. that inspires a worldwide network of partners, advocates and supporters through our comprehensive and clear-eyed approach to ocean conservation. Together, we are securing a healthy ocean and a thriving planet, forever and for everyone. POSITION SUMMARY The Director, International Government Relations is responsible for coordinating Ocean Conservancy’s (OC) international policy advocacy across conservation programs and the International Government Relations (IGR) team, ensuring OC shows up before governments and institutions with a single, credible voice. The Director runs the cross-program coordination systems that keeps OC’s international engagement coherent and coordinates a unified “One-OC” presence at major convenings like Our Ocean, the UN Ocean Conference and UNEA. The Director also builds cross-program capability in international advocacy and diplomacy through shared playbooks, coaching and strategic input. OC’s international advocacy is distributed across conservation programs and the IGR team rather than centralized in IGR alone. The Director’s role is to both directly drive and engage in international advocacy, and to also be the connective tissue that helps international efforts across programs add up to more than the sum of their parts. Reporting to the Vice President of External Affairs, the Director will work closely with program leads across OC’s conservation portfolio — including Biodiversity, Climate, and Plastics — as well as Communications and Development, to advance OC’s international policy goals. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Directly engaging in international advocacy and managing the IGR team Directly engage with governments and international institutions on behalf of Ocean Conservancy’s ocean conservation advocacy priorities. Manage IGR team direct reports. Ownership of the IGR team budget, annual workplan and internal reporting. Driving international advocacy strategies and coordination across teams Strengthen program staff’s effectiveness at international advocacy and diplomacy through strategic guidance on coalition-building, diplomacy and negotiation strategy. Run OC’s internal coordination systems, including cross-program coordination calls and organization-wide global visibility updates. Proactively identify and address coordination gaps. Coordinating key international multi-issue events and a unified international calendar Coordinate a unified “One-OC” approach at major multi-issue convenings (e.g., Our Ocean, UN Ocean Conference, UNEA) — defining institutional success, sequencing engagements and establishing a fair, transparent process for allocating scarce opportunities such as speaking roles, side events and high-level bilateral meetings. Maintain a shared international events calendar and planning tracker that programs actively use to plan engagements and that surfaces benchmark or venue conflicts early enough to proactively resolve. Coordinating country and institutional prioritization Maintain a single, current, shared view of OC’s priority country and institutional targets, including tiering and clarity on where deeper relationship investment is needed. Ensure country prioritization visibly shapes real engagement decisions — who at OC is engaging which governments and why. REQUIRED SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE Significant professional experience (5+ years) in international policy, diplomacy or government relations, ideally within the ocean, environmental or natural resources sector. Demonstrated ability to build and run coordination systems across multiple teams or stakeholders with competing priorities, without direct authority over those teams. Track record of building or contributing to international coalitions, including engaging both champion governments and more skeptical or opposed parties. Familiarity with international policy venues and processes relevant to ocean conservation (e.g., IMO, RFMOs, UNFCCC/COPs, UNEA, BBNJ, Our Ocean) strongly preferred. Excellent relationship-management skills, with the judgment to navigate sensitive and sometimes competing institutional interests with diplomacy and discretion. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex, cross-program information into clear, actionable guidance. Highly organized self-starter, comfortable building and maintaining shared systems (calendars, trackers, briefing materials) that other teams rely on. Highly collaborative, with an appreciation for working across program boundaries and influencing without direct authority. Willingness to travel internationally for negotiations, convenings and partner meetings, as this position will require international and domestic travel to support key multi-issue convenings, negotiations and partner engagements. Strong passion for Ocean Conservancy’s mission and values. EDUCATION/TRAINING Bachelor degree required, preferably in environmental policy, public policy, international affairs, international relations, marine policy or a relevant related field. COMPENSATION Ocean Conservancy is committed to fair pay practices and posts expected salary ranges for each of its positions. Compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s specialty skills, years of experience, location, and unique background. The starting salary range for this role is $130,000 – $140,000 annually. We would welcome the opportunity to connect with potential candidates whose salary requirements may be outside of the expected range. TO APPLY If you think you’d be a great fit for the job and are interested in joining Ocean Conservancy’s team, please apply here . Please include a resume and cover letter in one file on your application. HYBRID WORK ENVIRONMENT Ocean Conservancy embraces a hybrid work environment, which allows our staff the flexibility to work virtually and in-person while building strong connections across the institution. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER Ocean Conservancy provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. We encourage applicants who have a diverse level and range of relevant skills and experiences to apply. A 100% match is not required. We want to support employees’ career growth and in return, our employees help Ocean Conservancy grow into a stronger, more inclusive institution. Earn a certificate with the Council!
