item.title: Prin Regulatory Analyst
item.description: Prin Regulatory Analyst Organization: Baltimore Gas & Electric Co Location: Baltimore, MD Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Job Description Who We Are We’re powering a cleaner, brighter future. Exelon is leading the energy transformation, and we’re calling all problem solvers, innovators, community builders and change makers. Work with us to deliver solutions that make our diverse cities and communities stronger, healthier and more resilient. We’re powered by purpose-driven people like you who believe in being inclusive and creative, and value safety, innovation, integrity and community service. We are a Fortune 200 company, 20,000 colleagues strong serving more than 10.7 million customers at six energy companies — Atlantic City Electric (ACE), Baltimore Gas and Electric (BGE), Commonwealth Edison (ComEd), Delmarva Power & Light (DPL), PECO Energy Company (PECO), and Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco). We’re committed to creating an environment where every person can thrive. Our employee experience is grounded in four tenets that guide how we support our people: purposeful careers, growth opportunities, community impact, and support to thrive. In our relentless pursuit of excellence, we elevate diverse voices, fresh perspectives and bold thinking. And since we know transforming the future of energy is hard work, we provide competitive compensation, incentives, excellent benefits and the opportunity to build a rewarding career. Are you in? Primary Purpose PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION Act as project manager for regulatory filings, audits and/or special projects. The Revenue Policy function is to plan, coordinate, recommend and support strategies for timely development of filings and responding to informational and audit requests. Perform research and analysis of accounting, tax and financial issues associated with regulatory matters and preparation of executive level presentation materials as necessary. Apply critical analytical skills in the preparation of regulatory filings or strategic analysis including the drafting of testimony and required schedules, responses to discovery (data) requests of regulators and external parties and contributing to the development of filings and briefs related to revenue requirements. Monitor regulatory hearings, proceedings and meetings. Analyze impacts and communicate findings to BGE departments and other impacted Exelon operating groups. Position may be required to work extended hours for coverage during storms or other emergencies. Primary Duties PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES Act as project manager for regulatory filings, audits and/or special projects. Plan, coordinate and manage the implementation of the assigned filing, audit or project. This includes recommendations to appropriate management and other departments in the development of filings and positions on, and responses to, information requests. Manage activities of the regulatory and multifunctional staff as assigned. (35%) Perform accounting, tax, financial, economic and other quantitative and qualitative analyses of regulatory matters. Responsibilities include research, analysis, coordination with finance, accounting. legal and other departments, monitoring and the preparation of appropriate written and oral reports for management. (20%) Coordinate and provide quality assurance in the preparation or drafting of written testimony, regulatory schedules, special regulatory audits and post-filing implementation requirement activities. (20%) Participate in and/or monitor regulatory hearings, proceedings and meetings. Analyze impacts on the company and prepare appropriate reports to management identifying issues and suggesting appropriate actions to address issues raised by commission decisions and rule making. Communicate relevant information to regulatory departments and other Exelon departments effected by the regulatory issues. (20%) Promote and maintain regular relationships with state regulatory agency staff pertaining to the areas of ratemaking, economics and audit. (5%) Job Scope JOB SCOPE This position has a direct impact on the utility’s ability to successfully implement its regulatory strategy for utility cost recovery and strategic business objectives. The position has significant interrelationships both internally and externally. Key internal relationships include regulatory, finance, accounting, treasury, and legal, as well as other operational and support groups within BGE and its affiliates. Position requires strong aptitude for project management of cross-functional teams. In addition, the individual is regularly called upon to provide guidance, analysis, quality assurance and advice to company personnel with regards to complex regulatory issues. Financial modeling skills are preferred. The position requires that it be a trusted and reliable conduit of information to, and feedback from, the regulatory agencies and other internal and external parties involved in the regulatory processes that impact the Company. In doing so it is required that the position be able to interface with regulatory staff, intervenors and consultants demonstrating cooperation, tact, diplomacy and excellent judgment to further BGE’s credibility and strategic business objectives. Work is complex in nature, and involves both strategic thinking, technical and financial analysis, and an attention to detail, in order to quickly assimilate and implement new regulatory concepts under tight time constraints. At certain points in time, the position requires extended hours in order to prepare regulatory filings. This position will also, as appropriate, provide functional direction, leadership and instruction to others in the department on project teams demonstrating judgment and communication skills. Generally operates with minimal supervision. Minimum Qualifications MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Accounting or Engineering Experience is typically career level (7-10 years) in Accounting, Finance or related field. Excellent written and oral communication skills are essential. Commitment to highest standards of quality and integrity Possess a high degree of complex problem solving with solid financial, mathematical and analytical capabilities Demonstrated competencies in 1) accountability, 2) collaboration, 3) continuous learning and 4) high performance in ambiguous situations. Exhibit professionalism and stay current on industry proceedings and professional development. Demonstrated ability to effectively manage cross functional teams. In lieu of degree, 9-12 years of relevant experience. Preferred Qualifications PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Economics; CPA. Ten or more years of electric utility experience with five or more years’ experience with regulatory filings. Financial modeling skills preferred. CPA, revenue requirement, and regulatory accounting experience preferred. Benefits Annual salary will vary based on a candidate’s skills, qualifications, experience, and other factors: $107,200.00/Yr. – $147,400.00/Yr. Annual Bonus for eligible positions: 20% 401(k) match and annual company contribution Medical, dental and vision insurance Life and disability insurance Generous paid time off options, including vacation, sick time, floating and fixed holidays, maternity leave and bonding/primary caregiver leave or parental leave Employee Assistance Program and resources for mental and emotional support Wellbeing programs such as tuition reimbursement, adoption and surrogacy assistance and fitness reimbursement Referral bonus program And much more Note: Exelon-sponsored compensation and benefit programs may vary or not apply based on length of service, job grade, job classification or represented status. Eligibility will be determined by the written plan or program documents. Apply Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Manager, Public Affairs & Issues Management
item.description: Senior Manager, Public Affairs & Issues Management Organization: AIR Communities Location: Chicago, IL | Los Angeles, CA | Atlanta, GA | New York, NY | Dallas, TX | Denver, CO Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Compensation: USD 150,000 – USD 175,000 – yearly Company Description AIR Communities is a Blackstone portfolio company and one of the country’s leading real estate investment firms, focused on creating value through high-quality apartment communities, exceptional resident experiences, and disciplined investment and asset management. AIR is part of a scaled residential platform focused on meeting the need for high-quality, professionally managed rental housing. We create value by investing in our communities, elevating the resident experience, strengthening operations, and applying disciplined investment and asset management practices. Today, AIR brings together the strengths of a scaled operating platform, deep multifamily expertise, and a performance-oriented investment mindset. Our purpose is simple: create exceptional living experiences for residents, provide a supportive environment where teammates can do meaningful work, and generate durable value for investors. We do that by combining centralized capabilities, data-driven decision making, strong local execution, and a culture rooted in integrity, respect, collaboration, customer focus, and performance. Job Description Our offices are located in LA, Chicago, Atlanta, New York, Dallas, and Denver. Candidates should be able to commute to one of these offices daily or be open to relocation to be considered for the role. The Senior Manager role will be a critical member of our Public Affairs & Issues Management team, responsible for identifying, assessing, and resolving complex issues across the business. The individual will partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders (legal, government relations, communications, operations, etc.) at AIR Communities (a Blackstone multifamily portfolio company) and Blackstone to proactively mitigate risk, manage sensitive situations, and protect the company’s reputation. This role requires a self-directed, solutions-oriented person who can operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment, often with incomplete information and evolving dynamics. The ideal candidate combines experience, strong judgment, structured thinking, and practical execution, with the ability to quickly understand complex scenarios, distill key risks, and drive clear, actionable outcomes – while balancing the competing priorities of diverse internal and external stakeholders. Issues Navigation Serve as the central lead on escalated, sensitive, and high-profile issues (including crisis situations), owning the process from intake and initial escalation through resolution. Partner with AIR, and Blackstone stakeholders to assess risk, align on strategy, and execute coordinated responses. Develop communications materials required for issue prevention, response, and resolution. Support training and development of new processes, protocols and issues preparedness work. Proactively identify patterns, vulnerabilities, and emerging risks to help prevent issue recurrence. Expertly navigate issues across internal teams, third-party partners, and external audiences including media and elected officials. Reputational Risk Management Rapidly assess complex and ambiguous situations, identifying key drivers, risks, and downstream implications. Think big picture to anticipate reputational risks and opportunities, while also zooming into critical details to inform strategy and execution. Develop solutions that balance business objectives, operational realities, and reputational considerations. Navigate competing priorities and perspectives to drive alignment and resolution. Partner Collaboration Build strong relationships and work collaboratively across internal and external partners to ensure coordinated issue management and consistent execution. Collaborate closely with a small, high-performing cross-functional team to develop coordinated strategies, align stakeholders, and drive effective issue resolution. Act as a trusted advisor to internal stakeholders, providing clear, practical guidance on reputational and operational risks. Translate complex situations into concise, executive-ready summaries and recommendations. Support leadership and colleagues in making informed, timely decisions in high-pressure situations. Participate in a rotating on-call schedule and support high-priority issues during evenings, weekends, and other non-business hours as needed. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in communications, political science, or related field. 8 – 10+ years of high-stakes reputation management experience with a strong public affairs lens. Proven experience in issues management, strategic communications, crisis management, government affairs, corporate affairs, consulting, and/or a related field, including engagement with media, government officials, regulatory agencies, community stakeholders, and other external influencers. Proven experience managing complex issues across legal, operational, and reputational dimensions (internal and external). Proven track record of identifying risk, preventing issue recurrence, and improving processes over time. Experience operating within or alongside large institutional environments (e.g., private equity, asset management, REITs, or comparable organizations) strongly preferred. Experience working with PR agencies, lobbyists, and law firms. Experience developing and executing media relations plans and crisis communications frameworks, playbooks, and scenario plans. Strong understanding of social media and digital communications, with the ability to identify emerging risks, assess potential exposure, and develop effective response strategies. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and AI-enabled productivity tools, with the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new technologies and software platforms Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate multiple perspectives and develop well-reasoned, data-informed solutions. Comfort independently owning and driving projects to timely completion. Demonstrated ability to tailor communications for diverse audiences, including executive leadership. Exceptional writing skills and ability to synthesize complex information clearly and concisely. Strong collaboration and leadership skills, with the ability to influence without authority and mentor others. Additional Information AIR offers attractive total compensation packages designed to recognize and reward performance at the individual, team and company levels. We start with a competitive base salary and add bonus opportunities and benefit choices topped off with: Expected base salary of $150,000- $175,000 + Annual Bonus. You will be provided a pay rate that is in line with your skills and experience as they relate to the requirements of the job. 25% Rent Discount available Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance options available. HSA with company sponsored contributions, FSA (traditional and dependent care FSA). Short and long-term disability paid by the company. 401(K) plus 6% company contributions. Paid Vacation, 14 Paid Holidays, and Paid Sick Time. Tuition Assistance Program. Commuter Benefits and Pet-Insurance. Up to 100% Reimbursement on Professional Certification/Licensing for Job Related Curriculums. Paid parental leave of up to 16 weeks, following the birth or adoption of a child. Consumer discounts from various products and services including travel planning, wireless phones, health and fitness, home appliances, and more. 15 hours of paid time annually to give-back to your community. Opportunities for professional development and career growth including realistic job previews, in person and virtual leadership training, and performance improvement courses. What You Need to Know Application Deadline: The initial deadline for applications is 10/31/2026. Applications submitted after this date may still be considered on a rolling basis until the position/program is filled. We encourage all interested candidates to apply as early as possible. If a final decision has not been made by the initial deadline, subsequent applications will be reviewed as they are received. Candidates extended an offer will be required to undergo pre-employment screening that includes checking references, a four-panel drug screening that excludes marijuana testing, employment verification & criminal background check. item.title: Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs Organization: Abbott Laboratories Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries. The Opportunity The Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs will advance and protect Abbott’s interests with Congress, federal agencies, and key trade and business associations. This leader will drive public policy strategy across all Abbott businesses, analyzing legislative and regulatory developments and shaping the company’s positions on critical issues. The role is responsible for developing and executing advocacy strategies to influence federal policies, legislation, and regulations, with a particular focus on healthcare policy and the evolving role of technology in healthcare delivery and innovation. The successful candidate will proactively monitor emerging policy trends, assess potential business impacts, and develop strategic plans that effectively address issues affecting Abbott’s diverse portfolio. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor, helping to shape policy outcomes that support innovation, patient access, and business objectives. Location: Washington, D.C. What You’ll Work On Review and analyze legislative and executive branch activities to assess the level of impact on the company Develop strategic plans and recommendations to influence legislative and agency actions, and proactively identify opportunities for Abbott in the policy-making arena Develop and successfully implement action plans by working with relevant stakeholders, including business and corporate personnel, outside allies, coalitions and trade associations Advance and protect Abbott interests and reputation with key stakeholders by maintaining and developing relationships with policymakers and opinion leaders Brief and staff Abbott senior leadership during Washington D.C. policy-related meetings or visits by elected officials to Abbott facilities Increase the business’s understanding of, and participation in, the policy-making and political process on behalf of Abbott Experience You’ll Bring Required Qualifications University or bachelor’s degree required Minimum 10 years’ experience in positions of increasing responsibility and experience in the public sector or government affairs is required Demonstrated success in influencing the development of policy, and knowledge of the political process, is required Proven ability to work well with key policymakers, major association policy teams, and executives Established track record of policy development, negotiations, professional writing and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects under deadline pressure Strong understanding of the intent of legislation or proposed policies/regulation and the ability to assess the extent to which such legislation or regulations support or conflict with Abbott’s positions or interests Strong ability to communicate, synthesize key government issues, develop strategy and persuade constituencies towards specific actions and initiatives Proven ability to drive for results, motivate and positively influence individuals both inside and outside of the organization Recognized team player who seeks to become an integral part of an industry-leading government affairs group Demonstrated evidence of strong organizational skills, adept at managing complex array of projects/issues Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in political science, public policy, public health, or MBA/JD is a plus Knowledge of medical devices/diagnostics/nutrition areas of health care preferred The base pay for this position is $171,300.00 – $342,700.00. item.title: Public Policy & Government Relations
item.description: Public Policy & Government Relations Organization: Tempo Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Tempo is a layer-1 blockchain purpose-built for stablecoins and real-world payments, born from Stripe’s experience in global payments and Paradigm’s expertise in crypto tech. Tempo’s payment-first design provides a scalable, low-cost predictable backbone that meets the needs of high-volume payment use cases. Our goal is to move money reliably, cheaply, and at scale. Our north star is simplicity for users: fintechs, traditional banks, merchants, platforms, and anyone else looking to move their payments into the 21st century. We’re building Tempo with design partners who are global leaders in AI, e-commerce, and financial services: Anthropic, Coupang, Deutsche Bank, DoorDash, Mercury, Nubank, OpenAI, Revolut, Shopify, Standard Chartered, Visa, and more. We’re a team of crypto-optimists, building the infrastructure needed to bring real, substantial economic flows onchain. We like to move fast and swing for the fences — join us! The role You will be our first policy and government relations hire. You’ll build Tempo’s presence in Washington from the ground up. You’ll represent us on Capitol Hill, with regulators, and across industry coalitions, and you’ll help the company understand and shape the rules that govern stablecoins, digital payments and agentic commerce. We’re looking for a seasoned senior leader who is not afraid to roll up their sleeves. As our first policy and government relations hire, you’ll set the strategy and run it yourself. You will be our voice to Congress and regulators. You will also be a strategic partner to Legal, Product, Comms/Marketing, and GTM, shaping how policy factors into product decisions from the earliest stage. Context shifting will be critical to success; the best candidate will understand how to move between strategy and execution hour to hour and day to day. Responsibilities Build and run Tempo’s federal government relations strategy, with a focus on stablecoin, payments, digital assets and agentic commerce legislation and rule making Develop and maintain relationships with Members, committee staff and relevant regulators Engage on emerging AI and agentic commerce policy as it intersects with payments Track and analyze federal and key state policy developments, then turn them into clear guidance for leadership and product teams Draft comment letters, testimony, white papers, one-pagers, and briefing materials Build and manage Tempo’s presence in trade associations and industry coalitions, and build alliances across the payments, fintech, and AI ecosystems Support company leadership in DC engagement Manage outside lobbying and policy consultants as needed Own the policy function end to end as a hands-on individual contributor Required qualifications 8+ years of policy or government relations experience In-house government relations experience at a payments, fintech, financial services, or technology company Experience with payments policy, including stablecoins, money transmission, BSA/AML, card networks, real-time payments, or fintech regulation Strong relationships and credibility on both sides of the aisle Direct experience with digital asset policy, such as stablecoin legislation and implementation, market structure, or tax Excellent written and oral communication skills: you can turn complex technical and regulatory issues into crisp, persuasive material A self-starter comfortable working in a fast-moving startup, and quickly toggling between strategy and execution Preferred qualifications Prior Capitol Hill experience, preferably on financial services, banking, or agriculture issues Experience with AI or agentic commerce policy Multi-client experience at a lobbying firm, consultancy, or trade association Familiarity with federal agency rulemaking and regulatory engagement Attributes High motor; item.title: Global Public Affairs Manager
item.description: Global Public Affairs Manager Organization: Schneider Electric Location: Boston, MA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Job Description The Global Public Affairs Manager helps strengthen Schneider Electric’s Public Affairs capability worldwide by connecting colleagues, sharing expertise, and developing the tools, resources, and ways of working that enable teams to build trusted stakeholder relationships and protect the company’s license to operate. Based in Boston, the role connects the Global Public Affairs team with colleagues across Schneider Electric’s markets, bringing together insights, facilitating collaboration, and supporting the development of effective approaches to stakeholder engagement. The role contributes to global initiatives that strengthen the function’s effectiveness, visibility, and impact, while ensuring that insights and experience from across the organization inform the evolution of Schneider Electric’s global Public Affairs agenda. This is a high-visibility opportunity for an experienced Public Affairs professional to work across geographies and functions, contribute to strategic global initiatives, and help shape how the Public Affairs function operates and delivers value across the organization. Key Responsibilities Global Public Affairs Capability Building Assess capability, resource, and operating-model needs across the global Public Affairs network, in partnership with regional and market colleagues. Develop and maintain practical playbooks, templates, and guidance for stakeholder engagement, relationship management, engagement planning, partnership mapping, and impact measurement. Lead briefings, workshops, and onboarding sessions to strengthen Public Affairs capabilities and share effective practices across markets. Identify opportunities to improve Public Affairs tools, processes, and ways of working across the global network. Support markets with varying levels of Public Affairs maturity by facilitating knowledge-sharing and access to relevant resources and expertise. Global Projects and Cross-Market Collaboration Serve as a connector between the Global Public Affairs team and colleagues across Schneider Electric’s markets, facilitating the exchange of insights, expertise, and best practices. Identify opportunities for cross-market collaboration on issues affecting Schneider Electric’s stakeholder relationships, reputation, and broader business environment. Lead assigned global Public Affairs projects end-to-end, including planning, stakeholder coordination, delivery, and reporting. Maintain a repository of market case studies, stakeholder engagement practices, and lessons learned to support continuous improvement across the network. Facilitate collaboration between markets when stakeholder groups, business priorities, or reputational considerations extend beyond national or regional boundaries. Support the Global Director in advancing initiatives that strengthen the connectivity, effectiveness, and visibility of the global Public Affairs function. Stakeholder and External Environment Insights Monitor broader business, societal, geopolitical, and reputational developments that may affect Schneider Electric’s stakeholder environment and license to operate. Bring together relevant insights from across markets to identify common themes, emerging stakeholder expectations, and opportunities for cross-border collaboration. Translate complex developments into practical insights that support stakeholder engagement, corporate reputation, and Public Affairs planning. Prepare stakeholder briefings, engagement insights, landscape assessments, and strategic recommendations for global leadership and relevant colleagues. Draw on expertise from market teams and relevant subject-matter owners to strengthen the global understanding of emerging stakeholder dynamics. Identify and share external developments, innovative approaches, and emerging practices that may enhance the effectiveness of Schneider Electric’s Public Affairs network. Cross-Functional Partnership and Integrated Engagement Partner with Media Relations, Executive Positioning, Crisis Communications, market Public Affairs and Government Affairs teams, and relevant business functions to support coordinated engagement on issues of shared importance. Support alignment of stakeholder engagement and corporate reputation initiatives across functions and markets. Work with the Global Director and relevant colleagues to connect global initiatives with the expertise and experience of market teams. Contribute to integrated responses to emerging stakeholder and reputational issues that require collaboration across functions and geographies. Identify opportunities to strengthen collaboration between Public Affairs and adjacent corporate functions, ensuring that relevant perspectives are brought together in support of Schneider Electric’s broader priorities. Global Network Engagement Build trusted working relationships with Public Affairs and Government Affairs colleagues across regions and markets. Act as a two-way connector, bringing global resources, insights, and opportunities to colleagues while ensuring that market experience informs the evolution of the global Public Affairs function. Facilitate knowledge-sharing, peer learning, and collaboration across the global network. Identify opportunities to improve communication, coordination, and effectiveness across the Public Affairs community. Support the Global Director in strengthening the operating model, visibility, and impact of the global Public Affairs function. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. 7–10 years of experience in Public Affairs, corporate affairs, stakeholder engagement, or a related field. Demonstrated experience leading projects and coordinating cross-functional, cross-market, or agency contributors. Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across geographies and organizational boundaries. Strong judgment, with the ability to work independently, navigate a matrixed organization, and recognize when to escalate. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex developments into clear, actionable insights. High discretion and composure when handling confidential or time-sensitive matters. Fluent written and spoken English. Preferred Experience working across multiple markets or in a global or matrixed organization. Experience connecting local or regional insights to broader organizational priorities. Experience developing Public Affairs tools, training, or capability-building programs. Familiarity with Public Affairs measurement, evaluation, and data-driven reporting. Experience supporting markets with varying levels of Public Affairs maturity. Experience in the energy, industrial, infrastructure, or related sectors. Experience working across Public Affairs, Government Affairs, Communications, or related corporate functions. At Schneider, we believe that every employee is a talent who deserves equal opportunities. This means you matter. Every individual needs to feel valued, supported, and treated fairly to do their best work. Our Total Rewards is our way of saying: “We see you. We value you”. It’s more than just pay and benefits- it’s a meaningful investment in you. It is designed for you to perform, grow, feel safe, and elevate your potential to shine as an impact maker. For this U.S. based position, the expected pay range is USD 117,600 – USD 176,400 per year. This pay range includes base pay and short-term incentives. The compensation range for this full-time position applies to candidates located within the United States. Our pay ranges are determined by reviewing roles of similar responsibility and level. Within the pay range, individual pay is determined by several factors including performance, knowledge, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Schneider Electric is there when it matters most to you Our Total Rewards package outlines all the benefits and support you’ll enjoy as part of the Schneider Electric team: Care for Yourself and Your Family. We ensure you feel secure with benefits that help you and your family thrive: medical (with member reward points), dental, vision, and basic life insurance, Benefit Bucks, flexible work arrangements, paid family leaves, well-being programs, 12 holidays per year, and 15 days of paid time off per year. Invest and Plan Your Future. We help you plan and invest for the future with competitive pay and programs including base salary, incentives, company share ownership, and 401(k) with match. Grow Your Skills and Career. We support development through performance discussions, global opportunities, the Schneider Career Hub, and learning platforms like Coursera. Team Up in the Workplace. We encourage collaboration, recognition, sharing your voice, and an inclusive workplace. Support Your Community. We make a difference through volunteer leave, programs with the Schneider Electric Foundation, youth education initiatives, and military leave benefits. If you believe this job posting is not compliant with applicable state pay transparency laws in the U.S., please notify the Company as soon as possible upon discovery by completing this form Job Posting Compliance Form. At Schneider Electric, our values and behaviors are the foundation for creating a great culture to support business success. We believe that our IMPACT values – Inclusion, Mastery, Purpose, Action, Curiosity, Teamwork – starts with us. item.title: Senior Director of Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Director of Government Affairs Organization: Lot Sixteen LLC Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 TL/DR Lot Sixteen is a bipartisan lobbying and communications firm looking for a senior director of government affairs to join our team and advocate for our clients’ interests across a variety of pivotal industries. ‍The Firm Lot Sixteen is looking for a senior director of government affairs to join our growing team of exceptional government relations professionals. In this role, ownership of, and accountability for, planning and executing work across a wide variety of functions will be required. We are a pro-active bunch. We translate our words into actions. We insist on knowing what we are talking about. We view the identification of a problem or task as only the first of many steps required to get results. We prioritize solutions, develop detailed work plans, secure approval to execute those plans and get to work on implementation. We worry, so clients don’t have to. And we want this same approach from the person selected for this role. We are continuing tobuild an agency that feels like home, a team of friends who support each other as much as they challenge each other, and a client base whose trust and confidence in us is earned every day. At Lot Sixteen, we prioritize quality, value smart thinking, and strive for a more diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment. Accordingly, we aim to provide or exceed all the standard work perks and expectations, including: Competitive salary Generous benefits, including: Health and dental plan Retirement plan with company matching Commuter benefits All-you-can-eat snacks and all-you-can-drink coffee Colleagues who welcome your real family & friends and recognize that balancing both is an essential ingredient to happiness Downtown Washington, D.C. office location on McPherson Square, near 15th & K St. NW The Role‍ A senior director of government affairs at Lot Sixteen has a fairly diverse set of responsibilities, including roles in: Managing the day-to-day relationships with client contacts, and often serving as deputy account leads. Leading interactions with clients and proactively responding to client needs. Informing clients of bill introductions, amendment filings, regulatory actions, votes and other key developments in Washington through written memos and phone calls. Participating actively in client calls, internal brainstorming and rapid response efforts. Incorporating analysis into high-quality, client-facing communications. Conducting policy-oriented research and presenting findings to clients in presentations or written materials. Drafting, reviewing and editing written content and materials. Utilizing, creating and/or updating various databases. Monitoring congressional floor, committee and individual member office activities. Mentoring and training junior staff and new employees. ‍ The Candidate Did we just become best friends? Well… yeah… if you’re someone who: Cares deeply about your professional relationships and works hard to strengthen them. Thrives on meeting new people and has an affinity for storytelling. Likes the idea of representing and protecting clients’ business, reputational and policy interests. Prefers engaging in the policymaking process to opining on it. Finds fulfillment in developing and implementing solutions to problems that feel unsolvable. Enjoys writing, and is incredibly good at it (presentations, memos, speeches and zinger txt msgs). Can’t help yourself but to build coalitions among similarly-situated people and organizations. Feels an obligation to keep people in the loop, rather than cut them out of it. Prides yourself in looking around corners, contemplating scenarios and being prepared. Understands U.S. federal policy development and implementation processes. Has cultivated a real expertise on a particular set of issues. Prioritizes well in a fast-paced, demanding environment. Likes to step in and lend a hand on activities outside your wheelhouse. Finishes what you start, without anyone checking up on you. You are most likely to thrive in this role if you have at least six years of experience. We care less about where or how long you went to school than we do about how eager you are to continue learning. Experience in public service – on the Hill, in the military, at an agency or otherwise – would be outstanding. So would deep knowledge of and curiosity about the business implications of changes to public policy and the nuances of energy policy. Equally important: a willingness to admit what you don’t know and go find the answers. The ideal candidate for this role: Likes meeting new people Has an affinity for storytelling Prefers engaging in the policymaking process to opining on it Has cultivated a real expertise on a particular set of issues Builds coalitions of similarly situated people and organizations Seeks to understand U.S. federal policy development and implementation processes Prioritizes well in a fast-paced, demanding environment ‍ ‍Compensation, Benefits and Additional Details: The salary for this full-time, regular, exempt position is $110,000 per year. The Company may, at its sole discretion, provide end-of-year bonuses at up to 15% of base salary based on personal and firm performance. The payment of any bonus is contingent upon you being in good standing with the Company at the time the bonus is paid. Lot Sixteen offers generous company benefits, including 15 days of PTO per year; 11 paid holidays per year, plus our office is closed for the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day; 100% employer-paid medical and dental insurance, plus coverage for dependents; a 401(k) match; and Metro or parking benefits. Lot Sixteen operates with a hybrid office environment. Staff are expected to work from the office approximately 3 days per week, with the option to work remotely the other days. However, we encourage new and junior staff to take advantage of working in-person at the office in order to maximize learning opportunities and hands-on professional development. Interested? Please use this link to fill out and submit your application. ‍If you have questions regarding the application process, please email us at [email protected] . We look forward to hearing from you! item.title: Director of Government and Political Affairs
item.description: Director of Government and Political Affairs Organization: National Mining Association (NMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 About the job About The National Mining Association: America’s mining industry supplies the essential materials necessary for nearly every sector of our economy – from technology and healthcare to energy, transportation, infrastructure, and national security.The National Mining Association (NMA) is the only national trade organization that serves as the voice of the U.S. mining industry and the hundreds of thousands of American workers it employs before Congress, the federal agencies, the judiciary and the media, advocating for public policies that will help America fully and responsibly utilize its vast natural resources. We work to ensure America has secure and reliable supply chains, abundant and affordable energy, and the American-sourced materials necessary for U.S. manufacturing and economic security, all delivered under world-leading environmental, safety and labor standards. Job Summary: NMA is currently conducting a search for a full-time Director of Government and Political Affairs position in the association’s headquarters office in Washington D.C. Reporting to the Senior Vice President for Government and Political Affairs, this role will be critical role in the development and implementation of Congressional and government affairs strategies advocating for NMA policy priorities. Responsibilities: Responsible for working with other members of the government affairs team to develop and implement Congressional lobbying strategies advancing NMA’s legislative and policy goals through direct outreach to Members of Congress and staff which includes: Analyze the impacts of Congressional and regulatory actions on the mining industry Draft position documents Create supportive materials, developing statements, and letters Identify Congressional allies advancing the mining industry’s policies Manage and track legislation that affects the mining industry Draft memoranda on issues in Congress important to our members Coordinate and respond to member companies and industry allies Develop, cultivate, and maintain positive and new bipartisan relationships with Members of Congress, staff, and key Congressional Committees by educating, advocating, and being responsive to those offices to advance NMA’s legislative priorities Lead, build, manage, and collaborate with outside groups and coalitions to create a cohesive voice to shape consensus and garner a wider range of support for NMA’s legislative priorities Assist in coordinating internal committees to formulate the association’s positions and policies on specific policy issues Ensures that the government affairs team is informed in a timely and effective way about legislative, policy, regulatory, and political risks, and opportunities relevant to our membership Actively suggests targets for political giving through NMA’s Political Action Committees Attend the fundraisers of key political allies Required Education, Skills and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, an advanced degree (e.g., business, finance, or law) preferred and 7+ years of related work experience, preferably on Capitol Hill or administration Strong understanding of the legislative process Knowledge of political dynamics and its ability to impact legislative process and predict outcomes Impeccable communication and negotiation skills Previous experience working in a fast-paced environment, with demonstrated ability to meet deadlines while managing multiple projects and ever-changing priorities Highly- organized and detail-oriented Self-starter who takes initiative and can anticipate needs before they arise and resolve issues quickly Physical Demands: This position requires the ability to remain in a stationary position (standing and/or seated) more than half the time The person in this position must be able to maneuver (lift, move, carry, slide, etc.) less than 15 lbs. This position requires the ability to spend most of the time viewing computer monitors. NMA is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are committed to furthering our engagement with, support for, and understanding of, our community; supporting all team members in being themselves; and driving the ongoing diversification of our team. We believe that everyone has distinct characteristics, skills and backgrounds that make their experiences as members of the NMA team and the perspectives they bring to the office unique. We want to encourage and celebrate that uniqueness. Above all else, through our work, the ultimate goal is to maintain a welcoming culture for all. For us, “welcoming” means that all employees feel that they are accepted, respected and valued, that we have created a safe space for the discussion of and embracing differences, and that the entire team is invested in their success. NMA provides a robust benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as life and disability coverage. Additionally, employees receive commuter benefits to help with parking or public transportation costs. NMA also offers paid time off, sick leave, and holidays. Starting salary in the range of $132,940 to $179,860 commensurate with experience. Interested candidates are invited to apply to [email protected] . Applicants who may need accommodations are encouraged to contact NMA to request and arrange for accommodations. If you need assistance to accommodate a differing ability, you may request accommodation at any time. Please contact Human Resources at [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Vice President of Communications
item.description: Vice President of Communications Organization: Tusk Strategies LLC Location: New York City, NY | San Francisco, CA | Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Who We Are Tusk Strategies is a 35-person team of some of the most talented and tenacious communications, political, and policy strategists in the country. For over a decade, we have worked with leading startups, established companies, and organizations willing to think creatively and challenge the status quo. Our teams drive strategic communication, product launch, and public policy campaigns on behalf of our clients. Our nationally recognized Advanced Tech Practice runs communications and public affairs strategies for some of the buzziest and fastest growing start-ups in and out of Silicon Valley and is expanding rapidly. The Role As a Vice President of Communications reporting directly to the Partner leading Tusk’s Advanced Tech Practice, you will focus on earned, social, and paid media strategies that supercharge client policy and business aims. Other responsibilities will include: Devising innovative ways for our clients and their executive to build their reputation in the tech media and policy ecosystem through media appearances, conferences, podcasts, newsletters, and TV opportunities. Creating and executing communications strategies around major market expansions, fundraising announcements, policy announcements, product launches, and other milestones. Proactively identifying storylines to create ad hoc media opportunities. Drafting and editing content including op-eds, testimony, speeches, and press releases. Assisting with new business proposals by putting together creative ideas and tactics. What we look for from you. A minimum of 4 years of experience at a public affairs agency, in-house, in government, and/or on political or issue advocacy campaigns. Experience pitching blockchain technology, AI, blockchain, fintech, and other emerging technologies. Experience driving effective social media campaigns leveraging influencers and natural allies. Ability to provide examples of campaigns or projects that show how your creative communications efforts drove a successful media, business, or political outcome. Reporter contacts at relevant beats. Excellent writing skills. Ability to work on multiple projects at once and under tight deadlines.Willing to relocate to NYC or CA (SF/LA area) What you’ll get from us. Tusk fosters a collegial and collaborative environment where the best ideas for our clients win, no matter your title. To that end, we aim to consistently create opportunities for professional growth and to provide competitive benefits. Benefits include: Highly competitive base salary. Opportunity to earn new business commission. Eligible to earn an EOY bonus as a new employee. 401(k) with employer contribution of 3% of compensation. 100% covered premiums for medical, dental, vision; with dependents and spouses 50% covered. Unlimited vacation. Paid parental leave. Covered cell phone service. Hybrid work environment. The pay range for this position is expected to be between $125,000 and $150,000/year. However, the base pay offered may vary depending on multiple factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, experience, market factors, and business need. Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. Experience managing public policy issues and advocacy campaigns. Preferred qualifications: Experience with legislative processes and policy development at state or federal levels. Ability to build bipartisan coalitions and maintain key stakeholder partnerships. Leadership skills with a track record of cross-functional, independent execution. Strong political, analytical, and communication skills, with 50% travel ability. We support strategic initiatives by fostering trusted relationships, educating public officials, driving policy reform, and ensuring alignment between organizational goals and public policy framework. You will represent the organization before state and local policymakers, senior leadership, influential decision-makers, and agency executives to drive strategic initiatives. You will work collaboratively to support business growth and public policy objectives by proactively mitigating risks and addressing policy barriers. Additionally, you will participate in key trade associations critical to advancing our equities while protecting our license to operate. Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Develop comprehensive advocacy plans, policy positions, and materials in support of government policy goals. Build trusted relationships with key policymakers, officials, trade associations, and coalition partners. We own what we do. We WOW our customers. Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Focused on a bold vision to deliver Smarter Technology for All, Lenovo has built on its success as the world’s largest PC company with a full-stack portfolio of AI-enabled, AI-ready, and AI-optimized devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets), infrastructure (server, storage, edge, high performance computing and software defined infrastructure), software, solutions, and services. Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY). This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. Description and Requirements Key Responsibilities: Work together with the director, Government Relations NA, and the extended team to advance public policy topics for Lenovo in key states and communities across the US Develop and advance relationships with key external state and local stakeholders Independently identify, monitor, and analyze key issues and legislation at the state level and develop state policy strategies and outreach plans where appropriate Maintain regular communication with business units to support internal stakeholder awareness and review of relevant state actions Together with the legal department, advise business units on policy and regulatory matters that may impact the development or deployment of products and services Regularly and actively engage action, where appropriate Actively participate in state and local opportunities to represent Lenovo and its interests, including with industry trade organizations/committees, elected officials, NGOs, incentives, including funding available for investment and workforce development Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to develop stakeholder dialogue opportunities focused on advancing Lenovo business objectives and reputation Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in public relations, communications, political science, public affairs, law, business, economics, marketing, journalism, business/commerce, history, geography, or similar field 8+ years of experience in developing and managing strategic relationships to advocate and influence public/technology policy priorities at the state level 5+ years of experience working in the technology policy space A vast understanding of the North America technology market, ideally in the areas of laptop/IT hardware/mobile phones/cloud computing Keen understanding of the North American political system, environment, and institutions as well as cultural landscape, particularly at the state level in the US Solid network with the item.title: Public Policy Manager, External Affairs
item.description: Public Policy Manager, External Affairs Organization: Meta Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Meta is seeking a Public Policy Manager to lead external affairs strategy and engagement across key policy audiences, including government officials, industry coalitions, trade associations, and civil society organizations. In this role, you will develop and execute advocacy strategies that advance Meta’s policy priorities across legislative and regulatory environments, representing the company’s positions on issues spanning content governance, data privacy, competition, and emerging technology. You will serve as a senior external-facing voice for Meta, building and sustaining relationships with policymakers and stakeholders that shape the regulatory and political landscape for Meta’s products and platforms. Public Policy Manager, External Affairs Responsibilities Develop and execute external affairs strategies to advance Meta’s policy priorities with government officials, regulatory bodies, trade associations, and civil society stakeholders Represent Meta in direct engagement with policymakers, legislative staff, and external coalitions on issues including content governance, data privacy, competition policy, and emerging technology regulation Lead cross-functional coordination across policy, legal, communications, and product teams to align on advocacy positions and external messaging Analyze legislative and regulatory developments to assess business impact and develop proactive policy responses and stakeholder engagement plans Draft and review policy submissions, position papers, testimony, and advocacy materials for external audiences including government bodies and industry forums Build and maintain a network of relationships with senior government officials, industry partners, and third-party advocates to support Meta’s external affairs objectives Identify emerging policy risks and opportunities, and develop mitigation strategies in collaboration with regional and global policy teams Contribute to organizational strategy by setting goals and priorities for external affairs workstreams across multiple policy domains Leverage AI tools to improve the quality, speed, and scope of policy analysis, stakeholder mapping, and advocacy material development Minimum Qualifications 8+ years of experience in public policy, government affairs, external affairs, or a related field, with demonstrated experience engaging government officials or regulatory bodies Experience developing and executing advocacy strategies on technology policy issues such as content governance, data privacy, competition, or platform regulation Experience building and managing relationships with senior government officials, legislative staff, trade associations, or civil society organizations Experience drafting policy documents, position papers, regulatory submissions, or advocacy materials for external government or industry audiences Experience working across cross-functional teams including legal, communications, and product to align on policy positions and coordinate external engagement Preferred Qualifications Experience operating across multiple policy jurisdictions or regulatory environments, including international markets Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements) Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews) Experience working in or directly with a legislative body, regulatory agency, or executive branch office on technology policy matters Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to improve policy research, stakeholder analysis, or advocacy workflow efficiency Experience managing coalition relationships or coordinating multi-stakeholder advocacy campaigns across industry groups or civil society Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies About Meta Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics. For those who live in or expect to work from California if hired for this position, please click here for additional information. United States of America: $153,000/year to $224,000/year + bonus + equity + benefits Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Compensation details listed in this posting reflect the base hourly rate, monthly rate, or annual salary only, and do not include bonus, equity or sales incentives, if applicable. In addition to base compensation, Meta offers benefits. Learn more about benefits at Meta. Equal Employment Opportunity Meta is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor: Southeastern United States
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor: Southeastern United States Organization: Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck Location: Tampa, FL Date Posted: 10/09/2026 After opening its doors in Denver in 1968, Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck has since expanded around the country, with 14 offices, 600+ employees and 300+ attorneys and policy professionals nationwide. And with over 50 years in the industry, we’re committed to creating strong relationships with not only our clients, but with each other and our communities. Are you looking for a group of accomplished professionals to collaborate with? If so, we want you at Brownstein. At Brownstein, clients get access to the top legal minds in the industry, powerful policy knowledge, and best-in-class business acumen to solve businesses’ toughest challenges. Brownstein is a law and lobbying firm that has been making moves for more than 50 years to stay at the vanguard of its industry. You’ll find this firm at the heart of many of the most important cases, the most significant deals, and the country’s most pivotal legislation. Brownstein—we’re all in. For more information, visit us at bhfs.com. We are seeking a Senior Policy Advisor to join our State Government Relations practice. This position will support a portfolio of multistate clients, with a particular focus on legislative, regulatory, and political affairs across the Southeastern United States. This position will be based in our Tampa, FL office or performed remotely from anywhere within the Southeastern United States. The ideal candidate will bring a robust network of relationships throughout the region, deep knowledge of state government and political landscapes, and the ability to provide strategic counsel on complex policy challenges. The successful candidate will also demonstrate a proven ability to cultivate, maintain, and grow client relationships while delivering exceptional client service. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in supporting and expanding our growing Southern Team. Essential Job Duties: Monitor, analyze, and provide strategic guidance on legislative, regulatory, and political developments with a focus on the Southeastern United States. Serve as a trusted advisor to clients by delivering timely insights, policy analysis, and strategic recommendations on complex state government issues. Develop and execute state-level advocacy strategies designed to advance client objectives before legislatures, executive branch agencies, and other key policymakers. Build, maintain, and leverage relationships with elected officials, legislative staff, regulators, and influential stakeholders throughout the Southeastern United States. Lead the preparation of client-facing policy analyses, legislative updates, briefing materials, presentations, and strategic communications. Represent clients in meetings with policymakers, industry organizations, trade associations, and other stakeholder groups. Lead client engagements and provide proactive counsel regarding political environments, legislative opportunities, and emerging policy risks. Identify opportunities to deepen existing client relationships and contribute to business development efforts throughout the region. Collaborate with colleagues across the firm’s state government relations practice to develop integrated multistate advocacy strategies and deliver exceptional client service. Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned. Required and Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in political science, public policy, law, or related field. 5+ years of experience in state and local government relations. Must be located in the Southeastern United States. Deep understanding of the political, legislative, and regulatory landscape across the Southeastern United States. Established network of relationships with elected officials, legislative staff, executive branch leaders, regulators, and key stakeholders throughout the region. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams. Professional demeanor and ability to engage with clients and government officials. Willingness to travel frequently in support of client needs, strategic relationship management, business development, and professional networking, including significant travel throughout the Southeastern United States and attendance at industry conferences and events. Compensation and Benefits: Brownstein offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k + match, profit sharing, and vacation/sick/personal time off. We are offering a salary for this role ranging from $200,000-$275,000, depending on experience. To Apply: Please submit a cover letter and resume here . Brownstein is an equal opportunity employer. Brownstein will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, as amended by the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act of 2008, interpretive regulations and other authority, and applicable state laws. While Brownstein does not discriminate on the basis of citizenship, the successful candidate must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship of a work visa, or Brownstein assuming sponsorship of an existing work visa; including student visas with an OPT/CPT designation. item.title: Director, Government Relations
item.description: Director, Government Relations Organization: Illinois Bankers Association (IBA) Location: Springfield, IL Date Posted: 10/09/2026 About the job The Illinois Bankers Association (IBA) is seeking an experienced and relationship-driven Director,Government Relations to join our Government Relations team and help advance the priorities of the Illinois banking industry. The Director, Government Relations plays an important role in advancing IBA’s approved legislative,regulatory, and public policy priorities. Reporting to the Chief Policy Officer, this position leads day-to-day advocacy efforts on assigned issues and portfolios, develops relationships with policymakers and other key stakeholders, and serves as a representative of IBA and the banking industry. This is an opportunity for a skilled government relations professional to make a meaningful impact through advocacy, policy analysis, coalition engagement, grassroots activity, and member relations. The successful candidate will be comfortable working independently within established advocacy positions while keeping leadership informed of significant developments and emerging issues. Responsibilities include: Lead Government Relations & Advocacy Lead day-to-day advocacy on legislative, regulatory, geographic, relationship, or issue portfolios assigned by the Chief Policy Officer. Lead day-to-day Illinois General Assembly, Chicago, Cook County, or other local government engagement when assigned. Represent IBA in meetings, negotiations, hearings, regulatory proceedings, coalition discussions, and other advocacy forums. Build and maintain productive relationships with legislators, congressional offices, executive branch officials, regulators, local officials, legislative and committee staff, coalition partners, and industry stakeholders. Advance approved IBA priorities before the Illinois General Assembly, state and federal agencies, the Illinois congressional delegation, and relevant local governments. Participate in key IBA advocacy events, including Washington Visit, Springfield Lobby Day or Economic Investment Day, Let’s Talk Banking meetings, hearings, briefings, and conferences. Analyze Policy & Legislative Developments Monitor and analyze legislation, regulations, administrative actions, policy proposals, hearings, and emerging issues. Evaluate potential operational, financial, competitive, legal, and member impacts in collaboration with IBA leadership, legal counsel, member bankers, and subject matter experts. Prepare testimony, comment letters, issue briefs, talking points, correspondence, presentations, and other advocacy materials. Identify emerging opportunities and threats and provide timely recommendations to the Chief Policy Officer. Translate complex legislative and regulatory issues into clear implications, recommendations, and messages for members and leadership. Engage Members & Build Grassroots Advocacy Develop policy content, target audiences, recommended actions, and follow-up plans for assigned grassroots campaigns. Engage bankers whose relationships, expertise, and community perspectives can strengthen IBA’s advocacy efforts. Brief members for policymaker meetings, hearings, testimony, action alerts, and other advocacy activities. Respond to member inquiries on assigned policy matters and elevate legal, strategic, or politically sensitive matters as appropriate. Work with the PAC and Grassroots Coordinator to execute approved advocacy communications and evaluate campaign response. Support Leadership, Committees & Communications Prepare analysis, recommendations, presentations, and reports for the Government Relations Committee, Executive Committee, Board of Directors, PAC Board, and other groups. Collaborate with Communications staff on advocacy-related press statements, editorials, issue briefs, member alerts, social media content, and media materials. Serve as an IBA spokesperson on assigned public policy matters when authorized. Monitor media and public discussion surrounding assigned issues and identify emerging communications needs or reputational risks. Manage Priorities & Collaborate Across IBA Develop work plans and measurable objectives for assigned priorities and provide concise progress, outcome, and risk reporting. Maintain accurate policy files, relationship notes, testimony, correspondence, coalition records, and other work product. Lead cross-functional projects and coordinate event or campaign work and outside resources as assigned. Collaborate with colleagues across IBA departments and provide functional guidance on assigned initiatives. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in government, political science, public policy, law, communications, business, or a related field. At least five years of progressively responsible experience in government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, advocacy, regulatory affairs, or a related field. Experience working with legislative or regulatory processes and developing relationships with elected officials, government agencies, policymakers, coalitions, or other external stakeholders. Strong policy analysis, advocacy, negotiation, writing, public speaking, and relationship-building skills. Ability to translate complex legislation and regulations into clear implications, recommendations, messages, and actions. Ability to work independently, manage multiple time-sensitive priorities, and appropriately escalate significant issues. Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion with sensitive member, political, regulatory, and strategic information. Ability to travel throughout Illinois and periodically to Washington, D.C., and other locations. Willingness to attend evening, early-morning, overnight, and occasional weekend meetings and events. Preferred Qualifications: Illinois government relations experience. Financial services or banking industry knowledge. Advanced degree in a relevant field. Pay range: $100,000-$150,000 annually with a generous benefits package that includes employee health insurance, life insurance, and LTD paid by employer; dental, STD and vision offered; 401(k) with match; FSA available; PTO and paid holidays. Please send cover letter and resume to: [email protected] Interviews will begin October 13, 2026. Illinois Bankers Association is an equal opportunity employer. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Government Relations Manager
item.description: Government Relations Manager Organization: Signature Aviation Location: Orlando, FL Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Job Description Signature Aviation is seeking a Government Relations Manager to support the continued growth of the company’s Government Relations function. Reporting to the Director of Government Relations, this role will support the company’s state and local government affairs efforts while helping build programs that strengthen Signature’s relationships with policymakers, trade associations, airport sponsors, and communities across North America. This is an opportunity to join a growing team and help shape how Government Relations supports the business. The successful candidate will work across the company to strengthen grassroots engagement, improve how we leverage our trade association partnerships, expand stakeholder relationships, and develop tools and programs that make Government Relations a valuable resource for the organization. We’re looking for someone with experience in state and local government affairs or trade associations Responsibilities Essential Duties and Responsibilities: State & Local Government Affairs Monitor and analyze state legislative and regulatory developments affecting Signature Aviation and the aviation industry. Coordinate internal responses and prepare legislative summaries, issue briefs, presentations, talking points, and other government affairs materials. Build and maintain relationships with state and local elected officials, state agencies, municipal governments, airport sponsors, and other government stakeholders. Develop and maintain stakeholder maps and engagement plans for Signature’s operating locations. Trade Association Strategy & Engagement Maximize the value of Signature’s investments in national, state, and regional trade associations. Coordinate the distribution of legislative updates, policy developments, best practices, and other association resources across the organization. Identify opportunities for Signature leaders to participate in committees, leadership positions, speaking engagements, sponsorships, conferences, and other strategic initiatives. Track committee participation, sponsorships, and engagement opportunities to ensure the company fully leverages its trade association memberships. Enterprise Government Relations Programs Help build and grow Signature’s Government Relations function by developing new programs, tools, and resources that improve engagement across the company. Develop and coordinate a grassroots engagement program that helps Signature locations build meaningful relationships with elected officials, airport sponsors, and community stakeholders. Create and facilitate annual Government Relations training, playbooks, and engagement resources for Signature’s operating network. Coordinate community engagement initiatives that support business objectives and strengthen relationships in key markets. Maintain Government Relations databases, reporting tools, legislative trackers, and stakeholder resources. Partner with Operations, Legal, Communications, Commercial, Human Resources, and executive leadership on Government Relations initiatives. Support compliance with lobbying registration, ethics, and reporting requirements. Travel as needed to support government affairs activities, industry meetings, conferences, and stakeholder engagement. Qualifications Minimum Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, Communications, Business, Aviation Management, or a related field. Four to seven years of experience in government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, trade associations, public administration, or a related field. Experience working in or with state and local government—including state legislatures, governors’ offices, state agencies, municipal governments, or local elected officials—is strongly preferred. Experience with a trade association or advocacy organization is strongly preferred. Experience in aviation, transportation, infrastructure, or another regulated industry is preferred, but not required. Additional knowledge and skills: Strong understanding of state and local legislative and regulatory processes. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong organizational and analytical skills with attention to detail. Ability to translate policy developments into practical business insights. Experience supporting grassroots engagement, stakeholder outreach, or community engagement initiatives. Sound judgment, professionalism, and political awareness. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and legislative or stakeholder tracking platforms. Self-motivated with a desire to learn, take ownership of projects, and contribute to the continued growth of the Government Relations function. Interest in building a long-term career in the aviation industry. About Us With more than 225 locations worldwide, Signature Aviation is the largest global network of private aviation terminals, delivering safe, convenient, and elevated experiences to those we serve. As a premier hospitality organization and a certified Great Place to Work™, we are committed to redefining private air travel. Our nearly 6,000-strong team of aviation experts and enthusiasts is dedicated to delivering excellence to our guests and communities, and it starts with taking care of our team. Signature provides a variety of benefits, programs, and resources to support our team members’ overall well-being and professional development. We proudly volunteer and give back, focusing on elevating the neighborhoods where we operate, empowering the next generation of aviation professionals, and supporting our veterans. From your health to your financial wellness, there are several benefits for you and your family when joining Signature Aviation. Our Benefits: Medical/prescription drug, dental, and vision Insurance Health Savings Account Flexible Spending Accounts Life Insurance Disability Insurance 401(k) Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity and Accident Insurance Identity Theft and Legal Services Paid time off Paid Maternity Leave Tuition reimbursement Training and Development Employee Assistance Program (EAP) & Perks Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or other protected characteristics.
