item.description: Policy Manager Organization: Nautilus Solar Energy® Location: Chicago, IL | New York, NY | Boston, MA | Philadelphia, PA Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Description Nautilus Solar Energy® is seeking a Policy Manager to support the company’s legislative, regulatory, and political engagement across priority markets. This fully remote position will report to the Policy Director and will play a critical role in developing policy strategy, monitoring legislative and regulatory developments, coordinating with external stakeholders, and providing strategic analysis to support the company’s government affairs objectives. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker with strong analytical and project management skills who can translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into actionable business intelligence. This individual will serve as the department’s primary resource for policy analysis, legislative and regulatory monitoring, coalition coordination, and strategic planning. Responsibilities: Monitor legislative, regulatory, and political developments across Nautilus’ priority markets, with a primary focus on the Northeast. Analyze proposed legislation, regulatory proceedings, commission orders, and utility filings to identify business impacts and emerging opportunities. Prepare policy memoranda, legislative summaries, briefing materials, and strategic recommendations for executive leadership. Develop and maintain tracking systems for legislation, rulemakings, stakeholder engagement, advocacy priorities, policy databases, and market trackers. Support state-specific government affairs strategies; identify market opportunities and policy risks; and assist with legislative priorities, advocacy strategies, and regulatory positions. Conduct political and stakeholder analysis to support long-term business planning. Coordinate with lobbyists, trade associations, coalition partners, consultants, and external advisors. Prepare materials for coalition meetings, legislative visits, regulatory engagements, conferences, policy events, and stakeholder outreach. Support participation in state and national trade associations. Work with Legal, Development, Origination, Business Development, Finance, and Operations to align business objectives and government affairs strategy. Support executive leadership with policy briefings and decision memorandum Requirements Currently in the final year of a master’s program or has completed a master’s degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Environmental Policy, Energy Policy, Government Affairs, or a closely related field. Three to five years of experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, political strategy, or a related area. Legislative or regulatory experience, including experience working for or with a lawmaker, state legislature, regulatory commission, public utility commission, executive agency, or similar organization; energy or electricity-sector experience is strongly valued. Demonstrated understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes and how legislation and regulation can affect market-based business decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-level briefing materials. Exceptional analytical, organizational, and project management skills. Ability to manage multiple policy initiatives across several states and work independently in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment. Preferred Qualifications: Prior knowledge of community solar, distributed energy resources, distributed generation, virtual net metering, or utility regulation. Experience working in or with the clean energy industry, trade associations, state legislatures, public utility commissions, or executive agencies. Experience synthesizing legislative and regulatory developments into strategic recommendations for executive leadership. The Northeast is preferred, particularly candidates based in Boston, New York, or Philadelphia. item.title: Government Affairs Manager
item.description: Government Affairs Manager Organization: SentiLink Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 SentiLink stops more than 150,000 fraud attempts and verifies more than 3 million identities every day to protect both institutions and consumers. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details. At SentiLink, you’ll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other’s time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them. We’re well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we’re expanding into new markets, and we’re backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We’ve been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we’ve testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity. We want SentiLink to be the best place you’ve ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India. Role: SentiLink is expanding its government affairs work in Washington, DC and in a growing number of states, and we’re looking for a sharp, policy-savvy Government Affairs Manager to lead advocacy strategy with Congress, federal regulators, and industry coalitions, and to direct SentiLink’s full bench of state and federal lobbyists. In addition to advancing federal policy initiatives and direct lobbying, you’ll work closely with Public Sector sales, marketing/comms, and executive leadership to help shape the policy environment that supports SentiLink’s mission. This role gives you real ownership: you’ll set the strategy and cadence for every contracted lobbyist we work with, in Washington and in the states, so our advocacy stays sharp and our team is better enabled and more effective when they walk into the room with the right people. This role reports to the Head of Public Policy & External Affairs, and inherits a function with clear priorities and foundation already in place, with the expectation that you’ll expand it. It will require frequent in-person engagement with stakeholders across the DC area, including Capitol Hill (House and Senate, Republicans and Democrats), federal agencies, and industry events. This role requires you to be based out of Washington, DC. Responsibilities: Lead day-to-day federal advocacy, building and maintaining relationships across Congressional offices in both parties and chambers, with particular depth on Financial Services/Banking, Ways and Means/Finance, and Appropriations committee staff. Direct SentiLink’s bench of contracted federal and state lobbyists and consultants, setting priorities and a regular cadence of engagement, and translating their work into the budget-cycle and procurement insight our Public Sector sellers need to close. Serve as a trusted resource on policy issues affecting identity verification, fraud prevention, and financial services, in direct support of Public Sector sales cycles (RFP language, identity standards, procurement timing). Lead engagement with trade associations and coalitions (RDA, ETA, CBA, ABA, and similar), managing SentiLink’s participation and extracting more value from existing memberships. Build a state-level ability to monitor and report on state legislative and regulatory developments on issues related to data brokers, privacy and identity. Prepare briefing materials and talking points for internal and external stakeholders, and represent SentiLink in meetings, hearings, roundtables, and industry events. Requirements: 4+ years of experience in public policy, government relations, or legislative affairs, ideally with a combination of time on Capitol Hill, at a trade association, or a regulated fintech/financial services environment. Working knowledge of federal legislative and regulatory processes, especially related to financial services or identity, and the ability to pick up state-level processes quickly. Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills with bipartisan credibility. You’ve built (or are excited to build) working relationships across the aisle, House and Senate, not just within one party’s orbit. Excellent writing and public speaking ability: comfortable drafting comment letters, testimony, and briefing memos, and representing SentiLink on a conference panel or in a room of policymakers with equal confidence. Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data. A proactive, self-starting mindset and the ability to thrive in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment. Genuine interest in going deep on fraud, identity, privacy and data policy. This is not a generalist policy seat; you’ll be expected to develop real subject-matter depth quickly. Bonus Points: Familiarity with state legislative tracking tools. Exposure to public sector sales cycles or government procurement. Background in identity verification, fraud prevention, or tech policy. Compensation: 150,000 – 190,000 year + equity + benefits Perks: Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles) Flexible paid time off Regular company-wide in-person events Home office stipend, and more! Corporate Values: Deep Understanding Whatever It Takes Do Something Smart Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, State Government Affairs
item.description: Director, State Government Affairs Organization: GE Appliances, a Haier company Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.” As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way. We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together. The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: we come together, we always look for a better way, and we create possibilities. Interested in joining us on our journey? Director, Government Affairs leads GE Appliances’ state government affairs strategy across all 50 states. The role represents the company before state policymakers, trade associations, coalitions, and other external stakeholders while advising company leaders on legislative, regulatory, political, and public policy developments that may affect the business. How You’ll Create Possibilities Core Responsibilities: Develop and execute a nationwide state government affairs strategy aligned with GE Appliances’ business priorities Monitor, analyze, and prioritize state legislative activity, translating policy developments into business implications and action plans Represent GE Appliances before governors’ offices, state legislatures, agencies, legislative staff, trade associations, coalitions, and policy organizations Build and maintain strategic relationships with elected officials, policymakers, industry partners, and external stakeholders Partner with Legal, Compliance, Product, Technology, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Sustainability, Commercial, Communications, and other functions to develop company positions and advocacy strategies Lead or coordinate company responses to priority legislation, including testimony, comments, amendments, briefing materials, and other advocacy communications Manage external government affairs consultants and contract lobbyists when needed, ensuring alignment with company priorities, policy positions, ethical standards, and accountability expectations Prepare executives for government engagement and identify opportunities to showcase GE Appliances’ manufacturing footprint, innovation, workforce, investments, and economic impact Ensure lobbying, ethics, disclosure, political activity, and reporting compliance in coordination with Legal and Compliance Track legislative priorities, advocacy activities, outcomes, metrics, resources, and budget to demonstrate business impact What You’ll Bring to Our Team Minimum Qualifications: 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, government relations, or a related field, including significant government experience Strong knowledge of state legislative and regulatory processes and the ability to manage issues across multiple states Proven ability to analyze complex legislation, develop advocacy strategies, influence outcomes, and communicate clearly with senior executives and non-policy audiences Knowledge of the legal and operational construct of PACs Demonstrated ability to build relationships with policymakers, legislative staff, trade associations, industry partners, and other stakeholders Ability to work independently, collaborate across a matrixed organization, and travel as needed Preferred Qualifications: Advanced degree in law, public policy, government, business, or a related discipline. Experience within a staff position or closely working with House and Senate committees Experience leading state government affairs for a national company, trade association, or complex organization Experience managing a multi-state legislative portfolio and issues affecting manufacturing, consumer products, energy, environment, product regulation, technology, privacy, labor, tax, transportation, or related areas Established relationships with state policymakers, national organizations of state officials, business organizations, and government affairs professionals Experience directing outside lobbyists, consultants, trade associations, and coalitions Strong political judgment, executive presence, business acumen, and ability to advise senior leaders on political and legislative risk *This role is remote in the US. Our Culture Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail to [email protected] Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Head of Global External Affairs
item.description: Head of Global External Affairs Organization: Roche Diagnostics Location: Washington, DC | Santa Clara, CA | Branchburg, NJ | Pleasanton, CA | Indianapolis, IN | Tucson, AZ Date Posted: 10/09/2026 At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters. The Position Operating as the Head of Global External Affairs, you will be a pivotal member of the Quality, Regulatory & External Affairs (QR&E) global leadership team, with a direct reporting line to the Global Head of QR&E for Roche Diagnostics. This role serves as the senior global leader for Roche Diagnostics regarding policy architecture and high-stakes external stakeholder engagement, working closely with our regional and affiliate leaders. Leading dedicated global teams, you will position the organization as the authoritative voice for defining and harmonizing official policy across regulatory policy, healthcare, environmental, trade, and industry domains to drive Roche Diagnostics business priorities on key innovation and markets to serve. Furthermore, you will cultivate strategic alliances to advance these global positions, collaborating in lockstep with regional and country affiliates, Roche/Genetech Pharma and Group (as relevant) to implement a unified policy framework that accelerates enterprise business priorities for Roche Diagnostics. KEY ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES : Central Policy Setting & Governance Lead teams that serve as the central point for setting, maintaining, and governing Roche Diagnostics’ official policy positions on critical topics, including: Trade & Industry Policy: Navigating supply chain resilience, tariff/trade agreements, security and defense policies, and broader medtech industry standards. Regulatory Policy: Influencing global IVD/medical device regulations, standards harmonization, pre/post-market pathways, and emerging technology regulations (e.g., AI, software, digital healthcare, RUO, companion diagnostics and LDTs). Healthcare Policy: Shaping diagnostic valuation, funding models, personalized healthcare, and health system transformation. Environmental Policy: Partner with the Diagnostics Product Sustainability and Compliance Team to drive sustainable healthcare initiatives, green manufacturing policies, and circular economy expectations. Develop and cascade a streamlined, simplified matrix of global policy positions designed to give internal and external stakeholders absolute clarity on Roche Diagnostics’ stance. Champion enterprise-wide awareness regarding current and prospective healthcare trends influencing the business, while proactively managing high-stakes relationships with prominent global external bodies, including the WHO and OECD. Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement Act as the primary global representative and executive connector for Roche Diagnostics across regulatory entities, multilateral organisations, key external partners, and policy platforms outside the US. Partner closely with External Affairs International, Diagnostics US Government Affairs & Policy, Genentech’s Head of US Public Affairs & Market Access, and key members of the Roche Diagnostics Leadership Team to socialize, clarify, and align policy stances, driving a unified “One Roche” approach that optimizes broader enterprise leverage. Create, nurture, and leverage high-impact external affairs partnerships with industry associations, international non-governmental organizations, and patient advocacy coalitions to advance Roche Diagnostics’ strategic positions. Direct targeted advocacy strategies to ensure Roche Diagnostics proactively shapes the global policy agenda rather than reacting to it. Regional & Affiliate Alignment Affiliate Enabling: Work closely with regional and country-level teams to translate global policy positions into actionable local strategies, ensuring local execution directly advances global business priorities. Feedback Loop: Establish a robust global-to-local network to aggregate regional market insights, emerging country trends, and policy risks back into the central policy-setting process. Leadership & Culture Evolution Embody Roche’s leadership vision as a Visionary (setting clear policy direction), Architect (building agile policy framework mechanisms), Catalyst (forging external alliances and removing local barriers), and Coach (empowering global and regional policy leads). Cross-Functional Integration: Collaborate seamlessly across the broader QR&E function, Diagnostics Division, Diagnostics affiliates, Pharma Division and affiliates, Commercial, Legal, and Corporate Sustainability to ensure enterprise-wide policy cohesion. KNOWLEDGE/ SKILLS/ATTRIBUTES : Advanced degree (Master’s, Ph.D., or JD) in Public Policy, Health Policy, International Relations, Law, Environmental Affairs, or Life Sciences. Minimum 15+ years of global or multi-regional leadership experience in External Affairs, Policy Setting, or Government Relations within the In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Medical Device, or Pharmaceutical sectors. Proven track record of leading, mentoring, and developing high-performing global teams; skilled at building strong internal policy capabilities, fostering talent growth, and inspiring a collaborative culture within a complex, matrixed organization. Proven experience leading central policy development and successfully building multi-stakeholder partnerships across regulatory, healthcare, environmental, and trade domains. Demonstrated executive presence and media expertise, with a track record of influencing C-level executives, Board members, and key external global stakeholders while serving as an articulate spokesperson on complex policy matters. Exceptional strategic and analytical thinking skills with ability to simplify complex topics. Proven leadership skills, including the ability to lead in a complex and matrixed environment, building coalitions and advising senior executives. The ideal candidate brings: Exceptional ability to distill complex, multi-faceted issues (regulatory, environmental, trade) into simple, compelling, and unified policy stances. Outstanding track record acting as the principal spokesperson and negotiator with high-level external partners and public authorities. Strong capability to influence, align, and partner with regional and local country affiliates without direct hierarchical authority, uniting them around common business goals. Ability to balance long-term global policy shaping with the near-term commercial needs of regional business units. Location The primary location is Washington, D.C, with additional major DIA sites in Branchburg, NJ; Indianapolis, IN; Pleasanton, CA; Santa Clara, CA; Tucson, AZ; Basel and Rotkreuz (Switzerland); and Mannheim and Penzberg (Germany). Relocation benefits are available for this role. The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of Washington, D.C is $349,605.00 and $431,865.00. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits Where pay transparency applies, details are provided based on the primary posting location. For this role, the primary location is Washington DC. If you are interested in additional locations where the role may be available, we will provide the relevant compensation details later in the hiring process. Who we are A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact. Let’s build a healthier future, together. Roche is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company’s policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws. If you have a disability and need an accommodation in relation to the online application process, please contact us by completing this form Accommodations for Applicants. item.title: Executive Vice President, Public Affairs & Communications
item.description: Executive Vice President, Public Affairs & Communications Organization: Personal Care Products Council (PCPC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Job Type Full-time Description THE OPPORTUNITY The Personal Care Products Council (PCPC) is seeking an accomplished senior executive to lead the organization’s public affairs, policy communications, media relations, and external engagement efforts. Reporting directly to the President and CEO and serving as a member of PCPC’s executive leadership team, the EVP will help shape and execute the organization’s policy and communications strategy and serve as a highly credible voice for the cosmetics and personal care products industry. This is a policy-driven public affairs leadership role, not simply a communications position. The successful candidate will understand complex regulatory, political, and policy issues; translate them into compelling narratives and advocacy strategies; build consensus among diverse member companies; and effectively engage policymakers, media, industry partners, and other stakeholders. Given the importance of PCPC’s relationships with FDA, congressional policymakers, media, industry stakeholders, and other national trade associations, a strong preference will be given to candidates based in the Washington, DC area. THE MANDATE The EVP will: Lead strategy. Develop and execute an integrated public affairs, advocacy, communications, and external engagement strategy aligned with PCPC’s strategic priorities. Lead external engagement. Develop trusted relationships with media, industry organizations, coalitions, and other stakeholders. Represent PCPC publicly and serve as a principal external voice for the organization. Shape the narrative. Translate complex scientific, legal, regulatory, and policy issues into clear, persuasive messages that advance the industry’s interests and strengthen PCPC’s voice. Drive advocacy communications. Work closely with government affairs, regulatory, legal, scientific, and other PCPC teams to develop strategies around federal and state legislative and regulatory priorities. Build alignment. Navigate differing perspectives among member companies and build consensus around common industry positions. Cultivate strong relationships with key volunteer leaders and engage them effectively in PCPC’s advocacy efforts. Build trust and reputation. Establish and maintain a positive, credible reputation for PCPC and the overall industry among key stakeholders, partners, media, and other influential audiences. Earn trust through consistent, thoughtful engagement, sound judgment, transparency, and follow-through, recognizing that strong relationships and institutional credibility are essential to effective advocacy. Committee engagement. Serve as the staff lead for PCPC’s Communications Steering Committee, working closely with the Committee Chair and member company representatives to establish priorities, develop agendas, facilitate meetings, build consensus, and advance committee initiatives aligned with PCPC’s strategic objectives. Lead the function and drive partnership. Manage and develop the Public Affairs & Communications team; establish priorities, allocate resources, and oversee departmental performance. Develop and manage the department’s annual budget, including forecasting resource needs, establishing spending priorities, monitoring expenditures, and ensuring resources are aligned with PCPC’s strategic objectives. Build strong partnerships across PCPC and with external stakeholders and provide candid, strategic counsel to the CEO and Board. Manage issues and reputation. Anticipate emerging policy and reputational issues and partner with member companies to develop timely, coordinated responses to breaking news, crises, and other developments. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE The successful candidate will be able to take a complicated issue, quickly understand its substance and political dynamics, determine an appropriate advocacy strategy, develop the narrative, align PCPC’s membership, and effectively communicate the organization’s position to the right audience. This individual will be a trusted strategic counselor to the CEO and Board, an effective advocate for PCPC’s members, a collaborative leader within the organization, and a credible external voice for the industry. The successful candidate will also proactively shape the industry’s narrative by translating complex issues into clear, compelling stories that resonate with policymakers, media, and other audiences and strengthen understanding of the essential role of the beauty and personal care industry. THE IDEAL CANDIDATE The ideal candidate will be a seasoned public affairs executive who combines policy expertise, political judgment, communications excellence, executive presence, and the ability to build consensus and influence others. The candidate will bring: Deep Policy & Regulatory Expertise A sophisticated understanding of the U.S. federal and state policy and regulatory environment, with the ability to quickly understand complex issues and assess their political, regulatory, and reputational implications. Experience with the FDA and regulated industries is highly valued, as is familiarity with the regulatory environment affecting cosmetics and personal care products. Trade Association & Membership Experience Meaningful experience working in or closely with a trade association or membership organization, including an understanding of how to represent diverse member interests, develop consensus, and translate those interests into effective advocacy. Integrated Public Affairs Leadership A proven record of developing and executing integrated public affairs and policy communications strategies. The candidate should understand how communications, advocacy, government relations, coalition building, and stakeholder engagement work together to achieve policy objectives. Public Affairs Campaign Experience A track record of developing and executing public affairs campaigns that bring together advocacy, communications, coalition engagement, stakeholder outreach, and other tactics to advance policy or reputational objectives. Experience leading multi-channel campaigns and mobilizing diverse stakeholders around a common objective is preferred. Political Acumen Strong instincts for Washington and state political dynamics, including the ability to anticipate developments, understand stakeholder motivations, identify opportunities and risks, and determine when and how PCPC should engage. Executive Presence The credibility and confidence to engage effectively with CEOs, corporate executives, Board members, policymakers, journalists, association leaders, and other senior stakeholders. The candidate must be comfortable representing PCPC publicly and advising the CEO and Board candidly. Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement Demonstrated ability to build and sustain strategic relationships across a broad network of stakeholders, including coalition partners, NGOs, advocacy organizations, industry groups, scientific organizations and other external influencers. The candidate should have a track record of identifying opportunities for collaboration, aligning interests among diverse stakeholders, and leveraging partnerships to advance policy, advocacy, and reputation objectives while strengthening the industry’s voice and credibility. Leadership & Execution A demonstrated ability to lead and develop high-performing teams, establish priorities, manage resources, drive collaboration, and execute effectively in a fast-moving environment. The candidate should be strategic while remaining willing to engage directly in important issues and deliverables. Requirements EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS 15+years of progressively responsible experience in public affairs, policy communications, government relations, advocacy, or a related field. Significant experience working in a complex regulatory environment, ideally within a trade association, consumer products industry, public affairs firm, or government-facing organization. Demonstrated success developing and executing public affairs, advocacy, communications, media relations, and reputation-management strategies. Proven ability to support advocacy efforts through message development, coalition building, campaign strategy, and execution. Meaningful trade association or membership organization experience, with demonstrated success building consensus among diverse members and leaders. Strong familiarity with federal and state legislative and regulatory processes. Experience engaging directly with policymakers, regulators, government agencies, media, industry organizations, coalitions, and other external stakeholders. Proven experience serving as a spokesperson or senior external representative. Experience advising and working with a CEO, Board of Directors, C-suite executives, and other senior leaders. Demonstrated success leading, developing, and managing professional teams, including setting expectations, coaching and developing staff, managing performance, and building a collaborative, accountable team culture. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience preferred. WORK LOCATION & WORK ARRANGEMENT This position is based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area and operates under PCPC’s hybrid work model. The EVP will be expected to work regularly from PCPC’s Washington, DC office and maintain an in-person presence appropriate for the responsibilities of this executive leadership role. Given the position’s significant engagement with PCPC leadership, staff, member companies, policymakers, regulators, media, industry partners, and other stakeholders, the EVP must be available for in-person meetings and events in the Washington, DC area as business needs require. The position may also require domestic travel for member meetings, industry events, conferences, and other PCPC business. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS PCPC offers a competitiv

item.title: Director, Group Public & Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Director, Group Public & Regulatory Affairs Organization: Standard Chartered Bank Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/09/2026 Job Description: Job Summary • Standard Chartered is a leading international banking group, with a presence in some 50+ of the world’s most dynamic markets and serving clients in a further 85. Our purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, and our heritage and values expressed in our brand promise, Here for Good. Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong Stock Exchanges. • This role sits within Group Public & Regulatory Affairs (GPRA), which includes Government Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, and Strategic Policy Insights (SPI). The role sits in SPI and is responsible for delivering strategic, forward-looking policy insight across the United States and the Americas, with a focus on multilateral and supranational policy developments and engagement aligned to the Group’s strategy, footprint and purpose. Key Responsibilities Strategy • Shape and deliver policy engagement in Washington DC, the US and the Americas supporting the Bank’s broader policy priorities, global campaigns, and trade corridors. • Contribute to the Bank’s global approach to multilateral and supranational policy engagement, including via priority international platforms and institutions. Engage with multilateral, supranational and policy institutions in Washington, DC and beyond. Represent the Bank in external forums and policy discussions, positioning Standard Chartered as a constructive and credible participant. • Deliver policy positions, thought leadership and advocacy approaches aligned to Group objectives and external engagement priorities. Partner closely with Government Affairs and Regulatory Affairs teams in the US and across the Americas to align insight, positioning and engagement. • Strengthen external engagement (meetings, panels, events) on policy and advocacy topics, including supporting senior management engagement with policymakers, regulators and official-sector stakeholders. Draft and deploy briefing materials, talking points and key messages. • Support regional stakeholder planning, including inbound and outbound senior engagement involving the US, and global and regional initiatives on trade, market access and new business opportunities where policy engagement can add value. Business • Create and provide actionable, decision-oriented and scenario-based policy insight on US and Americas political, public policy and regulatory developments. Identify strategic implications, emerging risks and opportunities to support informed decision making across the Bank, in support of business and functional stakeholders. • Support regional and global leadership with policy-relevant perspectives, briefings and talking points, ensuring consistency with broader external narratives. • Help stakeholders understand and engage on global policy themes relevant to the Bank and contribute regional insight to broader analysis and engagement plans. • Work with in-country colleagues to monitor policy issues, develop aligned messaging where appropriate, and support effective execution of GPRA priorities. • Support engagement planning across the region, including priority travel and bilateral opportunities. Processes • Collaborate across GPRA to support consistent planning, coordination and continuous improvement. • Contribute to GPRA engagement in major global platforms and intergovernmental convenings. • Support development of policy products and outputs aligned to priority forums and global policy debates. • Act as a key link between US and Americas policy developments and broader SPI priorities. People & Talent • Work in partnership with Regulatory Affairs and Government Affairs colleagues across GPRA on insight, content and delivery. • Build effective partnerships within Strategy & Talent and across key partner functions. • Promote collaboration and high standards of conduct, embedding the Group Code of Conduct and Here for Good across day-to-day work. Risk Management • Ensure timely identification, analysis and dissemination of emerging public policy risks, and support appropriate internal and external engagement in response. • Work with GPRA and senior stakeholders to identify horizon risks that may materially affect the Bank. Governance • Support the development and operation of relevant Bank forums run by GPRA and SPI, as required. • Present to formal Bank governance forums and management meetings, as needed. Regulatory & Business Conduct • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct. • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct. • Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters. Key stakeholders • GPRA MT, Government Affairs and Regulatory Affairs • US & Americas senior management • Corporate Affairs, Brand & Marketing • Group Strategy • CIB (incl. Global Research) • Industry group / trade associations • External Stakeholders / policymakers Other Responsibilities • Embed Here for good and Group’s brand and values in GPRA. Perform other responsibilities assigned under Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures. Motivation • This role will work in a highly dynamic environment, working with senior internal stakeholders to build and deploy effective policy engagement strategies. • The role will engage across multiple external stakeholders relevant to policy and regulatory priorities, representing the Bank and driving outcomes. • The role and broader team is working to deliver a systematised model of engagement overseen by senior management. Skills and Experience Must-have Skills • Cross functional collaboration • Effective Communications • Regulatory Environment Other Skills • Managing Change • Planning; Tactical, Strategic • Industry Knowledge • Relationship Management Qualifications Key Experiences • Experience in the government, policy and/or regulatory system for banks is critical. It is ideal if the candidate has engaged with international platforms, multilateral forums, think tanks and trade associations. About Standard Chartered We’re an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we’ve worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you’re looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can’t wait to see the talents you can bring us. Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you’ll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion. Together we: Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term What we offer In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing. Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations. Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum. Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns. Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning. Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies – everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential. Recruitment Assessments Expected annual base pay range for the role is 153,476 USD to 230,214 USD. The final offer will be determined on an individualised basis using a number of variables, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience and education, internal relativity, and specific work location. At Standard Chartered Bank, Base pay is only part of the total compensation package. Discretionary variable pay and a range of attractive bank sponsored benefit programs are available and designed to foster employee overall health and well-being including, but not limited to, a best in class 401k plan with up to 8% employer match, robust medical plan coverage with employer funded Health Savings Accounts, inclusive family building benefits, and flexible/hybrid working arrangements for many of our positions subject to role specific considerations Some of our roles use assessments to help us understand how suitable you are for the role you’ve applied to. item.title: Regulatory Affairs Director, Large Loads and Market Policy
item.description: Regulatory Affairs Director, Large Loads and Market Policy Organization: National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/10/2026 Job Description Regulatory Affairs Director, Large Loads and Market Policy NRECA is a unique national trade association providing advocacy, financial services and business support services to over 900 consumer owned electric cooperatives across the country. NRECA employees are united by our mission, inclusive culture, collaborative workplace and commitment to service excellence. As a “best place to work” employer, we operate with integrity, transparency and a spirit of innovation. As a member of our Government Relations department, you will be joining a team that advocates on behalf of NRECA members on federal legislative and regulatory matters and in national policy forums and develops and trains our grassroots to impact policies at the federal, state and local level. NRECA has the top policy brand reputation among trade associations in Washington, D.C. for the last 4 consecutive years. Summary of Position NRECA seeks an experienced and strategic policy professional to advance its work on issues at the intersection of large-load growth, wholesale electricity markets, and electric cooperative policy. As electric demand growth accelerates due to data centers, advanced manufacturing, electrification, and other large energy users, electric cooperatives face new challenges and opportunities related to resource adequacy, transmission investment, generation planning, distribution infrastructure, reliability, and affordability. This position will help NRECA anticipate, assess, and influence policies governing how large new electric loads are integrated into the nation’s electric system and how associated costs, reliability obligations, and infrastructure investments are allocated. This position requires 5 full days in office with flexibility offered at the discretion of management. Key Responsibilities: Large Load Policy Collaborate with NRECA government affairs experts to monitor, assess, and develop policy positions on large electric loads, including data centers, advanced manufacturing, and other high-demand customers. Analyze regulatory, market, and policy developments and their impact on cooperative generation, transmission, and distribution systems. Evaluate issues involving load interconnection, infrastructure investment, cost allocation, reliability, resource adequacy, and resource planning. Engage with member cooperatives to understand operational challenges and opportunities associated with serving large electric loads and incorporate those insights into advocacy efforts. Support development of advocacy strategies and policy recommendations aligned with cooperative needs and evolving federal and market policies. Market Policy and Analysis Monitor and assess developments across organized wholesale electricity markets, including PJM, MISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE, and CAISO. Evaluate market approaches to large-load integration, resource adequacy, transmission planning, interconnection reform, market design, and infrastructure investment. Identify emerging trends, compare regional market practices, and assess implications for electric cooperatives. Partner with NRECA’s government relations team to develop policy positions on wholesale market, reliability, and resource adequacy issues. Advocacy and Strategy Development: Support engagement with federal agencies, regional market operators, Congress, the Administration, and other stakeholders on large-load and market policy issues. Anticipate emerging policy issues and help position NRECA to influence outcomes proactively. Develop policy papers, issue briefs, comments, presentations, member resources, and other advocacy materials. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Skills: 10+ years of relevant work experience demonstrating the ability to navigate emerging policy challenges where established frameworks and precedents may be limited. 7+ years written and oral policy advocacy in formal and informal agency and stakeholder proceedings. Experience building and working through coalitions and through outside consultants to advance advocacy goals. Bachelor’s degree required. Preferred Qualifications and Skills: Juris Doctor, Master’s or other advanced degree relating to area of responsibility preferred. Essential Physical Requirements: The worker is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading. Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg controls requires exertion of forces greater than that for sedentary work and the worker sits most of the time, the job is rated for light work. Salary Range: $186,000 – $230,000 annual salary Final compensation determined by individual qualifications, experience, and internal equity. Additional Requirement: The preceding job description has been written to reflect management’s assignment of essential functions. It does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status. NRECA is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with physical and mental disabilities. If you need special assistance or an accommodation while seeking employment, please e-mail [email protected] or call: 703-907-5992 – NRECA Arlington Human Resources. Please call 402-483-9275 – NRECA Lincoln Human Resources, for Lincoln, NE employment opportunities. We will make a determination on your request for reasonable accommodation on a case-by-case basis. item.title: Legislative Affairs Manager
item.description: Legislative Affairs Manager Organization: National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/10/2026 Job Description Legislative Affairs Manager NRECA is a unique national trade association providing advocacy, financial services and business support services to over 900 consumer owned electric cooperatives across the country. NRECA employees are united by our mission, inclusive culture, collaborative workplace and commitment to service excellence. As a “best place to work” employer, we operate with integrity, transparency and a spirit of innovation. As a member of our Government Relations department, you will be joining a team that advocates on behalf of NRECA members on federal legislative and regulatory matters and in national policy forums and develops and trains our grassroots to impact policies at the federal, state and local level. NRECA has the top policy brand reputation among trade associations in Washington, D.C. for the last 4 consecutive years. Summary of Position The person in this role oversees government relations activities across a portfolio of legislative issues relevant to NRECA members. They will develop a deep understanding of assigned issue areas as well as the advocacy toolkit. They will promote and influence federal policies, legislation, and actions favorable to rural electric cooperatives and related programs and issues on assigned portfolio of issues. This position requires 5 full days in office with flexibility offered at the discretion of management. Key Responsibilities Establishes and maintains relationships with Members of Congress and their staff. Presents electric cooperative positions and priorities to inform and persuade stakeholders. Uses knowledge of various advocacy strategies and tools, including grassroots, grass tops, and leveraging member involvement, to advance legislation and policy goals related to issue portfolio. Develops subject matter expertise of policy and legislative issues and works closely with professionals across the association to advance legislative priorities that benefit the NRECA membership. Uses understanding of issues to engage, influence and inform lawmakers and NRECA stakeholders. Reviews, analyzes and summarizes pending legislation which may impact electric cooperative members on assigned policy areas. Prepares and hones messages to assist lawmakers and staff to understand NRECA’s policy priorities. Presents lawmakers and Directors with timely and concise updates related to pending legislation. Works with Directors to draft legislation in accordance with policy resolutions of the Association. Conducts advocacy efforts in support of policy resolutions and assists in the formulation of policy resolutions that guide strategies on assigned legislative issues. Prepares and hones messages to assist Members of Congress and their staffs to understand the policy priorities of NRECA and the impact of policy on electric cooperative members. Develops a deep understanding of co-op landscape and issues to leverage issue-area knowledge and advocacy skillset on behalf of NRECA members. Creates and cultivates relationships with member cooperatives, including statewide managers, G&T managers and distribution managers, providing legislative updates and guidance while channeling their active participation in NRECA’s advocacy efforts. item.title: Content and Communications Specialist
item.description: Content and Communications Specialist Organization: Partnership for Civil Justice Fund (PCJF) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/10/2026 Full-time position, potentially geographically remote in Eastern time zone with strong preference given for location in Washington, D.C. The Washington, D.C. office operates on a hybrid schedule. Who We Are and What We Do: The Partnership for Civil Justice Fund (PCJF) brings high-impact free speech, civil rights and constitutional rights litigation and provides criminal defense to those who are targeted for prosecution because of their First Amendment-protected viewpoints and advocacy for justice. We protect and advance the rights of protestors to organize, assemble, and demand justice around the country. For over 30 years, the PCJF has been a leading voice in the legal fight to defend democracy and advance constitutional rights and social justice by litigating landmark civil rights, civil liberties, and First Amendment cases and by providing legal defense to justice movement organizations and activists targeted for their First Amendment-protected speech and activities. Our litigation work is integrated with outreach, education, and advocacy in partnership with other civil rights lawyers, affected communities, activists, and organizations in racial, social, and environmental justice movements. Our work is focused ultimately on creating meaningful social, political, and legal changes and dismantling systems of repression. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., with a West Coast office in the Bay Area, we litigate around the country. The Position If you are passionate about the mission of the organization and digital media, design, and storytelling we want to hear from you! We are hiring an experienced and creative Content and Communications specialist to join our team. We are looking for a sharp, meticulous, creative content creator who is an excellent writer and who possesses graphic and video design skills. The position requires understanding the importance of the underlying issues at stake and being able to distill those issues and elevate the narrative and voices that define the struggles for justice and constitutional rights, all in an active, compelling, engaging and professional voice. Previous experience and work in aligned advocacy and/or First Amendment legal issues is a plus. We are looking for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, team-centric environment and is a dynamic self-starter. A key member of our team, the Content and Communications Specialist will work closely with the Executive and Legal Directors to execute the organization’s communication strategy and will also collaborate with our grassroots and coalition partners, locally and nationally, to amplify crucial issues in the struggles for civil rights and free speech. Key Responsibilities: Translate our work and messaging into social, email, web and other content that is polished, professional, and compelling while maintaining legal accuracy and message precision. Draft and post concise and effective communications to grow our audiences including activists, constituents, media, and the general public, including press releases, emails, newsletters, and social media posts (Instagram, BlueSky, X, and Facebook). Increase social media engagement and following. Create and publish visual and written content at volume weekly to include social media posts, direct to camera scripts and regular website updates. Write, shoot, and produce short, engaging, and timely videos, including attorney explainer videos, that dive into key focus issues. Locate images that accompany and resonate with the topical messages of each post. The ability to produce reels and video product in rapid response to current events is essential. Develop compelling narratives that demonstrate the organization’s expertise and the importance of both the constitutional rights at stake and the social change issues underlying our impact litigation and defense. Understand and adopt the organization’s unique voice and identity to develop impactful messaging advancing our mission and priorities. Tell the stories of our cases, our courageous clients, their fights for justice, and the impactful and often groundbreaking legal issues undergirding those fights. Have a campaign mindset and facilitate the organization’s ability to impact and inform national discourse in response to breaking events to achieve the organization’s priorities and programmatic objectives. Create and execute online campaigns and calls to action, toolkits and other educational, engagement, and outreach efforts. Be constantly attuned to the news, to government repression of dissent and to issues of legal importance in order to propose communications and respond to breaking events. Develop and execute a communications calendar and create content nimbly and in rapid response to breaking events and critical issues. This involves working with partner organizations, mapping out activation moments, amplification requests, scheduling posts for algorithmic optimization, and relating all content back to the organizational strategies. Be an all-hands person who possess a roll up your sleeves, no job too small approach to tasks. Monitor analytics and compile reports, make recommendations on digital communications strategy and optimization of digital presence; seek to grow communities and reach. Articulate objective criteria for the success of our engagement and communication strategy. Maintain the organization’s constituent and press lists and database through the CRM system. Keep the website up to date, including uploading news and press releases, refreshing visuals and maintaining site organization. Coordinate with website developer to fix technical issues. Track media coverage of our work as well as online discussion and news related surrounding law, policy, case developments, politics, and other issues related to the organization’s work. Chronicle organization and social justice movement activities with visuals by capturing images on the ground at social justice events, protests, and actions. Key Requirements and Qualifications At least 3 years of professional experience in communications, graphics production, social media posts, public facing communications, short videos, and/or other demonstrable skills that show polished and well written content in the context of non-profit work, advocacy, or a related field. An excellent writer possessing the ability to reflect the organization’s voice and tone while engaging with multiple audiences and to move between the different voices needed for different platforms. Ability to write in rapid response to events in an engaging and active manner, with the ability to distill, persuade, and advocate. Excellent editing and proofreading skills, with keen attention to detail. Able to translate complex legal and policy language into understandable messages that inform and engage. Must be able to produce content that is professionally presented and that does not require others to proofread. Ability to maintain a high volume of tasks at one time, to multi-task, and to pivot immediately to breaking issues with adaptability. Demonstrated ability to plan, coordinate, and juggle a variety of detailed outreach projects, sometimes under a very tight deadline. Demonstrate initiative, including proactively identifying and addressing issues and making recommendations. Experience working with social justice movements preferred. High level of awareness as to current political/social issues and grassroots movements for justice, with a passion and talent for creating stories that move public opinion in favor of and inspire people to take action. Strong proficiency with social media, including experience maintaining organizational social media accounts and familiarity with emerging trends in digital organizing. Demonstrated graphic design skills and the ability to produce brochures, one-pagers, newsletters, reports, infographics, etc. Experience in developing and growing networks of digital supporters and capacity to develop an effective plan to do so. Mastery or high proficiency with graphic design and video editing software such as Canva, Adobe InDesign, CapCut, etc. Experience with WordPress and CRM software preferred. Experience with development a plus. Familiarity with free speech and/or civil rights legal issues a plus. Demonstrated ability to solve problems, anticipate next steps, take initiative, exercise discretion, and apply sound judgment. Ability and willingness to perform occasional evening and weekend work in response to breaking events, justice uprisings, or major legal case deadlines or outcomes. Consistent monitoring of incoming communications emails and Teams messages to ensure that critical press messages or breaking events are not missed. Outstanding interpersonal skills, sense of humor, and ability to work collaboratively with colleagues to get the information, input, and perspective necessary to produce quality work. APPLICATION DEADLINE Applications will be considered on a rolling basis with the priority deadline of October 16th. START DATE: ASAP SALARY The salary is expected to be within the range of $70,000 – $80,000 and will depend on the applicant’s experience and qualifications. Persons with extensively greater experience than listed above will be considered for a higher range. Benefits include outstanding health and dental insurance that is 100% employer paid; 15 days of paid vacation; additional personal and sick leave; 11 paid federal holidays; a 401(k) plan with employer contribution (after one year of service); Life insurance and AD&D insurance; Short Term Disability insurance; Long Term Disability insurance; and available vision plan. Please send a cover letter detailing why you are interested in this position at the PCJF, your resume, and a link to a portfolio showing past digital content that you’ve created (graphics, social media copy, e

item.title: Digital Marketing Director
item.description: Digital Marketing Director Organization: Project Slingshot Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/10/2026 About Us Project Slingshot exists to drag the truth into the light and break apart Big Ag’s deliberately constructed illusion. Job Description This is a remote position. About Project Slingshot Project Slingshot is a global nonprofit organization dedicated to ending factory farming. We do this by exposing the lies, cruelty, and power of Big Ag through disruptive campaigns that cut through the noise, capture public attention, and build unstoppable momentum for change. We’re unapologetic, fast-moving, and impact-driven. We don’t just want to participate in the conversation – we want to change it. The Role As Digital Marketing Director (US) you will lead our US marketing strategy, making sure our campaigns are not just seen, but felt. You’ll build and run high-impact digital, email and paid media programs that mobilize supporters, grow audiences, and put Slingshot in front of the people who can shift this fight. You’ll work closely with our global team, but with the autonomy to localize and innovate for the US context – ensuring every piece of content, every email and every ad campaign resonates, drives action, and delivers ambitious, measurable outcomes. You will know how to leverage cultural moments that help to seed marketing narratives among targeted audiences, and influence them to act. In this role you will manage a Digital Marketing & Social Media Manager to help drive engagement across our marketing and social activities in support of our campaign efforts. This is a remote position based in the US. What You’ll Do Digital strategy & execution Design and implement bold, high-impact digital and social media strategies tailored to US audiences, reaching diverse and varied communities. Drive paid media campaigns (primarily META and other key platforms), ensuring ROI and audience growth. Use data, testing and insights to evolve strategies and stay ahead of trends. Localize global campaign moments for the US market without losing the force of the original idea. Own the US marketing calendar and make sure it lines up with campaign and creative plans. Email & CRM Lead segmented email marketing campaigns that drive engagement, action and donor conversion. Build automations and journeys that nurture supporters through the funnel. Constantly refine audience segmentation and personalization. Partner with fundraising to make sure marketing and giving journeys reinforce each other. Content & storytelling Oversee creation of disruptive, compelling and on-brand digital content (copy, visuals, video). Craft impactful storytelling and copywriting that inspires, provokes and mobilizes. Ensure consistency and quality across all channels. Brief and work closely with our creative team to turn campaign strategy into work that travels. Cultivate influences relationships, partnerships and collaborations that deliver innovative story telling and expand audience reach and engagement. Analytics & optimization Monitor KPIs across social, email and digital campaigns. Produce actionable insights from analytics to inform strategy. Use performance data to test, iterate and continually improve. Report clearly to leadership on what is working, what is not, and what you are changing as a result. Leadership & collaboration Build and mentor a Digital Marketing & Social Media Manager. Collaborate closely with global colleagues to align strategies, share learnings and identify opportunities. Ensure US digital campaigns amplify and complement Project Slingshot’s global campaigns. Manage agency, freelance, influencer and platform relationships in the US market. Requirements We’d love someone who: Has significant experience in digital marketing, campaign strategy or movement-building – ideally with a cause-driven brand or a bold advocacy group. Is deeply familiar with social justice messaging, digital organizing and content-led engagement strategies. Has led teams and knows how to develop teams to deliver results. Has proven success in social media, paid ads and email/CRM strategies. Knows META Ads Manager, email marketing platforms (e.g. GetResponse, Mailchimp, Campaign Monitor or similar), analytics tools and automation systems in depth. Is skilled at using audience insights to craft strategies that inspire action. Writes strong copy, with a knack for storytelling that is bold, disruptive and emotionally compelling. Has a track record of driving audience growth and measurable impact. Is data-driven, experimental, and never satisfied with “good enough”. Brings knowledge or experience of farmed animal advocacy, broader animal protection, or high-profile nonprofit campaigning – with the ability to translate complex issues into powerful, public-facing narratives. Is passionate about Project Slingshot’s mission and hungry to play a part in ending factory farming. Success looks like Growing audience size and engagement across platforms, with clear evidence of what is driving it. Lead acquisition, conversion rates and supporter retention are all improving. High-impact US campaigns are landing – measured in reach, earned media and actions taken. Internal marketing processes are strong and cross-team collaboration is working without friction. Slingshot has real cultural presence and brand salience across US social justice spaces. Benefits Location & Working Pattern This role is remote and based in the United States. Project Slingshot is a fully remote organization. Most collaboration happens online, and you will have regular overlap with colleagues in the UK. There will occasionally be opportunities and expectations to travel for team meet-ups, campaign shoots, conferences, planning sessions and other in-person events. Travel costs will be covered by Project Slingshot. The Practical Details Location: Remote, US,, with some travel for in-person meetings Reports to: Chief Executive Officer, Co-Founders Compensation: $80,000 – $100,000 per year. Placement within the range is based on experience and location. Benefits: Paid time off, paid holidays, pension contribution The Application Process Step 1: submit your application here . You are also welcome to submit a cover letter and any examples of previous work. Step 2: our team will review all applications and arrange initial screenings Step 3: shortlisted candidates will be invited to multiple round interviews, and final candidates may also be invited to a paid test exercise. Our Commitment to an Inclusive Culture We strongly encourage people of every color, orientation, age, gender, origin, and ability to apply. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and harassment-free environment where everyone can feel part of our team and are supported to be able to deliver their best work. If you are interested in the position but do not meet the full criteria, we still encourage you to apply as we do not expect all candidates meet the criteria 100%. item.title: Communications and Media Relations Manager
item.description: Communications and Media Relations Manager Organization: European Cyclists’ Federation (ECF) Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 The European Cyclists’ Federation (ECF) is looking for a Communications and Media Relations Manager to join its Brussels-based team. About the European Cyclists’ Federation (ECF) • We are the single European umbrella federation of member-based civil society organisations advocating and working for more and better cycling. • We promote cycling as a sustainable and healthy means of transport and leisure. • With more than 60 member organisations from over 40 countries, we harness the power of European cycling movements as the only civil society advocacy voice at the pan-European level. • We are based in Brussels and our roots are in Europe, but the challenges we face are global, and we are ready to meet them as the world’s largest and best-known cyclists’ advocacy federation. About the position The Communications and Media Relations Manager leads ECF’s communications and visibility, while also supporting EuroVelo and Velo-city brands, towards EU institutions, the media, project partners and international stakeholders. You will report to the CEO, manage the Communications team, and work closely with the other teams across ECF to ensure that our messages are clear and that the voice of cyclists is heard and acted upon by policy- and decision-makers in Brussels, across Europe and beyond. A) Communications Strategy & Planning • Develop, implement and evaluate the annual communications and media relations plan, aligning activities with ECF’s organisational priorities and strategic objectives • Ensure consistency of messaging across all channels and audiences • Manage and allocate team resources according to priorities (currently 2.5 FTE) • Coordinate ECF’s visibility at key conferences and events, monitor speaking engagements and booth preparations where applicable • Lead on the drafting, design and publication of the ECF Annual Report B) Content Creation & Editorial Management • Oversee the creation of high-quality content (news, articles, speeches, newsletters, reports) based on ECF advocacy priorities and knowledge products • Develop core messaging and campaigns to support our advocacy and fundraising efforts • Plan and create content (written and visual) for ECF’s audiences, including the website, newsletters, social media, and press • Oversee communications for EU-funded projects and contribute to relevant deliverables and reporting C) Media Relations • Build and maintain strong relationships with journalists, media outlets, and opinion leaders • Draft and distribute press releases, media pitches, and statements • Coordinate media interviews, briefings, and press events • Monitor media coverage and manage reputational issues and crisis communications when needed D) Digital & Internal Communications • Manage ECF’s website, mailing system and digital communication channels (CMS, CRM, Brevo, newsletters, press releases, LinkedIn, Instagram, Bluesky) • Develop a digital communications strategy to ensure high engagement and grow ECF’s audience • Support all ECF teams with key messages, talking points, and presentations Who are we looking for? Background: • A degree in a relevant field and/or relevant professional qualifications in communications or journalism • At least 5 years’ experience in a communications role, e.g. in advocacy, public administration, PR consultancy or similar, with a proven track record • Experience in advocacy, campaigning and media relations • Experience managing a team • Experience working in an international and/or membership-based organisation is a plus Competencies, skills and attributes: • Highly motivated, open-minded, proactive and results-oriented • A team player who works well in diverse teams, and is an effective networker • Ability to plan and structure communications activities to maximise their impact • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English (near-native proficiency) • Design and social media skills and ability to explore different formats for different audiences and objectives (visuals, videos and graphics) Must have at recruitment • Proven experience in communications and media relations • Experience in advocacy communications and/or campaigning • Excellent writing and editing skills • Strong command of English What we offer ECF offers an employment package in line with similar non-governmental organisations based in Brussels, including a gross monthly salary of €4,200– €4,800, depending on relevant experience. Benefits include flexible working hours, up to 20 legal and 10 extra-legal vacation days (pro rata), public transport and cycling allowances, a work-from-home allowance, lunch vouchers, eco-cheques and an extra-legal pension scheme. How to apply? Please send your CV and cover letter in one PDF in English to [email protected] with the subject line: ‘First Name Last Name – Communications and Media Relations Manager’. Your application has to include: • Cover letter in English (max. 1 page) • CV in English (max. 2 pages) Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Closing date for applications: 23 October 2026, EOB. The preferred starting date is the end of November 2026, depending on the selected candidate’s availability. Thank you in advance to all those who take the time to apply for this position. Due to the high number of applicants expected, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Equal opportunity ECF is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of racial or ethnic origin, opinions, beliefs, gender, sexual orientation, health condition or disability Earn a certificate with the Council!
