item.title: Head of Unit HAGRID
item.description: Head of Unit HAGRID Organization: CEPS (Centre for European Policy Studies) Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 CEPS is seeking an outstanding Head of Unit to strengthen its research and policy engagement activities on European and global health, the pharmaceutical sector, and biotechnology. The successful candidate will contribute to CEPS’ mission providing independent, evidence-based policy analysis and recommendations to European and international decisionmakers. They will play a leading role in developing research agendas, building partnerships, acquiring research funding and contributing to high-level policy debates on the future of Europe’s economy, society and technological development. About us Founded in Brussels in 1983, CEPS (Centre for European Policy Studies) is a leading think tank and forum for debate on EU affairs, which has been consistently ranked among the world’s top 10 best think tanks. One of CEPS’ distinguishing features is its strong in-house research capacity and an extensive international network of partner institutes. CEPS’ funding comes from a variety of sources, mainly research grants and service contracts, but also from membership and conference fees. The CEPS GRID Unit (Global Governance, Regulation, Innovation and the Digital economy) was launched in January 2005 to explore policy and regulatory challenges in the areas of better regulation, the EU internal market, global governance, innovation policy, digital policy, and industrial policy. HAGRID (Health, Agriculture, Research, Innovation and Development) was originally established as a research team within the GRID Unit, focusing on the intersection of these areas. As the team has grown in both size and scope, HAGRID is now becoming a dedicated unit within CEPS. HAGRID’s research covers a wide variety of topics, including global health security governance and pandemic prevention, preparedness and response; global health systems and global health diplomacy, including the EU’s role in global health; EU health legislation and governance (e.g. European Beating Cancer Plan, European Health Data Space, Cardiovascular Health Plan…); health innovation and technologies; women’s health; the pharmaceutical sector; and One Health, among others. Main tasks • Lead, support and supervise a team, addressing recruitment needs, fostering well-being, and ensuring a collaborative work environment. • Secure sustainable funding through diverse sources, including client-based projects, foundation grants, and research programmes. • Manage the unit’s budget and resources to ensure financial sustainability and effective project execution, in collaboration with the Director of Finance and Administration. • Allocate human resources efficiently to projects, balancing deadlines and quality standards. Place du Congrès 1, B-1000 Brussels, Belgium • www.ceps.eu • Tel: 32 (0)2 229 39 11 • VAT: BE 0424.123.986 • Oversee performance management, including putting forward recommendations for promotion and salary adjustments in line with CEPS’ salary scales, and making recommendations regarding contract renewals. • Define and lead the unit’s research agenda, delivering high-quality research. • Ensure a steady flow of research outputs, including op-eds, policy briefs, and other publications, while contributing to communication activities like podcasts and events. • Maintain the quality and relevance of research conducted by team members, ensuring alignment with CEPS’ objectives. • Participate in CEPS Leadership Committee meetings and organisational activities to promote collaboration and integration. • Represent the unit and CEPS at public events and conferences, establishing yourself as a leading expert in your field. Your background and qualifications • You hold a PhD in economics, political science, public policy, international relations, law, public health, innovation studies, science and technology studies, engineering, or another relevant discipline. In exceptional cases, we could consider candidates not holding a PhD but having significant comparable research experience. • You have a minimum of eight years of relevant professional experience in research, policy analysis, public administration, international organisations, consulting, industry or related fields. • You possess recognised expertise in at least one of the following areas: European and global health policy and governance, pharmaceutical policy, biotechnology policy, and governance of emerging health technologies. • You have a strong record of publications and policy-relevant analytical work. • You have experience leading complex research projects and multidisciplinary teams. • You have a strong understanding of European policymaking and governance. • You have experience engaging with senior policymakers, regulators, business leaders, researchers and other stakeholders. • You have a proven track record in acquiring externally funded research projects, building partnerships and developing research networks. • You have excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Knowledge of additional languages is an asset. Profile of the ideal candidate • You have a relevant experience in managing and leading a team. • You combine intellectual excellence with a strong commitment to policy impact. • You are capable of identifying emerging policy challenges and developing innovative research agendas. • You can connect developments in technology, innovation, health, industry, competitiveness and geopolitics into coherent policy analysis. • You are entrepreneurial and able to build new activities, partnerships and funding opportunities. • You are an effective leader, mentor and team player. • You are comfortable working across disciplines and engaging with diverse stakeholder communities. • You can manage multiple priorities while maintaining high standards of analytical quality. • You are kind with a deep respect for diversity, and a strong sense of empathy towards colleagues. • You enjoy teamwork and are open to giving and receiving feedback. • You are enthusiastic about contributing to CEPS’ role as a leading independent voice in European and global policy debates. What CEPS offers We offer full-time employment, for an indefinite duration. The salary is in accordance with the CEPS salary scale. We also offer a benefits package (group and hospitalisation insurance, meal tickets, public transport reimbursement, 20 days legal holiday entitlement per year plus an additional two weeks during the ChristmasNew Year period when CEPS is closed, as well asthe possibility to telework in Belgium and 20 days per calendar year of teleworking from abroad). We would like the preferred candidate to start as soon as possible. The role will be based in Brussels. Career prospects This position offers a unique opportunity to shape policy debates on some of the most consequential challenges facing Europe and the world, including technological transformation, innovation, industrial competitiveness and global health. The successful candidate will enjoy substantial intellectual autonomy in developing research agendas, building partnerships and pursuing new funding opportunities, while benefiting from CEPS’ strong reputation, extensive network and convening power. The position provides direct access to European and international policymakers, business leaders, researchers and civil society organisations, creating opportunities to generate policy impact and contribute to high-level debates. CEPS also offers a Learning and Development Programme and encourages continuous professional growth through leadership of major research initiatives, international collaborations and engagement with emerging policy challenges. More information For further information about the position, please contact Andrea Renda, Director of Research, [email protected] Application and deadline Applicants are requested to: • Complete and submit this r ecruitment form by 25 October 2026, 23:59 CET; • Send their CV (in English) to [email protected] by 25 October 2026, 23:59 CET, with “Head of Unit – HAGRID” in the subject line. Please include a list of your publications,specifying your role in previous research projects, and the names and contact details of at least two referees (including your current or last employer). Shortlisted candidates may be asked to produce one or two letters of recommendation. For the CV, consider using the Europass template (https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/). Applications received after the deadline, incomplete applications, or applications that do not follow the above instructions will not be taken into consideration. Pre-selected candidates are invited to a short online interview. Based on these first interviews, shortlisted candidates will be invited to an in-person or online interview. CV and personal data of non-selected candidates are not shared with anyone outside CEPS and will be deleted immediately after the recruitment process. For more information, read our privacy policy available on the CEPS website. Even if you do not strictly have all the necessary competences for this role but you believe your experience and skills could be valuable and enable you to fulfil the tasks required, we would still highly recommend that you submit an application. CEPS is an equal opportunities employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all staff. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. item.title: Public Affairs Director
item.description: Public Affairs Director Organization: European Plastics Converters (EuPC) Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 About EuPC European Plastics Converters (EuPC) is the EU-level trade association representing the interests of plastics converting companies in Europe. Based in Brussels, EuPC brings together 24 national plastics associations and European sectoral organisations, representing more than fifty thousand converting companies that supply plastic products into key value chains such as packaging, building & construction, automotive & transport, and technical parts. EuPC’s mission is to provide a strong, united voice for plastics converters in EU policy debates, advance the transition towards a circular and climate-neutral economy, and ensure a competitive, innovation-friendly regulatory environment for the plastics converting industry. https://www.plasticsconverters.eu/ Role Purpose The Public Affairs Director reports to the Director General and drives EuPC’s political outreach and institutional engagement at EU level, advancing the interests of the European plastics converting industry across core policy files affecting polymers and their key end-use applications. The role requires shaping public affairs strategies and executing advocacy campaigns to represent the European plastics converters industry across a network of EU institutions, Member State representations, other industry associations, and the broader stakeholder community. Key Responsibilities EU institutional outreach and advocacy Drive high-level engagement with the European Commission, European Parliament, and Council. Position EuPC as a credible, trusted partner, build and maintain long-term relationships with policymakers, partners and opinion leaders; Represent EuPC in external meetings, roundtables, or conferences to enhance the sector’s visibility. Policy positioning, stakeholder management and Communications Monitor political developments and anticipate impacts; provide actionable intelligence and recommendations to the Director General and internal governance. Translate EuPC priorities into clear advocacy strategies, stakeholder maps, and engagement plans. Shape cross-association alignment by building coalitions and joint positions with European and national associations, ensuring consistency and leverage. Coordinate and draft position papers, policy briefings, presentations, newsletters and speeches. Internal coordination and governance support Ensure an effective two-way flow between advocacy efforts and member priorities, securingalignment across and among EuPC Divisions (Packaging, Building & Construction, and Mobility),internal committees, and team members. Support the Director General in preparing institutional engagements, strategic messaging, andexecutive-level meetings. Required Experience and Qualifications Minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience in EU public affairs, including working inassociations, public affairs consultancy, corporate in-house teams or institutions. Proven track record in designing advocacy strategies, executing engagement with EU officials,including successful delivery of advocacy outcomes. A well-established political network and a solid understanding of the EU regulatory and policylandscape impacting the sector, including developments in competitiveness, trade, circularity,innovation, environmental, and product legislation. Understanding of the plastics industry, including policy drivers and market dynamics across majorend-use applications. Master’s degree (or equivalent) Political Science, European Studies, Law, or a related field. Excellent command of English (additional EU languages are an asset). Core Competencies High-impact stakeholder engagement and political judgement; confident at senior level. Strategic planning with strong execution discipline; able to prioritise in a fast-moving environment. Persuasive communication: clear, concise writing and strong verbal advocacy. Coalition-building and diplomacy; comfortable aligning diverse member interests into workable positions. What we offer Full-time contract (40h/week). Starting Date: January 2027 The opportunity to contribute to shaping EU policies and to represent the interests of a large and innovative industrial sector at European level in a dynamic and collaborative working environment. A supportive and inclusive team culture that values initiative, self-starter spirit, and collaboration. A flexible working environment, including hybrid working arrangements where applicable. Competitive remuneration and benefits, in line with experience and qualifications. If interested, please submit your CV and a cover letter to [email protected] use Subject: PAD_Surname_Name_Application_2027 Application period ends 23rd October, 2026, at 6PM CET Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Principal Adviser, Parliamentary Strengthening
item.description: Principal Adviser, Parliamentary Strengthening Organization: International IDEA - The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 Context The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA) is an intergovernmental organisation dedicated to promoting sustainable democracy worldwide. Its mission is to strengthen democratic institutions and processes. The Institute serves as a catalyst for democracy building by offering global comparative knowledge, resources, tools and policy proposals, and by supporting democratic reforms in response to specific national requests. Its areas of work encompass democracy assessment and strategic foresight, electoral processes, constitutional governance and rule of law, political participation and representation, including parliamentary strengthening and money in politics, as well as democratic resilience and the intersection of democracy with gender and inclusion, climate change, technology, including AI, and security. Global Programmes implements International IDEA’s institutional areas of work and develops global comparative knowledge, approaches and tools to support democratic institutions and processes. It works closely with Regional and Country Programmes to support the application of global knowledge and expertise in different contexts. Parliamentary strengthening is a core component of International IDEA’s work on political participation and representation. Through partnerships with parliaments, parliamentary networks, practitioners and other stakeholders, the Institute seeks to strengthen parliamentary capacity and independence while promoting more effective, representative and accountable parliamentary institutions. Its flagship parliamentary strengthening portfolio, Inter Pares, funded by the European Union, supports these efforts by working with parliaments around the world to strengthen their capacity and independence. The Principal Adviser, Parliamentary Strengthening serves as International IDEA’s most senior expert in this field, providing intellectual leadership, setting the strategic direction and safeguarding the quality of the organisation’s parliamentary strengthening work. The role serves as the principal point of contact for Regional Programmes, partners and donors, and identifies strategic opportunities for engagement, including at the intersection of parliamentary strengthening and International IDEA’s broader thematic areas. Duties and Responsibilities Intellectual leadership for Inter Pares. Provides expert substantive guidance for the Inter Pares portfolio as its senior adviser, keeping the work substantively strong and coherent; New opportunities and partnerships. Identifies and develops new opportunities for International IDEA to engage meaningfully on parliamentary strengthening, including where it connects with the organization’s other areas of work, such as elections, political finance, gender equality, constitution building, climate change and democratic resilience; cultivates strategic partnerships and positions International IDEA to secure new funding and programme opportunities; Resource mobilization and donor engagement. Leads and supports resource mobilization efforts by identifying funding opportunities, engaging with existing and prospective donors, and contributing to fundraising strategies that advance parliamentary strengthening priorities; Portfolio development. Sets and safeguards the quality standard for parliamentary strengthening work across GP. Provides substantive guidance in the design and development of new project proposals; Support to regions. Supports International IDEA’s regional and country teams with expertise on parliamentary strengthening, so their work is well-grounded and consistent; Partner network. Maintains and strengthens International IDEA’s network of parliamentary partners, practitioners, and expert institutions; Contribution to collective leadership. Contributes to shared decisions and direction across International IDEA’s Global Programmes as a member of the Global Programmes Leadership Team; General Profile A recognised expert in parliamentary strengthening, with a strong professional reputation, publications, and standing in relevant expert networks; Able to set the direction and safeguard the quality of complex, multi-country work, and to guide the teams that deliver it without directly managing them; A credible, trusted representative of the organization with donors and partners, and in public and policy settings, with a strong understanding of the priorities, structures and ways of working of the European Union as the programme’s principal donor; Excellent communicator – in writing and in person – able to engage effectively with a wide range of institutional audiences and to build and sustain collaborative relationships across organizational boundaries; Strong strategic judgement, with the ability to spot and develop new opportunities and partnerships, and to act on them proactively; Acts in accordance with International IDEA’ s core values; Respect, Integrity and Professionalism; Integrates gender equality, diversity, and social inclusion (GEDSI) considerations into all tasks and activities, in alignment with the Institute’s Core Values and commitment to the GEDSI policy. Willing to travel, approximately 25% of the time Reporting line Director, Global Programmes Education and Experience Advanced university degree in political science, international relations, law, development studies, or a related field; A minimum 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in democracy support, governance, political participation and representation, parliamentary strengthening, or a closely related field, including substantial experience working on parliamentary development and democratic institutions; Demonstrated experience providing senior-level substantive advice and technical expertise on parliamentary strengthening, democratic governance, political representation, or related areas, preferably in an international or multi-country context; Proven experience cultivating and managing relationships with bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, development partners, parliamentary institutions and other key stakeholders; Demonstrated experience in the design, development and implementation of complex programmes or projects, including experience working across countries, regions and institutional contexts; Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across organizational units and thematic areas, including providing advice and expertise to Regional and Country Programmes and identifying connections between parliamentary strengthening and other areas of democratic governance; Excellent command of English; knowledge of another International IDEA working language (French, Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese or Russian) is an asset. Terms of Contract: International Post Fixed term appointment for two (2) years. Remuneration – EUR 7 258 NET per month + benefits Applying for this position: Applications should be submitted no later than 23:59 (CEST) 18 October 2026. Please note that all applications must be made in English. Selection Process: Evaluation of qualified candidates will include an assessment and up to two (2) interviews. Candidates selected to proceed to the next stage of the process will be contacted once all applications have been carefully reviewed. All candidates will be notified of the status of their application via email once the process has been finalized Use of AI in Recruitment International IDEA places strong emphasis on human input in recruitment. Candidates must disclose any use of AI tools. All application materials, written assessments, and interview responses (as applicable) must be entirely human-generated and reflect the candidate’s own knowledge, skills, and experience. The use of AI to generate content or misrepresent qualifications is not permitted. AI‑powered assistive technologies (such as screen readers or speech‑to‑text tools) may be used for accessibility purposes to ensure equal access to the recruitment process International IDEA is an equal opportunity employer which seeks to further diversify its staff in terms of gender, culture and nationality Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Associate litigation & investigations (junior to mid-level)
item.description: Associate litigation & investigations (junior to mid-level) Organization: A&O Shearman Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 Job description A&O Shearman is a new global industry-leading law firm, with nearly 50 offices in 29 countries worldwide. Our fluency in English law, US law, and the laws of the world’s most dynamic markets, enables us to provide unmatched insight and seamless delivery to clients. We work on challenging and important deals and disputes that have the potential to shape the future. We offer exceptional opportunities for our people; opportunities to work for the world’s leading businesses; to transform the status quo, and to deliver your best work, helping you and your career to thrive, while delivering unparalleled outcomes for our clients. Whether you’re helping clients solve complex challenges, transforming the ways we manage our business, or ensuring the smooth-running of our operations, this is an environment where you can belong and excel. We provide first-rate training and development, we are committed to an inclusive environment, and we provide support and ways of working that help you optimise your wellbeing. What truly defines a career with us? We recruit the best and ask for the best of you. And together, we will redefine success. Role purpose To support our continued growth A&O Shearman LLP Belgium is currently looking for a (junior) associate for our litigation & investigations practice in Brussels or Antwerp. Our Belgian team consists of 17 lawyers based in our Antwerp/Brussels offices. We advise clients on their most complex and business-critical disputes, combining first-class legal expertise with a pragmatic, commercial approach. We represent multinational corporations, financial institutions, investors and senior executives in a broad range of matters, including commercial litigation, arbitration, corporate disputes, investigations, white-collar crime, regulatory enforcement, restructuring and insolvency proceedings. As part of A&O Shearman’s global disputes platform, our Belgian team seamlessly collaborates with colleagues across jurisdictions to deliver coordinated, strategic solutions to cross-border challenges. Who we are looking for You have obtained a Belgian master’s degree in Law with strong academic results. You have 1-4 years’ experience in the litigation department of a reputable law firm. You have an excellent command of English and French (written and spoken). You are a team player with excellent legal capabilities, good communication skills and entrepreneurial mindset. What we can offer you You will join a closely integrated team, working on complex and high-profile Belgian and cross-border matters. You will benefit from early responsibility and direct exposure to top-tier clients and transactions. We make a long-term commitment to the development of our lawyers, with varied and intellectually stimulating work. You will have access to national and international secondment opportunities, allowing you to gain experience in other teams and cultures across the firm. We provide dedicated local and global training programmes, including professional skills development and language training. You will be supported by specialist know-how lawyers, dedicated business teams and advanced systems. In addition, we offer a work environment designed to support both performance and wellbeing: We provide a modern, purpose-designed office space, with a mix of collaborative areas and quiet working zones. We offer technology and infrastructure that support flexible and hybrid working. We have an in-house café with a barista. We provide access to a gym and optional personal training. We organise regular social events and team activities, fostering a strong community culture. We support flexible and hybrid working arrangements, depending on business needs and team requirements. Application process We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and welcome applications from all eligible candidates. We invite you to submit your application via the online tool available on our careers website ( www.aoshearman.com/careers ). Please note that applications submitted by email or via an agency will not be considered. To support your application , kindly upload your CV and cover letter (in English), as well as your Bachelor’s and Master’s transcripts. Only complete application files can be taken into consideration. As part of our recruitment process, and in order to comply with our legal obligations and internal policies, we require successful candidates to undergo a background screening. The screening also involves providing information on your criminal history through a separate private statement. We will only process information that is necessary and relevant to the position you are applying for. Access to this statement will be strictly limited to the local recruitment officer responsible for your application. Your background screening data will be deleted at the latest six months after receipt. Please see our data privacy notice for more details. If you have any questions, feel free to contact [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: EU Public Affairs Account Manager (Technology)
item.description: EU Public Affairs Account Manager (Technology) Organization: Hanbury Strategy Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/10/2026 About Hanbury Strategy We turn insight into impact. Whether a client is facing a communications challenge or has a policy goal, our exceptional team uses our understanding of politics, public opinion and the press to create campaigns that work. We have a relentless focus on achieving great results for our clients. Founded in 2016, Hanbury works with clients from offices in several countries, including Belgium (Brussels). The role Hanbury continues to focus on delivering client excellence and growing our business. We are looking to bring on board a driven Account Manager to help service existing public affairs accounts, with opportunities to help support our ongoing growth. The successful candidate will have a passion for politics and a strong working knowledge of EU politics and regulation, committed to delivering excellent client service in a fast-paced consulting environment. You will be a key member of a team that has an established track record in supporting clients in Brussels in the digital policy domain. Current work covers major pieces of legislation including the Cloud and AI Development Act (CASA), Cybersecurity Act II, the Digital Omnibus, and the Digital Networks Act (DNA). You will join a team providing expert regulatory and political analysis and engagement advice to some of the most exciting global companies, working closely with senior colleagues and with support from executives. You will have experience working for the EU institutions, a think tank, in-house, in a relevant trade association, or in consultancy. Main role and responsibilities You will work with colleagues at all levels, from Executives to Partners, driving the delivery of excellent work and client service. You will be involved in a range of tasks and projects, which might include: Drafting clear regulatory and political analysis for internal and external audiences on the latest EU digital policy developments. Managing projects independently while meeting deadlines. Conducting research on new subject matters. Serving and advising clients on complex EU policy, regulatory, and political developments. Attending external events to increase your knowledge and understanding of relevant sectors and share insights and connections with the wider team. Client management Act as the day-to-day account manager on a portfolio of digital-focused accounts, building strong client relationships. Handle general account administration effectively, demonstrating great attention to detail with little to no instruction or guidance, and delegating appropriately. Develop an understanding of client needs and make useful suggestions for key deliverables such as policy monitoring and detailed research. Demonstrate critical thinking to produce strategic advice for clients. Contribute positively to client meetings and take responsibility for status reports and other client reporting. Business development Demonstrate good presentation skills, playing a positive and active role in pitches and proposals. Start to build an external network. Leadership and development Take ownership of your own personal development, seeking out training opportunities and new approaches to innovate Hanbury’s ways of working. Work successfully with colleagues, including delegation, mentoring and time management, setting an appropriate example. Culture Share feedback and contribute ideas to help develop the culture within the team, on accounts, and across the wider organisation. Find a way to personalise and embody the Hanbury values day-to-day. The ideal candidate profile: Has a solid understanding of the EU digital political and regulatory landscape, with an interest in developing this further. Has a practical working knowledge of at least two major pieces of digital legislation in the acquis. Has two to three years’ experience working on digital policy topics for the EU institutions, a think tank, in-house, in a relevant trade association, or in consultancy. Can think laterally and has effective problem-solving skills. Can manage multiple deadlines effectively, with great attention to detail. Is dedicated to producing high-quality work and going the extra mile in a fast-paced environment. Has good presentation skills and excellent interpersonal skills. Has first-class verbal and written communication skills in English; additional EU languages are considered a plus. Wants to be part of a dynamic team and drive a positive working environment. Enjoys working with people with a diverse range of backgrounds and opinions. Has the right to live and work in Belgium. Benefits 26 days’ paid leave plus public holidays and time off over Christmas. Normal working hours are 9am to 6pm. Hybrid working. 4% group assurance (pension) employer contribution. Monizze Lunch Vouchers, Eco Vouchers, and a monthly travel allowance. Hospitalisation and health insurance policy. Work From Abroad (WFA) policy for up to four weeks a year. You will be based in Brussels, but asked to travel as necessary to London or other parts of Europe. Apply here . Applications must be received by Friday 23 October 2026. We will begin interviewing immediately and reserve the right to close the advertisement before the stated closing date once a suitable candidate has been identified. Please send your CV and a cover letter of no more than one page explaining: Why you want to work at Hanbury; and How your skills and experience match the role, including specific examples that demonstrate your suitability. item.title: Strategic Projects Lead – Legal
item.description: Strategic Projects Lead – Legal Organization: AfterQuery Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 10/10/2026 About AfterQuery AfterQuery is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it. Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC’s fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We’re based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI. Why Apply Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC’s fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we’re not slowing down. Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up. Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives. Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers. Responsibilities Project and client management: Partner directly with frontier AI labs on their legal data and evaluation needs — scoping the problem, translating it into a deliverable program, and driving revenue. Manage expert contractor teams: Recruit and lead practicing attorneys and specialists across practice areas and jurisdictions — litigation, corporate and M&A, regulatory, IP, tax, employment — and hold a high bar on the quality of what they produce. Shape AI training: Design the specifications behind legal reasoning datasets, contract and document review tasks, statutory and case-law interpretation problems, multi-step research workflows, and the rubrics used to grade them. Define what “correct” means: Build the grading standards and evaluation criteria that let a lab distinguish real legal reasoning from confident-sounding error, including citation integrity and jurisdictional accuracy. End-to-end execution: Own projects from scoping through final delivery, in a fast-moving environment where the spec often does not exist yet. Operational impact: Support initiatives across building, analysis, and coordination Required Qualifications 3+ years practicing law at a leading firm, in-house at a sophisticated company, a government or regulatory body, or a legal AI startup. JD (or equivalent qualification) and a track record of substantive legal work: you have drafted, negotiated, litigated, or advised, not just coordinated. Deep command of legal reasoning and research methodology, and strong opinions about what separates rigorous analysis from surface-level answers. High agency and the ability to execute in ambiguity; comfort defining the problem before solving it. Analytical ability; can break down complex legal problems and work flows into component parts. Genuine passion for AI and interest in entrepreneurship. Demonstrated track record of competitive success. Strong leadership and communication skills. Comfort with data and AI tools. Preferred Qualifications Python proficiency or hands-on experience with data analysis. Experience with legal technology, e-discovery, contract analytics, or AI-assisted legal workflows. Depth in a technically demanding practice area (securities, antitrust, tax, patent prosecution, complex regulatory). Multi-jurisdictional or non-US legal experience. Experience using AI tools to automate workflows and build products. Company Benefits (For Eligible Employees): Health Insurance: Medical, Vision, Dental 401(k) with Employer Match Daily Meals: Daily UberEats Stipend Monthly Wellness Stipend We are an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. Employment decisions are made without regard to legally protected characteristics under applicable federal, state, or local law. We comply with applicable pay transparency requirements and provide compensation ranges based on the position, qualifications, experience, and other relevant factors. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities and for sincerely held religious beliefs, as required by law. This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, qualifications, or working conditions associated with the position. We reserve the right to modify this job description as business needs change. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Regional Advocacy
item.description: Director of Regional Advocacy Organization: Texas Public Charter Schools Association Location: San Antonio, TX | Rio Grande Valley, TX Date Posted: 10/10/2026 The Texas Public Charter Schools Association is the voice of public charter schools in Texas. Its mission is to support and advocate for a policy and regulatory climate that ensures every student in Texas has access to ever-improving public school options. We work closely with our sister organization, Charter Schools Now. A. Job Summary The Director of Regional Advocacy is responsible for building and maintaining relationships with the public charter schools in their region. They collaborate with charter schools to develop connections with policymakers and build support for high-quality public charter schools. The position will be part of the regional engagement team. B. Essential Job Functions Advocacy Engagement & Activation Increase the advocacy and policy engagement of charter schools across the region. Cultivate partnerships with school advocacy leads to increase the advocacy participation of parents, teachers, alumni, and broader school communities for targeted engagement. Activate advocates to support or oppose policy proposals impacting charter schools. Manage charter stakeholder list-gathering initiative through creation of proposal, team coordination, data-gathering on which districts to target. Create systems and processes for 1:1 Relationship Matrix initiative and track all actions taken Campus Leader Support Serve as the primary point of contact for school leaders in the region, building trusted and strategic relationships. Monitor school events and activities through social media, newsletters, and email updates to stay informed and identify opportunities for engagement. Assist schools in planning impactful engagement moments throughout the year (e.g., heritage months, Veterans Day, and other key observances). Lawmaker & Policymaker Engagement Facilitate meaningful connections between schools and policymakers, including coordinating school visits, event participation, and opportunities for lawmakers to engage with school communities. Build and maintain strong relationships with lawmakers and their staff, and support schools in coordinating school- and community-based events. Support schools with Capitol tours and lawmaker office visits, in coordination with the government affairs team Collaborate with schools to coordinate appreciation and recognition efforts for pro-charter lawmakers (e.g., charter champion awards). Communications & Messaging Work across teams to ensure school stories and advocacy successes are captured and shared through reports, newsletters, videos, etc. Internal Collaboration & Data Tracking Collaborate across teams on assigned projects and initiatives, and ensure that engagement activities are aligned across departments and are incorporated into TPCSA’s database. Based on established metrics or grant requirements, track advocacy engagement to measure progress. C. Expectations This individual will be instrumental in advancing TPCSA’s ambitious goal of having more public charter schools engage in advocacy. The successful candidate will be an extremely organized and detail-oriented professional looking for an opportunity to thrive in a position where he or she will be given space to contribute meaningfully to a team. This is a full-time, exempt position. Employees are generally expected to work a 40-hour work week, with an understanding that occasionally there will be times when 50 or more hours a week may be required in order to complete projects. D. Qualifications Candidate must have a can-do, yes-and attitude and a dedication to the mission of supporting high-quality public school options for all kids. Candidate should embody TPCSA’s core values: Optimism. Drive. Hustle. Excellence. Candidate should be a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment. Candidate must possess a strong internal commitment to excellence and meeting deadlines, and a proven ability to take initiative and ownership over a project. Candidate must be flexible, with the ability to pivot and adapt to change as necessary. Candidate should have high standards for his or her own work, and should be accountable to meeting mutually agreed-upon targets and deadlines. Candidate should have strong verbal and written communication skills and a commitment to excellence. Candidate should have experience in grassroots activism, preferably building and leading grassroots efforts. Candidate should have the ability to think critically and problem-solve with little input. Desire to travel across the region to engage with stakeholders. Knowledge of charter schools and the charter movement is desired, but not required. E. Education Bachelor’s degree. At least 3 years of previous experience leading or specializing in advocacy work (ideally with strong experience in Texas regional and/or state-level politics). At least 5+ years of professional experience. F. Benefits Competitive Salary at $85,000/year Health Insurance, including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance Paid holidays and PTO Matching Plan for 401(k) contributions For more info about our team culture and our employee benefits, please visit: https://txcharterschools.org/careers/ G. Disclaimer This job description is not an employment agreement or contract. Nor is it an exhaustive list of all functions that the employee may be required to perform, and the employee may be required to perform additional functions. TPCSA reserves the exclusive right to revise the job description at any time without notice. Employment with TPCSA is at-will. An at-will employment relationship can be terminated at any time with or without reason or notice by either the employer or employee. This at-will relationship exists regardless of any statements made to the contrary. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily, with or without accommodations. If requested, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their job, absent undue hardship. H. Instructions for Application Qualified candidates should submit the following application materials in one PDF document: Resume describing your relevant experience and education Cover letter expressing your interest in this job and detailing how you embody TPCSA’s core values of optimism, drive, hustle, and excellence The PDF should be emailed to [email protected] Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Fellow, Finance and Insurance
item.description: Senior Fellow, Finance and Insurance Organization: R Street Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/10/2026 The R Street Institute—a free-market think tank headquartered in Washington, D.C. and with staff located across the country—seeks a collaborative Senior Fellow to join its Finance and Insurance policy program. If you are the right fit, you will report to the Policy Director for Finance and Insurance. If you want to join a mission-driven organization and work toward pragmatic policy solutions, this may be the opportunity for you! Your typical day at R Street might include researching and writing policy papers, op-eds, and blog posts about significant financial policy topics (e.g., new credit card regulations); engaging directly with leaders of key policy issue areas, such as Congressional staff considering proposed banking regulations; and interacting with a range of national and local media outlets to educate and provide context on topics like open banking policy. These examples are part of a broader umbrella of impactful finance, insurance, and housing policy areas including consumer credit, fintech policy, property and casualty insurance, capital formation, fraud and scams, and other relevant topics. Other Aspects of Your Role Conceive and coordinate high quality, highly credible, and timely research projects. Write a mix of op-eds, regulatory comments, and policy papers to help solve difficult problems and translate complex ideas in finance, insurance, and/or housing policy. Adapt policy, engagement, and communication strategy in a fluid legislative and regulatory landscape. Work with Government Affairs and Communications teams to identify and engage with target audiences, often encompassing subject matter knowledge, ranging from general audiences to expert stakeholders. Participate in conferences, media, state and/or federal policymaker briefings, and other engagements to communicate complex issues to varied audiences. Remain vigilant against ninja infiltrations. Skills and Qualifications High-level subject matter expertise in financial services legislative and regulatory policy. Professional experience in the financial services industry preferred. Demonstrated expertise and credentials in one or more of the following areas: consumer banking, commercial banking, investments, or property/casualty insurance. Fluency in insurance and/or housing policy strongly desired. Top-notch writing and editing skills in both short- and long-form products that translate complex analysis for policymakers and the public. Exceptional communication and advanced writing skills, including experience speaking with legislators and regulators. Experience testifying before legislative and regulatory bodies highly desirable. Willingness to speak publicly and/or appear on camera, including in interviews. Willingness to engage in the policy debate on social media or other creative venues a plus. Ability to synthesize research using methods common to the program’s work (e.g., legislative analysis, literature review, secondary analysis, descriptive statistics, case studies). Familiarity with econometric approaches a plus. Demonstrated ability to work productively with a wide variety of groups and individuals including state and/or federal policymakers, even those with whom you may disagree. Ability to adapt to new challenges and respond to rapid policy developments. Ability to provide strategic, research-backed policy insights. No particular educational background required—a proven record of achieving results is far more meaningful than credentials. Support for R Street’s passion for free markets and limited, effective government. A sense of humor and a desire to grow within a multifaceted organization. The R Street Institute consistently offers pragmatic, real solutions that foster American innovation, bolster competition, and safeguard individual liberty—all with the understanding that life in a democratic society sometimes requires compromises that don’t necessarily represent first, best solutions. We focus on deep scholarship and pragmatic policy solutions that many groups tend to neglect. Our goal is to publish timely, relevant research and analysis that advances a market-oriented society and limited, effective government. To that end, our motto is “Free Markets. Real Solutions.” Read more about our mission and impact. Workplace Some travel is required, including to Washington, D.C. and state capitals to meet with lawmakers and stakeholders as well as nationwide for relevant conferences and professional engagements. We offer a flexible working arrangement. This is a full-time position that can either work the majority of the week in our D.C. office or be fully remote. Compensation, Benefits, and Perks R Street strives to offer a compensation and benefits package that is competitive, transparent, and supportive of employee well-being. The salary range for this position is $160,000-$170,000, commensurate with experience. In addition to this competitive salary, we provide the following: Unlimited paid time off, including all federal holidays, the day after Thanksgiving, and two weeks holiday closure in December Alternating Fridays off A health insurance option entirely paid by the employer (even for families) Dental and vision insurance 401(k) contributions with up to a 4 percent match HSA employer contribution match Quarterly wellness reimbursement Mobile equipment/mobile plan reimbursement Home internet subsidy Annual educational and professional development reimbursement A choice between child care assistance, pet care assistance, and student loan repayment assistance At R Street, we strive for preeminence in every area in which we engage, driven by our commitment to excellence and innovation. Our culture thrives on action, creativity, and courage, with an unwavering focus on quality, credibility, and impact. We believe progress requires diverse experience and expertise, which is why we champion non-traditional yet prudent approaches to public policy. This principle guides how we build our programs, recognizing that each team member’s uniqueness strengthens our collective identity. We approach our mission with intellectual rigor, embracing free inquiry and honesty to ensure our work is grounded in solid research and thoughtful analysis. While serious about our purpose, we value the joy of collaboration and the fun that comes from working together. Our collaborative spirit fosters trust and transparency, with respect and openness guiding our actions. We celebrate our individual contributions while recognizing that we are stronger as one team, united in our work and relationships. Thus, R Street does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, creed, color, national origin, sexual orientation, era of military service, gender identity or expression, relationship structure, or anything else that’s illegal, immoral, or stupid to use as a basis for hiring. We plan to accept applications for this job until filled. We will contact qualified individuals for telephone screenings and conduct them on a rolling basis. Interviews take place virtually via Zoom. An early 2027 start date is anticipated due to our paid annual Winter Break. To apply, please copy and paste your cover letter into the text box and upload your resume as a Microsoft Word document or PDF at https://street.applytojob.com/apply/BnH7DBB0Yh/Senior-Fellow-Finance-And-Insurance?source=PAC . We encourage thoughtful use of AI tools. If you use them, please describe how they contributed to your work. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director Government Engagement
item.description: Senior Director Government Engagement Organization: Lightbridge Corporation Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/12/2026 At Lightbridge, we’re pioneering advanced nuclear fuel technology that’s designed to make reactors safer, more efficient, and more responsive to global energy needs. Our mission is bold and we’re looking for equally bold thinkers to help us bring it to life. If you thrive at the intersection of engineering and regulatory strategy, this is your opportunity to help shape the future of clean energy. Overview: The Senior Director of Government Engagement leads Lightbridge Corporation’s federal, state, and public policy engagement strategy and serves as a principal interface between the Company and policymakers and government stakeholders. The position is responsible for developing and maintaining productive relationships with the U.S. Congress, congressional committee and staff, the Executive Branch, federal agencies, state governments, national laboratories, industry associations, and other public-sector stakeholders whose policies, programs, funding, and decisions affect advanced nuclear energy, nuclear fuel, and Lightbridge’s commercialization objectives. Working closely with executive leadership, Legal, Regulatory Affairs, Business Development, Engineering, Finance, and Corporate Communications, the Senior Director advances policy priorities that support Lightbridge Fuel™, government partnerships, research and development, fuel qualification, manufacturing readiness, infrastructure development, and commercial deployment. Lightbridge is an advanced nuclear fuel technology company developing a proprietary next-generation fuel technology for existing and future water-cooled reactors. The position will have particular responsibility for congressional and federal executive-branch engagement, federal appropriations and authorization processes, government funding and public-private partnership opportunities, and strategic policy advocacy affecting advanced nuclear energy and nuclear fuel commercialization. This is a highly hands-on leadership position. The successful candidate will personally develop and maintain relationships with key policymakers and government officials, develop advocacy strategies, prepare executive-level materials, coordinate senior-level government engagements, and represent Lightbridge before Congress, federal agencies, and other stakeholders. The Senior Director will also ensure that all government engagement activities comply with applicable lobbying, ethics, disclosure, registration, and reporting requirements. Responsibilities: Develop and execute a comprehensive federal, state, and public policy strategy and engagement aligned with Lightbridge’s business, technology, government partnership, and commercialization objectives. Serve as a primary Company representative with Members of Congress, congressional committee leadership and staff, the Executive Branch, federal agencies, state governments, national laboratories, and other public-sector stakeholders. Build and maintain bipartisan relationships with policymakers and educate stakeholders on Lightbridge Fuel™, advanced nuclear technology, domestic nuclear fuel capability, energy security, and nuclear fuel innovation. Develop and execute legislative and administrative advocacy strategies supporting nuclear fuel research, qualification, manufacturing, deployment, and commercialization. Lead Congressional engagement related to federal appropriations, authorization legislation, agency programs, and government funding opportunities relevant to Lightbridge. Monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, budgetary, appropriations, authorization, and administrative developments affecting Lightbridge and the broader nuclear energy industry. Advise executive leadership on government policy developments, political and regulatory risks, funding opportunities, congressional priorities, and stakeholder considerations. Identify, develop, and support federal funding, research, infrastructure, public-private partnership, and economic-development opportunities aligned with Company objectives. Support Lightbridge’s engagement with the U.S. Department of Energy, Department of Energy Office of Nuclear Energy, Nuclear Regulatory Commission, national laboratories, Department of Defense, and other relevant federal organizations. Develop and maintain relationships with relevant Congressional committees, including the Senate and House committees responsible for energy, nuclear energy, appropriations, science and technology, and national security matters. Prepare executive briefings, policy papers, testimony, talking points, comment letters, presentations, Congressional briefing materials, and other government engagement materials. Plan and coordinate meetings, briefings, agency engagements, site visits, hearings, conferences, and other engagements involving government officials and Company leadership. Work with executive leadership and relevant Company functions to prepare for and execute high-level Congressional and Administration engagements. Represent Lightbridge in relevant industry associations, coalitions, policy forums, and nuclear energy advocacy organizations. Develop and coordinate coalitions and advocacy initiatives involving nuclear companies, utilities, national laboratories, research organizations, industry associations, and other strategic stakeholders. Manage external lobbying firms, government affairs consultants, policy advisors, and other government engagement service providers, establishing clear objectives, deliverables, and performance expectations. Coordinate with Legal and Regulatory Affairs to ensure government engagement activities align with regulatory strategy, corporate policies, and legal requirements. Manage external lobbying firms, government affairs consultants, policy advisors, and other government engagement service providers. Oversee compliance with applicable federal and state lobbying registration, disclosure, ethics, gift, and reporting requirements. Collaborate with Corporate Communications, Investor Relations, Business Development, and other functions to maintain consistent policy, stakeholder, and external messaging. Required Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, International Relations, Communications, Business, Law, Engineering, or a related discipline. At least 12 years of progressive experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, federal relations, public policy, or a related field. Substantial experience working for the U.S. Congress, a Congressional committee, federal agency, Executive Branch office, or in a government affairs/public policy role requiring extensive Congressional engagement. Strong preference for 8-10 or more years of experience working on Capitol Hill (or regular engagement therewith), particularly with the Senate or House committees responsible for energy, natural resources, appropriations/Energy & Water, science and technology, national security, or other matters relevant to nuclear energy. Demonstrated experience engaging Congress, congressional committees, federal agencies, presidential administrations, and senior government officials. Demonstrated experience developing and executing government affairs, legislative, appropriations, authorization, or public policy strategies. Strong understanding of federal legislative, regulatory, administrative, appropriations, authorization, and budget processes. Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain credible, bipartisan relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, federal officials, policymakers, industry representatives, and other stakeholders. Experience translating complex technical, scientific, regulatory, or business matters into clear and persuasive policy communications. Experience preparing executive briefings, policy analyses, testimony, presentations, talking points, and advocacy materials. Knowledge of federal and state lobbying compliance, ethics, disclosure, registration, and reporting requirements. Experience managing government affairs consultants, lobbying firms, trade association relationships, or external policy advisors. Strong executive communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-management skills. Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential, politically sensitive, or strategically important matters. Ability to manage multiple policy priorities and respond effectively to changing legislative and administrative developments. Ability to commute regularly to Washington, D.C. for in-person meetings, and periodically travel to government facilities, national laboratories, state capitals, conferences, and other stakeholder locations. Preferred Qualifications: Professional experience in the nuclear energy industry, nuclear fuel cycle, nuclear utility industry, nuclear fuel vendor, nuclear technology, advanced reactors, nuclear trade associations, or a nuclear-focused NGO. Prior service on or substantial experience working with the Senate or House Energy & Natural Resources, Energy & Commerce, Appropriations/Energy & Water, Science/Technology, Armed Services, or other committees with jurisdiction relevant to nuclear energy. Experience working with the U.S. Department of Energy, particularly the Office of Nuclear Energy, national laboratories, Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Department of Defense, or other energy and national-security organizations. Experience with federal appropriations, authorization legislation, agency budget processes, grant programs, cooperative agreements, public-private partnerships, or government-funded research and development. Knowledge of policies affecting nuclear fuel supply, advanced reactor deployment, HALEU, research infrastructure, energy security, domestic manufacturing, fuel qualification, and technology commercialization. item.title: Senior Manager, Global Oncology Communications, Bladder Cancer and GU Public Affairs
item.description: Senior Manager, Global Oncology Communications, Bladder Cancer and GU Public Affairs Organization: Johnson & Johnson Location: Raritan, NJ | Spring House, PA Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Description At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. Job Function: Communications & Corporate/External Affairs Job Sub Function: Product Communications Job Category: Professional All Job Posting Locations: Raritan, New Jersey, United States of America, Spring House, Pennsylvania, United States of America Job Description: We are searching for the best talent to join our team as a Senior Manager, Global Oncology Communications, Bladder Cancer and GU Public Affairs. This is a hybrid role available in Raritan, NJ or Spring House, PA. The Senior Manager, Global Oncology Communications, Bladder Cancer and GU Public Affairs supports Innovative Medicine Communications and Public Affairs by helping execute integrated global communications strategies that advance business priorities, strengthen stakeholder trust, and enhance Johnson & Johnson’s reputation in oncology, with bladder cancer as the primary area of focus within the genitourinary cancer portfolio. This role partners closely with Global Therapeutic Area Communications, R&D, Global Commercial Strategy, Medical Affairs, Public Affairs, regional and local market teams, and other enterprise partners to support clear narratives, aligned messaging and materials, and coordinated execution across global and local channels. The role operates within a highly matrixed, global-to-local model, contributing to product, reputation and organizational communications that support bladder cancer portfolio milestones, disease awareness, innovation storytelling, market-shaping priorities and key lifecycle moments, while helping ensure alignment across the broader GU strategy. Key Responsibilities Therapeutic Area Communications Strategy & Execution Support global and local communications and public affairs activations for the bladder cancer portfolio, while helping ensure alignment across the broader genitourinary cancer strategy. Provide support for prostate cancer communications and public affairs initiatives as needed, in alignment with broader GU priorities. Contribute market and stakeholder insights to the development of global communications and public affairs strategies for bladder cancer, aligned with business priorities, portfolio milestones and lifecycle moments, including data readouts, launches and growth initiatives. Translate complex scientific data and strategies into clear, compelling messaging across earned, owned, and paid channels. Adapt and deliver core messaging, content, and campaigns for local market impact. Support proactive communications that differentiate Johnson & Johnson as a global health innovator in bladder cancer, including disease awareness, innovation storytelling, product communications and reputation-building initiatives. Contribute to successful local product launches and support priority growth brands at key moments. Cross-Functional Leadership & Strategic Counsel Serve as a trusted partner to internal stakeholders across Global Therapeutic Area Communications, R&D, Global Commercial Strategy, Medical Affairs, Public Affairs, regional and local market teams. Provide day-to-day communications counsel to connect business objectives with communications outcomes and inform decision-making. Align communications strategies with public affairs, policy, and access considerations to support market shaping and stakeholder engagement. Collaborate with regional and global teams to co-create strategies and ensure strong pull-through of global priorities into local execution. Operate effectively in a matrixed model, helping connect senior leader priorities, cross-functional inputs and local market needs into coordinated communications plans. Global-to-Local Integration & Execution Enable a globally consistent, locally activated communications model by partnering with regional and global teams to adapt strategies, messaging, and materials. Ensure alignment with governance, regulatory, and compliance requirements in market. Contribute to coordinated execution of media, digital, stakeholder, congress and campaign activities in partnership with core capabilities teams. Public Affairs Integration Embed public affairs considerations into Therapeutic Area strategies to support policy, access, and market-shaping priorities. Partner with Public Affairs colleagues to align messaging, stakeholder engagement, and external positioning. Support activation value narratives that reinforce access, reimbursement, and policy objectives. Insights, Monitoring & Continuous Improvement Support monitoring and analysis of media, stakeholder, policy and competitive landscapes to identify risks, opportunities and emerging issues that may affect the bladder cancer portfolio. Contribute to measurement, reporting, and analytics to assess communications impact and inform strategy refinement. Capture insights and best practices to improve global toolkits, messaging, and execution models over time. Ways of Working & Operational Excellence Operate as part of a connected team, contributing to shared priorities, resources, and Communities of Practice. Leverage centralized tools, platforms, and capabilities (e.g., digital, media, measurement) to drive consistency and efficiency. Prioritize high-impact, external communications aligned to business value, with disciplined focus on key opportunities. Support simplification, scalability, and reduced duplication across communications efforts. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus Minimum of 8+ years of experience in communications, public affairs, or related field (corporate, agency, NGO, or government) with a strong track record of results Experience supporting global or regional communications strategies, including oncology, therapeutic area, product or portfolio communications; bladder cancer or genitourinary oncology experience preferred. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a matrixed, global environment and influence cross-functional stakeholders Strong writing, editing, and storytelling skills, including translating complex scientific content into accessible messaging Experience supporting media, digital, stakeholder engagement, congress and integrated communications campaigns. Strong organizational, analytical and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced, highly matrixed environment. Core Competencies Bladder cancer strategy: Contributes market insight to global narrative, positioning and messaging aligned to science, patient needs and business priorities in bladder cancer Global-to-local integration: Enables consistent and effective local adaptation and execution Strategic counsel & business acumen: Connects communications strategies to business outcomes and stakeholder impact Cross-functional collaboration: Aligns diverse stakeholders and drives coordinated execution across teams External communications excellence: Develops high-impact messaging and content across channels Public affairs integration: Aligns communications with access, policy, and stakeholder engagement priorities Analytics & insights: Uses data and insights to inform strategy and optimize performance Operational discipline: Supports scalable, efficient execution aligned with governance and best practices Collaboration & team mindset: Contributes to a high-performing, connected global team environment Johnson & Johnson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act. Johnson & Johnson is committed to providing an interview process that is inclusive of our applicants’ needs. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request an accommodation, external applicants please contact us via https://www.jnj.com/contact-us/careers , internal employees contact AskGS to be directed to your accommodation resource. item.title: Sr. Compliance Reporting Analyst
item.description: Sr. Compliance Reporting Analyst Organization: Leidos Location: McLean, VA Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Leidos has a new and exciting opportunity for a Sr. Compliance Reporting Analyst in our Intel Security Sector’s Analysis Solutions Business Area. Our talented team is at the forefront in Security Engineering, Computer Network Operations (CNO), Mission Software, Analytical Methods and Modeling, Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), and Cryptographic Key Management. At Leidos, we offer competitive benefits, including Paid Time Off, 11 paid Holidays, Immediate Vesting in our 401K, Flexible Schedules, Discounted Stock Purchase Plans, Technical Upskilling, Education and Training Support, Parental Paid Leave, and much more. Join us and make a difference in National Security! **To be considered you must have an active and current TS/SCI w/ Poly security clearance** Job Description The Sr. Compliance Reporting Analyst provides contractor support to a government customer responsible for compliance and oversight activities related to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) collection authority. The role focuses on the lawful access, querying, review, use, retention, dissemination, and purging of FISA-acquired information; protection of U.S. person information; prevention and detection of compliance incidents; and timely remediation and reporting. The role translates complex legal and policy requirements into operational and technical controls and verifies that those controls are implemented effectively across systems and processes, and mission teams. Primary Responsibilities: Plan, coordinate, and execute FISA compliance activities in accordance with applicable laws, intelligence authorities, policies, and procedures. Provide compliance guidance on the lawful access, querying, use, retention, dissemination, and purging of FISA-acquired information, including user access administration. Review FISA collection requests, dissemination products, and supporting documentation to ensure compliance with legal, policy, and classification requirements. Prepare for and support internal and external compliance reviews, audits, and oversight activities, including documentation, issue resolution, and corrective action tracking. Identify, investigate, document, and report compliance incidents; implement and maintain controls to mitigate risk and ensure timely remediation. Develop and maintain compliance documentation, SOPs, user guidance, training, and technical requirements; translate legal and policy requirements into operational processes and controls. Analyze compliance data and trends, collaborate with legal and technical stakeholders, and provide recommendations to improve compliance, data quality, and automated oversight capabilities. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree with 8–12 years of relevant experience, or a master’s degree with 6–10 years; equivalent experience may be substituted for a degree. Experience supporting FISA or SIGINT compliance, intelligence oversight, legal-policy implementation, or related mission functions. Knowledge of FISA compliance requirements, including targeting, minimization, querying, dissemination, retention, purging, incident reporting, and protection of U.S. person information. Experience conducting compliance reviews, audits, assessments, incident reporting, records management, and translating legal and policy requirements into operational or technical controls. Experience using compliance tracking systems, databases, document repositories, Microsoft Excel, and PowerPoint to manage data and develop reports and briefings. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to coordinate effectively across legal, technical, operational, and leadership stakeholders while managing competing priorities. Active TS/SCI clearance with polygraph and the ability to work full-time on-site at the government facility. Preferred Qualifications: 10+ years of experience supporting FISA compliance, intelligence authorities, legal policy, or SIGINT mission operations. Experience with SIGINT targeting tools, intelligence processes, and compliance policies. Experience designing or advising on SIGINT workflows, systems, policies, processes, and technical controls to enforce legal and compliance requirements. Direct experience supporting Section 702 compliance, including mission-user access, querying, minimization, dissemination, retention, purging, incident management, or oversight reviews. Familiarity with RISAA, Executive Order 14086, and related privacy, civil liberties, accountability, and transparency requirements. Experience implementing technical compliance requirements, leveraging automated oversight, data-quality controls, dashboards, metrics, and trend reporting. Familiarity with JIRA, Confluence, or similar collaboration tools, and experience with all-source intelligence, including cable traffic, data retention, and purging requirements. At Leidos, the opportunities are boundless. We challenge our staff with interesting assignments that allow them to thrive professionally and personally. For us, helping you grow your career is good business. We look forward to learning more about you – apply today. #CABARESTON #ASBA #HALO If you’re looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We’re not hiring followers. We’re recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We’re already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares. For U.S. Positions: While subject to change based on business needs, Leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above. Pay Range: Pay Range $92,300.00 – $166,850.00 The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.
