item.title: Account Director, Public Affairs
item.description: Account Director, Public Affairs Organization: Stratacomm Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Job Type Full-time Description Stratacomm is seeking a strategic, communications savvy and results-driven Account Director to join our Public Affairs Practice Group. At Stratacomm, we help our public and private sector clients advance their organization’s mission through integrated communications. This includes increasing awareness of programs and research, shaping policy, and building coalitions with stakeholders, such as policymakers, regulators, community leaders, industry and the public. You’re a seasoned communicator who knows how policy gets made and how to move it. You turn complex content into clear counsel that senior clients act on with legislative, regulatory, political and media dynamics in mind. You’ve built coalitions, prepared executives for hearings and interviews, and kept a steady hand through high-pressure moments. You can brief a CEO, sharpen a coalition message and coach a teammate through a high-stakes deliverable, all in a day’s work. You’re ready to own client relationships and lead a team of your own. As an Account Director, you’ll lead client relationships with independence, direct major public affairs programs from strategy through measurement, and take on formal supervisory responsibility for your own direct reports. Our public sector work centers on strategic communications that advance agency mission; this is not a lobbying role. What You’ll Do Lead day-to-day client relationships as a trusted strategic counselor; manage expectations on scope, timeline and outcomes, and deliver difficult news directly when it matters. Engage federal, state and local audiences with fluency; for public sector clients, lead communications that advance agency mission and public understanding. Translate client policy and business objectives into integrated public affairs strategy and own the rationale behind the work across workstreams and channels. Lead development of high-priority client materials, including strategic recommendations, narrative frameworks, legislative and regulatory communications, communications plans and executive presentations. Prepare executives and spokespeople for stakeholder engagements, congressional hearings, public comment opportunities and media interviews. Monitor the policy landscape to identify opportunities for clients and lead rapid response during fast-moving policy and political moments. Design and manage coalition and stakeholder engagement programs, including third-party validator strategy, aligned partner messaging, and grassroots and grasstops mobilization. Lead earned media strategy across trade, regional, national and top-tier outlets, and build thought leadership programs that position client executives as credible, authoritative voices. Plan and lead stakeholder gatherings (e.g., workshops, Capitol Hill days and fly-ins). Counsel clients through issues management, crisis preparedness and response, and internal and change communications. Supervise, coach and develop direct reports, helping them set goals, and owning feedback and performance reviews. Manage account scope, budgets, timelines and billing, along with agency partners, vendors and freelancers. Identify organic growth opportunities on existing accounts, lead new business pursuits and help grow the Public Affairs practice. Apply AI and digital tools with strategic judgment to raise the quality and efficiency of the work, and bring new applications back to your team. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in communications, public affairs, political science, public policy, journalism or a related field. Minimum of seven years of experience in public affairs or policy communications, preferably within a communications or government agency. Working knowledge of the legislative and regulatory process and of federal, state and local government audiences. Demonstrated experience building coalitions and running stakeholder engagement programs. Proven ability to manage senior client relationships and complex, multi-workstream programs. Experience supervising or mentoring team members and readiness to manage direct reports. Exceptional writing and editing skills across policy, media and executive materials, with the ability to distill complex issues into compelling messages. Sound judgment under pressure in rapid response and crisis situations. Strong desire and ability to contribute to the firm’s growth, marketing and business development. Established relationships with trade, political or sector media a plus. Specialized depth in an area such as public sector communications, coalition management, legislative and regulatory communications, or rapid response a plus. About Stratacomm Do great work. Have fun. Success will follow. Stratacomm was founded on these principles 30 years ago. Today, it is an independently owned, full-service strategic communications agency that helps clients raise awareness, enhance reputation, shape policy and build market share. With offices in Washington, D.C. and Detroit, in recent years, Stratacomm has been named one of Washingtonian’s 50 Great Places to Work, one of PR News’ Top Places to Work in PR and one of Metro Detroit’s Best and Brightest Companies to Work For. We are policy communicators, coalition builders, storytellers, digital strategists, content producers, program managers, social listeners, and more. With deep expertise in transportation and new mobility, energy and sustainability, government, and social change, our reputation is built on delivering exceptional client service and measurable results. Our three core values, People First, Curiosity and Creativity, and Outcomes that Matter, define how we show up for our clients and for each other. Stratacomm offers employees a best-in-class workplace culture, competitive benefits including 401(k) matching, medical, vision, dental insurance, Open PTO, Paid Parental Leave, and a Remote-First work policy, designed to fit your needs. Employees responded with 100% agreement to the statement “Stratacomm is a great place to work” on all recent engagement surveys. Stratacomm is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, religion, height, weight, or veteran status in employment. Salary Description 100k-130k Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II
item.description: Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II Organization: Tuvli Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Job Description Seeking Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II to coordinate and manage congressional and legislative affairs and support foreign assistance process management. The Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II is responsible for collaboration and coordination of foreign assistance to Europe, Eurasia, and Central Asia to support U.S. foreign policy objectives. The Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II will advise on Foreign Affairs committees and issues, recurring and arising. The Incumbent will be the primary office liaison with the Department of State legislative bureau coordinating and communicating with Senior Congressional Advisors. The Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II is the office’s liaison with State’s Legal Bureau (L), Office of Foreign Assistance (F), and other offices on Congressional related issues and taskers. Under the supervision of the Director of the Budget and Foreign Assistance Management section, the Incumbent(s) is responsible for the tracking and management of congressional reports, notifications, briefings, notes, and other related issues. The process includes routing and tracking the status of CNs, QFRs, reports, briefings, as well as assist with other documents and/or engagements in coordination within the resources and legislative team. Incumbent assures the accuracy of the documents, preparation for senior leadership, and needed revisions. The position also creates, drafts, and circulates fact sheets and dashboards on relevant topics. The Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II assist with some budget, administration, and management tasks such as: assisting with preparing and/or tracking taskers, creating templates, creating training documents, assuring points of contacts are current; and obtaining senior level approval and/or clearance on documents. Also assist in drafting and formatting country/topic specific products; track budgetary approval processes; manage document libraries on the shared drive/sites. Incumbent will support bureau participation in meetings with foreign officials and other international and multilateral events that feature discussion of foreign assistance, and/or participate him/herself. This includes press, website, and newsletters regarding ACE’s role and other related priorities. The Incumbent(s) will perform office support duties to include but not limited to assembling documents in orientation binders for new staff, delivering documents to various Department offices. Tuvli, an Akima company, is hiring for a Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II to support our DoS client located in Washington, DC. Responsibilities Congressional/Legislative Coordinator II shall provide professional service employees (Congressional/Legislative Liaison) for the following budget, communications, and administrative tasks: Track and coordinate Congressional reports, inquiries, and briefings for the office Manage the CN process includes routing and tracking the status of CNs, as well as assist with other reprogramming documents in coordination with the budget team Assist in drafting talking points and other official and/or Congressional documents and taskers. Liaise with ACE, intra- and interagency partners on clearances. Interface and coordinate directly within the office and front office leadership on drafting, scheduling, clearances, and process management. Advise office on Foreign Affairs committees and issues that recurring and arising with Congress; act as primary liaison with the Department of State Legislative bureau coordinating and communicating with Senior Congressional Advisors. Assist with the budget/resource planning, reporting, and execution processes Store and maintain files and documentation in SharePoint, including but not limited to approved Operational Plans, CNs, F memos, etc. Perform office support duties to include but not limited to assembling documents in orientation binders for new staff, delivering documents to various Department offices. Prepare briefing checklists, letters, reports, agendas, talking points, meeting minutes, and responses to congressional and interagency inquiries. Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree (in related field) or higher degree with at least 3 years’ experience in international politics/foreign policy, legal, communications, business management, social science, information technology, accounting, or other related fields. At least 1 year or more experience working with Congress or Congressional staffers/liaison on U.S. foreign policy goals and objectives as they relate to U.S. foreign assistance efforts in the region. Experience coordinating, drafting, and tracking documents/papers. Experience with Microsoft SharePoint, Excel, Power Automate, Power BI applications/functions, intermediate or advance level. English language (written and spoken) communications skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks, coordinate activities in multiple locations, act decisively in daily work, and work well in a multi-cultural team environment. Strong organizational, communication, interpersonal, and computer skills. Ability to work independently to assess priorities and manage daily coordination of details with minimal supervision. Excellent project management and interpersonal skills with basic knowledge on interrelated issues such as Military, Cybersecurity, Trafficking in Persons, Democracy, Rule of Law, Independent Media, and/or Economic Growth etc. Excellent writing, speaking, and research skills to produce independently prepared, authoritative documents under tight deadlines for consideration by senior managers Active Secret clearance. With major offices in Herndon, Denver, Amsterdam, Singapore and Malaysia, we have a global footprint and a unified team of employees committed to providing a premier customer experience and delivering the full spectrum of data center solutions, from core to edge, like no other data center provider can do. Focused on driving innovation and helping our customers define and deliver their own unique vision for the Edge, at any scale, in any market worldwide, for any requirement, we are building tomorrow’s data center infrastructure, today for some of the world’s most demanding Network, Content, and Cloud customers. About the role The Director, Public Affairs (West) must hold state government experience in Arizona and can be based in the Phoenix metro area, Denver, CO, or our global HQ in Herndon, VA What you’ll do Government Relations & Direct Lobbying: Develop and execute strategies and conduct lobbying meetings to influence legislation, regulations, and administrative policies at the local (e.g., city council, county commissioners court) and Arizona state levels, including various state agencies Legislative Monitoring & Analysis: Track and analyze proposed bills and ordinances in Arizona that impact the organization. Draft policy briefs, bill analyses, and impact reports for internal teams Coalition Building/Stakeholder Engagement: Represent the company in relevant industry coalitions, trade associations (e.g., Data Center Coalition), and coalitions to advocate for data center interests and influence positive outcomes in all forums. Manage outside advisors to execute on needed policy/legislative/operational actions to support the company’s objectives Stakeholder Engagement & Advocacy: Build and nurture strong relationships with key political figures, community leaders, and industry counterparts in Arizona. Lead grassroots advocacy campaigns and coordinate/assist with community outreach initiatives Thought Leadership, Messaging, Communication: Prepare policy briefs, white papers, talking points, testimony, other materials for internal teams or senior leadership. Prepare needed materials for external engagements to educate policymakers/other stakeholders on the role of data centers and AI infrastructure in the digital economy Coordinate with cross-functional internal teams Public Affairs & Government Relations Support: Provide support across the Public Affairs team and legislative teams as needed as they liaise with local officials, government agencies and communities, monitor legislative or regulatory developments, or manage political/community risks Community Engagement Support: Provide support as needed for community outreach/charitable/education programs as well as for public forums, open houses, and stakeholder meetings Manage and work with Outside counsel and consultants Compliance & Reporting: To the extent applicable, ensure lobbying activities comply with applicable laws, including necessary registrations. Ensure needed disclosure reports are filed Qualifications ~6 years experience in government affairs, public affairs or advocacy. Prior work in Arizona serving as a legislative staffer, agency official, or campaign manager is considered a plus Experience in local Arizona economic development is considered a plus Technical knowledge: Strong understanding of data centers, utility regulation, electricity markets, economic development, local/state governments or related experience. Comprehensive understanding of Arizona government, legislative/administrative processes, and key state/local funding or regulatory mechanisms Juris Doctor (J. D.), Master of Public Administration (MPA) or Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, Communications, or related filed. Legislative Acumen: Deep understanding of local governance, policy processes, and regulatory frameworks. Strategic Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Relationship Building: Network of contacts within the local legislative and regulatory community. Crisis Management: Ability to analyze data and respond quickly. item.title: Director, Public Affairs (Midwest)
item.description: Director, Public Affairs (Midwest) Organization: EdgeConneX Location: Herndon, VA | Indianapolis, IN | Chicago, IL Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Led by an experienced management team and supported by a strong investor group, including large and experienced institutions and strategic partners, EdgeConneX offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment where we are bringing flexibility, proximity, power, and connectivity to some of the world’s key businesses. With major offices in Herndon, Denver, Amsterdam, Singapore and Malaysia, we have a global footprint and a unified team of employees committed to providing a premier customer experience and delivering the full spectrum of data center solutions, from core to edge, like no other data center provider can do. Focused on driving innovation and helping our customers define and deliver their own unique vision for the Edge, at any scale, in any market worldwide, for any requirement, we are building tomorrow’s data center infrastructure, today for some of the world’s most demanding Network, Content, and Cloud customers. About the role The Director, Public Affairs (Midwest) must hold state government experience in Indiana and can be based in Indiana, Chicago or our global HQ in Herndon, VA What you’ll do Government Relations & Direct Lobbying: Develop and execute strategies and conduct lobbying meetings to influence legislation, regulations, and administrative policies at the local (e.g., city council, county commissioners court) and Indiana state levels, including various state agencies Legislative Monitoring & Analysis: Track and analyze proposed bills and ordinances in Indiana that impact the organization. Draft policy briefs, bill analyses, and impact reports for internal teams Coalition Building/Stakeholder Engagement: Represent the company in relevant industry coalitions, trade associations (e.g., Data Center Coalition), and coalitions to advocate for data center interests and influence positive outcomes in all forums. Manage outside advisors to execute on needed policy/legislative/operational actions to support the company’s objectives Stakeholder Engagement & Advocacy: Build and nurture strong relationships with key political figures, community leaders, and industry counterparts in Indiana. Lead grassroots advocacy campaigns and coordinate/assist with community outreach initiatives Thought Leadership, Messaging, Communication: Prepare policy briefs, white papers, talking points, testimony, other materials for internal teams or senior leadership. Prepare needed materials for external engagements to educate policymakers/other stakeholders on the role of data centers and AI infrastructure in the digital economy Coordinate with cross-functional internal teams Public Affairs & Government Relations Support: Provide support across the Public Affairs team and legislative teams as needed as they liaise with local officials, government agencies and communities, monitor legislative or regulatory developments, or manage political/community risks Community Engagement Support: Provide support as needed for community outreach/charitable/education programs as well as for public forums, open houses, and stakeholder meetings Manage and work with Outside counsel and consultants Compliance & Reporting: To the extent applicable, ensure lobbying activities comply with applicable laws, including necessary registrations. Ensure needed disclosure reports are filed Qualifications ~6 years experience in government affairs, public affairs or advocacy. Prior work in Indiana serving as a legislative staffer, agency official, or campaign manager is considered a plus Experience in local Indiana economic development is considered a plus Technical knowledge: Strong understanding of data centers, utility regulation, electricity markets, economic development, local/state governments or related experience. Comprehensive understanding of Indiana government, legislative/administrative processes, and key state/local funding or regulatory mechanisms Juris Doctor (J. D.), Master of Public Administration (MPA) or Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, Communications, or related filed. Legislative Acumen: Deep understanding of local governance, policy processes, and regulatory frameworks. Strategic Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Relationship Building: Network of contacts within the local legislative and regulatory community. Crisis Management: Ability to analyze data and respond quickly. The pay range for this role is: 214,000 – 234,000 USD per year (HQ) 214,000 – 234,000 USD per year (Indiana – Remote) 214,000 – 234,000 USD per year (Chicago – Remote) Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs (EU)
item.description: Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs (EU) Organization: EdgeConneX Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/12/2026 ­Led by an experienced management team and supported by a strong investor group, including large and experienced institutions and strategic partners, EdgeConneX offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment where we are bringing flexibility, proximity, power, and connectivity to some of the world’s key businesses. With major offices in Herndon, Denver, Amsterdam, Singapore and Malaysia, we have a global footprint and a unified team of employees committed to providing a premier customer experience and delivering the full spectrum of data center solutions, from core to edge, like no other data center provider can do. Focused on driving innovation and helping our customers define and deliver their own unique vision for the Edge, at any scale, in any market worldwide, for any requirement, we are building tomorrow’s data center infrastructure, today for some of the world’s most demanding Network, Content, and Cloud customers. About the role This role reports to our Global Head, Public Policy and Affairs, and will be based in either Amsterdam or Brussels The charter of this role is ensuring that the policy and regulatory workload across EdgeConneX’s European operation receives the sustained, hands-on attention it requires. The full scope of responsibilities and geographical coverage will develop over time in line with the growth of the 10-market European project portfolio What you’ll do EU and National Policy Monitoring and Analysis: Track, analyze, and report on emerging EU and national legislation and regulation impacting data center development, construction, operations, and power procurement across EdgeConneX’s European markets. Determine what matters, prioritize accordingly, and translate complex regulatory developments into clear, actionable intelligence for internal teams and senior leadership. Strategic Policy Advocacy: Develop and execute EU and national policy strategies that align with business priorities, to support data center development, construction, and operations, and to ensure access to power and permits. Represent EdgeConneX in policy committees and working groups within national data center trade associations across Europe, taking an active role in shaping industry positions and ensuring the company’s voice is heard in collective advocacy. Regulatory Engagement: Build working relationships and execute engagement strategies with key lawmakers, policymakers, regulators, and staff at both national and EU institutional level. Represent the company before the European Commission, European Parliament, national ministries, energy regulators, and other relevant entities as required. Coalition Building and Stakeholder Engagement: Represent the company in relevant EU and national industry coalitions and trade associations to advocate for data center interests and influence positive outcomes in all forums. Manage outside advisors to execute on needed policy, legislative, and operational actions to support the company’s objectives. Cross-Functional Alignment: Work with Development, Energy Procurement, Engineering, Public Affairs, Marketing and Communications, Sustainability, Legal, and other internal teams to align policy strategy with business objectives and assess the impact of regulatory developments on internal departments and operations. Work closely with the Sustainability team to track and respond to relevant policy developments on energy transition, carbon reporting, water use, and other ESG-related regulatory requirements. Thought Leadership, Messaging, and Communication: Prepare policy briefs, regulatory horizon scans, white papers, talking points, and other materials for internal teams or senior leadership. Prepare materials for external engagements to educate policymakers and other stakeholders on the role of data centers and AI infrastructure in the digital economy. Project-Level Public Affairs Support: Provide targeted hands-on support to the Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs, EU on public affairs activities related to specific development projects across the European portfolio, including stakeholder mapping, briefing preparation, meeting support, and coordination of external PA consultants across multiple markets. Manage: Manage and coordinate outside counsel and consultants across European markets. Travel: Regular travel across Europe is required. The nature of the role demands in-person presence at trade association meetings, government engagements, and project-level public affairs activities across multiple markets. Qualifications Experience: 7 to 10 years of experience in EU policy, public affairs, regulatory affairs, or government relations, ideally with exposure to energy, digital infrastructure, technology, or industrial sectors. Technical Knowledge: Strong command of EU legislative processes and institutional dynamics, with a practical understanding of how national politics interact with the Brussels agenda. Policy Expertise: Familiarity with key EU policy files including the Energy Efficiency Directive, AI Act, Data Act, European Green Deal, and national permitting and grid access frameworks. Communication Skills: Proven ability to translate complex regulatory developments into clear, concise, and actionable outputs for a business audience. Education: Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Law, European Studies, Public Policy, or a related field. Skills: Strong analytical capabilities, excellent communication skills both verbal and written, hands-on execution mindset, and the ability to work collaboratively and independently in a matrixed, multi-market environment. item.title: Manager-Government Affairs
item.description: Manager-Government Affairs Organization: American Transmission Co. (ATC) Location: Pewaukee, WI | Cottage Grove, WI Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Summary of Responsibilities: Shape the Future of Energy Policy. Build Meaningful Relationships. Make a Lasting Impact. At American Transmission Co. (ATC), we do more than move electricity across the grid. We help power communities, support economic growth, and enable a reliable energy future. Behind that mission is a team of professionals who build trusted relationships, solve complex challenges, and help shape the policies that impact our business and the industry we serve. We’re looking for a Manager, Government Affairs to lead ATC’s government affairs strategy and advocacy efforts across local, state, and federal levels. This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of public policy, business strategy, stakeholder engagement, and energy infrastructure. If you’re passionate about influencing policy, building relationships, and helping organizations navigate complex regulatory environments, this could be the next step in your career. Essential Responsibilities: What You’ll Do As Manager, Government Affairs, you’ll serve as a trusted advisor and key representative of ATC, helping advance the company’s priorities while building strong relationships with policymakers, regulators, industry partners, and stakeholders. Lead the development and execution of ATC’s government affairs strategies and advocacy priorities. Monitor legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments and assess potential impacts to ATC and the electric transmission industry. Develop policy positions, advocacy strategies, and recommendations that support business objectives. Build and maintain productive relationships with elected officials, government agencies, regulators, trade associations, customers, and industry stakeholders. Provide timely policy analysis, strategic guidance, and executive briefings to senior leaders. Represent ATC at hearings, meetings, conferences, coalition activities, and public forums. Coordinate external engagement efforts and prepare leaders and subject matter experts for interactions with policymakers and stakeholders. Oversee lobbying disclosure reporting, required filings, recordkeeping, consultant relationships, and government affairs operational processes. Manage ATC’s political contribution programs and related reporting activities. Lead and develop employees while collaborating across Legal, Regulatory, Communications, Operations, Planning, and other business functions. This role requires approximately 30% travel, including overnight travel. Who Will Be Successful in This Role? The ideal candidate is a politically savvy leader who understands how public policy and government decisions influence business outcomes. They are equally comfortable building relationships with legislators and regulators, advising executives on emerging policy issues, coordinating advocacy efforts, and leading a team toward strategic goals. Successful candidates are: Strategic thinkers who connect policy developments to business priorities. Trusted relationship builders who establish credibility across diverse stakeholder groups. Influential communicators who can simplify complex topics and drive informed decision-making. Collaborative leaders who work effectively across teams and functions. Adaptable professionals who remain effective in dynamic and fast-moving environments. Strong executors who balance strategy, compliance, operational excellence, and results. What You’ll Bring Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Public Administration, Public Policy, Political Science, Public Affairs, Communications, Business, Law, or a related field. Six or more years of progressive experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, advocacy, or a related field. Experience serving as a liaison to legislative, executive, or regulatory bodies. Demonstrated success building productive relationships with government officials, agencies, and industry stakeholders. Experience analyzing legislative and regulatory developments and developing policy recommendations or advocacy strategies. Experience overseeing political contribution programs and associated reporting requirements. Experience leading employees, major functional programs, or significant cross-functional initiatives. Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree in Law, Public Policy, Business Administration, or a related field. Experience in the electric utility, energy, transmission, infrastructure, or another highly regulated industry. Experience coordinating external consultants, trade associations, coalitions, or advocacy groups. Experience representing organizations in hearings, meetings, conferences, or public forums. Knowledge of lobbying disclosure requirements, political contribution governance, reporting obligations, and compliance processes. Why ATC? Purpose-Driven Work: We’re energized by meaningful and challenging work that contributes to the greater good, from powering everyday life to grid modernization. People-Centric Culture: We are difference makers. We lead with trust, value collaboration, and foster a supportive environment where people grow, contribute openly, and make a difference. Flexibility & Balance: Our work environment encourages autonomy, connection, and choice with accountability. Growth & Development: Curiosity, coaching, and engagement fuel careers. We invest in our people through cross-functional opportunities, skill-building, and assignments that stretch potential and build careers. Comprehensive Rewards: Compensation, benefits, and well-being offerings are thoughtfully and competitively designed to support employees’ unique needs. Reliable Innovation: Grounded in the communities we serve, we play a critical role in powering the grid, with the agility to innovate, lead, and drive progress in a time of transformational change in the industry. A Shared Future: We commit to creating an environment where people can do their best work, thrive, and drive success for our customers and stakeholders, delivering a lasting impact for all. Join our Great Place to Work, where we build and operate the power grid that enables modern life, and where every role contributes to something bigger than any one of us. The targeted base pay for this position is $148,300 to $173,300 annually.* Base pay is one component of our comprehensive total rewards package which includes an annual incentive bonus, employer-sponsored pension plan, 401(k) match, HSA contribution, life & disability insurance, health care benefits, generous time off plans, flexible work arrangements, and much more. *The pay range is a general guideline. Employment offers are evaluated individually and consider qualifications, experience, academic achievements, internal equity, and business needs. Pay exceeding the posted range is considered for uniquely qualified candidates. Interested internal candidates, with questions, please consult your Human Resources Business Partner. Equal Opportunity Employer: Applicants have rights under employment laws. ATC is an equal opportunity employer that seeks to foster diverse teams of talented people working safely together. We respect and embrace diversity of all aspects and hire, train and promote employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, genetics, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage women, minorities, veterans and individuals with a disability to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any characteristic protected by law. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Corporate Attorney
item.description: Associate Corporate Attorney Organization: CoBank Location: Greenwood Village, CO Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Job Description Benefits Overview A career at CoBank can offer you the opportunity to make a personal impact on the people and communities where we do business. In order to be the best, we hire the best! Remarkable Benefits Offered by CoBank Careers with a purpose Time-Off Packages, 15 days of vacation, 10 paid sick days and 11 paid holidays Competitive Compensation & Incentive Hybrid work model: flexible arrangements for most positions Benefits Packages, including Medical, Dental and Vision coverage, Disability, AD&D, and Life Insurance Robust associate training and development with CoBank University Tuition reimbursement for higher education Outstanding 401k: up to 6% matching and additional 3% non-elective contribution & Student Loan Match Community Impact: United Way Angel Day, Volunteer Day and Associate Directed Contribution Associate Resource Groups: creating a culture of respect and inclusion Recognize a fellow associate through our GEM awards Job Description Provides legal advice, including direction on transactional matters, commercial loan and other general legal transactions and issues. Assists more senior level attorneys in the provision of legal advice to in-house clients, in transactions, vendor and loan agreements and other legal matters. Reviews legal publications and pending legislation and advises management of changes that impact CoBank. Executes smaller, less complex tasks delegated by more senior level attorneys and may represent CoBank in negotiations. Essential Functions Provides legal services, legal counsel, guidance, recommendations, and proactive advice, in consultation with their supervisor, on legal issues to assigned individual banking groups/divisions/management. Conducts legal research and issues legal opinions. With respect to transactional matters, prepares, reviews, negotiates and/or interprets various legal instruments and documents of all types such as contracts, confidentiality agreements, leases, loan agreements, collateral documents, organizational documents and other agreements. Reviews and analyzes loan or lease and collateral documentation and drafts legal audits memoranda for assigned individual banking groups; consults with and advises relationship managers and other associates concerning loan transactions. Reviews paralegal work on various matters, including signatory authority reviews, collateral summaries and title insurance issues. Education JD From an approved law school required Admission in state bar required Work Experience 1 year of experience in commercial transactions or representing lenders and borrowers in negotiating, documenting, and closing a wide range of commercial financing transactions required 2 years of experience in commercial transactions or representing lenders and borrowers in negotiating, documenting, and closing a wide range of commercial financing transactions preferred Knowledge of other areas of law related to transactions (e.g., environmental law) Basic knowledge of the laws and regulations affecting the Farm Credit System Basic knowledge of corporate and commercial law in the context of commercial loan transactions, including real estate and personal property collateral, participations, and syndications. Physical Exertion Details Sedentary Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally (Occasionally: activity or condition exists up to 1/3 of the time) and/or a negligible amount of force frequently (Frequently: activity or condition exists from 1/3 to 2/3 of the time) to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time, but may involve walking or standing for brief periods of time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met. Travel Requirement Details Occasional Travel occurs infrequently (typically, once a month or less). About CoBank The typical base pay range for this role is between $100,000 – $123,000. Compensation may vary based on individual job-related knowledge, skills, expertise, and experience. This position is eligible for a discretionary annual incentive program driven by organization and individual performance. The listed salary, other compensation and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. This job will be posted for a minimum of five (5) business days or until the position is filled. CoBank reserves the right to adjust compensation for all positions and to modify or discontinue benefits programs at any time in its sole discretion, subject to applicable law. CoBank is a cooperative bank serving vital industries across rural America. The bank provides loans, leases, export financing and other financial services to agribusinesses and rural power, water and communications providers in all 50 states. The bank also provides wholesale loans and other financial services to affiliated Farm Credit associations serving more than 76,000 farmers, ranchers and other rural borrowers in 23 states around the country. CoBank is a member of the Farm Credit System, a nationwide network of banks and retail lending associations chartered to support the borrowing needs of U.S. agriculture, rural infrastructure and rural communities. Headquartered outside Denver, Colorado, CoBank serves customers from regional banking centers across the U.S. and also maintains an international representative office in Singapore. REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION We are committed to ensuring that our online application process provides an equal employment opportunity to all applicants, including qualified individuals with disabilities. If you are an applicant with a disability, or are assisting an applicant with a disability, and require accessibility assistance or would like to request a reasonable accommodation for any aspect of the application process, including completing an application, interviewing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please submit a request by emailing [email protected] . Include your contact information and specific details about your requested accommodation. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. CoBank is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. item.title: Counsel (Policy, Oversight, Ethics)
item.description: Counsel (Policy, Oversight, Ethics) Organization: Democracy Defenders Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Democracy Defenders Action, a 501(c)(4) organization Full time, Exempt, Remote Organizational Overview The Democracy Defenders family of organizations (a c3, c4, legally separate PAC, and The Contrarian) is a leader in the fight against authoritarianism, working strategically in the courts and court of public opinion to restore American democracy by: upholding the rule of law, safeguarding free and fair elections, and fighting corruption. Role Purpose The Counsel leverages their legal research, writing, and analysis skills to support a portfolio of accountability, transparency, and ethics in government initiatives, playing a key role in all aspects of DDA’s 2027 government reform agenda. As a member of the Policy, Oversight, and Ethics (POE) department, the Counsel will report to the Deputy Director for Anticorruption and Ethics and work closely with senior department members on various matters, cultivating expertise across a spectrum of pro-democracy, anti-authoritarian issue areas and tactics. To best protect, strengthen, and rebuild our democracy, it is critical that DDA’s staff reflects the diversity of backgrounds and experiences represented in the democracy we seek to defend. Applicants of all backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Responsibilities In collaboration with the Chief Counsel and Director for Anticorruption and Ethics (department director), the Deputy Director for Anticorruption and Ethics (direct manager), and senior department members, identify, track, and respond to potential corruption, unethical activities, and misconduct by government officials. Prepare administrative complaints, regulatory comments, and Freedom of Information Act requests, including complaints under the criminal conflict of interest laws, the Hatch Act (political activity), and the federal appropriations laws. Assist in POE’s legislative and policy reform initiatives in coordination with relevant POE team leads, including conducting research and drafting letters, preparing senior leadership for hearings and meetings, and preparing talking points and testimony. Assist in producing high-quality written content, including policy reports, op-eds, summary documents, and more, in both long-term and rapid-response scenarios. Review financial disclosure reports and ethics documents for individual violations of law, potential conflicts of interest, and overall trends that may point to vulnerabilities in government programs. Provide subject matter expertise and research support on corruption-related litigation (as directed by Counsel in our Litigation and Rapid Response depts). Translate matter updates and impact for the Communications and Fundraising departments, connecting specific matters to our larger pro-democracy and anti-authoritarianism effort. Work closely with organizations and principals across the political spectrum and coordinate mission-aligned working groups. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Juris Doctorate (JD) degree from an accredited law school. Membership in good standing with a state bar in the United States, with the ability to waive into the DC bar if necessary. 2 – 8 years of legal work in one or more of the following areas: administrative law, constitutional law, privacy and data security laws, election law, federal civil service laws, or public records laws. Familiarity with congressional or executive oversight, investigative, or regulatory complaint procedures or comparable private sector procedures. Strong verbal and interpersonal communication skills. Excellent legal writing, analytical, and research abilities. Sound judgement and discretion in handling sensitive information. Proven ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize effectively, and collaborate with various stakeholders. Unwavering commitment to defeating election sabotage and denial, fighting autocracy, and building a resilient democracy; Experience (professional, volunteer, or otherwise) advancing democracy, election integrity, and the rule of law. Commitment to diversity and inclusivity and an ability to work with colleagues and stakeholders across diverse cultures, backgrounds, and beliefs. Willingness to perform weeknight and weekend work as needed. Willingness to travel occasionally for meetings in DC or conferences. Role and Compensation Details This role is ideally based in the Washington DC/DMV area. Candidates who are available for in person tasks and meetings will be given preference, but we are open to this role being remote for the right candidate. The Oversight Counsel sits in our Policy, Oversight, and Ethics department and reports to the Deputy Director, Anticorruption and Ethics. This role primarily supports Democracy Defenders Action and Democracy Defenders Fund. The salary range for this position is $85,000 – 140,000, commensurate with experience. DDA provides a comprehensive benefits package including 20+ days of PTO, 12 holidays, health insurance (100% paid for employee and 50% paid for family), 401K with match, tech and home office stipends, coworking space access, and recurring teambuilding opportunities. If you are unsure about applying, we encourage you to make a case as to why you are a compelling candidate. A human reviews all application materials, and we are eager to hear from candidates who may not meet all of the qualifications, who possess transferable skills, and who have non-traditional work histories. Democracy Defenders Action is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Vice President, Health Policy
item.description: Vice President, Health Policy Organization: Feeding America Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Work. Serve. Thrive. Imagine a place where your talent can make a meaningful difference in peoples’ lives. Working at Feeding America is a uniquely rewarding experience in which our employees work together as vital parts of a much larger mission. We are innovative, mission-focused, diverse, collaborative, values-driven and focused on results. Feeding America is the nation’s largest charity and the leading domestic hunger-relief charity in the United States. Our mission is to feed America’s hungry through a nationwide network of member food banks and engage our country in the fight to end hunger. This position is based out of Feeding America’s Washington DC office. At Feeding America, we believe in offering a flexible work environment. Employees can be in the office an average of 2 days a week (when not travelling for work) and work from home on other days. Employees also have access to a 30-day “work anywhere” program during the course of each calendar year that can be combined with PTO and/or holidays. The Opportunity The Vice President, Health Policy leads enterprise strategy, advocacy, and external influence to increase federal and state support for Feeding America’s food-as-medicine initiatives and priority health policy objectives, including protecting and strengthening critical health programs serving people facing food insecurity. The Vice President, Health Policy positions Feeding America as a national thought leader in legislative and administrative health policy, including engagement with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Medicaid, the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), and other relevant federal health programs. Advances comprehensive legislative, regulatory, lobbying, and funding strategies that strengthen Feeding America’s healthy food and food-as-medicine agenda. Coordinates across Government Relations; Health, Research & Evaluation; and other internal teams to align health policy priorities with Farm Bill, commodities, Child Nutrition, federal and state funding opportunities, and other organizational priorities. Provides strategic direction on high-level policy and funding opportunities by translating federal parameters into actionable state- and network-level guidance. Serves as Feeding America’s primary registered lobbyist and organizational representative on health policy. Compensation Here at Feeding America national organization, equality is central to our mission and is an integral part of our compensation policies and structures. As such, we maintain transparent salary ranges and clearly defined practices for how our team, including new hire salary offers, moves through these ranges. You can expect us to offer the best salary up front based on these clearly defined pay practices with little room for negotiation. We make exceptions for highly experienced (multiple years of at-level experience) new hires in accordance with our pay practices. Once hired, employees have the opportunity to progress through salary ranges via regular merit increases and step promotions. Salary Range: $203,952 – $227,946 Based on Experience Responsibilities: Sets and leads enterprise health policy and funding strategy to advance Feeding America’s federal health care and food-as-medicine priorities, including protecting and strengthening Medicaid, positioning the organization and network for grants, authorities, waivers, and other federal health funding pathways, and strengthening programs that serve people facing food insecurity. Aligns Government Relations; Health, Research & Evaluation; and other internal teams around shared priorities, execution plans, and decision-making processes. Leads federal legislative and regulatory advocacy on health policy, food-as-medicine initiatives, Medicaid, HRSA programs and authorities, and related health programs. Develops legislative proposals, regulatory recommendations, testimony, speeches, presentations, and other advocacy materials while contributing to health-related provisions of the Farm Bill, nutrition legislation, budget, appropriations, and other federal policy priorities. Builds and leverages strategic relationships with Congressional offices, Administration officials, HHS, HRSA, other federal agencies, health-sector coalitions, policymakers, and external partners. Serves as a primary representative and advocate for Feeding America, advancing organizational priorities and strengthening the organization’s influence across the political spectrum. Positions Feeding America as a national thought leader on hunger, health, food as medicine, and public policy. Serves as a spokesperson and subject matter expert in policymaker engagements, coalitions, hearings, public forums, conferences, and other external settings. Directs policy and funding intelligence, research, analysis, and communications to inform organizational strategy and influence policymakers. Oversees proactive monitoring of legislative, regulatory, agency, grant, waiver, demonstration, and other federal and state funding developments; identifies emerging risks and opportunities; and guides the development of policy memoranda, funding opportunity analyses, fact sheets, reports, speeches, and other internal and external communications. Provides strategic counsel and network support to the CEO, Board of Directors, Executive Team, National Advisory Council (NAC), Chief Government Relations Officer, Policy Engagement and Advocacy Committee (PEAC), Holistic Support Advisory Committee, network members including food banks, affiliates and partner state associations. Translates complex federal policy and funding opportunities into clear state- and network-level guidance, technical assistance, and actionable strategies for diverse audiences. Educates and mobilizes key audiences including policymakers, stakeholders, partner organizations, network leaders, and the public. Advances understanding of hunger, food insecurity, health policy, and evidence-based solutions that support Feeding America’s mission and advocacy goals. Supports fundraising and donor-funded initiatives in partnership with Development and Health, Research & Evaluation teams. Provides subject matter expertise for donor cultivation, funding strategies, proposal development, grant execution, budget and timeline management, reporting, and accountability for funded project outcomes. Required Experience and Qualifications: 10+ years of progressively senior experience in health policy, public policy advocacy, government relations, issue campaigns, or grassroots mobilization, with a demonstrated record of influencing federal or state policy outcomes. Experience working on Capitol Hill, in an Administration, political campaign, federal or state government, or policy advocacy organization. Exceptional executive-level written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders, policymakers, board members, and external partners with clarity, judgment, and credibility. Deep knowledge of health policy, Medicaid, HHS, HRSA, federal and state legislative and regulatory processes, congressional committee structures, and the relationship between federal and state health agencies. Proven ability to think strategically, exercise sound judgment, and lead effectively within teams and broad coalitions that include diverse perspectives, political viewpoints, and organizational priorities. Ability to translate complex federal funding authorities, agency guidance, and program requirements into timely, actionable policy and funding strategies for state associations, food banks, and coalition partners. Accomplished people leader with demonstrated ability to develop direct reports, support network advocates, and build high-performing, mission-aligned teams. Preferred Competencies, Experience and Certifications: Federal health policy experience strongly preferred. Required Leadership Competencies: Fosters an Enterprise Mindset Fosters an Open and Supportive Environment Leads with Accountability Collaborates Internally and Externally Focuses on People and Teams Manages Organization and Business Complexity Communicates with Impact and Influence Feeding America’s goal is to attract, develop, retain, and promote a talented diverse workforce where all employees feel a sense of belonging and contribute to a culture that values differences, ideas, and experiences. We intentionally seek out diverse perspectives and skills on our teams, knowing that it makes us stronger as an organization and better equipped to serve our neighbors in need. We encourage all individuals, including those from historically under-represented communities and individuals with lived experience of hunger, to apply. Feeding America participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Vice President – General Counsel (4317) Organization: Seven Hills Foundation Location: Worcester, MA Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Description Vice President, General Counsel Seven Hills Foundation | Executive Leadership Salary: $250,000.00 to $285,000.00 per year Seven Hills Foundation is seeking an accomplished and strategic Vice President, General Counsel to serve as the organization’s chief legal advisor and a trusted member of the executive leadership team. Reporting directly to the President & CEO, the Vice President, General Counsel will provide strategic legal guidance to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership across all divisions of Seven Hills Foundation. This is an exceptional opportunity for an experienced attorney who combines strong legal expertise with business judgment, leadership, and a commitment to mission-driven work. What You’ll Do As Vice President, General Counsel, you will: Serve as the organization’s chief legal advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership. Provide strategic counsel on corporate governance, business operations, compliance, risk management, and regulatory matters. Lead legal strategy related to contracts, employment matters, litigation, real estate, insurance, and corporate transactions. Oversee litigation, including outside counsel, litigation strategy, discovery, and settlement negotiations. Lead legal support for mergers, acquisitions, affiliations, and other strategic transactions, including due diligence and transaction negotiations. Advise on federal and state regulatory requirements, including employment law, HIPAA, privacy, healthcare/mental health regulations, and funder requirements. Partner with Human Resources, Quality & Compliance, Finance, and other leadership teams on complex and sensitive organizational matters. Develop and deliver legal training for managers and leaders. Lead the Legal Department and manage its budget and outside legal resources. Help develop policies and procedures that support compliance, sound governance, and organizational best practices. Why Seven Hills Foundation? At Seven Hills Foundation, legal leadership is about more than managing risk. It is about helping a mission-driven organization grow responsibly, protect the people and communities it serves, and make sound decisions that support its long-term future. The Vice President, General Counsel will have the opportunity to work closely with executive leadership and the Board while influencing strategy across a complex and dynamic organization. If you are an experienced legal executive ready to make a meaningful impact through strategic, mission-driven leadership, we encourage you to apply. Qualifications: What We’re Looking For Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school. Admission to the bar in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and New Hampshire, or ability to obtain admission in all three states. 10+ years of legal experience, with substantial in-house experience preferred. 10+ years of management experience. Demonstrated expertise in areas such as employment law, contracts, corporate governance, litigation, real estate, healthcare/mental health law, regulatory compliance, and/or M&A. Proven ability to negotiate complex matters, assess risk, solve problems, and exercise sound judgment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. Strong leadership, organizational, analytical, and relationship-building skills. Experience in human services, healthcare, behavioral health, or nonprofit organizations is a plus. Qualifications Required Education: – Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school. – Active membership in good standing with the state bar. Required Experience: – Minimum of 10 years of legal experience, preferably in a healthcare or non-profit organization. – Proven track record in a senior legal position, with experience in managing legal teams and advising executive leadership. – Extensive experience in handling complex legal matters, including litigation, compliance, and regulatory issues. – Demonstrated experience in strategic planning and execution within a legal framework. Required Skills and Abilities: – Strong leadership skills with the ability to mentor and develop a legal team. – Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a keen attention to detail. – Superior communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to convey complex legal concepts to non-legal stakeholders. – High level of integrity and ethical standards in all professional dealings. – Ability to work collaboratively with other departments and external partners to achieve organizational goals. – Proficiency in legal research and staying updated with changes in laws and regulations affecting the organization. item.title: Senior Director, Global Tuberculosis
item.description: Senior Director, Global Tuberculosis Organization: Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Overview The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. CHAI’s Global TB Program Overview Tuberculosis is the world’s deadliest infectious disease. Beyond 10 million people fall ill each year, and 1.2 million die, with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa and South and Southeast Asia. Roughly 40% of TB cases remain undiagnosed, fuelling ongoing transmission in communities. Children under five, people living with HIV, and those in underserved or displaced populations face the greatest risk. CHAI partners with governments, multilateral organizations, and suppliers to close critical gaps across the TB care cascade. Our work spans three interconnected domains: Screening and diagnosis: accelerating the adoption of digital chest X-ray with AI, near-point-of-care molecular diagnostics, tongue swabs, and sample pooling strategies that bring accurate, rapid testing closer to patients. Treatment and prevention: expanding access to shorter, more effective regimens for both active and latent TB, with particular focus on community-based delivery of TB preventive therapy to children under five and other high-risk household contacts. Market shaping: negotiating price reductions, supporting generic product development, and ensuring sustainable supply of quality-assured TB commodities, from rifapentine-based preventive regimens to next-generation diagnostic platforms. The program currently operates across 13 countries in Africa and Asia. CHAI’s Global TB Team provides strategic direction, technical leadership, and coordination across these country programs, while managing relationships with key funders and partners including the Global Fund, Gates Foundation, Unitaid, FCDO, GiveWell, Stop TB Partnership, and national TB programs. Position Overview New diagnostic tools, shorter treatment regimens, and growing political will are converging to create a real opportunity to reduce the toll of TB. At the same time, uncertain funding landscapes, fragmented health systems, and the sheer scale of the undiagnosed burden demand a leader who can operate with both strategic ambition and operational discipline. We are looking for a Senior Director who will serve as CHAI’s most senior voice on TB, both internally and externally. This person will set a clear programmatic vision, articulate it compellingly, and bring a wide range of audiences along country teams translating strategy into action, government leaders deciding how to allocate scarce resources, and funders weighing where to invest. That funder base includes long-standing partners such as the Gates Foundation and Unitaid, whose support remains central to the program, as well as a growing set of evidence-driven philanthropists who assess TB investments on cost-effectiveness and counterfactual impact. The Senior Director will need to sustain and deepen the first set of relationships while building the second, making the case for TB with rigour and in the terms each funder uses. The TB landscape involves a rich ecosystem of multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, research institutions, civil society, and national programs, each with distinct mandates, priorities, and ways of working. Success in this role requires someone who can build trust and find common ground across that ecosystem, forging alignment where interests converge and navigating constructively where they diverge. Reporting to the Vice President, HIV, Hepatitis and TB, the Senior Director will be responsible for shaping a portfolio that spans community-based prevention pilots, diagnostic technology introduction, market shaping interventions, and operational research across multiple countries. The Senior Director will lead a team that includes two Directors who serve as the program’s scientific and technical leads, bringing deep expertise in TB diagnostics, treatment, prevention, and market shaping. The Senior Director’s role is strategic ownership of the overall program direction, impact model, and funder relationships, working in close partnership with these Directors to ensure technical excellence and programmatic coherence across the portfolio. The ideal candidate brings a rigorous, quantitative approach to deciding where resources do the most good and a track record of delivering sustainable public health impact in low- and middle-income countries. They will set a compelling strategic direction that galvanizes teams and partners and translates into measurable, large-scale impact in the countries where TB takes its greatest toll. Responsibilities Strategy and Program Leadership Define and communicate a bold strategic direction for CHAI’s global TB portfolio, translating organizational priorities, donor expectations, and the evolving needs of high-burden countries into a coherent vision that the team, partners, and governments can rally behind. Scan the horizon for shifts in TB financing, epidemiology, policy, and the diagnostic and therapeutic pipeline; position CHAI to respond proactively and shape the conversation. Make disciplined strategic choices about where CHAI should focus, including decisions to scale, pivot, or wind down workstreams based on evidence of impact per dollar, counterfactual value, and changing conditions. Develop multi-year programmatic plans, budgets, and performance management systems that drive accountability and continuous improvement across the portfolio. Champion the translation of evidence and operational learning into scalable, government-led program models. Orient the program at every stage toward government ownership, from design through financing and scale-up, so that impact endures beyond CHAI’s engagement. Resource Mobilization and Funder Engagement Lead development and execution of CHAI’s TB resource mobilization strategy, sustaining and growing support from long-standing institutional donors while building a significant new base of support from evidence-driven philanthropy, and building resilience against shifts in the global aid landscape. Manage major donor relationships and program finances, including with the Global Fund, Gates Foundation, Unitaid, FCDO, and GiveWell, ensuring high-quality reporting, proactive risk management, and disciplined deployment of resources. Build relationships with funders who prioritize cost-effectiveness, including foundations, individual philanthropists, and pooled funds associated with the effective giving community. Make the case for TB investment in the terms these funders use: cost per death or disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted, counterfactual impact, room for more funding, and the quality of the underlying evidence. Engage directly with funders’ research and grant making staff, responding to detailed questions about assumptions, uncertainty, and track record, and using that scrutiny to strengthen the program. Identify and pursue non-traditional funding opportunities, positioning CHAI’s TB work within broader global health and development agendas, including the growing interest in AI-enabled health solutions. Analytical and Technical Leadership Set the intellectual agenda for CHAI’s TB work: define the questions the organization should be asking, identify where conventional approaches are falling short, and push the team to develop stronger answers. Own the TB program’s impact model: the cost-effectiveness estimates, assumptions, and uncertainty behind CHAI’s investment case. Revise it as evidence changes and defend it with funders, partners, and governments. Ensure country and regional teams receive strong technical guidance on complex programmatic, policy, and scientific questions spanning diagn
