item.title: Communications Senior Associate
item.description: Communications Senior Associate Organization: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Key Information Role: Communications Senior Associate Salary: $81,000 – $100,000 USD annually (pre-tax) Location: Remote, restricted to candidates in the UK or US (Eastern Time Zone only). Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Job type: Full-time, permanent position. Start date: As soon as possible, ideally by late November 2026. Application deadline: Friday, October 23, at the end of the day (23:59) PDT. Contact: Please email [email protected] if you have any questions about the hiring process. About the Position We are looking for a Communications Senior Associate to both serve as the operational backbone of our communications function and contribute to content creation in their own right. This role would suit someone who thrives on execution from inception of content through to delivery and enjoys shaping polished content, from social media posts to newsletters, web copy to publications. The Communications Senior Associate will track projects, value accuracy and attention to detail, and be ready to step in and shape content when needed. They will enjoy translating complex technical research into accessible, accurate, and punchy content, coordinating with policy, research, and programs teams to deliver on time. They’ll be comfortable switching between projects and priorities, and be driven by the fast-moving AI policy environment. Reporting to the Communications Manager, this role provides essential support to the implementation of communications strategy and plans that advance IAPS’s mission. As a remote-first organization, we seek candidates with the ability to take the initiative and move work forward independently, while staying closely connected and collaborative with colleagues. This role involves a high level of coordination, so it would suit candidates who are comfortable engaging regularly with teammates and stakeholders. This is a fully remote position only open to candidates in the US (Eastern Time Zone only) or UK who have valid work authorization. The annual salary range is $81K-$100K USD, or the equivalent in GBP (using a historical average conversion rate). Candidates based in London or Washington, DC are eligible for a location uplift. All salaries are pre-tax. We have a preference for candidates who can work full-time (40-hours per week). Time Zones and Working Hours: This role will be best suited for applicants based in the UK or US East Coast (Eastern Time); therefore, we will only be considering applicants in those geographic regions. Travel: Please note that international travel, including at least for a length of two weeks for our annual organization-wide retreat and programming events, is an essential requirement for this position. We ask that you only apply if you are able to meet the travel requirements for this position. Key Responsibilities Operations & Execution Track communications deliverable from assignment to publication or launch, and flag deadline risks early. Manage business as usual workflow, approvals, and handoffs through the publications process, coordinating with teams across the organization. Oversee production of digital and multimedia content, managing contractors and agencies. Ensure quality control helping to raise the editorial bar. Lead regular updates of Style Guide, branding, and templates. Content Creation Draft and edit copy for web, social platforms, and organizational newsletters. Repurpose longer research/policy content into shorter, platform-ready formats (a report into a carousel, a brief into a LinkedIn post). Leverage digital platforms and spot opportunities for new content formats that promote and extend the reach of our research to key stakeholders. Provide communications inputs to programming and events. Support the drafting of executive communications and thought leadership when capacity requires it. What We Are Looking For Required Skills and Experience 5+ years in a communications role that combined hands-on writing/content production with project or editorial operations. Experience in policy or think tank environments is preferred. Strong writing and editing skills — comfortable working with technical and complex materials. Demonstrated initiative and solutions-oriented mindset, with ability to prioritize among multiple demands. Sharp attention to detail and ability to unblock production. Experience with CMS, project management, and communications tools (Payload, WordPress, Trello, Mailchimp etc.) Experience with social media platforms. Desired Skills and Experience Familiarity with AI policy, national security, or governance issues. Ability to juggle competing projects and priorities. High attention to detail. Familiarity with using analytics to improve communications outputs. Solid judgment and ability to spot communications risks. What We Offer Compensation Annual salary within the following range for a full-time position, prorated for part-time work: $81,000 – $100,000 USD (pre-tax). Compensation is paid in your local currency. For example, if you are a UK resident, we would pay the equivalent to the amounts above but in GBP. We use a set methodology to determine conversion rates, which are reviewed regularly. The exact salary will be based on the candidate’s prior relevant experience and location (candidates in DC and London will receive relatively higher salaries). Other Benefits Comprehensive global benefits package, including generous health insurance. Generous paid time off (PTO) and unpaid leave, including: Unlimited vacation with a minimum 30 days off per year (which includes public local holidays). Unlimited (within reason) personal and sick leave. Parental leave: up to 6-9 months of a combination of paid and unpaid leave that can be taken within the first 2 years after a child’s birth or adoption. Technology budget equivalent to $5,000 USD every 3 years for purchasing work and office equipment. Coworking support (including in-person desk space in our hub locations) and AI tools budget to help you be your most productive self. Annual team retreat and other opportunities for paid travel of generally 1-2 weeks per trip, including stipends to help cover the cost of dependent care while traveling. We encourage proactive professional development and offer learning opportunities, including conferences, workshops, training, and professional certifications. Hiring Process-Specific Information We are not able to sponsor visas for this role. Evaluation Stages: There are 4 steps in our evaluation process for this role: (1) Application questions, (2) paid work test to demonstrate ability to create communications products (3) interviews with members of the Communications and Policy teams and (4) reference checks. We may insert a brief additional step to help us fairly assess candidates. If used, this step will be communicated in advance. Inclusivity and fairness: IAPS is committed to building an inclusive, equitable, and supportive community for you to thrive and do your best work. Please don’t hesitate to apply for a role regardless of your age, gender identity/expression, political identity, personal preferences, physical abilities, veteran status, neurodiversity or any other background. We provide reasonable accommodations and benefits, including, for example, flexible work schedules and locations, mental health coverage through medical benefits (as available), as well as technology budgets and professional development time that can be used, for example, to purchase assistive technology or engage in job coaching. Accessibility: We’re committed to running an inclusive and accessible hiring process. We warmly invite you to reach out to [email protected] with any questions or accessibility requests such as chat box use during interviews. Extension Requests: We will try to accommodate extension requests that are made before the deadline and are for up to three days. We generally cannot accommodate extension requests made on or after the application deadline, or are longer than three days, and cannot accept late submissions to ensure fairness to other applicants. About IAPS IAPS is a nonpartisan think tank that engages experts across the U.S., allied, and partner nations to deliver concrete, technically sound policy research. We believe that AI and AGI are poised to bring transformative change over the coming years, and want to play an active role in shaping its future. Our work involves: Conducting forward-looking policy research in areas including preparedness, information and supply chain security, and international coordination needed to navigate strategic competition with adversaries who may misuse AI. Cultivating policy talent — IAPS is forging a community of researchers and practitioners from across many policy areas and backgrounds to meet this critical moment. Providing relevant and timely insights to stakeholders across Congress, the executive branch, industry, academia, and civil society. Follow these links to read more about our work and our team, and sign up to our newsletter. To apply, please click the ‘ Apply Now ‘ button. We ask that you spend no more than two hours preparing your responses to the prompts in the form. Note Before Applying: Please do not include a cover letter, photograph, or headshot of yourself, or any personal information that is not relevant to the role for which you’re applying (including marital status, age, identity traits, etc.). Additionally, please do not ask our staff members involved in the hiring process to meet with you. To ensure fairness, we try to minimize these interactions, and requests for meetings with the hiring committee members during the process will be declined. Contact: Please email [email protected] if you have any questions. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. More News & Resources « Webinar Economic Messaging Crash

item.title: Deputy Campaign Director
item.description: Deputy Campaign Director Organization: Design It For Us Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/12/2026 SALARY $70000 – $100000 (Yearly) HEALTHCARE Employer-sponsored health insurance offered DESIRED SKILLS Managed Paid Staff EMPLOYMENT TYPE Non-Profit MINIMUM LEVEL OF EXPERIENCE Departmental Staff (a role in a specific department. Ex: Organizer, Finance Assistant, Social Media Manager) APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Submit your application for our consideration using the following form . We will accept applications on a rolling basis. This announcement will remain posted until the position is filled. Please note that only those individuals whose qualifications match the current needs of this position will be considered applicants and will receive responses from DIFU. Thank you for your interest. APPLY BY October 30, 2026 JOB DESCRIPTION Given Big Tech’s profound array of harms and dangers for kids, teens, and young adults, Design It For Us (DIFU) has been at the forefront of elevating the lived experiences of young people and building partnerships with youth activists and organizations towards our shared objective of creating the digital future young people deserve. Design It For Us has grown in its size and scope, and is now looking for a Deputy Campaign Director to support and help drive Design It For Us’ campaign initiatives and expand our capacity and impact. The campaigner will work closely with the Managing Director, Campaigns & Policy Director, and the Co-Chairs of the DIFU coalition to co-create, spearhead and steward members through creative, timely and scaled place-based actions and events, while maintaining working relationships with state and national leaders. We’re looking for someone with youth organizing and advocacy campaigning experience. Previous success in elevating the voices of Gen Z and a demonstrated ability to take an idea and turn it into reality are critical to this start-up organization. The ideal candidate won’t be afraid to jump in and identify rapid-response or partnership opportunities, while also creating, tracking, and managing new and ongoing efforts and measuring impact. As the Deputy Campaign Director, you will: Collaborate closely with DIFU leadership to bring their vision to life Lead in the creation and execution of events, actions and other advocacy initiatives, including lobby days, demonstrations and rallies. Partner with Co-Chairs to organize youth leadership and general members around campaign activities Work directly with Co-Chairs to build and maintain infrastructure that enables members to participate in the advocacy initiatives you are responsible for driving Identify and build necessary grassroots structure to drive DIFU’s youth-led initiatives Build and grow partnerships with allied organizations and individuals to execute DIFU’s work Engage with Co-Chairs to expand DIFU’s membership through long-term organizing strategy Deliver successful campaigns and initiatives that drive forward DIFU’s mission Employ multi-disciplinary campaign management – able to come up with campaign actions, manage youth volunteers, organize coalition-building events, and more Track, manage and execute campaign tactics to drive incremental, structural change to the Big Tech business model Build relationships with external partners and manage coalition campaign efforts Create and maintain project trackers and keep campaign plans up to date Become well-versed in best practices and legal requirements for working with minors Understand the difference between c3 and c4 work and be able to uphold and reflect critical requirements in your work Project manage cross-functional teams to support all of the above One month in, you’ll know you’re successful in this role because you’ll: Have established a regular communication cadence with the leaders of DIFU Understand the short-term and long-term needs for DIFU Be comfortable discussing the objectives and policies of DIFU Have an understanding of the position we uniquely hold in the movement, and across our target states Three months in, you’ll know you’re successful in this role because you’ll: Help build out new actions and events, and support Co-Chairs in building additional outreach efforts for such events Successfully start supporting the expansion of DIFU’s membership through our leadership pipeline and engagement opportunities Be writing organizing and campaign plans, soliciting ideas and feedback from your colleagues and the DIFU leadership, and be implementing them Engage with external partners and represent DIFU in meetings, coalition calls, and at events About You: You’re deeply concerned about how the business model behind social media and AI products poses an existential threat to our wellbeing, and are driven to bring about long-term structural reforms to the industry You’re committed to the values of diversity and inclusion and excited to bring an equity lens to tech accountability work You have at least 1 year of prior full-time professional experience working in advocacy and coalition building and/or technology You have at least 1 year of prior full-time professional experience working with young people or elevating the voices of young people on public policy issues, on and off college campuses You’re organized, detail-oriented, and focused even in a fast-paced work environment You’re comfortable working on tight deadlines and balancing multiple projects; you’re confident when it comes to prioritization, especially in rapid response moments You’re self-motivated and don’t need too much oversight to move ideas into action or accomplish work by an agreed-upon deadline You have experience working with partner organizations, coalitions and/or allies on shared goals or campaigns You’re a strong communicator who isn’t afraid to speak up or ask questions; you’re skilled at leading presentations or pitching a campaign idea You have experience designing and executing strategic advocacy campaigns In addition, it would be a bonus if: You’re familiar with the ins and outs of advocacy campaigning, and have held a prior campaigner role You’re familiar with the impact of tech on digital natives You have experience in policy analysis You’re experienced in project planning and comfortable with lateral management You’re familiar with social media platforms, including both the largest platforms like Instagram or TikTok, as well as smaller or alternative platforms Benefits Comprehensive benefits package that includes employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance; employer contribution to 401 (k); stipend for work-from-home supplies and cell phone expenses; and 25 days of PTO that can be used for sick or vacation days in addition to paid holidays. About Design It For Us Design It For Us is a youth-led coalition leveraging grassroots power to disrupt Big Tech’s harmful business models. The coalition is led by a team of people between the ages of 18 and 26 and supported by an array of youth-led organizations, staff, and advisors fighting for a better online world for everyone. We’re building something new and necessary: a first-of-its-kind movement to design an online world where we can all thrive. Design It For Us is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit of Global Impact. About Global Impact Global Impact serves as a trusted philanthropy advisor, intermediary, and nonprofit partner for greater giving. We offer advisory and infrastructure services that drive strategic philanthropy for our nonprofit, public, and private sector clients. With 70 years of experience, we have raised more than $3 billion with our partners for global causes. Global Impact is part of Global Impact Ventures, a family of mission-driven organizations that serve all of philanthropy for a better world. At Global Impact, we passionately celebrate our culture, values, and community. We are committed to cultivating and nurturing a workplace for all. Global Impact encourages ALL interested candidates to apply for this position. Global Impact Careers Global Impact is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer and complies with all applicable employment laws. It is against Global Impact’s policy for any employee to discriminate against an applicant for employment or another employee on the basis of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, pregnancy, or childbirth or related conditions including lactation, military status or any other classification protected by applicable discrimination laws. Furthermore, it is against Global Impact’s policy for any employee, Board member, volunteer, partner, or vendor to discriminate in any way against an employee on the basis of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, pregnancy, or childbirth or related conditions including lactation, military status or any other classification protected by applicable non-discrimination laws. Global Impact celebrates a culture of belonging and is committed to cultivating and nurturing a workplace of diversity, equity, and inclusion. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Associate Director, Social Media
item.description: Associate Director, Social Media Organization: Braven Location: Atlanta, GA | Chicago, IL | New York, NY | Newark, NJ Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Description Job Title: Associate Director, Social Media Team: Communications & Marketing Location: Hybrid in Atlanta (GA), Chicago (IL) preferred, New York (NYC), or Newark (NJ) Employment Type: Full-time FLSA Classification: Exempt Start Date: ASAP About Braven Braven is a national nonprofit that prepares promising college students to secure a strong first opportunity after college graduation through a career-accelerating program. We work with higher education and employer partners to offer a life-changing experience that begins with a semester-long course for college students, followed by support that lasts through graduation. Together, our ambition is to help rebuild the middle class and revitalize the American Dream. To learn more, take a look at Braven’s . About the Role In order to achieve its ambition of serving 80,000-100,000 Fellows over the next decade, Braven is hiring an Associate Director, Social Media who will own and grow Braven’s social media presence into a dynamic engine for storytelling, community building, and mission amplification. As a key member of the Communications & Marketing team, you will develop and execute a bold social strategy creating platform-native content, building engaged audiences, and translating Braven’s impact into compelling digital narratives that resonate with students, partners, donors, and the broader public. This role is on the Communications & Marketing team and reports directly to the Senior Director, Communications. What You’ll Do Social media strategy and channel ownership (40%) Develop and own Braven’s social media strategy across Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X/Twitter, and emerging platforms, setting goals, KPIs, and a content calendar aligned to organizational priorities Partner with regional teams to align local social efforts with national brand standards, providing guidelines, templates, and real-time feedback to ensure consistency across all Braven markets Monitor platform trends, algorithm changes, and cultural moments to keep Braven’s presence timely, relevant, and audience-first Manage and grow all Braven social accounts with a consistent brand voice that reflects the energy and ambition of our Fellow community Content creation & storytelling (50%) Produce high-quality, platform-native content, including short-form video, graphics, reels, carousels, and copy, that brings Fellow stories and program impact to life Partner with central and regional teams to surface compelling narratives and translate them into engaging social content Maintain a content library of evergreen assets, testimonials, and multimedia resources for cross-channel use. Work with the Associate, Communications and Marketing to ensure we’re helping to amplify the incredible stories of our higher ed partners Community engagement and influencer relations Foster authentic engagement by actively responding to comments, DMs, and mentions and building relationships with followers and partners Identify and cultivate relationships with student ambassadors, Fellows, and aligned influencers who can amplify Braven’s reach organically Analytics, reporting, and optimization (10%) Track and report on social media performance metrics (e.g., reach, engagement, follower growth, and conversion) and use data to iterate on strategy Present regular insights and recommendations to leadership, translating analytics into clear opportunities for growth. Other duties as assigned. Requirements Minimum Requirements Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience 5+ years of experience managing social media for an organization, brand, or cause, including hands-on content creation and channel strategy Demonstrated ability to produce short-form video and visual content (experience with tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe suite, or equivalent) Proven track record of growing social audiences and driving measurable engagement Preferred Qualifications Experience in the nonprofit, higher education, or social impact sector Familiarity with social media management platforms (e.g., Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Later) and analytics tools Experience with paid social advertising and boosting content strategy Strong copywriting skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across platforms and audiences Comfort working in a fast-paced, startup-like environment with a lean team and high ownership Ability to take initiative, self-direct projects from concept to completion, and embrace ambiguity, embodying Braven’s value of Embrace the Journey Demonstrated commitment to building strong and welcoming cultures that help to develop others. Exemplification of Braven’s core values. Experience that has informed your belief in Braven’s mission and has prepared you to work with, or for, Braven’s student Fellow population. Please know that no one ever meets 100% of the preferred qualifications. If much of this describes you, we encourage you to apply. Work Demands Ability to work in-person in Atlanta (GA), Chicago (IL) preferred, Boston (MA) or Newark (NJ) 3 days per week Ability to travel to quarterly retreats with the External Affairs team and potentially other events Additional Requirements Authorized to work in the U.S. Braven doesn’t offer employment visa sponsorship Application & Interview Process While the interview process may vary slightly, the general process will be: Phone screen with Talent Team member Performance Task Interview with Hiring Manager Panel Interview with Key Partners Reference Checks Benefits Compensation and Benefits Braven offers competitive base salaries based on the midpoint of the market among not-for-profit organizations of similar size, with opportunities for salary growth over time. We believe in compensating staff members fairly in relation to each other, their qualifications, and their impact on behalf of the organization, and take internal and external equity seriously. Given our commitment to equity, Braven does not negotiate salary offers; instead, each salary offer is determined carefully using external and internal benchmarking. Starting salary within the range is determined by role scope and qualifications, with new hires starting at the lower end to allow for growth with performance. Braven does not base compensation on individual candidate salary expectations and is committed to maintaining internal equity. The starting salary ranges, by geographic market, for this role are set forth: $79,200-$87,100 in Atlanta, $83,600-$92,000 in Chicago, and $92,000-$101,100 in New York City and Newark. This is based on a 50-hour work week. This is a full-time, regular, exempt, and benefits eligible position where you will be working at 100% capacity. Braven also provides competitive, comprehensive benefits, recognition, and career development. While Braven reserves the right to change benefits at any time, current benefits include: Unlimited vacation time in addition to org-wide holidays and week-long shutdowns in July and the end of the calendar year (this is a minimum of 19 days per year) Braven supports your path to parenthood and beyond with $25,000 in lifetime Carrot benefits for fertility, family-building, and hormonal health Match of your 401K contribution up to 5% of your base annual salary, starting your first full month Coverage of 85% of health insurance premium for employee and dependents 12 weeks of paid parental leave A one-month paid sabbatical after 4 years on staff Please note that Braven is firm in its compensation philosophy; therefore, only candidates who believe our total rewards package aligns with what they are looking for in their next opportunity are encouraged to apply. Location We gather in the office 3 days a week (Tuesday through Thursday) and work remotely 2 days a week (Monday and Friday). Therefore, this role requires teammates to live within commuting distance of one of our hubs: Atlanta, Chicago preferred, New York or Newark. We believe in the magic, connection, and collaboration that happens when people work together face-to-face, and we believe in giving people flexibility to focus, balance personal priorities, and save themselves two commutes per week. Braven is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected factor. We encourage talented individuals of all backgrounds to apply. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, Community Engagement
item.description: Manager, Community Engagement Organization: Liliʻuokalani Trust Location: Honolulu, HI Date Posted: 10/12/2026 Job Purpose The Community Engagement Manager is responsible for leading Liliʻuokalani Trust’s community engagement strategy across all islands by building authentic relationships with Native Hawaiian communities, partners, participants, and ʻohana. This position ensures that the voices, experiences, and aspirations of the communities served are intentionally gathered, synthesized, and integrated into organizational planning, program design, evaluation, and continuous improvement. The Manager supervises Community Engagement Specialists and works collaboratively across the organization to strengthen trust, partnerships, and community-informed decision making. Essential Responsibilities Strategic Community Engagement Develop, implement, and continuously refine an organization-wide community engagement strategy that advances Liliʻuokalani Trust’s mission, strategic priorities, and commitment to Native Hawaiian communities. Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of community engagement initiatives that strengthen relationships with participants, ʻohana, community leaders, Native Hawaiian organizations, schools, cultural practitioners, nonprofits, government agencies, and other strategic partners. Identify opportunities to expand community partnerships that increase access to Trust programs, services, and resources while fostering long-term collaborative relationships. Ensure community engagement efforts are culturally grounded, trauma-informed, strengths-based, and reflective of Native Hawaiian values, traditions, and community priorities. Develop annual engagement plans, priorities, and performance goals that align with departmental and organizational objectives. Serve as a strategic advisor to leadership regarding community engagement opportunities, emerging issues, and partnership development. Community Voice & Relationship Management Develop and oversee comprehensive community listening strategies that intentionally gather the voices, experiences, aspirations, and concerns of Native Hawaiian communities, partners, and stakeholders. Lead the design and facilitation of listening sessions, community forums, focus groups, interviews, surveys, advisory groups, and other engagement activities. Build and sustain trusted relationships with community organizations, Native Hawaiian leaders, educational institutions, service providers, and public agencies. Ensure that community relationships are nurtured through regular communication, transparency, responsiveness, and meaningful collaboration. Identify emerging community needs, opportunities, trends, and challenges that may influence organizational strategy and program development. Serve as an ambassador for Liliʻuokalani Trust by representing the organization at community meetings, conferences, networking events, and collaborative initiatives. Organizational Insight & Strategic Decision Support Translate qualitative community feedback into meaningful organizational insights that support strategic planning, program development, evaluation, and continuous improvement. Partner with the Director of Impact & Insights to identify recurring themes, emerging issues, and opportunities across communities. Collaborate with the Research & Evaluation team to analyze community engagement findings and integrate qualitative data into broader organizational reporting. Prepare executive summaries, reports, presentations, and recommendations that communicate community perspectives to organizational leadership. Ensure community voice is consistently incorporated into organizational decision-making processes and strategic initiatives. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner closely with Program teams to support participant recruitment, engagement, retention, and community outreach efforts. Collaborate with the Research & Evaluation team to design community-informed evaluation activities, qualitative research, and data collection strategies. Work alongside the Quality Assurance team to identify opportunities to improve participant experiences based on community feedback. Coordinate with the Communications team to ensure messaging accurately reflects community priorities and strengthens organizational relationships. Collaborate with the Access & Referral team to strengthen referral pathways, increase community awareness of Trust services, and improve access to programs. Support cross-department initiatives by providing community engagement expertise during organizational projects, strategic planning efforts, and new program development. Performance Measurement & Continuous Improvement Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure the effectiveness, reach, quality, and impact of community engagement activities. Evaluate engagement strategies using qualitative and quantitative data to identify successes, gaps, and opportunities for improvement. Develop dashboards and reports that communicate engagement outcomes, participation trends, partnership growth, and community satisfaction. Recommend improvements to community engagement processes, tools, and methodologies based on evaluation findings and community feedback. Ensure community engagement practices remain aligned with organizational priorities, industry best practices, and evolving community needs. Community Partnership Development Identify, cultivate, and maintain strategic community partnerships that support the Trust’s mission and expand opportunities for Native Hawaiian kamaliʻi and ʻohana. Work collaboratively with community organizations to develop mutually beneficial partnerships that leverage shared resources, expertise, and community assets. Represent the Trust in collaborative planning efforts, coalitions, advisory groups, and statewide initiatives. Monitor partnership effectiveness and recommend strategies for strengthening long-term collaboration and collective impact. Administrative & Operational Leadership Develop and manage annual work plans, project timelines, and engagement calendars for the Community Engagement team. Monitor departmental priorities and ensure projects are completed on time and within scope. Support budget planning and resource allocation for community engagement initiatives. Maintain accurate documentation of community engagement activities, partnership agreements, meeting outcomes, and engagement metrics. Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and documentation standards. Perform other duties as assigned in support of departmental and organizational objectives. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Community Development, Public Administration, Social Work, Native Hawaiian Studies, Public Health, Communications, Sociology, Organizational Leadership, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in community engagement, partnership development, community organizing, public engagement, or a related field. Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience, including leading, coaching, and developing professional staff. Experience designing and implementing community engagement strategies across multiple stakeholder groups. Experience facilitating community meetings, listening sessions, focus groups, and collaborative partnerships. Experience synthesizing community feedback into actionable recommendations that inform organizational strategy, program design, or continuous improvement. Experience working collaboratively across multiple departments and with external partners to achieve shared goals. Required: Demonstrated experience engaging with Native Hawaiian communities and building authentic, trust-based relationships with Native Hawaiian individuals, ʻohana, community leaders, cultural practitioners, and Native Hawaiian organizations. Required: Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Native Hawaiian history, culture, values, community systems, and the unique strengths, opportunities, and challenges of Native Hawaiian communities, with the ability to apply this understanding to community engagement, relationship building, and partnership development. Job Competencies Knowledge of Native Hawaiian culture, community engagement principles, stakeholder engagement, qualitative research methods, and partnership development. Excellent relationship-building, facilitation, communication, leadership, strategic planning, analytical, and project management skills. Ability to build trust, lead multiple initiatives, influence organizational decision-making, and collaborate across departments. Able to work flexible hours, including nights and weekends, to meet key deadlines. Able to travel to meet strategic needs. Organization Competencies Alignment with Queen’s legacy: Understanding and appreciation of Queen Liliuokalani’s story, her legacy and the Hawaiian Culture is foundational to staff’s commitment to working with our Hawaiian children, families and communities. Demonstrates respect for and appreciation of Hawaiian values history, and culture, understanding its implication in one’s work, in fostering meaningful relationships, and in embracing the community served. Ho`omau i ka `imi Na`auao (Continuous Learning and Improvement): Committed to creating and reinforcing an environment of continuous learning and improvement. Ho`ike i na Mana`o Pono (Effective Communication): Communicates with those we serve and each other in a consistent manner that results in mutual understanding, harmony, and action. No’ono’o loi (Critical Thinking and Problem Solving): Actively and skillfully understands, conceptualizes, applies, analyzes, synthesizes, and/or evaluates information and develops and supports fact-based analyses and recommendations Ho’o kumu a’e or `Imi hakuhia (Innovation): Identifies and integrates creative ideas into new or existing services and promotes effective problem-solving. item.description: Communications & Marketing Manager Organization: American Medical Rehabilitation Providers Association (AMRPA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Internal Number: 4 General Purpose of the Position This position is responsible for leading the development and execution of comprehensive communications and marketing strategies to enhance the association’s visibility and member engagement. This position is an essential part of the team and will play a crucial role in promoting the many advocacy, education, and operational programs at the association. This position will involve performing all aspects of communications and marketing, including maintaining relationships with key media figures, amplifying AMRPA policy initiatives, securing opportunities for AMRPA to share our perspectives on policy issues, crisis communications management, and expanding awareness of AMRPA in general. This position reports directly to the AMRPA President. outreach, background briefings, one-pagers, social media content, member-facing summaries, website copy, op-eds, or other materials designed to increase visibility of AMRPA’s policy leadership Build issues involving IRFs, post-acute care reform, and/or other issues affecting Association members Develop crisis communications plan, core message framework, and support readiness Monitor national, data-driven decisions for continuous improvement Manage the association’s social media presence, creating captivating content, engaging with AMRPA members, and driving audience interaction across various platforms Develop editorial calendar aligning communications with both policy milestones and AMRPA operations-focused content Responsible for directly handling or ensuring all AMRPA created PowerPoints, presentations, videos, reports, website content, and other materials are visually professional and polished Respond to phone and email inquiries from members and prospective members about ‎specific and general ‎association inquiries Stay well informed about member organizations and relevant developments within the medical rehabilitation field Other duties as assigned that align with Hill experience a plus. Demonstrate existing relationships or ability to establish relationships with healthcare, Medicare, congressional, regulatory, and trade press reporters Strong customer service orientation and the ability to interact effectively with members and customers on the phone, through email communications, and in-person at events Polished communication skills, both written and verbal Experience with social media platforms in a business context as well as email marketing platforms Strong attention to detail, follow through, proactive communication both internally and externally, and organizational and planning skills is required Efficiently manage multiple projects, prioritizing deliverables through effective communication and established processes Proficient in Microsoft Office products (Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel), CRMs (Word Press, Salesforce), Canva, and databases (Association Management Systems) Ability to learn new technology and software required Reliability in maintaining established schedule, managing time and priorities, and meeting commitments and deadlines Proactive and collaborative working style Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. item.title: Director, Government Relations
item.description: Director, Government Relations Organization: McAllister & Quinn Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Description About McAllister & Quinn McAllister & Quinn is a federal and foundation grants consulting and government relations firm headquartered in Washington, D.C. We offer our 200+ clients a unique blend of comprehensive grant consulting, strategic advising, and government relations services. Specifically, McAllister & Quinn provides our clients with the knowledge and skills to seek federal and private foundation grant opportunities that strategically fit their organization’s priorities. We support our clients’ efforts in crafting competitive applications; developing or increasing funding streams through the congressional appropriations process; and facilitating public-private and international partnerships that further their mission. We are committed to securing funds for our clients that are transformational for the organizations who are awarded them, the people who work at these organizations every day, and the communities that surround them. The social impact of our work drives us daily to succeed in securing funding for our industry clients and is a major component of why we do what we do. We know that our success leads to better outcomes, changed lives, and a more equitable society for generations to come. Primary Duties and Responsibilities The Director will report to the Senior Managing Director, Government Relations, and collaborate with an experienced team that directly supports one of the Managing Partners’ personal client portfolios. This role combines client service, congressional engagement, appropriations strategy, and policy research. Responsibilities include: Assist the Managing Directors and Senior Managing Director with client and project management Support the Research Analyst in maintaining organized, accurate records using internal filing systems and data management tools Participate in and help facilitate client meetings and calls Schedule and participate in legislative meetings and liaise with congressional staff on behalf of clients Help prepare detailed itineraries and memos for client visits to Capitol Hill, including relevant information about elected officials, staff members, and districts or states; ensure all materials are printed and organized before each visit Conduct substantive research on issue and topic areas related to specific clients’ interests, priorities, and relevant trends, as well as item.title: AI Policy Manager, Legislation
item.description: AI Policy Manager, Legislation Organization: Meta Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Meta is looking for a senior policy leader to own our legislative and regulatory strategy on AI models and frontier AI, joining our global AI Policy team. This role sits at the center of the fastest-moving policy debate in technology. Frontier model regulation is being written now, in Congress, in US state legislatures, in national parliaments, in Brussels, and in regulator consultations worldwide. The person in this role will shape both what those rules say and how Meta responds to them. You will set strategy, counsel product and research teams building frontier models on what compliance will require, and brief senior leadership and executives on the decisions that matter. The remit is genuinely global. You will operate with significant autonomy across a broad and ambiguous portfolio, and you will be a primary external face of the company on frontier AI with legislators, regulators, civil society, academics, and industry coalitions. AI Policy Manager, Legislation Responsibilities Own the frontier AI legislative and regulatory portfolio. Anticipate, track, and analyze legislative and regulatory developments on AI models and frontier AI across the US Congress, US state legislatures, and international jurisdictions; distill them into clear, decision-ready guidance for internal partners Develop Meta’s positions. Set substantive policy positions on frontier AI legislation issues, including model evaluations and safety frameworks, transparency and content provenance, open source and model release policy, agentic systems, and incident reporting, and drive them to alignment across a complex internal stakeholder set Build and execute legislative strategy. Design advocacy strategies with clear objectives, target venues, coalition partners, and measures of success; drive them through to outcomes Draft and negotiate legislative text. Produce redlines, amendments, and model language on frontier AI proposals, and lead engagement with legislative offices, committee staff, and drafters on the Hill and in state and foreign legislatures in partnership with our Regional Policy and External Affairs teams Counsel product on compliance. Partner with product, research, engineering, and legal teams building frontier models to translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, and translate product and technical realities back into policy positions and advocacy asks Brief executives and senior leadership. Prepare and deliver written briefings and verbal recommendations to senior leaders and executives on frontier AI policy developments and the decisions they require, making clear recommendations under uncertainty and with incomplete information Lead regulatory engagement. Own responses to formal consultations, calls for evidence, and requests for information from regulators, agencies, and standards bodies, and represent Meta in those processes Represent Meta externally. Serve as a company representative in meetings with legislators and their staff, regulators, agencies, civil society, academics, and industry coalitions and trade associations, and speak at public convenings and closed-door briefings Collaborate cross-functionally. Work closely with Legal, Communications, Regulatory Readiness, Competition, Government Affairs, and regional policy teams to build and land aligned positions Build scalable frameworks. Create durable analytical frameworks, playbooks, and positions that other policy teams can apply to new proposals without starting from scratch Minimum Qualifications 10+ years of experience working on technology law or policy, in government, industry, private practice, civil society, or a combination Demonstrated expertise in AI policy, with substantive depth on frontier AI models, including their development, evaluation, deployment, and release, and on the regulatory debates surrounding them Technical fluency in how frontier models are built, evaluated, and deployed, sufficient to engage credibly with research and engineering teams and with technically sophisticated regulators Demonstrated leadership of legislative or regulatory advocacy strategies, from formation through to measurable outcomes, without day-to-day direction Experience analyzing and drafting legislation or regulation, including redlines and amendments Demonstrated experience briefing and advising senior leaders and executives, and making clear recommendations under uncertainty Demonstrated experience representing an organization externally with legislators, regulators, or coalitions Demonstrated skills and experience creating short- and long-form analyses, position papers, and talking points for both internal and external audiences Experience leading cross-functional work with legal, communications, and product or technical counterparts, including driving alignment across teams with competing priorities Experience prioritizing competing policy workstreams based on impact, deadlines, and stakeholder needs in fast-moving regulatory environments Experience creating scalable policy solutions and frameworks for policy teams to use based on knowledge of the AI policy environment Preferred Qualifications JD degree 14+ years of experience working on technology law or policy Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews) Experience working across multiple regions of the world, particularly the US, EU, and UK Experience leading multi-stakeholder coalitions, trade association working groups, or standards processes Advanced degree in public policy, computer science, or a related technical field Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements) Established relationships with legislators and their staff, regulators, or the AI policy research community Experience advising product, research, or engineering teams on translating regulatory requirements into product decisions, and vice versa Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Policy Research Associate
item.description: Policy Research Associate Organization: Nature Conservancy Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Description What We Can Achieve Together: The Policy Research Associate will support the evaluation, prioritization and advancement of state and local policies that can provide effective and scalable contributions to the adoption of regenerative agriculture practices and water quality improvements across the country, primarily though not exclusively at the state level. They will work with interdisciplinary teams to identify, compile, and research promising water policy interventions, develop legislative or administrative solutions for those interventions, and work with government relations professionals and others to implement those solutions at the state or federal level. The Research Associate will help identify and foster relationships with third-party contractors, including consultants, other NGOs, universities, among others to build TNC’s policy research capabilities. Responsibilities & Scope May supervise administrative staff and/or volunteers, interns, or temporary staff. Financial responsibility to complete projects appropriately and assist with budget development and meeting fundraising goals for local and worldwide conservation. Ensures program compliance with internal policies and external requirements. Works within scope of program’s strategic goals. Provides research and policy analysis in support of legislative and/or policy priorities. May aid with preparation of program materials including presentations, memos, and other communications. Influences the outcome of policy and/or corporate initiatives at the federal, state, and local levels. Develop strategic partnerships with relevant agencies, conservation organizations, and/or industry. Work independently, working with supervisor as needed. May require occasional domestic travel for multi-day retreats, meetings, and conferences May work long/flexible hours as needed to coordinate with staff and partners across the US or region. This is a full-time, 2-year grant-funded position with the possibility of extension based on continued grant funding. Working location is remote from a home office within the continental United States. We’re Looking for You: The Policy Research Associate will play a vital role in the development and support of replicable policy interventions at the state and local level to advance the outcomes of the North America Agriculture Program’s Water Policy Accelerator. They will serve as a subject matter expert on projects with other teams and will be responsible for assisting our government relations staff in advancing interventions to water quality challenges. A priority area for this work will be to research and design policy interventions that expand the implementation of Edge of Field practices, such as vegetative buffers and wetlands, as well as identifying and developing policy solutions to other water policy challenges. This position will report into the North America Agriculture Program, working closely with an interdisciplinary team from North America Policy and Government Relations, Global Conservation Campaigns, numerous state Business Units, and external stakeholders. The Policy Research Associate will have strong analytical skills, experience in policy analysis, and an understanding of law and the legislative process. The successful candidate will be able to work effectively independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, highly matrixed organization; and be adaptable to shifting needs and priorities. What You’ll Bring: Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree and 3 years related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience. Fluency in English Experience researching information from divergent sources and compiling it into a cohesive reporting structure. Experience with legislative or policy initiatives at the state level. Experience presenting to and communicating with government or corporate staff and/or program leadership. Experience working with partners and government agencies. Desired Qualifications: Juris Doctor Degree or Master’s Degree in Public Policy or related field. Experience drafting legislation and negotiating with interested parties. Experience developing or implementing federal or state policies, including funding/grant programs. Experience with programs, laws and stakeholders who engage on agriculture, water and land-use policy related work in the United States. Salary Information: The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $60,000 – $85,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate’s location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment. The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law. Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings! TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to [email protected] with Request for Accommodation in the subject line. item.title: Government & Policy Affairs Director
item.description: Government & Policy Affairs Director Organization: Pacific Life Insurance Company Location: Washington, DC | Newport Beach, CA Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Job Description: Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own. We’re actively seeking a talented Government & Policy Affairs Director to join our government and policy affairs team in Washington DC (preferred) or Newport Beach, CA. The Government & Policy Affairs Director will have primary responsibility for managing the political contributions program for Pacific Life. The Director will perform marketing, communications, event planning, compliance, membership development, and political programming in connection with the Pacific Life Political Action Committee (PAC). The Director will also engage in broader advocacy and public policy development in support of the enterprise. How you’ll help move us forward: Seek to grow PAC membership and contributions, support and develop an active and engaged PAC community, perform political compliance and contribution reporting functions, and develop contribution strategies for federal candidates in partnership with other members of the Government & Policy Affairs team. Help manage state political contribution strategy and compliance in key states. Responsible for compliance with campaign contribution laws and regulations. The Director will be conversant with Federal Election Commission (FEC) regulations and procedures pertaining to PAC’s, including regular reporting of receipts and disbursements. The Director will ensure that strong compliance procedures are in place to meet all reporting and disclosure requirements. Report regularly to the PAC Board and senior leadership on PAC operations and performance utilizing data-driven analysis and benchmarking techniques. The Director will serve in the capacity of corporate secretary for the PAC Board, preparing briefing materials, analysis, and financial reports for the PAC Board that highlight important trends to support Board decision-making. Some travel required to our Newport Beach Omaha, and Charlotte offices (approx. 15%). Support the advocacy function and represent the company before lawmakers, regulators, and state and federal trade associations. The candidate will help educate public officials and their staffs on public policy that impacts Pacific Life and its customers. The candidate will have the opportunity to advocate on a diverse set of public policy issues, with emphasis on tax, retirement security, financial services, and workforce benefits. The experience you bring: Minimum of 8 years relevant experience Must have experience managing a PAC for a large company or trade association with responsibility for overseeing compliance, fundraising, event planning, and communications. Strong writing, public speaking, and communications skills. Strong marketing, event planning, and membership development skills to support and engage PAC members. Growth Mindset. Ability to introduce new ideas and problem solve in support of broader goals. Strategic Mindset and Project Management. Ability to develop a plan and execute against that plan, managing both strategy and tactics to drive a project to completion. Strong teamwork, relationship, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work with teams and coalitions. #LI-AJ1 Base Pay Range: The base pay range noted represents the company’s good faith minimum and maximum range for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered to a candidate will be dependent upon several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications and geographic location. Also, most employees are eligible for additional incentive pay. $152,010.00 – $185,790.00 Your Benefits Start Day 1 Your wellbeing is important to Pacific Life, and we’re committed to providing you with flexible benefits that you can tailor to meet your needs. Whether you are focusing on your physical, financial, emotional, or social wellbeing, we’ve got you covered. Prioritization of your health and well-being including Medical, Dental, Vision, and Wellbeing Reimbursement Account that can be used on yourself or your eligible dependents Generous paid time off options including: Paid Time Off, Holiday Schedules, and Financial Planning Time Off Paid Parental Leave as well as an Adoption Assistance Program Competitive 401k savings plan with company match and an additional contribution regardless of participation You Can Be Who You Are We are committed to a culture of diversity and inclusion that embraces the authenticity of all employees, partners and communities. We support all employees to thrive and achieve their fullest potential. What’s life like at Pacific Life? Visit Instagram.com/lifeatpacificlife EEO Statement: Pacific Life Insurance Company is an Equal Opportunity /Affirmative Action Employer, M/F/D/V. If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran, you have the right to request an accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access our career center as a result of your disability. To request an accommodation, contact a Human Resources Representative at Pacific Life Insurance Company. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Aviation Safety Writer
item.description: Aviation Safety Writer Organization: Airline Owners & Pilots Association Location: Frederick, MD Date Posted: 10/13/2026 JOB SUMMARY: The AOPA Air Safety Institute (ASI) is dedicated to advancing general aviation (GA) safety through cutting-edge research, comprehensive analysis, and dynamic educational outreach. As an Aviation Safety Writer, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the voice, quality, and impact of ASI’s content across multiple platforms, including digital and print publications, video scripts, social media, newsletters, and promotional materials. Your editorial experience, storytelling ability, and knowledge of general aviation will be instrumental in engaging audiences, supporting AOPA membership growth, and advancing ASI’s mission. This role requires strong writing, editing, and project coordination skills. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Content Creation (90%) Produces original, insightful, and engaging written safety content that provides fresh perspectives on general aviation safety topics. Writes engaging, insightful, and compelling Accident Case Study video scripts, requiring strong attention to detail, fact-gathering, and the ability to convert NTSB investigation reports and dockets into meaningful narratives with applications for general aviation pilots. Ensures all materials (publications, video scripts, research reports, newsletters, press releases, social media posts, etc.) are well-researched, accurate, aligned with ASI’s mission, and delivered promptly. Participates in collaborative brainstorming, including expressing thoughts clearly, using active listening, and checking for understanding. Acknowledges and shows respect for others’ points of view. Contributes original ideas that derive insights from personal flying experiences, aeronautical knowledge, industry contacts, familiarity with companies and communities within general aviation, and understanding of major issues affecting the industry. Administrative (10%) Manages the ASI content release calendar and promotion frequency; maintains updated calendars tracking distribution of ASI assets across AOPA and ASI channels. Manages a small team of freelance writers who contribute to ASI’s work, ensuring their work aligns with ASI’s standards of excellence. Provides clear guidance, feedback, and quality control to maintain the integrity of all editorial outputs. **Although this job description aims to capture the majority of the position duties, other duties may be assigned based on business and departmental needs. REQUIRED JOB QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s degree in English, Journalism, or a related field OR significant professional experience. Proven experience in aviation writing, editing, and managing editorial quality, with a strong portfolio demonstrating leadership in content creation and editorial project coordination. Minimum FAA Private Pilot Certificate with an instrument rating. Certificated Flight Instructor (CFI) preferred. Ability to lead creative projects and drive content innovation. Strong organizational and project management skills are essential. Strong writing, editing, and verbal communication skills, with a keen eye for detail and a commitment to accuracy. Demonstrates initiative, punctuality, teamwork, and a positive attitude toward constructive feedback. Self-motivated with a strong commitment to continuous professional development. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and comfortable adapting to new tools and technologies as needed. PREFERRED JOB QUALIFICATIONS: Experience in all facets of journalism/corporate communications functions (including video production/writing, public & media relations, and ghostwriting) WORKING CONDITIONS: This position works in an office setting. Typical working hours are 8:30 am – 5 pm, Monday through Friday, with a one-hour lunch break. Some evening and weekend work may be required. Generally, a climate-controlled environment with occasional exposure to outdoor weather conditions when attending aviation-related events, including exposure to higher altitudes and confined spaces if in a general aviation aircraft. Some travel may be required to various general aviation or industry-related events. Travel is by aircraft (general aviation and commercial) and by road or public transit. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands of this position are typical of a standard office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will regularly be required to: Sit for extended periods while working at a computer or attending meetings. Use hands and fingers to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment. Communicate effectively via email, phone, and in-person, which requires clear speech, hearing, and vision. Occasionally lift or move items weighing up to 15 pounds, such as boxes of materials or equipment. Occasionally stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms during the course of normal office activities. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: This position is located at AOPA’s Frederick, MD, office. The salary range for this position is: $68,000 – $76,000, depending on education and experience. BENEFIT INFORMATION: Flight Training (earn your Private Pilot License for free) & Annual Flight Proficiency Program (so you can keep flying and remain proficient) Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance is available for employees and their dependents the 1st of the month following their start date Flexible Spending Plans Health Savings Plan with employer contribution (for eligible participants) 401(k) Retirement Plan with a company match, and annual discretionary supplemental employer contribution Company paid Short and Long-term Disability Insurance Company paid Life Insurance and AD&D insurance with the option to buy up Paid Time Off (PTO): 17 days accrued during first year (accruals increase based on tenure) Paid Holidays: 12 holidays Personal days: 3 (prorated based on hire date) Volunteer day: 1 (prorated based on hire date) Work From Home Fridays Paid Parental Leave AOPA Membership Employee Assistance Program Wellness Program (earn medical insurance premium discounts) Gym Reimbursement Program Supplemental insurance options (critical illness, accident, hospital indemnity) Tuition Reimbursement Program Discount on AOPA swag Business casual dress code Free coffee, tea, hot cocoa Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Specialist, State Government Relations
item.description: Specialist, State Government Relations Organization: Alzheimer's Association Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Position Summary: The Specialist, State Government Relations provides research, supports legislative tracking and drafts written products that support the department’s state policy work. The position operates in a fast-paced environment and is responsible for (1) tracking state legislation; (2) conducting policy research and summarizing findings; (3) drafting state policy resources and department communications; (4) coordinating logistics for the annual State Dementia Services Coordinator Summit; (5) working on programs, projects, and briefings sponsored by the State Government Relations department; and (6) providing administrative and meeting support to department staff. This position will interact considerably with other members of the State Government Relations team, staff in other departments within the policy office, and state government relations staff in the field in all 50 states who are advancing state policies around access to diagnostics and treatment, insurance coverage, Medicaid, caregiving and public health. This position reports to the Director of State Policy and is based in the Association’s Home Office in Washington, D.C. Responsibilities: Essential functions and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: ● Assists with state legislative tracking and supports the use of the tracking system by field staff. ● Conducts policy research and drafts state policy materials. ● Drafts and edits State Government Relations team products and communications including weekly newsletter content, department news updates, policy resources for field staff, website and intranet information, and annual summaries of state government relations activities. ● Assists with the management of all major state policy data sources and databases and collects related information from field staff. ● Develops PowerPoint slides for team presentations to internal and external audiences. ● Leads on logistical coordination and execution of the State Dementia Services Coordinator Summit, an annual convening of state agency officials. ● Provides administrative support to the State Government Relations team including supporting all on-site and virtual meetings, preparing meeting materials, and assisting with meeting follow-up activities. ● Other duties, programs, projects, and briefings sponsored by the State Government Relations department, as assigned. Qualifications: ● A bachelor’s degree is required. ● A minimum of two years of professional experience in a government affairs setting, with strong written and oral communications skills. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: ● Excellent written and oral communications and interpersonal skills are essential. ● Strong research and analytical skills, with the ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and proactively communicate progress and issues. ● Detail-oriented and highly organized with effective time management and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. ● Strong PowerPoint and other computer skills (Microsoft 365, videoconferencing, databases). ● Previous experience working in a government affairs office or within state or federal government. ● Ability and willingness to work occasional evenings and weekends as needed for the job and to travel up to 5%. Job Title: Specialist, State Government Relations Position Location: Washington, D.C. (in-person/hybrid required to be in office 2-3 days per week) Work Hours: Full-time based on a 37.5-hour work week Position Grade & Compensation: Grade 406 The Alzheimer’s Association’s good faith expectation for the salary range for this role is $70,000 – $77,000 Reports To: Director, State Policy Who We Are: The Alzheimer’s Association is the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer’s care, support and research. Our mission is to lead the way to end Alzheimer’s and all other dementia– by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support. The Alzheimer’s Association announced a landmark $100 million investment in research for 2023. This unparalleled commitment is illustrative of the momentum we are building in dementia research — our investments today will lead to breakthroughs tomorrow. At the Alzheimer’s Association, our employees are at the core of all we do. Our network of more than 1,900 employees across the United States makes a difference each and every day for those impacted by Alzheimer’s and those at risk for the disease. We warmly invite qualified applicants to consider this opportunity to make a life-changing impact on the millions living with Alzheimer’s, their caregivers and those that may develop the disease in the future. Read on to learn more about the role, then visit our website www.alz.org/jobs to explore who we are and why we’ve been recognized as a Best Place to Work for the last twelve years in a row. At the Alzheimer’s Association®, we believe that diverse perspectives are critical to achieving health equity — meaning that all communities have a fair and just opportunity for early diagnosis and access to risk reduction and quality care. The Association is committed to engaging underrepresented and underserved communities and responding with resources and education to address the disproportionate impact of Alzheimer’s and dementia. The Alzheimer’s Association commitment remains steadfast in engaging all communities in our full mission. The Association provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment to the fullest extent required by law, including, but not limited to, on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, gender identity, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. Employees working 24 hours/week or more are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, flex accounts, short and long-term disability, life insurance, long term care insurance, tuition reimbursement, generous Paid Time Off, 12 annual holidays and Paid Family Leave, as well as an annual Cultural & Heritage Day and Volunteer Day of their choosing. They are also eligible for our gold standard 401(k) retirement plan. Please click HERE for more information. Full time employees (37.5 hours/week), will enjoy all of the above plus an annual School Visitation Day and an Elder Care Facility Day of their choosing.
