item.title: Director of Policy and Government Affairs
item.description: Director of Policy and Government Affairs Organization: Advocates for Community Health (ACH) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Job description POSITION SUMMARY Advocates for Community Health (ACH) is seeking a Director of Policy and Government Affairs to help lead its Washington D.C.-based policy and advocacy strategy and operations. As a national 501c4 nonprofit, nonpartisan membership association for community health centers, ACH advocates to meaningfully influence federal public policy by harnessing the innovation and effectiveness of forward-leaning community health centers and systems. ACH and its policy and advocacy initiatives are ambitious, nimble, and strategic in their design and approach in order to advance the delivery of health care to underserved populations and cultivate new opportunities to support patients and communities in need. The Director will be expected to have experience on Capitol Hill, in the White House, and/or in federal administrative agencies (or equivalent), be a self-starter, and have the skills, experience, and relationships to be a key leader in the government affairs function of the organization. The candidate will be responsible for the timely development and execution of government relations strategies. This role requires experience with Congress and federal government agencies, political affairs, public policy, grassroots advocacy, management, and industry affairs. The Director of Policy and Government Affairs will report to ACH’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Government Affairs. RESPONSIBILITIES/DUTIES Strategic Development: Work with SVP of Policy and Government Affairs, other ACH team members, and consultants to define the strategic direction of the organization’s policy and advocacy objectives and the investments necessary to achieve those objectives. Work with SVP of Policy and Government Affairs, other team members, and consultants to develop comprehensive strategies and campaigns meant to achieve specific organizational goals related to federal legislation, regulations, and other federal initiatives. Strategic Execution: Proactively execute strategies to achieve high impact organization-approved federal advocacy goals, in coordination with team members and consultants. This includes direct lobbying, leveraging grasstops assets, coordination with the internal communications team on communications tactics and collateral, engagement of external stakeholders, advocacy materials development, and other responsibilities as needed. Congressional and Administrative Engagement and Relationship Building: Develop, maintain, and strengthen relationships with key policymakers on a bipartisan basis, including but not limited to members of Congress and Congressional staff, administrative and regulatory officials and staff, and other leaders in the federal executive and legislative branches, with a key focus on those with jurisdictional influence over the Health Center Program and related programs and policies. Writing and Other Communications: In a clear, strategic, and sensitive professional manner, draft communications collateral for a variety of relevant audiences, including ACH members, Congressional members and staff, Administration personnel, external stakeholders, and others. This includes regular policy updates, handouts, letters, op-eds, blog posts, and other collateral as needed, in coordination with the communications team, policy team, and consultants. In doing so, meet internal and external deadlines. Collaborate closely with ACH’s communications and marketing team on communications products and collateral, ensuring close coordination between communications and policy. Assist SVP of Policy and Government Affairs with preparation of presentations to the Board, for relevant external conferences and convenings, and other events. Policy Development and Analysis: Working with team members and consultants, develop policy positions to advance the interests of ACH and its members. Anticipate emerging government, public, or community/social issues of importance and position ACH to address those issues. Advance ACH’s policy analysis and research working closely with SVP of Policy and Government Affairs and consultants. ACH Events Planning & Execution: In collaboration with the SVP of Policy and Government Relations, internal team members, and consultants, play a leading role in the smooth execution of ACH’s Annual Member Meeting and Hill Day. This includes program development, identifying and preparing speakers, panel moderation, ACH member engagement, Hill Day planning, preparation, and scheduling, and other responsibilities as assigned. As needed, assist colleagues and consultants with the execution of other ACH convenings, including the annual Innovation Summit and periodic Learning Collaboratives. Lead execution of Hill-focused events, including strategically necessary Congressional briefings and occasional ad hoc Hill Days for ACH members. Coalition Management, Stakeholder Engagement, and Thought Leadership: Manage ACH-led coalitions in coordination with consultants, including developing long-term strategy, drafting and socializing meeting agendas and policy goals, engaging with coalition members to ensure strong relationships and commitment to coalition goals, and overall ensuring the coalition’s forward momentum and viability. Represent ACH on advocacy coalitions poised to drive the organization’s policy objectives, ensuring ACH is a leading voice in relevant health policy conversations. Develop, maintain, and strengthen partnerships with relevant external stakeholders to advance ACH’s value proposition and thought leadership positioning. Represent ACH as a speaker at external conferences and convenings as needed. This may require travel. Other Duties: Play a leading role in running ACH’s Political Action Committee, including executing PAC events and giving, maintaining records for compliance, developing long and short-term strategies, and engaging the PAC Board. Proactively seek opportunities to provide value to ACH members, including ensuring timely responses to member inquiries. Be responsible for ACH’s compliance with the Lobbying Disclosure Act, including timely LD-2 and LD-203 filings and ensuring internal records are up to date. QUALIFICATIONS 8+ years of experience developing, managing, and successfully executing advocacy, government relations, and/or public policy strategies/campaigns in a corporate, nonprofit, association, and/or Capitol Hill/Administration setting. Bachelor’s degree required. Health policy background preferred. PAC experience a plus. Must be willing to register as a federal lobbyist. Leadership experience and the ability to effectively manage multiple projects or roles in a rapidly evolving environment is important for this role. The candidate should be a self-starter, thrive in a fast paced, nimble environment, and be able to navigate high-impact and complex situations. Professional presence and strong verbal and written communications skills, as well as public speaking and presentation skills. An eagerness to execute a hands-on approach to build credibility, relationships, and knowledge. The ability to persuasively communicate complex concepts into concise and credible messages at the highest levels of government and business, with a proven track record of delivering high-volume and high-quality work. A collaborative style, with the ability to offer creative pathways or alternative solutions both internally and externally. Excellent analytical and organizational skills. BENEFITS Generous PTO plan including paid holidays Health, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD and Life Insurance plans offered Access to ACH’s 403(b) retirement plan Company laptop and cell phone Job Type: Full-time Pay: $125,000 – $150,000 TO APPLY Please send a cover letter and resume to [email protected] . item.title: Senior Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Government Affairs Organization: Edwards Lifesciences Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Senior Director, Government Affairs Innovation starts from the heart. Edwards Lifesciences is the global leader of patient-focused innovations for structural heart disease and critical care monitoring. With millions of patients served in over 100 countries, each team makes a meaningful contribution by improving patient outcomes and discovering lasting solutions for unmet patient needs. Our Director, Government Affairs position is a unique career opportunity that could be your next step towards an exciting future. Position Summary: The Senior Director of Government Affairs will lead high-impact federal advocacy and help shape public policy positions that support Edwards Lifesciences’ patient-focused mission, innovation agenda, and business objectives. The role will build and sustain relationships with Congress, the Administration, federal agencies, trade associations, patient organizations, and other stakeholders while translating a changing political, legislative, regulatory, payment, and competitive landscape into clear strategies and actions for the company. This leader will serve as a trusted counselor to senior executives and a connector across Public Affairs, business units, Legal and Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, Global Health Economics and Reimbursement, Corporate Strategy, Communications, Patient Engagement, and other internal partners. The position requires both strategic judgment and hands-on execution in a fast-moving, highly regulated environment. How you will make an impact: Develop and execute a comprehensive, federal government affairs strategy aligned with enterprise priorities and patient access goals. Build and deepen relationships with members of Congress, congressional staff, and federal agencies, with particular focus on expanding Edwards’ network of credible policy champions. Monitor and assess legislation, regulation, political developments, and emerging policy proposals affecting medical technology, structural heart innovation, patient access, reimbursement, tax, trade, competition, supply chain, manufacturing, and the broader life sciences ecosystem. Translate policy developments into concise business implications, options, recommendations, and action plans for senior leadership and cross-functional partners. Lead the development of policy positions, advocacy materials, executive briefings, hearing and meeting preparation, written comments, coalition strategies, and stakeholder engagement plans. Represent Edwards before policymakers, trade associations, coalitions, patient and provider organizations, and other external stakeholders, ensuring a consistent and credible company voice. Coordinate closely with Global Health Economics and Reimbursement colleagues on coverage, payment, and health care delivery priorities, including alignment between policy development and advocacy execution. Partner with Legal and Compliance to conduct government affairs activities in accordance with lobbying, ethics, political activity, and other applicable requirements. Support Edwards Political Action Committee strategy and engagement, as appropriate, in partnership with PAC leadership and in compliance with applicable law and company policy. Lead complex, cross-functional projects from issue identification through execution, measurement, and follow-up; establish clear ownership, timelines, and outcomes. Develop internal understanding of government affairs priorities by engaging business leaders and subject-matter experts and by providing timely, audience-appropriate updates. Mentor colleagues and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative, accountable, and high-performing Government Affairs team culture. This position is on-site, expected to be based in Edwards Lifesciences’ Washington, D.C. office. What you will need (required): Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in government, public policy, political science, health policy, law, business, life sciences, or a related field. Minimum 14 years experience of previous related experience in state government affairs or equivalent work experience based on Edwards criteria Required and Other: Experience in all aspects of running a Political Action Committee Experience in healthcare, with substantial experience in government relations, sales, tendering or pricing, reimbursement function, regulatory in multinational pharmaceutical or medical device companies or equivalent work experience based on Edwards criteria Preferred What else we look for (preferred): Advanced degree in public policy, law, health policy, business, or a related discipline. Substantial progressive experience in federal government affairs, public policy, Congress, the Executive Branch, a trade association, consulting, or a corporate government affairs function, including leadership on complex legislative or regulatory issues. Demonstrated success developing and executing bipartisan advocacy strategies and building trusted relationships with policymakers and external stakeholders. Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process and the ability to navigate complex health care and business policy issues. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to make complex issues clear, concise, and decision-ready for executive audiences. Record of sound judgment, discretion, integrity, and compliance in a highly visible external-facing role. Ability to manage multiple high-stakes priorities, work independently, and deliver results under tight deadlines. Ability to travel as needed for meetings, events, and engagement with internal and external stakeholders. Experience in medical technology, life sciences, health care, or another highly regulated industry. Established bipartisan network in Washington, D.C., including relationships with congressional committees and federal agencies relevant to health care and business policy. Knowledge of Medicare coverage and payment, FDA policy, tax, trade, competition, supply chain, manufacturing, and innovation policy relevant to the medical technology sector. Experience leading coalitions, trade association engagement, grassroots or employee advocacy, and PAC-related activities. Aligning our overall business objectives with performance, we offer competitive salaries, performance-based incentives, and a wide variety of benefits programs to address the diverse individual needs of our employees and their families. For Washington D.C., the base pay range for this position is $191,000 -$271,000 (highly experienced). The pay for the successful candidate will depend on various factors (e.g., qualifications, education, prior experience). Applications will be accepted while this position is posted on our Careers website. Edwards is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer including protected Veterans and individuals with disabilities. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: VP of Government Affairs
item.description: VP of Government Affairs Organization: Heartland Dental Location: Effingham, IL | St. Louis, MO | Remote Date Posted: 10/13/2026 Vice President, Government Affairs Looking for an Experienced Government Affairs Professional for Exciting Growth Company About Heartland Dental: With more than 1,760 dental offices supported across 39 states and Washington, D.C. and over 2,900 supported doctors, Heartland Dental is the largest dental support organization (DSO) in the United States. Founded in 1997, Heartland Dental has a proven track record of growth and success. Quite simply, Heartland Dental’s vision and mission are the reason the Company exists, and the mission/vision bring to life all that we do. Heartland Dental’s vision is to be a world-class company and the leader in dentistry. Our mission is to support dentists and their teams as they deliver the highest quality dental care and experiences to the communities they serve while providing exceptional careers and creating value for our stakeholders. In a Nutshell: If you’re an energetic government affairs professional with 10 plus years of experience, and ready to advance your career with the nation’s leading DSO in the healthcare field, keep reading. Yes, a dynamic personality is important – we need someone who is open, positive, and mentally flexible and has an interest in new challenges, building your leadership skills, and participating in the rapid growth of our Company. It is a roll-up your sleeves job. The successful candidate will have the thinking ability and experience to strategically identify opportunities; the drive, grit and common sense to execute tactical tasks; and the personality and executive presence to build relationships and lead initiatives with multiple stakeholders. This individual will act as a primary government affairs liaison between the Company and the Association of Dental Support Organizations (ADSO). This position will report directly to the SVP, General Counsel and will be part of the Company’s Legal, Compliance and Regulatory Team. Working Environment: Remote. Support offices are available in St. Louis, MO or Effingham, IL with other Heartland Dental team members if you live in one of those areas. Moderate travel (10-20%) is required as part of this government affairs work and to attend company related events, leadership trainings, goals meetings, and team offsites. Occasional weekend or evening work may be needed for critical deadline periods or urgent matters. Position Description and Expectations We are looking for an individual that can advance Heartland Dental’s nationwide government affairs presence through forward thinking, a strong commitment to communicating the Heartland Dental story and a willingness to roll up sleeves, execute and make things happen. Here’s what you could expect to fill your time during Year One with our Company: First and foremost, working to build yourself and the role through ongoing leadership opportunities; Extensive onboarding to learn about Heartland Dental, how we support doctors and offices, and to develop a wide range of relationships, both internally and externally, to successfully advance the government relations activities; Monitor, analyze and report on legislative, regulatory, political and industry developments affecting Heartland Dental, supported doctors and supported offices. Assess the business impact of those developments, identify risks and opportunities, and provide practical recommendations to stakeholders; Review enacted laws identified through legislative monitoring resources; determine which laws potentially affect Heartland Dental, supported doctors and offices; and timely communicate the relevant legal changes in easy-to-understand language to the appropriate internal stakeholders; Collaborate with ADSO, other DSOs, trade associations, government affairs professionals and internal business partners to advance Heartland Dental’s government affairs and public policy objectives; Collaborate with ADSO to help develop advocacy materials, policy communications and educational resources to support those efforts; Collaborate with ADSOs to identify opportunities for supported providers who are interested in serving on state dental boards and provide guidance and support throughout the application and selection process; Attend and represent Heartland Dental at key industry, regulatory, legislative, and professional association meetings, conferences, and events to advance advocacy priorities, build relationships, and monitor developments affecting the practice of dentistry and/or the dental support organization industry; Ensure compliance with applicable lobbying, advocacy, ethics, registration and reporting requirements; and Perform other duties, projects and responsibilities as assigned by the SVP, General Counsel or as business needs require. Beyond Year One: As the function matures, this role is expected to grow in scope, deepening Heartland Dental’s presence/involvement in priority states, developing internal reporting and advocacy infrastructure, mentoring or building out additional government affairs resources as the Company’s footprint expands, and measuring the function’s impact against defined policy and business objectives. Minimum Requirements Bachelor’s degree required. Minimum of 10 years of experience with primary focus on state or federal government relations. Experience supporting a multi-state region strongly preferred. Demonstrated senior-level knowledge of legislative and political processes and the roles and functions of government branches. Strong political acumen and analytical skills. Demonstrated leadership in managing government relations initiatives and external partners. Ability to develop tactical strategies that support company vision and goals and take a proactive, long-term view of business objectives. Proven ability to build and sustain collaborative relationships with legislators, legislative staff, regulators, internal leaders, peers and colleagues. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex or controversial topics. Ability to analyze complex legal, regulatory and policy documents. Skilled negotiator with the ability to influence diverse stakeholders. Strong judgment, discretion and ability to maintain confidentiality. Ability to communicate legislative and regulatory changes clearly and concisely in language that internal stakeholders can understand. Desirable Qualification(s) Dental industry experience and familiarity Experience in health care government affairs, with a preference for multi-site health care experience Physical Requirements Ability to perform the essential duties of the position satisfactorily with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties. Prolonged periods sitting or standing and working on a computer. Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times. We put our people first at Heartland Dental, and that shows in our generous benefits package. Company retains the sole discretion to change the duties of the position at any time. We provide all employees and applicants for employment the protections of federal, state, and local laws affording equal opportunity in employment. Click to Apply! – VP of Government Affairs – Heartland Dental – Candidates can click that link or Visit our website, jobs.heartland.com , and search “Vice President, Government Affairs”. Select the role from the list provided, then click on the “Apply” button. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Counsel, Corporate
item.description: Counsel, Corporate Organization: Airbnb Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. Airbnb’s Legal Department is a global team that will require working with diverse international colleagues around the world. The successful candidate will be someone who is adaptable, collaborative and embodies Airbnb’s Core Values. Candidates will be required to approach complex legal issues with a balance for local and global perspectives, while being adaptable to cultural differences and nuances. A genuine and demonstrated interest in Airbnb and a commitment to ethics, integrity and fostering a workplace that emphasizes diversity and belonging is a must. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb’s Legal Department embodies the company’s innovative, forward-thinking spirit. At the frontier of the sharing economy, Airbnb is breaking new ground in matters of policy, law and government relations. Where some see obstacles, we see the opportunity to find creative, practical solutions, right at the cutting edge. Our adventurous, fast-moving legal team is committed to building a team of talented, collaborative and self-motivated legal professionals across the globe who believe in Airbnb’s mission and leading as a 21st century company. The Difference You Will Make: Airbnb is looking for an experienced attorney to join our Corporate Legal team. Reporting to Airbnb’s Lead Counsel, Corporate, you will partner closely with Airbnb’s Corporate Development team and other legal and cross-functional teams on M&A as well as other corporate and investment transactions. From time to time, you may also provide legal support for other teams (e.g., Sustainability, Treasury) as part of the Corporate Legal team’s general practice. A Typical Day: Lead and support mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, warrants and other corporate transactions through all stages of a transaction lifecycle, including assessment of potential targets, deal structuring, due diligence, negotiation and deal execution Provide strategic legal advice to senior management and other internal stakeholders regarding M&A strategy, risk management and execution Draft, review and negotiate transaction documents, including letters of intent, definitive agreements and ancillary documents Work collaboratively with multiple cross-functional teams across the company Manage outside counsel, including the coordination of efforts to ensure effective legal support during the transaction process Contribute to the development of internal legal processes and best practices for M&A transactions Assist and collaborate on other Corporate Legal matters Your Expertise: JD and 5+ years of relevant experience working at a law firm or in-house, focused on M&A and corporate transactions Track record of independently running deal workstreams Willingness to roll up sleeves (no job too big, no job too small) Strong organizational and process management skills Excellent verbal and written communication skills Sound business judgment, attention to detail and the ability to find practical and creative solutions to both legal and business problems High level of integrity, professionalism, intellectual curiosity and willingness to grow Positive attitude, sense of humor and high EQ Passion for the Airbnb mission Licensed in a US state This position is US – Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from. Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging: Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: [email protected] . Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process. We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application. Equal Employment Opportunity: Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Airbnb are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. How We’ll Take Care of You: Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits. Pay Range $196,000—$230,000 USD Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing. We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb. item.title: Chief Compliance Officer, Swap Dealer
item.description: Chief Compliance Officer, Swap Dealer Organization: FalconX Location: New York, NY | San Mateo, CA Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Who are we? FalconX is a pioneering team of operators, investors, and builders committed to revolutionizing institutional access to the crypto markets. Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry’s foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape. Location: Hybrid-Based (New York City, NY or San Mateo, CA) Chief Compliance Officer, U.S. Swap Dealer FalconX is the most advanced digital asset platform for institutions. We provide trade execution, credit & treasury management, prime offering and market making services. Given our global operations, industry-leading technology and deep liquidity, we have facilitated client transactions of $1 trillion in volume. Our products & services are regulated, compliant and trusted. We are a team of financial professionals focused on capital markets comprised of compliance, institutional sales and trading leaders, operations experts, business strategists, engineers, and product builders. We prioritize learning. Outcomes are mission-critical, but we also believe that learning in success and in failure will drive our continued success. Our industry is emergent – there’s no shortage of experiments to get involved with and to continue growing and learning together. Impact FalconX Bravo, Inc. is a registered Swap Dealer. We are seeking an experienced Chief Compliance Officer for our registered Swap Dealer. This person will advise internal stakeholders on implementation and development of CFTC, and NFA swap dealer requirements, including day-to-day oversight and program enhancements relating to policies and procedures, employee training, risk assessments, issues management, governance and management reporting, and metrics. Our department prevents, detects and mitigates compliance and regulatory risks across the firm and helps to strengthen our culture of compliance. As a company involved in digital assets, this role will also be relied on for training and knowledge sharing. The team monitors existing and new rules and regulations; designs and implements controls, policies, procedures and training to all colleagues. We look for those who possess sound judgment, curiosity, and are able to adapt to a changing regulatory digital asset landscape. Qualifications: A minimum of 10+ years of legal or compliance experience/background preferably with investment or commercial bank, law firm, consulting firm or regulatory organization. Demonstrated experience with the implementation and execution of swap dealer compliance program at a registered swap dealer. Demonstrated understanding of the requirements of the Dodd-Frank Act and associated regulations relating to swap dealers, including applicable CFTC, NFA and FRB rules and regulations. Experience interacting with regulators, in particular, CFTC, NFA, and FRB. Experience reporting to senior management. Experience managing teams across geographical regions Familiarity with sales and trading of over-the-counter derivatives, with particular focus on foreign exchange and interest rate derivatives. Outstanding written (drafting & editing) and spoken communication abilities. Excellent teamwork, interpersonal and conflict resolution skills. Highly organized and capable of dealing with multiple, complex projects simultaneously Responsibilities: Advise and implement enhancements to the overall Swap Dealer Compliance Program, including oversight of policies and procedures Respond to regulatory inquiries, audits, examinations and investigations, and liaison with the CFTC and NFA Manage and report on any incidents of non compliance, maintaining a non compliance issue log and monitor remediation of open items, reporting to the CCO on a regular basis Manage and resolve any conflicts of interest that may arise by determining reasonable steps that should be taken to resolve or mitigate the conflict of interest Provide reporting to management and Board of Directors. Escalate reporting when relevant Developing and conducting periodic testing to monitor whether internal controls are operating effectively and in compliance with the swap dealer requirements Develop swap dealer compliance training to all relevant personnel including swap associated persons, compliance team and other relevant groups Education & Additional Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; experience in compliance, legal or other control-related function in the financial services firm, regulatory organization, or consulting firm, or a combination thereof Experience in area of focus; strong working knowledge of Swap Dealers and the related operations and financial requirements Strong willingness to train and provide proactive guidance to colleagues on Swap Dealer requirements and impact of regulatory compliance Preparing or contributing annual compliance reports and other compliance materials for executive management, boards of directors and regulators. Compensation: This is a full-time position with an expected annual compensation of $191,000 – 252,000 in the New York City Metro area. The actual compensation for a successful candidate may vary based on factors such as skill set, relevant experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. This position also offers other forms of compensation and benefits consisting of overtime compensation (when applicable), relocation assistance (if applicable), performance-linked bonus, paid time off (including sick time) benefits, paid Company holidays, participation in the Company’s equity and 401k retirement plan, competitive employee health, dental, and vision benefits each subject to the terms and conditions of the governing plan documents and Company policies. Notice at Collection and Privacy Policy Applicants located in California and/or applying to a role based in California, please refer to our Notice at Collection and Privacy Policy here. Inclusivity Statement FalconX is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, equitable, and safe workspace for all people. Our roles are intended for people from all walks of life. We encourage all those interested in applying to our organization to submit an application regardless if you are missing some of the listed background requirements, skills, or experiences! As part of our commitment to inclusivity, FalconX would like to acknowledge that the EEOC survey has limited potential responses that you can select. For legal reasons, FalconX must use this language to align with federal requirements, however, we want to ensure that you are able to provide a response to our own voluntary survey questions about your identity that best aligns with your most true self. FalconX is an equal opportunity employer and will not discriminate against an applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, sex (including gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), age, physical or mental disability, veteran or military status, genetic information, citizenship, or any other legally-recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local law. Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act and other applicable state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are normally done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on FalconX. Please inform FalconX’s People team at [email protected] , if you need assistance with participating in the application process. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Sr. Manager, Policy Communications
item.description: Sr. Manager, Policy Communications Organization: Pinterest Location: New York, NY | Los Angeles, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/14/2026 About Pinterest: Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product. Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible. At Pinterest, AI isn’t just a feature, it’s a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI. Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here . Pinterest is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Policy Communications to lead its Policy Communications team. In this role, you will lead in shaping the public narrative around Pinterest’s policy and trust & safety priorities – including responsible AI and youth safety – at a pivotal moment for the industry and on a global scale. You will guide the development and execution of media relations and communications campaigns that strategically support Pinterest’s public policy, regulatory and safety objectives, with the goal of creating an environment for the company’s continued growth and success. You will devise communications materials that crisply articulate Pinterest’s products, company values and safety approach to media, policy audiences, industry voices and other key opinion formers in a complex, fast-moving regulatory landscape. The right person for this opportunity must be proactive, entrepreneurial and be comfortable with ambiguity with substantial policy communications experience to make quick, well-informed decisions. You will work cross-functionally with leaders across Pinterest and serve as a trusted advisor. You will also work with external stakeholders to shape the environment for Pinterest’s policy and safety goals to succeed. What you’ll do: Shape the industry news and policy debates that most directly affect Pinterest through proactive campaigns and rapid-response communications. Partner with cross-functional teams across Government Affairs, Legal, Compliance and Trust & Safety to develop and drive a strategic media relations agenda that translates Pinterest’s policy and safety objectives into successful communications campaigns that set the stage for Pinterest’s continued success. Develop and strengthen relationships with key tech policy press, publications, broadcasters, opinion formers, experts, emerging media platforms, Hill staff and third-party stakeholders to advance Pinterest’s reputation and priorities. Anticipate, monitor and manage reputational issues, threats, and fast-moving regulatory developments with effective communications plans and strategies. Partner with cross-functional leaders across Pinterest to ensure Pinterest’s mission and business are well-understood and well-perceived. Represent Pinterest at relevant conferences, panels, and industry events, articulating the company’s policy and safety positions effectively and fostering constructive dialogue. Draft press releases, blog posts, FAQs, and key messages. What we’re looking for: Minimum 10 years of experience in media, corporate, political, government or agency communications. Experience driving policy- and safety-focused media campaigns that distill complex concepts into clear, engaging narratives in the public policy and regulatory sphere. Strong relationships with key technology and policy press and influencers. Sharp written and verbal communicator with exceptional judgement, business acumen, and problem-solving skills. Experience with global regulations and policies across consumer technology, online safety, content enforcement and privacy. Experience as on the record spokesperson and communicator on complex policy and legal topics. Relocation Statement: This position is not eligible for relocation assistance. Visit our PinFlex page to learn more about our working model. In-Office Requirement Statement: We recognize that the ideal environment for work is situational and may differ across departments. What this looks like day-to-day can vary based on the needs of each organization or role. As a result, there are no set in office expectations, however candidates should anticipate commuting based on business need and therefore should be based in the following cities: Washington DC; San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York and Chicago This position is not eligible for relocation assistance. #LI-HYBRID #LI-PW1 At Pinterest we believe the workplace should be equitable, inclusive, and inspiring for every employee. In an effort to provide greater transparency, we are sharing the base salary range for this position. The position is also eligible for equity. Final salary is based on a number of factors including location, travel, relevant prior experience, or particular skills and expertise. Information regarding the culture at Pinterest and benefits available for this position can be found here . US based applicants only $146,561—$301,744 USD Our Commitment to Inclusion: Pinterest is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We want to have the best qualified people in every job. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion or religious creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, status as a protected veteran, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information or characteristics (or those of a family member) or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state or local laws. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you require a medical or religious accommodation during the job application process, please complete this form for support. By submitting this application, I certify that all information submitted in my application and throughout the hiring process is true, accurate, and complete to the best of my knowledge. I understand that any false statement, omission, or misrepresentation may disqualify me from employment consideration or result in termination if discovered after hire. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Compliance Manager [IC3]
item.description: Compliance Manager [IC3] Organization: Sourcegraph Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Who we are Our mission is to bring clarity and control to the world’s most complex codebases. AI is accelerating code creation, but the infrastructure to understand, oversee, and evolve that code hasn’t kept pace. Sourcegraph gives engineering organizations full visibility across their systems, precise context for their agents, and the ability to execute coordinated code changes at scale. As agentic development becomes the dominant engineering paradigm, we provide the context layer teams need to take control of their codebase. With Code Search, Deep Search, MCP, and Agentic Batch Changes, we deliver on that mission today – giving engineering teams and their AI tools the cross-repo context to navigate massive codebases with confidence, and the ability to make changes across hundreds of repositories at once. Companies like Stripe, Reddit, and Leidos rely on Sourcegraph to ship faster and with higher quality. We’re backed by a16z, Sequoia, and Redpoint, and proud to operate as a globally distributed team that values high agency, direct communication, and customer love. If you want to build the infrastructure that lets every engineering team – and every agent they deploy – operate on their codebase with confidence, join us. Hours & location 🌎 While we hire almost anywhere in the world, we have a preference for someone to reside in the following locations for this role. However, if you feel qualified, we welcome you to apply regardless of location. No matter what, working hours must overlap with GMT-3 for at least 20 hours/week. Preferred locations: USA Why this job is exciting As our Compliance Manager, you will own and drive Sourcegraph’s governance, risk, and compliance program, with a primary focus on compliance. This is a highly cross-functional role that works closely with Security, Engineering, IT, Legal, People, Sales, and other teams across the company. You will be responsible for maintaining and evolving our compliance program, including owning certifications such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001 and preparing Sourcegraph for additional frameworks as the business grows. This is not a role where you will simply coordinate work across a large compliance organization. We are looking for someone who has personally owned audit and certification programs end to end: designing and tailoring controls, collecting evidence, training internal teams, working directly with auditors, managing remediation, and driving follow-up work through completion. 📅 Within one month, you will… You will build strong working relationships across Security, Engineering, IT, Legal, People, Sales, and other key stakeholders. You will develop a clear understanding of Sourcegraph’s existing governance, risk, and compliance program, including our ISMS, risk register, controls, certifications, audit processes, and current areas of focus. You will understand how our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 programs operate today, including key owners, evidence requirements, open risks, and upcoming milestones. You will begin participating directly in day-to-day compliance activities and identify opportunities to improve or simplify existing processes. 📅 Within three months, you will… You will have taken ownership of Sourcegraph’s ongoing SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance programs. You will independently manage key audit activities, including control testing, evidence collection, stakeholder coordination, auditor requests, findings, and remediation. You will evaluate existing controls and tailor them to Sourcegraph’s environment rather than relying on overly prescriptive or generic auditor recommendations. You will actively maintain Sourcegraph’s risk register, ISMS processes, policies, and compliance documentation. You will help internal teams understand their compliance responsibilities and provide practical guidance that allows them to meet requirements without creating unnecessary process. You will support customer-facing compliance activities, including security questionnaires and compliance-related questions from prospective and existing customers. 📅 Within six months, you will… You will have successfully led Sourcegraph through an audit or major certification milestone. You will own the operating rhythm of the GRC program, including ISMS meetings, risk management activities, control reviews, documentation updates, and audit preparation. You will have established a forward-looking compliance roadmap covering renewals, upcoming audits, new frameworks, regulatory requirements, and opportunities to improve how the program operates. You will be able to independently identify control gaps or deficiencies, assess their risk, recommend practical solutions, and drive remediation with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will have introduced automation, AI, or other process improvements that reduce manual compliance work while maintaining or improving program quality. About you You have built or operated compliance programs in a fast-moving technology environment and have personally owned major compliance initiatives from beginning to end. You are comfortable operating independently, getting into the details, and doing the work yourself while coordinating with stakeholders across the organization. You understand that frameworks such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001 define requirements but often leave significant flexibility in how an organization satisfies them, and you know how to translate those requirements into controls that fit the business. You are also comfortable working with technical teams and modern cloud environments. You can understand enough about infrastructure, systems, access controls, software development, and security processes to ask the right questions and effectively translate between auditors and technical teams. 5+ years of experience in governance, risk, compliance, information security compliance, or a related role. Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of SOC 2 and ISO 27001 programs, ideally within a SaaS, technology startup, or similarly fast-moving environment. Experience personally managing external audits and certification processes, including audit preparation, evidence collection, control testing, stakeholder training, auditor interaction, remediation, and follow-up. Strong understanding of risk management, control design, ISMS governance, and compliance program operations. Experience adapting compliance controls to an organization’s actual environment rather than applying generic or overly prescriptive requirements. Familiarity with cloud-based technology environments and the security and compliance considerations associated with a distributed or remote workforce. Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to drive cross-functional initiatives from inception through completion. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to explain compliance requirements clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. A hands-on mindset and willingness to personally execute the work required to keep the compliance program operating effectively. Curiosity about AI, automation, and emerging technology, with an interest in using new tools to improve compliance workflows. Nice-to-haves: Experience with additional security, privacy, or compliance frameworks such as GDPR, HIPAA, HITRUST, FedRAMP, FISMA, PCI DSS, or related standards. Experience supporting security questionnaires, customer assurance processes, or sales-related compliance activities. Experience with GRC platforms, compliance automation tools, or building internal automation for evidence collection and control monitoring. Relevant certifications such as CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CRISC, or similar credentials. Level 📊 This job is an IC3. You can read more about our job leveling philosophy in our Handbook. Compensation We pay above-market salaries because we want to hire exceptional people who can focus on building great products, not worrying about paying bills. As an open and transparent company, our compensation philosophy and pay bands are visible to every Sourcegraph teammate, and we strive to make our approach equitable, explainable, and competitive. Your base salary is determined by the IC3 pay band for your location zone (1-4). Our pay bands are informed by market data and designed to ensure competitive compensation wherever you live. During the recruiting process, we’ll discuss the range applicable to you based on job level, relevant skills, experience, qualifications, and location zone. The starting salary for the IC3 pay band in each zone is: Zone 2: $137,718 USD Zone 3: $102,899 USD In addition to competitive cash compensation, we offer meaningful equity (because when Sourcegraph succeeds, we want you to succeed, too) and generous perks & benefits. Interview process Below is the interview process you can expect for this role (you can read more about the types of interviews in our Handbook). It may look like a lot of steps, but rest assured that we move quickly and the steps are designed to help you get the information needed to determine if we’re the right fit for you… Interviewing is a two-way street, after all! We expect the interview process to take 5 hours in total. 👋 Introduction Stage – we have initial conversations to get to know you better… [30m] Recruiter Screen [30m] Hiring Manager Screen 🧑‍💻 Team Interview Stage – we then delve into your experience in more depth and introduce you to members of the team, including cross-functional partners… [Async] Working assignment [60m] Assignment Walkthrough + Review [60m] Resume Deep Dive [60m] Technical Interview 🎉 Final Interview Stage – we move you to our final round, where you gain a better understanding of our business and values holistically… [30m] Values [30m] Leadership We check references and conduct your background check Please note – you are welcome to reques

item.title: Director, AML/BSA Compliance
item.description: Director, AML/BSA Compliance Organization: Current Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Director, AML/BSA Compliance About Current Current is a leading consumer fintech platform transforming financial access for everyday Americans with over six million members. We provide access to financial solutions that seamlessly work together to solve the needs of our members and enable all Americans to build better financial futures. Based in NYC, our results-driven environment drives us to build better products, grow faster, and empower everyone on our team to have an impact on our business and mission to improve financial outcomes. Position Overview We are looking for a Director of AML/BSA Compliance. This is a senior leadership role responsible for providing guidance and being a hands-on leader that will focus on continuously enhancing and overseeing Current’s Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program. This individual will serve as a subject matter expert and advisor to executive leadership and colleagues, ensuring Current meets all AML/BSA obligations while sustaining the member-first culture that drives our growth. This role will report to the Head of Compliance. In addition, you will be a seasoned, pragmatic, and collaborative leader that is able to effectively interact and build relationships across business lines and functions; able to understand and support business and strategic growth priorities while advancing the AML/BSA program in compliance to all applicable regulatory requirements. Key Responsibilities Oversee and continuously drive enhancements to Current’s AML/BSA compliance program, including policies, procedures, and internal controls across all product lines Lead, mentor, and develop a team of AML/BSA subject matter experts. Be a pragmatic and approachable leader that creates a culture of continuous learning and accountability. Develop, maintain and perform AML/BSA risk assessments, evaluate existing and pending regulations, and provide regulatory guidance on new product development Advise on product and technology development in response to changing regulations, identify and develop monitoring and testing routines Effectively partner with Business Line, Data, Engineering, and Functional colleagues across Current to support business strategies, while ensuring Current’s compliance to AML/BSA regulatory requirements Oversee first and second line transaction monitoring systems, alert dispositioning processes, and case management workflows Provide effective oversight of Current’s Know Your Customer (KYC), Customer Due Diligence (CDD) / Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) programs, ensuring onboarding and ongoing controls align with bank partner and associated regulatory requirements Evaluate and effectively manage Current’s OFAC sanctions screening program across all products Develop and deliver AML/BSA training programs as needed Partner with Product, Engineering, and first-line business teams to further enhance AML/BSA controls into new features, product launches, and member onboarding flows Ensure timely and accurate filing of all required regulatory reports, including Unusual Activity Reports (UARs), other required reporting to partner banks, and other FinCEN/OFAC-required submissions as they may arise Maintain current knowledge of BSA/AML regulations, including OFAC sanctions requirements, guidance from FinCEN, federal and state regulators, and banking partners Lead responses to audits, inquiries, and other reviews; serve as the primary point of contact on behalf of Current and its bank sponsors Monitor regulatory developments in consumer fintech and translate emerging requirements into actionable program enhancements Advise the Board of Directors, Risk Committee, and senior leadership on AML/BSA risks and program effectiveness Promote a strong culture of compliance that complements Current’s mission of financial inclusion About you 10+ years of experience in building and overseeing BSA/AML/OFAC programs, with at least 5 years in a leadership role Previous experience as a senior AML/BSA leader or designated AML/BSA Officer Experience across consumer fintech, or traditional financial institutions; while not mandatory, managing AML/OFAC compliance for earned wage access, debit card, payment products, or secured credit card products would be ideal Deep knowledge of BSA/AML regulations, FinCEN guidance, OFAC requirements, and the USA PATRIOT Act Experience with automated transaction monitoring platforms and model risk governance for AML models Demonstrated success in achieving exceptional results as a leader and across reporting lines Pragmatic, solutions-oriented, and comfortable providing nuanced approaches Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing compliance teams in a fast-moving environment Strong communicator who is adept at building relationships with external partners as well as internal partners across the company Educational qualifications in Compliance, Law, or a related field. Compliance certifications (e.g., CAMS, CRCM) will be ideal This role has a base salary range of $200,000 – $260,000. Compensation is determined based on experience, skill level, and qualifications, which are assessed during the interview process. Current offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. BENEFITS Competitive salary Meaningful equity in the form of stock options 401(k) plan Discretionary performance bonus program Biannual performance reviews Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100% for you and your dependents Flexible time off and paid holidays Generous parental leave policy Commuter benefits Fitness benefits Healthcare and Dependent care FSA benefit Employee Assistance Programs focused on mental health Healthcare advocacy program for all employees Access to mental health apps Team building activities Our modern office with open floor plan, stocked kitchen, and catered lunches Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Advisor
item.description: Policy Advisor Organization: ControlAI Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Role Description We’re hiring a dynamic, strategic advocate to brief members of Congress and the broader US government on the national security threat posed by superintelligent AI. This role, one of our first hires in the United States, will work closely alongside our Executive Director, Connor Leahy, and is central to growing ControlAI’s campaign to prohibit superintelligence. At its heart, this position is about building a broad, bipartisan base of support. We’ll likely hire more than one Policy Advisor, and are interested in a wide range of candidates, including: Individuals with experience in US national security Candidates with media and communications skills or experience Former Hill staffers A typical day might involve emailing dozens of legislative staffers in the morning, supporting a senior leader delivering a briefing over lunch, holding meetings with congressional offices in the afternoon, and working to refine our briefing materials in the evening. Successful candidates will thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment that operates more like a startup than a typical nonprofit. They’ll demonstrate exceptional persistence and won’t be deterred by cold outreach and hearing “no” dozens of times. We will consider both early career and experienced candidates. For more experienced candidates, we are open to a Senior Policy Advisor title and a higher compensation range. We recommend reading this article and its follow-up to get a sense of whether you’d be a good fit for this role. Key Responsibilities Include: Campaign-style execution: Lead outreach to congressional offices, craft targeted messages, and relentlessly following up to secure meetings with members. Track and report on progress toward goals and deliverables. Policy advocacy: Meet and brief congressional staffers, members of Congress, and civil servants on the state of AI, the threat of human extinction posed by superintelligence, and ways the US can lead in advancing solutions. Relationship building: Cultivate relationships with stakeholders across the US government. Refining our communications and materials: Help test ControlAI’s messaging, iterating quickly and continually optimizing based on feedback and results. Prepare compelling, informative materials for policymakers, translating the extinction risk posed by superintelligence into accessible, understandable content. Signs that you are a good fit: Excellence-driven: You are goal-driven, comfortable with ambiguity, and energized by ownership. You take personal responsibility for outcomes and produce high-quality work, striking the right balance between thoroughness and timeliness. You operate with a high degree of autonomy, seeking out new ways to solve problems. Relentless persistence: You are urgent and seek to overcome obstacles rather than waiting for direction. You get impatient when projects are not moving forward as they should, and take proactive action to move them along. You don’t take “no” as a final answer; you always find another angle or path. Skilled communicator: You have exceptional interpersonal communication skills and feel comfortable engaging in substantive conversations with policymakers. You enjoy crafting compelling narratives and making complex ideas digestible, memorable, and understandable. You are clear, persuasive, and audience-aware in writing, in person, and in your ability to create materials. You stay on-message even in the face of disagreement, and handle pushback with confidence and skill. Constantly learning and improving: You are deeply self-reflective. After every congressional meeting, you instinctively ask yourself what you can learn to improve the next time. Six months into the role you’ll be far more effective than you are at first, because your skills compound over time. Honesty and Courage: Integrity matters to you. You do not shy away from discussing the risk of extinction from superintelligence. You show courage by sharing the true state of the world, providing an example that policymakers can emulate. Bipartisan credibility: You are effective and credible across political perspectives. Deep passion for ControlAI’s mission: You believe preventing the risk of extinction from superintelligence is one of the most important and impactful ways you could spend your time. We are not looking for technical experience or experience with the field of AI safety. We have found that exceptional mission-aligned individuals can learn much of what is needed to succeed in this role quickly. This is also not the role for someone who is most interested in doing research or writing reports; this is a position with a bias for action. We encourage you to apply even if you do not feel you have all of the skills and experience listed. If you’re on the fence, we’d love to see your application. $90,000 – $160,000 a year The exact salary will depend on qualifications. Most candidates will start between the low end and midpoint of the range. We are open to a Senior Policy Advisor title for exceptional candidates, with commensurate salary on the higher end of the range. About ControlAI ControlAI is a non-profit organization that works with a singular mission to prevent the extinction risk posed by superintelligence and secure a great future for humanity. Nobel Prize winners, top AI experts and even the CEOs of major AI companies have warned that superintelligence poses an extinction risk for humanity. Yet, most decision-makers and most of the public are still in the dark about these risks. ControlAI exists to change this. We help hundreds of thousands of people understand where AI is going, and take civic action to secure their future. We meet hundreds of lawmakers to inform them about the risks, and convince them to take a public stance. We help dozens of them take action to spur a national conversation about superintelligence, and put measures in place nationally and internationally. We do this across all democratic institutions, from lawmakers to the media, civil society, and all citizens. We operate like a startup: clear objectives, measurable goals, and real-world results over long-term research. ControlAI’s impact has been covered in media outlets including the Guardian and TIME Magazine. In the UK, we have briefed over 160 cross-party parliamentarians and No. 10 Downing Street, with our superintelligence campaign gaining support from more than 110 British lawmakers. Based on this successful approach, we’re now scaling our congressional outreach efforts in the US. This position will be a core part of that effort. Application Process We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis and will interview strong candidates as they apply. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible to receive priority consideration. The application process consists of a resume review, a brief screening interview, a two-hour work task, a comprehensive interview with our US Director, and a conversation with our CEO. We will communicate details of the interview process to candidates as they proceed, and expect the process to take between 4 and 6 weeks for most candidates. Other Details Location: Our US office is in Washington, D.C. This is an in-person role, with the potential for relocation assistance to D.C. for exceptional candidates. The role requires occasional travel, including international travel. ControlAI is not able to sponsor visas to the US for this position; candidates must already have US work authorization. Hours: This is a full-time role. Benefits: ControlAI provides a comprehensive benefits package including generous paid time off, health insurance, and a 401(k) match. ControlAI US Inc. is a 501(c)4 social welfare organization and an equal opportunity employer. We encourage everyone to apply regardless of age, race, veteran status, physical abilities, or any other characteristic protected under federal, state, or local law. item.title: Public Policy Coordinator
item.description: Public Policy Coordinator Organization: National Network to End Domestic Violence (NNEDV) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/14/2026 JOB ANNOUNCEMENT POSITION: Public Policy Coordinator JOB FAMILY: Coordinator REPORTS TO: Public Policy Director SALARY RANGE: $60,000-$65,000 FLSA STATUS: Exempt CLOSING DATE: October 28, 2026 JOB SUMMARY The Public Policy Coordinator supports NNEDV’s Public Policy team by handling administrative duties, assisting with key projects, and managing logistics for policy-related activities. This role plays a crucial part in coordinating events, managing timelines, organizing team resources, and contributing to research and advocacy efforts that advance justice and safety for survivors. The Public Policy Coordinator collaborates with internal teams and engages with external stakeholders to further NNEDV’s mission and policy initiatives. RESPONSIBILITIES Administrative and Project Support: Provide administrative support to the Public Policy team, including scheduling, note-taking, and assisting with follow-up actions. Manage and organize the team’s file drive and maintain team timelines for large projects. Assist with NNEDV’s annual Domestic Violence Counts survey and report, managing survey data, communicating with participants, and addressing data issues as needed. Compile and summarize research for team initiatives and maintain organized records of relevant policy information. Draft reports for funders and other stakeholders, as well as advocacy letters, fact sheets, and other policy-related documents. Event Coordination: Coordinate logistics for annual events such as Advocacy Days, Congressional briefings, and other signature events, including hotel procurement, materials creation, speaker arrangements, Zoom support, and post-event follow-up. Support planning and execution of virtual and in-person events to ensure smooth, well-organized experiences for participants. Policy Monitoring and Research: Learn and manage Quorum government affairs system to track legislation and manage stakeholder engagement. Monitor relevant listservs to track policy conversations, summarize discussions, and respond to requests for information and assistance. Develop and execute action alerts through NNEDV’s advocacy platform (Quorum), updating alert content and coordinating distribution through emails and social media. Attend national policy meetings, summarize action items for the team, and contribute to policy strategy development. Communications and Relationship-Building: Work with the Communications team to update policy content on NNEDV’s website. Update team listservs and written materials, ensuring that resources remain current and accessible. Build relationships across NNEDV teams, member coalitions, and external partners to promote collaboration and maximize the impact of Public Policy initiatives. Recruit, onboard, and support interns, providing guidance and managing assignments. Other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS Education and Experience: Minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience, preferably in a policy-related setting (experience in legislative or executive branches a plus). Experience with event planning, scheduling, and logistics coordination. Skills and Abilities: Strong commitment to NNEDV’s mission and public interest work. Excellent attention to detail, superb organizational skills, and the ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Proficient in writing, editing, and proofreading with a strong grasp of grammar, punctuation, and copyediting. Proficiency in Zoom, Excel, Word, Adobe, SurveyMonkey, Quorum, InDesign, and content management systems. Ability to manage timelines effectively and adapt activities to meet project goals. Location: This is a remote position; however, this person needs to reside in the DMV area with the ability to be in person at commitments on the Hill and others within the DC area. ADA Statement: NNEDV is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability, please contact HR. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement: NNEDV is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants. We do not discriminate based on race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, religion, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are dedicated to fostering a work environment that is fair, respectful, and free from discrimination, ensuring that all employees have the opportunity to succeed and thrive. TO APPLY Please email your resume and a cover letter explaining how your experience aligns with this role to [email protected] . Be sure to include ‘Public Policy Coordinator’ in the subject line.
