item.title: Public Relations Manager
item.description: Public Relations Manager Organization: PaintCare Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Public Relations Manager Position Summary PaintCare is seeking a dynamic and detail-oriented Public Relations Manager to support the organization’s communications, media relations, and public affairs initiatives. This position will play a key role in increasing awareness of PaintCare’s paint stewardship programs and community partnerships through earned media, press conferences and events, stakeholder engagement, and strategic communications. The Public Relations Manager will coordinate media outreach efforts across PaintCare’s growing network of state programs, oversee communications related to PaintCare-sponsored murals and other public good initiatives, and support state capital outreach events that showcase PaintCare’s environmental and economic impact. The position also contributes to crisis communications planning, writing press releases and related materials, developing compelling stories that highlight PaintCare’s mission and accomplishments, and media monitoring. Key Responsibilities Media Relations & Earned Media Develop and execute media outreach strategies that generate positive earned media coverage for PaintCare programs and activities. Research, develop, and maintain relationships with reporters, editors, producers, and influencers covering environmental sustainability, recycling, public policy, community development, and local news. Draft, distribute, and track press releases, media advisories, pitches, op-eds, and other media materials. Coordinate media interviews, press conferences and other press events, site visits, and spokesperson opportunities. Monitor media coverage, compile press clips, and prepare reports measuring media performance and exposure. Assist in developing annual communications plans that support organizational and program objectives. Coordinate media interview training sessions for PaintCare field staff and leadership. Community Impact & Public Mural Program Manage PaintCare’s sponsored public mural and community public good initiatives utilizing recycled or reused paint. Coordinate with community organizations, artists, local governments, and other project partners to maximize visibility and community engagement. Develop project narratives, media materials, case studies, and digital content that highlight environmental and social benefits. Identify opportunities to position PaintCare as a leader in innovative paint reuse and community sustainability efforts. Support event planning, ribbon cuttings, mural unveilings, and community recognition activities. Public Affairs & State Capital Engagement Coordinate and support annual outreach and information sharing events in state capitals and other government engagement activities. Assist with event logistics, media outreach, messaging, briefing materials, presentations, and stakeholder communications. Develop fact sheets, talking points, and communications materials that highlight PaintCare program achievements, milestones, and performance metrics. Coordinate with internal stakeholders and government affairs partners to promote PaintCare’s impact among policymakers and key external audiences. Strategic Communications Collaborate with communications, program, and executive teams to identify newsworthy stories and promote organizational achievements. Develop content that communicates PaintCare’s environmental, economic, and community benefits in clear and compelling ways. Assist in creating messaging frameworks and communications resources for program launches, milestones, partnerships, and special initiatives. Support content development for newsletters, websites, social media, and stakeholder communications as needed. Crisis Communications & Reputation Management Support the development and updating of crisis communication plans and response protocols. Assist with preparing holding statements, media responses, Q&As, and stakeholder communications during sensitive issues. Monitor emerging issues and media inquiries and escalate concerns appropriately. Help ensure consistent, accurate, and timely communications during challenging situations. Coordinate crisis communications practice drills and provide prep sessions to field staff Additional Responsibilities Maintain media contact databases and communications calendars. Track communications metrics and prepare summary reports. Support special events, conferences, trade shows, and community outreach opportunities. Perform other communications and public relations duties as assigned. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in Public Relations, Communications, Journalism, Public Affairs, Marketing, or a related field. 2-5 years of experience in public relations, media relations, communications, public affairs, or a related role. Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Experience writing press releases, media pitches, speeches, talking points, and other communications materials. Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Experience coordinating events and working with external stakeholders. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and media monitoring platforms. Preferred Experience working in environmental, sustainability, nonprofit, recycling, public policy, or government affairs organizations. Knowledge of earned media strategies and media measurement tools. Familiarity with crisis communications principles and best practices. Experience working with legislative or government audiences. Knowledge of community engagement and stakeholder outreach programs. Desired Competencies Strategic thinker with strong news judgment. Excellent relationship-building skills. Creative storyteller with an ability to identify compelling narratives. Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy. Self-starter who can work independently and collaboratively. Location and Travel This position is located at ACA headquarters in Washington, D.C. and will operate within a hybrid work environment (working both onsite and remotely). Occasional overnight travel throughout the U.S. will be required for staff meetings, events, media opportunities, legislative outreach activities, project planning, team meetings, and stakeholder meetings. Employment, Salary, and Benefits This is a full-time, regular position. Salary is dependent on experience, but on estimate can range from $75,000 to $85,000 PaintCare, through the ACA, provides generous compensation, benefits [401(k), vacation days, medical, dental, and life insurance], and reimbursement for travel expenses. Apply To apply for this position, please visit https://american-coatings-association.breezy.hr/ . Please submit a resume and cover letter stating your motivations for applying and your salary requirements. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. About PaintCare PaintCare is committed to making it easy and convenient for households, businesses, and institutions to recycle postconsumer (leftover) paint in states with paint stewardship laws. A nonprofit organization created by paint manufacturers, PaintCare sets up drop-off locations for leftover paint, arranges for recycling and proper disposal, and conducts public education. PaintCare has managed more than 80 million gallons of paint, stain, and varnish in 12 states and the District of Columbia. For additional information, visit www.paintcare.org. item.title: Senior Corporate Counsel, Regulatory
item.description: Senior Corporate Counsel, Regulatory Organization: Pomelo Care Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Pomelo Care is the leading virtual medical practice for women and children, providing care across pregnancy, postpartum, pediatrics, menopause, and perimenopause. We combine proactive, 24/7 clinical care with technology that helps us reach patients earlier, identify risks sooner, and deliver personalized care throughout their journey. Our team includes clinicians, technologists, operators, and problem-solvers working together to make high-quality care more accessible for families nationwide. About The Role: Your north star: Deliver impactful healthcare regulatory guidance to enable Pomelo’s business growth and operations in collaboration with the legal and compliance team and business leaders across the organization. We are seeking an exceptional and highly motivated healthcare attorney to join our growing, collaborative team. Reporting to our Associate General Counsel, Healthcare & Technology, this role is responsible for healthcare regulatory matters, and offers the opportunity to work closely with various teams across the organization. The ideal candidate will bring in-depth knowledge of healthcare laws and regulations, strong legal acumen, and a pragmatic, business-forward approach to navigating the regulatory environment. Who you are: You have a JD from an ABA accredited law school and are licensed to practice in at least one state. You have a minimum of 7 years of legal experience. In-house experience at a healthcare company is required, and startup or high-growth experience is strongly preferred. You bring deep experience across the federal and state regulations that govern how virtual care is delivered and paid for: professional licensure, scope of practice and supervision requirements, telehealth rules, CPOM and MSO/PC structures, AKS, FCA and other fraud and abuse laws, healthcare marketing and patient communications rules, and Medicaid reimbursement. You have experience with ERISA, group health plan design, and the plan-side requirements that come with health plan and employer partnerships. You have supported a virtual-first or telehealth provider, including launching clinical services in new states, and have partnered closely with clinical leadership on clinical model design. You are pragmatic and business-forward. You right-size the risk, land on a clear recommendation, and explain the “why” in plain language a non-lawyer can act on. You have excellent interpersonal and communication skills, capable of effectively managing cross-functional projects and business priorities. The ability to establish a rapport and working relationship with business leaders is paramount. You have meticulous attention to detail and are comfortable working with ambiguity. You have the ability to manage shifting priorities within a fast-paced environment. Why you should join our team By joining Pomelo, you will get in on the ground floor of a fast-moving, well-funded, and mission-driven startup that always puts the patient first. You will learn, grow and be challenged, and have fun with your team while doing it. We strive to create an environment where employees from all backgrounds are respected. We value working across disciplines, moving fast, data-driven decision making, learning, and always putting the patient first. Benefits and Perks: Comprehensive Health, Dental, and Vision coverage for employees and their families High deductible Health Plans with Health Savings Account (HSA) options Flexible Spending Account (FSA) Equity grant participation 401(k) program Competitive vacation policy 16 weeks paid parental leave Fully remote work flexibility (within the US) Compensation: The expected base salary range offered for this role is $225,000-$245,000. This role is also eligible for an annual performance bonus and equity, giving you an ownership stake in Pomelo’s mission. Actual compensation may vary based on relevant experience, skills, competencies, and certifications. We are committed to hiring the best team to improve outcomes for all mothers and babies. To solve the complex challenges facing the diverse population we serve, we need diverse perspectives, actively welcoming people of all races, ages, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, national origins, religions, disabilities, and veteran statuses. We strive to cultivate an inclusive and respectful environment where team members thrive by working across disciplines, moving fast, making data driven decisions, learning continuously, and always putting the patient first. item.title: Senior Social Media & Content Manager
item.description: Senior Social Media & Content Manager Organization: Fieldguide Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/14/2026 About Us Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by augmenting the work of assurance and audit practitioners with AI agents. The value we bring firms: Expertise, amplified. We are based in San Francisco and have raised over $125M+ in venture funding from top Silicon Valley investors to accomplish our ambitious vision, including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and more. We are the leading transformation partner for agentic audit and advisory with more than 50% of the top 100 CPA firms as customers, including several Big 4, and an industry-leading NPS to match. We save up to 75% of time on manual tasks and unlock over 4x capacity for audit practitioners, helping provide the work-life balance that is rare in the profession. Fieldguide is on the same growth curve as the later-stage vertical AI leaders, but you would be joining early enough to have a meaningful impact. Fieldguide values diversity, both in backgrounds and in experiences to help build the future of audit and advisory. We are deliberate in preserving a winning culture with our FFLOWI values – Fearless, Fast, Lovable, Owners, Win-Win, Inclusive – providing space for teammates to do their career’s best work through a tightly knit support network. If you want to shape the most important shift in how commerce and capital markets establish trust, alongside world-class teammates, Fieldguide would love to build with you. About the Role We’re hiring a Social Media and Content Manager to join the Fieldguide team. You’ll set the social strategy and own the content calendar that brings it to life, taking our product releases, thought leadership, and customer stories and rebuilding them into short form and serialized content, built to earn attention on a feed, while shaping how our biggest company moments show up on social from concept through execution. You’ll partner closely with our product and marketing teams to determine how and where we show up to the industry. What You’ll Do Set social strategy and own execution, from concept through the content calendar that carries them. Repurpose and reconstruct long-form assets (blog posts, eGuides, research reports, webinars) into social-native formats. Write and manage recurring short form content for subject-matter experts and functional leads — byline series, resource articles, and campaign-driven event and demand-gen copy. Own and evolve the team’s content systems: calendar, briefing templates, and social brand guidelines, as the function scales. Work directly with demand gen, product, and the broader content and communications team to scope campaigns and content from concept through final delivery. Who You Are Deep, hands-on social experience — you’ve personally run organic social strategy and execution for a brand: running the calendar, managing stakeholders, setting the cadence, and making platform-specific judgment calls. A knack for translating complex subject matter — you can take dense, technical, or dry material and repurpose it into scroll-stopping content for native social formats An instinct for visual storytelling — you know how to pair copy with the right format (carousel, short video, graphic) without waiting on a designer for every post. Innately curious —A team player who’s comfortable being edited and iterating, and brings genuine curiosity about how audit and advisory professionals engage online. More about Fieldguide: Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are: Fearless – Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls. Fast – Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection. Lovable – Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences. Owners – Execute & run the business with ownership. Win-win – Create mutual value & earn trust for life. Inclusive – Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams. Some of our benefits include: Comprehensive health coverage (medical, vision, dental), plus life and disability insurance Equity stock options Paid public holidays, flexible PTO and flexible work schedules 401(k) plan through Human Interest Wellness benefits Technology and work from home reimbursement Paid parental leave Compensation Base Salary $145K – $165K Apply for this Job Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Public Affairs & Strategy – R-433001
item.description: Director, Public Affairs & Strategy – R-433001 Organization: Humana Location: Washington DC | Louisville, KY | New York,NY | Nashville, TN Date Posted: 10/14/2026 Become a part of our caring community The Director, Public Affairs & Strategy will lead high-priority, cross-functional work at the intersection of Humana’s business strategy, healthcare policy, and advocacy. This leader will own complex workstreams from initial framing through recommendation and execution, partnering directly with senior leaders to structure issues, develop policy positions, and build coordinated strategies that advance enterprise priorities. The ideal candidate is a highly strategic and structured leader with deep healthcare expertise, strong executive presence, and the judgment and emotional intelligence to influence and collaborate across the organization. This role requires an individual who can create clarity from ambiguity, operate with a high degree of ownership and independence, and translate complex business and policy issues into clear recommendations and disciplined execution. This role reports to the SVP, Strategy & Public Affairs. Key Responsibilities Lead complex workstreams end to end: Define scope, priorities, workplans, milestones, and decisions; anticipate needs and drive work through implementation with limited direction. Advise senior leaders: Frame complex business and policy issues, surface tradeoffs, synthesize perspectives, and translate insights into clear recommendations. Develop strategies to advance enterprise priorities: Connect healthcare policy developments to business objectives and build coordinated strategies across stakeholders, messaging, risks, and execution. Drive analysis and execution: Lead research, quantitative and qualitative analysis, and scenario planning while establishing clear accountability, timelines, and follow-through. Create executive-ready deliverables: Distill complex information into concise, high-quality presentations, briefings, memos, and decision materials. Lead through influence: Build trust and alignment across functions, navigate differing perspectives, manage external consulting partners, and maintain a high bar for rigor, quality, and results. Use your skills to make an impact Required Qualifications: BA/BS degree; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred. 7+ years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, healthcare strategy, enterprise transformation, public affairs strategy, or a similarly rigorous, high-performance environment. Deep knowledge of the U.S. healthcare industry, preferably including payer and/or provider experience. Proven ability to independently structure ambiguous problems, lead complex cross-functional work, synthesize quantitative and qualitative findings, and translate insights into actionable recommendations. Demonstrated ability to take full ownership of complex workstreams and drive execution with limited direction. Exceptional project leadership, executive communication, and stakeholder-management skills. Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and stakeholders without formal authority. High emotional intelligence with the ability to build trust, navigate disagreement, and foster alignment across diverse perspectives. Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, attention to detail, and comfort operating in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Leadership Attributes Successful candidates will demonstrate: Strategic and structured: Creates clarity from ambiguity, approaches complex issues with a structured mindset, and connects policy developments to enterprise priorities. Ownership and execution: Takes full accountability for outcomes, anticipates needs, drives work forward with limited direction, and consistently delivers high-quality, synthesized work. Influential and collaborative: Builds trust, works effectively across organizational boundaries, navigates disagreement constructively, and creates alignment without relying on formal authority. Clear and concise: Distills complexity into the core insight, decision, and recommendation and communicates effectively with senior executives. Low ego, high standards: Collaborates openly, welcomes different perspectives, and puts enterprise outcomes ahead of personal ownership while maintaining a high bar for rigor, quality, and execution. Location & Travel This role offers flexibility in location and may be performed remotely. Candidates are not required to reside near a Humana market office; however, travel will be expected on an as-needed basis to support business priorities, including travel to Louisville, KY; the Washington, DC metro area; Chicago, IL; Nashville, TN; and New York, NY. Work at Home Requirements: To ensure Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees’ ability to work effectively, the self-provided internet service of Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees must meet the following criteria: At minimum, a download speed of 25 Mbps and an upload speed of 10 Mbps is required; wireless, wired cable or DSL connection is suggested. In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Humana reserves the right to require associates to upgrade their internet service if necessary. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information. Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana’s offices for training or meetings may be required. Scheduled Weekly Hours: 40 Pay Range: $184,800 – $254,100 The compensation range below reflects a good faith estimate of starting base pay for full time (40 hours per week) employment at the time of posting. The pay range may be higher or lower based on geographic location and individual pay will vary based on demonstrated job related skills, knowledge, experience, education, certifications, etc. This job is eligible for a bonus incentive plan. This incentive opportunity is based upon company and/or individual performance. Description of Benefits: Humana, Inc. and its affiliated subsidiaries (collectively, “Humana”) offers competitive benefits that support whole-person well-being. Associate benefits are designed to encourage personal wellness and smart healthcare decisions for you and your family while also knowing your life extends outside of work. Among our benefits, Humana provides medical, dental and vision benefits, 401(k) retirement savings plan, time off (including paid time off, company and personal holidays, paid parental and caregiver leave), short-term and long-term disability, life insurance and many other opportunities. About Us About Humana: Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) is a leading U.S. healthcare company. Through our Humana insurance services and our CenterWell healthcare services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it. These efforts are leading to a better quality of life for people with Medicare and Medicaid, families, individuals, military service personnel, and communities at large. Learn more about what we offer at Humana.com and at CenterWell.com . Equal Opportunity Employer: It is the policy of Humana not to discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability or protected veteran status. It is also the policy of Humana to take affirmative action, in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and VEVRAA, to employ and to advance in employment individuals with disability or protected veteran status, and to base all employment decisions only on valid job requirements. This policy shall apply to all employment actions, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, upgrading, promotion, transfer, demotion, layoff, recall, termination, rates of pay or other forms of compensation and selection for training, including apprenticeship, at all levels of employment. item.title: Manager, Communications-Consumer Products
item.description: Manager, Communications-Consumer Products Organization: National Football League (NFL) Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Reporting to the Director of Communications, this role manages communications for the league’s Consumer Products business, works as a part of the international communications team supporting the League’s office in Canada, and oversees communications for Digital Media Partnerships and IT/Technology. Working across these teams, the role will develop proactive strategies that strengthen key business relationships, advance league priorities, and engage consumer, business, and trade audiences. The ideal candidate brings experience in a fast-paced consumer or brand environment and can effectively manage multiple internal and external stakeholders. Responsibilities: Develop and execute communications strategies for the league’s Consumer Products business, including product launches, campaigns, partnerships, and key retail moments. Partner with internal teams and external organizations to increase awareness of NFL products and support business objectives across NFLShop.com and key retailers. Manage the communications agency supporting the Consumer Products business, including priorities, deliverables, and results. As a member of the international communications team, serve as the day-to-day comms point for the NFL office in Toronto supporting all Canada-related priorities. Partner with communications colleagues across league offices and the 32 clubs to amplify priority stories and key moments. Work regularly with league executives, business leaders, partners, and other external stakeholders. Build and maintain relationships with consumer, business, sports, entertainment, fashion, and technology media. Contribute to issues and crisis communications as needed, supporting timely and coordinated responses. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in communications or related field. Minimum 4 years of professional experience in communications, public relations, media relations, or a related field. Experience working for a consumer-facing brand, communications agency, sports or entertainment organization, or similarly fast-paced business. Strong writing, editing, pitching, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor stories for traditional, digital, social-first, and trade audiences. Demonstrated success developing and executing proactive communications campaigns, announcements, and media strategies. Knowledge of cultural and consumer trends, particularly across sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, lifestyle, media, or technology. Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Experience collaborating across functions and building effective relationships with colleagues, leaders, agencies, partners, and media contacts. Sound judgment and the ability to work effectively in high-profile, high-pressure situations. Experience supporting issues or crisis communications is preferred. Other Key Attributes / Talent Characteristics: Strategic thinker: Connects communications plans to business goals and identifies proactive storytelling opportunities. Collaborative partner: Builds trust across teams and works effectively with executives, clubs, agencies, partners, and other stakeholders. Adaptable operator: Stays organized and composed while managing changing priorities, tight deadlines, and multiple workstreams. Proactive team player: Takes initiative, contributes ideas, and is comfortable working hands-on to move projects forward. Creative storyteller: Finds fresh, relevant ways to reach new audiences across established and emerging platforms. Sound judgment: Handles sensitive information responsibly and acts with integrity. Travel: Regular travel to NFL events such as the Super Bowl and Draft. Terms /Expected Hours of Work: NFL employees are required to work a minimum of 40 hours per week in the office. Salary / Pay Range This job posting contains a pay range, which represents the range of salaries or hourly rates that the NFL believes, in good faith, at the time of this posting that it might be willing to pay for the posted job in the location(s) specified. The NFL expects to hire for this position near the middle of the range. Only in truly rare and exceptional circumstances, where an external candidate has experience, credentials, or expertise that far exceed those required or expected for the position, would the NFL consider paying a salary or rate near the higher end of the range. Salary $95,000 – $115,000 USD At the NFL, in-person work at our offices is a top priority because it allows us to collaborate more effectively, build stronger connections, and maintain the culture that drives our success. This role requires onsite presence at an NFL office or stadium location, and remote and/or hybrid working options are not offered. NO RELOCATION ASSISTANCE WILL BE PROVIDED. The NFL is committed to building an inclusive work environment that reflects our incredible fan base. We provide an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all employees and applicants without regard to status as protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws. WHO WE ARE: NFL Core Values: Respect: Everyone matters. We celebrate diverse opinions, honor hard work, and value every contribution. Integrity: We do what’s right, even when it’s tough. We hold ourselves accountable and always follow through. Team Responsibility: We support each other and our communities. No one is bigger than the game, and every action impacts others. Resiliency: We set high standards, overcome adversity, and adapt to challenges, always striving for excellence. NFL Leadership Attributes: Build Talent: We develop and nurture potential, empowering individuals to grow and succeed. Execute: We take action with precision, delivering results that drive our goals forward. Inspire: We motivate others through vision, energy, and a commitment to excellence. Live Our Values: We embody our core principles in every decision and action. Know the Business: We stay informed, understand our industry, and make decisions that strengthen our position. Think Big: We challenge the status quo, envision bold possibilities, and strive for transformative impact WHO YOU ARE: Talent Attributes: What we expect for our employees: Embody an enthusiastic, proactive can-do attitude Embrace grit, free from ego or entitlement Excel as a relationship builder, with the ability to influence Eager learner, driven by passion rather than just ambition Encompasses an incredible work ethic with an agile mindset Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Government Affairs and Public Policy
item.description: Director, Government Affairs and Public Policy Organization: Walmart Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Position Summary… What you’ll do… Walmart’s Federal Government Affairs team is seeking a strategic, experienced, and mission-driven Director of Federal Government Affairs to lead our advocacy and engagement on key healthcare issues in Washington, D.C. This role will serve as the company’s lead lobbyist on federal healthcare policy, representing Walmart before Congress, the Administration, and key stakeholders. The Director will also act as a trusted advisor to internal teams, helping shape Walmart’s healthcare strategy through policy insight and engagement. About the team: Walmart’s Federal Government Affairs team leads Walmart’s engagement on federal policy issues, advocating before Congress, the Administration, and key stakeholders. This team shapes strategic engagement and policy priorities that advance and protect business goals. The team coordinates across functions to counsel the business on risk, influence public policy, manage complex stakeholder relationships, and provide actionable insights to leadership. The team fosters a culture of continuous learning, teamwork, ethical decision-making, and strategic foresight to address emerging policy challenges. It supports the company’s mission by leading effective policy advocacy that advances Walmart’s strategy. What you’ll do: Serve as Walmart’s lead advocate on federal healthcare policy before Congress, the Administration, and other key stakeholders. Develop and execute a strategy for legislative and regulatory issues impacting Walmart’s Health & Wellness & Benefits teams. Build and maintain relationships with Walmart’s Health & Wellness and Benefits teams to align policy strategy with business priorities. Monitor, analyze, and provide guidance on federal legislation and regulations related to, but not limited to, employer-sponsored insurance plans, reimbursement systems, Medicare, Medicaid, and pharmacy operations. Represent Walmart in external forums, including industry coalitions, trade associations, and public policy events. What you’ll bring: Demonstrated experience in leading healthcare policy, with direct experience on Capitol Hill or in a federal healthcare agency. Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process. Proven ability to build relationships, lead cross-functional teams, influence across stakeholders. Demonstrated expertise in coalition building, negotiation, and conflict resolution to influence policy outcomes. Strategic thinker with sound judgment and a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset. Collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex policy issues into actionable insights. Committed to Walmart’s mission to help people save money so they can live better. At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short-term and long-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see https://one.walmart.com/notices. Live Better U is a Walmart-paid education benefit program for full-time and part-time associates in Walmart and Sam’s Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor’s degrees, including English Language Learning and short-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to a specific plan or program terms. The annual salary range for this position is $143,000.00 – $286,000.00 Additional compensation includes annual or quarterly performance bonuses. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Political Science, or related field and 5 years’ experience managing projects or campaigns in politics, public affairs, or related field OR 7 years’ experience managing projects or campaigns in politics, public affairs, or related field. Preferred Qualifications… Outlined below are the optional preferred qualifications for this position. If none are listed, there are no preferred qualifications. Advanced graduate degree; experience leading large-scale/national or multi‑market government affairs initiatives within the region or area of expertise., People management experience. Primary Location… 80 M St Se, Washington, DC 20003-3544, United States of America Walmart and its subsidiaries are committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace and has a no tolerance policy regarding the use of illegal drugs and alcohol on the job. This policy applies to all employees and aims to create a safe and productive work environment. item.title: Policy Analyst
item.description: Policy Analyst Organization: U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/15/2026 The U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI), established in 1911, is a nongovernmental, not-for-profit international organization dedicated to addressing the needs and rights of refugees and immigrants. USCRI, working with 200 affiliates, provides legal, social, and health services to refugees, unaccompanied migrating children, trafficking survivors, and other immigrants in all 50 states, El Salvador, Honduras, Kenya, and Mexico. USCRI advocates for the rights of refugees and immigrants both nationally and globally, helping to drive humanitarian policies, practices, and law. To learn more about our work, please visit our website at www.refugees.org. OVERVIEW USCRI’s Policy and Advocacy Team leads the development of the organization’s position on global advocacy; international, federal, and local policies; litigation; and the root causes and conditions of crisis, movement and resettlement for refugees and other uprooted populations. Policy Analysts work in cooperation with programmatic and communications staff and report to the Associate Director of Global Advocacy and Communications. Working with programmatic and communications staff, Policy Analysts bring refugee and immigration issues to the attention of national and international policy makers and organizations of influence. They conduct research, write in-depth, topic-specific issue papers, conduct briefings, analyze legal decisions and international instruments, and serve as well-informed experts on global refugee and migration issues, concepts, and trends. This is an in-person position at the agency’s headquarters in Arlington, VA. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Write issue papers, reports, comments, and other advocacy materials on global refugee and migration topics; Conduct research, including travel to assess conditions for uprooted populations; Make presentations, conduct informational sessions, and provide briefings in a variety of venues; Work with the Associate Director and other senior staff to chart the organization’s policy and advocacy direction; Collaborate with communications staff to ensure well-researched, in-depth support for USCRI external messaging; Represent USCRI at advocacy meetings with government officials, international representatives, and other organizations, and engage in other networking activities; Assist in fundraising activities to support field research and advocacy. Perform other job-related duties as assigned by the supervisor. All of the above duties and responsibilities are essential job functions subject to reasonable accommodation. All job duties indicated are not to be an exhaustive statement, and other job-related duties may be assigned as required by the supervisor(s). All of the above duties and responsibilities are essential job functions subject to reasonable accommodation. All job duties indicated are not to be an exhaustive statement and other job-related duties may be assigned as required by the supervisor(s). POSITION REQUIREMENTS Undergraduate degree required; master’s level or law degree strongly preferred; Five years of professional experience in immigration, human rights, or related fields; Strong writing skills; Analytical skills, critical thinking, and ability to construct sound arguments and positions; Excellent verbal and interpersonal communication skills; Sound judgment, curiosity, creativity, integrity and dedication to the human rights of refugees and other uprooted populations; Excellent time-management, attention to detail, and organizational skills; Ability to work as a team member and independently, with a high-level of self-motivation and ability to meet goals and deadlines in a fast-paced environment; Expertise on issues related to displaced and refugee children a plus; Ability to conduct quantitative data analysis and research using inferential statistics, and an ability to communicate statistical findings to diverse audiences is a plus; Ability to travel (sometimes at short notice); Spanish, French or other language skills preferred, but not required APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest and qualifications with your online application . References and a writing sample will be required at the time of the final interview. No telephone calls, please. Position will remain open until it is filled. PHYSICAL DEMANDS Use of manual dexterity, tactile, visual, and audio acuity; Use of repetitive motion, prolonged periods of sitting and standing, and sustained visual and mental applications and demands; and Occasional lifting (up to 25 pounds), bending, pulling, and carrying. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants is an equal opportunity employer. We maintain a policy of equal employment opportunity without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, domestic partnership status, marital status, physical or mental disability, AIDS/HIV status, age, political affiliation, genetic information, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. item.title: Policy Marketing Manager
item.description: Policy Marketing Manager Organization: NVIDIA Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world. NVIDIA is seeking a Policy Marketing Manager to support the execution of marketing programs that communicate the value of NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform to policymakers. This role is positioned at the crossroads of technology, public affairs, and marketing, helping translate NVIDIA’s policy priorities into compelling content, campaigns, and experiences! Does this sound like an exciting challenge? If so, come show us what you’ve got! What you’ll be doing: Content Development: Create and manage owned content including policy briefs, blog posts, social media content, executive presentations, and one-pagers tailored. Campaign Execution: Support the planning and execution of paid and organic marketing campaigns. Event Support: Coordinate NVIDIA’s participation at policy forums, government affairs events, and industry conferences, helping manage logistics, materials, and on-site presence. Social Media: Manage day-to-day social media activations across LinkedIn and other platforms, building audience engagement within the policy and government affairs community. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Government Affairs, Communications, Legal, and broader Marketing teams to ensure consistent messaging across all channels. Market Monitoring: Track policy developments, regulatory activity, and the geopolitical landscape to help inform timely and relevant marketing content. Partner & Ecosystem Marketing: Support programs that highlight how NVIDIA’s partner ecosystem, including OEMs, cloud providers, and system integrators, aligns with government and policy priorities. What we need to see: 4+ years of experience in marketing, communications, or public affairs, ideally at the intersection of technology and government or policy. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Strong writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and policy topics for non-technical audiences. Experience managing social media accounts and paid amplification campaigns in a professional or advocacy context. Familiarity with the U.S. policy landscape and an understanding of how technology intersects with regulatory, legislative, and geopolitical issues. Ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with experience coordinating events or cross-functional projects. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience working in or with government, think tanks, trade associations, and advocacy organizations. Understanding of AI policy and technology governance debates. Experience with content management systems, marketing automation tools, or analytics platforms. Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/ Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 108,000 USD – 172,500 USD for Level 3, and 136,000 USD – 212,750 USD for Level 4. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 16, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Communications Specialist – Senior Associate
item.description: Communications Specialist – Senior Associate Organization: Lafayette Group Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Communications Specialist – Senior Associate Join our team of high-end strategy and management consultants and professionals who have served on the front lines of homeland security, law enforcement, criminal justice, emergency management, and the military. Have an immediate impact and grow your career quickly at the same time! Job Summary: Lafayette Group is seeking a dynamic and experienced Communications Specialist to develop and execute strategic communications that amplify the release of cybersecurity products, guidance, alerts, and other public-facing materials for government stakeholders. The Communications Specialist will help craft communications across multiple platforms, including social media, press releases, stakeholder emails, web content, GovDelivery notifications, and more. This role requires a strong writer, strategic thinker, and communications professional who can translate complex cybersecurity information into clear, targeted messaging for external audiences while collaborating effectively, maintaining meticulous attention to detail, and supporting fast-moving communications efforts that remain aligned with agency priorities, key messages, and stakeholder needs. Job Responsibilities: Develop strategic communications plans and messaging to support the release of cybersecurity products, guidance, alerts, advisories, reports, tools, and other public-facing materials. Craft targeted external messaging for a range of CISA stakeholders, including government partners, critical infrastructure owners and operators, industry, cybersecurity practitioners, media, and the public. Write, edit, and coordinate communications products across multiple channels, including social media posts, press releases, stakeholder emails, web content, email alert notifications, talking points, briefing materials, and message maps. Translate complex cybersecurity information into clear, accurate, audience-appropriate language that supports stakeholder awareness, understanding, and action. Partner with technical subject matter experts, product owners, program leads, external affairs staff, external stakeholders (e.g., U5, interagency), and other communications partners to shape product release strategies. Additionally, work across CSD to connect dots and fill information gaps to optimize customer service, stakeholder relationships, and information sharing. Create and manage Microsoft Teams chats and coordination channels for product and messaging alignment across the division, External Affairs, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders to support a cohesive communications approach and ensure teams are prepared for release-day rollout. Develop and maintain key messages, stakeholder-specific talking points, and communications materials that align with CISA priorities and external affairs objectives. Recommend the most effective communications channels, timing, and tactics to reach intended audiences and amplify product visibility. Support integrated communications campaigns that connect cybersecurity product releases to broader agency initiatives, priorities, and public messaging. Coordinate with social media, web, media relations, stakeholder engagement, and internal communications teams to ensure consistent messaging across platforms. Monitor cybersecurity news, stakeholder priorities, and emerging issues to inform communications planning and product release messaging. Support rapid-response communications for time-sensitive cybersecurity products, alerts, vulnerabilities, and emerging threat information. Ensure external communications are accurate, clear, timely, accessible, and consistent with approved style, branding, plain language, and clearance processes. Track communications tasks, timelines, reviews, and approvals to support coordinated and timely product releases. Provide guidance and quality control for communications products developed by junior staff or supporting team members. Required Qualifications: Ability to obtain and maintain DHS Suitability (EOD). Bachelor’s degree in communications, public affairs, public relations, journalism, marketing, English, or a related field. Six or more years of experience in communications, public affairs, public relations, media relations, external affairs, or strategic communications. Experience developing external messaging for public-facing campaigns, announcements, releases, or stakeholder communications. Excellent writing, editing, proofreading, and message development skills. Ability to translate technical or complex information into clear, concise, audience-focused communications. Experience coordinating communications products through review and approval processes. Ability to manage multiple assignments, deadlines, stakeholders, and communications channels in a fast-paced environment. Strong project management skills and ability to coordinate multiple communications products for different teams or initiatives at the same time. Desired Qualifications: Experience supporting cybersecurity, technology, national security, homeland security, critical infrastructure, or science-based communications. Experience developing communications for federal government agencies or public-sector clients. Familiarity with CISA’s cybersecurity mission, stakeholder audiences, and public-facing communications channels. Experience supporting product release communications, awareness campaigns, or integrated external affairs strategies. Experience working with technical subject matter experts to clarify complex concepts and develop accurate public-facing messaging. Location: Hybrid / Client-site (Arlington, VA) Federal Contracts: This position involves working on federal contracts that require all workers on the contract to be U.S. Citizens. Additionally, some contracts may require the ability to obtain a security clearance. Salary Range: $75K-$90K LGI carefully considers various factors when determining salary, including but not limited to education and training, professional experience, knowledge, skills and competencies, licensure and certifications, contract-specific affordability, and organizational requirements. New employees are not usually hired at the top of the estimated salary range and salary decisions depend on the circumstances and factors for each case. Salary is only one aspect of LGI’s generous total compensation package. Lafayette Group provides equal employment opportunities to all persons and prohibits employment decisions based on race, religion, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, or sexual orientation. item.title: Press Affairs Officer
item.description: Press Affairs Officer Organization: HunaTek Government Solutions Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Position Summary: HunaTek is seeking a Press Affairs Officer to provide support to the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs, under our contract with the Department of State. This position is located in Washington, DC and is contingent upon contract award. The contractors will serve as press officers on the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs (WHA) press team, supporting WHA Front Office and Global Public Affairs (GPA) priorities. Key Duties and Responsibilities Serve as a member of the five-person Press Unit and report to the WHA Spokesperson. Respond to press queries and serve as a press advisor for the WHA Front Office, WHA desk officers, and more than 50 posts in the field. Maintain a strong relationship with the Bureau of Global Public Affairs Office of Press Relations and Office of International Media Engagement. Field requests from the Office of Press Relations and provide bureau-wide clearances for press guidance, toppers, media queries, Spokesperson statements, and Secretary statements. Brief the Department Spokesperson and GPA staff on WHA posture and strategic messaging in preparation for the Department’s Daily Press Briefing. Monitor news developments in U.S. media and foreign media reporting from U.S. missions overseas to identify and advise WHA leadership of breaking news stories. Attend policy-related meetings at the bureau, Department, and interagency levels and provide readouts/notes. Identify and compile a daily digest of speeches, briefings, interviews, Congressional testimony, press releases, press guidance, media notes, and fact sheets on WHA-related issues from bureaus across the Department and broader interagency for dissemination to U.S. officials and the public. Coordinate public affairs events, obtain clearances, prepare agendas, reserve conference rooms or spaces for interviews/meetings, and secure speakers as appropriate. Escort journalists and other press-related visitors for media events at the State Department. May work excess hours on call on weekends for unusually busy periods under supervision. Skills and Qualification Required: Bachelor’s degree. Secret security clearance. Skill in applying and adapting written and oral communication principles, techniques, and methods; analytical methods; and interpersonal relations practices to assigned tasks. Ability to independently select, interpret, and apply guidelines and instructions for public affairs products, modifying and adapting them to address situations not explicitly covered by existing guidance. Ability to clearly convey detailed program information, both orally and in writing, and provide meaningful recommendations to improve information materials. About Us: At HunaTek, we build teams of people from all backgrounds with varying levels of experience, knowing firsthand that diversity of thought will strengthen our ability to deliver for our customers. We work hand in hand with Federal civilian and military staff, pulling together to further the interests of our nation and home and abroad. Whenever possible, we provide opportunities for our employees to learn new skills, obtain certifications, attend industry events, and have some fun together. Our Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to make sure our employees and their families have access to good health care, are insured against catastrophic health events, can put money aside for retirement and are able to maintain a healthy work-life balance. These benefits include: Comprehensive medical, dental and vision Long-term and short-term disability insurance and term life insurance 401(K) with safe harbor contribution Paid time off and 11 paid holidays Tuition and career development assistance A selection of voluntary benefits This job description will be reviewed periodically as duties and responsibilities change with business necessity. Essential and marginal job functions are subject to modification. Equal opportunity employer as to all protected groups, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. item.description: Social Media Coordinator (94780) Organization: The Freeman Company Location: Washington, DC | San Diego, CA Date Posted: 10/15/2026 About Us For five decades, mdg has been a leader in the association and event marketing space. And while we’ve been leading, we’ve also been learning: learning what motivates audiences now, how to build loyalty, and which performance tools actually impact registration numbers. We specialize in audience development and attendee acquisition for associations and trade shows, working across strategy, creative, digital, and communications to make that happen. We don’t copy and paste strategies or use technology for show. We dig deep into unique situations and apply what makes sense, instead of what’s expected. Summary mdg is looking for a Social Media Coordinator to join our growing Communications team. This is an entry-level position for someone who is organized, detail-oriented and excited to build a career across social media and influencer marketing. Reporting to the Associate Director of Influencer, the Social Media Coordinator will support the day-to-day execution of social media and influencer campaigns for a variety of clients in the events and trade show industry. The role will work closely with members of the social media and influencer teams to support social media reporting, scheduling and monitoring, content creation, influencer outreach, content management and campaign reporting. The ideal candidate is highly organized, comfortable managing multiple projects and deadlines, and eager to learn how social media and influencer marketing can help events build awareness, strengthen credibility and drive measurable results. This position will support our Communications team. It is eligible to work a hybrid schedule, generally requiring work in-office and/or show site 2-3 days per week. The ideal candidate will be based out of any of the following locations: Washington, DC San Diego, CA Essential Duties & Responsibilities Social Media Content Scheduling & Reporting Schedule and publish approved social media content across LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook and X. Support social media managers in maintaining accurate and up-to-date content calendars. Conduct quality assurance before content is published, including reviewing copy, links, tags, formatting and creative assets. Pull and organize performance data across social platforms and social media management tools. Help identify notable performance trends, top-performing content and opportunities to improve future content. Social monitoring & research: Research relevant industry trends, platform updates and emerging content formats and share useful findings with the broader social team. Content creation: Assist with light content creation, including drafting social copy, desiging social assets and editing video assets. Influencer Marketing Creator outreach & negotations Support influencer outreach and follow-up communication. Track outreach status, responses and next steps across active campaigns. Help coordinate campaign details with creators, including timelines, deliverables and required materials. Maintain professional and timely communication throughout the campaign process. Content and campaign management: Help ensure creators have the messaging, assets, links and logistical information needed to complete their work and track creator deliverables, deadlines, content submissions, approvals and posting status. Content creation Campaign reporting: Support influencer campaign reporting, including performance summaries, earned media value and other campaign KPIs. Education & Experience 1–5 years of professional, internship or relevant hands-on experience in social media, influencer marketing, communications, public relations, marketing or a related field. Strong understanding of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook and X and an interest in how brands use social media to reach and influence their audiences. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines and stakeholders. Comfortable working with data and interested in understanding what content and campaigns are driving results. Strong judgment and professionalism when communicating with clients, creators and internal teams. Experience with social media management, influencer marketing, social listening, analytics or content creation tools is a plus. Experience with platforms such as Agorapulse, Favikon, Canva, CapCut or similar tools is a plus. Travel Requirements Travel up to 25% What We Offer The Freeman Company provides benefits that aim to empower our people and their families to thrive mentally, physically, and financially. These are a handful of the types of programs and benefits our full-time people may be eligible for. There may be some variances in specific benefits across regions. Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance Tuition Reimbursement Paid Parental Leave Life, Accident and Disability Retirement with Company Match Paid Time Off Hourly range of $24.00-$28.00 based upon experience Diversity Commitment At The Freeman Company, our commitment to diversity and inclusion is helping us to create not only a great place to work, but also an environment where our employees, our customers and our communities around the world can reach their goals and connect with each other. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status and other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. #LI-Hybrid #TFCmdg Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director Legislative Policy
item.description: Director Legislative Policy Organization: Ernst Young (EY) Location: Washington, DC | McLean, VA | Baltimore, MD Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Requisition ID: 1751455 Location: Washington, McLean and Baltimore At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence. We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world. The opportunity This position is responsible for assisting in the development and implementation of the strategic plans for successfully achieving specific legislative and regulatory results consistent with the firm’s business strategy. In doing so, this position must work effectively with the other members of the Office of Public Policy and representatives from across the firm. In addition, work with representatives of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) and the other major public company auditing firms on issues of importance to the profession. Monitor regulatory and legislative developments, recognizing issues that may affect the firm, and communicating those issues within the Office of Public Policy and elsewhere across the firm. Strategic thinking skills and experience addressing complex challenges – thus enabling recommendations and solutions to be identified for challenges or issues that arise. Schedules are driven by Congress. Evening, weekend and early morning activities in support of relationship building with stakeholders. Your key responsibilities Identify and manage regulatory and legislative issues of concern to the firm and profession. Have superior knowledge of laws and regulations affecting our business, including but not limited to the areas of cyber and privacy policy, emerging technologies, securities, as well as associated politics at the national and state level across the country. Have fluency with the priority congressional committees, including House Energy and Commerce, and Senate Commerce committees, the House Financial Services, and Senate Banking. Represent EY on public policy issues before Congress, presidential administrations, and various regulatory agencies. Responsible for lobbying in both the US House of Representatives and the US Senate – members and staff. Responsible for day-to-day firm relationships with members and staff on Capitol Hill – deepening their comprehension of the firm and public company auditing profession issues. Represent the EY Political Action Committee (PAC) and provide general political and fund-raising support. Contribute to the firm’s policy formation mindful of congressional stakeholders. Skills and attributes for success A thorough understanding of US congressional and administration policymaking processes, including an understanding of the roles and decision makers in the executive agencies, the White House, the Senate and the House, as well as the role of think tanks and trade associations. Ability to understand congressional, regulatory and technical point of view. Strong verbal and writing skills to synthesize complex material and make the most effective written and verbal presentations/arguments for EY and the profession. Experience advising/influencing senior-level policy makers/executives. Strategic thinking skills and experience addressing complex challenges. Understanding of policies affecting the accounting profession and the various service lines within EY. To qualify you must have Bachelor’s degree in Political Science and/or related degree. Law degree and/or equivalent work experience preferred. Approximately 10+ years of political/government experience. Ideally, you’ll also have Preferred work experience would include a combination of government affairs; a government agency, or with a member of Congress or committee. Number of key relationships developed and the ability to be the face of the firm on the Hill and within the administration is more important than number of years of experience for qualifying for this position. What we offer you At EY, we harness our collective strength to empower you to shape your future with confidence through professional growth, personal fulfillment and an inclusive culture. Learn more at ey.com/us/careers. We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. The base salary range for this job is: New York City, Boston, and Washington DC Metro Areas, Washington State, and Southern California offices – $314,500 to $597,500 Bay Area California offices – $327,600 to $622,400 All other offices locations in the US, including Sacramento – $262,100 to $547,700 Individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options. Under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. You’ll also be granted time off for designated EY Paid Holidays, Winter/Summer breaks, Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being. Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today . To make the most of your application experience, please limit yourself to two applications within a six-month period. EY accepts applications for this position on an on-going basis. At EY, our values set the foundation for how we work and the behaviors we expect of our people. Any misrepresentation or falsification of information or lack of integrity at any point in the recruiting process may result in withdrawal of your candidacy, revocation of an offer or immediate termination of employment. EY | Building a better working world EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets. Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow. EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories. All in to shape the future with confidence. EY provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, genetic information, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected basis, including arrest and conviction records, in accordance with applicable law. EY is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities including veterans with disabilities. If you have a disability and either need assistance applying online or need to request an accommodation during any part of the application process, please call 1-800-EY-HELP3, select Option 2 for candidate related inquiries, then select Option 1 for candidate queries and finally select Option 2 for candidates with an inquiry which will route you to EY’s Talent Shared Services Team (TSS) or email the TSS at [email protected] .
