item.title: Internal Communications & Events Manager
item.description: Internal Communications & Events Manager Organization: Choice Hotels International Location: Bethesda, MD Date Posted: 10/15/2026 JOB SUMMARY: The Internal Communications & Events Manager leads strategic employee communications and high-impact internal events that connect team members to company priorities, culture, and business goals. This role develops and executes communication strategies for enterprise initiatives, executive messaging, change management efforts, and employee engagement programs while producing engaging internal events and experiences. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator, storyteller, and project leader who can translate complex information into clear, compelling messages and deliver exceptional employee experiences that drive engagement and business results. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Communications Strategy & Planning Develop and execute internal communication strategies that advance business priorities, organizational initiatives, and employee engagement goals. Partner with leaders and key stakeholders to create communication plans aligned with company objectives and audience needs. Craft clear, compelling messaging and communication materials for a variety of employee audiences. Lead executive communications, organizational announcements, culture initiatives, and enterprise-wide messaging efforts. Develop communication frameworks, toolkits, and resources that enable leaders to communicate effectively and consistently. Evaluate communication effectiveness and recommend improvements based on business outcomes and employee feedback. Campaign Development & Associate Engagement Lead integrated communication campaigns that support key business initiatives, organizational change efforts, and employee experience programs. Design multi-channel communication strategies that increase awareness, understanding, and engagement. Partner with stakeholders to identify audience needs, objectives, and success measures. Monitor campaign performance and leverage insights to continuously improve future communications. Internal Events & Production Lead the strategy, planning, and execution of internal events, including leadership meetings, town halls, recognition programs, and employee engagement experiences. Collaborate with business leaders to define event objectives, key messages, and desired outcomes. Manage event budgets, timelines, project plans, vendors, and production schedules. Develop event content, executive presentations, speaker materials, communication plans, and run-of-show documentation. Coordinate internal teams and external partners to deliver seamless, high-quality event experiences. Ensure events reinforce company culture and support broader business and communication objectives. Operational Communications & Incident Response Serve as the lead communications partner during employee-impacting operational issues and business disruptions. Assess communication needs, recommend response strategies, and deliver timely, accurate updates during rapidly evolving situations. Manage communications related to office closures, severe weather, facilities issues, technology disruptions, safety matters, and other operational events. Maintain communication tools, templates, and processes that support effective incident response and business continuity communications. Demonstrate sound judgment, discretion, and composure under pressure. Strategic Partnership & Communications Counsel Advise leaders and stakeholders on communication strategy, change management, messaging, timing, audience engagement, and channel selection. Lead communications planning for high-profile initiatives requiring coordinated, cross-functional support. Partner closely with Human Resources and other business functions to align employee-facing communications and initiatives. Build strong relationships across the organization to identify communication opportunities and improve overall communication effectiveness. Champion strategic, enterprise-wide communication approaches that drive greater consistency and business impact. QUALIFICATIONS: Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, Event Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience. 5+ years of experience in internal communications, corporate communications, employee communications, or a related field. 3+ years of experience leading communication strategy, planning, and execution for internal events, employee engagement programs, or organizational initiatives. Demonstrated success managing communication campaigns and events from strategy through delivery. Experience supporting executive communications, change communications, and time-sensitive operational communications. Exceptional writing, editing, storytelling, and presentation development skills. Strong project management, organizational, and stakeholder management capabilities. Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong visual and creative judgment with an understanding of brand standards and audience engagement best practices. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Organizational Communication, Marketing, or a related field. Experience in hospitality, travel, entertainment, media, retail, or other customer-centric industries. Experience managing large-scale employee events, leadership meetings, conferences, or recognition programs. Experience working with external agencies, creative partners, production companies, or event vendors. Experience with employee engagement platforms, collaboration tools, or internal communications technology. COMPENSATION & SALARY RANGE: Salary Range: $99,919 to $117,000 annually This role is also eligible for an annual bonus under Choice’s Management Incentive Plan (MIP). Pay ranges listed are what Choice Hotels reasonably expects to pay. Actual pay may be higher or lower and ranges may be adjusted in the future. Pay positioning within the range is influenced by factors including—but not limited to—education, experience, skills, certifications, performance, geographic location, business needs, seniority, and travel requirements. WORK LOCATION & HYBRID SCHEDULE: This position is based at Choice Hotels International’s corporate headquarters in North Bethesda, Maryland. Regular onsite presence at this location is required. Associates are expected to follow the established hybrid work schedule, working onsite Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays. RELOCATION & SPONSORSHIP: Please note that relocation assistance is not available for this position. Additionally, Choice Hotels is not able to provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future for this role. Choice prioritizes our associate wellbeing by offering a comprehensive benefits program that is both competitive and flexible to help you achieve your wellbeing goals – here are just a few: Competitive compensation and benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage Leave and paid time-off for holidays, vacation, personal, family, volunteer, sick, jury duty, bereavement, military, and religious observance Financial benefits for retirement and health savings Employee recognition programs Discounts at Choice hotels worldwide About Choice Choice Hotels International, Inc. (NYSE: CHH), is one of the largest lodging franchisors in the world. With 7,500 hotels in 45+ countries and territories, we offer a range of high-quality lodging options in the upper upscale, upper midscale, midscale, extended stay, and economy segments. We’re the hotel company for those who choose to bet on themselves — the striver, the dreamer, the entrepreneur — because that’s who we are, too. At Choice, we are united by the simple belief that tomorrow will be even better than today — for associates, our company, and our franchisees. At our worldwide corporate headquarters in North Bethesda, Maryland, at our technology center in Scottsdale, Arizona, and through our associates around the globe, every voice is heard and every idea is listened to, no matter what area of the company they come from. We are united in supporting the entrepreneurial dreams of our thousands of franchise owners, which propels us forward — giving our work at Choice a purpose larger than our business. Our corporate office locations: North Bethesda, MD — Located at Pike & Rose, our worldwide headquarters is less than 15 miles from Washington, D.C., one block away from the North Bethesda Metro station, with easy access to I-495, complimentary parking, electronic charging stations, restaurants and retail. Scottsdale, AZ — Located at the northwest corner of Loop 101, the Scottsdale office is home to our technology, eCommerce and customer service organizations, with easy access to complimentary parking, electronic charging stations, restaurants and retail. Minneapolis, MN — Select roles are based in our Minneapolis office on Highway 394, near the intersection with Highway 100, only five minutes from downtown. Field/Remote — Select roles designated as field/remote will require associates to work from a home office, connecting virtually with Choice team members and leadership on Zoom, with possible required travel depending on the role. Choice’s Cultural Values Welcome and Respect Everyone | Be Bold | Be Quick | Listen | Be Curious | Show Integrity Choice’s Leadership Principles Act with Intention | Lead with Authenticity | Grow & Deliver Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.description: Coordinator, Government Affairs Organization: American Dental Association (ADA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Description Who We Are: It all starts with purpose. We are a purpose-driven nonprofit with a dynamic staff culture. With a meaningful purpose, motivated staff, and excellent benefits, working here will definitely have you smiling! The ADA’s headquarters is located in one of Chicago’s most iconic buildings, designed by a world-renowned architectural firm, and is close to public transportation. With more than 350 colleagues, the ADA Staff are some of the most talented people in the Chicago, Washington D.C., and Boston area. We were named a 2024 Best-in-Class Employer by Gallagher and Top Workplace by the Chicago Tribune in 2019 and 2021! Come join our team! Job Responsibilities: The Coordinator of Government Affairs will provide administrative, operational, financial, compliance, and communications support to the Government Affairs division. Responsibilities include coordinating daily operations; tracking projects and deadlines; scheduling meetings and conference calls; preparing agendas, reports, and other materials; monitoring and reporting financial activity; processing invoices; administering contracts and purchase orders; coordinating vendors; supporting compliance reporting and records management; managing website content; coordinating event logistics; and assisting with communications and public affairs activities. The Coordinator serves as a central administrative resource for CGA, Lobby Day, the State Lobbyist Conference, divisional meetings, and other Government Affairs activities. The position also provides backup support to the Manager of Government Affairs and assists with divisional operations, compliance activities, and special projects. Must Have: Bachelor’s degree or experience in lieu of degree 3 years (or 7 years in lieu of a degree) experience coordinating projects, meetings, and administrative operations across cross-functional teams in administrative, operations, communications, public affairs, government affairs, legislative offices, trade associations, nonprofit organization, or executive support environments Knowledge of administrative and office operations, project coordination, records management, and the legislative, regulatory, advocacy, or association management environment Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to draft correspondence, format policy documents, manage website content, coordinate communications projects, and support public affairs and advocacy initiatives Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain confidentiality, and work effectively with staff, vendors, consultants, government officials, and external stakeholders Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite Travel twice per year, 1-3 nights per trip, to attend meetings Position may require more than the standard number of hours of work within a work week, before or after hours work, and/or weekend work Nice to Have: Knowledge of meeting and event coordination, compliance reporting, and stakeholder communications Experience in a government affairs, public affairs, congressional, legislative, advocacy, association management, nonprofit, communications or executive office environment Just a few of the benefits offered to employees: Promotes Work/Life Balance Hybrid Work Schedule (2-3 days from home) Health insurance/ dental reimbursement plan Ample Paid time off 401(k) Flexible Spending Account Life insurance Tuition reimbursement Paid Parental Leave Pet Insurance Student Loan Refinance 2 days off to work at a charity event of your choice The ADA values a variety of backgrounds and experiences and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified job candidates. item.title: Senior Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs Organization: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 You are a strategic health policy leader who sees the story behind the regulation, the opportunity inside complexity, and the real impact policy decisions have on physicians and patients. You know physician payment, reimbursement, coding, quality, and regulatory affairs, but what sets you apart is your ability to connect the details to a bigger purpose. At AAOS, you can bring that expertise to a mission-driven organization where your work helps shape national conversations, strengthen advocacy, and support the future of musculoskeletal care. If this sounds like you, please read on! The Senior Director, Policy and Regulatory Affairs leads AAOS regulatory health policy initiatives and serves as a key advisor on physician payment policy, reimbursement, coding, quality reporting, and broader health policy issues impacting orthopaedic surgeons. This role represents AAOS in medical specialty society and stakeholder meetings, supports engagement with federal regulatory agencies, and works closely with internal teams, volunteer leaders, and external partners to advance AAOS policy priorities. What You’ll Do Lead regulatory health policy initiatives on behalf of AAOS, with a focus on physician payment policy, reimbursement, coding, quality reporting measures, and alternative payment models. Analyze health policy issues of strategic importance to AAOS and partner with Government Relations leadership to develop policy positions, advocacy strategies, and related initiatives. Represent AAOS in medical specialty society meetings, stakeholder discussions, and meetings with federal regulatory agencies and other external partners. Manage AAOS involvement in the AMA/Specialty Society Relative Value Scale Update Committee, AMA CPT Editorial Process, and American College of Surgeons Surgical Quality Alliance. Supervise and support a health policy team that includes policy analysts and coding and reimbursement professionals. Staff and support AAOS committees and workgroups focused on coding, coverage, reimbursement, health care systems, clinical quality, value, registries, and related advocacy priorities. Draft and review official AAOS comments to federal agencies, including HHS, CMS, AHRQ, CDC, and other regulatory bodies. Develop member-facing communications, educational content, articles, policy statements, and advocacy resources related to public and private health insurance payment issues. Build and maintain relationships with government officials, third-party carrier representatives, medical society leaders, staff, and other key stakeholders. Maintain historical records of AAOS policy positions and support development of the Policy Compendium. Travel: Up to 15 days of travel per year Qualifications: Required: 7-10 years of relevant experience in health policy, physician payment policy, reimbursement, coding, or a closely related area. Extensive knowledge of the Medicare resource-based physician payment system and related regulatory processes. Strong understanding of health policy issues affecting physicians, medical specialty societies, and health care delivery. Excellent analytical, written communication, verbal communication, organizational, management, and interpersonal skills. Experience leading projects, managing competing priorities, and working independently in a deadline-driven environment. Supervisory experience and the ability to coach, develop, and support a high-performing team. Proficiency with common business applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and web-based research tools. Desired: Master’s degree. Experience staffing committees within a medical association, professional society, or health care policy organization. Salary Range: $152,000-$168,000, depending on qualifications and experience. If you are excited by the opportunity to shape health policy, influence regulatory conversations, strengthen advocacy on behalf of orthopaedic surgeons, and help advance work that supports the musculoskeletal community, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and bring your ideas, curiosity, and policy expertise to a role where you can make a real impact. Please share the following: Clearly communicate why you are the ideal candidate for this role, providing specific examples and experiences as proof points. Resumes must be accompanied by a cover letter with salary expectations to be considered. Please note: This hybrid position is based in Washington, DC and requires the ability to commute to the office at least twice per week. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future employer sponsorship. AAOS does not sponsor, and will not sponsor, applicants or employees for purposes of obtaining or maintaining work authorization. item.title: Senior Director, Government and Political Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Government and Political Affairs Organization: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 You are a strategic advocate and relationship builder who turns complex policy priorities into advocacy strategies that move people and create measurable impact. You have the strategic instincts, political insight, and presence to earn trust with legislators, senior leaders, physician advocates, coalition partners, and industry stakeholders. You are ready to set a bold national advocacy agenda, lead a high-performing team, shape persuasive communications, and represent AAOS with confidence in high-profile settings. If you want to use your influence and expertise to strengthen the voice of the orthopaedic community and expand the impact of Orthopaedic PAC, this is the opportunity to lead at a meaningful scale. If this sounds like you, please read on! In this role, you will direct AAOS priorities and positions across federal and state legislative activity, strategically manage its presence in both arenas, and develop integrated advocacy and political strategies. As a registered lobbyist, you will work closely with the federal, regulatory, and state legislative affairs team to connect regulatory, political, and advocacy agendas into coherent strategies that advance the AAOS advocacy agenda. You will oversee grassroots strategy; staff responsible for the Political Action Committee of the AAOS; and all political advocacy activities. You will arrange AAOS volunteer visits to Washington, DC, and execute in-district fundraising, meet and greets, and site visits. You will also oversee legislative materials for internal and external audiences, lead quality control for all Office of Government Relations materials, partner with the Communications lead to keep public-facing materials—including the website—updated, coherent, consistent, and professionally presented, oversee budget and target spreadsheets for PAC receipts and disbursements, plan and execute all materials related to political activities, and ensure the Quorum tool is used appropriately across PAC, grassroots, and advocacy functions. What You’ll Lead • Government affairs strategy: Lead AAOS federal and state lobbying, advance policy priorities, guide legislative strategy, and build senior-level relationships with Congress. Primary committee focus includes House Ways and Means; House Energy and Commerce; Senate Finance; Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions; House and Senate Appropriations; and House and Senate Judiciary, with secondary responsibility for House and Senate Armed Services. • Political and PAC strategy: Set political and PAC giving strategy, represent AAOS at political events, and prepare leaders and fellows with effective talking points and materials. • Coalitions and advocacy: Direct coalition participation, grassroots advocacy, Congressional Ambassadors, and member alerts while aligning AAOS messaging with industry groups and other stakeholders. • Team and issue leadership: Supervise lobbying staff, monitor and interpret priority federal activity, set expectations, evaluate performance, and provide team support. • Legislative communications: Oversee legislative tracking and audience-specific updates, including fact sheets, articles, letters to Congress, Legislative Alerts, and other analytical communications. • BOC and BOS support: Lead federal affairs support for the BOC, BOS, their committees, and related boards. Serve as lead staff for the BOC Committee on Economic Issues, providing policy analysis, strategy, guidance, materials, updates, memoranda, budget management, position statements, advisory statements, and articles for AAOS publications. Political Action Committee Leadership • Grow fundraising and engagement: Lead the Advisor’s Circle and soft-dollar program, develop new funding sources, attract donors, oversee the PAC mobile program, and explore new technologies, big data, and social channels. Coordinate volunteer participation in Congressional retreats, fly-ins, fundraisers, Washington events, convention, presentations, webinars, travel, and monthly Advisor’s Circle calls to support Orthopaedic PAC’s self-sufficiency. • Direct PAC operations: Set the dollars-out strategy, assign staff to Congressional Members and fundraisers, manage RSVPs and the PAC events calendar, oversee contributions and attendee lists, and coordinate with fundraisers, state orthopaedic societies, PAC members, specialty societies, and other medical organizations. • Represent and promote AAOS: Attend fundraisers, coffees, candidate interviews, and meet and greets with Members of Congress and staff. Build relationships with national party committees, Congressional staff, fundraisers, the physician PAC community, MaDPAC, and the Annual Physician PAC Forum to advance AAOS priorities and visibility. • Lead events and field engagement: Manage AAOS-hosted fundraisers and check-delivery events, including promotion, attendance, and strategy. Oversee the traveling PAC booth and represent OGR and Orthopaedic PAC at Grand Rounds, member practices, state and specialty society meetings, and other events while soliciting contributions and hosting fundraisers. • Drive PAC communications: Promote PAC activity, results, and performance through the website, quarterly PAC Newsletter, PAC Annual Report, AAOS Now, Advisor’s Circle, Advocacy Now, AAOS In-the-States, the AAOS Resident Newsletter, and other political advocacy materials. • Align strategy and quality: Connect regulatory, political, and advocacy priorities; maintain quality control across OGR materials; partner with Communications to keep public-facing content current, consistent, and professional; and ensure Quorum is used effectively across PAC, grassroots, and advocacy functions. Travel: • Up to 60 days per year Qualifications: Required: • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree • Six years of government relations experience • Experience running a PAC through at least two election cycles • Supervisory experience • Skilled at networking and negotiating • Association management experience • Knowledge of the legislative process and grassroots advocacy • Experience managing multiple projects, with strong organizational skills and attention to detail • Ability to convey concepts clearly and write effectively for a range of publication styles, including issue papers, web pages, newsletters, advocacy action alerts, fundraising appeals, year-end reports, event promotions, advertising copy, and others • Strong interpersonal, writing, and oral communication skills • Proficiency in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Desired: • Corporate fundraising experience • Database management ability • Experience with industry-specific PAC and grassroots software programs • Familiarity with the medical PAC community • Contacts on the Hill and with Members of Congress Salary Range: $176,000-$192,000, depending on qualifications and experience. Ready to lead with influence? If you are a strategic, relationship-driven government affairs leader who can connect policy, advocacy, political engagement, and PAC growth, we want to hear from you. Apply today and help advance the voice and priorities of the orthopaedic community. Please share the following: • Clearly communicate why you are the ideal candidate for this role, providing specific examples and experiences as proof points. • Resumes must be accompanied by a cover letter with salary expectations to be considered. Please note: This hybrid position is based in Washington, DC and requires the ability to commute to the office at least twice per week. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future employer sponsorship. AAOS does not sponsor, and will not sponsor, applicants or employees for purposes of obtaining or maintaining work authorization. item.title: Director, Trade and Supply Chains
item.description: Director, Trade and Supply Chains Organization: Climate Leadership Council (the Council) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Organizational Summary: The Climate Leadership Council (the Council) is a 501(c)(3) organization whose mission is to develop and promote market-based policies that advance U.S. competitiveness, security, and economic opportunity as the central strategy for lowering global emissions. Position Overview: Trade policy is now climate policy. How the United States accounts for carbon at the border, secures critical mineral supply chains, drives energy exports, and finances investment abroad will shape both American competitiveness and the pace of global decarbonization. The Director, Trade and Supply Chains will lead the Council’s work at that intersection. The portfolio spans three priority areas central to the Council’s policy agenda: carbon border adjustments; critical minerals and supply chain security; and international investment and export promotion. The Director will be responsible for shaping a research agenda, developing policy positions, engaging stakeholders, and supporting policymaker education on Capitol Hill and in the administration. This is a substantive and visible role. The Director will represent the Council in meetings with members of Congress, administration officials, and their staff; build working relationships with business, industry, and environmental partners; and serve as a public voice for the Council at conferences, briefings, and in the press. The Director will be a member of senior staff and partner with colleagues across policy, government relations, and communications to turn strong ideas into durable support for policy change. This role is a fit for someone with deep trade or supply chain policy expertise who can translate complex issues for any audience and who is energized by working with industry, lawmakers, and the broader policy community. The Council offers: Flexible hybrid work environment Generous benefits package Free on-site fitness center Central location steps from Metro, with secure bike storage Apply: Interested candidates should send a resume and cover letter to [email protected] . Responsibilities include: Direct a portfolio of Council priority policies, including developing research products, crafting and refining proposals, soliciting input from stakeholders, delivering written analysis, crafting compelling messaging, and providing educational support to policymakers. Work with executive leadership to develop priorities for market-based climate policy, which includes border carbon adjustments, critical minerals, international investment and export strategy, and other policy areas. Partner with the Senior Vice President in identifying discrete policy goals consistent with Council priorities, establishing research and engagement priorities, and delivering progress. Closely monitor relevant developments in the field and report key findings to the internal team and stakeholders. This will involve tracking research, analysis, legislative developments, and advocacy as well as attending events both virtually and in person. Produce research and analysis consistent with the Council’s research goals and in support of advancing its policy priorities. Build opportunities for collaboration with existing and new external stakeholders toward effective policy design, including having one-on-one meetings, presenting policy ideas at various forums, preparing programming materials, leading group meetings, and cultivating new strategic relationships. Represent Council work in meetings with Members of Congress, Hill staff, and administration officials. Advise policymakers, including by providing policy ideas, legislative feedback, research support, educational documents, and connections to relevant stakeholder partners. Work with executive leadership and other colleagues to amplify the Council’s policy priorities through public conversation, stakeholder engagement, executive action, or legislative action. Share ownership of the Council’s convening and engagement function, including Hill briefings, policy working groups, public events, salons, and platform opportunities for stakeholders, by originating ideas, contributing expertise and relationships, and partnering with Communications & Public Affairs and Government Relations on execution. Manage workflow and work product of associate-, analyst-, and/or manager-level staff. Identify and secure outside contractors, consultants, and influential scholars to conduct and publish research for the Council; manage contractual agreements and related processes, actions, and measurables. Support the CEO, EVP/COO, Chief of Staff, and other senior leaders to secure funding for policy programs and other organizational priorities through engagement with corporate and philanthropic partners. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required. 8–10 years of experience with demonstrated expertise in domestic or international climate, trade, or foreign policy. Experience on Capitol Hill or in the administration preferred. Strong knowledge of climate, trade, and/or foreign policy, including border carbon adjustments, critical minerals and supply chain security, greenhouse gas reporting, trade agreements, international negotiations, and export finance. Experience in crafting policy for Congress or the executive branch, especially in areas relevant to the Council’s policy priorities. Experience and expertise in project management with ability to effectively manage outside consultants and complicated timelines. Experience supervising, developing, and mentoring staff. Strong Hill, Administration, and policy community relationships are a plus. Ability to balance multiple projects, meet pressing deadlines, anticipate needs, and adjust in a changing environment. Strong verbal and written communication skills, including comfort presenting to senior audiences and speaking publicly on behalf of the Council; media experience a plus. Most importantly, we are seeking individuals who are highly ambitious, focused on positive outcomes, eager to work collaboratively in a challenging political arena, and who operate with impeccable integrity. Location: This position is based in DC in a traditional office setting, subject to the organization’s telework policy. Currently, the organization is operating in a hybrid environment (3 days in office). Compensation: Competitive salary range based on experience: $150,000-200,000; full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 403(b), etc. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: In-State Political and Partnerships Director
item.description: In-State Political and Partnerships Director Organization: Who Decides Location: Remote (AZ, GA, MI, NH, NM, NV, NC, PA, SC, VA, WI) Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Location: In States – Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Nevada, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Virginia, Wisconsin Job Type: Contract Reports to: National Political Director About Who Decides Who Decides will bring labor, parents, educators, civil-rights groups and other trusted organizations together around a common AI safety agenda for Democrats. Right now, a few executives inside a handful of companies are making all the decisions as AI reshapes entire industries, education, communities, and safety, and as the most powerful models grow beyond our ability to control them. The public has virtually no say, and neither political party has staked out a comprehensive agenda. Who Decides exists to make sure Democrats do, by building the coalitions needed to win elections on AI safety and govern AI so that the public sets the rules for the technology. The Role We are looking for several qualified In-State Political and Partnerships Directors across the Country who can serve as trusted and well-connected coalition builders and organizers with existing deep relationships across the Democratic ecosystem or the ability to quickly navigate and create relationships in a given state. Each State Director will work to build a durable in-state network of partner organizations and stakeholders to ensure AI Safety is salient and resonating in all relevant work politically and advocacy adjacent. State Directors will be reliable, on-call resources for local partners and leaders when AI questions come up. Qualifications Years of Experience: 2-4 years of relevant experience with state based issue advocacy or political work. History of creating and maintaining strong relationships and partnerships in the workplace ecosystem. Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong organizational and time management skills, with an ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. Personable and extroverted- this role will involve lots of outside partnership and collaborations. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, hybrid work environment. Must live In-State Expertise and background in AI helpful but not required. To Apply Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and contact information for two references to [email protected] . Please include ” In-State Political and Partnerships Director” in the subject line. We look forward to hearing from you! Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Organization: NBCUniversal Location: Universal City, CA Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Company Description NBCUniversal is one of the world’s leading media and entertainment companies. We create world-class content, which we distribute across our portfolio of film, television, and streaming, and bring to life through our global theme park destinations, consumer products, and experiences. We own and operate leading entertainment and news brands, including NBC, NBC News, NBC Sports, Telemundo, NBC Local Stations, Bravo, and Peacock, our premium ad-supported streaming service. We produce and distribute premier filmed entertainment and programming through our powerhouse film and television studios, including Universal Pictures, DreamWorks Animation, and Focus Features, and the four global television studios under the Universal Studio Group banner, and operate industry-leading theme parks and experiences around the world through Universal Destinations & Experiences, including Universal Orlando Resort, home to Universal Epic Universe, and Universal Studios Hollywood. NBCUniversal is a subsidiary of Comcast Corporation. Visit www.nbcuniversal.com for more information. Our impact is rooted in improving the communities where our employees, customers, and audiences live and work. We have a rich tradition of giving back and ensuring our employees have the opportunity to serve their communities. We champion an inclusive culture and strive to attract and develop a talented workforce to create and deliver a wide range of content reflecting our world. Job Description The NBCUniversal State & Local Government Affairs team develops and executes advocacy strategies that advance NBCUniversal’s business priorities and protect the company’s operations at the state and local levels. The team engages directly with state and local elected officials and manages relationships with trade associations and other third-party organizations to build support for NBCUniversal’s public policy agenda. NBCUniversal is looking for a Director, Government Affairs, to support the company in Los Angeles. This Director position will report directly to the Senior Vice President, Head of Public Policy with matrix reporting to Vice President of Government and External Affairs. Here You Can: Develop and maintain relationships with policymakers, industry associations, community organizations, business groups and other key stakeholders in Los Angeles County and the City of Los Angeles. Manage the public policy environment affecting NBCUniversal’s Los Angeles-area business operations including identifying risks, opportunities, and strategic advocacy priorities. Identify, monitor, and analyze national trends in state and local public policy, including legislative and regulatory proposals affecting the company. Partner with internal stakeholders across NBCUniversal, including Legal, Compliance Communications, and relevant business units, to assess policy impacts, and to develop advocacy strategies for advancing business objectives. Advocate externally for policy positions that advance NBCUniversal’s corporate objectives and protect its business interests. Clearly articulate the company’s policy positions through briefing materials, written responses, presentations, and internal policy discussions. In partnership with NBCU’s Vice President of Government and External Affairs, develop and execute advocacy and stakeholder engagement strategies on issues affecting NBCUniversal in key jurisdictions across the country. Support advocacy efforts designed to inform public opinion and influence legislative and regulatory decision-making through education, effective communication, and coalition building. Represent NBCUniversal at industry conferences, public hearings, and other relevant events, serving as a credible ambassador for the company’s positions and interests. Draft letters, presentations, testimony, and other materials communicating the company’s positions on legislative and regulatory matters. Stay informed about industry developments, emerging state and local policy issues, and evolving regulatory frameworks. Advise senior leadership on emerging legislative, regulatory, and political developments, providing strategic recommendations regarding potential risks, opportunities, and business impacts Qualifications Here You’ll Need: Bachelor’s degree in political science, international affairs, government, public affairs, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. At least seven years of experience in public policy, government affairs, government service, or a related field such as crisis and issue management. Demonstrated experience developing and executing government affairs, public policy, or stakeholder engagement strategies in a complex, highly matrixed environment. Deep knowledge of local legislative processes in Los Angeles County and/or the City of Los Angeles. Solid political network in Los Angeles. Exceptional writing and verbal skills, including the ability to distill complex policy issues into clear explanations and compelling messages. Outstanding project management, analytical, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate legislative and regulatory proposals and assess their potential impact on the company. Excellent organizational skills and proficiency with Microsoft suite of products such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Hybrid: This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time. This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $130,000- $170,000 (bonus and long-term incentive eligible) Additional Information As part of our selection process, external candidates may be required to attend an in-person interview with an NBCUniversal employee at one of our locations prior to a hiring decision. NBCUniversal’s policy is to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, gender identity or expression, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, membership in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. NBCUniversal will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories, or arrest or conviction records, in a manner consistent with relevant legal requirements, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative For Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, where applicable. If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran and require support throughout the application and/or recruitment process as a result of your disability, you have the right to request a reasonable accommodation. You can submit your request to [email protected] . Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Organization: Red Bull Location: Washington, DC | New York, NY Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Company Description Lead Red Bull’s U.S. government affairs strategy by monitoring and assessing political, legislative, and regulatory developments affecting the company, the beverage industry, and the broader business environment. Build and maintain strong relationships with policymakers, government agencies, trade associations, coalition partners, and external stakeholders to advance Red Bull’s interests and influence policy outcomes. Provide strategic guidance and clear policy recommendations to business leaders, manage external consultants and advocacy efforts, and drive cross-functional collaboration to identify opportunities, mitigate risks, and support the company’s long-term objectives. The purpose of this role is to lead the development and execution of Red Bull North America’s U.S. government affairs strategy, ensuring the business is well positioned to navigate evolving political, legislative, and regulatory matters. Reporting to the Senior Director, Government Affairs (North America), this role serves as a key liaison between the U.S. business, policymakers, industry associations, external advisors, and global stakeholders. The position advances Red Bull’s policy priorities, supports responsible industry engagement, identifies and mitigates regulatory risks, and delivers actionable insights that help inform business strategy and decision-making. Candidates are also eligible to sit in New York City, NY. Job Description GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS AND STAKEHOLDER RELATIONS Build and maintain relationships with federal, state, and local policymakers, government officials, trade associations, industry coalitions, and other external stakeholders. LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS AND REGULATORY INTELLIGENCE Monitor, analyze, and communicate developments in U.S. legislation, regulation, political activity, advocacy, and media that may affect Red Bull, its partners, customers, consumers, or the beverage category. POLICY STRATEGY AND ISSUES MANAGEMENT Develop, own and communicate Red Bull’s policy positions, strategic priorities, and practical solutions; assess risks and opportunities; and recommend appropriate engagement strategies for the U.S. CONSULTANT, COALITION, AND TRADE ASSOCIATION MANAGEMENT Manage political and government affairs consultants, coordinate coalition activity, and represent Red Bull in relevant trade associations and industry groups. INTERNAL ADVISORY AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COORDINATION Provide timely government affairs insights, briefings, talking points, and policy communications to business leaders while coordinating with Science, Regulatory, Legal, Communications, Commercial, and global teams. STRATEGIC ENGAGEMENT AND BUSINESS SUPPORT Engage and represent the company in meetings, hearings, conferences, stakeholder outreach, and other government affairs initiatives that advance Red Bull’s interests, strengthen the company’s reputation, and help mitigate regulatory barriers and risks. COMPLIANCE AND GOVERNANCE Ensure compliance with lobbying, ethics, gift, reporting, and political activity requirements for North American SRGA team. Qualifications 7+ years of experience in government affairs, legislative or congressional offices, regulatory agencies, trade associations, political organizations, public affairs consultancies, federal and state advocacy strategy, or a related field. Strong knowledge of the U.S. federal, state, and local political, legislative, and regulatory landscape. Experience with food, beverage, dietary supplement, caffeine, nutrition, consumer-product, or related policy issues preferred. Demonstrated ability to monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative, regulatory, political, and advocacy developments. Strong stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with policymakers, government officials, trade associations, consultants, coalitions, and industry partners. Experience developing policy positions, briefing materials, talking points, stakeholder maps, and executive recommendations. Experience managing external consultants, coalitions, and trade-association relationships. Strong political judgment, strategic thinking, risk assessment, and issue-management skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues clearly to business and external audiences. Ability to work independently and cross-functionally in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities, and travel as needed. Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, Economics, or a related field. English required, German, French, Spanish or other language a plus. Additional Information This position is open to U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, or individuals who are currently authorized to work in the United States on a valid visa. The base salary range for this position is $120,000 – $180,000 + cash incentives. Actual salary offers may vary based on work experience. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified. Our current Benefits include: Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision Plans, 401k Match, Family Leave, PTO & Paid Holiday Schedule, Pet, Legal, and Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement (Benefits listed may vary depending on the nature of your employment and/or work location). Red Bull North America, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, or any other classification protected by Federal, state, or local law. item.title: Legislative Director
item.description: Legislative Director Organization: AARP Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Job ID 2026-7825 Department Social Impact & Engagement Salary $121,500.00 – $135,000.00 Yearly Overview: AARP is the nation’s largest nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering people 50 and older to choose how they live as they age. With a nationwide presence, AARP strengthens communities and advocates for what matters most to the more than 100 million Americans 50-plus and their families: health and financial security, and personal fulfillment. AARP also works for individuals in the marketplace by sparking new solutions and allowing carefully chosen, high-quality products and services to carry the AARP name. As a trusted source for news and information, AARP produces the nation’s largest-circulation publications, AARP The Magazine and the AARP Bulletin. AARP’s Community, State and National Affairs (CSN) Group includes Government Relations, Programs, Volunteer Engagement, Community Outreach and Advocacy at the federal, state and local levels. It delivers on AARP’s social mission by educating and engaging people 50-plus and their families, strengthening communities, and championing issues that help give people financial and health security. The Legislative Director for Housing, Transportation, and Broadband serves as AARP’s federal lobbyist, leading advocacy efforts to advance policies that help people live where they choose, stay connected to their communities, and thrive as they age. This role ensures that AARP’s housing, transportation, and broadband federal advocacy reflects and supports the organization’s extensive state and local work, translating community priorities and on-the-ground experiences into effective federal legislative and regulatory strategies. You will own and manage an established and emerging portfolio of issues, build and maintain strong relationships with policymakers and stakeholders, and drive policy outcomes that reflect the needs of older Americans. Responsibilities: Serves as a point of contact on a specific portfolio of issues. Interacts with federal and state elected officials and staff members in a lobbyist capacity. Research and identify public policy issues of interest to the organization and prepare summaries and reports on the facts and issues. Analyzes federal and state legislative and regulatory proposals, communicates regularly with state office staff regarding the organization’s policy goals, and contributes to internal and external advocacy materials. Builds strong relationships with members of Congress, federal or state officials, internal and external stakeholders, professional associations, and coalitions to achieve the organization’s public policy agenda. Identifies and recommends opportunities to advance the organization’s priorities. Works closely with colleagues in States, Campaigns, Policy Development, Programs, Office of Inclusive Impact, and other departments across AARP to drive robust and proactive advocacy on their portfolio of issues for Americans 50 and older. Serves as a spokesperson with press and with legislative and non-legislative audiences on a specific portfolio of issues as they relate to older adults to position the organization as a credible source of information on legislative and regulatory issues. Identifies, supervises and works with outside consultants and issue experts to advance the organization’s advocacy agenda. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Law, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 8+ years of progressively responsible federal legislative, agency, or lobbying experience, such as direct lobbying before Members of Congress and congressional staff, serving in a federal agency role, or working in a congressional office as a Legislative Assistant, Legislative Director, committee staff, or in a comparable role. Demonstrated understanding of the connection between federal, state, and local advocacy, with experience translating community-level priorities into effective federal advocacy strategies. Strong understanding of how Congress operates, including legislative strategy, committee processes, timing considerations, political dynamics, and the exercise of sound political judgment. Federal legislative experience, with the ability to adapt quickly across a range of policy areas, strategically navigate changing congressional priorities and emerging policy opportunities, respond effectively to shifting priorities and emerging issues, and a passion for learning new issues. Experience analyzing federal legislation and regulations; drafting and presenting policy materials such as issue briefs, comment letters, testimony, and formal statements; and translating policy analysis into actionable advocacy strategies. Proven ability to work in a non-partisan and inclusive manner, building trust and credibility with diverse stakeholders and facilitating collaboration on complex or sensitive issues. Preferred: Experience supporting or advancing federal legislation related to housing or transportation and the interest in learning broadband and other issues as assigned. AARP will not sponsor an employment visa for this position. Additional Requirements Regular and reliable job attendance. Effective verbal and written communication skills. Exhibit respect and understanding of others to maintain professional relationships. Independent judgement in evaluation options to make sound decisions. In office/open office environment with the ability to work effectively surrounded by moderate noise. Hybrid Work Environment AARP observes Mondays and Fridays as remote workdays, except for essential functions. Remote work can only be done within the United States and its territories. Compensation and Benefits AARP offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including a 401(k); 100% company-funded pension plan; health, dental, and vision plans; life insurance; paid time off to include company and individual holidays, vacation, sick, caregiving, and parental leave; performance-based and peer-based recognition and tuition reimbursement. AARP does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. item.title: Senior Director, Communications
item.description: Senior Director, Communications Organization: Chamber of Progress Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Chamber of Progress is looking for a Senior Director of Communications to lead all aspects of the organization’s aggressive communications strategy. This role will promote the organization’s work on issues related to technology, financial, and civic innovation policy at the federal, state, and local level. This role oversees national and international media relations, litigation communications, broadcast and podcast pitching, our report and polling launches, rapid response, management of our Communications Director, and all aspects of the organization’s public facing communications. This is a critical role at an extremely press-forward organization. Responsibilities Drive the organization’s media and communications strategy Devise creative strategies to inject Chamber of Progress’ views into press coverage and policy debates Conceive of earned media strategies to help us win our top policy campaigns – particularly defeating bad bills and passing good ones Oversee our launch process for policy papers, reports, and polling; maximize earned, paid, and own-channel visibility for launches Supervise Communications Director, who leads our state and local communications, social media, and op-ed writing & pitching program. Serve as primary liaison to journalists covering tech, transportation, crypto, labor, economic policy, politics, and the 2028 presidential campaign Pitch story ideas and interviews to online, print, broadcast, and podcast outlets Write and edit all press statements and social media posts Be the guardian of the organization’s voice and reputation in the media Oversee outside consultants assisting with broadcast & podcast pitching, as well as consultants managing projects Train staff members to speak with media on their areas of expertise Develop and implement a strategy for maintaining and growing the organization’s presence on digital media platforms. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required Senior Director: At least 10 years of post-college work experience Relentlessness – you are the kind of person who never rests on your laurels Prior experience in communications roles in Congress, the Executive Branch, advocacy groups, political campaigns, or PR / public affairs firms Experience pitching and working with journalists Deeply interested in the news Extremely creative Experience creating and driving public affairs campaigns to achieve public policy goals Outstanding writing, editing, and communication skills Fluency with social media platforms and digital tools People management experience is preferred Well-organized and proactive about problem solving Experience with tech and innovation policy is helpful but not required Bias toward action Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines Role is located in Washington, DC. Compensation and Benefits Full-time exempt position, with starting salary and level dependent upon experience level Starting salary between $140,000 – $180,000 annually Chamber of Progress provides an excellent benefits package to all of its full-time employees including: A 401(k) retirement program with 4% employer matching; Employer subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance; 15 days of vacation in the first year of employment; 8 paid holidays per year plus the week between Christmas Eve and New Years Day; 12 weeks of paid parental leave. About Chamber of Progress Chamber of Progress (progresschamber.org) is a new center-left tech policy industry coalition working to help usher in a progressive high-tech future and ensure that all Americans benefit from technological leaps. We’re not just another business group. Everyone knows that a local “chamber of commerce” promotes business and free markets. We’re an industry group, but instead of focusing on commerce, Chamber of Progress is promoting a progressive high-tech society, economy, workforce, and consumer climate. Chamber of Progress supports public policies promoting: – Economic progress, including combatting income inequality; promoting a bigger, modern social safety net; encouraging progressive taxation; and supporting reliable, win-win online marketplaces; – Social progress, including promoting inclusive democracy; supporting bold action against climate change; promoting digital opportunity for all; and advocating for healthy and equitable online communities. – Consumer progress, including promoting the principle that tech should always serve consumers’ interests; “building back better” by investing in communities and regulated innovation; increasing access to goods and information; and balancing consumer and worker concerns. EEO Statement Chamber of Progress is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce at all levels of the organization. We value and encourage the contributions of our employees and strive to create an environment where everyone can reach their full potential. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law. This applies to all aspects of employment, including hiring, transfer, promotion, compensation, eligibility for benefits, and termination. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. item.description: Public Relations Sr Account Exec., Arts & Culture Organization: Anat Gerstein, Inc. Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Anat Gerstein Inc., a full service communications firm serving the nonprofit sector, is seeking an arts and culture communications and public relations professional with five to ten years of relevant experience who will work on collaborative teams in our Arts & Culture practice to: manage accounts; provide strategic communications counsel; and to craft and execute public relations plans that help drive ticket sales, visitation, fundraising, and thought leadership for cultural organizations that include museums, Off-Broadway and regional theaters, multidisciplinary presenters, and arts education providers. We are seeking a creative, results-driven individual who can generate earned and owned stories that move people to action. The ideal candidate is an informed and passionate “news junkie” who excels at writing, story development and ideation, project management, and has experience with traditional and social media. They should have a solid track record of public relations experience in the arts and culture sector—agency and client services experience highly preferred, or experience handling communications in-house at a cultural institution, and relevant press and sector contacts. Client services in the firm’s Arts & Culture practice are primarily strategic communications planning and execution for media relations and social media but can extend to donor communications, advocacy communications, collateral development, and events. JOB REQUIREMENTS Develop and execute multi-channel communications programs for a variety of arts and culture organizations, based on clients’ institutional goals and target audiences. The ideal candidate will become part of each client’s team, always working to guarantee the highest level of service with proactive ideation, responsiveness, and care. JOB QUALIFICATIONS Qualified candidates must possess the following skills and attributes: Demonstrated drive to deliver the highest quality work with clients’ best interests and goals in mind. Motivated and organized self-starter, capable of managing multiple projects and ensuring successful execution. Skilled manager able to supervise a more junior direct report, support peers, and manage up to the practice area’s leadership. Highly collaborative and professionally generous; we work to support one another. Excellent written and oral communications skills. Experience developing and pitching culture stories that result in press coverage, as well as with drafting and securing publication for op-eds, letters, or first person essays. Experience developing engaging and creative social media content or collaborating with marketing and digital teams. Creative thinker who brings ideas, always on the lookout for innovative or clever ways to promote a client, program, or story. Strong multi-tasker able to work under tight deadlines. Excellent relationship and interpersonal communication skills. 5 to 10 years in an arts communications role, ideally working for an agency or cultural nonprofit. Location: New York City, NY | Albany, NY Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Anat Gerstein, Inc. is a full-service communications firm that exclusively works with nonprofit and government organizations that support and enrich communities across New York City and beyond. We are rapidly growing and regularly recognized as one of the top communications firms serving nonprofits and supporting good causes. Our firm and staff have been named a leading nonprofit consultant, a top political PR power company, Crain’s Notable Business and Notable Leader in PR, Communicators of the Year, and more. We are looking for a creative, high-energy, self-starter with experience working on city or state public policy issues through government, political campaigns, advocacy, public affairs, or journalism, along with excellent oral and written communications skills and experience with traditional and social media. Candidates should have a demonstrated interest in government and advocacy, and understand how strategic communications can advance policy goals and influence public debate. This position may be based in either our New York City office or remotely in Albany. Candidates should be able to work from one of these locations on a regular basis. Drafting newsletters, op-eds, testimony for government hearings, website copy, and speeches. Drafting donor and participant communications. Experience working on New York City or New York State policy, advocacy, or political issues is strongly preferred. Creative, strategic thinker, always on the lookout for innovative ways to promote a client, program, or story. Team player willing to support a team of professionals to consistently improve service and outcomes. Strong multitasker who thrives under tight deadlines. Demonstrated understanding of how advocacy campaigns influence public policy through communications, media relations, coalition-building, and engagement with government stakeholders. Values diverse experiences. Outstanding relationship-building and interpersonal communication skills. Strong familiarity with and interest in New York City and New York State news media. item.title: Director of Media Relations and Executive Communications
item.description: Director of Media Relations and Executive Communications Organization: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 POSITION SUMMARY Reporting to the Vice President for Global Communications, the Director is responsible for helping craft and execute communications strategy for the Council’s president. In collaboration with the Executive Office, the Director will develop proactive plans to elevate the profile and voice of CFR’s president as the lead “brand ambassador” of the Council to further its mission as a non-partisan source of independent analysis and research. This includes working on earned media opportunities, social media presence and engagement, and written content (including weekly newsletters, opinion essays, and long-form articles). The Director will also seek to expand and deepen the range of media targets and audiences and incorporate social media activity to further the president’s engagement and voice. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC office at least three days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Effective Monday, September 14, 2026, CFR employees will be based on-site at least four days per week. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Work with the VP for Global Communications and the President’s office to develop and execute a proactive strategy for the president’s media engagement on a wide range of geopolitical and geoeconomic issues. This includes: Mapping opportunities based on the president’s thought leadership as well as external moments on the global security calendar. Building and maintaining relationships across a wide range of media outlets. Identifying innovative ways to engage media, including through partnerships, collaborations, and events. Drafting briefing memos, talking points, and Q&A, as well as potential op-eds and newsletter content. Work with the VP, the Executive Office, and the Digital audience strategy team to develop and expand the president’s profile on social media, taking advantage of video, photos, and live events to generate compelling content in the president’s voice. Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree in a related field. A minimum of 7-10 years of relevant experience in media relations and public affairs, preferably supporting and leading similar strategic and crisis communications efforts for institutional principals. Familiarity with the foreign policy media ecosystem and contacts with national and international media outlets. Experience using media tracking tools and databases such as MuckRack, Cision, Critical Mention, TV Eyes, and/or Meltwater. Related Skills & Other Requirements Superior writing, verbal, and digital communications skills. Strong working knowledge of media relations and issues management. Strong judgment in media relations matters. Demonstrated ability to effectively engage with reporters, editors, columnists, producers, and bookers. Track record drafting statements, talking points & Q&As. Comfortable working in a digital environment using digital tools, including website content management systems. Comfortable providing counsel to senior executives. Self-starter and strategic thinker with the ability to prioritize and synthesize. Strong collaborator with solid negotiation and stakeholder management skills. Proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced, results-oriented, collaborative environment. Able to work under pressure quickly, effectively, and efficiently. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position here . Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $145,000 – $155,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. item.description: Communications Specialist Organization: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 POSITION SUMMARY The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is seeking a Communications Specialist to support the planning and execution of earned media strategies for CFR’s Studies department, helping to advance the visibility of their work. Reporting to the Associate Vice President, this role will draft and edit press releases, media advisories, and targeted pitches; develops resource materials for journalists, editors, producers, and bookers; and maintains press distribution lists and media mention tracking. The Communications Specialist contributes to the full range of team operations such as staffing events, supporting virtual media briefings on breaking news, monitoring the communications inbox, and assisting with intern recruitment and supervision. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC office at least three days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Effective Monday, September 14, 2026, CFR employees will be based on-site at least four days per week. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Support planning and execution of earned media strategies in support of CFR scholarship, specifically the work of CFR fellows and the Studies Department as a whole. This includes engaging fellows in D.C. and coordinating with counterparts in Meetings, Publications, and Events. Under the guidance of the D.C.-based AVP and in collaboration with the Senior Specialist and colleagues across the team, help promote Studies products (such as CFR books and reports) and announcements (for example, of events and new fellows and initiatives), including through the drafting and editing of news releases and media advisories. In coordination with the Senior Specialist, engage Research Assistants to help track fellows’ availability and media appearances, update expert pages, and maintain a running catalog of media mentions. Work with the Senior Specialist and AVP to map media targets based on issues and audiences. Help craft resource guides and materials for media targets (reporters, editors, columnists, bookers, producers) with CFR content, fellows profiles, and other collateral to position CFR as a resource consistently and during key news cycle moments. Alongside other members of the team: Staff DC-based events and book photography Add media mentions for the weekly report for Leadership Help update media highlights on CFR.org Help monitor and act on media inquiries in the Comms inbox Assist with onboarding new members of the comms team Help manage DC-based events and help book photography Help interview, select, and supervise DC-based interns Take turns with team members to organize and manage virtual media briefings on fast-breaking global news Compile and update press distro lists covering various topics/regions Draft and send targeted media pitches for events, publications, and initiatives Draft and send press notes, press releases, and media advisories Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent At least 2 years of related experience in media relations, communications, media industry, or journalism. Previous experience working with monitoring databases and engagement tools (e.g., Muck Rack, Cision/PR Newswire, Meltwater). Previous experience working with CRMs and ESPs. Related Skills & Other Requirements Excellent writing and editing skills and experience writing news releases and copy editing. Proven knowledge of and demonstrated interest in current U.S. foreign policy and international affairs. Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in a fast-paced team environment. Strong working knowledge of international issues and familiarity with media landscape. Candidates must be proactive, organized, and able to excel in a deadline-driven environment. Candidates must have the ability and willingness to work flexible hours when necessary. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position here. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $63,000 – $70,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations.
