item.title: Associate Director, Local Journalists Initative
item.description: Associate Director, Local Journalists Initative Organization: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Position Summary CFR Outreach works to raise the profile of CFR and develop relationships with communities across the United States. Current initiatives focus on college and university students, educators, and administrators; state and local officials; local journalists; and congregational leaders and representatives of faith-based organizations. Working with the vice president, senior director of the National Program and Outreach department, and the director of Outreach, the associate director is the lead staffer for the Local Journalists Initiative, which helps print, broadcast, and digital-first journalists across the country draw connections between the local issues they cover and national and international dynamics. This position will manage the day-to-day workflow of the initiative and one support staffer, while also supporting programming across the National & Outreach department. The associate director will also work closely with CFR’s Global Communications team on local media strategy, which will include how the Council’s scholarship can help drive local news coverage and commentary, and how such local engagement can bolster CFR’s reputation and standing proactively with key stakeholders more broadly. The Local Journalists Initiative provides a forum for journalists at local outlets across the country to engage with CFR experts, other thought leaders, and a network of peers on a range of issues at the nexus of the global and the local, while also sharing best practices for grounding local reporting in global context. The initiative strives to disseminate CFR analysis to inform reporting and to foster dialogue among its constituent network of journalists. Outreach is conducted through events and programming (including webinars, briefings, and workshops), public-facing digital content (such as email campaigns and newsletters), conference participation nationally, and more. This position is based in CFR’s New York office at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Lead the CFR Local Journalists Initiative and its virtual and in-person programmatic offerings, which include a webinar series, media briefings, CFR’s annual Local Journalists Workshop, the CFR Local Journalism Boot Camp for young journalists, and CFR representation at external conferences and professional gatherings across the country. Frame event agendas and generating speaker/topic ideas for virtual and in-person events. Take a lead role on the scheduling and implementation of events—including managing contracts and catering when applicable; drafting, editing, and managing correspondence; preparing meeting materials; and writing summary reports. Oversee day-to-day workflow for the initiative and one support staffer. Monitor, report, and advise on the Local Journalists Initiative budget. Collaborate with the vice president, senior director, and director of Outreach on Local Journalists Initiative programmatic and outreach strategy, efforts, and innovation. Work closely with CFR’s Global Communications team on local media strategy to include development of a nationwide map of media targets based on issues, engagement potential, government relations needs, and CFR Studies Program priorities. Research and identify partnership opportunities and external conferences to attend, schedule meetings, and write meeting recap notes. Grow CFR’s Outreach community and expand its impact through audience development by identifying and building relationships with new and diverse contacts in local journalism outlets across the country. Overseeing the creation of a bi-monthly newsletter for journalists featuring a curated selection of CFR content. Contribute to communications and resource dissemination efforts by maintaining webpages, conducting email campaigns, placing advertisements, and managing a new LinkedIn group for past participants of the Local Journalists Workshop. Track metrics and conducting qualitative and quantitative analysis across program offerings for reporting purposes and as a basis for strategic decision-making. Manage event records in CRM, running advanced queries, and maintaining clean contact records. Collaborate with staff in other departments—particularly Global Communications—as well as with external partner organizations on coordinating schedules, organize events, and share information relevant to various crosscutting projects. Provide general project support for institutional projects as well as for the department, including attending and working at National Program and Outreach events held outside of business hours Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education and Experience BA in international relations, journalism, or related field and proven interest in current U.S. foreign policy and international affairs issues. MA preferred. Five or more years of experience working in outreach, strategic partnerships, international relations, government, or community engagement. Nuanced and deep understanding of the journalism landscape across the country at a local level required. Event or program management experience preferred. Related Skills & Other Requirements Ability to multitask and manage multiple ongoing projects simultaneously; superior organizational and time management skills, as well as attention to detail. Excellent verbal and written communication skills to communicate effectively with multiple audiences; strong writing, proofreading, and editing skills. Ability to meet demanding deadlines with a positive attitude and interact with members and the public in a professional manner. Team player with capacity to take initiative, demonstrate flexibility, and work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Experience working with high-level contacts or in member relations; ability to maintain confidentiality and to use appropriate discretion. Microsoft Word and Excel skills. Microsoft Dynamics CRM or other database experience preferred, and the aptitude to learn and utilize different technologies. Availability to work flexible hours and overtime, as necessary. Ability to travel several times each year. Ability to assist with packing boxes/materials for shipping and physically setting out meeting materials for workshops and conferences. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position here . Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $85,000 – $95,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. item.title: Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Organization: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/15/2026 Position Summary CFR’s Government Affairs operation is focused on actively engaging members of Congress and their staff, executive branch officials, and Washington, DC-based diplomats to provide timely, relevant, and useful analysis to further inform policymaking. Through discussion and examination of the critical challenges facing the United States and the international community, the program seeks to serve as both a direct resource and convener of leading thinkers and practitioners in a nonpartisan forum. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Help craft and set strategy for outreach to members of Congress and congressional staff in innovative and policy relevant ways. Maintain a professional network on Capitol Hill and leverage that network to advance institutional priorities. Moderate and oversee some program events, roundtables, and briefings for policymakers and their staff. Coordinate private consultations for members of Congress and their staff to ensure CFR expertise and products are incorporated into the policymaking process. Develop and implement unique and custom outreach strategies for CFR initiatives and other bespoke institutional priorities. Invite and oversee relationships with outside experts participating in CFR programming. Develop strong working relationships with CFR fellows to promote their expertise and scholarship. Track international affairs developments on Capitol Hill. Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education and Experience 8+ years of related experience, with event planning experience required. Bachelor’s degree in international relations, government, public policy, or other related field is required; master’s degree preferred. Congressional or government relations experience required. Related Skills & Other Requirements Strong judgement, discretion, and strategic instincts to operate in high-level, dynamic, and confidential environment. Established relationships across significant segment of House or Senate environment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including with senior principles. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to multi-task and problem solve independently. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment both independently and on a team. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position here . Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $145,000 – $155,000, depending on experience. item.title: Director of Policy & Coalition Building
item.description: Director of Policy & Coalition Building Organization: Public Counsel Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 10/15/2026 JOB TITLE Director of Policy & Coalition Building JOB TYPE Exempt/non-bargaining DEPARTMENT Policy REPORTING TO Vice President, Chief Advocacy Officer GRANT FUNDED POSITION No SALARY RANGE OR HOURLY RATE $135,000–$165,000 ABOUT PUBLIC COUNSEL Public Counsel is a nonprofit public interest law firm dedicated to advancing civil rights and racial and economic justice, as well as to amplifying the power of our clients through comprehensive legal advocacy. Founded on and strengthened by a pro bono legal service model, our staff and volunteers seek justice through direct legal services, promote healthy and resilient communities through education and outreach, and support community-led efforts to transform unjust systems through litigation and policy advocacy in and beyond Los Angeles. Public Counsel organizes its work through seven legal teams: Child, Youth & Family Advocacy, Community Development, Consumer Rights & Economic Justice, Homelessness Prevention, Immigrants’ Rights, Education Equity, and our impact litigation team, Opportunity Under Law. Public Counsel has a staff of approximately 170. We are committed to building a diverse staff and encourage applications from people of color, people with disabilities, and people of all gender identities, gender expressions, and sexualities. We recognize the essential role of staff in achieving our goals, and we have set a long-term intention to provide competitive compensation, benefits, training, mentorship, and overall workplace wellness, making Public Counsel a leader among nonprofit law firms. POSITION OVERVIEW Reporting to the Vice President, Chief Advocacy Officer, the Director of Policy & Coalition Building provides strategic leadership for Public Counsel’s policy advocacy and coalition-building efforts across the organization. The Director works closely with program leaders and staff to identify policy priorities, strengthen coordination of existing policy work, and develop systems that enable Public Counsel to leverage its expertise and resources effectively. The Director builds and maintains relationships with community organizations, coalitions, policymakers, and other partners; provides guidance and technical assistance on policy advocacy; and helps connect policy work with Public Counsel’s direct services and impact litigation efforts. The Director also works collaboratively with the Directors of Litigation and Pro Bono, the Communications and Development teams, and other organizational leaders to advance Public Counsel’s policy goals and visibility. The ideal candidate is a strategic, collaborative, and highly organized leader who brings strong policy expertise, relationship-building skills, and a commitment to client- and community-centered advocacy. ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES Strategic Policy Leadership & Internal Organization Develop and advance a coordinated organizational approach to policy advocacy that supports Public Counsel’s mission, advances systems change, and amplifies the expertise of legal teams and staff Assess and organize Public Counsel’s existing policy work, identify opportunities for coordination and joint advocacy, and establish systems for tracking, sharing, and reporting policy activity and outcomes Work with legal team leaders and staff to identify policy priorities and develop strategies that leverage Public Counsel’s expertise and resources Develop and maintain internal guidelines, tools, and resources for policy advocacy, including processes for developing organizational positions and addressing compliance, lobbying, and disclosure requirements Convene and facilitate cross-team policy working groups and other fora to promote information-sharing, collaboration, and coordinated advocacy Advise organizational leadership and staff on policy strategy, including how policy advocacy can complement and strengthen direct services and strategic litigation Coalition, Community & Government Relations Build and maintain strong relationships with grassroots organizations, community leaders, coalition partners, policymakers, government officials and staff Advance a community-centered model of coalition building and advocacy that supports community-led policy initiatives and incorporates partner priorities into Public Counsel’s policy strategies Identify and cultivate opportunities for Public Counsel to participate in, lead, or support coalitions and policy campaigns consistent with organizational priorities Provide guidance and support to Public Counsel staff in developing and maintaining external policy relationships and navigating political and coalition dynamics Represent Public Counsel’s policy priorities with policymakers, coalition partners, community organizations, funders, media, and other external audiences Build relationships with pro bono, academic, and other partners to bring additional expertise and capacity to Public Counsel’s policy advocacy Policy Development, Advocacy & Analysis Provide technical assistance to staff in identifying policy opportunities, developing policy proposals, and crafting legislative and administrative advocacy strategies Monitor and analyze relevant federal, state, and local legislation, regulations, and policy developments and help assess their implications for Public Counsel’s clients, communities, and policy priorities Support the development of legislation, policy proposals, comment letters, testimony, public comments, policy briefs, and other advocacy materials Work with staff and coalition partners to develop and advance policy campaigns, including strategies for legislative, administrative, and other policy advocacy Help ensure that Public Counsel’s policy positions are coordinated, consistent with organizational priorities, and informed by client and community perspectives Partner with the Communications team to translate complex policy issues into clear, accessible messages and elevate the visibility and impact of Public Counsel’s policy advocacy Organizational Capacity Building & External Engagement Identify policy-related training and capacity-building needs across the organization and develop or facilitate training, mentorship, and other resources to strengthen staff policy advocacy skills Develop and improve systems, tools, and processes that make policy advocacy more efficient, coordinated, and accessible to staff across Public Counsel Work with organizational leadership and the Development team to identify funding opportunities and strengthen grants and external visibility Represent Public Counsel at conferences, panels, community forums, meetings with elected officials, and other public and professional settings Contribute to organizational leadership and agency-wide initiatives, including efforts to advance equity, inclusion, racial and economic justice, and community-centered advocacy ESSENTIAL JOB SKILLS AND ABILITIES Bachelor’s degree, with an advanced degree in public policy, law, public administration, communications, or a related field preferred At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in policy advocacy, legislative affairs, government relations, coalition building, public affairs, community organizing, or a related field, with substantial experience leading policy initiatives Significant experience maintaining strong, trusting relationships with community organizations, grassroots advocates, coalitions, elected officials, legislative staff, and other external stakeholders Strong organizational item.title: Director of Communications
item.description: Director of Communications Organization: Health and Reentry Project Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/16/2026 About the Health and Reentry Project (HARP) Access to health care is vital for successful second chances, yet many people returning to communities after incarceration cannot get needed care because the system serving them is fragmented and inefficient. The Health and Reentry Project (HARP) is a dynamic national nonprofit organization that builds safer, healthier communities by improving access to health care for people leaving incarceration. HARP brings together diverse stakeholders, including law enforcement, corrections, and health care leaders; community-based organizations and advocates; and people directly impacted by the justice system to drive collective progress. The Opportunity HARP is seeking a Director of Communications to develop and execute a proactive communications strategy for the organization. HARP is growing rapidly and needs a communications leader who can scale our strategy to match. The ideal candidate will craft clear and compelling communications that resonate across a wide range of perspectives and strengthen HARP’s position as the go-to resource in the health and reentry policy space. This new position reports to HARP’s Executive Director and is part of the senior leadership team. Responsibilities Strategy and Leadership Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Executive Director on external positioning, branding, and narrative framing. Develop and execute a communications plan and supporting calendar aligned with HARP’s mission and strategic priorities, and evaluate and update it regularly. Build and maintain HARP’s organizational voice, messaging, and visual identity across all platforms to advance HARP’s visibility and brand. Marketing Create compelling materials that clearly communicate HARP’s value to a wide range of audiences, including policymakers, state and federal agencies, local officials, advocates, stakeholders, and the public. Develop and implement a comprehensive marketing strategy for HARP’s new State Technical Assistance Center (STAC) and other core areas of work. Communications Methods and Execution Enhance and manage HARP’s product development process from conception to publication, including oversight of external contractors and design vendors. Write and edit content across channels, including social media posts, newsletters, blogs, op-eds, and press releases. Expand HARP’s digital presence, including the website, social media, and email communications; manage relationships with web and design contractors. Track and report on digital performance metrics to continuously improve reach and engagement. Support rapid-response communications around relevant policy developments and breaking news. Develop and maintain an editorial calendar that amplifies HARP’s publications, policy work, and stakeholder engagement. Build and maintain HARP’s media list; support HARP leadership and staff in direct engagement with reporters, managing external PR resources and relationships as needed. Preferred Qualifications/Experience Minimum of 10 years of experience in communications, with a track record in policy, nonprofit, membership association, consulting, or government settings. Bachelor’s degree required. Clear track record of developing and executing high-impact communications strategies. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly to diverse audiences. Demonstrated leadership experience, including launching or establishing communications processes, such as workflows, templates, and shared standards, in a collaborative, results-oriented culture. Experience with digital communications tools, content management systems, social media, and basic performance analytics. Exceptional strategic thinking capabilities with a builder mindset; a proven ability to translate vision into concrete, scalable operational plans while spotting opportunities for replicability and increased impact. A collaborative leader and team player willing to roll up their sleeves. A foundational learning orientation characterized by intellectual humility and curiosity; a leader who actively seeks diverse perspectives, values feedback, and thrives in a dynamic “learning while doing” environment. Comfort operating in a nonpartisan environment that bridges multiple sectors and perspectives. Experience managing external contractors and vendors. Familiarity with health policy, criminal justice, or related fields, or the curiosity and skill to quickly learn complex policy issues. HARP is a small but growing team that values team members who: Are organized, detail-oriented, results-focused, and thrive in a work culture that prioritizes growth and learning. Maintain good humor and a positive attitude while juggling multiple priorities and meeting deadlines. Express ideas clearly and concisely, both in writing and orally. Are self-motivated and able to work independently on a small team in a remote or hybrid work environment. Are committed to creating an inclusive environment that values sharing and learning from diverse perspectives and experiences. Location Remote within the continental United States. Compensation & Benefits The salary range is $120,000–$160,000, commensurate with experience, and may be adjusted based on the candidate’s location. HARP offers a competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, a 401(k), and more. Please apply through LinkedIn or HARP’s application portal . Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Policy Manager
item.description: Policy Manager Organization: Alliance of Community Health Plans (ACHP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 About the job REPORTS TO: Vice President, Policy LOCATION: Washington, D.C. COMPENSATION: $65,000 – $85,000 WHO WE ARE The Alliance of Community Health Plans (ACHP) represents the nation’s top-performing non-profit health organizations to improve affordability and outcomes in health care. ACHP member organizations embrace a unique partnership model in health care, bringing together health plans and providers on behalf of the patients and communities they serve. ACHP advocates on behalf of its members, highlighting tested solutions impacting communities nationwide and a proven approach that delivers better value for patients, employers and taxpayers. ACHP is committed to a diverse workforce that respects all points of view. We encourage different perspectives, identities and backgrounds, regardless of job function, to create a more resilient organization that supports a strong, equitable health industry. We foster this by encouraging openness and transparency that creates opportunities for all. POSITION SUMMARY The Manager, Policy, is a valued member of the ACHP Federal Affairs team, focused on public policies such as Digital Transformation, AI, Duals and Medicare. This individual has deepening knowledge in federal policy affecting the health insurance industry, particularly regional health plans, and other stakeholders. The Manager partners with senior management, other federal affairs team members, member plan government relations leaders and subject matter experts to develop and implement a robust policy agenda. This role affords excellent career growth opportunities. Successful candidates are self-starters, flexible, collaborative and committed to ACHP’s mission promoting non-profit, high-quality, payer-provider organizations. This individual thrives in fast-paced, high-energy environments that reward initiative and creativity. All strong candidates must have experience responsibly using AI tools, including verifying accuracy and authenticity of information. CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Policy Tracking, Analysis and Development (50%) Build expertise in assigned policy areas and advance policy initiatives from analysis through recommendations and implementation. Lead or support member company workgroups to identify shared priorities, build consensus and develop actionable policy recommendations and responses. Anticipate, monitor and assess legislative and regulatory developments; support translating implications for member companies. Gather member company data and operational examples to demonstrate the impact of policy proposals and the value of regional, nonprofit health plans. Partner with Market Competitiveness and Clinical Innovation colleagues to develop evidence-based policy insights that demonstrate and advance the distinct value of ACHP member companies. Policy Communications (30%) Translate complex policy issues into clear, concise and compelling materials tailored to member executives, policymakers and other audiences. Develop and deliver presentations and briefings that explain policy implications, articulate ACHP’s priorities and recommend action. Draft persuasive, analytically rigorous comment letters, issue briefs, talking points and proposed legislative and regulatory language. Partner with Communications colleagues to translate policy analysis and member experiences into advocacy materials, member newsletters, publications and external messaging. Ensure policy communications are accurate, timely and consistent with ACHP’s positions and strategic objectives. Relationship Building and Strategic Engagement (20%) Cultivate strong relationships with member company leaders and subject matter experts to inform ACHP’s priorities and advance its legislative and regulatory agenda. Support relationships with Administration officials, think tanks, associations and other health care stakeholders to expand ACHP’s influence and identify opportunities for collaboration. Equip senior leadership with timely analysis and briefing materials to support effective engagement. Coordinate with advocacy colleagues to align policy recommendations with congressional engagement and advocacy opportunities. Other duties as assigned. PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND OTHER QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree. 2-3 years of experience in public policy, health advocacy or health sector; or relevant graduate degree. Working knowledge of federal health policy and the legislative and regulatory processes, with experience engaging in the Washington policy environment. Demonstrated ability to research and analyze complex policy issues, assess implications for health plans and develop clear recommendations with guidance from senior colleagues. Experience managing assigned projects, meeting deadlines and coordinating input from colleagues or external stakeholders. Confidence deploying AI in safe, secure manner to enhance the work product, generate efficiency and strengthen ACHP’s knowledge base. Strong writing and presentation skills, including the ability to translate technical information for diverse audiences. Practical AI fluency. Experience using AI tools to support research, tracking and development of policy materials. Ability to build productive relationships with member company representatives, policymakers and health care stakeholders. Proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and professional communications platforms such as LinkedIn. WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS Work is in a hybrid office environment, with three in-office days per week. Must reside in the DMV area. Position is hybrid but not remote. Some travel required. APPLICATION PROCESS Please send your resume and cover letter to ACHP Human Resources at [email protected] . Include ‘Manager, Policy’ followed by your first initial and last name in the subject line of your email. item.title: Policy Entrepreneurship, Manager/Senior Manager
item.description: Policy Entrepreneurship, Manager/Senior Manager Organization: Federation of American Scientists (FAS) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Why FAS? The Federation of American Scientists (FAS) takes seriously our role as a beacon and voice for the science community. FAS has a rich history: after the devastating bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, a group of atomic researchers — deeply concerned about the use of science for malice — created an organization committed to using science and technology to benefit humanity. The group they created — the Federation of Atomic Scientists — soon became the Federation of American Scientists in recognition of the hundreds of scientists across diverse disciplines who joined together to speak with one voice for the betterment of the world. Today, we are a group of entrepreneurial, intrepid changemakers, forging a better future for all through the nexus of science, technology and talent. We value equity, inclusion, and transparency. As a collective, we are building an organization focused on being impact-driven, customer-focused, and growth-oriented as a force for good in the world. The Role FAS is entering a pivotal moment. Science and technology institutions are under unprecedented pressure, and the need for evidence-based, nonpartisan policy leadership has never been more urgent. FAS is responding by deepening its practice of policy entrepreneurship (PE), the discipline of moving ideas into action through strategic engagement with the people and windows that drive change. The Policy Entrepreneurship Manager or Senior Manager will work at the intersection of science policy, government affairs, and organizational execution – with a particular focus on catalyzing reform of the R&D enterprise using that to learn from how research is planned, funded, evaluated, and communicated. This role is in one of FAS’s most active and highest-leverage portfolios and will be expected to manage research projects and relationships with executive and legislative branch decision-makers, sense policy windows, draft policy products, and support the broader team’s PE infrastructure. This is a role for someone who is detail oriented, energized by fast-moving environments, and has experience and/or domain expertise in the science of institutional design, function of science, and/or metascience. The incumbent must be comfortable working collaboratively and through ambiguity, and be deeply motivated by getting good ideas into government. Working across several time-sensitive projects this position will have opportunities to work directly with senior leaders in FAS such as CEO, Director of Policy Entrepreneurship (PE), and/or Director of Government Affairs (GA), and will be a key contributor to the Day One Community. The role will report to the Director of Fellowships and Products. This role may be filled at the Manager or Senior Manager level, depending on the candidate’s experience and qualifications. What You’ll Do Actively Drive Policy Projects Track, manage, and advance priority projects across FAS’s PE portfolio with clear accountability for next steps, relationships, and timelines including work such as envisioning the future of NSF, building federal R&D performance metrics, and learning from the incorporation of AI into science and research systems. Support project leads (such as the CEO, PE Director, and/or GA Director) in preparing for and following up on high-stakes meetings with congressional staff and executive branch officials (such as OMB, OSTP, NSF, DOE, NIH). Manage select timebound projects as they are stood up using agile-based approaches. Draft, refine, and coordinate feedback on policy memos, briefs, and other materials that translate complex S&T ideas into actionable recommendations for specific policy customers. Contribute to the FAS’s rapid response capacity by identifying and pursuing emerging policy windows of opportunity to help mobilize FAS’s quick and effective response. Manage and Deepen Relationships Represent FAS in meetings with executive and legislative branch policymakers in Washington, DC, serving as a trusted and credible interlocutor. Help expand and maintain FAS’s network of collaborators, policy customers, congressional staff, agency officials, and external partners. Contribute to demand sensing by continuously monitoring policy signals, RFIs, legislative calendars, and budget windows to surface timely opportunities for FAS engagement. Skills and Expertise: Must Haves This is a demanding role at the intersection of policy, relationships, and organizational execution. The right candidate will bring: A Hire at the Manager Level: Skills Strong written communication: able to draft concise, persuasive policy memos and briefs with clarity and credibility. Relationship management: able to build trust quickly with senior government officials and manage ongoing stakeholder relationships with professionalism and judgment. Project management: able to track multiple active projects simultaneously, surface blockers, and keep things moving without needing to be told. Political and institutional savvy: understands how the executive and legislative branches work, how policy windows open and close, and how to read a room. Collaboration and agility: thrives in fast-moving, matrixed environments; comfortable pivoting when priorities shift; brings energy and ownership to cross-functional work. Expertise At least 5 years of experience in science policy, government affairs, legislative strategy, or a closely related field. Direct experience engaging with executive branch agencies and officials (NSF, DOE, NIH, OMB, OSTP, or similar) and/or congressional staff on S&T issues. Demonstrated ability to produce policy-relevant written products (memos, briefs, analysis) that have reached and influenced real decision-makers. Ability to rapidly come up to speed on technical issues or domain areas that may be unfamiliar and translate findings into practical policy recommendations. Familiarity with federal science funding, research enterprise policy, metascience, and/or technology governance is strongly preferred. Experience in a policy entrepreneurship, rapid-response, or advocacy environment where speed, judgment, and strategic communication are core to the work. A Hire at the Senior Manager Level: Skills Strategic judgement: able to identify policy opportunities, assess tradeoffs, and set priorities across multiple initiatives with limited oversight. Communication and influence: able to translate complex issues into persuasive recommendations, tailor messaging to direct audiences, and build alignment among stakeholders with competing perspectives. Project leadership and collaboration: able to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives, coordinate subject matter expertise, and adopt plans as policy conditions and priorities change. Political and institutional savvy: able to anticipate evolving executive and legislative development, advise on policy opportunities and risks, and independently shape engagement strategies that advance policy objectives. Expertise At least 8 years of relevant experience leading in science policy, government affairs, legislative strategy, or a closely related field Demonstrated ability to independently manage strategic relationships (NSF, DOE, NIH, OMB, OSTP, or similar) with executive branch officials and or congressional staff to advance science and technology policy objectives. Proven ability to translate complex or unfamiliar issues into actionable policy recommendations, lead the development of influential written products, and exercise sound judgement in rapidly changing policy environments. Experience in federal science funding, research enterprise policy, metascience, and/or technology governance is strongly preferred. Experience in a policy entrepreneurship, rapid-response, or advocacy environment where speed, judgment, and strategic communication are core to the work. To Sum It Up You are a science policy practitioner who is as comfortable in a meeting with a Senate staffer as you are drafting a memo to hit a policy window. You bring sharp political instincts, credible relationships, and a genuine commitment to using science and technology to benefit people. You want to work somewhere that takes policy entrepreneurship seriously as a discipline and you’re ready to help FAS make that vision real. Work Environment This position will be a hybrid role based in Washington DC, meaning that both remote and in-person work can be accommodated, generally two to three days per week on-site at FAS offices, and two to three days per week remote. For this role, much of the work will be relationship building and meeting with federal government officials within Washington, DC. Regular in-person presence in DC is expected. This body of work is a high priority for FAS now and in the coming years. This position is a twelve month termed role with an opportunity for extension if additional funding is available. This position is included in a union-represented collective bargaining unit, and specific terms and conditions of employment are subject to collective bargaining. Salary Range The salary range for this role is $95,000 – $105,000 for the Senior Manager level and is $80,000 – $90,000 for the Manager level, commensurate with experience. Hiring Statement Don’t check off every box? Apply anyway! Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every listed qualification. At FAS we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and developing new voices. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to apply anyway — you might just be the right candidate. The Federation of American Scientists is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender

item.title: Legislative Affairs & Congressional Correspondence Analyst
item.description: Legislative Affairs & Congressional Correspondence Analyst Organization: Nakupuna Companies Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 About the job Overview Nakupuna Companies is looking for a Legislative Affairs and Congressional Correspondence Analyst to support a client of the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW). The ideal candidate is an expert communicator and able to work with and directly support senior executives in the Department of War (DoW). Responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons. Provide congressional affairs support to program leadership for engagements with Congressional members and their staff. Prepare draft minutes and/or verbal reports of conferences and meetings. Prepare, produce, and provide briefings and presentation materials for senior leadership. Maintain a comprehensive record of materials provided to Congress for reference and purposes of consistency. Draft responses to congressionally related internal DOW requests in preparation for interaction with Congress. Provide policy analysis in support of program offices. Review the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and advise on potential impact to program offices. Author legislative proposals and testimonials for congressional hearings in collaboration with program offices. Monitor, track and manage responses to Congressional inquiries. Coordinate with related offices to ensure complete, accurate, and timely responses. Create and edit articles, news releases, fact sheets, talking points and other written content to stimulate internal and external interest in command accomplishments and enhance understanding of the command, its workforce and mission. Participate in regular meetings (in-person and virtual) to stay abreast of organizational accomplishments and to keep the organization informed of current and upcoming public relations activities. Qualifications Skills/Qualifications: T he ideal candidate will be familiar with and have experience with the following technical knowledge, skills, and abilities: Demonstrated experience in congressional and legislative affairs. Familiarity with Capitol Hill and congressional hearings. Excellent writing skills. Effective communication and problem-solving skills. Must possess strong organizational skills and great attention to detail. Takes initiative and exercises personal accountability for achieving high quality outcomes. Responds promptly to customer needs. Excellent Microsoft Office skills. Experience with CATMS and other DoW systems is preferred. Education and Experience: 5-10 or more years of relevant experience and Bachelor’s degree required. A Master’s degree is preferred. Location: Work is performed on Government site at the Pentagon five days a week. Clearance: This position requires a Secret security clearance. Must be a U.S. citizen. Physical Requirements: The ideal candidate must at a minimum be able to meet the following physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation: Ability to perform repetitive motions with the hands, wrists, and fingers. Ability to engage in and follow audible communications in emergency situations. Ability to sit for prolonged periods at a desk and working on a computer. The Nakupuna Companies use a market-based compensation strategy to ensure that our employees are compensated within applicable market ranges commensurate with multiple factors, including but not limited to the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability, organizational requirements, and position location. The projected compensation range for this position is $120,000 to $145,000 (annualized USD). The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Nakupuna Companies’ total compensation package for employees. item.title: Vice President, CIB Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Vice President, CIB Regulatory Affairs Organization: JPMorgan Chase Location: Washington, DC | New York, NY Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Base Pay/Salary Washington,DC $142,500.00-$220,000.00; New York,NY $142,500.00-$220,000.00 Job Description Are you ready to shape the future of market structure regulatory policy at one of the world’s leading financial institutions? Join us as a Vice President to drive impactful public policy strategies and represent the firm’s interests before key governmental agencies. This is a unique opportunity to join a dynamic team, engage with senior management, and shape the regulatory landscape to drive market resilience, liquidity and efficiency. Your expertise will help advance our policy priorities and strengthen our relationships with critical stakeholders. Job Summary As a Vice President with the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB) Regulatory Affairs team, you will contribute to the development and execution of regulatory strategies that support our CIB businesses, with a focus on our Markets franchise. You will engage with multiple internal business units, support critical internal and external relationships, and help shape the firm’s regulatory policy priorities. Your contributions will drive meaningful outcomes for our business, our clients, and the communities we serve. Job Responsibilities Support the CIB Regulatory Affairs team, contributing to strategic direction and driving execution of regulatory and public policy initiatives. Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance the firm’s policy priorities with US regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. Build and maintain strong relationships with CIB stakeholders, ensuring alignment on regulatory objectives and priorities. Manage and deepen relationships with US regulators, policymakers, and industry groups, representing the firm in external meetings and discussions. Prepare and deliver comprehensive briefing materials, including memos and presentations, for senior management. Coordinate with corporate and business partners to develop regulatory policy positions, with a focus on our CIB franchise, including Markets and Securities Services. Lead and direct cross-functional project teams, ensuring successful project completion and effective communication. Ensure timely and effective communication of the firm’s regulatory policy positions through written responses, meetings, and public forums. Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on the firm’s business and strategy. Contribute to a collaborative and inclusive team culture, promoting professional growth and high performance. Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills Bachelor’s degree required. 6 – 8 years of relevant experience in a policy and/or government role, or in a policy/government adjacent business role. Demonstrated experience driving public policy priorities at a trade association, corporation, or governmental entity. Proven ability to build and manage relationships with senior management, regulators, and industry stakeholders. Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts and strategies clearly. Strong organizational and project management skills, with high attention to detail and follow-through. Analytical and independent problem-solving skills, with sound judgment and collaborative decision-making abilities. Experience preparing and presenting materials for senior executives. Positive self-starter with excellent time management and prioritization skills. Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills Deep understanding of US securities market regulatory policy issues. Experience working directly with US financial regulators or in a government affairs capacity. Familiarity with the legislative and regulatory process affecting financial services. Experience with high-impact advocacy campaigns or regulatory initiatives. Professional qualifications from reputable training institutes or professional bodies. Advanced degree in public policy, law, finance, business, or a related field. About Us JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world’s most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management. We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process. We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants’ and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation. JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans About the Team Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we’re setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success. ​The Corporate Responsibility (CR) department mission is to advance a stronger, more durable and safe financial system and an inclusive economy and society for clients, customers and communities around the world. The department includes sub-departments focused on policy advocacy and lobbying, philanthropy, sustainability, impact finance, community engagement and data analysis and research. item.description: Policy Analyst and Staff Action Officer Organization: ANSER Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Company Overview: ANSER enhances national and homeland security by strengthening public institutions. We provide thought leadership for complex issues through independent analysis, and we deliver practical, useful solutions. ANSER values collaboration, integrity, and initiative and we are client focused in all that we do. Because we were established for the purpose of public service and not for profit, we measure our success in the impact of our service. Position Overview: ANSER is seeking a Policy Analyst and Staff Action Officer to support the Department of War (DoW) Chief Information Officer (CIO). In this role, you will develop and maintain organizational policies and governance documentation, support executive task management and organizational priorities, and manage SharePoint resources for records and knowledge management. You will also coordinate stakeholder engagements and support strategic forums to promote policy compliance and alignment with organizational priorities. Day to Day Responsibilities: Support the implementation and continuous improvement of administrative and project management processes to promote compliant and efficient organizational operations. Manage organizational calendars, priorities, and task flow to support leadership decision-making and strategic priorities. Develop, assess, implement, and maintain organizational policies, procedures, standards, and governance documentation. Evaluate existing policies and recommend improvements to enhance organizational effectiveness and mission execution. Administer SharePoint collaboration sites to support policy documentation, records management, and organizational knowledge sharing. Coordinate meetings, working groups, and stakeholder engagements supporting policy and strategic initiatives. Maintain personnel documentation and records to support organizational compliance. Participate in organizational meetings, workforce forums, and strategic planning sessions to identify and address evolving policy and regulatory requirements. Use CATMS or similar task management systems to track, coordinate, and close organizational actions. Required Qualifications: Active TS/SCI security clearance. 12+ years of experience in policy analysis, governance, organizational management, project management, or a related field. Master’s degree in Information Technology, Government, Public Policy, Business Administration, National Security Affairs, or a related field. Will accept an additional two years of related experience in lieu of master’s degree. Experience developing, assessing, and improving organizational policies, procedures, and governance documentation. Experience supporting policy development, administrative processes, or project management within a government or defense-related environment. Experience using SharePoint for records management, document control, or organizational knowledge sharing. Recent experience using CATMS or a similar task management system. Experience coordinating meetings, working groups, and stakeholder engagements across multiple organizations. Experience preparing policy documentation, reports, briefings, or other executive-level materials. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting C3 operations, policy, or governance forums. Prior experience supporting an Office of the Secretary of War (OSW)-level organization. Familiarity with Department of War or federal government organizational structures and processes. We recruit, employ, train, compensate, and promote regardless of race, color, gender, religion, national origin, ancestry, disability, age, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.description: Senior Principal, Aerospace Standards Government & Industry Engagement Organization: Fullsight Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 SAE Industry Technologies Consortia (ITC), Performance Review Institute (PRI) and SAE International (SAE), deliver shared solutions to industry’s common challenges. Join us and create a higher standard for a better world. The Senior Principal, Aerospace Standards Government & Industry Engagement plays a key role in managing high-level relationships and shaping strategy for the Aerospace Standards program in Washington, DC. In this role, you will represent and promote SAE International’s aerospace standards interests with government agencies, industry organizations, and other key stakeholders in the Washington, DC area. You will lead government and industry relations efforts, advance aerospace standards initiatives, and support colleagues across the organization with Washington, DC-based activities. This position has a direct impact on expanding the acceptance and use of SAE standards across the aerospace sector. Essential Functions Support and promote the SAE Aerospace Standards program in Washington, DC by developing and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders — including FAA, DoD, NASA, AIA, ALPA, A4A, and GAMA — to increase the acceptance and use of SAE standards by government and industry Explore and identify opportunities in expanding and emerging technologies to support industry standards development in new technical areas Coordinate and support assigned activities and committees to ensure timely and efficient development of aerospace standards and standards-related products and services, including those focused on new technology and innovation. Motivate and guide stakeholder leadership involved in Aerospace Standards activities, fostering effective engagement and collaboration across government and industry partners. Build and convert a pipeline of government-funded opportunities that expand SAE standards development into emerging and high-growth technology areas. Minimum Requirements 10 years of experience in business and/or associations, including at least five years of experience working with government agencies in Washington, DC, or equivalent Bachelor’s degree in public policy, engineering (Aerospace, Electrical, or Mechanical preferred), or a related field Demonstrated project management experience Proven experience managing high-level stakeholder relationships Experience in the aerospace industry, operations, or regulatory environment Skilled at high-level government interface, with the ability to effectively represent an organization in government venues Skilled at engaging with industry organizations and associations Ability to organize, promote, and manage meetings and seminars effectively Understanding of the consensus standards development process Strong organizational and planning skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to interact effectively with individuals of diverse backgrounds Strong computer skills, including proficiency in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and standard office applications Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team Preferred Qualifications Ability to assimilate information and identify opportunities and challenges related to government and industry policy is preferred A strong understanding of government perspectives and a solid understanding of aerospace industry perspectives is a plus Working Conditions and Physical Requirements This position operates in a standard office environment. The role requires the ability to work for extended periods at a computer or desk, with or without reasonable accommodation. Domestic and international travel is required approximately 40% of the time to support government and industry engagement, attend meetings, and represent the organization at relevant events and venues. This position may be performed on a hybrid or remote basis, depending on organizational needs and role requirements. Candidates should be prepared to work on-site or travel as business needs dictate. The organization is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of this position. Candidates requiring accommodation during the application or interview process, or in performing job functions, are encouraged to make that need known so that appropriate arrangements can be considered. This position may be performed on a hybrid or remote basis, depending on organizational needs and role requirements. Candidates should be prepared to work on-site or travel as business needs dictate. #SAE ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION SAE Industry Technologies Consortia® (SAE ITC) enables organizations to define and pilot best practices. SAE ITC industry stakeholders are able to work together to effectively solve common problems, achieve mutual benefit for industry, and create business value. The Performance Review Institute® (PRI) is the world leader in facilitating collaborative supply chain oversight programs, quality management systems approvals, and professional development in industries where safety and quality are shared values. SAE International® (SAEI) is a global organization serving the mobility sector, predominantly in the aerospace, automotive and commercial-vehicle industries, fostering innovation, and enabling engineering professionals. Since 1905, SAE has harnessed the collective wisdom of engineers around the world to create industry-enabling standards. Likewise, SAE members have advanced their knowledge and understanding of mobility engineering through our information resources, professional development, and networking. Fullsight is a shared services group working across three affiliate organizations, SAE ITC, SAE International, and Performance Review Institute (PRI), uniformly delivering HR, IT, Legal, Customer Success, Finance, and Procurement services, which enables us to distribute resources across all parts of our businesses. item.title: Senior Director, Global Engagement
item.description: Senior Director, Global Engagement Organization: Adobe Location: San Jose, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 The opportunity This position is a senior leadership role within the Government Relations team, responsible for designing and accomplishing our global plans for external engagement, third-party coalition building, and narrative development. This individual will be the architect of how the organization develops its public policy story externally. They will mobilize allies and manage relationships with trade associations, think tanks, advocacy organizations, and civil society groups. The goal is to promote the company’s policy agenda at the federal, state, and international levels. This is a highly visible position that combines policy expertise with communications competence, partner management, and campaign strategy. What you will do Design and implement a global strategy for engaging third-party organizations including trade associations, NGOs, think tanks, academic institutions, and advocacy coalitions Build, maintain, and activate a portfolio of external allies to advance our public policy priorities across federal, state, local, and international jurisdictions Identify and cultivate new coalition partners and external validators in priority issue areas including technology policy, AI governance, data privacy, competition, and digital infrastructure Narrative Development & Strategic Communications Lead the development and execution of public affairs narratives and messaging frameworks that support the organization’s policy campaigns Oversee original research initiatives — including polling, public opinion surveys, and customer perception studies — to inform engagement strategy and policy positioning Translate complex technical and policy issues into compelling, accessible content crafted for multiple external audiences including government officials, journalists, and the general public Develop and distribute thought leadership content, white papers, briefing materials, and public-facing reports on key policy issues Messaging and Referenceable Data/Arguments Partner with Communications to build strong messaging around our business and governmental policy initiatives that can be used to advance them publicly and with governments. Work to get our public policies referenced in bills, legislation and regulations you can talk about publicly Work with 3rd parties and research firms to produce outside referenceable material that supports our positions Work with the appropriate parts of the company to get more visible media moments with Adobe and public policy/govt so our voice is bigger and more impactful for the company. Campaign Strategy & Execution Build and lead coordinated public engagement initiatives that combine grassroots advocacy, earned media, coalition activation, and direct policymaker engagement Manage rapid-response efforts during legislative or regulatory developments, coordinating external partners and internal team members to deliver timely, aligned messaging Track developments globally and assess implications for coalition strategy and narrative positioning Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as an advisor to policy teams, providing guidance on engagement and coalition strategy Partner with legal, communications, and government affairs leadership to ensure all engagement activities follows lobbying disclosure requirements and company policies What you will bring 15+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, political consulting, essential communications, or a related field Demonstrated track record of designing and delivering successful third-party engagement strategies and public affairs campaigns at the national or global level Deep experience managing relationships, advocacy organizations, think tanks, and other external partners Proven expertise in public opinion research, polling methodology, and translating research findings into action Experience working with or within Congress, the Executive Branch, state legislatures, or government bodies Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt messaging for a range of recipients such as policymakers, media, and the public About Adobe Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity. Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours. Let’s Adobe together At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture, focus on people, purpose and community, Adobe for All, comprehensive benefits programs, the stories we tell, the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create. Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more. Adobe aims to make our Careers website and recruiting process accessible to any and all users. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation to navigate our website or complete the application process, email [email protected] . AI Use Guidelines for Interviews: Our interviews are designed to reflect your own skills and thinking. The use of AI or recording tools during live interviews is not permitted unless explicitly invited by the interviewer or approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation. If these tools are used inappropriately or in a way that misrepresents your work, your application may not move forward in the process. At Adobe, we empower employees to innovate with AI — and we look for candidates eager to do the same. As part of the hiring experience, we provide clear guidance on where AI is encouraged during the process and where it’s restricted during live interviews. See how we think about AI in the hiring experience. Expected Pay Range: Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several U.S. geographic markets, and we pay differently based on those defined markets. The U.S. pay range for this position is $155,100 – $371,950 annually. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the job location during the hiring process. In California, the pay range for this position is $239,200 – $371,950 At Adobe, for sales roles starting salaries are expressed as total target compensation (TTC = base + commission), and short-term incentives are in the form of sales commission plans. Non-sales roles starting salaries are expressed as base salary and short-term incentives are in the form of the Annual Incentive Plan (AIP). In addition, certain roles may be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of a new hire equity award. State-Specific Notices: California: Fair Chance Ordinances Adobe will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records for employment in accordance with state and local laws and “fair chance” ordinances. Colorado: Application Window Notice If this role is open to hiring in Colorado (as listed on the job posting), the application window will remain open until at least the date and time stated above in Pacific Time, in compliance with Colorado pay transparency regulations. If this role does not have Colorado listed as a hiring location, no specific application window applies, and the posting may close at any time based on hiring needs. Massachusetts: Massachusetts Legal Notice It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. item.title: Regulatory Policy Specialist
item.description: Regulatory Policy Specialist Organization: Xcel Energy Location: Denver, CO | Minneapolis, MN | Amarillo, TX | Eau Claire, WI Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Xcel Energy (NASDAQ: XEL) is a leading energy provider and Fortune 500 company, dedicated to serving millions of electricity and natural gas customers across eight states: Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar – delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy. Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact – both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best. Xcel Energy supports a hybrid work model to enable collaboration and flexibility. Many roles are expected to work onsite three days per week (Tuesday–Thursday); however, work location expectations vary based on role, team, and business needs. Position Summary Work directly with senior management to develop regulatory case filings and strategies that support the company’s strategic goals and objectives. Consult with subject matter experts throughout the company to develop filings and strategies consistent with company goals. Communicate and work effectively with regulatory case management teams to ensure filings consistent with strategies. Prepare supporting testimony in regulatory proceedings, administrative rulemaking and legislative hearings as necessary. Coordinate regulatory compliance activities in assigned jurisdictions. Essential Responsibilities Responsible for the development, compilation and editing of regulatory case filings. Provide clear written explanations of complex issues. Applying regulatory experience, understand and identify key facts in order to develop effective messages. Responsible for ensuring documents created are concise and well-organized. Also responsible for ensuring these documents conform to the style, tone and formatting conventions as part of standardized, consistent approach to regulatory filings. Demonstrates technical expertise by maintaining a thorough understanding of the regulatory structure of Xcel Energy companies and the regulatory environment in which we operate. Responsible for advocating the company’s positions with regulators and stakeholders in a variety of forums (e.g. regulatory proceedings, administrative rulemakings, legislative hearings, etc.). Develop, compile and edit large, complex filings. Support multiple projects while delivering high quality work product. Ensure proper controls of documents are maintained; soliciting and screening feedback from stakeholders to incorporate as appropriate. Communicate (written and oral) regularly with senior management and internal customers to ensure awareness of current regulatory case filings and issues that impact the company. Work directly with senior management throughout the company to develop and promote regulatory and legislative policy positions. Work effectively with regulatory case management teams to ensure filings are consistent and production of work is efficient. Work and write in a time constrained environment. Assist with the drafting of discovery responses. Applying regulatory experience, evaluate responses for effectiveness in responding to the question presented. Ensure appropriate context consistent with the company’s request. Responsible for the development of key messages for presentations to external regulatory agencies and legislative committees. Responsible for the development of presentations for internal audiences. Work in partnership across the business area and teams to achieve results. Assist witnesses in development of pre-filed testimony. Minimum Requirements – BA/BS. – Five to seven years or equivalent experience in regulatory field. – Specific experience in dealing with regulatory filings required. – Occasional overnight travel and extensive overtime required. – Must be proficient in use MS Office Suite. Our culture is grounded in shared values and employee commitments that guide how we work, support one another, and grow together. Our Values Connected, Committed, Trustworthy, Safe Our Employee Commitments Work that makes a difference A team you can count of Opportunities to grow Rewards that help you thrive Xcel Energy provides job applicants reasonable accommodations for disabilities throughout the application process. If you are in need of an accommodation to complete the application process, now or at any time in the future, please complete the Applicant Accommodation Request Form. Non-Bargaining The anticipated starting base pay for this position is: $112,200.00 to $159,400.00 per year This position is eligible for the following benefits: Annual Incentive Program, Medical/Pharmacy Plan, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account, Health Care Flexible Spending Account, Health Savings Account (HSA) (if enrolled in eligible health plan), Limited-Purpose FSA (if enrolled in eligible health plan and HSA), Transportation Reimbursement Account, Short-term disability (STD), Long-term disability (LTD), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Fitness Center Reimbursement (if enrolled in eligible health plan), Tuition reimbursement, Transit programs, Employee recognition program, Pension, 401(k) plan, Paid time off (PTO), Holidays, Volunteer Paid Time Off (VPTO), Parental Leave Benefit plans are subject to change and Xcel Energy has the right to end, suspend, or amend any of its plans, at any time, in whole or in part. In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information including but not limited to dates of school attendance and graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. Deadline to Apply: 11/03/26 EEO is the Law (PDF) | Equal Opportunity Statement (PDF) | Employee Rights (PDF) All Xcel Energy employees and contractors share responsibility for protecting the company’s information and systems by adhering to cybersecurity policies, standards, and best practices, recognizing that cybersecurity is everyone’s responsibility. Accessibility Statement Xcel Energy endeavors to make https://www.xcelenergy.com and https://jobs.xcelenergy.com accessible to any and all users. If you are in need of an accommodation to complete the application process, now or at any time in the future, please complete the Applicant Accommodation Request Form. For any other application related questions, including application follow-ups or technical issues, please use our Recruiting Assistance, Electra, for assistance. Electra can be found in the lower right-hand corner of our Xcel Energy Careers site. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
