item.title: Head of State Gov Relations
item.description: Head of State Gov Relations Organization: eBay Location: San Jose, CA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 At eBay, we’re more than a global ecommerce leader — we’re changing the way the world shops and sells. Our platform empowers millions of buyers and sellers in more than 190 markets around the world. We’re committed to pushing boundaries and leaving our mark as we reinvent the future of ecommerce for enthusiasts. Our customers are our compass, authenticity thrives, bold ideas are welcome, and everyone can bring their unique selves to work — every day. We’re in this together, sustaining the future of our customers, our company, and our planet. Join a team of passionate thinkers, innovators, and dreamers — and help us connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all. About the Role eBay is seeking an experienced Government Relations leader to lead our state and local government relations work across the United States. Reporting to the Head of Americas Government Relations, this role will develop and implement eBay’s state policy strategy. It will lead a team of state GR professionals and represent eBay with policymakers and external collaborators. The successful candidate will be a strategic and creative advocate who understands how public policy intersects with business strategy. They will anticipate emerging legislative, regulatory and political developments, assess their potential impact on eBay, and interpret those developments as distinct business risks, opportunities and recommended actions. They will help set priorities across states and issues and develop proactive strategies to promote eBay’s interests. This role goes beyond traditional lobbying. The ideal candidate will combine direct government engagement, grassroots and influential advocacy, alliances, public affairs, and thought leadership. They will also use events and other tools to develop policy discussions and deliver results. They will also be comfortable applying AI and new technologies to improve policy intelligence, strategy development and team efficiency. Responsibilities Develop and complete a coordinated state Government Relations strategy aligned with eBay’s business priorities and the broader Americas GR agenda. Foresee developing legal, administrative, and governmental trends across the states; assess their implications for eBay; and recommend strategic responses. Prioritize among states and topics, balancing immediate legislative needs with longer-term policy objectives. Develop proactive policy campaigns and approaches to engagement that help build policy discussions before legislation or regulation is fully formed. Translate complex policy developments into clear business risks, opportunities, and practical recommendations for business leaders and cross-functional partners. Find opportunities where public policy and outreach efforts can support eBay’s priorities, innovation, growth and seller community. Represent eBay with governors’ offices, state legislators, attorneys general, regulators, trade associations and other key stakeholders, building durable relationships across the political spectrum. Develop integrated advocacy strategies that combine direct government engagement with grassroots and grasstops advocacy, coalitions, public affairs, thought leadership, events and third-party voices. Partner with Communications and other teams to develop narratives, thought leadership and external engagement strategies that advance eBay’s policy objectives. Lead, develop and prioritize the state GR team, creating clear accountability and helping team members grow as strategic policy advisors and effective advocates. Work closely with Legal, Communications, Tax, Product, Trust & Safety and other functions to develop strategies that are both politically effective and operationally workable. Work with colleagues across Americas GR to identify broader policy trends, coordinate strategies and bring state insights into regional priorities. Use AI, data and new technologies to improve policy intelligence, research, prioritization, collaborator engagement and team efficiency. Qualifications 10+ years of relevant experience in Government Relations, public policy, public affairs, political strategy or a related field, with significant experience working on state policy. Deep understanding of state legislative, regulatory and political processes and demonstrated success navigating complex multi-state policy environments. Demonstrated ability to set policy priorities, develop strategy and anticipate emerging risks and opportunities rather than simply respond to legislation. Proven ability to translate public policy issues into clear business implications and practical mentorship for business leaders. Experience leading teams and setting priorities across multiple issues and jurisdictions. Proven ability to develop and carry out cohesive advocacy approaches that extend beyond direct lobbying, including grassroots or grasstops engagement, coalitions, public affairs, thought leadership and events. Strong relationships and credibility with policymakers, political stakeholders and external organizations. Strong business judgment and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to quickly understand new products, technologies and business models. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with senior business leaders and cross-functional teams. Demonstrated ability to operate independently, manage competing priorities and achieve outcomes in a fast paced environment. Comfort using AI alongside new and developing technologies to enhance efficiency, analysis and decision-making. Preferred Qualifications Experience in corporate Government Relations, particularly within technology, ecommerce, marketplaces, retail or another consumer-facing industry. Experience engaging governors’ offices, attorneys general and senior state officials. Experience developing and executing multi-state advocacy campaigns. Experience working closely with Communications or Public Affairs teams on integrated external strategies. Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred. Additional Details The base pay range for this position is expected in the range below: $195,200 – $260,600 Base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a target bonus and restricted stock units (as applicable) in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as PTO and parental leave). Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, employees will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. Remote roles are not eligible for U.S. visa sponsorship. eBay is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, and disability, or other legally protected status. If you have a need that requires accommodation, please contact us at [email protected] . We will make every effort to respond to your request for accommodation as soon as possible. View our accessibility statement to learn more about eBay’s commitment to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. We use cookies to enhance your experience and may use AI tools for administrative tasks in the hiring process. To learn how we handle your personal data and use AI responsibly, please visit our Talent Privacy Notice, Privacy Center and AI Hiring Guideline. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Energy Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager
item.description: Energy Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager Organization: CyrusOne Location: Dallas, TX Date Posted: 10/16/2026 CyrusOne is seeking a talented and highly motivated energy policy professional to support the company’s energy policy, regulatory, and advocacy efforts across North America. The Energy Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager will play a key role in monitoring policy and regulatory developments, conducting research and analysis, supporting advocacy initiatives, and helping advance CyrusOne’s positions on energy, infrastructure, and utility-related matters. Reporting to the Director, Energy Policy & Regulatory Affairs, this position will work closely with internal business partners and external stakeholders to identify opportunities and risks arising from legislative, regulatory, market, and policy developments. The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of the energy industry, including utility regulation, energy infrastructure, wholesale and retail energy markets, renewable energy development, and public policy issues affecting data center growth and operations. Responsibilities: Policy Analysis & Regulatory Monitoring Monitor federal, state, provincial, regional, and local legislative, regulatory, and policy developments impacting CyrusOne’s business interests. Research and analyze energy, utility, market, infrastructure, and regulatory issues affecting data center development and operations. Track utility commission proceedings, legislative initiatives, market reform efforts, and regulatory proceedings relevant to the company’s growth strategy. Summarize complex policy and regulatory developments and communicate implications to internal stakeholders. Maintain awareness of emerging trends related to energy infrastructure, grid reliability, transmission development, renewable energy, and sustainability initiatives. Advocacy Support Support the development and execution of advocacy initiatives that advance CyrusOne’s energy and infrastructure priorities. Assist in preparing policy position papers, briefing materials, presentations, comments, testimony, talking points, and stakeholder communications. Coordinate internal review and approval processes for policy-related materials. Support engagement with industry associations, coalition partners, consultants, and other external stakeholders. Assist in preparing for meetings with policymakers, regulators, utilities, and industry organizations. Stakeholder Engagement Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal business partners and external stakeholders. Participate in industry meetings, conferences, regulatory workshops, and stakeholder forums. Coordinate information gathering from subject matter experts, consultants, and stakeholders to support policy positions and business objectives. Collaborate with Land Strategy, Power & Energy, Market Intelligence, Development, Legal, Sustainability, and other teams to understand policy impacts on business initiatives. Business Support & Strategic Analysis Provide policy and regulatory research support to business leaders and project teams. Assist in evaluating regulatory risks and opportunities associated with development projects, utility initiatives, and energy procurement activities. Support development of strategic recommendations related to regulatory and policy matters. Contribute to internal planning efforts by providing analysis of energy market and policy trends. Develop reports, presentations, and analytical materials to support executive decision-making. Additional Responsibilities Maintain organized records of policy developments, regulatory activities, stakeholder engagement efforts, and advocacy initiatives. Support special projects and strategic initiatives as assigned. Perform other duties as required. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, Energy Management, Economics, Environmental Policy, Business, or a related field. 7+ years of experience in energy policy, regulatory affairs, government affairs, public affairs, utility regulation, energy markets, or a related field. Experience working for or with utilities, regulators, governmental agencies, energy companies, trade associations, consulting firms, or related organizations. Working knowledge of energy markets, utility regulation, energy infrastructure, renewable energy policy, and regulatory processes. Experience monitoring and analyzing legislative, regulatory, and policy developments. Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills. Ability to communicate complex policy and regulatory topics to a variety of audiences. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Ability to travel as business needs require. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting regulatory proceedings, legislative initiatives, or energy policy advocacy efforts. Knowledge of wholesale energy markets, transmission policy, electric utility regulation, renewable energy policy, or energy procurement programs. Familiarity with issues affecting data centers, digital infrastructure, large commercial and industrial energy users, or infrastructure development. Experience working with utility commissions, regional transmission organizations (RTOs), independent system operators (ISOs), legislative bodies, or trade associations. Demonstrated interest in energy infrastructure, grid modernization, reliability, decarbonization, and emerging energy technologies. Experience preparing policy submissions, regulatory comments, briefing documents, or stakeholder communications. Education / Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, Energy, Economics, Environmental Studies, Business, Engineering, or a related field required. Master’s degree, Juris Doctor (JD), or other relevant advanced degree preferred. #LI-LC1 #LI-Remote CyrusOne is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status. CyrusOne provides reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and any other state or local laws. We will respond to requests for reasonable accommodations to assist you in applying for positions at CyrusOne, or to submit a resume. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director, External Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, External Affairs Organization: Tract Location: Alexandria, VA | Denver, CO Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Overview Tract is a team of digital infrastructure experts dedicated to accelerating responsible data center growth by developing master-planned data center parks with access to pre-positioned power and fiber in key markets where hyperscale and AI demand is going. Our approach is collaborative with governments, utilities, cities, and regions to ensure development is targeted for the optimal locations to maximize the economic development benefits for the community while being good stewards of the land and minimizing the impact on neighbors. Tract is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with real estate holdings throughout the United States. Position Overview We are looking for an experienced, organized, detail-oriented, and relationship-driven Senior Director of External Affairs to join our growing team to drive federal, state, and regional/local governmental and energy external affairs and community outreach throughout the United States. The role of the Senior Director, External Affairs will be responsible for developing, prioritizing, tracking, and communicating Tract’s external affairs priorities at the national, state, and local level across the United States. This position will collaborate with a matrixed set of external and internal stakeholders, supporting and implementing the political engagement strategy necessary to allow Tract to push forward the industry and development of master-planned campuses. This position will develop strategies to manage the political opportunities presented from changing regulations to the public perception of data centers. Many of these challenges occur at the local level, however this person will support efforts to develop positive support from National, State, and Non-governmental advocacy organizations throughout the process. Aggregating the capital investment, tax generation, and direct and indirect jobs projected for these developments create highly impactful opportunities for State economic development. Tract desires to create momentum for our mission at the highest levels of government, paving the way for our project teams to be able to do what they do best, delivering the highest quality developments. Numerous issues and challenges vie for attention from Nation and State leaders, Tract’s future opportunities depend on staying one step ahead of policy. Tract wants to tell our story in our own voice, and we are looking for someone who can create those opportunities. Reporting to the Vice President, Business Development and External Affairs, a strong Senior Director, External Affairs candidate demonstrates a strong political acumen, a thorough understanding of national, state, and local-level public policy and can be effective with all constituents. They will build and maintain networks of contacts both within Tract and externally with national and state-level policy makers and can clearly articulate ideas to senior internal and external audiences. This role requires one with great judgment and impeccable ethics with the desire to succeed in a demanding, innovative, and entrepreneurial setting. This role is intended to serve as an execution-oriented partner to the Vice President, with responsibility for disciplined tracking, reporting, follow-through, and day-to-day management of assigned policy matters. Job Responsibilities The Senior Director, External Affairs will work closely with internal stakeholders to understand the interests of Tract and our clients as they relate to governmental affairs developments, involving subject matter experts as appropriate to help craft a consistent narrative and approach to gain the political support required to reach successful outcomes. They will prepare briefing and presentation materials for engagements with policymakers, regulators, and clients, write comment letters to policy makers and contribute to thought leadership on relevant policy topics. The Senior Director will monitor legislation and federal/regulatory developments, manage outside lobbyist updates, prepare weekly reports, draft bill summaries, and escalate risk to the Vice President and appropriate Tract senior leaders. Additionally, as appropriate, the Senior Director may take primary responsibility for a subset of markets prioritized by the Vice President, Business Development and External Affairs (e.g., three to five Western states in the continental U.S.). In addition to other duties assigned by supervisors, the Senior Director, External Affairs will have the following key primary functional responsibilities: State Government Affairs Develop, prioritize, track, and communicate Tract’s priorities at the state-level. Take initiative to define and implement response strategies across states and jurisdictions in coordination with the Vice President. Represent Tract’s views and interests with trade associations, consultants, and clients. Manage outside lobbyist and consultant workstreams, including agendas, action items, follow-up, deliverables, and weekly reporting. Support site RFI process to gather available sites that meet our well-defined parameters. National Government Affairs Monitor federal developments involving Congress, DOE, FERC, NERC, federal permitting, large-load interconnection, energy reliability, tax policy, and AI/data center infrastructure policy. Identify and monitor key U.S. public policy issues and Data Center Development trends that impact Tract and shape Tract’s position on these opportunities. Provide technical recommendations on legislative and regulatory proposals, collaborating closely with Senior Leadership, Legal and other teams to ensure alignment across Tract. Coordinate lobbying activity, as needed, on incentives, regulation, energy, land use, and related policy matters. Build and maintain networks of contacts with national-level policy makers. Provide expert level information on priority issues with key stakeholders across the business. Community Affairs Represent Tract positively and consistently with Tract values within the community in coordination with Tract local project teams. Assist with relationship management with adjacent neighbors and community groups. Education & Experience Bachelor’s degree in one of the following: Political Science, Communications, Public Relations, Speech, Journalism, or other related and/or equivalent degrees. JD highly preferred. Five to eight years’ experience in external affairs, public policy, government relations, legislative affairs, energy policy, infrastructure, economic development, or closely related fields. Experience managing projects, consultants, coalitions, or legislative processes preferred. Previous demonstrated success supporting major infrastructure development projects throughout the United States preferred. Required Traits, Expertise, and Skills Strong political acumen with a thorough understanding of national, state and local-level public policy and the ability to be effective with all constituents. Excellent written communication skills including internal reports and external engagements. Ability to produce concise, accurate, decision-ready written work under time pressure, including bill summaries, state updates, risk assessments, briefing memos, and executive-ready talking points. Precision, follow-through, legislative tracking, deadline management, and synthesis in a high-paced environment. Exceptional verbal communication skills including internal presentations, external speaking engagements, and governmental engagement at the highest levels. Ability to problem solve, leveraging federal, state, and local relationships, corporate resources, and executive support to advance Tract’s message and projects. Ability to read, analyze and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or government regulations. Ability to respond effectively to the most sensitive inquiries while continuing to drive Tract’s message. Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of legislative and regulatory documents and information. Responsible, ethical, and collaborative mindset with a can-do attitude and pride in work product Strong work ethic, with ability to manage time and energy independently toward well-understood target outcomes. Curiosity coupled with the ability to network in structured and unstructured environments to quickly identify, understand, and communicate opportunities and challenges. Eagerness to be a part of building something unique, special, and valuable with a top-notch team of diverse professionals who lead in their respective sectors. Location: Denver, CO office; Alexandria, VA office; Remote; Travel Requirement: This position will require occasional travel to Tract Headquarters or Tract markets. Expected Salary Range: $175,000 – $200,000 Base Salary + Discretionary Bonus Tract Employment Tract employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties as assigned to meet the organization’s ongoing needs. Tract is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at [email protected] . Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: advisor, Public Policy
item.description: advisor, Public Policy Organization: Starbucks Location: Seattle, WA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Now Brewing – advisor, Public Policy Leaders! #tobeapartner At Starbucks, we’re committed to being a different kind of company—one that not only celebrates coffee and connection, but also thoughtfully engages in the policy issues that shape our business and the communities we serve. As advisor, public policy, you will help advance Starbucks public policy and advocacy work on workforce, benefits, economic development, and related issues that impact our partners, our business, and the communities we serve. This role supports the development and execution of policy strategies aligned to enterprise priorities, translates complex policy developments into clear business implications and recommendations, and helps ensure Starbucks shows up as a trusted, constructive voice in policy conversations. As a public policy advisor, you will… Support the development and execution of integrated policy strategies. Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative and regulatory developments that may impact business operations or long-term policy priorities. Identify emerging policy trends, risks, and opportunities; develop clear insights, recommendations, and decision-ready materials for leaders and cross-functional teams. Build and maintain trusted relationships with trade associations, coalitions, policy experts, and external advisors to help advance policy priorities. Coordinate with third-party partners to gather insights, develop shared advocacy approaches, and mobilize external support for policy priorities. Develop clear advocacy materials, including executive briefings, policy memos, talking points, testimony, comment letters, and legislative updates. Partner across business teams to align on policy positions and engagement strategies. Conduct advocacy activity in alignment with lobbying, ethics, disclosure, and political compliance requirements. We’d love to hear from people with: Five or more years of experience in public policy, government affairs, legislative affairs, or related roles, preferably with experience in workforce, economic development, or related policy issues. Industry experience in food & beverage, retail, or related industries. Knowledge of legislative and regulatory processes at the federal, state, or local level, with experience engaging policymakers or external stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Practiced facilitator with strong interpersonal and analytical skills. Ability to work well independently and with others. Self-starter with excellent judgment and high integrity. Bachelor’s degree is preferred in political science, public policy, communications, or a related field. As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools. Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities. You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement. Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com. *If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above. For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above. The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity. At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate. We believe we do our best work when we’re together, which is why we’re onsite four days a week. Join us and inspire with every cup. Apply today ! Starbucks Coffee Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment in a manner consistent with all federal, state and local ordinances. Starbucks Coffee Company is committed to offering reasonable accommodations to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at [email protected] or 1(888) 611-2258. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager, State Government Affairs & Health Policy
item.description: Manager, State Government Affairs & Health Policy Organization: DaVita Kidney Care Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 10/16/2026 No Brag, Just Fact! Over the last decade, we set out to be the world’s greatest dialysis company, and over the next decade, we’re poised to build the greatest healthcare community the world has ever seen. When you join the DaVita Village, you’re joining a winning team. Through our commitment to training, growth, and quality, we consistently achieve superior clinical outcomes while giving teammates the opportunity to excel in an award-winning environment that enables them to thrive both professionally and personally. The Manager, State Government Affairs & Health Policy supports the State Government Affairs team by tracking, organizing, and advancing priority state legislative and regulatory workstreams. The position will manage coordinated work related to non-compete legislation, monitoring of AI legislation and regulations, and stakeholder and subject matter expert engagement in support of advocacy for dialysis patients and the kidney care industry. The role requires strong project management, policy analysis, written communication, and cross-functional coordination skills. Job Duties: Monitor and summarize state legislation, regulations, agency guidance, and policy developments affecting dialysis patients and DaVita’s business operations. Maintain organized, accurate, and timely trackers, dashboards, calendars, and work plans across multiple state policy workstreams. Lead tracking and internal coordination related to state non-compete legislation and regulations, including issue summaries, state comparisons, implementation timelines, and potential business or workforce impacts. Coordinate internal stakeholders and subject matter experts to assess policy proposals, develop organizational positions, and support advocacy on behalf of dialysis patients and the kidney care industry. Prepare concise briefs, issue summaries, talking points, fact sheets, presentations, comment letters, testimony, and other advocacy materials for state policymakers, regulators, trade associations, coalitions, and internal leaders. Partner with Legal, Compliance, Operations, Clinical, Human Resources, Communications, and other teams to evaluate policy impacts and align advocacy strategies. Monitor state legislative sessions, agency proceedings, hearings, rulemakings, and relevant association or coalition activity; provide timely updates and recommended next steps. Support state government affairs leaders, external consultants, and coalition partners with research, materials, project coordination, and execution of advocacy plans across multiple states. Maintain records and documentation needed to support applicable lobbying, ethics, and disclosure requirements. Use of Quorum bill tracking tool. Job-related knowledge: Understanding of state legislative, regulatory, and administrative processes, including bill progression, rulemaking, public comment, and implementation. Knowledge of state health policy, Medicaid, healthcare delivery, workforce policy, or related issues; experience with kidney care or dialysis policy is preferred. Ability to analyze legislation and regulations, identify operational and patient impacts, compare requirements across states, and translate complex material into concise, actionable guidance. Familiarity with non-compete and healthcare workforce policy is preferred. Job-related skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear policy summaries and advocacy materials for varied audiences. Strong project management, organizational, prioritization, and follow-through skills across simultaneous workstreams and deadlines. Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and legislative or regulatory tracking platforms; experience with AI-enabled productivity tools is preferred. Ability to build productive working relationships and coordinate effectively with internal subject matter experts, external stakeholders, consultants, associations, and coalitions. Sound judgment, attention to detail, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive or rapidly evolving policy matters. Intellectual, creative, and/or communication abilities: Critical thinking and policy analysis Ability to create structure, maintain visibility, and drive accountability across complex projects Clear, concise written and verbal communication Collaborative approach to stakeholder and subject matter expert engagement Adaptability and comfort working in a fast-moving, multi-state policy environment Qualifications: BA or BS degree in public policy, political science, government, health policy, healthcare administration, communications required. Three or more years of experience in state government affairs, public policy, legislative or regulatory affairs, healthcare advocacy, a governmental agency, a trade association, or a related private-sector role is preferred. Experience managing multi-state policy tracking, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, and supporting legislative or regulatory advocacy is strongly preferred. Experience in Medicaid, healthcare workforce policy, kidney care, or dialysis policy is a plus. This position is remote and minimal travel is required. Here is what you can expect when you join our Village: A “community first, company second” culture based on Core Values that really matter. Clinical outcomes consistently ranked above the national average. Award-winning education and training across multiple career paths to help you reach your potential. Performance-based rewards based on stellar individual and team contributions. A comprehensive benefits package designed to enhance your health, your financial well-being and your future. Dedication, above all, to caring for patients suffering from chronic kidney failure across the nation. Join us as we pursue our vision “To Build the Greatest Healthcare Community the World has Ever Seen.” Why wait? Explore a career with DaVita today. Go to http://careers.davita.com to apply. What We’ll Provide: More than just pay, our DaVita Rewards package connects teammates to what matters most. Teammates are eligible to begin receiving benefits on the first day of the month following or coinciding with one month of continuous employment. Below are some of our benefit offerings. Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, paid time off, PTO cash out Support for you and your family: Family resources, EAP counseling sessions, access Headspace®, backup child and elder care, maternity/paternity leave and more Professional development programs: DaVita offers a variety of programs to help strong performers grow within their career and also offers on-demand virtual leadership and development courses through DaVita’s online training platform StarLearning. #LI-JS5 At DaVita, we strive to be a community first and a company second. We want all teammates to experience DaVita as “a place where I belong.” Our goal is to embed belonging into everything we do in our Village, so that it becomes part of who we are. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and comply with state and federal affirmative action requirements. Individuals are recruited, hired, assigned and promoted without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. This position will be open for a minimum of three days. The Salary Range for the role is $78,000.00 – $119,000.00 per year. If a candidate is hired, they will be paid at least the minimum wage according to their geographical jurisdiction and the exemption status for the position.New York Exempt: New York City and Long Island: $66,300.00/year, Nassau, Suffolk, and Westchester counties: $66,300.00/year, Remainder of New York state: $62,353.20/year New York Non-exempt: New York City and Long Island: $17.00/hour, Nassau, Suffolk, and Westchester counties: $17.00/hour, Remainder of New York state: $16.00/hourWashington Exempt: $80,168.40/year Washington Non-exempt: Bellingham: $19.13/hour, Burien: $21.71/hour, Everette: $20.77/hour, Unincorporated King County: $20.82/hour, Renton: $21.57/hour, Seattle: $21.30/hour, Tukwila: $21.65/hour, Remainder of Washington state: $17.13/hour For location-specific minimum wage details, see the following link: DaVita.jobs/WageRates Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and experience. DaVita offers a competitive total rewards package, which includes a 401k match, healthcare coverage and a broad range of other benefits. Learn more at https://careers.davita.com/benefits Colorado Residents: Please do not respond to any questions in this initial application that may seek age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You may also redact this information from any materials you submit during the application process. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. item.title: Federal Government Affairs Specialist -26001ES
item.description: Federal Government Affairs Specialist -26001ES Organization: Valero Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Description Valero is the best-in-class producer of essential fuels and products that are foundational to modern life. We invite you to join our ~10,000 employees to drive exceptional results for our company, the energy industry and our community. As a Federal Government Affairs Specialist you will be responsible for logistical functions of Valero’s Political Action Committee (PAC) federal disbursements, Valero Washington D.C. office event planning, and office operations for the Valero Federal Affairs team. Extensive contact with internal personnel as well as individuals, elected officials, fundraisers, and other industry government affairs staff. At Valero, this role performs duties that support our commitment to advancing the future of energy through innovation, ingenuity, and unmatched execution, including: • Maintain the budget and coordinate logistics for Valero’s Political Action Committee (PAC) federal disbursements and D.C. office political events; serve as the liaison with vendors on all related matters, and correspond with participants regarding logistics, deadlines, etc., to ensure successful events. • Oversee all office operations, including onsite meetings, travel, expenses, fundraisers, and other administrative duties. • Arrange additional special events, meetings, fundraisers, travel for guests visiting DC from headquarters or other associates. • Serve as the first point of contact for the DC office and handle the daily responsibilities of office management. • Participate with the federal affairs team with all third-party engagement, including political groups and trade associations. • Interface with corporate headquarters and senior executives’ offices in a friendly and efficient manner. • Balance competing priorities and manage both the day-to-day operations and supports the longer-range goals of the office and the division to which the government relations operations reports, including assisting with production of federal lobbying disclosures. • Screen requests for time, post corporate meetings, and initiate review processes for invitations to internal and external events. • Collect and process all event fees, distribute payments to contractors, and review and submit all event billing for approval. This position is salaried exempt status, which means you are not eligible for overtime pay. Qualifications Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s or higher level degree in Political Science, Public Administration, or related field required. 5+ years of experience in the area of government relations, working in state or federal government, fundraising, lobbying, or related work experience required Able and willing to work on-site and in-person, required. Preferred Requirements: • Experience in managing administrative duties of a political action committee preferred. • Previous experience working in Congress, fundraising, or the Administration preferred. Location: Washington, DC Need more reasons to work for a company that is both professionally challenging and culturally rewarding? Take a look at some of our best-in-class benefits: Competitive Pay and Annual Bonus Program 100% match on 401(K) up to 7%, with immediate vesting Company-sponsored Pension Plan Comprehensive Healthcare and Wellness Program Benefits described above are highlights only, subject to an employee’s eligibility and work location. Position level and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Valero’s employees and team-focused culture drive our success. We’re invested in our dedicated workforce through a comprehensive, customizable benefits package, while supporting a caring culture that delivers a rewarding work environment built on teamwork, excellence and career growth. To explore the ways we build a stronger team, visit Valero.com/Careers. Valero is an EEO Employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to legally protected status, including race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. Please be advised, if you are viewing this position on a website that lists an estimated salary rate/range, it was not provided by Valero. Valero’s market specific salary rate/range will be provided during the recruiting process and tends to be higher than what is estimated by such websites. The posting may close earlier than the advertised date based on applications received. Note: Valero’s pre-employment process includes successful completion of a background check and hair-analysis drug screen. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: US Congressional Lead, Global Affairs
item.description: US Congressional Lead, Global Affairs Organization: OpenAI Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 About the job About The Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and – in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders – seek to further regulation, industry standards, and safe and beneficial development of AI tools. About The Role As a US Congressional Lead on the Global Affairs team, you will help develop strategies and advance OpenAI’s engagement with the U.S. Congress, including developing and managing relationships with House and Senate lawmakers and staff. You will support OpenAI’s U.S. Global Affairs team in meetings, briefings, hearings and other engagements with Congress. You will also facilitate collaboration with civil society and industry partners relevant to Congressional engagement and in alignment with OpenAI’s mission. OpenAI releases industry-leading research and tools. You will face new challenges as the impact of cutting edge generative AI technologies continues to be explored and as the needs of the organization evolve. Day-to-day work may encompass anything from helping to shape strategic initiatives and policy documents to preparing our leaders for engagements with government officials or representing OpenAI in private and public forums. We are looking for a self-directed and creative individual with Capitol Hill experience, experience managing private sector and civil society relationships, plus an understanding of AI-related legislative and regulatory issues and processes. This role is based in Washington, DC and may require frequent travel to participate in meetings and events with key stakeholders. We offer relocation assistance to new employees. You Should Thrive In This Role If You Are well versed in the issues around emerging AI technologies, especially in the U.S. Congressional context. Are an enthusiastic and effective coalition builder who thrives as a member of a high performing, peer-led global team. Are highly organized, and are used to working as an accountable individual contributor as well as a team player. Are passionate about the promise of technology and the future of artificial intelligence but thoughtful about its potential risks. We’re Looking For a Blend Of Demonstrated experience (8+ years) and credibility in working with Republicans in the U.S. federal government, particularly the legislative branch. Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the U.S. government, institutions, and processes, and the key policy issues and debates related to AI. Extensive experience in technology policy, with experience working with the Commerce, Judiciary, and/or Appropriations Committees. Track record of effectively working with cross-functional teams, especially communications, policy and legal teams, and aligning a diverse range of internal and external partners Sound judgment and outstanding personal integrity Ability to execute in fast and flexible environments through rapid cycles of analysis, decision, and action Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical and policy concepts to diverse audiences Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and project management skills Genuine care and knowledge about the impact of technology on society About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology. Compensation Range: $252K – $280K Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Sr Manager, State Government Affairs – Remote Hybrid within Central Region
item.description: Sr Manager, State Government Affairs – Remote Hybrid within Central Region Organization: Kraft Heinz Company (KHC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Job ID R-106252 Position Summary The Senior Manager, State Government Affairs plays an important role within the Government Affairs team by supporting Kraft Heinz Company’s (KHC) state‑level advocacy efforts. This role helps advance company policy priorities in key states by executing legislative and regulatory strategies, maintaining relationships with policymakers and stakeholders, and partnering cross‑functionally to mitigate risk and support business objectives. This position reports to the Associate Director of State Government Affairs and works closely with internal and external partners to help protect and promote KHC’s interests at the state level. Primary Responsibilities Manage government affairs activities for an assigned group of states in alignment with broader state and federal advocacy strategies. Serve as a state lobbyist in priority states, including drafting and negotiating bill language, supporting sponsor engagement, delivering or coordinating testimony, and assisting with committee and floor strategy. Develop and maintain bipartisan relationships with state legislators, executive branch staff, and committee members; support engagement plans and relationship‑tracking efforts. Act as a policy subject‑matter resource in one or more KHC‑relevant areas; assist in preparing position statements, regulatory comments, briefing materials, and executive talking points. Represent KHC in state rulemaking processes and select external stakeholder or industry forums. Participate in building and maintaining coalitions with other companies, trade associations, chambers of commerce, and aligned organizations to advance shared policy goals. Monitor state legislative, regulatory, and ballot activity; summarize developments and provide timely updates with recommended next steps. Support the management of outside consultants and contract lobbyists, including coordination of work plans, budgets, and compliance requirements. Partner cross‑functionally with Legal, Regulatory, R&D, Supply Chain, ESG, Commercial, HR, and Communications teams to support issue management and state‑level response efforts. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required Strong understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes, including lobbying and ethics compliance Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate policy developments into business‑relevant insights Solid project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams Sound judgment, high integrity, and discretion when handling confidential or sensitive matters Willingness to travel as needed Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree (JD, MA, MBA, or similar) Experience in a corporate or trade association government affairs function Prior experience working in or with state government (legislative staff, executive branch, or state agency) Required Experience 6–8 years of experience in state government, public policy, or state lobbying Demonstrated experience supporting or executing legislative or regulatory strategies, including drafting materials and engaging policymakers Exposure to at least one or two policy areas relevant to KHC (e.g., food policy, packaging, agriculture, environmental policy, tax, workforce/labor) Experience working with external consultants or coalition partners preferred Familiarity with state policy organizations such as NCSL, CSG, or NGA is a plus EEO Policy Kraft Heinz is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minorities/Women/Veterans/Disabled and other protected categories. Our Total Rewards philosophy is to provide a meaningful and flexible spectrum of programs that equitably support our diverse workforce and their families and complement Kraft Heinz’ strategy and values. New Hire Base Salary Range: $120,800.00 – $151,000.00 Bonus: This position is eligible for a performance-based bonus as provided by the plan terms and governing documents. The compensation offered will take into account internal equity and may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors Benefits: Coverage for employees (and their eligible dependents) through affordable access to healthcare, protection, and saving for the future, we offer plans tailored to meet you and your family’s needs. Coverage for benefits will be in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and associated governing plan documents. Wellbeing: We offer events, resources, and learning opportunities that inspire a physical, social, emotional, and financial well-being lifestyle for our employees and their families. item.title: Legislative Affairs Manager
item.description: Legislative Affairs Manager Organization: Sierra Space Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Sierra Space Careers: At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth. Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond. Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space. We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team. About the Role Sierra Space is seeking a high-performing Legislative Affairs Manager to support and advance the company’s federal legislative strategy and help translate business, program, and growth priorities into effective congressional engagement. The role will develop and manage relationships with congressional personal-office staff, support legislative strategy and advocacy, lead congressional site visits and engagements, oversee the company’s Political Action Committee (PAC) , and provide analytical and operational support across the Government Relations & Strategic Communications organization. This role is designed for a high-performing government relations professional who combines strong political judgment and relationship-building skills with exceptional analytical, organizational, and written communication capabilities. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to take on increasing legislative responsibility as experience and relationships grow. The position requires someone who can move comfortably between external advocacy and internal execution: building trusted relationships on Capitol Hill, collaborating closely with business and program leaders, preparing senior executives for key engagements, and ensuring the Government Relations & Strategic Communications team operates with disciplined planning, tracking, and follow-through. About You Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission. We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. The Legislative Affairs Manager is a key member of the Government Relations team, responsible for providing expert analysis, strategic insights, and high-level advocacy to influence public policy and legislative actions. This senior-level position requires extensive experience in government operations, policy analysis, and public affairs, with a focus on the U.S. Federal budget process and legislative activities related to the Department of Defense (DoD) and NASA. The role involves representing Sierra Space at high-profile industry events, government meetings, and with senior executives. In this role, you will conduct expert-level research and analysis on legislative, regulatory, and policy issues relevant to the organization. You will monitor and provide strategic insights on federal government activities, including legislation, regulations, and budget processes, with a focus on Department of Defense (DoD) and NASA programs. Additionally, you will prepare comprehensive reports, briefs, and presentations on findings to support the Government Relations team and senior leadership. You will develop and implement advanced advocacy strategies and campaigns to influence public policy and legislative actions while maintaining and leveraging a deep understanding of the hierarchy and structure of decisional authority within legislative and National Security organizations. Tracking and reporting on key legislative and regulatory developments, you will provide actionable recommendations to drive organizational strategies. Representing Sierra Space externally at high-profile industry events, government meetings, and with senior executives and officials, you will build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including government officials, agencies, and industry partners. Furthermore, you will lead and manage complex projects and processes, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and the timely completion of deliverables, while mentoring and providing guidance to junior members of the Government Relations team. Key Responsibilities Coordinate and support Sierra Space’s legislative affairs strategy to advance strategic business priorities and growth initiatives, including engagement with Members of Congress and congressional personal-office staff to build understanding and support for Sierra Space programs and capabilities. Develop and maintain trusted relationships with congressional personal-office staff, serving as a day-to-day point of contact for a portfolio of House and Senate offices relevant to Sierra Space’s business and policy priorities. Support broader congressional engagement, including coordination with relevant committee staff when appropriate and in partnership with senior Government Relations & Strategic Communications leadership. Monitor congressional activity, legislation, hearings, markups, policy developments, and other activity relevant to Sierra Space; synthesize developments into concise, actionable updates for internal stakeholders. Manage Sierra Space’s congressional engagement process, including content development, briefing materials, white papers, engagement tracking, and follow-up. Coordinate and support executive engagements in the Washington, D.C. area, including congressional meetings and other priority government stakeholder engagements. Lead and oversee visits by Members of Congress and congressional staff to Sierra Space facilities, partnering across the business to establish objectives and message, coordinate agendas, briefing materials, executive preparation, security, communications, and site logistics. Develop trusted relationships across Sierra Space’s businesses, programs, and functions to ensure Government Relations & Strategic Communications priorities are informed by business objectives and to maximize the function’s impact on company growth initiatives and strategic captures. Partner closely with business and program teams to understand company capabilities, customer priorities, program developments, and growth objectives and translate them into effective congressional engagement. Build and maintain trusted relationships with federal agency staff as appropriate, industry associations, coalition partners, and industry stakeholders. Manage and grow the Sierra Space PAC, including solicitation planning, participation and contribution tracking, fundraising activity, and strategic giving support; oversee the outside PAC administration and compliance firm responsible for required filings and day-to-day compliance activities. Coordinate closely with Sierra Space’s outside government relations’ consultants, helping align advocacy activities, congressional outreach, deliverables, and consultant support with company priorities. Own and maintain key Government Relations & Strategic Communications operating tools, including budget tracking, consultant and contact trackers, congressional engagement, legislative trackers, team priorities, etc. Coordinate and develop routine Government Relations & Strategic Communications updates and other recurring leadership reporting, gathering inputs across the team and distilling activity into clear, decision-useful summaries. Support preparation for Executive Leadership Team and Board engagements, including presentations, briefing materials, dashboards, background research, and coordination of inputs across the Government Relations & Strategic Communications team. Conduct research and analysis on legislative, political, policy, budget, customer, and industry issues relevant to Sierra Space and translate findings into concise recommendations or briefing products. Help coordinate cross-functional Government Relations & Strategic Communications priorities, deadlines, deliverables, and follow-up to ensure commitments and leadership requests are completed on time. Support special projects and emerging priorities for the Senior Vice President of Government Relations & Strategic Communications and the broader organization. Minimum Qualifications: Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree or Masters +3 years of experience). Typically 5+ years of related experience, including time as mid-level professional staff on Capitol Hill or within U.S. government agencies and/or National Security organizations. Demonstrated experience providing expert analysis of federal budgets and the legislative process. Experience representing government offices or industry interests externally before senior government officials and/or senior executives. Knowledge of the requirements and resourcing processes within the Department of Defense and NASA. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain professional relationships with congressional staff and other external stakeholders. Strong understanding of the federal legislative process and congressional organization. Strong project and process management skills. Exceptional written communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into concise executive-level materials. Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment with a high degree of judgment and discretion. Demonstrated proficiency preparing presentations, briefing materials, trackers, and lead

item.title: Head of Policy, Government Relations & Public Relations
item.description: Head of Policy, Government Relations & Public Relations Organization: Hussh Location: Kirkland, WA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 About Hussh Hussh’s mission: make information (especially private personal information) a real financial asset for the human it belongs to, with the human in control of every machine, always. The technology company builds private personal AI (Private Agent One, iMoney, the puppy home supercomputer). The asset manager runs permanent capital on the world’s fastest growers of absolute free cash flow. There is a reason a technology company leads with policy: the law is what must change. Today, a human’s information can be taken and sold without their consent, and the companies that do it call it an industry. We are building the alternative, and campaigning, in the open, for the law to catch up. Our privacy-law campaign has already reached more than a thousand lawmakers, regulators, and institutions. It has one owner today. It should have you. Hussh is 100% privately owned and profitable (founder-funded, no outside investors), and we hire the best and pay the best. The campaign exists because the mission demands it: information into an asset, and personal superintelligence available to everybody. A bet on AI in the biggest manner, made with partners, never against them. The value test governs the campaign too: every audience we reach must receive more than we ask of them, and the trust that builds becomes equity, for the mission and for everyone who works with us, invests with us, or does business with us. Brand, culture, and values carry the same weight here as the product. The role Mission: one owner for the outside world that isn’t the market. The law, the government, and the public story. This is deliberately one role, not three. Policy, government relations, and public relations are the same fight on three fronts: the privacy law must change (policy); the people who write it must know us (government relations); the public must understand why it matters (public relations). Split them and you get three strategies. We need one. You will work daily with Anoushka Gehani, our Founding Public Policy Data Scientist. She owns the data science and the campaign experimentation she built; you own the function, the relationships, and the load she has been carrying solo. The senior data team sits in your org as the evidence engine. Policy is a CEO-level concern at Hussh, and this seat reports to the CEO because of it. What you’ll do The doctrine you will represent: the target is always the law, never the builders. The technology companies and AI labs are partners, never adversaries. The threat is the selling of a human’s information without their consent. Full stop. Own the privacy-law campaign end to end: the agenda (what law changes, in what order), the lawmaker and regulator pipeline (federal, state, and data-protection authorities abroad), and the cadence that keeps every relationship warm. Run government relations as a discipline: who we talk to, what we ask for, what we never ask for. Written down, and followed. Hold the public story: one narrative, told consistently. The company speaks when it has something true to say, never to fill silence. Press that doesn’t serve the mission is a cost, not a win. Build the evidence program with the data team: research and analysis that make the policy case undeniable. Evidence first, advocacy second, always. Work inside counsel’s clearance on every policy position and every regulator-facing statement. You advocate; counsel clears. That rule survives everything. What success looks like in 6 months The campaign runs on rails you own: one dashboard, one cadence, lawmaker and regulator relationships compounding with named next steps. Nothing going cold. The policy agenda is written and sequenced, with an evidence program behind each item. Anoushka’s side of the house has the senior partnership it was missing, and her campaign experimentation has a function around it, not just a founder’s admiration. Hussh’s public voice is disciplined and unmistakable: fewer words, every one earned. What you bring You have changed or shaped an actual policy outcome: legislation, regulation, or a public campaign with measurable results. Not advocated. Moved something. Active relationships with lawmakers, regulators, or their senior staff: current, not historical. You can argue the same truth three ways: to a skeptical committee, a hostile reporter, and a friendly regulator. The discipline of few words: every touch weighed, nothing throwaway, nothing that didn’t earn its place. Nice to have Privacy, data-protection, or technology-policy specialization; familiarity with US state privacy law and international regulators. A combined policy + communications background: this role is built for someone who has refused to choose between them. Experience building an evidence/research program behind an advocacy agenda. What we offer $180,000–$250,000 base, a 20–30% target bonus, and a founding equity grant on a 4-year vest. The real offer: a mission with a theory of change, a campaign already in motion, a CEO who treats policy as a first-order concern, and the chance to be the person who helped make a human’s information *theirs* in law, not just in our product. Work authorization We welcome candidates on OPT and STEM OPT. We may not be able to sponsor a visa. We cannot consider international applicants without US work authorization. Applications without it are automatically rejected. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
