item.title: Manager, National Security Government Relations
item.description: Manager, National Security Government Relations Organization: Blue Origin Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 10/16/2026 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! This role is part of Blue Origin corporate functions, providing centralized support across Blue Origin business unit teams, functions, and locations. At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our diverse team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! We are a diverse team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safe, routine spaceflight. This position will directly impact the future of U.S. space policy and will require your commitment and detailed attention toward public policy. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin’s vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth. As part of a hardworking team of diverse policy experts, you will support Blue Origin’s strategic legislative priorities. You will lead the team’s impact on all aspects of national security space policy. The Government Relations team you’re joining interfaces with national and local legislative bodies and executive agencies. You will develop and implement the strategy to shape legislation in support of team objectives. This includes crafting messaging and materials and representing Blue Origin and its policy interests with external and internal stakeholders. This position reports to the Vice President of Government Relations. You and the team interface directly with company leadership, as well as the business units, communications, legal, and sales teams. Additional duties include leading USG engagements, managing external consultants, engaging our nationwide supplier base, and supporting strategy for State and Local Government Relations initiatives and efforts. Strong knowledge of USG space programs, budgets and history, relationships with relevant congressional stakeholders, and experience leading and implementing legislative strategy are required for this position. We are looking for someone to apply their expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to usher in a new era of safe and affordable launch and in-space capabilities for USG customers. Passion for our mission and vision is required! Qualifications: Bachelors degree 6+ years of congressional experience or related partnership experience with local/state government, C level executives, or similar. Experience developing and implementing successful legislative strategies Excellent communications skills, both oral and written Able to support multiple projects in a fast-paced environment Comfortable working with Members of Congress, agency leadership, VIPs and representing Blue Origin with diverse stakeholders Excellent organizational skills for tracking government programs and budgets, and congressional issues, while meeting deadlines Knowledge of DOD space programs and budgets Proficient in the Congressional Budget processes Ability to obtain a Top Secret Clearance Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and contribute to a culture of inclusion Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Desired: Knowledge of commercial space industry Base Pay Range for: VA applicants is $121,023.00 – $169,432.20 Other site ranges may differ Culture Statement Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. Export Control Regulations Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Background Check Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training. Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical Benefits Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program. Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week) Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays. Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company’s intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company’s results, or other factors at the company’s sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. Equal Employment Opportunity Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here. Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at [email protected] . item.title: Sr. Manager, Stakeholder Relations – Central Region
item.description: Sr. Manager, Stakeholder Relations – Central Region Organization: AES Location: Remote (TX) Date Posted: 10/16/2026 Are you ready to be part of a company that’s not just talking about the future, but actively shaping it? Join The AES Corporation, the largest US-based global power company with a team of 8,300 employees across 12 countries. AES has been ranked #1 by BloombergNEF in renewable energy sales to corporations in the US and Americas for five consecutive years, providing electricity for millions of people worldwide. We are proud to foster a strong workplace culture, earning prominent positions in Great Place to Work™ rankings across the markets where we operate. AES was also named one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies for the 13th consecutive year in 2026, highlighting our dedication to integrity, transparency, and responsible business practices. Our spirit of innovation continues to earn industry recognition. AES is the only seven-time winner of the Edison Electric Institute’s Edison Awards in the twenty-first century, a distinction honoring global leadership in advancing the electric power industry. If you’re ready to be part of a company that’s not just adapting to change, but driving it, AES is the place for you. We’re not just building a more sustainable future, we’re powering it. Apply now and energize your career with a true leader in global energy. AES is accelerating the energy transition to a lower carbon world with sustainable and affordable power. The Company is a global leader in energy storage and is quickly becoming one of the leading developers of solar and wind projects in the Americas. Additionally, AES has embarked on numerous digital initiatives over the past few years, including deployment of AI and machine learning, to enhance performance at existing businesses and to develop new products for our customers. At AES, we raise the quality of life around the world by changing the way energy works. Everyone makes an impact every day in our small, global teams. Job Summary The Sr. Manager, Stakeholder Relations – Central Region leads locally tailored engagement for energy infrastructure and multi-technology campus development across the Central Region, with a primary focus on Texas. The role supports projects from prospecting through development, permitting, construction and execution, with near-term emphasis on projects in active execution and continuity through transition to Operations. Depending on project scope, campuses may integrate generation, storage, data centers or other large-load infrastructure; configurations are project-specific. As a key representative of AES, this position serves as a bridge with local communities, fostering positive interactions between the company and the community. The Sr. Manager functions as a local spokesperson for the organization, taking on external responsibilities to elevate AES’ presence and reputation within the region. This role is a people leader responsible for empowering, inspiring and developing a talented regional team of industry-leading engagement professionals. The successful candidate will be a transformational leader who builds team capability, creates an inclusive and high-performing environment, and helps team members grow while delivering strong results. The role also provides expert guidance and support to the team, leveraging deep knowledge in community relations to drive performance toward strategic objectives. The breadth of engagement extends beyond local communities to include customer counterparts, unions, nonprofits, local governments, EPC partners, industry associations, economic development organizations and local news organizations, among others. The successful candidate has demonstrated experience designing and executing community benefit agreements and other benefit structures, and cultivating innovative, responsive and meaningful partnerships in service of local communities and responsible infrastructure development. Job Functions People Leadership and Team Development Lead, coach and develop a talented team of stakeholder engagement professionals, setting clear priorities and expectations while empowering team members to make decisions, grow their capabilities and deliver industry-leading engagement. Foster an inspiring, inclusive and high-performing culture; provide timely feedback and development opportunities; and apply a transformational leadership approach to strengthen the team for current and future business needs. Strategic Community Engagement Develop and execute local engagement plans for Central Region energy projects and campuses across prospecting, site and acquisition diligence, early planning, development, permitting, construction and execution, with a particular emphasis on Texas. Support stakeholder and community diligence for potential new projects AES may seek to acquire. Advise project teams on community needs, stakeholder relationships and near- and long-term risks, aligning engagement with project milestones and responsible development. Build cross-functional alignment with Development, Permitting, Execution, Finance, Legal, Government Relations, Operations, Communications and other relevant internal teams. Coordinate with customers and development partners on engagement strategies, siting considerations and stakeholder expectations. Translate community insight into feasible responses and clear engagement responsibilities across interconnected projects and technologies. Manage engagement spending and resources within approved processes and oversee relevant consultants or agencies when requested. Mobilize coalitions of individuals and organizations to demonstrate support for AES’ energy projects. Local Policy and Inclusive Participation Maintain informed understanding of Texas and relevant state, municipal and local-level political landscapes, in coordination with AES’ Government Relations team. Build professional, nonpartisan relationships with elected officials and staff, regulators, trade and business groups, community and educational organizations, and public and private institutions. Monitor local proceedings and support transparent public participation and appropriate project advocacy. Engage a broad and diverse local audience through respectful, culturally competent consultation, including underrepresented communities. Conduct Indigenous engagement where applicable, consistent with the AES Voluntary Tribal Engagement Policy. Create accessible opportunities to understand concerns and influence engagement planning. Maintain accessible, responsive inquiry and notification channels. Listen, document feedback, communicate timely responses, and work with project teams and partners to resolve concerns. Escalate unresolved issues appropriately and communicate outcomes to stakeholders, maintaining continuity as projects move into execution. Community Benefit Agreements and Social Impact Partnerships Cultivate innovative, responsive and meaningful local partnerships through the AES Social Impact Program. Lead the design and implementation of community benefit agreements and other community benefit structures. Listen and co-design with local stakeholders and relevant partners, assess feasible benefits with project teams, and negotiate and structure agreements in alignment with AES’ Social Impact Program and compliance requirements. Ensure partnerships are ethical, and the long-term benefits serve community priorities and responsible development and are not an exchange for public support or approvals. Implement agreed commitments, track accountability and outcomes, and report progress in adherence to internal and external reporting requirements. Coordinate outreach and volunteer activities where relevant and aligned with company and community priorities. Stakeholder Intelligence and Accountability Maintain accurate stakeholder lists, interaction records, feedback, commitments and engagement reporting using designated CRM tools. Analyze local sentiment, social and traditional media, and emerging political or community issues to identify near- and long-term risks and opportunities. Lead stakeholder risk management and communications across the project lifecycle, including issue escalation and executive-facing risk reporting. Provide practical guidance to project teams and maintain transparent, accountable engagement across assigned projects. Economic Development, Communications and Events Apply understanding of economic development and tax incentive structures relevant to Texas and assigned state energy and large infrastructure development. Support the negotiation and approval of relevant economic and tax incentives, alongside relevant internal team members and external consultants and partners. Partner with Communications to develop clear, locally tailored, multichannel project information, advocacy materials, talking points, presentations and public displays. Coordinate construction messaging and local media opportunities, explain relevant issues and support issue and crisis communications with the responsible teams. Plan and deliver public meetings, community events, virtual engagement and site visits, including preparation, presentations and follow-up. Represent AES professionally in business, government and community settings, advancing informed dialogue and practical collaboration. Required for All Jobs Performs other duties as assigned. Demonstrates AES values: Safety First, Highest Standards, and All Together. Complies with all policies and standards. Qualifications Education Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience in a relevant field such as community engagement, advocacy, public relations, public affairs, environmental studies, communications, local government or a similar field. Required. Master’s degree in Public Relations, Communications, Business Administration or a related field. Preferred. Work Experience Minimum of 9 years of related work experience in stakeholder engagem

item.title: Public Relations Specialist
item.description: Public Relations Specialist Organization: Interactive Government Holdings, Inc. (IGH) Location: Bethesda, MD Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Description Organization Established in 2006, Interactive Government Holdings, Inc. (IGH) is a leading professional services and technology provider to the Federal Government. Our mission is to serve uniformed service members globally and their support systems locally. We utilize strategy, data science, and technology to make the programs we execute more efficient for the people our programs serve. IGH has a national and international program staff and a corporate headquarters located in Springfield, Virginia. We are proud of our ability to shape tomorrow while ensuring all active-duty personnel and reservists can carry out their critical missions and tasks today. Job Description Interactive Government Holdings (IGH) is seeking a qualified, trained and capable individual to serve as a Public Relations Specialist to lead strategic communication initiatives and manage high-impact projects. This hybrid role requires a professional who excels in crafting compelling messages, engaging diverse audiences, and ensuring communication projects are planned, executed, and delivered on time. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in public relations, project management with PMP certification, and a deep understanding of healthcare or public sector communications Position Requirements Major responsibilities include (not all inclusive): Support the Walter Reed Public Affairs Develop and execute public affairs strategies to promote Walter Reed’s mission, services, and initiatives. Write and edit press releases, talking points, newsletters, and other communication materials. Coordinate media relations, including responding to inquiries, arranging interviews, and maintaining relationships with media outlets. Craft messaging for internal and external stakeholders, ensuring consistency with organizational goals. Monitor media coverage and provide analysis on the effectiveness of public affairs campaigns. Plan and execute events, such as press conferences, media briefings, and community engagement activities. Support leadership with crisis communication strategies and plans. Support updates Internal Website and Social Media sites, Participate in Strategic, Access to Care and Emergency Management Communications Meetings Compile weekly external communication reports. Submit products to the PAO for review prior to posting on the website and/or intranet. Update content on external webpage and social media. Assist with NCR PAO meetings, attend DHA & NCR meetings. Generate editorial ideas for articles and discuss/refine ideas with lead PAO. Meet daily and weekly deadlines and ADHOC suspense to support the mission. Develop news-pegs, angles, and balanced articles from multiple-sources including interviews with market staff members, military and civilian, patients, and visitors for news releases, feature stories and special publications. Schedule interviews with Subject-Matter Experts, working closely with other PAO offices with the approval from the Government Lead. Write, rewrite, and edit copy based on AP Style, using active sentences, traditional leads, bridges, transitions, and news format. Assist Visitors and numerous callers, Take Media Queries, Coordinate/Moderate Press Interviews, Arrange Media Visits Moderate Press Interviews, generate 2-3 editorial ideas a month, deliver social media post week or as needed based upon the mission. Assist an average of 10 callers per day, Assist with 4 DV visits per month: Updated Website and Social Media sites several times a day. Distribute an average of 2 communications reports weekly. Performance Element: oversees, researches, plans, writes, executes, and evaluates a wide number of communications plans, operations plans and community relations plans, with an emphasis on plans producing measurable results. Develops messaging, communications plans and supporting media and products for target audiences. Coordinates with DHA public affairs leaders on the dissemination of critical information and communications services, plans, activities, community relations initiatives and products. Coordinates dissemination of information/communications with the MTFs to ensure the Defense Health Agency messages and information are told to internal audiences to effectively communicate the Military Health System message. Formulates strategies for major issues, management and coordinates messages and theme development for the Market office that are executed through the MTFs. Provides strategic counsel to the senior leaders of and the Market MTFs. Develops speeches and briefings to effectively communicate key themes and messages to a wide range of audiences. Coordinates on public website content to support the MHS/DHA communication objectives. Performance Standard: Enhances effectiveness and efficiency of communications plans and community relations plans, with an emphasis on plans producing measurable results. Operationally define strategic partnerships and alliances within current and future Agency and Market contexts. Performance Element: Coordinates with MTF and DHA communications and marketing teams to ensure messages and products are disseminated to MTFs within the NCR Market Office and provide feedback as appropriate. Provides input to multiple websites and oversees all social media platforms used by the MTFs under the Market Office. Reviews locally produced internal communications products to ensure a consistent HA/ MHS/ DHA message is delivered in multiple communications venues and outlets. Coordinate with the DHA Headquarters SRATCOM team for communications product support. Review, analyze and evaluate the accomplishments of the Market Office in accordance with the Military Health System and the Defense Health Agency public affairs and communications program. Assesses media coverage of activities and recommends methods and techniques for disseminating information that will increase public awareness and stakeholder support. Develop and execute network-based operations model for strategic communications to patients and staff through multiple venues and products that support the Network structure and MTF patient engagement that will optimize the NCR Network and DHA for greater performance. Analyzes and makes recommendations concerning conflicting and divergent input from MTF staff, and other stakeholders within their area of responsibility to obtain a consensus position among differing viewpoints, and to assist program officials in the achievement of the public affairs program objectives. Develops and manages the Market Office communications planning programs, to include providing input into the MHS/ DHA Strategic Communication plan involving Market Military Treatment Facilities, to facilitate better understanding and support of military health missions, roles, and responsibilities. Develops and applies new approaches to complex public affairs problems of the MHS by developing and evaluating information programs to enhance understanding among public opposed or indifferent to MHS / DHA Programs, including the Defense Health Plan. Controls the strategic and synchronous release of information to inform internal and external audiences about the MHS and DHA. Provides crisis communications planning support and advice on the impact of activities, including time-critical resolution of unfavorable media incidents that may escalate to national media and/or Congressional interest. Analyzes the Market Office and subordinate MTF’s public affairs problems and issues and determines new approaches for informing various individuals and key groups about MHS/DHA programs. Facilitate relationships with representatives of the numerous Medical Organizations and Medical Support Organizations, Military Service Organizations, Veterans Service Organizations, other Federal Organizations and Non- Governmental Organizations at the regional level providing information about MHS/ DHA programs, policies, and services. Develops and coordinates communications plans with local subject matter experts to disseminate information to a wide range of audiences. Evaluates techniques to incorporate the latest developments in the field into effective and efficient communications plans, programs, and strategies. Provides supporting materials as required. Establishes and maintains relations with various communications organizations, including the news media in enlisting their cooperation in providing the public with information about the MHS/DHA programs and initiatives. Identifies existing or potential public perception problem areas and recommends an integrated strategy covering all communications and outreach aspects. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in communications, Public Relations, Project Management, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in public affairs, project management, or a combination of both roles. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages to diverse audiences. Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency with project management tools and software, as well as digital communication tools. Familiarity with healthcare systems or military communications is highly desirable. Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is a plus. Knowledge of principles, methods, practices, and techniques of strategic communication, by selecting and using the appropriate communication tools, to assist in facilitating and implementing a command information program which targets an assortment of audiences at varying levels of interaction. Knowledge and skill for developing written and oral and social media materials designed to convey complex information and clarify the organization’s operations, programs, and activities to various audiences. item.title: Senior Policy Manager, Public Policy
item.description: Senior Policy Manager, Public Policy Organization: Intuit Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Company Overview Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. With tens of millions of customers worldwide using products such as TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp, we believe that everyone should have the opportunity to prosper. We never stop working to find new, innovative ways to make that possible. Job Overview Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. Approximately 100 million consumers, small and mid-market businesses, and accountants around the world use Intuit products including TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, and Intuit Enterprise Suite. Our mission is to power prosperity around the world. By bringing together the power of AI and human intelligence, we help our customers put more money in their pockets, save time by eliminating work, and have greater confidence in the financial decisions they make. Intuit’s Global Corporate Affairs and Public Policy team brings the voice of our customers to policymakers and works to shape public policy environments that enable our customers to prosper. Intuit is seeking exceptional Senior Policy Managers to lead public policy strategy on issues critical to Intuit’s customers and business, spanning: AI, data, and technology policy — shaping the environment for free, frictionless, compliant data use and responsible AI deployment that powers increasingly personalized, Done-for-You customer and expert experiences. Money and financial services policy — advancing the policy conditions that let Intuit help customers access capital, manage money, and build financial confidence. Small and mid-market business policy — championing the policy changes that help entrepreneurs and growing businesses start, succeed, and scale. Across all of these areas, we are looking for strategic thinkers and highly effective advocates who can anticipate the direction of public policy, develop compelling policy positions, and build and execute strategies that shape legislative and regulatory outcomes. The successful candidate will serve as a policy adviser to senior leaders across Intuit and as a credible, authoritative external voice for the company, advocating directly with policymakers and regulators and leveraging trade associations, coalitions, think tanks, and civil society to advance Intuit’s priorities. Responsibilities Serve as Intuit’s leading public policy expert in your issue area — connecting it to relevant Intuit strategic big bets. Develop and execute a proactive public policy strategy aligned with Intuit’s business and customer priorities. Anticipate legislative and regulatory developments and identify emerging policy opportunities and risks. Move beyond monitoring policy developments to actively shape legislative and regulatory outcomes through sophisticated strategies. Build trusted relationships with policymakers, regulators, and their staff across Congress, the Administration, federal agencies, and other relevant institutions. Drive Intuit’s agenda through trade associations and industry bodies, taking an active leadership role in developing collective positions. Build coalitions with industry peers, customer and business organizations, think tanks, academics, civil society, and other stakeholders. Establish Intuit as a credible, constructive thought leader, representing the company at conferences, policy forums, roundtables, and other external engagements. Serve as a trusted strategic adviser to senior business, Product, and Technology leaders, translating complex policy developments into clear business implications and recommendations. Partner closely with Legal, Privacy, Data, AI, Product, Engineering, Security, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs teams to develop durable policy positions. Translate complex technical, economic, or policy concepts into clear, persuasive arguments for both policymakers and internal stakeholders. Help develop and execute Intuit’s global policy strategy in your issue area, connecting U.S. developments with emerging frameworks in other strategically important markets. Collaborate with colleagues across the Global Public Policy team, recognizing that policy issues increasingly intersect across Intuit’s strategic priorities. Qualifications Experience in government, Congress, a regulatory agency, technology company, trade association, think tank, or another relevant public policy environment. Deep subject-matter expertise in one or more of: AI governance, privacy and data protection, emerging technology policy, money and financial services policy, or small/mid-market business policy — together with a strong understanding of the broader policy landscape. A demonstrated record of shaping policy outcomes through direct government advocacy, trade associations, coalitions, and third-party engagement. Ability to develop proactive policy strategies that connect external legislative and regulatory developments with business and product strategy. Strong political and strategic judgment, with an understanding of the interaction between policy, customer trust, business strategy, and corporate reputation. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, able to make technically and complex issues clear and persuasive to senior policymakers and business leaders. Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving technology company, navigate ambiguity, and build strong partnerships across multiple functions and business units. A highly collaborative mindset and willingness to work across policy portfolios and geographies as part of a small, high-performing Global Public Policy team. What Success Looks Like Success means Intuit is not simply prepared for policy change in your area — Intuit is helping shape it. The successful candidate will ensure that: Policymakers and regulators understand Intuit’s technology, customers, and approach to responsible innovation. Intuit is a strong, credible voice in trade associations and coalitions shaping relevant policy debates. Senior leaders have an early and sophisticated understanding of emerging policy opportunities and risks. A forward-looking policy agenda is deeply integrated into Intuit’s customer and business priorities. Strong coalitions are built around policy outcomes that benefit Intuit’s customers. Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender. The expected base pay range for this position is: Washington $194,500 – $263,500 Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Morgan Health External Communications – Vice President
item.description: Morgan Health External Communications – Vice President Organization: JPMorgan Chase Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Base Pay/Salary New York,NY $123,500.00-$185,000.00; Washington,DC $123,500.00-$185,000.00 Job Description Morgan Health is a division of JPMorgan Chase focused on improving the quality, opportunity and affordability of employer-sponsored health care in the United States. Morgan Health strategically invests in health care companies that improve employer-sponsored health care, supports the JPMorgan Chase Benefits Plan in evaluating offerings for employees, shares insights with employers, and advocates for policies that drive innovation in the employer health care market. With a substantial employee base covered by its self-insured plan and a diverse client base engaged in the U.S. health care system, JPMorgan Chase is deeply committed to the Morgan Health mission. Morgan Health is seeking a Vice President of External Communications to highlight its efforts to improve employer-sponsored health care. As an External Communications Vice Present within Morgan Health, your work will include engagement with Morgan Health portfolio companies, promotion of data insights and research, advancement of key priorities (such as small business health care affordability), as well as policy advocacy. You bring experience leading content workstreams, including crafting impactful narratives—distilling complex health care topics into compelling stories—and driving integrated strategies across media channels. You will report to the Head of External Communications. Job Responsibilities: Support external content strategy and editorial calendar to maintain Morgan Health’s visibility and external engagement on key topics. Translate survey insights and data into compelling stories; Work with technical partners, including Morgan Health Data Science and Research and Policy and Advocacy teams, to extract key headlines from research. Create high-impact content by writing, editing, and shaping narratives that translate our work into clear, compelling communications. Partner across Morgan Health to build a steady content pipeline and align to priority workstreams and stakeholder needs. Drive content distribution and optimization across priority channels (Morgan Health website, LinkedIn, etc.), using performance insights to iterate and improve. Monitor external stories and health care trends to help define Morgan Health’s perspective and inform narrative development and content strategies. Support leadership visibility by identifying external opportunities and developing messaging, briefs, and related materials. Identify and execute opportunities to amplify Morgan Health through broader JPMorgan Chase channels and partners, ensuring brand and channel alignment. Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills: 8+ years of health care communications and content experience Experience working with research and data, including in partnership with health care research and/or advocacy groups Exceptional writer/editor with demonstrated ability to consistently create content directly Demonstrated ability to own internal client relationships, manage stakeholders, and operate in a matrixed organization. Strong judgment, attention to detail, and project management skills. Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills: Multimedia content production experience (or strong ability to partner with producers/creative). Executive thought leadership and LinkedIn content strategy experience. To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT). About Us JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world’s most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management. We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process. We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants’ and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation. JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans About the Team Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we’re setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success. Responsibilities Develop and distribute internal communications aligned with strategic messaging. Draft and publish workforce messages promoting FO events such as All Hands meetings. Gather and summarize key topics for the weekly newsletter to engage the workforce. Collaborate with stakeholders, designers, and technical teams to develop and update digital content. Create and implement visually appealing, user-friendly web pages and newsletters. Ensure compliance with Section 508, GDPR, CCCA, and other regulatory standards. Identify and resolve website issues, coordinating with IT and external vendors as needed. Gather content requirements and update web text, images, videos, and multimedia. Provide editorial quality control and support mass email distribution via EDGE Mass Email Tool. Work with various stakeholders to develop and deploy new communication strategies. Act as a technical liaison between users, managers, and developers. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree (four years of relevant experience may substitute in lieu of a degree) and 10+ years of relevant communications experience. Hands-on direct experience with Joomla, EDGE, and excellent writing skills are required. Excellent verbal and written communication skills Strong project management skills; ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines Expert level of hands-on experience with Joomla, EDGE, SharePoint, WordPress, Microsoft Office Suite Salary Range USD $200,000.00 – USD $200,000.00 /Yr. The Markon pay range for this position is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law. Look no further than Markon, a premier consulting firm deeply dedicated to advancing our nation’s most critical missions. At Markon, we don’t just offer jobs – we offer opportunities for personal and professional transformation. Empowering our employees to lead, innovate, and excel, we foster an environment where new ideas are not just welcomed but celebrated. As a perennial Washington Post Top Workplace, we prioritize the well-being and success of our team members, ensuring they can bring their best selves to work. Headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, Markon has garnered national recognition for our unwavering dedication to excellence in serving the intelligence community, as well as federal civilian and defense agencies. Our growing reach extends across 17 states, 116 countries, and 5 continents, where our team of dynamic professionals collaborates to deliver unparalleled program and project management services. Markon values people and the tremendous impact each individual can make – which is why we’re consistently recognized as one of the best places to work in federal government consulting. Here, you can help solve the nation’s most important challenges, surrounded by colleagues who help you grow, advance, and succeed. We are deeply dedicated to what matters – bringing out the best in each other to advance our clients’ missions. Join us and make a meaningful impact. Markon is an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: State and Industry Affairs Manager
item.description: State and Industry Affairs Manager Organization: National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Organization Summary The National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW), the Washington, DC-based trade association representing an industry that encompasses hundreds of thousands of U.S. businesses and over $8.4 trillion in annual revenue. Job Summary Reporting to NAW’s Chief Government Relations Officer and coordinating with NAW’s federal, legal and political team, the State and Industry Affairs Manager will be a key team member of a growing government relations practice managing NAW’s policy interests at the state level. Using software and news sources, as well as developing their own relationships with government officials, regulatory bodies, and industry stakeholders, the Manager will monitor state level legislation and regulation that may impact member companies. Key policy areas include taxation, labor and workforce regulations, warehousing and transportation, technology and extended producer responsibility, among others. The Manager will develop relationships directly with NAW member companies and trade associations, coordinating across departments to engage members on policy and political issues to further the grassroots advocacy efforts of NAW. Essential Job Responsibilities Issue Monitoring and Analysis – Use of software, news sources, and/or consultants to stay informed about legislative and regulatory developments at the state level that may impact the distribution industry, conducting thorough analysis to assess potential implications and inform strategic advocacy efforts. Member Communication – Produce a bi-weekly State GR Newsletter for distribution to NAW member companies on key state legislative activities. Grassroots Strategy and Communications – Manage NAW’s grassroots communications, including identifying and drafting timely grassroots alerts as part of the state and Federal GR programs, and NAW’s Legal Policy Center. Coalition Building – Build and maintain relationships with peers in industry associations, advocacy groups, and other stakeholders to amplify NAW’s advocacy efforts and advance shared policy objectives. Compliance and Reporting – Ensure compliance with relevant state lobbying and disclosure requirements, and accurately report on advocacy activities, expenditures, and outcomes. Policy Advocacy – Engage as needed with state legislators, regulatory agencies, and other policymakers to advocate for legislation and regulations that support the interests of the wholesale distribution industry. Requirements Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Strong understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes, especially as they relate to free enterprise business issues and the interaction of the business community with policy makers. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex issues to diverse audiences and tailor messaging to achieve advocacy objectives. Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships with policymakers, stakeholders, and industry peers. Ability to analyze policy issues, identify opportunities for advocacy, and develop effective advocacy strategies. Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Team player with a willingness to pitch in on projects outside of job description to further NAW and NAW’s member companies’ goals. Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree in in political science, public policy, law, or a related field, required 3+ years of experience in government, government affairs, public policy, advocacy, or related roles, with a proven track record of successful advocacy at the state level Other Requirements: Strong Microsoft Office Suite skills and familiarity with other common business technology tools. Knowledge of the wholesale-distribution industry, desirable. Work Environment: The position is based at NAW’s headquarters office in Washington, DC, near Metro Center. NAW is currently offering a hybrid work model. Employees are required to be in the office Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and upon request for mandatory meetings or events. Employees are provided the opportunity to work remotely on Monday and Friday. The hybrid work model is subject to change. Travel: up to 5-10%* *This position requires limited travel within the United States. Travel may include visits to NAW member companies, state capitals, industry conferences, stakeholder meetings, and other relevant events. The travel frequency may vary depending on legislative and regulatory developments, advocacy priorities, and other business needs, but candidates should be prepared for travelling 5-10% of working time. Experience level and other factors will determine the final salary level, with a starting salary range of $70,000–$80,000/year. The position also offers competitive benefits, including health and wellness coverage, a 401(k) plan, and other benefits for eligible employees. item.title: National Social Media Coordinator
item.description: National Social Media Coordinator Organization: National Marine Sanctuary Foundation Location: Silver Spring, MD Date Posted: 10/20/2026 What We Need The National Marine Sanctuary Foundation, a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that is a leading voice for U.S. protected waters, is seeking a National Social Media Coordinator, a position responsible for developing and implementing social media initiatives for the National Marine Sanctuary System. Specifically, the National Social Media Coordinator will support work that is part of the scope of a cooperative agreement between the National Marine Sanctuary Foundation and NOAA Office of National Marine Sanctuaries focused on engaging the public with the 18 site in the National Marine Sanctuary System. The National Social Media Coordinator will play a key role in supporting the National Marine Sanctuary System on behalf of the Foundation by managing headquarters-level social media accounts for NOAA’s Office of National Marine Sanctuaries (ONMS), including Facebook, X, YouTube, Flickr, LinkedIn, and Instagram. The selected candidate will develop strategies and initiatives to increase organic reach, contribute to stronger engagement with key stakeholders, and be a voice in helping to ensure that social media efforts are in alignment with ONMS strategic priorities. The National Social Media Coordinator will work day-to-day as a member of the ONMS Communications and Engagement Division. The position will be based in NOAA’s ONMS headquarters office in Silver Spring, MD. A belief in our mission, excellent project management skills, as well as a strong team mentality, is a must. The National Marine Sanctuary Foundation is committed to a culture of inclusion, equity, and belonging. We are dedicated to attracting and retaining a diverse staff. We honor experiences, perspectives, and unique identities, and welcome the contributions that you can bring to the dedicated team. With a diverse team of employees, we can grow and learn better together and achieve our mission to protect the health of the ocean, coasts and Great Lakes for current and future generations. What You’ll Do The person in this role will be a creative, analytical thinker with strong content development skills and a passion for digital media. As the National Social Media Coordinator, you’ll be embedded with the NOAA Office of National Marine Sanctuaries, and be responsible for: Day-to-day management of headquarters-level social media channels, including curating posts, sourcing assets and additional information, collaboration with other teams, managing and monitoring social media platforms, and engaging with the social community and responding to posts and messages in a timely manner. Script and edit video content to be posted to social media platforms, adapting format to platform needs. Manage the development and execution of all social campaigns to drive public engagement and strengthen National Marine Sanctuary System awareness and brand equity. Own and manage the social media calendar, coordinating releases with the communications and media team. Share strategies and recommendations for social media platforms, best practices, industry trends, tech applications, and emerging opportunities. Lead quarterly update, brainstorming, and content ideation sessions with field site social media coordinators. Provide communication and social media expertise and problem solving to field site social media coordinators on a case-by-case basis, and manage and update social media policies, including ONMS best practices. Monitor and evaluate all social media for both headquarters and site channels, providing regular and specific event reports on coverage and influence with analysis and recommendations based on the data. Identify opportunities for partner outreach, including maintaining Letters of Agreement with formalized partnerships. Serve as liaison to NOS and NOAA social media team leads. Ensure all posts are fact-checked and proof-read, and that all necessary permissions have been obtained before sharing images or video. Produce error-free, plain-language content that adheres to ONMS messaging and the Associated Press style guide. Ensure products meet Section 508 requirements, including closed captioning and text descriptions for video products. Participate in outreach or special events as needed. Manage social media volunteer interns, as needed. Work closely with the National Marine Sanctuary Foundation social media coordinator to ensure close connections on national campaigns. Host the Get Into Your Sanctuary Photo Contest, taking place annually from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend. This includes complete management and organization of winning photos, contestant information, submissions received, social media promotion and announcing, as well as additional outreach as needed. Maintain proficiency in NOAA diving standards and training, including CPR/First Aid/O2 administration, maintain dive gear Assist production team in the field with media management and additional camera work as needed. Who You Are As the National Social Media Coordinator, you’re a mission-driven, internet-savvy individual who has a passion for sharing the marine environment, and can develop and activate digital strategies that bring the wonder and value of the entire National Marine Sanctuary System to life for your audience. You have a commitment to engaging storytelling, a strong sense of initiative, and work well independently. Required Qualifications 3–5 years of progressive responsibility directing and shepherding social media campaigns and development of media content, including experience creating videos; Excellent communication, organizational, writing, and project management skills; Experience producing plain-language web content, with a focus on social media for a federal agency, non-profit organization, congressional office, private company, or other professional organization; Expert experience in social media analytics/insight reporting (Meta Business Suite and X, LinkedIn, and YouTube analytics) ; Knowledge of Associated Press news writing style; High level of accuracy and attention to detail; Ability to perform under tight deadlines and juggle multiple tasks and projects; Demonstrated initiative, ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented and collaborative environment; Proficient with video editing software, preferably with the Adobe Creative Suite and Da Vinci Resolve software; Adept in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign) ; Adept with Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace; Experience working for or with federal or state agencies. Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of working with/engaging influencers; Knowledge of HTML web coding and graphic design; Experience and/or knowledge of national marine sanctuaries; A sincere interest in, and commitment to, ONMS’ and the Foundation’s missions. Why You Will Love Us The National Marine Sanctuary Foundation (“Foundation”) is a leading voice for U.S. protected waters, working with communities to conserve and expand those special places for a healthy ocean, coasts, and Great Lakes. The Foundation works in close partnership with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to increase stewardship of our ocean and Great Lakes through on-the-water conservation projects, and education and public outreach activities, and by support for research. Together, we safeguard species and the places they call home, and support coastal communities and economies. Dedicated and passionate staff committed to marine and Great Lakes Conservation Generous leave policy, plus paid time off the week between December 25 and January 1; and 12 paid holidays Health benefits: Medical with an FSA option; dental, and vision Foundation paid Life and Disability Insurance Preparing for the Future: 403(B) with employer contribution after one year of service Commuter Benefits Compensation and Benefits: $65,000 – $72,000 per year based on experience. The Foundation offers a competitive benefits package. Apply through the Foundation’s online portal . A resume, cover letter, and three professional references are required. Applications received by October 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET will be preferred. _____________________________________________________________________ The National Marine Sanctuary Foundation is committed to equal opportunity and a collaborative work environment. We are dedicated to attracting and retaining a diverse staff. We honor experiences, perspectives, and unique identities, and welcome the contributions that you can bring to the dedicated team. With a diverse team of employees, we can grow and learn better together and achieve our mission to protect the health of the ocean, coasts and Great Lakes for current and future generations. item.title: Communication Coordinator, Internal Communications
item.description: Communication Coordinator, Internal Communications Organization: Nature Conservancy Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Description What We Can Achieve Together: The Communication Coordinator, Internal Communications, serves as the operational backbone of the Global Internal Communications team, helping maintain the processes, workflows, tools, and resources that support effective communications across the organization. In this role, they coordinate communications projects, support key staff-facing channels, draft and edit communications materials, and assist with analytics and reporting. They work closely with internal stakeholders, vendors, and partner teams to deliver clear, consistent, and engaging communications that inform and connect employees. By providing strong coordination and execution support, the Communication Coordinator enables the Internal Communications team to focus on strategic communications, employee engagement, organizational change, and leadership communications. We’re Looking for You: You are a highly organized communicator who enjoys bringing structure, coordination, and follow-through to complex projects. You excel at managing details while keeping an eye on the bigger picture, ensuring work moves forward smoothly and stakeholders stay informed. In this role, you’ll support the planning and execution of internal communications projects, channels, events, and team operations. You’ll help manage project timelines, track deliverables, coordinate stakeholder follow-up, monitor team inboxes, and support translation and vendor workflows. You’ll also play a key role in planning and delivering organization-wide events and communication initiatives.You are excited to support employee-facing channels that help keep staff informed, engaged and connected across the organization. You are comfortable working across multiple priorities and helping teams stay organized. You’ll support communication intake and governance processes, ensuring requests are appropriately routed, required information is collected, and projects align with established workflows and priorities. You enjoy creating structure behind the scenes and helping teams work more efficiently through strong coordination, consistent processes and thoughtful execution. You are a strong writer and editor who can draft, adapt and proofread content for a variety of internal communications channels. The ideal candidate is curious about employee engagement and communications effectiveness. You’ll help maintain dashboards, reporting tools, and performance metrics, and use data to identify trends and insights that inform content, channel, and audience engagement strategies. You are comfortable working independently, exercising sound judgment and managing projects from start to finish. Strong attention to detail, project coordination skills, and a collaborative mindset are essential for success in this role. What You’ll Bring Bachelor’s degree in a related field and 2+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Strong project coordination skills, including managing timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder relationships. Excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Experience supporting employee, internal or organizational communications across multiple channels, including newsletters, email, intranet, or digital platforms. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Experience collaborating with internal stakeholders, partners, or vendors. Strong judgment, initiative, and follow-through when working independently. Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Comfort working with data, dashboards, reporting tools, and communications metrics. Interest in using audience insights and engagement data to improve communications. Familiarity with communications platforms, content management systems, newsletter tools or digital publishing technologies. Multi-lingual skills and cross-cultural experience are a plus. Salary Information: The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $27.88 – $41.75 hourly rate. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate’s location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment. Who We Are: The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor. One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.” What We Bring: Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world! TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here. We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ. Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible. Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub. The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law. The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy’s background screening process. Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings! TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to [email protected] with Request for Accommodation in the subject line. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Communications Manager (Hybrid)
item.description: Communications Manager (Hybrid) Organization: Pathways to Housing DC (Pathways DC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Salary: $70,000 annually About Pathways to Housing DC Everyone deserves a place to call home. Founded in 2004, Pathways to Housing DC (Pathways DC) provides home, health, and hope to more than 3,500 individuals each year who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. Leveraging 22 years of experience and a bold vision, Pathways DC programs and services include Homeless Street Outreach and support services at the Downtown DC Day Services Center; Housing Case Management; Outpatient Mental Health Treatment; a Youth Drop-In Center; Medical Respite Homes; and more. Our programs and services have a vast reach and impact–serving individuals with mental health challenges; women fleeing domestic violence; Veterans fighting new battles following the traumas of war; and youth exiting the foster care system with no real place to ever call home. We know that with the right resources at the right time, homelessness in our community is solvable. As the originator of the Housing First model in the region, Pathways DC is proud to provide housing across all eight Wards in Washington, DC and with an expanding footprint in Montgomery County, MD. Our scope helps to promote client choice and self-determination in our work and builds a high housing retention success rate each year. The Opportunity Behind every program at Pathways DC are people, relationships, and stories that help explain how Housing First works. As our Communications Manager, you’ll help bring that work to audiences across the DC region and beyond. Working closely with the Director of Institutional Advancement and development colleagues, you’ll develop and carry out a communications plan that builds awareness of Pathways DC, engages supporters, and supports fundraising. You’ll manage our digital channels and create content that helps donors, partners, and community members understand our programs and the people we serve. This newly created position offers room to shape how we communicate. We’re looking for someone who enjoys finding a story, asking questions, and turning what they learn into clear, engaging content. You should also enjoy the work that keeps communications running: planning a content calendar, coordinating reviews, organizing assets, and getting materials out on time. You’ll work with colleagues across programs and locations, spending time in the field to gather stories, photos, and video. You’ll bring care to how those stories are told, respecting each participant’s dignity, privacy, and choices. The development team works remotely, with occasional in-person work at the DC office, program sites, and events. At Pathways DC, you’ll join a mission-driven team committed to ending homelessness and helping individuals achieve housing stability, recovery, and improved quality of life. Every day, you’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the lives of the people we serve. Key Responsibilities Plan and manage communications Work with the Director of Institutional Advancement to develop and carry out a communications plan, aligning outreach with organizational and fundraising priorities. Manage a content calendar across email, social media, our website, publications, and events. Coordinate content requests, reviews, approvals, and publication deadlines with colleagues across the organization. Maintain a consistent organizational voice and visual identity, and develop practical guidelines and templates for staff. Keep website content accurate and current, including program information, stories, events, and opportunities to support Pathways DC. Track and report on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for all digital activity, including website traffic, email open rates, and social media growth. Use analytics to adjust strategy, maximize donor conversion rates, and improve audience reach. Develop content and tell our story Act as the brand guardian, ensuring consistent messaging, tone, and visual identity across all platforms. Write and edit newsletters, website content, social media posts, impact reports, presentations, and other public-facing materials. Build relationships with program colleagues to identify stories and gather information from across the organization. Translate program data and complex information into clear, accessible content for various audiences. Interview staff and program participants, following organizational consent and confidentiality practices. Capture and edit photography and video at programs and events for use across communications channels. Ensure stories and images respect participants’ preferences and avoid stigmatizing or sensational language. Engage audiences and support fundraising Manage email and social media communications, tailoring content and formats to each channel. Partner with the Individual Giving Manager and other development colleagues on fundraising appeals, donor updates, and campaign materials. Develop communications and materials for fundraising and community events, including invitations, promotional content, signage, and follow-up. Track newsletter, website, and social media performance and use the results to improve content and outreach. Test new approaches to reaching and engaging donors, partners, and community members. Coordinate design and production Design and produce materials using tools such as Canva and Adobe Creative Cloud. Maintain an organized, accessible archive of photography, video, design files, templates, and completed materials. In partnership with the Director of Institutional Advancement, coordinate freelancers and vendors, as needed, for photography, video, design, printing, and other production needs. Manage production timelines and review materials for accuracy, readability, accessibility, and consistency. Use technology, including AI tools where appropriate, to support drafting, editing, and recurring workflows. Verify AI-assisted work and follow organizational standards for confidentiality and responsible use of information. Qualifications We recognize that relevant experience comes from a wide range of personal, professional, and educational opportunities. We take a broad view of each candidate’s experience and do not require a particular degree. Required qualifications At least three years of relevant communications, marketing, journalism, or content development experience. A minimum of a High School Diploma/GED Strong writing and editing skills, with experience adapting content for different audiences and channels. Experience managing digital communications, including email, social media, and website content. Experience creating visual materials using Canva, Adobe Creative Cloud, or comparable tools. Ability to capture and edit photos and short videos for digital communications. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects, coordinate feedback, and meet deadlines. Comfort interviewing people and working with colleagues to gather stories and information. Sound judgment when handling sensitive information, participant stories, and public-facing communications. Ability to work independently, take initiative, and stay in communication with colleagues. Interest in Pathways DC’s mission and willingness to learn about Housing First. Ability to attend occasional in-person meetings, program visits, and events in the Washington, DC area. Nice to have, but not required: Experience with nonprofit communications or fundraising campaigns. Familiarity with Meta Business Suite, Adobe InDesign, email marketing platforms, or website content management systems. Experience using communications metrics to improve content and audience engagement. Familiarity with accessible design and digital content practices. Experience working in housing, homelessness services, behavioral health, or a related field. Benefits: Beyond the rewarding work of seeing lives transformed every day, Pathways DC is proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package to our staff, including: 15 days of paid vacation to start 11 paid holidays 10 paid sick/wellness days Health insurance for individuals, partners, and families Employer-sponsored Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) Dental and vision insurance Employer-paid short and long-term disability insurance Employer-paid life insurance 403(b) retirement plan with employer match Employer-paid Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Optional employee-paid benefits, including legal coverage, and pre-tax commuter benefits To Apply Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest and relevant experience through ADP Workforce Now . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage you to apply early by November 15, 2026. Pathways to Housing DC is an Equal Opportunity Employer and values diversity in the workplace. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds and lived experiences to apply.
