item.title: Deputy Vice President, Law (Artificial Intelligence)
item.description: Deputy Vice President, Law (Artificial Intelligence) Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Deputy Vice President, Artificial Intelligence for the Law team to support its legal and policy efforts related to emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) and related issues of importance to the biopharmaceutical industry. The Deputy Vice President will serve as PhRMA’s lead legal strategist on issues involving data governance and privacy; national and biosecurity; AI-related safety and product liability; AI governance and regulatory oversight and transparency; and AI infrastructure and competitive access impacting the biopharmaceutical industry. This role will provide strategic legal counsel across the organization, lead cross-functional initiatives, engage with member companies and external stakeholders, and help shape PhRMA’s positions on rapidly evolving legal and policy issues at the intersection of technology, innovation, and healthcare. The position requires a forward-thinking legal leader who can anticipate emerging risks and opportunities, navigate complex regulatory frameworks, and help advance industry priorities in an increasingly digital environment. The Deputy Vice President will: Provide strategic legal counsel to PhRMA leadership and staff on AI, data governance and privacy, biosecurity, and technology-related issues affecting the association and its members, in coordination with internal subject matter experts and issue area leads. Lead the development and implementation of PhRMA’s legal strategy related to artificial intelligence, data privacy, biosecurity, data governance, and emerging technologies of interest to the biopharmaceutical industry. Monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, litigation and policy developments related to AI, data governance and privacy, biosecurity, and related legislative and regulatory developments at the federal, state, and international levels, in coordination with internal subject matter experts and issue area leads. Assess emerging legislation, regulatory proposals, liability frameworks, and data governance issues affecting the biopharmaceutical industry and provide actionable recommendations to leadership, in coordination with internal subject matter experts and issue area leads. Develop and maintain expertise on emerging legal and regulatory frameworks on AI, including AI governance requirements, privacy and data governance laws, biosecurity considerations, and digital health regulations addressing the use of AI. Represent PhRMA before government agencies, policymakers, coalitions, trade associations, and other stakeholders on legal matters related to AI, data governance and privacy, biosecurity, and other emerging technology issues. Lead and facilitate member company legal workgroup(s) (as deemed necessary) focused on AI governance and regulations, data governance and privacy, and other emerging technology and biosecurity issues. Coordinate with PhRMA colleagues, departments, member companies, outside counsel, consultants, and industry partners to develop and advance policy positions and advocacy strategies. Draft legal analyses, position papers, comment letters, guidance documents, presentations, and other materials for internal and external audiences. Collaborate with PhRMA attorneys and IT staff on contracts, AI governance, and operational issues involving technology vendors, data-sharing arrangements, cybersecurity matters, and AI-enabled tools, as requested. Collaborate with PhRMA attorneys on related legal issues, including FDA regulatory, intellectual property, and international, as requested. Build and maintain strong relationships with member company legal, privacy, national security, and government affairs professionals. Support crisis response efforts related to biosecurity, data governance and privacy, and other emerging technology issues as needed. Perform other duties as assigned. Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a visionary, relationship-driven, and impact-focused individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Deputy Vice President leverages deep expertise to guide strategic priorities, anticipates challenges, and aligns departmental efforts with broader organizational goals. A successful DVP is a trusted advisor, skilled in stakeholder influence and resource management, and leads cross-functional initiatives with clarity, confidence, and purpose. Professional Experience Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an accredited law school. Active membership in good standing with at least one state bar. Minimum of 10 years of relevant legal experience in privacy, biosecurity, artificial intelligence, technology law, digital health, data governance, regulatory law, or related fields consistent with PhRMA’s Deputy Vice President level expectations. Demonstrated expertise in federal data governance and privacy laws, emerging AI governance and regulatory frameworks, and other related technology and national security laws/biosecurity programs. Significant experience advising organizations on complex legal, regulatory, and policy matters involving technology and data. Experience engaging with government agencies, policymakers, trade associations, industry coalitions, or other external stakeholders. Strong understanding of the legal and policy implications of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automated decision-making systems, and other emerging technologies. Exceptional writing, editing, analytical, and presentation skills. Proven ability to synthesize complex legal and technical concepts for executive and non-technical audiences. Demonstrated experience leading strategic initiatives and managing multiple high-priority projects simultaneously. Experience developing and maintaining productive relationships with senior stakeholders. Ability to exercise sound judgment and manage sensitive and confidential matters. Strong project management and organizational skills. Must be willing to travel as requested and be responsive/available after hours and on weekends. Preferred Experience Experience within the biopharmaceutical, healthcare, life sciences, technology, or highly regulated sectors. Experience leading industry workgroups, coalitions, or public policy initiatives. Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP), Certified Information Privacy Manager (CIPM), or similar credentials. Experience managing outside counsel and consultants. Potential Salary $243,200-$346,700 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: www.PhRMA.org www.Innovation.org www.AmericasMedicines.org www.Facebook.com/PhRMA www.Twitter.com/PhRMA What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a well-being program, an on-site fitness facility, back-up care, health advocate service, an employee assistance program, and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated onboarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast-paced career with their personal goals. Equal Opportunity Employer PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. The job description contains an overview of the activities and duties for this role. Responsibilities may change and new ones may be assigned at any time. item.title: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances, Federal
item.description: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances, Federal Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Director for the Advocacy and Strategic Alliances team to support its stakeholder engagement and advocacy efforts related to prescription medicine access and affordability. The Director will have a particular focus on Medicare Part B and issues affecting physician-administered medicines, including the implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act’s (IRA) Medicare drug price negotiation program, and Most Favored Nation (MFN) and related government pricing policies. The Director will develop and execute stakeholder engagement strategies that advance PhRMA priorities, with a primary focus on health care providers and provider organizations, as well as patient advocacy organizations representing the oncology mental health communities, and other health care constituencies. The role will assess how emerging federal policy proposals affect providers and patients and translate those implications into effective external engagement strategies. The Director will work closely with colleagues across PhRMA, member companies, and external partners to coordinate advocacy strategies and ensure stakeholder perspectives inform and strengthen PhRMA’s broader policy and advocacy efforts. The Director will report to the Deputy Vice President, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances. The Director will: Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and advocacy strategies related to government price controls and access to medicines, with particular emphasis on Medicare Part B, the Medicare drug price negotiation program, MFN and related federal policy developments. Serve as a primary Alliance resource on issues affecting Medicare Part B and physician-administered medicines, translating complex policy developments into actionable stakeholder engagement strategies. Assess the implications of federal pricing and reimbursement policies for providers, patients, and other health care stakeholders and identify opportunities to engage constituencies in support of shared priorities. Build, strengthen, and maintain relationships with health care providers and provider organizations, with particular attention to constituencies affected by Part B policy and reimbursement changes. Develop and maintain strategic relationships with patient advocacy organizations – including those focused on oncology and mental health – and other health care stakeholders whose priorities intersect with PhRMA’s policy agenda. Identify areas of alignment among diverse constituencies and develop opportunities for collaboration, coalition-building, and coordinated advocacy. Monitor the federal legislative, regulatory, and political environment to identify emerging developments related to government price controls, Medicare Part B, the IRA, MFN, and other policies affecting access to medicines. Coordinate closely with PhRMA’s Policy, Federal Advocacy, Public Affairs, International and other teams to ensure Alliance strategies are informed by PhRMA policy positions and integrated with broader organizational priorities. Work with internal subject matter experts to translate complex policy issues into clear, compelling materials and messages appropriate for stakeholder audiences. Develop briefing materials, presentations, talking points, stakeholder analyses, engagement plans, and other written products that accurately reflect PhRMA’s established positions. Represent PhRMA with external organizations and stakeholders on established policy positions relevant to the role’s portfolio. Plan and execute stakeholder meetings, roundtables, briefings, coalition activities, and other engagement opportunities designed to advance shared policy objectives. Gather stakeholder perspectives and intelligence and communicate relevant developments, opportunities, and risks to PhRMA leadership and cross-functional colleagues. Support select international advocacy initiatives involving pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies, including issues where international price controls intersect with U.S. policy proposals and stakeholder interests. Coordinate with member companies to obtain input, identify stakeholder opportunities, and support alignment around advocacy strategies and priorities. Manage projects and, as appropriate, consultants and external partners, including timelines, deliverables, and coordination across multiple workstreams. Continuously evaluate engagement strategies and recommend adjustments based on changes in the policy environment, stakeholder landscape, and organizational priorities. Perform other duties as assigned. Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a mission-driven, agile, and solutions-oriented individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Director brings strong subject matter expertise, manages multiple complex projects simultaneously, and guides others toward shared objectives. This role requires clear communication, effective relationship management, and the ability to translate strategic goals into actionable plans. A successful Director demonstrates foresight, critical thinking, and the ability to build consensus across diverse stakeholders. Professional Requirements Bachelor’s degree required (Master’s degree in Health Policy, Public Policy, Communications or related field preferred). 6+ years of relevant professional experience, including experience in leadership roles Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder projects or initiatives Experience with Medicare Part B policy, prescription drug pricing and reimbursement, government price controls, or related health policy issues. Exceptional writing, editing, and presentation skills, with experience developing content for executive audiences Experience engaging health care providers, patient advocacy organizations, disease-specific organizations, or other health care constituencies. Demonstrated sound judgment and ability to work independently while recognizing issues that require broader organizational coordination or leadership guidance. Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities Demonstrated experience managing staff and/or overseeing consultants and vendors Excellent verbal communication, presentation, active listening, and interpersonal skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools; experience with project management and budget tracking systems preferred Must be willing to travel and be responsive/available after hours and on weekends. Preferred Experience Advanced degree in public policy, health policy, public health, law, political science, or a related discipline. Experience working on Medicare Part B, physician-administered medicines, Medicare drug price negotiation, IRA implementation, MFN, or other pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement issues. Established relationships with health care provider organizations, oncology organizations, patient advocacy organizations, mental health organizations, or related constituencies. Experience developing or executing coalition-based advocacy campaigns at the federal level. Experience working with Congress, federal agencies, trade associations, advocacy organizations, or other organizations involved in federal health policy. Familiarity with international pharmaceutical pricing, reimbursement, market access, or government price-control policies. Potential Salary $110,500-151,900 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: www.PhRMA.org www.Innovation.org www.AmericasMedicines.org www.Facebook.com/PhRMA www.Twitter.com/PhRMA What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a well-being program, an on-site fitness facility, back-up care, health advocate service, an employee assistance program, and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated onboarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team me

item.title: Director of US Government Engagement
item.description: Director of US Government Engagement Organization: Q-CTRL Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 About the team At Q-CTRL, the Government Engagement team works at the intersection of policy, international engagement, and national security to influence how governments govern and fund the development and adoption of quantum technologies. As trusted and respected leaders in the sector, we build enduring relationships with politicians, policymakers, and defense forces around the world to secure opportunities for Q-CTRL to deliver cutting-edge sovereign capability. We empower all areas of the business to understand and navigate government decision-making. About the role Reporting to the Global Head of Government Engagement, you’ll lead Q-CTRL’s US government engagement activities, working closely with our business development, technical, product, and marketing teams. You’ll shape policy and funding initiatives, build trusted relationships, and secure opportunities for Q-CTRL to partner commercially and strategically with government to deliver quantum computing and quantum sensing capabilities that advance US defense and economic interests. What you’ll be doing: Develop and execute Q-CTRL’s US government engagement strategy, setting clear priorities for policy, legislative, and funding outcomes that support our growth and the adoption of quantum technologies. Build and maintain trusted, bipartisan relationships with congressional offices and committees, the Department of War, federal agencies and state governments. Serve as a trusted representative of company interests in political and policy forums, including engagements supporting business development with the USG. Shape policy, legislation, and funding decisions through targeted advocacy, including developing proposals for authorization and appropriations processes and building support among key decision-makers. Work closely with business development and technical colleagues to identify, assess, and secure government funding and partnership opportunities, connecting Q-CTRL’s capabilities with government priorities and mission needs. Monitor and anticipate policy, legislative, budget, and regulatory developments, translating them into timely advice and recommended actions for company leadership. Represent Q-CTRL in industry associations, think tanks, and policy forums, building coalitions that advance shared priorities and establish Q-CTRL as a trusted voice on quantum technology. Other duties within the Employee’s skills and experience, or with reasonable training. Ideally you’ll have: 7+ years of relevant experience in government, congressional affairs, public policy, or government relations, for example as a congressional staffer, government official, military officer, or lobbyist. A demonstrated track record of shaping government decisions, with tangible achievements in policy development, legislation, or public funding. A strong understanding of US federal policymaking and the legislative, authorization, appropriations, and agency budget processes, including when and how to engage effectively. An established network across Capitol Hill, the executive branch, key federal departments, and the ability to build trusted relationships across political affiliations and institutions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex technical information into clear, persuasive arguments tailored to government audiences. A collaborative approach and the ability to work across business functions to raise Q-CTRL’s profile and secure commercial opportunities. It would be fantastic if you have these skills/experience but not essential: Experience working with the Department of War and congressional defense committees, including familiarity with defense budgets, acquisition pathways, and the transition of emerging technologies into operational use. Experience working in a technology startup or scaleup, particularly in a role connecting government engagement with commercial growth. Experience in the advanced technology, defense, or aerospace sectors. Experience shaping policy or funding for quantum or other critical technologies, such as AI, semiconductors, space, or advanced sensing. Experience with state government engagement, economic development initiatives, and allied technology cooperation through frameworks such as AUKUS. We take a multidisciplinary approach to quantum computing research, bringing together experts from diverse fields. We particularly value versatile and self-motivated problem solvers. If you are passionate about making quantum computers useful, we strongly encourage you to apply, even if you do not meet all of the requirements listed above. Salary The targeted base salary range for this position is between $210,000 – $260,000 and will ultimately be determined by specific job-related skills, experience, level, location and other contributing factors. This role will be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus and the opportunity to equity and other forms of compensation outside of the targeted base salary range. This position is eligible for Q-CTRL’s U.S. health insurance benefits, subject to plan eligibility requirements, as well as HSA, FSA, PTO, Company paid parental leave, 401k with an employer match, and a Learning, Development and Wellness allowance. For more information on benefits at Q-CTRL, please visit our careers page at https://q-ctrl.com/careers. Should you have any questions related to the compensation package, please speak directly with the Talent Acquisition representative. About Q-CTRL Q-CTRL is the global leader in AI-powered quantum control infrastructure software. We build the tools that make quantum technology useful, solving the hardest challenges in quantum computing and quantum sensing to deliver real-world impact. Founded in 2017, we operate globally with offices in Sydney, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Huntsville, Berlin, and Oxford. Our teams bring together technical and multi-disciplinary expertise across the product lifecycle, and we’re hiring talent to help scale every part of the business. We work quickly to turn cutting-edge science into deployable technology. In 2024 we raised US$113 million in Series B funding, the largest aggregate investment for a quantum software company. Six months later we delivered the first commercial quantum advantage with Ironstone Opal, our field-validated quantum navigation solution for defense and industry. At Q-CTRL, we prioritize outcomes over hours. We offer flexibility, equity potential, and competitive benefits that reflect our high-performance culture. If you’re ready to help shape the future of quantum, we’d love to hear from you! Please be advised that our communications will only come from the @q-ctrl.com domain. All our active job postings are available on our company website. To recruitment agencies, we do not accept unsolicited branded profiles and are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. We are seeking a creative, energetic, and results-driven Social Media, Marketing & eCommerce Manager to elevate our brand presence, create compelling content, and drive business growth through innovative digital marketing strategies. Position Summary The Social Media, Marketing & eCommerce Manager will lead the company’s digital presence through social media management, content creation, photography, videography, graphic design, website management, and eCommerce initiatives. This role is ideal for a highly creative storyteller who can capture the excitement of our events and transform it into engaging content that drives brand awareness, customer engagement, and sales. To Apply: Please submit your resume along with a portfolio showcasing your photography, videography, graphic design, and social media work to [email protected] om .. Produce and edit high-quality photos and videos for marketing, advertising, and social media. Create event highlight reels, promotional videos, behind-the-scenes content, and client testimonials. Create engaging social media campaigns, reels, stories, and promotional content. Monitor analytics and optimize campaigns to improve engagement and reach. Sales Support Collaborate with the sales team to support business development efforts. Develop marketing materials that assist with client acquisition and retention. Creative mind and eye for detail. Strong photography and videography skills with a professional portfolio. Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere Pro, InDesign) and Canva. Experience creating content for social media platforms. Knowledge of SEO, Google Analytics, and digital advertising. Strong communication, organizational, and project management skills. Ability to work independently while managing multiple deadlines. Preferred Hospitality, catering, events, restaurant, or luxury brand experience. Experience with WordPress, Shopify, WooCommerce, or similar platforms. Video animation and motion graphics experience. Drone photography/videography experience. item.title: Government Affairs Manager
item.description: Government Affairs Manager Organization: Governors Highway Safety Association Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 The Governors Highway Safety Association (GHSA) is seeking a full-time Government Affairs Manager. The Government Affairs Manager plays an important role in advancing the organization’s legislative and regulatory advocacy priorities while helping shape the policy landscape for roadway safety. The Government Affairs Manager supports the activities of the Government Affairs Team across federal policy, regulatory, and industry engagement efforts. Responsibilities include direct engagement with federal policymakers, conducting policy and legislative research, developing advocacy materials and strategic communications, monitoring policy developments, supporting member engagement activities and contributing to the execution of GHSA’s advocacy strategy. Federal Advocacy (35%) Policy Research (30%) Policy Communication (15%) Government Affairs Team Support (15%) CEO Partnership Support (5%) Ideal candidates will have 3+ years of professional experience working in policy, advocacy, public affairs, government relations, communication, or related work. A bachelor’s degree is required. Experience conducting research and tracking/monitoring policy developments, required. The position requires up to 10% travel. GHSA represents the state and territorial highway safety offices that implement programs to address behavioral and highway safety issues, including occupant protection, impaired driving and speeding. GHSA provides leadership and advocacy for the States and Territories to improve traffic safety, influence national policy, enhance program management, and promote best practices. GHSA is located on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C. For more information about the Governors Highway Safety Association, see www.ghsa.org . GHSA is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. GHSA believes in the fundamental principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion and is committed to actively fostering varying experiences and perspectives. Starting salary is $75,000 – $85,000 + Benefits. GHSA offers telecommuting up to 2 days per week dependent on business needs. Interested candidates should send their resume and salary expectations to Elizabeth Richards at [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director of State Legislative and Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Senior Director of State Legislative and Regulatory Affairs Organization: Can Manufacturers Institute (CMI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 The Senior Director of State Legislative and Regulatory Affairs serves as CMI’s chief state lobbyist and regulatory affairs lead, representing the metal can industry before state legislatures, state regulatory agencies, and key stakeholders. This senior-level position for an experienced legislative and regulatory advocate is responsible for developing and executing effective state-level legislative and regulatory strategies that support the association’s mission and policy objectives. The internal CMI team, contracted state lobbyists, and aligned partner organizations will help this role deliver on CMI’s state government affairs agenda. This professional will work closely with CMI’s other government affairs staff member, who manages federal issues, to ensure state and national priorities are aligned and actions are communicated effectively to members. In addition to advocacy work, the Senior Director provides strategic guidance and staff leadership to the association’s technical and regulatory committees. Advocacy is a key activity at CMI. This critical position requires understanding the broad policy implications of legislation, policy decisions, and regulatory actions, and how CMI’s resources can be deployed to influence outcomes and advantage the metal can industry. Understanding political dynamics and the process of state administrative and legislative actions is essential for CMI to create leverage points and positive outcomes. Key Responsibilities: State Legislative Affairs (45%) Lead CMI’s state legislative advocacy efforts that enable the metal can industry to thrive, focusing on chemicals, food safety, product stewardship, recycling (e.g., extended producer responsibility), sustainability, energy, tax, and related policy areas. Draft position papers, testimony, comments, and legislative amendments, as well as serve as CMI’s lead spokesperson with state lawmakers and their staff, with insights derived from member engagement and other sources. Develop and execute state government relations strategies to elevate CMI’s presence and influence in key states on priority issues with a focus on developing long-term legislative champions and advancing industry priorities. Build and maintain relationships between CMI and allies, partners, and key state government stakeholders, including through initiating and supporting coalitions where appropriate. Coordinate opportunities for CMI members and staff to engage with and influence state lawmakers, including via direct meetings and fundraising. Accurately monitor relevant state bills via CMI’s legislative tracking tools. Manage contract lobbyists, public relations firms, and other outside members of the team that support CMI’s state advocacy efforts. State Regulatory Affairs (45%) Collaborate with CMI’s technical consultant to monitor via CMI’s tracking tools for regulatory developments affecting the can industry, prepare and submit regulatory comments, keep members aware of key regulatory actions, and proactively collect and disseminate information to influence regulatory actions for the benefit of the can industry. Lead development of a state regulatory strategy that results in CMI generating information and taking action that advances can industry priorities on key regulatory issues in critical states both in the near-term and long-term. Serve as the association’s point person for engagement with key state regulatory agencies (e.g., CalEPA, CalRecycle, CA Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment, WA Department of Ecology) with insights derived from member engagement and other sources. Committee Management (10%) Staff CMI’s regulatory/technical committees, which currently are the Food Safety and Product Stewardship Committee and the Environmental Health and Safety Committee, such that meetings are scheduled and effectively run, member questions and needs are appropriately addressed, relationships between CMI and its members are strengthened, and CMI gets the guidance and information from members that it needs to translate committee expertise into actionable public policy positions and actions. Qualifications: Experience Minimum of five years’ experience working in senior-level positions in government relations, regulatory affairs, or public policy. Experience inside of or engaging a state legislature or a regulatory agency is highly desired. Previous success in developing and successfully executing a state legislative or regulatory agenda is highly desired. Previous management of external consultants or lobbyists is preferred. Knowledge Deep understanding of the state legislative and regulatory process. Knowledge of packaging; chemicals; food safety; sustainability; recycling (e.g., extended producer responsibility); product stewardship; energy; environmental health and safety; or tax is a plus. Knowledge of technical matters relevant to the metal can industry through academic training or professional experience is highly desired; alternatively, an eagerness to learn these matters with a proven ability to learn technical information quickly. Skills Demonstrated ability to develop and implement effective advocacy strategies that create political momentum on issues of importance. Effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex technical data into concise advocacy materials. Adaptive and collaborative—essential in a small-staff association team. Strategic thinker with strong political instincts and policy analysis capabilities. Skilled in building consensus and maintaining relationships with policymakers, regulators, and industry stakeholders. Comfortable managing multiple priorities and working independently with strong project management capabilities. Why Join Us: Lead the charge for a historic industry providing critical goods on high-profile policy issues that are critical for the association and that matter generally for the economy and the environment. Work directly with senior industry leaders who are shaping the future of packaging. Join a collaborative, high-energy, small but mighty team where your expertise and initiative are valued, you have the freedom to act nimbly, and your growth is supported. Competitive salary and benefits with the ability to work remotely. Travel: Occasional domestic travel (15-20%) required for advocacy meetings, conferences, and member engagement. Travel likely higher during state legislative sessions. If the candidate is remote, roughly quarterly travel to Washington, DC for meetings with the entire staff in-person. Compensation: Range of $140,000-$200,000 plus benefits such as retirement, long-term disability insurance, health insurance, telephone stipend, professional development, and PTO, plus all federal holidays. About Can Manufacturers Institute (CMI): CMI is the national trade association of the U.S. metal can manufacturing industry and its suppliers. U.S. metal can manufacturers account for the annual domestic production of approximately 142 billion food, beverage, aerosol, and general line cans; employ more than 20,000 people with facilities in 32 states; and generate about $27.5 billion in direct economic activity. CMI members include steel and aluminum food, beverage, aerosol, and decorative can manufacturers, plus aluminum, steel, coating, and ink suppliers. The small-staff trade association of six individuals manages programs for the benefit of the metal can industry, mostly on trade, sustainability, and product stewardship. CMI staff work closely with the members to promote and protect the metal can industry, which provides the safest, highest-quality, and most sustainable packaging. Qualified candidates are invited to submit a resume and optional cover letter to [email protected] outlining relevant experience and interest in the position. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, ArchiPac
item.description: Director, ArchiPac Organization: American Institute of Architects (AIA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/20/2026 Salary Range: $115,000.00 To $120,000.00 Annually The American Institute of Architects (AIA) AIA will provide you with the opportunity to advocate for the value of architecture and give architects and design professionals the resources they need to do their best work. The collective voice of architects is essential, and our work drives positive change through the power of design. Each one of us at AIA is a leader committed to demonstrating our mission and values and designing a better future for our country and planet. Even in times of change, AIA’s values remain constant: We stand for equity and human rights. We stand for architecture that strengthens our communities. We stand for a sustainable future. We stand for protecting communities from the impacts of climate change. We stand for economic opportunity. We stand for investing in the future. We speak up, and policymakers listen. The American Institute of Architects, as part of the global community, is building a culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion within the profession of architecture to create a better built environment for all. Achieving this vision has a direct impact on the relevance of the profession of architecture and the world’s prosperity, health, and future. Job Summary Reporting to the Sr. Director, Federal Affairs, this role is responsible for the development and management of AIA’s political action committee, ArchiPAC; directing all PAC donor retention and recognition strategies; PAC and federal lobbying and legal compliance; AIA member to member programs; political fundraising; political disbursements strategy; political events; and other outreach or project oversight as assigned. Job Duties Work with colleagues in Government Affairs and Public Policy to develop and implement a strategic disbursement plan for ArchiPAC contributions to federal candidates and members of Congress, informed by AIA’s policy priorities, advocacy agenda, political environment, and opportunities to strengthen relationships with federal policymakers. Build and maintain relationships with political operatives, campaign committee leadership, federal candidates and officeholders, campaign staff, and other political influencers across the political spectrum in Washington, DC. Develop and execute a comprehensive, proactive fundraising strategy designed to significantly grow ArchiPAC participation, the number of contributors, and total receipts from eligible AIA members. Identify, develop, and continuously improve ArchiPAC fundraising channels, including the AIA membership-renewal contribution option, member portal giving opportunities, ArchiPAC.org, email solicitations, direct mail, telephone outreach, peer-to-peer fundraising, conferences, receptions, fundraising events, and other member touchpoints. Partner with AIA Membership, Digital, Technology, Brand and Engagement, and other internal teams to improve the member giving experience and integrate ArchiPAC opportunities into appropriate AIA platforms, communications, events, and member journeys. Regularly evaluate ArchiPAC fundraising performance, participation rates, donor retention and acquisition, average contribution levels, campaign performance, and other metrics, and recommend strategies to increase participation and revenue. Develop and implement contributor cultivation, stewardship, renewal, recognition, and upgrade strategies, including targeted approaches for first-time donors, recurring contributors, leadership-level donors, and other priority member audiences. Develop and oversee educational and promotional materials that clearly explain what ArchiPAC is, why voluntary member participation matters, how ArchiPAC supports AIA’s federal advocacy goals, and how members can participate. Develop compelling ArchiPAC content highlighting supported candidates, political engagement, advocacy successes, member testimonials, donor stories, and examples demonstrating how political engagement strengthens AIA’s ability to advance the profession’s federal policy priorities. Maintain and continuously improve ArchiPAC.org and related digital content to ensure members have clear, current, accessible information about the PAC, its activities, supported candidates, fundraising opportunities, and impact. Plan and execute ArchiPAC fundraising and educational events, receptions, conference activations, donor programs, and other engagement opportunities at AIA national meetings and other appropriate venues. Develop and expand peer-to-peer fundraising strategies that equip AIA volunteer leaders, donors, firms, and other member advocates with the tools, messages, and resources needed to encourage eligible members to support ArchiPAC. Serve as staff liaison to the ArchiPAC Steering Committee and ArchiPAC peer-to-peer fundraising groups, providing strategic guidance, political updates, fundraising performance information, and recommendations for member engagement. Provide regular updates and counsel to AIA leadership, Government Affairs and Public Policy leadership, and the ArchiPAC Steering Committee regarding ArchiPAC fundraising, participation, political giving, supported candidates, and relevant developments in the federal political environment. Create, develop, implement, and coordinate ArchiPAC political and fundraising strategies, including long-term strategic planning, annual work plans, fundraising goals, performance measures, and budgets. Manage ArchiPAC accounting and third-party compliance software, including accurate maintenance of contributor and transaction data, receipts and disbursements, internal reconciliation and reporting, and preparation and filing of required Federal Election Commission reports. Serve as ArchiPAC Treasurer and ensure the correctness and timeliness of required federal filings and the compliance of ArchiPAC activities with applicable federal campaign-finance law and AIA policies. Remain current on federal campaign-finance laws, regulations, FEC guidance, political fundraising practices, and emerging trends relevant to ArchiPAC, and advise AIA leadership and colleagues regarding federal PAC compliance and best practices. Collaborate with AIA’s Brand and Engagement team and other communications partners to develop integrated strategies for promoting ArchiPAC through member email, websites, newsletters, print and digital publications, social and video content, events, and other communications channels. Direct the development of written communications, videos, web content, fundraising appeals, educational materials, donor communications, testimonials, case studies, and other creative content designed to increase member understanding of and participation in ArchiPAC. Partner with AIA state and local components, where appropriate, to promote eligible member participation in ArchiPAC and strengthen engagement with AIA’s federal advocacy program. This role does not administer, advise, oversee, or provide compliance support for state or local PACs. Frequent contacts: AIA staff AIA State Component staff and leaders AIA National leaders and Board members AIA Members Congressional candidates and staff National Party Committee contacts Professional fundraisers and volunteers ArchiPAC vendors and consultants Representatives from other organizations Qualifications Proficient analytical, writing, speaking, organizational and interpersonal skills are essential. Ability to balance big-picture strategies, demonstrate attention to detail and manage multiple priorities and responsibilities. Sound judgment and initiative to work independently. Strong organizational skills. Commitment to produce excellent work and resolve complex issues according to deadlines and budgets; creative, flexible, and high energy, including the ability to work non-routine hours. Demonstrated success of working in a team environment, coordinating, and communicating with colleagues and others, conveying ideas with tact and diplomacy, and resolving problems collaboratively. Experience working with and guiding multiple constituencies, such as national boards and state and local organizations, associations, and volunteers. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, Access, etc.) and experience using PAC/FEC-compliant software. Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 7 years of professional experience, including 3-5 years of demonstrated success with political action committee development and management, including experience handling all aspects of administration and reporting. The individual must have experience in campaign and legislative processes and command of FEC regulations. Advanced level and demonstrated fundraising experience a must. Supervisory Requirements: None What we offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package that reflects our company values and workplace culture, including: Medical and dental 401(k) Flexibility Paid time off Flexible spending accounts Income protection- (Life Insurance Coverage up to 2x salary) & disability plans at no cost. Tuition and membership reimbursements AIA employees have access to a variety of other programs, including: Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and their family members SmartBenefits transportation program, featuring up to $55 monthly in public transportation as well as pretax METRO parking Computer purchase program Fitness club discounts Prepaid legal services program Identity theft protection Travel Requirements: 10% travel required if working outside of DC, MD, VA area. Work Location Hybrid/Remote from the Washington DC area (DC, MD, VA) only Applicants from states not listed above are ineligible. item.title: Senior Compliance Manager, Analytics & Program Effectiveness
item.description: Senior Compliance Manager, Analytics & Program Effectiveness Organization: Moloco Location: Menlo Park, CA Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About Moloco: Moloco is an AI-native performance advertising company, bringing the power of AI advertising to the open internet. Founded in 2013 by machine learning engineers who had built AI advertising systems inside the world’s largest technology companies, Moloco began from a shared mission: to build that same engine for the open internet. Today, Moloco is one company with two businesses, built on the same compound AI system. Moloco Ads is our AI-native performance advertising platform, helping mobile app marketers acquire, retain, and re-engage high-value users across the open internet. Moloco Commerce Media is our AI-native retail media platform, enabling retailers and marketplaces to turn their platforms into thriving ad businesses. Both are powered by CARA (Compound Ad Recommendation Architecture), the AI system behind every Moloco product. At Moloco, we bring together those who’ve already solved hard problems and those with the drive to. Here, we work on some of the complex problems in AI advertising, at a scale and level of sophistication very few companies can offer. Come build what’s next. The Impact You’ll Be Contributing to Moloco: The Senior Compliance Manager, Analytics & Program Effectiveness within the Enterprise Compliance Office (ECO) leads the design, measurement, and continuous improvement of Moloco’s global compliance program, turning regulatory, policy, and governance requirements into clear frameworks, workflows, evidence standards, reporting, and metrics. This hands-on role owns the compliance metrics framework and carries program ownership for defined ECO initiatives, making compliance scalable, auditable, measurable, and easier for business teams to execute. This role reports to the Enterprise Compliance Officer and partners across Legal, Security/GRC, Product, Engineering, People, Finance, business teams, Internal Audit, and Compliance Champions. You’ll gather inputs, validate information, influence outcomes, drive issues, action items, and commitments to closure, escalate risks or delays early, and build working expertise at the intersection of compliance, operations, and data-driven decision-making across privacy, product and advertising compliance, third-party risk, enterprise-wide policies and governance, training, regulatory tracking, and other compliance domains. This role is based near our Menlo Park, CA office and follows a hybrid in-office schedule. The Opportunity: Lead the build and day-to-day operation of defined ECO services, translating regulatory, policy, and governance requirements into clear frameworks, artifacts, and repeatable processes, and continuously improving program infrastructure (playbooks, templates, trackers, repositories, workflows) to reduce rework and friction over time. Design, build, and own the compliance metrics framework and dashboards that demonstrate program efficacy (KPI/KRI definitions, data sources, thresholds, owners, data-quality process), including comprehensive program effectiveness and Compliance Champion network metrics, and produce recurring Risk Committee, Board, and executive reporting (e.g., quarterly posture reports, Board-ready dashboards) that turns data into clear narratives, trend analysis, and recommended actions, not just numbers. Set documentation and evidence standards and oversee the quality of audit-ready documentation and evidence maintained by the ECO and control owners: complete, accurate, version controlled, traceable from risk to control to evidence, and easy to retrieve for governance, audit, and executive review. Analyze compliance data, documentation, evidence, and workflows and independently investigate issues and open questions (with thoughtful follow-ups) to identify gaps, inconsistencies, trends, and leading indicators; drive practical solutions that close documentation, control, or process gaps and improve effectiveness, quality, efficiency, and operational rigor. Support risk, policy, and regulatory services: maintain the consolidated risk register and provide data-driven input to enterprise, product/feature-level, and market-entry or acquisition risk assessments and prioritization; support the policy and standards lifecycle and exceptions and risk-acceptance process (policy inventory, review cadence, ownership, exceptions tracked through approval, expiry, and renewal); and, with Legal, support the regulatory inventory and obligations register and track regulatory-change implementation (owners, milestones, evidence of completion). Own issue management and remediation, tracking issues, remediation items, and commitments to closure (owners, severity, timelines, dependencies, decisions, closure evidence, escalations) and reporting on aging, overdue items, and root-cause trends. Run program governance for defined initiatives (materials, status updates, metrics, dashboards, RAID logs, decision registers, other artifacts) and support ECO forums such as the Executive Risk Committee and First-Line Compliance Champion Committee. Design and operate the standardized ECO intake, triage, and routing workflow, including enterprise escalation criteria, and use intake data (volume, cycle time, SLA performance, handoffs, rework drivers) to inform prioritization and capacity and resourcing planning. Lead use of AI-assisted tools for analysis, monitoring, and reporting, and set controls that flag tool-output errors, anomalies, or inconsistencies before they are relied upon. Support audit and regulatory readiness: compile the compliance evidence pack, control narratives, and known-issues and remediation tracker, and serve as day-to-day compliance contact for Internal Audit and external reviewers. Lead implementation and operation of third-party risk management tools, processes, and platforms, overseeing tracking of third-party reviews, merging and maintaining counterparty data, developing analytics and reporting, monitoring risk indicators, and driving mitigation and remediation follow-through. How Do I Know if the Role is Right For Me? A bachelor’s degree in business, law, risk, compliance, political science, data/information science, or a related field; an advanced degree or certification (e.g., CCEP, CRISC, CIPM, CRMA, PMP) is a plus. 8+ years of experience in compliance, legal operations, risk, audit, privacy, security governance, program or project management, or regulatory operations, preferably in a technology, media, or AdTech environment; high-growth or startup experience is a plus. Experience leading compliance, audit readiness, regulatory, or remediation programs, including overseeing evidence coordination, documentation review, status tracking, and issue management, and building or scaling a compliance operating model, program, or function (not just executing individual tasks), with working knowledge of the three-lines-of-defense model and second-line oversight versus first-line control execution. Demonstrated track record owning compliance or risk metrics, analytics, and reporting, including designing KPI/KRI frameworks and executive dashboards that measure program effectiveness rather than just activity (metrics, thresholds, data lineage, data-quality controls) and presenting results to senior leaders, committees, or a Board. Strong program leadership in a fast-paced, global, matrixed environment with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities: managing parallel initiatives, workplans, owners and dependencies, momentum, and issue resolution, and leading through influence, including senior stakeholders without direct authority. Analytical mindset to review data, documentation, evidence, and workflows, identify gaps, inconsistencies, root causes, and improvements, and recommend clear actions. Strong documentation, record-keeping, and communication skills, with attention to detail, accuracy, completeness, and consistency, and the ability to produce clear materials for cross-functional teams, senior leaders, and executive, committee, or Board review. Highly organized, proactive, and self-directed, with a hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves approach, sound risk-based judgment on when to escalate, and demonstrated curiosity about new regulatory areas, frameworks, business models, and compliance domains. Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, GRC platforms, and other program, project, workflow, or knowledge-management systems, and sound fluency with AI tools (e.g., Claude, Co-work, or similar) for drafting, analysis, summarization, tracking, and workflow efficiency. Advanced data skills, including SQL, BI/dashboard tools, and Excel/Sheets, to build reporting, metrics, and trend analysis, and the ability to work with data and engineering partners to source, validate, and maintain compliance data. Bonus: exposure to one or more of product/advertising compliance, privacy, information governance, third-party risk management, AI governance, or compliance training; PMO experience or project/program management certification a plus. Why You’ll Love this Role: If you like turning data into insight and complexity into operational clarity, this role sits at the heart of the ECO. You’ll help build a compliance program, creating the metrics, workflows, documentation, and program discipline that make compliance practical, auditable, and sustainable, with broad exposure across these partner teams, and contribute directly to initiatives that protect the business and enable responsible growth. Compensation & Benefits U.S.-based employees have access to medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, short-term and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, and well-being benefits and perks. U.S.-based employees also receive up to 12 scheduled paid holidays per calendar year and one Thrive Day off per quarter. Additionally, all employees have Flexible Time Off (FTO). The succes

item.title: Legal Engineer
item.description: Legal Engineer Organization: Ontra Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About Ontra Ontra is the leader in AI-powered solutions for the private markets. Powered by industry-leading AI, data from over 2 million contracts, and a global network of legal professionals, Ontra automates critical private market workflows across the fund lifecycle. Ontra’s solutions transform unstructured data trapped in static documents into actionable intelligence, enabling firms to accelerate contracts, streamline compliance, and automate entity management. Trusted by more than 1,000 global GPs, investment banks, law firms, and advisors – including nine of the top ten PEI-ranked firms worldwide – Ontra helps firms focus on what’s important. Our Culture Ontra is built for people who want real ownership from day one in an environment that’s built to support it. Our customers are sophisticated, and our work reflects that. AI is engrained in how we work, and curiosity about it is part of who we are. Ontranauts are sharp, genuinely collaborative, and invested in each other’s success. They are excellent at what they do and even better to work with. That combination is rare, and we don’t take it for granted. Learn more about our values. For this job, we are currently only hiring candidates based in the New York City Metropolitan area. About the Role Ontra is seeking a Legal Engineer focused primarily on our AI-native services and Contract Automation businesses, reporting to our General Manager, Legal Engineering. This is a multifaceted role: part prompt engineer, part legal workflow designer, part product advisor, and part builder. We’re looking for someone excited to collaborate with product and service delivery teams and customers to develop AI-powered legal workflows, create and deliver comprehensive enablement materials, monitor industry trends to keep our products cutting-edge, and spearhead initiatives to enhance operational efficiency using AI. If you are a detail-oriented systems thinker who moves fast, experiments, and enjoys brainstorming how AI can make legal work faster and more accurate while retaining a human touch, we’d love to get to know you! What You’ll Do Product Development Collaboration: Work closely with Product and service delivery teams to develop and refine contract review, drafting, and negotiation workflows, ensuring they align with client needs and industry standards. Enablement Material Creation: Develop and deliver training materials such as webinars, 1:1 training, and self-directed courses to educate Ontra employees and legal network members on contract workflows and practical AI use. Market Monitoring: Keep an eye on relevant markets, including legal AI, contract automation, and legal service delivery to inform workflow improvements. Efficiency Initiatives: Drive operational efficiency by piloting AI-first legal workflows, evaluating outputs against legal playbooks, and measuring quality and turnaround time. Experiment with prompts and prototypes, iterate quickly on feedback, and turn promising ideas into practical improvements. Stakeholder Consultation: Act as a technical subject matter expert by providing consulting support on AI-native services and Contract Automation projects, participating in meetings with product managers, development teams, and clients. What You’ll Bring Relevant Experience: 1+ years of directly relevant legal experience with a focus on transactional law. Experience drafting, reviewing, or negotiating NDAs, vendor contracts, and other commercial contracts is a plus. Experience in private practice and/or in-house in an investment bank or asset manager is a plus. Educational Background: Possession of a JD, LLM, or LLB, with US qualifications preferred but not mandatory. Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication abilities; prior experience in a customer-facing role is advantageous. Organizational and Problem-Solving Skills: Demonstrated organizational excellence and high ownership, with a proactive approach to building systems, problem-solving, teamwork, and results orientation. Practical AI Experience: Hands-on use of AI tools such as Claude, GPT, Harvey, or Legora in legal or professional work is required. Comfortable refining prompts, checking outputs for accuracy, and recognizing when human legal judgment is needed; experience with every named tool is not required. AI Workflow Building: Experience building a reusable AI skill or custom workflow, or experimenting with Codex or Claude Code to create a small app or more involved workflow is preferred. Exploratory or personal projects are welcome; coding experience is not required. New York City Area: Must be willing to work 3 days per week (typically, Tuesday-Thursday) in office, building and iterating on workflows directly alongside our attorneys and engineers. Hiring Locations We currently hire exclusively in the locations listed below. Select jobs may have more specific location requirements due to business needs. United States Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington APAC Hong Kong EMEA United Kingdom Benefits Snapshot Twice yearly team offsites for in-person collaboration Paid flexible time off policy Paid parental leave and benefits Employer-supported retirement contributions, varying by country Monthly phone and internet reimbursement Company-sponsored learning and development resources, department budgets for professional development, and a robust onboarding program Various options for medical, dental, and vision insurance Travel Occasional travel is required for Ontra employees, including typically at least twice per year to attend team and larger group off-sites for in-person collaboration. For some roles, additional travel may be required based on the requirements of the role and business need. Inclusivity Ontra is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Ontra will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact [email protected] . Note on Employment Verification: All employees hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in their particular location. Note to External Agencies: We are not accepting any blind submissions or resumes/CVs from recruitment agencies. Any candidates sent to Ontra will NOT be accepted or considered as a submission without a signed agreement in place. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Compliance Manager, BSA/AML Program
item.description: Associate Compliance Manager, BSA/AML Program Organization: Upstart Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About Upstart At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence. As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress. We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you. If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you. The Team: Upstart’s Bank Secrecy Act/Anti-Money Laundering Compliance team is responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the company’s enterprise BSA/AML Program, Customer Identification Program (CIP), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), sanctions, and suspicious activity compliance programs. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, Fraud, and Enterprise Risk to ensure our products and services are built on a strong foundation of regulatory compliance and effective risk management. We build scalable, risk-based programs that evolve alongside our products and regulatory expectations. As the Associate Compliance Manager, BSA/AML Program at Upstart, you will serve as a BSA/AML subject matter expert for Upstart Bank’s secured and unsecured lending products and support the development of new deposit products. Using a risk-based approach, you will evaluate changes to identify risks, develop controls, and measure ongoing performance of changes to ensure products and services are implemented within a strong compliance framework. How you’ll make an impact Lead the design, execution, and continuous improvement of BSA/AML, Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), transaction monitoring, and sanctions screening processes for secured lending, unsecured lending, and deposit account products. Serve as a BSA/AML Compliance advisor for deposit product initiatives, partnering with Product, Legal, Operations, Engineering, and Enterprise Risk throughout product development and implementation. Develop and manage BSA/AML compliance initiatives, including new deposit product launches, regulatory enhancements, and control improvements. Administer ongoing customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence programs for deposit accounts in alignment with Upstart’s Customer Identification Program (CIP), Red Flags Program, and BSA/AML compliance procedures. Evaluate relevant risks and typologies to develop appropriate transaction monitoring rules and efficient investigations processes Monitor evolving regulatory requirements, including FinCEN guidance, OFAC sanctions, and FFIEC BSA/AML examination expectations, to translate regulatory changes into scalable business processes and controls. Develop key risk indicators (KRIs), key performance indicators (KPIs), and management reporting that provide actionable insights into BSA/AML program effectiveness. Translate regulatory requirements and risk trends into clear recommendations for business stakeholders and senior leadership. Drive remediation efforts for examination, audit, monitoring, and testing findings while strengthening the overall BSA/AML compliance control environment. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 5+ years of experience in BSA/AML compliance, financial crimes compliance, or a related Risk or Compliance role within a bank or other regulated financial institution. Experience implementing and managing customer onboarding processes including identity verification, customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), sanctions screening, and ongoing monitoring processes. Working knowledge of regulatory requirements, including the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), USA PATRIOT Act, and Customer Due Diligence Rule, and BSA/AML risks associated with deposit products Experience developing and delivering AML risk assessments, KRIs/KPIs, and management reporting while leading cross-functional compliance initiatives. Strong organizational, analytical, communication skills. Ability to identify gaps in policies and procedures and drive resolution and closure Experience in audit and exam readiness, including evidence gathering, testing and monitoring, addressing findings, responding to requests. Preferred Qualifications Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS), Certified AML and Fraud Professional (CAFP), or equivalent certification. Experience implementing and optimizing an AML system, including data integration, rules configuration, testing, and validation. Experience supporting deposit products, including high-yield savings accounts, certificates of deposit, brokered deposits, or similar banking products. Familiarity with implementing BSA/AML tools for transaction monitoring, case management, and customer screening Experience working with examiners, auditors, and other third-parties. Knowledge of regulatory change management and implementing new BSA/AML requirements. Ability to investigate complex compliance issues, perform root cause analysis, and provide guidance to support issue resolution Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote Time zone requirements The team operates on the East/West coast time zones. Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time. #LI-REMOTE #LI-MidSenior At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k). United States | Remote – Anticipated Base Salary Range $115,800—$160,100 USD What you’ll love At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect: Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly Retirement benefits to help you plan for the future, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada) Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with discounted stock purchase options for eligible employees (US only) Comprehensive health coverage designed to support you and your family, including medical, dental, vision, and wellness resources for US and supplemental health coverage for Canada. Health Savings Account contributions from Upstart for eligible plans (US only) Income protection benefits, including life insurance and disability coverage for added financial security Paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays, in line with local requirements Paid family and parental leave to support caregiving and major life moments (duration varies by country) Family-centered benefits to support fertility, parenthood, and caregiving needs Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering mental health support and life-centered resources Financial wellness resources, including access to financial planning tools and a financial concierge service (US Only) Annual wellness allowance to support your physical and emotional well-being and personal development, based on what matters most to you Annual productivity allowance to invest in relevant tools and resources you need to do your best work, no matter where you work from Connection and community through team events, all-company updates, and employee resource groups (ERGs) Onsite perks, including catered lunches and fully stocked micro-kitchens when working from one of our offices in the Bay Area, Austin, Columbus, and New York City For roles based in Canada, please note that we are not currently able to hire in Quebec. Upstart is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. Just as we are dedicated to improving access to affordable credit for all, we are committed to inclusive and fair hiring practices.
