item.title: Associate Director, Strategic Engagement
item.description: Associate Director, Strategic Engagement Organization: Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Associate Director, Strategic Engagement Full Time Salary Range: $110,000 to $130,000 Annually The Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC) is a Washington, DC-based think tank that brings together leaders from across the political spectrum to develop and advance practical, bipartisan solutions to the challenges facing Americans. Through policy development and advocacy, BPC and its advocacy affiliate, BPC Action, work to turn ideas into meaningful results in Washington and beyond. Our work spans some of the nation’s most consequential domestic policy issues, with a focus on lowering the everyday cost of living for families, expanding opportunity, strengthening the American economy, and improving the effectiveness of government. What if your ability to bring people together could help shape the future of Social Security, retirement security, and America’s economic stability? We are seeking an Associate Director, Strategic Engagement to help build the partnerships and bipartisan coalitions needed to advance meaningful economic policy solutions. Working within BPC’s Economic Policy Program (EPP), this individual will play a key role in stakeholder engagement and coalition-building, with an initial focus on Social Security solvency and retirement savings, while also supporting efforts related to federal tax and fiscal policy. With Social Security facing significant long-term financing challenges and millions of Americans lacking access to employer-sponsored retirement plans, the need for thoughtful, bipartisan solutions has never been more important. This role offers an opportunity to engage influential stakeholders, broaden support for evidence-based policy recommendations, and help translate shared priorities into meaningful legislative progress. Responsibilities: Lead the design and execution of a stakeholder engagement and coalition-building strategy across EPP, with a primary focus on Social Security solvency and retirement security and additional engagement on tax and fiscal policy. Build, maintain, and expand relationships with policy organizations, advocacy groups, employers, business and labor representatives, state and local officials, academics, industry leaders, and other stakeholders whose perspectives can inform and advance EPP’s policy work. Coordinate with BPC Action and external policy organizations to support the development of aligned messages to policymakers. Plan and manage expanded stakeholder convenings that bring employers, state and local officials, labor and business representatives, and advocates from adjacent policy areas into a coordinated conversation about responsible reform. Support the American Savings Education Council (ASEC), including its Partner Summits, to advance cross-sector dialogue among government, industry, advocacy, and academic leaders. Partner with BPC’s tax and fiscal policy teams to develop and execute stakeholder engagement strategies around federal tax policy, the federal budget and debt, and other fiscal policy priorities. Identify opportunities to connect stakeholders across traditionally separate policy communities—including retirement, Social Security, tax, and fiscal policy—to strengthen BPC’s ability to build broader constituencies for bipartisan economic policy solutions. Track relationships and engagement across coalitions, ensuring sustained momentum between convenings and clear follow-through on commitments. Required Skills and Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, government, economics, public administration, communications, or a related field. 5-8 years of relevant professional experience in coalition-building, stakeholder engagement, advocacy, government relations, or public affairs. Demonstrated ability to build and sustain relationships among stakeholders with differing viewpoints, including congressional offices, advocacy organizations, and private-sector representatives. Strong political acumen and the ability to navigate complex policy and stakeholder environments diplomatically. Excellent organizational skills, with experience managing convenings, working groups, or multi-stakeholder initiatives. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate policy concepts for congressional and external audiences. Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and manage competing priorities effectively. Strong commitment to objective, evidence-informed analysis, and bipartisan policymaking. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. BPC does not sponsor employment visas. Preferred Skills and Qualifications: Familiarity with one or more areas of economic policy, particularly Social Security, private-sector retirement savings, federal tax policy, or federal fiscal policy. Experience working on Capitol Hill, within a federal agency, think tank, trade association, or advocacy organization. Experience supporting fundraising, donor engagement, or grant reporting. What We Offer: BPC offers a highly competitive salary and provides generous benefits. Compensation The anticipated hiring range for this position is $110,000 to $130,000. BPC considers a variety of factors when making compensation decisions, including relevant experience, skills, education, training, knowledge, internal equity, and organizational and business needs. Medical Benefits BPC offers medical coverage through CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield with a choice of three plans, one of which is HSA eligible with an annual BPC contribution. All medical plans cover in-network preventive care at 100% and include prescription drugs. Dental and Vision coverage through MetLife includes no-cost options for you and your family. Additional benefits include: Retirement Savings: 403(b) employer matching contributions of up to 7% of salary, plus an additional 2% non-elective employer contribution (both available after 90 days of employment) Generous Paid Time Off: 15 vacation days, 2 personal days, 15 sick days, 11 paid holidays, and a paid end-of-year break Tuition Reimbursement: Up to $5,250 annually after one year of employment Professional Development: Up to $2,000 after six months of employment Commuter Benefits: Up to $130 per month in Metro benefits Employer-Paid Insurance: Life, accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D), and disability insurance Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs): Health care, dependent care, and parking Mental Health & Wellness Support: Access to Spring Health and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Working at BPC BPC operates on a hybrid schedule, with staff in the office three days a week, Tuesday through Thursday, and the option to work from home on Monday and Friday. Application Process Individuals interested in this position should submit a resume and a cover letter. Incomplete applications will not be considered. More About BPC and BPC Action Founded in 2007, the Bipartisan Policy Center and its advocacy affiliate, BPC Action, are unique in their approach to solving the nation’s most pressing issues. BPC brings together diverse perspectives from across the political spectrum to develop practical policy solutions, while BPC Action works directly with legislators and policymakers to help turn those solutions into results. What sets BPC apart is our ability to operate at the intersection of policy development and political advocacy. We build consensus across the aisle and work with leaders from both parties to advance meaningful reforms. Ideas BPC brings together respected policy experts, former congressional and administration officials, private-sector leaders, current and former policymakers, and other experts to develop solutions to America’s most pressing challenges. Action Policy development is only the beginning. BPC Action advances bipartisan solutions by providing political and technical assistance, identifying and supporting legislative champions, and leveraging relationships with policymakers to help move ideas through Congress. Results In 2025, BPC and BPC Action helped support the introduction of more than 120 bills in the House and Senate and helped advance more than 40 bills beyond committee. We engaged with more than half of all congressional offices, expanding our reach across both parties. BPC is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Please apply via our Bipartisan Policy Center careers website at Careers • Bipartisan Policy Center Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Commercial Litigation Recovery Lead (Hybrid)
item.description: Commercial Litigation Recovery Lead (Hybrid) Organization: Enova Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 10/21/2026 We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas or take over sponsorship at this time. #BI-Hybrid #LI-Hybrid About the role: As the Commercial Litigation Recovery Lead at Enova, you will serve as the team’s go-to advisor on litigation strategy, collections policy, and matters at the intersection of legal and operational risk. You will direct outside counsel on routine and complex commercial collections litigation, help set and enforce partner performance expectations, and translate portfolio insights into recommendations that shape how Enova recovers on defaulted small business loans. As a hands-on leader, you will support the Litigation, Bankruptcy, and Analytics segments, step in on escalated or contested matters, and assist with vendor management, training, and team development. The role reports to the Recovery Litigation Manager. Responsibilities: Manage the relationships with Enova’s outside law firm network and OCAs, serving as the primary point of contact for partner leadership on performance, strategy, and escalations. Direct outside counsel in routine and complex commercial collections litigation, collaborating on enterprise-wide and case-specific strategy, including post-judgment remedies such as garnishment, levies, and asset recovery. Ensure litigation and collections activity across the internal team and partner network complies with applicable federal and state law. Partner with Collections, Fraud, Legal, and Analytics to develop and implement strategies that increase recovery across the pre- and post-charge-off lifecycle for Enova’s small business portfolios. Lead projects to help the recovery litigation team drive efficiency, improve processes, and increase production. Support the Recovery Litigation Manager with training, coaching, and quality control for recovery team members, and with monthly and executive reporting on partner and litigation performance. Preferred Qualifications: Juris Doctor from an accredited law school. Prior experience working in a law firm, in-house legal department, or collection agency environment. Experience with post-judgment remedies and creditor-side commercial bankruptcy. Experience building or managing vendor scorecards, SLAs, or performance-based placement models. Requirements: 3–5 years of experience in commercial collections, creditor-side litigation, commercial financial services or fintech, or creditor-side bankruptcy, with demonstrated exposure to managing outside counsel or third-party vendors. Working knowledge of the laws and regulations governing commercial debt collection and judgment enforcement, or the ability to acquire it quickly. Strong negotiation, critical thinking, and judgment; able to weigh legal risk against business outcomes and make sound recommendations under pressure. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to set expectations with external partners and present to senior leadership. Demonstrated ability to manage projects independently, hold others accountable to deadlines, and operate with minimal oversight. Proficiency in Excel and comfort navigating multiple systems of record (e.g., Salesforce, vendor management and litigation tracking platforms). Compensation: The budgeted annual salary range for this position is $85,000 to $110,000. Actual annual salary will be determined based on qualifications, skills, experience, and level assessed during the hiring process and may fall outside of the range shown. Additional compensation for this role may include a bonus. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in Company benefits, described in more detail here. Benefits & Perks: Our hybrid roles require in-office work Tuesday through Thursday, with remote flexibility on Mondays and Fridays. This schedule fosters collaboration, team connection, and strategic planning, enhancing communication and effectiveness to drive results. Health, dental, and vision insurance including mental health benefits 401(k) matching plus a roth option (U.S. Based employees only) PTO & paid holidays off Sabbatical program (for eligible roles) Summer hours (for eligible roles) Paid parental leave DEI groups (B.L.A.C.K. @ Enova, HOLA @ Enova, Women @ Enova, Pride @ Enova, South Asians @ Enova, APEX @ Enova, and Parents @ Enova) Employee recognition and rewards program Charitable matching and a paid volunteer day…Plus so much more! About Enova Enova International is a leading financial technology company that provides online financial services through our AI and machine learning-powered Colossus™platform. We serve non-prime consumers and businesses alike, while offering world-class technology and services to traditional banks—in order to create accessible credit for millions. Being a values-driven organization is at the core of Enova’s success. We live our values by listening to our customers, challenging assumptions, thinking big, setting high expectations, and hiring and developing the best. Through our values and our commitment to making Enova an awesome place to work, we maintain an environment of inclusion and culture where our employees can thrive. You can learn more about Enova’s values and culture here. It is our policy to provide equal employment opportunity for all persons and not discriminate in employment decisions by placing the most qualified person in each job, without regard to any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. California Applicants: Click here to review our California Privacy Policy for Job Applicants. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Creative Lead, Paid Social
item.description: Creative Lead, Paid Social Organization: Hims & Hers Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals. About the Role: We’re standing up a new in house video arm for paid social at Hims & Hers, bringing high volume ad production in house so we can move faster and work across every category and both brands, Hims and Hers. The Creative Lead is a foundational hire in that build, not a role slotting into an existing team. It’s a hands on role based in Los Angeles, with in person attendance on set on a varied schedule that follows the shoots, not a typical office week. As Creative Lead, you’re the creative engine of the pod, partnering with a marketing Creative Strategist who sets the initial vision, direction, and scripts for each concept. From there, it’s on you to bring that vision to life visually, directing the shoot, shaping the look, and pulling in your Producer and editorial counterparts to get each concept shot, cut, and shipped at volume. This is a hands on, wear many hats role. You’re not waiting around for a finished brief, you’re a genuine creative partner from the earliest idea, and you’re comfortable adapting fast as priorities, categories, and brands shift. You’ll work across both Hims and Hers and each category, taking direction from Strategists on either line of business and executing it with your own creative craft. Producing at the volume this pod needs means staying hands on across the whole path from concept to a launched, high performing ad, not just owning one piece of it. You Will: Partner with the marketing Creative Strategist from the earliest concept stage, translating their vision and scripts into a fully realized visual approach. Own the visual execution of the pod’s output end to end, bringing the Strategist’s scripts and concepts to life on screen, and contributing to copy or hooks when it helps. Be ready to direct shoots in person, giving real time notes to talent, crew, and production, and step behind the camera yourself (when needed) for lean, quick turnaround setups. Adjust lines on set when needed to keep the words and the visuals in sync. The scripts themselves come from the Strategist, but your read on what’s working in the room matters. Shoot roughly 5 to 10 variants per concept to feed the post production iteration pipeline. Partner closely with the Producer on shoot planning, covering locations, talent, props, wardrobe, and shot lists. Collaborate with editorial and post production on every cut, giving clear, specific feedback to keep the work aligned with the original creative vision. Maintain a high bar for craft across the board, composition, typography, color, motion, clarity, and voice, even at high volume and speed. Translate what’s winning in performance back into visual direction for future concepts and shoots, sharing insights with the Strategist to help shape future scripts. You Have: 6 to 9 years of experience in art direction, video direction, or design, with copywriting or scripting as a secondary skill, and a portfolio spanning concept development and video first paid social or branded content, not just execution of others’ briefs. Demonstrated experience developing visual treatments, along with giving clear creative direction to crews, talent, and editors. Hands on shooting experience, comfortable operating a camera yourself for lean shoots, not only directing a crew. Comfortable contributing to copy, hooks, or scripts when it’s useful, even though scripts are typically owned by the Creative Strategist. Proven ability to concept and ship video first ads quickly in fast paced, high volume environments, balancing craft and business needs to deliver effective solutions with minimal guidance. Deep understanding of platform best practices for Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snap, and emerging short form formats. Comfort collaborating across functions with editorial, production, and other internal creative teams, including distributed or offshore teams, to protect creative vision through iteration. Comfort adapting your craft and creative point of view across multiple brands, categories, and audiences within a shared production system, rather than staying limited to a single brand. Strong creative instincts across both visual storytelling and voice, with proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, and other relevant AI creative tools. Comfort working with performance data as a guide for creative decisions, not just craft instinct, exercising sound judgment in balancing creative risk against practical constraints driven by the business. A true go getter, comfortable wearing multiple hats and adapting fast as the needs of the business change, in a lean, fast moving in house team rather than an agency structure. Portfolio Requirements Please include a link to your portfolio or reel showing your role in concept development, storyboarding, visual direction, and scripting or copywriting where relevant, not just finished footage. Be clear about your specific contribution, whether concept, storyboard, director, DP, writer, or editor, on each project. Our Benefits (there are more but here are some highlights): Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP) 401k benefits with employer matching contribution Offsite team retreats We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you’re not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match. Hims considers all qualified applicants for employment, including applicants with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act, and any similar state or local fair chance laws. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Hims & Hers is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at [email protected] and describe the needed accommodation. Your privacy is important to us, and any information you share will only be used for the legitimate purpose of considering your request for accommodation. Hims & Hers gives consideration to all qualified applicants without regard to any protected status, including disability. Please do not send resumes to this email address. To learn more about how we collect, use, retain, and disclose Personal Information, please visit our Global Candidate Privacy Statement. Apply for this Job Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Product & Commercial Counsel
item.description: Senior Product & Commercial Counsel Organization: Docker Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About Docker Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world’s largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout. We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default. _______________________________________________________________________ The Senior Product & Commercial Counsel will report to Docker’s Head of Legal. This is a hybrid role at the intersection of product counseling and commercial negotiation. You will serve as the primary legal partner to Docker’s Product Management and Engineering teams across the full product lifecycle, from concept and design through launch, monetization, and end of life, while also assisting with negotiating the commercial provisions that bring those products to market. Your subject matter depth in open source software licensing and cloud services will directly impact how Docker builds, licenses, and delivers its products to millions of developers and thousands of enterprise customers worldwide. Your work will be instrumental in helping the Company reach its growth objectives while protecting its intellectual property and managing product and licensing risk. This position will be a core member of the extended Legal team, working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, GRC, Sales, and Deal Desk, with exposure to Docker’s senior executives and the opportunity to grow beyond the initial responsibilities and role based on expanding company needs. Responsibilities: Primary function will be to serve as embedded product counsel to Docker’s Product Managers and Engineering teams, providing pragmatic, business-oriented advice on new products, features, pricing and packaging changes, Early Access and beta programs, and end-of-life decisions. Advise on open source software matters, including license analysis and compatibility (Apache, MIT, BSD, GPL, LGPL, AGPL, and source-available licenses), inbound and outbound OSS usage, contribution and CLA policies, and compliance obligations across Docker’s products and distribution channels. Secondary function as needed, draft and maintain Docker’s product-facing legal terms, including service-specific terms, subscription and licensing agreements, Early Access and beta terms, fair use and acceptable use policies, and documentation supporting new monetization models. Structure and negotiate commercial provisions in customer and partner agreements relating to product licensing, cloud services, hybrid on-premise and SaaS deployments, IP ownership, indemnification, warranties, and support commitments, in partnership with Sales and Deal Desk. Counsel on AI-enabled product features, including training data provenance, output ownership, third-party model licensing, and evolving AI regulatory requirements. Collaborate with GRC on the intersection of product design and regulatory obligations, including software supply chain security expectations and emerging regimes such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Support IP strategy, including trademark usage guidelines, brand protection in product and marketing contexts, and coordination with outside counsel on IP matters. Monitor and analyze legal and regulatory developments affecting developer tools, open source, cloud services, and AI, advising the organization on necessary updates and adjustments. Help build scalable playbooks, templates, and self-service resources that allow Product and GTM teams to move quickly within well-defined guardrails. Qualifications: J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar. 6+ years of relevant legal experience, with a meaningful portion in-house at a software, cloud, or developer tools company; a combination of law firm and in-house experience is ideal. Deep familiarity with open source software licensing, including copyleft and permissive license regimes, license compatibility analysis, and OSS program governance. Hands-on experience drafting and negotiating SaaS, software licensing, and cloud services agreements, including enterprise customer negotiations of IP, indemnity, and liability provisions. Working technical fluency with developer software concepts such as virtual containers, registries, CI/CD, APIs, and software supply chain security; direct familiarity with Docker’s products or comparable developer platforms is a strong plus. Understanding of AI and LLM legal issues, including model licensing, training data, and applicable regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act. AI-Native work capability. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex legal concepts into clear, actionable guidance for Product Managers and Engineers. Sound, risk-calibrated judgment and a bias toward practical solutions that enable the business. Proven ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and to manage competing priorities independently. Ability to collaborate with diverse teams and build strong working relationships. What to expect First 30 days Meet with the Head of Legal to understand Docker’s product, licensing, and IP vision. Read Docker’s product terms, subscription agreements, and OSS policies. Read Docker’s Legal, Products, and security-related Notion pages. Become familiar with Docker’s product portfolio, licensing models, and distribution channels. Forge relationships with Docker’s Product Management, Engineering, GRC, Deal Desk, and Sales teams. Begin reviewing product feature launches and customer requests for product-related commercial terms. First 90 days Take ownership of the legal review process for new product and feature launches. Establish a formalized intake and review cadence with Product Management for roadmap items with legal implications. Deliver a fact and data driven assessment of Docker’s product terms and OSS compliance posture with a 6 month and 12 month improvement roadmap. Lead the negotiation of product and licensing provisions in active customer and partner deals as assigned by the Head of Legal. Collaborate with Docker counsel on customer contractual requests relating to licensing, IP, and cloud services and provide feedback. Become familiar with Docker’s Compliance program and controls. First year You have maintained an appropriate meeting cadence with Docker’s Product Management, Engineering, GRC, Deal Desk, and Sales teams. You have provided a monthly update report to the Head of Legal for eStaff updates. You have built and deployed playbooks and templates that streamline product legal review and commercial negotiations to meet the demands of domestic and international growth. You have built the brand of the product legal function as a trusted partner, industry leader, and facilitator of Docker’s growth and customer satisfaction. Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role. Compensation & Equity United States: $178,500– $255,000 + equity ______________________________________________________________________ Posting Information Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role. AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process. Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent. ______________________________________________________________________ Perks & Benefits Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration. Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work. Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break. Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success. Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work. Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning. Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment. Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker’s long-term success as we continue to grow. Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country. Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old. Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community. #LI-REMOTE Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Privacy Counsel
item.description: Senior Privacy Counsel Organization: Abnormal AI Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About the Role Abnormal AI is an AI-native cybersecurity company. We use behavioral AI to stop the attacks that get past everything else, and our products depend on processing data responsibly, at scale, across a growing set of global jurisdictions. We are looking for a Senior Privacy Counsel to own significant portions of our global privacy program — the legal judgment, the day-to-day operational execution and oversight, and the AI-enabled tooling that ties the two together. This is a senior privacy role, reporting to and operating under the direction of the AGC, PPIP. You will advise product and engineering on building privacy into an AI-native platform, support AI governance from the legal and privacy side, provide product-privacy legal counseling alongside the Director, Legal (Product), and partner with the Privacy Manager, who handles much of the operational execution, to run the day-to-day privacy program (DSARs, assessments, ROPA, notices, audits). You will help build and operate the AI automation, working with Legal Ops and other internal teams, that makes the program scale, and serve as a privacy voice with customers via commercial legal. We want someone with the expertise, drive, and assertiveness to own initiatives and drive them to completion with limited oversight — as comfortable writing a lawful-basis analysis as they are shipping a workflow that automates it. Why Join Us Help build and scale the privacy function at a category-defining, AI-native cybersecurity company. Build, not just advise, with real license to design AI automation that changes how privacy work gets done. Work at the intersection of privacy, AI governance, product counseling, and security, on problems that are genuinely new. Competitive salary, benefits, and equity, and a clear path to grow the role toward greater program ownership as the program scales. What You Will Do Global privacy program execution. Support the design of, and drive implementation and continuous improvement of Abnormal’s global privacy program, partnering with applicable stakeholders on strategy, policies, standards, and controls, across GDPR/UK GDPR, EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA, EU Data Act, US state privacy laws, and other applicable international frameworks. Advise and execute on the international data transfer strategy (SCCs, UK IDTA, EU–US Data Privacy Framework, transfer impact assessments) as data flows and product footprint expand across jurisdictions. AI governance execution. Drive the day-to-day execution of the AI governance program from the legal and privacy side, including EU AI Act classification and related obligations, seeing initiatives through to completion in partnership with R&D, Security, and AI governance stakeholders. Privacy by Design for AI products and product counseling. Partner with the Privacy Manager and R&D to embed privacy into the design of new AI-driven features, including model data governance, secondary data-use analysis, and the privacy implications of behavioral AI. Set privacy diligence standards for AI/LLM vendors and model providers. Partner with the Director Legal, Product to provide ongoing product and privacy legal counseling to R&D for product and feature development. Privacy operations. Partner with the Privacy Manager to help oversee the privacy operations program — DSARs and data-subject rights, Records of Processing Activities and data mapping, impact assessments (DPIA/PIA/TIA/LIA), retention, consent and cookie management, and audit support (SOC 2, ISO 27701/42001). Contribute to privacy governance forums, as appropriate. Build and operate AI automation. Use AI to make the privacy program scale. Design, deploy, and improve AI-enabled privacy workflows (e.g., DPIA triage and drafting, subprocessor determination) with Legal Operations and engineering. A build-it role, not just a use-it one — specify, prototype, and iterate, holding tooling to a high accuracy and human-review bar. Legal & Regulatory Horizon Scanning. Monitors emerging legal and regulatory developments, including privacy and AI regulation, in current and target expansion markets; flagging jurisdiction-specific requirements to the AGC, PPIP to inform market entry or launch decisions, and translates confirmed guidance into execution support for R&D (product and privacy considerations) and GTM (contracting posture, customer requirements). Vendor, subprocessor, and customer contracts (escalation point). Serve as the privacy subject matter escalation point for the Commercial and Procurement teams on vendor, subprocessor, and customer agreements (DPAs, SCCs, subprocessor terms). Partner with the AGC, PPIP to set the privacy positions and playbook the teams work from. Incident and breach response. Advise on and help lead the privacy and legal aspects of incident response, including AI incidents, breach assessment, notification decisions, and mitigation, working within the company’s procedures and regulatory deadlines. Data Protection Officer support & regulatory engagement. Support the DPO function as a day-to-day advisor, conducting first-line assessments, and support delegate-level assessments in line with the company’s DPO governance framework. Serve as a privacy contact for supervisory-authority inquiries, customer privacy audits, and security questionnaires. Track developments across the privacy and adjacent-regulatory landscape (e.g., NIS2, DORA, and EU Data Act), and translate regulatory change into concrete program action decisions. Must Haves J.D. from an accredited law school and member in good standing of at least one U.S. state bar. CIPP/E, CIPP/US certifications 6-8+ years of relevant experience, with strong depth in privacy and data protection law and program execution. Deep, current expertise in European privacy and digital regulation — GDPR/UK GDPR and working familiarity with NIS2, DORA, the EU AI Act, and the EU Data Act — and how they interact for an AI company. Demonstrated experience operating in or advising technology companies, ideally in cybersecurity, SaaS, or cloud, including AI/ML products. Meaningful experience contributing to and helping run a privacy program (beyond pure advisory work) in a fast-moving, global environment. Experience providing product legal counseling alongside privacy. Pragmatic judgment. Starts from the business objective and finds the compliant path, offering options and conditions rather than a reflexive “no,” and earning trust as an enabler, not a gate. Strong drafting and judgment on complex privacy agreements (DPAs, SCCs, subprocessor terms), and the ability to set positions, act as an escalation point for the teams who negotiate them, and flag novel issues for escalation. Sound judgment applied to significant, novel, and ambiguous issues, with accountability for outcomes and escalating direction calls as appropriate, while developing subject-matter credibility internally. The drive and assertiveness to own initiatives and drive them to completion with minimal oversight, and the ability to lead through influence, including to persuade diverse senior stakeholders. Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex privacy issues to business stakeholders. Fluency with AI tooling and the ability to build and iterate on automation workflows — you have used AI to do real work and can specify, prototype, and refine it, holding it to a high accuracy and human-review standard. Nice to Have Experience supporting a DPO, including familiarity with independence and governance expectations. Familiarity with privacy and data protection regimes beyond the EU/US — e.g., LGPD (Brazil), PIPEDA (Canada), APPI (Japan). Experience supporting Works Councils and multi-jurisdiction employee/candidate privacy. Experience with privacy tooling and with AI/LLM-based workflow automation. Familiarity with security and privacy audit frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701/42001). CIPM, CIPT, AIGP certifications #LI-ME1 Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Base salary range: $199,800—$235,000 USD A note on AI in our process: Abnormal AI uses AI-assisted tools to help our recruiting team prepare for candidate interviews. These tools analyze resume content and role requirements to suggest interview questions and areas for the interviewer to explore.They do not make hiring decisions or screen candidates automatically. Every decision about a candidacy is made by a person. Further, if your application is successful and Abnormal AI makes a conditional offer of employment, we will carry out pre-employment checks which must be successfully completed to progress to a final offer. All processes and pre-employment checks are in line with prevailing legislation and Abnormal AI’s policies relevant to our security and privacy standards. Abnormal AI is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. item.title: Commercial Counsel
item.description: Commercial Counsel Organization: Fireworks AI Location: San Mateo,CA | New York, NY Date Posted: 10/21/2026 About Us: Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that’s building the future of enterprise AI. About the Legal team We’re building the infrastructure that democratizes access to intelligence. By serving state-of-the-art models to enterprises and advancing open source, we enable organizations to truly own their own intelligence. Our legal team exists to make that mission possible, responsibly and at scale, because we believe broad access to AI is one of the most consequential things we can build for society. Our legal team is defined by high integrity, high character, and high trust. We’re low-ego, collaborative, kind, and supportive people who are genuinely excited to be part of a team. We win together or not at all. About the role As Commercial Counsel, you’ll be a foundational member of a growing legal team, serving as a trusted partner to our go-to-market organization as it scales rapidly. You’ll own commercial contracting across the deal lifecycle — drafting, negotiating, and closing customer agreements — and show up confidently and credibly across the table with our customers and partners. Beyond core sales support, you’ll also counsel our marketing team on sponsorship and partnership agreements, and handle standard vendor and procurement matters. This role initially reports to the General Counsel. What you’ll do. Serve as lead commercial counsel on customer contracts, NDAs, and related agreements supporting the sales organization. Partner strategically with sales teams to structure deals, manage risk, and keep deals moving without sacrificing sound judgment. Advise marketing on sponsorship agreements and go-to-market campaigns. Handle standard vendor and procurement agreements. Help build the scalable templates, playbooks, and processes a founding legal function needs. Minimum Qualifications 9+ years of relevant experience, with a mix of law firm and in-house ideal. Experience in hypergrowth environments preferred. A JD and membership in at least one US state bar. Strong command of commercial contracting, able to operate independently and show up confidently in negotiations. Comfort supporting a fast-moving, rapidly maturing sales organization, and translating legal complexity into practical guidance. Fastidious attention to detail, excellent organizational skills, and energized by standing up process rather than inheriting it. AI-forward, builder’s mindset, with a demonstrated ability to use AI tools to streamline daily workflows and accelerate efficiency. Total compensation for this role also includes meaningful equity in a fast-growing startup, along with a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package. Base salary is determined by a range of factors including individual qualifications, experience, skills, market data, and work location. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. Why Fireworks? Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving. Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally. Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results. Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Securities Counsel
item.description: Securities Counsel Organization: Faraday Future (FF) Location: El Segundo, CA Date Posted: 10/21/2026 The Company: Faraday Future (FF) is a California-based mobility company, leveraging the latest technologies and world’s best talent to realize exciting new possibilities in mobility. We’re producing user-centric, technology-first vehicles to establish new paradigms in human-vehicle interaction. We’re not just seeking to change how our cars work – we’re seeking to change the way we drive. At FF, we’re creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact. Your Role: We’re seeking a Securities Counsel who can support our fast-growing business across corporate, securities, commercial, and regulatory matters. You’ll work closely with the Head of Legal and cross-functional teams to provide practical advice that keeps us compliant and supports our growth in the capital markets. Key Responsibilities: Securities and Capital Markets Manage the Company’s SEC filings, securities compliance, and public disclosure matters, including periodic and current reporting, securities offering and registration filings, insider reporting, material event disclosures, and related regulatory matters. Support corporate governance and disclosure controls, including board and committee matters, Regulation FD compliance, and administration of the insider trading policy. Support the Company’s capital markets and financing transactions, including equity, debt, and other securities financings, registered offerings, private placements, and exempt offerings under Regulation D and Regulation S; provide legal support on transaction structuring and the drafting, review, negotiation, and closing of transaction documents, and coordinate with investors, underwriters, placement agents, and outside counsel. Manage or support compliance with Nasdaq listing rules and continued listing requirements, including related filings, notifications, shareholder approval requirements, and communications with Nasdaq. Provide practical legal guidance to internal teams on the Securities Act, Exchange Act, Investment Company Act, Investment Advisers Act, FINRA rules, and related AML and custody requirements. Draft, review, and negotiate commercial and financial agreements, including underwriting, placement agent, brokerage, custody, investment advisory, and technology service agreements. Support M&A transactions, strategic partnerships, and cross-border corporate structuring, and oversee subsidiary maintenance in coordination with outside counsel. Support responses to SEC comments and inquiries, Nasdaq inquiries, and other securities regulatory matters. General Corporate Legal Support Support corporate governance and entity matters, including board and committee materials, resolutions, minutes, consents, and maintenance of corporate records, in coordination with the Legal team. Draft, review, and negotiate routine commercial agreements, including customer, vendor, licensing, nondisclosure, consulting, and technology service agreements. Coordinate with outside counsel on subsidiary maintenance, cross-border corporate structures, and applicable governmental and regulatory filings and ongoing compliance requirements. Provide practical legal support to internal business and functional teams on day-to-day operational matters, including employment, data privacy, anti-corruption, and intellectual property, involving specialist counsel as appropriate. Help develop scalable legal processes and a corporate governance framework appropriate for a U.S. public company. Basic Qualifications: J.D. or LL.M. degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing. 4–7 years of experience at a leading law firm or in-house legal department. Strong foundation in corporate and securities law, with experience advising on fund structures or investment products preferred. Excellent communication, drafting, and project management skills. Pragmatic, detail-oriented, and able to balance legal risk with business goals. Preferred Qualifications: Fluency in both Mandarin and English. Experience with registered and private fund vehicles, exempt offerings (e.g., Regulation D and Regulation S), or cross-border investment structures. Prior in-house experience at a public company or financial institution. A genuine interest in securities regulation, capital markets, and financial services legal operations. Annual Salary Range: $130,000 – $160,000 Perks + Benefits Healthcare + dental + vision benefits (Free for you/discounted for family) 401(k) options Casual dress code + relaxed work environment Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere Faraday Future is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. item.title: Manager, Social Content Production
item.description: Manager, Social Content Production Organization: Faraday Future Location: El Segundo, CA Date Posted: 10/21/2026 The Company: Faraday Future is a California-based technology company focused on the design, engineering, and development of intelligent, connected electric vehicles and related artificial intelligence–enabled technologies. Founded in 2014, the Company’s mission is to disrupt the automotive and technology industries by creating user-centric, technology-first experiences. The Company, together with its controlled subsidiaries, operates across multiple technology-driven areas, including AI electric vehicles, robotics, and its crypto business (AIXC), all under its upgraded Global EAI Industry Bridge Strategy, marking the beginning of a new chapter in AI mobility and Web3 integration. The Company aims to leverage the latest technologies and world’s best talent to realize exciting new possibilities across all of these lines. Faraday Future’s automotive business exemplifies its vision for luxury, innovation, and performance, while its FX strategy aims to introduce mass production models equipped with state-of-the-art luxury technology derived from the FF brand, targeted towards a broader market with middle-to-low price range offerings. FF is committed to redefining mobility through AI innovation. Join us in shaping the future of intelligent transportation and technology by creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact. Your Role: The Manager, Social Content Production will serve as the head of the Social Content Production Mechanism within the Global Social Media Center (GSMC). This role sits at the core of GSMC’s mid-end capability layer, responsible for translating social content strategy into high-quality, platform-ready, and scalable content assets. The Senior Manager will build and lead a cross-functional production team — encompassing content direction, short-form editing, VFX, AIGC creation, and content operations — while concurrently owning the Instagram account and serving as the Social Content Strategist for brand narrative and product storytelling. This is a player-coach role requiring both creative vision and operational rigor to sustain a high-output, AI-augmented content production engine. Key Responsibilities: Production Mechanism Leadership: Build, lead, and continuously optimize the Social Content Production Mechanism — a mid-end team comprising a Content Director, VFX Artist(s), Film Cutter, AI Creative Director, and Content Operations. Own content production SOPs, template systems, and delivery standards that enable all platform Account Owners to execute at speed and quality. Content Standards & Asset Library: Establish and govern content production standards, reusable template libraries, and multi-platform format guidelines (short-form video, image-text, Reels, etc.). Ensure all produced assets are structured for downstream reuse by Content Commerce, matrix accounts, and live streaming. Social Content Strategy: Own the brand narrative design and Message House for the social layer. Drive modularization of product messaging into platform-native content formats. Lead the long-to-short content adaptation process, ensuring product and brand stories are consistently translated across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X, and LinkedIn. AI & Automation Integration: Actively integrate AIGC tools (e.g., Runway, ElevenLabs, Midjourney, and similar) into the production pipeline. Collaborate with the AI Workflow Center to connect content production with automation workflows, including content versioning, matrix distribution, and live clip generation. Instagram Account Ownership (Concurrent): Serve as the Instagram Account Owner, overseeing official account content, Executive IP content, and brand matrix account operations on IG. Responsible for content planning, brand visual expression, publishing cadence, and platform KPIs including follower growth, engagement rate, and Reels performance. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with the Visual Creative Center (VCC) for high-end asset adaptation, with Content Commerce (CCC) for matrix content training and production support, and with the Brand Department for narrative alignment. Serve as the production liaison for product launch content cycles (S3 system). Outsourcing & Resource Management: Manage the relationship with the China-based outsourcing production company for overflow video production, design support, and surge capacity. Define briefing standards, quality benchmarks, and delivery timelines for all external production partners. Performance Tracking & Optimization: Monitor content production output metrics, platform performance data, and asset reuse rates. Feed insights back into the production pipeline to continuously raise content quality, format efficiency, and cross-platform impact. Basic Qualifications: Experience: 5+ years of experience in social media content production, digital content creation, or branded video production, with 2+ years in a team lead or management capacity. Experience supporting multi-platform social strategies at scale is required. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Film, Media Production, Marketing, or a related field. Production Expertise: Deep hands-on knowledge of short-form video production workflows for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. Proficiency in post-production tools (Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, or equivalents). Content Strategy: Demonstrated ability to translate brand and product narratives into engaging, platform-native content. Experience developing brand messaging frameworks, content SOPs, or editorial guidelines. AI Content Tools: Working knowledge of AIGC creation tools (e.g., Runway, Midjourney, ElevenLabs, or similar). Comfortable building AI-assisted workflows into a production team’s daily operations. Leadership: Proven track record of building and managing creative production teams. Able to lead a cross-functional group of editors, designers, VFX artists, and content ops with clarity and accountability. Bilingual: Strong proficiency in both English and Mandarin Chinese, with the ability to develop content for both CN and US audiences. Cross-Functional Agility: Comfortable working across social media, commerce, brand, and marketing functions in a fast-moving, matrix-style organization. Preferred Qualifications: Experience in the technology, EV, robotics, or AI hardware sectors Familiarity with AI workflow automation platforms (e.g., ManyChat, PostEverywhere, Frameloop, or similar distribution/automation tools) Experience managing content production for both domestic (US/China) and international (Middle East, Southeast Asia) audiences Prior experience as a platform Account Owner with direct KPI ownership (follower growth, engagement, reach) Understanding of content commerce ecosystems, including how social content feeds into conversion and lead generation funnels Perks + Benefits Healthcare + dental + vision benefits (Free for you/discounted for family) 401(k) options Casual dress code + relaxed work environment Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere “Soul of Faraday” community outreach team Faraday Future is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. item.title: Senior Manager, PR & Social Media
item.description: Senior Manager, PR & Social Media Organization: CB Insights Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/21/2026 The Role You’ll Play CB Insights is looking for a Senior Manager of PR & Social Media to help build our reputation as the authority on private technology companies. Your job is to turn what we uniquely know into stories people want to pay attention to – and then find creative ways to make those stories travel. You’ll work closely with our analysts, executives, and startup founders to uncover stories behind the companies and technologies shaping the future. You’ll use PR and social to amplify our point of view, grow our audience, and make CB Insights a source people actively follow for what matters in private tech. This is a highly creative, hands-on role for someone with strong editorial instincts, deep media expertise, sharp creative taste, and an instinct for bold ideas that earn attention. Your Key Responsibilities Content & Storytelling Turn CB Insights’ research and analyst judgment into compelling stories about the companies and technologies shaping the future. Build founder and operator interviews into a consistent storytelling engine that brings our intelligence and the people behind it to life, while attracting more founders into the process. Partner with analysts to develop strong points of view that give people a reason to follow CB Insights. Social Media Build a distinctive social presence that grows the audience for CB Insights and our analysts. Turn our strongest research, stories, and points of view into bold, original social formats that earn attention and give people a reason to follow CB Insights. Develop analysts and executives into recognizable voices in the areas where CB Insights has expertise. Build relationships with influential people and communities that can help our content reach the right people. Activate our community, events, and recognized companies to help amplify the stories and insights they’re part of. PR & Earned Media Build relationships with tier 1 journalists and influential industry publications most relevant to our customers. Drive earned media around our flagship lists and research to expand their reach and strengthen CB Insights’ authority. Develop timely media angles around the markets and companies our analysts cover and rate, helping amplify their point of view and build credibility. Turn major partnerships into broader stories that strengthen our credibility, and introduce CB Insights to new audiences. Shape the CEO’s external communications and point of view across major company, market, and industry moments. Prepare executives and analysts to represent CB Insights effectively in interviews, with clear messaging, strong talking points, and practical coaching. What You Bring to the Table 5+ years of experience in public relations and social media, ideally focused on technology. Strong creative instincts and a track record of developing unconventional ideas that break through. Exceptional editorial judgment and an instinct for finding the story inside data, research, and conversations. Excellent writer who can make complex ideas clear and interesting. Proven ability to build strong journalist relationships and earn meaningful coverage. Deep understanding of how to build an audience through social and earned distribution. Experience developing executives or other experts into credible public voices. Highly creative and willing to experiment with unconventional ways to earn attention. Ability to operate independently and take an idea from concept through creation and distribution. #LI-Hybrid Please note this is a US-based role. In addition to base salary listed below, this role is also eligible for a bonus opportunity. Compensation $122,000 – $155,000 USD What we’re all about CB Insights is the leader in predictive intelligence on private companies—turning exclusive data on millions of firms into early, trusted signals on future performance and direction. The company pioneered predictive intelligence with its Mosaic Score—the first system to reliably forecast the outlook for a private company—and has since built it into a comprehensive platform of AI and data capabilities. Today, leading strategy, investment, and business development teams rely on CB Insights to identify the right companies, markets, and opportunities before their competitors do. CB Insights Leadership Principles At CB Insights, everyone is expected to be a leader. These leadership principles are like an operating system for our culture. Use the principles as a practical guide to making decisions. We are what we repeatedly do. By living the principles outlined below, we will build an outstanding company and do insanely great work. Solve customer problems. It’s our highest calling. Designing a product? Start from the customer problem it solves. Updating our sales process? Flip it around, and simplify the customer buying process. Think BIG! Start small. Great changes start with a first step. Find it. Take it. Build a system around what works. This is the secret to bringing a vision to life. Go and see with your own eyes. Meet the customer, use the product, talk to the field. Great systems aren’t built from afar. Priorities: Choose one. Leaders give the gift of clarity. They find the most important thing and do it. Max power. Top speed. Danger zones: Bureaucracy. May the best ideas and execution win. Complexity. Leaders use frameworks and systems to simplify. No commitment. Leaders don’t compromise just to get along. Debate. Disagree. But once a decision is made, commit. Leaving what’s important unsaid or undone. No “circling back.” Data informs. Insight transforms. Pull the thread. Ask why. Leaders are curious. They use what they learn to create clarity. Insist on excellence. Leaders set high standards and overcome obstacles. They do the kind of work they’re excited to share with the world. Live off the land. Leaders creatively use resources already available to them – especially AI – to execute and automate their work. Good judgment. Leaders have it. Where it comes from: insight, listening, first-hand experience. How to apply it: carefully on big, hard to reverse decisions. Swiftly on limited, easy to reverse ones. Help others. Leaders know we’re building this together. You’ll want to work here if You are excited about how AI is transforming tech You are hungry for feedback and the chance to grow Your instinct is to work smarter not harder You love developing as a SME with a strong POV You are motivated by challenges and big ideas You believe in personal accountability What we offer: Industry Insight: over 500k+ people follow our tech newsletter: sign up here Holistic compensation: Competitive cash compensation, comprehensive healthcare coverage (PPO, HSA, and FSA options), multiple mental health resources, 401(k) with company match, annual professional development stipend, and generous paid time off. About Our Pay Practices We believe in recognizing and rewarding excellence. Our commitment to fairness means that compensation decisions are informed by qualifications, location, internal equity, and current market data. While we aim to hire at our established Hiring Target, starting pay may vary based on factors such as market rates, the qualified pool of candidates, and individual experience. Equal Opportunity Employer: At CB Insights we know that innovation comes from collaboration, belonging, and diverse perspectives. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer – all applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. item.title: Legal Counsel
item.description: Legal Counsel Organization: Razer Location: Irvine, CA Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Joining Razer will place you on a global mission to revolutionize the way the world games. Razer is a place to do great work, offering you the opportunity to make an impact globally while working across a global team located across 5 continents. Razer is also a great place to work, providing you the unique, gamer-centric #LifeAtRazer experience that will put you in an accelerated growth, both personally and professionally. Job Responsibilities : As Legal Counsel, you will provide practical, business-oriented legal support to Razer’s global business and long-term objectives, in line with the parent company’s legal strategy. This is a general corporate counsel role with a strong commercial contracting focus, while also supporting intellectual property, brand protection, IP transactional, technology, regulatory, and dispute-related matters. The role requires sound legal judgment, commercial pragmatism, and the ability to work closely with product, sales, marketing, customer advocacy, human resources, finance, and regional teams. Essential duties and responsibilities: Draft, review, negotiate, and close a broad range of commercial agreements, including customer, vendor, distributor, services, technology, software, marketing, licensing, and strategic partnership agreements. Provide practical day-to-day legal advice to product, sales, marketing, customer advocacy, human resources, finance, and regional business teams on commercial, corporate, regulatory, technology, and operational matters. Support intellectual property and brand protection matters, including brand usage, trademark and copyright issues, marketing clearance, trademark protection and prosecution, infringement reviews, enforcement strategy, and coordination with external counsel where needed. Support IP-related transactions and commercial arrangements, including license agreements, collaboration agreements, sponsorships, co-marketing arrangements, content-related agreements, and technology transactions. Assist with commercial, IP, brand protection, and technology-related disputes, including pre-litigation strategy, claims assessment, settlement support, and coordination with internal stakeholders and external counsel. Create, improve, and implement scalable legal processes, policies, playbooks, templates, and training materials to support efficient legal service delivery across the business. Provide training on contract management, brand usage, marketing practices, data privacy, AI-enabled workflows, and practical risk management. Stay current on legal developments affecting consumer technology, gaming, digital content, AI-enabled tools, privacy, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, and brand protection. Other duties as assigned. Pre-Requisites : Qualifications: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 4+ years of post-qualification experience in a law firm and/or in-house legal department, preferably supporting technology, consumer electronics, gaming, digital content, or other fast-moving commercial businesses. Strong commercial contracting experience is required, with the ability to advise on a broad range of corporate, commercial, regulatory, technology, and operational legal matters. Experience with intellectual property, brand protection, licensing, content, software, marketing, or technology transactions is strongly preferred. Litigation, dispute resolution, or pre-litigation claims management experience is useful, particularly in commercial, technology, IP, or brand protection matters. Strong negotiation, drafting, analytical, and risk-assessment skills, with the ability to balance legal risk, business objectives, and operational speed. Ability to provide clear, practical, and commercially minded legal advice to stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Ability to build strong cross-functional relationships and manage multiple matters independently in a fast-paced, global business environment. Familiarity with AI-enabled workflows, digital content platforms, software products, and emerging technology issues is preferred. Education/Experience: J.D. degree from an accredited United States law school. Certificate and licenses: Membership in one of the US State Bars required. Salary Ranges: $81,115.00 – $135,192.00 (per annum) Disclaimer: Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location. Razer is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that diverse teams drive better ideas, better products, and a stronger culture. We are committed to providing an inclusive, respectful, and fair workplace for every employee across all the countries we operate in. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, colour, nationality, ancestry, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, marital status, or any other characteristic protected under local laws. Where needed, we provide reasonable accommodations – including for disability or religious practices – to ensure every team member can perform and contribute at their best. Are you game? item.title: Senior Manager, Digital Securities & Market Structure Policy
item.description: Senior Manager, Digital Securities & Market Structure Policy Organization: Coinbase Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you’re ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase. As the Senior Manager, Digital Securities & Market Structure Policy, you’ll be a critical stakeholder in Coinbase’s engagement with the SEC on digital asset market structure, trading, and issuance rulemaking. You’ll be deeply engaged in the rulemaking process, bringing deep corporate finance, trading, and issuance expertise to bear on active rule proposals, comment letter strategy, and requests for no-action or exemptive relief. This role shapes how Coinbase navigates the evolving U.S. securities regulatory landscape, translating proposed and final rules into actionable guidance for Legal, Product, and executive stakeholders. What you’ll do: Drive Coinbase’s engagement on active and pending SEC rulemakings related to market structure, trading, and securities issuance, ensuring Coinbase’s positions are well-represented throughout the rulemaking lifecycle. Lead the development of Coinbase’s comment letter strategy in response to SEC proposals affecting digital asset markets, drafting or directing substantive responses that advance Coinbase’s regulatory objectives. Build and maintain relationships with SEC staff and Commissioners’ offices, positioning Coinbase as a credible, constructive participant in the policy process. Translate proposed and final rules into internal guidance for Legal, Product, and executive stakeholders, identifying compliance implications, operational requirements, and strategic opportunities. Partner with Legal to assess regulatory risk and compliance implications of new rules, including evaluating paths for no-action letters or exemptive relief where necessary. Represent Coinbase externally in industry working groups and regulator engagements on market structure policy, shaping industry-wide positions and coalition strategies. Required Skills and Experience: 10+ years of experience in securities law, market structure policy, or corporate finance, with direct, hands-on experience working at or with the SEC on rulemaking processes. Deep understanding of the SEC rulemaking process and Administrative Procedure Act, with demonstrated experience drafting or responding to public rulemaking comments. Substantive expertise in either trading market structure or securities issuance and corporate finance mechanics, with the ability to apply that knowledge to active digital asset rule proposals. Proven ability to translate complex regulatory text into actionable guidance for cross-functional teams, with direct experience briefing senior executives and external regulators on policy implications. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)). Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus): $252,620—$297,200 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of 3 applications within a 6-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. US Applicants: View Employee Rights, Know Your Rights, and E-Verify Notice of Participation. Accommodations: If you are an individual with a disability who needs a reasonable accommodation, email us your request and contact info at accommodations[at]coinbase.com.
