item.title: Communications Manager, Policy & Public Affairs
item.description: Communications Manager, Policy & Public Affairs Organization: Coinbase Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you’re ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase. We’re hiring a Communications Manager, Policy & Public Affairs to join our Communications team and lead the narratives that shape how the public, press, and policymakers understand crypto. This team sits at the center of Coinbase’s highest-stakes regulatory and legislative moments, translating complex policy positions into clear, compelling stories that win public support. You’ll own our policy communications strategy end to end, serving as the primary architect of narratives that connect crypto to financial freedom and consumer choice across the US political landscape. What you’ll do: Own the communications strategy for high-stakes legislative and regulatory initiatives, ensuring Coinbase has a clear, consistent voice across every policy moment. Partner with legal and policy teams to translate complex litigation, regulatory filings, and policy positions into winning public narratives. Lead earned media execution by leveraging deep relationships with national political, financial, and technology journalists to drive proactive coverage and manage rapid-response cycles. Drive digital communications across X and other social platforms to speak directly to policymakers, thought leaders, and the crypto community. Shape advocacy communications that elevate consumer voices and demonstrate the real-world impact of pro-innovation policy to legislators and regulators. Build long-term brand authority by maintaining Coinbase’s position as the most trusted leader in the crypto space through multiple election and regulatory cycles. Required Skills and Experience: 7+ years in high-stakes political communications, including direct experience in Congressional offices, political campaigns, or agency rapid-response environments. Proven track record as an on-the-record spokesperson managing high-pressure national media inquiries with consistent, disciplined messaging. Demonstrated ability to drive news cycles and move public opinion through X and other digital platforms, with a portfolio of measurable results. Deep fluency in the US regulatory and legislative landscape, with experience translating policy complexity into accessible public narratives. Track record of building and maintaining relationships with Tier 1 political and financial journalists that consistently result in earned coverage. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. Job #: P76576 #LI-remote Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)). Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus): $170,765—$200,900 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of 3 applications within a 6-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. US Applicants: View Employee Rights, Know Your Rights, and E-Verify Notice of Participation. Accommodations: If you are an individual with a disability who needs a reasonable accommodation, email us your request and contact info at accommodations[at]coinbase.com. item.title: Senior Director, Legal, Commercial Transactions
item.description: Senior Director, Legal, Commercial Transactions Organization: Equinix Location: Dallas, TX Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Who are we? Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet. A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work. Job Summary: We are more than legal professionals protecting Equinix’s interests. We are valued business partners, known as responsive, consistent and proactive. We take customer service seriously and strive for excellence in our execution. Equinix’s dynamic growth trajectory keeps us on our toes and constantly learning. Our strong relationships with our internal clients, fueled by our solution-driven orientation and creative yet practical advice, bring us to the table early and often and lead to interesting and rewarding work in support of Equinix’s overall business objectives. Our global Legal department may span four continents, but we are One Legal – a true team working together across borders in support of our shared strategic objectives. We work hard but take time to celebrate our accomplishments – both professional and personal, with a healthy dose of fun thrown in along the way. We look forward to coming to work every day to support Equinix and each other and highly value the “team first” culture we have created. We are proud that our collective effort has led to Equinix One Legal being named as one of the Top Innovative Law Departments in North America by the Financial Times. This open role of Senior Director, Americas will be responsible for supporting the one of the 2 Strategic accounts teams and is the leader of the Global Contracts Americas region team. Responsible for the team’s contracting support for named accounts and as lead representing the Americas Region, this role is instrumental in leading these teams and closing complex, strategic deals and keeping abreast of the legal developments in the region. This role advises the business in alignment with corporate goals and objectives and risk thresholds in a manner that supports the objectives for the global business. Adept at using and leveraging technology to better scale the organization, this role oversees deals which have significant impact to the business, specifically the Americas business and is charged with building relationships with our Americas stakeholders and in concert with others in the Global Contracts team, to take charge of specialized areas which are entrusted to them by the Vice President Global Contracts or the Chief Legal Officer as the case may be. Location Americas-based. The role must be positioned to provide effective leadership and senior stakeholder coverage across Americas working hours, while operating globally across time zones. Reports to Vice President, Legal, Global Contracts. Key Responsibilities This role is a senior people leader, commercial lawyer and trusted business adviser responsible for these mandates: Americas leadership: Lead and coordinate Global Contracts’ presence and engagement across the Americas, representing GC with Americas business leadership and ensuring that regional priorities are understood, translated into clear legal support strategies and delivered effectively. Global Strategic Accounts leadership: Lead the Strategics team and the legal support for its globally significant portfolio of named customers, currently comprising a defined group of AI, Neocloud, accounts and Channel partners. Global Contracts leadership: Act as an active member of the Global Contracts leadership team, contributing to the function’s strategy, culture, talent, transformation, operating model and overall performance. This is a highly visible role at the intersection of legal leadership, major deal execution, emerging technology and business strategy. The role will lead complex, high-value and high-impact negotiations; guide and develop a geographically dispersed team; and provide clear, commercially grounded advice to senior leaders across Sales, Customer and Revenue, Finance, Operations, Product, Technology and other functions. The Senior Director will bring a strong vision for the development of the Americas Global Contracts organisation and the Strategics team. They will use technology, data, disciplined operating practices and effective people leadership to improve the speed, quality, consistency and scalability of legal support, working closely and collaboratively with the rest of the One Legal team globally. Key Responsibilities 1. Americas leadership and business partnership Serve as the senior Global Contracts (GC) leader for the Americas (Canada, US, Latin America, South America), representing GC in senior business forums and building trusted relationships across Sales, Finance, Operations, Product and Technology. Translate Americas priorities and risks into clear legal support plans, ensuring GC is engaged early and support is responsive, consistent and commercially pragmatic. Provide senior escalation support on significant Americas and strategic matters (including complex customer negotiations, strategic opportunities, disputes, public-sector opportunities outside the US Federal business), coordinate Americas-based GC colleagues, and manage external counsel where required. 2. Leadership of Strategics team and its named-account portfolio Lead the team, setting its vision, strategy and operating model, with overall accountability for legal support to its portfolio of named AI, Neocloud, SaaS and semiconductor accounts, Channel/OEM accounts. Maintain close oversight of account strategy, pipeline, risk, resourcing and escalations, and ensure effective delivery across the full deal lifecycle. Partner with the Channel Lead on Channel go-to-market support, collaborate with other GC and One Legal leaders where needed and/or portfolios intersect, and shape the team’s future structure as it matures. 3. Complex deal leadership and negotiation Personally lead or oversee the most complex, strategic and high-value transactions, operating as an experienced and credible negotiator across customers, partners, external counsel and senior stakeholders. Balance commercial, legal and operational considerations, present clear recommendations to executives, and drive matters to closure. Convert deal experience into scalable positions, templates and training, while mentoring the team to build negotiating capability and domain knowledge. . 4. People leadership and capability development Lead, coach and develop a team of lawyers and contracts professionals, setting a clear vision, objectives and a collaborative, high-performing “team first” culture. Provide clear direction, candid feedback and meaningful development; manage performance fairly and recognise strong contribution. Close capability gaps through mentoring and succession planning, and develop future leaders able to work across boundaries. 5. Global Contracts leadership Act as a full member of the GC leadership team, contributing to strategy, operating model, talent, culture and resourcing. Work with peer leaders to build consistency across teams while respecting portfolio and regional differences. Support global initiatives (policy, process, technology, transformation) and model enterprise leadership across GC and One Legal. 6. Technology, transformation and scale Champion technology, including AI tools, to improve service delivery, reporting and decision-making, and drive standardisation to increase capacity. Ensure the team adopts GC platforms, processes and knowledge resources, using data to monitor workload, risk and performance. Lead transformation in a way that builds team capability and confidence, not just system adoption. 7. Governance, risk and operational excellence Work with the VP, Global Contracts to apply practical risk frameworks, policies and escalation paths, ensuring consistency with Company policy and governance. Oversee work allocation, resourcing, budget and external counsel use, with clear reporting on significant matters and risks. Promote collaboration with shared-services teams and drive operational excellence through accountability and continuous improvement. Qualifications, Skills and Experience The successful candidate will bring: A law degree and admission to practise in a relevant jurisdiction (e.g. a state in the United States of America). Substantial post-qualification legal experience appropriate for a Senior Director role, preferably including at least 15 years of experience in a similar role (having at least five years of strong law-firm experience is a preference). Deep experience in negotiating and in commercial contracting and in leading complex, strategic, high-value and high-impact transactions. Demonstrated success as a people leader, with a genuine interest in managing, coaching and developing lawyers and contracts professionals. A clear leadership vision and experience evolving a team’s capabilities, structure, operating model or strategic direction. Experience supporting senior business leaders in an international, fast-moving and commercially demanding environment. Experience operating successfully in a matrix organisation and working across functions, reporting lines, geographies and time zones. Strong commercial and legal judgement, with the ability to assess risk, balance legal and business considerations and recommend practical solutions. Executive presence and the confidence to advise, challenge and influence the most senior leaders in the organisation. Excellent communicat

item.title: Senior Director Global Regulatory, Digital
item.description: Senior Director Global Regulatory, Digital Organization: AstraZeneca Location: Gaithersburg, MD Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Job Title: Senior Director Global Regulatory, Digital Location: Gaithersburg At AstraZeneca, we put patients first and strive to meet their unmet needs worldwide. Working here means being entrepreneurial, thinking big and working together to make the impossible a reality. If you are swift to action, confident to lead, willing to collaborate, and curious about what science can do, then you’re our kind of person. Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects. Our dedication to sustainability is also central to our culture and part of what makes AstraZeneca a great place to work. We know the health of people, the planet and our business are interconnected which is why we’re taking ambitious action to tackle some of the biggest challenges of our time, from climate change to access to healthcare and disease prevention. Introduction to Role: The Senior Director, Global Regulatory Digital Strategy is accountable for the development and implementation of a robust digital strategy which aligns to and meets the needs of the Global Regulatory business. In this role, you will partner extensively with senior Regulatory business leaders to ensure understanding of business priorities and needs. You will also partner extensively with other key internal stakeholder groups (e.g., IT, Enterprise AI Unit, Enterprise Data Office, Regulatory Systems, Process Excellence, Change Mgmt., Finance, etc.) as well as drive collaboration with key external industry partners/peers/agencies to ensure delivery and implementation of a robust Global Regulatory Digital Strategy encompassing people, process and technology. You will lead the development and implementation of a Global Regulatory data strategy that enables successful achievement of the overall Digital strategy. To assure success in this space, you will work closely with and influence other internal Regulatory data teams as well as data offices across R&D, IT and at the AZ-enterprise level. You will also lead a team of digital product owners that will assist in strategy development as well as drive the successful achievement of annual strategy goals. You will mentor and guide these resources to ensure continuous learning and effective engagement to drive strategy delivery to plan and timelines. This leadership role will also ensure proper digital governance in collaboration with the Regulatory Technology Governance Council (RTGC) and Regulatory Management Board (RMB). The Senior Director, Global Regulatory Digital Strategy will drive the evolution and continued improvement of both the RTGC as well as Regulatory’s Global digital portfolio management capabilities to ensure and safeguard successful achievement of the Global Regulatory Digital Strategy. As the Senior Director, Global Regulatory Digital Strategy, you will bring strong Regulatory and leadership skills as well as extensive demonstrated success in the digital arena (e.g., AI, agentic AI, data, digital strategies, product ownership, etc.). Accountabilities: Strategic Leadership: Develop and implement a digital strategy (data strategy inclusive) that supports the Regulatory mission and objectives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals. Digital Transformation: Partner with digital initiative sponsors to leverage innovative technology, people and process improvement opportunities to drive speed, efficiency, transparency, and increased business value across Regulatory. Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders (IT, Process, Change Mgmt., and Regulatory bodies/consortia/vendors) to ensure digital strategies meet current regulatory requirements and future industry expectations. Innovation: Identify and implement innovative digital solutions to that address business priorities. Team Management: Lead and mentor a team of digital professionals focused on delivery of innovation use cases while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and professional development. Data & Analytics: Design and deliver a robust data foundation that enables advanced AI and analytics capabilities across Global Regulatory. Utilize data analytics and reporting tools to measure the effectiveness of digital strategies and make data-driven decisions. Compliance: Ensure all digital initiatives are compliant with regulatory standards and best practices. Governance: Lead the development and evolution of digital governance and portfolio delivery capabilities to safeguard and ensure achievement of business value that aligns with the digital strategy. Digital Expertise: Proficient on current and future digital trends across Pharma or other relevant industries to ensure the Regulatory Digital Strategy remains relevant and competitive. Fiscal Mgmt.: Oversee all financial aspects related to the digital team and portfolio. Lifecycle Management: Partner with Regulatory Systems team to define and ensure appropriate product owner transitions from innovation team to product maintenance team Essential Skills/Experience: Bachelor’s degree in AI/ML, data science or a related field 7+ years’ leadership experience in digital transformation in healthcare, Pharma or a drug development environment 5+ years’ experience in portfolio management and governance Demonstrated ability to lead, influence, and inspire teams towards achieving strategic goals. Strong ability to work collaboratively with various stakeholders, including regulatory bodies and senior leadership. A forward-thinking mindset with a passion for leveraging technology to drive change. Proficient in using data to drive strategic decisions and measure outcomes. A thorough understanding of regulatory compliance and the ability to ensure digital initiatives meet these standards The annual base pay (or hourly rate of compensation) for this position ranges from $212,994 to $319,441. Our positions offer eligibility for various incentives—an opportunity to receive short-term incentive bonuses, equity-based awards for salaried roles and commissions for sales roles. Benefits offered include qualified retirement programs, paid time off (i.e., vacation, holiday, and leaves), as well as health, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans. AstraZeneca is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion and providing a workplace that is free from discrimination. AstraZeneca is committed to accommodating persons with disabilities. Such accommodation is available on request in respect of all aspects of the recruitment, assessment and selection process and may be requested by emailing [email protected] (opens in new window). Closing Date 25-Oct-2026 Our mission is to build an inclusive environment where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and employees. In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please complete the corresponding section in the application form. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Manager, AML/BSA Officer
item.description: Senior Manager, AML/BSA Officer Organization: Mission Lane Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind? We’re looking for a Senior Manager, AML/BSA Officer to own Mission Lane’s AML/BSA Program end to end as our designated AML/BSA Officer, reporting to the Chief Risk Officer. The impact you’ll make Behind every credit card account opened through a Mission Lane sponsor bank, including Mission Lane Bank, N.A. (Proposed), is our promise to protect it as carefully as the customer would themselves. It has to hold up against people actively trying to abuse the system. When that defense works, it’s invisible: a customer never has to think twice about whether their account, or their identity, is safe, while they keep building toward what’s next. The Senior Manager, AML/BSA Officer is who makes sure it keeps working. You’ll own the execution of the AML/BSA Program from day one. This is a build role: you’ll be establishing Mission Lane’s second-line AML/BSA function as our bank charter comes online. This is a step change from where we are today. You’ll operate with independence, exercising judgment on when a risk needs to go to senior management or the Risk Committee of the Board, and you’ll be the person examiners and regulators come to first. In this role, you’ll own End-to-end execution of Mission Lane’s AML/BSA Program as our designated AML/BSA Officer Suspicious activity investigations, escalations, and SAR filings Independent, second-line judgment on AML/BSA risk, including direct escalation of material issues to senior management and the Risk Committee of the Board AML/BSA risk assessments, and remediation tracked through to closure Regular and ad hoc reporting to senior management and the Board on program effectiveness and SAR activity The primary relationship with examiners and auditors on AML/BSA matters Second-line oversight support for OFAC, fraud, and related financial crimes programs, in partnership with Customer Operations, Risk, and Legal You’ll thrive in this role if You’ve built or matured an AML/BSA program before, and you know what it takes to earn credibility with examiners, regulators, and business partners at the same time. You operate independently. You know when something needs to go to senior leadership or the Board, and you don’t need a lot of structure to get there. You can turn dense regulatory requirements into guidance the business can actually act on. You know how to be the person asking the hard question, in a way that builds trust instead of friction. You’re motivated by standing up a program from the ground up, not by running one that already exists. Minimum Qualifications 5+ years of AML/BSA experience, including 3+ years administering AML/BSA programs and interacting directly with regulators Active CAMS certification Strong knowledge of AML/BSA laws and regulations and financial services regulatory compliance frameworks, including second-line oversight and effective challenge expectations Proven ability to independently manage investigations and SAR filings Experience managing and developing a team of compliance or risk professionals Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering executive-level reporting and presentations Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment Able to work remote, with required travel as needed, approximately ~6+ times per year Preferred Qualifications Experience standing up or maturing an AML/BSA program at a de novo bank or newly chartered institution Experience in a credit card or consumer lending environment Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) for regulatory and Board reporting Experience supporting OFAC or broader financial crimes programs in addition to AML/BSA Compensation: Annual full-time starting base salary range: $140,000-$165,000 This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs. Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment. About Mission Lane: Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia. It all started with a realization: nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do. In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores. Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors. Our commitment to a workplace built on respect and dignity is guided by our core value of Unity. We believe that everyone plays a vital role in our shared purpose, and we actively cultivate an environment where all individuals have the opportunity to do their best work. By fostering a culture of empathy and collaboration, we create a strong sense of belonging and support for every team member. Mission Lane is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status. Mission Lane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants who need them for medical or religious reasons, as required by law. Applicants can initiate an accommodation request by contacting [email protected] . Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters. Application Integrity: Our cardholders trust us with their financial well-being, and this trust starts with the integrity of the people on our team. We’re looking for team members who share our dedication to transparency and truth. Please verify that the information in your application is accurate and complete. Providing any information to Mission Lane that is not completely truthful at any point during the application or hiring process may result in removal from the hiring process, disqualification from future opportunities, withdrawal of an offer or other sanctions for candidates and, in addition for employees, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. item.title: Sr. Director Global Law, North America
item.description: Sr. Director Global Law, North America Organization: Mondelēz Global LLC (MDLZ) Location: Chicago, IL | East Hanover, NJ Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Are You Ready to Make It Happen at Mondelēz International? Join our Mission to Lead the Future of Snacking. Make It Matter. The Role Mondelēz Global LLC (MDLZ) is seeking a Sr. Director – Global Law, North America and Global Professional Services Spend Area to serve as the lead lawyer for Mondelez Supply Chain, Procurement in North America (NA) and Global Procurement Professional Services Spend Area. This senior leader role leads and executes the legal strategy of NA’s Supply Chain initiatives and negotiations of commercial agreements with NA and global suppliers. Operating within a highly matrixed environment, this position collaborates directly with senior leaders to drive outcomes, manage risk and enable business objectives. Based in Chicago, IL or East Hanover, NJ, this role reports to the VP & Chief Counsel Global Law and dotted line to the SVP & Chief Counsel, North America. Key Responsibilities Leading a small team of lawyers, including one in Mexico, you will be responsible to: Drive solutions and enable business objectives in a responsible, risk-calculated manner. Ensure sound, strategic legal counsel is provided to MDLZ and its affiliates related to NA’s Supply Chain initiatives, including projects and transactions with external manufacturers and logistic suppliers, and cross-border transactions. Set the legal strategy for negotiations of commercial agreements with NA and global suppliers, including providing strategic guidance related to contractual risk and its cross functional review and approval. Drive a continuous improvement agenda for global contracting strategy, processes, policies, governance, ways of working and technology, identifying and executing opportunities to evolve efficiency, simplification and innovation. Deliver proactive advice on contracting related topics and evolve templates and negotiating standards and positions. Partner with the Litigation NA lead to provide sound and strategic legal advice on negotiation strategies related to contractual claims against suppliers. Build, inspire and empower an inclusive, high performing team that drives solutions through strong business judgment, commercial acumen and calculated risk-taking. This role requires a humble, adaptable, resilient and courageous leader who excels with strong communication skills, sound business judgment, commercial acumen, action bias, a continuous improvement mindset and high learning agility. Required Qualifications 12+ years’ experience in a large, international law firm and multi-national corporate in-house legal department. Juris Doctor (J.D.) or equivalent legal degree from an accredited institution; ability to be licensed in the jurisdiction where employed. Deep expertise in U.S. and international contract law and experience in successfully and strategically supporting Supply Chain initiatives and negotiations with global suppliers. Proven ability to successfully pursue supplier-related claims. Demonstrable experience with technologies, including CLM and AI tools, as part of a contemporary proactive and risk-based contract strategy. Substantial management skills, business judgment and commercial acumen with a capacity to enable decisions with integrity and give risk-calibrated advice demonstrating command of overall business objectives and the risks/rewards of each situation. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; team player who collaborates well with others and can manage numerous matters concurrently in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Comfortable with ambiguity and uncertainty; the ability to remain calm under pressure, adapt nimbly, build trust, instill confidence and influence others to take decisions with imperfect information rather than waiting for full certainty. Experience distilling and communicating complex legal issues for non-legal and multi-cultural audiences, including senior business and functional leaders. Ability to oversee and effectively and efficiently manage internal and external counsel. High degree of initiative, self‐direction, and willingness to challenge the status quo to help drive continuous improvement. Preferred Qualifications 5+ years of experience managing and developing teams. Experience in driving change in a matrixed organization. Experience in dealing with Supply Chain projects in Mexico. Fluency in Spanish. Salary and Benefits: The base salary range for this position is $174,100 to $287,265; the exact salary depends on several factors such as experience, skills, education and location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for participation in a highly competitive bonus program with possibility for overachievement based on performance and company results and eligibility to participate in our long-term incentive program.In addition, Mondelez International offers the following benefits: health insurance, wellness and family support programs, life and disability insurance, retirement savings plans, paid leave programs, education related programs, paid holidays and vacation time. Some of these benefits have eligibility requirements. Many of these benefits are subsidized or fully paid for by the company. No Relocation support available Business Unit Summary The United States is the largest market in the Mondelēz International family with a significant employee and manufacturing footprint. Here, weproduce our well-loved household favorites to provide our consumers with the right snack, at the right moment, made the right way. We have corporate offices, sales, manufacturing and distribution locations throughout the U.S. to ensure our iconic brands—including Oreo and Chips Ahoy! cookies, Ritz, Wheat Thins and Triscuit crackers, and Swedish Fish and Sour Patch Kids confectionery products —are close at hand for our consumers across the country. Mondelēz Global LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Persons with Disabilities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Applicants who require accommodation to participate in the job application process may contact 847-943-5460 for assistance. item.title: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Lead, Federal
item.description: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Lead, Federal Organization: Peregrine Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies, and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally. Our Team At Peregrine, we build software to power critical decision-making for public safety and emergency response organizations. These organizations use our technology to protect lives, protect property, and deliver their best service to the public. We are motivated to help institutions solve their hardest problems through better decision-making. We are passionate about creating cutting-edge, highly scalable data platforms that enable organizations to transform the way they interact with their data. As a team of service-oriented entrepreneurs, we trust each other, help each other, and dive into challenges together. We each strive to be empathetic, curious, inclusive, brave, and exceptional in our execution. Our customers are our partners; we listen to their needs, learn from their experiences, and develop effective software solutions to help them achieve transformational outcomes for their communities. Further, our team is advised by leading experts and practitioners in emergency management, justice, and civil liberties. These experts ensure we develop technology that is both operationally effective and trust-enhancing. Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local governments, federal agencies, and private-sector institutions turn complex and disconnected data into operational intelligence. Our platform supports mission-critical decisions in environments where security, availability, data protection, and customer trust are imperative. As Peregrine expands our work with federal customers, we are building the security and compliance capabilities necessary to operate some of our most sensitive deployments. The Role We are looking for a senior Governance, Risk, and Compliance leader to own Peregrine’s FedRAMP High program and establish the security and compliance foundation required to support Department of War (DoW) deployments at DoD Impact Level (IL) 4, IL5, and IL6, ICD 503 accreditation for Top Secret environments, and agency-specific system authorizations. This is not a generalist compliance or audit-support role. You will translate federal and defense requirements into implementable technical and operational controls and work across Security, Engineering, Product, Legal, Federal Deployment, and GTM to guide those controls through assessment, authorization, and continuous operation as Peregrine’s federal business evolves. Clearance and eligibility. You currently hold, or are able to obtain, an active U.S. security clearance (required), and are based in Washington, D.C. Our Washington, D.C. office is located in the Dupont Circle neighborhood, and this role is expected to be hybrid, with 4 in-office days per week. What You’ll Do Own Peregrine’s FedRAMP High authorization program — sustaining and expanding our existing ATO through continuous monitoring, remediation, and reauthorization, including Peregrine’s transition from FedRAMP Rev. 5 toward applicable FedRAMP 20x requirements. Translate FedRAMP, NIST, federal agency, DoW and Intelligence Community requirements into technical and operational controls and establish the control architecture necessary to support IL4, IL5, and ultimately IL6 deployments alongside ICD 503 environments. Lead agency-specific system authorizations, from initial engagement through ATO issuance and ongoing sponsorship. Partner with Security and Infrastructure Engineering to evaluate system boundaries, Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM), network security, encryption and key management, logging, vulnerability and configuration management, hardening, supply-chain security, and incident response against federal and DoW requirements. Lead authorization artifacts, control implementation statements, evidence, assessment responses, and continuous-monitoring deliverables while ensuring documented controls are supported by architecture, configuration, automation, procedures, and operating evidence. Drive assessment findings and control gaps to closure and develop scalable control ownership, evidence collection, monitoring, and compliance-automation practices that improve the efficiency and quality of Peregrine’s assurance program. Ensure external security representations accurately reflect implemented controls and evidence, and advise Peregrine’s Federal and customer-facing teams during procurements, technical evaluations, security reviews, and customer engagements. About You You are comfortable operating as a senior individual contributor with broad organizational influence and can drive programs across engineering, security, product, legal, operations, and customer-facing teams. You approach compliance as an engineering and risk-management discipline and are willing to challenge weak implementations, unsupported assertions, and inadequate evidence. You can turn complex or evolving requirements into defensible implementation strategies and communicate technical security issues clearly to engineers, executives, assessors, customers, and government security officials. Preferred Certifications 10+ years of experience in information security, GRC, security assurance, or cybersecurity risk management, including personally leading significant portions of obtaining and maintaining FedRAMP High authorization for a cloud service provider (CSP) with one or more cloud service offerings (CSOs). Expertise in FedRAMP program management and federal Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementation through assessment, authorization, and remediation, plus at least two years of continuous monitoring — including 3PAO or government assessor engagement, authorization-package development, POA&M and accepted-weakness remediation, and agency or Authorizing Official engagement. Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 and SP 800-37, FedRAMP, the DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide, DoD cybersecurity risk management (RMF and the successor Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct), DISA SRGs/STIGs, applicable FIPS requirements, control overlays, and federal assessment and authorization practices. Technical understanding of cloud security architecture, including hands-on experience with AWS or AWS GovCloud, Kubernetes or containerized environments, Infrastructure as Code, and modern CI/CD. Experience designing sustainable compliance operations, including control ownership, evidence and weakness management, continuous monitoring, change management, and machine-readable assurance evidence such as OSCAL. Experience advising customer-facing teams through federal procurements, technical evaluations, and customer security reviews. An active or recently active U.S. government security clearance and U.S. citizenship. Bonus Points Direct experience establishing and maintaining DoD IL4, IL5, or IL6 environments. Experience with ICD 503 accreditation and the authorization of National Security Systems, classified systems, or cross-domain solutions. Experience supporting federal or defense customers in environments involving CUI or other sensitive government information. CISSP, CISA, CGRC, CISM, CCSP, or comparable security certifications. Annual Salary + Benefits + Equity (if applicable) + Bonus (if applicable) $158,000 – $184,000 USD Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, certifications or licenses, and specific work location. Information on the benefits offered is here. Peregrine Technologies is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We celebrate diversity and are a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. item.title: Senior Fellow, Energy and Environment
item.description: Senior Fellow, Energy and Environment Organization: R Street Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/21/2026 The R Street Institute—a free-market think tank headquartered in Washington, D.C. and with staff located across the country—seeks a collaborative Senior Fellow for its Energy and Environment program. If you are the right fit, you will report to the Energy and Environment Program Director. If you want to join a mission-driven organization and work toward pragmatic policy solutions, this may be the opportunity for you! Your typical day at R Street may include producing research and written work on market-driven approaches to disaster mitigation; educating state and federal legislators on potential efficient environmental regulations; presenting at events on water scarcity policies managed through clearer water rights and markets rather than mandates; engaging with the media; and coordinating with allies, both in the EcoRight space and the wider environmental community. Other Aspects of Your Role Develop and advance market-driven approaches to environmental challenges, grounded in the evidence on climate change and in R Street’s commitment to limited, effective government Conceive, manage, and coordinate environmental policy projects, including those led by R Street’s other energy and environment subject matter experts Monitor state and federal environmental policy developments and adapt engagement strategy in a fluid legislative and regulatory landscape Work with the Government Affairs and Communications teams to engage target audiences, from the informed public to expert stakeholders and policy makers on practical solutions such as resilience and adaptation to natural disasters Provide regulatory and legislative testimony and brief state and federal policymakers and regulators directly Support director in program strategy and meetings with donors and other stakeholders Remain vigilant against ninja infiltrations Skills and Qualifications Deep environmental policy expertise, including knowledge on resilience and adaptation methods to address the effects of natural disasters and knowledge of limited, efficient, and effective government regulation structures that address environmental issues without overreach Top-notch writing and editing skills in both short- and long-form products that translate complex analysis for policymakers and the public Exceptional communication and advanced writing skills, including experience speaking with legislators and regulators Demonstrated ability to work productively with a wide variety of groups and individuals including state and/or federal policymakers, even those with whom you may disagree Willingness to speak publicly and/or appear on camera, including in interviews Ability to provide strategic, research-backed policy insights Knowledge of permitting and siting policies related to energy and environmental issues is preferred, but not required Knowledge of market-based carbon accounting policies/proposals is preferred, but not required Knowledge of the relationship between insurance markets and natural disasters and climate change is preferred, but not required No particular educational background required—a proven record of achieving results is far more meaningful than credentials Support for R Street’s passion for free markets and limited, effective government A sense of humor and a desire to grow within a multifaceted organization The R Street Institute consistently offers pragmatic, real solutions that foster American innovation, bolster competition, and safeguard individual liberty—all with the understanding that life in a democratic society sometimes requires compromises that don’t necessarily represent first, best solutions. We focus on deep scholarship and pragmatic policy solutions that many groups tend to neglect. Our goal is to publish timely, relevant research and analysis that advances a market-oriented society and limited, effective government. To that end, our motto is “Free Markets. Real Solutions.” Read more about our mission and impact. Workplace Some travel is required, including to Washington, D.C. and state capitals to meet with lawmakers and stakeholders as well as nationwide for relevant conferences and professional engagements. We offer a flexible working arrangement. This is a full-time position that can either work the majority of the week in our D.C. office or be fully remote. Compensation, Benefits, and Perks R Street strives to offer a compensation and benefits package that is competitive, transparent, and supportive of employee well-being. The salary range for this position is $160,000–$170,000, commensurate with experience. In addition to this competitive salary, we provide the following: Unlimited paid time off, including all federal holidays, the day after Thanksgiving, and two weeks holiday closure in December Alternating Fridays off A health insurance option entirely paid by the employer (even for families) Dental and vision insurance 401(k) contributions with up to a 4 percent match HSA employer contribution match Quarterly wellness reimbursement Mobile equipment/mobile plan reimbursement Home internet subsidy Annual educational and professional development reimbursement A choice between child care assistance, pet care assistance, and student loan repayment assistance At R Street, we strive for preeminence in every area in which we engage, driven by our commitment to excellence and innovation. Our culture thrives on action, creativity, and courage, with an unwavering focus on quality, credibility, and impact. We believe progress requires diverse experience and expertise, which is why we champion non-traditional yet prudent approaches to public policy. This principle guides how we build our programs, recognizing that each team member’s uniqueness strengthens our collective identity. We approach our mission with intellectual rigor, embracing free inquiry and honesty to ensure our work is grounded in solid research and thoughtful analysis. While serious about our purpose, we value the joy of collaboration and the fun that comes from working together. Our collaborative spirit fosters trust and transparency, with respect and openness guiding our actions. We celebrate our individual contributions while recognizing that we are stronger as one team, united in our work and relationships. Thus, R Street does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, creed, color, national origin, sexual orientation, era of military service, gender identity or expression, relationship structure, or anything else that’s illegal, immoral, or stupid to use as a basis for hiring. We plan to accept applications for this job until filled. We will contact qualified individuals for telephone screenings and conduct them on a rolling basis. Interviews take place virtually via Zoom. An early 2027 start date is anticipated due to our paid annual Winter Break. To apply, please copy and paste your cover letter into the text box and upload your resume as a Microsoft Word document or PDF at https://street.applytojob.com/apply/PUezjYTzxG/Senior-Fellow-Energy-And-Environment?source=PAC . We encourage thoughtful use of AI tools. If you use them, please describe how they contributed to your work. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President for Community and Government Relations
item.description: Vice President for Community and Government Relations Organization: University at Buffalo, The State University of New York Location: Buffalo, NY Date Posted: 10/21/2026 Job Title: Vice President for Community and Government Relations Reports to: President Department: Office of the President Job Summary The State University of New York at Buffalo (UB) seeks a highly proactive, energetic, and advocacy-minded individual to lead community and government relations. Reporting directly to the President and serving on the university’s senior leadership team, the Vice President for Community and Government Relations leads UB’s engagement with government officials, community partners and advocacy organizations. As UB’s chief community and government relations officer and chief lobbyist, the vice president advances the university’s legislative, budgetary and community engagement priorities. The vice president advances UB’s reputation, influence and strategic impact through external engagement and partnerships. The vice president promotes a coordinated “one university” approach that aligns advocacy and messaging, communicates UB’s contributions and strengthens relationships with external partners and surrounding communities. About the State University of New York at Buffalo The University at Buffalo is entering a defining era under President Caroline A. Genco. A New York State flagship and premier public research university, UB enrolls approximately 30,000 students in more than 500 undergraduate, graduate and professional degree programs and sponsors 16 NCAA Division I teams. Founded in 1846, UB is the largest and most comprehensive institution in the State University of New York system and a member of the Association of American Universities. UB is consistently recognized for academic excellence, research impact and affordability. Job Description Key Priorities and Impact Areas will include, but are not limited to: Strengthening Institutional Alignment and Relationships Ensures that UB’s state, federal, and local government relations strategy and long-term advocacy initiatives align with the university’s strategic priorities. Represents UB with senior government officials and community leaders. Coordinates with SUNY System Administration Office of Government Relations, the Research Foundation of New York, and the University at Buffalo Foundation on government and community relations matters. Establishes and maintains strategic partnerships with higher education associations, business organizations, civic groups, community organizations, and advocacy coalitions to advance university mission and priorities. Advancing the Mission Shapes policy conversations related to higher education, workforce development and regional and state innovation. Leads advocacy efforts to further UB’s priorities, which results in securing funding and sustaining investment aligned with UB’s priorities in student success, research and infrastructure. Leveraging Location and University Relationships Advises the President and President’s executive team on matters relating to the government, political, and community issues impacting the university. Develops strong relationships and communication networks with university leaders and within the university community and partners to achieve shared understanding of issues impacting the university and develop effective advocacy strategies. Strengthens and sustains UB’s relationships within the Western New York community by developing and implementing a comprehensive stakeholder engagement strategy that strengthen relationships with community leaders, nonprofit organizations, economic development entities, neighborhood organizations, business leaders, and regional partners. Coordinates with University Communications to align communications strategies with government and community relations priorities. Supporting the University’s President and Strategic Plan Prepares briefings and talking points for the President and university leaders regarding government relations priorities. Coordinates and arranges meetings with elected officials for faculty, staff, senior university leadership, and the President and advises the President on any potential risks, opportunities, and response strategies. Positions UB as a central partner in addressing the region’s and state’s most pressing challenges including economic mobility, educational access and workforce readiness. Serves as a visible and respected voice presenting UB’s interests and contributions. Building and Leading a High-Performing Function Develops a cohesive, high-performing team that executes coordinated strategies across university units and levels of government. Establishes clear performance measures and assess the effectiveness of advocacy, engagement and partnership initiatives with measurable outcomes. The successful candidate will: Build Networks — Develops internal and external relationships that advance institutional priorities, visibility and impact. Exercise Sound Judgment — Builds productive relationships at all levels; remains discreet, collaborative and composed under pressure. Build Stakeholder Alignment — Navigates competing priorities and perspectives while building alignment among university, government, community and SUNY partners. Instill Trust — Demonstrates integrity, credibility and transparency, earning the confidence of the President and key stakeholders. Communicate Effectively — Delivers clear, compelling and audience-centered communications that inform and inspire action. Build Collaborative Relationships — Navigates complex political, governmental, institutional and community environments while advancing UB’s objectives. Deliver Results — Leads cross-functional initiatives that achieve goals, improve processes and strengthen collaboration with sound political judgment and professional integrity. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree At least 10 years of experience in government and community relations, state government, or legislative experience in large, matrixed organizations. Expertise in the NYS legislative and budget process. Expertise in the NYS political landscape and/or federal political issues impacting higher education. Competency in the federal legislative and appropriations processes. Demonstrated working experience with elected officials, staff, and government and all levels of employee categories as colleagues and partners. Experience with policy analysis and lobbying compliance. At least five years of experience supervising staff. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in a related field, or law degree. Demonstrated commitment to supporting and developing a collaborative team. Other Requirements: This position will require evening and weekend work hours as needed. This position will include lobby days in Albany and Washington, D.C., creating opportunities for engagement with elected officials, alumni in elected office, and area representatives in compliance with state and federal lobbying laws. This role serves at the pleasure of the university and is an “at will” position. UB is distinguished by–and committed to maintaining—a vibrant culture of collaboration in which all constituents value the perspectives of others and feel secure in sharing their own with dignity and respect. It is the policy of the University at Buffalo and its affiliated organizations to provide and promote merit-based equal employment opportunities for all employees and applicants without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetics, marital or familial status, military or veteran status, arrest and/or criminal conviction record (unless based on a bona fide occupational qualification or other lawful exception), or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. This commitment applies to hiring, compensation, promotion and all other terms and conditions of employment. To apply for this position, please visit: https://www.ubjobs.buffalo. edu/postings/65419 . item.title: Senior Public Affairs Professional
item.description: Senior Public Affairs Professional Organization: #SustainablePublicAffairs Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 10/21/2026 SENIOR PUBLIC AFFAIRS PROFESSIONAL Job details #SustainablePublicAffairs is looking for a senior public affairs professional to join its young and bright team and advice sustainable frontrunner clients that want to make an ambitious, positive impact on EU policies. Category: Full-time Location: Brussels The ideal candidate embraces #SustainablePublicAffairs’ mission to make the practices of sustainable frontrunners the norm for the rest of their industry. This means you are a proactive, big-picture thinker, not afraid to have an opinion, and encourage your team members to express their views. You are able to offer creative solutions to complex issues while contributing to the growth of this young, fast-growing organisation. You enjoy contributing to the organisation and developing a team. Your personal growth is only limited by yourself: we encourage a lot of autonomy to develop our existing portfolio of frontrunner clients but also broaden it, and we count on your out-of-the-box thinking and entrepreneurial spirit to make your client’s narratives stand out from the crowd. Your Role and Key Responsibilities 1. Client and Advisory: Provide strategic advice on EU public and regulatory affairs to a portfolio of sustainable frontrunner clients. Manage accounts and client relationships, including: Managing day-to-day operations and work programmes independently; act as main point of contact for clients. Anticipating and understanding what the client needs and translating this into unique strategies and narratives for existing and new EU policy files. Developing and implementing impactful EU public affairs strategies, performing regular fitness checks, identifying threats and opportunities and how best to respond. Providing supporting analysis for the drafting of position papers, briefings, speeches and presentations. Develop a good knowledge of current policy developments and how they are affecting our clients’ business. Establish a strong network with policymakers, industry/trade associations, media, and others to raise the profile of clients’ issues and solutions. Think outside of the box and propose creative solutions to ensure client objectives are reached. Think ahead: consider longer-term outlook on potential future workstreams and resources. 2. People Management: Mentor colleagues working on your client team in terms of content and deliverables, ensuring they have the skills they need to deliver quality work. Be the go-to person for team members to advise on day-to-day responsibilities and broader professional development. Safeguard the general wellbeing of colleagues, actively propose ideas to improve teamwork. 3. Support broader #SustainablePublicAffairs activities: Be a well-known name in your network for content expertise and expand this network through e.g. public speaking, publishing thought-leadership pieces, moderating events. Seek out new business leads and collaborate with management on business development activities such as proposal preparation, delivery and contract (re-)negotiations. Encourage and embody a collaborative, knowledge-sharing mindset. Qualifications & Requirements University degree or equivalent. 5 to 7 years of public affairs work experience on EU policy, with an expertise and strong interest in energy, finance and/or climate policy files, managing a portfolio of clients. A solid knowledge of EU decision-making processes and the political and regulatory landscape within the EU. Excellent communication skills in English, both verbal and written; any additional European language will be considered as a plus. An analytical mind able to translate technical content into easily understandable summaries and recommendations, enjoying delving into the detail whilst seeing the big picture. Robust skills in managing stakeholder relationships and engaging at all levels effectively. A broad network within the EU environment. A proven track record of managing a team and individuals, mentoring, coaching and challenging them, contributing to their professional growth. A quick learner with a positive, highly efficient work attitude who can easily switch from working in a team to working independently, with the willingness and interest to work on a range of other topics. Hardworking, willing to go the extra mile, and quality-focused with a keen eye for detail. A kind person and a team player, contributing to the team spirit and keen to hang out with colleagues from time to time! How to apply Please send your CV and a short motivation to [email protected] at your earliest convenience. We will fill the position as soon as we identify the right candidate. To be as inclusive as possible, we encourage you not to use pictures in your CV or cover letter. About #SustainablePublicAffairs #SustainablePublicAffairs is a first-of-its-kind public affairs agency with a mission to foster policy-driven growth for sustainable business cases. We are committed to working with those who go beyond current regulatory standards, conducting positive advocacy by raising EU ambition on climate, energy and the environment in order to incentivise a race to the top. Our approach is certified by B Corp and we have been named the “Best sustainability-focused public affairs consultancy – Global” by Corporate Vision in the Global Business Awards 2023. #SustainablePublicAffairs is proud to promote a diverse, inclusive, collaborative, and flexible working environment at our the Norrsken House: For more info, please see our Diversity & Inclusion Charter. item.title: Director, Public Affairs
item.description: Director, Public Affairs Organization: STACK INFRASTRUCTURE (STACK) Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 10/23/2026 THE COMPANY: STACK INFRASTRUCTURE (STACK) provides digital infrastructure to scale the world’s most innovative companies. We are an award-winning industry leader in building, owning, and operating highly efficient, cost-effective wholesale, colocation, and cloud data centers. Each of our national facilities meets or exceeds the highest industry standards in all operational categories of availability, security, connectivity, and physical resilience. STACK offers the scale and geographic reach that rapidly growing hyperscale and enterprise companies need. The world runs on data. Data runs on STACK. The Director of Public Affairs leads government relations and public policy supporting STACK’s data center development and operations across North America. The Director develops strategies to move projects forward, manage political and regulatory risk, and support STACK’s growth. The role is a senior external representative of the company and is responsible for building productive relationships with government officials, economic development organizations, community leaders, utilities, industry groups, clients, and partners. The Director works closely with Development, Site Strategy, Energy, Sustainability, Operations, Construction, Legal, and Communications to account for political, regulatory, economic development, and community issues in site selection and project execution. The role also keeps senior leaders informed of state and local developments and coordinates public affairs support across projects. The position may be based remotely or at STACK’s headquarters in Denver, Colorado. Responsibilities include: Monitor state and local legislation, regulations, ordinances, ballot measures, and policy trends affecting data center development, including land use, energy, utilities, taxes, incentives, permitting, and environmental requirements. Develop public affairs and advocacy plans for priority markets and projects. Prepare position papers, comment letters, testimony, and other materials as needed. Build relationships with state and local officials, planning and zoning bodies, utility commissions, economic development organizations, community leaders, and industry groups. Bring political, regulatory, utility, and community considerations into site selection, market reviews, project planning, permitting, and approval strategies. Represent STACK at public hearings, stakeholder briefings, industry meetings, and other forums. Work with decision-makers to address issues and keep project approvals on track. Advise senior leaders and project teams on local requirements, political and regulatory developments, stakeholder concerns, and risks or opportunities in priority markets. Prepare presentations, briefing memos, talking points, public statements, FAQs, and other materials for company leaders and external audiences. Coordinate with internal teams, clients, trade associations, and other partners on project timelines, advocacy efforts, reporting, and stakeholder commitments. THE DETAILS: Location: Denver, Colorado or remote Benefits: Healthcare, Dental Care, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, Paid Leave Programs Travel: Domestic travel based on business needs, up to 30% Must be eligible to work in the United States Must pass comprehensive background screening MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s degree. A degree in public policy, political science, or a related field is preferred. At least seven years of experience in government relations, public affairs, legislative or regulatory policy, or a related field, including responsibility for complex initiatives. Experience in data centers, digital infrastructure, energy, real estate development, utilities, telecommunications, or industrial development is preferred. Experience analyzing legislation, regulations, ordinances, and policy developments and applying that analysis to business and project decisions. Good political judgment and an ability to evaluate stakeholder dynamics, spot issues early, manage reputational risk, and escalate concerns when needed. Strong writing and speaking skills, with an ability to explain complex policy and technical issues clearly to senior leaders and external audiences. Ability to manage work across several markets, jurisdictions, projects, and deadlines. Experience managing outside counsel, lobbyists, consultants, or related budgets is preferred. Compensation Range: $140,980.00 – $163,240.00 THIS MIGHT BE RIGHT FOR YOU IF: You are a strong communicator, you are persuasive and clear, blending analytics with experience in decision-making. You do not get flustered easily. You can juggle multiple priorities while balancing urgent requests with shifting timelines and deliverables. You are a team builder. You take the time to understand and develop the strengths of your resources while formulating long-term plans for the growth and success of the team. You are naturally curious and driven toward continual improvement. While you celebrate your successes, you take time to review and analyze campaigns for future learning. WHY STACK? We offer a competitive compensation package with strong benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, flexible spending accounts – even a cell phone subsidy. We foster a culture of appreciation, including peer-to-peer recognition and rewards programs. Fun is part of our DNA, with events, game nights, happy hours, and barbecues. We’re growing – this is a great time to join and make an impact! STACK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, national origin, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law Note to external agencies: We are not accepting any blind submissions or resumes/cvs from recruitment agencies. Any candidates sent to STACK Infrastructure, Inc. will not be accepted or considered as a submission without a signed agreement in place. Fees will not be paid in the event a candidate submitted by a recruiter without an agreement in place is hired; such resumes will be deemed the sole property of STACK Infrastructure, Inc. Are you passionate about shaping policy and building lasting relationships with government officials to drive meaningful change? Charter’s State Government Affairs team is responsible for educating local and state officials about Charter’s policy positions and advocating for laws, regulations, and ordinances that advance the company’s business priorities, achieving Charter’s franchising, legislative, and regulatory goals at the state and local level. We are seeking a bright, determined, and committed Government Affairs Manager to join the team and help coordinate and support strategies that drive the growth of Charter’s Northeast Markets at the state and local level. Your focus on state government affairs initiatives and strategic planning will help drive the company’s continued success. socialize relevant legislative introductions with corporate policy leadership Support meetings with New York State, New York City, and New Jersey consultants, stakeholders, and subject matter experts and disbursement processes Support regulatory management and filings in New York State, New York City, and New Jersey Maintain a responsive constituent affairs portfolio to address elected and stakeholder inquiries Support local franchising needs, projects and administrative tasks as needed Assist in compliance activities related to lobbying disclosure regulations and election law Represent the company before external constituencies, including elected officials and other state and local government agencies, commissions and authorities, and organizing and representing the company at environment Frequent travel required Able to work nights and weekends, variable schedule(s) as necessary WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO SPECTRUM Required Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent state and local government Ability to multi-task and keep numerous projects on track and on budget Ability to prioritize and organize effectively Ability to maintain confidentiality of information item.title: M&E & Communications Officer
item.description: M&E & Communications Officer Organization: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/23/2026 Application Deadline : 6 November – 17:00 CET Contract Duration One-year fixed term with possibility of extension or renewal Language Proficiency Fluency in spoken and written English. Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Portuguese would be an asset. Location Global, remote Background The Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) is an independent civil society organization headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, with a globally dispersed Secretariat working across 43 countries. Founded in 2013, GI-TOC brings together a global network of more than 810 independent experts and a team of over 150 staff dedicated to understanding and responding to organized crime. Through research, analysis, policy engagement and support to civil society actors, GI-TOC works to deepen understanding of organized crime and strengthen effective, rights-based responses. The GI-TOC works to: Identify, analyse and map criminal trends and patterns of regional instability, and their impact on illicit flows, governance, development, security, conflict and the rule of law. Connect and support civil society actors working on organized crime and corruption, and on their links to instability and conflict. Strengthen local monitoring and analysis of national, regional and international organized crime and insecurity trends. Job Summary GI-TOC is looking for an Monitoring Evaluation and Communications Officer to work across its two flagship environmental crime programmes. The role sits between programme administration and research, and needs both skill sets. You will set up M&E systems across major projects in Latin America, Asia and Africa, working with environmental defenders, civil society organisations, law enforcement and the private sector. You will help build a body of practice on measuring the disruption of environmental crime networks and illicit economies, a field where good methods are still scarce. And you will make sure the impact of GI-TOC’s and its partners’ work reaches key audiences. This is a growth role. Extensive M&E experience is not required, but you will be expected to upskill quickly and with dedication. Main Responsibilities and Specific Tasks Monitoring, evaluation and learning: set up M&E systems across projects; collect information to set and track baselines, targets and indicators across both programmes; review and evaluate narrative reports from partners, grantees and country teams; gather and write up stories of impact; and contribute to learning and impact reporting. Measuring disruption: help build a body of practice on measuring the disruption of environmental crime networks and illicit economies. Donor relations: support donor reporting and correspondence, and help keep commitments, deadlines and deliverables on track. International coordination: support coordination across country teams, observatories and partners in Europe, Latin America, Africa and Asia. Communications: make sure the impact of GI-TOC’s and partners’ work reaches key audiences, preparing summaries, impact stories, newsletters and briefing materials in liaison with GI-TOC’s communications team. Bridging teams: act as a connector between programme, research, data and communications colleagues, and with close GI-TOC partners, so information flows and work is coherent across projects. Required Skills and Experience Essential University degree in a relevant field. Some professional experience in programme support, research, M&E or communications. Familiarity with M&E concepts, practices and approaches, such as results frameworks, theories of change, indicators and outcome harvesting. Excellent written English and the ability to turn complex information into clear material. Highly organised, careful with detail, and able to manage several workstreams at once. Strong interpersonal skills, and able to build relationships across teams and organisations Desirable Formal M&E training or experience on donor-funded programmes, especially EU or Norad. Knowledge of environmental crime, organised crime or natural resource governance. Experience producing communications content. Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Portuguese. Personal Attributes We work best with people who take initiative, are creative but careful with detail, and have a strong drive to bring organisation and coherence to our projects and to pursue impact. You will need to be internally well networked, and comfortable working across teams, time zones and partners. GI-TOC operates a flexible working environment and encourages staff to achieve a suitable work-life balance and supports professional development and learning. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted. The Global Initiatives makes use of BambooHR’s ATS system to receive and review your application. All correspondence related to your application will be sent via our domain globalinitiative.bamboohr.com. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
