item.title: Director, Scientific and Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Director, Scientific and Regulatory Affairs Organization: International Bottled Water Association (IBWA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Overview The International Bottled Water Association (IBWA) is a trade association that advocates on behalf of the No.1 packaged beverage in the United States: bottled water. IBWA’s membership consists of U.S. and international bottlers and distributors that produce and deliver bottled water products and the suppliers that serve them. IBWA is the authoritative source of information about all types of bottled waters, including spring, mineral, purified, artesian, and sparkling. IBWA is committed to working with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which regulates bottled water as a packaged food product, to establish comprehensive and stringent standards for safe, high-quality water. IBWA member bottlers must also adhere to the IBWA Bottled Water Code of Practice, which mandates additional standards that in some cases are more stringent than federal and state regulations, including mandatory annual plant inspection by an independent, third-party organization. Summary of Position Responsibilities The Director of Scientific and Regulatory Affairs serves as a technical, scientific, and regulatory expert for IBWA. This role is responsible for proactively engaging federal and state regulatory agencies, providing technical assistance to lawmakers, and delivering direct regulatory, technical, and scientific guidance to IBWA members. The Director ensures that all industry positions are grounded in credible science and supports the management of the association’s certification, technical, and inspection programs to defend and promote the safety and quality of bottled water. This position reports directly to the Vice President of Scientific & Regulatory Affairs. Education Requirements Minimum bachelor’s degree in biological, chemical, or environmental science, or a similar discipline. An advanced degree in the above fields is highly desirable. General Qualifications · Approximately 5 – 15 years of life, physical, and environmental sciences experience · 3 – 5 years of management experience · Ability to grasp complex scientific and regulatory issues · Ability to communicate forward-looking alternative options and costs to association committees and directors · Initiative to implement board-approved policy · Service-minded attitude · Experience with a trade association is preferred; industry or government experience in food, beverages, or water is highly useful. · Demonstrated, active professional network and established working relationships with key regulatory officials at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), as well as relevant congressional committees and key federal policymakers. · Strong communications skills, both written and oral, are essential to persuasively articulate industry positions in international, federal, and state legislative and regulatory arenas, and in public forums as the industry’s lead scientific and technical spokesperson with the media. · Management skills and experience negotiating research projects and contracts, overseeing independent consultants, staff administration, and volunteer consensus building and motivation are necessary skills. · Must perform the position’s functions in a style and manner that clearly conveys that the concerns and needs of members, both small and large, will be addressed with equal attention and consideration by IBWA. Position Responsibilities Basic Responsibilities · Serves as a technical and regulatory expert and authority on all scientific and technical affairs which substantiate bottled water as a high-quality, safe food product. · Provides direct technical and regulatory affairs services and guidance to IBWA members to support their compliance, operations, and market success. · Plans, organizes, and directs research projects, technical programs, regulatory education activities, and meetings of the organization to help ensure that objectives are attained, plans fulfilled, and member needs are met. · Through management and leadership, provides counsel to the Technical Committee, Environmental Sustainability Committee, Communications Committee, Education Committee, Government Relations Committee, and Board of Directors to provide forward-looking programming and constructive growth of the Association through credible documentation of industry positions. · Maintains effective relationships with other organizations, both public and private, and ensures that the position of the Association and its members is enhanced in accordance with the policies and objectives of the Association. Specific Responsibilities · Regulatory Engagement: Maintains and actively leverages an existing network of key contacts within federal regulatory agencies (e.g., FDA, EPA, USDA, HHS, FEMA) and among congressional policymakers. Serves as a trusted, immediate liaison between the bottled water industry and these agencies on matters of food safety, protection, and rulemaking, proactively navigating rulemakings, advancing industry positions, and engaging key decision-makers without an onboarding delay. · Policymaker Assistance: Provides expert technical and scientific assistance to federal and state lawmakers and policymakers to inform evidence-based public policy impacting the bottled water association. · Member Guidance: Delivers comprehensive technical and regulatory affairs services to members requesting information in the areas of quality control, current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs), Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA), Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP)/ Preventive Controls programs, food security and defense, testing, analytical methods, and processing techniques. · Issue Management: Through networking with government, industry, and research organizations, identifies emerging issues affecting the industry. Keeps members informed of the issues and recommends strategies and tactics that will further the objectives of the Association. Protects the collective interests of the members by engaging in a broad spectrum of technical and scientific activity. · Research & Advocacy: Recommends sponsorships of research and the development of information that addresses bottled water safety, defends industry products, and proactively promotes industry growth. Supports an approved program of action to earn understanding and acceptance among consumers, government, and media. · Committee Leadership: Provides administrative support and technical & regulatory expertise for a number of committees, including the Education Committee, the Environmental Sustainability Committee, and the Technical Committee. Attends meetings and prepares materials to assist each in furthering the Association’s objectives. · Foundation Management: Provides technical & administrative support to the Drinking Water Research Foundation (DWRF). Coordinates and supports scientific research and fundraising, and helps maintain the website. · Cross-Departmental Counsel: Works with the Government Relations and Communications Committees so that all legislative and regulatory positions, testimony, and public relations pronouncements are grounded in credible documentation with technical and scientific integrity. · Program Management: Working with the Vice-President, supports & monitors the compliance and performance of IBWA-administered programs, including the inspection and education programs. Contributes to the development of an online training platform and training courses focused on food safety, bottled water quality, manufacturing operations, and other industry-relevant topics. · Education & Certification: May serve as a seminar instructor at Association-sponsored meetings. Supports certification programs and related policies, procedures, and budgets. May conduct internal and external technical and regulatory training seminars for members, government officials, and other groups. · Other Duties: Performs other duties as assigned. As needed, obtains and maintains any security clearances necessary to accomplish associated tasks. Compensation $85,000 – $115,000 or commensurate with experience. Annual salary to be determined by the President and CEO. Reporting & Evaluation · Reports to the IBWA Vice President of Scientific & Regulatory Affairs · Performance of this job will be evaluated annually Equal Employment Opportunity IBWA is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. IBWA does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. To Apply Please send cover letter and resume to [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Policy Director
item.description: Associate Policy Director Organization: Friends of the Global Fight Against AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (Friends) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/24/2026 About Friends: Friends of the Global Fight works to build and sustain U.S. support for the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. We educate policymakers in Congress and the administration about the impact of the Global Fund, an international public-private partnership which has saved more than 72 million lives from deadly infectious diseases. We mobilize faith, private sector and civil society champions of the Global Fund and related programs and produce original policy analysis of U.S. leadership in global health. The role: The Associate Policy Director is a core member of Friends’ congressional engagement and policy operations, combining substantive policy work with project coordination and operational responsibilities. They develop their own network of policymakers and stakeholders, contribute to policy research and writing, manage the logistics of our U.S. government relations, coordinate major events and visiting delegations, and produce reporting that keeps our board and funders informed. The Associate Policy Director reports to the Policy Director and works closely with the CEO, Chief Policy Officer and colleagues on the communications and operations teams. Key responsibilities: Congressional engagement · Schedule and manage meetings with House and Senate offices, both in DC and in-district, for Friends staff, Global Fund leadership, and visiting partners and delegations. · Build and maintain relationships with personal office, committee and leadership staff across Congress. · Prepare briefing materials, talking points and leave-behinds that are tailored to specific Members of Congress and their staff. · Track and analyze friends’ Congressional engagement and identify targets for education and cultivation. · Research and track legislation, hearings and oversight initiatives related to global health and foreign assistance. · Generate and submit targeted appropriations requests for funding for global health programs. Research and Writing · Support short- and long-term research and analysis projects on the Global Fund, bilateral assistance programs and health issues in low- and middle-income countries. · Develop policy briefs, internal memos, and published written content that supports Friends’ policy objectives. Events and convenings · Plan and manage Capitol Hill events, receptions, dinners and convenings, including room bookings, catering, invitations, agendas, and post-event deliverables. · Coordinate visits by leadership of Global Fund and other partner organizations, including scheduling, briefing packages and on-the-day support. Partnerships and coalitions · Build and maintain relationships with partners in faith-based organizations, the private sector, and civil society organizations in the U.S. and abroad, including a Friends-led initiative to support a network of civil society organizations working on health policy in five countries in Africa. · Represent Friends within coalitions and working groups of global health and foreign assistance policy organizations. · Opportunities for international and domestic travel to represent Friends at meetings and events with partner organizations. Administrative duties · Recruit, supervise and mentor up to two interns working in-person or remotely. · Support the preparation of Board materials, grant reports, funder updates and other organizational reporting requirements, ensuring accuracy and timely submission. · Assist with logistical and administrative needs related to external engagements, travel and special projects. Qualifications: · 3-5 years of experience in government relations, policy advocacy, Capitol Hill, or global health or development. · Working knowledge of Congress, including the appropriations process, and familiarity with U.S. global health programs and the Global Fund. · Excellent writing skills, with the ability to draft clear and concise products for a range of audiences, occasionally on short deadlines. · Highly organized and able to manage many meetings, events and deadlines at once. · Comfortable proactively building relationships with Hill staff, faith and private sector partners and international colleagues. · Communicative, collaborative and entrepreneurial with the ability to work independently or “manage up” as the situation demands. · Bachelor’s degree required. Graduate degree in public health, international affairs or public policy is a plus. Compensation: The salary range for this position is $70,000–$80,000, commensurate with experience. Friends offers a competitive benefits package, including: · Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance · Retirement plan with employer contribution · Generous paid time off and federal holidays · Hybrid work schedule with a Washington, DC office · Professional development support How to apply: Please send a cover letter, resume, and writing sample with the subject heading Associate Policy Director to [email protected] . No phone calls, please. Please note that due to the volume of applications we receive, we can only respond to applicants whose qualifications closely match the job description. Friends is an equal opportunity employer. All Friends staff work hybrid and are routinely expected to be in-person in Washington, DC, depending on public health conditions and organization needs. item.title: Senior Associate, Influencer
item.description: Senior Associate, Influencer Organization: Weber Shandwick Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Job Description: Who We Are Weber Shandwick is more than a leading global PR agency – we’re an engagement agency and we’re working in and around the cutting edge of the new media landscape. We’re storytellers, content creators, and we engage people IN the story. Our success is built on a deep commitment to client service and to our people. We embrace creativity and collaboration, and we engage stakeholders in new and creative ways to build brands and reputations. Senior Associate, Influencer PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Support development of influencer strategy across multiple tiers (celebrity, mid-tier, micro) Discover, vet, and recommend influencer talent aligned to client goals and campaign objectives Manage influencer outreach, negotiations, contracting, and onboarding processes Support content production, asset management, and timeline tracking across influencer programs Coordinate approvals across client, legal, and integrated agency teams Collaborate with paid social team to optimize influencer content for amplification Monitor cultural trends, social media behaviors, and emerging creators to keep our work ahead of the curve Proactively identify process improvements, contribute ideas to evolve our influencer approach, and bring new opportunities to the table Help manage reporting, performance tracking, and learnings for ongoing optimization Ensure seamless collaboration with social, creative, PR, and paid teams to maintain an integrated approach QUALIFICATIONS 2 years’ experience working in influencer marketing, preferably at an agency or in-house at a brand Fluent in social platforms (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, emerging platforms) and adept at identifying talent trends Understanding of the relationship between influencer content and paid media; experience coordinating with paid teams Comfortable supporting influencer contracting and negotiations Sharp project management skills — you’re highly organized, detail-oriented, and deadline-driven Culturally curious — you stay plugged into what’s trending, what’s next, and who’s shaping conversations Self-starter who takes initiative, problem-solves independently, and isn’t afraid to bring fresh thinking to the table Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple workstreams and stakeholders Team player who thrives in a collaborative, integrated environment Is this you? Be a driver of culture: Must have true passion and understanding of pop culture and are part of the community (be it music, gaming, fashion, food, internet culture, etc) This job is the intersection of creative, strategy, marketing, technology, content creation and production; your energy must be driven by your lifestyle. You must influence creative ideations: from the ideas presented, to the influencers selected, to the content created, all the way down to the language used in post copy. Have high cultural competencies: Understand the role and importance of diversity, equity & inclusion (DE&I) You must be culturally vigilant with the ability to understand, communicate with and effectively interact with people across cultures. Have “Gravitas” in the influencer space and skin-in-the-game: Deep understanding of the influencer landscape is required. Proven ability to build, speak and grow relationships with change agents and cultural makers (celebrities, influencers, artists, thought leaders) directly or via their agents. You must be open to a public-facing role; willingness to speak publicly about influencer trends when opportunities present itself to the WS Influencer Team. Know how to identify and manage diverse vendors and partners: in an industry where technologies (saas platforms, AI, managed services, etc) are popping on the daily, at high volume, no less, you must have experience working with RFPs and meeting with leading tech companies to understand their services and identify their uniqueness (and keep up with their ongoing changes in our WS influencer database) Be ready to lead at any moment: working with your leads, you will learn to “step up to the plate” and lead effectively in the client’s and agency’s best interests while also helping to cultivate, mentor and coach mid to junior staff members on the influencer team. Hustle: identify influencer opportunities (organic or new) to ensure influencer marketing continues to be a strong marketing discipline and revenue driver on your assigned account or at Weber Shandwick. Think like a lawyer: you understand how important it is to be in compliance with best practices (FTC updates, platform requirements), continuously build our excellence by partnering with DXTRA legal and finance to ensure risk and liabilities are reduced and tamed for every campaign you touch. Have experience building engaged audiences: on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok, Clubhouse and other distribution platforms. Know how to build a story: you will build client presentations that tell smart, compelling stories, never “rinse and repeat” which requires you to be highly motivated, energetically charged and inspired at all times. Be curious, always: You are willing to learn a little bit of everything, and open to take on anything. Salary range: $59,000 USD – $65,000 USD Where an employee or prospective employee is paid within this range will depend on, among other factors, actual ranges for current/former employees in the subject position; market considerations; budgetary considerations; tenure and standing with the company (applicable to current employees); as well as the employee’s/applicant’s background, pertinent experience, and qualifications. Weber Shandwick is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. Weber Shandwick recruits qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, age, ethnic or national origin, protected veteran status, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status or citizenship status. #LI-JP1 $59,000-$65,000 Omnicom’s policy requires employees to work in the office for a minimum of three days a week, unless additional in-office days are directed by their agency or manager. Our objective is to increase this requirement over time, and many of our agencies as well as Omnicom’s corporate group already require five days of in-office attendance. Omnicom is committed to hiring and developing exceptional talent. We agree that talent is uniquely distributed, and we’re focused on developing inclusive teams that can bring the best solutions to everything we do. We strongly believe that celebrating what makes us different makes us better together. Join us—we look forward to getting to know you. We will process your personal data in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice. item.title: Associate, Corporate & Public Affairs
item.description: Associate, Corporate & Public Affairs Organization: Weber Shandwick Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Who We Are Weber Shandwick is more than a leading global PR agency – we’re an engagement agency working at the cutting edge of the new media landscape. We’re storytellers and content creators who engage people IN the story. Our success is built on a deep commitment to client service and our people, embracing creativity and collaboration to build brands and reputations. About the Role Weber Shandwick is seeking a curious, creative, and collaborative Associate to join our team in Washington, D.C. This role is on our Corporate and Public Affairs team, part of Weber Advisory—a unit delivering trusted, agile C-suite counsel by blending communications expertise with cultural insights to accelerate stakeholder and business value. In this role, you will execute communications, reputation management, and earned media strategies for clients operating at the complex intersection of business, policy, media, and culture. You will take ownership of assigned workstreams, working directly with senior team members to develop research, create materials, and staff projects while learning to balance multiple shifting priorities and deliver for our clients. This position will be based in our Washington, D.C. office on a hybrid schedule. About You You are curious about how business, policy, and the media intersect, and you adapt well when priorities shift. You are detail-oriented with a knack for organization, and you’re committed to delivering an exceptional client experience. You follow current events and news trends closely, excel at translating that knowledge into actionable insights, and do your best work as part of a collaborative team. Responsibilities: Media Relations & Strategy: Build and maintain targeted media lists, draft compelling pitches and press releases, and conduct outreach to reporters across business, policy, and trade publications. Content Development: Draft press releases, statements, talking points, social media copy, and briefing materials for senior review and client delivery. Monitoring & Analysis: Track client news, issues and policy developments, and compile daily and weekly coverage reports for clients. Research & Intelligence: Conduct research on companies, issues, stakeholders and competitors, and summarize findings in clear memos for the team. Strategic Ideation: Actively participate in team brainstorms, bringing fresh, culturally resonant ideas to advance client priorities. Account Support: Prepare for and participate in client meetings, including drafting agendas, capturing notes and action items, and updating trackers and status documents. Growth & New Business: Actively participate in new business efforts by contributing to research and drafting proposals. Basic Qualifications: Entry-level or 1 year of professional/internship experience in communications, PR, or a related field (agency, Capitol Hill, strategic consulting firm, political campaign, trade association, or similar setting). Familiarity with PR and media relations fundamentals. Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with the ability to translate complex policy or corporate issues into clear, compelling narratives for various audiences. Bachelor’s degree. Competencies: Curiosity & Cultural Acumen: A genuine interest in how business, policy, politics, and the media shape one another; a commitment to staying informed about current events and trends. Adaptability: Ability to work effectively when priorities shift or information is incomplete and maintain quality work throughout changing plans. Analytical Mindset: Ability to synthesize research and data into strategic, actionable recommendations. Detail-Oriented: Meticulous attention to detail with a commitment to delivering clear, precise, and accurate work and meeting deadlines. Collaboration & Communication: Strong interpersonal and written communication skills with a collaborative spirit and willingness to support teammates; comfortable asking for help and contributing to team discussions. Ownership & Initiative: Resourceful problem-solver who takes ownership of projects, sees them through from start to finish, and proactively takes on challenges as a quick learner. Work Ethic: Ability to prioritize multiple tasks, manage deadlines consistently, and maintain a strong work ethic in a fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment. ABOUT US Ok, our turn. Who is Weber Shandwick? Weber Shandwick is the earned-first global communications agency. Led by world-class strategic and creative thinkers and activators, Weber Shandwick has won some of the most prestigious awards in the industry, including being named #1 in the Public Relations and Brand Strategies category on Fast Company’s 2024 + 2025 Most Innovative Companies list, one of Fast Company’s Best Workplace for Innovators in 2023, PRWeek’s 2024 Global Agency of the Year, ranked #1 on PRovoke’s Global Creative Index in 2024 and honored on Ad Age’s A-List in 2025, 2024 & 2020 and Best Places to Work in 2019, in addition to being awarded Campaign Global’s PR Agency of the Year in 2023. Weber Shandwick was the most awarded PR agency at the 2023 and 2024 Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity for the past three years, including earning the PR industry’s first-ever idea-led Cannes Grand Prix in the Brand Experience & Activation category and cumulatively earning more than 250 Cannes Lions. Weber Shandwick has also been named PR Agency of the Year by Campaign US in 2021, honored as PRovoke’s Global Agency of the Decade in 2020 and ranked #1 on PRovoke’s Global Creative Index in 2021 and 2022. Additionally, the firm was named PRWeek’s Global Agency of the Year in 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018 and was awarded PRWeek’s Purpose Agency of the Year in 2020 and 2021. Weber Shandwick also received Honorable Mention on the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Global Marketing Agencies in 2021, as the only PR agency featured. Weber Shandwick is part of Omnicom Public Relations and Omnicom (NYSE: OMC). For more information, visit https://www.webershandwick.com/. Salary Range : 50,000 – 55,000 To the extent permissible by local law, Omnicom’s policy requires employees to work in the office for a minimum of three days a week, unless additional in-office days are directed by their agency or manager. Omnicom is committed to hiring and developing exceptional talent. We agree that talent is uniquely distributed, and we’re focused on developing inclusive teams that can bring the best solutions to everything we do. We strongly believe that celebrating what makes us different makes us better together. Join us—we look forward to getting to know you. We will process your personal data in accordance with our Recruitment Privacy Notice. item.title: Director, Technology Communications
item.description: Director, Technology Communications Organization: Invariant LLC Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Description Do you have a passion for building brands, positioning executives, shaping consequential conversations, and earning meaningful media attention? Do you want to help technology companies explain why their work matters to business, policy, and public audiences? Invariant seeks a Senior Manager or Director to join its growing Technology & Innovation communications practice. In this role, you will help lead communications strategy and execution for technology companies at critical moments of growth, change, and public attention. You will work directly with founders and senior executives while growing into greater responsibility for client strategy, team leadership, and business development. Our clients range from Fortune 500 companies to venture-backed startups working across artificial intelligence, defense, space, digital infrastructure, enterprise technology, and other emerging sectors. You will help founders and C-suite executives solve complex challenges, create opportunities for growth, and break through crowded media environments to reach the audiences that matter most to their businesses. Invariant is a different kind of firm. We approach communications, public affairs, government relations, and business strategy as interconnected disciplines. You will do challenging, consequential work here. If that sounds interesting to you, come join us. What You’ll Do – Help lead communications strategy and execution across a portfolio of technology clients, taking on greater strategic and client leadership responsibility based on experience and performance. – Develop and execute media relations strategies that translate client business and policy priorities into timely, credible stories for business, technology, policy, and trade media. – Build and maintain relationships with reporters, editors, producers, podcast hosts, and other influential voices; identify news hooks and pursue opportunities with creativity, persistence, and sound editorial judgment. – Lead communications around funding rounds, partnerships, product launches, executive milestones, policy developments, and other moments that can materially affect a company’s trajectory. – Build communications infrastructure for clients with limited internal capacity, including messaging, media materials, editorial calendars, workflows, and measurement. – Counsel founders and C-suite executives, with increasing independence, on reputation management, market positioning, crisis preparedness, stakeholder engagement, and high-stakes communications moments. – Develop integrated campaigns that connect earned media, executive positioning, thought leadership, digital channels, and public affairs to clients’ business objectives. – Collaborate across communications, government relations, public affairs, research, and digital strategy, and contribute to new-business research, proposals, and pitches. What Makes This Role Unique You will work closely with senior counselors while earning increasing authority over client relationships, strategy, and team leadership. The role offers exposure to founders, senior executives, policymakers, investors, and media working at the center of consequential technology debates. You should be energized by translating between complex technology, founder vision, and audience reality. This role requires intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the grit to keep moving when the first approach does not work. Depending on experience, you may independently lead accounts or grow into that responsibility with support from more senior colleagues. Who You Are – Seven or more years of strategic communications and media relations experience, with level determined by the scope, independence, and leadership demonstrated; agency experience and work with technology or high-growth companies strongly preferred. – Demonstrated success developing media strategies, identifying strong stories, pitching reporters, and converting ideas into meaningful coverage and relationships. – Strong media instincts and a genuine desire to deepen expertise in media relations, executive positioning, and issues management. – Fluency in the pace and constraints of startups and other high-growth companies, with the resourcefulness to produce strong work with small teams and imperfect information. – The ability to manage several client relationships and workstreams without losing command of details, deadlines, or strategic priorities. – Existing relationships with technology, business, policy, national security, or trade media, combined with the initiative to build new relationships continuously. – Exceptional intellectual curiosity and the ability to quickly master complex technologies, business models, and policy environments, then translate them into clear and compelling narratives. – A strategic and creative problem-solver who anticipates client needs, generates original ideas, and finds another route when an obvious approach stalls. – Strong judgment about how earned media, podcasts, newsletters, social channels, events, and emerging formats can work together to reach specific audiences. – Proficiency with artificial intelligence tools and curiosity about how emerging capabilities can improve research, analysis, quality control, and client service. – An exceptional writer and editor who can produce sharp media pitches, executive materials, messaging, thought leadership, and strategic recommendations. – Composure and good judgment in fast-moving environments with competing clients, tight deadlines, and changing priorities. – The ability to give clear direction, deliver candid feedback, develop junior colleagues, and earn trust with senior clients and firm leaders. – An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in contributing to business development, evolving the practice’s offerings, and building Invariant’s position in technology communications. – Proficiency with media databases such as Cision and Meltwater, as well as Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Compensation & Benefits The target salary range for this role is $175,000-$200,000 annually. The base salary and title will be determined based on skills, experience, scope, and market data. This role also participates in Invariant’s discretionary bonus structure, which considers individual performance and client revenue impact. In addition, our total rewards package includes: – Annual discretionary bonus based on individual performance and that of the firm – Commissions on new business development – Robust medical, dental, and vision plans with employer HSA contributions – Generous retirement matching – Educational assistance – Professional development assistance – Unlimited time off – Other benefits Equal Opportunity Invariant is committed to creating a diverse culture and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. item.title: Senior Strategist, Federal Advocacy, Advocacy & Partnerships
item.description: Senior Strategist, Federal Advocacy, Advocacy & Partnerships Organization: Vera Institute of Justice Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/24/2026 About the team: Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department is responsible for coordinating the vision, strategy, and staff development across Vera’s initiatives to pass legislation, change policy, and create change at scale. We work to ensure that the goals of our advocacy campaigns align with the people and communities most impacted by criminal justice and immigration policies, and we collaborate with movement and advocacy partners to produce the knowledge and ideas needed to change policies and legislation at the right time. Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department serves the following core functions: Providing state and local government and movement strategy guidance to Vera’s national and place-based initiatives, with a focus on lobbying, campaigns, and coalition work; Federal policy expertise to lead Vera’s advocacy strategies in Washington, D.C.; Vera Insights, a rapid-response data and evidence team responsible for developing and producing data and knowledge to key partners and audiences; and Coordination with Vera Action, Vera’s sister 501(c)(4) organization. About the role: The Senior Strategist, Federal Advocacy is a key member of Vera’s Advocacy & Partnerships department and serves as a strategist and advocate focused on advancing Vera’s federal policy priorities and defending against federal actions that threaten them. The Senior Strategist develops and executes federal advocacy strategies to advance legislation, federal budget and appropriations priorities, administrative policies, and other federal policy changes aligned with Vera’s goals. The Senior Strategist monitors and analyzes the federal political and policy environment, identifies opportunities to advance Vera’s priorities, develops strategies to influence federal decision-makers, and builds relationships with congressional offices, federal agencies, national advocacy organizations, and other key stakeholders. This role will work closely with movement and coalition partners to build power and advance shared federal policy goals. At a moment when federal policymakers are pushing a return to failed “tough-on-crime” policies, Vera’s role is to bring the data, evidence, and solutions about what works into federal policy debates, particularly with government and grasstops stakeholders. Vera’s February 2026 platform, A New Federal Paradigm for Safety, Accountability, and Justice, reflects the kind of popular, evidence-based federal solutions Vera champions, organized around six planks: strong, accountable policing; ending the overdose crisis; supporting strong mental health and deescalating crisis; tackling gun violence; safe streets and good quality of life; and a fairer, more accountable justice system. On immigration, Vera works to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable, expand access to deportation defense and universal legal representation for people facing deportation, and push back against the expansion of DHS’s power. The Senior Strategist will serve as a lead strategist on assigned federal policy priorities, helping determine when and how Vera should engage in federal legislative, appropriations, regulatory, and administrative processes. The role requires strong political judgment, an understanding of federal policymaking, excellent communication skills, and the ability to move complex advocacy campaigns forward in a dynamic environment. 1. Develop and execute federal advocacy strategies and campaigns Work with the Director of Federal Advocacy and other members of the Advocacy & Partnerships department to develop and execute federal advocacy strategies for Vera’s core issues and policy priorities, including legislation and policy change related to safety, accountability, and justice. Manage assigned federal advocacy campaigns from strategy development through implementation, including coordinating tactics, timelines, partners, and deliverables. Develop and execute bipartisan congressional strategies by identifying key decision-makers, committees, legislative opportunities, and champions, while building and maintaining relationships with congressional offices and federal policymakers to advance Vera’s policy priorities. Lead or support the development, drafting, tracking, and advancement of federal legislation, including identifying legislative opportunities, shaping bill language, developing legislative strategies, and supporting efforts to secure congressional support. Develop and execute federal budget and appropriations advocacy strategies, including tracking the federal budget and appropriations process, identifying funding priorities and threats, developing requests and recommendations, and engaging relevant congressional offices and committees. Identify and pursue opportunities to influence federal regulations, executive actions, agency policies, guidance, and other administrative decisions. Monitor federal legislative, budgetary, regulatory, administrative, and political developments and assess their implications for Vera’s priorities and advocacy strategy. Translate political and policy intelligence into actionable recommendations, identifying strategic openings, potential risks, and appropriate moments for engagement. Develop advocacy materials, including policy briefs, talking points, legislative recommendations, congressional materials, testimony, sign-on letters, and other communications designed to influence federal decision-makers. Collaborate with the Director of Federal Advocacy and the Chief Advocacy Officer to determine where Vera should engage, lead, partner, or strategically remain outside of federal campaigns and policy debates. 2. Federal coalition building, partnerships, and external engagement Build and maintain strategic relationships with national advocacy organizations, movement partners, grasstops and grassroots organizations, congressional offices, federal agencies, and other stakeholders relevant to Vera’s federal policy priorities. Identify, develop, and participate in federal coalitions that can advance Vera’s policy and legislative goals. Help develop and implement joint advocacy strategies with coalition and movement partners, including coordinated congressional engagement, public advocacy, legislative campaigns, and other tactics. Represent Vera in strategically important federal advocacy meetings, coalitions, briefings, congressional meetings, policy discussions, and other external spaces. Coordinate with national movement partners to identify opportunities for collective action and build broader support for federal policy priorities. Support strategic communications and public advocacy efforts designed to build momentum for federal policy change. Serve as a strategic connector between Vera and relevant federal advocacy networks, ensuring Vera is positioned to identify and respond to emerging federal policy opportunities. 3. Federal policy analysis, intelligence, and internal coordination Maintain a current understanding of federal legislative, budgetary, regulatory, administrative, and political developments relevant to Vera’s policy priorities. Produce concise, timely analysis and recommendations for Vera leadership and Advocacy & Partnerships colleagues on significant federal developments and opportunities for advocacy. Develop and maintain systems for tracking federal legislation, appropriations, regulatory and administrative developments, congressional activity, key relationships, coalition activity, and campaign progress. Collaborate with Vera’s policy, research, communications, and other relevant staff to ensure federal advocacy strategies are informed by Vera’s research, expertise, and policy analysis. What qualifications are we looking for? Required: Bachelor’s degree and 4+ years of relevant experience. In lieu of degree requirement, applicable work or life experience may be considered. Demonstrated experience working on criminal justice, immigration, public safety, or related public policy issues. At least 3 years of experience planning and leading federal advocacy campaigns. Including managing complex campaigns and projects from strategy development through implementation. Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies involving multiple stakeholders, decision-makers, and advocacy partners. Demonstrated ability to analyze political and policy developments and translate them into advocacy strategy. Experience developing advocacy materials, including legislative recommendations, talking points, policy briefs, testimony, congressional materials, and other advocacy communications. Preferred: 3+ years of issue advocacy and community organizing experience. Experience building and/or leading coalitions in partnership with national, grasstops, and grassroots organizations. Experience working directly with congressional offices, congressional committees, federal agencies, or other federal policymakers. Experience with federal appropriations, budget advocacy, or fiscal policy. Experience developing or advancing federal legislation, regulations, executive actions, or administrative policy. Experience working on criminal legal system or immigration policy at the federal level. 2+ years of electoral political experience and organizing experience. Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you’ll bring: Strong knowledge of federal advocacy strategy, policymaking, and power building. Demonstrated understanding of Congress and the federal legislative process, including congressional committees, legislative vehicles, hearings, and congressional decision-making. Demonstrated understanding of the federal budget, appropriations, and administrative processes. item.title: Compliance Analyst
item.description: Compliance Analyst Organization: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Location: Kansas City, MO Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Job Description: The Information Technology division of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) has an exciting opportunity for a Compliance Analyst. This position Designs, governs, and maintains NAIC’s security and compliance control framework. Supports multiple regulatory, contractual, and assurance frameworks, including SOC 2, GovRAMP, PCI DSS, and NIST SP 800-53, with a primary focus on ensuring controls are clearly defined, consistently implemented, effectively monitored, and aligned with organizational risk. Partners closely with Security, IT, Legal, Internal Audit, and business stakeholders to strengthen governance, reduce audit findings, support regulatory readiness, and drive continuous improvement across the enterprise’s cybersecurity and compliance programs. This is a full-time hybrid position, in a positive and flexible environment. Residency within 100 miles of the Kansas City office is required. Responsibilities Include: Conduct Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) activities, including security risk assessments for new vendors, periodic reassessments of existing vendors, reviews of security and privacy contract language, and oversight of vendor remediation activities. Develop, maintain, and oversee security policies, standards, procedures, and supporting documentation, ensuring alignment with business requirements, industry best practices, and applicable frameworks including SOC 2, NIST SP 800-53, GovRAMP, and PCI DSS. Coordinate the annual review, update, approval, and publication of security policies, standards, and compliance documentation. Support governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) initiatives by developing, documenting, and monitoring security controls that support compliance obligations and organizational risk management objectives. Coordinate Business Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery (DR) activities, including documentation maintenance, testing exercises, lessons learned, and ensuring plans are reviewed and updated at least annually. Support security awareness and training programs, including annual training content updates, completion tracking, metrics reporting, and audit evidence collection. Minimum Education and/or Experience Required: Bachelor’s degree and 5-7 years of experience in governance, risk, compliance, or information security or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience with SOC 2, NIST SP 800‑53, GovRAMP, or similar frameworks. Familiarity with vendor risk assessments and policy management. Preferred Experience: Relevant certifications (CISA, CRISC, CISSP) are a plus Systems & Technology Requirements: Microsoft Office Suite/365, AWS, Jira Cloud, GRC platforms Travel: This position does not require overnight business travel. Employees are responsible for their personal transportation to/from the home and office, including events, meetings, and training required by the NAIC. Compensation: $81,000- $100,000 commensurate with education and experience. Sponsorship: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. Interested in learning more about the amazing benefits the NAIC offers? Visit our Benefits page for more information. The NAIC is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer Applicants for all positions are considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin or ancestry, marital status, pregnancy, genetic information, military or veteran status, disability, or any other basis protected by applicable law. About Us LEARN MORE ABOUT THE NAIC Company Overview The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) is a member-focused, non-profit Association supporting state insurance commissioners, and their departments, to effectively regulate the insurance industry and protect consumers. Headquartered in Kansas City, New York, and Washington DC, our 150-year-old Association offers the coordination of expertise in policy and regulation among state departments, data and technology, financial regulatory support, training and education, and resources for ongoing collaboration among the states and jurisdictions. Diversity Statement Our member-driven Association supports the dynamic and diverse needs of state regulatory agencies and the consumers of insurance products and services. Through our ongoing commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, we believe our employees provide a wide range of experience and expertise to generate better ideas and solve complex problems consumers and our members face as insurance products and regulations evolve over time. Guiding Principles • We put customers first • We are committed to continuous improvement • We succeed by working together • We do what it takes to get the job done • We communicate often • We treat colleagues with respect and honesty Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Associate Director – State Policy and Advocacy
item.description: Associate Director – State Policy and Advocacy Organization: American Kidney Fund (AKF) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 10/24/2026 Base Pay $100,000.00 – $105,000.00 / Year Relocation Expense Covered No Required Degree 4 Year Degree Travel 40% Manage Others No Minimum Experience 4 Years Description The Associate Director of State Policy and Advocacy, supports the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy and AKF’s Office of Government Affairs in the development and implementation of state-level public policy efforts across the United States. Reporting to the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy, this role covers legislation and regulation in the kidney disease and related health care space across the United States. The Associate Director of State Policy and Advocacy, advances state legislation and regulations to support and improve policies for kidney disease patients and organ donors, while working to combat legislation that threatens care and access for people with kidney disease. This position works closely with colleagues across the Office of Government Affairs and the AKF Advocacy Network to translate complex health policy issues into effective advocacy that advances AKF’s mission to fight kidney disease and help people live healthier lives. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES State Government Advocacy – (50%) This functional area encompasses direct engagement with state lawmakers, agencies, and stakeholders to promote AKF’s state public policy agenda and advance kidney disease policy priorities. Develop working bipartisan relationships with state lawmakers, state agencies, stakeholders, and advocates, including key healthcare policymakers, patient advocacy organizations, state insurance commissioners, and other state agencies overseeing health care programs. Communicate AKF positions strongly and effectively on issues such as charitable premium assistance, transplant and living kidney donors, Medigap, and other issues of importance to AKF and people with kidney disease. Monitor activity in state legislatures and state agencies in the region regarding issues affecting people with CKD and ESRD; assist the Senior Director in efforts to combat legislation that threatens care and access for kidney disease patients. Track ongoing and potential threats to our constituents utilizing state legislative tracking software and record all interactions with legislators and regulators. Collaborate independently with colleagues in the Office of Government Affairs and across the organization to develop grassroots action plans that strategically engage AKF patient-advocates to achieve desired state policy outcomes. Organizational Support & External Representation (45%) This functional area covers external representation at state policy conferences, production of advocacy materials, and cross-departmental collaboration to support AKF’s state advocacy efforts. Represent AKF at key state policy conferences, including the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC), the National Council of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL), the Council of State Governments (CSG), and the National Conference of State Legislators (NCSL). Write and send comment letters on behalf of AKF related to state legislation and regulatory activity. Communicate effectively and work closely with colleagues in the AKF Office of Government Affairs, other AKF departments, and the AKF Advocacy Network. Support significant out-of-town travel as required (approximately 40% of position). Other Duties as Assigned (5%) Additional responsibilities as determined by the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy or organizational leadership. Requirements EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE Required Bachelor’s degree with a major in Political Science or in a related field. 4–5 years of experience in a similar role with advocacy and state health policy development experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Excellent writing, interpersonal, presentation, and communication skills; strong online research skills. Proficient project management skills; well-organized and detail-oriented with excellent proofreading skills; strategic thinker and proactive problem solver able to work independently and within a team framework. Ability to proactively track and coordinate multiple projects and complete work in a timely manner, and communicate across teams the work, its importance, and coordinate cross team collaboration as required. Ability to handle confidential matters with a high level of integrity and demonstrated flexibility. Valid driver’s license; ability to lift 20 lbs; ability to work weekends or evenings as required. Preferred Specific knowledge of End-Stage Renal Disease, patient access and health insurance issues at the state level. Established relationships with state legislative or agency staff. Experience with Quorum or similar legislative tracking platforms. Demonstrated professional experience working in or supporting public policy, advocacy, government relations, or related initiatives. COMPETENCIES State Legislative and Regulatory Knowledge Written and Verbal Communication Stakeholder and Relationship Engagement Grassroots Advocacy Coordination Independent Initiative and Self-Direction Project Management and Tracking Adaptability and Problem Solving Mission-Driven and Patient-Centered Focus The salary range displayed is for a successful candidate hired in the DMV area. The salary range may be adjusted to reflect cost of living factors for candidates living outside of this location. Employee benefits: In addition to your competitive salary, paid holidays, vacation, sick and personal days; health, dental, and vision coverage; life insurance and disability coverages; and a generous matching 403(b) retirement plan, we’ll shower you with perks, including: Culture: We ensure our team knows how much they are valued, as demonstrated by our Quality Work Environment (QWE) Task Force and employee-led recognition and social events throughout the year. Compressed work week: Start the weekend early with shorter workdays on Fridays—closing at 3 p.m. from Labor Day to Memorial Day and 2 p.m. in the summer. Flexibility: Employees work from home most of the time with 1-4 days a month in the office. Clear expectations: You’ll know what you need to do to succeed; annual raises and bonuses for all employees are based on your performance. Location: Convenient location and a short walk to the popular Pike and Rose shopping center Parking: Arrive and leave work comfortably, thanks to an underground parking garage whose cost is paid for by AKF. Metro subsidies are provided for those who do not drive. Dress code: Business casual through the week and casual on Fridays. AKF offers a hybrid work schedule with employees working in the office 1-4 days per month and telework the rest of the time. This position also requires approximately 40% travel. item.title: Director, Corporate Communications & Reputation
item.description: Director, Corporate Communications & Reputation Organization: Danone Location: White Plains, NY Date Posted: 10/24/2026 About the job At Danone, we believe communications has the power to shape reputation, influence conversations, and drive business impact. We are looking for a strategic and creative communications leader to help define how Danone’s story is told across media, executive platforms, industry conversations, and emerging digital channels. As Director, Corporate Communications & Reputation, you will lead corporate storytelling and reputation-building efforts that strengthen Danone’s visibility, credibility, and influence. You will partner with senior leaders across the business to identify compelling stories, elevate executive thought leadership, and connect Danone’s purpose and business priorities to the conversations shaping the future of food, nutrition, health, and sustainability. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who combines strong communications fundamentals with a passion for innovation, creativity, and the evolving role of communications in an AI-driven world. In this role, you will: Shape and evolve Danone USA’s corporate narrative and reputation strategy. Translate business priorities and emerging trends into compelling stories and communications opportunities. Develop integrated communications campaigns across earned, owned, and digital channels. Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on messaging, visibility, and thought leadership. Build and maintain strong relationships with key media and external stakeholders. Lead executive communications and visibility initiatives across media, events, and social platforms. Partner across Communications, Corporate Affairs, Marketing, and the global communications network to deliver integrated storytelling programs. Coach and develop team members while fostering a culture of creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning. The salary range for this position is $165,000-237,000 USD. The exact salary offered will depend on several factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, geographic location, internal equity, and market conditions. Danone North America additionally offers a performance-based bonus and has a strong benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription Drug Coverage, 401k Plan, Wellness Program, Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement, Flexible Time Off, and Paid Parental Bonding Leave, among other benefit plan options. To give our employees flexibility, Danone is a hybrid work environment. This role is considered a “hybrid” position that allows for flexible work, meaning it is a role where collaboration with key stakeholders in Danone Hubs occurs. While you may have the option to work from home on a schedule as agreed to with your supervisor, you are also expected to regularly report to your assigned office location at least 3 days per week. About you You are a strategic communicator who thrives at the intersection of storytelling, reputation management, and business strategy. You are curious, collaborative, and energized by the rapidly changing communications landscape. You bring sound judgment, strong relationship-building skills, and the ability to simplify complex topics into stories that resonate with diverse audiences. You are comfortable advising senior leaders, navigating ambiguity, and balancing long-term reputation building with real-time communications opportunities. Qualifications 12+ years of experience in corporate communications, reputation management, public affairs, public relations, or a related field. Experience developing and executing integrated communications and thought leadership strategies. Strong media relations experience and demonstrated success securing impactful earned media coverage. Experience advising senior executives and supporting executive visibility initiatives. Exceptional writing, storytelling, and strategic communications skills. Proven ability to lead complex projects and collaborate across functions. Experience managing agencies, external partners, and cross-functional teams. Interest in emerging trends shaping communications, including AI, digital influence, and evolving media consumption behaviors. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Legal Counsel
item.description: Senior Legal Counsel Organization: Recurrent Energy Location: Austin, TX Date Posted: 10/25/2026 At Recurrent Energy, our mission is to power the world with solar energy and create a better and cleaner Earth for future generations. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Canadian Solar Inc., we are a leading global developer, owner, operator, and asset manager of utility-scale solar and energy storage projects. Through Recurrent Energy Power Services, we provide operations, maintenance, monitoring, engineering, and asset management services that support renewable energy facilities across North America. With a proven track record spanning six continents, Recurrent Energy brings together experts across every stage of the renewable energy lifecycle, from project origination, development, financing, and construction to operations, maintenance, and long-term asset management. Our work is helping shape a cleaner, more resilient energy future worldwide. Backed by the innovation, strength, and global reach of Canadian Solar, we are helping accelerate the transition to a sustainable energy future while creating meaningful opportunities for our employees to grow, innovate, and make a lasting impact. Guided by our values of Trust, Collaboration, Accountability, Excellence, and Inclusiveness, we are building a cleaner world for generations to come. If you’re passionate about renewable energy and driven to make a difference, join Recurrent Energy to power the world with clean energy and create a better, cleaner future for generations to come. Position Title: Sr. Legal Counsel Department: Legal Location: Austin, TX/Remote U.S. Position Summary Reporting to the Legal leadership team, the Senior Legal Counsel will be a key member of the North America Legal Team, providing practical, business-focused legal support for the company’s established and growing utility-scale solar energy and energy storage development pipeline and Operations and Maintenance (O&M) business across the United States and Canada. This is a broad, high-impact role spanning real estate and land acquisition, environmental and permitting matters, project development, O&M contracting, subcontracting, warranty matters, corporate and commercial law, and related governance and litigation management. The Senior Legal Counsel will collaborate regularly with Project Development, Project Finance, Construction, Operations, Business Development, Procurement, Finance, Tax, IT, and other functional teams. The ideal candidate is a strong technical lawyer, pragmatic business partner, clear communicator, and creative problem-solver who can translate complex legal issues into actionable advice. Key Responsibilities Act as a primary legal partner for North American renewable energy development and O&M activities, providing timely, practical, and commercially focused advice. Lead strategic real estate legal support for site control, project finance, and M&A transactions, including due diligence and the drafting, review, negotiation, and management of real estate provisions in letters of intent, term sheets, real estate agreements, and closing deliverables. Review title commitments, title pro formas, title policies, and surveys, and oversee title curative work connected with project development, financing, construction, and operations. Provide legal support across project development matters, including project design, site control, real property tax abatements, permitting and environmental matters, interconnection, offtake, and financing opportunities. Draft and negotiate O&M agreements, services and supply agreements, subcontracts, warranties, requests for proposal documents, non-disclosure agreements, and related security arrangements, including bonds, letters of credit, and guarantees. Support due diligence in M&A and other strategic transactions as the development and O&M businesses grow. Advise Operations, Business Development, Procurement, Finance, Tax, IT, Project Finance, Construction, and other internal stakeholders on corporate, commercial, operational, and risk matters. Review regional contract documents for alignment with global legal framework requirements and company policies, codes, and procedures. Coordinate litigation matters, provide clear instructions to outside counsel, and manage external legal resources efficiently. Interact with title companies, environmental and tax consultants, outside counsel, customers, regulators, lenders, investors, and other external counterparties. Provide general corporate real estate support relating to corporate facilities and assist with corporate governance matters, policies, and procedures. Develop and oversee practical internal legal processes and create efficient, scalable solutions for the delivery of legal services to internal clients. Develop legal strategies for new and innovative transactions, including financing structures and site-control approaches for emerging renewable energy projects. Communicate legal risk, transaction structures, and recommended solutions clearly to commercial teams, senior management, and executives. Perform all responsibilities with sound judgment, discretion, confidentiality, and the highest ethical standards. Qualifications & Experience J.D., LL.B., or equivalent law degree from an accredited or reputable law school. Licensed and in good standing to practise law in at least one U.S. state or Canadian province or territory, or eligible to qualify in the applicable jurisdiction. 2-8 years of relevant legal experience gained with a leading law firm, corporate legal department, or a combination of both. Candidates with strong directly relevant experience at the Legal Counsel level may also be considered. Substantial experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating sophisticated real estate, commercial, services, supply, O&M, construction-related, or project agreements. Demonstrated experience in one or more of the following: renewable energy project development, real estate and site control, permitting and environmental matters, interconnection, offtake, project finance, M&A, or O&M contracting. Experience with utility-scale solar energy and/or battery energy storage projects is preferred but not required. Ability to support due diligence and M&A activities and to identify, communicate, and help mitigate material legal and commercial risks. Familiarity with energy project agreements, security arrangements, and corporate governance matters. Litigation management experience is preferred. Demonstrated ability to work effectively with outside counsel, customers, regulators, title companies, consultants, lenders, investors, and senior leaders Capabilities for Success Strong business judgment and the ability to provide clear, practical, and solutions-oriented legal advice. Excellent organizational, analytical, negotiation, project management, and planning skills, with meticulous attention to detail. Ability to manage a significant workload, shifting priorities, and complex matters in a fast-paced environment with limited oversight. Clear and confident communicator who can explain complex issues to commercial teams and present risks and structures to executives. Self-starter who builds trusted relationships across functions and works effectively as part of a collaborative team. Entrepreneurial, creative, strategic, responsive, and committed to high-quality execution. Ability to maintain discretion and confidentiality and exercise consistently sound judgment. Recurrent Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status. For more information about Recurrent Energy, please visit www.recurrentenergy.com Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Chief Compliance Officer, Ramp Advisory LLC
item.description: Chief Compliance Officer, Ramp Advisory LLC Organization: Ramp Location: New York, NY | Miami, FL | San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 10/25/2026 About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp is seeking an experienced Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) for Ramp Advisory LLC, our SEC-registered investment adviser. This is a high-accountability, build-and-own role. You will own and be accountable for the firm’s compliance program in house, and be the gatekeeper who protects clients and the firm while keeping pace with how fast Ramp ships product. You will report to Ramp’s Head of Compliance, with direct access to Ramp Advisory’s senior leadership. What You’ll Do Serve as Ramp Advisory LLC’s designated CCO, with independent authority over the design, execution and effectiveness of the compliance program Act as the firm’s primary point of contact with the SEC, and represent the program, product and key compliance decisions with regulators Maintain the firm’s policies and procedures, Code of Ethics, and Form ADV and amendments, and conduct the annual compliance review Provide compliance advice and sign-off on marketing materials, customer disclosures, onboarding agreements and product changes Own books and records, communications monitoring, complaints handling, employee training, and access-person and personal-trading requirements Oversee key financial partners and vendors from a compliance standpoint Shape customer onboarding strategy, partnering with Product, Engineering and Customer Experience to build scalable controls and monitoring Build and maintain the firm’s anti-money laundering program What You Need 8+ years in investment adviser compliance, including prior experience as a CCO or deputy CCO of an SEC-registered adviser Experience in the fintech space Deep working knowledge of the Advisers Act and SEC expectations Direct experience supporting SEC examinations and interfacing with regulators Experience overseeing custodian, broker-dealer or sub-adviser relationships Sound, independent judgment: the ability to make and defend compliance decisions in real time, grounded in regulatory guidance, and to hold a position with senior stakeholders AI fluency and demonstrated experience using AI and automation to build and scale compliance programs Comfort operating as a standalone compliance lead in a fast-moving environment Experience building controls and leading program design initiatives in partnership with engineering teams and cross-functional partners Nice-to-Haves Experience building or scaling a compliance program at a high-growth company Experience with cash management or fixed income strategies Experience with digital or technology-enabled advisory models Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. Other notices Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.
