item.title: Ambassador Program Impact Manager
item.description: Ambassador Program Impact Manager Organization: Represent Justice Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/25/2026 Salary: $82,000-$98,000 At Represent Justice, our mission is to turn stories into action by building narrative power within criminal legal system-impacted communities and mobilizing audiences to transform the legal system. Our theory of change involves building up a critical mass of system-impacted storytellers using film and media to mobilize audiences to take action to transform the legal system. Represent Justice is also a legal reform organization that seeks to reduce harm, advocate for community healing and transformation, and critique the systems that impede true justice. As an organization dedicated to uplifting the stories and solutions of those closest to the problem, we believe in thoughtful analysis and partnership with criminal justice reform movement leaders across these issues, to implement our vision for a fair system and an end to mass incarceration and extreme sentencing. The Ambassador Program Impact Manager helps connect Represent Justice’s Ambassador stories, Ambassadors, and films to opportunities for meaningful engagement and impact. Reporting to the Vice President of Partnerships & Engagement, this role works across interconnected areas: Ambassador engagement and impact campaigns. The Manager builds and nurtures relationships with Represent Justice Ambassadors, external organizations, community partners, and audiences; identifies opportunities to strategically activate Represent Justice films and Ambassadors; and supports impact campaigns that use storytelling to advance narrative change and systems change goals. The ideal candidate is a strategic connector who can identify alignment across people, organizations, films, campaigns, and issue areas—and then translate that alignment into concrete opportunities. This person should be equally comfortable building relationships internally, externally, supporting campaign execution, coordinating Ambassador participation, pitching films and partnership opportunities, and ensuring that promising film screening and speaker activation ideas move from conversation to action. Best-in-Class Benefits and Culture: Our client values their employees’ time and effort. Their competitive compensation of $82,000-$98,000 annually, depending on experience, and an extensive benefits package, enhances their commitment to your success. Our client’s benefits package includes: Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance provided Robust retirement planning: 403(b) plan available with employer matching Well-being and work-life balance: Paid time off, paid holidays, and remote work choices provided Plus, they work to maintain the best possible environment for their employees, where people can learn and grow with the company. They strive to provide a collaborative environment where everyone feels encouraged to contribute to their processes, decisions, planning, and culture. As Ambassador Program Impact Manager, you should have: The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Must have: No specific degree is required. Candidates should have at least 3-5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in criminal justice reform advocacy, partnerships, campaigns, organizing, nonprofit management, community engagement, social impact, program management, organizing, film impact, or a related field. Relevant higher education or professional training may complement, but does not substitute for, demonstrated experience successfully performing this work. Demonstrated experience managing advocacy, social-impact, organizing, narrative-change, or issue-based campaigns. Ability to understand a story, film, project, or campaign and clearly articulate its relevance to different audiences and prospective partners. Strong strategic instincts and demonstrated ability to connect people, organizations, issues, campaigns, and opportunities. Strong project-management skills and demonstrated ability to manage multiple diverse priorities, relationships, deadlines, and workstreams simultaneously. Demonstrated ability to independently move projects forward, identify next steps, follow through on commitments, and escalate challenges appropriately. Ability to work effectively across teams and navigate shared ownership, competing priorities, and organizational dependencies. Strong judgment and professionalism when representing an organization externally. Commitment to equity, accountability, co-creation, and centering directly impacted leadership. Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, including utilizing and encouraging language that uplifts and humanizes system-impacted communities, always maintaining professionalism. Ability to work in partnership with directly impacted leaders and communities, with an ability to support lived-experience leadership while bringing strong campaign, partnership, and organizational expertise to the work. Ability to interface effectively and collaboratively with Represent Justice Ambassadors, partners, stakeholders and other staff members. Nice to have: Existing relationships within criminal justice reform, advocacy, organizing, policy, or social-impact networks. Experience with documentary film impact campaigns, impact producing, film distribution, or social-impact entertainment. Experience in legislative advocacy, lobbying, policy campaigns, grassroots organizing, or coalition building. Experience developing or supporting film screenings, community activations, advocacy events, or public programs. Experience facilitating meetings, trainings, panels, coalition conversations, or community discussions. Experience working with speakers, storytellers, fellows, artists, Ambassadors, or other directly impacted leaders. Familiarity with narrative-change and culture-change strategies. Experience using CRM and project-management platforms to track relationships, campaigns, and deliverables. Experience working across both national and state/local advocacy environments. Responsibilities of the Ambassador Program Impact Manager Impact & Advocacy Campaigns (20%) Support the development and implementation of impact campaigns that connect Represent Justice films and storytelling to advocacy, organizing, policy, and narrative-change opportunities. Help identify timely advocacy, legislative, cultural, and community opportunities where Represent Justice films, Ambassadors, and storytelling resources can add value. Research relevant advocacy campaigns, organizations, coalitions, policy developments, conferences, convenings, and other opportunities that align with Represent Justice films and organizational priorities. Support advocacy screening campaigns, community activations, partner events, panels, digital campaigns, and other opportunities that move audiences from storytelling toward engagement or action. Work with advocacy and community partners to identify appropriate calls to action and opportunities for audiences to engage beyond film screenings. Track campaign activities, partnerships, outcomes, learnings, and follow-up opportunities to support evaluation and future strategy. Ambassador Pitching & Opportunities (60%) Develop and implement meaningful opportunities for Ambassador engagement across Represent Justice programming, including film impact campaigns, advocacy partnerships, screenings, speaking opportunities, media and digital opportunities, trainings, workshops, and community events. Serve as a key organizational and internal liaison for connecting Ambassadors to opportunities that align with their stories, expertise, interests, lived experience, goals, and capacity. Build strong, respectful, and consistent relationships with Represent Justice Ambassadors and ensure they have clear information regarding relevant opportunities and expectations. Proactively identify and pitch opportunities for Ambassador engagement across Represent Justice programming and externally, including film screenings, community and advocacy events, film festivals, conferences, panels, media and digital opportunities, and trainings. Support outreach and relationship-building with organizations, screening hosts, advocacy partners, community groups, and other potential partners interested in engaging with Ambassador films and storytellers. Provide light event and screening management support for Ambassador film engagements, including coordinating panel participation, speaker logistics, run-of-show details, host communications, briefings, and other preparation necessary for successful events. Collaborate with internal teams to thoughtfully integrate Ambassadors into film campaigns, advocacy opportunities, external partnerships, communications opportunities, and organizational programming. Help prepare Ambassadors for external-facing opportunities by ensuring they understand the audience, purpose, goals, logistics, and relevant context. Facilitate regular communication and feedback loops with Ambassadors to understand their interests, experiences, goals, and evolving needs. Identify and share resources that strengthen Ambassadors’ ability to use storytelling, narrative strategy, advocacy, and public engagement to advance their individual and collective goals. Work in consultation with the Community Wellness Manager to incorporate trauma-informed practices into Ambassador engagement and external opportunities. As needed, support Ambassador-produced short film projects by helping coordinate program timelines, connect Ambassadors to appropriate internal resources, and troubleshoot or escalate needs. Help coordinate and facilitate Ambassador trainings, workshops, or learning opportunities as appropriate, in alignment with broader Ambassador Program goals

item.title: Federal Lobbyist
item.description: Federal Lobbyist Organization: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/25/2026 Americans for Prosperity (AFP) is the premier grassroots organization focused on advocating solutions to the country’s greatest challenges. We recognize that tens of millions of Americans are frustrated with the extreme partisanship in government that keeps common-sense reforms from being passed, and instead seek to stand with policy leaders who are committed to finding a better way. Americans for Prosperity is part of the Stand Together philanthropic community. As a Federal Lobbyist (internal title: Federal Legislative Liaison), you will advocate for AFP’s positions in Washington, D.C., working under the direction of the Director of Federal Affairs. Your goal: break down the barriers that stand in the way of people realizing their full potential. You will focus on federal legislative advocacy in three key policy areas: economics, energy, and AI and emerging technology. This role is ideal for a motivated government affairs professional with a few years of Capitol Hill, state legislative, or advocacy experience who is ready to take on greater lobbying responsibility. You will build relationships with congressional offices, coalition partners, trade associations, and think tanks, and grow into a trusted voice for AFP on the Hill. You should share our commitment to advancing every individual’s right to economic opportunity through free markets. How You Will Contribute Build and maintain relationships with congressional staff, members of Congress, and federal agency contacts to advance AFP’s legislative priorities on economics, energy, and AI PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. item.title: Policy Communications Lead
item.description: Policy Communications Lead Organization: Wing Location: Palo Alto, CA Date Posted: 10/25/2026 About Wing: Wing offers drone delivery as a safe, fast, and sustainable solution for last mile logistics. Consumer appetites for on-demand services are increasing, but current delivery methods are inefficient, costly, and contribute to road accidents and air pollution. Wing’s fleet of highly automated delivery drones can transport small packages directly from businesses to homes on-demand, in minutes. We design, build, and operate our aircraft, and offer drone delivery services on two continents. Our technology is designed to be easy to integrate into existing delivery and logistics networks, offering a scalable drone delivery solution for a broad range of businesses. Wing is a part of Google’s parent company, Alphabet, and our mission is to create the preferred means of delivery for the planet. If you’re ready to do the greatest work of your life, come join us. About the Role Wing is looking for a Policy Communications Lead to join our Communications team. This role is hybrid based in Palo Alto, CA or based remotely in the United States. You’ll set and execute the communications strategy for how Wing engages the people who decide whether and where we can operate: federal regulators, state and local officials, community groups, and the reporters who cover them. As drone delivery scales, public attention on noise, privacy, safety, and oversight is rising, and rules are increasingly written city by city. This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad scope and real influence. You’ll lead without direct reports, working with Government Affairs, Legal, Policy, Marketing, Operations, and our retail and logistics partners to build a record that communities and officials can verify. What You’ll Do Own Wing’s policy and regulatory communications strategy across federal, state, and local audiences Advise senior leaders and executives on how Wing’s public positioning affects permitting, legislation, and litigation Partner with Government Affairs and Legal to align messaging on rulemakings, legislation, litigation, and permitting proceedings, and know when to escalate Build the community-facing evidence base (noise, flight volume, operating hours, data and privacy practices) with Operations, and keep it accurate and current Prepare executives and spokespeople for hearings, council meetings, and high-stakes media interviews Lead issues and rapid-response communications when a market comes under scrutiny, including coordinating with partners on how Wing is described Develop pre-launch and pre-permit outreach toolkits that market teams can use at scale Monitor policy, media, and community sentiment, and translate it into clear risk assessments and recommendations for leadership Manage agency and consultant relationships for policy and issues communications Build a network of credible third-party voices, including host communities, partners, and outside experts What You’ll Need 12+ years of experience in policy communications, public affairs, or issues management Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience Experience scaling, operationalizing, or commercializing at a previous company A track record of leading communications strategy for regulatory, legislative, or other high-scrutiny issues, not only executing it Experience advising senior leaders and influencing cross-functional teams without formal authority Experience working with reporters on policy-driven or contested stories Ability to explain technical topics credibly without oversimplifying Strong judgment under pressure, including making calls with incomplete information and escalating appropriately to Legal and leadership The US base salary range for this full-time position is the salary range below + bonus + equity + benefits. Wing’s salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your location during the hiring process. Salary Range $238,000 – $252,000 USD Wing is an equal opportunity employer and it is Wing’s policy to comply with all applicable national, state and local laws pertaining to nondiscrimination and equal opportunity. Employment at Wing is based solely on a person’s merit and qualifications directly related to professional competence. Wing does not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), or any other basis protected by law. If you have a need that requires accommodation during the interview process due to a disability or special need, please let us know by completing our Candidate Accommodations Request Form. item.title: Senior Brand Marketing Manager, Social and Community
item.description: Senior Brand Marketing Manager, Social and Community Organization: Splice Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/25/2026 WHO WE ARE: Splice is a creative platform for people who make music. Serious producers choose Splice Sounds to bring their ideas to life. A subscription to Splice inspires and accelerates creative success for digital music creators with an industry-leading catalog of sounds and samples and an expanding AI stack. With a rent-to-own marketplace of DAWs and plugins, the Splice experience seamlessly integrates into any music production workflow, regardless of DAW (Digital Audio Workstation). Via Splice, an unparalleled team of sound designers and sample creators are fueling the success of a growing global community of chart-topping producers, students, and DIY creators. HOW WE WORK: At Splice, DISCO is a rallying cry for collaboration, accountability, and unity within our organization; Direct, Inclusive, Splice Together, Creator Centric, and Optimistic. Our shared success depends on our ability to support one another, work well together, and communicate directly. By embracing flexibility and a unified approach, we can navigate anything that’s thrown at us. Splice embraces a culture of remote work. You’ll see your colleagues showing up from across the US and the UK. In order to keep us working well as a team, we have regular communication, including Town Halls, departmental all-hands and get-togethers. When you join Splice, you join a network of colleagues, peers, and collaborators. Are you ready? SENIOR BRAND MARKETING MANAGER, SOCIAL & COMMUNITY LOCATION: Remote (US) — Los Angeles preferred, but not required THE ROLE Splice is looking for a full-time Senior Social & Community Manager to own the voice of Splice across our organic social portfolio and our Discord community. This is one of the most visible roles on the team and is central to the strategic direction of Splice: what you publish, how you show up, and what you learn from our audience shapes how the business thinks about creators. You’ll plan and publish content, run programming that brings producers together, engage directly with them in the comments, DMs, and Discord, and use performance data to sharpen what we make next. This is a hands-on role for someone who lives in the culture of music production. You make music yourself, you know what resonates with creators, and you can turn that instinct into content and community moments that earn attention. You’ll work closely with our brand, community, and product teams to translate what’s happening at Splice into things our community actually wants to see and take part in. As our portfolio grows, so does the role, with the opportunity to take on social and community channels for additional Splice brands. WHO WE ARE Splice is a creative platform for people who make music. Serious producers choose Splice Sounds to bring their ideas to life. A subscription to Splice inspires and accelerates creative success for digital music creators with an industry-leading catalog of sounds and samples and an expanding AI stack. With a rent-to-own marketplace of DAWs and plugins, the Splice experience seamlessly integrates into any music production workflow, regardless of DAW (Digital Audio Workstation). Via Splice, an unparalleled team of sound designers and sample creators are fueling the success of a growing global community of chart-topping producers, students, and DIY creators. HOW WE WORK At Splice, DISCO is a rallying cry for collaboration, accountability, and unity within our organization; Direct, Inclusive, Splice Together, Creator Centric, and Optimistic. Our shared success depends on our ability to support one another, work well together, and communicate directly. By embracing flexibility and a unified approach, we can navigate anything that’s thrown at us. Splice embraces a culture of remote work. You’ll see your colleagues showing up from across the US and the UK. In order to keep us working well as a team, we have regular communication, including Town Halls, departmental all-hands and get-togethers. When you join Splice, you join a network of colleagues, peers, and collaborators. Are you ready? WHAT YOU’LL DO Social Own the organic social strategy and publishing calendar across all Splice channels, from ideation through scheduling, posting, and platform-native optimization, and decide where we show up as platforms and audience behavior change Create and edit content yourself, from concept to final cut, with a fast turnaround and a strong point of view on what will land Show up in the comments, DMs, and replies as the voice of Splice, engaging producers directly, surfacing their work, and building real relationships in the process Spot and act on cultural moments, trends, and sounds in real time, including reactive posting outside of the calendar Partner with brand, product, and community teams to turn launches, artist packs, and platform news into content that feels native to each channel rather than an announcement Source and amplify community and creator-generated content, coordinating directly with producers and artists Community Manage and grow the Splice Discord server, keeping conversation active and welcoming day to day Plan and run recurring community programming, including beat battles, community challenges, and remix competitions, from concept and rules through promotion, judging, and recognition of winners Start and sustain regular conversations that give producers a reason to come back, share their work, and give each other feedback Work with moderators and internal teams to keep the community healthy, and bring what you hear in Discord back to the wider business Data and reporting Track performance across social and community channels and translate the numbers into clear recommendations: what to double down on, what to stop, and what to test next Use data to make decisions on content, programming, and channel investment, and report on channel health, community growth, and engagement to the business on a regular cadence Develop workflows to move faster and produce more, across ideation, scripting, editing, asset generation, and analysis Growth As the Splice portfolio grows, take on strategy and management of social and community channels for additional brands, with the scope of the role growing alongside the portfolio JOB REQUIREMENTS 5+ years managing social channels for a brand, artist, label, or creator-facing company, with examples of work you can point to Experience owning a multi-channel organic social presence, not a single platform Experience speaking directly to a creator audience, ideally in music, but adjacent creative categories will be considered You make music with a DAW. You understand production workflows from the inside and can talk to producers as a peer A proven track record of building and engaging a community, not just growing follower counts, including hands-on experience running a Discord server or a comparable community space Experience planning and running community programming such as contests, challenges, or competitions Native fluency across the major social platforms, including the formats, editing conventions, and publishing tools for short-form video, long-form video, and text-based channels Strong comfort with social and community analytics, and the ability to turn data into decisions and clear reporting for a business audience Hands-on experience and a genuine appetite for new tools as they emerge Strong writing and a natural instinct for tone. You can be funny, direct, and human without sounding like a brand account NICE TO HAVES Based in Los Angeles, with the ability to attend shoots, sessions, and creator meet-ups in person Experience with Blender or other 3D rendering/animation tools, and the ability to create original content with them Comfortable being on camera and featured in Splice content Existing relationships in the producer, artist, or label community Motion design, photography, or audio editing chops SPLICE BENEFITS: Compensation & Equity: Competitive pay with annual reviews and equity opportunities. Time Off: Unlimited PTO to recharge and thrive. Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents. Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with immediate vesting and company match. Parental Support: 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave for non-birthing parents, and 18-20 weeks for birthing parents. Flexible Work Options: Work remotely or connect at our office hubs and creative spaces worldwide. Professional Growth: Annual learning budget, leadership programs, and team ambassador opportunities. Community & Connection: Inclusive events, team meet-ups, and vibrant Employee Resource Groups. The national pay range for this role is $112,000 – $140,000 Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience. Splice is an Equal Opportunity Employer Splice provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. item.title: Senior Covenant Lawyer – Distressed
item.description: Senior Covenant Lawyer – Distressed Organization: 9fin Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/25/2026 About 9fin 9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion. Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets. Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption. We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide. The Opportunity 9fin is looking for a corporate finance attorney who geeks out about a good credit agreement or indenture and who has broader ambitions to write and be a thought-leader in the industry they love. This role will help our distressed editorial teams understand all the nuances of interesting bond and loan documents that could factor into restructuring and liability management exercises. It is perfect for an experienced finance attorney who is looking to recalibrate their work-life balance to allow for a little more life, but who loves their work. We’re growing our groundbreaking coverage of complex out-of-court restructurings with an emphasis on distressed coverage. The role will report into our New York office with flexibility to work from home / remotely as needed. This role offers a unique opportunity for a legal professional to use their expertise within a rapidly growing start-up environment, with opportunities to refine an already valuable skillset while learning all of the new skills that comes with working with technologists, credit analysts and journalists. What you’ll work on Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on: Reviewing leveraged finance and high yield documentation to produce commercially focused and insightful analysis on distressed scenarios and the primary market Writing topical reports on secondary situations, collaborating closely across 9fin’s team of lawyers and credit analysts Answering client questions about the covenant packages of specific borrowers and issuers Using 9fin’s proprietary technology to build and expand our restructuring and LME databases Delivering seminars, teach-ins and podcast segments as a subject matter expert Representing 9fin in the press and at industry conferences and events About You This role will be a great fit if you have the following: JD with 5+ years of experience within a capital solutions, leveraged finance, capital markets, restructuring and/or special situations team at a top-tier law firm Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating high yield bond and/or leveraged loan documents, restructuring support agreements, and Chapter 11 documentation Keen commercial awareness of leveraged finance and restructuring markets Strong technical understanding of how leveraged finance covenants and definitions operate Existing network of relationships within the leveraged finance community Excellent relationship building skills Effective written and verbal communication skills, able to explain complex covenant concepts to non-lawyers concisely Ability to work both independently and collaboratively Our benefits We’re a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel. Financial & Insurance Competitive Salary: $256,000-$340,000 Equity Options 401(k) (9fin pay 3%, employee contributions are uncapped) Private Health Insurance, with Dental and Vision Paid sick leave Disability Insurance (New York) Commuter Benefit Time off 25 vacation days per year Local public holiday Work abroad for up to 3 months a year 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available Training & Culture Professional learning and development budget Bi-annual team socials Summer and Winter company social events Hybrid Policy 9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role. 9fin is an equal opportunities employer At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Communications Manager, Policy, Safety & Reputation
item.description: Senior Communications Manager, Policy, Safety & Reputation Organization: Zoox Location: Foster City, CA Date Posted: 10/25/2026 Zoox is building autonomous mobility from the ground up — a purpose-built robotaxi designed for riders, not retrofitted from an existing car. As we scale from testing to public commercial service, few things matter more than earning and keeping the trust of the public, regulators, and the communities we operate in. This role sits at the center of that work. We’re looking for a Senior Communications Manager of Policy, Safety & Reputation to lead communications across these important business functions. You will set the strategy and execute it, driving proactive campaigns and building relationships that contribute directly to the mission at Zoox. You will also build trust through proactive and reactive communications work across reputation, safety, and policy. In this role you will: Partner cross-functionally with policy, safety, legal, product, and other teams at Zoox to build communication campaigns that further elevate our safety, policy, and reputation initiatives. Own and support a broad range of external communications programs and events aligned with policy and communication objectives. Track the AV regulatory landscape in partnership with policy and turn developments into forward-looking communications strategies. Develop relationships with media and manage inbound and reactive requests across safety and reputation-related topics and issues. Proactively tell our safety story telling and framework to key external stakeholders. Anticipate communications risks and establish risk-mitigation strategies. Serve as a trusted communications partner to safety, product, legal, and policy on sensitive, fast-moving matters. In partnership with our Public Affairs team, build communications programs that support our key community and policy in-market initiatives. Support reactive communications efforts with speed, accuracy, and judgment. Provide communications counsel and support to team members across the organization Work cross-functionally within existing working groups on safety and trust to represent communications. Qualifications 8+ years in communications or policy communications, with deep experience handling safety, regulatory, or reputation-sensitive issues. A proven track record managing high-stakes, technical communications, ideally in a heavily regulated industry (AV, aviation, automotive, energy, healthcare). Experience running proactive policy communications campaigns that successfully shaped narratives or regulatory outcomes. Experience in issues management and developing reactive communications under pressure and tight timelines. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex technical topics accurately for broad audiences. Strong executive management skills and a proven ability to work collaboratively cross-functionally. High attention to detail and program organization skills. Sharp instincts for what builds and what breaks public trust. Bonus Qualifications Experience in autonomous vehicles, mobility, or emerging technology. Familiarity with the federal and state AV regulatory environment. $164,000 – $197,000 a year Base Salary Range There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate’s relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position. Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Paralegal, Equity Administration and Regulatory Support
item.description: Paralegal, Equity Administration and Regulatory Support Organization: Midi Health Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/25/2026 About Midi Health At Midi Health, we are redefining healthcare for women in midlife. Our virtual care model connects patients with specialized clinicians, and our growth depends on a legal foundation that is organized, accurate, and built to scale. We are seeking a Paralegal, Equity Administration & Regulatory Support to help Midi’s legal team across equity administration, regulatory filings, entity management, and finance coordination. This role will administer our equity program and serve as a key liaison between Legal and Finance. It will help keep Midi and its affiliated professional entities in good standing across many states. The ideal candidate is a detail-driven, proactive paralegal who brings structure to recurring deadlines, owns their work from intake to completion, and knows when to escalate to an attorney. This role works closely with the legal team, Finance, People, Clinical Operations, outside counsel, and service providers. Key Responsibilities: Equity Administration Administer Midi’s equity program and maintain accurate capitalization records in Carta or a similar platform. Prepare equity grant documents and board approvals, and process grants, exercises, cancellations, transfers, and terminations. Track vesting, post-termination exercise periods, and 83(b) election documentation. Coordinate with Finance and outside providers on 409A valuations and stock-based compensation reporting. Monitor equity issuances for securities law compliance and state notice filings. Respond to employee equity questions and escalate tax, securities, or plan interpretation questions to the appropriate attorney or advisor. Support financings, secondary transactions, and other corporate matters by managing diligence requests, data rooms, signature packets, and closing documents. Finance and Legal Liaison Serve as the day-to-day liaison between Legal and Finance on entity, equity, audit, tax, and contract-related matters. Coordinate franchise tax payments, filing fees, and registered agent invoices with Finance. Help manage outside counsel and legal vendor invoices, budget tracking, and spend reporting. Support audit requests, including legal confirmations, equity reconciliations, and corporate documentation. Track and document intercompany agreements and payments between Midi and its affiliated professional entities, in coordination with Finance and Legal. Help maintain contract records and key obligation trackers relevant to Finance, including payment terms, renewals, and notice deadlines. Regulatory Filings and Compliance Calendar Prepare, file, and track state and federal regulatory filings for Midi and its affiliated professional entities, under attorney supervision. Support state-level filings for professional entities, including formations, ownership and officer changes, and other required updates. Help prepare and maintain healthcare regulatory applications, renewals, and supporting documentation, coordinating with Clinical Operations and licensing teams as needed. Maintain a centralized compliance calendar of filing deadlines, renewals, annual reports, and other recurring obligations. Research state filing requirements and procedures, and flag changes or issues for attorney review. Entity Management and Registered Agent Oversight Serve as the primary point of contact with Midi’s registered agent and oversee its services across all jurisdictions. Receive, log, and route service of process, government notices, and other registered agent correspondence promptly to the appropriate attorney. Maintain the good standing of all entities, including annual reports, franchise tax filings, foreign qualifications, amendments, and withdrawals. Maintain corporate records, minute books, entity charts, officer and director lists, and the entity management system. Prepare board and stockholder consents, secretary’s certificates, good standing certificates, and other governance documents. Support board meetings by preparing materials, tracking approvals, collecting signatures, and maintaining records. About You Excellent attention to detail: You know the importance of proofreading, accuracy, and consistency in filings, records, and communications. A strong sense of urgency: You thrive in a fast-paced, demanding environment and never let a deadline slip. A problem solver with sound judgment: You take ownership of questions sent your way, whether from Finance, an employee, or a service provider, and you understand when attorney escalation is needed. An organized, proactive project manager: You can manage many recurring obligations across multiple entities and jurisdictions, and you build frameworks to execute them reliably. Excellent written and verbal communication: You write clear issue summaries and explain processes simply to non-lawyers. Curious and eager to learn: You believe technology can make legal work better and help the team serve the business. Confident with people at all levels: You work comfortably with executives, finance leaders, clinicians, employees, and outside advisors. Comfortable with ambiguity: You ask thoughtful questions and focus on details while understanding the legal team’s broader priorities. Discreet: You handle confidential corporate, equity, and personnel information with professionalism. Experience & Qualifications Minimum 3 years of hands-on equity administration experience using Carta, Shareworks, or a similar platform. Minimum 5 years of experience as a corporate paralegal at a law firm, in-house legal department, or both. Experience working with Finance on audits, tax filings, equity reporting, or legal spend. Hands-on experience with entity management across multiple states, including annual reports, foreign qualifications, and registered agent coordination. Healthcare, digital health, or other regulated-industry experience is a strong plus, particularly with professional entities or healthcare licensing filings. Experience at a venture-backed or high-growth company is a plus. Bachelor’s degree or paralegal certificate preferred. Proficiency in Google Workspace or Microsoft Office, Slack, and e-signature platforms. Comfort with entity management systems, CLM tools, and AI tools is a strong plus. Compensation The base salary range for this role is $120,000 – $135,000 annually. Final compensation will depend on experience, skills, and qualifications. This role is eligible for equity and benefits. Why Join Midi? At Midi, you will help build the legal infrastructure that allows specialized midlife healthcare to reach more women. You will work with a mission-driven team that values accuracy, ownership, and practical problem solving. Midi’s benefits currently include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k), flexible paid time off, parental leave, a new-hire equipment stipend, and a monthly remote-work stipend. #LI-MB1 At this time, Midi is unable to provide visa sponsorship. All Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship needs. Please note that all official communication from Midi Health will come from an @joinmidi.com email address. We will never ask for payment of any kind during the application or hiring process. If you receive any suspicious communication claiming to be from Midi Health, please report it immediately by emailing us at [email protected] . Midi Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to pay equity and ensure that all qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Our compensation philosophy is based on fair, objective criteria and the impact of the role, regardless of an applicant’s salary history. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Head of Internal Communications
item.description: Head of Internal Communications Organization: Vanta Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/25/2026 At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. As Vanta’s Internal Communications Director, you’ll help set the internal beat of the company making sure every team member understands the messages that matter, while also defining how we communicate with each other as we scale The People team builds the systems, culture, and experience that let Vanta’ns do their best work as we grow quickly across the globe. Internal comms sits at the heart of that mission: making sure every Vanta’n understands our strategy, our story, and what’s expected of them, no matter how fast we’re moving. Reporting to the Head of People, this is a build-from-scratch mandate. You’ll define the strategy, the infrastructure, and the cadence for how Vanta communicates. You’ll have room to bring your own voice and instincts into how we do it, from the words we choose for a key company moment to how an all-hands actually feels in the room. Then you’ll roll up your sleeves to make it happen. What you’ll do as an Internal Communications Director at Vanta: Shape how Vanta tells its own story internally and ensure that key messages land at exactly the right moment. Build and manage internal comms infrastructure: the channels, cadences and best practices for how the company communicates (Slack norms, docs, wikis, etc.). Own key internal company-wide moments end to end, including all-hands, major announcements, and org-wide notifications, from planning through delivery. Partner closely with the People team as a strategic sounding board on sensitive or high-stakes communications Serve as a strategic communications partner across the business, triaging and prioritizing company-wide communication requests and partnering with stakeholders to translate complex topics into clear, effective messaging. Partner with Marketing and External Comms to keep our internal and external narrative aligned and consistent. Act as a trusted advisor to the C-team and Leadership Team on how and when to communicate major business updates. Build and protect company culture and morale through comms, keeping the energy and momentum visible as Vanta grows. Evolve Vanta’s internal comms strategy and toolkit as the company scales, experimenting with new formats and channels. Measure and iterate on what’s working, bringing a data-informed lens to internal comms. How to be successful in this role: 8-10+ years of experience building and running an internal comms strategy, ideally at a high-growth company. Proven track record on building an internal comms strategy and executing on that strategy Strong writer and storyteller who can translate complex or sensitive topics into clear, human messaging. Comfortable operating at both altitudes. Can set strategy but is equally willing to execute (write the email, run the all-hands, edit the deck). Executive influence and partnership. Able to partner with and influence the C-team and Leadership Team. Experience partnering with People/HR teams on sensitive organizational communications. Excellent judgment and prioritization skills, with the ability to balance competing communication requests, advise stakeholders on what requires company-wide visibility. A natural sense for culture and energy. Someone who brings personality and vibes, not just polished corporate messaging. Creative and willing to take risks and try new things. Comfortable pitching bold or unconventional ideas, and knows how to calibrate when to push and when to dial it back. Leverage AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work – demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship. What you can expect as a Vanta’n: Industry-competitive salary and equity Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents Health & wellness stipend Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office Family planning benefits Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time 11 company-paid holidays Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events! Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials. #LI-remote At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply. About Vanta We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world’s leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that’s real-time and transparent. Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Compliance Director, Trust Company and Custody Operations
item.description: Compliance Director, Trust Company and Custody Operations Organization: Vestwell Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/25/2026 Vestwell is the financial technology company powering the new savings economy. The New York City-based fintech platform redefines how people save for the critical aspects of life across retirement, education, and healthcare savings needs. Today, Vestwell enables over 790,000 businesses and more than 2.75 million active savers, with over $57 billion in assets saved across all 50 United States. Vestwell offers a range of products, including workplace-delivered retirement plans, employer-offered student loan repayment benefits, and various savings accounts for education, emergencies, and individuals with disabilities. Vestwell’s platform serves a diverse clientele, including financial advisers, employers, third-party administrators, financial institutions, payroll providers, government agencies, and individual savers. To learn more, visit vestwell.com Who Are We Looking For? We are seeking an experienced and strategic Compliance Director of Trust Company and Custody Operations to lead and manage regulatory compliance and operational oversight across our trust company, custodial, and trading operations. This individual will play a key role in ensuring compliance with all applicable regulations related to 401(k) plans, ERISA, and trust and custody services. The ideal candidate will bring a deep understanding of regulatory requirements, operational excellence, and a proven track record in managing regulatory operations within financial services or trust company and retirement plan administration. What Will You Be Doing? Lead the regulatory operations function with a focus on qualified retirement plans, particularly 401(k) plans, IRAs, and Emergency Savings Accounts. Create and implement procedures and internal controls for all trading activities within our custodial operations and proactively monitor our teams and systems for compliance with applicable laws and regulations. Ensure compliance with ERISA, Internal Revenue Code (IRC), DOL, IRS, trust company regulations, and SEC regulations. Oversee and enhance controls related to trust and custody operations, as well as state savings programs, ensuring alignment with fiduciary standards and regulatory expectations. Provide regular reporting to internal stakeholders and Risk Committee about material risks, incidents, and the effectiveness of risk mitigation strategies. Partner with internal stakeholders (legal, compliance, product, operations) to interpret new and existing regulations and apply them to business practices. Monitor regulatory developments and proactively advise senior leadership on potential business impacts and required changes. Serve as the lead for the Legal Team to lead the Vestwell Trust Company SOC 1 audit and New Hampshire Banking Department regulatory exam. Liaise with external auditors, regulatory agencies, and third-party service providers during examinations, audits, inquiries, or other matters as needed. Oversee and support regulatory reporting and filings (e.g., Form 5500, IRS/DOL disclosures). Manage a team of regulatory operations professionals, providing leadership, coaching, and performance oversight. Drive continuous improvement and automation of regulatory and compliance processes and controls. Requirements The Necessities Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field required; advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., JD, CPA, CRSP, QKA, CISP) preferred. Minimum of 10+ years of experience with a proven track record in regulatory compliance or operations in the retirement, trust, or custodial services industry. Deep knowledge of ERISA, 401(k) regulations, trust company laws, custody services, and applicable IRS/DOL regulations. Experience managing operational risk, compliance audits, and regulatory examinations. Strong leadership and team management skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across functions. Exceptional organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Experience working with recordkeeping platforms, trust accounting systems, or custodial platforms is a plus. The Extras Start up experience This role will be based in the New York City office, and will be part of Vestwell’s hybrid in-office operation. The expected base salary range for this position is $160K – $180K base. This position is eligible to participate in the Company Bonus Pool and is eligible to receive new hire equity in the Company. Please note that salary bands are based on NY and other similar metro areas and may differ based on where the role is ultimately hired. Full-Time Employee Benefits We’re an innovative, high-growth company with an exciting future ahead. At Vestwell, we prioritize employee wellbeing through comprehensive health benefits, generous time off, and a dedicated Employee Wellbeing Committee. Our hybrid work model offers flexibility while providing access to our collaborative offices in Midtown Manhattan, Austin, King of Prussia, and Scottsdale. And, of course, as a company focused on helping people save for the future, we offer a competitive 401(k) plan. Interview Process Our interview process starts the same for every candidate with 1-2 introductory conversations to learn more about your background, interests, and what you’re looking for, while also giving you the opportunity to learn more about Vestwell and the team. From there, the process varies by role but typically includes a skills or experience-based assessment, such as a coding interview, portfolio review, or deeper discussion of your relevant experience. Successful candidates then move on to a virtual or in-person interview panel. Before extending an offer, we complete a reference check with a current or former manager and a peer. Throughout the process, we prioritize transparency, clear communication, and minimizing surprises. For your awareness you will only receive correspondence from [email protected] any other domain not ending in vestwell.com is not our Recruitment team. Vestwell’s Privacy Policy. Attention California residents: In the course of conducting our business and complying with federal, state, and local government regulations governing such matters as employment, tax, insurance, etc., we must collect Personal Information from you. Should you accept employment with Vestwell you may view our California Privacy Rights Act here: Vestwell’s California Privacy Rights Policy. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: VP, FCM, Tokenization & Stablecoin Compliance Officer
item.description: VP, FCM, Tokenization & Stablecoin Compliance Officer Organization: DriveWealth Location: Austin, TX | Dallas, TX | Denver, CO | Miami, FL | Chicago, IL | New York City, NY | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA Date Posted: 10/25/2026 About Us DriveWealth is on a mission to make investing easier. We believe that everyone should have the ability to control their financial future, and that access to financial markets should not be limited by geography, wealth, or legacy systems. We are a global B2B financial technology organization dedicated to democratizing access to financial independence around the world. Our mission is realized through an API-based platform, empowering our partners to offer seamless investing and trading experiences to clients worldwide, all from their mobile devices. Our technology provides partners with a modern, extensible toolkit, enabling traditional investment workflows and innovative techniques like fractional share ownership. DriveWealth has evolved into a global platform offering trading of US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options. There’s never been a better time to build a category-defining business and there has rarely been a team better positioned for this opportunity. Our culture blends the pace and agility of a fintech start-up with the impact, stability, and discipline of Wall Street. We encourage creativity and experimentation while ensuring institutional-grade execution and regulatory compliance in everything we do. Join us and help build the future of global investing! About The Role DriveWealth LLC is seeking a highly motivated and seasoned VP, FCM, Tokenization & Stablecoin Compliance Officer in either our New York or Chicago office to lead compliance for the firm’s expansion into event-based prediction markets and stablecoin/tokenization initiatives. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will build and lead the compliance program supporting DriveWealth’s FCM registration and NFA membership, alongside the firm’s growing digital asset and stablecoin footprint. In this leadership role, you will provide expert guidance on complex regulatory matters spanning CFTC and NFA rules governing futures commission merchants, prediction and event contract markets (including our relationship with Kalshi), and the regulatory frameworks applicable to stablecoin issuance, custody, and tokenization. This is a build role: as firms across the industry, including Robinhood and other fintech and brokerage platforms, expand into similar products, we are seeking a leader who has directly navigated this regulatory landscape and can stand up a compliant, scalable program while shaping firm-wide controls within an innovative and entrepreneurial culture. What You’ll Do Program Build-Out & Team Leadership Program Development: Build and lead the compliance function supporting DriveWealth’s FCM registration, NFA membership, and stablecoin/tokenization initiatives, hiring and developing staff as the business scales. Workflow Oversight: Manage and re-prioritize team workloads across FCM, prediction market, and stablecoin/tokenization workstreams to ensure multiple projects and regulatory deadlines are met simultaneously. Quality Assurance: Review and approve detailed reports and surveillance investigations prepared by staff covering prediction market trading activity and stablecoin/tokenized asset transactions to ensure accurate summarization of issues and logical solutions. Regulatory Advisory & Operations Business Advisory: Advise business units on CFTC, NFA, and applicable state and federal digital asset regulatory obligations tied to prediction markets and stablecoins, as well as new rule proposals and firm policies. Compliance Frameworks: Design, implement, and maintain effective compliance frameworks aligned with CFTC, NFA, state money transmitter and stablecoin regulatory regimes (e.g., the GENIUS Act), and other regulatory obligations. Policy Governance: Oversee the development and maintenance of Written Supervisory Procedures (WSPs) for FCM operations, and internal policies governing stablecoin reserves, redemption mechanics, and tokenized asset custody. Strategic Partnership: Proactively partner with Kalshi and other prediction market venues, stablecoin/tokenization technology partners, the firm’s Financial Crimes team, business management, risk, and technology to ensure sound business operations and facilitate the firm’s success. Monitoring & Surveillance Level 2 Oversight: Perform Level 2 compliance reviews of prediction market and stablecoin/tokenization activity directly in the early stages of this role, transitioning to a supervisory capacity as the team is built out, ensuring firm-wide adherence to internal standards throughout. Surveillance Logic: Enhance surveillance and monitoring frameworks covering event contract trading patterns and stablecoin transaction activity by refining detection logic and identifying patterns in large trade and transaction datasets, partnering with the firm’s Financial Crimes team on BSA/AML and Travel Rule monitoring. Regulatory Reporting: Develop and analyze data for Compliance management reports, including FCM financial/segregation reporting and stablecoin reserve attestations, and provide periodic status updates on key issues. Examinations & Inquiries Exam Leadership: Lead the firm’s response to regulatory exams and inquiries from the CFTC, NFA, state money transmitter regulators, and other applicable authorities related to FCM and stablecoin/tokenization activities. Audit Support: Coordinate the collection of documentation and ensure timely follow-up for all regulatory inquiries. You Bring Bachelor’s Degree; J.D. or other advanced degree a plus. 12+ years of Compliance, Legal, Regulatory, or Financial Services experience, including at least 5+ years focused directly on futures/derivatives (FCM) compliance and/or stablecoin, tokenization, or digital asset regulatory compliance. Deep understanding of CFTC and NFA rules governing futures commission merchants, prediction and event contract markets, and derivatives clearing, along with direct, hands-on experience with stablecoin issuance, tokenization, digital asset custody, and related regulatory frameworks (e.g., the GENIUS Act, OCC guidance, and state money transmitter licensing). Comfortable partnering closely with the firm’s Financial Crimes team on BSA/AML and Travel Rule matters as they apply to these products. Required: Series 3 (National Commodity Futures Examination), with Series 30 (NFA Branch Manager) strongly preferred; FINRA Series 7 and 24 and NFA Swaps Proficiency Requirements (Swaps Certificate) are a plus. An AML certification (e.g., CAMS) is a plus for coordinating with the firm’s Financial Crimes team, though this role does not own BSA/AML program responsibilities. Proven build experience: Track record standing up or scaling a compliance program for a new product line, ideally at a firm expanding into prediction markets and/or digital assets, such as Robinhood, Kalshi, or a comparable platform. Strong ability to work with large trade and transaction datasets and translate complex, cross-regulatory requirements into practical control updates. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to interface with all levels of management and build effective relationships. Location This role is open to candidates in the following locations: Office/Hybrid: New York City, Chicago. Remote: Austin, Dallas, Denver, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, or Seattle. If based in New York or Chicago: This role is expected to come into the office on a cadence set by the Hiring Manager/Team. If based in Austin, Dallas, Denver, Miami, San Francisco, or Seattle: This is a fully remote role, though you may need to visit our onsite offices from time to time. If you’re not based in one of the locations listed above, this role is not a fit, and we cannot accommodate remote work outside these locations. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth does not sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. Pay Range: $225,000 – $250,000 USD Working at DriveWealth We do our best work when we’re in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We’ve found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you’re here, you’re working directly with the people making the decisions. To support that work, we provide competitive compensation, equity, and a 401(k) match. We also offer Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, Disability insurance, and Paid Parental Leave, along with a wellness reimbursement, a company-provided phone, and a personal development allowance. Finally, we value the time you spend away from the office with generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and observed holidays. Work Authorization Applicants must possess the legal right to work in the country where the position is located at the time of application. DriveWealth requires all employees to provide original documentation verifying their work authorization on or before their first day of employment. For US-based roles: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. DriveWealth does not provide visa sponsorship or support for employment authorization, including transfers, at this time. Offers of employment are strictly contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the Company. item.title: Vice President/Director, Medicaid & Home Care Policy
item.description: Vice President/Director, Medicaid & Home Care Policy Organization: National Alliance for Care at Home (Alliance) Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Salary Range: $145,000.00 To $200,000.00 Annually About Us The National Alliance for Care at Home (Alliance) is the leading authority in transforming care in the home. As a national trade association, we represent providers of home care, home health, hospice, palliative care, and other services delivered where people want them most—at home. We are an inclusive thought leader, advocate, educator, and convener, serving as a unified voice for providers and the individuals they care for across all stages of life. Position Overview The National Alliance for Care at Home is hiring one position on our Policy, Quality, Regulatory, and Compliance team focused on Medicaid home and community-based services (HCBS) and home care policy. This role will be filled at either the Director or Vice President level, depending on the successful candidate’s experience. The scope of responsibility, decision-making authority, and compensation differ by level, as described below. Candidates at any experience level within these ranges are encouraged to apply, and final title and level will be determined through the interview process. Compensation VP level: $185,000 to $200,000 annually Director level: $145,000 to $160,000 annually This role is a key contributor within the Policy, Quality, Regulatory, and Compliance (PQRC) team, working closely with the Chief Government Affairs Officer to advance policies that strengthen, support, and expand access to the broad array of home and community-based services (HCBS) available under Medicaid and private pay home care services. This is a great opportunity for someone to serve as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert, helping to ensure our members stay ahead in a rapidly changing home health landscape. To succeed in this role, you will be an analytical thinker, a skilled communicator, and one who thrives in a fast-moving, ever-changing, and time-sensitive environment. This position is based in our Alexandria VA, office and we prefer candidates who currently reside in the Washington, DC metro area (DMV). We will also consider candidates located outside the region who are willing to relocate, or who can travel to the Alexandria office on a periodic basis (approximately two times [6 days] per month) to meet with the team and attend key meetings support in-person collaboration, stakeholder engagement and events as needed. About the Role Both levels serve on a cross-functional legislative, regulatory, research, and policy development team, working closely with the Chief Government Affairs Officer to advance policies that strengthen, support, and expand access to Medicaid HCBS and private-pay home care services. Both levels supervise one direct report, a State Policy Specialist. At the Director level, this person will research and draft policy positions, testimony, and regulatory comments for review and delivery by the Chief Government Affairs Officer; support relationship-building with Congressional, CMS, and MACPAC contacts; and build toward independent representation of the Alliance at state association events as expertise develops. At the Vice President level, this person will independently recommend Medicaid policy positions to the Board and Public Policy Advisory Committee; build and maintain direct relationships with Congressional staff, CMS officials, MACPAC commissioners, and state Medicaid agencies; and represent the Alliance directly through Congressional testimony, regulatory comment letters, and public advocacy forums. Primary Responsibilities (Both Levels) Staff and support the Medicaid Advisory Council (MAC), including member recruitment, meeting scheduling, agenda development, and consensus building. Provide analysis of legislation and regulations affecting Medicaid HCBS and home care. Develop research and policy-focused white papers on Medicaid HCBS and home care. Supervise and mentor the State Policy Specialist. Support state associations with state-specific Medicaid HCBS advocacy needs. Represent the Alliance at state association speaking engagements. Develop and deliver educational programming on Medicaid HCBS policy for members and partners. Build coalitions with organizations that share common policy views on Medicaid HCBS. Required Qualifications Director Level Five to Eight (5-8) years of experience in healthcare policy and advocacy preferred. A background with Medicaid HCBS policy issues is highly preferred. Bachelor’s degree in health administration, political science, public health, or related field required. MA in Public Policy, MPH, or JD a plus. Vice President Level Eight or more (8+) years of experience in healthcare policy and advocacy preferred. A background with Medicaid HCBS policy issues is highly preferred, including direct interaction with CMS, state Medicaid agencies, and/or Congress. Bachelor’s degree in health administration, political science, public health, or related field required. MA in Public Policy, MPH, or JD preferred. Healthcare background and advanced knowledge of Medicaid HCBS policy affecting homecare and hospice. Key Competencies (Both Levels) A service-oriented focus on exceeding members’ expectations and delivering value. Excellent interpersonal and presentation, and writing skills. Demonstrated influencing skills and ability to collaborate with colleagues at all levels of the organization, including advising executive leadership and members. Ability to build effective coalitions and engagement on advocacy issues. Strong project management skills to effectively deliver tasks and project deadlines. Demonstrated ability to contribute to cross-functional teams with various initiative leads (education, membership, policy, and others) to accomplish overall organizational goals. Ability to work independently to manage multiple concurrent and complex projects and initiatives with different stakeholders across the Association. Excellent writing skills with the ability to effectively communicate information to diverse audiences. Compensation & Benefits This position is classified as a full-time, exempt position. At the VP level this role has a salary range of $185,000 to $200,000 annually to commensurate with related experience. At the Director level this role has a salary range of $145,000 to $160,000. The Alliance offers an excellent benefits package, which includes medical, dental and vision coverage, life insurance, short-and long-term disability plans, retirement, tuition reimbursement, generous leave and more! To Apply Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until the position is filled; however, preference will be given to applications received by the close of business on October 30, 2026. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. No telephone inquiries, please. This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. EEOC The Alliance is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability, please reach out to the Alliance HR team. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
