item.title: Policy & Advocacy Coordinator
item.description: Policy & Advocacy Coordinator Organization: National Alliance for Care at Home (Alliance) Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Salary Range: $24.04 To $28.85 Hourly About Us The National Alliance for Care at Home (Alliance) is the leading authority in transforming care in the home. As a national trade association, we represent providers of home care, home health, hospice, palliative care, and other services delivered where people want them most—at home. We are an inclusive thought leader, advocate, educator, and convener, serving as a unified voice for providers and the individuals they care for across all stages of life. Position Overview Reporting directly to the Vice President, Policy & Legislative Affairs, the Policy & Advocacy Coordinator is a key member of the Policy, Quality, Regulatory, and Compliance (PQRC) team. This role supports the effective execution of cross-functional business initiatives across the team. This role coordinates workflows, tracks deliverables, supports process improvements, prepares materials, and helps ensure the department has the information, tools, and follow-through needed to meet organizational priorities. The ideal candidate is highly organized, technologically proficient, solution-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Primary Responsibilities Although other duties may be assigned, the Policy & Advocacy Coordinator’s duties include the following. Policy Administration Support Coordinate projects, workflows, and deliverables that support organizational priorities across Public Policy, Regulatory Affairs, Government Relations, and Quality & Compliance. Draft and format responses to inquiries via email and re:Members as directed by the VP of Policy and Legislative Affairs, and General Operations. Develop and organize meeting materials, project summaries, process documents, presentations, and follow-up action items. Coordinate meetings, timelines, project milestones, and follow-up activities for the PQRC team and general operations. Prepare clear internal communications, status updates, workflow summaries, and operational briefings to support cross-functional alignment. Create, maintain, and refine operational tools and materials using Microsoft Excel, Word, Visio, and PowerPoint, including tracking spreadsheets, formatted documents, process maps, dashboards, and presentations. Office Coordination & Operational Support Provide office coordination support, including visitor coordination, front desk coverage, mail distribution, deliveries, and related operational needs as required to support business operations. This role is responsible for front desk coverage 3 days a week in the office. Support a professional and responsive office environment for visitors, staff, vendors, and cross-functional partners. Coordinate incoming mail, deliveries, and office materials to ensure timely routing and follow-through. Support accurate capture, routing, and documentation of materials requiring entry into internal systems. Coordinate office logistics and operational requests in partnership with Facilities and appropriate department contacts. Facilities, Vendor & Departmental Coordination Serve as the point of contact for shredding services and coordinate related pickups. Serve as the primary liaison with building management staff on office-related needs. Coordinate meeting logistics, meals, vendor scheduling, and facilities-related support for cross-functional initiatives and operational activities as needed. Required Qualifications BA/BS or relevant experience and high school diploma. Familiarity with or interest in health care policy, home care/aging services, and/or the legislative and regulatory process. Demonstrated knowledge of healthcare legislation and regulations preferred. 1-3 years of prior administrative, front desk, or office coordinator experience preferred. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proven prioritization and problem-solving capabilities. Professional, polished demeanor with a positive, service-oriented attitude. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities. Tech-savvy, with intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio. Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information (draft legislative positions, coalition strategy, member advocacy data) with discretion. Reliable, punctual, and comfortable working in-person at the front desk on a set schedule. Key Competencies Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong ability to craft professional emails, and stakeholder-facing correspondence. Customer service mindset and an ability to build and maintain positive relationships. Strong organizational and project management skills; Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to juggle multiple priorities and deadlines. Demonstrated ability to track deliverables, logistics, and support project management across departments. Ability to identify issues or discrepancies, follow established procedures for resolution, and escalate complex problems to a supervisor when necessary. Ability to complete assigned tasks with minimal supervision and work effectively as part of a team. Must be reliable and trustworthy. Ability to work from the assigned office three (3) days a week on a regular basis, subject to change based on the needs of the business. This position is based in our Alexandria VA, office and we prefer candidates who currently reside in the Washington, DC metro area (DMV), or who are willing to relocate. The role is currently a hybrid telework arrangement with three (3) days a week in the Alexandria, VA office and may be subject to change with the needs of the organization. Compensation & Benefits This position is classified as a full-time, non-exempt position with a starting hourly rate of $24.04 – $28.85/hour to commensurate with related experience. item.title: Senior Program Manager
item.description: Senior Program Manager Organization: The Hunt Institute Location: Cary, NC Date Posted: 10/26/2026 The Hunt Institute’s mission is to provide unbiased research, technical expertise, and learning opportunities that equip and empower educators and policymakers to drive equitable reforms and become audacious champions for education. Since its establishment in 2001, the organization has emerged as a recognized and credible leader in the movement to transform American public education and a go-to source for reliable, objective, and timely information. The Institute works at the intersection of education policy and politics, supporting state and national officials and empowering them to drive education reform. Its mandate is to inspire and equip elected officials and senior policymakers to make informed decisions that improve the lives of all children. The Institute’s primary audience consists of governors, legislators, and other elected and state-level policymakers. About the role The Hunt Institute is seeking a Senior Program Manager (SPM) to join our State Engagement team. The SPM develops sessions and content for State Legislators Retreats, Hunt State Policy Fellows, and support other Institute work as needed, including conducting research and analysis on relevant policy issues and providing information for reports, policy briefs, primers, and case studies for dissemination. The Senior Program Manager will report directly to the Director of State Engagement. The position is based out of The Hunt Institute’s office in Cary, North Carolina. What you’ll do Program Strategy & Execution Plans, develops, implements, and coordinates Hunt Institute project(s) or program(s). Manages, and oversees the daily administrative components of program(s)/project(s). Define program goals, objectives, and success metrics, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities. Coordinate and communicate with internal and external stakeholders, providing regular program updates and reports. Manage program budgets, ensuring projects are completed within budgetary constraints. Create agendas, identify speakers, track registration, coordinate with the events & State Engagement team, and serve as overall manager of assigned Hunt Institute programs and events. Lead program evaluation and post-program reviews to assess successes, challenges, and lessons learned. Project Management Manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet tight deadlines. Identify and implement improvements to strengthen The Hunt Institute’s support for state early learning education and policy. Ensure project schedules and timelines facilitate meaningful participation from elected officials. Provide grant deliverable details regarding impact for grant and funder applications and reports. Perform all related duties and responsibilities as assigned. Qualifications Commitment to the mission and vision of The Hunt Institute, alongside a passion for challenging entrenched systems of educational inequity towards the bettering of public education for all children. Awareness of key state and national education policy issues. Exceptional project management skills. A strong work ethic, with a results-oriented philosophy and personal qualities of trustworthiness, openness, accessibility, kindness, flexibility, and a sense of humor. Ability to handle multiple assignments and accomplish deadlines; ability to pay attention to accuracy and detail while thinking broadly. Bachelor’s degree is required. Minimum three years’ experience. Excellent interpersonal skills and flexible, responsive work style. Ability to travel (anticipated 10 – 15%). Ideal candidates will also demonstrate: Knowledge of state and national P-16 education policy. Resourcefulness and good judgment. Leadership by example. The value of diversity of thought, backgrounds, and perspectives. Integrity/ethics beyond reproach. Constant seeking to apply best practices. Exceptional attention to detail, strong project management, and the ability to handle multiple deadlines simultaneously. Willingness to travel and work outside regular business hours as needed for event schedules. Willingness to work collaboratively and consider new ideas. Commitment to The Hunt Institute’s mission, vision, financial growth, and success. Benefits and Compensation The Hunt Institute offers competitive compensation and an attractive benefits package, including employer paid health, dental and vision insurance, and a 401(k) plan with an employer matching contribution policy. We feel passionately about equal pay for equal work, and transparency in compensation is one vehicle to achieve that. The salary recruitment range for this position is $79,240- $87,164 Work Schedule This position is based out of our office at 5000 Centregreen Way, Suite 150, Cary, NC, 27513. This is a hybrid position requiring on-site presence at our office in Cary, NC, three days per week. The remaining two days may be completed remotely from your home office. Employees are expected on-site on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays to collaborate on team projects and attend strategic planning meetings. Occasional evenings and weekends may be required. Office hours: 8:30am-5:00pm Equal Employment Opportunity At The Hunt Institute, Equal Employment Opportunity is our commitment and goal. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status or any other protected status designated by federal, state or local law. Applicants are encouraged to confidentially self-identify when applying. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a reference check and background investigation. item.title: External Affairs Manager
item.description: External Affairs Manager Organization: Propelus® Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Propelus® simplifies workforce compliance management across healthcare. Our innovative technology and strategic partnerships empower millions of professionals, their employers, and regulators to work together, creating a connected and efficient healthcare ecosystem. As a trusted leader for over 20 years, Propelus has focused on bringing more good into the lives of the people and organizations serving healthcare. We deliver seamless compliance solutions to millions. We leverage market-leading technology and essential data to simplify complex operations, reduce risk, and champion a safer, healthier, and happier workforce. About the Role Propelus serves clinicians, licensing boards, and healthcare organizations that rely on accurate licensure and continuing education information. The rules behind that work keep changing across states, agencies, and professional boards. As External Affairs Manager, you’ll help Propelus stay ahead of those changes. You’ll track legislative and regulatory developments, manage relationships with key healthcare stakeholders, and keep the External Affairs function organized and running smoothly. What You’ll Do Policy & Regulatory Intelligence Track legislation, rulemaking, board actions, licensure compacts, and CE requirements across priority states and national bodies. Spot developments that affect Propelus, its customers, or its market, and share them with the right teams. Turn complex policy into clear summaries, briefings, and talking points. Keep legislative calendars, deadlines, and implementation dates current. Coordinate with contract lobbyists and manage their agreements, deliverables, and lobbying compliance filings. State Association Partnerships & Stakeholder Engagement Build relationships with state healthcare associations, workforce centers, educational institutions, and professional organizations. Coordinate Propelus’s participation in coalitions, task forces, conferences, and other forums. Keep relationship records up to date (contacts, notes, commitments) and make sure follow-ups happen. Prepare the VP for external meetings with research, briefing materials, and logistics. Operations Run the day-to-day rhythm of External Affairs: priorities, timelines, meetings, events, and deliverables. Build repeatable processes, templates, and systems (HubSpot, Quorum) that help the function grow. Bring gaps, risks, and decisions that need attention to the VP early. Support special projects, including RFPs, events, partner needs, and internal communications. Expected Travel: roughly 20% We’d Like You To Have: Experience: 5+ years in government relations, regulatory affairs, public policy, or association management, ideally in healthcare, professional licensure, or another highly regulated industry. Policy fluency: A strong grasp of state legislative processes, agency rulemaking, and licensing boards. You can read a bill or rule and explain why it matters. Relationships: A record of building productive relationships with associations, regulators, educators, and workforce organizations. Communication: Clear, concise writing and speaking for both internal and external audiences. Lobbying compliance: Familiarity with lobbying registration and disclosure requirements, and experience working with contract lobbyists. Organization: You can manage many bills, jurisdictions, and relationships at once without losing the big picture. Independence: Comfort working independently and knowing when to escalate. Builder mindset: You enjoy creating structure in a growing function. It Would Be Great If You Had: Experience with healthcare licensure, continuing education, nursing workforce policy, or professional regulation. Familiarity with FSMB, NCSBN, CLEAR, and interstate licensure compacts. If your experience is close but doesn’t fulfill all requirements, please apply. We’re building the best team in healthcare and are focused on hiring individuals with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences to support us in doing good, what’s human, and making a difference. Benefits and Perks for Propelus Employees US Employees: Health Insurance: We cover up to 100% of the premium for employee medical insurance. Plans for spouses and children are made affordable through Propelus’ generous contribution Employees can choose from HSA, FSA, and traditional insurance options for medical, dental, and vision coverage for themselves and dependents. Dental and Vision plans, both including an option with 100% of the premium covered for employees Generous PTO: Accrual: (full-time US): 0–4 yrs 20 days | 5–9 yrs 25 days. | 10+ yrs 30 days per year (accrues quarterly: Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1; and is available immediately). US-based teams observe 14 paid holidays each year Floating Holiday: One floating holiday is yours to request on any day of your choice. This is separate from your PTO. Birthday Holiday: Your birthday deserves celebrating! You get 1 paid day off during your birth month, separate from your PTO. Volunteer Time Off: 16 hours available to you, that allow you to make an impact on causes that are meaningful to you. Additional leave options: to support you in embracing life centricity State & local leave laws Where state or local leave laws provide additional protections, Propelus will comply with whichever regulation is more favorable to the employee. 401K with company matching, as well as financial planning education and resources. Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA): We support personal well-being by offering an annual lifestyle spending account that you can use for what matters most to you—whether it’s a gym membership, a meditation app, WFH equipment, or fresh produce delivered to your door. Think of it as a bonus for the expenses and experiences you value most. Employee Assistance Programs: provides 24/7/365 support by phone and online — family clinical counseling, legal & financial services, plus child and elder care referrals. Carrot Fertility & Hormonal Support: Inclusive hormonal health, fertility, and family-building benefits with funds toward eligible care. Beyond Med: A licensed discount plan organization (DPO) giving you access to elective care like acupuncture, dermatology, fertility, GLP-1, and more — at discounted rates. Spot Pet Insurance: A financial safety net for your furry family. Get reimbursed for emergencies, lab fees, behavior, x-rays, surgeries, cancer, and more. LATAM (Costa Rica and Colombia) Employees: Your health is our top priority! We cover 100% of employee health insurance premiums. Our plans include national and international coverage, so you’re protected no matter where you are. Propelus Flex Club: Our flexible benefits platform gives you monthly points to redeem on what you need most. Plus, you’ll get access to exclusive discounts just for being part of our team. (Details are country specific) Generous PTO: National Holidays (Colombia): 18 days National Holidays (Costa Rica): 12 days Birthday Holiday: Your birthday deserves celebrating! You get 1 paid day off during your birth month, separate from your PTO. Volunteer Time Off: 16 hours available to you, that allow you to make an impact on causes that are meaningful to you. We’ve got you covered with a life insurance policy, paid 100% by the company. You can also add your beneficiaries at an exclusive, discounted rate. Carrot Fertility & Hormonal Support: Inclusive hormonal health, fertility, and family-building benefits with funds toward eligible care. Benefits and Perks for ALL Propelus employees include but are not limited to: A remote first company, global and distributed, with two office locations for those nearby who want a change of scenery. Employees celebrating their 10 and 20 year work anniversary are eligible to take a trip sponsored by Propelus within one year of their 10th and 20th anniversary date. Awarded one of BuiltIn’s 2025 Best Places to Work and honored as a Silver Stevie® Award Winner in the 2025 Stevie Awards For Great Employers. Professional development allowance to help you grow in the ways that mean the most to you. Check us out for yourself at our careers page or our Propelus culture Instagram accounts. Typical Interview Process: Interview #1: Brief intro screen with our People Ops team Interview #2: Introduction with the Hiring Manager Interview #3: Team Panel Interview #4: Alignment interview with Senior Leadership If you don’t move forward to the next round, we’ll make sure you know as soon as possible. Tips for applicants: Focus on your application. At Propelus, everyone has an equal opportunity based on their merit. Reaching out to the team or providing referrals will not change your chances. We work remotely and communicate asynchronously, so writing is a key skill at Propelus. Please answer the application questions with your own thoughtful responses. Replies like “See resume” or N/A won’t lead to an interview. Have some fun with it, we actually read these! We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Propelus. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Candidates from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Full-time positions are scheduled to work 40 hours per week, M-F unless required otherwise by projects. Part-time positions are scheduled to work a maximum of 30 hours per week. Equipment, benefits, and perks are not provided to part-time or temporary employees. item.description: Director of External Relations Organization: Ohio Chamber of Commerce Location: Columbus, OH Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Experience: 5+ years of experience FLSA: Exempt Reports To: Senior Vice President, External Relations Status: Full Time (40+ hours) Salary Range: Base + Generous Commission Location: Downtown, Columbus Responsibilities Include: Primarily responsible for recruiting new members to the Ohio Chamber of Commerce. Researching & qualifying potential leads through the lens of the Ohio Chamber of Commerce. Communicating public policy priorities to prospects. Maintaining a robust prospect list. Selling sponsorships to member companies for Ohio Chamber events. Engaging current members for increased dues each quarter. item.title: Director, State and Local Government Relations (Southern California)
item.description: Director, State and Local Government Relations (Southern California) Organization: Anduril Industries Location: Costa Mesa, CA Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE TEAM The Anduril Government Relations (GR) team is responsible for developing and implementing Anduril’s government affairs strategy with the federal legislative and executive branches as well as state and local government officials. ABOUT THE JOB We are looking for a Southern California based Director, State and Local Government Relations to join our rapidly growing team. In this role, you will be responsible for shaping and implementing GR strategy at the state and local level in partnership with Anduril government relations and key functional and business lines. In this role, you will set and lead engagement strategy at the state and local level in coordination with Anduril’s state and local and federal team, including designing, planning, and executing state and local strategies in support of Anduril priorities in partnership with state and local government officials, the federal government relations team and key stakeholders. You will also represent the company before a range of audiences to include elected and appointed state and local government officials and their staff, relevant business and industry groups, state and local stakeholders, and other audiences. In this role, you must have extensive knowledge and experience with the legislative, economic development, and policy making processes as well as an understanding of permitting and building process at the California state legislative and executive branch as well as the county and local levels, and an understanding of how these processes impact Anduril and an ability to proactively shape Anduril’s state and local priorities in California. While this position is Southern California based with a focus on California state and local, you will also be expected to engage with additional state and local governments in support of Anduril locations across the United States to include opportunities to expand into new locations and new states in partnership with Anduril’s federal, state, and local government relations team. You should be a strategic self-starter with strong communication skills, both verbally and in writing, and work well as part of a team. If you are someone who takes initiative and finds innovative solutions to drive forward priorities as part of a dynamic, fast paced team-oriented environment, this job might be for you. WHAT YOU’LL DO Be a proactive strategic agent on behalf of the company priorities and help to define the strategic goals and priorities and to develop and execute a strategic engagement plan, with a focus on informing state and local policy makers and stakeholders with the objective of best advancing the near and long-term interests of the company Support the creation and execution of specific government relations strategies to enhance the strategic positioning in the industry and increase the understanding of the company and its business objectives at the state and local level Lead company-wide effort to enact strategic priorities at the state and local level Work with executives, communications, legal, corporate development, divisions, events, external consultants, and other teams to identify business and policy opportunities and advise them on legislative and policy objects to achieve company-wide goals at the state and local level In partnership with functional and business lines, support participation at relevant local and state related industry trade groups, including development of strategies to leverage trade group memberships to advance policy initiatives and goals. Design and lead engagement strategy with state and local government officials and stakeholders in support of Anduril priorities Coordinate and oversee government relations related visits and events at Anduril facilities Draft and manage the company’s engagement process at the state and local level, to include but not limited to overseeing the drafting and submission of white papers, power points, testimony and hearing prep, and other deliverables as required Monitor, analyze, and engage the annual policymaking process in relevant states to support the company’s priorities Collaborating internally and externally on Anduril priorities, messaging and general outreach to ensure coordination and integration across the business development teams, independent consultants and senior leadership at the company as it relates to state and local priorities REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelors degree Salary and position will be commensurate with experience Minimum 8 years experience in the government relations, and/or California state executive or legislative arena. Demonstrated success in planning and implementing strategies to promote government relations priorities and influence change at the state and local level. Lobby registration in the State of California, local jurisdictions, and other states as required. Registration at the federal level may be needed as well. Extensive knowledge of California state and local legislative and executive process, as well as an understanding of state and local stakeholders in California and these processes impacting the company’s business development agenda Ability to build coalitions and to develop and maintain relationships with key state and local officials and industry and trade associations Excellent verbal and written communication skills Proven ability to work independently and as part of a team to pursue short and long-term goals Ability to work and be an integral part of an action-oriented, decision-making working environment Willingness to travel at the state and national level approximately 30% or greater. Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance US Salary Range $175,000 – $225,000 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril’s total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We’ve observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates. Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency’s authenticity by reaching out to [email protected] . Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender’s email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to [email protected] . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts. Data Privacy To view Anduril’s candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/. By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. item.title: Director, Government Relations
item.description: Director, Government Relations Organization: Anduril Industries Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE TEAM The Anduril Government Relations (GR) team is responsible for developing and implementing Anduril’s government affairs strategy with the federal legislative and executive branches as well as state and local government officials. ABOUT THE JOB Anduril is seeking talented Government Relations professionals to join the team in Washington, DC. We are actively hiring for multiple roles across several key business lines, each offering unique technology focus areas, as well as Government Relations professionals with significant national security expertise in the legislative or executive branch with significant experience in budget, authorization, appropriations, and broader national security policy making. Anduril Government Relations directly supports Anduril’s divisions and associated business lines. This role will be aligned across capability portfolios based on expertise and experience as well as the demands of existing and emerging business lines and capabilities. Specific focus areas include, but are not limited to the below: Maritime: Anduril’s growing maritime business line is building the next generation of autonomous maritime capability. In addition, Anduril recently announced Arsenal-2, a new, software-defined shipyard in Maryland, which will build complex components and large scale assemblies as a supplier in the submarine industrial base. Missiles and Advanced Effects: Anduril’s growing advanced weapons and autonomous effects portfolio. Anduril’s Advanced Effects business line develops and manufactures autonomous air vehicles, cruise missiles, interceptor missiles, loitering munitions, and one-way effectors designed to give the U.S. military affordable, high-volume strike options to resolve the critical munitions gap. Space: Anduril’s growing space business line is expanding our AI-powered capabilities, enhancing space domain awareness, space control, and command and control for national security applications. We’re developing fully integrated hardware and software systems to address growing threats in space to maintain a decisive advantage in this contested warfighting domain. Unmanned and Counter Unmanned Systems: Anduril builds a comprehensive, AI-driven suite of Counter-UAS (C-UAS) solutions designed to detect, track, identify, and defeat unmanned aerial threats. In addition, Anduril builds unmanned aerial systems (UAS) ranging from small Group One sized quadcopters to larger UAS systems. Command and Control and Autonomous Systems: Anduril’s Lattice is the software platform that powers the capabilities of its software-defined weapons, and easily integrates with third-party and government-owned capabilities to create a comprehensive, extensible network of sensors and effectors. As a Member of the Government Relations team, you will develop engagement strategies with Members of Congress and their staff, Committee Staff, Congressional Leadership teams, Caucuses and other bodies, as well as the executive branch in partnership with the Business Lines. You will also represent the company before a range of audiences to include Members of Congress and their staff, Committee Staff, executive branch officials, industry groups, and others as appropriate. You must have significant knowledge and experience of the national security related US federal budget/appropriations and policymaking processes and how these processes impact and support the company’s business development agenda. You should be a self-starter with strong verbal and written communication skills, and work well as part of a team. If you take initiative and find innovative solutions to drive forward priorities in a dynamic, fast paced team-oriented environment, this might be the job for you. WHAT YOU’LL DO As a key Member of the Government Relations team, roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Support the development and execution of near term and long term government relations strategies to build the company’s reputation, enhance the strategic positioning in the industry, and increase the understanding of the company and its business objectives in Washington, DC. Develop and implement GR strategy across business lines and fiscal years and engage on company-wide efforts to enact strategic national security policy and funding priorities through the congressional and executive branch processes. Support the planning and execution of appropriations and authorization strategies leading to direct revenue capture for multiple business lines, to include the engagement strategy with Members of Congress and their staff, Congressional Leadership teams, Caucuses and other bodies to increase support for budgetary and policy requests that have direct and material impact on Anduril revenue targets. Coordinate and oversee visits by congressional Members and staff to Anduril facilities in the United States and, as required, internationally. Support the company’s congressional engagement process to include the drafting and submission of policy and funding requests and supporting documentation, white papers, power points, congressional testimony and hearing prep, and other required deliverables. Monitor, analyze, and engage the annual congressional policymaking process to support the company’s priorities with a particular focus on annual appropriations, and defense and homeland security policy. Collaborate internally and externally on Anduril priorities, messaging and general outreach to ensure coordination and integration across the business development teams, independent consultants and senior leadership at the company. Support the company’s Political Action Committee priorities. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS At least 10+ years of experience in the national security, government relations, and/or federal executive or legislative arena is recommended. Title and Salary will be commensurate with experience. Has considerable defense/national security experience on Capitol Hill or government relations related positions either for the Executive Branch or in a similar defense industry position. Demonstrated success in planning and implementing strategies to promote government relations priorities and influence change in the legislative policy and budget process. Extensive knowledge and understanding of US federal appropriations and policy making processes, including executive agencies, the White House, Senate and House and an understanding of how these processes impact the company’s business development agenda. Experience with defense policy and budget issues and knowledge of the defense and national security sector and key stakeholders. Ability to build coalitions and to develop and maintain relationships with key Congressional and executive branch officials and industry and trade associations. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Proven ability to work independently to pursue short and long-term goals. The ability to work and be an integral part of an action-oriented, decision-making working environment. Bachelors degree required. Graduate degrees welcome but not required. Ability to travel approximately 25% or greater. Must be available to work on-site in our DC Office Position will require individual lobbyist registration under the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995. Currently possesses or is eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance US Salary Range $191,000 – $253,000 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril’s total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We’ve observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Currently possesses or is eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance US Salary Range $146,000 – $194,000 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril’s total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We’ve observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates. Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @

item.title: Fixed Income Compliance Officer, Vice President – Securitized Products and Rates
item.description: Fixed Income Compliance Officer, Vice President – Securitized Products and Rates Organization: Morgan Stanley Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 10/26/2026 We are seeking someone to join Global Compliance as a Vice President who will provide advisory compliance support for the Securitized Products Sales & Trading, Origination and Lending and the Rates Sales & Trading businesses. Candidate will be expected to provide advice on FINRA, CFTC, Federal Reserve, OCC and SEC rules, regulations and interpretive guidance, as well as applicable internal policies and procedures Department Overview The Global Compliance Department manages a Firmwide Compliance Risk Management program, including Compliance risks that transcend business lines, legal entities and jurisdictions of operation. Fixed Income Compliance The Fixed Income Division (“FID”) Compliance Group provides a comprehensive advisory and control service to FID to monitor business activities for adherence to both Firm and regulatory requirements. FID is divided into three primary business areas: 1) Macro (including Interest Rates and FX); 2) Credit Complex (including Credit Corporates, Securitized Products and Municipal Securities); and 3) Commodities. The FID Compliance Group provides advisory support to each business unit within FID. Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world. What you’ll do in the role: Provide Compliance support for the Securitized Products Sales & Trading, Origination and Lending desks and the Rates Sales & Trading desks, as well as related support functions Demonstrate ability to effectively review and analyze complex situations and apply judgment to resolve issues in a timely manner with minimal supervision. Proficient in time management and able to initiate and manage projects. Communicate with business management, risk management, Sales & Trading, Origination and Lending desk personnel regularly and address issues on a real-time basis Actively monitor regulatory developments and trends, participate in industry forums to address new rule proposals, and take appropriate action to ensure the business unit understands and complies with new or amended regulations, including updates to desk policies and procedures and training Assist other control functions in the maintenance of written supervisory procedures Interact with operations and technology support to ensure trading technology and trading practices remain compliant with Firm policies and industry regulation Assist in regulatory reviews, audits, and other examinations Assist in developing policies, procedures, and training Candidate should be proficient in time management and able to initiate and manage projects. What you’ll bring to the role: Minimum 7-10 years of fixed income compliance or legal experience In-depth understanding of Securitized Products suite including agency and non-agency securities (ABS, RMBS, CMBS, CLO, CMO), swaps and security-based swaps, residential mortgage loan trading and securitization, commercial mortgage origination and securitization and consumer loans In-depth understanding of Rates Products suite including Treasury market practices, Treasury primary dealer auction activities, interest rate swaps and futures Detailed knowledge of broker-dealer regulatory compliance including FINRA, CFTC and SEC regulations Excellent communication skills, with the confidence, credibility, and ability to work effectively within the organization, and communicate and interact with both junior and senior business personnel Strong organization skills with the ability to multitask and prioritize J.D. (optional), Bachelor’s Degree required WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY: At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values – putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back – aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what’s best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work. To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices​ into your browser. Expected base pay rates for the role will be between 120000 and 205000 per year at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs. Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents. Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences. item.title: (Sr) Account Director – Public Affairs
item.description: (Sr) Account Director – Public Affairs Organization: Issues Management Group (IMG) Location: Boston, MA Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Issues Management Group (IMG), one of Boston’s top strategic communication and public affairs firms, is looking for an Account Director or Senior Account Director to join the firm’s Public Affairs team. Serving as a key member of our Public Affairs team, a(n) Account Director/Senior Account Director will work closely with our lobbyists to advocate for legislation, educate policymakers, track legislative proposals for clients, and develop strategies to influence policy outcomes. IMG has a hybrid work model. This role is based in our downtown Boston office with eligibility to work remotely two days each week. The salary range for this role is $80,000 to $100,000. The actual salary and title offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position and years of relevant experience. RESPONSIBILITIES Day-to-day interaction with clients including responding to inquiries as appropriate Conduct legislative monitoring and tracking Draft memos, policy briefings, blogs, client updates, and advocacy materials Serve as a central person on the team to ensure that account tasks are moving forward to support client goals Help lead client calls and presentations Generate creative ideas to advance client priorities Translate policy into practical impact Draft and/or edit testimony on legislation of interest to our clients Monitor hearings and sessions to provide real-time takeaways Schedule and staff legislative meetings Prepare briefings for clients in advance of meetings Conduct research memos on topics of interest to the MA policy landscape Participate in the writing of legislative strategy plans and messaging for clients Articulate what the various steps are in the Massachusetts legislative and budget processes, answering questions and connecting strategies to how the process works Build relationships with elected officials and staff Attend fundraisers and networking events outside normal work hours Communicate frequently with the senior staff on each account to keep them appraised of account activity REQUIREMENTS/QUALIFICATIONS 3-7 years of public affairs, advocacy, or State House experience required; MA State House experience strongly preferred. Client servicing work experience is a plus Excellent writing and editing skills Detail-oriented collaborator with experience managing projects and deadlines effectively General knowledge of the Massachusetts legislative process Experience working with local and state officials Strong organizational, time management, and problem-solving skills; ability to communicate effectively while working remotely and in-person Ability to execute multiple tasks with minimal supervision while maintaining confidentiality Strong work ethic, enthusiastic attitude, and proactive nature Excellent interpersonal skills with a collaborative, team-oriented mindset Comfortability with speaking and presenting to clients Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook) We hire candidates who are smart, determined, and bring something new to the table. If you excel at what you do, we want to talk with you. As an equal opportunity employer, Issues Management Group will not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other facet of your identity. If you are looking for a company with an intellectually stimulating, collaborative, and respectful culture, new challenges and growth opportunities, and a range of industries to dive into, Issues Management Group may be the place for you. Our generous compensation and benefits program includes great health and dental plans, a 401(k) plan, profit sharing, a new business success program, early release Fridays, and your birthday off. We have a terrific professional development program as well. To learn more visit issuesgroup.com. To apply, please submit your resume to [email protected] . ABOUT ISSUES MANAGEMENT GROUP Issues Management Group (IMG) is a strategic advisory firm at the intersection of communications, public affairs, and digital transformation. We empower organizations to navigate complexity, mitigate risk, and realize their business ambitions in today’s rapidly evolving environment. Headquartered in Boston with an office in New York City, our team brings together senior counsel, sector expertise, and data-driven insight to help clients not only respond to critical moments—but proactively shape what’s next. We serve as trusted partners to organizations across sectors, including healthcare, real estate, public service, corporate and professional services, education, energy, and life sciences, delivering integrated solutions that drive measurable business outcomes. item.title: Senior Manager, Government Relations
item.description: Senior Manager, Government Relations Organization: ASME Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Role Summary ASME is seeking a Senior Manager, Government Relations to join our Government Relations group. This role advances ASME’s public policy priorities through direct advocacy with Congress and the Executive branch, with a focus on copyright and intellectual property, incorporation by reference of standards, clean energy, manufacturing, and related mechanical engineering issues. The Senior Manager strengthens relationships across government, industry, and the private sector, while advising ASME teams on legislative and executive policy developments that may affect the enterprise. The role has significant external visibility and requires sound judgment when handling sensitive matters that may affect ASME’s reputation and credibility. Key Responsibilities Advocate for ASME priorities in Congress and the Executive branch, including copyright and intellectual property, incorporation by reference of standards, clean energy, manufacturing, and related mechanical engineering issues. Represent ASME in industry and advocacy coalitions related to ASME’s public policy interests. Build and maintain relationships with government institutions and officials, Members of Congress, executive agencies, and industry counterpart organizations. Analyze proposed legislative and regulatory actions and advise ASME leadership and internal and external working groups on potential impacts. Track legislative and regulatory developments and prepare summaries, briefing materials, talking points, position statements, and correspondence for ASME leadership and representatives. Coordinate with ASME standards and certification teams on incorporation-by-reference matters and provide policy guidance to other ASME business units. Develop strategies and lead execution of Government Relations initiatives, including strategic advocacy efforts, member fly-in events, and coalition participation. Contribute to the ASME Policy Impact newsletter, social media, and related communications. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in political science, communications, a technical field, or a similar field, or additional equivalent work experience. Minimum of six years of public policy experience on Capitol Hill or in the Executive branch, and/or government affairs experience within industry or a trade association. Demonstrated experience developing and effectively advocating policy positions to Congress and the Executive branch. Strong knowledge of government regulatory processes and legislative procedures, with established relationships across congressional offices. Contacts and familiarity with relevant House and Senate Committees and Executive agencies that play a role in ASME operations. Experience with program planning and management, along with the business acumen to understand how government affairs and ASME business units interconnect. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure in a highly fluid environment. Demonstrated collaboration, teamwork, openness to diverse opinions, enterprise perspective, ownership, and accountability. Work Arrangement This role is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement and will be based in ASME’s Washington, D.C. office, subject to ASME’s hybrid-work policies and business requirements. Compensation and Benefits The DC Metro annual base salary range for this position is $125,000–$135,000 per year. The actual compensation offered will be determined based on factors including qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, and internal equity. This position may also be eligible for consideration for a discretionary bonus, subject to ASME’s applicable policies and eligibility requirements. Additionally, ASME offers eligible employees a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage; health savings and flexible spending account options; life and disability insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; paid vacation and safe and sick leave; paid holidays; parental leave; employee assistance and wellness programs; and professional-development opportunities. Eligibility and benefit levels vary based on employment status and the terms of the applicable plans. For additional information, please visit ASME’s Benefits page. About ASME ASME helps the global engineering community develop solutions to real-world challenges. Founded in 1880 as The American Society of Mechanical Engineers, ASME is a nonprofit professional organization that enables collaboration, knowledge sharing, and skill development across all engineering disciplines, while promoting the vital role of the engineer in society. ASME codes and standards, publications, conferences, continuing education, and professional development programs provide a foundation for advancing technical knowledge and a safer world. From college students and early-career engineers to project managers, corporate executives, researchers, and academic leaders, ASME’s members are as diverse as the engineering community itself. ASME is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. At ASME, we nurture an inclusive environment, and we encourage, support, and celebrate diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, gender identity & expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, citizenship status, disability, or protected veteran, military status, or any other basis protected by law. Our Equal Employment Opportunity policy pertains to every aspect of an individual’s relationship with the organization, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, compensation, benefits, training and development, promotion, programs, and all other terms and conditions of employment. Only those candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Staff Attorney (UCIP Team)
item.description: Staff Attorney (UCIP Team) Organization: Unrepresented Condemned Inmate Project (UCIP) Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 10/26/2026 The Unrepresented Condemned Inmate Project (UCIP) Staff Attorney will oversee a caseload of unrepresented incarcerated capitally sentenced people and provide vigorous advocacy on their behalf. CAP is a nonprofit legal resource center funded by the Judicial Council of California to implement the constitutional right to counsel for indigent death row inmates challenging their convictions and sentences on direct appeal and through habeas corpus proceedings. Role and Responsibilities The UCIP Staff Attorney will be responsible for overseeing a caseload of unrepresented incarcerated capitally sentenced people whose cases require ongoing record collection work, communications with clients (and client advocacy in certain instances), and vigilant attention to applicable changes in the law. Most clients will be without appellate or habeas counsel; some may have appellate counsel; and clemency clients may be included as office priorities require. The UCIP attorney must have superior communication skills to work with a range of people – including clients, client family members, records clerks, court clerks, correctional facility personnel, colleagues, trial counsel, and both in-house and sister agency legal experts who may be called upon to advise on the complex issues arising in capital cases in light of recent legislation. Specific duties include: For new clients, conducting intake and initial record collection, working with trial counsel, collecting the trial file, and drafting Case Information Reports. For all clients, including Morgan petitioners, becoming familiar with the facts of each case and any briefing; evaluating cases for Racial Justice Act review and the applicability of second look sentencing; and reviewing transcripts or supervising law student interns who do so. Maintaining regular, ongoing contact with clients, client families, and other witnesses; gathering records and life history documents; and locating witnesses and collecting, or supervising the collection of, their records. Assisting incarcerated clients with administrative appeals and other prison issues as needed. Training and supervising law and paralegal students to meet RJA and second look legislation needs, record collection and life history investigation goals, and UCIP publications goals. Serving as the UCIP’s and the office’s research attorney on legal questions concerning document gathering and records collection. As part of this responsibility, the UCIP attorney develops expertise in the law governing public and non-public information (e.g., CPRA, FOIA, and HIPAA). Preparing for and participating in CAP’s New Case Trainings for clients on the caseload as counsel is appointed. Conducting interdisciplinary research and continuing education (historical, cultural, psychological, medical, and legal) through reading and attending training events. Assisting with urgent, time-sensitive projects that arise for the UCIP or the CAP office. The UCIP attorney should be able and willing to travel to correctional facilities around the state to meet with clients. Minimum Qualifications Admission to the California Bar. Proven litigation skills, with at least two years of law practice and substantial experience in capital trial, appellate, and/or habeas corpus representation preferred. Superior legal analysis and writing skills. Understanding of death penalty jurisprudence and demonstrated commitment to vigorous advocacy on behalf of indigent defendants. Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), WordPerfect, and legal research databases (e.g., Westlaw, Lexis). Demonstrated ability to manage multiple litigation tasks and perform essential duties in the face of time constraints and interruptions. Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including the ability to develop and maintain good working relationships with outside counsel, clients, clients’ families, witnesses, expert consultants, court personnel, prison personnel, and CAP colleagues – in person, by email, and by telephone. Proven organizational and project management skills, including planning, negotiating, effective problem-solving, and conflict resolution. Ability to travel to correctional facilities statewide and to obtain clearance to visit a prison. Working Conditions CAP’s office is in downtown San Francisco, close to public transportation. The position requires some time in the office, and a hybrid schedule is available. Salary Range Staff Attorney: $90,000 – $105,000, depending on experience To Apply Applications must be received by October 31, 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and early submission is strongly encouraged. Send us a cover letter, resume, writing sample, and three references. General correspondence about this position may be addressed to the Attorney Selection Committee at: [email protected] . CAP is committed to cultivating an environment that embraces and promotes diversity. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or age, are encouraged to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! This role supports AZA’s communication strategy through writing, editing and distributing content for communications and media relations purposes. This role contributes to the awareness of AZA through media outreach, collaboration with member facilities and storytelling. This position ensures content aligns with organizational priorities, editorial standards and accessibility practices. This position works closely with members of all departments within AZA. item.title: Policy Principal – DMEE
item.description: Policy Principal – DMEE Organization: Advanced Energy United (AEU) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/26/2026 About Advanced Energy United Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country. We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy. If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team. We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously. Position Description Advanced Energy United (United) is currently seeking a Policy Principal to help shape political strategy on our Decisionmaker Education and Engagement team (DMEE). The DMEE team builds relationships with governors, state regulators, state energy officials, and policymakers to equip them with the information and resources to understand advanced energy products, services, and business models – as well as the policy and political solutions we need to unleash them. Through political events, conferences, and business roundtables, United engages key decision-makers around the benefits that advanced energy technologies and services can provide to their constituents and helps to solve the challenges in obtaining these benefits. Reporting directly to the Policy Senior Director, the Policy Principal will cultivate relationships and inform strategies to help achieve the DMEE team’s goals. The ideal candidate is energized by thinking about how political dynamics and relationships affect energy policy decisions. Successful applicants must have experience related to political and/or advocacy campaigns, bolstered by exceptional project management, relationship building, and communication skills. While you do not need to be a state energy policy expert to be considered for this role, strong candidates will possess an interest in energy policy issues and be comfortable with communicating with decision-makers regarding United’s state policy priorities. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, proactive, comfortable with ambiguity, and flexible. Candidates will need to travel to meet with key stakeholders approximately 1-2 times per quarter. Responsibilities Own the political strategy for building relationships with key decision-makers in a portfolio of Midwest states Develop effective communication strategies that incorporate state-specific energy outlooks and political landscapes and deploy those strategies to represent United in front of state decision-makers Build, maintain, and own relationships with key stakeholders, including policymakers, advocacy groups, coalitions, industry experts, and regulators Use project management tools and systems effectively to deliver success on both short and long-term goals. Maintain and organize information to contribute to program knowledge management and retention Communicate campaign progress, outcomes, and key metrics for internal and external stakeholders, including United’s member companies Contribute to strategy and tactic ideation and development to continuously improve our program efficacy Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. 3-6 years of professional experience, with ideally 2 or more years in roles that engage with elected officials. A commitment to and track record of leading work that aligns with United’s Core Values. Experience working on advocacy or policy affecting the advanced energy industry is a plus. A knack for assessing your audience and tailoring your engagement and communication strategies accordingly. Successful applicants must demonstrate the ability to build rapport with key stakeholders quickly. Aptitude for conveying the essential components of technical subject matters effectively to decision-makers. Track record of successfully supporting multi-stakeholder programs or campaigns. Independent self-starter with an entrepreneurial spirit; candidates must be very comfortable working with colleagues in a remote environment, owning new projects, managing their own calendar, and delivering on high expectations. Strong interpersonal skills required; candidates must be able to enthusiastically develop and maintain productive relationships with key stakeholders, including policymakers, advocacy groups, industry experts, and regulators. Existing relationships or background working in the Midwest is a plus, particularly in Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, or Wisconsin. Experience managing confidential information and intelligence. Comfort working amidst ambiguity and quickly changing political dynamics Willingness to travel as needed (approximately 1-2 times per quarter). item.title: Policy Principal – Enabling Building Electrification & Affordability
item.description: Policy Principal – Enabling Building Electrification & Affordability Organization: Advanced Energy United (AEU) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/26/2026 About Advanced Energy United Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country. We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy. If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team. We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously. Position Description Advanced Energy United is currently seeking a well-rounded early-career candidate with interest and/or experience in policy and political advocacy for a position focused on gas transition, building electrification, and electric affordability issues. This Principal will work collaboratively to support existing state and regional teams to accelerate electrification of the building stock in legislative, administrative, regulatory, and political venues in states across the country. In the near term, this work will focus on long-term gas infrastructure planning and non-pipeline alternatives, clean heat and electrification programs, electric rate design, and electric ratemaking. Reporting to our Managing Director of Programs and Strategy, this Principal will join a team of subject matter experts to provide insight, strategy, and experience to our on-the-ground policy teams that are engaged on state legislation, in public utility commission dockets, and with governors. The transition to clean buildings will require use of all of the tools in the toolbox, including reforming utility business models, closing the “spark gap,” and reimagining utility resource and infrastructure planning. The work includes educating decisionmakers on financial and economic risks of the status quo, storytelling around the vision of clean, affordable, and resilient homes for all, coalition building, and developing advocacy strategies on some of the most complex issues in utility regulation of our day. The ideal candidate will have 4-6 years of relevant experience in state energy legislation or regulation and some exposure to, or experience with, utility planning and ratemaking issues. They will have a good understanding of the utility business model and public utility commission proceedings. They should be a creative, flexible, and opportunistic self-starter with strong organization and prioritization skills, be able to support day-to-day execution of strategic plans, and have an appetite to get into the weeds while still seeing the bigger picture. Excellent writing and communications skills are a must. Candidates must be able to travel to meet with members, stakeholders, and decisionmakers. Responsibilities Work with United’s state, regional, and federal teams to execute on short- and long-term policy goals in key states across legislative, regulatory, and administrative venues; Draft materials needed for education and advocacy efforts, including regulatory comments, legislative testimony, presentations, fact sheets, and other written and visual materials, and deliver verbal presentations as requested. Develop and maintain excellent working relationships with Advanced Energy United staff, member companies, allies, as well as key legislative, regulatory, and administrative staff. Work with Advanced Energy United’s communications team to identify opportunities to seek earned media coverage, including op-eds, editorial board meetings, etc., in key media outlets. Coordinate efforts with coalition allies in support of aligned goals; represent United and its members on coalition calls. Help support and organize education sessions, coalition meetings, decisionmaker meetings and stakeholder outreach. Travel on an as needed basis (up to 25%) to targeted states for staff trainings, advocacy days, meetings with key allies and stakeholders, communications outreach, and industry events. This includes representing United on panels, in meetings, and with media. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; 4 to 6 years of professional experience, with at least two focused in clean energy and utility policy; A baseline understanding of utility regulation and state energy decision-making environments; An ability to think strategically and politically, even in technical venues; Experience participating in coalitions and engaging with state legislative or regulatory processes; Entrepreneurial approach, flexible attitude, and ability to operate in a remote environment; Ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment; Excellent communications skills, both written and verbal, including an ability to digest highly technical information and translate it for audiences of different backgrounds; Intellectual curiosity, inquisitive nature, and excellent listening and problem-solving skills; Performance-oriented individual with a strong work ethic, demonstrated initiative and commitment to achieving goals; Strong interpersonal skills required. Physical Requirements The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee is required to sit for long periods of time; reach with hands and arms; may need to balance, stoop, kneel or crouch, walk up and down stairs.
