Position Description Advanced Energy United is currently seeking a highly energetic, smart, self-starting Senior Policy Principal with a background in legislative work and/or issue advocacy to lead United’s state-level legislative and political engagement in Massachusetts, Connecticut and Rhode Island. The Senior Principal will be responsible for building and maintaining relationships with legislative and administrative decision-makers, managing and executing on United’s policy advocacy strategy, and working collaboratively with other United team members to win policy outcomes that accelerate the energy transition and expand markets for the advanced energy industry. New England states have passed some of the nation’s most ambitious clean energy goals and are home to tremendous clean energy resources, but there is much work to be done to make those clean energy goals a reality. Our current policy priorities include advancing transmission solutions needed to support deployment of large-scale clean energy resources; ensuring our electric grid is strengthened to support electric vehicles and building electrification; and maximizing the use of distributed energy resources. Key Skills for Success A Mind for Policy: Market opportunities for the advanced energy industry are driven by policy. The ideal candidate will have a working knowledge of legislative and regulatory processes, and experience with energy policy specifically is a plus. Small “p” Political Awareness: Recognizing opportunity, understanding power dynamics and building coalitions to seize policy opportunities are keys to success for winning victories on our issues. The ideal candidate doesn’t need to have a background in politics but does need to be familiar with political processes and be excited about engaging in the political side of policy-making. Project Management Skills & A Drive to Get Things Done: The ideal candidate will be able to coordinate and drive team efforts from start to finish, keeping organized and navigating relationships with partners in multiple arenas. Responsibilities Lead Advanced Energy United’s work in Massachusetts, Connecticut and Rhode Island, working collaboratively with United policy team members on developing and implementing strategies to accelerate the transition to 100% clean energy and electrified transportation, and meet short- and long-term policy objectives as part of United’s policy portfolio. These could be legislative, administrative, or regulatory, or a mix of all three. Work with Advanced Energy United member companies to develop policy positions and reach consensus on policy positions on key issues. Manage lobbyist relationships on the ground and their engagement in legislative strategy and execution. Organize member engagement opportunities through direct decision-maker engagement including lobby days, legislator and candidate education, earned media, and participation in legislative, regulatory, and administrative processes, as needed. Develop and maintain excellent working relationships with coalition partners, allies, and key legislative and administrative staff. Engage in coordination and advocacy efforts with coalition allies in support of clean energy goals. Create reports, presentations, fact sheets, and other written and visual materials needed for education and advocacy efforts and deliver verbal presentations as necessary. Work with our communications team to identify opportunities for Advanced Energy United to seek earned media coverage. Draft press statements, do media interviews, write blog posts, participate in webinars, and create opportunities to showcase advanced energy. Travel on an as needed basis (up to 20%) within Massachusetts, Connecticut and Rhode Island and occasionally elsewhere, for advocacy days, meetings with key allies and stakeholders, communications outreach, and other efforts on behalf of Advanced Energy United. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree (Economics, Political Science, Public Policy, Engineering, or Communications focus preferred) or applicable comparable experience; Master’s degree is a plus. Minimum of five years of professional experience in legislative policy development, campaign work, or organizing in the energy sector; working with business leaders is a plus. A strong preference will be given to candidates with relevant experience in New York. Interest in energy and transportation issues and an understanding of the importance of policy advocacy to advance an organizational agenda. Entrepreneurial approach, flexible attitude, and ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Experience in professional settings leading team efforts toward an agreed upon goal, and being responsible for delivering quality finished products. item.title: Senior Principal -Western Markets and Regulatory Policy
item.description: Senior Principal -Western Markets and Regulatory Policy Organization: Advanced Energy United (AEU) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/26/2026 About Advanced Energy United Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country. We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy. If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team. We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously. Position Description The Western United States is in the midst of the most significant wholesale electricity market transformation in a generation. CAISO’s markets are transitioning to independent regional governance under the newly formed Regional Organization for Western Energy (ROWE), while SPP’s Markets+ and RTO West represent parallel options for utilities across the region, and states and stakeholders are actively shaping how these markets — and the transmission system that underpins them — will work for decades to come. These decisions will determine how quickly and cost-effectively the West can integrate clean energy, unlock resource diversity across state lines, and deliver reliable, affordable power to consumers. Advanced Energy United is looking for a Senior Principal who can represent advanced energy companies at this pivotal moment, ensuring that market and transmission rules are designed to accelerate — not hinder — the clean energy transition. The Senior Principal will support, and eventually lead, the organization’s advocacy related to western wholesale electricity market expansion and development. The role will have a primary focus on the development of the Regional Organization for Western Energy (ROWE) and its governance, markets, and services, and related initiatives at the California Independent System Operator (CAISO). Dependent on need and strategy, the Senior Principal may also engage in SPP Markets+ and RTO West, and in relevant non-market regional initiatives such as transmission planning, resource adequacy program design, and interregional coordination across the Western Interconnection. In addition to participation in specific market initiatives, the incumbent will work in education and advocacy regarding energy markets and regional coordination with individual Western utilities/balancing authorities and state decision makers. Responsibilities Lead the execution of United’s strategy on Western wholesale electricity market development and related initiatives, in collaboration with other policy team members. Work with the Senior Director to develop and refine strategy as needed. Serve as a consistent, credible face for Advanced Energy United across regional and state forums, bringing deep technical expertise and a constructive, solutions-oriented voice that builds trust with utilities, regulators, and other market participants, and reinforces the organization’s reputation as a pragmatic, non-partisan partner in advancing Western markets. Monitor and analyze emerging policy, regulatory, and governance developments affecting western electricity markets primarily, and to a lesser extent regional transmission planning. Assess market design proposals, identify opportunities to improve policies on behalf of the advanced energy industry, and develop relevant regulatory comments, testimony, policy briefs, and technical analyses. Prepare updates for regular member and partner communications. Organize the DER Sector within the Stakeholder Representatives Committee of the ROWE. Work with both United member and non-member companies to create sector structure and processes, select a representative of the DER Sector to serve on SRC (including potentially serving as the DER Sector representative), and participate in SRC processes. Monitor and engage on regional transmission planning initiatives (e.g., Western Transmission Expansion Collaborative and CAISO’s transmission planning process) as they intersect with market design. Build and maintain strong working relationships with policymakers, utilities, market operators, United member companies, coalition partners, and other relevant stakeholders. Work in coordination with coalition allies in support of policy goals. Collaborate with internal policy teams to ensure coordinated advocacy and align regional market strategies with state policy priorities. Support related organizational initiatives related to transmission planning, resource adequacy, interconnection reform, and wholesale market modernization. Work with United’s communications team to identify opportunities for United to seek earned media coverage. Write blogs, draft press statements, and participate in webinars or other externally facing opportunities. Mentor junior staff and contribute to organizational strategic planning. Travel on an as needed basis (up to 25%) around the region for stakeholder meetings, meetings with key allies, conferences, and other efforts on behalf of United. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in economics, engineering, public policy, law, environmental policy, or related field. Advanced degree preferred (or substitute additional market experience) 5+ years of professional experience in energy policy, with at least some of that experience focused on wholesale electricity markets, utility regulation, or transmission. Knowledge of Western wholesale electricity markets and regional market design a plus. Excellent analytical, writing, and presentation skills. Policy analysis experience applying legal, economic, or engineering analytic frameworks to structure compelling arguments. Entrepreneurial approach, performance orientation, flexible attitude, and ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Excellent interpersonal, relationship-building, and communications skills, both written and verbal. The employee is required to sit for long periods of time; reach with hands and arms; may need to balance, stoop, kneel or crouch, walk up and down stairs. Job type: Full-time, regular (residence in the U.S. required) Location: Remote. Must reside in the U.S., with a strong preference for residence in the West Start date: October 2026 Salary: Starting at $95,000 Advanced Energy United Perks Include: Remote work and flexible schedule Medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and their families Medical premiums covered for employees at 100% Flexible spending plans for health care and dependent care Profit sharing opportunities and annual merit-based compensation increases $75/month personal wellness reimbursement $50/month phone stipend Up to $200 reimbursement for home office set-up Accrued Paid Time Off, 11 federal holidays, and an annual end-of-year closure Parental Leave Professional development reimbursement 401(k) plan (with matching incentives) WMATA Transit Smart Benefits (DC, MD, VA employees) Advanced Energy United is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, sex, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. item.title: Senior Communications Director
item.description: Senior Communications Director Organization: American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) Location: Remote Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Salary Range: $185,000 – $215,000 POSITION DESCRIPTION The Senior Communications Director is a battle-tested campaign strategist and war-room leader who operates at the speed of political campaign news cycles. Reporting to the CEO and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, the Senior Communications Director leads an aggressive, high-velocity communications engine designed to win votes, persuade targeted policymakers, and shape national narratives across federal and state battlegrounds. The Senior Director pivots instantly as news breaks, executing intra-day rapid response, deploying high-impact spokespeople, driving rapid-turnaround paid, earned, and digital campaigns, and fiercely countering opponent narratives to advance ABIC’s mission and priorities. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES Proactive Narrative Framing & Campaign Execution Proactively define and drive ABIC’s national and battleground narrative; develop offensive messaging playbooks designed to persuade targeted policymakers, sway fence-sitters, and win key legislative votes on immigration solutions. Transform communications operations into a high-velocity daily campaign apparatus, constantly injecting ABIC’s narrative positioning into fast-moving news cycles to dictate media coverage across targeted state and federal markets. Rapid Response & War-Room Management Build and lead a nimble, war-room rapid-response capability to monitor breaking federal and state legislative and political developments, instantly draft counter-messaging, issue reactive press statements, and position ABIC spokespeople during high-velocity news cycles. Direct real-time media monitoring to deploy messaging, statements, and op-eds continuously throughout the day to drive headlines and control the narrative as news develops. Spokespeople Deployment & Management Build, train, and manage a rapid-deployment spokespeople group featuring business CEOs, influencers, and bipartisan coalition voices. Ensure ABIC spokespeople are prepped, cleared, and deployed onto broadcast, print, radio, and digital outlets within minutes of news breaking across key battlegrounds. Opposition Counter-Strategy & Narrative Defense Direct aggressive counter-messaging operations designed to neutralize opponent talking points, dismantle hostile narratives, and support ABIC’s priorities. Implement real-time digital and media intelligence to track opponent campaigns, identify narrative threats early, and launch immediate strategic counter-offensives. QUALIFICATIONS Campaign & War Room Record: Proven track record of executive leadership in senior-level political or issue campaigns, high-stakes advocacy war rooms, or fast-paced legislative fights. Rapid Response Track Record: Demonstrated experience operating in high-pressure, rapid-response political or media environments, with a track record of driving headlines and controlling narratives during fast-moving news cycles. Intra-Day Deployment Experience: Proven ability to manage daily media cycles, pre-clear high-level surrogates, and execute rapid response across TV, radio, digital, and print throughout the day. Legislative Persuasion Focus: Deep understanding of how to align communications strategy directly with vote-counting, policymaker persuasion, and constituency mobilization under tight deadlines. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Submit a resume and cover letter to [email protected] with the subject line: Senior Director of Communications_First Name, Last Name EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT ABIC is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. We strongly encourage candidates of all backgrounds, including those from communities directly affected by immigration policy, to apply. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS ABIC offers a competitive salary of $185,000 – $215,000, commensurate with experience, along with: 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance, plus 70% coverage for family Unlimited PTO and 11 paid company holidays 401(k) match up to 4% $1,000 annual Lifestyle Spending Account Additional benefits, including life and disability insurance, an Employee Assistance Program, telemedicine, and a monthly cell phone stipend, are outlined in full for candidates during the offer process. ABIC members include CEOs, retired CEOs, business associations, small business owners, as well as hospitals and universities. item.title: California State Director
item.description: California State Director Organization: American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) Location: Remote (CA) Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Salary Range: $80,000 – $105,000 Reports to: National Field Director ABOUT ABIC The American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) promotes common sense immigration reform that advances economic competitiveness, provides companies with the talent they need, and allows the integration of immigrants into our economy as consumers, workers, entrepreneurs, and citizens. ABIC members include CEOs, retired CEOs, business associations, small business owners as well as hospitals and universities. ABIC works in partnership with diverse immigrant advocates to support pro-immigrant legislation at the state and federal levels. For more information, visit https://abic.us. POSITION SUMMARY ABIC is seeking a California State Director to build business support for immigration reform locally and nationally, with a primary focus on California. Candidate must be based and reside in California. The State Director will develop and execute strategies to engage CEOs, trade associations, chambers of commerce, and small business leaders, as well as immigrant organizations, to advance bipartisan support for common-sense immigration solutions. This role requires strategic analysis, high-level relationship development, coalition building, and strong political judgment. The California State Director serves as a public-facing leader and plays a critical role in advancing ABIC’s campaigns to protect immigrants and expand economic opportunity. Successful Directors manage expectations and meet deadlines, organize and present timely data and information, maintain confidentiality, demonstrate honesty and trustworthiness, and make a solid positive impact. Effective Directors are self-motivated, responsible, agile team players who can work independently while collaborating closely with national staff and other state teams. RESPONSIBILITIES Strategic Leadership & Planning Develop and implement state and/or sector specific strategies aligned with federal campaign priorities, prioritizing STATE-specific strategies. Analyze the political and economic conditions affecting industries reliant on immigrant workforces. Map key business, political, and coalition stakeholders and prioritize engagement. Develop a distinct and unique center-right issue campaign approach tailored to California. Adapt strategies as new developments arise Relationship Building & Coalition Development Serve as a public‑facing leader for ABIC’s work in California. Build and manage relationships with CEOs, business leaders, trade organizations, chambers of commerce, and small business owners. Recruit business leaders to publicly support immigration reform efforts. Facilitate coalition calls, meetings, op‑eds, public letters, and press events. Government & Policy Engagement Develop relationships with federal, state and local lawmakers and their staff, across the state. Educate policymakers on business perspectives related to immigration reform. Ensure key business leaders are being engaged in policy and with policy makers to advance state or federal campaigns. Fundraising & External Relations Collaborate with the Director of Philanthropy to engage donors, corporate partners, and coalition supporters. Support fundraising efforts and donor engagement in California. Work with the communications team to develop media strategies and manage press engagement. Organizational Leadership Assist in the management of in-state consultants and ABIC staff. Collaborate with other state directors and national staff on strategy, tactics, and best practices. Ensure strong data management, tracking of coalition engagement, and internal coordination. QUALIFICATIONS Deep commitment to advocating for a path to citizenship and comfort advocating for undocumented immigrants. Experience working with a broad diversity of stakeholders, including CEOs, business leaders, and directly impacted individuals. 5–7 years of experience in political, advocacy, organizing, or fundraising roles. Experience building coalitions and executing issue campaigns. Experience engaging or educating government officials. Strong strategic thinking and political analysis skills. Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. Competency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Google Suite. Experience with EveryAction or similar CRM systems. Experience using data systems to manage member relationships and engagement. Familiarity with Asana or similar project management tools preferred. Spanish language proficiency is preferred but not required. ABIC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for employees. We do not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity), national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, age, status as a protected veteran, or other legally protected characteristics. Compensation: We offer a competitive compensation package. Please note all salaries are commensurate with experience. Compensation may be adjusted based on geographic location, including cost-of-living differentials for employees residing in higher-cost areas. ABIC also provides an attractive benefits package including health insurance, retirement plan, unlimited paid time off, and standard holidays. How to Apply: Please email your resume and cover letter to Angelene Winn, ABIC Director of Operations, at [email protected] and include “California State Director” in the subject line. The position will remain open until filled. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Digital Manager
item.description: Digital Manager Organization: American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) Location: Chicago, IL Date Posted: 10/26/2026 Salary Range: $80,000- $100,000 POSITION DESCRIPTION: ABIC’s Digital Manager is a social media and digital content leader who is both a strategic thinker and a hands-on content creator using impactful and targeted storytelling to grow and engage audiences across multiple platforms and inspire action. They manage and execute all aspects of ABIC’s social media presence, from strategy development and identifying key audience-specific platforms to content production, rapid response engagement, community growth, influencer engagement, and spokesperson social media training. The Digital Manager understands how to communicate complex immigration issues to diverse audiences and translate policy into compelling, accessible, platform-native content. This role supports the core work of ABIC, including stewardship of the ABIC brand and its sector-focused councils across agriculture, healthcare, construction, Hispanic communities, and food. The position is responsible for coordinating and executing initiatives that serve both the broader ABIC organization and its individual councils. Key responsibilities include managing and supporting a range of activities such as events, announcements, websites, and social media content that align with ABIC’s overall strategy while also addressing the unique needs of each council. This role requires balancing organization-wide priorities with council-specific efforts, at times operating within the ABIC umbrella and at other times supporting councils as distinct entities. The position is writing-intensive and requires strong content development skills, including drafting messaging, communications materials, and digital content across platforms. It also involves significant cross-team coordination, working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to ensure alignment and successful execution of initiatives. In addition, the role will develop and manage sector-focused media relationships, engaging with a range of voices such as social media influencers, traditional press, and industry-specific businesses to amplify ABIC’s visibility and impact across its priority sectors. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategic Leadership & Platform Management: Develop and implement a comprehensive multi-platform social media strategy aligned with ABIC’s mission and advocacy priorities, with audience growth, engagement, and support as a primary goal. Support the development and execution of hyperlocal and sector-specific digital campaigns and events that respond to legislative, media, and industry developments, creating tailored strategies to engage business leaders in specific regions and sectors. Turn complex immigration policy proposals, fact sheets, and research into accessible, engaging social content. Lead platform-specific daily content creation, developing messaging, videos, and other content assets for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, and emerging channels; manage platform budgets to maximize impact and reach. Determine best practices for timing, cadence, and content distribution using data and real-time indicators and platform trends on political digital culture. Ensure messaging alignment across platforms and teams, working in collaboration with the communications and campaign teams to deliver consistent, strategic narratives. Coordinate with external freelancers, videographers, and digital vendors, overseeing outreach, onboarding, collaboration, and content review as needed; manage external consultant for ABIC website updates. Media Strategy, Storytelling and Engagement: Produce high-impact short-form and long-form videos, graphics, explainers, and narrative digital content on a daily basis, owning content planning, creative direction, scripting, storyboarding, shooting, and editing. Use a variety of content strategies to develop clear, engagement-driven campaigns, challenges, live sessions, and interactive formats that reflect ABIC’s values and goals. Develop a vibrant, engaged online community that includes digital creators, immigrant advocates, entrepreneurs, business leaders, workers, policymakers, and aligned influencers who can amplify ABIC’s work. Manage cross-platform comments, messages, and audience engagement with an authentic, informative, mission-driven voice. Monitor political developments, news cycles, Congressional activity, and immigration-related trends to identify rapid-response moments and create and publish timely, accurate, compelling content within hours or minutes of key developments. Work closely with communications and campaign staff to surface real-time relevant business leader storytelling moments, ensuring they are strategically aligned with broader policy narrative and campaign efforts, and digital engagement is maximized. Support targeted storytelling and visibility campaigns at the state, local, and national levels, informing, equipping, and inspiring ABIC staff, coalition partners, and spokespeople (including immigrant leaders and business owners) on how to create and publish effective social content. Capture on-the-ground moments from ABIC events, briefings, and actions for rapid deployment. Create and manage an editorial calendar to maintain timelines, content calendars, and campaign milestones. Data and Tracking: Define, track, and analyze engagement data across social platforms to assess performance, refine messaging, and improve campaign impact, ensuring all communications are informed by audience behavior and campaign goals. Produce regular reports and analyze performance to refine strategy, using insights to optimize content formats, posting times, tone, and targeting. Monitor competitor and peer accounts for benchmarking and inspiration. Monitor national and state media and policy trends to identify timely opportunities to share business voices in alignment with campaign priorities. Maintain processes and systems for story sourcing, outreach timelines, content creation, and campaign delivery, ensuring consistency, speed, and collaboration across teams. Qualifications A deep commitment to advocating for a path to citizenship and comfort and ease advocating for undocumented immigrants. Knowledge of and background in immigration issues at national, state, and local levels is preferred but not required. A bachelor’s degree is required, with a minimum of 5 years’ experience in social media, digital content creation, or digital communications; public policy or organizing background preferred but not required. Proven track record of growing social audiences and producing high-performing content, especially on TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. Ability to record and edit videos in a fast-paced environment for social platforms Strong editorial judgment for when and how to respond to political, cultural, and media moments, and expertise in rapid response and real-time digital engagement. Strong writing and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate lived experience and business perspectives into persuasive, social media-ready content and experience supporting narrative campaigns and collaborating across internal teams and external stakeholders in a fast-paced environment. A deep understanding of social media strategies and comfort using engagement analytics to inform campaign decisions. Excellent organizational and project management skills, with a strong ability to manage competing priorities, timelines, and deliverables with precision. Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills, an ability to listen to and balance, negotiate and work with a variety of internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work effectively with colleagues coordinating relationship management and events with a broad team. Experience with, Google Analytics, LinkedIn, Muckrack, X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Hootsuite, and Sprout Social Competency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Google Suite, and Asana, or similar platforms. Skilled in video shooting, editing, and mobile/desktop production tools (Adobe Creative Cloud, CapCut, Canva, etc.). Experience with EveryAction or similar systems and the ability to utilize data systems to track performance and engagement. Ability to travel occasionally for events, shoots, and field content capture. ABOUT ABIC The American Business Immigration Coalition (ABIC) promotes common sense immigration reform that advances economic competitiveness, provides companies with both the high-skilled and low-skilled talent they need, and allows the integration of immigrants into our economy as consumers, workers, entrepreneurs, and citizens. ABIC members include CEOs, retired CEOs, business associations, small business owners as well as hospitals and universities. ABIC works in partnership with diverse immigrant advocates to support pro-immigrant legislation at the state and federal levels. For more information, visit https://abic.us. ABIC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for employees. We do not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity), national origin, political affilation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, age, status as a protected veteran, or other legally protected characteristics. Compensation: This position will be full-time. We offer a competitive compensation package. Please note all salaries are commensurate with experience. ABIC also provides an attractive benefits package including health insurance, retirement plan, unlimited paid time off, and standard holidays. How to Apply: Please email your resume and cover letter to Angelene Winn, ABIC Director of Operations, at [email protected] and include in the subject line “ABIC Digital Manager.” The position will remain open until fill
